docs.title: Dependency Management and Static Analysis
docs.text:
TESTING.md owns local audit commands. The workflow guide owns CI coverage. An audit covers installed packages and vulnerability information available at that run, not every optional environment or all possible vulnerabilities.

bandit.yaml records the current B610 exception. Review exceptions and findings against affected code. No repository-wide guarantee that every risky serialization or subprocess path has been audited is implied.

docs.title: Security Features and Limits
docs.text:
Structural validation, grammar admission, coherence scores and determinism serve mathematical or application contracts. They do not provide authentication, authorization, confidentiality or protection from hostile code. Applications must establish those boundaries for their deployment and data.

Security fixes should include a focused reproducer or regression where feasible, the affected trust boundary and any compatibility or cache migration requirement. Follow CONTRIBUTING.md for ordinary review and private reporting for undisclosed issues.

docs.title: TNFR Testing Guide
docs.text: This page owns local validation instructions. pyproject.toml defines tools and dependencies; the workflow guide describes CI, whose executable commands belong to the linked workflow YAML. Expected mathematics and contracts follow AGENTS.md and the source being tested. A passing test establishes its asserted behavior and domain, not a general physical theorem.

docs.title: Run the repository tests
docs.text:
Run commands from the repository root with the interpreter of a separate environment. Install the editable project and the dependency groups used by the main CI test job:

python -m pip install -e ".[test,numpy,yaml,orjson]"
python -m pytest

test is the compatibility alias for test-all; NumPy is already a core dependency. There are no dev or all extras. Smaller extras such as test-unit install only their declared tools and may not support collection of the whole repository. Aggregate extras reference the smaller groups so their dependency bounds have one owner; the compatibility alias does not maintain another dependency list. The maintained benchmark instruments are standalone CLIs, so these groups do not install pytest-benchmark. The test-performance extra remains available as an explicit optional plugin for downstream tests; it does not define a benchmark-directory test suite.

The default testpaths in pyproject.toml selects the routine engine gate: nodal execution, operator/grammar contracts, numerical admission, public diagnostics, caches, CLI and SDK. It includes the complete operator and SDK directories and the listed production-field owners. The broad historical research/certificate directories are not part of every routine run. Production Hilbert-space, projector, generator and auxiliary-runtime boundary tests are included even though their files live under tests/mathematics. CI also collects the complete retained inventory on Python 3.11, catching test module name collisions and import errors outside the routine execution gate. Collection alone does not execute fixtures or validate their assertions. pythonpath = ["src"] imports the working tree, and addopts = "-m 'not slow'" excludes marked slow cases. No custom collection plugin or second test registry is involved. The test dependency requires pytest 7.4 or newer, supporting the standard testpaths wildcard configuration.

Use the explicit root path for the complete retained inventory, or a research module/directory when its owner changes:

python -m pytest tests --collect-only -q
python -m pytest tests -q
python -m pytest tests/physics/test_phase_alignment_metric.py -q
python -m pytest tests/mathematics -q

Explicit paths take precedence over testpaths. Research tests remain executable evidence for retained conditional results; they have not been declared obsolete merely because they are outside the routine gate. Add a new production-field regression to testpaths when it belongs in that gate. A routine pass is not a claim that every mathematical campaign was replayed.

Choose affected mechanisms through the theory-to-execution map, then inspect their source and tests. That map links shared implementations, representative controls and theorem owners; this guide does not maintain a second inventory of research results or individual test cases.

For a repository-wide audit, preserve the starting working tree and review complete defect families across their actual consumers. A scalar-boundary fix needs both direct and adapter coverage; a rollback fix needs shared views, container nesting and restoration order. Pair invalid-domain controls with ordinary executions, independent expected values and the model's intentional rounding conventions. An unusual result is not a defect merely because a different model would reject it.

Collect the full inventory before broad execution. Choose the non-slow suites and any additional slow owners explicitly, preserving frozen-producer guards. Finish source changes and independent review before the final regression run; if code changes during that run, its result cannot alone validate the new source. Record the final interpreter, selection, skipped scope and checks. For long runs, retain verbose output and JUnit XML so failures remain identifiable before completion; keep a failed run's evidence when validating its corrections. Close the audit when reproduced defects in that scope are corrected and its checks pass, without interpreting that finite coverage as proof of no further bugs or of the physical claims.

docs.title: Shared evidence maintenance
docs.text:
The evidence workflow separates maintained artifact mechanics, model-specific audits and immutable archived programs. For changes to their shared owners, select exact-record, archive and restoration controls separately from scientific producers:

python -m pytest tests/research/test_artifact_io.py tests/research/test_frozen_source.py tests/scripts/test_restore_frozen_source.py tests/mathematics/test_validated_taylor_arithmetic.py tests/mathematics/test_validated_box_taylor.py tests/physics/test_sine_flow_kernel.py -q

Exercise duplicate/nonfinite JSON, exact tags before scalar comparison, unsafe or duplicate archive names, expanded-byte limits, altered hashes and refusal to replace an existing record. Restoration controls use disposable synthetic Git repositories and read-only inspection of the committed freeze. Verify the full pinned base, admitted supplemental files and destination rejection; do not create a real reserved workspace or invoke an evaluator during regression.

Retained Taylor reconstruction checks primitive shape/source admission and Horner/remainder/endpoint arithmetic. It does not prove stored derivative enclosures or replace a consumer's source, law, event or strict Picard checks. The shared sine field still needs independent edge-sum and jet controls for its layouts and held coefficients. Select changed consumers and existing read-only evidence audits in addition to these shared tests.

Exact arithmetic controls must include fractions carrying fixed-width integer components, alongside ordinary Python integers. Normalize admitted components before matrix products, interval rounding, comparison flows and Taylor powers; otherwise overflow can invalidate an enclosure or a positivity certificate. Equivalent representations must retain the same mathematical bounds without widening each kernel's admitted scalar or container domain.

Reuse expensive parsed records and archive bytes through module-scoped fixtures; copy a fixture before a mutation test. Pure test helpers must not import other test modules' autouse fixtures. Keep no-execution guards scoped and reversible, so an audit cannot leak patched producers or subprocess calls into unrelated tests. Overrides inside an execution guard must unwind before the guard itself; check restoration in the same process as subsequent evidence readers. Historical report keys such as current refer to their recorded source. Rebuild their summaries from retained primitive captures; a present-engine wiring test needs a distinct protocol identity and its actual pressure path. Shared arithmetic must not collapse a producer and its independent mathematical expectation into the same implementation. Current-code regression does not update frozen evidence or authorize the pending research response.

docs.title: Grammar and scoped-program integration
docs.text:
Select the shared owner and its public consumers together. Operator changes need direct glyph, public class and atomic-stage coverage where supported; word changes need initialized and uninitialized grammar, live target/history, accepted-prefix behavior and strict rejection controls. Runtime and program boundaries belong to operator events and program execution.

Exercise signed scalar and circular phase admission before diagnostics or mutation. Test observed Mutation secants, immutable stage snapshots, all-target preflight, graph-owned atomic commit and restoration boundaries. A valid word does not promise increasing coherence or future stability. Optional callbacks, monitors, activity policies and pressure refresh must match the studied path.

docs.title: Select research checks by contract
docs.text:
Use the theory-to-execution map to select the affected proof, shared implementation and test owners. Inspect those tests before invoking them: explicit research paths override the routine testpaths, and a producer's availability does not authorize new evaluated responses.

Changed responsibility Required checks State, pressure, phase or capacity admission Primitive invalid/finite domains, alias authority, boundary values, every consumed row and actual clocks; keep held and refreshed pressure distinct Exact identity or theorem Independent incidence/matrix calculations or counterexamples, all hypotheses, branch/lift choices and unavailable domains; the theorem's scope is not proved by a literal fixture Numerical certificate Outward bounds, independent high-precision controls, source inclusion, arithmetic/representation limits, residuals and explicit failure or unavailability Event or collective action Actual support and weights, same-snapshot proposal, live policy/history, complete work and successor law; continuous closure alone does not admit an event Memory, reduction or observation Hidden initialization/input, actual observation map, consumed internal correlations and finite prediction errors; equal summaries need not predict equal futures Frozen evidence reader Read-only primitive/source reconstruction, original failures and verdicts, archive integrity and no-producer guards; never regenerate evidence to make a check pass CLI, SDK or export adapter Wiring separately from costly scientific execution, strict JSON/availability, shared kernels, cold imports and source/configuration provenance

For the organized-source word, independent passivity, joint mean/form budgets and scalar capacity recurrence have separate owners. Include asymmetric states, unequal positive capacities and nonzero means. Exact event work, sequential binary64 capacity products and complete represented execution are distinct. A scalar capacity count is not repeated-word execution or autonomous renewal.

Do not replay the retained collective pressure-handoff producer during routine regression: its original unresolved interval-width outcome remains evidence. Likewise, the prepared-envelope, relative-probe and maintained-successor instruments keep their frozen protocols, budgets and response permissions. Select their read-only evidence consumers for documentation or parser changes. The research program's current question alone schedules new research evaluation under its stated admission conditions.

docs.title: Boundaries that need explicit regression coverage
docs.text:
Boundary Required distinction and controls Primitive admission Reject Boolean/nonfinite physical scalars, malformed support, stale state and unrepresentable arithmetic before a solver, cache or reserved sample is consumed. Preserve each owner's domain and work caps. Rebuilt evidence Alter primitive source/law fields independently of cached bounds and favorable flags. Recompute all consumed derived fields; equality of projected values is not source authentication. Exact geometry Test zero resultants, circular cuts, strict equality and unresolved denominators. Rounded pi, a small residual or overlapping intervals does not establish an exact equilibrium, symmetry or antipodal state. Correlated uncertainty Retain source balls, mean/parity correlations, phase lifts and observation budgets. Coordinate boxes and projections cannot silently replace the set consumed downstream. Include small positive errors below an interval grid. Complete evolution Check both form and phase rows, transformed clocks, source terms, conserved means and actual support weights. Derive expected rows independently from edges, including asymmetric and multiply connected cases. Reduction and memory Vary hidden/internal state at fixed collective observations. Retain initial conditions, fast transients, port association, generated discarded modes, memory and nonlinear remainder. Tangent invariance need not close the nonlinear law. Events and work Check the actual pre-event state, jump, storage work and changed mean leaf. Continuous loss cannot fund an event without a reservoir law. An admitted jump or controller does not establish autonomous occurrence. Formation and maintenance Separately check initial absence, entry, whole-window identity, boundary exchange, retention and later response. Exact invariant-family membership or local stability does not prove acquisition. Partial and all-time claims Preserve completed horizon, original requested horizon, channel-specific resolution and unavailable bounds. Finite tracking, convergence and cross-flow contraction are different claims; a failed sufficient margin is not an observed trajectory failure. Controls and alternatives Match the complete source, law, clock and information budget. Keep counterexamples to omitted premises, including low-storage nonconsensus states, phase-blind response and same-observation/different-future states. Classification Verify independent critical states, Hessian directions and domain boundaries. Numerical case enumeration does not replace a completeness proof; positive-loss results cannot be transferred to zero loss. Observation and export Preserve unavailable fields, exact fractions and source associations. Test read-only behavior, actual report types, atomic output and cold imports separately from expensive scientific execution.

For collective formation, a common center or bounded distance on a finite support cannot alone distinguish a composite from ordinary passage. Retain actual relative geometry, primitive phase and internal/boundary state; constituent shapes and trajectories may change. Require an independently specified signal floor, an initially absent identity and a discriminating continued response without resetting the acquired state.

A validated reduction must dominate its approximation and preparation errors on the claimed horizon. Keep full-form and phase margins separate, check strict first-exit or Picard conditions, and retain operator order in noncommuting convolutions. Failed certification leaves that claim unavailable. It does not justify changing an evaluated allowance or replaying a frozen producer.

Model-specific coordinate caps, coefficients and acceptance inequalities belong to their mathematical/contract owners. Read those premises when selecting coverage; the shared checklist does not broaden any theorem's domain.

docs.title: Current checks and retained evidence
docs.text:
Distinguish three kinds of validation when a research owner changes:

  • Current-source contracts: shared engine, SDK or CLI behavior, including numerical admission, unsupported domains, read-only behavior and atomicity.
  • Mathematical controls: independent identities, counterexamples and exact coefficient probes under their hypotheses. Rational probes do not replace the actual irrational constants in an ideal theorem.
  • Retained evidence audits: frozen inputs, source fingerprints, saved intervals/checkpoints and original verdicts, without producer replay. Current-source regression is separate from historical execution evidence.

The evidence workflow owns artifact mechanics and restoration; the benchmark guide owns declared producer invocation. Source archives and content digests associate records with declared code; they do not authenticate chronology or independently revalidate omitted numerical steps. Follow the particular result owner's retained-execution premises.

For example, the formed C9 bundle audit checks committed records without replaying their producers. Its shared synthetic helper controls are selected separately:

python -m pytest tests/physics/test_sine_formed_evidence.py tests/research/test_sine_evidence_helpers.py -q

The evidence helpers supply reusable test mechanics, not an alternative source of mathematical conclusions. Reuse parsed records through module fixtures and isolate mutations. Synthetic intervals and stubbed producers test consumer logic, not the execution of the historical run.

Preserve every original failure, partial result and inconclusive verdict. An export-recovery recomputation keeps its separate source and history; a later successful record cannot become a successful first attempt. New analytical handoffs or tighter current bounds leave the original evaluated response intact. Missing committed artifacts fail their audit. Optional local records may cause an explicit skip, never an inferred pass or automatic regeneration.

Local execution is serial by default. The main CI scheduling policy is python -m pytest -n 2 --dist loadfile, retaining not slow. Files stay on one worker to reuse module fixtures; workers isolate Python state. Timing benchmarks need a separate serial run.

Choose an affected directory, module or test for bounded validation:

python -m pytest tests/core_physics -q
python -m pytest tests/operators/test_u3_hard_invariant.py -q
python -m pytest tests/sdk -q
python -m pytest tests/cli -q
python -m pytest tests/sdk --collect-only -q

To include all retained slow tests, use python -m pytest tests -o addopts="". To select only marked slow tests, pass their paths and -m slow. Inspect python -m pytest --markers and collection: a registered marker can select no tests. Standalone scripts need the editable installation or an explicit PYTHONPATH=src; pytest's source-path configuration does not reach them.

docs.title: Organization
docs.text:
tests/ contains top-level modules and subject directories. Search for the affected API rather than maintaining another inventory of individual tests. Core nodal behavior is in core_physics/, operators in operators/, specialized certificates in physics/ and public network usage in sdk/. CLI integration checks the same study recipe through Python and the module entry point, including malformed input, diagnostic availability, output replacement and logging isolation. Catalog checks do not execute a study. conftest.py and utils.py own shared helpers. The core scope map identifies the engine tests that replace retired self-contained illustrations.

Consolidation removes work, not just collected test identifiers. Test each invalid boundary at its shared owner, then retain distinct consumer-wiring, rollback and representation cases instead of repeating the entire Cartesian product at every wrapper. Reuse an expensive producer only when its results are read without mutation; keep independent numerical oracles and negative controls. Do not turn removed parameter grids into hidden loops or replace meaningful assertions with finiteness checks. Operator labels alone do not justify energy-sign or conservation assertions with arbitrary tolerances.

The maintained standalone arithmetic utility has a separate test path:

python -m pytest applications/primality-test/tests -q

Run it separately because its local import root differs from the core suite. The root default selection does not include it. The primality guide owns setup and scope. The factorization lab and advanced primality adapters are archived, outside the maintained test surface and automatic regression mappings. Their retained tests are recovery material, not release gates. Core arithmetic/Paley proofs and tests remain maintained. Compatibility tests exercise absent/external-package admission without executing the retired lab.

Research producers under benchmarks/ have declared entry points and provenance requirements; a default pytest run does not implicitly cover them. Do not regenerate retained evidence for an unrelated change.

For examples with run_protocol and build_report, reuse the real report through a module fixture for numerical and scope checks. The shared example helper checks main separately with a sentinel protocol and synthetic report, without rerunning a scientific producer.

Reusable independent oracles belong in test support modules rather than in another collected test suite. The pair oracle helper shares fine support, exact jets and high-precision reductions without importing production certificates or pytest fixtures. Each consuming suite retains its own complete-law assumptions, preparation budgets and module-scoped reports. When optimizing a shared certificate kernel, compare complete exact projections on representative available and unavailable cases as well as these independent controls; timing differences alone cannot establish unchanged evidence.

Runtime facade tests own the two cold import orders for the P2/REMESH example families; those checks still use fresh processes and resolve the actual public APIs.

Cold subprocesses that test this checkout explicitly request the source_tree_environment fixture from conftest.py and pass it as subprocess.run(..., env=source_tree_environment). It copies the process environment and prepends pytest's configured source paths to PYTHONPATH, without changing the parent's environment. Pytest's pythonpath setting only updates its own interpreter; a fresh Python process can otherwise import a different installed package. Keep the fixture opt-in: tests of installed-package discovery or intentional import isolation retain their declared environments. Working directories, timeouts and optimized-mode flags remain test-specific.

The Makefile target make test uses the routine engine selection; make test-all includes the retained research suites, still excluding slow. make dev-test adds coverage over src, including compatibility shims. Research producers use the individually documented entry points in the benchmark guide, not a directory-wide pytest campaign. make validate checks importability, references, documentation integrity and SDK tests.

docs.title: Structural regression evidence
docs.text:
Assert the contract of the changed path. Record representation, graph/support, coefficients, primitive triad, input history, step size and operator sequence as relevant. An operator jump and a continuous solver step need different expected results. For a full grammar word, verify initiation, closure and contextual admission; distinguish fragments explicitly.

Do not assume all operators increase coherence or that SHA freezes every later EPI update. Its capacity attenuation, pure-EPI diffusion and a multichannel trajectory have different scopes. Inspect the operator contracts and grammar scope before asserting an invariant. Initialization may set fixture state directly; test subsequent evolution through the API under review.

When stochastic behavior changes, control the RNG and record its seed, initial state and execution order. A seed alone does not fix timestamps, external data or every backend. When relevant, compare available tetrad fields with estimator provenance and unavailable-field reasons. Diagnostic scores are not acceptance thresholds unless that specific policy is being tested.

docs.title: Backends and optional dependencies
docs.text:
tests/conftest.py accepts --math-backend and TNFR_TEST_MATH_BACKEND. The command-line option takes precedence; the selected value sets TNFR_MATH_BACKEND and clears the backend cache before collection.

python -m pytest tests/mathematics/test_backends.py --math-backend=numpy -q -rs

Install compute-jax or compute-torch before requesting those optional adapters. Explicit per-test backend requests are not replaced by the session setting. Review skip reasons with -rs and report adapters actually exercised. NumPy is required by the shared conftest; a missing installation is not evidence of successful NumPy-free execution.

docs.title: Code quality and documentation checks
docs.text:
Install tools needed for the check; options are configured in pyproject.toml:

python -m pip install -e ".[dev-minimal,test-quality,typecheck]"
python -m black --check src/tnfr
python -m flake8 src
python -m pydocstyle src/tnfr
python -m mypy src/tnfr
python -m pyright src/tnfr

Pass affected files for a focused edit where supported. Black and isort use 88 columns; pydocstyle uses NumPy conventions. CI's advisory checks are listed in the workflow guide. make format modifies files; it is not a read-only validation step.

The lazy physics namespace has one maintained export map and a generated typing facade. After changing that map, run python scripts/generate_physics_stub.py --write; validate it with python scripts/generate_physics_stub.py --check. The generator reads the source AST without importing TNFR, and the facade tests check typed exports, runtime object identity and cold import boundaries.

For shared relational report export, select tests/sdk/test_relational_reports.py. Preserve every registered owner-managed type, actual-class and subclass admission, native label validation, exact fractions and unavailable fields. Cold-process controls must show that export does not import unrelated research owners. Use guarded zero-horizon reports or synthetic wiring for producer-backed types; an SDK export test must not regenerate a selected scientific response.

Optional pre-commit setup requires installing pre-commit separately before pre-commit install. .pre-commit-config.yaml configures Black, isort, pydocstyle and a local Bandit-command guard. That guard uses Bash, which must be available on Windows. The hooks do not perform a code review; CI's formatting gate checks all tracked files selected by those hooks.

For Markdown-only changes, use the relevant reference check. For site or documentation-infrastructure changes, also run integrity and build checks:

python scripts/verify_internal_references.py --ci
python scripts/check_documentation.py
python -m pip install -e ".[docs]"
python scripts/prepare_docs.py
python -m mkdocs build --strict

The reference checker accepts --dirs followed by files or directories, including logical research chapter paths, to bound the check; an unknown selected path fails instead of silently checking nothing. The staging script validates the modular catalog and canonical chapter files before replacing build/docs-source/, then stages the small program, chapters at their original routes and other repository owners. MkDocs renders that generated source into site/. Chapter links and frozen evidence associations retain their original contexts. Edit canonical research chapters directly, or use the optional reader workflow in Contributing, never either generated tree. The documentation stager queries Git once for recursive source trees: tracked files remain eligible even when an ignore pattern matches, and untracked nonignored work remains eligible. Git-ignored generated artifacts are omitted. The existing extension and directory rules still apply within the repository; names of parent directories do not exclude maintained sources. An extracted source tree without Git metadata uses those positive rules alone; a failed inventory in a Git checkout stops before replacing the previous stage.

The documentation integrity check also validates the theory catalog, its generated navigation, operator contracts, grammar roles and glossary cards/index. Its 4,000-line limit applies to each chapter, program and maintained guide; the program also has a 96-KiB file budget to prevent a return to a corpus-sized preview. Research storage changes need the tests/scripts/test_research_book*.py contracts plus the affected documentation and retained-evidence readers, without replaying scientific producers. Regenerate views with python scripts/check_documentation.py --write-generated after changing their source declarations, then rerun the read-only check. It executes the Python block in the README's Quick start section and compares its captured output with that section's declared output. Publication metadata uses the same strict JSON reader as the engine, including duplicate-key rejection.

docs.title: Package content and size checks
docs.text:
Use the release extra and inspect both built package formats before publication:

python -m pip install -e ".[release]"
python -m build
python scripts/check_distribution.py dist
python -m twine check dist/*

The distribution check compares package modules, stubs and schemas with the checkout, admits only the intended archive paths and rejects linked or malformed members. Its report exposes compressed and expanded sizes. Default review budgets are 10 MiB compressed per archive, 32 MiB expanded per archive and 1 MiB per file. A budget is a packaging review threshold, not a mathematical or performance limit; inspect unexpected contents before deliberately changing the configured limits. Use --help for the supported overrides.

This checks the wheel and source distribution built for PyPI. Repository source archives and the documentation site have different contents and size requirements; see publication payloads. Frozen scientific evidence must retain its original bytes and dependencies. Removing it merely to meet a package budget would not validate the package.

docs.title: Lightweight development bundle
docs.text:
Every release also delivers TNFR-<version>-light-development.zip and its .zip.sha256 sidecar as GitHub release assets. This is the minimum development handoff for another agent: code, theory, ontology, documentation, instructions, examples and tests from the selected commit, without Git history or installed dependencies. The builder derives the version from that commit, not the live working tree, and excludes bulky docs/assets/ evidence while retaining the site's mathjax.js. Omitted evidence remains in the full repository/Zenodo archive and is individually recorded for retrieval; omission does not authorize deleting or regenerating frozen results.

Build an initial candidate from a committed tree with Python 3.11+ and Git:

python scripts/build_development_bundle.py --revision HEAD --output-dir artifacts/development-bundle

For publication, set --revision to the exact release commit/tag and pass --expected-tag with the actual release tag. The tag must be v followed by the version declared by that tree. Keep this output separate from dist/; the bundle is not a PyPI distribution.

Before accepting each release bundle:

  1. Verify the archive and sidecar, selected commit/version, byte-exact retained files, mirrored agent instructions and the declared omitted-evidence manifest.
  2. Extract into a fresh directory. Read generated START_HERE.md and AGENTS.md and run python scripts/development_bundle_evidence.py verify there. The standard-library helper checks retained files and reports missing evidence explicitly; its list and fetch commands support retrieval of original evidence by pinned revision and SHA256.
  3. Follow onboarding to install dependencies and run the README example and affected contract checks. Report the actual environment and selection; checksum verification does not execute the engine or validate research. Research checks needing omitted files require those files to be retrieved first. Do not substitute missing evidence with regenerated responses.

The publication workflow independently builds the bundle and verifies its extracted contents without installing engine dependencies. A manual run retains it as an Actions artifact; a release run also attaches the ZIP and sidecar to the release. The source archive and existing Zenodo integration remain the full evidence distribution; no separate Zenodo deposit is required for this development handoff.

docs.title: Security checks
docs.text:
Follow SECURITY.md for reporting and trust boundaries:

python -m pip install -e ".[security]"
python -m pip_audit
python -m bandit -r src -c bandit.yaml

The dependency audit covers installed packages, including extras actually installed; it does not automatically cover every optional dependency. Bandit's configured exception is recorded in bandit.yaml. A clean report does not guarantee that dependencies or code contain no vulnerabilities.

docs.title: Validation workflow and reporting
docs.text:
1. Identify the affected contract and existing owners. Reproduce a suspected bug before the fix when feasible; distinguish a new counterexample from a measured baseline.
  2. Add meaningful regression coverage when behavior or an important boundary changes. A small documentation correction need not add numerical tests.
  3. Run affected checks. Broaden to dependents, optional backends or the default suite when changed scope or a failure justifies it. Do not rerun unrelated expensive research producers as a routine checklist item.
  4. Report actual commands, interpreter and relevant dependency versions, pass/fail/skip counts, warnings and untested scope. Do not label a failure pre-existing without baseline evidence.

The structural_rng fixture supplies NumPy's generator with seed zero. structural_tolerances supplies atol=1e-12 and rtol=1e-10; these are not exact-theorem eligibility gates. Choose scale-appropriate numerical tolerances and keep them distinct from represented exact equality. The autouse cleanup resets selected global state; restore additional state your test changes.

Coverage is feedback, not proof of a physical invariant. With test dependencies installed, a selected run can generate a report:

python -m pytest tests/sdk --cov=tnfr --cov-report=term-missing

The current project configuration does not enforce a coverage percentage. The Python 3.11 CI job instead uses --cov=src to retain the whole source-directory scope, with -n 2 --dist loadfile. Pytest-cov combines the workers' data and produces terminal and XML reports. Do not wrap distributed pytest with coverage run: that alone measures the controller instead of combining worker execution. Coverage of Python subprocesses launched inside tests is a separate configuration and is not enabled here.

docs.title: Retained C6 campaign reproduction
docs.text:
The union/history report tests that reconstruct the retained B54/B55 lineage are marked slow, including tests whose shared fixtures perform that work. These fixtures can be costly; inspect their declared scope and budget before selection. Previous timings are not runtime ceilings. Lightweight lineage and output-overwrite rejection tests remain available when their research paths are selected; the finite-state union oracles run independently of the retained campaign. C6 is outside the routine engine gate.

Select the expensive report checks explicitly:

python -m pytest -m slow tests/physics/test_c6_winding_union_report.py tests/physics/test_c6_winding_history_report.py -q

For the independent small-state controls:

python -m pytest tests/physics/test_c6_carried_return_unions.py -q

This classification changes selection by cost, not assertions or scientific scope. Report the expensive campaign as unrun when omitted, and retain failures from earlier attempts. A passing reduced suite does not certify the historical report or close C6 global stability.

docs.title: GitHub Actions Workflows
docs.text: This page owns the workflow inventory. Linked YAML is authoritative for triggers, permissions, conditions and commands. TESTING.md owns local validation instructions. Configuration describes what a run attempts; it does not establish current GitHub run health, branch protection or enabled secrets.

docs.title: Maintained workflows
docs.text:
Workflow Trigger and configured scope ci.yml Push and PR to main/master. Blocking formatting hooks, flake8 and default pytest selection on Python 3.10–3.13 with two pytest-xdist workers; combined coverage report on 3.11. Pydocstyle, mypy, pyright and vulture report advisories. docs.yml Filtered push/PR to main and manual invocation. References, documentation integrity, staging and strict MkDocs build; publishes Pages only on pushes to main. verify-references.yml Filtered Markdown/notebook changes on PRs and pushes to main/develop. Independent local Markdown target and fragment check. pip-audit.yml Push/PR to main/master, Monday 05:00 UTC and manual invocation. Audits the installed core, test-all and serialization environment; captures available reports and fails when the JSON audit fails. pypi-zenodo.yml Published GitHub release or manual invocation. Builds/checks PyPI distributions and an independent lightweight development bundle. Publishes to PyPI on release or when the existing manual force-publish input is true; attaches the bundle only on release events. lint-workflows.yml Filtered workflow/script changes on PRs and pushes to main. Searches for unsupported Bandit SARIF invocation; this is not a general Actions schema linter. copilot-setup-steps.yml Manual invocation or edits to its own workflow. Installs a Python 3.11 development/test environment and verifies importability.

Black and isort hooks exclude docs/assets/, build/, the archived applications/factorization-lab/ and applications/primality-test/archive/. These retain frozen programs or historical source outside the maintained execution surface. Their bytes must remain available for provenance and recovery checks; formatting maintained sources does not authorize rewriting those copies.

The default pytest selection is the routine engine/API gate and excludes slow tests as configured in pyproject.toml. The full retained research inventory is collected on Python 3.11 to detect import and test-name collisions, but its research fixtures are not executed by that collection. Execution is explicitly selected with pytest tests; it is not replayed by every CI job. CI does not declare a universal coverage percentage, prove physical theorems or certify every optional backend. Audit coverage excludes optional compute, documentation and deployment environments unless their dependencies happen to be installed through the declared groups.

The factorization lab and advanced primality adapters are retired, not implicit CI or self-optimization regression targets. The basic primality utility has the separate maintained test selection in TESTING.md.

The main test matrix uses -n 2 --dist loadfile; worker scheduling changes execution order, not test selection or assertions. Each file stays on one worker, so its module fixtures are reused across its tests. Workers own separate Python state and session fixtures. Tests that write files must retain independent temporary paths. Python 3.11 uses pytest-cov to combine worker coverage over src. The existing configuration does not enable coverage of separate Python subprocesses launched by tests.

Pytest-benchmark automatically disables timing measurements under xdist, while still running benchmarked functions and their assertions. The current tests/ suite has no consumers of its benchmark fixture; this matrix is not a timing benchmark. Run future performance measurements separately without xdist.

Each Python test job attempts to retain its JUnit report for 14 days, including when tests fail. The 3.11 job also retains its combined coverage XML when produced. A report from an interrupted run covers only the tests reached; its presence does not establish completion or success.

docs.title: Documentation publication
docs.text: The documentation workflow validates repository sources, stages them through prepare_docs.py, builds with strict MkDocs settings and publishes that site on eligible pushes. PRs validate without publication. Changes to either operator contracts or grammar roles also trigger the gate, so registry edits cannot bypass checks of their generated documentation tables. Edit source owners, not generated site copies. The site includes retained evidence and linked source files. Recursive staging uses the checkout inventory to omit ignored generated artifacts while retaining tracked evidence and untracked nonignored work; source archives without Git retain the declared positive copy rules. See the staging checks. Pages publishes site/ to gh-pages with force_orphan: true, replacing the deployment history rather than accumulating a copy of every former site.

docs.title: Package publication
docs.text:
pypi-zenodo.yml installs the checkout and its declared core dependencies with the build tools so metadata validation can use the shared JSON reader. It then checks publication metadata and, for a release event, requires the tag to match the declared package version. It then performs build, distribution content/size and Twine checks and publishes using the repository secret PYPI_API_TOKEN, which must contain an API token scoped to the tnfr PyPI project. This token-based path disables attestations and does not request an OIDC token; it does not provide trusted-publishing attestations. It neither creates a release nor runs the numerical test suite. Release preparation must consider relevant validation evidence; the workflow does not itself enforce a dependency on successful CI runs. A normal manual invocation builds/checks only; its existing force-publish input enables publishing.

An independent development-bundle job uses the standard-library builder scripts/build_development_bundle.py to create the mandatory TNFR-<version>-light-development.zip and .zip.sha256 from the checked-out commit. It validates the release tag/version and verifies the extracted bundle with its included evidence helper. It requires neither PyPI credentials nor engine dependencies, and its output is outside dist/. Both manual and release runs retain an Actions artifact. Only release events attach the ZIP and sidecar to the existing release; only this job has contents: write. Existing matching assets are accepted by size and SHA256; conflicting assets fail without overwriting. This job's checksum/extraction checks do not replace the onboarding and selected execution checks required during release preparation.

Publishing a GitHub release therefore also requests PyPI publication. Before that trigger, review validation runs for the exact commit being released: blocking CI formatting/static checks and its test matrix (including SDK tests), the dependency audit, and the documentation/reference checks selected by that commit's paths. Check the workflow-invocation lint result when it is triggered. A skipped, cancelled or absent run is not a passing result, and success on an earlier revision does not validate the release commit. Advisory findings remain advisory; assess their relevance without presenting them as enforced gates.

The final Zenodo step only prints a reminder. A separately configured external integration may archive a release; this workflow does not upload an archive or verify a DOI. No GitHub/PyPI/Zenodo settings are inferred from this file.

docs.title: Published payloads
docs.text:
Output Contents and publication path PyPI wheel Installable tnfr package, typing/schema data and package metadata. The publication job uploads built distributions; it does not upload the repository or site. PyPI source distribution Maintained build inputs selected by MANIFEST.in, including package source and small root metadata. Research evidence, tests, generated sites and optional application trees are outside this package payload. Lightweight development ZIP Exact source snapshot for agent/developer handoff: code, theory, documentation, instructions, examples and tests, with generated onboarding, a manifest and verified retrieval of omitted docs/assets/ evidence. The publication workflow attaches it and its SHA256 sidecar to each GitHub release. It contains neither Git history nor installed dependencies. GitHub source ZIP/TAR The release tag's repository tree, including committed research evidence. GitHub's source downloads are distinct from wheel/sdist assets and do not contain Git history. Zenodo archive The complete source archive retained through the separately configured GitHub integration. The lightweight development ZIP does not replace this evidence archive or require another deposit. Verify the actual version DOI and archive after publication. Documentation site Rendered documentation plus retained downloadable source/evidence, deployed separately to gh-pages. Its size is not the installed package size. Actions reports JUnit, coverage and dependency-audit reports retained by their respective jobs; they are not package contents or release archives.

Repository archives can grow as frozen responses and source snapshots are retained. A compressed evidence archive may expand substantially, and repeated source records can be required to reproduce different evaluated runs. Preserve those records rather than treating all archive growth as generated waste. Review the distribution check's contents and byte sizes to identify which payload actually changed.

docs.title: Research verification boundary
docs.text: Ordinary CI exercises the declared engine/API selection. Research campaigns use the explicitly selected owners in Testing and benchmarks. A routine pass is not an automatic benchmark, reproducibility certificate or replay of every retained experiment. Retirement and recovery records belong to the archive, not this workflow inventory.

docs.title: Maintenance rules
docs.text: Keep dependency groups and interpreter matrices consistent with pyproject.toml. Check referenced paths and distinguish advisory steps from gates. When retiring automation, preserve useful evidence and update this inventory. Never report a past finding count, external setting or passing run as a permanent property of the repository.

docs.title: Pull request template
Problem and resulting behavior
Scope
Validation
Review notes
docs.text:
• [ ] I checked affected definitions and existing implementation owners.
  • [ ] This description reports validation actually performed and its limits.
  • [ ] Relevant documentation and meaningful regression coverage are updated, or their absence is explained.

See CONTRIBUTING.md and TESTING.md. For undisclosed vulnerabilities, follow SECURITY.md.

docs.title: TNFR: contributor and agent instructions
docs.text: TNFR Python Engine 0.0.3.9. Rules for changing the repository and evaluating its claims. Keep .github/agents/my-agent.md byte-identical to this file. The README introduces TNFR; the owner map routes definitions, contracts and implementation work.

docs.title: 1. Scientific and editorial responsibility
docs.text:
TNFR investigates organized mathematical objects: their identity, dynamics, interactions and emergent properties under explicit premises. Develop these foundations using the NFR ontology, without prescribing the investigation's outcome. Networks represent constituents and relations; graph construction alone does not establish an object's identity or collective behavior. The engine, conditional mathematics and finite computational evidence support this work. Proofs and numerical experiments do not constitute empirical validation; a uniquely selected fundamental law remains open.

Justify canonical TNFR structure and dynamics against definitions, hypotheses, derivations and counterexamples; neither a manuscript nor a runtime registry establishes their necessity. Evaluate implemented claims against these premises, then implementation and relevant tests. Code establishes implemented behavior, not mathematical truth; labels, summaries and filenames prove nothing. Foundational and constitutive premises remain revisable: identify the affected model and scope, preserving valid conditional results and counterexamples.

  • Use English for code, documentation, comments, commits, issues and PRs; preserve verbatim quotations and raw data in their original language.
  • Lead reader-facing explanations with registered English operator names, such as Emission (AL) and Coherence (IL). Use simple glyph codes without apostrophes for compact words and formulas; derive names from the registry.
  • Distinguish definitions, supplied laws, derived identities, conditional theorems, finite observations, policies and open hypotheses.
  • Explain the present model directly. Definitions belong with their chapters, usage in guides and task status in the research program; overviews are neither delivery logs nor copies of derivations.
  • Arithmetic encodings, graph analogies, auxiliary Hamiltonians and diagnostic scores retain their own premises. External identifications require an independent model and measurement bridge.
  • Accept changes against the relevant contract. Corrections and negative results need not increase coherence or support a preferred interpretation.

docs.title: 2. Foundations
docs.text:
Write x=EPI, p=DeltaNFR. The unforced continuous nodal row is

\[\frac{\partial\mathrm{EPI}}{\partial t}=\nu_f\,\Delta\mathrm{NFR}.\]

A complete model specifies pressure and every consumed phase, capacity, support, clock, input and event law. Holding a quantity fixed is an explicit premise. Do not invent or coerce coordinates the model does not consume.

  • Form: signed real EPI and uniform-real BEPIElement use shared signed-scalar admission. Complex/nonuniform BEPI or magnitude projection cannot substitute for signed form.
  • Capacity: nonnegative. Zero freezes the unforced form row even at nonzero pressure, not the complete state. Inverse-mass identification needs its own model and measurement bridge.
  • Phase: circular; use wrapped differences and shared U3 admission. A form-derived regional angle is not primitive phase unless the complete law preserves that identification.
  • Pressure: an independently specified driver. Reconstructing p=x_dot/nu_f from the evaluated response is circular and fails at zero capacity. The nodal identity does not uniquely select a pressure mixture.
  • Clock: declare it and retain [p]=[x]/([nu_f][t]). Transform every evolution row under a clock change. Structural rates need a laboratory-unit bridge; synchronization need not define a monotone clock.
  • Support and identity: distinguish supplied state, initialization, admitted events, formation, maintenance and physical identification. Define an NFR's identity and evolution; nesting or configured child creation does not derive the substrate's origin.

Read the form foundation, parameter foundation and selected law's owner before changing definitions. Regular chart changes, exact symmetries and lossy observations require different proofs.

docs.title: 3. Execution and operator contracts
docs.text:
Choose the execution path before applying a result or changing its consumer:

Path Shared owner and boundary Operator studies StudySpec / run_study own tnfr network; extend them before CLI-specific execution or validation. Cycles count complete words, not seconds. The runner sets topology and execution seeds; TNFR.create(..., seed=...) sets only the topology seed. Continuous flow Reuse dynamics/integrators.py with pressure, capacity, clock and rate/residual evidence. Held and refreshed pressure are different models. Retain the live Gamma registry source in dx/dt=nu_f*p+Gamma; unforced certificates require Gamma absent or zero. Native relational flow RelationalExchangeModel / Network.step_relational select dynamics/relational.py, with admitted support, held capacity, phase domain and storage premises. This differs from the general operator runtime and the separate normalized-sine comparison. Detached observations/proofs Regional reports, hypothetical attachments and capture/transit checks install no laws, edges or event selectors. Apply every hypothesis; Euler steps, continuous theorems and validated enclosures provide different evidence.

The 13 operators use operators/operator_contracts.py. Read executable token values from TNFR.operators() and words from list_sequences(), not display names or parallel catalogs. Preserve word order and live preconditions; direct glyphs, public classes and atomic stages have different secondary effects.

Bind operator requests to actual NFR targets, consumed state/history and their selection origin. Supplied words and configured state-dependent selectors are not derived occurrence laws; collective selection needs its own descent proof.

Record the selected operator admission policy in prospective studies. Activity thresholds do not establish NFR existence or absence; retain legacy-policy controls when admitting a new event domain.

Grammar bases belong to operators/grammar_canon.py; role sets derive through shared predicates and grammar_types.py. U1-U6 are admission/monitoring contracts, not universal stability or autonomous-selection theorems. GRAMMAR_REJECTION_MODE="raise" prevents blocked-step substitution. Read the grammar and operator owners before changing semantics.

Mutation requires active capacity, a live finite signed two-sample EPI secant strictly above its configured threshold, and independent grammar context. Timestamped history ends at the live state; step-indexed history declares operator-step units. Nodal-product predictions cannot replace observed trigger evidence. Missing/stale evidence rejects execution or yields explicit abstention.

Named events are hybrid jumps, not invented finite-duration pressure flows. Atomic stages propose from one immutable snapshot, validate every target and commit graph-owned state together; callback rollback and future stability do not follow. Capture optional diagnostics only when requested. Network REMESH has its own history/mixing contract; its node advisory does not execute delayed mixing. Use the event contracts and relational contracts.

docs.title: 4. Numerical and observation integrity
docs.text:
Admit values before float conversion, caching or array construction: _exact_time.py owns represented-real admission, types.py signed scalar EPI, and alias.py attribute access. Invalid authoritative values cannot fall through to another alias. Reject nonfinite inputs, Boolean physical scalars or clocks, and nonzero values lost during materialization. Finite inputs still require representable output arithmetic. Reuse shared Boolean parsing and parameter resolution instead of competing defaults.

Pressure support differs by channel: EPI uses conductance weights; phase, capacity and degree contrast use unique outgoing neighbors, including zero-conductance edges. Capacity contrast drives form, not capacity evolution. Neighbor-resultant phase pressure is not globally a pairwise Laplacian. Pure-EPI diffusion retains its fixed/reversible/positive-capacity hypotheses; see the pressure contract.

Use physics/fields.py for fields, metrics/common.py for coherence reductions and diagnose_network for detached stored-state observations. Other readers may maintain rebuildable caches only within their declared mutation scope. The structural field guide and API contracts own these boundaries:

  • The tetrad is diagnostic, not complete state or a future predictor. Geometry uses edge length with weight fallback; diffusion uses conductance.
  • Curvature may be undefined at zero resultant. Coherence-length fit and spectral fallback retain separate provenance and availability.
  • Stored pressure, refreshed fields, predicted rates and measured temporal evidence differ; snapshots and operator labels cannot prove conservation.
  • Missing observations/baselines remain unavailable, not zero or passing flags. Invalid thresholds cannot certify safety. Preserve rejection contracts; tolerance alerts are not exact equality, equilibrium or endpoint nonincrease.
  • C, Si, classifiers and thresholds are diagnostics/policies. Using them in a controller does not derive that controller; pi-based formulas do not establish universal physical constants.

JSON readers use utils.io.json_loads; SDK exports use the shared atomic writer. Retain duplicate-key rejection, finite-number admission and explicit projected-value availability. Recipes/exports are neither complete checkpoints nor provenance authentication.

A report-consuming calculation must re-admit primitive state, law and evidence and rebuild consumed derived fields. Cached bounds/verdicts cannot replace premises. Compute with normalized values before retaining an equivalent source association: Python equality is neither scalar admission nor authentication. Distinguish circular observations from continuous phase lifts; declare the lifts used by collective means. A lift-dependent storage remainder need not be nonnegative. Preserve proved cycle/mean correlations: overlapping marginal state budgets do not prove entry.

docs.title: 5. Research and evidence discipline
docs.text:
The research program owns the global objective, current state, priorities and sole active question. Its technical chapters retain definitions, proofs and counterexamples in their original contexts. The old plan, strategy and portfolio routes are generated compatibility views, not active instructions. Before resuming research, read the program's current task and complete any open documentation prerequisite there. Its ordered checklist is the persistent continuation record; do not rely on conversation memory or create another queue. After the gate closes, reassess the next scientific question against the global objective instead of automatically continuing the most recent example. Existing examples/theorems do not activate campaigns. On closing a gate, update the program's current question and link the result chapter. Preserve unresolved dependencies and frozen evidence without per-turn logs or duplicate result inventories. Follow F1-F4:

  1. Define identity, sufficient constituent/boundary state, domains, units, observations and discarded information.
  2. Declare all laws, separating assumptions, derived restrictions and remaining freedom. Supplied forcing/controllers are not inferred causes.
  3. Check joint consistency, symmetry, boundaries, balances and events on the actual model.
  4. Make a discriminating prospective prediction, or prove an equivalence or obstruction. Freeze preparation, law, clock, observation, horizon and numerical budget before evaluating the reserved response.

Apply the NFR ontology and operator contracts to the actual execution path. Declare the object's preparation, symmetries and supported actions; state whether identity is supplied, acquired or assessed only on a finite interval. A collective event needs its own admission, descent and occurrence argument even when continuous collective dynamics closes. Established organizations test foundations under their premises; they do not imply that every compatible law acquires them or realizes every registered operator.

Reuse the theory-to-execution map. Combine results only after matching complete law, support, capacity, clock, preparation and retained coordinates. Methods can transfer between models; their coefficients and verdicts do not automatically transfer. Matching equilibria and full tangents does not transfer nonlinear remainders, source transport or acquisition/capture certificates; re-admit regularity and bounds for the actual law. Tangent reduction need not close a nonlinear law. Eliminating hidden state can introduce memory and retains hidden initialization and forcing. Formation, recovery, winding, lifetime and maintenance have separate obligations: response peaks, pulses, recurrence, invariant families and finite retention do not establish formation or autonomous scale selection. An admissible connection or passive event does not select its occurrence.

Account for support-event storage jumps separately from continuous loss. Loss is not an event reserve without a declared reservoir and law; event passivity is an additional premise. Integrate justified reusable mechanisms in shared engine owners and consumers. Auxiliary constructions and arithmetic applications retain their own premises; finite comparisons do not select a unique ontology.

Any later empirical evaluation follows P1-P5: independent observation/preparation and clock models, separate calibration/reserved evaluation, alternatives, then partial observation, memory and maintenance under the same protocol. Collective measurement maps are allowed; EPI need not equal a sensor reading. Use workstation-accessible terrestrial data or laboratory-scale protocols, without extraterrestrial observations or large facilities.

Record source/configuration, support/node order, inputs, seeds, precision, backend, pressure refresh, events and residuals; a seed alone is insufficient. Preserve frozen protocols, source archives, responses and verdicts. Corrections need separate evidence: do not rewrite evaluated predictions or regenerate frozen producers for unrelated changes.

docs.title: 6. Documentation and implementation owners
docs.text:
Need Owner Introduction / first use README Research objective and current question Research program; linked chapters own definitions and proofs; Theory catalog is generated navigation Concept classification Glossary; change definition/proof owners before summaries Package boundaries / shared execution Architecture Guide responsibilities / website navigation Documentation map Usage / execution contracts CLI/SDK, API contracts, regional workflows Development / checks Contributing, Testing, Workflows Illustrations / instruments Examples, benchmarks

Catalogs generate website menus; operator contracts and grammar roles generate their checked tables. Glossary checks validate declarations/references, not scientific truth. Do not create duplicate catalogs, rule tables or glossaries.

theory/RESEARCH_PROGRAM.md is the sole research planning entry point. Keep it small enough for ordinary editor and Markdown-preview use. Each linked chapter has one canonical Markdown file at its declared path; edit that file directly. theory/research_catalog.json contains only ordering, titles and compatibility routes. It generates navigation, not a second theory or task queue. The optional scripts/research_book.py reader supports both this layout and historical monolithic captures. Never reassemble the maintained corpus into one preview page or edit generated website copies; Contributing gives the workflow.

The program has a 96-KiB file budget. Each research chapter, the program and each maintained docs owner also has a 4,000-physical-line editorial limit, checked by scripts/check_documentation.py. Split chapters by model and responsibility while preserving their published routes and evidence. Retain useful conditional results and counterexamples. Superseded instructions and corrected errors belong in Git recovery records, not active guidance. Frozen source captures remain historical evidence, never another task queue. Retire superseded drivers, duplicate plans and unused compatibility layers only after checking imports, public consumers and evidence dependencies. For unchanged committed files, record recovery revision/blob and replacement rather than another historical copy. Preserve uncommitted work, unique proofs, counterexamples, frozen protocols and evaluated responses.

docs.title: 7. Development and verification workflow
docs.text:
Inspect instructions, local changes, relevant source and tests before editing; preserve unrelated work. Start from the mathematical question and consumer. Use the owner map to locate the definition, selected law, implementation and tests before proposing a change. Prefer shared kernels, retain useful adapters and keep APIs stable or document and test an explicit migration. Update implementation and its contract/theory owner together; keep this file focused on working rules.

After catalog/registry edits, refresh generated views with python scripts/check_documentation.py --write-generated. Edit maintained inputs, not build/docs-source/ or site/.

  • Check postconditions, invalid domains, representation boundaries, atomicity and provenance. Valid words need not increase C; Resonance need not synchronize, and Dissonance need not create a bifurcation.
  • Exercise shared owners with independent expected results or meaningful counterexamples; fixture literals asserted against themselves are not evidence.
  • Reuse expensive reports through module fixtures. Test CLI/report wiring separately when scientific execution is unnecessary; retain cold-import, isolation and provenance controls.
  • Run affected contracts and explicitly select research owners whose models or claims changed. The routine engine/API gate is not full research coverage; Testing owns selection and dependencies.
  • For docs, verify mirror, generated views, links, executable examples and strict site build. Report checks and material limitations.
  • For distribution changes, check fresh wheel and source archives with scripts/check_distribution.py and the release checks in Testing.
  • Every release must include a verified lightweight development bundle and its SHA256 sidecar as GitHub release assets. Build from the exact release commit with scripts/build_development_bundle.py; retain code, theory, instructions, examples and tests, plus onboarding and verified retrieval of omitted evidence. Follow Testing for source/version, extraction and helper checks. Preserve the complete repository/Zenodo archive separately.

Distinguish grammar rejection, live-state rejection, solver defects, unavailable observations and unsupported theorem domains. Coherence decrease violates only contracts promising otherwise. Commits/PRs state the problem, resulting behavior, mathematical scope and validation, using the repository template where present.

docs.title: 8. Canonical invariants
docs.text:
These six invariant identifiers retain this order for registry references. Detailed admission and verification belong to the linked contracts.

  1. Preserve continuous nodal flow and declared hybrid jumps with their provenance.
  2. Enforce circular phase admission before U3 coupling/resonance.
  3. Retain declared nested structure and test the applicable U5 contract.
  4. Use registered semantic operators or explicitly justified new contracts; numerical evolution uses the shared integrator.
  5. Preserve structural units and expose the relevant structural telemetry.
  6. Make execution reproducible under fixed source, configuration, inputs, seed, target order, precision and backend; a seed alone is insufficient.

docs.title: Arithmetic utility and application archive
docs.text:
These source projects reuse selected TNFR utilities for supplied arithmetic problems. They are separate from the core engine under src/tnfr and from the active generative research queue in the execution plan. Their formulas, heuristic scores and compatibility names do not establish physical emergence or a new primality/factorization complexity result.

Project Retained purpose Boundary Primality utility Maintained standalone arithmetic-pressure descriptors, numerical predicate and basic CLI Consumes divisor/factor statistics; does not generate primes through nodal dynamics Factorization lab archive Non-maintained source and recorded outputs retained at their original paths Known acceptance and completeness defects prevent using its certificates as factorization evidence

The optional tnfr.primality adapter retains access to the basic utility. tnfr.factorization and the SDK factorization methods are deprecated bridges for a separately supplied legacy package; they do not activate the archived checkout. Generic manifest, observation and dry-run orchestration belongs to the engine and no longer needs the lab. The main engine wheel and source distribution exclude both application trees.

Only the basic primality utility remains in the maintained application test selection in TESTING.md. The lab and advanced primality adapters are historical material, with source identities and migration guidance in their respective guides. They create no active research campaign. The number-theory document owns mathematical scope. Exact arithmetic identities, Paley/CRT results and their independent core tests remain maintained; retiring these applications changes none of those proofs.

Historical JSON captures and the lab's notebooks/archive/ retain their original bytes, including recorded old paths. They are evidence of the recorded run, not current invocation instructions or validation of the current source.

docs.title: TNFR spectral factorization lab — archived
docs.text:
Reference only; not maintained or part of the current application workflow. The source and historical outputs remain at their original paths to preserve uncommitted changes and recorded path associations. The retirement record identifies retained source, recovery revisions, retired integration tests and concrete counterexamples.

This pipeline combines supplied Jacobi-residue graphs, spectral heuristics, arithmetic statistics and partition workflows. Its acceptance and completeness labels are not reliable factor certificates. It establishes neither autonomous factor recovery from the nodal equation nor a complexity improvement or a cryptographic capability. This page records the archived implementation's scope; it is not an installation or execution recommendation.

The maintained arithmetic utility and number-theory owner retain exact arithmetic and independently proved residue-graph results. The Paley, CRT and cyclotomy constructions have their own hypotheses; sharing a graph operator does not validate this application's candidate pipeline.

docs.title: Results and verification
docs.text:
The retirement is based on implementation counterexamples, not only a change of research priority:

  • The structural verifier can accept candidate 6 for target 35 while its own support_divisible field is false.
  • An integer size_hint can enable an exception to the stabilization condition.
  • A composite signature for 35 with candidates [5, 7, 11] can report completeness although their product is 385.
  • Both modes compute arithmetic telemetry by factoring the input. Integer-size candidates, divisibility checks and trial-division fallback remain involved; a spectral result does not isolate the source of factor information.
Archived result Actual boundary candidate_factors Heuristic seeds, arithmetic refinements and partition hints; neither complete nor necessarily prime tnfr_certified_factors, tnfr_verification Configured acceptance scores with a separate divisibility observation; the acceptance rule need not require divisibility factor_signature, composite_signature Serialized records; hashes check recorded content, not the truth of powers or completeness certificate_path, partition paths Analysis/workflow records; a proposed word is not an executed operator trace

Independent proper-divisor, primality, product and multiplicity checks are necessary before interpreting any historical factor list. Passing them would not show that recovery came from a TNFR mechanism.

docs.title: Setup and public interfaces
docs.text:
The engine no longer adds this directory to its import path. The deprecated tnfr.factorization.factorize, TNFR.factorize and Network.factorize interfaces remain compatibility bridges for a separately supplied legacy tnfr_factorization package. Missing or archived-checkout implementations produce retirement guidance; an external implementation produces a deprecation warning. Keeping these names does not maintain or certify the archived lab. See the API migration.

Generic manifest preparation, dry-run assessment and report validation remain engine responsibilities. They do not bootstrap this lab, reconstruct a residue graph from a modulus, or apply a proposed operator word implicitly.

The retained source owners are the lab API, candidate pipeline, partition planner, seed handling and snapshot records. Their original CLI and helper files are historical source, not supported entry points. The lab has no separate setup.py or pyproject.toml.

docs.title: Candidate policy and configuration
docs.text:
Historical pure=True changes a process-wide environment policy for the call. It skips arithmetic-statistic hints and gcd refinement in the initial candidate stage, but does not make the complete pipeline arithmetic-free:

  • _compute_arithmetic_telemetry factors the input to obtain Omega, tau and sigma in both modes.
  • Even-number hints, integer-size seeds and later partition-size divisibility checks remain.
  • Empty initial candidates reach trial division without a pure-mode guard; its default bound is isqrt(n).
  • TNFR_PURE_MODE_VERIFY_DIVISIBILITY filters one initial stage, not every later candidate or final acceptance label.

Automatic modulus selection rounds upward to at least n and 5, with residue 1 mod 4, without proving primality. Distinct inputs can therefore share a graph (35 and 37 both select modulus 37). Explicit overrides enforce only the lower bound 5, while prime-modulus Paley identities require their own domain. Support is supplied arithmetically, not formed by a nodal law.

The low-level constructor defaults to a node cap of 4097; None removes it. The historical high-level wrapper and CLI pass None when omitted. CLI zero also removes the cap, unlike the constructor. These differences matter when interpreting retained records, as do cache, backend and mode.

Archived JSON projections encode nonfinite diagnostics as null with numeric_availability reasons. When projection changes the payload, numeric_projection.retained_hash_scope distinguishes internal hash inputs from exported bytes. This is neither provenance authentication nor a guarantee that the underlying diagnostic has physical meaning.

docs.title: Telemetry and mechanism boundaries
docs.text:
The lab's field names differ from canonical tnfr.physics.fields:

Lab field Computation or source phi_s Normalized edge density, without nodewise pressure or path distance phase_gradient Selected spectral gap divided by node count phase_curvature Largest supplied eigenvalue divided by node count coherence_length Positive backend value, otherwise inverse selected gap Arithmetic EPI, capacity, pressure Static factor/divisor readouts without phase or autonomous evolution Energy/Noether proxies Algebraic lab features, without an established balance or conserved charge

On regular unit-weight graphs the fallback combinatorial spectrum is d * spectrum(L_rw). Its inverse selected gap is not the normalized diffusion timescale 1 / (nu * lambda_2(L_rw)) without degree/time conversion. The selection discards eigenvalues at or below 1e-9, so it need not select the true second eigenvalue.

Partition pressure reduction includes a fixed attenuation surrogate. It is not operator execution or a convergence theorem. Grammar-valid proposals, configured thresholds and finite score changes do not prove U5, autonomous selection, conservation or a factorization mechanism.

docs.title: Verification and evidence
docs.text:
Archived tests and benchmark source are retained for interpretation and recovery, outside the maintained test selection and automatic validation maps. Their finite passing cases do not override the counterexamples above. Do not rerun frozen producers to update these records.

Historical JSON, notebook records and captured paths retain their original bytes. Partition hashes cover selected members, telemetry and metadata in supplied order, excluding other state; they are not complete checkpoints. Snapshot demonstrations use synthetic persistence records.

The current testing policy covers independent core arithmetic controls, the basic primality utility and compatibility admission. The root LICENSE.md remains authoritative.

docs.title: TNFR arithmetic primality package
docs.text: This optional arithmetic application contains the standalone tnfr-primality 1.1.0 compatibility package. It evaluates static arithmetic-pressure formulas from supplied divisor and prime-factor statistics. It does not evolve a nodal network, derive phase, or establish a cryptographic performance advantage. This README owns current usage; TNFR number theory owns mathematical scope.

docs.title: Mathematical criterion and runtime scope
docs.text:
For an integer n >= 2, the default pressure is

DeltaNFR(n) = (Omega(n) - 1)
             + (tau(n) - 2)
             + (sigma(n)/n - (1 + 1/n))

Omega counts prime factors with multiplicity, tau counts divisors and sigma sums divisors. In exact arithmetic each term is nonnegative and all three vanish for primes. Every composite has positive pressure; for unit weights its first two terms already sum to at least 2. Thus the exact zero set is precisely the primes. Any positive coefficient triple preserves that zero set, which leaves the coefficients undetermined: unit weights are the package's selected normalization, not a uniquely derived physical constant.

The implementation first enumerates divisors and factors the input. Its O(sqrt(n)) arithmetic-loop scale is not a bit-complexity improvement over established primality algorithms. Floating division and sqrt-based loops are separate implementation limits; finite tests are not a proof for arbitrary Python integers. No universal accuracy or timing guarantee follows from the exact-real identity.

docs.title: Installation and primary API
docs.text:
From the repository root:

python -m pip install ./applications/primality-test

The basic package is independent of the engine and retains Python 3.8+ support. Its runtime uses the standard library. The optional dev extra installs the local test/build tools; documentation uses the root repository's .[docs] extra and documentation checks.

from tnfr_primality import (
    OptimizedTNFRPrimality,
    tnfr_component_breakdown,
    tnfr_delta_nfr,
    tnfr_is_prime,
    tnfr_structural_triad,
)

is_prime, pressure = tnfr_is_prime(997)
components = tnfr_component_breakdown(221)
summary = tnfr_structural_triad(221)
optimizer = OptimizedTNFRPrimality()
results = optimizer.batch_test([17, 21, 97])
API Return and configuration tnfr_delta_nfr(n, *, zeta=1, eta=1, theta=1) Floating pressure; n < 2 returns positive infinity. Positive coefficients are premises of the zero-set result, not enforced by this function. tnfr_is_prime(n, *, tolerance=1e-10) (abs(pressure) < tolerance, pressure) using unit coefficients. This is a strict numerical predicate; custom tolerances can alter classification. tnfr_component_breakdown(...) Weighted pressure components and arithmetic statistics; the retained key omega means multiplicity count Omega. tnfr_structural_triad(...) Compatibility bundle with EPI, vf, delta_nfr, local_coherence, components. Despite its name it does not return canonical (EPI, capacity, phase); phase is absent. OptimizedTNFRPrimality Cache of final pressure values, batch loop, timing statistics and a classical sieve followed by pressure checks. is_prime uses fixed strict tolerance 1e-10. The bounded cache retains its first entries; it is not an LRU policy.
