Arithmetic EPI/capacity formulas are configured readouts of the same statistics. Returning them does not derive their dynamics or make the integer a maintained NFR. Neither these bundles nor arithmetic certificates constitute an executed operator sequence or the complete structural tetrad.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
The standard installed command maps to tnfr_primality.cli:main:

tnfr-primality 17 97 997
tnfr-primality 221 --timing
tnfr-primality --batch --optimized 17 21 97
tnfr-primality --validate 1000

python -m tnfr_primality and python -m tnfr_primality.cli use this same basic parser without importing advanced adapters. Options include --optimized, --batch, --timing, --benchmark, --validate, --compare, --stats, --sieve and --json-output. --validate compares finite arithmetic outputs; it does not validate TNFR as a physical theory.

python -m tnfr_primality 2 4 1 --json-output
python -m tnfr_primality --validate 100 --json-output

JSON mode emits one document on stdout. Number rows contain number, is_prime, delta_nfr, delta_nfr_available, method and time_ms. For n < 2, unavailable pressure is null with availability false, rather than a nonstandard JSON infinity. Validation uses the basic tested/correct schema; sieve output is {"primes": [...]}. Benchmark and comparison modes retain their basic reports. Human progress and requested cache statistics go to stderr.

docs.title: Optional repository integration
docs.text:
The engine's tnfr.primality adapter can use these basic arithmetic functions. It does not need an advanced module or a full extra. Core engine arithmetic also remains independently available under tnfr.mathematics.

The former advanced adapters and CLI are retired. tnfr-primality-advanced, tnfr-primality-legacy and the full, benchmark and docs extras are no longer installation targets. Use tnfr-primality or the basic module command for supported arithmetic output; advanced-only options are rejected. Archive recovery preserves their source identities and unique working-tree examples/tests outside runtime discovery and package payloads.

The former optional PrimeCertificate route classified supplied arithmetic terms against a tolerance. It did not independently authenticate those terms or prove primality from an untrusted report. Its retirement changes neither the exact zero-set theorem nor the core arithmetic implementation. Package threshold names do not redefine phase bounds, fields or operator grammar.

docs.title: Executable examples
docs.text:
After installing this application, run the maintained example:

python applications/primality-test/examples/basic_usage.py

It reports selected unit coefficients, factor multiplicity and cache timings. It neither benchmarks arbitrary integer sizes nor validates physical TNFR. The advanced example and former promotional benchmark belong to archive recovery, not the current learning or performance route.

docs.title: Verification and limits
docs.text:
From the repository root:

python applications/primality-test/test_installation.py

The installation checks cover imports, selected known integers, caching and batch behavior. The application suite checks basic CLI/module parity, strict JSON, examples, package contents and the absence of advanced auto-imports:

python -m pytest applications/primality-test/tests -q

Their finite timings depend on the environment and workload; a speedup for repeated cached inputs is not a new primality complexity result. For benchmark comparisons retain inputs, cache state, implementation branch and environment. The main engine's arithmetic implementation remains under src/tnfr/mathematics; this compatibility package is not an additional source of TNFR-wide physical laws. The root LICENSE.md applies.

docs.title: Retired advanced arithmetic adapters
docs.text:
This directory is a recovery record, not an executable package, benchmark or test suite. The active application evaluates static arithmetic statistics through tnfr_primality.core, its bounded cache and the basic CLI.

The manifest identifies removed committed sources by Git revision and blob. Their Git text has LF line endings; the exact CRLF working bytes are also retained in the external cleanup backup recorded there. Unique uncommitted work is preserved here byte for byte with .txt suffixes:

  • Advanced example.
  • Mixed example tests; the maintained test keeps the basic example controls.

The archived example depends on retired adapters and is not a current usage recipe. Its claims and fallback behavior are not current contracts. Recover a complete old implementation from the recorded revision when historical inspection requires it; do not import these files into current execution.

The package whitelist and MANIFEST.in exclude this directory from wheel and source distributions. The root source repository retains this recovery record.

docs.title: Benchmark and research instrument guide
docs.text: This directory contains performance measurements, conditional model probes, reserved-response producers and read-only record audits. These roles are not interchangeable. The theory catalog owns mathematical claims; the execution plan is the sole task queue. A retained instrument is not automatically an active research campaign, and a filename containing emergent proves no emergence.

docs.title: Observation, auxiliary models and performance
docs.text:
Role Instruments Boundary Static and temporal observation Static interface, temporal, multichannel, external phase gate Interface guide owns measurement preparation, label availability, estimator limits and fair comparisons Terrestrial transport comparisons TCLab, Volts comparison, Volts loader TCLab protocol, passive transport; exploratory maps are not admitted physical variables Field diagnostics Method battery, curvature example Tetrad; declared diagnostic scope, not autonomous dynamics or universal safety thresholds Arithmetic and spectral comparisons arithmetic_*.py, composition, commutant, Paley, residue/prime/word controls Arithmetic; supplied encodings, exact algebra or finite comparisons REMESH/Riemann projections remesh_infinity_riemann_*.py Riemann scope; parked spectral controls, not RH or complete-runtime stability proofs Auxiliary geometry emergent_*.py, pulse and symmetry probes Ontology boundaries; supplied graph/wave/simplex models, not identified particles or physical dimensions Actual performance Node lookup, offset batching Source, seed, workload, timings and trajectory hashes; no universal speedup claim

The complete source inventory can be read without importing or running scripts:

rg --files benchmarks -g '*.py'

Paths remain stable where tests, imports and frozen source manifests consume them. Grouping the instruments here avoids moving a scientific producer merely to make a directory look tidier. Inspect the source and its owner before using an unlisted family member; do not batch-execute this inventory.

docs.title: Reuse the mechanism appropriate to the question
docs.text:
Use the SDK for operator studies and its regional/relational guide for shared observations, explicit joint evolution and capture admission. Benchmarks add preparations, comparisons and evidence, not a second production solver.

Prefer a read-only record audit when the needed trajectory already exists. An audit separates record consistency, the original decision and compatibility with current source/runtime. Some THOL/C6 audits require local records under artifacts/research/ that are not versioned or supplied by cloning the repo; missing records make those checks unavailable. Sparse checkpoints cannot authenticate omitted steps or reconstruct a continuous integral. A content digest does not establish physical acquisition, trustworthy chronology or a complete transitive dependency archive unless that archive is explicitly included.

Use derived memory and the scale bridge for closure questions. The auxiliary gasket instruments reuse the pure graph preparation, including its ordered outer corners. That supplied construction is not a THOL event or a selected physical dimension. The Bell instrument uses those corners at every level. Its CHSH bound belongs to the supplied auxiliary graph model. Retained outputs remain associated with the source and graph preparation that produced them.

A rank calculation for rational surrogate coefficients is not a nonlinear closure proof for actual irrational coefficients. An observation of winding, a standing mode or a supplied potential does not identify a physical particle.

docs.title: Running and reporting
docs.text:
Install the repository in editable mode, then run the selected instrument from the repository root. Dependencies and command-line support differ by module:

python -m pip install -e ".[dev-minimal]"
python -m benchmarks.nodal_lookup_scaling --sizes 10 --repeats 2
python -m benchmarks.stable_node_offset_scaling --sizes 6 --repeats 2 --scoped

These small examples exercise timing/report plumbing; meaningful performance comparisons require identical input, source, hardware, backend, warm-up and measurement scope. Retain absolute times and trajectory agreement, not just a speed ratio. --wheel selects a separate baseline without installing it. pytest benchmarks --benchmark-only is not a supported directory-wide suite; scientific regression tests live under tests/. The optional test-performance extra supplies a third-party plugin only when explicitly requested.

docs.title: Freeze before evaluating a reserved response
docs.text:
The two-law observation theorem retains two completed analytical instruments: organized_law_contrast_kernels encloses the fixed scalar moments, and organized_law_record_separation reads that immutable evidence to check the complete nonlinear error budget. Both use the shared exclusive analytical runner and committed declarations; neither evolves a trajectory or reads a physical response. Their archived attempts and results are the regression inputs. Do not rerun these completed assessments for routine verification.

The following producers accept --prepare --output PATH; evaluation uses the same command and path without --prepare:

Producer module under benchmarks Role source_relative_form_response Held-source prediction and ablation phase_form_exchange_comparison Prepared constitutive probes, not a trajectory relational_capacity_response Capacity intervention relational_coefficient_acquisition One known-source P2 acquisition; full retained state/error chain and source archive relational_capacity_sampling_response Four fixed K3 candidate/arm cases; single-origin Taylor enclosures and frozen sample/contrast error gates relational_seeded_response Fixed regular source/receiver short response; exact-pi interval initial state, whole-time proof and storage ledger relational_receiver_barrier One fixed full eleven-node sine source; whole-prefix receiver potential and dissipative full-storage tail, with failed or unresolved evidence retained relational_local_recovery Prepared local recovery relational_region_interaction Transmitted regional response relational_formation_response, relational_capture_response Finite sector/endpoint responses relational_memory_response Matched-grid memory prediction and full-engine comparison relational_mediation_response Matched-grid mediator-capacity intervention; retained memory versus instantaneous and omitted-memory controls relational_transit_proof Continuous proof audit; --zero-form and --reverse-form are mutually exclusive controls conservative_regional_organization Whole-time regional observation or reversible preparation, selected by the declaration; --declaration PATH requires an explicit new --output PATH and the same declaration in both preparation/evaluation invocations

For example, use a fresh path for a current-source regression:

python -m benchmarks.relational_capacity_response --prepare --output artifacts/relational-capacity/result.json
python -m benchmarks.relational_capacity_response --output artifacts/relational-capacity/result.json

The inverse-geometry instrument has a third, independently retained prediction stage. For a separately declared current-source check, use one fresh path for all three invocations:

python -m benchmarks.return_path_geometry_response prepare --output artifacts/research/return_path_geometry_response/current-check.json
python -m benchmarks.return_path_geometry_response predict --output artifacts/research/return_path_geometry_response/current-check.json
python -m benchmarks.return_path_geometry_response evaluate --output artifacts/research/return_path_geometry_response/current-check.json

This fixed known-source protocol checks a bounded initial derivative. It does not run a positive-time trajectory or supply an independent physical measurement. The analytic conservative_regional_winding instrument instead writes one certificate and source archive; it has no --prepare stage and executes no solver. Its --declaration chooses the preparation, not a parameter search.

conservative_regional_organization --analyze-channels SOURCE_RESPONSE --output NEW_PATH is a third kind of operation: a retrospective analysis of saved whole-time tubes. It does not take --declaration, replay a solver or rewrite the original response. Keep the separate analysis source archive, original file hashes and original verdict. A successful file audit or a new channel bound does not convert a negative acquisition result into a success.

sine_metric_connection uses a separate declaration and mandatory output:

python -m benchmarks.sine_metric_connection --prepare --declaration PATH_TO_DECLARATION --output artifacts/research/sine_metric_connection/new-response.json
python -m benchmarks.sine_metric_connection --declaration PATH_TO_DECLARATION --output artifacts/research/sine_metric_connection/new-response.json

Preparation verifies the literal rational saddle recipe without evolving it. Evaluation executes both declared directions once through the shared engine, retaining whole-time matrix and identity evidence, including partial failures. Its study-level pass requires the same-orbit connection and both complete horizons. An image of the prepared family remains distinct from an independent winding-zero source box. The retained declaration is not permission to replay an already evaluated response or scan alternative budgets.

The retained evidence bundle contains the original response, protocol and evaluated source archive. Its manifest records their unchanged byte hashes. Read the result owner for the distinction between certified connection prefixes and the incomplete declared horizon; the producer's original passed=false is retained.

The same-source constitutive audit consumes that bundle without rerunning the producer. Its fixed one-percent cubic-current comparison uses the unchanged source's full conserved storage and a proved sector barrier; see the contract and retained result. It is a read-only model comparison, not another trajectory campaign.

Preparation and evaluation are separate invocations. Keep sibling prediction or protocol files and any source archives together. For a separately identified numerical correction of relational_seeded_response, use a fresh output path and supply --correction-of PRIOR_RECORD to both invocations. This retains the prior bytes' digest and labels the calculation as a correction, not an independent blind replication.

For the fixed source/receiver target-budget study, pass --study target-budget and an explicit fresh --output to both invocations. This declares total time one from the original exact initial state; it does not substitute the previous response's rounded endpoint. A separately frozen continuation can pass the same --horizon 9/8 to both invocations, still starting from the original IVP. The shared owner admits a positive exact horizon of at most 256 steps; no automatic extension is performed. A resolved negative budget and a resolved positive budget both pass the numerical discrimination gate. Read the separate target verdict: positive storage is not successful formation. The default short study and its retained declarations remain unchanged.

Admission binds declared inputs and recorded source/runtime fingerprints; changing source bytes, line endings or dependency versions can invalidate a replay. Prepare a new pair rather than rewrite the first experiment. Use the CLI rather than feeding raw JSON into producer functions that expect native exact-rational mappings.

docs/assets/ contains immutable first predictions, responses and source archives linked by each theorem owner. New output belongs in artifacts/. The commands above describe instrument use, not an instruction to replay every retained experiment. Consult the execution plan before a new scientific run; documentation, interface and admission checks normally reuse saved evidence or independent bounded fixtures. Failed decisions must remain visible; an inconclusive certificate is not a pass. The later continuous transit certificate does not replace the earlier finite-executor verdict. Consensus (target_sector=0) and unavailable evidence are different results; do not interpret the sector as a Boolean.

For every new numerical claim, retain source/configuration, input construction, seed, backend/precision, law or operator sequence, raw artifact and provenance. Separate calibration from evaluation and disclose supplied labels or factors. Finite measurements establish their measured scope, not universal physical laws.

docs.title: Read-only temporal-acquisition audit
docs.text:
Inspect the existing P2 response without regenerating it:

python -m tnfr.research.relational_acquisition artifacts/research/relational_coefficient_acquisition/result.json

This command reads the sibling protocol and archive, then reconstructs saved contrast/error evidence through the shared auditor. It has no prepare/evaluate mode and writes no artifacts. Exit 0 means record consistency, not that the experiment passed; recorded_passed and reconstructed_passed retain the original verdict separately. Exit 1 denotes inconsistent evidence and 2 missing/unavailable files. Local artifacts may be absent after cloning; their absence is not permission to replay the producer. The contract owns admission, work limits and the authentication boundary.

docs.title: Multichannel observation records
docs.text:
The multichannel instrument computes one window series for both ranking and block summaries. Malformed ARFF rows reject the record rather than silently removing samples; binary labels must remain aligned with signal samples. The byte limit covers cached payloads and expanded ZIP members as well as the download. Unavailable class means serialize as null; reports use the shared strict JSON and atomic writer.

Check auc_available and auc_unavailable_reason before interpreting scores. When windows or a label class are absent, retained legacy AUC values of 0.5 are compatibility placeholders, not measured chance performance. Available orientation-free rankings remain same-sample descriptions, not reserved forecasts; the interface guide owns the methodological boundary.

docs.title: Retired instruments
docs.text: The retirement record and recovery manifest identify unsupported timing comparisons, obsolete threshold/U2 investigations and orphan utilities removed in this audit. Useful mathematical results, negative boundaries, maintained tests and frozen evidence remain with their owners; retirement does not assert that every alternative model is impossible.

docs.title: Documentation ownership and navigation
docs.text:
This map routes the maintained documentation for the checked-out source. Usage guides show how to call an interface, contracts specify admission and outputs, and the research program owns the objective, current question and chapters containing definitions, hypotheses and proofs. Its generated chapter index provides navigation.

Start with the root README for installation and an organized mathematical object, then use the example learning route and recovery-report guide to inspect its state, law, identity and response. Continue with the CLI/SDK object workflow or the regional workflows for the supported actions and observations. For their mathematical meaning, the theory index connects definitions and proofs to engine modules, tests and SDK entry points. Numerical evidence and conditional certificates retain the premises of their source objects; they are not empirical validation.

Choose the execution contract before following an example:

  • Native relational evolution: the joint execution guide and contract describe the argument-based law, held capacity and phase-domain checks.
  • Normalized-sine constructions and comparisons: the formed-object workflow and comparison contract retain their distinct smooth law. These observation, certificate and forecast APIs do not change the law executed by Network.step_relational. Alternative reciprocal mobilities have their own complete laws; shared storage does not transfer every theorem between them.
  • Operator words: CLI and SDK and event contracts cover registered operators, grammar and live admission. Word counts are not elapsed structural time.
  • Continuous nodal flow: API contracts and the architecture flow identify pressure, integrator, clock and source responsibilities. Held pressure, refreshed pressure and operator events have different execution semantics.

Use the regional workflow index to find an interface and the theory reading routes to assess its scientific claim. A captured state, supplied invariant family, finite enclosure and physical measurement have different source obligations. Common variables or storage do not join their theorems. The research program selects research work; an available guide does not authorize a campaign.
