docs.title: Capture and constitutive dependence
docs.text:
The actual-source basin theorem closes a specific generative dependency: the acquired and observed host, joined to its independently prepared donor at fixed eta=1e-5, reaches a specified strict relative minimum on five declared origin intervals. The conclusion retains the full fine state and original errors. It is stronger than stationary existence, finite retention or mean-only attraction. The ontology still distinguishes this conditional organization from physical binding, autonomous support formation and identification as a material constituent.

The five target labels describe symmetry-related relative registrations. Their multiplicity is not a species count. Graph symmetry constrains the allowed reduced torque, but does not by itself fix its nonzero harmonics, sign or stable zeros. The sine proof uses its supplied potential in host shape elimination, the fifth-order restoring coefficient, the uniform remainder and source transport. Those premises cannot be removed by calling the resulting registration a property of topology alone.

Constitutive robustness is a separate property from capture under one law. The retained harmonic alternative already has own-law preparation and finite interaction results. It is a declared counterlaw with the same primitive domains, reciprocal support and loss structure, rather than a newly fitted explanation. The own-law weak-contact classification changes the attracting registrations themselves: its admitted tube contains ten minima and ten index-one saddles, and the five sine-attracting relative origins are saddles under the alternative. Own-law normal curvature and uniform torque remainders retain all fine directions in this verdict. Marked identity and support symmetry therefore do not determine these attracting geometries for the retained pair.

The separate own-source theorem carries the actual alternative-law preparation, its observation history and every original error through the changed weak contact. It retains marked identity at every donor origin and assigns an attracting destination on ten declared intervals. On one common primitive preparation interval, sine and the alternative have disjoint asymptotic registrations, each with its own reached state. This supplies an acquired-outcome distinction without a finite settling deadline or an independent physical readout.

The separate joint transition theorem quantifies a local loss of stability within the existing constitutive family. Its critical deformation scales cubically with contact strength, with explicit joint derivative errors for 0<eta<=1e-12. All 52 normal phase directions remain positive while the soft registration undergoes a supercritical pitchfork. The central critical state has quartic restoring storage and remains asymptotically attracting, without exponential stability. The marked identity survives the local transition.

This distinguishes robustness at fixed contact from a deformation tolerance uniform as contact vanishes. It is stronger than qualitative hyperbolic persistence, but it does not certify the transition at eta=1e-5, capture intermediate-law sources or select a unique fundamental law. The comparison coordinate connecting deformation and contact is not a new autonomous evolution rule. A stationary shape elimination also does not supply the effective dynamics of a parent interacting with another organization: retained slow state and causal memory remain separate obligations. Existing closure and event counterexamples must be checked before treating either as a new research gap.

The related conditional questions retain their own boundaries. Narrowing basin gaps or enlarging eta refines the same conditional construction without yet distinguishing an independent premise. The original unit-strength stationary problem concerns a different supplied law. Assembly work and event admission already explain why a permitted contact is not an occurrence law; another proof of that distinction would not classify the maintained organization. The execution plan owns the single next gate and its complete-law scope. Endpoint capture and the local transition distinguish retained identity from law-dependent registration. docs.title: Independent constitutive, event and observation premises
docs.text:
The mathematical methods are established kernel and Schur-complement arguments. Their useful consequence here is the separation of inputs: connectivity does not specify phase curvature; a positive tangent does not specify a recovery rate; and a neutral tangent does not specify nonlinear attraction. Circular nonnegative potentials with the same Hessian can have different restoring orders or local stability. A cancelled exported mean signal also need not remove internal restoration.

This closes the named structural dependency without selecting the potential, kinetic rows, critical tuning or occurrence of contact. The matched-conductance example is a discriminator for that distinction, not grounds for further contact variants. Independent law justification and physical admission remain open for their existing reasons.

The phase-response classification tests one distinct premise: every nontrivial primitive phase rotation must be visible to some query of the declared current channel. Exact Fourier support determines its invisible subgroup, but both retained counterlaws are already faithful. Circle-valued state and full-state identity do not impose faithfulness on every current or collective observable. A many-to-one flow quotient can lose native U3 or winding information even when both continuous rows descend exactly.

The free probe and small-phase comparison provide conditional access, including full fine-state errors, preparation resources and distinguishable or overlapping reading sets. The latter removes large initial mean forms as a requirement for every observation in this family. Neither result supplies a new restriction on the current, kinetic rows or accessible physical preparations. A lower information or attachment cost does not become a selection principle without independent justification for that requirement. The reciprocal resource envelope also bounds what changing contacts can supply; it does not produce an occurrence law or transfer its weighted comparison model to native phase-pressure support.

The remaining distinction is between an unresolved proof and an absent premise:

  • Complete-law justification. Held capacity and support already complete those channels in the selected models. The NFR requirements allow boundary-dependent inherited laws and memory; they do not require cosine storage, first-resultant sufficiency or unchanged scalar profiles across every contact. The retained countermodels already satisfy the weaker requirements. Selecting among them needs additional independent content, not another derivation from the same premises or replacement of the nodal row.
  • Equivalence and observation. The form chart foundation, complete interface maps and scalar calibration theorem have stated transformation classes. Disjoint record sets exclude equivalence preserving that preparation, clock, input and observation contract. They do not classify arbitrary nonlinear state conjugacies with changed inputs and readouts. A broader equivalence question first needs a justified operational class; an unspecified class is not a missing theorem to solve by enumeration.
  • Generative occurrence. The operator activation audit and event premises already separate candidate access, eligibility, action, cost and occurrence. A reservoir or source port retains its own preparation and constitutive law. Its availability does not derive those inputs. Autonomous capacity, support and preparation become necessary for a claim consuming them; they are not prerequisites to every conditional formation or physical comparison.
  • Independent physical bridge. The small-phase theorem consumes a supplied relative phase and fine-state budget, a declared clock and an observation law. Gain and exposure allowances presume those inputs. The recovery preparation counterexample shows why voltage precision alone cannot certify unobserved relative phases. The electrical review separately retains complete-law and preparation mismatches. Those older models supply no bridge for the eighteen-node comparison; their numerical apparatus limits do not transfer to it either. A collective sensor map is allowed, with independent preparation, loading, clock and reduction errors.

There are still conditional mathematical questions, including receiver acquisition or an all-future exclusion beyond its finite nonacquisition result. That question requires a new source-valid invariant-domain or capture argument; extending the finite run does not supply one. It is not evidence that another law or engine mechanism is already justified. The same distinction applies to deferred unit-strength stationary classification and capacity/support models.

These certificates do not derive an independently justified occurrence selector or select a unique complete law. This is a boundary of their stated premises, not a proof that such a mechanism cannot exist. The constitutive entry condition requires a named new premise or observation, its independent basis and the retained alternative it can exclude. For an autonomous generative claim, the input may instead be a justified source/occurrence mechanism with its own capability; it need not select the current. Physical comparison need not await unique law selection or substrate origin once its own bridge is admitted. The sole queue selects a bounded foundational implication to investigate. Further numerical precision does not fill a missing constitutive or occurrence premise. A named conditional capability, such as localized identity transport, can instead be studied under an explicitly supplied complete law.

docs.title: Dissipative and Open-System Diagnostics
docs.text:
Status: scoped auxiliary model with exact finite-dimensional identities and numerical trajectory diagnostics.

This note describes the density-operator tools in src/tnfr/physics/dissipative_conservation.py. The matrix density operator rho used by these tools is distinct from the structural density rho_s = Phi_s + K_phi used by the graph-field conservation diagnostics. No implemented map identifies the two objects.

The module therefore does not extend the TNFR structural balance to all open systems as a theorem. It supplies a conventional finite-dimensional GKSL model that can be studied alongside TNFR telemetry. Likewise, a collapse operator is an environmental-model input; it is not evidence of a U1--U6 grammar violation.

docs.title: 1. GKSL generator
docs.text:
For a density operator rho, Hamiltonian H, and collapse operators L_k,

\[ \dot\rho=-i[H,\rho]+D[\rho], \qquad D[\rho]=\sum_k\left( L_k\rho L_k^\dagger- \frac12\{L_k^\dagger L_k,\rho\} \right). \]

The dissipator is trace preserving because

\[ \operatorname{Tr}D[\rho]=0. \]

For Hermitian H, compatible finite collapse operators and nonnegative time, the exact GKSL generator has a completely positive trace-preserving semigroup. build_lindblad_delta_nfr and the numerical exponential implement that model within their validation and arithmetic tolerances; an approximate output needs its own residual checks. Spectral non-expansion of an arbitrary matrix is weaker than the GKSL conditions and does not independently prove complete positivity.

The factory also admits signed real auxiliary scaling factors, and the matrix-exponential engines admit signed real time increments. Applying the forward GKSL conclusion to these APIs requires nu_f * scale >= 0 and dt >= 0, in addition to the generator premises above. Negative factors or time increments retain an algebraic exponential interpretation without that forward-channel guarantee. These supplied matrix factors do not redefine TNFR's nonnegative nodal capacity.

docs.title: Unitality
docs.text:
The dissipative part is unital precisely when

\[ D[I]=\sum_k(L_kL_k^\dagger-L_k^\dagger L_k)=0. \]

is_unital_dissipator checks this residual numerically. Pure dephasing is unital. Zero-temperature amplitude damping is not: it drives states toward the pure ground state.

All functions that accept collapse operators interpret them as the effective operators of the modeled generator. If a Liouville generator is multiplied by a positive factor a = nu_f * scale, the equivalent dissipative inputs are sqrt(a) L_k, together with Hamiltonian a H; passing the unscaled L_k would under-report instantaneous dissipative rates.

docs.title: 2. Universal norm bounds
docs.text:
For the Frobenius norm on states and spectral norm on collapse operators, submultiplicativity gives, term by term,

\[ \|D[\rho]\|_F \le 2\sum_k\|L_k\|_2^2\,\|\rho\|_F =2\sum_k\|L_k\|_2^2\sqrt{P}, \qquad P=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho^2). \]

This is the bound returned by compute_dissipation_bound. It is universal but usually loose. It does not vanish for every pure state. For example, with L=sqrt(gamma)|0><1|,

\[ D[|1\rangle\langle1|] =\gamma\left(|0\rangle\langle0|-|1\rangle\langle1|\right)\ne0. \]

Combining the first bound with Cauchy--Schwarz yields

\[ \left|\frac{dP}{dt}\right| =\left|2\operatorname{Tr}(\rho D[\rho])\right| \le4\sum_k\|L_k\|_2^2P. \]

compute_instantaneous_purity_rate evaluates the exact signed dissipative contribution. compute_purity_decay_bound retains its historical public name, but now returns the valid bound on the absolute purity-change rate.

docs.title: 3. Purity and entropy require channel hypotheses
docs.text:
The Hamiltonian commutator does not change purity, so

\[ \frac{dP}{dt}=2\operatorname{Tr}(\rho D[\rho]). \]

Its sign is not fixed for a general GKSL generator. For a unital semigroup, purity is non-increasing and von Neumann entropy

\[ S(\rho)=-\operatorname{Tr}(\rho\log\rho) \]

is non-decreasing. Without unitality, both directions can occur.

docs.title: Amplitude damping
docs.text:
For a qubit with L=sqrt(gamma)|0><1| and eta=exp(-gamma t), write the initial state as

\[ \rho(0)=\begin{pmatrix}1-p&c\\c^*&p\end{pmatrix}. \]

Then

\[ \rho_{11}(t)=\eta p,\qquad \rho_{01}(t)=\sqrt\eta\,c, \]

and

\[ P(t)=(1-\eta p)^2+(\eta p)^2+2\eta|c|^2. \]

An initially excited pure state first loses purity, reaches P=1/2, and then regains purity as it approaches the pure ground state. Initial purity alone is insufficient to predict this curve: two states with equal purity can have different p and c. predict_amplitude_damping_purity therefore gives an exact result only when passed the full 2 x 2 density matrix. Scalar input is a deprecated compatibility interpolation and emits DeprecationWarning.

docs.title: Pure dephasing
docs.text:
When gamma denotes the off-diagonal amplitude decay rate,

\[ \rho_{ij}(t)=e^{-\gamma t}\rho_{ij}(0)\quad(i\ne j), \]

while populations remain fixed. Consequently,

\[ P(t)=\sum_i|\rho_{ii}(0)|^2 +e^{-2\gamma t}\sum_{i\ne j}|\rho_{ij}(0)|^2. \]

This is the convention used by predict_dephasing_purity. It matches both the qubit operator sqrt(gamma/2) sigma_z and the complete projector family sqrt(gamma)|k><k|.

docs.title: 4. Contractivity and stationary states
docs.text:
A CPTP map contracts trace distance between two states:

\[ T(\mathcal E(\rho),\mathcal E(\sigma)) \le T(\rho,\sigma), \qquad T(\rho,\sigma)=\frac12\|\rho-\sigma\|_1. \]

If rho_ss is fixed by the same map, its trace distance from a trajectory is therefore non-increasing. verify_dissipative_balance reports the ratio of these trace distances when a reference state is supplied through the historical steady_state parameter. The standalone balance function has no generator and cannot verify that the reference is actually stationary. Without a reference, the result is explicitly unevaluated; the function does not silently certify contractivity. Arbitrary pairs of snapshots also do not prove that an underlying map is CPTP. The tracker, which does own a generator, rejects a supplied steady state with a nonzero stationarity residual.

steady_state_from_generator solves the stationary and trace-one constraints by least squares and verifies positivity and the generator residual. A generator can have a stationary manifold. Pure dephasing, for example, fixes all density matrices diagonal in the dephasing basis. The returned state is one minimum-norm representative, not a uniqueness certificate.

analyze_dissipation_rates reports the stationary-mode count, stable decay rates, positive-real-part modes, and the trace-preservation residual. A positive spectral gap reports the slowest resolved strictly decaying mode. It does not exclude nonzero purely imaginary modes: those can oscillate indefinitely. Convergence toward the stationary subspace additionally requires absence of such neutral nonstationary modes and unstable modes. The implementation reports both explicitly. Convergence to one unique state further requires a one-dimensional stationary space. These are statements about the admitted GKSL model; an arbitrary matrix spectrum alone proves neither a quantum channel nor a TNFR evolution law.

docs.title: 5. What each diagnostic means
docs.text:
Diagnostic Implemented quantity Scope Purity change rate (P_after-P_before)/dt Signed; either sign is possible Entropy change rate (S_after-S_before)/dt Signed; monotone for unital channels State change rate norm_F(rho_after-rho_before)/dt Includes coherent and dissipative motion Dissipator action norm norm_F(D[rho_before]) Instantaneous environmental term Dissipation bound 2 sum norm_2(L_k)^2 sqrt(P) Universal Frobenius bound Fixed-point contraction ratio T_after/T_before Requires a supplied stationary state Frobenius-norm loss rate (norm_F(rho_before)-norm_F(rho_after))/dt Purity proxy; not a Noether charge Change tier Maximum absolute purity/entropy rate Empirical reporting bin

The compatibility names purity_decay_rate, entropy_production_rate, actual_dissipation, and charge_leak_rate remain accessible. Their canonical counterparts state the measured quantity without assuming a sign or a Noether interpretation.

The four change tiers (weak, moderate, strong, large) use configured rate thresholds 0.001, 0.05, and 0.2. They are descriptive bins rather than physical phase boundaries. classify_dissipative_regime retains legacy keys for compatibility and always reports grammar_status_inferred=False.

docs.title: 6. Validation and reproducibility
docs.text:
Public calculations reject density matrices that are non-square, non-Hermitian, non-finite, non-positive, or not trace one. Collapse operators must be finite square matrices of the same dimension. Time steps, rates, and times must be finite and non-negative where their definitions require it. Original scalar and real/imaginary matrix components are admitted before binary64 conversion. Boolean/text coercion and nonzero materialization loss reject, including in numerical tolerances. This represented-input boundary does not replace the density, collapse-operator or generator hypotheses.

Finite inputs alone do not guarantee representable diagnostic arithmetic. Snapshot purity, the public action, norm bounds, purity rates, observed balance secants and unitality comparison reject nonfinite computed values before classification. Generator spectral scales, eigenspectra and residuals obey the same requirement before stationarity, trace-preservation or mode verdicts. Nonzero collapse-norm squares lost to underflow also reject. Range-safe Frobenius evaluation can avoid overflow from squaring finite components, but does not certify an unrepresentable result. Missing collapse/reference data still produce explicit NaNs and unevaluated flags. The separate infinite trace-distance ratio denotes an initial distance at or below the configured floor and a final distance above it; it is a failed contraction observation, not an accepted overflow.

Snapshot capture reuses the spectrum computed during density admission. For ordinary NumPy collapse arrays, built-in balance calculations reuse the admitted densities and operator spectral norms within that invocation. Public calls still re-admit mutable snapshot arrays and recompute consumed diagnostics; cached report fields are not premises. Generic conversions and replaced public diagnostic helpers retain their live dispatch. The action bounds keep their Frobenius and spectral norms, and contraction ratios keep trace distance. The tracker appends a record to its snapshot history and diagnostic series only after all admission and diagnostic calculations succeed.

The executable demonstration compares exact amplitude damping and dephasing channels, including the non-monotone purity of amplitude damping and the monotone mixing of unital dephasing:

  • 28_dissipative_systems_demo.py

Direct regression coverage:

  • test_dissipative_conservation.py

Related implementation:

  • dissipative_conservation.py
