docs.title: Supplied state and complete models
Form (EPI)
docs.text:
• Status: maintained
  • Basis: primitive
  • Emergence: not-claimed
  • Definition: Structural configuration x in a declared form space; the graph scalar chart is signed real.
  • Domain: Declared form units X; finite real values or uniform-real BEPI for scalar-only consumers.
  • Premises: Choose the state space and chart before specifying evolution.
  • Dependencies: none
  • Owner: Form foundations.
  • Evidence: Types and implementation.
  • Implementation: Scalar admission.
  • Tests: EPI domain.
  • Limits: Magnitude cannot substitute for the signed structure of richer BEPI; EPI is not automatically voltage, energy or matter.

docs.title: Reorganization capacity (nu_f)
docs.text:
• Status: maintained
  • Basis: primitive
  • Emergence: not-claimed
  • Definition: Nonnegative multiplier of pressure in the nodal form rate, relative to the declared clock.
  • Domain: Finite nonnegative rates in inverse structural-clock units; zero suppresses the unforced form row.
  • Premises: Supply capacity or independently admit its evolution; Hz_str does not identify laboratory seconds.
  • Dependencies: clock
  • Owner: Capacity foundations.
  • Evidence: Capacity-law admission.
  • Implementation: Nodal arithmetic.
  • Tests: Nodal contracts.
  • Limits: Capacity is neither the actual form derivative nor angular frequency without another law; zero does not imply full equilibrium.

docs.title: Primitive phase (phi, theta)
docs.text:
• Status: maintained
  • Basis: primitive
  • Emergence: not-claimed
  • Definition: Circular synchronization coordinate in S¹, using a declared real lift where required.
  • Domain: Finite represented angles in radians; wrapped differences require a branch convention.
  • Premises: Phase evolution requires an independent supplied or derived row.
  • Dependencies: none
  • Owner: Parameter ledger.
  • Evidence: Primitive phase closure.
  • Implementation: Circular admission.
  • Tests: Circular semantics.
  • Limits: Phase is not itself a monotone clock or an angle derived from EPI contrasts.

docs.title: Support, conductance and distance
docs.text:
• Status: maintained
  • Basis: primitive
  • Emergence: not-claimed
  • Definition: Support names neighbors; conductance weights form transport; path distance supplies a separate observation geometry.
  • Domain: The graph model declares direction, multiplicity, isolates and admissible weights.
  • Premises: Initial support and any support evolution or intervention must be stated.
  • Dependencies: none
  • Owner: Relation foundations.
  • Evidence: Zero-relation boundary; pressure contract.
  • Implementation: Support transport.
  • Tests: Regional cut.
  • Limits: A zero-conductance edge can remain a phase neighbor. Normalized transport weight is not an absolute interaction rate; distance is separate. No autonomous relation-birth law is derived.

docs.title: Structural clock
docs.text:
• Status: maintained
  • Basis: primitive
  • Emergence: not-claimed
  • Definition: Declared parameter t relative to which continuous rates and timestamps are interpreted.
  • Domain: Declared time units T and finite admitted intervals; Boolean durations and lost nonzero values are invalid.
  • Premises: Clock changes transform the complete law, including capacity evolution.
  • Dependencies: none
  • Owner: Clock covariance.
  • Evidence: Joint unit changes.
  • Implementation: Time admission.
  • Tests: Parameter covariance.
  • Limits: Operator-word counts are not elapsed seconds; synchronization alone supplies no physical clock.

docs.title: Fractal-Resonant Node (NFR)
docs.text:
• Status: maintained
  • Basis: primitive
  • Emergence: not-claimed
  • Definition: A supplied nodal unit; a collective NFR additionally needs a declared pattern identity, retained internal state and interaction model.
  • Domain: A node or specified region; collective representations retain constituents unless a justified reduction removes information.
  • Premises: Specify membership, identity/equivalence and consumed state before testing formation or persistence.
  • Dependencies: epi, capacity, phase, support
  • Owner: Substrate and scale.
  • Evidence: Formation and identity obligations; retained pair state.
  • Implementation: SDK observation, collective-state reader.
  • Tests: Observation scope, realizable pair state.
  • Limits: A node, nested child or named region is not proved autopoiesis or matter. Identity can persist while internal state changes; nesting alone proves neither predictive closure nor formation.

docs.title: Structural pressure (DeltaNFR)
docs.text:
• Status: maintained
  • Basis: constitutive
  • Emergence: not-claimed
  • Definition: Response p driving form change; its realization is selected independently of the written nodal product.
  • Domain: Tangent response in the chosen form chart, with units [x]/([nu_f][t]).
  • Premises: Supply the pressure law and its consumed state. The native form/phase/capacity/topology mixture is one specified realization.
  • Dependencies: epi, capacity, phase, support, clock
  • Owner: Pressure scope.
  • Evidence: Specified relational map.
  • Implementation: Native pressure.
  • Tests: Pressure orientation.
  • Limits: Stored and refreshed pressure differ. The full mixture is not generally a fixed-metric gradient; retrospective derivative reconstruction is not prediction.

docs.title: Nodal equation and complete closure
docs.text:
• Status: maintained
  • Basis: identity
  • Emergence: not-claimed
  • Definition: The unforced continuous form row is dx/dt = nu_f * p.
  • Domain: An admitted form chart, pressure, capacity and clock.
  • Premises: This model identity requires additional laws for all consumed state and events to determine a full evolution.
  • Dependencies: epi, capacity, pressure, clock
  • Owner: Nodal equation.
  • Evidence: Integrated form.
  • Implementation: Canonical derivative, integrators.
  • Tests: Nodal equation, forcing scope.
  • Limits: Declared Gamma adds an independent rate and can move form at zero capacity. Hybrid jumps are separate; the identity does not select their occurrence.

docs.title: Conditional relational exchange law
docs.text:
• Status: maintained
  • Basis: constitutive
  • Emergence: not-claimed
  • Definition: Joint rows xdot = nu_f(-eq/d + wg) and thetadot = (w/beta)nu_f*q/H, where q_i=sum_neighbors(x_i-x_j) and d_i is the degree.
  • Domain: Fixed connected simple reciprocal unit support with at least two nodes, held nonnegative capacities, e≥0, w,beta>0 and admitted phase chamber.
  • Premises: Native pressure and joint storage plus the owner's capacity/locality premises and common-phase-clock convention.
  • Dependencies: nodal-equation, phase-metric
  • Owner: Capacity-separable law.
  • Evidence: Conditional phase-row classification; storage/locality classification.
  • Implementation: Relational engine.
  • Tests: Exchange execution.
  • Limits: This opt-in law differs from operator execution. The nodal identity does not select its coefficients or locality premises; compatible passive countermodels can change response while sharing equilibria.

docs.title: Conditional smooth-sine exchange law
docs.text:
• Status: maintained
  • Basis: constitutive
  • Emergence: not-claimed
  • Definition: With K=diag(nu_i/d_i), unit graph Laplacian L and S_i=sum_neighbors sin(theta_j-theta_i), the baseline rows are xdot=-eKLx+(w/pi)KS and thetadot=(w/(betapi))KL*x.
  • Domain: Fixed finite connected simple reciprocal unit support with at least two nodes, held nonnegative capacities, e>=0, w,beta>0 and finite signed form/circular phase.
  • Premises: Select both rows, cosine storage and clock without forcing/events. Conservation, locality and phase-information assumptions remain conditional constitutive premises.
  • Dependencies: nodal-equation, phase, capacity, support
  • Owner: Complete smooth-law comparison.
  • Evidence: Balance and continuation; constitutive nonselection.
  • Implementation: Shared comparison/rates, admission.
  • Tests: Complete-law controls, admission.
  • Limits: This changes native form and phase rows, not merely phase admission. Storage, smoothness or a shared tangent does not uniquely select it. Individual theorems impose additional premises; detached readers do not replace Network.step_relational.

docs.title: Derived structure and scoped dynamical results
Relative resultant, phase metric and mobility
docs.text:
• Status: maintained
  • Basis: derived
  • Emergence: not-claimed
  • Definition: z_i = sum_j exp(i(theta_j-theta_i)); g_i = Arg(z_i)/pi; H_i = piabs(z_i)*sinc(Arg(z_i)); phase mobility is nu_i/H_i.
  • Domain: Reciprocal unit support without isolates, nonzero z_i and Arg(z_i) in (-pi,pi); H_i is positive on this regular chart. Acute edges suffice.
  • Premises: Use the unweighted neighbor resultant and sinc(a)=sin(a)/a, continuously extended to 1 at zero.
  • Dependencies: phase, support, capacity
  • Owner: Relational geometry.
  • Evidence: Phase-row derivation; regular-domain admission.
  • Implementation: Captured relational field.
  • Tests: Regular execution.
  • Limits: Zero-resultant and branch boundaries are not successful zero values. A certified chart is not a trajectory/rate enclosure; unresolved represented states can reject.

docs.title: Joint storage and signed exchange work
docs.text:
• Status: maintained
  • Basis: derived
  • Emergence: not-claimed
  • Definition: For S = E_D + beta*V, with E_D = sum_edges (x_i-x_j)^2/2 and V = sum_edges [1-cos(theta_j-theta_i)], the ideal balances are Sdot=-sum D_i and E_D_dot=-sum D_i+sum J_i. Count unordered edges once.
  • Domain: The selected native or baseline smooth-sine law on held unit support. With q=Lx, both have D_i=enu_iq_i^2/d_i; native exchange is J_i=wnu_iq_ig_i, while sine exchange is J_i=(w/pi)(nu_i/d_i)q_i*S_i.
  • Premises: Use one complete unforced continuous law with held support; boundary inputs and support-event jumps require their separate balance terms.
  • Dependencies: relational-law, sine-law
  • Owner: Joint balances, sine channel work.
  • Evidence: Native work identity; sine balance.
  • Implementation: Native field work, sine rate/work kernel.
  • Tests: Native work, sine complete-law controls.
  • Limits: Storage is not physical or tetrad energy. Equal storage/loss need not give equal trajectories. Instantaneous power, accumulated work and endpoint storage differ; retain boundary work, signed remainders and numerical/event defects.

docs.title: Pure-EPI diffusion and relaxation
docs.text:
• Status: maintained
  • Basis: derived
  • Emergence: conditional
  • Definition: Isolated form pressure is -L_rw*x; fixed positive capacities and reciprocal nonnegative conductance give consensus when the positive-conductance graph is connected.
  • Domain: Source-free form channel, fixed conductance/support and held positive capacities; disconnected components and isolates have separate conclusions.
  • Premises: Only EPI pressure, no forcing/events. The generator conserves the conductance-strength/capacity-weighted form total.
  • Dependencies: nodal-equation, support
  • Owner: Diffusion stability.
  • Evidence: Ideal theorem.
  • Implementation: Structural diffusion.
  • Tests: Diffusion controls.
  • Limits: Other channels, directed support or changing capacities need separate proofs. Relaxation toward consensus does not establish NFR formation.

docs.title: Conditional pattern formation and recovery
docs.text:
• Status: maintained
  • Basis: derived
  • Emergence: conditional
  • Definition: Recovery restores a declared identity near it; formation reaches that identity from a preparation lacking it. Retention is an additional time-domain claim.
  • Domain: Each native recovery/capture or sine formation theorem retains its own support, loss, capacity and initial/target domains.
  • Premises: Match the complete law, environment, clock and uncertainty throughout entry and any retained interval.
  • Dependencies: relational-law, sine-law, storage-work, winding, nfr
  • Owner: Native recovery, sine formation/retention.
  • Evidence: Native validated transit; conservative same-orbit theorem.
  • Implementation: Native transit, sine formation certificate.
  • Tests: Native transit, same-orbit formation.
  • Limits: Sufficient storage is not entry. An existential source ball or a mapped-source prefix does not automatically supply an independent numerical preparation ball. Physical identity and source selection remain open.

docs.title: Conditional moving-pattern retention
docs.text:
• Status: maintained
  • Basis: derived
  • Emergence: conditional
  • Definition: A declared geometric identity persists over a specified interval while the full state can evolve.
  • Domain: Conservative unit sine C5 identities with full environment retained; moving-reference and energy-speed certificates have separate domains.
  • Premises: Supplied initial identity, full-state uncertainty, positive chart margins and the selected storage/travel bound.
  • Dependencies: sine-law, storage-work, winding, closure
  • Owner: Moving-reference window, energy-speed retention.
  • Evidence: Relative-storage bootstrap; whole-network travel bound.
  • Implementation: Reference window, cycle retention.
  • Tests: Full-row window controls, cycle retention.
  • Limits: Maintenance is not attraction or first acquisition. Backward-valid windows constrain possible entry; regional storage alone cannot replace the full environmental budget.

docs.title: Conditional structural resonance
docs.text:
• Status: maintained
  • Basis: derived
  • Emergence: conditional
  • Definition: A positive finite-frequency maximum of a declared stable input/output gain.
  • Domain: Normalized-sine tangent dynamics at a critical pattern, with positive capacity/loss/coupling and a positive-definite phase Hessian modulo the common origin.
  • Premises: Specify probe and readout, retaining full support; collocated and remote-response theorems have different observation hypotheses.
  • Dependencies: sine-law, phase, capacity, support, clock
  • Owner: Resonance foundations.
  • Evidence: Work-conjugate gain theorem; observation-dependent modes.
  • Implementation: Sine resonance assessments.
  • Tests: Independent tangent and response controls.
  • Limits: A gain peak neither supplies its probe nor proves periodic motion, formation or physical resonance. RA execution and the auxiliary graph-wave model are separate mechanisms.

docs.title: Conditional autonomous nonlinear pulse
docs.text:
• Status: maintained
  • Basis: derived
  • Emergence: conditional
  • Definition: Nonstationary periodic form/phase exchange under a complete autonomous law.
  • Domain: Zero-loss sine law: isolated unit P2, nonnegative capacities of positive sum, 0<E<2beta; separately, the exact doubled-C5 family with common positive held capacity, 0<H<betacos(2*pi/5).
  • Premises: Supplied support, nonzero preparation, positive beta/coupling and clock; replica internal coordinates obey the exact invariant-family conditions.
  • Dependencies: sine-law, phase, capacity, support, clock
  • Owner: Permanent-pulse admission.
  • Evidence: P2 libration and dissipative obstruction, exact internal pulse and observation-dependent period.
  • Implementation: P2 pulse, replica pulse.
  • Tests: P2 controls, replica field/period.
  • Limits: Exact continuous periods do not certify Euler orbits. Replica labeled/unordered periods differ by two; means stay fixed while constituents move. Sufficiently small nonzero replica pulses are transversely unstable. Conservation selects neither zero loss nor amplitude and cannot create motion from equilibrium.

docs.title: Collective contact pulse and internal feedback
docs.text:
• Status: maintained
  • Basis: derived
  • Emergence: not-claimed
  • Definition: Mean form contrast and lifted contact phase obey projected rows with feedback from unequal contacts.
  • Domain: Conservative unit-capacity sine law on C5 with five private leaves, using declared continuous contact phase lifts and clock tau=t/pi.
  • Premises: Retain actual nodal state and contact deviations; collective storage h_c and the signed remainder H-5h_c depend on the chosen lifts.
  • Dependencies: sine-law, storage-work, phase, closure
  • Owner: Actual mean-contact balance.
  • Evidence: Projected feedback and storage identity.
  • Implementation: Collective-pulse observer.
  • Tests: Independent full-row/lift controls.
  • Limits: The mean coordinates need not close or be periodic. A transfer sign or initial derivative proves neither winding acquisition, maintained identity, resonance nor a physical reservoir.

docs.title: Conditional parametric pulse instability
docs.text:
• Status: maintained
  • Basis: derived
  • Emergence: conditional
  • Definition: Exponential transverse growth generated by periodic coefficients of a full autonomous variational law, established by an unstable return multiplier.
  • Domain: Sufficiently small positive internal amplitude in the exact conservative doubled-C5 pulse family, with the full twenty real state directions retained.
  • Premises: Use the pulse theorem's exact family, capacity and clock; retain collective feedback and the amplitude-dependent period.
  • Dependencies: autonomous-pulse, storage-work
  • Owner: Complete variation and symmetry-correct return.
  • Evidence: Exact small-amplitude splitting and analytic remainder.
  • Implementation: Detached variation and asymptotic splitting assessments.
  • Tests: Full fine Jacobian, harmonic solvability and return-scope controls.
  • Limits: Existence of a small-amplitude instability interval supplies no numeric threshold or chosen-amplitude verdict. Neutral shear is distinct from exponential growth; leaving a waveform need not destroy geometric identity.

docs.title: Conditional nonlinear recurrence
docs.text:
• Status: maintained
  • Basis: derived
  • Emergence: conditional
  • Definition: Full form/circular-phase state returns arbitrarily close to its initial state at unbounded positive times, without requiring a period.
  • Domain: Conservative sine law on finite connected unit support with positive held capacities, a positive energy sublevel and a nonzero-width conserved-mean interval.
  • Premises: Positive beta/coupling; no input, clipping or events. Use circular phases and the theorem's ambient volume measure.
  • Dependencies: sine-law, phase, capacity, support, clock
  • Owner: Full nonlinear recurrence.
  • Evidence: Compactness, invariant volume and exceptions.
  • Implementation: Family-level recurrence.
  • Tests: Invariant/domain controls.
  • Limits: The result is almost everywhere, not a verdict for one chosen state, grid or fixed-energy surface. It gives no return time or frequency. Winding protection needs an independent phase-sector barrier, not recurrence alone.

docs.title: Derived form geometry
docs.text:
• Status: maintained
  • Basis: derived
  • Emergence: not-claimed
  • Definition: Regional EPI contrasts determine Cartesian/Gram observations and, away from zero contrast, an orientation angle.
  • Domain: Supplied ordered regions, declared form chart and any independent held source used as an orientation reference.
  • Premises: Project and differentiate the admitted fine law; retain source-relative information when a source distinguishes orientations.
  • Dependencies: epi, nodal-equation
  • Owner: Derived form phase.
  • Evidence: Inherited observations, source-relative response.
  • Implementation: Form geometry, source-relative form.
  • Tests: Form geometry, source response.
  • Limits: The derived angle is unavailable at zero contrast and is not automatically the primitive phase consumed by pressure.

docs.title: Conditional dynamical scale inheritance
docs.text:
• Status: maintained
  • Basis: derived
  • Emergence: conditional
  • Definition: A fine-to-collective map intertwines the admitted evolution with a stated law family and explicit unit changes.
  • Domain: The supplied synchronized replica submanifold of the native or separately declared sine law; retained internal coordinates are required away from synchronization.
  • Premises: Fixed replicated support, fiber-compatible capacities/state and complete law; iterated maps must compose.
  • Dependencies: relational-law, sine-law, support, capacity, phase, clock
  • Owner: Scale inheritance.
  • Evidence: Native exact replication, replica composition and constitutive freedom.
  • Implementation: Native field, retained sine state.
  • Tests: Complete replica rows, counterfamily inheritance.
  • Limits: This does not derive generic fractality, a fractal dimension, spontaneous hierarchy or unique dynamics. Discarding internal coordinates requires closure or memory evidence; a repeated graph alone is insufficient.

docs.title: Coarse closure and hidden-state obstruction
docs.text:
• Status: maintained
  • Basis: derived
  • Emergence: not-claimed
  • Definition: A retained state y=R(z) closes when DR(z)F(z) agrees on each fiber of R under the declared fine law.
  • Domain: Each linear, native or sine reduction has its own realizable state/support domain; observed outputs need not constitute such a state.
  • Premises: Specify law, observation, admissible fine states and discarded information. An autonomous subsystem must retain boundary dynamics or derived memory.
  • Dependencies: nodal-equation, relational-law, sine-law
  • Owner: Composition and closure, global pair state.
  • Evidence: Instantaneous interface versus future state; exact pair realizability/closure.
  • Implementation: Linear realization, retained pair state.
  • Tests: Linear closure, global pair rows and realizability.
  • Limits: Instantaneous interaction sufficiency, future closure and recovery from observations differ. On doubled C5, (X,Z) supplies currents but realized (X,Z,P,U,W) retains predictive internal information through cancellation. These are derived coordinates, not new constitutive parameters; tangent or snapshot agreement alone proves no nonlinear closure.

docs.title: Controlled predictive approximation
docs.text:
• Status: maintained
  • Basis: derived
  • Emergence: not-claimed
  • Definition: A bound on the difference between a selected full-state observation and an independently evolved reduced prediction from an admitted initialization.
  • Domain: The retained source-child result uses its 45-node reciprocal law, unit held capacities, acute energy domain and no events; other reductions require their own bounds.
  • Premises: Match law, clock, initialization, conserved means, domain and norm; retain hidden-state forcing and accumulated error, not only a snapshot discrepancy.
  • Dependencies: closure, storage-work, capacity, sine-law
  • Owner: Independent-core comparison.
  • Evidence: Hidden relaxation and instantaneous error; uniform accumulated prediction error.
  • Implementation: Shared tracking certificate.
  • Tests: Certificate contracts, complete-law proof controls.
  • Limits: Exact closure, instantaneous tolerance and accumulated prediction error are different claims. This bound does not select an NFR identity, establish formation, transfer across events or changing capacities, or demonstrate a runtime speedup.

docs.title: Derived hidden-state memory
docs.text:
• Status: maintained
  • Basis: derived
  • Emergence: not-claimed
  • Definition: Eliminating unobserved coordinates retains their propagated initialization and history-dependent influence in the visible equation.
  • Domain: A complete fine law and fixed observation; diffusion and nonlinear relational results have different hypotheses.
  • Premises: Retain hidden initialization and forcing; admit approximation error separately.
  • Dependencies: closure
  • Owner: EPI memory, relational memory.
  • Evidence: Exact elimination; nonlinear forecast scope.
  • Implementation: EPI memory, coordinate elimination.
  • Tests: Linear memory, nonlinear controls.
  • Limits: Memory selects no microscopic law. A signed remainder is not a sufficient hidden state; exact elimination does not imply forgetting, irreversible damping or a finite-history approximation.

docs.title: Retained relational phase offset
docs.text:
• Status: maintained
  • Basis: derived
  • Emergence: conditional
  • Definition: Recovery of the same internal twist can leave a preparation-dependent common phase relative to a retained reference.
  • Domain: The ideal native isolated unit C5 law near an acute winding-one twist, with centered perturbations and a common phase frame.
  • Premises: Positive homogeneous capacity/coefficient conditions, a declared reference/readout and the selected contact or isolation protocol.
  • Dependencies: phase, relational-law, pattern-recovery
  • Owner: Retained collective phase.
  • Evidence: Skew-pairing derivation; finite contact and retained record.
  • Implementation: Cycle memory, contact/retention.
  • Tests: Independent mechanism, finite error budgets.
  • Limits: Common phase is not an intrinsic isolated-ring label. A port signal alone is not a lasting receiver record; later interventions, nondestructive readout and physical identity need separate admission. These readers execute no contact.

docs.title: Supplied bridge interfaces
docs.text:
• Status: maintained
  • Basis: derived
  • Emergence: not-claimed
  • Definition: A supplied bridge changes degree, form contrasts and phase resultants; both endpoint fields and the signed support-event cost are retained.
  • Domain: Admitted simple unit native graphs before/after attachment or relocation, with unchanged nodal state and the owner's component/phase-domain conditions.
  • Premises: Supply the candidate; retain internal state/relative frames and the same law. Passivity and recovery require additional premises.
  • Dependencies: relational-law, phase-metric, storage-work
  • Owner: Support-event interfaces.
  • Evidence: Bridge identity; event nonselection.
  • Implementation: Shared attachment and relocation observers.
  • Tests: Static attachment, relocation and budget controls.
  • Limits: A detached report neither changes support nor selects occurrence/time. Represented costs are not trigonometric enclosures; admission alone authenticates neither work nor subsequent recovery.

docs.title: Cycle winding
docs.text:
• Status: maintained
  • Basis: derived
  • Emergence: not-claimed
  • Definition: Integer cycle count from consistently wrapped oriented phase gaps divided by 2*pi.
  • Domain: A supplied oriented cycle and declared branch/availability conditions.
  • Premises: Constancy along a path requires exclusion of relevant branch crossings and accounting for support changes.
  • Dependencies: phase, support
  • Owner: Native cycle boundary, conservative regional passage.
  • Evidence: Native phase-domain invariant; sine whole-window passage.
  • Implementation: Winding certificates.
  • Tests: Winding admission.
  • Limits: Winding, acute geometry and maintained identity differ. A principal-branch crossing need not be singular for the smooth sine law; an integer snapshot proves neither formation nor physical charge/spin.

docs.title: Diagnostics and their availability
Coherence read-out (C)
docs.text:
• Status: maintained
  • Basis: diagnostic
  • Emergence: not-claimed
  • Definition: Configured map C=1/(1+mean(abs(p))+mean(abs(xdot))) in declared pressure/rate scales.
  • Domain: Admitted finite stored arguments; local and aggregate reductions have different scopes.
  • Premises: The reciprocal observation is selected, not uniquely derived from the nodal equation.
  • Dependencies: pressure, nodal-equation
  • Owner: Telemetry scope.
  • Evidence: Core metric definitions.
  • Implementation: Shared kernel.
  • Tests: Coherence reduction.
  • Limits: High C proves neither complete equilibrium nor stability, identity or formation. Stored rates need not be fresh nodal predictions.

docs.title: Pressure/rate equilibrium test
docs.text:
• Status: maintained
  • Basis: diagnostic
  • Emergence: not-claimed
  • Definition: A tolerance predicate on pressure and form-rate magnitudes, exposed by is_structural_equilibrium.
  • Domain: Declared finite arguments and nonnegative tolerances.
  • Premises: Supplied quantities and tolerances determine the diagnostic verdict.
  • Dependencies: pressure, nodal-equation
  • Owner: Diagnostic scope.
  • Evidence: Equilibrium boundary.
  • Implementation: Shared predicate.
  • Tests: Equilibrium scope.
  • Limits: A tolerated zero form rate is not a full phase/capacity/support fixed point, particularly at zero capacity or with forcing.

docs.title: Sense Index (Si)
docs.text:
• Status: maintained
  • Basis: diagnostic
  • Emergence: not-claimed
  • Definition: Configured clipped mixture of normalized capacity, phase dispersion and pressure magnitude.
  • Domain: Admitted inputs and current normalization policy.
  • Premises: Selected weights and reductions define the score; controllers may explicitly consume it.
  • Dependencies: capacity, phase, pressure
  • Owner: Si definition and consumers.
  • Evidence: Diagnostic closure limits.
  • Implementation: Sense Index.
  • Tests: Study diagnostics.
  • Limits: Controller use does not promote Si to an emergent law, complete state or proved stability margin.

docs.title: Structural-field tetrad
docs.text:
• Status: maintained
  • Basis: diagnostic
  • Emergence: not-claimed
  • Definition: Interface (Phi_s, abs(grad phi), K_phi, xi_C) observing pressure aggregation, local phase structure and coherence range.
  • Domain: Each constituent retains its independent data and availability conditions.
  • Premises: Four complementary questions motivate the interface; completeness is a separate mathematical obligation.
  • Dependencies: potential, phase-gradient, phase-curvature, coherence-length
  • Owner: Diagnostic degrees and reconstruction.
  • Evidence: Dynamical non-reconstruction.
  • Implementation: Shared fields.
  • Tests: Read-out consistency.
  • Limits: The tetrad does not reconstruct general form, capacity, support, history or future evolution; unavailable fields cannot certify a complete safety verdict.

docs.title: Structural potential (Phi_s)
docs.text:
• Status: maintained
  • Basis: diagnostic
  • Emergence: not-claimed
  • Definition: Nonlocal aggregation Phi_s(i)=sum_j p_j/d(i,j)^2 over other nodes under the declared distance convention.
  • Domain: Admitted pressure and lengths, with specified unreachable/zero-distance handling.
  • Premises: The inverse-square aggregation is a selected observation kernel.
  • Dependencies: pressure, support
  • Owner: Structural fields.
  • Evidence: Topology-dependent bounds.
  • Implementation: Potential field.
  • Tests: Field observations.
  • Limits: Potential is not universally bounded by pi, the relational storage or an independently derived physical interaction potential.

docs.title: Phase gradient magnitude
docs.text:
• Status: maintained
  • Basis: diagnostic
  • Emergence: not-claimed
  • Definition: Mean absolute wrapped separation from the node's declared neighbors.
  • Domain: Finite phases and supported neighbor conventions; circular bound pi.
  • Premises: Mean separation is the selected local diagnostic.
  • Dependencies: phase, support
  • Owner: Structural fields.
  • Evidence: Gradient scope.
  • Implementation: Phase gradient.
  • Tests: Field observations.
  • Limits: A warning cut is not a derived instability threshold or a future-transition proof.

docs.title: Circular phase curvature (K_phi)
docs.text:
• Status: maintained
  • Basis: diagnostic
  • Emergence: not-claimed

docs.title: Card template and admission checks
docs.text:
Revise a card and its responsible owner together, retaining a stable lowercase ID. Use the exact field order below and replace instructional values with scoped statements or references. Dependencies contains existing comma-separated card IDs or none; it is a declared prerequisite graph, not a mathematical proof.

<a id="new-concept"></a>

### Concept title

- **Status:** maintained or candidate
- **Basis:** primitive, identity, constitutive, derived, diagnostic, policy, auxiliary or hypothesis
- **Emergence:** not-claimed or conditional
- **Definition:** State what the concept means.
- **Domain:** State where it is defined and executable.
- **Premises:** Name supplied assumptions and choices.
- **Dependencies:** existing-id, another-id
- **Owner:** Link the maintained theory/docs definition owner.
- **Evidence:** Link the evidence; a derived concept needs a theory derivation anchor.
- **Implementation:** Link its src owner, or write none: followed by a reason.
- **Tests:** Link relevant test files, or write none: followed by a reason.
- **Limits:** State what does not follow from the declaration.

The glossary checker validates card structure, labels, local references, declared dependencies and index freshness. A maintained implemented concept needs linked tests; derived claims need a derivation section and declared dependencies; hypotheses retain candidate status. These checks cannot verify a proof, test adequacy or physical truth, and never promote a concept automatically.

Reproducibility also requires fixed source, configuration, inputs, ordering, precision and execution path; a seed alone is insufficient. Use TESTING.md for validation and the research program for the next research task.

docs.title: Structural Tetrad: Diagnostic Degrees and Reconstruction Scope
docs.text: Status: Four canonical diagnostic channels. Universal minimality and complete state reconstruction are open questions with explicit hypotheses required. Definitions are centralized in the field guide; proofs and counterexamples are centralized in the mathematical scope note.

docs.title: 1. Statement
docs.text:
The structural tetrad (Φ_s, |∇φ|, K_φ, ξ_C) is the engine's selected readout of pressure accumulation, local phase stress, local circular curvature, and spatial correlation. All four fields retain canonical status.

The selection is a diagnostic design. It does not establish that every scalar observable is a function of four reported quantities, or that the tetrad determines a full graph state and its evolution under

∂EPI/∂t = ν_f · ΔNFR.

A completeness claim must specify a state space, admissible observables, gauge identifications, and what information is retained by the readout. A minimality claim must additionally prove that no selected channel is redundant for that specified task. These stronger claims are not established by naming four structural questions or by computing the fields on a collection of graphs.

docs.title: 2. Four diagnostic questions
docs.text:
Question Field Construction How much pressure accumulates from other nodes? Φ_s Distance-weighted aggregation of ΔNFR How misaligned is a node with its neighbors? |∇φ| Mean magnitude of wrapped phase differences How does its phase differ from the neighborhood mean? K_φ Wrapped deviation from the circular mean At what spatial scale does coherence correlate? ξ_C Correlation-decay fit with spectral fallback

This organizes local phase information and non-local aggregation/correlation. Φ_s is a per-node value with global dependence; it is not a purely local quantity. ξ_C compresses a spatial correlation profile into a length. The table does not exhaust every possible graph observable.

docs.title: 3. The operator-derivative tower
3.1 Construction
docs.text:
ΔNFR → distance-kernel aggregation → Φ_s
phase → wrapped neighbor differences → |∇φ|
phase → circular-neighborhood deviation → K_φ
local coherence → spatial correlation → ξ_C

The first two phase operations are related to first and second derivatives. For an undirected graph, an oriented incidence matrix gives an edge gradient, and composing it with its weighted adjoint gives the graph Laplacian. For small phase spread within a consistent branch and matching neighbor weights, circular curvature approaches L_rw φ. The equality is a linearized description; the exact implemented field uses circular means and wrapping.

docs.title: 3.2 Algebraic generation does not terminate information at second order
docs.text:
Higher Laplacian powers are compositions of the same operator. This fact does not mean their actions are linearly dependent or recoverable from lossy pointwise summaries. If L has at least four distinct eigenvalues, then I, L, L², and L³ are linearly independent. Otherwise a polynomial of degree at most three would vanish at four distinct eigenvalues.

The finite-dimensional cutoff is controlled by L's minimal polynomial. It depends on the graph and is not universally second order. In addition, |∇φ| discards signs and ξ_C discards most of the correlation profile. A generating set of operators and a sufficient set of state statistics are different mathematical objects.

docs.title: 3.3 Dynamical non-reconstruction
docs.text: At fixed graph, phase, EPI, and pure-EPI pressure, a uniform rescaling of ν_f leaves the tetrad unchanged while scaling ∂EPI/∂t = ν_f ΔNFR. Consequently the tetrad alone does not determine the full dynamical state. The structural triad, frequency, pressure law, and graph remain part of the model.

docs.title: 3.4 Conditional reconstruction in the pure EPI channel
docs.text:
The negative result above identifies capacity as a necessary predictive model parameter. A graph-specific positive result is also available when the complete nodal structural-potential field is retained.

For fixed connected reciprocal nonnegative conductance with positive nodal strengths and fixed positive capacities, let K be the canonical inverse-square shortest-path kernel on its declared distance domain. With unit pure-EPI channel coefficient, pressure gives

Phi_s = -K L_rw x,    x = EPI.

Write O=-K L_rw. Since L_rw 1=0, uniform EPI shifts are always invisible to Phi_s. If rank(O)=N-1, this is the only invisible EPI direction. Appending the fixed-capacity conserved mean

m(x) = sum_i (d_i/nu_i)x_i / sum_i(d_i/nu_i)

makes [O; m] injective and hence reconstructs absolute EPI in exact arithmetic. Together with the capacity vector and known graph, this determines the future pure-diffusion trajectory. Thus, for this restricted algebraic task, the full potential field plus one zero-mode scalar is sufficient for form reconstruction, while capacity remains necessary to determine the clock/generator. Numerical promotion additionally requires scale-aware rank and residual checks.

epi_diffusion_reconstruction_certificate computes the potential and augmented ranks with separate scale-aware SVD thresholds, then requires a small relative reconstruction residual before it reports numerical success. The exhaustive NetworkX graph atlas through six nodes gives rank(O)=N-1 on all 142 connected simple graphs in that finite domain. This is a measured finite-domain result, not a proof for every graph, weight or structural-potential kernel.

Algebraic rank is also weaker than robust reconstruction. On a four-node weighted star with edge weights [10^-3, 10^3, 10^3], the rank remains N-1 but the nonzero singular-value condition number exceeds 10^10. Thus an exact observer can be practically unstable under extreme geometry. Uniformly scaling all conductances to 10^-8 or 10^8 also preserves the structural nullity but can make the unscaled augmented observer numerically singular. The certificate reports its thresholds, condition number and relative residual so downstream inverse methods can distinguish algebraic identifiability from numerical resolution.

Global tetrad summaries remain insufficient because they discard the nodal potential field. Changing capacity ratios also removes the fixed conserved mean, as shown by the time-varying result in TNFR_DIFFUSION_STABILITY_THEOREM.md.

docs.title: 4. Field scales and selected thresholds
docs.text:
The exact phase-wrap maximum π must be distinguished from policy values expressed as fractions of π. The numerical values below remain unchanged in canonical.py.

Field Exact or conditional mathematical scale Canonical telemetry policy Φ_s ‖Φ_s‖∞ ≤ ‖B_G‖∞ ‖ΔNFR‖∞ for a fixed distance kernel Per-node π/4; U6 drift π/2 |∇φ| At most π by wrapped-angle definition Warning level π/16 K_φ Absolute value at most π by wrapping Warning level 0.9π ξ_C Spectral reference 1/√λ_gap when a positive graph gap is used Configured diameter and mean-distance comparisons

docs.title: 4.1 Structural potential
docs.text:
The canonical exponent is α = 2 in B_ij = d(i,j)⁻². The resulting field is linear in ΔNFR and unbounded under pressure rescaling. Even at zero phase, unit pressure on K₄ gives Φ_s = 3. No phase-wrap argument can enforce π/4 or π/2 for this linear field without an additional pressure/geometry constraint.

The chain sums Σ d⁻² = ζ(2) and Σ d⁻⁴ = ζ(4) are correct particular values. They do not uniquely select exponent 2: absolute chain sums converge for all α > 1 and independent unit-variance pressure sums for all α > 1/2. Graph families with growing distance shells need their own summability assumptions. The inverse-square kernel is the canonical modeling choice, not a uniqueness theorem from those series.

docs.title: 4.2 Phase gradient
docs.text:
The mean of absolute wrapped neighbor differences is bounded by π. The warning value π/16 is selected policy; a measured synchronization onset depends on the experiment's frequency spread, topology, and coupling protocol.

Canonical aggregate coherence is

C(t) = 1 / (1 + mean|ΔNFR| + mean|dEPI|).

It does not identify the spatial location of phase stress. It also is not scale invariant: with dEPI = 0 and uniform |ΔNFR| = 1, C(t) = 1/2; doubling pressure gives 1/3. Only the separate normalized dispersion statistic C_disp = 1 − σ_ΔNFR/ΔNFR_max is invariant under proportional positive pressure scaling when its denominator is nonzero.

docs.title: 4.3 Circular curvature
docs.text: Where the circular mean is available, K_φ = wrap(φ_i − circular_mean(neighbors)) gives |K_φ| ≤ π by definition. The 0.9π threshold is an operational margin inside that exact bound. The shared reader accepts every nonzero represented phasor resultant without an arbitrary small-magnitude cutoff; exact represented cancellation on nonempty support makes curvature unavailable. Isolates retain the documented zero convention. These arithmetic availability conditions do not prove a trigonometric singularity or a singularity of a continuous manifold.

docs.title: 4.4 Correlation length
docs.text:
The current estimator first fits decay of a pressure-derived coherence correlation against graph distance. If that fit is unsuitable, it uses a spectral reference from the graph: the inverse square root of its smallest normalized-Laplacian eigenvalue above 1e-9. On an admitted connected undirected graph this is 1/√λ₂ only when that gap clears the numerical cutoff. A fitted correlation length need not equal that reference for every state; exponential spatial decay is itself a fitting assumption.

On disconnected graphs, a second-smallest eigenvalue and a smallest positive eigenvalue need not coincide. Reports must identify the estimator/fallback and graph regime. A failed fit or large estimate alone does not prove a phase transition.

docs.title: 5. Diagnostic removal studies
docs.text:
Each field addresses a distinct diagnostic task: accumulated pressure, local mismatch magnitude, local curvature, or correlation range. This motivates retaining all four channels. A formal non-redundancy study should construct explicit pairs of states with identical retained readouts and a differing omitted readout, or specify a detection problem and prove the omitted channel changes the decision.

Descriptions such as “a blind spot appears” require the actual fixture, readout resolution, and detection threshold. Passing many implementation tests does not prove universal irreducibility. Nor does usefulness of each channel prove that no additional observable can carry independent information.

The strong claim of a minimal complete representation therefore remains open until its target state space and equivalence relation are specified and the appropriate injectivity and non-redundancy results are proved.

A positive example with those choices fixed is the P5 reflection quotient. Its three even coordinates and constrained quadratic hidden-mode matrix reconstruct form up to reflection under the declared pure-EPI law. This is not the four-field tetrad, a universal state basis, or a reduction to three dimensions near the reflection-fixed stratum. The linked derivation owns the injectivity, rate, decoder and field-covariance results.

docs.title: 6. Energy, currents, and conservation
docs.text:
The tetrad can participate in energy-like diagnostics with phase and pressure currents:

V = ½ Σ_i (Φ_s(i)² + |∇φ|(i)² + K_φ(i)²),
T = ½ Σ_i (J_φ(i)² + J_ΔNFR(i)²).

These are nonnegative functionals of measured fields. Their existence does not establish state reconstruction, does not make ΔNFR equal to −∂V/∂EPI, and does not turn all implemented operators into Hamiltonian transformations. Conjugate coordinates belong to a separately specified substrate model.

Likewise a continuity residual or measured energy descent is evidence about the tested trajectory. Universal Noether conservation and asymptotic stability require the stated symmetry, flow, and Lyapunov hypotheses. The mathematical scope is developed in the variational note and the conservation note; the tetrad's canonical diagnostic status does not supply those proofs.

docs.title: 7. Symmetry-restricted research
docs.text:
Symmetry can restrict which sectors a graph readout detects. A statement about the tetrad on a particular prime-ladder graph with uniform parameters must name that graph, its action, and the parameter restrictions. Invariance under that action constrains reach; it does not imply that the tetrad spans every vector in the invariant sector.

The REMESH-∞ and Riemann programs use separate projection and observability constructions. Their particular graph certificates do not establish a universal complete “smooth structural sector” on arbitrary networks. See REMESH_INFINITY_DERIVATION.md and TNFR_RIEMANN_RESEARCH_NOTES.md for the precise program assumptions and open conjectures.

docs.title: 8. Verification scope
docs.text:
Claim Supported scope Four canonical field APIs exist Definitions and implementation contracts Phase magnitudes are at most π Exact wrapped-angle bounds Potential is linear in pressure Exact fixed-kernel identity Potential has a uniform π-fraction maximum False without additional pressure/geometry assumptions Three operations bound every diffusion relaxation time False; the 21-node path is a counterexample Laplacian compositions prove tetrad completeness False inference; operator generation is not reconstruction Tetrad is a universal minimal sufficient state statistic Not established; task-specific quotients require explicit injectivity and dynamics proofs Full Φ_s plus one zero-mode scalar reconstructs EPI Conditional on rank(-K L_rw)=N-1, fixed graph and pure EPI pressure Rank condition holds on every connected graph Open; measured on all 142 connected simple graph-atlas cases through six nodes Full-rank potential reconstruction is uniformly well-conditioned False across unrestricted weights; extreme weighted stars are arbitrarily ill-conditioned candidates

Operator gains, discretization steps, numerical clamps, and safety thresholds remain configured policies unless an explicit derivation with its assumptions is supplied. A formula using π alone is not sufficient evidence of a physical necessity.

docs.text:
• AGENTS.md: canonical synthesis.
  • Field definitions and APIs.

  • Fundamental theory: broader theory context.

docs.title: Aggregate operators and native transitions
docs.text:
This owner asks when several registered constituent actions are exactly one registered action on a specified aggregate. It uses the existing shared operator implementation and ordered-language descent criterion. The native collective calculus instead retains the constituent state needed to describe native execution. A sufficient coordinate description does not itself establish operator inheritance. This owner also identifies the state needed when an inherited partial transition reaches its clipping boundary. The research program owns the research queue.

The results below concern a declared arithmetic aggregation and restricted event or native-transition domains. They neither define the only possible collective NFR nor derive a universal collective law, organizational identity or physical event occurrence. A configured selector remains a supplied policy even when its decisions descend to the aggregate.

docs.title: A sufficient domain for one aggregate Resonance
docs.text: Conditional result. Two consecutive Resonance (RA) actions on a pair of nonadjacent twins can inherit exactly one registered RA on their aggregate, with unchanged factors. Internal form and capacity contrasts can both be nonzero. Paired phases, a common strict form sign and semantic kind, and duplicated consumed grammar context supply one sufficient domain. These are additional premises, not consequences of averaging or necessities of TNFR.

docs.title: State, support and execution domain
docs.text:
Use the unit, undirected doubled C5 support from the native calculus: block i contains two nonadjacent nodes, each connected to both members of blocks i-1 and i+1 (indices modulo five). The comparison graph is the simple unit C5. Its node i is assigned the following aggregate channels:

x_(i,-)=M_i-d_i,       x_(i,+)=M_i+d_i,
v_(i,-)=V_i-e_i,       v_(i,+)=V_i+e_i,
theta_(i,-)=theta_(i,+)=mu_i,
Q_i=(M_i,V_i,mu_i,kind_i,context_i).

Here x=EPI is signed form and v=nu_f is capacity. The phase coordinates use an explicit common real lift of width less than both mathematical pi and the represented runtime pi. They are not form-derived angles. Each coarse edge represents one neighboring block; equal fine multiplicity, rather than summed conductance, supplies the neighbor-average identity. This statement is about RA's actual unweighted compatible-neighbor reader, not a proposed diffusion law. The exact phase argument uses the ideal circle of period 2*pi, with represented coefficients and cutoff, and compares endpoints on that common lift. Runtime modulo by represented 2*pi and trigonometric rounding are separate realization errors, not exact circle identities.

Require the following common domain at each completed-pair boundary:

  • Every fine form belongs to one convex interval strictly inside the shared hard-clipping rails. The interval is either wholly above the operational trigger T=1e-9 or wholly below -T. All nodes have one common nonempty epi_kind. Thus a convex blend preserves both strict sign and kind.
  • All primitive values and configuration consumed by the selected path pass their actual admission. In particular V_i>|e_i|, and the fine and coarse amplified capacity proposals have finite representable arithmetic. A finite continuation needs sufficient headroom at every occurrence; direct RA does not itself impose the runtime's later VF_MAX clamp.
  • Fine and coarse graphs share the admitted factors rho=RA_epi_diff, b=RA_vf_amplification, c=RA_phase_coupling, with 0<rho<=1, b>0, 0<c<=1, and the same admitted U3 phase limit L. Every requested block has at least one live compatible neighbor.
  • Both twins and their coarse node have equal, separately owned consumed grammar context: bounded trace, persistent U2 debt, prior-Coherence flag, effective local operator ordinal and retention policy. The common context must admit RA under the shared grammar policy. For example, supplied Emission (AL), Coherence (IL) history with zero debt is sufficient; it is not a necessary precursor or a derived history.

Use the strict caller enforce_canonical_grammar followed by apply_glyph, with GRAMMAR_REJECTION_MODE="raise". A supplied coarse target expands into the two fine targets consecutively. There is no interleaved action, flow, pressure preparation, phase coordinator, capacity adaptation or callback between them. Support stays fixed. Both actions retain the direct path's secondary effects; this is neither a public-class equivalence nor an atomic stage. Existing valid stored pressure can be retained, but no pressure law is inferred or refreshed by these RA requests.

Optional telemetry may be collected and compared separately. It is not included in Q: two actual fine occurrences do not become one occurrence record. Exclude custom observers that feed additional state into execution.

docs.title: Same selected data, same registered action
docs.text:
On the declared common lift, the live admitted block set and its selected means are

J_i={j in {i-1,i+1}: abs(mu_j-mu_i)<=L},       J_i nonempty,
S_i=(sum_(j in J_i) M_j)/|J_i|,
eta_i=Arg_I(sum_(j in J_i) exp(i*mu_j)).

The phase lift of width less than pi makes the selected resultant nonzero and fixes its angle in the same interval. U3's wrapped differences give exactly this J_i. Both fine targets select both members of each block in J_i and no others. Consequently their selected form mean is

sum_(j in J_i) ((M_j-d_j)+(M_j+d_j))/(2*|J_i|) = S_i.

Their selected phase resultant is twice the coarse resultant, so their phase target is exactly eta_i. The two twins are nonadjacent: the first action changes none of the second's neighbors. Both consume these same selected data despite executing sequentially. The common strict form interval gives abs(S_i)>T, so every target uses the same registered capacity factor f=1+b. Common kind and convex, unclipped form mixing admit all fine identity proposals and the coarse proposal.

Applying the actual RA row to each twin and taking its mean and difference therefore gives

M_i'=(1-rho)*M_i+rho*S_i,       d_i'=(1-rho)*d_i,
V_i'=f*V_i,                    e_i'=f*e_i,
mu_i'=(1-c)*mu_i+c*eta_i,       a_i'=0.

These three mean rows and the unchanged kind are exactly one registered coarse RA with the same factors. All other blocks are unchanged. In ideal real arithmetic, writing P_i for the completed fine pair and R_i for the registered coarse action, this proves

Q(P_i(s)) = R_i(Q(s))

on the stated domain, including the consumed local grammar projection below. This is stronger than copying identical nodes: for rho<1, a nonzero internal form contrast survives, and any nonzero capacity contrast is amplified. Their event response need not be visible in the coarse primary channels for those channels to obey the same registered event rule.

docs.title: Admission, context and finite composition
docs.text:
For the compared actions, sign, kind, factor and represented-arithmetic admission are premises on the whole fine domain, not deductions from a coarse pass. With these premises, paired phases identify U3 admission on both sides. An empty live J_i rejects both paths before the first fine event. Identical valid contexts identify the remaining incremental grammar decisions. Resonance is U2-neutral and has no U4 transformer/trigger requirement; it does not erase an already excessive persistent debt.

Each twin appends one RA and advances its local ordinal from k to k+1; the coarse target does the same. Persistent debt and prior-Coherence remain unchanged. The projected history is the common associated local history, not a concatenation of both traces or a sum of their ordinals. This supplies the consumed context equality needed by the partial-transition criterion.

Only completed pairs belong to this projection domain. After the first fine event, target phases and histories can differ. That intermediate state retains its fine description and pending second target; it is not the coarse endpoint. A second-target rejection outside the sufficient domain does not roll back the accepted first target.

Convex form mixing and phase motion preserve their respective common intervals, common kind and paired phases at completed-pair boundaries. Induction therefore gives the same projected successors for any finite supplied sequence of complete pairs, provided live U3 admission and output representability remain valid. Recompute J_i, S_i and eta_i after earlier completed pairs; adjacent targets consume the updated state. If the initial lift diameter is strictly less than L, phase convexity keeps every neighbor compatible throughout such a finite sequence. This stronger sufficient corollary removes the U3-renewal obligation, but not finite capacity headroom. Repeated RA fragments are not automatically closed grammatical sentences; incremental admission does not discharge unconsumed U5/U6 or complete-word closure obligations.

docs.title: Exact scope and represented controls
docs.text:
The algebra above is exact-real mathematics with the specified coefficients. Binary64 reductions of two versus four selected nodes, two-stage blends, trigonometric means and capacity products need not be bit-identical. Threshold-adjacent selection/trigger decisions and overflow require their own margins. A finite coarse capacity alone cannot certify finite fine proposals. This result makes no unrestricted binary64 admission-equivalence or numerical-enclosure claim.

The shared-runtime controls freeze independent predictions before dispatch on one rational source and its all-negated form counterpart. Both have nonzero internal form and capacity contrasts, paired phases and supplied AL/IL contexts. They execute block 0 followed by adjacent block 1, using unchanged default factors. Block 0 admits two neighboring blocks; block 1 admits only the updated block 0, excluding its other neighbor by the actual U3 gate. Thus the comparison tests live partial selection rather than requiring all edges to be compatible. It verifies the mean rows, surviving contrasts, kind, local context and singleton-prefix boundary with an explicit floating residual tolerance. The controls stay in a positive non-wrapping phase chart; they do not certify runtime wrap equivalence to the ideal circle.

Separate sign, kind and persistent-debt controls keep the coarse request admitted while the second fine request rejects and the first remains committed. Their aggregate primary channels are rebuilt from the modified fine primitives. A heterogeneous kind or history has no proved aggregate map: those negative controls explicitly supply the first member's label and context. They demonstrate the insufficiency of that choice outside the theorem, not an alternative canonical projection.

Optional RA metrics expose four fine event records versus two coarse records for the two-block sequence, with twice as many selected neighbors per fine target. Stored pressure and structural time remain unchanged; these direct events create no physical temporal secants. No native selector, complete runtime call or trajectory is executed by these controls.

docs.title: Why one inherited operator is not a complete collective law
docs.text:
The existing joint form/capacity calculus already separates event inheritance from the subsequent nodal row. With paired phases, write each prepared fine pressure as p_-=B+C, p_+=B-C, where C=k*d+b_v*e on the declared regular support. Its mean pressure can equal the ordinary coarse native pressure B. Nevertheless, after a common RA boost f, retaining that prepared pressure through the flow gives

fine mean form rate = f*(V*B-e*C),
ordinary coarse form rate = f*V*B.

The covariance -f*e*C generally remains nonzero in the positive event domain. This reuses the existing held-pressure result; it supplies no new pressure law. Constituent pressure peaks, normalized Si, temporal samples and native request selection have further information requirements. They do not descend merely because mean pressure or this event descends.

The admitted aggregate action consequently establishes a restricted cross-scale operator correspondence. A complete collective dynamical law, organizational identity, its maintenance or acquisition, and the occurrence of the supplied paired requests remain separate questions under the NFR ontology.

docs.title: Fine Resonance does not universally inherit one aggregate Resonance
docs.text:
The complete-call map retains associated constituent state. A stronger claim would identify the admitted two-target Resonance (RA) action with one registered RA on a collective node whose capacity is the arithmetic mean V=(v_-+v_+)/2, using the same amplification factor b. This is a specified aggregation candidate, not a definition required by TNFR. Its capacity row alone has a necessary obstruction, independently of how aggregate form, phase, kind, neighbors or grammar might be completed.

Assume both constituent capacities are positive and exactly one selected signed mean activates amplification. In exact-real arithmetic with the represented factor, the admitted fine action gives

V_star=V+b*v_active/2,
0<v_active/2<V,
V < V_star < (1+b)*V,                       b>0.

These are ideal inequalities, not universal binary64 strict inequalities: an amplification can round away at a small factor or capacity. Represented separation needs its own margin, as in the default-sized control below.

One registered RA with input capacity V has only the two possible capacity outputs V and (1+b)*V, according to its own selected-mean trigger. Neither equals the fine aggregate above. Therefore no choice of aggregate trigger, retained hidden information or grammar can make these capacity rows agree while keeping this capacity map and the unchanged registered factor. This is failure of that universal operator-intertwining claim, not another claim that means omit information. It already holds for an event endpoint, before flow, coordination or capacity adaptation.

The existing composition source supplies an admitted control: v_-=7/8, v_+=9/8, V=1, and only the odd constituent activates amplification. Thus V_star=1+9*b/16, strictly between the two aggregate outputs. The control compares the existing fine response with both branches of the shared registered capacity proposal; it introduces no new source or trajectory.

When both triggers agree, this capacity obstruction disappears. Matching capacity is not sufficient: aggregate form/sign/kind, phase action, U3 and associated grammar still need their own common-domain proof under the ordered-action criterion. An effective factor b*v_active/(2*V) would reproduce this one capacity row, but would be a state-dependent collective rule, not the unchanged registered RA factor. Different aggregate capacity maps also require independent justification. The result does not exclude richer collective NFRs, formation, or all forms of operator inheritance across scales.

docs.title: An actual selected native transition at uniform capacity
docs.text:
Conditional result. On a separate uniform-capacity sector, a fine doubled-C5 network and an ordinary coarse C5 have the same projected ideal native transition under the existing default selector, without supplying an operator word. Nonzero internal form contrasts are allowed. The transition retains form means, common capacity, paired primitive phases, semantic kind, associated grammar/lag context, phase gains and clock. It need not retain fine pressure normalization, Si, stability counters or complete temporal histories. This is a partial reduction of a specified runtime model, not an identification of the two complete graph states.

The proof combines the native writer domain, the conditional moment rows and the ordered-language criterion. The new obligation is descent of the actual selected transition to an ordinary coarse runtime, after discarding internal form contrast. A conditional common request or equal mean pressure alone did not prove it.

docs.title: Retained state and admitted completions
docs.text:
Use the same fixed unit doubled C5 and simple C5 supports as above, with consecutive fine twins and corresponding coarse target order. Now impose one globally common positive capacity nu, interior to the runtime rails:

x_(i,-)=M_i-d_i,      x_(i,+)=M_i+d_i,       |d_i|<=D,
v_(i,-)=v_(i,+)=nu,   theta_(i,-)=theta_(i,+)=mu_i.

D>=0 is a fixed declared internal-form bound, not a fitted diagnostic. The common phase lift has width less than both mathematical and represented pi. As above, phase identities use the ideal circle with represented coefficients; runtime wrapping and reduction rounding have separate scope. Every node has the same nonempty semantic kind. At each block, retain one common, nonempty bounded grammar trace, persistent debt within its allowed capacity, prior-Coherence flag and local operator ordinal. Fine twins have separately owned copies. The shared positive retention window preserves a nonempty trace. Retain the two actual per-block lag counters a_i=since_AL and r_i=since_EN, the global phase gains, clock and runtime ordinal.

Keep the existing default mixed pressure, fresh default Si, default selector, strict grammar rejection, direct glyph path, hard clipping, default phase controller/coordinator and snapshot capacity adaptation. The form step is one held-pressure Euler interval of length delta=1/16, with the live built-in Gamma source of type none. No overridden selector, supplied word, custom pressure/integrator, optional mathematics engine or callbacks are included. Default validators still run. The fine and coarse runtime use the same declared clock, step size, policy configuration and target order.

All consumed primitive state, context, clocks and arithmetic must be admitted. Fine old rates, accelerations, physical histories and stability counts can differ; their validity is not inferred from aggregate admission. Existing temporal samples have valid times and signed forms. They are auxiliary completions of the retained state, not invented coarse observations.

For automatic REMESH, retain an admitted stable_frac history whose length is less than the configured stability window. With the specified absence of callbacks, the built-in step does not append that stream: pressure/Si, coordination, adaptation and the EPI archive have different writers. Thus the short-history guard remains invariant and the actual REMESH gate abstains. The archive itself still updates. Registering an observer that fills the stream changes this execution domain; it cannot inherit this abstention.

Let q denote the retained state above, including the short-history guard and fixed configuration. A complete coarse runtime state s_c is any admitted completion with those retained values. The claim is

q(F_f(s_f)) = q(F_c(s_c))   whenever q(s_f)=q(s_c)

on the margin domain below. F_f and F_c are the ideal real-arithmetic, common-lift maps of the declared fine and coarse native stage formulas. Actual binary64 invocations have the separate residual checks below. This does not treat q(s) as a complete checkpoint or assert that discarded outputs agree. The projected successor is independent of the admitted completion while these premises hold.

docs.title: Selection and associated grammar really descend
docs.text:
Fresh Si has nonnegative normalized components. Uniform positive capacity makes its capacity term the full default normalized weight alpha, where alpha>si_hi (approximately 0.7585>0.5). Consequently every unforced base decision is Coherence (IL), even if fine and coarse pressure maxima and Si values differ. This uses the default selector, which does not apply the parametric selector's soft repetition policy.

The batch increments lags before comparison and then chooses

g_i = AL  if a_i+1 > AL_MAX_LAG,
      EN  else if r_i+1 > EN_MAX_LAG,
      IL  otherwise.

Emission (AL) has priority when both limits are exceeded. With the actual defaults the limits are five and three. These decisions depend only on retained counters and are frozen before the ordered event sweep. Duplicated nonempty grammar context admits the same choice on both twins and their coarse node. Nonempty traces avoid a coarse-zero/fine-nonzero U1a mismatch; bounded debt admits these choices without a fallback. Their direct path has no Resonance sign-identity gate. Homogeneous kind removes Reception (EN)'s otherwise constituent-dependent semantic-kind propagation.

Each constituent and its coarse representative append one selected glyph and advance the same local ordinal once, with the shared debt/prior-Coherence update. The lag successor is also the same:

AL: (a_i',r_i')=(0,min(r_i+1,EN_MAX_LAG)),
EN: (a_i',r_i')=(a_i+1,0),
IL: (a_i',r_i')=(a_i+1,r_i+1).

Neither concatenated twin histories nor a doubled local ordinal is used. The actual number of fine events remains twice the coarse count.

docs.title: Mean flow and hidden contrast
docs.text:
Write N_i(z)=(z_(i-1)+z_(i+1))/2, k=w_epi and l=w_phase/pi_rep, using the resolved default pressure weights. Preparation on the common arc gives

B_i=k*(N_i(M)-M_i)+l*(N_i(mu)-mu_i),
p_(i,-)=B_i+k*d_i,       p_(i,+)=B_i-k*d_i.

Capacity contrast is zero; regular degree contrast is also zero on both supports. Thus B_i is exactly the ordinary coarse prepared pressure. It is held through this call's events and integration, not refreshed after an Emission or Reception jump.

Use the existing factors b_AL=AL_boost, m=EN_mix, h=IL_dnfr_factor. During the live ordered sweep, let Y_i be the event mean, A_i the event contrast multiplier and H_i the pressure multiplier. Their rows are

AL: Y_i=M_i+b_AL,                  A_i=1,     H_i=1,
EN: Y_i=(1-m)*M_i+m*N_i(live Y),    A_i=1-m,   H_i=1,
IL: Y_i=M_i,                       A_i=1,     H_i=h.

For Reception, earlier complete pairs have already changed the live neighbor mean. Both twins see exactly the same neighbor average as the coarse node; they are nonadjacent, so the first twin does not alter the second's inputs. Once clipping is excluded by the shared margins, these rows are precisely the ordinary coarse registered actions. At a singleton prefix the internal state/context need not belong to the paired chart.

Uniform capacity removes the covariance that obstructed the unequal-capacity flow. The shared Euler integrator gives

M_i'=Y_i+delta*nu*H_i*B_i,
d_i'=(A_i-delta*nu*H_i*k)*d_i,
mean stored form rate=nu*H_i*B_i.

The first row is the ordinary coarse held-pressure form step. The multiplier uses incoming contrast in the prepared pressure: multiplying the event contrast by a newly refreshed diffusion factor would be a different model. Old rate and physical history still determine individual accelerations and stored temporal records, but do not change this selected primary successor.

docs.title: Phase gains and capacity feedback
docs.text:
Events in this sublanguage leave primitive phase and capacity unchanged. Duplicated phases give the same normalized global resultant magnitude and angle on both graphs, and the same local neighbor-resultant angle. Equal per-block glyph histories duplicate every raw count while preserving every proportion, including the disruptor fraction. The actual phase controller therefore sees the same inputs and previous gains, takes the same branch and produces the same updated gains k_G,k_L.

On the common lift its ordinary coordinator is

mu_i'=(1-k_G-k_L)*mu_i+k_G*beta+k_L*N_i(mu),
beta=Arg_I(sum_j exp(i*mu_j)).

The default nonnegative gain bounds have sum below one, so the lifted phase hull remains inside its incoming interval and fine phases stay paired. This is the actual configured relaxation step, not a new continuous phase law or an identification of capacity with angular velocity.

Capacity qualification can differ: it consumes prepared Si and held post-event pressure. The counts and write eligibility therefore need not descend. Nevertheless every immutable neighboring capacity mean equals nu, so both an eligible proposal and an ineligible no-write leave capacity equal to nu. The shared fixed-point guard preserves this equality in the represented controls too. No assumption of equal counters or equal due flags is needed for the primary capacity successor. This statement depends on global uniformity, not merely equal capacities inside each pair.

docs.title: An aggregate-testable margin and its stopping boundary
docs.text:
Let (x_min,x_max) be the common form rails. Admit a step only when all incoming means, live event means and predicted flow means satisfy

x_min+D < M_i, Y_i, M_i' < x_max-D,
abs(A_i-delta*nu*H_i*k) <= 1.

All quantities in this test use retained state, configuration and the already determined lag choices; no hidden fine response is read. For the defaults 0<m<1 and 0<h<1, the common sufficient step bound delta*nu*k<=2-m implies the second inequality for all three actions. The event multipliers obey 0<=A_i<=1. Hence every fine lift with |d_i|<=D stays inside the rails at events and flow endpoints, and |d_i'|<=D. For a single Euler interval the held form interpolation also stays inside those rails. Inactive clipping justifies, rather than assumes from a single evaluated lift, the affine rows used in the proof.

The retained context, gains, common capacity and phase domain are preserved. At the successor, evaluate the next margin using the new retained state. Induction gives a unique projected transition along any finite segment for which the margins continue to hold. Margin failure stops this certificate; it does not claim that the native engine rejects or that no larger domain can work. An empty interior interval, changed callbacks/selector/support, invalid temporal evidence or nonrepresentable arithmetic cannot be repaired by a coarse pass. No all-time form-rail invariant is asserted.

docs.title: Frozen complete-call controls and limits
docs.text:
The native transition controls use common capacity 1/2, nonuniform paired phases, common kind and supplied AL/IL history. Fixed lag counters select AL at block 0, EN at adjacent block 1 and IL elsewhere through the actual default machinery. Independent primitive forecasts precede every native invocation. Two fine sources have opposite nonzero contrasts and the same coarse state; one ordinary coarse source provides the comparison. Each graph executes exactly one runtime.step with delta=1/16, followed only by fresh preparation and a detached next request check. The shared existing forwarding observer captures actual stages without substituting a selector, glyph word or evolution kernel.

The chosen block 2 has B_2=k/512 and contrast k/128 on the first fine lift. Its two post-IL pressures fall on opposite sides of the default stability cutoff. The fine and coarse qualification/count/write outcomes therefore differ while all capacities stay exactly 1/2. Opposite contrasts swap constituent outcomes. This deliberately distinguishes primary closure from equality of diagnostics or complete execution state.

Mean forms, hidden contrast multipliers, held pressures, stored rates, phase gains and endpoints, context, actual lag updates, REMESH abstention and refreshed next choices have independent checks. Binary64 residuals are checked against an explicit tolerance, not promoted to bit-exact real-circle identities or a universal validated enclosure. The tests do not constitute a trajectory campaign, a source-acquisition result or a physical observation.

The theorem establishes a nontrivial lossy native transition with retained policy memory. Complete temporal histories, stability counts, fine pressure peaks, Si, sampling and telemetry remain outside q; valid completions still carry them for actual execution. Additional observables need their own descent proof. The sector contains only the default reachable IL/AL/EN actions; the separately inherited Resonance event generally leaves its uniform-capacity premise. A persistent collective NFR identity, entry into this domain and a law selecting that domain remain unproved.

docs.title: Finite validity horizon under recurrent Emission
docs.text:
Conditional result. The default lag policy prevents indefinite renewal of the strict, unclipped domain of the uniform-capacity transition. Emission (AL) adds positive form recurrently. Ordered Reception (EN) and the held form flow retain a positive part of that input, while the adverse phase contribution has a finite total bound. Consequently a strict form margin must fail after finitely many calls, unless another premise fails earlier. This is a limit of that partial affine description under the specified policy, not a failure of the engine or an exclusion of collective organization in other domains.

Keep all premises of the preceding ideal transition, including the actual default selector, strict grammar, globally uniform capacity, paired phases, common kind/context, target order, no callbacks and REMESH abstention. The argument uses the ideal real-arithmetic stage formulas with resolved represented coefficients. It does not assert a validated binary64 horizon. No additional trajectory, source search or continuation law is used.

docs.title: Ordered events retain positive input
docs.text:
Index calls by n=0,1,..., so M_n is the vector of incoming block means. Let N be the C5 neighbor-mean matrix, and put

z=delta*nu*k,      lambda=1-m-z,
b_AL=GLYPH_FACTORS['AL_boost']>0,
m=GLYPH_FACTORS['EN_mix'],      h=GLYPH_FACTORS['IL_dnfr_factor'].

Here k is the resolved default EPI pressure weight and delta=1/16. The proof requires lambda>0, a stronger bound than the earlier contrast nonexpansion criterion. The actual defaults satisfy it throughout the admitted positive capacity interval: using the represented VF_MAX, z_max<0.071925, 1-m>0.758546 and lambda>0.686622. These are outward rational comparisons, not identities between separately rounded constants. In particular the proof does not require h=1-m.

The complete ordered event sweep has an affine representation

Y_n=E_n*M_n+b_n.

Each Reception updates its row to a convex combination of its current value and the two live neighboring rows. Emission and Coherence (IL) have identity linear parts on form. Products of these updates give

E_n>=0,       E_n*1=1,       (E_n)_(i,i)>=1-m,
b_n>=0,       (b_n)_i=b_AL whenever block i executes AL.

Every target is updated only once. Immediately before its own Reception update its row is still the corresponding identity row, so its diagonal keeps at least 1-m; previous neighbor updates can add more. There is no factor (1-m)^5 at this stage. Similarly a block's own Emission input is not removed by later updates of other targets. Neighboring Reception may carry that positive input into additional rows.

Let H_n have entries one for AL/EN and h for IL. The independent pressure was prepared before these events, so the held Euler transition is

M_(n+1)=W_n*M_n+b_n+f_n,
W_n=E_n+z*diag(H_n)*(N-I),
f_n=delta*nu*(w_phase/pi_rep)*diag(H_n)*(N-I)*mu_n.

It is not a diffusion matrix applied to E_n*M_n+b_n. That alternative would refresh pressure from event-modified form and change the model. Since 0<h<1, the off-diagonal entries of W_n are nonnegative, its diagonal is at least lambda, and its row sums equal one. Thus W_n is nonnegative and row-stochastic. Such a matrix preserves a constant lower bound and does not increase the sup norm of an adverse forcing term. Neither the event sweep nor this argument assumes conservation of the arithmetic sum of forms; ordered Reception and target-dependent pressure retention do not supply that conservation law.

docs.title: Six-call recurrence and a finite phase budget
docs.text:
The actual Emission counter increments before comparison with five and resets only on an accepted AL. With an admitted nonnegative initial lag a_i, its first AL is on one-based call max(1,6-a_i), then every sixth call.
