docs.title: Capture of three acquired C9 organizations on an oriented contact cycle
docs.text:
Both prescribed contact cycles capture every member of the original independently acquired source family. The equal control converges to the aligned winding-one organization. The unequal control instead converges to a uniquely determined shifted registration on the same marked support. All three internal windings remain one throughout the complete fine evolution. These conclusions retain the original residual coordinates; none of the sources is reset to its nominal equilibrium.

This is a conditional full-state result for the supplied sine law, held unit capacities and externally supplied attachment. It adds source-to-target capture to the exact inherited network law. The contact amplitudes and cycle registration remain in that law: convergence does not remove their chart obstruction. The result neither identifies a physical interaction nor supplies the occurrence or energy source of the attachment event. The NFR ontology permits a joined identity to retain those boundary data.

docs.title: Complete fine law and actual carried sources
docs.text:
Retain the 27 labelled nodes \((r,\ell)\), in order \(9r+\ell\), with \(r=0,1,2\) and \(\ell=0,\ldots,8\), and put \(\alpha=2\pi/9\). Each constituent has its unit-conductance C9 support. The supplied oriented contact cycle is \(e=(0,1),(1,2),(2,0)\). At an oriented contact \((r,t)\) add the undirected edges

\[ (r,\ell)--(t,\ell)\quad\hbox{of weight }1-s_e,\qquad (r,\ell)--(t,\ell+1)\quad\hbox{of weight }s_e, \tag{1} \]

with indices modulo nine. The two fixed controls are

\[ s^{\rm eq}=(1/2,1/2,1/2),\qquad s^{\rm un}=(1/4,1/2,3/4). \tag{2} \]

Every node has cross conductance two and total weighted degree four. There are 27 internal and 54 added positive edges in either control.

Use signed real form \(x\), primitive phase with the specified continuous lifts \(\theta\), the actual weighted Laplacian \(L_f\), and the same structural clock \(\tau=(1023/1024)t\). With \(\gamma=1/(1023\pi)\), the complete post-contact law is

\[ \begin{split} S_i(\theta)&=\sum_{j\sim i}w_{ij}\sin(\theta_j-\theta_i),\\ x'&=\tfrac14[-L_fx+\gamma S(\theta)],\qquad \theta'=\tfrac{\gamma}{4}L_fx,\\ H(x,\theta)&=\tfrac12x^TL_fx+ \sum_{\{i,j\}}w_{ij}[1-\cos(\theta_j-\theta_i)],\\ H'&=-\tfrac14\|L_fx\|_2^2,\qquad (\mathbf1^Tx)'=(\mathbf1^T\theta)'=0 . \end{split}\tag{3} \]

Primes mean derivatives in \(\tau\); both evolution rows acquire the factor \(1023/1024\) in original time. Capacities remain one. The pressure in the nodal form row is independently specified by (3), and no additional input or live source is present after attachment. This detached weighted comparison retains the execution boundary in the network-law owner; it is not the native unique-neighbor phase channel or an operator sequence.

Take three independent copies of the original sine class-one ramp preparation. Each original coordinate error is at most \(10^{-10}\), with separate exact zero sums for form and phase errors on each C9. The shared isolated recovery is consumed at its original acquisition time \(100\), uninterrupted dwell \(10^{13}\), and handoff \(\tau_h=100+10^{13}\). It supplies

\[ \begin{split} \Theta_{r,\ell}&=\alpha(\ell-4),\qquad \theta(\tau_h^-)=\Theta+y^{\rm src},\\ \|x_r(\tau_h^-)\|_2&\le\varepsilon,\qquad \|y^{\rm src}_r\|_2\le\varepsilon,\qquad \varepsilon=10^{-70},\\ \mathbf1^Tx_r(\tau_h^-)&=\mathbf1^Ty^{\rm src}_r=0 . \end{split}\tag{4} \]

All actual coordinates and their fixed lifts pass unchanged through the event. Only support changes. Independence means that every combination of the three admitted source members is included; no favorable cross-constituent correlation is imposed.

The recovery proof is used at sine deformation zero. Matching equilibria or tangents of another constitutive law would not admit its nonlinear recovery here. The earlier two-object and three-object contacts have their own different supports and are not source or work premises of (1).

docs.title: The joined stationary registration
docs.text:
The registered family has

\[ x_{r,\ell}=X_r,\qquad \theta_{r,\ell}=\Phi_r+\alpha(\ell-4). \tag{5} \]

The retained phase origins have common mean zero. Write

\[ m_e=1-s_e+s_e e^{i\alpha}=\rho_e e^{i\phi_e},\qquad \Delta_e=\Phi_t-\Phi_r,\qquad J_e=\rho_e\sin(\Delta_e+\phi_e). \tag{6} \]

The exact collective law uses the cycle incidence matrix \(B\), positive at each tail, and the unweighted three-node Laplacian \(L=BB^T\):

\[ X'=\tfrac14[-LX+\gamma BJ],\qquad \Phi'=\tfrac{\gamma}{4}LX . \tag{7} \]

In particular, equal currents on the three oriented contacts give zero net current at every fine node, because each node has the same two port weights. The internal sine currents cancel pairwise. Thus the following targets are stationary for all 54 fine evolution rows, not merely for their constituent means.

For the equal control,

\[ x_*=0,\qquad \Phi_*=(0,0,0),\qquad \theta_*=\Theta,\qquad J_e=\tfrac12\sin\alpha . \tag{8} \]

The nonzero edge-current terms have zero divergence. This balance is not an independently identified transport of a physical conserved quantity.

For the unequal control put

\[ \begin{split} \rho_h&=\sqrt{1-\tfrac38(1-\cos\alpha)},\qquad \rho_l=\cos(\alpha/2),\\ \phi&=\arg(3/4+(1/4)e^{i\alpha}),\\ F(a)&=\rho_h\sin a-\rho_l\sin(\pi/3-2a). \end{split}\tag{9} \]

There is a unique root \(a\in[347/1000,348/1000]\). Indeed, the endpoint signs are negative and positive, respectively, and

\[ F'(a)=\rho_h\cos a+2\rho_l\cos(\pi/3-2a)>0 \tag{10} \]

throughout that interval. Set \(b=\pi/3-2a\) and

\[ \begin{split} \Delta_*&=(a-\phi,\ b-\alpha/2,\ a-\alpha+\phi),\\ P&=(0,\Delta_{*,01},\Delta_{*,01}+\Delta_{*,12}),\qquad \Phi_*=P-\tfrac13(\mathbf1^TP)\mathbf1,\\ x_*&=0,\qquad \theta_{*,r,\ell}=\Phi_{*,r}+\alpha(\ell-4). \end{split}\tag{11} \]

The three differences sum to zero. Their registered arguments are \((a,b,a)\), so (9) gives the common current \(\rho_h\sin a=\rho_l\sin b\). The mean-zero choice in (11) retains the original common origin; it does not independently reset the three frames.

For orientation, these quantities are approximately

\[ \begin{split} a&=0.3470833235,\quad b=0.3530309041,\\ \Delta_*&=(0.1780325616,\ 0.0039650537,\ -0.1819976153),\\ \Phi_*&=(-0.1200100590,\ 0.0580225026,\ 0.0619875563). \end{split}\tag{12} \]

The proof and implementation use outward rational enclosures of (9)--(11), not these displayed decimals. The unequal aligned state has \(X'=\gamma\sin\alpha\,Bs/4\ne0\); it is a source reference that moves, not the target.

Orient each fine edge consistently with its internal cycle or supplied contact, and choose a fixed integer \(n_e\) so that

\[ \delta_e(\theta)=\theta_j-\theta_i+2\pi n_e \tag{13} \]

equals \(\alpha\) on each target internal edge, and equals \(\Delta_{*,e}\) or \(\Delta_{*,e}+\alpha\) on the respective contact ports. This handles the seams of the lifted C9s. The integers remain fixed; \(\delta_e-\delta_{*,e}=y_j-y_i\) for \(y=\theta-\theta_*\). Both controls satisfy the strict bound

\[ |\delta_{*,e}|<p_*:=22/25 \quad\hbox{for every fine edge}. \tag{14} \]

The target has winding one in all three original marked C9s. Its phase Hessian satisfies

\[ \nabla^2 U(\theta_*)\succeq\cos(22/25)L_f, \]

so, using the full-support gap proved below, its nonconstant eigenvalues are greater than \( (2/5)\cos(22/25)>0 \). This certifies the local target geometry; source entry still requires the full barrier argument.

docs.title: Actual support work and initial excess
docs.text:
Let \(L_c\) be the added-support Laplacian. Its maximal degree is two, so \(0\preceq L_c\preceq4I\). The unchanged source incurs the exact support work

\[ W=\tfrac12x^TL_cx+ \sum_{\text{added }e}w_e[1-\cos\delta_e(\theta)] . \tag{15} \]

At \(x=0,\theta=\Theta\), both controls have the same nominal work

\[ W_* =9\sum_es_e(1-\cos\alpha) =\tfrac{27}{2}(1-\cos\alpha)>0 . \tag{16} \]

For unequal weights the added potential gradient at \(\Theta\) is not zero. It is, however, constant within each constituent. Therefore its linear term against \(y^{\rm src}\) vanishes by the three separate zero-sum constraints in (4). This source correlation is essential; a collection of independent coordinate bounds without the exact zero means would not justify dropping the first variation.

All added edge angles along the segment from \(\Theta\) to the actual source have magnitude below \(\alpha+2\varepsilon<1\), so their cosine Hessians are positive. Their global absolute second derivatives are at most one. Since \(\|x\|_2^2,\|y^{\rm src}\|_2^2\le3\varepsilon^2\), Taylor's formula and the bound on \(L_c\) give

\[ \boxed{W_*\le W\le W_*+12\varepsilon^2.} \tag{17} \]

The strictly positive nominal work must be externally supplied. Previous continuous loss is not credited as a reservoir, and neither passivity nor autonomous event occurrence follows. The exact correction \(12\varepsilon^2\) is retained separately from the irrational enclosure of \(W_*\), rather than being erased by the interval grid.

Let \(H_*=H(0,\theta_*)\) and \(E_{\rm nom}=H(0,\Theta)-H_*\). For the equal control \(E_{\rm nom}=0\). For the unequal control, counting all fine copies gives

\[ E_{\rm nom} =9\left[ 2\rho_h\cos a+\rho_l\cos b -\tfrac32(1+\cos\alpha) \right],\qquad 0<E_{\rm nom}<27/100 . \tag{18} \]

Its value is approximately \(0.26115033\). The inequality is certified by enclosing the root before evaluating (18), independently of any evolved response. The target energy retains both the internal baseline and the contact constants; no energy offset is discarded from (15).

For the complete graph \(0\preceq L_f\preceq8I\). The complete potential gradient at \(\Theta\) is still constant within each constituent, so the same zero-sum cancellation applies. Consequently the actual initial excess, including all fine residuals, satisfies

\[ E_{\rm in}:=H(x(\tau_h^+),\theta(\tau_h^+))-H_* \le E_{\rm nom}+24\varepsilon^2 . \tag{19} \]

This calculation is performed at the actual carried source, without setting its internal deviations to zero or moving it to (11).

docs.title: Full-state trapping and winding retention
docs.text:
The required barrier is not restricted to the registered family (5). On the global mean-zero leaf define the fine phase cell

\[ \mathcal D=\{(x,y):\mathbf1^Tx=\mathbf1^Ty=0,\quad |\delta_e(\theta_*+y)|<2\ \hbox{for every fine edge}\}. \tag{20} \]

The bound \(2<\pi\) retains every winding, but some individual edge Hessians can be negative in this cell. We therefore prove a storage bound relative to the admitted target directly; no global convexity or acute-sector theorem is being assumed.

For \(V(z)=1-\cos z\), \(|t|\le p_*=22/25\), and \(|z|\le2\), Taylor's integral formula gives

\[ \begin{split} V(z)-V(t)-\sin t\,(z-t) &=(z-t)^2\int_0^1(1-v)\cos((1-v)t+vz)\,dv\\ &\ge c_*(z-t)^2,\qquad c_*>3/20, \end{split}\tag{21} \]

where

\[ c_*= \frac{\cos(22/25)-\cos2-(28/25)\sin(22/25)} {(28/25)^2}>3/20 . \tag{22} \]

For the inequality, the absolute interpolation argument is at most \((1-v)p_*+2v\), and cosine decreases with absolute argument on \([0,2]\). Integrating that lower cosine bound gives (22). Outward rational trigonometric bounds verify the last strict inequality; \(c_*\) is approximately \(0.1515229882\).

The target is a full fine-node critical point. Thus summing the linear terms in (21), with their actual weights and edge orientations, gives zero. Throughout the closed cell,

\[ E:=H-H_*\ge \tfrac12x^TL_fx+\tfrac3{20}y^TL_fy . \tag{23} \]

This includes all 52 nonconstant fine directions. The Laplacian dominates the Cartesian support consisting of the unit C9 edges and conductance \(1/4\) matching contacts between every pair of constituents. The nonzero gap of that support is

\[ \min\{2-2\cos\alpha,\ 3/4\}>2/5 . \tag{24} \]

The additional shifted and matching conductance is positive semidefinite. Therefore, on the global mean-zero leaf,

\[ E\ge \tfrac3{50}\bigl(\|x\|_2^2+\|y\|_2^2\bigr). \tag{25} \]

The strict gap in (24) gives strict inequality for a nonzero state in the weaker bound (25).

To admit the unequal source, a Euclidean radius alone is unnecessarily weak. Retain the actual edge correlations through effective resistance. For a fine edge \(e=\{i,j\}\), define the topology-only number

\[ R_e=(e_j-e_i)^TL_f^+(e_j-e_i). \tag{26} \]

Weighted Cauchy--Schwarz on the zero-mean quotient gives

\[ (y_j-y_i)^2\le R_e\,y^TL_fy . \tag{27} \]

For the two rational conductance supports (2), exact rational arithmetic gives

\[ \begin{array}{c|c} \text{control}&\max_{\text{fine edges}}R_e\\ \hline s^{\rm eq}&217703/419823\\ s^{\rm un}&743902545880/1319494263111 \end{array} \qquad R_e<3/5 . \tag{28} \]

These finite algebraic certificates can be reproduced without spectral rounding. Form the 27-by-27 rational Laplacian from (1), remove the row and column of node 26 to obtain the positive definite grounded matrix \(A\), and solve \(Az=b\) exactly for each reduced incidence column \(b\). Then \(R_e=b^Tz\); the residual \(Az-b=0\) verifies the calculation. Simultaneous cyclic rotation of all three C9s leaves nine edge orbits, so one representative of each orbit suffices. The maxima occur on shifted contacts, on every contact in the equal case and on \((0,1)\) in the unequal case. The argument uses the complete weighted graph, not a marginal bound assigned separately to each constituent.

At a first phase-cell boundary some \(|\delta_e|=2\), so (14) implies \(|y_j-y_i|\ge2-p_*=28/25\). Equations (23), (27) and (28) then give the full-state boundary barrier

\[ \boxed{E_{\partial\mathcal D} \ge \frac{3}{20}\frac{(28/25)^2}{3/5} =\frac{196}{625}.} \tag{29} \]

All actual sources begin in \(\mathcal D\), since their edge angles at attachment are at most \(\alpha+2\varepsilon<1\). Their excess (19) satisfies

\[ E_{\rm in}\le E_{\rm nom}+24\varepsilon^2 <196/625 . \tag{30} \]

The exact loss law (3) forbids reaching (29). Every complete fine trajectory from (4) therefore stays in \(\mathcal D\) for all future unforced time. The actual dynamics, not just its collective restriction, retains winding one in every constituent. All means and edge correlations used in the barrier belong to the same state.

The resulting explicit identity bound is

\[ \|x(\tau_h+T)\|_2^2+ \|\theta(\tau_h+T)-\theta_*\|_2^2 \le \frac{50}{3}(E_{\rm nom}+24\varepsilon^2), \qquad T\ge0 . \tag{31} \]

For the equal control the strict gap improves this to joint norm less than \(20\varepsilon\). For the unequal control the displacement from the original aligned source to the shifted target is part of the same full-state excess; it is not treated as a negligible residual.

docs.title: Uniqueness in the cell and convergence
docs.text:
The target is the only critical phase geometry on the trapped mean-zero leaf. For any edge values \(|z|\le2\), \(|t|<22/25\),

\[ \sin z-\sin t =2\cos((z+t)/2)\sin((z-t)/2). ag{32} \]

Both \(|z+t|\) and \(|z-t|\) are below \(72/25<\pi\). Therefore \((z-t)(\sin z-\sin t)>0\) whenever \(z e t\). For any other phase geometry in the closed cell, connectedness and the fixed mean imply that at least one \(y_j-y_i e0\). Hence

\[ y^T igl( abla U( heta_*+y)- abla U( heta_*) igr) =\sum_e w_e(y_j-y_i) [\sin\delta_e( heta_*+y)-\sin\delta_{*,e}]>0 . ag{33} \]

Since \( abla U( heta_*)=0\), another critical point is impossible. This is strict radial monotonicity relative to the target, not a claim that the Hessian is positive everywhere in the cell.

The vector field (3) is globally Lipschitz in lifted coordinates. The trapped sublevel is compact on the fixed mean leaf by (25) and has positive distance from the phase boundary by (29)--(30). On it, zero dissipation requires \(L_fx=0\), hence \(x=0\). An invariant trajectory in that set must also have \(S( heta)=0\), because otherwise the form row immediately leaves \(x=0\). Equation (33) then forces \( heta= heta_*\). The invariant-set argument applied to (3) proves

\[ (x( au_h+T), heta( au_h+T))\longrightarrow(0, heta_*) \quad ext{as }T\longrightarrow\infty . ag{34} \]

No quantitative settling time is asserted. The theorem admits every declared carried source to the target's full-state basin; it is stronger than local stability of a supplied equilibrium, but applies only to these two supports and their declared source family.

docs.title: Retained identity, implementation and independent controls
docs.text:
After contact, only the global form and lifted phase means in (3) remain conserved. The three constituent means generally move. The target shift in (11), the fine residuals, and the contact-cycle registration all belong to one complete state and law. They cannot be combined as independent marginal budgets or erased by resetting local phase origins.

The exact six-coordinate family (5) remains a useful restriction, but the reached sources need not lie on it. The full-state proof above retains their internal coordinates until convergence. It does not supply an exact memory-free quotient for arbitrary off-family states, a quantitative transient response, autonomous support formation, constitutive uniqueness or a physical identification.

The separate assembly-work obstruction shows that even simultaneous internal reorganization cannot make either attachment passive from these recovered sources while retaining acute winding-one child endpoints. docs.title: Collective boundary constraints and the scope of restoration
docs.text:
This owner states a conditional consequence of the supplied two-row constitutive flow: a positively curved boundary removes exactly the old zero-curvature directions that its actual phase constraints distinguish. The full flow, rather than a static stiffness alone, determines relaxation. The result uses ordinary positive-semidefinite linear algebra and local dynamical systems arguments. It is not an additional TNFR axiom or a selection principle for a fundamental constitutive law.

The form foundation, parameter foundation and NFR participation contract retain their separate responsibilities. The conditional critical parent in the interaction owner provides one concrete control below; its preparation and physical identification are not premises supplied by this theorem.

docs.title: 1. Actual model and equilibrium
docs.text:
Use an orthonormal chart of the relative phase space after removing the common phase rotation. Use the supplied nondimensional structural chart and held unit nodal capacities. Both the relative phase displacement and signed form have dimension \(n\). The total form is zero and the common phase origin is fixed. Hold the connected support, its symmetric positive-definite relative conductance Laplacian \(L\), the positive constant \(\gamma\), and the clock \( au\). The complete unforced model is

\[ x'= rac{-Lx-\gamma abla U( heta)}4,\qquad heta'= rac{\gamma Lx}4,\qquad {}'= rac{d}{d au}. ag{1} \]

Assume \(U\) is sufficiently smooth on the declared local phase chart. Its storage and continuous loss are

\[ H(x, heta)= rac12x^ op Lx+U( heta),\qquad H'=- rac14\|Lx\|^2. ag{2} \]

The cancellation in (2) follows directly from both rows of (1); it does not select \(U\). Fix an admitted equilibrium \(x_*=0\), \( abla U( heta_*)=0\). All subsequent Hessians are evaluated at this same equilibrium:

\[ M= abla^2U( heta_*)=M_0+B^ op K B,\qquad M_0\succeq0,\qquad K\succ0. ag{3} \]

For pairwise boundary edges, \(B\) is their oriented phase-difference map restricted to the relative chart, and \(K_{ee}=w_e V_e''(\delta_{e,*})\). Thus \(K\) contains the actual constitutive curvatures at the actual gaps, not merely positive conductances \(w_e\). The old contribution \(M_0\) must also be re-admitted at \( heta_*\); a displaced equilibrium need not retain an old endpoint's Hessian. More general boundary observations are allowed only when their complete Hessian really has (3). A nonlinear observation with nonzero current can add Hessian terms omitted by an incidence-only formula.

The theorem does not assume that a support addition is passive. Adding a pairwise edge of weight \(w_e\) in both rows changes the storage by \(w_e[(x_i-x_j)^2/2+V_e( heta_i- heta_j)]\), under that edge's declared potential normalization. That event work is separate from (2).

docs.title: 2. Which collective directions does the boundary restore?
docs.text:
For every relative phase vector \(v\),

\[ v^\top Mv=v^\top M_0v+\|K^{1/2}Bv\|^2. \tag{4} \]

Both terms are nonnegative. A zero quadratic value of a symmetric positive-semidefinite matrix is equivalent to membership in its kernel. Consequently

\[ \boxed{\ker M=\ker M_0\cap\ker(K^{1/2}B).} \tag{5} \]

Let \(T\) be any full-rank basis of \(\ker M_0\), with \(k_0\) columns. Under \(K\succ0\), the number of surviving relative phase zero modes is

\[ k=\dim\ker M=k_0-\operatorname{rank}(BT). \tag{6} \]

The criterion concerns restrictions on the old neutral space. Adding edges, increasing conductance or preserving a graph symmetry does not alone determine this restricted rank or the actual curvature signs.

If \(K\succeq0\) includes zero-curvature rows, (5) still holds, but (6) uses \(\operatorname{rank}(K^{1/2}BT)\). Such rows impose no quadratic restoring constraint. If \(K\) is signed, neither nonnegativity in (4) nor the kernel-intersection conclusion follows in general.

docs.title: 3. Full-flow modes, initialization and nonlinear scope
docs.text:
Put \(y=\theta-\theta_*\), and order the full linear state as \((y,x)\). The actual Jacobian and its relative quadratic pencil are

\[ J=\begin{pmatrix} 0&\gamma L/4\\ -\gamma M/4&-L/4 \end{pmatrix},\qquad Q(s)=s^2L^{-1}+\frac s4I+\frac{\gamma^2}{16}M. \tag{7} \]

Eliminating \(x\) gives \(L^{-1}y''+y'/4+\gamma^2My/16=0\), so no simultaneous diagonalization of \(L\) and \(M\) has been assumed. For an eigenpair \(Q(s)v=0\), multiplication by \(v^*\) gives \(a s^2+b s+c=0\), with \(a>0,b>0,c\ge0\). Its nonreal roots have negative real part and its nonzero real roots are negative. All nonzero full-flow eigenvalues therefore lie strictly in the left half-plane.

For \(k>0\), to count the zeros and admit their initialization, let \(W\) be any full-rank basis of \(\ker M\), and set \(G_W=W^\top W\). Define

\[ R=\begin{pmatrix}W\\0\end{pmatrix},\qquad C=G_W^{-1}\begin{pmatrix}W^\top&\gamma W^\top\end{pmatrix}. \tag{8} \]

Direct substitution yields \(JR=0\), \(CJ=0\), \(CR=I_k\). A generalized zero eigenvector satisfying \(Jz=Ra\) would give \(a=CJz=0\). Hence zero is semisimple. The full \(2n\)-dimensional flow has exactly \(k\) zero modes and \(2n-k\) strictly stable modes. Its zero spectral projector and retained linear amplitude are

\[ P_0=RC= \begin{pmatrix} WG_W^{-1}W^\top&\gamma WG_W^{-1}W^\top\\ 0&0 \end{pmatrix},\qquad a_0=G_W^{-1}W^\top(y_0+\gamma x_0). \tag{9} \]

The Gram matrix is essential when \(W\) is not orthonormal. In the linearized system, \(C(y(\tau),x(\tau))\) is constant and the stable component decays. Formula (9) is a linear spectral initialization; it is not a nonlinear phase-only measurement or an exact nonlinear quotient.

If (5) has trivial kernel, then \(M\succ0\) and \(J\) is Hurwitz. The smooth actual nonlinear flow is locally exponentially attracting. For example, a positive solution of \(J^\top P+PJ=-I\) gives a local quadratic Lyapunov function after bounding the nonlinear remainder. This statement supplies no numerical radius, uniform contact limit or source-capture certificate.

If a kernel survives, (5)--(9) alone imply no nonlinear attraction. A separately admitted center manifold can retain nonlinear normal lag, and its tracking initialization need not equal (9) beyond first order. The critical-parent initialization proof is a model-specific example of the additional work.

A sufficient higher-order local admission is a strict local minimum of the full storage, an isolated stationary point in a small compact sublevel component, and containment of that component in the identity chart. Equation (2), \(L\succ0\), and invariance imply that a trajectory with identically zero loss has \(x=0\) and \(\nabla U=0\). LaSalle's argument then gives local asymptotic attraction. Neither strict higher-order storage nor isolation follows from the kernel rank.

docs.title: 4. Static normal compliance and dynamic elimination
4.1 Exact quadratic static reduction
docs.text:
Complete the old kernel basis \(T\) by a matrix \(S\) such that \(\mathcal R=[T\ S]\) is invertible. Orthogonality is unnecessary. Write \(y=Tq+Sz\), and define

\[ A=S^\top M_0S\succ0,\qquad D=BT,\qquad E=BS. \tag{10} \]

Because \(M_0T=0\), the exact quadratic phase storage has block matrix

\[ \mathcal R^\top M\mathcal R= \begin{pmatrix} D^\top KD&D^\top KE\\ E^\top KD&A+E^\top KE \end{pmatrix}. \tag{11} \]

Minimizing over the admitted normal coordinate gives

\[ z_*(q)=-(A+E^\top KE)^{-1}E^\top KDq \tag{12} \]

and the exact effective static stiffness

\[ \begin{split} M_{\rm stat} &=D^\top[K-KE(A+E^\top KE)^{-1}E^\top K]D\\ &=D^\top(K^{-1}+EA^{-1}E^\top)^{-1}D. \end{split} \tag{13} \]

The second form follows by the matrix inversion identity; it applies to strictly positive \(K\). The bracket is positive definite, so

\[ \ker M_{\rm stat}=\ker D,\qquad 0\preceq M_{\rm stat}\preceq D^\top KD. \tag{14} \]

The upper value is the result of artificially freezing the normal coordinates. Equality along a given \(q\) holds precisely when \(E^\top KDq=0\). Thus normal compliance can reduce the stiffness without changing which directions are restored under these premises. For diagonal edge \(K\), zero-curvature rows can be deleted before using the inverse expression; more generally restrict to its positive eigenspace. The first Schur expression remains available for \(K\succeq0\).

Normal invertibility also admits a local nonlinear stationary minimizing graph by the implicit-function theorem. This is static elimination at fixed retained coordinate. It does not establish that this graph is invariant under (1).

docs.title: 4.2 The actual spectral and initial-state reduction
docs.text:
Transform the full pencil by congruence, \(\widehat Q(s)=\mathcal R^\top Q(s)\mathcal R\). Its normal block has positive mass, damping and stiffness, and is invertible for \(\operatorname{Re}s\ge0\). The retained spectral equation uses

\[ Q_{\rm dyn}(s)= \widehat Q_{TT}(s) -\widehat Q_{TS}(s)\widehat Q_{SS}(s)^{-1} \widehat Q_{ST}(s),\qquad Q_{\rm dyn}(0)=\frac{\gamma^2}{16}M_{\rm stat}. \tag{15} \]

Only its zero-frequency value is fixed by (13). For the linear initial-value problem, the transformed Laplace right-hand side is

\[ \widehat f(s)= \mathcal R^\top\left[ \left(sL^{-1}+\frac14I\right)y_0+\frac{\gamma}{4}x_0 \right], \tag{16} \]

and elimination retains \(\widehat f_T-\widehat Q_{TS}\widehat Q_{SS}^{-1}\widehat f_S\). The normal initialization is not generally removed. The frequency dependence corresponds to normal dynamics and, in a reduced time-domain description, memory. Any cancellation or exact Markov closure needs its own proof.

For a small explicit control, take

\[ L=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&2\end{pmatrix},\quad M=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\quad T=e_1,\quad S=e_2. \tag{17} \]

Here \(M_{\rm stat}=0\) and the static cross block vanishes, but \(\widehat Q_{TS}=-s^2/3\) and \(\widehat Q_{SS}=2s^2/3+s/4+\gamma^2/16\). Dynamic coupling and hidden initialization remain. Even a zero static cross block cannot justify discarding those terms.

The existing native effective-connection proof already distinguishes static curvature from dynamic recovery on its own admitted acute model. Equations (10)--(17) apply that method to an old critical kernel with actual boundary constraints; they do not transfer its coefficients or verdicts between laws. The shared derive_coordinate_memory implementation already provides the exact block-memory identity for an admitted linear generator and declared retained coordinates. It does not authenticate the graph, equilibrium or nonlinear closure. No additional solver is required for this theorem.

docs.title: 5. One fixed-total-conductance control on the critical parent
5.1 Matched model and restricted boundary rank
docs.text:
Use the previously admitted 54-node critical parent and one nine-node neighbor from the single-port interaction owner. Hold its actual \(\gamma,\tau\), a fixed \(0<\eta\le10^{-12}\), and its own critical constitutive parameter \(\lambda_c(\eta)\). The parent has hosts \(c=0,\ldots,4\), donor \(c=5\), and the neighbor is \(c=6\); every child has nine slots. The aligned equilibrium is unchanged by the following additions because the new gaps vanish and \(j_{\lambda_c}(0)=0\), \(j_{\lambda_c}'(0)=1\).

Compare exactly the same total per-slot added conductance \(\epsilon=\epsilon_1+\epsilon_2>0\):

  • A single port places weight \(\epsilon\) on each of the nine same-slot host-2-to-neighbor edges.
  • A split port places weight \(\epsilon_1>0\) on those edges and weight \(\epsilon_2>0\) on each of the nine same-slot donor-to-neighbor edges.

These are alternative attachments from the same disconnected parent-plus-neighbor support with zero external weights, not a sequential event changing the single attachment into the split one. The comparison reallocates the host-port weight; it does not add a second copy of that port at unchanged weight. Both rows use the same weights. There is no new controller, clock or input.

Let \(t\) be the parent's physical host-minus-donor phase coordinate and \(d\) the neighbor-minus-parent mean phase. The parent critical tangent has slot-constant entries at the two ports

\[ h=w_{2,j}=\frac16+u_{2,t}(0)>\frac17,\qquad g=w_{5,j}=-\frac56,\qquad a=h-g=1+u_{2,t}(0)>0. \tag{18} \]

The old relative phase kernel is two-dimensional: the parent's critical direction and the independent relative mean phase. On this kernel the boundary observations are \(d-ht\) and \(d-gt\). One port has restricted rank one. Positive weights on both ports have rank two because \(h\ne g\). The single port retains one quartic critical direction; the split port removes both old relative phase zero directions.

The 63-node relative phase space has dimension 62. Its 56 fine phase directions remain positive: the parent's 48 and the neighbor's eight, with positive-semidefinite boundary additions. The remaining old normal directions are also positive. Thus the split model has \(M_{63}\succ0\), and all 124 full relative flow eigenvalues lie strictly in the left half-plane for every fixed positive pair \((\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2)\). Its smooth full flow is locally exponentially attracting. The single-port model instead has one zero and 123 stable modes; its quartic attraction needs the separate proof already given in the interaction owner.

docs.title: 5.2 Exact normal compliance at the aligned equilibrium
docs.text:
The distinction survives relaxation of the internal host shape. Let \(P=I-\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top/5\), \(\ell=Pe_2\), \(u_0=u(0)\), and let \(D_5\) be the forward rim-difference map. Write \(b=2\pi/5\) and \(b_c=b(c-2)\). In the mean-zero host space define the actual own-law Hessian

\[ \begin{split} A_H=P\{& D_5^\top\operatorname{diag} [j_{\lambda_c}'(b+D_5u_0)]D_5\\ &+\eta\,\operatorname{diag} [j_{\lambda_c}'(b_c+u_{0,c})]\}P\big|_{\mathbf1^\perp} \succ\frac15I,\qquad \chi=\ell^\top A_H^{-1}\ell\in(0,4). \end{split} \tag{19} \]

These are the admitted parent normal bounds, not a fit to the new response. The last inequality uses \(\|\ell\|^2=4/5\). At fixed physical \(t\), let \(y\) denote host normal displacement from the stationary parent tangent. The exact quadratic phase storage is

\[ U_2=\frac92\left[ y^\top A_Hy+ \epsilon_1(d-ht-\ell^\top y)^2+ \epsilon_2(d-gt)^2 \right]. \tag{20} \]

The factor nine retains all slots. Fine coordinates minimize at zero: their gradient vanishes on the carrier and their actual quadratic form is positive. Thus (20) is the full quadratic static reduction, not an assumption that the fine state can be omitted dynamically.

Put \(k=\epsilon_1\epsilon_2/(\epsilon_1+\epsilon_2)\). Minimization first over \(d\) and then over \(y\) gives

\[ d_*=\frac{\epsilon_1(ht+\ell^\top y)+\epsilon_2gt}{\epsilon}, \qquad y_*=-\frac{ka}{1+k\chi}A_H^{-1}\ell\,t, \tag{21} \]

and

\[ \boxed{K_{\rm eff}=\frac{9ka^2}{1+k\chi}},\qquad \frac{9ka^2}{1+4k}<K_{\rm eff}<9ka^2. \tag{22} \]

The upper numerator alone freezes the internal host normal state. The denominator is its exact compliance correction. In the single-port limit \(k=0\), the quadratic stiffness vanishes irrespective of the positive total conductance. Equation (22) is a static stiffness, not a decay rate.

docs.title: 5.3 Coupled dynamic control
docs.text:
The released means provide a direct reason to retain that distinction. Let \(r\) be neighbor-minus-parent mean form and retain \(d\) as above. Define

\[ c=\frac7{24},\quad m=\frac{9\gamma^2}{4\|w\|^2},\quad S_0=\epsilon_1+\epsilon_2,\quad S_1=\epsilon_1h+\epsilon_2g,\quad S_2=\epsilon_1h^2+\epsilon_2g^2. \tag{23} \]

Projection of the actual two-row Jacobian onto the three zero modes at zero added contact gives the leading small-contact matrix on \((t,r,d)\):

\[ \begin{pmatrix} -mS_2&0&mS_1\\ c\gamma S_1&-cS_0&-c\gamma S_0\\ 0&c\gamma S_0&0 \end{pmatrix}. \tag{24} \]

It follows by summing the two marked boundary contributions, with the same parent critical projection and \(6:1\) mean weights as in the interaction owner. The two-row cancellation in the critical left projection removes a direct retained mean-form term from its first row; it does not remove the other two equations. Here \(S_0S_2-S_1^2=\epsilon_1\epsilon_2(h-g)^2>0\). For a fixed positive split ratio all entries scale with the total contact, and the three formerly neutral modes must be treated together. Positive split weights can even give \(S_1=0\), while \(S_2>0\). That cancellation of the leading receiver mean-form response to the critical coordinate does not eliminate restoration. It does not assert cancellation of arbitrary raw-state responses.

docs.title: 5.4 Identity, event work and the local domain
docs.text:
All conclusions are local to the same marked constituent identities. The inherited small phase chart also admits the donor port: its new gap is bounded by \(1/20+1/24+1/50=67/600<3/25\), where the actual \(j_{\lambda_c}'\) is greater than \(9/10\). The old host-port and internal chart bounds remain in force. The second nine-edge port adds nine independent cycles: eight donor-neighbor mixed-slot cycles and one same-slot triangle \(c=2\to6\to5\to2\), using the existing host-2-to-donor spoke. Their windings are zero at the aligned equilibrium and stay zero in this cut-free local chart. The previously marked constituent and parent periods retain their original values. Each attachment's event admission starts from the common disconnected parent-plus-neighbor baseline. For the split attachment, the new contact work is the sum of the two actual edge additions, including their form-difference terms. Continuous loss cannot erase the obligation to account for that work.

For each fixed admitted parameter pair, choose a sufficiently small closed full-state relative ball inside this identity chart. The positive Hessian makes the post-contact storage excess on its boundary strictly positive. A primitive pre-contact state inside the ball whose old excess plus the actual contact work is below that boundary barrier enters a local invariant sublevel component and is attracted to the equilibrium. The inside-ball premise cannot be replaced by a global low-energy statement. This is a conditional event-and-domain admission, not a claim that an existing prepared source satisfies it. docs.title: 6. Counterexamples identify the missing premises
docs.text:
A graph and its loss do not select curvature or a relaxation rate. For one relative coordinate take \(L=l>0\) and \(U(q)=a(1-\cos q)\). The origin is stationary and its polynomial is

\[ \frac{s^2}{l}+\frac s4+\frac{\gamma^2a}{16}=0. \tag{25} \]

Positive, zero and negative \(a\) give, respectively, stable modes, a zero mode, and a positive mode; distinct positive values give different rates at the same \(L\). Alternatively, a positive conductance sine edge has opposite curvature signs at its stationary gaps zero and \(\pi\). Its graph and continuous loss identity are the same. The equilibrium and actual law are therefore indispensable inputs to (3).

Old semidefiniteness and positive boundary curvature have separate roles. With \(M_0=\operatorname{diag}(-1,0)\), \(B=(0,1)\), \(K=1\), the boundary distinguishes the old kernel but the total Hessian remains indefinite. With \(M_0=\operatorname{diag}(1,0)\), \(B=(1,0)\), \(K=-1\), the total Hessian is zero: signed curvature has created an additional cancellation kernel. With \(K=0\), any nonzero \(B\) imposes no quadratic constraint. These controls prevent extending (6) to unsigned topological rank without its hypotheses.

A positive Hessian at a nonstationary state is insufficient. For \(U(q)=1-\cos(q-a)\) with small nonzero \(a\), the Hessian at zero is positive but the gradient is nonzero. The point is not an equilibrium of (1) and has no equilibrium-attraction verdict.

A surviving kernel does not decide higher-order attraction. Consider the smooth periodic nonnegative potentials

\[ U_4(q)=(1-\cos q)^2=\frac{q^4}{4}+O(q^6),\qquad U_6(q)=(1-\cos q)^3=\frac{q^6}{8}+O(q^8). \tag{26} \]

They have the same zero Hessian at zero, while their first restoring currents are \(q^3\) and \(3q^5/4\). Both have isolated local storage minima; their higher-order laws are different. The equally nonnegative periodic potential \(U_-(q)=4-(1-\cos q)^2\) instead has a quartic local maximum at zero and the same zero Hessian. Nearby zero-form states have strictly lower storage than that equilibrium, so (2) prevents them from converging to it. Nonnegative storage and a positive-semidefinite tangent thus do not prove attraction. The additive constant in \(U_-\) changes no current or loss; this control does not also impose the incompatible normalization \(U_-(0)=0\). These are fixed-support local constitutive controls; they do not claim equal support-event work, which depends on the declared potential normalization.

Static elimination does not discard dynamical state. Equation (17) has zero static cross curvature and nonzero dynamic coupling. Formula (16) retains the hidden initial state. The actual critical-parent state witnesses likewise distinguish instantaneous full-state rates from a slaved center law. Neither matched coarse means nor a static minimizer is a complete state of the arbitrary nearby flow.

docs.text:
