Diffusion fixes the clock to \(\sigma=k_q\tau\); equality of the two reciprocal coefficients then forces

\[ A_qj=\rho_qj,\qquad a^2=\rho_q>0, \qquad\gamma_{\rm eff}=\gamma\sqrt{\rho_q}. \tag{7} \]

This defines the equivalence class; it does not exclude all nonlinear conjugacies with different inputs or observations. Matching contacts have \(A_1=I\), so their profile condition is automatic.

Require the organized storage and local derivative data to agree with sine at the consumed gaps \(\delta=0,\alpha,2\alpha\):

\[ V(\delta)=1-\cos\delta,\quad j'(\delta)=\cos\delta,\quad j''(\delta)=-\sin\delta. \tag{8} \]

Negative gaps then follow by parity. On the declared target supports, these conditions match target storage, the complete tangent and the full quadratic field. The target vector field itself vanishes for every odd current: opposite currents cancel at cycle nodes and symmetric contacts, and aligned bridge currents are zero. Matching those sums therefore does not require matching each nonzero edge current individually. Both nonzero winding gaps are included even though the composition in (4) uses winding one. They admit the same local target comparison on the earlier supports consuming winding two and aligned bridges; they do not transfer that model's acquisition proof.

Odd real-analytic periodicity supplies a sine series \(j(\delta)=\sum_{n\ge1}b_n\sin(n\delta)\) with real exponentially decaying coefficients. Equivalently, use a holomorphic extension to some open strip about the real circle and any smaller closed strip to bound the coefficients. This justifies the termwise shifts, integrals and all finite-order derivatives used below. Conversely, exponential decay supplies the required analytic current.

For each sine harmonic,

\[ A_3\sin(n\delta)=\frac{1+2\cos(n\alpha)}3\sin(n\delta). \tag{9} \]

Differentiating (7) at zero and applying (8) gives

\[ \rho_3j'(0)=\tfrac13[j'(0)+2j'(\alpha)] =\frac{1+2\cos\alpha}{3}=r_3. \tag{10} \]

Since \(j'(0)=1\), necessarily \(\rho_3=r_3\). Uniqueness of Fourier coefficients in (9) now gives

\[ b_n=0\quad\text{unless }n\equiv1\text{ or }-1\pmod9. \tag{11} \]

Let \(\mathcal N\) be those positive integers and put \(s_n=1\) for \(n\equiv1\pmod9\), \(s_n=-1\) for \(n\equiv-1\pmod9\). For \(k=0,1,2\), the retained frequencies obey \(\cos(nk\alpha)=\cos(k\alpha)\) and \(\sin(nk\alpha)=s_n\sin(k\alpha)\). The normalized potential is

\[ V(\delta)=\sum_{n\in\mathcal N}\frac{b_n}{n} (1-\cos n\delta). \tag{12} \]

Consequently (8) is equivalent to three moment conditions:

\[ \boxed{\quad \sum_{n\in\mathcal N}\frac{b_n}{n}=1,\qquad \sum_{n\in\mathcal N}nb_n=1,\qquad \sum_{n\in\mathcal N}s_nn^2b_n=1. \quad}\tag{13} \]

For necessity, use the potential value at \(\alpha\), the derivative at zero and the second derivative at \(\alpha\); \(1-\cos\alpha\) and \(\sin\alpha\) are nonzero. For sufficiency, substitution gives every value in (8), including the entire set at \(2\alpha\). The second winding therefore adds no independent moment after the interface restriction (11), although it remains part of the matched-target claim.

Equations (11)--(13), real exponential coefficient decay and \(V(\delta)\ge0\) for every real \(\delta\) are jointly necessary and sufficient for this comparison. Nonnegativity is a separate global condition; these equalities do not imply it. This classification never assumes first-neighbor-resultant sufficiency. That different information premise would remove the higher harmonics by a separate argument.

The stronger edge-current requirement \(j(k\alpha)=\sin(k\alpha)\) for \(k=1,2\) is equivalent to the additional condition \(\sum_ns_nb_n=1\). It is not redundant. For example, the perturbation current

\[ h(\delta)=57\sin\delta-708\sin8\delta +185\sin10\delta+221\sin17\delta \]

has zero perturbations of all three moments in (13), but its signed current moment is 729. Its normalized potential \(Q=\int_0^\delta h(s)\,ds\) obeys \(|Q(\delta)|\le11328(1-\cos\delta)\): apply \(1-\cos(n\delta)\le n^2(1-\cos\delta)\) to each coefficient. Thus \(V=1-\cos\delta+eQ\), \(|e|\le1/22656\), is a nonnegative counterexample to deducing that fourth condition from the actual matched target fields. The next family satisfies even the stronger condition.

docs.title: An explicit nonnegative nonsine family
docs.text:
For the exact real parameter \(|\epsilon|\le1/324\), define

\[ P(\delta)=\cos\delta(1-\cos9\delta)^2,\qquad V_\epsilon(\delta)=1-\cos\delta+\epsilon P(\delta),\qquad j_\epsilon=V_\epsilon'. \tag{14} \]

These functions are analytic, periodic and have the required parity. The elementary bound \(|\sin(9z)|\le9|\sin z|\) for real \(z\) gives \(1-\cos9\delta\le81(1-\cos\delta)\). Combining it with \(1-\cos9\delta\le2\) proves

\[ |P(\delta)|\le162(1-\cos\delta),\qquad \tfrac12(1-\cos\delta)\le V_\epsilon(\delta) \le\tfrac32(1-\cos\delta). \tag{15} \]

Thus the potential is nonnegative globally and vanishes only at full turns. Its positivity is proved without sampling phase or selecting a trajectory. Expanding its five harmonics gives

\[ P(\delta)=\tfrac32\cos\delta-\cos8\delta-\cos10\delta +\tfrac14\cos17\delta+\tfrac14\cos19\delta. \tag{16} \] Frequency \(n\) Current coefficient \(b_n\) Residue sign \(s_n\) 1 \(1-3\epsilon/2\) +1 8 \(8\epsilon\) -1 10 \(10\epsilon\) +1 17 \(-17\epsilon/4\) -1 19 \(-19\epsilon/4\) +1

All other coefficients vanish. Each is in (11), and direct substitution satisfies (13) and the additional edge-current moment. There is also a local verification: at every \(\delta=k\alpha\), the factor \((1-\cos9\delta)^2\) has a zero of order four. Hence

\[ P=P'=P''=P'''=0,\qquad P''''(k\alpha)=6\,9^4\cos(k\alpha). \tag{17} \]

The organized target, storage, full tangent and quadratic field therefore agree with sine. The cubic field generally changes:

\[ j_\epsilon'''(k\alpha) =[-1+39366\epsilon]\cos(k\alpha). \tag{18} \]

Every nonzero admitted \(\epsilon\) is genuinely nonsine in the declared chart. In particular, \(P'(\pi/2)=-1\) gives the exact static witness

\[ j_\epsilon(\pi/2)=1-\epsilon\ne1. \tag{19} \]

The unchanged derivative \(j_\epsilon'(0)=1\) excludes a mere global current multiplier. This is a different complete nonlinear vector field, not a finite measured response or a claim excluding every possible nonlinear state conjugacy.

The coefficient identities hold algebraically outside the admitted interval, but positivity need not survive. For example, taking \(\epsilon=2\) in (14) gives \(V_2(\pi)=2-8=-6\), while preserving all three target moments and the additional edge-current moment. This explicitly separates the global storage condition from the linear matching conditions; that value is rejected by the static family's admission.

This freedom has arbitrarily many independent directions. For each integer \(m\ge2\), the even trigonometric polynomial \(P_m(\delta)=\cos\delta(1-\cos9\delta)^m\) has only the same residue frequencies, and has a zero of order \(2m\) at every target gap. Any finite sum

\[ V=1-\cos\delta+\sum_{m=2}^M a_mP_m(\delta),\qquad \sum_{m=2}^M81\,2^{m-1}|a_m|\le\tfrac12 \tag{20} \]

obeys (11)--(15)'s nonnegative lower bound and all target conditions. The bound follows from \((1-\cos9\delta)^m\le81\,2^{m-1}(1-\cos\delta)\). The distinct polynomial powers are linearly independent. There is thus no finite count of alternatives selected by these constraints. The uniform derivative constants below apply only to (14), not automatically to every finite sum in (20).

docs.title: Own-law regularity and local target identity
docs.text:
For (14), summing absolute Fourier derivative coefficients gives

\[ \begin{split} |j_\epsilon'|&\le1+328|\epsilon|\le163/81,\\ |j_\epsilon''|&\le1+\tfrac{8913}{2}|\epsilon| \le3187/216<15. \end{split}\tag{21} \]

At any edge target \(0,\pm\alpha,\pm2\alpha\), its potential curvature is exactly the sine curvature, whose minimum is \(\cos(4\pi/9)>1/6\). One algebraic proof of the latter bound sets \(c=\cos(4\pi/9)\in(0,1/2)\); it is the root there of \(8c^3-6c+1=0\), a strictly decreasing polynomial with positive value at \(c=1/6\). The mean value estimate from (21) consequently gives

\[ V_\epsilon''(\delta)>\frac{11}{120}>0 \quad\text{when the edge is within }1/200 \text{ of one of those target gaps}. \tag{22} \]

This re-admits a local convex cell for the actual potential. On any of the connected target supports with these edge gaps, opposite cycle currents and zero aligned bridge currents still make the target an equilibrium. On the two-C9 three-offset support the extra opposite cross currents likewise cancel at alignment. Its full tangent is

\[ \mathcal J= \begin{pmatrix} -D^{-1}L&-\gamma D^{-1}L_c\\ \gamma D^{-1}L&0 \end{pmatrix}, \qquad Q=\tfrac12x^TLx+\tfrac12y^TL_cy, \tag{23} \]

where \(D\) is the actual positive degree matrix and \(L_c\) the target curvature-weighted Laplacian. Both \(L\) and \(L_c\) have only the common-origin kernel on a connected support, because every target curvature is positive. Restricting to fixed conserved \(D\)-weighted form and lifted phase means removes those two origins. For regular interfaces these are the ordinary means. Along the linear tangent, \(Q'=-x^TLD^{-1}Lx\). The only trajectory in its zero-loss set has \(Lx=0\), then \(L_cy=0\), so the relative tangent is asymptotically stable and, in finite dimension, Hurwitz. Smooth nonlinear continuation therefore gives local asymptotic stability for the actual law; (22) also provides its own strictly convex storage neighborhood.

This is an independently admitted local identity, conditional on starting sufficiently close with sufficiently small full excess storage. It gives neither the old radius \(1/12\), a source-to-cell route, a uniform recovery dwell, nor a contact certificate for a previously acquired fine state. Nonlinear remainders, source transport and event bounds must be rebuilt before asserting any of those properties. The entire invariant family (4) need not be transversely stable at every collective phase.

docs.title: Both evolution rows, storage and observations inherit together
docs.text:
For every current admitted by the classification, not only (14), \(A_qj=r_qj\). Integrating this equality and evaluating at zero gives

\[ A_qV(\Delta)=(1-r_q)+r_qV(\Delta). \tag{24} \]

Indeed, \(A_1V(0)=0\), while \(A_3V(0)=2V(\alpha)/3=1-r_3\) by target matching. Let \(B_q=18(1-\cos\alpha)+9q(1-r_q)\). The full fine storage and loss on (4) are exactly

\[ H_V|_{\mathcal M}=B_q+9q[\tfrac12u^2+r_qV(\Delta)], \qquad\frac{dH_V}{d\tau}=-18qk_qu^2. \tag{25} \]

The inherited chart and clock are forced within the declared map class:

\[ \sigma=k_q\tau,\qquad X_r=\sqrt{r_q}Z_r, \qquad\gamma_{\rm eff}=\gamma\sqrt{r_q}. \tag{26} \]

For \(z=Z_1-Z_0\), both complete rows and the full storage become

\[ \begin{array}{ll} \displaystyle\frac{dZ_0}{d\sigma}=z+\gamma_{\rm eff}j(\Delta),& \displaystyle\frac{dZ_1}{d\sigma}=-z-\gamma_{\rm eff}j(\Delta),\\ \displaystyle\frac{d\Phi_0}{d\sigma}=-\gamma_{\rm eff}z,& \displaystyle\frac{d\Phi_1}{d\sigma}=\gamma_{\rm eff}z, \end{array} \tag{27} \] \[ H_V|_{\mathcal M}=B_q+9qr_q[\tfrac12z^2+V(\Delta)], \qquad\frac{dH_V}{d\sigma}=-18qr_qz^2. \tag{28} \]

For (14), \(\epsilon\) is unchanged by either interface. The reciprocal coefficient is unchanged only for matching contacts. Three-offset contacts still require its change and the form chart; a fixed-\(\gamma\) family is not closed under this complete comparison. Unit fine capacities are retained, and \(k_q\) is a derived common rate, not an inferred capacity law or an inverse mass.

Uniform constituent form inputs \(b_r(\tau)\) and independently supplied phase inputs \(c_r(\tau)\) preserve (4). They transform respectively to \(b_r/(k_q\sqrt{r_q})\) and \(c_r/k_q\) in (27), with their original time argument transformed as well. The full continuous balance is

\[ \frac{dH_V}{d\tau}=-18qk_qu^2+ 9q[u(b_1-b_0)+r_qj(\Delta)(c_1-c_0)]. \tag{29} \]

Dividing by \(k_q\) and using (26) reproduces the same work in (28). A uniform form jump \(a_r\) becomes \(a_r/\sqrt{r_q}\); a uniform phase jump keeps its angle. Their work is the difference of the full storage. A raw form observation reads \(X_r=\sqrt{r_q}Z_r\), not \(Z_r\). Any more general observation is composed with the same fine embedding and chart. Independent sensor calibration and discarded constituent information remain separate obligations.

Finally, attaching the specified support without changing state requires the exact event work

\[ \mathcal W_q=\sum_{j,s\in\mathcal S_q} \left[\tfrac12(x_{1,j+s}-x_{0,j})^2+ V(\theta_{1,j+s}-\theta_{0,j})\right]\ge0. \tag{30} \]

On (4) it is \(9q[\tfrac12u^2+(1-r_q)+r_qV(\Delta)]\). At the aligned target it is zero for matching and \(18(1-\cos\alpha)>0\) for three offsets. The additive constant in (24) is therefore retained even though it disappears from continuous derivatives. Positive work needs a declared external supply, and neither passivity nor the continuous law selects event occurrence.

docs.title: What the classification establishes
docs.text:
The two named interfaces constrain the harmonic content and the matched targets constrain three coefficient moments. Even imposing the fourth moment for individual edge-current equality, together with nonnegative storage, these requirements still admit the explicit nonsine laws above. Thus same-profile organized composition does not select a unique current in the stated analytic class. Repeating either proved algebraic interface map leaves those profiles unchanged; it does not construct the nested geometries, sources or events needed to repeat the physical organization.

Composition at different phase registrations, other cycle sizes, every possible interface, a first-resultant information restriction or a different operator-descent requirement would add premises. None follows from this two-interface calculation. Any further selection principle must be justified against retained NFR and boundary state rather than chosen to remove the counterexample. The execution plan owns that decision; this proof creates no parallel research queue.

The oriented weighted-interface comparison now isolates one such extra premise: unchanged profiles across its declared open interface interval select sine within this class. The other currents still inherit exact boundary-dependent laws, so that conditional selector does not follow from the NFR ontology or invalidate the present counterfamily.

The regional barrier and work comparison gives a further consequence of this same counterfamily on its admitted interval: even its true winding-boundary storage minima are not fixed by the matched target and composition properties. Regional powers can also differ at identical complete state and storage. This does not transfer a source outcome or select a preferred law.

docs.title: Implementation and independent controls
docs.text:
The detached static owner _composition_compatible_constitutive.py admits the exact parameter domain of (14), derives its finite harmonic coefficients and observes edge jets and both complete collective rows. The static pair instrument fixes the fine reciprocal coefficient to \(1/(1023\pi)\), while the proof permits any positive fine coefficient with its correspondingly mapped comparison value. It reuses the shared registered-interface geometry and complete chart data without transferring a sine acquisition certificate. It represents the explicit stronger counterfamily, not a decision procedure for global nonnegativity of every analytic series in the classification. Its interval-angle adapter reuses the same finite harmonic evaluator for the full-state regional work observer. The sine member retains its original observation arithmetic; phase intervals enclose phasors rather than asserting that every corner of the sine/cosine rectangle lies on the unit circle.

Its independent controls rebuild the potential and derivatives, target moments, exact nonsine witness, full fine-state restriction, storage and transformed observations. These algebraic and static tests check implemented behavior; they do not evaluate a trajectory, form an organization under the new law, freeze a physical protocol or regenerate previous scientific evidence.

docs.title: Constitutive freedom in regional identity barriers and work
docs.text:
Matching the organized target, its storage, full tangent, quadratic field and the previously declared registered-composition conditions does not fix a C9 winding boundary's storage minimum or regional boundary power. The admitted analytic family below gives exact counterexamples to both claims. Its true first-boundary minima for winding zero and one vary affinely with the constitutive parameter on one explicit interval. Regional power also varies at one fixed complete state whose regional, contact and complete storage values are unchanged.

These are static and conditional complete-law results. A minimum over a phase-cell boundary is not the work consumed by an actual trajectory, an activation law or a proof that a source reaches that boundary. The frozen sine-source loss is preserved in its own model. The research program remains the sole queue.

docs.title: Actual complete law and the matched properties
docs.text:
Use the fixed equal-contact support of the receiver model: 27 labelled nodes, three unit C9 regions, and contacts from oriented region pairs \((0,1),(1,2),(2,0)\) with offsets zero and one, each of weight one half. Every node has weighted degree four. All fine form and phase coordinates, region membership and boundary registrations are retained. Capacities are held at one and conductances remain fixed. There are no inputs, resets, support events or operator invocations.

Write \(\alpha=2\pi/9\), \(\gamma=1/(1023\pi)\), and use the structural clock \(\tau=(1023/1024)t\). The parameter \(\lambda\) below is the constitutive parameter of the composition-compatible counterfamily, not the slow-clock factor \(\gamma^2\). Restrict it to

\[ |\lambda|\le E:=1/10000, \qquad P(d)=\cos d(1-\cos9d)^2, \qquad V_\lambda(d)=1-\cos d+\lambda P(d), \qquad j_\lambda(d)=V_\lambda'(d). \tag{1} \]

With the actual weighted Laplacian \(L\), declare both rows:

\[ S_{\lambda,i}(\theta) =\sum_jw_{ij}j_\lambda(\theta_j-\theta_i),\qquad x_\tau=\tfrac14[-Lx+\gamma S_\lambda(\theta)],\qquad \theta_\tau=\tfrac\gamma4Lx. \tag{2} \]

The form row supplies pressure under unit capacity. It is not inferred from an observed form response. In the original clock both rows acquire the factor \(1023/1024\); structural units have no laboratory-unit bridge.

The current is odd, analytic and periodic. Its potential is even and periodic. The bounds proved for the original family give

\[ |P(d)|\le162(1-\cos d),\qquad |P(d)|\le4, \qquad V_\lambda(d)\ge(1-162E)(1-\cos d)\ge0. \tag{3} \]

The five-term Fourier expansion also gives

\[ |P''(d)|\le328, \qquad |j_\lambda'(d)|\le1+328E. \tag{4} \]

Thus the lifted vector field is globally Lipschitz. The fine law retains common form and phase origins, graph relabellings preserving all marked data, and simultaneous form/phase sign reversal. Both global means are conserved; individual regional means need not be.

For the actual support, the complete storage and its loss are

\[ H_\lambda=\tfrac12x^TLx+ \sum_{\{i,j\}}w_{ij}V_\lambda(\theta_j-\theta_i), \qquad (H_\lambda)_\tau=-\tfrac14\|Lx\|^2. \tag{5} \]

This follows directly from \(\nabla_\theta H_\lambda=-S_\lambda\) and both rows of (2). It re-admits the balance for the changed law rather than transferring an evaluated sine trajectory.

At every gap \(k\alpha\), the factor \((1-\cos9d)^2\) has a fourth-order zero. Hence

\[ P=P'=P''=P'''=0\quad\text{at }d=k\alpha. \tag{6} \]

The internal winding-one twist retains its storage, current, tangent and quadratic field. The same is true of the equal-contact joined target \(x_*=0\), \(\theta_{*,r,j}=\alpha(j-4)\): its actual fine gaps are zero or \(\pm\alpha\) modulo a turn. Substituting (6) preserves the fine-node current cancellation from the target proof. This concerns the full 54-dimensional target field. It does not identify the aggregate contact phase lag with a fine-edge gap or transfer the unequal-contact target.

The family also retains its previously proved profile-preservation properties under the matching and three-offset interfaces defined by its classification owner. That result does not assert profile preservation under every interface, including the two-offset contacts used here. Nor do the matching target data transfer source acquisition, nonlinear transport, capture radii or event contracts. This remains a detached complete-law comparison under the NFR admission, without a physical identity or a newly selected fundamental law.

docs.title: The true C9 first-boundary minima
docs.text:
Retain the principal-branch integers of a marked region at release and continue its registered gaps until their first boundary contact. For initial winding \(w\in\{0,1\}\), define the compact set

\[ \mathcal B_w=\left\{\delta\in[-\pi,\pi]^9: \sum_j\delta_j=2\pi w,\quad \max_j|\delta_j|=\pi\right\}, \qquad B_w(\lambda)=\min_{\delta\in\mathcal B_w} \sum_jV_\lambda(\delta_j). \tag{7} \]

Every point of this set represents a consistent circular C9 phase configuration with the retained winding sum. At least one gap is on the boundary; winding at that boundary is not assigned. Minimization in (7) retains all other gaps and permits simultaneous boundary contacts.

Put \(c=\cos(\pi/8)\). The exact result on the full interval (1) is

\[ \boxed{B_0(\lambda)=B_1(\lambda) =2+8(1-c)+\lambda\beta,\qquad \beta=8c(1+c)^2-4.} \tag{8} \]

In particular, the number \(9/4\) in the regional sine theorem remains a valid conservative bound in its stated sine domain; it was not claimed to be the sharp value now computed at \(\lambda=0\).

To prove (8), select one boundary gap. Its potential is always

\[ V_\lambda(\pi)=V_\lambda(-\pi)=2-4\lambda. \tag{9} \]

If the other eight have sum \(\pi\) or \(-\pi\), their equal-gap candidate has cost

\[ C_\lambda=8V_\lambda(\pi/8) =8(1-c)+8\lambda c(1+c)^2. \tag{10} \]

The following elementary rational bounds will isolate every minimizer:

\[ c>23/25,\qquad 1/4<\cos(5\pi/12)<1/3. \tag{11} \]

For the first, \(\sqrt2>7/5\) gives \(c^2=(2+\sqrt2)/4>17/20>(23/25)^2\). For the second, use \(\cos(5\pi/12)=(\sqrt6-\sqrt2)/4>1/4\), since \(\sqrt6>1+\sqrt2\), and \(\cos(5\pi/12)=\sin(\pi/12)<\pi/12<1/3\).

By (3) and (11),

\[ C_\lambda<16/25+32E. \tag{12} \]

If any of the remaining eight gaps has magnitude at least \(5\pi/12\), its potential alone is at least \(2/3-4E\). The other seven potentials are nonnegative. Thus their total exceeds the candidate by more than

\[ 2/3-4E-(16/25+32E) =2/75-36E=173/7500>0. \tag{13} \]

Every minimizing remaining gap consequently lies in \((-5\pi/12,5\pi/12)\). Throughout that interval,

\[ V_\lambda''(d)=\cos d+\lambda P''(d) >1/4-328E=543/2500>0. \tag{14} \]

Strict convexity and Jensen's inequality now prove that eight gaps with sum \(\pm\pi\) have their unique minimum at eight identical gaps \(\pm\pi/8\). This is a global minimum over the full constrained face, because (13) excluded every omitted large-gap point.

For winding zero, either selected boundary sign leaves the opposite sum \(\mp\pi\), so this proves (8). For winding one, a selected \(+\pi\) leaves sum \(\pi\). The remaining possibility is a selected \(-\pi\) with sum \(3\pi\). The global inequality \(1-\cos d\ge2d^2/\pi^2\), followed by Cauchy--Schwarz and (3), bounds that remaining cost below by

\[ \frac2{\pi^2}\frac{(3\pi)^2}{8}-32E=9/4-32E. \]

Its excess over the candidate in (12) is greater than

\[ 9/4-16/25-64E=4009/2500>0. \tag{15} \]

It cannot minimize. This also excludes configurations with further boundary gaps. The minimizing configurations are therefore one \(+\pi\) and eight \(+\pi/8\) for winding one; for winding zero they have one \(\pm\pi\) and eight \(\mp\pi/8\), with arbitrary choice of the marked boundary edge. Substituting (9)--(10) gives (8).

docs.title: A fixed constitutive discriminator and the donor/receiver trade-off
docs.text:
The expression for \(\beta\) is increasing in \(c>0\). Equation (11) gives \(23<\beta<28\). In particular the two already declared endpoint laws satisfy

\[ B_w(1/10000)-B_w(-1/10000)=\beta/5000>23/5000. \tag{16} \]

This is an exact unequal-minimum result, not a sampled comparison or a comparison of arbitrary boundary-state energies. It refutes selection of the regional first-boundary minimum by the matched target and registered composition properties alone.

For a zero-form winding-one internal twist, the internal baseline remains \(9V_\lambda(\alpha)=9(1-\cos\alpha)\). For a flat zero-form receiver it remains zero. Their geometric storage differences to the first boundary are therefore

\[ R_D^*(\lambda)=B_1(\lambda)-9(1-\cos\alpha),\qquad R_R^*(\lambda)=B_0(\lambda). \tag{17} \]

Both have the same slope \(\beta\), and \(R_R^*-R_D^*=9(1-\cos\alpha)\) is unchanged. Raising this common barrier increases both donor headroom and the receiver's necessary entry storage. It does not selectively guarantee transmission with retention.

These baselines are ideal internal states, not source-release certificates. For independently established bounds \(\|x_r\|\le X\) and \(\|\theta_r-\vartheta\|\le b\), with \(\vartheta=\alpha(j-4)\) or zero, (4) and the stationary internal gradient do give the own-law static upper bound

\[ H_{\lambda,r}\le U_{\lambda,r}(\vartheta) +2X^2+2(1+328E)b^2. \tag{18} \]

The cycle Laplacian bound \(L_I\preceq4I\) proves both terms. Establishing that a changed-law trajectory reaches such a state is a separate obligation; the sine source bounds, velocity defect, release time and capture margins cannot supply it. A boundary minimum also omits positive form storage, accumulated loss, contact work and the direction of passage.

docs.title: Regional work changes at identical complete state and storage
docs.text:
For each region retain the notation of the regional balance, now using the actual changed current:

\[ \ell_r=L_{I,r}x_r,\quad b_r=(L_Cx)_r,\quad s_{\lambda,r}=(S_{\lambda,I})_r,\quad c_{\lambda,r}=(S_{\lambda,C})_r. \]

Direct differentiation of the internal storage gives

\[ \begin{split} H_{\lambda,r}&=\tfrac12x_r^TL_{I,r}x_r +\sum_{\text{internal }e}V_\lambda(\delta_e),\\ D_r&=\tfrac14\|\ell_r\|^2,\\ P_{\lambda,r}&=-\tfrac14\ell_r\cdot b_r +\tfrac\gamma4(\ell_r\cdot c_{\lambda,r} -s_{\lambda,r}\cdot b_r),\\ (H_{\lambda,r})_\tau&=-D_r+P_{\lambda,r}. \end{split} \tag{19} \]

The internal reciprocal terms cancel by (2); the contact terms retain their state dependence. Including the contact storage recovers (5). The first-exit proof applies with the actual \(B_w(\lambda)\) and the actual integrated power in (19). Neither the sine power history nor a larger static barrier determines the changed-law history.

There is an exact static witness on the same weighted support. Number nodes \(9r+j\), and choose

\[ x=e_9,\qquad \theta=(\pi/2)e_0. \tag{20} \]

Subtracting the common form and phase means puts this witness on the global mean-zero leaf without changing any following value. Every consumed phase gap is zero or \(\pm\pi/2\). At these gaps the potentials agree with sine, while

\[ j_\lambda(\pi/2)=1-\lambda, \qquad S_\lambda=(1-\lambda)S_0. \tag{21} \]

The exact internal storage, internal loss, contact storage and total loss are independent of \(\lambda\):

\[ (H_{\lambda,0},H_{\lambda,1},H_{\lambda,2})=(2,1,0), \quad (D_0,D_1,D_2)=(0,3/2,0), \quad H_{\lambda,C}=3, \quad H_\lambda=6, \quad D_{\rm all}=19/4. \tag{22} \]

For example, the sole nonzero form node has degree four, so its complete form storage is two. Its Laplacian column has squared norm \(4^2+2\cdot1^2+4\cdot(1/2)^2=19\). The phase node has two internal and two units of contact conductance, giving internal phase storage two and contact phase storage two. The remaining contact storage is form.

Nevertheless, evaluation of (19) gives

\[ (P_{\lambda,0},P_{\lambda,1},P_{\lambda,2}) =\left(-\frac\gamma8(1-\lambda), -1+\frac\gamma8(1-\lambda),0\right), \qquad P_\lambda-P_0=(\gamma\lambda/8,-\gamma\lambda/8,0). \tag{23} \]

For region zero, \(\ell_0=0\); its contact form gradient is \(-1/2\) at nodes zero and eight, and its internal current is \((1-\lambda)(-2,1,0,\ldots,0,1)\). Their dot product gives the first entry. The other entries follow from the same retained contacts. The regional storage rates sum to \(-5/2\), and contact storage has rate \(-9/4\), yielding the unchanged total rate \(-19/4\).

Thus identical complete state, every regional and contact storage, and complete instantaneous loss do not determine regional power across this admitted constitutive class. The sign of the difference in (23) changes with \(\lambda\); this does not claim that the regional power itself changes sign. The witness is a supplied mathematical state, not a state shown reachable from the original two-ramp source.

The branch-normal velocity at any identical complete state remains \(\gamma b_e^TLx/4\), independently of \(\lambda\), because the phase row is unchanged. The changed current instead changes the form row and subsequent evolution. A different barrier or instantaneous work value therefore does not by itself establish a different crossing outcome.

These counterexamples identify nonlinear constitutive information left free by the matched target and composition requirements. They neither select a preferred member of the family nor transfer the evaluated sine source to it. Acquisition, donor maintenance, complete joined capture and physical identification retain their separate obligations.

docs.title: Implementation and independent controls
docs.text:
The boundary assessment rebuilds the primitive constitutive law before evaluating (8), its strict proof margins and the ideal donor target margin. Laws outside (1) but inside the family's admitted interval remain valid laws; this narrower theorem returns unavailable minima for them. It imports no release or source report. The independent controls evaluate the factored potential, actual equal-network target gaps, boundary configurations and the inequalities consumed by the global proof.

The shared regional observer accepts the entire already admitted family, \(|\lambda|\le1/324\), using the single potential/current owner. It retains the admitted law and both complete rows. Its default zero member preserves the sine arithmetic; the separate source-retention assessment remains sine-only. Signed form follows shared scalar materialization, while primitive phase lifts retain their admitted represented values. A rounded quarter turn is not the exact state in (20). The regional controls therefore use a represented nonzero angle and independently evaluate its actual potential/current. The shared exact-phasor controls check (21). None of these controls evaluates a trajectory or regenerates frozen evidence.

docs.title: The original receiver source across the admitted constitutive interval
docs.text:
This owner admits the unchanged two-ramp source under every law in the fixed interval \(|\lambda|\le1/10000\), then compares its actual slow phase with the preserved sine reference enclosures. Source preparation, support, capacities, clocks and error allowances stay fixed. The comparison does not integrate a new trajectory or transfer the sine outcome through matching target derivatives. It rebuilds the changed-law source transport, velocity defect, residual and observation margins.

The retained numerical horizon is the 76 evaluated sine steps, ending at elapsed slow time \(19/2\). This was the stopping horizon of the preserved response, whose original prospective maximum was \(32\). No continuation to that unevaluated maximum, parameter-interval reduction or preparation change is part of this comparison. The research program remains the sole queue.

docs.title: Complete law and primitive preparation
docs.text:
Use the actual equal-weight 27-node support, law and units from the constitutive barrier owner. Set

\[ \Lambda=1/10000,\quad P(d)=\cos d(1-\cos9d)^2,\quad V_\lambda(d)=1-\cos d+\lambda P(d),\quad j_\lambda=V_\lambda',\quad |\lambda|\le\Lambda. \]

The parameter is constant along each trajectory. With \(A=L/4\), \(\gamma=1/(1023\pi)\) and \(\varepsilon=\gamma^2\), define

\[ F_{\lambda,i}(\theta)=\tfrac14\sum_jw_{ij} j_\lambda(\theta_j-\theta_i), \qquad x_\tau=-Ax+\gamma F_\lambda(\theta),\quad \theta_\tau=\gamma Ax. \tag{1} \]

Here \(\tau=(1023/1024)t\), capacities are held at one, and support and conductances are fixed. Both rows acquire the factor \(1023/1024\) in the original clock. Phase angles are measured in radians; form, time and storage retain this model's structural units, with no laboratory-unit bridge supplied. There is no forcing, event, reset or installed operator word. All form and phase coordinates remain, on the conserved global mean-zero leaf. The complete own-law storage obeys

\[ H_\lambda=\tfrac12x^TLx+\sum_{\{i,j\}}w_{ij} V_\lambda(\theta_j-\theta_i),\qquad (H_\lambda)_\tau=-\tfrac14\|Lx\|^2. \tag{2} \]

Keep the original primitive source

\[ \begin{split} q_j&=j-4,\quad m=\tfrac{2046}{9}(355/113)^2, \quad \alpha=2\pi/9,\\ Q_{r,j}&=q_j\quad(r=0,1),\qquad Q_{2,j}=0,\\ x(0)&=mQ+\eta_x,\qquad \theta(0)=\eta_\theta,\\ |\eta_{x,r,j}|&\le r_x=10^{-10},\qquad |\eta_{\theta,r,j}|\le r_\theta=10^{-10}. \end{split} \tag{3} \]

Each error vector has its separately declared zero sum in each original region. Every allowed combination is retained; only the global means remain conserved after evolution begins. In particular, the nominal reflection/sign symmetry does not restrict the original error directions. The rational ramp coefficient is not replaced by an exact multiple of \(\pi\).

The nominal initial storage is \(150m^2\), with \(72m^2\) internal and \(78m^2\) on contacts, for every admitted law. Rebuilding the actual support gives \(\|L(mQ)\|_1=117m\) and \(\|L(mQ)\|_2=m\sqrt{2277/2}\). At nonzero phase error, \(|P(d)|\le9^4d^4/4\), and the total edge weight is \(54\). Consequently the complete initial storage is bounded below by \(150m^2-117mr_x\), and above by

\[ 150m^2+117mr_x+108(r_x^2+r_\theta^2) +216\,9^4\Lambda r_\theta^4. \tag{4} \]

The lower bound uses the actual nonnegative potential; the added quartic term accounts for the changed potential at the original phase errors.

docs.title: Uniform own-law transport and slow-velocity defect
docs.text:
The Fourier coefficients of \(P'\) give

\[ |P'|\le57/2,\quad |P''|\le328, \quad J=1+(57/2)\Lambda,\quad M=\sqrt{27}J,\quad K=2(1+328\Lambda)=1291/625. \tag{5} \]

Thus \(\|F_\lambda\|_2\le M\) and \(\|DF_\lambda\|_2\le K\) on all phase lifts. The same actual support has \(\|A\|_2\le2\) and mean-zero heat gap \(g=1/10\). These graph properties are independent of \(\lambda\); the changed force and derivative bounds are freshly supplied by (5).

Put \(a=\gamma x\), \(z=\theta+a\), and \(P_*=\alpha Q\). Both exact rows become

\[ a_\tau=-Aa+\varepsilon F_\lambda(\theta),\qquad z_\tau=\varepsilon F_\lambda(\theta). \tag{6} \]

Define

\[ A_0=\gamma(m\sqrt{120}+\sqrt{27}r_x),\qquad d_0=\sqrt{120}|\gamma m-\alpha| +\sqrt{27}(r_\theta+\gamma r_x), \] \[ B(T)=e^{-gT}A_0+\varepsilon M/g,\qquad b(T)=d_0+B(T)+\varepsilon MT. \tag{7} \]

The mean-zero heat estimate applied to the variation-of-constants formula for \(a\), followed by the exact mixed row, proves

\[ \|\gamma x(T)\|_2\le B(T),\qquad \|\theta(T)-P_*\|_2\le b(T). \tag{8} \]

The form bound \(B(400)/\gamma\) remains valid for every \(\tau\ge400\). No phase-only model has replaced the form dynamics.

At \(T=200\), (8) gives donor winding one and receiver winding zero. On \(200\le\tau\le400\), use the uniform phase bound \(d_0+B(200)+400\varepsilon M\) to retain the donor branch integers. Receiver retention before release has a separate whole-time proof. The commuting internal/contact Markov heat kernels on the fixed support give \(|\Delta(e^{-A\tau}Q)_{2,j}|<4\), as derived in the heat-shape argument. Applying its variation-of-constants identity to the actual changed force, with \(|F_{\lambda,i}|\le J\), gives, for \(0\le\tau\le400\),

\[ |\Delta\theta_{2,j}(\tau)| <4\gamma m+2r_\theta+4\gamma r_x+4\varepsilon\,400J<\pi. \tag{9} \]

This reuses a law-independent heat estimate with its new force bound, not the sine source's winding verdict.

In slow time \(s=\varepsilon\tau\), the actual phase velocity is \(\theta_s=Ax/\gamma\). Its defect from the changed descent field is

\[ r_\lambda=\theta_s-F_\lambda(\theta)=-x_\tau/\gamma. \]

Differentiating both actual rows gives

\[ (r_\lambda)_\tau =-(A+\varepsilon DF_\lambda)r_\lambda -\varepsilon DF_\lambda F_\lambda. \tag{10} \]

This vector stays on the global mean-zero leaf. With

\[ \kappa=g-\varepsilon K>0,\qquad R_0=\frac{m\sqrt{2277/2}}{4\gamma} +\frac{2\sqrt{27}r_x}{\gamma}+K\sqrt{27}r_\theta, \]

the symmetric Jacobian and (5) imply

\[ \|r_\lambda(\tau)\|_2 \le R_0e^{-\kappa\tau}+\frac{\varepsilon KM}{\kappa}. \tag{11} \]

The shared outward rational kernels rebuild all inequalities for the full interval and original errors. They certify

\[ b(400)<21/100000,\qquad B(400)/\gamma<1/50, \qquad \|r_\lambda(\tau)\|_2<\rho=11/10^6 \quad(\tau\ge400). \tag{12} \]

The source assessment retains the primitive law interval, source cost, support, clock, source errors and all margins. The numerical budget in (12) follows from the changed-law inequalities; it is not admitted merely because the sine assessment used the same displayed budget.

docs.title: Preserved reference evidence and eight derivative cones
docs.text:
Use elapsed slow time \(u=\varepsilon(\tau-400)\). Equation (12) admits every original-source trajectory as

\[ (\theta_\lambda)_u=F_\lambda(\theta_\lambda)+r_\lambda, \quad \|r_\lambda\|_2<\rho, \quad \|\theta_\lambda(0)-P_*\|_2\le b(400). \tag{13} \]

The actual defect retains form memory; it is not an independently supplied forcing in the complete law.

The original response archive contains one outcome and 76 immutable step records at their recorded paths. This comparison pins those bytes:

Artifact Bytes SHA-256 organized-receiver-enclosure-v1.response.zip 741711 77b38c4785a57a355aa0d86a318b7acd22702e69de317687e93222ab5758d044 Retained outcome JSON inside the archive 189956 2dbb6e1b738f33f1189ba0de1436b5682c8109000d0ea400250d9a7ae763b79c

The retained outcome's ordered step receipts check all 76 step payloads; strict JSON and exact-number admission precede interval construction. Support, source, clock, node order, step order and reference-center carry must match the original validated-reference owner. Byte association is not mathematical proof or external authentication. The original proof supplies the reference enclosures: the retained Picard and Taylor derivative enclosures remain explicit numerical premises and are not derived from their byte receipts. The new calculation rebuilds every consumed changed-law residual, cone, growth bound and observation margin. It does not accept the old source verdict or logarithmic growth rates as changed-law certificates.

Each original step has length \(h=1/8\), starts from a rational local reference center \(c\), and encloses the exact sine reference \(y'=F_0(y)\), \(y(0)=c\). The retained data include its whole-step box \(T\), endpoint polynomial and remainder enclosures, and next rational center. The reader rebuilds the validated endpoint box \(Y\) from those enclosures, then recomputes its full Euclidean recentering radius \(d\) relative to that next center, using the lifted metric \(2I_{13}\). The old cached radius does not supply this new radius. Thirteen symmetric coordinates are lifted to all 27 coordinates as in the original reference proof. The actual uncertainty always occupies the full mean-zero tangent leaf.

Rebuild \(V=F_0(T)\). For each of eight fixed subintervals \([a_k,b_k]=[(k-1)h/8,kh/8]\), form the coordinatewise intersection

\[ T_k=T\cap\bigl(c+[a_k,b_k]V\bigr) \cap\bigl(Y-[h-b_k,h-a_k]V\bigr). \tag{14} \]

The first cone follows by integrating \(y'\in V\) forward from \(c\); the second follows by integrating backward from its validated endpoint. Both hold for the same exact reference trajectory. Therefore \(y(u)\in T_k\) throughout that subinterval. An empty intersection rejects the reconstruction; it does not give a zero residual. Equation (14) uses no new trajectory, Taylor coefficients, time integration or new reference center.

docs.title: Full-state residual transport on fresh prospective domains
docs.text:
Write

\[ F_\lambda=F_0+\lambda G,\qquad G_i(y)=\tfrac14\sum_jw_{ij}P'(y_j-y_i). \]

On each cone, evaluate the factored derivative directly,

\[ P'(d)=-\sin d(1-\cos9d)^2 +18\cos d(1-\cos9d)\sin9d, \tag{15} \]

accumulate signed edge currents at each node, and let \(g_k\) be the outward Euclidean norm upper bound. Subtracting two independent current intervals and dividing by \(\Lambda\) would discard the cancellation in (15) and is not this residual construction. The residual uses the reference cone only; it is not evaluated at a hypothetical changed-law endpoint.

For the actual-reference difference,

\[ (\theta_\lambda-y)'= F_\lambda(\theta_\lambda)-F_\lambda(y) +\lambda G(y)+r_\lambda. \tag{16} \]

The derivative perturbation is bounded in operator norm by

\[ \|DF_\lambda-DF_0\|_2 \le328\Lambda\|L/4\|_2\le656\Lambda=41/625. \tag{17} \]

This follows edgewise from the weighted Hessian and remains valid on the entire mean-zero leaf, including all transverse source errors.

Define the outward scalar comparison

\[ \Psi(e,\mu,t,\beta)=e^{\mu t}e+\phi(\mu,t)\beta, \quad \phi(\mu,t)= \begin{cases}(e^{\mu t}-1)/\mu,&\mu\ne0,\\t,&\mu=0. \end{cases} \tag{18} \]

Given the carried full phase-error radius \(e\), first construct

\[ \beta_{\max}=\rho+\Lambda\max_k g_k,\qquad R=\tfrac54\left[\Psi(e,K,h,\beta_{\max})+2^{-80}\right]. \tag{19} \]

The global derivative bound \(K\) proves that the actual changed-law phase stays within \(R\) of the reference throughout the step. This prospective domain does not rely on a future local growth estimate.

On the full convex domain \(T+\{v:\mathbf1^Tv=0,\|v\|\le R\}\), rebuild a sine logarithmic-growth upper bound \(\mu_0\) using the shared full-leaf cosine/Loewner and exact PSD construction. Its reflected blocks cover all 26 mean-zero directions. The original step's cached growth rate applies to its original radius and cannot substitute for this new calculation. Equation (17) then supplies

\[ \mu=\mu_0+656\Lambda. \tag{20} \]

This one fresh domain covers all eight subintervals. With \(\Delta=h/8=1/64\), carry

\[ e_k=\Psi(e_{k-1},\mu,\Delta,\rho+\Lambda g_k), \quad k=1,\ldots,8, \qquad E_{\rm step}=\max_{0\le k\le8}e_k. \tag{21} \]

The scalar comparison is monotone or constant on each subinterval, so the endpoint maximum bounds the whole subinterval. Require the strict check \(E_{\rm step}<R\). At the original step boundary, change to the next retained rational reference center and add its full recentering radius exactly once:

\[ e_{\rm next}=e_8+d. \tag{22} \]

There are no reference resets at the eight artificial subinterval boundaries. The actual complete state is never reset. Initial admission proves that the release error plus the retained reference's rounding error is strictly below \(21/100000\), then starts the comparison at exactly \(e_0=21/100000\); it does not discard that rounding error.

The fixed comparison uses all 76 original steps, the full symmetric law interval, eight derivative cones per step, outward rational arithmetic and fresh full-leaf growth bounds. It keeps the same structural clocks and original source errors. A broad bound may lose sign and temporal correlations; such loss is a limitation of this sufficient scalar comparison, not a restriction on the actual parameter's constancy or a new stochastic law.

docs.title: Observations and decision scope
docs.text:
Rebuild winding margins from the actual reference boxes and new full-state errors. Whole-time receiver retention uses its fixed winding-zero branch integers and requires every internal edge to remain strictly inside \((-\pi,\pi)\) throughout every validated interval. Combined with (9), a passing corridor certifies receiver winding zero from preparation through the retained stopping horizon for the entire source and law family.

Terminal donor loss is a different observation. It requires the complete new endpoint ball to lie in a winding different from one for each claimed donor. A center winding or the original sine endpoint margin alone is insufficient. A failed sufficient donor radius cannot establish donor retention, donor loss or future acquisition. Receiver retention may be certified even when the donor endpoint observation is unavailable.

A failed comparison domain, budget or observation remains explicitly unavailable for that claim. It is neither a negative physical result nor an exclusion of the compared constitutive laws. Any newly certified finite nonacquisition concerns only the fixed source, law interval and horizon; it does not decide later formation or regeneration. No physical measurement bridge, preferred law or autonomous preparation follows.

docs.title: Result: uniform finite receiver nonacquisition
docs.text:
The fixed eight-cone comparison closes all 76 prospective domains. Its terminal full-source phase radius satisfies

\[ e_{76}<287/1000, \qquad e_{76}\ \text{is approximately }0.286189004. \tag{23} \]

The receiver's winding-zero corridor passes throughout every subinterval: the minimum strict edge-branch margin exceeds \(27/25=1.08\) radians after including the complete new phase error. Its terminal margin also exceeds \(1.08\). Combining this retained-reference comparison with the own-law initial-layer result (9) proves

\[ w_2(\tau)=0\quad\text{for every original admitted source, every }|\lambda|\le1/10000, \quad 0\le\tau\le400+\frac{19}{2\gamma^2}. \tag{24} \]

Thus the receiver has not acquired winding one anywhere in this entire finite interval. In particular, receiver acquisition with continuously retained donors and joined winding-one capture does not occur within this horizon for the admitted source and constitutive family.

The donor endpoint decision is separate. The new ball is wider than the endpoint radius permitting a robust winding-zero reading for either donor. Both corresponding sufficient branch margins are below \(-349/1000\). Their negativity makes this changed-law donor observation unavailable; it proves neither retention nor loss. The original whole-source donor-loss conclusion at \(\lambda=0\) remains valid from its narrower, separately preserved enclosure. It is not extended to all \(\lambda\) by the present comparison.

Equation (24) is an analytic consequence of freshly admitted complete laws and preserved reference evidence. It is not a new reserved response, an evaluation of changed-law trajectories or an experimental measurement. The law interval and source are unchanged, and the result does not come from a scan that selects favorable parameters. The global Euclidean comparison discards some parameter and state correlations; its uncertain donor reading records that limitation explicitly.

The new statement changes the quantified model class: finite receiver nonacquisition holds uniformly over the admitted interval, even though its true first-boundary minima and same-state regional powers differ. Those static constitutive changes therefore do not suffice to produce receiver formation on this source and horizon. They do not rule out later acquisition, other preparations or other justified complete laws. An all-future claim would need a source-valid invariant domain or another complete-state argument retaining form, contacts and own-law dissipation; neither this finite comparison nor a donor endpoint label supplies it.

The internal research entry point compare_constitutive_receiver_prefix(root) re-admits the fixed source, reads the pinned archive and applies the shared _compare_constitutive_receiver_step kernel. Its report retains the numerical premises and makes the unavailable donor endpoint explicit. From the repository root, reproduce the source, scalar comparison, kernel and complete-prefix checks with:

python -m pytest tests/physics/test_constitutive_receiver_source.py tests/physics/test_constitutive_receiver_comparison.py tests/research/test_constitutive_receiver_evidence.py tests/test_comparison_flow.py -q

These checks rebuild bounds from the retained evidence; they neither regenerate the reference nor evaluate a changed-law trajectory.

docs.title: Interaction at a marked boundary of a critical parent
docs.text:
A critical parent can transmit its internal registration to an additional organized neighbor through an explicitly marked boundary. The inherited local state has three coordinates at zero contact. At positive contact two of these modes become stable, while one critical mode remains. The neighbor changes that mode's relaxation coefficient through the geometry of the joined state.

This is a conditional, local theorem for supplied support and prepared organizations. It does not establish the occurrence of contact, acquisition of the additional neighbor, or entry of any original source into the local domain.

Premise Declaration Parent The 54-node critical organization in the transition owner, at fixed \(0<\eta\le10^{-12}\) and \(\lambda=\lambda_c(\eta)\) Neighbor One additional C9 with the same internal carrier and constitutive law Boundary Nine same-slot edges from host child c=2 to the neighbor, all of supplied weight epsilon Dynamics Both rows use all edge weights; unit capacity, gamma, quarter factors and tau remain unchanged Local state All 63 forms and phases, zero total form, fixed total phase, and all fine coordinates Small-contact description A local three-dimensional center manifold at epsilon=0; constants and neighborhoods may depend on fixed eta Positive-contact description Local critical attraction at each fixed epsilon>0, with its own neighborhood and transverse rates Evidence Exact fields, projection, stationary elimination, center-manifold coefficients and static controls; no trajectories, scans or source replay

docs.title: 1. Complete joined law and the cost of contact
docs.text:
Keep the parent labels c=0,...,5 and add c=6 for the neighbor. Each child has j=0,...,8, with primitive node order 9*c+j. The parent's 144 edges retain their weights: 99 old internal/rim edges of weight one and 45 spokes of weight eta. The neighbor has nine internal edges of weight one. Add \(\{(2,j),(6,j)\}\), j=0,...,8, with weight epsilon. Write \(L_\epsilon=L_0+\epsilon L_{\rm b}\).

All edges use the same potential and current:

\[ V_\lambda(a)=1-\cos a+\lambda\frac{(1-\cos9a)^2}{6\,9^4}, \qquad j_\lambda(a)=\sin a+ \lambda\frac{\sin9a-\tfrac12\sin18a}{2187}, \qquad \lambda=\lambda_c(\eta). \tag{1} \]

For the full phase potential \(U_\epsilon=\sum_e w_eV_\lambda(\theta_b-\theta_i)\), the exact equations are

\[ x'=\frac{-L_\epsilon x-\gamma\nabla U_\epsilon}4,\qquad \theta'=\frac\gamma4L_\epsilon x,\qquad H_\epsilon=\frac12x^TL_\epsilon x+U_\epsilon,\qquad H_\epsilon'=-\frac14\|L_\epsilon x\|^2. \tag{2} \]

Here \(\gamma=1/(1023\pi)\) and prime means the unchanged tau clock. Total form and total lifted phase are conserved. The form row supplies the pressure under held unit capacity. There is no external input or later event in these equations. Work on the zero-total-form leaf and a fixed-total-phase local chart.

If the boundary is inserted without changing the primitive state, its storage jump is exactly

\[ \Delta H=\epsilon\sum_{j=0}^8 \left[\frac12(x_{6,j}-x_{2,j})^2+ V_\lambda(\theta_{6,j}-\theta_{2,j})\right]\ge0 . \tag{3} \]

This is supplied event work. Continuous loss is not its reservoir, and the event is not declared passive or autonomously selected. The jump is zero at the exactly aligned equilibrium, which does not by itself explain why the event occurs.

The local identity chart uses alpha=2*pi/9, \(\theta_{c,j}=\alpha(j-4)+\Phi_c+q_{c,j}\), with \(\sum_jq_{c,j}=0\), and the parent's original compatible lifts. For example, the open neighborhood

\[ \|h\|_2<6\eta,\qquad \|q\|_\infty<1/100,\qquad |t|<1/20,\qquad |d|<1/20 \tag{4} \]

has the same parent marked class, neighbor winding one, and zero winding on the eight independent new mixed slot cycles. Here t and d are defined below; the old host shape is \(h_c=\Phi_c-\Phi_5-t-b_c\), with \(b_c=(2\pi/5)(c-2)\) and \(\sum_{c=0}^4h_c=0\). Every new boundary gap has magnitude less than \(1/20+1/120+6\eta+1/50<2/25\). Thus the boundary remains in a single circular chart with \(j_\lambda'>9/10\), using \(\cos a-2/243\le j_\lambda'(a)\). The old internal and rim bounds remain those of the transition owner. This is a local identity domain, not a source-entry certificate.

docs.title: 2. Exact carrier and collective boundary equations
docs.text:
The seven-child carrier \(q=0\), with forms constant within each child, is exactly invariant: internal currents cancel and every remaining edge joins equal slots. Its equations use the weighted seven-vertex graph in both rows, with the same quarter factors. This is a twelve-dimensional relative system, not a stationary approximation. The other 112 relative fine form/phase directions are retained when testing its local stability.

Let \(X_c\) be the child mean form, and define

\[ \begin{split} A&=\frac16\sum_{c=0}^5X_c,& B&=X_6,& r&=B-A,\\ \Omega&=\frac16\sum_{c=0}^5\Phi_c,&\Psi&=\Phi_6,&d&=\Psi-\Omega,\\ t&=\frac15\sum_{c=0}^4\Phi_c-\Phi_5,& \xi&=X_2-A,&s&=\Phi_2-\Omega . \end{split} \tag{5} \]

The mean coordinates r and d are neighbor minus parent. On fixed global means, \(A=-r/7,\ B=6r/7\), and the phase means are \(\Omega=-d/7,\ \Psi=6d/7\), up to the fixed common origin. The actual marked port has form offset xi and phase offset s.

On the carrier, direct summation of the complete rows gives

\[ \begin{split} r'&=-\frac{7\epsilon}{24} [r-\xi+\gamma j_\lambda(d-s)],\\ d'&=\frac{7\gamma\epsilon}{24}(r-\xi),\\ t'&=\frac{3\gamma\eta}{2} \left(\frac15\sum_{c=0}^4X_c-X_5\right) -\frac{\gamma\epsilon}{20}(r-\xi). \end{split} \tag{6} \]

For a noncarrier state, the first line uses the actual averaged boundary current

\[ \overline j_{\rm b} =\frac19\sum_jj_\lambda(d-s+q_{6,j}-q_{2,j}) \tag{7} \]

in place of \(j_\lambda(d-s)\); the other two mean rows are still exact as written. Thus (6) is not an unqualified closure in t,r,d. The zero fine means cancel the linear Taylor term, giving the own-law error bound

\[ |\overline j_{\rm b}-j_\lambda(d-s)| \le\frac{J_2}{18}\|q_6-q_2\|_2^2,\qquad J_2=\frac{10}{9}. \tag{7a} \]

The isolated parent's critical phase curve, at fixed parent mean, has host origins \(t/6+b_c+u_c(t)\) and donor origin \(-5t/6\). At t=0 the marked port c=2 has \(u_2(0)=0\) by reflection. Let w be that curve's tangent and put

\[ N=\|w\|_2^2=\frac{15}{2}+9\|u_t(0)\|_2^2,\qquad h_\eta=w_{2,j}=\frac16+u_{2,t}(0),\qquad m_\eta=\frac{9\gamma^2}{4N}. \tag{8} \]

The own-law bound \(\|u_t(0)\|_2<6\eta\) gives \(h_\eta>1/6-6\eta>1/7\). Extend w by zero on the neighbor. The critical spectral coordinate

\[ \zeta=\frac{w^T(\theta_P-\theta_{P,*}+\gamma x_P)}N \tag{9} \]

ignores the parent common means because w has zero sum. Projecting the actual joined rows gives

\[ \zeta'=-\frac{\gamma^2}{4N}w^T\nabla U_P(\theta_P) +\epsilon m_\eta h_\eta\,\overline j_{\rm b}. \tag{10} \]

Every boundary form-diffusion term cancels in this row. The cancellation requires the same boundary weights in both complete rows. Physical t instead has the explicit form term in (6); it is not identical to zeta on arbitrary states.

docs.title: 3. Three local coordinates at zero contact
docs.text:
At epsilon=0, fix the parent's critical state and the aligned neighbor carrier, with all forms zero. The full relative state has 124 dimensions. The parent contributes one center direction and 105 stable directions. The neighbor's eight relative phases and eight relative forms are stable, since its phase Hessian is \(\cos\alpha L_9>0\) on its relative space. The two independent component-mean differences r,d have zero rows. There are therefore three semisimple zero eigenvalues and 121 strictly stable eigenvalues. On the exact carrier the count is three center and nine stable directions.

For each fixed eta, the finite-smoothness center construction used in the local parent dynamics applies after adjoining \(\epsilon'=0\). Choose a finite \(C^k\) manifold, k at least five, equivariant under reflection and with the product of the parent center curve and the two mean coordinates at epsilon=0. The local spectral gap exists at fixed eta; no lower bound uniform in eta is asserted. The analytic extension to negative epsilon needed for the parameter theorem is only a proof device, not an admitted negative-weight model.

Use physical t,r,d as center coordinates and write z=(t,r,d). All three reverse under the reflection fixing c=2, while epsilon is unchanged. The aligned state is an exact equilibrium for every epsilon. The local rows are therefore odd in z. At zero contact the actual center port has

\[ s=h_\eta t+O_\eta(t^3),\qquad \xi=O_\eta(t^3),\qquad \zeta=t+O_\eta(t^3). \tag{11} \]

The equalities concern the invariant center curve. The stationary shape supplies the same tangent, but not an invariant trajectory. At nonzero epsilon the graph corrections in (11) are \(O_\eta(\epsilon\|z\|)\).

Let \(b_\eta>0\) be the parent's critical cubic coefficient, already derived in its unchanged tau clock:

\[ b_\eta=m_\eta A_5\eta^5 B_s(0,\mu_c,\eta),\qquad A_5=5\varphi^{10},\qquad 55<B_s(0,\mu_c,\eta)<70 . \tag{12} \]

The notation A_5 here is the torque coefficient, not the mean A in (5). Put c=7/24. Projection of the full field gives

\[ \begin{split} t'&=-b_\eta t^3+ \epsilon m_\eta h_\eta(d-h_\eta t)+R_t,\\ r'&=-c\epsilon[r+\gamma(d-h_\eta t)]+R_r,\\ d'&=c\gamma\epsilon r+R_d,\\ R_t&=O_\eta\!\left(|t|^5+ \epsilon\|z\|^3+\epsilon^2\|z\|\right),\\ R_r,R_d&=O_\eta\!\left( \epsilon\|z\|^3+\epsilon^2\|z\|\right). \end{split} \tag{13} \]

For the first row, the parent linear field vanishes under its left center vector. Consequently a first-order correction to the stable graph cannot add a term linear in epsilon*z to (10). The direct boundary term is the one displayed in (13), since \(j_\lambda'(0)=1\). Changing from zeta to physical t changes the derivative only by \(O_\eta(\epsilon^2\|z\|+\epsilon\|z\|^3+|t|^5)\), using (11). This explains why the explicit raw form term in (6) is absent from the leading center t row; it has not been dropped from the full law. The other rows follow from (6), and reflection excludes quadratic state remainders.

The leading linear contact matrix, in the order (t,r,d), is

\[ \epsilon \begin{pmatrix} -m_\eta h_\eta^2&0&m_\eta h_\eta\\ c\gamma h_\eta&-c&-c\gamma\\ 0&c\gamma&0 \end{pmatrix}. \tag{14} \]

It has one zero eigenvalue and two with negative real part: the remaining polynomial is

\[ s^2+(c+m_\eta h_\eta^2)s+ c m_\eta h_\eta^2+c^2\gamma^2 . \tag{15} \]

The two additional decay rates are of order epsilon at fixed eta. Eliminating these mean coordinates at epsilon=0 would erase genuine neutral state and cannot give a uniform instantaneous scalar law.

At epsilon=0 the leading full-state center initialization is \((\Pi_\eta(\theta_P,x_P),r,d)\), where \(\Pi_\eta=\zeta+O_\eta(\|(\delta\theta_P,x_P)\|^2)\). Here the parent map consumes its mean-subtracted phase and form coordinates; the linear w projection already performs that removal. For small contact, the three-dimensional slow spectral subspace is separated from the other 121 directions and changes by O_eta(epsilon). Its linear initialization, expressed in physical coordinates on that subspace, is \(P_{3,\epsilon}\delta Z\), with \(P_{3,\epsilon}=P_{3,0}+O_\eta(\epsilon)\) and \(P_{3,0}\delta Z=(\zeta,r,d)\). The corresponding nonlinear tracking initialization retains the discarded-state correction in all three coordinates. In particular, availability of r and d as physical coordinates on the invariant graph does not make its tracking initial means equal to the raw means of an arbitrary off-manifold state. No uniform nonlinear initialization error, neighborhood or tracking rate as eta or epsilon tends to zero is asserted.

docs.title: 4. A fixed positive contact changes the critical relaxation
docs.text:
There is a stronger exact local conclusion at every fixed epsilon>0. At the aligned state the new gaps are zero and \(j_\lambda'(0)=1\). Its phase Hessian is

\[ M_{63}=\operatorname{diag}(M_{P,*},\cos\alpha L_9) +\epsilon L_{\rm b}. \tag{16} \]

All three terms are positive semidefinite. Before adding the boundary, their kernel consists of the parent critical tangent and the two component rotations. On the fixed-global-phase space, the boundary eliminates one linear combination. Its remaining critical vector is

\[ \begin{split} \widetilde w_P&=w-\frac{h_\eta}{7}\mathbf1_P,& \widetilde w_N&=\frac{6h_\eta}{7}\mathbf1_N,\\ \widetilde N&=\|\widetilde w\|^2 =N+\frac{54}{7}h_\eta^2. \end{split} \tag{17} \]

Its two endpoints agree on every new edge. Conversely, equality on those edges imposes d=h_eta*t on the two old relative kernel directions, leaving only (17). Thus the relative phase Hessian has 61 positive directions and one zero. The complete 124-dimensional pencil

\[ s^2L_\epsilon^{-1}+\frac s4I+\frac{\gamma^2}{16}M_{63} \tag{18} \]

has one simple zero eigenvalue and 123 eigenvalues with negative real part, by the scalar quadratic and kernel Schur-complement arguments applied to this actual joined Hessian.

The stationary normal elimination can also be identified exactly. In the local chart, the 56 fine phase directions remain positive. The old 48 directions and the neighbor's eight directions already have positive internal curvature; new edges add nonnegative curvature because their gaps satisfy (4). At the carrier their fine gradients vanish. Integrating the fine Hessian therefore forces q=0 at any nearby normal stationary state.

At fixed physical t, neighbor stationarity then requires \(j_\lambda(d-s)=0\). The strict local monotonicity of this current gives d=s. All boundary currents vanish, and the parent's projected host equations uniquely recover its unchanged u(t). Let \(s_*(t)=t/6+u_2(t)\). With global phase fixed, the joined stationary curve is exactly

\[ \widetilde\Theta_P(t)=\Theta_P(t)-\frac{s_*(t)}7\mathbf1_P, \qquad \widetilde\Theta_N(t)= \alpha(j-4)+\frac{6s_*(t)}7+\text{fixed common origin}. \tag{19} \]

Its boundary energy is zero. Its reduced phase potential is the same \(9\mathcal W(t)\) as the parent, plus the constant internal neighbor potential. The positive normal Hessian ensures local uniqueness of this normal elimination at fixed t.

Apply the invariant-center calculation to this joined system. The normalized left vector is \((\widetilde w,\gamma\widetilde w)/\widetilde N\). As in the parent derivation, the actual invariant curve agrees with the stationary curve through degree two; its cubic normal correction is annihilated by \(\widetilde w^TM_{63}=0\). The resulting cubic coefficient is

\[ t'=-b_{\eta,\epsilon}^{\rm joined}t^3+O_{\eta,\epsilon}(t^5), \qquad b_{\eta,\epsilon}^{\rm joined} =b_\eta\frac{N}{N+(54/7)h_\eta^2}>0 . \tag{20} \]

For each fixed positive epsilon this coefficient has the stated exact value, independent of epsilon. Neighborhoods and transverse decay rates do depend on epsilon. Since u_t=O(eta),

\[ \frac{b_{\eta,\epsilon}^{\rm joined}}{b_\eta} \longrightarrow\frac{35}{36}\quad\hbox{as }\eta\to0 \tag{21} \]

along the proved critical family, without a uniform dynamical-limit claim. The effect comes from the larger tangent norm in (17); the stationary quartic potential is unchanged. This is an inherited change in relaxation, not a physical mass identification or a change to primitive capacity.

docs.title: 5. Joined initialization, identity and asymptotic decay
docs.text:
The positive normal Hessian and the unchanged strictly positive quartic reduced potential make the aligned joined state a strict local minimum of H_epsilon on the fixed-mean leaf. At each fixed positive eta and epsilon, a small compact sublevel is invariant and lies inside the identity chart. Storage loss and connected support force x=0 on its zero-loss invariant set; local stationary classification leaves only the critical equilibrium. Thus the full joined state is Lyapunov stable and asymptotically attracting, including all fine perturbations admitted locally.

The contact work can be included in an explicit sufficient admission condition. Choose a small closed full relative ball \(\mathcal B\) inside the identity chart and this strict-minimum neighborhood, and set

\[ \mathcal E_{\eta,\epsilon} =\min_{\partial\mathcal B} [H_\epsilon(Z)-H_\epsilon(Z_*)]>0 . \tag{21a} \]

If the primitive state immediately before the event is already inside this ball and

\[ H_0(Z_0)-H_0(Z_*)+\Delta H(Z_0) <\mathcal E_{\eta,\epsilon}, \tag{21b} \]

the joined trajectory cannot leave the ball. The reference has zero boundary work, so \(H_\epsilon(Z_*)=H_0(Z_*)\), and (21b) is exactly the post-event sublevel condition with the paid jump (3). This is a local, sufficient admission; neither a numerical ball radius nor a global low-energy capture criterion is supplied.

Finite-smoothness center reduction and stable tracking apply with 123 stable directions. The same graph-slope and quadratic-defect argument as in the parent initialization proof gives

\[ \begin{split} \Pi_{\eta,\epsilon}^{\rm joined}(\delta\theta,x) &=\frac{\widetilde w^T(\delta\theta+\gamma x)} {\widetilde N} +O_{\eta,\epsilon}(\|(\delta\theta,x)\|^2)\\ &=\frac{N\zeta+(54h_\eta/7)(d+\gamma r)} {N+(54/7)h_\eta^2} +O_{\eta,\epsilon}(\|(\delta\theta,x)\|^2). \end{split} \tag{22} \]

The linear identity uses the physical component means, so it retains the neighbor's form and phase rather than replacing them with their stationary values.

The zero set of this nonlinear initialization map is the local 123-dimensional strong-stable manifold. Outside it, the physical parent registration has the asymptotic behavior

\[ t(\tau)\sim \frac{\operatorname{sgn}\Pi_{\eta,\epsilon}^{\rm joined}} {\sqrt{2b_{\eta,\epsilon}^{\rm joined}\tau}} . \tag{23} \]

The exceptional set approaches exponentially. These conclusions hold at fixed positive contact and on the corresponding local invariant neighborhood. They do not give a finite prepared-source capture time or uniform approximation error.

At epsilon=0, r and d are additional neutral coordinates. At positive epsilon their decay rates tend to zero with epsilon, while the eventual critical curve requires d=s_*(t). Consequently the positive-contact asymptotic coefficient (20) cannot be substituted into the zero-contact transient problem. The small-contact and long-time limits have separate obligations.

docs.title: 6. What the marked boundary observes, and what means omit
docs.text:
A direct field calculation makes the inherited interaction discriminating. Put all forms to zero, keep the fine carrier, choose the parent's stationary shape u(t), and set d=0. The parent and neighbor means then agree, but their marked port gap is \(-s_*(t)\). The receiver's exact initial form rate is

\[ X_6'=\frac{\epsilon\gamma}{4}j_\lambda(s_*(t)) =\frac{\epsilon\gamma h_\eta}{4}\,t +O_\eta(\epsilon t^3). \tag{24} \]

Reflection gives opposite rates for sufficiently small nonzero t and -t, despite identical parent means and identical neighbor state. The relevant internal registration is therefore consumed by this actual boundary. These two preparations also have exactly equal old storage and equal contact-event work: the same reflection makes the parent reduced potential even and \(s_*(t)\) odd, while \(V_\lambda\) is even. Means and storage therefore do not remove this marked-port distinction. For this same preparation the raw physical t' is initially zero: every form is zero in its exact phase row. The preparation lies on a stationary shape graph, not on the invariant center manifold, so the center t row in (13) must not be used as its instantaneous rate.

Even retaining t,r,d does not close the exact field for arbitrary nearby states. Keep every phase at the aligned equilibrium. Compare zero forms with a perturbation adding a form delta to each node in child 2 and subtracting delta from each node in another host child. All other forms stay zero. The complete means and t,r,d remain zero, and the phase identity is identical, but xi=delta in the perturbed state. Its mean rates differ by

\[ \Delta t'=\frac{\epsilon\gamma}{20}\,\delta,\qquad \Delta r'=\frac{7\epsilon}{24}\,\delta,\qquad \Delta d'=-\frac{7\gamma\epsilon}{24}\,\delta . \tag{25} \]

The old host-versus-donor form contrast is zero, so no omitted parent term is needed for these differences.

Equations (24)--(25) are exact local preparation-and-field witnesses, not integrated responses. They establish both the usefulness of the internal mode and the limits of a mean-state description. The center manifold supplies a justified local description with initialized stable transients, not an instantaneous quotient of every admissible full state.

docs.title: 7. Scope and static controls
docs.text:
The boundary, its weight and its occurrence remain supplied. The local identity and relaxation theorem is conditional on entering the declared neighborhood. No original acquisition, observation word or frozen response was rerun; no source certificate was transferred from another law or support. The additional C9 is assumed organized here. Neither the supplied contact nor the change of critical relaxation is a newly identified physical force.

The result adds a complete-state interaction consequence to the stationary and unforced parent results: the parent exports its internal registration through a marked port, while a neighbor changes the inherited relaxation and initialization. The retained state and boundary have been specified before any numerical or physical evaluation.

The boundary-constraint criterion identifies which parts of this conclusion use positive curvature and complete kinetics, and which retain the particular constitutive law. Its fixed-total-conductance split-port control removes the surviving neutral mode; it does not transfer this single-port cubic coefficient.

Static interaction tests check the 63-node edge sums, mean orientations, projected three-coordinate matrix, full kernel and tangent norm, added storage, and the independent preparation witnesses. They do not solve a trajectory or search for a root. The execution plan owns subsequent work.

docs.title: Derived form phase and inherited closure
docs.text:
Directed diffusion, sufficient amplitude/phase observations, wave-coordinate scope and regular continuation.

Section numbers are stable locators across this document family. The parameter reference owns the reading map; the research program alone owns active tasks. Each result retains its stated model and scope.

docs.title: 21. Derived form phase, wave coordinates and genuine continuation
docs.text: A phase observed in form, independently stored primitive phase, and a phase law chosen to realize a desired motion are different objects. The following reuse of transport, memory and source geometry separates them. No result below establishes sustained identity or physical particle emergence.

docs.title: Variable contract for the derived form family
docs.text:
This contract instantiates the parameter properties for the directed-triangle family. It does not redefine the engine's primitive variables. Use form unit X, declared clock unit T, and the orthonormal regional frames displayed below.

docs.title: Shared engine observation of the form coordinates
docs.text:
The form geometry owner now exposes these coordinates and their instantaneous nodal pushforward through observe_regional_form(graph, regions) and the SDK's Network.regional_form(regions). The ordered triples are supplied reporting frames. Observation itself requires no directed-cycle topology, common capacity or pure-EPI pressure; those are additional premises of the autonomous reductions below.

For each triple, it retains the rational raw contrasts a=x_0-x_1, b=x_0+x_1-2*x_2, representing z=a/sqrt(2)+i*b/sqrt(6), and the mean. Squared amplitude is exactly a^2/2+b^2/6 for the materialized fine inputs. The full Gram retains Re(Q_ab)=a_a*a_b/2+b_a*b_b/6 and sqrt(12)*Im(Q_ab)=b_a*a_b-a_a*b_b. The corresponding derivatives project the actual shared rounded nodal product with its retained arithmetic defect. This is a read-only integration of the derived observation, not a new constitutive pressure or replacement primitive phase law. docs.title: 21.1 Directed form rotation and exact eliminated-state memory
docs.text:
Take outgoing unit support i -> i+1 (mod 3), common fixed capacity nu>0, and pure-EPI pressure. For the existing orthonormal basis U=[(1,-1,0)/sqrt(2), (1,1,-2)/sqrt(6)], write the two real form coordinates as z=u+i*v. The outgoing Laplacian and exact Cayley owner give

\[ \dot z= u\left(- rac32-i rac{\sqrt3}{2} ight)z,\qquad \dot{\arg z}=- rac{\sqrt3 u}{2},\qquad rac{d}{dt}|z|^2=-3 u|z|^2. \]

The angle requires z!=0; the Cartesian law is defined everywhere. Reversing the edges reverses the rotation; reciprocal symmetrization removes it while preserving contrast decay. Directed support supplies orientation, so the form-only reflection obstruction in section 17 is not contradicted. No frequency is fitted, but the origin of that support remains a premise. The radius contracts by exp(-2*pi*sqrt(3)) per turn, independently of capacity. This is transient rotation, not a maintained pattern.

Put a=3*nu/2, b=sqrt(3)*nu/2. Eliminating the second coordinate gives

\[ \dot u=-au+be^{-at}v(0)-b^2\int_0^t e^{-a(t-s)}u(s)\,ds, \qquad \ddot u+3 u\dot u+3 u^2u=0. \]

Both the negative memory kernel and its hidden initial source are derived. A second-order observable equation thus follows from first-order nodal evolution without added microscopic inertia. The general elimination algebra is reusable; epi_memory's reversible graph adapter is not extended to this directed example. Actual fresh-pressure controls give different u_dot for equal observed u and different hidden v, while primitive phase stays zero. Controls: directed form phase and memory.

docs.title: 21.2 A coupled amplitude and phase law derived from fine diffusion
docs.text:
Join two equally oriented unit directed triangles by reciprocal unit links between corresponding vertices. Each node has two outgoing neighbors. This declared support differs from the reciprocal-prism model. With pure-EPI pressure and common fixed capacity nu, the exact complete scalar-state coordinates are two means and two complex contrasts:

\[ \dot\mu_a= rac u2(\mu_b-\mu_a),\qquad \dot z_a=\left(- rac{5 u}{4}-i rac{\sqrt3 u}{4} ight)z_a + rac u2 z_b. \]

For z_a=r_a exp(i psi_a) with positive amplitudes, these imply

\[ \dot r_a=- rac{5 u}{4}r_a+ rac u2r_b\cos(\psi_b-\psi_a),\qquad \dot\psi_a=- rac{\sqrt3 u}{4} + rac u2 rac{r_b}{r_a}\sin(\psi_b-\psi_a). \]

The sine interaction, its coefficient and amplitude ratio follow from the fine generator; no synchronization gain is supplied. For delta=psi_1-psi_0, delta_dot=-(nu/2)*(r_0/r_1+r_1/r_0)*sin(delta). Equal amplitudes form an invariant restricted family with delta_dot=-nu*sin(delta). Outside it, equal angles can have different future rates. Angles alone are not sufficient state; at zero amplitude the Cartesian coordinates remain the continuation variables.

The complete contrast budget is

\[ rac{d}{dt}(|z_0|^2+|z_1|^2) =- rac{3 u}{2}(|z_0|^2+|z_1|^2)- u|z_0-z_1|^2. \]

Derived interaction, synchronization and rotation therefore coexist with strict loss. This is a constructive emergent observable phase law. Identifying it with primitive phase or canonical phasor-argument pressure still requires full vector-field matching; a sine term alone is insufficient. Controls: coupled reduction and phase-only obstruction.

docs.title: Inherited observation identity and source work
docs.text:
The fine model above now admits an exact observation-specific closure, rather than only a phase-only counterexample. Retain the same supplied directed support, fixed common positive capacity, orthonormal regional frames and pure-EPI law. Primitive phase is held and unused, Gamma is absent, and no operator event, clipping or numerical time step enters this continuous result. The selected observations are regional contrast squares, relative orientation and their cross-region contributions to the contrast budget. They are not the complete fine state or its tetrad.

On the positive-amplitude chart, put q=r_1/r_0, delta=psi_1-psi_0. The polar equations already derived from the fine generator give

\[ \dot q= rac{ u}{2}(1-q^2)\cos\delta,\qquad \dot\delta=- rac{ u}{2}(q+q^{-1})\sin\delta. \]

Thus the two angles together with the amplitude ratio have a closed evolution while both amplitudes stay positive. An absolute amplitude is additionally needed to predict form magnitude or its quadratic budget: common scaling preserves all angles and q, but multiplies that budget by the scale squared. Equal amplitudes supply a restricted invariant family, not a reason to discard the ratio for arbitrary preparations.

A division-free description also covers zero regional amplitude. Define

\[ I_a=|z_a|^2,\qquad c=\operatorname{Re}(\overline z_0z_1),\qquad s=\operatorname{Im}(\overline z_0z_1). \]

These quantities obey I_0,I_1>=0 and c^2+s^2=I_0 I_1. Direct differentiation of the inherited Cartesian law gives the closed system

\[ egin{aligned} \dot I_0&=- rac{5 u}{2}I_0+ u c,& \dot I_1&=- rac{5 u}{2}I_1+ u c,\ \dot c&=- rac{5 u}{2}c+ rac u2(I_0+I_1),& \dot s&=- rac{5 u}{2}s. \end{aligned} \]

The common internal rotation cancels in this observation. The constraint defect has derivative -5*nu*(c^2+s^2-I_0*I_1); realizable initial data remain realizable under the inherited linear Cartesian flow. Conversely, any such data with I_0>0 reconstruct a representative z_0=sqrt(I_0), z_1=(c+i*s)/sqrt(I_0). If I_0=0<I_1, take z_0=0, z_1=sqrt(I_1); at total zero both vanish. The common orientation is discarded. This proves sufficiency for the selected observations without claiming a globally unique minimal state for TNFR.

Write E=I_0+I_1, D=I_0-I_1. Its exact finite-time modes are

\[ egin{aligned} (E+2c)(t)&=e^{-3 u t/2}(E+2c)(0),\ (E-2c)(t)&=e^{-7 u t/2}(E-2c)(0),\ D(t)&=e^{-5 u t/2}D(0),\qquad s(t)=e^{-5 u t/2}s(0). \end{aligned} \]

Here nu*c is the cross-region contribution to each dI_a/dt under the displayed split. This is an inherited contrast-square budget, not laboratory energy, primitive unit-phasor resultant amplitude, external Gamma or a separately supplied sustaining source. Positive contributions at both regions do not imply conservation of that contribution: the complete balance still satisfies E_dot=-(3*nu/2)*E-nu*|z_0-z_1|^2. The model cannot maintain nonzero contrast indefinitely. At z_0=0, z_1!=0, it nevertheless has I_0_dot=0 and I_0_ddot=nu^2*I_1/2>0: local contrast can start growing by transfer while total contrast decreases. No angle or event is invented at the zero-amplitude boundary.

Same angular history, different radial response. With both fine regional means initialized to 1/2, compare real positive contrasts (z_0,z_1)=(5,5)/128 and (1,7)/128. Both have E=25/8192 and relative phase zero. Their continuously lifted observed phases follow the identical law psi_a(t)=-sqrt(3)*nu*t/4 for all t>=0 (modulo 2*pi for circular phases): after removing this common rotation, the real linear coupling preserves positive amplitudes.
