docs.title: 1. Exact finite Fourier representation
docs.text:
Use the unitary transform hat u_k=N^-1/2 sum_j u_j exp(-2*pi*i*k*j/N). Let c=T/2, k0=N/4, b_m=1-|m|/Q and S2=sum_{|m|<Q} b_m^2. The nominal complex bookkeeping variable of source A has Fourier coefficients

\[ \widehat z^A_{k_0+m}(0)=\frac{a b_m}{\sqrt{S_2}} e^{-2\pi i(k_0+m)c/N},\qquad |m|<Q, \]

and zero coefficients elsewhere. The real channels are separately retained: on that positive band hat x=hat z/2, hat theta=hat z/(2i); the opposite coefficients follow by conjugacy of each real channel. Source B is the exact spatial reflection of A, so hat x^B_k=hat x^A_{-k} and likewise for phase. No extra relative phase is selected from the response.

For lambda_k=1-cos(2*pi*k/N), the actual tangent block is

\[ B_k=\lambda_k\begin{pmatrix}-\sigma&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma=\pi e/w. \]

With omega=sqrt(1-sigma^2/4)>0, its exact propagator is

\[ U_k(s)=e^{-\sigma\lambda_k s/2} \left[\cos(\omega\lambda_k s)\,\mathrm{Id} +\frac{\sin(\omega\lambda_k s)}\omega \begin{pmatrix}-\sigma/2&-1\\1&\sigma/2\end{pmatrix}\right]. \tag{1} \]

The instrument requires sigma*T<=1, in addition to its positive-loss law admission. This keeps every decay argument within the shared unit-exponential domain and ensures the square root is separated from zero. It is a numerical instrument domain, not a new restriction on TNFR generally. The fixed model satisfies it. Form and phase must not be replaced by a single scalar complex propagator: positive form loss mixes the two bookkeeping carrier directions.

Take D theta_j=theta_j-theta_{j+1} and d_k=1-exp(2*pi*i*k/N). If alpha and beta are the Fourier coefficients of the two tangent edge-phase differences, the mixed form forcing is the cyclic convolution

\[ \widehat g_k(s)=\frac{\overline d_k}{4N} [\alpha*\beta*(\alpha+\beta)]_k. \tag{2} \]

The two unitary Fourier products each contribute N^-1/2; omitting this normalization would give an incorrect signal. The cubic integrand has separate form and phase channels U_k(T-s)*(hat g_k(s),0).

Both tangent phase histories occupy only the two radius-15 bands. Equation (2) occupies the two radius-45 bands around +/-N/4 after modular folding, 182 modes in total. No cubic output mode is discarded. This finite support statement concerns the cubic predictor, not the nonlinear full flow. The instrument requires 3(Q-1)<N/4, N<=4096 and Q<=32 for this representation.

Reflection exchanges A and B and preserves their mixed forcing, so g is reflection-even. Its Fourier coefficients are real and equal at opposite modes, as are those of the propagated integrand. The implementation intersects the two independently enclosed equal real coefficients and checks that the imaginary enclosures contain zero before retaining this exact symmetry. It retains both partners when applying Parseval's norm.

docs.title: 2. Outward arithmetic and the integration error
docs.text:
Elementary functions, square roots and final coefficient boxes use the shared 128-bit outward rational intervals. For polynomial convolution, their dyadic endpoints become exact integers on the same grid. All four endpoint products are enclosed, and integer sums are accumulated before a single outward projection per output coefficient. This is an optimization of a finite polynomial reduction, not an alternative interval arithmetic or a floating FFT. An opaque evaluation closure captures constants rebuilt from fresh primitive source and model inputs; externally supplied derived reports are not consumed. Trigonometric argument reduction subtracts an integer multiple of an outward pi/2 interval, then applies the exact quarter-turn identities and the shared sine/cosine owners to the residual. Choosing that integer from a midpoint is only a representation choice: the identity holds for every integer, including at uncertain quadrant boundaries. The residual interval retains pi uncertainty.

Let qmax=2*pi*(Q-1)/N. On the input and output Fourier supports, respectively,

\[ K_{\rm in}=(1+\sigma)(1+q_{\max}),\qquad K_{\rm out}=(1+\sigma)(1+3q_{\max}) \]

bound the tangent operator norm: its rotational part has norm one and its loss part norm sigma, while 1-cos(pi/2+q)<=1+|q|. Actual tangent propagators are contractive. Each differentiated input has norm at most a*K_in^j. The trilinear forcing has norm at most 8*a^3, using ||D||<=2. Differentiating its three inputs and the final propagator gives, by the multinomial theorem, the whole-window integrand derivative bound

\[ \|f^{(j)}(s)\|_2\le8a^3\Lambda^j, \qquad \Lambda=K_{\rm out}+3K_{\rm in} =(1+\sigma)(4+6q_{\max}). \tag{3} \]

This retains the actual damped generator in every derivative. It does not infer an error from the difference of two sampled numerical answers.

Use an n-point Gauss-Legendre rule on each of P equal panels. Its nodes are certified by exact rational sign bisection of the degree-n Legendre polynomial: n disjoint sign-changing intervals exhaust its roots. Outward weights are 2/[(1-r^2)*P_n'(r)^2]. The positive Peano kernel gives the same remainder constant for the Euclidean vector norm as for a scalar, with no dimension multiplier. Equations (3) and the Gauss remainder imply

\[ E_G\le 8a^3 T\left(\frac{\Lambda T}{P}\right)^{2n} \frac{(n!)^4}{(2n+1)((2n)!)^3}. \tag{4} \]

Choose n=12. Starting at one panel, double P until this prior bound is at most one tenth of eta_num=a^3/1000, or the frozen limit 65,536 prevents another doubling. This selection reads no integrand or response. For the fixed inputs, Lambda<23/5 and P=64 suffices; hence 768 integrand evaluations are prescribed before the response is known.

Node, weight, initial coefficient, propagator and convolution rounding are retained in the accumulated spectral boxes. The Euclidean norm of their component radii bounds the vector arithmetic error. The separate outward Parseval norm interval retains norm-reduction uncertainty; the numerical certificate uses E_G plus the larger of these two arithmetic allowances. All source materialization is included. The final cubic norm interval expands the quadrature norm interval by E_G. If the total error exceeds eta_num, numerical certification is unavailable even if a computed lower bound is positive. There is no automatic higher-precision retry.

docs.title: 1. Which geometry enters this model?
docs.text:
Three distinct geometries must be retained:

Geometry Role in the present model Boundary Support and coefficients The supplied unit cycle determines incidence D, Laplacian L and the actual exchange paths; held capacities enter the complete law. A drawn embedding or changed edge length alone does not change these rate rows. Edge length defines the localization observation, separately from conductance. Relative form and primitive phase Neighbor form differences drive phase motion; sine phase differences drive form. Phase differences determine the storage curvature and its critical configurations. The Fourier carrier of z=x+i*theta is not primitive circular-phase winding. Organization and boundary A spatial window, profile, carrier band or partition specifies an observation of the retained full state. Its boundary remains coupled to the complement. Overlap, compatible grouping and concentration do not establish actual entry into a new identity or its maintenance.

These distinctions reuse the relation foundation, collective phase-offset conditions and regional work accounting. They do not introduce an extra geometric force or select a new law.

The moving centers in the prepared-transport proof are comparison references, not imposed trajectories in (1). Actual form and phase evolve under both complete rows and can alter the observed profiles and their paths within the proved error bounds. A common organization could involve deflection, changed relative motion or internal rearrangement of the incoming patterns. It need not be a third separate object, and its definition must not require that the original patterns first separate. Any inferred position or velocity remains an observation of the field on fixed sites, with its own availability and error; the elementary support vertices do not move in this model.

A proper contiguous window on a cycle induces a path. It has no internal graph cycle on which to transfer the earlier C9 constituent-winding identity. Closing that path by ignoring its environmental endpoints would change the support. A localized identity can instead retain relative form/phase structure and boundary exchange, but it needs its own prospective formation criterion.

docs.title: 2. An all-time basin for the original preparation family
docs.text:
Let D be the oriented incidence matrix of a simple unit cycle C_N, N>=3, and L=D^T D, A=L/2. Retain signed real form, real continuous phase lifts, held unit capacities, beta one, positive e,w, and no forcing or events. In the declared clock tau=w*t/pi, with sigma=pi*e/w>0, the complete rows are

\[ x'=-\sigma Ax-\tfrac12D^T\sin(D\theta),\qquad \theta'=Ax. \tag{1} \]

Both ordinary means are conserved. Each source member retains its own means; they need not equal the nominal zero means. A constant form or phase reference can be subtracted without changing (1). The following source premise concerns one consistent real lift relative to such a constant reference:

\[ \|(x(0),\theta(0))\|_2\le M,\qquad H_0=2M^2<1. \tag{2} \]

This is a sufficient source condition, not a phase reconstruction from form, a physical preparation certificate or an admission from a cached verdict.

docs.title: Storage and geometric trapping
docs.text:
The existing structural storage and its actual clock-transformed balance are

\[ H(x,\theta)=\tfrac12x^TLx+\sum_e[1-\cos(D\theta)_e], \qquad H'=-\tfrac\sigma2\|Lx\|_2^2\le0. \tag{3} \]

Here H is the original storage, not the packet localization diagnostic. For a cycle, ||L||<=4, and 1-cos u<=u^2/2, so

\[ H(0)\le2\|x(0)\|^2+2\|\theta(0)\|^2\le H_0. \tag{4} \]

Initially every lifted edge difference has absolute value at most 2M<sqrt(2)<pi/2. A first exit from this zero-winding acute component would have an edge at +/-pi/2, contributing one to H. All other storage terms are nonnegative, contradicting H<=H_0<1. Therefore every future edge remains in the same lifted acute component, and in fact

\[ \cos(D\theta)_e\ge1-H_0>0,\qquad (1-H_0)L\preceq\nabla^2V(\theta)\preceq L,\quad V=\sum_e[1-\cos(D\theta)_e]. \tag{5} \]

This bound concerns phase-storage curvature, not the tetrad's diagnostic curvature. It is valid for all nonnegative structural time, without extending the finite moving-template error tube. The unwrapped gaps still telescope to zero around the cycle, so the circular winding remains zero. Changing that winding would require an edge to cross a circular cut, which is also excluded by the stronger acute trap.

docs.title: The only limiting state on each mean leaf
docs.text:
The bounded gaps and fixed phase mean bound every lifted phase coordinate. The form term in H bounds centered form because L is positive on its mean-zero space. The invariant sublevel is thus compact on each mean leaf. The full vector field is globally smooth with bounded sine currents and linear form dependence, so forward continuation is available.

In the zero-dissipation set, Lx=0, hence form is uniform and theta'=0. An invariant trajectory there must also have D^T sin(Dtheta)=0: otherwise the form row leaves that set, since its ordinary mean derivative is zero. Taking its inner product with theta gives

\[ 0=\sum_e (D\theta)_e\sin(D\theta)_e. \]

Every summand is nonnegative and vanishes only at zero in the retained acute chart. Thus every gap vanishes. The sector-capture/LaSalle argument therefore yields

\[ x(\tau)\longrightarrow\overline x(0)\mathbf1,\qquad \theta(\tau)\longrightarrow\overline\theta(0)\mathbf1. \tag{6} \]

This is convergence to one state on each actual source member's conserved mean leaf. It supplies neither a convergence rate nor a finite settling time. The original finite packet identities can remain valid during transport even though they eventually relax. Equation (6) excludes a nonuniform stationary asymptote in this source family; it does not exclude finite-lived additional structure before that limit.

docs.title: Application without a new response calculation
docs.text:
The two nominal Fejer preparations have orthogonal complex carrier bands and joint norm sqrt(2)*a. Each primitive full-state error is at most epsilon, and the joint source is their exact sum. Hence the entire original family satisfies (2) with

\[ M=(\sqrt2+1/500)a,\qquad a=2^{-12},\qquad H_0=2(\sqrt2+1/500)^2a^2<\frac3{12500000}=2.4\,10^{-7}. \tag{7} \]

For example sqrt(2)<70711/50000 proves the last strict rational bound. Neither the computed endpoint defect nor the unresolved uniform interaction verdict is a premise of (7). The conclusion therefore applies to all original source errors, despite the distinct endpoint discrimination limitation. The same estimate gives an all-time phase-Hessian lower factor greater than 1-2.4e-7. It does not give an all-time ||z||<2a bound, preserve the two carrier projections forever, or quantify the lifetime of another pattern.

docs.title: 3. Why the source's geometry cannot be omitted
docs.text:
Small storage alone does not imply consensus for arbitrary circular sources on this same support. A separately supplied twist with constant principal edge gap 2*pi/N, uniform form and N>4 is a critical configuration: the incoming sine currents cancel and its Hessian is cos(2*pi/N)*L. It is a strict local minimum on the relative-phase leaf and has the existing positive-loss local recovery property. On C_1024 its storage satisfies

\[ H_{\rm twist}=N[1-\cos(2\pi/N)]\le\frac{2\pi^2}{N}<1. \tag{8} \]

It has winding one and no all-small zero-component lift around the cycle. It therefore does not satisfy the source condition (2). This counterexample shows why support, storage and the phase component must be matched together. It is an extended prepared pattern, not a localized object formed by the current encounter. It supplies no route across the inaccessible phase boundary.

docs.title: 4. An exact carrier geometry, without a localized envelope closure
docs.text:
For N divisible by four, the repeated period-four family

\[ \theta=(\varphi,\psi,-\varphi,-\psi,\ldots),\qquad x=(r,s,-r,-s,\ldots) \]

is invariant under both complete rows. On this subspace A acts as identity; direct neighbor addition gives

\[ \varphi'=r,\quad \psi'=s,\qquad r'=-\sigma r-\sin\varphi\cos\psi,\quad s'=-\sigma s-\sin\psi\cos\varphi. \]

The invertible relative coordinates u=varphi+psi, v=varphi-psi consequently satisfy

\[ u''+\sigma u'+\sin u=0,\qquad v''+\sigma v'+\sin v=0. \tag{9} \]

Their initial velocities retain r,s; this exact change of coordinates does not discard form or install a pendulum as a new law. It exhibits nonlinear internal dynamics selected by a compatible carrier geometry under the actual positive loss. The family repeats throughout the support and supplies no localized envelope, acquisition from outside that family or self-binding. The finite-width prepared packets are not confined to this four-dimensional family. Their other modes and boundary exchange cannot be dropped by using (9).

At the consensus tangent, the two modal exponents are lambda(k)*[-sigma/2 +/- sqrt(sigma^2/4-1)], with lambda(k)=1-cos k. Thus their second k derivatives vanish at the current +/-pi/2 carriers. For the frozen underdamped coefficients their third derivatives do not vanish. Equation (9) retains exact carrier nonlinearity, but neither it nor this dispersion fact supplies a controlled modulation or localization theorem.

docs.title: 5. Formation of a common relational pattern
docs.text:
The geometric circumstances already matter in (1)--(8): the support supplies paths, the prepared phase component determines accessible critical geometry, and the storage/loss law restricts which regions of state space can be reached. The unchanged small pair cannot acquire another stationary trapping geometry. Its certified nominal nonadditivity can coexist with this obstruction.

The generative target is a common organization of the incoming patterns: their relative arrangement and joint evolution acquire an identity absent initially. It may move, deform or have bounded internal relative motion; neither unchanged outgoing trajectories nor an extra separate object is required. Retain constituent and environmental boundary information consumed by that identity. If the original constituent identities cease to apply, record that reorganization rather than retaining their labels as evidence of persistence.

An admissible finite-lived claim specifies:

  • Relational identity. A positive-width class on the actual joint state, with a nonvanishing signal floor and specified relative geometry, primitive phase information and internal response. Any collective center, trajectory or phase registration needs an observation rule, ambiguity handling and error bounds; a band observation is not an independent dynamical constituent.
  • Formation. The original source class lacks that common identity with a margin. Both complete rows must carry it into the declared class. Initial support connectivity, the presence of two packets or transient overlap does not establish this acquisition.
  • Joint retention. The relation remains in a declared nontrivial domain for a specified interval beyond ordinary passage, with environmental work, dispersion and loss accounted for. Bounded distance alone is vacuous on a finite cycle; a common moving center alone can also follow two separating packets. The incoming patterns need not separate before this test begins.
  • Continued response. The reached organization has a discriminating later response without resetting its acquired state. Compare the same-source linear passage and separate histories so that overlap, interference and independently continuing packets cannot alone pass the formation test.

A third Fourier band or the difference of three histories alone does not satisfy those conditions. The parent-acquisition architecture illustrates this proof structure; its supports, windings and coefficients do not transfer.

Specify whether the claim concerns the exact nominal preparation or every member of the original source family. A family claim must carry its correlated preparation errors through initial absence, entry, retention and response; the joint source is the sum of the same two uncertain constituent sources. Retain their actual conserved means. Nominal feasibility does not establish family-wide formation, and the unresolved earlier interaction bound neither proves nor forbids a direct formation argument.

Declare the observation's domain and availability through overlap and deformation. Treat an identification as an exact symmetry only when it preserves the complete law; a lossy observation retains its stated information and error limits. Independent registration of each incoming packet must not discard their relative phase or origin. If an observed region changes membership, include transport across its moving boundary rather than reusing a fixed-region balance unchanged. Loss of the original packet labels is distinct from loss of the retained fine state. A sufficient full-state description can support an organization claim without an autonomous reduced law; that stronger claim needs its own closure or memory argument.

The signal floor, absence margin, entry and retention windows, and later response discriminator need independent reasons and an error budget before evaluating a formation response. Declare the same-source passage control's law and comparison interval. The actual damped tangent and conservative transport reference are distinct controls; using the latter retains its damping-error allowance. Finite overlap or an arbitrarily small deformation alone cannot establish a sustained identity. If linear passage or independently evolving packets also pass the proposed formation test, it does not yet discriminate the target. Prior inspected responses remain prior information; they cannot be relabelled as reserved evidence for a newly chosen criterion.

The existing endpoint bounds still restrict the unchanged source family. At tau=256, each nonzero band observation has less than 1/25 of its squared norm outside its radius-96 reference window; the two reference centers have cycle distance 256. If a common cycle ball of radius r contains more than 1/25 of each band's squared norm, it must intersect both reference windows. The cycle-distance triangle inequality then gives 256<=2(96+r), hence r>=32. This necessary geometric restriction neither excludes wider or two-lobed composites nor establishes one above that radius. It concerns the retained band observations, not an additive decomposition of local total density. Radius 32 is not a newly selected formation threshold.

No such composite identity or binding mechanism is certified here. Comparing nonlinear coupling with dispersion and loss requires the actual carrier geometry: at the present pi/2 carrier the tangent's quadratic dispersion vanishes. A quadratic-dispersion envelope law cannot be imported as a formation theorem. Changing preparation, support, loss or events would define a separately admitted case, preserving the present evidence.

docs.title: 6. Actual-state coincidence and a finite capture obstruction
docs.text: This section tests specified geometric requirements for candidate compact-capture identities. It defines a capture class, not a complete NFR identity or a physical binding criterion. The full state, primitive phase lift and environmental influence remain retained. Every conclusion below covers the whole original source family on [0,256], without consuming the evaluated interaction defect.

docs.title: 6.1 One preparation bound for the actual state and passage controls
docs.text:
Write v=v_A+v_B for the existing opposite-carrier reference, and let U(tau) be the actual damped tangent propagator. Compare three histories:

  • the actual joint flow z_AB=Phi_tau(u_A+u_B);
  • the same-source linear control y=U(tau)(u_A+u_B);
  • the sum of separate nonlinear flows z_A+z_B.

The primitive errors remain shared as originally specified; the joint source error is at most 2*epsilon, not epsilon. In the notation of the encounter bound, the first two template errors are at most E and 2*epsilon+sqrt(2)*a*d, respectively. For the separate-history sum, contractivity applied to the summed tangent and the two individual Duhamel remainders gives

\[ E_s=2\epsilon+\sqrt2\,a d+\frac{64}{3}Ta^3 =E+\frac{32}{3}Ta^3. \tag{10} \]

This uses the individual bootstraps as well as the joint bootstrap; it does not assume that the damped generator is complex-linear or that the bands are closed nonlinear subsystems. The unchanged inputs give, using the same outward bounds as the encounter proof,

\[ E_s/a<\bar h=\frac{13}{250}. \tag{11} \]

For each of these histories Z, put f=P_+Z, g=P_-Z. Orthogonal projection therefore gives ||f-v_A||,||g-v_B||<a*hbar and ||f||,||g||>237*a/250. These are observations of two real channels expressed as z=x+i*theta, not independently evolving constituents or complex EPI.

docs.title: 6.2 A coincidence class on the actual state
docs.text:
Define normalized diagnostic weights and a relative-distance observation by

\[ \mu_+(j)=\frac{|f_j|^2}{\|f\|^2},\qquad \mu_-(l)=\frac{|g_l|^2}{\|g\|^2},\qquad K_\ell(Z)=\sum_{d_N(j,l)\le\ell}\mu_+(j)\mu_-(l). \tag{12} \]

The product defines a deterministic diagnostic, not an assumption of physical or probabilistic independence. K lies in [0,1] and measures relative bulk proximity without assigning sites to constituents, selecting peaks or prescribing motion. It is invariant under common cycle translations and reflection with band exchange. It discards internal phase and shape information; it supplies neither a closed future law nor a decomposition of the actual local squared density into two independent energies.

For a declared distance ell, define the majority-coincidence class by the signal floors ||f||,||g||>=237*a/250 and K_ell>=1/2. The threshold means a majority of the diagnostic pair weight. It is a stated observation policy, not a universal TNFR constant. The definition allows deformation and displacement and has an interior on the full state domain. Initial absence, entry into this class and persistence there can now be tested independently. For any candidate identity that includes this geometric requirement, additional phase, response or memory conditions cannot rescue a trajectory that fails it.

To bound K, use an auxiliary reference-window radius r. If each band has outside fraction at most eta, then two elementary geometric implications are

\[ \begin{array}{ll} D=0,\quad\ell\ge2r &: K_\ell\ge(1-\eta)^2,\\ D>2r+\ell &: K_\ell\le1-(1-\eta)^2, \end{array} \tag{13} \]

where D is the cycle distance between reference centers. The first line includes every pair from the two cores; the second excludes every such pair by the triangle inequality. All remaining pair weight is at most 1-(1-eta)^2. Equality in the second line's separation condition is not admitted by this argument.

Choose the auxiliary proof radius r=48, half the existing localization radius. It changes neither the source nor the law. The transport tail bound and (11) yield

\[ H=\frac{16384}{47^3}<\frac4{25},\qquad \eta<\left(\frac{2/5+13/250}{1-13/250}\right)^2 =\left(\frac{113}{237}\right)^2<\frac14. \tag{14} \]

For every 96<=ell<160, the actual joint state and both passage controls consequently satisfy

\[ K_\ell(0)<\frac7{16},\qquad K_\ell(128)>\frac9{16},\qquad K_\ell(256)<\frac7{16}. \tag{15} \]

The norm floors keep K continuous. Thus the majority-coincidence class is absent initially with a margin greater than 1/16, entered during encounter with that margin, and exited before the original endpoint. This is an analytical entry/exit result, not a newly sampled response. Both controls exhibit it, so coincidence acquisition alone fails to discriminate formation. More generally, K_ell<7/16 whenever |256-2*tau|>96+ell. For example, at ell=96 it is excluded at every outgoing checkpoint 224<tau<=256. Choosing a checkpoint strictly below 256 would leave time for a later readout, but coincidence already fails there and stays excluded through 256. No crossing time or behavior at equality is asserted.

docs.title: 6.3 Circular registration and a relative-retention bound
docs.text:
A second observation restricts relative motion without identifying a peak. For any nonzero band y, let

\[ M(y)=\sum_j e^{2\pi i j/N}|y_j|^2. \tag{16} \]

A nonzero norm does not ensure a nonzero M. Here the Fejer reference at center c gives an independent availability argument. Character orthogonality and the adjacent-coefficient autocorrelation imply

\[ M(v_c)=a^2\kappa_Q e^{2\pi i c/N},\qquad \kappa_Q=\frac{\sum_m b_m b_{m+1}}{\sum_m b_m^2} =\frac{2Q^2-2}{2Q^2+1}. \tag{17} \]

The admitted bands avoid wraparound aliases in this adjacent sum. For ||y-v_c||<=a*h, the norm-one diagonal character matrix gives

\[ |M(y)-M(v_c)|\le a^2 h(2+h). \tag{18} \]

When beta=h(2+h)<kappa_Q, the moment stays nonzero and the disk in (18) bounds the angular error by asin(beta/kappa_Q). Define the positional bound delta=N*asin(beta/kappa_Q)/(2*pi). This is a circular first-moment center, not a center of mass or an autonomous collective coordinate. For (11), kappa_16=170/171, beta=6669/62500, and

\[ \frac\beta{\kappa_{16}}<\frac19-\frac1{6\,9^3} \le\sin(1/9),\qquad \delta<\frac{1024}{18\pi}<19. \tag{19} \]

Each actual center can be lifted continuously within delta of its own reference 128-tau or -128+tau. Since 256+2*delta<512, their signed relative center s has a single continuous principal branch and

\[ |s(\tau)-(256-2\tau)|\le2\delta. \tag{20} \]

If s stays in any fixed real interval of width W throughout [t_0,t_1], subtracting its endpoint bounds proves

\[ t_1-t_0\le\frac W2+2\delta<\frac W2+38. \tag{21} \]

This allows common translation, deformation and relative oscillation inside the interval. It excludes only longer confinement of this observed relation; it does not bound instantaneous velocity or every possible relative identity. The reference passage traverses an interval of width W in time W/2. Equation (21) limits extra residence without assuming a relative force law.

docs.title: 6.4 Exclusion at the preexisting localization scale
docs.text:
The same result also tests a capture class using the existing radius 96 and fraction 24/25: both bands would have to place at least 24/25 of their squared norms inside one common radius-96 ball. This allows arbitrary common centers and deformed profiles.

For a band with fraction at least 1-f in a radius-r ball, r<N/4, put alpha=2*pi*r/N. Its core moment lies in the angular cone [-alpha,alpha] about that ball's center, with magnitude at least (1-f)*||y||^2*cos(alpha). The tail moment has magnitude at most f*||y||^2. If f/[(1-f)*cos(alpha)]<1, the observed center is consequently within

\[ r+\frac N{2\pi}\arcsin\frac f{(1-f)\cos\alpha} \tag{22} \]

of the ball center. For r=96,f=1/25, alpha=3*pi/16, cos(alpha)>4/5 and 5/96<sin(1/18), so the second term is less than 10 sites. Two bands in that common ball would therefore have center separation less than 212. But (20) makes the actual separation greater than 218 both initially and at tau=256. The common-ball class is excluded at those times. At tau=128 the original joint band-tail certificate puts both bands in the same radius-96 ball with fraction greater than 24/25; the actual damped linear control also satisfies that certificate, since its template error is smaller. Entry alone again cannot identify a new organization.

Conclusion and scope. Persistent majority coincidence at the outgoing checkpoints in (15), prolonged relative confinement forbidden by (21), and common-ball capture through tau=256 at the preexisting width/fraction are excluded for the original source family. These are failures of necessary conditions, not merely unsuccessful sufficient certificates. They leave open shorter-lived organizations during encounter, wider or two-lobed structures, internal phase/response identities, and reorganizations for which the old bands no longer define the relevant relation. No full composite identity, retention mechanism or discriminating continued response is established. The nominal nonlinear interaction remains valid alongside these exclusions.

docs.title: 7. The actual relative rate and its missing internal information
7.1 Differentiate the observation under both complete rows
docs.text:
The position bound (20) alone cannot bound a velocity: a small positional error may oscillate rapidly. Instead differentiate the actual observation under (1). With z=x+i*theta, the exact two-real-channel field is

\[ z'=iAz-\frac\sigma2 A(z+\bar z)+R(\theta),\qquad R(\theta)=-\frac12D^T[\sin(D\theta)-D\theta]. \tag{23} \]

The conjugate term retains the form-only loss. Dropping it would replace the actual positive-loss law by a complex-linear model. Since the opposite projectors satisfy P_+bar(z)=bar(P_-z) and commute with A, their exact rows are

\[ f'=iAf-\frac\sigma2 A(f+\bar g)+P_+R,\qquad g'=iAg-\frac\sigma2 A(g+\bar f)+P_-R. \tag{24} \]

These are observed rates with the full state retained, not autonomous band equations: R consumes the actual primitive phase, including omitted modes. Define the real-linear directional derivative

\[ \mathcal D_y(v)=\sum_j\chi_j(\bar y_jv_j+y_j\bar v_j), \qquad \chi_j=e^{2\pi i j/N}. \tag{25} \]

For M(y)!=0 and a continuous center lift,

\[ M(y)'=\mathcal D_y(y'),\qquad c_y'=\frac N{2\pi}\operatorname{Im}\frac{\mathcal D_y(y')}{M(y)}, \qquad s'=c_f'-c_g'. \tag{26} \]

The character chi is complex. Replacing (25) by twice a real part outside the sum would incorrectly force the moment derivative to be real. Its real linearity permits a conservative, dissipative and nonlinear contribution to (26), each evaluated at the same actual state. The nonlinear contribution compares the full field with its actual damped tangent at that state. It is not the difference between observed velocities on the nonlinear trajectory and U(tau)u, whose states and moment denominators generally differ. Similarly, the curve z_A+z_B has remainder R(theta_A)+R(theta_B); evaluating the joint field on that sum would instead use R(theta_A+theta_B). The following rate certificate concerns the actual joint flow only, even though its geometric majorants also cover the passage controls.

docs.title: 7.2 Adjacent frequencies control transport without a large carrier error
docs.text:
Use the unitary discrete Fourier transform and lambda_k=1-cos(2*pi*k/N). For either projected band y, the conservative part of its moment derivative is exactly

\[ \mathcal D_y(iAy)=i\sum_k(\lambda_k-\lambda_{k+1}) \widehat y_k\overline{\widehat y_{k+1}}. \tag{27} \]

Only adjacent modes with both coefficients present contribute. In B_+, write k=N/4+m, with -Q+1<=m<=Q-2, and put Delta=pi/N. Then

\[ \lambda_k-\lambda_{k+1} =-2\sin\Delta\cos((2m+1)\Delta),\qquad v_m=\frac{\sin\Delta}{\Delta}\cos((2m+1)\Delta). \tag{28} \]

The sign reverses on B_-. Thus the carrier frequency cancels before the estimate. Since |2m+1|<=2Q-3, elementary sine/cosine inequalities give

\[ |1-v_m|\le\left[\frac16+\frac{(2Q-3)^2}{2}\right]\Delta^2. \tag{29} \]

Also sum_k |yhat_k||yhat_{k+1}|<=||y||^2, by Cauchy--Schwarz. Equations (26)--(29) compare the two conservative center rates with -1 and +1 without treating a reference trajectory as the actual motion.

Let h be an admitted common band-template error, U=1+h, and m_0=kappa_Q-h(2+h)>0. The previous moment argument gives ||f||,||g||<=a*U and |M(f)|,|M(g)|>=a^2*m_0. Bounds on the three rate contributions, per center, are

\[ C=\left[\frac16+\frac{(2Q-3)^2}{2}\right] \left(\frac\pi N\right)^2\frac{U^2}{m_0},\qquad D=2N\frac e w\frac{U^2}{m_0},\qquad V=\frac{32N}{3\pi}a^2\frac U{m_0}. \tag{30} \]

Here C bounds the conservative deviation from the indicated unit speed. For D, use both band norms in ||A(f+bar(g))||<=2(||f||+||g||) and |D_y(v)|<=2||y||||v||. The clock coefficient sigma=pi*e/w cancels the pi in (26); the conjugate-band loss term is not discarded. For V, the joint bootstrap ||z||<2a and ||R||<=(4/3)||theta||^3 give ||R||<(32/3)*a^3. Neither the sharper cubic-response radii nor an evaluated response are needed. V bounds the magnitude of a nonlinear contribution; it does not determine its sign.

docs.title: 7.3 Uniform strict passage of the original source family
docs.text:
Use the original inputs and the already admitted h=13/250. Direct rational inequalities give U^2/m_0<5/4, U/m_0<6/5. With (pi/1024)^2<1/106000, 1024*e/w<1/1000 and pi>3, (30) yields

\[ C<\frac1{200},\qquad D<\frac1{400},\qquad V<\frac1{3840},\qquad C+D+V<\frac{149}{19200}<\frac1{100}. \tag{31} \]

The nonzero moments and the continuous relative branch were proved throughout [0,256] for every original preparation. Consequently, on that whole interval,

\[ |c_f'+1|<\frac1{100},\qquad |c_g'-1|<\frac1{100},\qquad |s'+2|<\frac1{50},\qquad -\frac{101}{50}<s'<-\frac{99}{50}. \tag{32} \]

This is an instantaneous-rate theorem, not a derivative inferred from a position tube or a numerical trajectory. The observed relative center cannot stop, reverse or remain fixed for a positive interval. Since its initial value is positive and its endpoint value negative by (20), the two registered centers coincide exactly once in this interval. This does not assert that every coincidence observable crosses its threshold only once.

Integrating the strict negative rate strengthens (21): residence of s in a fixed interval of width W lasts at most 50*W/99. This is a restriction on the declared relative coordinate, allowing deformed profiles. It does not exclude every internal, wider or shorter-lived common identity. Neither the rate bound nor nonzero-moment availability is extended beyond tau=256.

docs.title: 7.4 Equal observed geometry can have a different nonlinear rate
docs.text:
The geometry still does not supply a generally autonomous rate law. The following exact static counterexample uses the same complete positive-loss law on C_12, with Q=2, B_+={2,3,4} and B_-={8,9,10}. It is not a member of the original C1024 source family and makes no claim about closure restricted to that family.

Choose 0<q<pi/4, for example q=1/16, and set

\[ u_j=q[\cos(\pi j/3)+\cos(\pi j/2)],\qquad Z_F=u\ (x=u,\theta=0),\quad Z_P=iu\ (x=0,\theta=u). \tag{33} \]

Both have zero means and squared norm 12*q^2; the phase-only state's largest edge gap is 2q<pi/2. They can be arbitrarily small. Multiplication by i preserves every band intensity pointwise, hence both band norms, every K_ell, both moments and both observed centers agree. Direct character sums give M_+=M_-=3*q^2>0, so both states have the same regular local relative center s=0. Multiplication by i here changes the allocation between form and primitive phase; it is not a symmetry of the complete law.

At the form-only state, the actual field is (-sigma+i)Au, and

\[ M_\pm'=\frac{3q^2}{2}(-3\sigma\mp i),\qquad s_F'=-\frac6\pi. \tag{34} \]

At the phase-only state, the field is the real vector F=S(u)/2. For this finite sum write tilde for 1/N Fourier coefficients, so Fhat_k=sqrt(12)*Ftilde_k; the profile has utilde_k=q/2 at modes 2, 3, 9, 10. Its two relevant field coefficients and the adjacent zero coefficient are

\[ \widetilde F_2=\frac{\sin(q/2)-\sin(2q)-\sin(3q/2)}{12},\qquad \widetilde F_3=-\frac{2\sin(q/2)+\sin(2q)+2\sin(3q/2)}{12},\qquad \widetilde F_4=0. \tag{35} \]

Substitution in (25), or direct sums in site coordinates, gives

\[ M_\pm'=\mp\frac{iq}{2}[3\sin(q/2)+\sin(3q/2)],\qquad s_P'=-\frac{6\sin(q/2)+2\sin(3q/2)}{\pi q}. \tag{36} \]

Since sin(t)<t for positive t,

\[ s_P'-s_F'=\frac2{\pi q}[3q-3\sin(q/2)-\sin(3q/2)]>0. \tag{37} \]

The actual damped tangent evaluated at either state gives s'=-6/pi. Thus the form-only state has zero nonlinear correction, whereas the phase-only state has the strictly positive correction (37). Equal observed geometry does not determine even this nonlinear contribution: the lost form/phase allocation is consumed by the sine pressure. Both displayed rates remain negative in the chosen small domain. The positive correction slows passage; it establishes neither a restoring force nor retention at s=0.

Scope of the completed rate question. The original source family has strict one-pass relative motion over the admitted interval, while a general instantaneous rate law based only on the band intensities/centers fails the projectability test. The two statements have different source/support scope and are compatible. Neither supplies a full NFR identity, a physical force or a new constitutive law. Any further retention claim needs an independently justified internal relation and complete-state or memory treatment of the information it consumes.

The retention-mechanism owner examines that boundary: supplied reflection and the uncoupled period-four energies do not establish formation. A different on-grid carrier admits a cubic focusing comparison, with separate source, residual and maintenance obligations. It does not alter the original family's passage theorem.

docs.title: 8. Shared arithmetic and controls
docs.text:
The private _bound_cycle_consensus_basin reader in the transport owner re-admits the complete positive-loss model, cycle size and independent initial norm bound before computing (2)--(5). A failed strict bound yields unavailable sufficiency; it is not a verdict about an evaluated state or finite formation. Existing finite transport/source reports and their schemas remain separate.

The geometry controls check the actual storage derivative and clock, independent source bounds, strict admission boundaries, the low-storage winding counterexample and the period-four reduction from direct neighbor rows. They do not execute a trajectory or replay the frozen response producer. The proof and source premises, rather than a passing diagnostic score, establish the conditional all-time claim.

The private _bound_localized_mobile_geometry reader in the mobile budget owner rebuilds the preparation budgets from fresh primitives. It bounds the shared three-history error, band norms, tails, first moments and relative registration with outward arithmetic. Moment, branch and proximity availability remain separate; no old identity or cubic-response verdict is treated as a premise. The relative-geometry controls exercise independent coefficient/moment identities, pair-weight geometry, lossy observations, arithmetic boundaries and incompatible inputs. The reader evaluates neither K on a trajectory nor a formation verdict, and preserves the existing response-budget schema and frozen evidence.

The same owner's _bound_localized_mobile_relative_rate rebuilds those geometric bounds before using (30). It exposes the conservative deviation, dissipative correction and nonlinear correction separately. Band-rate availability, a continuous principal relative branch and a certified strictly negative relative rate are distinct; failure of the last condition does not prove reversal. The rate controls derive the moment differentiation, conjugate-band rows, adjacent-frequency bound and C12 counterexample independently. No state reader, FFT execution path or new integrator is installed. The rate certificate is for the actual joint flow; the other histories' geometric bounds do not transfer their rates.

docs.title: Retention mechanisms and the complete-law envelope boundary
docs.text: Scope: mechanism admission and one local finite-input variational evaluation under the existing positive-loss cycle law. Exact balances and cubic coefficient identities are proved below; envelope profiles solve an auxiliary modulation equation. A full-state residual theorem and a relative-storage comparison specify how to validate such a reference against the actual law, retaining near resonances. The first correction panel is evaluated in section 17; the full horizon, nonlinear envelope maintenance and interaction-generated composites remain unproved. The original source and strict-passage result remain unchanged. The research program alone selects further work and owns reactivation of the deferred variational dependency.

docs.title: 1. Retained law and internal relations
docs.text:
Keep the complete two-row model: signed real form x, a continuous real phase lift theta, unit cycle conductances and lengths, held unit capacities, beta one, no input or events, and the clock tau=w*t/pi. For e,w>0, sigma=pi*e/w, A=L/2,

\[ x'=-\sigma Ax-\tfrac12D^T\sin(D\theta),\qquad \theta'=Ax. \tag{1} \]

Writing z=x+i*theta retains two real channels. It gives

\[ z'=F_\sigma(z)=iAz-\sigma A\operatorname{Re}z+R(\operatorname{Im}z), \quad R(\theta)=-\tfrac12D^T[\sin(D\theta)-D\theta]. \tag{2} \]

This is neither complex EPI nor an identification with a quantum state. The actual positive-loss tangent J_sigma has the existing contractive Euclidean semigroup. A proposed envelope is an approximate full-state history, not an invariant subspace or a replacement for either row.

docs.title: Supplied symmetry does not establish acquisition
docs.text:
Reflection Jz(j)=z(-j) commutes with (1). The original nominal joint preparation is reflection symmetric, so that relation is preserved exactly. The same-source linear control also preserves it. The relation is supplied initially and does not discriminate a newly formed organization.

For primitive errors of norm at most epsilon each, the initial antisymmetric part has norm at most 2*epsilon. Within the original joint norm bootstrap ||z||,||Jz||<2a, the shared derivative estimate ||DR||<=4S^2 with S=2a gives

\[ \left\|\frac{z(\tau)-Jz(\tau)}2\right\| \le 2\epsilon\exp(16a^2\tau). \tag{3} \]

This robust retention is still retention of a prepared symmetry. It cannot replace initial absence and discriminating acquisition in the formation contract.

The exact period-four family reduces to independent damped pendula u and v. With E_u=u'^2/2+1-cos(u) and similarly for v,

\[ H=\frac N2(E_u+E_v),\qquad E_u'=-\sigma u'^2,\quad E_v'=-\sigma v'^2. \tag{4} \]

There is no transfer term between these two modal energies. For any pendulum solution q and nonnegative time shift delta, u(tau)=q(tau) and v(tau)=q(tau+delta) give an exact pair. Such a relative registration can be supplied; these equations do not select it through mutual exchange. Decay toward zero also destroys an oscillation's phase observability. Localized modulation and its boundary cannot be removed by invoking this reduction.

docs.title: 2. What can accumulate locally under this law?
docs.text:
The regional balance owner requires boundary exchange. Here an exact cycle-specific expression makes the consumed phase information explicit. Orient cycle edges consistently, put y=Dx, u=Dtheta, and let edge indices j and k be neighbors on the edge cycle. Their rows are

\[ y'=-\tfrac\sigma2 L_e y-\tfrac12L_e\sin u,\qquad u'=\tfrac12L_e y,\qquad L_e=DD^T. \tag{5} \]

For h_j=y_j^2/2+1-cos(u_j), define

\[ F_{jk}=\tfrac12(\sin u_j\,y_k-y_j\sin u_k) +\tfrac\sigma4(y_j^2-y_k^2)=-F_{kj}. \] \[ h_j'=-\sum_{k\sim j}F_{jk} -\tfrac\sigma4\sum_{k\sim j}(y_j-y_k)^2. \tag{6} \]

Direct differentiation of h and substitution of (5) prove (6). Summing over all edges recovers H'=-(sigma/2)||Lx||^2. On a fixed subset, internal currents cancel; an increase requires inward boundary current to exceed local dissipation. Form gaps and sine phase gaps determine that current, so intensities or centers alone cannot infer it. Positive total loss does not exclude transient regional accumulation. Conversely, positive inflow does not prove retention or select a boundary. Moving membership requires its separate transport accounting; (6) is for fixed sets.

docs.title: 3. The cubic balance selects a different candidate regime
docs.text:
Let an on-grid carrier satisfy kN in 2*pi*Z, and write

\[ \lambda=1-\cos k,\quad v=\sin k,\quad d=\tfrac12\cos k, \quad g=\lambda^2/8,\quad h_3=\frac{\sin^3(k/2)\sin(3k/2)}6,\quad \lambda_3=1-\cos(3k). \tag{7} \]

Use a positive bookkeeping scale varepsilon, distinct from the original source error epsilon, and slow variables X=varepsilon*(j+v*tau), S=varepsilon^2*tau, phi=kj+lambda*tau. The candidate carrier travels with site velocity -v.

docs.title: Exact cubic harmonics and a two-channel reconstruction
docs.text:
The cubic part of R is R_3(theta)=D^T(Dtheta)^3/12. At locally constant B, substituting theta=Im(B*exp(i*phi)) gives exactly

\[ R_3=-ig|B|^2B e^{i\phi}+ig|B|^2\overline B e^{-i\phi} -ih_3B^3e^{3i\phi}+ih_3\overline B^3e^{-3i\phi}. \tag{8} \]

For example, a forward phase gap has coefficient (exp(ik)-1)B/(2i); cubing and applying the backward incidence row gives all four terms. Keeping only the resonant first term would discard an actual part of the form row.

Cancellation through cubic order uses the auxiliary equation

\[ iB_S=d B_{XX}+g|B|^2B \tag{9} \]

and the full reconstruction

\[ z_{\rm app}=\varepsilon B e^{i\phi}+\varepsilon^3 C, \quad C=a_{-1}|B|^2\overline B e^{-i\phi} +a_3B^3e^{3i\phi}+a_{-3}\overline B^3e^{-3i\phi}, \tag{10} \] \[ a_{-1}=-\lambda/16,\qquad a_3=-\frac{h_3}{3\lambda-\lambda_3},\qquad a_{-3}=-\frac{h_3}{3\lambda+\lambda_3}. \tag{11} \]

Require lambda>0 and nonzero displayed denominators. The operator partial_tau-iA multiplies a constant harmonic exp(i*l*phi) by i*(l*lambda-lambda(l*k)); (11) cancels the three nonresonant terms of (8). Envelope derivative errors remain and are bounded in section 5. Both real coordinates are reconstructed as x_app=Re(z_app), theta_app=Im(z_app); neither row is declared exact by (9).

The carrier k=pi/4 is already mode 128 of the unchanged C_1024 support. It has positive curvature and no third-harmonic resonance:

\[ \lambda=1-\frac{\sqrt2}2,\quad d=\frac{\sqrt2}4,\quad g=\frac{3-2\sqrt2}{16},\quad h_3=\frac{\sqrt2-1}{48}, \] \[ (a_{-1},a_3,a_{-3})= \left(-\frac{2-\sqrt2}{32},\frac1{96}, -\frac{3\sqrt2-2}{672}\right). \tag{12} \]

This is an analytical candidate, not a searched optimum. For general k, third-harmonic resonance and spatial aliases must be checked; spatially aliased terms can still have distinct temporal frequencies.

docs.title: The actual damping does not disappear
docs.text:
Equation (9) is a conservative comparison equation. All actual damping can be retained in the residual of (10), as in section 5. Alternatively, writing gamma=sigma/varepsilon^2 yields the leading damped modulation

\[ iB_S=dB_{XX}+g|B|^2B-i\frac{\gamma\lambda}{2}B. \tag{13} \]

Its counterrotating damping corrector is -i*gamma*conj(B)*exp(-i*phi)/4. This follows by multiplying its coefficient by -2i*lambda, giving the omitted damping coefficient -gamma*lambda*conj(B)/2. For a periodic envelope, d/dS integral |B|^2=-gamma*lambda*integral |B|^2 under (13). Fixed positive sigma therefore cannot be suppressed in a varepsilon -> 0 limit or replaced with zero to certify a desired profile. The residual bound below applies to the conservative reference (9)--(11); using (13) and its additional corrector requires redoing that bound.

docs.title: 4. Which relation can the auxiliary balance maintain?
docs.text:
For d,g>0, (9) admits the exact line profile

\[ B(X,S)=\rho\operatorname{sech}(X/L)e^{-i\Omega S},\qquad \rho^2L^2=\frac{2d}{g}=\frac{8\cos k}{\lambda^2},\qquad \Omega=\frac d{L^2}=\frac{g\rho^2}{2}. \tag{14} \]

This follows from sech''=sech-2*sech^3. The relation locks the envelope shape, height, width and slow internal phase in the comparison equation; the corresponding carrier frequency is lambda-varepsilon^2*Omega. It is not a freely chosen stationary shape of the original nodal law.

The sign restriction is substantive. For a smooth real decaying profile f, d*f''+g*f^3=Omega*f has first integral d*f'^2/2=Omega*f^2/2-g*f^4/4. Exponential decay requires Omega/d>0, and a nonzero turning amplitude requires Omega>0. Thus this bright-profile balance requires d>0. At the original k=pi/2, d vanishes and this quadratic-dispersion mechanism is unavailable. This does not exclude every higher-order modulation or nonperturbative mechanism at that carrier.

docs.title: Periodic references and the source scale
docs.text:
The line sech cannot be sampled across a cycle seam and treated as a smooth periodic solution. An exact periodic alternative of (9), with kappa and rho strictly positive, is defined by

\[ B=f(X)e^{-i\Omega S},\quad f''=\kappa^2(2-m)f-\frac{2\kappa^2}{\rho^2}f^3,\quad f(0)=\rho,\quad f'(0)=0, \] \[ 0<m<1,\quad \rho^2=2d\kappa^2/g,\quad \Omega=d\kappa^2(2-m),\quad (f')^2=\frac{\kappa^2}{\rho^2} (\rho^2-f^2)(f^2-\rho^2(1-m)). \tag{15} \]

The solution oscillates smoothly between rho*sqrt(1-m) and rho. Separation of variables gives period 2K(m)/kappa, where K(m)=integral_0^(pi/2) (1-m*sin(u)^2)^(-1/2) du. Choose that period to equal varepsilon*N; this supplies a genuinely periodic reference with one maximum per cycle. Its trough, concentration, derivative bounds and error allowance still need a quantitative admission. No value of m, width, horizon or source tolerance has been evaluated here. For fixed N and m, that period condition fixes the site-scale height varepsilon*rho=2*K(m)*sqrt(2*d/g)/N and inverse width varepsilon*kappa=2*K(m)/N. Changing varepsilon alone only reparametrizes this reference; the derivative bounds change with it. It is not a free parameter for reducing the physical residual on fixed support.

The line-profile scale already explains why the original small preparation cannot simply be renamed. Write physical site width ell=L/varepsilon and height b=varepsilon*rho; (14) implies

\[ b\ell=K_*:=\frac{\sqrt{8\cos k}}{\lambda},\qquad K_*>8 \quad\hbox{at }k=\pi/4. \tag{16} \]

For the literal sampled sech with integer center and 1<=ell<=N/4, at least ell sites have distance at most ell. Since sech(1)^2>1/4, its norm squared exceeds b^2*ell/4>=K_*^2/N. On C_1024 its norm therefore exceeds 1/4, whereas the entire original joint tube has norm below 1/2048. This is a scale incompatibility of this particular reference; it is not a theorem excluding all small nonlinear localized states. The full corrected periodic reference must have its own source admission.

docs.title: A single retained envelope is not capture of two incoming patterns
docs.text:
For patterns to remain within a common width O(varepsilon^-1) over a slow interval O(varepsilon^-2), their leading group velocities must differ by at most O(varepsilon), unless a different, nonperturbative mechanism changes them. Near pi/4, nonzero cosine makes this require carrier separation O(varepsilon). Replacing the original carriers with +/-pi/4 still leaves velocity difference sqrt(2): focusing alone does not capture that counterpropagating pair. Distant carriers can share a velocity; they require a separately derived multiple-envelope system. The equal-velocity carrier control derives the local cubic channels for pi/4 and 3*pi/4, retaining temporal labels within spatial aliases. Its modulation restrictions do not provide a full-law formation or maintenance certificate.

A prepared profile satisfying (14) or (15) already contains its phase/shape relation. Even successful full-law maintenance would not establish its acquisition from two initially independent patterns. That claim additionally needs initial absence, a compatible relative preparation, retained boundary state, entry and a discriminating continued response under the same law.

docs.title: 5. An explicit conditional bridge to the complete law
docs.text:
Here is a sufficient finite-time validation method, rather than an appeal to a formal asymptotic symbol. Let B solve (9), be periodic in X with period varepsilon*N, and have continuous bounded derivatives through order three in X and order one in S on the full proposed slow interval. Define uniform bounds b_j>=sup|partial_X^j B|, j=0,...,3, and b_S=|d|*b_2+g*b_0^3>=sup|B_S|. All bounds include intervening X values, not just graph samples. Put

\[ A_0=|a_{-1}|+|a_3|+|a_{-3}|,\qquad A_1=\sum_{l\in\{-1,3,-3\}}|a_l|\,|v-\sin(lk)|, \quad D_k=|1-e^{ik}|, \] \[ G=\varepsilon(D_kb_0+\varepsilon b_1) +2\varepsilon^3 A_0b_0^3. \tag{17} \]

Every phase gap of (10) has magnitude at most G. For r_app=z_app'-F_sigma(z_app), a uniform per-site bound is

\[ \begin{aligned} r_*={}&\varepsilon^4\left[ \frac{b_3}{6}+3A_1b_0^2b_1 +\frac{b_1}{2}(D_kb_0+\varepsilon b_1)^2\right]\\ &+\varepsilon^5 A_0\left[3b_0^2b_S+3b_0b_1^2 +\frac32b_0^2b_2\right]\\ &+\varepsilon^3 A_0b_0^3G^2+\frac{G^5}{120} +2\sigma(\varepsilon b_0+\varepsilon^3 A_0b_0^3), \qquad \|r_{\rm app}\|_2\le\sqrt N\,r_* . \tag{18} \end{aligned} \]

The terms have separate derivations:

  • Taylor expansion of the leading nearest-neighbor row leaves varepsilon^4*b_3/6 after (9). Corrector transport differs from the leading group velocity and is bounded using |partial_X F_l(B)|<=3*b_0^2*b_1.
  • Freezing B in the cubic phase gaps changes each gap by at most varepsilon^2*b_1. The cubic difference inequality supplies the last term in the first bracket.
  • The corrector's slow derivative and second spatial remainder use |partial_S F_l|<=3*b_0^2*b_S and |partial_X^2 F_l|<=6*b_0*b_1^2+3*b_0^2*b_2.
  • Its addition changes each phase gap by at most 2*varepsilon^3*A_0*b_0^3, giving the cubic correction term. The global Taylor inequality |sin(u)-u+u^3/6|<=|u|^5/120 gives the fifth-order term.
  • The final term bounds the entire actual damping row, using the nearest-neighbor bound |A Re(z_app)|<=2*sup|z_app|.

The Euclidean sqrt(N) factor is retained; localization or cancellations cannot silently replace it. The residual is a pair of real-row errors, including the phase row, not a fitted effective pressure.

Let the initial full-state error be at most delta>=0 and propose a strictly positive error radius r and horizon T over 0<=tau<=T. In that radius every actual and intervening phase gap is bounded by G+2r. Since

\[ DR(\theta)=\tfrac12D^T\operatorname{diag}(1-\cos D\theta)D, \qquad \|DR\|\le(G+2r)^2=:L_*, \tag{19} \]

variation of constants under the actual contractive J_sigma and Gronwall give the sufficient bootstrap condition

\[ E_*:=e^{L_*T}\bigl(\delta+T\sqrt N\,r_*\bigr)<r. \tag{20} \]

A first exit at norm r contradicts this estimate, so the full-state error stays at most E_* throughout the interval. A required acute phase chart can be admitted separately by G+2r<pi/2. Reference norm and concentration floors must exceed their error allowances before any retained identity is certified. If (20) fails, this sufficient method is inconclusive; no nonexistence or dynamical instability follows.

This is a conditional theorem with explicit finite constants. It has not been instantiated for a prepared envelope. In particular, at T=S_*/varepsilon^2, the fixed positive sigma contribution must still be evaluated. A formal small residual or a profile of (9) alone cannot certify that window. Using localization-aware norms or a damped reference may improve the method, but each needs its own proved bound.

docs.title: A scoped obstruction to this coarse certificate
docs.text:
For the proposed periodic family (15), one can decide a limitation without selecting a profile or evaluating a response. Fix the actual original law coefficients e=2^-20, w=1-e, so sigma=pi/(2^20-1), retain N=1024, and take k=pi/4. Put b=varepsilon*rho and define one slow internal-phase time by

\[ T_\phi=\frac1{\varepsilon^2\Omega} =\frac2{g b^2(2-m)}. \tag{21} \]

Consider the particular certificate requiring both (20) and the acute-chart condition G+2r<pi/2, with r>0. Since 1/4<lambda<1/3, g<1/72, D_k>1/2 and pi<4, this condition forces r<1 and b<4. Consequently

\[ T_\phi b>\frac1{g b}>18,\qquad T_\phi\sqrt N\,r_*>1152\sigma >\frac{3456}{2^{20}}>\frac1{400}. \tag{22} \]

Here the second inequality uses the actual positive damping term r_*>=2*sigma*b; b_0 is at least the profile maximum rho. Also

\[ L_*T_\phi\ge G^2T_\phi \ge\frac{32}{\lambda(2-m)}>48. \tag{23} \]

Even at zero initial error, the published sufficient majorant therefore obeys

\[ E_*>\frac{1+48+48^2/2}{400} =\frac{1201}{400}>1>r, \tag{24} \]

using exp(u)>=1+u+u^2/2 for nonnegative u. The contradiction persists for any T>=T_phi. Thus this coarse acute-chart certificate cannot validate the periodic conservative reference for a full nonlinear phase time. Changing width, refining source error or increasing arithmetic precision cannot repair this bound within the stated class.

This is a theorem about a sufficient method, not an obstruction to actual nonlinear maintenance. It does not exclude (20) without the additional acute condition, shorter intervals, other reference histories or other error estimates. A structure-sensitive stability argument or an explicitly damped reference with its own residual would change the method's premises. The present calculation does not establish that either alternative succeeds.

The existing moving-reference relative-storage identity is a reusable method for retaining reactive cancellations. Its earlier conservative graph, exact reference and quantitative constants do not transfer here. Positive loss, two-row reference residuals, moving phase curvature and the uncontrolled common means must all be re-admitted before using such storage to bound this full-state error. Relative storage is not automatically decreasing along a moving reference.

docs.title: 6. Relative storage retains the complete error balance
docs.text:
Let (x_*,theta_*) be a differentiable, independently specified reference on the same cycle and clock, with residuals in both actual rows:

\[ r_x=x_*'+\sigma Ax_*+ frac12 abla V( heta_*),\qquad r_ heta= heta_*'-Ax_*,\qquad V( heta)=\sum_e[1-\cos(D heta)_e]. ag{25} \]

Use matched continuous phase lifts, u=x-x_*, eta=theta-theta_*, a=Dtheta_*, b_e=(Deta)_e, and define

\[ \mathcal E= frac12u^TLu+V( heta_*+\eta)-V( heta_*) - abla V( heta_*)^T\eta. \]

Direct differentiation and substitution of both rows give the exact identity

\[ egin{split} \mathcal E'={}&- frac\sigma2\|Lu\|^2 +\sum_e[\sin(a_e+b_e)-\sin a_e-\cos a_e\,b_e]a_e'\ &-u^TLr_x-[ abla V( heta_*+\eta)- abla V( heta_*)]^T r_ heta. ag{26} \end{split} \]

The form/phase exchange cancels. The moving-curvature term does not cancel and has no fixed sign. This extends the earlier moving-pattern identity to the actual positive loss and an approximate reference; it does not transfer that owner's graph, exact reference or constants.

docs.title: Means, coercivity and the retained coordinates
docs.text:
Let P project off the constant nodal vector. All inverse powers of L below act only on its mean-zero subspace. Put

\[ y=(L^{1/2}u,L^{1/2}\eta),\quad U=DL^{-1/2},\quad U^TU=I, \quad \ell_1=4\sin^2(\pi/N). \]

Suppose ||y||<=rho and ||a||_infinity+rho<=chi<pi/2. With kappa=cos(chi)>0, Taylor's integral formula gives

\[ \tfrac\kappa2\|y\|^2\le\mathcal E\le\tfrac12\|y\|^2, \qquad \|(u,\eta)\|^2\le\ell_1^{-1}\|y\|^2 +N(\bar u^2+\bar\eta^2). \tag{27} \]

The missing means have exact independent equations bar(u)'=-bar(r_x), bar(eta)'=-bar(r_theta). They need their initial values and residual integrals. Constant form or phase errors have zero relative storage; neither a full-state estimate nor a zero-mean residual may be inferred from storage alone. The factor ell_1^-1 is the actual finite-cycle coercivity cost, not a carrier-band approximation.

Taylor expansion of the moving term in (26) gives

\[ \mathcal E'=-\tfrac\sigma2\|Lu\|^2+y^TM(\tau)y +\mathcal R_3+\mathcal W_r,\qquad M=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\0&-\tfrac12U^T\operatorname{diag}(\sin a\,a')U\end{pmatrix}, \tag{28} \] \[ |\mathcal R_3|\le\frac{\|a'\|_\infty\rho}{6}\|y\|^2, \qquad |\mathcal W_r|\le\|y\|\mathfrak r,\qquad \mathfrak r=\|(L^{1/2}r_x,L^{1/2}r_\theta)\|. \]

For the second bound, write the sine difference as t_e b_e, where t_e=int_0^1 cos(a_e+s*b_e) ds and |t_e|<=1, and apply Cauchy--Schwarz to the two residual rows together. No pressure is reconstructed from a response and no error mode is discarded.

docs.title: 7. A conditional comparison that retains near resonances
docs.text:
There is a precise alternative to taking the absolute value of all of M before integration. Define the skew principal tangent on the mean-zero coordinates by

\[ J_0=\begin{pmatrix}0&-A\\A&0\end{pmatrix}. \]

This is a comparison operator inside the proof. Actual damping stays in (26) and in the error equation; the physical law is still (1).

For the reconstruction (10), its leading edge wave can be written a_0=Im(c(tau)*exp(i*lambda*tau)), where c is the complex edge amplitude obtained by applying D to varepsilon*B(X,S)*exp(i*k*j). Its coefficients vary with the envelope. With omega=2*lambda, set

\[ H=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\0&\frac{i\lambda}{4} U^T\operatorname{diag}(c^2)U\end{pmatrix},\qquad M_{\rm fast}=\operatorname{Re}(e^{i\omega\tau}H). \tag{29} \]

Indeed -(a_0*a'_{0,fast})/2=Re(i*lambda*c^2*exp(2i*lambda*tau)/4). All envelope derivatives, generated harmonics and the difference between sine and its argument remain in M-M_fast. This is an exact decomposition of (28), not a declaration that its remainder vanishes.

docs.title: The finite-dimensional homological equation
docs.text:
Choose an orthonormal complex eigenbasis J_0 v_alpha=i*mu_alpha*v_alpha, with all nonconstant cycle modes and both frequency signs. For a complex symmetric matrix H use the congruence coefficients Hhat_alpha,beta=v_alpha^T H v_beta. The transpose is intentional: these are quadratic forms, not Hermitian expectation values. The congruence preserves the Frobenius norm. On these coefficients the operator i*omega*C+J_0^T*C+C*J_0 has divisor i*(omega+mu_alpha+mu_beta).

Fix a positive threshold Delta before any bound evaluation. Retain every entry with |omega+mu_alpha+mu_beta|<=Delta in H_near, including zero divisors. Let H_far=H-H_near, and define the symmetric matrix C by

\[ \widehat C_{\alpha\beta}= \begin{cases} -2\widehat H_{\alpha\beta}/[i(\omega+\mu_\alpha+\mu_\beta)], &|\omega+\mu_\alpha+\mu_\beta|>\Delta,\\ 0,&\text{otherwise}. \end{cases} \tag{30} \]

Reconstruct C by inverse congruence and set K=Re(exp(i*omega*tau)*C). The matrices K and Re(exp(i*omega*tau)*C') are real symmetric. Direct differentiation, with the same fixed spectral split, proves

\[ K'+J_0^TK+KJ_0=-2\operatorname{Re}(e^{i\omega\tau}H_{\rm far}) +\operatorname{Re}(e^{i\omega\tau}C'). \tag{31} \]

In particular, conservative sufficient bounds are

\[ \|K\|_2\le 2\|H_{\rm far}\|_F/\Delta,\qquad \|\operatorname{Re}(e^{i\omega\tau}C')\|_2 \le2\|H'_{\rm far}\|_F/\Delta. \tag{32} \]

Actual operator-norm bounds may be sharper. A changing cutoff would add terms not covered by (31). The split does not delete perturbations: near entries remain in M_ret=M-M_fast+Re(exp(i*omega*tau)*H_near).

docs.title: Positive metric, actual loss and a full-state bootstrap
docs.text:
On a prospective interval admit uniform bounds

\[ \|K\|_2\le k_*<\kappa,\quad \|M_{\rm ret}\|_2\le m_*,\quad \|\operatorname{Re}(e^{i\omega\tau}C')\|_2\le d_*,\quad \|a'\|_\infty\le a_*. \]

Define E_c=E+y^T K y/2. Equations (27) and (31) imply

\[ \frac{\kappa-k_*}{2}\|y\|^2\le E_c \le\frac{1+k_*}{2}\|y\|^2. \tag{33} \]

For completeness, the exact error equation in these coordinates is y'=J_0*y+f_sigma+f_nl-rhat, with ||f_sigma||<=2*sigma*||y|| and ||f_nl||<=chi^2*||y||. The latter follows from sin(a+b)-sin(a)-b=(int_0^1 cos(a+s*b) ds-1)*b, ||L^(1/2)D^T||=4, and 1-cos(q)<=chi^2/2 in the admitted chart. Here rhat=(L^(1/2)r_x,L^(1/2)r_theta); it is not an additional forcing law.

Substitution in the derivative of E_c proves

\[ E_c'\le-\tfrac\sigma2\|Lu\|^2+c_*\|y\|^2 +(1+k_*)\|y\|\mathfrak r,\qquad c_*=m_*+\tfrac12d_*+k_*(2\sigma+\chi^2)+a_*\rho/6. \tag{34} \]

Thus q=sqrt(2*E_c) has the comparison majorant

\[ q(\tau)\le Q(\tau):=e^{\alpha\tau} \left[\sqrt{1+k_*}\|y(0)\| +\frac{1+k_*}{\sqrt{\kappa-k_*}} \int_0^\tau e^{-\alpha s}\mathfrak r(s)\,ds\right], \qquad \alpha=\frac{c_*}{\kappa-k_*}. \tag{35} \]

At zeros of E_c use a regularized square root and pass to the limit. If the initial chart holds and Q(T)<rho*sqrt(kappa-k_*), a first exit from ||y||<rho contradicts (33)--(35). Equations (27) and the independently integrated means then control the complete nodal error. This is a conditional theorem; every bound is uniform over the declared interval and source ball. Small residuals alone do not supply k_*<kappa or that bootstrap.

Actual positive damping has not been removed: (34) retains its negative storage production and bounds its interaction with K explicitly. A better use of the negative term requires an additional proved estimate. A damped envelope reference also needs its own residual under (25). Neither is supplied by selecting a cutoff. The bound improves on (20) only when its admitted constants and full-state margins demonstrate that improvement.

docs.title: 8. Which curvature terms cannot be averaged away?
docs.text: Two exact coefficient calculations delimit the preceding construction. They concern the frozen leading carrier in the homological equation, not a solved localized reference. They are not trajectory observations.

docs.title: The carrier block has a nonzero resonant source
docs.text:
Temporarily write the leading reference as theta_*=b*sin(phi_j), phi_j=k*j+lambda*tau, with real amplitude b, and take a same-carrier error z-z_*=(alpha+i*beta)*exp(i*phi_j). This complex notation still represents two real errors. Exact spatial summation on C1024 at k=pi/4 gives

\[ \mathcal E_0=N\lambda(\alpha^2+\beta^2),\qquad \left\langle-\tfrac12\sum_e a_ea_e' b_e^2\right\rangle =-\tfrac N2\lambda^3 b^2\alpha\beta. \tag{36} \]

The brackets denote the principal fast average, with frozen error quadratures, not averaging an evaluated nonlinear response. The term can have either sign. Its homological divisor is zero: 2*lambda-lambda-lambda=0. A bounded periodic quadratic correction cannot have a nonzero constant derivative along this periodic principal motion. Therefore this source cannot be removed by such a correction.

Its maximum magnitude relative to E_0 is 2*g*b^2. In the conservative auxiliary envelope's carrier-rotating frame, linearization about constant amplitude gives alpha'=0, beta'=-2*g*b^2*alpha in the fast clock at this order: amplitude error changes the phase rate. The resulting shear has linear-in-time entries, not an exponential-instability proof. Over the formal phase time (21), the Euclidean logarithmic-norm bound for this auxiliary shear has exponent g*b^2*T_phi=2/(2-m), of order one. This coefficient calculation does not bound all other modes or certify the localized envelope. In particular, the actual loss, spatial modulation and residual remain in (34)--(35).

docs.title: Adjacent modes invalidate an exact-resonances-only shortcut
docs.text:
For distinct modes q=k+h, r=k-h, the principal divisor is exactly

\[ \delta_h=\lambda(q)+\lambda(r)-2\lambda =2\cos k(1-\cos h),\qquad h=2\pi/N. \tag{37} \]

It is nonzero but small. Use unitary Fourier coefficients z_q,z_r, d_q the incidence symbol with |d_q|^2=2*lambda(q), and A_b=|d_k|*b. Put P_qr=d_q*d_r*z_q*z_r*exp(-2i*(lambda*tau+arg(d_k))). The principal moving production on this pair is -A_b^2*lambda*Im(P_qr)/8; along J_0, P_qr'=i*delta_h*P_qr. Consequently its compulsory zero-homogeneous correction is

\[ \mathcal Q_{qr}=-\frac{A_b^2\lambda}{8\delta_h} \operatorname{Re}P_{qr},\qquad \sup_{(z_q,z_r)\ne(0,0)} \frac{|\mathcal Q_{qr}|}{\lambda(q)|z_q|^2+\lambda(r)|z_r|^2} =\frac{2g b^2}{|\delta_h|}. \tag{38} \]

The supremum is over nonzero pair errors; equality uses equal weighted modal magnitudes and the appropriate relative phase. For the amplitude scale imposed by periodic family (15), this ratio is

\[ R_h=\frac{2K(m)^2}{N^2\sin^2(\pi/N)}. \tag{39} \]

It exceeds one half even as m tends to zero. Shrinking the bookkeeping varepsilon at fixed physical profile cannot make it vanish. The continuous elliptic integral K increases from pi/2 to infinity, so the class contains an amplitude with K(m)=pi. For that analytic witness R_h>2, while b=2*pi*sqrt(2d/g)/1024<1/16 because sqrt(2d/g)<9 and pi<7/2. Its leading phase gaps are small. Yet the canonical principal correction has a direction below -2*E_0. The relative-storage Hessian itself is at most E_0 since cos(a)<=1; adding this correction loses positivity.

This is a scoped obstruction to eliminating all nonzero divisors around J_0 while retaining only exact resonances with a small correction over that frozen-carrier amplitude class. It does not exclude (30), which can retain these adjacent modes, or all positive time-dependent metrics. Adding a large homogeneous metric changes the normalization and its error bounds. Including the slow phase rate or loss in a different inverse changes the divisors and requires a separate calculation. The actual localized envelope has spatially varying coefficients and additional couplings; (39) is not a nonexistence or instability theorem for it.

docs.title: 9. The spatially varying periodic reference has explicit finite bounds
docs.text: The following calculation applies to the whole periodic family (15), not its frozen carrier. Fix the analytical rule Delta=lambda/2 for (30). Retain the original support and loss, N=1024, sigma=pi/(N^2-1), and k=pi/4. No profile parameter, source tolerance or response is selected or evaluated. The formulas below are uniform in the continuous translation of the profile and in time.

docs.title: Physical profile and derivative budgets
docs.text:
Write the site-scale profile as F(s)=varepsilon*f(varepsilon*s) and put

\[ \zeta=\frac{2K(m)}N,\quad b=\zeta\sqrt{2d/g},\quad \omega_s=d\zeta^2(2-m)=\frac{g b^2(2-m)}2,\quad \psi_j=kj+(\lambda-\omega_s)\tau. \]

The full reconstruction (10) is exactly z_app,j=F(j+v*tau)*exp(i*psi_j)+F(j+v*tau)^3*sum_l a_l*exp(i*l*psi_j). The bookkeeping varepsilon has disappeared. The first integral and its derivative give the uniform bounds

\[ \|F\|_\infty\le b,\quad B_1=\frac{\zeta b m}{2}\ge\|F'\|_\infty,\quad B_2=\zeta^2 b m\ge\|F''\|_\infty,\quad B_3=\frac{\zeta^3 b m(4+m)}2\ge\|F'''\|_\infty. \tag{40} \]

For example, set s=1-(F/b)^2 in [0,m]. Then F'^2=zeta^2*b^2*s*(m-s), whose upper bound follows from s*(m-s)<=m^2/4. Also F''=zeta^2*F*(2s-m) and F'''=zeta^2*(-4-m+6s)*F', proving the other two inequalities. The exact slow derivative of the profile factor is -i*omega_s*F. It must not be omitted when differentiating the moving metric.

Let A_h=sum_l |l*a_l|, with the three harmonic coefficients from (11). For the leading edge amplitude c of (29) and the harmonic contribution to the phase gap, define

\[ \begin{split} C_0&=D_k b+B_1,\qquad C_1=|v|(D_k B_1+B_2)+\omega_s C_0,\\ G_h&=2A_0b^3,\qquad V_h=6|v|A_0b^2B_1+2|\lambda-\omega_s|A_h b^3,\\ G&=C_0+G_h,\qquad a_*=\lambda C_0+C_1+V_h. \end{split} \tag{41} \]

The fundamental theorem of calculus across one site proves ||c||_infinity<=C_0, ||c'||_infinity<=C_1. Differentiating every harmonic, including its spatial transport, gives the bounds G_h and V_h. Consequently ||a||_infinity<=G and ||a'||_infinity<=a_* for the complete reference.

To specify exactly the inherited scalar residual budget under audit, put S_0=d*B_2+g*b^3 and rewrite (18) without varepsilon:

\[ \begin{split} r_*={}&B_3/6+3A_1b^2B_1+(B_1/2)C_0^2\\ &+A_0(3b^2S_0+3bB_1^2+\tfrac32b^2B_2) +A_0b^3G^2+G^5/120+2\sigma(b+A_0b^3). \tag{42} \end{split} \]

Here S_0>=omega_s*b; it deliberately retains the already proved scalar budget. No lower bound on the actual residual is asserted by any positive term of (42). Sharper use of the exact slow derivative, harmonic phases or damping row would define a different budget needing its own proof.

docs.title: All-mode bounds without a dimension factor from the Frobenius norm
docs.text:
For a smooth N-periodic function use its continuous Fourier coefficients with normalization 1/N, and let W be their absolute sum. Parseval and Cauchy--Schwarz, with sum_(n!=0) 1/n^2=pi^2/3, give

\[ W(F)\le b+\frac{N B_1}{2\sqrt3}=:W_0,\qquad W(F')\le\frac{N B_2}{2\sqrt3}=:W_1. \tag{43} \]

The second bound uses the zero mean of a periodic derivative. Absolute convergence makes sampling legitimate: discrete Fourier coefficients sum aliased continuous coefficients, so their absolute sum cannot increase. Translation changes the phases of the continuous coefficients, so the same alias bound holds uniformly over shifts; discrete aliased coefficients need not acquire one common phase. Multiplication obeys W(f*g)<=W(f)*W(g) and the one-site difference has norm at most two. Thus the sampled edge amplitudes satisfy

\[ W(c)\le Z_0:=D_kW_0+W_1,\qquad W(c')\le Z_1:=2(|v|W_1+\omega_s W_0). \]

This is a norm of Fourier coefficients, not a restriction to selected carrier modes. In the normalized eigenbasis of J_0, each congruence entry of H has magnitude lambda*|hat(c^2)(-q-r)|/8. The factors from U have modulus one on every nonconstant mode. Summing over both frequency signs bounds every absolute row and column sum by lambda*W(c^2)/4. The symmetric near/far mask cannot increase these sums. The Schur bound, unitary invariance of matrix norms and (30) therefore prove, for the fixed Delta=lambda/2,

\[ \begin{split} k_*&=Z_0^2\ \ge\|K\|_2,\qquad d_*=2Z_0Z_1\ \ge\|\operatorname{Re}(e^{i\omega\tau}C')\|_2,\\ m_*&=\tfrac\lambda4 Z_0^2 +\tfrac12\left[(G_h+G^3/6)a_*+C_0(C_1+V_h)\right] \ \ge\|M_{\rm ret}\|_2. \end{split} \tag{44} \]

For the last remainder, write sin(a)*a'-a_0*a'_(0,fast)=(sin(a)-a_0)*a'+a_0*(a'-a'_(0,fast)). The harmonic gap is at most G_h and |sin(a)-a|<=G^3/6, giving the second term of m_*. Thus (44) includes spatial transport, slow phase, generated harmonics and sine curvature, with no frozen-envelope assumption. Metric positivity still requires k_*<cos(chi) separately. These are explicit sufficient constants, not a claim that this cutoff is optimal.

docs.title: The inherited scalar defect cannot close this bootstrap
docs.text:
Use the constant residual allowance mathfrak r_*=2*sqrt(N)*r_* in (35), justified by ||L^(1/2)||=2, and the natural derivative budget a_* from (41). Even with zero initial error, the resulting majorant cannot close its edge-error ball over T>=T_phi=1/omega_s, for any 0<m<1 and positive radius rho satisfying the chart premises. This conclusion does not depend on the size of the retained-block bound or on the cutoff.

To prove it, set c_5=D_k^5/120. The published allowances obey

\[ a_*\ge\lambda D_k b,\quad r_*\ge2\sigma b+c_5b^5,\quad T_\phi>\frac1{g b^2},\quad \delta_\kappa:=\cos(\chi)-k_*\le1. \tag{45} \]

If metric positivity fails, there is already no certificate. Otherwise alpha>=a_*rho/(6*delta_kappa)>0. The constant-residual term in (35) and exp(x)-1>=x^2/2 imply

\[ \frac{Q(T_\phi)}\rho \ge\frac{(1+k_*)a_*\mathfrak r_*T_\phi^2} {12\delta_\kappa^{3/2}} \ge\frac{a_*\mathfrak r_*T_\phi^2}{12}. \tag{46} \]

For the fixed carrier, lambda>1/4, D_k>3/4, g<1/72 and c_5>1/512; the original loss satisfies sigma>3/N^2. Using u+v>=2*sqrt(u*v) for positive u,v gives

\[ \begin{split} \frac{a_*\mathfrak r_*T_\phi^2}{12} &>\frac{\sqrt N\lambda D_k}{6g^2} \left(\frac{2\sigma}{b^2}+c_5b^2\right)\\ &\ge\frac{\sqrt N\lambda D_k}{3g^2}\sqrt{2\sigma c_5} >\frac{81\sqrt3}{128}>1\qquad(N=1024). \tag{47} \end{split} \]

Thus Q(T_phi)>rho, whereas (35) requires Q(T_phi)<rho*sqrt(delta_kappa)<=rho. Larger horizons or initial errors only increase this particular majorant. Neither choosing another width nor eliminating every other growth allowance repairs it.

There is a separate obstruction if one attempts only to improve the cubic error term while retaining the same scalar forcing allowance and global edge-to-node conversion. Even granting zero growth, zero initial error and zero mean error, the resulting full-state allowance U_T obeys

\[ \frac{U_{T_\phi}}{\sqrt N\,b(1+A_0b^2)} \ge\frac4{g(2-m)\sqrt{\ell_1}(1+A_0b^2)} \left(\frac{2\sigma}{b^2}+c_5b^2\right) >\frac{9\sqrt3}{8}>1. \tag{48} \]

Here G+rho<pi/2 implies b<4; A_0<1/16 gives 1+A_0b^2<2, and sqrt(ell_1)<8/N. The same arithmetic-geometric-mean bound proves the final inequality. The denominator in (48) is already an upper bound on the reference norm. This allowance therefore cannot certify an error smaller than the signal itself, even before resonance growth. It is not a lower bound on actual error or a failure of the exact flow.

Method decision. Equations (40)--(44) supply the previously missing spatially varying constants, but the inherited scalar defect treatment fails before their optimization could matter. Equations (47)--(48) exclude that specified combination of residual, nonlinear remainder and norm conversion, not all relative-storage methods or all conservative references. A damped reference has not been proved necessary. Retaining the defect's phase, spatial support and two-row correlations in its transport, or a different justified residual/observation estimate, changes the premises. Merely bounding the retained block more tightly does not.

docs.title: 10. Signed defect transport retains phase, aliases and both rows
docs.text:
The next comparison changes the failed allowances, rather than optimizing (42). Let h_0=2*pi/N, omega= lambda-omega_s, and expand the continuous periodic profiles in Fourier coefficients normalized by 1/N. The real coordinates of the complete reference in section 9 are

\[ x_*=X_1\cos\psi+X_3\cos3\psi,\qquad \theta_*=\Theta_1\sin\psi+\Theta_3\sin3\psi, \] \[ X_1=F+a_{-1}F^3,\quad\Theta_1=F-a_{-1}F^3,\quad X_3=(a_3+a_{-3})F^3,\quad\Theta_3=(a_3-a_{-3})F^3. \tag{49} \]

The profiles are evaluated at j+v*tau. Retain spacetime labels (n,l) with n an integer and l=1,3 initially, their conjugates, and all labels generated by the nonlinearity. Define
