\[ q_{nl}=nh_0+lk\pmod{2\pi},\qquad \Omega_{nl}=nh_0v+l\omega,\qquad v_{nl}=\left(\widehat X_l(n)/2,\widehat\Theta_l(n)/(2i)\right), \quad v_{-n,-l}=\overline{v_{nl}}. \tag{50} \]

Set v_nl=0 outside the reference harmonics l=+/-1,+/-3; nonlinear residuals can still have nonzero coefficients at those other labels. Spatial aliasing does not identify temporal frequencies: replacing n by n+N leaves q unchanged but changes Omega by 2*pi*v. Nor does a nonzero carrier ensure constant reference means: some aliased labels have q zero and Omega nonzero. Both effects must remain in a full-state comparison.

Take d_q=1-exp(i*q) for the oriented incidence. With a_nl=d_q*(v_nl)_theta, convolution * on the integer label lattice, and S(a)=sin(a)-a, the exact coefficient formulas are

\[ \widehat S(a)=\sum_{j\ge1}\frac{(-1)^j}{(2j+1)!} a^{*(2j+1)},\qquad J_q=\lambda_q\begin{pmatrix}-\sigma&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}, \quad\lambda_q=1-\cos q, \] \[ r_{nl}=(i\Omega_{nl}I-J_q)v_{nl} +\left(\tfrac12\overline{d_q}\,\widehat S(a)_{nl},0\right). \tag{51} \]

These are the signed residuals of both real rows under the actual law. Smooth periodic profiles give absolutely summable coefficients and first temporal derivatives. The absolutely convergent sine series justifies the convolutions and interchange of sums. Cancellations in (51) occur before taking a norm; independently bounding its derivative, tangent and sine terms would generally destroy the small defect one is trying to assess.

docs.title: Actual positive-loss harmonic transport
docs.text:
For a real temporal frequency Omega, define the entire matrix kernel

\[ \mathcal K_q(\tau,\Omega) =\int_0^\tau e^{J_q(\tau-s)}e^{i\Omega s}\,ds =\tau e^{i\Omega\tau}\varphi_1(\tau(J_q-i\Omega I)), \qquad \varphi_1(Z)=\sum_{j\ge0}\frac{Z^j}{(j+1)!}. \tag{52} \]

When its inverse is admitted, the equivalent expression is K_q=(exp(i*Omega*tau)*I-exp(J_q*tau))*(i*Omega*I-J_q)^-1. For q nonzero, the determinant is lambda_q^2-Omega^2+i*sigma*lambda_q*Omega, which cannot vanish for positive sigma and real Omega. The entire expression remains the owner of the zero-mode and small-denominator limits. At q zero, K is (exp(i*Omega*tau)-1)/(i*Omega)*I, with value tau*I at Omega zero.

For the actual 0<sigma<2, put s_sigma=sqrt(1-sigma^2/4) and a_q=sigma*lambda_q/2. Direct squaring of C_sigma=[[-sigma/2,-1],[1,sigma/2]] gives

\[ e^{J_q\tau}=e^{-a_q\tau} \left[\cos(\lambda_qs_\sigma\tau)I +\frac{\sin(\lambda_qs_\sigma\tau)}{s_\sigma}C_\sigma\right]. \tag{53} \]

The branch factors in (52) are [exp(i*Omega*tau)-exp((-a_q +/- i*lambda_q*s_sigma)*tau)] / [a_q+i*(Omega -/+ lambda_q*s_sigma)]. Their corresponding spectral projectors are not orthogonal and cannot be replaced by unit weights. At all modes the full matrix satisfies ||K_q||_2<=tau, since the actual semigroup is contractive. Thus no uniform nonzero detuning or unproved number-theoretic condition on aliases is needed. Resolved nonresonant labels may have a much smaller effect than this general bound.

The signed linear defect response is

\[ h_j(\tau)=-\sum_{n,l} e^{iq_{nl}j} \mathcal K_{q_{nl}}(\tau,\Omega_{nl})r_{nl}. \tag{54} \]

For Parseval, sum the separate time-dependent contributions within each spatial mode first, then use ||h||_2^2=N*sum_q ||hat(h)_q||_2^2. No inverse Laplacian occurs. In particular, K_q*(i*Omega*I-J_q)*v=(exp(i*Omega*tau)*I-exp(J_q*tau))*v; the linear part of (51) and the nonlinear coefficient must still be combined before replacing (54) by an absolute bound.

docs.title: Finite truncations need their own tail allowance
docs.text:
The exact representation is not a license to omit small coefficients. For any scalar N-periodic profile P with ||P'''||_infinity<=C_3, integration by parts gives, for an integer cutoff M at least one,

\[ \sum_{|n|>M}|\widehat P(n)|\le\frac{C_3}{h_0^3 M^2},\qquad \sum_{|n|>M}|nh_0\widehat P(n)|\le\frac{2C_3}{h_0^2M}. \tag{55} \]

Use C_3=B_3 for F and C_3=6B_1^3+18bB_1B_2+3b^2B_3 for F cubed. Equation (55) controls both the omitted coefficients and their temporal derivative, including translation. The factor |l*omega| for each harmonic must also be retained. For phase-gap coefficient sums bounded by A, truncating the sine series after degree 2P+1 leaves the separate absolute-sum allowance

\[ \sum_{j>P}\frac{A^{2j+1}}{(2j+1)!} \le\frac{A^{2P+3}}{(2P+3)!} \left[1-\frac{A^2}{(2P+4)(2P+5)}\right]^{-1}, \tag{56} \]

provided the displayed denominator is positive. A phase-gap truncation of absolute-sum size epsilon additionally changes S by at most (cosh(A)-1)*epsilon, where A bounds every interpolating coefficient norm. The incidence factor |d_q|/2<=1 does not enlarge this form-residual sum. If the complete omitted two-row residual has coefficient-norm sum at most epsilon_r, its contribution to (54) is at most sqrt(N)*T*epsilon_r. This explicit tail treatment replaces the fixed fifth-order allowance; it is not permission to reduce a tail without a declared finite budget.

docs.title: 11. A response-corrected reference has an exact phase row
docs.text:
Equation (54) solves h'=J_sigma*h-r_app, h(0)=0, where r_app is the signed vector residual of (51), distinct from the scalar allowance r_* in (42). Define the independent corrected reference z_c=z_app+h. Its full-law residual is exactly

\[ r_c=\left(R(\theta_{\rm app})-R(\theta_{\rm app}+h_\theta),0\right). \tag{57} \]

Indeed z_c'=J_sigma*z_c+R(theta_app). Its phase row is exact, and both reference means remain at their initial values. Aliased mean drift in the original reference is canceled by the zero-mode part of (54); it was not assumed absent. This is a prescribed response correction, not a trajectory of the nonlinear law and not a supplied pressure replacing that law.

Equation (57) is generally first order in h. For example, at a nonconstant reference with gaps a in (-pi,pi), take h_theta=t*theta_app. Then the inner product of r_c,x/t with theta_app tends to -sum_e a_e^2*(1-cos(a_e))/2<0. A quadratic-error claim would be false. A genuinely quadratic residual would instead require solving the full variational correction h'=J_sigma*h+(DR(theta_app)*h_theta,0)-r_app, with its actual time-dependent Jacobian. That is a different linear problem and needs a separate bound.

For that full variational correction h_v=(u_v,eta_v), the exact remaining form source is R(theta_app)+DR(theta_app)*eta_v-R(theta_app+eta_v). If its phase-gap norms are bounded by H_v0 and H_v2 in infinity and Euclidean norm, respectively, Taylor's theorem gives

\[ \|r_v\|_2\le \left[\tfrac12\min(1,G_{\rm app})H_{v0}+H_{v0}^2/6\right]H_{v2}. \]

Indeed the edge remainder is sin(a+b)-sin(a)-cos(a)*b, bounded by |sin(a)|*b^2/2+|b|^3/6, and ||D^T||/2=1. This is genuinely quadratic in h_v and needs no acute-chart assumption. It does not supply the time-dependent coupled-mode propagator or a quantitative bound on h_v.

For (54), if ||Dtheta_app||_infinity<=G_app, ||Dh_theta||_infinity<=H_0, and ||Dh_theta||_2<=H_2, the exact sine secant gives the conditional source allowance

\[ \|r_c\|_2\le \left(\tfrac12G_{\rm app}^2+\tfrac12G_{\rm app}H_0 +H_0^2/6\right)H_2. \tag{58} \]

It starts at zero when h does and depends on the signed transported defect. It has neither the standalone damping nor the fifth-order floor in (42). The actual damping remains in (52)--(54). Bounding (58) by a large constant can still be inconclusive; the exact residual (57) and time dependence remain available. The total error to the original reference is h+e, where e=z-z_c; the correction h must always be reported.

docs.title: 12. Full-state metric without a spectral-gap conversion
docs.text:
A second constructive change removes the ell_1^-1/2 factor in (48). For a reference (x_*,theta_*), let xi=(u,eta) be the full nodal error, including its means, and start with E_0=||xi||_2^2/2. Write a=Dtheta_*, B=DR(theta_*), and M(B)=[[0,B/2],[B/2,0]]. Its exact quadratic production is xi^T M(B) xi=u^T B eta. The real errors have no Fourier-band restriction.

Use the original leading edge wave a_0=Im(c*exp(i*lambda*tau)), retaining ||c||_infinity<=C_0 and ||c'||_infinity<=C_1 from (41). Thus ||a_0||_infinity<=C_0. Admit ||a-a_0||_infinity<=H_gap and G=C_0+H_gap. For z_app, H_gap=G_h; for z_c one may use H_gap=G_h+H_0. The exact splitting is

\[ B_0=\tfrac18D^T\operatorname{diag}|c|^2D,\qquad B_f=-\tfrac18D^T\operatorname{diag}(c^2)D,\qquad B=B_0+\operatorname{Re}(e^{2i\lambda\tau}B_f)+B_{\rm rem}, \] \[ \|M(B_{\rm rem})\|_2 \le G^4/24+(G+C_0)H_{\rm gap}/2. \tag{59} \]

Taylor's inequality |1-cos(a)-a^2/2|<=|a|^4/24 and ||D||=2 prove (59). There is no moving-curvature a' term in this energy. An acute chart is not a positivity premise for the metric below.

docs.title: Static and oscillating corrections preserve every coordinate
docs.text:
On the mean-zero space solve A S+S A=B_0, and set S zero on constants. The positive Sylvester integral and 0<=B_0<=C_0^2*A/4 give

\[ S=\int_0^\infty e^{-As}B_0e^{-As}\,ds,\qquad 0\le S\le C_0^2I/8,\qquad \|S'\|_2\le C_0C_1/4. \tag{60} \]

With K_0=diag(S,-S), direct multiplication yields J_0^T K_0+K_0 J_0=-2M(B_0). The incidence factors remove the apparent small denominator; no inverse spectral-gap bound is used.

For the oscillating matrix H=M(B_f) use the fixed Delta=lambda/2 homological split (30). In eigenvectors (f_q,-i*s*f_q)/sqrt(2), s equal to plus or minus one, opposite signs give zero congruence entries. Same-sign entry magnitudes are |d_q*d_r|*|hat(c^2)(-q-r)|/16. The inequality |d_q*d_r|<=lambda_q+lambda_r bounds the far inverse. Only the negative/negative block can be near resonant. Its real part has half the complex operator norm: it joins two orthogonal conjugate eigenspaces. The real far inverse is bounded by half the sum of its two branch norms. The row-sum estimates of section 9 consequently give, for K=K_0+K_f,

\[ k_*=(C_0^2+3Z_0^2)/8\ge\|K\|_2,\qquad d_*=(C_0C_1+3Z_0Z_1)/4, \] \[ m_*=5\lambda Z_0^2/64+G^4/24+(G+C_0)H_{\rm gap}/2. \tag{61} \]

Here d_* bounds the uncanceled coefficient derivative K_0'+Re(exp(2i*lambda*tau)*C_f'), not the complete derivative K'. The latter includes the canceled fast terms. The value m_* bounds the retained quadratic production after those cancellations. Means remain under the identity metric, since every correction has zero constant rows and columns. These are new Euclidean constants, not transferred Bregman constants with the spectral factor removed by assertion.

docs.title: Nonlinear remainder, actual loss and a prospective bootstrap
docs.text:
Assume ||xi||<=rho, k_*<1, and set

\[ n_\rho=\sqrt2\min(1,G)\rho+\tfrac23\rho^2,\qquad c_*=m_*+d_*/2+k_*(2\sigma+G^2)+(k_*+\tfrac12)n_\rho. \]

Taylor's theorem, ||Deta||_infinity<=sqrt(2)||eta||_2 and ||D||=2 give ||R(theta_*+eta)-R(theta_*)-B*eta||<=n_rho*||eta||. The baseline nonlinear work then costs at most n_rho*||xi||^2/2, using ||u||*||eta||<=||xi||^2/2. For E_c=xi^T(I+K)xi/2, both actual rows imply

\[ \frac{1-k_*}{2}\|\xi\|^2\le E_c\le\frac{1+k_*}{2}\|\xi\|^2, \quad E_c'\le-\sigma u^TAu+c_*\|\xi\|^2 +(1+k_*)\|\xi\|\|r\|. \tag{62} \]

The terms 2*sigma and G^2 in c_* bound the interaction of K with the actual damping and reference Jacobian, respectively. Thus, for uniform admitted constants, initial full-state error delta, and alpha=c_*/(1-k_*),

\[ \|\xi(\tau)\|\le\frac{Q(\tau)}{\sqrt{1-k_*}},\qquad Q(\tau)=e^{\alpha\tau}\left[ \sqrt{1+k_*}\,\delta+ \frac{1+k_*}{\sqrt{1-k_*}} \int_0^\tau e^{-\alpha s}\|r(s)\|\,ds\right]. \tag{63} \]

The strict condition Q(T)<rho*sqrt(1-k_*) proves the whole interval by first exit. No Poincare factor or unobserved mean coordinate remains. If an acute phase chart is separately needed, require G+sqrt(2)*rho<pi/2. For the response-corrected reference, insert (57) or its proved allowance (58), and include ||h|| in the final error to z_app. Time-dependent source bounds must not be replaced by their endpoint values without a proof; h starts at zero but can vary thereafter.

This changes both mechanisms behind (47)--(48): the residual is transported before its nonlinear remainder is bounded, and the error metric controls the full nodes directly. It supplies a conditional comparison with no inherited scalar-defect floor. It does not prove that (63) closes on the periodic family. The remaining quantitative obligation is a certified bound on (54), (57), their Fourier/sine tails and the nonlinear allowance over a phase time, with a nonzero localization and signal margin.

docs.title: 13. A canonical-profile preflight rejects a positive coefficient budget
docs.text:
The signed comparison above remains conditional. Its first quantitative preflight fixes the self-complementary profile parameter m=1/2, exact nominal initial state and T=T_phi=1/omega_s. Keep the same C1024 law and carrier. The declared finite budget is profile cutoff |n|<=12, sine degree seven and the shared 128-bit outward arithmetic. The preflight stops at a failed necessary condition before constructing those finite sums. No profile search, prepared nonlinear response or trajectory is used.

The particular allowance tested here replaces each signed kernel vector by a positive full-two-row norm, then uses that norm to bound its phase component. For an invertible M_nl=i*Omega_nl*I-J_q, set

\[ B_{nl}(t)=\min\left(t\|r_{nl}\|_2, 2\|M_{nl}^{-1}r_{nl}\|_2\right),\qquad U_q(t)=\sum_{q_{nl}=q}B_{nl}(t). \tag{64} \]

At the singular mean label use t*||r_nl||. Contractivity and (52) justify both branches of (64). Sum within each spatial alias class before Parseval, giving the explicit positive allowances

\[ H_0^+(t)=\sum_q|d_q|U_q(t),\qquad H_2^+(t)=\left(N\sum_q|d_q|^2U_q(t)^2\right)^{1/2}, \] \[ S^+(t)=\left(\tfrac12G_{\rm app}^2 +\tfrac12G_{\rm app}H_0^+(t)+(H_0^+(t))^2/6\right)H_2^+(t). \tag{65} \]

Here G_app=C_0+G_h is specifically the published allowance (41), and S^+ instantiates (58). Finite outward enclosures retain positive tail allowances. These operations are justified upper bounds, but discard vector directions and temporal cancellation inside the alias sums. The lower bounds below apply to this chosen allowance, never to the norm of the signed sum (54), the actual correction or its exact residual.

docs.title: A necessary source moment eliminates a radius search
docs.text:
More generally, use any nonnegative residual allowance S(t) in (63). For uniform k_*<1, gap allowance G and s_G=min(1,G), its exponent satisfies

\[ \alpha\ge a_1\rho,\qquad a_1=\frac{\sqrt2 s_G(k_*+1/2)}{1-k_*}. \]

Since exp(x)>=x for nonnegative x, even at zero initial error the bootstrap implies the necessary condition

\[ \frac{Q(T)}{\rho\sqrt{1-k_*}}\ge \frac{\sqrt2 s_G(k_*+1/2)(1+k_*)}{(1-k_*)^2} \int_0^T(T-t)S(t)\,dt <1. \tag{66} \]

If the displayed lower bound is at least one, no positive choice of rho closes this majorant. This is a necessary test for a sufficient error method, not a necessary condition for actual retention. It detects the interaction of positive residual accumulation with the conversion from full nodal error radius to pointwise phase-gap error in n_rho.

docs.title: One retained coefficient already forces failure
docs.text:
Let f_0=hat(F)(0). The first integral (15), with F/b=sqrt(1-m*sin(phi)^2) and ds=dphi/[zeta*sqrt(1-m*sin(phi)^2)], gives the period averages directly:

\[ f_0=\frac{\pi\sqrt{2d/g}}N,\qquad \widehat{F^3}(0)=f_0 b^2(1-m/2). \tag{67} \]

Thus no Fourier quadrature is needed for the retained label (0,1). At m=1/2, put z_0=3b^2/4, and define X=f_0*(1+a_-1*z_0), Theta=f_0*(1-a_-1*z_0) and Omega=lambda-omega_s. Its reference coefficient is (X/2,-i*Theta/2). The profile is even, and the complete phase row is odd under simultaneous reflection of the envelope and carrier arguments. The actual sine divergence preserves that oddness: the two neighbor shifts exchange under reflection. Its spacetime coefficients are therefore purely imaginary. Consequently, for some real beta_r, the exact signed residual has the form

\[ r_{01}=\left(A_r+i\beta_r,C_r\right),\qquad A_r=\sigma\lambda X/2,\quad C_r=(\Omega\Theta-\lambda X)/2. \]

No bound on beta_r or sine truncation is used. The exact resolvent numerator has imaginary first component Omega*A_r and real second component lambda*A_r+sigma*lambda*C_r=sigma*lambda*Omega*Theta/2. Hence, writing D_0=lambda^2-Omega^2+i*sigma*lambda*Omega,

\[ \|r_{01}\|\ge\sigma\lambda X/2,\qquad 2\|M_{01}^{-1}r_{01}\|\ge \frac{\sigma\lambda|\Omega|\sqrt{X^2+\Theta^2}}{|D_0|}. \tag{68} \]

All required inequalities follow from elementary fixed-profile bounds. The elliptic integral definition gives pi/2<K(1/2)<=pi/sqrt(2). At the unchanged carrier, 1/4<lambda<1/3, 1/4<d<1/2, 8<sqrt(2d/g)<9, and D_k>3/4. Using 3<pi<22/7 and pi^2<10 gives

\[ \frac{24}N<f_0\le b<\frac{81}{2N}<\frac1{25},\qquad \frac{27}{8N^2}<\omega_s<\frac{15}{N^2},\qquad \frac3{N^2}<\sigma<\frac{16}{5N^2}<\omega_s. \tag{69} \]

Also G_app<1/24: for this fixed m, (40)--(41) give C_0<(513/512)b and G_h< b^3/8. These loose bounds suffice. Equation (69) implies Omega>=lambda/2, while |a_-1|<1/16 implies X>=f_0/2. Since X^2+Theta^2>=2*f_0^2 and |D_0|<=3*lambda*omega_s, (68) yields

\[ B_{01}(t)\ge\frac{\sigma\lambda f_0}{5}\,t \qquad(0\le t\le T). \tag{70} \]

Indeed the first branch in (64) is at least sigma*lambda*f_0*t/4; the second is at least sigma*lambda*f_0*T/(3*sqrt(2)), larger than sigma*lambda*f_0*t/5. The conjugate label has the same bound and lies at the distinct spatial mode -k. Thus the chosen H_2^+ is at least sqrt(2N)*D_k*B_01, and

\[ S^+(t)\ge C_*t,\qquad C_*=\frac{\sigma\lambda f_0G_{\rm app}^2D_k\sqrt{2N}}{10}. \tag{71} \]

For the corrected reference G is at least G_app. Because G_app<1, min(1,G)>=G_app even if the corrected gap allowance exceeds one. If the metric is positive, alpha>=G_app*rho/sqrt(2) for every radius. Equations (63) and (71), again using exp(x)>=x, give

\[ \frac{Q(T)}\rho\ge \frac{\sigma\lambda f_0G_{\rm app}^3D_k\sqrt N T^3}{60} >\frac{7776}{625}>12. \tag{72} \]

For the last strict rational bound use (69), G_app>=D_k*b>18/N, D_k>3/4, lambda>1/4, T>N^2/15 and sqrt(N)=32. The bootstrap requires Q(T)/rho<sqrt(1-k_*)<=1. If metric positivity fails instead, there is already no certificate. Nonzero initial error, additional positive mode allowances, tails and outward arithmetic can only worsen this particular bound.

Preflight result. The declared positive coefficient budget fails at the canonical profile before its finite Fourier/sine sums need evaluation. It cannot be repaired by radius selection, extra modes or precision. This does not exclude other profile parameters, the exact signed phase-projected transport, a different nonlinear work estimate, or actual maintenance. In particular, (72) is neither an observed error nor a lower bound on an actual response. The next comparison must retain information lost between (54), (64) and (65), or admit a genuinely different correction law; repeating their positive-norm chain is not a quantitative advance.

docs.title: 14. A finite signed variational representation has controlled tails
docs.text:
Keep the canonical m=1/2 reference and full phase interval of section 13. Write V(t)=[[0,B(t)],[0,0]], with B(t)=DR(theta_app(t)), so that h_v'=(J_sigma+V(t))*h_v-r_app and h_v(0)=0. The first-order feedback is included in this linear comparison, not in a modified constitutive law. V couples modes; separate constant two-by-two tangent propagators do not by themselves propagate this equation.

The declared finite representation uses profile cutoff 24, the exact cube of that finite profile, sine degree seventeen, cosine degree sixteen and 256 chronological Jacobian insertions. Retained time integrals and their coefficients are exact mathematical objects here. The result below bounds analytical truncation error; no retained sum, prepared response or trajectory is evaluated. Shared rational/128-bit interval controls on constants do not certify a future sum's accumulated arithmetic error.

docs.title: Chronology, resonance and the factorial tail
docs.text:
Let S(t)=exp(J_sigma*t). Define operator terms for s<=t by

\[ U_0(t,s)=S(t-s),\qquad U_{j+1}(t,s)=\int_s^t S(t-u)V(u)U_j(u,s)\,du, \] \[ h_0(t)=-\int_0^t S(t-u)r_{\rm app}(u)\,du,\qquad h_{j+1}(t)=\int_0^t S(t-u)V(u)h_j(u)\,du. \tag{73} \]

The integrals preserve matrix order and signed vector addition. With L=G_app^2 and R_*>=sup||r_app||, contractivity of S and induction over the ordered simplex give

\[ \|U_j(t,s)\|\le\frac{[L(t-s)]^j}{j!},\qquad \|h_j(t)\|\le R_*t\frac{(Lt)^j}{(j+1)!}. \tag{74} \]

The series converge uniformly on the whole interval even when LT>1. Their sums solve the full variational initial-value problem. This is not an assertion that its one-step Volterra map is a contraction. For a nonnegative integer P, beta>=LT and beta<P+2, summing the decreasing factorial ratios bounds the omitted orders j>P by

\[ E_U\le\frac{\beta^{P+1}}{(P+1)!} \left(1-\frac\beta{P+2}\right)^{-1},\qquad E_h\le R_*T\frac{\beta^{P+1}}{(P+2)!} \left(1-\frac\beta{P+3}\right)^{-1}. \tag{75} \]

These positive bounds apply only to omitted orders. Replacing the retained terms in (73) by (74) would discard the phase information being preserved.

In the spatial Fourier basis, write f=1-cos(a), a=Dtheta_app. The coupling is

\[ B_{qr}(t)=\tfrac12\overline{d_q}d_r \sum_{\alpha:\,Q_\alpha=q-r} \widehat f_\alpha e^{i\Omega_\alpha t}. \tag{76} \]

Each chronological path changes spatial mode by Q_alpha and retains its own temporal frequency. Spatial aliases cannot merge those frequencies. The d factors annihilate constant rows and columns. Thus terms h_j with j>=1 have zero means; h_0 alone cancels the original reference's mean drift. The exact corrected reference still has a complete exact phase row.

Successive integrations of exponential factors are entire divided differences of the exponential function. For nodes z_0,...,z_d, their ordered-simplex representation is

\[ \exp(t\cdot)[z_0,\ldots,z_d] =t^d\int_{\substack{u_j\ge0\\\sum_{j=0}^d u_j=1}} \exp\!\left(t\sum_{j=0}^d u_jz_j\right)\,du. \tag{77} \]

The simplex measure has volume 1/d!. Along a variational path the nodes are actual damped tangent eigenvalues plus accumulated imaginary forcing frequencies; the final source node is purely imaginary. Their real parts are nonpositive, giving modulus at most t^d/d!. Coincident nodes use the entire limit, for example t^d*exp(t*z)/d! when all nodes equal z. There is no lower-detuning premise. If branch factors are used, retain the actual nonorthogonal projectors from section 10. Chronological products of different B(t) generally do not commute.

docs.title: The full linear propagator has a moderate uniform gain
docs.text:
The direct metric of section 12 applies at zero error radius to J_sigma+V(t), using the original reference gap G=G_app, H_gap=G_h. Put c_lin=m_*+d_*/2+k_*(2*sigma+G_app^2) and alpha_lin=c_lin/(1-k_*). Its homogeneous energy bound gives

\[ \|U(t,s)\|\le \sqrt{\frac{1+k_*}{1-k_*}}\exp(\alpha_{\rm lin}(t-s))<2^8 \qquad(0\le s\le t\le T). \tag{78} \]

Here is a fixed-profile verification rather than an assumed conditioning constant. Equations (40)--(43) and (69) imply W_0<11b/8, W_1<b/256, C_0<b, Z_0<9b/8, and k_*<b^2<1/625. Also

\[ G_{\rm app}/b<D_k+1/512,\qquad G_{\rm app}^2T<\frac{224}{3}\left(\frac{385}{384}\right)^2 <151/2, \tag{79} \]

using lambda>2/7, D_k>3/4, and b^2T=4/(3g). For the metric terms, C_1*T<25/4, Z_1*T<37, C_0<33/800 and Z_0<9/200 give d_*T<4/3. Equation (79) and D_k<4/5 also give G_app<b, and G_h<b^3/8. The near-block term obeys 5*lambda*Z_0^2*T/64<945/256; the remaining terms of m_* have sum at most b^4*T/6<1/20. Hence m_*T<81/20. Finally sigma*T<1 and (79) give k_*(2*sigma+G_app^2)*T<78/625<1/8. Therefore

\[ \alpha_{\rm lin}T<\frac{581}{120}\frac{625}{624}<5,\qquad \sqrt{\frac{1+k_*}{1-k_*}}<21/20. \]

Since exp(1)<3, their product is less than (21/20)*3^5<256, proving (78). This controls all modes, including means; it does not bound the inhomogeneous signed correction by a small observed value.

docs.title: Finite profile, source and Jacobian inputs
docs.text:
At m=1/2, the elliptic nome is q_e=exp(-pi)<1/20. The Jacobi dn Fourier formula, with the nome convention, gives

\[ \widehat F(0)=f_0,\qquad \widehat F(n)=\frac{2f_0q_e^{|n|}}{1+q_e^{2|n|}}\quad(n\ne0). \tag{80} \]

DLMF's elliptic modulus is sqrt(m), distinct from the carrier k. The normalization follows from (67) and the period N; all coefficients are positive. Thus W(F)=b and W(F^3)=b^3. These are properties of the admitted profile, not evaluated trajectory data. Let F_M retain |n|<=24. Its cube is formed exactly, so its support extends to |n|<=72. The geometric tail allowance

\[ E_F=\frac{4f_0q_e^{25}}{1-q_e}<2^{-110},\qquad W(F-F_M)\le E_F,\qquad W(F'-F_M')\le h_0\left(25+\frac{q_e}{1-q_e}\right)E_F<E_F/4 \tag{81} \]

uses f_0<1/32 and h_0<1/160. Also W(F')<=4*f_0*h_0*q_e/(1-q_e)^2<2^-14. Products give W(F^3-F_M^3)<=3b^2E_F; differentiating the product gives a bound [6bW(F')+3b^2/4]E_F<b^2E_F for its derivative error.

Use the complete reconstruction (49) with F_M to obtain w_M and its gap a_M. Positivity of the retained profile coefficients bounds every convex interpolation of a and a_M in coefficient absolute-sum norm by

\[ A\le D_kb+W(F')+2A_0b^3<1/16, \qquad W(a-a_M)<4E_F. \tag{82} \]

Let S_17 be the sine polynomial through degree seventeen minus its linear term, and C_16 the polynomial for 1-cos through degree sixteen. Define

\[ \widetilde r=w_M'-J_\sigma w_M+ (\tfrac12D^TS_{17}(a_M),0),\qquad \widetilde B=\tfrac12D^T\operatorname{diag}(C_{16}(a_M))D, \qquad \widetilde V=\begin{pmatrix}0&\widetilde B\\0&0\end{pmatrix}. \tag{83} \]

This preserves the signed source terms before their final addition. The source and Jacobian have different truncation allowances. In particular,

\[ \epsilon_B:=\sup\|V-\widetilde V\| \le 8\sinh(A)E_F+ \frac{2A^{18}}{18!}\left(1-\frac{A^2}{19\cdot20}\right)^{-1} <2^{-109}. \tag{84} \]

Here 8*sinh(1/16)<1; the second term is less than 2^-122. For the source, use W(x)+W(theta) to bound its two-row coefficient norm. The profile substitution costs less than 3E_F in state and 3E_F in time derivative; ||J_sigma|| in that sum norm is below four. The sine substitution costs less than E_F, while its separate series tail is A^19/19!/(1-A^2/(20*21)). Including the nodal factor sqrt(N)=32 yields

\[ \epsilon_r:=\sup\|r_{\rm app}-\widetilde r\|_2<2^{-99}. \tag{85} \]

These deliberately loose bounds control only removed input terms. They do not substitute absolute coefficient sums for the retained solution.

docs.title: Combined analytical error and remaining computation boundary
docs.text:
Let h_tilde solve the finite-input linear equation h_tilde'=(J_sigma+V_tilde)*h_tilde-r_tilde, with zero initial value. Equations (18) and (42) give R_*<32: the bounds b,B_1,B_2,B_3,C_0,G_app,S_0,sigma<1/16, A_0<1/16 and A_1<1/8 already imply r_*<1/32<1 by direct substitution. Equation (69) gives T<2^19. Set M_*=2^8 from (78). Variation of constants for the input difference, using sup||h_v||<=M_*R_*T, gives

\[ E:=\sup\|h_v-\widetilde h\| \le M_*T\epsilon_r+M_*T\epsilon_B(M_*R_*T+E). \]

Since M_*T*epsilon_B<1/2, this small input-perturbation term can be absorbed. It is not a contraction assumption on the full V evolution. Consequently

\[ E<2M_*T\epsilon_r+2M_*^2R_*T^2\epsilon_B <2^{28}\epsilon_r+2^{60}\epsilon_B <2^{-71}+2^{-49}. \tag{86} \]

For the finite inputs, (79) and (84) give sup||V_tilde||*T<76; also sup||r_tilde||<33<64, so its product with T is below 2^25. Use their signed chronological recurrence (73) through order 256, calling the finite sum h_tilde^[256]. Exact rational factorial comparisons in (75) give

\[ \frac{76^{257}}{257!}\left(1-\frac{76}{258}\right)^{-1}<2^{-80}, \qquad \frac{76^{257}}{258!}\left(1-\frac{76}{259}\right)^{-1}<2^{-88}. \]

The second, forced coefficient has an additional factorial from the source integration. It implies

\[ \sup_{0\le t\le T}\|h_v(t)-\widetilde h^{[256]}(t)\| <2^{-71}+2^{-49}+2^{-63}<2^{-48}. \tag{87} \]

This passes the declared 2^-40 analytical representation target. It is not a smallness claim about h_v itself or the nonlinear error to the reference. Every retained term is a finite signed sum of entire ordered kernels, so (87) is constructive in exact arithmetic. Naive path enumeration is nevertheless very large: the truncated Jacobian alone can reach |n|<=1152, |l|<=48, and the source |n|<=1224, |l|<=51. These are label bounds, not permission to truncate later generated modes. Efficient accumulation, certified compression and numerical roundoff still need an implementation and their own resource admission. A symbolic finite representation is not an executed 128-bit solver.

docs.title: A defect certificate can avoid enumerating chronological paths
docs.text:
The finite inputs have the direct action V_tilde(t)*(u,eta)=(D^T[C_16(a_M(t))*Deta]/2,0). Evaluating the retained profile and its derivative on the N nodes costs O(NM) by direct summation; the Jacobian action then costs O(N). The polynomial nonlinearities are evaluated on those same nodes, without deleting spatial aliases or their actual time dependence. This representation does not build a lifted path matrix or change the finite-input equation.

Duhamel's formula and (78) bound its exact propagator by M_*exp(M_*epsilon_B*(t-s))<2^9. For a continuous, piecewise continuously differentiable approximation h_hat on a finite partition, define its complete equation defect d_hat=h_hat'-(J_sigma+V_tilde)*h_hat+r_tilde. Variation of constants gives

\[ \|h_v(t)-\widehat h(t)\| <2^{-71}+2^{-49} +2^9\left[\|\widehat h(0)\|+ \int_0^t\|d_{\widehat h}(s)\|\,ds\right]. \tag{88} \]

This is an alternative evaluation certificate for the same exact h_v. It compares directly with h_tilde, so no chronological truncation term is needed in (88). A numerical implementation must enclose coefficient, arithmetic, derivative and between-sample errors in d_hat; pointwise solver tolerances do not establish this integral. The small input tails and the large retained forcing must remain separate. The first-panel result evaluates one local approximation; no full-interval evaluator is resource-admitted.

An evaluated approximation h_hat must additionally certify its error to h_tilde^[256], or supply the defect certificate (88). Only then may its combined error allowance enlarge phase-gap bounds by sqrt(2)*epsilon_h in infinity norm and 2*epsilon_h in Euclidean norm, and its full-state bound by epsilon_h. Those enlarged bounds describe the exact h_v used in the quadratic residual of section 11. A finite-input approximation is not itself an exact-phase-row reference unless its own source and representation defects are retained.

The remaining nonlinear bootstrap, initial-error ball, signal/localization margin and same-source linear discrimination are still unproved. This result closes finite analytical representability and its truncation budget; it does not establish maintenance or evaluate the whole representation.

docs.title: 15. Matrix-free inputs and whole-interval validation requirements
docs.text: The finite-input equation (83) admits a direct nodal implementation without enumerating chronological paths. Its fixed domain remains N=1024, m=1/2, M=24, sine degree seventeen and cosine degree sixteen. Evaluation of these prescribed inputs is distinct from integration of their forced linear equation, and neither is a nonlinear prepared response.

docs.title: Enclosing the finite profile and its signed source
docs.text:
The elliptic constant is enclosed using the arithmetic-geometric mean identity. Start with a_0=1, g_0=sqrt(1/2) and apply eight simultaneous updates

\[ a_{j+1}=(a_j+g_j)/2,\qquad g_{j+1}=\sqrt{a_jg_j}. \]

The exact sequences bound their common limit by g_8<=AGM<=a_8. Outward interval arithmetic therefore encloses the complete elliptic integral by pi/(2*[g_8.lo,a_8.hi]); agreement of rounded iterates is not a stopping criterion or an assumed exact value. DLMF uses modulus sqrt(m), while this owner uses parameter m. The nome is evaluated as exp(-pi/4)^4, within the existing unit-decay enclosure's domain.

These constants determine all the coefficients of F_M, the slow frequency, and an interval containing the exact T. The numerical input evaluator may use the rectangle [0,T.hi]; that is an enclosure of the physical horizon, not a changed model clock. Time and both action vectors are admitted before conversion or arithmetic. The factory consumes no cached bounds or verdicts.

Evaluate F_M and its spatial derivative at j+v*tau. Differentiate (49) with both translation speed v and carrier frequency lambda-omega_s. Form the exact cube of the retained profile at the same node, then compute both signed source rows in (83) before taking a norm. Spatial harmonic recurrences reuse fixed roots and two time rotations; they do not merge distinct temporal frequencies merely because their spatial samples alias.

For any admitted real rows u and eta, the complete matrix-free action is

\[ (J_\sigma+\widetilde V)(u,\eta)= \left(-\sigma Au-A\eta+ \tfrac12D^T[C_{16}(a_M)D\eta],\ Au\right). \tag{89} \]

The incidence convention is Dy_j=y_j-y_(j+1) and D^Tz_j=z_j-z_(j-1). Thus both constant directions and both row means are retained. Every output uses the same immutable input evaluation; editing a displayed report must not change its captured action law. No dense 2048 x 2048 matrix is needed. Direct profile evaluation costs O(NM) and a Jacobian action costs O(N). The original recurrence retained O(N+M) live storage; the reusable spatial basis below explicitly trades O(NM) storage for fewer interval operations per evaluation. These are finite input costs, not a bound on a complete solution's work.

docs.title: Reusing fixed spatial work in the same finite inputs
docs.text:
Equation (80)'s finite Fourier profile already separates spatial and temporal factors. With C_jn=cos(n*h_0*j), S_jn=sin(n*h_0*j), c_n=cos(n*h_0*v*tau) and s_n=sin(n*h_0*v*tau), write

\[ F_M(j+v\tau)=f_0+2\sum_{n=1}^M f_n(C_{jn}c_n-S_{jn}s_n), \] \[ F'_M(j+v\tau)=-2h_0\sum_{n=1}^M nf_n(S_{jn}c_n+C_{jn}s_n). \]

These are exact identities for the same retained profile, including its derivative. Spatial roots may use (j*n) mod N; n remains unreduced in the temporal rotation and derivative. Distinct temporal frequencies do not merge when their spatial samples alias. Preweight immutable spatial rows once, then contract them against the M temporal harmonics at each time. The carrier k=pi/4 has only eight spatial classes, so its rotated first and third harmonics also need only eight reconstructions per time. The exact pointwise cube and its derivative 3*F_M^2*F'_M remain in (49). An identity for the untruncated elliptic profile cannot replace this finite cube without accounting for the difference.

The shared dyadic linear reduction retains interval uncertainty during these contractions and the Lobatto transform. For scale S=2^128, represent an admitted interval by integer center numerator C and radius numerator R over 2S. For a dot product, accumulate the signed integer center and a conservative radius

\[ C_* = \sum_i C_iD_i,\qquad R_* = \sum_i\bigl(|C_i|E_i+R_i(|D_i|+E_i)\bigr). \]

The interval (C_*+[-R_*,R_*])/(4S^2) encloses every product sum; applying an exact rational scale and one final outward projection retains that enclosure. This does not assume independent errors or remove their widths. Public consumers admit all primitives before preparing or using encoded rows. Immutable fixed bases can be reused; evaluated states, report verdicts and time-dependent phases are not authoritative cache keys.

This reuse changes arithmetic ordering and enclosure widths, not the finite functions or the analytic interpolation tails. Rational harmonic and derivative controls must establish the algebra independently; overlap between old and new interval boxes alone would not prove correctness. Existing floating FFTs can propose coefficients but cannot replace these outward reductions. The older Fejer-source spectral factory and its reflection shortcut have different preparation hypotheses. Direct full spacetime convolution is also unnecessary here: the finite sine/cosine polynomials retain their existing nodal Horner evaluation and aliases.

docs.title: Why a componentwise box propagation does not transfer
docs.text:
The existing general comparison kernels have finite dimension and derivative order contracts; increasing their limits would not prove suitability here. There is also a mathematical obstruction to their coordinatewise absolute Jacobian treatment over this horizon. Write A=I-(P+P^T)/2 on the cycle. The one-sided diagonal/absolute-offdiagonal majorant of J_sigma maps spatially uniform coordinate radii by

\[ \binom{r_x}{r_\theta}'= \begin{pmatrix}0&2\\2&0\end{pmatrix}\binom{r_x}{r_\theta}. \tag{90} \]

The negative form diagonal cancels its two positive neighbor terms; |A| has row sum two. This radius comparison grows as exp(2*tau) along its positive eigenvector, although the actual tangent is contractive. For the finite-input Jacobian, 1-C_16(a_M)>1/2 throughout the admitted gap domain. Its coordinate majorant still dominates the uniform-radius block [[0,1],[2,0]], with positive growth sqrt(2). Hence replacing the full-state cancellation by this majorant is unsuitable for the declared small-error target on T. This excludes a comparison method, not the actual dynamics, other norms or every possible interval solver.

docs.title: A continuous residual budget includes joins and small-norm arithmetic
docs.text:
For piecewise continuously differentiable h_hat on a finite partition, let j_i=h_hat(t_i+)-h_hat(t_i-) be its interior joins. Applying the same full-interval propagator once to each source and join gives

\[ \sup_{0\le t\le T}\|h_v(t)-\widehat h(t)\| <2^{-71}+2^{-49}+2^9\left[ \|\widehat h(0)\|+ \sum_i\int_{t_i}^{t_{i+1}}\|d_i(s)\|\,ds+ \sum_{i\text{ interior}}\|j_i\|\right]. \tag{91} \]

The partition covers the whole physical interval; a final enclosure through T.hi is sufficient. No repeated gain of 512 is imposed at every step. Continuous pieces with exactly shared endpoints have zero joins. Recentring or rounding an endpoint is otherwise an additional source, not free error removal. The initial term is computed from the approximation even though the exact correction starts at zero.

The prospective numerical target is 2^-24, separate from the previous 2^-40 analytical representation target. A sufficient numerical budget is that the entire bracket in (91) is at most 2^-34: its contribution is 2^-25, and adding the proved input tails stays below 2^-24. With zero initial error and joins, a uniform complete defect below 2^-53 is sufficient since T<2^19. This is an accuracy policy for the linear comparison, not a proved nonlinear retention margin.

Small defect norms require scaling before squaring. For nonnegative exact coordinate bounds b_i, set s=max(b_i) and use s*sqrt(sum((b_i/s)^2)), with the zero case handled exactly. Rounding an unscaled square to the absolute 2^-128 grid can introduce a norm floor of 2^-64, independently of the actual defect's size. A 128-bit grid therefore does not by itself certify 128-bit relative norm accuracy.

The fixed input preflight evaluates normalized times 0,1/2,1, enclosing the latter two with the same T interval, and requests a midpoint-radius Euclidean allowance below 2^-80 for the state, derivative, gap and source. This checks input implementation and arithmetic only. Even exact state and defect samples cannot prove (91): take a unit constant spatial direction w, annihilated by the actual full variational matrix, and h_hat(t)=a*P(t/T)*w, with P(s)=s^2*(s-1/2)^2*(s-1)^2. In the homogeneous zero-initial comparison, both h_hat and its defect vanish at those three samples, while ||h_hat(T/4)||=9*|a|/4096. No pointwise tolerance can replace the between-sample derivative and residual enclosure.

The remaining implementation obligation is a bounded-cost continuous approximation with a whole-panel signed residual and admitted join errors. Point input enclosures, finite representability and a small coefficient rounding error do not supply that approximation or evaluate h_v.

docs.title: A direct Taylor realization is sufficient but computationally large
docs.text:
The finite inputs are entire functions of complex time. In a unit complex disk around any real expansion time, every reconstruction frequency has absolute value below 3/2. Since exp(3/2)<6, each real row's coefficient absolute-sum bound is at most 6*(b+A_0*b^3)<1/4. Consequently the full complex state norm is below 16, its derivative norm is below 24 and its phase-gap coefficient norm is below 1/2. The cosine polynomial implies ||V_tilde||<1/2, while ||J_sigma||<17/8. The complete generator norm is therefore below three. The nonlinear sine remainder has norm below 32*(sinh(1/2)-1/2)<1, giving ||r_tilde||<73<96 on the disk.

Admit a local expansion center with norm at most 2^35. Variation of constants along a radius of this disk bounds its analytic solution by 27*(2^35+96)<Y=2^40. For its exact Taylor coefficients c_n, Cauchy's estimate gives ||c_n||<=Y. Let P_16 be its degree-sixteen polynomial, R the omitted series and A(t)=J_sigma+V_tilde(t). Its complete signed equation defect is -R'+A*R, so a panel of length delta less than one has

\[ \int_0^\delta\|d(s)\|\,ds \le Y\frac{\delta^{17}}{1-\delta}(1+3\delta). \tag{92} \]

Indeed integrating the derivative tail cancels each coefficient's factor n; the remaining term is bounded by three times the integrated state tail. For a fixed grid with panel lengths at most 1/64, summing (92) gives

\[ \sum_i\int\|d_i\| <2^{40}2^{19}2^{-96}\frac{67}{63}<2^{-36}. \tag{93} \]

This leaves room inside the declared 2^-34 budget for finite coefficient arithmetic and joins, but does not bound those additional errors. With exact coefficients, initialize each panel at the preceding polynomial's endpoint so joins vanish. The exact forced solution satisfies sup||h_tilde||<512*64*2^19=2^34; the defect bound and first-exit induction therefore keep these exact polynomial centers below 2^35. Finite implementations must check their centers and pay their extra defects.

This realization uses step exactly 1/64 except for its final shortened panel. It requires more than 2^22 panels and at most 2^25, using T>N^2/15 and T<2^19. Seventeen coefficients in each of 2048 real coordinates already entail more than 2^37 scalar coefficient entries across the run, before series products and validation. That count excludes a direct full-grid Python rational campaign from the present implementation route. It is neither a complexity lower bound for the variational problem nor a failure of its dynamics. A practical method must reuse time dependence across panels or retain exact tangent transport, and certify its changed remainder before any full-interval run. Raising the existing derivative-order or dimension limits alone does not do so.

docs.title: 16. Signed Chebyshev panels retain the continuous defect
docs.text: The next representation uses panels of length at most sixteen, with degree-96 input and candidate polynomials. It preserves the same complete variational equation and clock. The finite polynomial validator retains the continuous defect. Canonical input interpolation and a candidate are evaluated separately in the first-panel result; a manufactured polynomial test alone does not evaluate that correction.

docs.title: Source bounds sharpen without a response evaluation
docs.text:
The bound R_*<32 was deliberately loose. Substitute the primitive upper bounds b<=81/(2N), zeta<=9/(2N), D_k<=49/64, d<=1/2, g<=1/72, A_0<=1/16, A_1<=1/8 and sigma<=16/(5N^2) into the positive expression (42), with B_1=zeta*b/4, B_2=zeta^2*b/2, B_3=9*zeta^3*b/8 and T<8N^2/27. Exact rational inequalities give

\[ r_*<2^{-21},\qquad 32r_*T<4,\qquad \sup\|\widetilde h\|<512(4+T\epsilon_r)<2^{12}. \tag{94} \]

This improves a supplied upper allowance, without evaluating the signed source or inferring any lower bound on the correction. It does not close a nonlinear maintenance estimate.

docs.title: Uniform input interpolation on the whole panel
docs.text:
Map a panel to s in [-1,1], with t=t_c+(Delta/2)s, Delta<=16. Use 97 Chebyshev-Lobatto nodes and the Bernstein ellipse with parameter rho_E=1+sqrt(2). Its imaginary time semiaxis is at most eight. On that strip, q_e*exp(8h_0|v|)<1/19, because h_0<1/160 and exp(1/20)<20/19. The positive Fourier coefficients then give W(F_M)<(1/32)(1+4/18)<1/24. Each reconstructed real row has coefficient norm at most 27/24+3^8/(16*24^3)<5/4, so the full state norm is below 64 and its derivative norm below 96. The gap norm is below 5/2. The finite cosine and sine polynomial majorants consequently imply

\[ \|\widetilde V(t)\|<32,\qquad \|\widetilde r(t)\|<1024 \quad (|\operatorname{Im}t|\le8). \tag{95} \]

For example, cosh(5/2)-1<13 bounds the cosine polynomial, and sinh(5/2)-5/2<11 bounds the sine remainder; the two incidence factors give the operator factor two. The reconstruction frequency bound 3/2 controls its derivative. These analytic input extensions do not extend a physical solution past its admitted horizon.

The Chebyshev interpolation bound is 4M*rho_E^-d/(rho_E-1) for degree d and an analytic norm bound M on the ellipse. It also follows directly by bounding the Chebyshev coefficients using Cauchy's formula and the aliases at Lobatto nodes; the same triangle inequality applies to vector and operator norms. Since (1207/500)^96>2^122 and sqrt(2)>707/500, (95) gives the safe degree-96 interpolation allowances

\[ \epsilon_{B,\rm panel}<2^{-114},\qquad \epsilon_{r,\rm panel}<2^{-109}. \tag{96} \]

Interpolate the scalar edge multiplier before applying D and D^T, and both signed source rows on the same affine clock. Enclose all sample values and transform coefficients; (96) bounds analytic interpolation error only. A floating transform's output is not an outward coefficient enclosure. Point evaluations already supplied by the input owner can be reused under these premises. A practical builder may share the fixed spatial roots and local time offsets. Advancing rectangular interval rotations indefinitely is not justified: their widths can grow under |cos|+|sin| even when the exact rotation is an isometry. Re-enclose each panel's center rotation or prove a separate propagation bound.

docs.title: Reconstruct the signed equation before bounding its norm
docs.text:
Let the candidate p, signed source r_poly and scalar edge multiplier C_poly have degree at most 96 in ordinary Chebyshev coefficients, including the full constant coefficient. Form the complete polynomial residual

\[ d_{\rm poly}=\frac2\Delta p_s-J_\sigma p -(\tfrac12D^T[C_{\rm poly}Dp_\theta],0)+r_{\rm poly}. \tag{97} \]

The identity T_j*T_k=(T_(j+k)+T_|j-k|)/2 retains every generated coefficient through degree 192. In particular, projecting the residual back to degree 96 would silently delete part of the equation being checked. Differentiate the polynomial in its affine panel coordinate and retain both mean directions. The shared finite-polynomial owner computes signed products by exact packed integer convolution of dyadic Laurent coefficients, then projects each result outwards with the existing interval type. It neither changes the shared Taylor-jet order limit nor discards a tail. Explicit factor-degree and packed-bit limits bound its work.

For coefficient vectors p_k and d_k, define P_i=sum_k||p_k||_2 and R_i=sum_k||d_k||_2, using scaled norms of the outward coefficient boxes. Since |T_k(s)|<=1,

\[ \int_{t_i}^{t_{i+1}}\|d(t)\|\,dt \le\Delta_i\left[R_i+\epsilon_{r,\rm panel} +\epsilon_{B,\rm panel}P_i\right]. \tag{98} \]

The panel owner re-admits primitive coefficient tables, duration, sigma and error premises, and rebuilds (97), coefficient norms and both endpoint enclosures. Internal algebra reuses the locally normalized rows; dyadic integer norm reductions preserve the exact scaled rational sum before the shared square root. Its local result is conditional on the supplied polynomial inputs enclosing the actual source and Jacobian on the same panel. Default zero input errors assert exact polynomial inputs; they do not authenticate a canonical preparation. The validator supplies no response, propagator gain or retention flag. Initial mismatch and joins still belong to (91).

For example, if every panel satisfies P_i<=2^35 and R_i<=2^-54, (96) and T<2^19 give a total integrated defect below 2^-35+2^-59<2^-34. With zero initial error and joins, (91) then meets the declared 2^-24 numerical target. Nonzero initial error and joins must share the same budget. Neither these policies nor small analytic input tails show that a candidate passes them.

docs.title: Candidate generation and the remaining resource boundary
docs.text:
On a real panel, keep the exact contractive S(s)=exp(J_sigma*s) and iterate only the small Jacobian term in (73), starting at the carried endpoint. The primitive gap bound and (84) give Delta*sup||V_tilde||<16/625<1/32. This local Volterra map is a contraction; the same estimate does not establish a full-interval contraction. For a starting endpoint of norm at most 2^13, its uniterated source term has norm below 2^14. Twenty Jacobian insertions leave a functional-series tail below 2^14*(1/32)^21/(1-1/32)<2^-90. This establishes a candidate route, not an implemented quadrature or a polynomial residual certificate. Every approximated integral and coefficient must still pass (97)--(98).

A fixed grid of length sixteen, except the last shortened panel, uses at most 2^15 panels. The validator stores O(Nd) coefficients and performs O(Nd) interval bookkeeping and O(N) packed integer products per panel; the bit cost of each product depends on the integer backend and coefficient magnitudes. No dense spatial matrix or Python quadratic coefficient-product loop is required. This reduces the prospective number of panels and makes signed polynomial validation executable. It does not establish the cost of building 97 canonical input samples or generating a candidate on each panel.

The polynomial controls independently check signed products, interval corners, carrying, derivatives and work limits. The panel controls check whole-polynomial cancellation, time scaling, uncertainty and invalid domains. Their full-size synthetic countercontrol deliberately omits generated degree-97 through degree-192 source terms and requires their nonzero residual to survive. This is software evidence, not a canonical variational correction. Section 17 evaluates the first canonical panel; a resource-admitted full interval remains pending.

docs.title: 17. Canonical first-panel construction and result
docs.text:
The bounded evaluation fixes the first normalized-clock panel [0,16], the same C1024, m=1/2 reference, degree 96, and zero initial correction. The input builder prepares its own authoritative finite-input closure and encloses all 97 Lobatto samples. The shared transform uses ordinary Chebyshev coefficients, including the full constant term:

\[ a_k=\frac{2w_k}{d}\sum_{j=0}^d w_j f_j\cos(kj\pi/d), \qquad w_0=w_d=1/2,\quad w_j=1\ (0<j<d). \tag{99} \]

Dyadic integer center/radius dot products enclose every signed sum before one final interval projection per coefficient. Sampling uncertainty and transform roundoff remain in the coefficient boxes; the analytic tails (96) remain separate. A finite sampled polynomial alone supplies no such between-node tail for an arbitrary function.

docs.title: A proposal method with independent posterior validation
docs.text:
For a degree-d row f, define B_d f as its antiderivative projected to degree d and re-centered to vanish at s=-1. Its retained coefficients are b_1=f_0-f_2/2, b_j=(f_(j-1)-f_(j+1))/(2j) for 2<=j<=d, and b_0=-sum_(j=1)^d (-1)^j b_j, with unavailable coefficients zero. For d=1, the first formula gives b_1=f_0. The discarded exact-integral term is f_d*(T_(d+1)-(-1)^(d+1)T_0)/(2(d+1)). Its derivative is part of the posterior equation defect; projecting the proposal does not delete it from validation.

Let q=sqrt(1-sigma^2/4), alpha=sigma/2+iq and mu=-sigma/2+iq. The complex encoding psi=x+alpha*theta gives psi'=mu*A*psi for the constant tangent, since mu*alpha=-1. The inverse is theta=Im(psi)/q, x=Re(psi)-(sigma/2)*theta. A full complex spatial FFT retains all 2N real coordinates; no same-mode conjugacy or half-spectrum omission is imposed. For cycle eigenvalue lambda_j=1-cos(2*pi*j/N), factor the temporal matrix

\[ I-(\Delta/2)\lambda_j\mu B_d. \tag{100} \]

There are at most N/2 distinct nonzero factors on the even cycle. These small temporal matrices are separate from a dense full-state generator. Pivoted factorization avoids dividing by a frequency difference. Reuse the factors for the signed source solve and twenty fixed feedback updates. Each feedback product is evaluated with 2d+1 Lobatto points, retaining its degree-2d polynomial before projecting the next proposal to degree d.

The candidate owner uses this finite iteration count as a proposal policy. The exact-Volterra contraction and insertion tail in section 16 do not certify the projected iteration or its floating arithmetic. Binary64 produces only candidate coefficients; re-admit their represented values as exact rationals and set their constant coefficients so the proposed initial state is exactly zero. The independent outward validator then reconstructs both signed equation rows, all degree-192 products and the real full-state norm. Its acceptance depends on that rebuilt defect, not a solver tolerance or iteration delta.

The prospective local policy is P<=2^35, R<=2^-54 and initial endpoint enclosure norm at most 2^-70, with the separate analytic input errors in (96). Record input, proposal and validation costs separately. Keep the first outcome, including failure, without changing the profile, degree, iteration count, precision or panel after observing it. This local gate does not evaluate the rest of T, its joins, a nonlinear bootstrap or a source-to-composite response. A full-interval cost estimate is a resource assessment, not a prediction that later panels will pass.

docs.title: Retained local result and cost boundary
docs.text:
The frozen protocol declares this single evaluation before its response. The freeze, source manifest and source archive associate the evaluator, runtime and pre-evaluation proof bytes. They do not authenticate chronology or execution. The first attempt is preserved with its primitive response and result.

The numerical policy passes on this panel. Rounded-up decimal bounds are:

Whole-panel quantity Upper bound Candidate full-state norm P 9.913e-6 Complete polynomial defect norm R 3.005e-21 Integrated defect, including analytic input tails 4.808e-20 Initial enclosure norm 4.145e-36 Finite-input correction error, 512*(initial + integrated defect) 2.462e-17

The candidate has exactly zero initial state as rational coefficients; the small enclosure width is nevertheless charged to the error allowance. All degree-192 terms remain in the residual. The last row bounds error to the finite-input linear correction on [0,16], conditional on the retained input enclosures and section 16's analytic tails. It does not include the earlier exact-model input truncation allowances in (88), and is not an error bound for a nonlinear trajectory. The source and edge coefficient-radius summaries are respectively below 8.858e-33 and 1.527e-35; these are arithmetic widths, not the analytic input tails.

The resource policy fails its input threshold: preparation took 666.814 s against 600 s. Of that cost, sampling took 648.298 s and interpolation 16.842 s. The proposal took 5.521 s and interval validation 37.433 s, within their respective 180 s and 120 s thresholds. Total recorded time, including artifact I/O, was 713.873 s. The thresholds assess the completed attempt; they are not abort timers or mathematical restrictions on the law. The length-sixteen grid, with a shortened last panel, has 8,988 panels over the exact horizon. Repeating this observed total cost would take about 74.3 sequential days; this is a conditional cost extrapolation, not a runtime bound or evidence that later panels satisfy the numerical policy.

The input controls check canonical preparation, clocks, interpolation and separate error channels. The candidate controls compare independent dense small-cycle equations, retain all spatial modes and reject equating a projected fixed point with zero continuous defect. The evidence audit checks archive associations and re-admits primitive coefficients to rebuild the signed defect and verdict without running any canonical producer. It does not independently regenerate the retained sample enclosures.

This closes one local construction and its numerical assessment. The retained first attempt starts at zero; repeating that preparation would reset the correction and would not solve the full-interval problem. The maintained input reuse and carried-state construction below are separate implementation improvements. Initial mismatches, join defects and every panel's signed residual must share (91)'s budget. The deferred-dependency contract in the sole execution plan owns reactivation and further admission. No whole-horizon correction, nonlinear maintenance, composite acquisition or physical identification follows from this panel.

docs.title: Exact endpoint carry without resetting accumulated error
docs.text:
The maintained candidate owner also accepts two incoming scalar rows. It admits their exact or represented values before numerical work; an uncertain interval is not an incoming point. Add the full spatial Fourier transform of psi_0=x_0+alpha*theta_0 to the constant temporal coefficient on the right-hand side of (100). The same modal factors and twenty feedback updates then propose the carried panel. The zero-initial entry point delegates to this constructor and preserves its declared preparation.

After admitting the proposed tail coefficients as rationals, set a_0=y_0-sum_(k=1)^d (-1)^k*a_k separately in each row. Thus the left endpoint is exactly the supplied y_0 even when its rational representation is not binary64. Carrying the preceding polynomial's exact rational right endpoint sum_k a_k makes the mathematical join exactly zero. An interval midpoint or a rounded endpoint is a different preparation whose mismatch must be charged; overlapping endpoint boxes do not prove a zero join.

This does not make the incoming approximation equal to the true solution. Equation (91) retains its existing global error and applies gain 512 once to initial error plus all integrated defects and join norms. Neither a restart nor repeated multiplication of that gain is justified. Independent small-system controls check both real rows, nonzero means, homogeneous damped transport and two-panel joins. They do not evaluate a second canonical panel or admit its precision.

docs.title: Input-reuse cost pilot and result
docs.text:
The implementation pilot keeps the first panel, all 97 sampling locations, degree 96 and the analytic input errors fixed. It builds only the optimized source and edge interpolants, then revalidates the exact candidate already stored in the first response. No candidate generator, old frozen producer or nonlinear trajectory is executed. Reusing those coefficients tests changed input arithmetic without generating a new scientific response or rewriting the first outcome.

The numerical policy remains P<=2^35, R<=2^-54, exact zero initial state and initial enclosure norm at most 2^-70. The prospective local resource thresholds are 180 s for inputs and 120 s for validation. Retain the first outcome without automatic retries. Report cold preparation, sampling and transformation separately. An explicit full-grid resource scenario uses at most 24 sequential hours and 8 GiB of retained artifacts as engineering policies, not dynamical hypotheses. Its time extrapolation combines the new input/validation measurements with the old proposal cost; its storage extrapolation uses the original per-panel response size. Neither is a bound or a full-run admission. Repeated all-panel snapshots and simultaneous allocation of the whole coefficient history are not required by (91); a future storage design must retain auditable primitives and checkpoints within a declared budget.

The separate protocol, freeze, source manifest and source archive retain this implementation and associate all eight previous evidence files. Its first response and report pass every local numerical and resource check. The same retained candidate still has finite-input correction error below 2.462e-17 on [0,16]. This is a revalidation of its existing polynomial, not a newly generated variational response or an improvement to the physical model.

Measured phase Original attempt (s) Input-reuse pilot (s) Complete input construction 666.814 109.466 Input sampling 648.298 90.324 Input interpolation 16.842 15.548 Complete interval validation 37.433 36.908

Complete input construction is about 6.09 times faster in these recorded runs. The new cold factory cost is 2.042 s, including preparation of the 100,352 encoded spatial entries; the cached basis uses three integers per entry. Its memory tradeoff is explicit. Different process conditions may change these timings; the single retained comparison is not a universal speed guarantee. The pilot's 150.687 s total excludes candidate generation, so it is not directly comparable to the original complete-attempt total.

The mixed-cost full-grid scenario still gives about 15.80 sequential days before artifact I/O and 59.16 GiB at the original response size. Both exceed their stated 24-hour and 8-GiB engineering policies. The new archive omits the reused candidate and must not be used as a complete per-panel storage estimate. Input sampling remains material; transformation, validation and evidence storage also need explicit treatment before a full run. The read-only audit checks the two evidence associations and rebuilds the complete signed defect and policy assessments from retained primitive coefficients. It does not regenerate inputs, candidates or old responses.

docs.title: 18. Admission result and execution boundary
docs.text:
The original symmetry and separated carrier energies do not supply a discriminating formation mechanism. Positive curvature at an exact lower carrier supplies a concrete phase-sensitive envelope balance, generated harmonics and a conditional complete-law validation method. This identifies a candidate nonlinear retention relation needing a separate preparation. The coarse acute-chart method is excluded on a full nonlinear phase time, so a different proved stability or residual treatment is needed before a quantitative retention certificate. Equations (25)--(35) now give a complete-law relative-storage comparison with explicit means, metric positivity, moving coefficients, residuals and positive loss. The carrier resonance and small-divisor calculation require retaining a near-resonant block; exact-resonance-only cancellation is not uniformly a small positive correction. This resolves a method-admission question, not its quantitative use for a localized reference. Equations (40)--(44) now supply uniform profile, retained-block and moving-metric bounds. The specified scalar defect allowance prevents a full phase-time certificate even if all other growth is suppressed; sharpening resonance constants or source precision cannot resolve this particular failure. Equations (49)--(63) provide a different treatment: signed two-row harmonic transport, explicit aliases and tails, a response-corrected reference and a full Euclidean comparison without spectral-gap amplification. Its transported-defect and nonlinear budgets still need a quantitative closure before any maintenance claim. The canonical-profile preflight (64)--(72) now excludes the specified positive coefficient-norm implementation of that comparison before a coefficient or trajectory campaign. Signed phase transport and nonlinear work correlations remain unassessed by this obstruction. The full variational comparison now has a finite phase-resolved representation with explicit profile, Jacobian, source and chronological tails, whose combined analytical error is below 2^-48 on the fixed phase interval. Its finite inputs and sparse action have a shared private implementation. The Chebyshev panel validator now retains the signed continuous defect and all generated degrees, with explicit uniform input interpolation bounds. Raising the general comparison solver's dimension cap would lose the cancellations, and the admitted direct Taylor realization has excessive work for this route. The first canonical panel now passes its numerical policy, while its input construction exceeds the local cost threshold. Shared signed input arithmetic and exact nonzero endpoint carry now have maintained implementations. The separate reuse pilot passes its local policies, while its full-grid time/storage scenario still fails. Full-interval resource admission and a canonical joined correction remain unresolved. Their reactivation conditions belong to the sole execution plan; the calculation is deferred, with its shared implementations and frozen evidence retained. The whole-horizon correction and nonlinear maintenance bound remain unevaluated. No result here proves that two patterns acquire the relation.

The static controls derive the local balance, cubic harmonics, correctors and envelope identities independently. The relative-storage controls check the two-row balance, missing means, coercivity, resonant production and small-divisor obstruction. The periodic-bound controls check derivative budgets and the scalar-defect exclusion. The phase-defect controls check actual-loss modal transport, two-row projection, aliases, signed convolutions, correction residuals and full-state metric identities. The defect-budget controls check the independent profile averages, source-moment condition, resolvent floor and strict rational obstruction, including its distinction from an actual oscillatory response. The variational controls check chronological order, coupled-mode structure, resonance limits, factorial and coefficient tails, propagation gains and separated input errors. Their arithmetic controls reuse the existing positive-series tail owner; they do not instantiate the large finite variational sum. The finite-input controls check independent reconstruction derivatives, sparse actions, scalar and clock admission, the declared three-point arithmetic preflight and the distinction between samples and a continuous residual certificate. They execute neither a trajectory nor frozen evidence. The actual rate implementation remains the shared sine owner; transport and nonlinear budgets retain their shared comparison owner. No envelope runtime or replacement nodal law is installed. Quantitative maintenance, a source-to-composite experiment and physical identification remain separate obligations in the sole execution plan.

docs.title: Same-band source admission and regional work
docs.text: Scope: a bounded two-lobe preparation on one carrier band, a geometric screen absent throughout that source class, an exact necessary screen-work condition, and a strictly signed nominal nonlinear rate distinction between resource-matched initial controls. A lobe is a region of concentrated full-state amplitude; a chosen sum does not supply independent dynamical constituents or an NFR identity. This is analytical admission, not an evaluated trajectory, formation result or physical identification. The research program owns this branch's status and any later response evaluation.

docs.title: 1. Complete state and a bounded one-carrier preparation
docs.text:
Retain the complete C1024 law, with unit conductances and lengths, held unit capacities, beta one, no input or support event, and the supplied real lift of primitive circular phase. Write x=EPI, z=x+i*theta, (Dq)_j=q_(j+1)-q_j for cycle incidence, L=D^T D and A=L/2. The bookkeeping complex field retains two real rows:

\[ x'=-\sigma Ax-\tfrac12D^T\sin(D\theta),\qquad \theta'=Ax,\qquad \tau=wt/\pi,\quad w=1-2^{-20},\quad \sigma=\pi2^{-20}/w>0. \tag{1} \]

The prime denotes the fixed normalized clock. Carrier phase is not primitive phase, and |z|^2=x^2+theta^2 is a localization diagnostic rather than local structural storage. The full state, including generated modes and error means, remains retained. Neither this preparation nor a Fourier observation closes the dynamics on one band.

Set N=1024, Q=16, k=pi/4, a=2^-12 and delta=a/1000. Reuse the Fejer normalization and tail bound only, without transferring the earlier carrier's transport certificate:

\[ b_m=1-|m|/16\quad (|m|<16),\qquad S_2=171/16, \qquad f(j)=\frac{\sum_{|m|<16}b_m e^{2\pi imj/N}}{\sqrt{NS_2}}. \tag{2} \]

The profile is real, nonnegative, even, periodic and unit-normalized. For each supplied psi in [-pi,pi], define the preparation class

\[ z_\psi^0(j)=a e^{ikj}[f(j)+e^{i\psi}f(j-512)],\qquad z(0)=z_\psi^0+r,\qquad \|r\|_2\le\delta. \tag{3} \]

The primitive form is the real part of (3), and its imaginary part is the supplied real phase lift. Explicitly, their nominal values are a[f(j)cos(kj)+f(j-512)cos(kj+psi)] and a[f(j)sin(kj)+f(j-512)sin(kj+psi)]. The two terms are preparation labels on the same band, modes 113 through 143. There are no independent band projections that recover them from an evolved total field.

The exact initial overlap and norm are

\[ s=\langle f,f(\cdot-512)\rangle =\frac{\sum_m b_m^2(-1)^m}{S_2}=\frac1{171},\qquad \|z_\psi^0\|_2^2=2a^2(1+s\cos\psi). \tag{4} \]

Indeed the numerator of the overlap is 1/16, while the squared-weight sum is 171/16. Thus changing relative phase at fixed component amplitude does not generally hold total norm fixed. Arbitrary errors are retained, not projected onto the nominal band. The triangle inequality gives

\[ a\sqrt{340/171}-\delta\le\|z(0)\|_2 \le a\sqrt{344/171}+\delta, \qquad \frac{1409}{1000}a<\|z(0)\|_2<\frac32a. \tag{5} \]

Since ||f||_infinity=2/sqrt(171), primitive admission also gives

\[ \|z(0)\|_\infty\le a(4/\sqrt{171}+1/1000)<a/3, \qquad |D\theta(0)|<2a/3=1/6144<\pi/2. \tag{6} \]

The nominal mean vanishes because the band omits zero. Error means remain: |mean z(0)|<=delta/sqrt(N)=a/32000. Equation (1) conserves both real means; it does not set them to zero.

The exact structural storage and initial bounds are

\[ H=\tfrac12\|Dx\|_2^2+\sum_j[1-\cos(D\theta)_j],\qquad H'=-\tfrac\sigma2\|Lx\|_2^2, \qquad 0\le H(0)\le\tfrac12\|Dz(0)\|_2^2<\tfrac92a^2<1. \tag{7} \]

The bound uses 1-cos u<=u^2/2 and ||D||_2<=2. Together with the initially acute lift, the storage balance prevents a first edge crossing of +/-pi/2, which would contribute one to H. This familiar chart bound does not preserve the initial localization or full-state norm, and does not prove organization.

docs.title: 2. A total-field concentration screen initially absent
docs.text:
For a real observation center c on the unit-length cycle, let W(c,96) be the radius-96 ball. Let W_1=W(0,96) and W_2=W(512,96). The reused spatial-tail inequality gives, for each shifted unit profile,

\[ \|\mathbf1_{W_i^c}f_i\|_2^2\le b:=\frac{1024^3}{16\cdot16^3\cdot95^3} =\frac{16384}{857375}<\frac1{49}. \tag{8} \]

The nominal components are not disjoint, but both initial lobes have a nonvanishing regional signal even with arbitrary allowed error and phase:

\[ \|\mathbf1_{W_i}z(0)\|_2 \ge a[\sqrt{1-b}-\sqrt b]-\delta>\frac45a. \tag{9} \]

Here the other lobe contributes at most a*sqrt(b) because the two source windows are disjoint. Outside their union, ||1_(W_1 union W_2)^c z(0)||_2<=2a*sqrt(b)+delta<3a/10. These inequalities describe two separated concentrations, without assigning them unique constituent identities under future overlap or deformation.

The proposed common-window screen requires ||z||_2>=a and one radius-96 window containing at least 3/4 of the total squared norm. It is a geometric prerequisite for a narrower possible organization, not a complete relational identity. It does not consume independent component projections.

For every c, at least one source center is at cycle distance at least 256. Since 256>96+96, W(c,96) misses that source window. Its component contribution is therefore at most a*sqrt(b); the other component's full norm is a. Equations (5) and (8) imply

\[ \frac{\|\mathbf1_{W(c,96)}z(0)\|_2^2}{\|z(0)\|_2^2} \le\left(\frac{1+\sqrt b+1/1000} {\sqrt{340/171}-1/1000}\right)^2 <\left(\frac{8007}{9863}\right)^2<\frac23. \tag{10} \]

Thus the 3/4 concentration requirement fails with margin greater than 1/12 for every center, phase and member of the source-error ball. The signal floor holds independently by (5), and the cycle triangle inequality also covers fractional centers. This is a fresh same-band total-field argument; the previous disjoint-band absence test has not been reused.

Later entry into this screen could occur by ordinary interference or dispersion, and by itself would not establish acquisition, retention or a collective response. A two-lobed organization wider than this screen is not excluded by its failure. The formation contract still requires a retained relation, a justified lifetime and a discriminating response on the continued full state.

docs.title: 3. Exactly matched initial resources without deleting phase
docs.text:
Equal component amplitudes do not match total norm across arbitrary psi, by (4). They do not match exact H either. The quadratic storage comparison is H_2=||Dz||_2^2/2, and

\[ 0\le H_2-H\le\frac1{24}\sum_j(D\theta)_j^4. \tag{11} \]

Replacing exact H by this comparison would discard a phase-dependent remainder. Rescaling amplitudes to match norm alone supplies another preparation and does not certify matched storage or initial loss.

A useful matched pair is instead +psi and -psi. Let (Jq)_j=q_(-j) and define the real-linear isometry

\[ \mathcal S(x,\theta)=(Jx,-J\theta),\qquad (\mathcal S z)_j=\overline{z_{-j}}. \tag{12} \]

Evenness of f and its antipodal shift gives S z_psi^0=z_(-psi)^0. Pair errors by r_(-psi)=S r_psi; independently chosen errors of equal norm need not match resources. For forward edge index j, put (J_e q)_j=q_(-j-1), y=Dx and u=Dtheta. Then

\[ y(\mathcal S z)=-J_e y(z),\qquad u(\mathcal S z)=J_e u(z),\qquad h_j=\tfrac12y_j^2+1-\cos u_j. \tag{13} \]

Consequently the paired full preparations have exactly equal norm, total H and ||Lx||_2^2, hence equal initial global loss. Pointwise localization and edge storage are reflected. For an edge subset E, H_E(Sz)=H_(J_e E)(z); a same-region comparison requires J_e E=E, otherwise its reflected region must be paired explicitly. Means are conjugated, including the retained error means, rather than erased. No fitted amplitude or hidden reservoir is involved.

The map S is not a positive-time symmetry of (1). It matches initial resources while changing the allocation of signed form and phase, whose actual subsequent rows must be evaluated separately. Reflection J alone is a graph symmetry; adding phase reversal changes this conclusion. The paired source classes establish a valid initial control, not equality of their future trajectories or a sign for future regional work.

docs.title: 4. A necessary prefix-work condition for the absent screen
docs.text:
The concentration diagnostic and structural storage are different observations. A positive local storage rate alone cannot establish entry into (10). Fix a node window W, put P_W=diag(1_W), alpha=3/4 and B_W=P_W-alpha*I, and retain the quadratic screen gap

\[ V_W(z)=x^TB_Wx+\theta^TB_W\theta =\|P_Wz\|_2^2-\alpha\|z\|_2^2. \tag{14} \]

Screen entry in that window requires V_W>=0 and the separate signal floor ||z||_2>=a. For every admitted source, (10) gives V_W(z(0))<-||z(0)||_2^2/12. No regional-storage bound was substituted for that initial diagnostic margin.

Differentiate (14) using both actual rows in (1). With u=Dtheta,

\[ \begin{split} V_W'&=\mathcal L_W(z)+\mathcal N_W(z),\\ \mathcal L_W(z) &=-2\sigma x^TB_WAx+2\theta^T(B_WA-AB_W)x,\\ \mathcal N_W(z)&=(DB_Wx)^T(u-\sin u). \end{split} \tag{15} \]

Here L_W is the rate under the actual damped linear tangent evaluated at the same full state, not a nonnegative loss estimate. A restricted quadratic observation has boundary transport and can grow even while global structural storage decreases. N_W is the exact nonlinear rate insertion relative to that tangent. Its cubic-sine comparison is

\[ \mathcal N_{W,3}=\tfrac16(DB_Wx)^Tu^{\circ3},\qquad |\mathcal N_W-\mathcal N_{W,3}| \le\tfrac1{120}\sum_j |(DB_Wx)_j|\,|u_j|^5. \tag{16} \]

The elementwise cube is not an envelope equation. Under joint amplitude scaling this leading rate is fourth order; the remainder is sixth order. Both still consume full form, primitive phase and the selected boundary. The sine Taylor remainder proves (16) globally on real lifts.

If a solution first satisfies the screen in W at a time T, necessarily

\[ \int_0^T [\mathcal L_W(z(\tau))+\mathcal N_W(z(\tau))]\,d\tau \ge -V_W(z(0))>\frac{\|z(0)\|_2^2}{12}. \tag{17} \]

This is a source-dependent necessary condition, not a sufficient entry criterion. For entry in any radius-96 window, apply (17) to the successful window held fixed over the prefix; its initial absence holds for every center. A moving-window rate or continued moving identity requires its own membership transport. The norm floor and later maintenance remain separate obligations.

If W is invariant under node reflection, B_W commutes with J. Equation (13) then gives

\[ V_W(\mathcal Sz)=V_W(z),\qquad \mathcal N_W(\mathcal Sz)=-\mathcal N_W(z). \tag{18} \]

The dissipative contribution in L_W is unchanged and its conservative commutator contribution changes sign. Thus relative-phase allocation can change the linear part of the same criterion as well. Equation (18) does not prove that N_W is nonzero on a particular source or stays signed along its future evolution.

docs.title: 5. Structural regional work and its nonlinear rate insertion
docs.text:
The existing exact local storage balance uses L_e=DD^T, y=Dx, u=Dtheta and

\[ F_{jk}=\tfrac12(\sin u_j\,y_k-y_j\sin u_k) +\tfrac\sigma4(y_j^2-y_k^2)=-F_{kj}. \]

For a fixed edge subset E define

\[ \begin{split} H_E&=\sum_{j\in E}(y_j^2/2+1-\cos u_j),\\ I_E&=-\sum_{j\in E,\,k\notin E,\,k\sim j}F_{jk},\\ D_E&=\tfrac\sigma4\sum_{j\in E}\sum_{k\sim j}(y_j-y_k)^2. \end{split} \qquad H_E'=I_E-D_E. \tag{19} \]

An internal edge pair appears twice in the local-loss sum, as required by the local balance. Taking E to be the full edge set gives the global loss in (7). The inward current is signed; neither it nor a global loss budget is an event reserve or a guarantee of acquisition.

For comparison, use the same structural H_E and the damped tangent

\[ x'_{\rm lin}=-\sigma Ax-A\theta,\qquad \theta'_{\rm lin}=Ax. \tag{20} \]

This tangent is real-linear in the two state channels. Its positive-loss term acts on form, so a uniform complex carrier rotation does not generally commute with its propagator. Each phase preparation must retain both rows; rotating one precomputed history is not an exact control for another.

At an identical supplied full state their derivative difference is

\[ G_E(z):=\left.\frac{dH_E}{d\tau}\right|_{F_\sigma(z)} -\left.\frac{dH_E}{d\tau}\right|_{J_\sigma z} =\tfrac12(P_Ey)^TL_e(u-\sin u),\qquad P_E=\operatorname{diag}(1_E). \tag{21} \]

Only the form-rate difference contributes because the phase rows agree. This exact instantaneous insertion is not H_E(joint)-H_E(A)-H_E(B) and not an endpoint difference between evolved histories. Its leading term and remainder are
