docs.text:
The real derivative bounds from (1) are

\[ J_0=\frac{1459}{1458}<\frac{1001}{1000},\quad J_1=\frac{245}{243}<\frac{101}{100},\quad J_2=\frac{10}{9},\quad J_3=\frac83, \qquad |j^{(r)}|\le J_r\quad(0\le r\le3). \tag{5} \]

Let D be the forward C5 incidence, L5=D^T D and \(P=I-\mathbf1\mathbf1^T/5\). Define

\[ \begin{split} c_b&=\cos b=\frac{\sqrt5-1}{4},& a&=j'(b)=c_b+\frac{\sqrt5}{486},\\ A&=aL_5,&G&=A^+,& \lambda_1&=a(2-2\cos b),& \lambda_2&=a(2-2\cos2b). \end{split} \tag{6} \]

G acts on the zero-mean host space. The elementary bounds \(3/10<c_b<1/3\) give \(\lambda_1>2/5\); also \(a<8/25\) and \(2-2c_b<7/5\) give \(\lambda_1<9/20\). The bound a<8/25 follows, for example, from \(c_b<5/16\) and \(\sqrt5/486<1/216\). Consequently \(\|G\|_2<5/2\), and \(\|D\|_2<2\).

On the internal carrier q=0, ground the donor phase at zero and seek host phases \(t+b_c+u_c\), with zero-mean u. The four projected stationary equations are exactly

\[ \begin{split} u&=-G\{D^TN(Du)+\eta Pj(t+b+u)\}=:\mathcal K_t(u),\\ N(d)&=j(b+d)-j(b)-a d. \end{split} \tag{7} \]

The scalar b in N is the rim gap; the b inside the vector current is \((b_c)_{c=0}^4\). All current derivatives below are evaluated on real arguments. Since \(|N(d)|\le J_2d^2/2\), the map satisfies on \(\|u\|_2\le6\eta\)

\[ \begin{split} \|\mathcal K_t(u)\|_2 &\le\frac52\left[4J_2(6\eta)^2+ \eta\sqrt5\frac{1001}{1000}\right]<6\eta,\\ \|D_u\mathcal K_t\|_2 &\le Q:=\frac52\left[48J_2+\frac{101}{100}\right]\eta =\frac{16303}{12000000}<\frac1{500}. \end{split} \tag{8} \]

The bounds use \(\|D^TN(Du)\|_2\le4J_2\|u\|_2^2\) and \(\|D^T\operatorname{diag}(N'(Du))D\|_2\le8J_2\|u\|_2\). Thus, for every real t, there is exactly one projected stationary shape u(t) in the declared host ball. It is smooth in t by the invertible projected derivative. This is an own-law real contraction; the complex growth bounds of the sine current are not reused.

Write \(f(t)=j(t+b)\), \(u_1(t)=-Gf(t)\). Each active frequency 1, 9 and 18 has zero sum on the five host vertices. Direct subtraction of (7) and differentiation in t give

\[ \begin{split} \|u-\eta u_1\|_2 &\le\frac52\left[4J_2\,36+6\frac{101}{100}\right]\eta^2 <416\eta^2,\\ \|u_t\|_2 &\le\frac{(5/2)\sqrt5(101/100)}{1-Q}\eta<6\eta,\\ \|u_t-\eta u_{1,t}\|_2 &\le\frac52\left[8J_2\,36+6J_2+6\frac{101}{100}\right]\eta^2 <832\eta^2. \end{split} \tag{9} \]

In the last line, retain separately the rim derivative defect, \(\eta[j'(t+b+u)-j'(t+b)]\), and \(\eta\operatorname{diag}(j'(t+b+u))u_t\). These terms are what bound the derivative of the actual shape, rather than just its values.

docs.title: 3. Collective torque and its finite C1 remainder
docs.text:
Let W(t) be the alternative wheel potential evaluated at its projected stationary shape. The remaining stationary equation is

\[ T(t)=W'(t)=\eta\sum_{c=0}^4j(t+b_c+u_c(t))=0. \tag{10} \]

Cyclic relabeling makes W and T periodic with period 2*pi/5. Reflection and phase inversion make W even and T odd. Both claims use uniqueness of the shape in (8), as well as the actual symmetries of (1). Therefore \(T(m\pi/5)=0\) exactly for every integer m. Symmetry alone does not determine their curvature.

Put \(\varepsilon=1/2187\). The five-point Fourier identities give

\[ \begin{split} f^TGf &=\frac5{2\lambda_1} [1+\varepsilon^2-2\varepsilon\cos(10t)] +\frac{5\varepsilon^2}{8\lambda_2},\\ \sum_cj'(t+b_c)u_{1,c} &=-\frac12\frac d{dt}(f^TGf) =-K\sin(10t),\qquad K=\frac{25}{2187\lambda_1}>\frac1{40}. \end{split} \tag{11} \]

Indeed the ninth harmonic is spatially mode minus one on this rim, whereas the eighteenth is mode minus two. Only frequencies 1 and 9 have a nonconstant cross term in f^TGf; their inner product is \(-5\cos(10t)/2\). The eighteenth-harmonic square contributes the constant last term. Equation (11) is an exact coefficient identity, not yet a finite-eta verdict.

Taylor's formula, (5) and (9) bound the actual torque and its derivative:

\[ \begin{split} |T(t)+K\eta^2\sin(10t)|&<960\eta^3,\\ |T'(t)+10K\eta^2\cos(10t)|&<3001\eta^3, \qquad t\in\mathbb R. \end{split} \tag{12} \]

Here are explicit constants for both remainders:

\[ \begin{split} C_0&=\sqrt5\frac{101}{100}\,416+ \frac{J_2}{2}\,36<960,\\ C_1&=\sqrt5\left(J_2\,416+\frac{101}{100}\,832\right) +\frac{J_3}{2}\,36+J_2\,36<3001. \end{split} \tag{13} \]

The rational upper bound \(\sqrt5<161/72\), obtained from \(161^2-5\,72^2=1\), proves the displayed strict inequalities. For C0, subtract the exact linear term and use the actual current's quadratic J2 Taylor remainder. For C1, expand \(j'(t+b+u)(1+u_t)\): the two linear defects use 416 and 832, the second-order j' remainder contributes \(J_3\|u\|^2/2\), and the product \([j'(t+b+u)-j'(t+b)]u_t\) contributes \(J_2\|u\|\|u_t\|\). No unbounded derivative of a remainder is inferred from a value estimate.

docs.title: 4. Twenty stationary registrations in the declared domain
docs.text:
On the relative-origin circle, let

\[ I_k=\left[\frac{k\pi}{10}-\frac\pi{60}, \frac{k\pi}{10}+\frac\pi{60}\right], \qquad k=0,\ldots,19. \tag{14} \]

These intervals are disjoint. At their endpoints and everywhere outside their interiors, \(|\sin(10t)|\ge1/2\). The leading torque magnitude there exceeds \(\eta^2/80\), while its error is at most \(960\eta^3=0.0096\eta^2<\eta^2/80\). It has opposite signs at the two endpoints of every interval and no zeros outside the intervals.

Within I_k, \(|\cos(10t)|\ge\sqrt3/2>4/5\), and its sign is \((-1)^k\). The leading derivative magnitude exceeds \(\eta^2/5\), while its error is at most \(3001\eta^3=0.03001\eta^2<\eta^2/5\). Thus the actual torque is strictly monotone in each interval and has exactly one simple zero there.

For even k, the zero is exactly \(t=k\pi/10=m\pi/5\), by the symmetry already proved. Its derivative is negative. For odd k, the unique zero in I_k has positive derivative. The proof does not assign its exact position or assert that it differs from its interval center. There are exactly ten of each type.

The four host shape directions have positive curvature. In fact the rim weights in the domain satisfy the lower bound proved in section 5, so the host shape block exceeds \(L_5/4-\eta J_1I>I/5\). Eliminating that block gives the scalar Schur complement W''=T'. Consequently the wheel relative Hessian is positive definite at the ten odd-interval zeros, and has four positive directions and one negative direction at the ten exact even-interval zeros.

docs.title: 5. Full-state stationary exclusion and stability
docs.text:
The full fine directions cannot create additional stationary points inside (4). To prove this for the actual alternative, let \(C_6(v)=1-v^2/2+v^4/24-v^6/720\). Along the straight segment from the carrier phases to any q in (4), compatible internal gaps obey \(|\delta|<18/25\), and rim gaps obey \(0<\delta<13/10\). For example, \(\pi<22/7\) gives \(\alpha+1/50<18/25\) and \(b+12\eta+1/50<13/10\). Since \(j'(\delta)\ge\cos\delta-2/243\), exact rational cosine bounds give

\[ C_6(18/25)- rac2{243}> rac7{10},\qquad C_6(13/10)- rac2{243}> rac14. ag{15} \]

Spoke curvatures may be negative, but are bounded below by -J1. Let P_f subtract each child's slot mean. On its 48-dimensional range, the internal C9 Laplacian has gap greater than 2/5, while the largest eigenvalue of the nine disjoint spoke stars is six. Every Hessian along that segment therefore satisfies

\[ P_{ m f} abla^2U P_{ m f} ig|_{\operatorname{ran}P_{ m f}} >\left[ rac7{10} rac25-6\eta rac{245}{243} ight]I = rac{226751}{810000}I> rac14I. ag{16} \]

For any collective phases, the carrier has \(P_{ m f} abla U=0\): internal currents cancel and wheel currents are constant in the slot. Integrating (16) consequently gives \(q^TP_{ m f} abla U( heta)>\|q\|^2/4\) for nonzero q.

At a full equilibrium, the phase row in (2), connected support and zero total form first force x=0. The form row then forces \( abla U=0\), which by (16) forces q=0. The projected host equation and contraction force h=u(t). Thus all full stationary states in (4) are exactly the twenty wheel equilibria already classified; noncarrier directions were retained and excluded by their own-law curvature, rather than discarded before testing stationarity.

At a carrier, \(j'(\alpha)=\cos\alpha\) exactly. In slot-first order the phase Hessian has the product form

\[ M_{54}=\cos\alpha\,L_9\otimes I_6+I_9\otimes M_{ m wheel}. ag{17} \]

The 48 fine directions remain positive by (16), while the five relative collective directions have the inertia from section 4. The ten minima therefore have 53 positive relative phase directions. The ten saddles have 52 positive directions and one negative direction, with no extra zero direction besides common phase rotation.

This phase curvature controls the actual complete two-row dynamics. On the relative space its own linearization has the symmetric pencil

\[ s^2L_\eta^{-1}+ rac s4I+ rac{\gamma^2}{16}M_{54}. ag{18} \]

For a positive phase Hessian, the scalar quadratic identity obtained by testing an eigenvector has all roots with negative real part. For an index-one Hessian, the pencil increases strictly for positive real s from one negative direction to a positive matrix, giving exactly one positive eigenvalue. The imaginary part of the same scalar identity excludes nonreal eigenvalues with nonnegative real part; invertibility of the relative Hessian excludes s=0. All remaining eigenvalues have negative real part. Thus the ten minima are locally exponentially attracting on fixed-mean leaves, and the other ten are hyperbolic index-one saddles of the full law.

docs.title: 6. The unchanged own-law source enters a full-state trap
docs.text:
Keep the original outer-one family from the retained alternative acquisition, its complete alternative-law observation history, and the independently recovered donor from that same owner. The twelve primitive form/phase error allowances stay in [0,1e-10], with all 96 relative directions and their original zero-sum constraints. The donor origin beta is supplied at primitive preparation. Its isolated rotation does not change its relative recovery trajectory.

All acquisition times, recovery dwells, commands and observation windows are unchanged. In particular the full fifteen-event word precedes contact; its final cumulative command vanishes, while every continuous drift and form change remains. Only the 45 new spoke weights are changed to eta in the subsequently supplied contact model (2). The earlier unit-contact observations and frozen responses are neither reused as weak-contact predictions nor re-evaluated.

Write

\[ V_9=9V(\alpha)=9(1-\cos\alpha),\qquad V_5=5V(b),\qquad V_*=6V_9+9V_5. \tag{19} \]

The retained own-law acquisition inequalities give host excess above 5V9+9V5 below 0.009588 and its product-cell boundary excess B above 0.01451. These are existing strict rational summaries of the preserved source evidence, not newly evaluated endpoints. The same cycle-boundary formula applies after adding the donor C9: the old cycles now comprise six C9 and nine C5 cycles, with unchanged old edge weights.

docs.title: 6.1 Observation drift and new contact work remain explicit
docs.text:
For a fresh analytical upper bound \(\bar\gamma=1/3000>\gamma\), put X=1/100 and T_o=1/5000. The own-law current bound J0 in (5) gives

\[ \begin{split} B_o&=X+\bar\gamma J_0T_o<\frac{101}{10000},\\ d_x&=(2B_o+\bar\gamma J_0)T_o<\frac1{200000},\\ m_o&=2\bar\gamma B_oT_o<\frac1{500000000}. \end{split} \tag{20} \]

Heat contraction bounds every host form during the word by B_o; its degree-four form row then bounds each net form change by d_x. The phase row bounds each continuous phase drift by m_o after removing only the explicit command. Every one of the 90 host edges has net form-gap change at most 2d_x and net phase-gap change at most 2m_o. The square-difference identity and \(|V'|\le J_0\) therefore give

\[ H_H(T_o)-H_H(0)\le360B_od_x+180J_0m_o<\frac1{50000}. \tag{21} \]

This endpoint comparison does not cancel the paid work of intermediate events or identify the reached endpoint with the pre-word state.

The donor retains form and relative-phase norms at most \(q_D=10^{-70}\). Its target phase gradient vanishes, its C9 Laplacian norm is below four, and \(|V''|\le J_1\), so \(H_D\le V_9+2(1+J_1)q_D^2<V_9+5q_D^2\). The weighted support event changes no coordinate and has work

\[ \begin{split} W_\eta&=\eta\sum_{c,j} \left[\tfrac12(x_{D,j}-x_{H,c,j})^2+ V(\theta_{D,j}-\theta_{H,c,j})\right],\\ W_\eta&\le45\eta\left[\tfrac12(B_o+q_D)^2+ 2+\frac2{19683}\right] <\frac{901}{10^6}. \end{split} \tag{22} \]

The extra 2/19683 is the global upper bound on the alternative's nonnegative added potential. This is supplied attachment work; past loss does not fund the event or select its occurrence.

Combining these own-law inequalities proves, for every original beta and every admitted original error member,

\[ H(0)-V_*<0.009588+\frac1{50000}+\frac{901}{10^6}+5q_D^2 <\frac{1051}{100000}<\frac3{250},\qquad B-[H(0)-V_*]>\frac1{250}. \tag{23} \]

Time zero is the actual final contact, not a reset. The pre-contact phase inclusions from the own-law source and complete observation word place every old edge in its original acute branch. The donor has the same winding-one C9 branch. No energy inequality is used to invent this initial branch information.

docs.title: 6.2 The old identity is retained for every future time
docs.text:
The own-law acute convexity proof establishes \(V''>0\) on the entire closed interval [-pi/2,pi/2]. Thus Jensen's inequality on the actual old cycles gives the boundary excess B from that owner. The 198 signed old-edge faces consist of 54 positive and 54 negative internal faces, 45 positive rim faces and 45 empty negative rim faces. Negative internal faces have larger cost; negative rim faces cannot accommodate winding one. The added donor cycle changes their number, not the minimum cycle-face formula.

Form storage and the weighted spoke potential are nonnegative. Hence every old-cell boundary has \(H\ge V_*+B\), independently of beta. Equations (2) and (23) exclude the first such boundary encounter. All six internal windings, nine rim windings and 32 zero mixed host periods persist for the whole future trajectory. The retained sublevel stays a positive distance from the old acute faces.

At fixed positive eta, connected support and zero total form make the form coordinates bounded by their storage. The two old support components have bounded relative phase lifts inside the old cell; their remaining relative origin is a circle. Thus the full trapped state is precompact modulo common phase rotation. This argument keeps all fine coordinates and does not assert invariance of the smaller stationary tube (4).

docs.title: 7. Own-law fine relaxation and classification of source limits
docs.text:
First improve the phase domains using the alternative potential itself. For a winding-one C9 cycle with one gap fixed at s, write \(F_9(s)=V(s)+8V((2\pi-s)/8)\). The added potential is nonnegative and vanishes at alpha. Therefore the existing rational cosine inequality gives \(F_9(\pi/3)-V_9>1/25\) for this law as well. The negative face has larger cost by even acute convexity. Since the full excess is below 3/250, every actual internal gap has magnitude below pi/3 for all future time.

Let \(a_c=\frac19\sum_jx_{c,j}\), \(z_{c,j}=x_{c,j}-a_c\), and keep the fine phase q from (3). Let P_f subtract each child's mean and \(L_f=L_\eta|_{\operatorname{ran}P_f}\). The graph gives \(2I/5<L_f\le10I\). The segment from the actual phases to their carrier at the same child means keeps internal gaps in (-pi/3,pi/3) and rim gaps acute. Its own-law projected phase Hessian satisfies

\[ m_f I\le\mathcal A_f\le11I,\qquad m_f=\frac{19}{100}, \qquad P_f\nabla U=\mathcal A_f q, \tag{24} \]

because its lower bound is \((1/2-2/243)(2/5)-6\eta J_1>19/100\), and its upper norm is at most \(10J_1<11\). The rim contribution is nonnegative by own-law acute convexity. The projected gradient at the carrier is exactly zero, for every set of origins, as in section 5.

The exact fine equations and a fixed quadratic proof function are

\[ \begin{split} q'&=\frac\gamma4L_fz,& z'&=-\frac14L_fz-\frac\gamma4g_f,&g_f&=P_f\nabla U,\\ F&=\frac12\|q+\gamma z\|^2+\frac{\gamma^2}{2}\|z\|^2,& F'&=-\frac{\gamma^2}{4} (q^Tg_f+z^TL_fz+2\gamma z^Tg_f). \end{split} \tag{25} \]

Young's inequality bounds the absolute cross term by \((m_f/2)\|q\|^2+(242\gamma^2/m_f)\|z\|^2\). Since \(2/5-242\gamma^2/m_f>m_f/2\), \(F\le\|q\|^2+\|z\|^2\), \(\|q\|^2\le4F\), and \(\gamma^2\|z\|^2\le2F\),

\[ F(\tau)\le F_0e^{-\rho\tau},\qquad \rho=\frac{19\gamma^2}{800},\qquad \|q\|^2\le4F_0e^{-\rho\tau},\qquad \gamma^2\|z\|^2\le2F_0e^{-\rho\tau}. \tag{26} \]

These are own-law bounds: the Hessian norm eleven and cross-term constant 242 replace the sine values. A matching constituent tangent alone would not justify (24)--(26).

docs.title: 7.1 The actual collective equations keep their fine remainder
docs.text:
Let L_W be the weighted wheel Laplacian and S_W its current under j. Averaging the actual rows gives

\[ a'=\frac{-L_Wa+\gamma[S_W(\Phi)+r]}4,\qquad \Phi'=\frac\gamma4L_Wa. \tag{27} \]

On each wheel edge, the mean-zero fine gaps cancel the linear Taylor term. The own-law constant J2 bounds the quadratic remainder, giving

\[ \begin{split} \|r\|_1&\le\frac{J_2}{9}\sum_{\{c,d\},j} w_{cd}(q_{c,j}-q_{d,j})^2 \le\frac{80}{27}F_0e^{-\rho\tau},\\ |r_D|&\le\frac{\eta J_2}{18}\sum_{c,j}(q_{c,j}-q_{D,j})^2 \le\frac{40}{27}\eta F_0e^{-\rho\tau}. \end{split} \tag{28} \]

The donor bound retains the spoke factor eta. Neither its force nor the host remainder is set to zero during the actual transient.

Jensen across the nine rim slot cycles gives, at every future time, \(V_{\rm rim}(\Phi_H)-V_5<(H-V_*)/9<1/750\). Every averaged acute winding-one rim gap is positive. To bound its upper endpoint, put

\[ \begin{split} C_8(v)&=1-v^2/2+v^4/24-v^6/720+v^8/40320,\\ R_5&=\frac{1545}{1000}-C_8(29/20) -4C_8\!\left(\frac{2(157/50)-29/20}{4}\right). \end{split} \]

The own-law constrained face cost exceeds its sine counterpart minus \(5\max(V-(1-\cos))=10/19683\). Exact rational arithmetic gives \(R_5-10/19683>1/750\). Hence every actual averaged rim gap lies in (0,29/20). With C6 from section 5, \(C_6(29/20)-2/243>1/10\). The segment from the actual host shape h to the stationary shape u(t) therefore has projected host Hessian

\[ \frac9{100}I\le\mathcal A_H\le5I, \qquad g_H=\mathcal A_H[h-u(t)], \tag{29} \]

where g_H is the projected host potential gradient at the actual mean phases. Its lower bound is \(L_5/10-\eta J_1I>9I/100\). This controls the actual shape outside the small stationary ball (4).

docs.title: 7.2 Every retained source converges to one classified equilibrium
docs.text:
An equilibrium in the larger retained sublevel first has x=0 by (2). Equation (24) then forces q=0; equation (29) forces h=u(t). Its last stationary equation is T(t)=0. Thus every stationary point in the actual trap belongs to the twenty-target classification of section 4. This is a full-state conclusion within the admitted old-cell sublevel, not a classification of distant or nonacute states.

The precompact orbit has a nonempty compact connected omega-limit set. Storage has one limiting value, constant along every orbit in that invariant limit set. Equation (2) then forces L_eta*x=0, hence x=0; invariance of the form row forces S=0. The omega-limit is consequently contained in the finite classified equilibrium set modulo common rotation. Connectedness makes it a singleton. Every retained source therefore converges to one of those twenty relative equilibria.

On the full phase torus, the conserved product \(\prod_i e^{i\theta_i}=e^{i9\beta}\) leaves only 54 common-rotation representatives of each relative equilibrium. The same connected-limit argument therefore gives one full circular equilibrium. Once each primitive phase stays in a proper arc about its limit, its continuous lift stays in one corresponding real chart and converges there as well. No finite-total-variation bound is asserted by this argument.

This uses the actual law, trap and finite equilibrium classification, without importing a global analytic-convergence theorem from sine. It does not yet choose a destination or exclude saddle capture. The following source restriction supplies that additional conclusion.

docs.title: 8. Ten explicit intervals of actual preparation reach strict minima
docs.text:
For k=0,...,9, define the primitive donor-origin center \(\beta_k=(2k+1)\pi/10\). At the fixed eta in (1), every original own-law preparation with

\[ |\beta-\beta_k|\le\frac1{10}\quad\pmod{2\pi} \tag{30} \]

converges to the unique attractive equilibrium whose relative origin lies in the interval of radius pi/60 centered at \(-\beta_k\). The inequality uses the lift nearest the chosen center. All twelve original allowances, all 96 relative directions and the complete own-law history are retained. No initial residual or observed endpoint is replaced by a stationary or exactly reflected source.

docs.title: 8.1 A coupled comparison bounds shape and origin transport
docs.text:
Let bars with subscript H denote the average over five host children. Keep h and t from (3), and put

\[ \begin{split} p_c&=a_c-\overline a_H,& e&=h-u(t),& K_H&=L_5+\eta I\quad\hbox{on the zero-mean host space},\\ \chi&=\gamma(\overline a_H-a_D),&y&=t+\chi,\\ \delta&=\eta\sum_c[j(t+b_c+h_c)-j(t+b_c+u_c)]+r_D. \end{split} \tag{31} \]

The actual donor current is T(t)+delta. The two complete mean rows (27) give exactly

\[ \begin{split} t'&=\tfrac32\eta\chi,& \chi'&=-\tfrac32\eta\chi-\tfrac{3\gamma^2}{10}(T+\delta),\\ e'&=\tfrac\gamma4K_Hp-u_t t',& p'&=-\tfrac14K_Hp-\tfrac\gamma4g_H+\tfrac\gamma4Pr_H,\\ y'&=-\tfrac{3\gamma^2}{10}(T+\delta). \end{split} \tag{32} \]

The corrected origin y retains the relative mean form through chi. It is an auxiliary coordinate, not a new phase measurement or a claim of instantaneous form relaxation.

Define \(\mathcal E^2=\|e+\gamma p\|^2/2+\gamma^2\|p\|^2/2\). Then \(\|e\|\le2\mathcal E\), and (28) gives

\[ |\delta|\le5\eta\mathcal E+ \frac{40}{27}\eta F_0e^{-\rho\tau}. \tag{33} \]

Here \(2\sqrt5J_1<5\). The fixed-shape terms in the derivative of \(\mathcal E^2\) are \(-\gamma^2(e^Tg_H+p^TK_Hp+2\gamma p^Tg_H)/4\). Use (29), \(I<K_H<5I\), and Young's inequality with m_H=9/100. Since \(1-50\gamma^2/m_H>m_H/2\), these terms yield decay \(\mathcal E'\le-9\gamma^2\mathcal E/1600\). The moving-shape term uses the actual u_t from (9), and is bounded by \(28\eta^2|\chi|\); the fine forcing contributes at most \(\gamma^2\|Pr_H\|\).

Also \(\lambda_1>2/5\) in (6) gives K<3/100 in (11). The finite torque bound (12) consequently gives \(|T|<(3/100+960\eta)\eta^2<\eta^2/20\). With upper right derivatives at vanishing norms, the complete comparison is

\[ \begin{split} \mathcal E'&\le-\frac{9\gamma^2}{1600}\mathcal E +28\eta^2|\chi|+\frac{80}{27}\gamma^2F_0e^{-\rho\tau},\\ |\chi|'&\le-\frac32\eta|\chi|+\frac32\gamma^2\eta\mathcal E +\frac3{200}\gamma^2\eta^2 +\frac49\gamma^2\eta F_0e^{-\rho\tau}. \end{split} \tag{34} \]

docs.title: 8.2 The reached preparation controls the entire transient
docs.text:
The host and donor form totals are separately zero before contact. The host lifted phase total is zero; each prescribed observation jump has zero global phase increment. The donor total is 9*beta. Therefore the actual contacted endpoint satisfies exactly \(\chi(0)=0\) and \(t(0)=y(0)=-\beta\).

The retained own-law fine error before observation is below 1e-6, a coarse container of its much smaller preserved bound. Using (20) and subtracting child means gives \(|q_{c,j}(0)|<1/400000\), \(|z_{c,j}(0)|<21/1000\) and \(|\gamma z_{c,j}(0)|<7/10^6\). The donor errors are smaller. Consequently

\[ F_0<27[(1/400000+7/10^6)^2+(7/10^6)^2]<10^{-8}, \qquad \mathcal E(0)<\frac15. \tag{35} \]

For the second inequality, own-law rim convexity in the domain from section 7 gives \(\|h(0)\|^2<2/75\), hence \(\|h(0)\|<1/6\). Equations (8) and (20) give \(\|u\|<6\eta\) and \(\|p(0)\|<\sqrt5B_o<1/40\). Substitution into the definition of E proves (35). These estimates use the reached state rather than narrowing any primitive allowance.

Set \(\mathcal X=\mathcal E+20\eta|\chi|\) and \(\lambda=\gamma^2/200\). At the fixed eta, \(9/1600-30\eta^2>1/200\), \(\eta>\gamma^2/20\), and \(80/27+(80/9)\eta^2<3\). Thus (34) gives

\[ \begin{split} \mathcal X'&\le-\lambda\mathcal X+ \frac3{10}\gamma^2\eta^3+3\gamma^2F_0e^{-\rho\tau},\\ \mathcal E(\tau)&\le D_*e^{-\lambda\tau}+60\eta^3,& D_*&=\mathcal E(0)+160F_0<\frac{21}{100},\\ |\chi(\tau)|&\le\gamma^2 [D_*+60\eta^3+\eta/100+(8/27)F_0] <\frac{\gamma^2}{4}<10^{-6}. \end{split} \tag{36} \]

The transient coefficient is \(3\gamma^2/(\rho-\lambda)=160\); the nondecaying shape bound is \(((3/10)\gamma^2\eta^3)/\lambda=60\eta^3\). The last line follows by integrating the second row of (34) using \(\chi(0)=0\). The nonzero shape remainder is retained; it does not assert exact tracking of the stationary shape during motion.

docs.title: 8.3 The inward torque separates each selected source from saddles
docs.text:
Fix a center t_c=-beta_k, and first consider the upper strip \(1/10\le y-t_c\le1/5\). Equation (36) puts \(10(t-t_c)\) strictly between 0.99 and 2.01. This interval is inside \((0.99,\pi-0.99)\), and \(\sin(0.99)\ge0.99-0.99^3/6>4/5\). Since t_c is an odd multiple of pi/10, the leading torque in (12) has the restoring sign here. Its full finite remainder gives

\[ T(t)>\left[\frac1{40}\frac45-960\eta\right]\eta^2 =0.0104\eta^2>\frac{\eta^2}{100}. \tag{37} \]

Equations (33) and (36) bound the nondecaying part of |delta| by \(300\eta^4\), smaller than \(\eta^2/100\). The corresponding lower strip has the opposite restoring sign by the same leading-torque and absolute-remainder bounds. No exact reflection symmetry about an odd interval center is assumed.

Only the decaying part can drive y outward in either strip. Its entire possible adverse displacement is

\[ \begin{split} J&=\frac{3\gamma^2}{10}\int_0^\infty [5\eta D_*e^{-\lambda\tau} +(40/27)\eta F_0e^{-\rho\tau}]\,d\tau\\ &=300\eta D_*+\frac{3200}{171}\eta F_0<\frac1{1000}. \end{split} \tag{38} \]

The prepared interval (30) gives \(|y(0)-t_c|\le1/10\). If y first reached t_c+1/5, take its last prior crossing of t_c+1/10. Integrating (32) between those times would give \(1/10\le J<1/1000\), a contradiction. The lower strip gives the same conclusion. Therefore

\[ |y(\tau)-t_c|<\frac15,\qquad |t(\tau)-t_c|<\frac15+10^{-6}<\frac\pi{12}. \tag{39} \]

The source already converges to one classified equilibrium by section 7.2. The only stationary origin allowed by (39) is the unique minimum in the central odd interval (14): its radius is pi/60, while the nearest exact saddle is pi/10 from t_c. Hence this is the source's destination. Its local exponential attraction eventually controls the complete state on the conserved-mean leaf. Continuous phase lifts then converge to the corresponding lifted equilibrium. No uniform entrance time or finite settling deadline has been proved.

The ten certified intervals are disjoint. Fix any one original allowance tuple and every primitive error and relative source member, retaining the full prescribed history; vary only the primitive donor origin beta. Preparation and the own-law finite-time flow depend continuously on beta. On the zero-total-form state space with common phase rotation removed, the distinct attracting equilibria have disjoint open basins. Every gap between successive certified intervals contains at least one saddle-converging origin for this fixed member: otherwise the connected interval joining its two certified endpoints would be covered by those disjoint open basins, although the endpoints have different destinations. The own-law convergence and finite classification justify the saddle conclusion. Other gap destinations, exceptional counts and measures are not determined.

docs.title: 8.4 A common primitive preparation interval separates the two laws
docs.text:
Take the common primitive preparation interval \(|\beta-\pi/10|\le1/10\), with the original primitive allowances, commands and durations under each complete law. This entire interval lies inside the sine theorem's \(|\beta|\le3/5\) source basin. The sine law therefore selects t_infinity=0. The alternative instead selects its unique minimum in

\[ -\frac{7\pi}{60}<t_\infty<-\frac{5\pi}{60}. \tag{40} \]

The wrapped asymptotic relative-origin difference exceeds pi/12 for every allowed pair of own-law source members. This compares the same declared primitive preparation class and commands, not identical reached endpoints or transplanted source bounds. Each law carries its own acquisition, observation backaction, storage and complete subsequent evolution. The two own-law certificates establish the contrast without generating another trajectory or re-evaluating a frozen response.

The conclusion is an asymptotic mathematical discriminator. It has no finite reading time, laboratory clock, independently admitted sensor or observation-error budget. It does not by itself select which law describes nature.

docs.title: 9. Meaning and implementation boundary
docs.text:
The sine law at this same eta has attracting origins t=2kpi/5. Every one is among the alternative's exact saddle origins. The ten alternative attracting origins lie instead in the odd intervals (14). This finite-strength comparison resolves a constitutive dependence of the collective registration while preserving the declared constituent profile and old marked identity. It does not follow from graph symmetry alone.

The stationary proof is local to (4); the source proof separately extends its use to the larger retained energy sublevel. Neither result classifies all nonacute or distant organizations. Ten actual-source intervals now reach alternative minima, while the prototype common primitive interval has distinct destinations under the two laws. Own-law acquisition, observation history, attachment work and transient fine-state transport are part of that conclusion. Matching the isolated constituent tangent did not transfer the sine source basin.

These labeled registrations are not physical species. Their difference neither selects a unique fundamental law nor supplies a physical clock, measurement bridge, autonomous contact occurrence or collective operator. The ontology retains those separate obligations.

The static controls check the derivative bounds, weighted full-state identities, fivefold Fourier coefficient, contraction and C1 margins, full-state curvature, actual-source budgets, moving-shape transport and inward-torque inequalities. Those controls support the written proof; they do not sample roots or evaluate a trajectory. This analytical result installs no new runtime law or source producer. The execution plan owns its status and any later admission.

docs.title: Work required to assemble recovered organizations
docs.text:
Status: conditional endpoint obstruction for the three recovered sine winding-one C9 objects and the two fixed oriented contact supports. Every simultaneous form/phase reset that retains their acute winding-one internal geometry requires positive net storage work. Allowing internal deformation and arbitrary relative phase origins does not remove that requirement. This is a lower-bound theorem, not the sharp minimum, an event selector or a claim about physical binding. The research program alone assigns subsequent work.

The acquired network capture theorem already establishes convergence after a supplied, unchanged-state contact. Its positive contact work is a separate premise. The present result tests whether simultaneous internal reorganization can pay that cost for the actual recovered children, using the reset-accounting principle from support events. The weighted sine storage below is its own model; native unique-neighbor phase storage and registered operator execution are not substituted for it.

docs.title: Complete endpoint model and retained identity
docs.text:
Retain nodes \((r,j)\), ordered as \(9r+j\), with \(r=0,1,2\) and \(j=0,\ldots,8\). Each marked child retains all nine original unit-conductance cycle edges. Write \(\alpha=2\pi/9\), \(x=\mathrm{EPI}\in\mathbb R^{27}\), and let \(\theta\) denote primitive circular phase. Capacity is held at one. The before support \(E_0\) is the disjoint union of the three cycles. The after support \(E_s\) additionally contains, for each oriented contact \(e=(r,t)\in\{(0,1),(1,2),(2,0)\}\),

\[ (r,j)--(t,j)\quad\text{with weight }1-s_e,\qquad (r,j)--(t,j+1)\quad\text{with weight }s_e . \tag{1} \]

All indices are modulo nine, all added edges are undirected, and

\[ s^{\rm eq}=(1/2,1/2,1/2),\qquad s^{\rm un}=(1/4,1/2,3/4). \tag{2} \]

No old edge is removed or reweighted. Each final node has weighted degree four. The complete support-dependent storage, with its absolute edge baselines retained, is

\[ H_E(x,\theta)=\frac12\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}w_{ij}(x_i-x_j)^2 +\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}w_{ij}[1-\cos(\theta_j-\theta_i)] . \tag{3} \]

The phase weights in (3) are actual conductances. A comparison that replaces them with unique-neighbor weights changes this model.

This is detached endpoint accounting for the same sine model as the capture owner. That owner declares the complete continuous laws, the structural clock \(\tau=(1023/1024)t\), pressure, held capacity and loss. No finite duration is assigned to a reset, and no new continuous row is introduced. The units of work below are the declared structural storage units of (3); there is no laboratory energy identification.

The initial endpoint is an actual member of the original three-source family, after acquisition time \(100\) and uninterrupted recovery dwell \(10^{13}\). At the unchanged handoff \(\tau_h=100+10^{13}\), the shared recovery at sine deformation zero gives

\[ \begin{split} \Theta_{r,j}&=\alpha(j-4),\qquad \theta^-_{r,j}=\Theta_{r,j}+y^-_{r,j},\\ \|x^-_r\|_2&\le\varepsilon,\qquad \|y^-_r\|_2\le\varepsilon, \qquad \varepsilon=10^{-70},\\ \mathbf1^Tx^-_r&=\mathbf1^Ty^-_r=0 . \end{split}\tag{4} \]

The three copies have independent original coordinate errors at most \(10^{-10}\), with their declared separate zero means. No source is reset to \((0,\Theta)\), no new dwell is selected, and no favorable correlation between children is imposed.

Admit hypothetical finite after coordinates \((x^+,\theta^+)\) subject to the following endpoint identity restriction. For each marked child let \(\delta^+_{r,j}\) be the principal circular gap from node \((r,j)\) to \((r,j+1)\). Require

\[ -\pi/2<\delta^+_{r,j}<\pi/2,\qquad \sum_{j=0}^8\delta^+_{r,j}=2\pi . \tag{5} \]

Thus every retained child is internally strictly acute and has winding one. Its internal shape, absolute and relative phase origins, and every finite signed form may change. Endpoint means need not equal the source means. Proving an obstruction in this larger class also covers any subclass that conserves them. New contact gaps need not be acute.

Condition (5) is an explicit endpoint class, not a consequence of winding alone or a declaration that any such state was acquired dynamically. In particular, the capture theorem permits nonacute transient gaps in its larger trapping sector. Its no-reset capture certificate is not transferred to arbitrary endpoints here. An admitted algebraic reset is not yet a registered operator: live preconditions, collective descent and occurrence remain separate obligations of the NFR ontology and operator contracts.

Common form translation, common phase rotation and simultaneous cyclic relabeling preserve (3)--(5). Separate child phase rotations preserve internal storage but generally change contact storage; they are retained coordinates, not independently removable gauges of the joined model.

docs.title: The actual source has only a small internal excess
docs.text:
Put

\[ V(z)=1-\cos z,\qquad B_0=27V(\alpha). \tag{6} \]

On the acute interval, \(V''(z)=\cos z>0\). Jensen's inequality and the winding constraint in (5) give, separately for each child,

\[ \sum_{j=0}^8V(\delta^+_{r,j}) \ge9V\!\left(\frac19\sum_j\delta^+_{r,j}\right) =9V(\alpha). \tag{7} \]

Thus every after endpoint has old-support storage at least \(B_0\), including its nonnegative form contribution. Equality in phase requires all internal gaps to be \(\alpha\).

The source in (4) is also in that acute winding sector. Let \(L_0\) be the Laplacian of the three unit cycles. Its largest eigenvalue is at most four. The internal phase gradient vanishes at \(\Theta\); this is a fine-node identity because each node has opposite sine currents from its two cycle neighbors. Taylor's integral formula and \(\nabla^2 U\preceq L_0\) give

\[ \begin{split} H_{E_0}(x^-,\theta^-)-B_0 &\le\tfrac12(x^-)^TL_0x^- +\tfrac12(y^-)^TL_0y^-\\ &\le2\|x^-\|_2^2+2\|y^-\|_2^2 \le12\varepsilon^2. \end{split}\tag{8} \]

Combining (7) with (8),

\[ \boxed{B_0\le H_{E_0}(x^-,\theta^-)\le B_0+12\varepsilon^2.} \tag{9} \]

All residual coordinates remain in this bound. The exact rational term \(12\varepsilon^2\) must remain separate from an outward interval for the irrational baseline \(B_0\); rounding it away would incorrectly replace a reached state with the ideal minimum.

docs.title: Every retained winding forces positive contact storage
docs.text:
Consider one oriented contact \(e=(r,t)\) and one node index \(j\). Set \(a=\theta^+_{t,j}-\theta^+_{r,j}\), interpreted modulo a turn, and \(\delta=\delta^+_{t,j}\). The two port contributions are

\[ \begin{split} C_{e,j} &=(1-s_e)V(a)+s_eV(a+\delta)\\ &=1-\operatorname{Re}\{e^{ia}(1-s_e+s_e e^{i\delta})\}\\ &\ge 1-|1-s_e+s_e e^{i\delta}|=:f_{s_e}(\delta). \end{split}\tag{10} \]

Seam integers do not change the cosines or the phasor identity. This inequality minimizes over one source phase independently; it remains a lower bound when the actual 27 phases impose further correlations.

For \(u=s(1-s)\) and \(0<s<1\), write

\[ \rho_s(z)=\sqrt{1-2u(1-\cos z)},\qquad f_s(z)=1-\rho_s(z). \tag{11} \]

On \([-\pi/2,\pi/2]\), \(\rho_s^2\ge1-2u\ge1/2\), so the derivatives are regular and

\[ f_s''(z)=\frac{u\cos z}{\rho_s(z)} +\frac{u^2\sin^2z}{\rho_s(z)^3}>0 . \tag{12} \]

The endpoint positivity follows from the second term; at zero the first term is positive. Applying Jensen to the nine target-child gaps gives

\[ \sum_{j=0}^8 C_{e,j} \ge\sum_j f_{s_e}(\delta^+_{t,j}) \ge9f_{s_e}(\alpha)=9[1-\rho_{s_e}(\alpha)]. \tag{13} \]

Every contact has its own target child with winding one, so summing these three inequalities is valid on the same complete endpoint. Define

\[ G(s)=9\sum_{e}[1-\rho_{s_e}(\alpha)]. \tag{14} \]

The added form storage is nonnegative, hence (7) and (13) imply the full-state lower bound

\[ \boxed{H_{E_s}(x^+,\theta^+)\ge B_0+G(s).} \tag{15} \]

No invariant registered-family assumption or collective tangent reduction appears in this argument.

A simpler independent lower bound follows from \(1-\sqrt{1-z}\ge z/2\) for \(0\le z\le1\):

\[ G(s)\ge 9V(\alpha)\sum_es_e(1-s_e)>0. \tag{16} \]

For the two fixed controls,

\[ \begin{array}{c|c|c} &G(s)&\text{simpler lower bound}\\ \hline s^{\rm eq}&27[1-\cos(\pi/9)]&\tfrac{27}{4}V(\alpha)\\ s^{\rm un}&9[3-2\sqrt{1-\tfrac38V(\alpha)}-\cos(\pi/9)] &\tfrac{45}{8}V(\alpha) \end{array} . \tag{17} \]

The two values of \(G\) are approximately \(1.62829924\) and \(1.35048908\), respectively. These decimals are explanatory; the certificate uses outward rational trigonometric and square-root bounds. The same enclosures give \(V(\alpha)>1/5\). Thus even the simpler bounds give \(G(s^{\rm eq})>27/20\) and \(G(s^{\rm un})>9/8\), far above the exact source excess in (9).

Equations (14)--(17) are not claims of a sharp joined minimum. Simultaneous equality in the child Jensen bounds requires uniform internal twist. At such a state, equality in every contact's phasor bound would require \(\Phi_t-\Phi_r=-\arg(1-s_e+s_e e^{i\alpha})\) modulo a turn. The left sides sum to zero around the three-contact cycle, while the sum of those arguments is \(\pi/3\) for both controls, as established by the network compatibility theorem. Thus the separately relaxed contact minima are incompatible. The positive lower bound remains valid without solving the sharper coupled minimization.

docs.title: Required work and passive path obstruction
docs.text:
The exact storage jump for a simultaneous reset and attachment is

\[ W_{\rm event}=H_{E_s}(x^+,\theta^+)-H_{E_0}(x^-,\theta^-). \tag{18} \]

It includes both internal reorganization and all added-edge costs. The counterfactual algebraic decomposition

\[ \begin{split} W_{\rm event}={}&H_{E_0}(x^+,\theta^+)-H_{E_0}(x^-,\theta^-)\\ &+H_{E_s}(x^+,\theta^+)-H_{E_0}(x^+,\theta^+) \end{split}\tag{19} \]

does not impose an execution order. Equations (9) and (15) show that contemporaneous internal release is insufficient:

\[ \boxed{W_{\rm event}\ge G(s)-12\varepsilon^2>0.} \tag{20} \]

In particular, the internal term can release at most \(12\varepsilon^2\), whereas the new contacts cost at least \(G(s)\). The source has already relaxed close to its minimum within the retained acute winding sector. The obstruction applies to every original admitted source and every after endpoint in (5), not merely a nominal target or one attempted reset.

The unchanged-state attachment from the capture theorem costs approximately \(3.15840002\), with its own exact residual correction. Equation (20) allows a reset to reduce that cost but excludes making it storage-passive under the declared endpoint restrictions. It neither constructs an optimal reset nor certifies capture from a proposed reset endpoint.

The finite hybrid balance also excludes an evasion by passive staging. Suppose every continuous segment has its separately admitted storage law \(H'=-D\), \(D\ge0\), every event uses the actual complete storage jump \(J_k\), and all segments and jumps use the same storage normalization (3). For any such finite hybrid path from (4) to an endpoint in (5),

\[ H_{\rm final}-H_{\rm initial} =-\int D\,d\tau+\sum_kJ_k, \qquad \sum_kJ_k\ge G(s)-12\varepsilon^2+\int D\,d\tau>0. \tag{21} \]

Consequently no path with every event passive, \(J_k\le0\), has these endpoints. Even permitting individually positive jumps while demanding a nonpositive total jump budget cannot satisfy (21). If independently declared supplied-work budgets obey \(J_k\le W_k\), their sum must also obey the same positive lower bound. Past loss is not an available reserve without a separately specified storage coordinate and reservoir law.

This uses telescoping accounting, not a theorem admitting an arbitrary intermediate support or trajectory. Each intermediate law, regularity domain and event must be admitted separately. The result does not supply a schedule, finite stopping time, non-Zeno proof or autonomous occurrence argument. Temporary edge removal cannot evade the endpoint inequality if the declared final support is restored and the same complete storage is used throughout. Permanently removing or reweighting original edges changes the final-support premise instead.

docs.title: Deletion and limits of the conclusion
docs.text:
At any final endpoint in (5), removing all added contacts without changing the coordinates changes storage by

\[ H_{E_0}(x^+,\theta^+)-H_{E_s}(x^+,\theta^+) =-H_{\rm contacts}(x^+,\theta^+)\le-G(s)<0. \tag{22} \]

The three marked cycles and their acute winding-one endpoint identities remain. This is frozen-state endpoint accounting, not a post-deletion recovery theorem or an assertion that the preceding acquired trajectory is internally acute at a specified finite time.

Thus held-support convergence does not establish storage binding against an admitted contact-deletion action. A negative deletion jump also does not select that action's occurrence. Both attachment and detachment still require an event model; no physical binding energy is identified here.

The obstruction retains its declared acute endpoint identity class, late recovered source, original internal edges, two fixed contact controls and weighted sine storage. It does not exclude attachment earlier during acquisition, endpoints outside the acute class, an identity change, removal or reweighting of original edges, or a separately justified storage or reservoir law. Those would change premises and require their own source, event and capture analysis. No such extension is executed here.

docs.title: Implementation and independent controls
docs.text:
The assembly-work certificate re-admits primitive inputs, rebuilds the selected weighted support and original source recovery, and derives the contact lower bounds from the shared contact-amplitude owner. It retains the exact source excess separately from interval-rounded nominal terms and makes source-dependent claims only when that recovery is certified. Incoming report verdicts are not premises.

The independent controls exercise the actual support, nonuniform acute winding endpoints, finite form/phase reset accounting, strict work signs, original residual scope, deletion, and invalid or unavailable source inputs. These are analytic and static checks. No original source producer, trajectory, reserved response or physical dataset is regenerated.

docs.title: Conserved charge observations under the organized sine law
Model, observation class and scientific scope
docs.text:
This owner classifies restricted conserved observations of the complete organized sine law. It distinguishes a local contribution from a general collective property: additivity across regions does not imply that each contribution reads only one node. The classification below imposes that additional information restriction explicitly. It is not a theorem excluding physical charge or all collective charge maps.

The physical comparison below closes with an exact obstruction to a specified density-only electroquasistatic realization. A separate modal proof also excludes one homogeneous local edge redistribution as a smooth complete density state, including near an acute C9 twist. These conclusions leave descriptions with retained internal material state open. They do not admit a physical dataset or infer an electromagnetic origin for TNFR.

Keep a fixed finite connected simple unit graph \(G=(V,E)\), with \(n=|V|\ge2\), its unnormalized Laplacian \(L\), held unit capacities, and the complete quarter law

\[ x'=\frac{-Lx+\gamma S(\theta)}4,\qquad \theta'=\frac{\gamma Lx}4,\qquad S_i(\theta)=\sum_{j\sim i}\sin(\theta_j-\theta_i),\qquad \gamma=\frac1{1023\pi}>0. \tag{1} \]

Prime denotes the declared tau clock of the organized contact. All \(x_i\in\mathbb R\) are signed form, and all phases lie on \(\mathbb T=\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)\). Both rows use the same quarter factor, including on graphs with unequal degrees. There is no forcing, coordinate reset, support event, variable capacity or additional phase velocity. This is a detached theorem for the smooth-sine comparison; it neither selects the law nor executes a registered operator. The actual 144-edge contact graphs are members of this support class.

The complete field preserves \(\sum_i x_i\), by pairwise cancellation. It also preserves \(\sum_i\widetilde\theta_i\) on any consistently transported set of continuous phase lifts. The latter is not a single-valued real observation of the circular state. Common form translation is an exact symmetry of (1), but calling that symmetry unobservable is a separate observation premise. These distinctions retain the form foundation, parameter foundation, common-origin owner and collective-property ontology.

docs.title: Identical local contributions: an exhaustive classification
docs.text:
Let \(f:\mathbb R\times\mathbb T\to\mathbb R\) be \(C^2\), the same function at every node, and define

\[ Q_f(x,\theta)=\sum_{i\in V}f(x_i,\theta_i). \tag{2} \]

Each contribution consumes its own form and circular phase only. It does not consume neighbor states, incident edges, a region label, a hidden reference, history, a phase lift or the state of a measuring apparatus. Require (2) to be conserved for every solution and initial state in the full domain of (1), not only along a selected acquired family or inside one winding chamber.

Conditional classification. Under these hypotheses,

\[ \boxed{f(x,\theta)=a x+b,\qquad Q_f=a\sum_i x_i+bn,} \tag{3} \]

for constants \(a,b\in\mathbb R\). Conversely every expression (3) is conserved on the fixed support. The proof only needs \(C^1\) regularity; the stated \(C^2\) class is a sufficient convenient domain.

docs.title: Proof
docs.text:
Conservation for every initial state implies the pointwise identity

\[ 0=4Q_f' =\sum_i f_x(x_i,\theta_i) [- (Lx)_i+\gamma S_i(\theta)] +\gamma\sum_i f_\theta(x_i,\theta_i)(Lx)_i. \tag{4} \]

First take \(x_i=s\) for every node. Give one vertex \(k\) phase \(\beta\), and every other vertex phase \(\alpha\). Its degree \(d_k>0\) because the graph is connected and has at least two nodes. The form Laplacian and entire phase row vanish. Only edges incident on \(k\) contribute to (4), giving

\[ 0=\gamma d_k\sin(\alpha-\beta) [f_x(s,\beta)-f_x(s,\alpha)]. \tag{5} \]

Thus \(f_x(s,\alpha)=f_x(s,\beta)\) whenever the sine is nonzero. Continuity supplies the remaining pairs of angles. Since \(s\) was arbitrary, integration in form gives

\[ f(x,\theta)=A(x)+B(\theta), \tag{6} \]

where \(B\) is a single-valued periodic function.

Next take all phases equal, so \(S=0\). The last term of (4) is \(\gamma B'(\alpha)\sum_i(Lx)_i=0\). Give vertex \(k\) form \(r\) and every other vertex form \(s\). The remaining identity is

\[ 0=-d_k(r-s)[A'(r)-A'(s)]. \tag{7} \]

For any unequal \(r,s\), their derivatives agree. Hence \(A'(x)=a\) is constant. Finally (4) reduces, for every form vector and phase state, to

\[ 0=\gamma B'(\theta)^T Lx. \tag{8} \]

Because \(L\) is symmetric and its kernel on a connected graph is \(\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}\), (8) implies \(B'(\theta_i)=B'(\theta_j)\) for all nodes. Phase assignments are arbitrary, so \(B'\) is constant on the circle. Periodicity gives \(\int_0^{2\pi}B'(u)\,du=0\), making that constant zero. This proves (3). The converse follows from the conserved form sum and fixed node count.

docs.title: Common-origin invariance is an additional restriction
docs.text:
If, in addition, the observation must satisfy

\[ Q_f(x+c\mathbf1,\theta)=Q_f(x,\theta) \quad\text{for every real }c, \tag{9} \]

then (3) changes by \(anc\), forcing \(a=0\). Only the constant \(bn\) remains. Declaring every reference node to carry zero contribution fixes \(b=0\). Therefore there is no nonzero, state-dependent, origin-invariant conserved observation in the identical local class (2) on this full domain.

This result does not require the actual form sum to vanish. Conversely, the zero form totals in the acquired contact preparations are facts about those preparations, not a derivation of universal neutrality. A symmetry-invariant interpretation of charge cannot be imposed merely because the underlying differential equations have that symmetry.

docs.title: A retained form reference permits a nonzero inventory
docs.text:
Extend the observation data by one independently declared scalar reference \(r\), held with \(r'=0\). Its constancy is an explicit premise; it is not a new law inferred from an evaluated response. For each fixed \(r\), the same proof gives

\[ f(x,\theta;r)=a(r)x+b(r). \tag{10} \]

Require covariance of the observation under a common change of the form chart and its retained reference,

\[ f(x+c,\theta;r+c)=f(x,\theta;r). \tag{11} \]

Comparison of the coefficients of \(x\) in (11) gives \(a(r+c)=a(r)=\kappa\). Its constant term then gives \(b(r)=b_0-\kappa r\). Normalization \(f(r,\theta;r)=0\) fixes \(b_0=0\), leaving exactly

\[ q_i=\kappa(x_i-r),\qquad Q_A=\kappa\sum_{i\in A}(x_i-r). \tag{12} \]

The scale \(\kappa\) is not supplied by TNFR. If \(q_i\) is proposed in coulombs and form in a declared unit X, then \([\kappa]=\mathrm C/\mathrm X\). A physical clock would separately need a conversion from tau to seconds. Neither unit assignment nor (11) establishes such a measurement bridge.

For a fixed region \(A\subseteq V\), edge cancellation in (1) gives

\[ Q_A'= \frac\kappa4\sum_{\substack{i\in A,\ j\notin A\\i\sim j}} [x_j-x_i+\gamma\sin(\theta_j-\theta_i)]. \tag{13} \]

The complement receives the opposite boundary current, and \(Q_V'=0\). Thus (12) is additive, signed and transported. This is the uniform-quarter counterpart of the existing degree-normalized regional inventory; its weights and clock cannot be copied from that different law. Storage loss does not destroy (12), and the boundary phases remain consumed state.

If \(r\) instead evolves, the regional row has the additional term \(-\kappa |A|r'\). If node membership, scale, support or form changes in an event, its actual inventory jump needs separate accounting. Conserved continuous totals do not establish event conservation, admission, descent or occurrence. The constant \(bn\) in (3) similarly changes when the node count changes; it is not a conserved physical particle number without an applicable support-event law.

docs.title: A self-centered reference has a different meaning
docs.text:
Choosing \(r=\bar x_V=n^{-1}\sum_i x_i\) makes (12) invariant under a common form shift and keeps \(r'=0\) under (1). This is allowed, but it is a collective reference rather than a contribution with only its own node as input. It enforces \(Q_V=0\) by definition. Regional excesses can be nonzero and still satisfy (13).

The reference set must remain part of the observation. If it is enlarged from \(V\) to a disjoint set \(V\cup W\), with \(m=|W|>0\), the same unchanged region \(A\subseteq V\) acquires

\[ Q_A^{V\cup W}-Q_A^V =\kappa\frac{|A|m}{n+m} (\bar x_V-\bar x_W). \tag{14} \]

Equation (14) is a change of the declared observation reference, not a current or an instantaneous physical influence from \(W\). It proves that arbitrary re-centering against a new environment cannot be treated as the same localized charge measurement. A fixed external reference or a fixed whole support avoids that reassignment, while retaining its additional reference premise. No charge quantization follows from either choice.

docs.title: Boundaries and collective possibilities beyond the site classification
docs.text:
The full-state and information hypotheses are essential:

  • If \(\gamma=0\), phase is frozen and every periodic \(\sum_i B(\theta_i)\) is conserved. The phase-elimination step (5) fails, as it must. Equation (1) has strictly positive gamma.
  • On a declared continuously lifted phase chart, a linear lifted-phase sum is conserved. Changing one representative by \(2\pi\) changes that sum, so it is not a globally single-valued real charge on the circular state. This distinction does not forbid periodic collective functions of the total lifted phase, which are outside (2).
  • For a single isolated node, both rows vanish and every function of its state is conserved. The connected support with at least two nodes is a premise, not an incidental convenience.
  • Conservation only within a selected winding chamber or acquired source family is weaker than conservation on the full model domain. The proof uses uniform-phase and arbitrary-form configurations; it cannot classify a map defined only near a formed organization. Winding may be locally conserved until a branch crossing, without being a smooth global single-node sum.

docs.title: Independent electroquasistatic reference and observation map
docs.text:
The physical reference is a specified macroscopic regime, not a proposed microscopic origin of electric charge. Use fixed isotropic linear permittivity epsilon>0, a prescribed nonnegative smooth conductivity sigma(z) of compact support, no impressed current, and potential tending to zero at spatial infinity. Position z and physical time t_lab are independently defined, and rho_e is the free-charge density; the fixed linear dielectric response has no independent polarization state. In the electroquasistatic approximation the conventional equations are

\[ -\epsilon abla^2\phi= ho_e,\quad E=- abla\phi,\quad J=\sigma E,\quad \partial_{t_{lab}} ho_e=- abla\cdot J = abla\cdot(\sigma abla\phi). ag{16} \]

The separate premises are documented in the authors' MIT edition of Electromagnetic Fields and Energy: charge conservation, section 2.3, quasistatic approximation and its error, section 3.3, Poisson's equation, section 4.2, and Ohmic constitutive law, section 7.1. These source sections were reviewed on 2026-10-10. Fixed conductivity and instantaneous linear polarization exclude independent material memory, chemical drive and magnetic induction at the retained order. They are restrictions of this reference, not universal electromagnetic assumptions. A physical application would have to bound the neglected fields and material-law error; a structural clock or small numerical step does not do so.

For a localized smooth charge distribution the specified boundary condition gives the potential

\[ \phi(z)= rac1{4\pi\epsilon} \int rac{ ho_e(z')}{|z-z'|}\,d^3z'. ag{17} \]

This is the reference model's superposition integral, section 4.5. It makes the full spatial density sufficient to determine the electric field in this setting. It does not make the net charge sufficient. For example, ideal equal-and-opposite point charges of magnitude Q_*>0 at +a e_x,-a e_x, or at +a e_y,-a e_y, both have zero total. Potential probes at R e_x,R e_y, with R>a>0, give the response matrix

\[ rac{Q_*}{4\pi\epsilon} \left( rac1{R-a}- rac1{R+a} ight) egin{pmatrix}1&0\0&1\end{pmatrix}. ag{18} \]

Its rank is two. This is an algebraic static extended-source control with specified sources and ideal noninvasive probes, not an acquisition or transport experiment. It establishes why the earlier TNFR response-rank obstruction is not by itself a discriminator against conventional electric charge. It does not require the two reference sources to arise under (1).

docs.title: A candidate complete density observation, before calibration
docs.text:
Supply fixed disjoint spatial cells with normalized smooth shapes w_i(z), each supported in its cell, so integral w_i=1. Their locations, sizes and orientations are input geometry, not deductions from slot labels or graph conductances. Consider the candidate

\[ q_i=\kappa(x_i-r),\quad \rho_e(z)=\sum_i q_i w_i(z),\quad \tau=b(t_{lab}-t_0),\quad b>0,\quad\kappa\ne0. \tag{19} \]

Here r is fixed as in (12), kappa has units C/X, w_i has units m^-3, and b converts seconds to the declared structural clock. The ideal cell observation is integral_cell rho_e=q_i; a potential observation would instead consume (17) and the sensor's specified spatial weighting. Every charge derivative transforms as dq_i/dt_lab=b*kappa*x_i'. Neither x_i nor theta_i has been called voltage or physical position.

This is a fully stated candidate map class, not independently calibrated apparatus. docs.title: Full-density closure obstruction under the retained law
docs.text:
With fixed sigma, epsilon, geometry and boundary data, (16)--(17) assign one density derivative to each complete density. In particular rho_e=0 everywhere implies phi=E=J=0 and rho_e_dot=0. This is a consequence of Poisson plus the stated current law and boundary condition. Electrostatics alone does not specify charge transport. Zero net charge, or zero charge only in a region with externally imposed field, would not give this conclusion.

Reuse the actual same-slot 54-node support of organized external interaction. Let alpha=2*pi/9. At every host node (c,j) set x_H=r, theta_H=alpha*j; at every donor node set x_D=r, theta_D=alpha*j+beta. Compare beta=0 and beta=pi/2. These are two allowed mathematical initial states of the complete quarter law on exactly the same support. They are not asserted to be reached members of the frozen acquisition box. Their old internal and outer phase profiles are well defined; no finite maintenance certificate is inferred.

The complete density (19) is zero for both. All form Laplacians and all phase rates vanish initially. The two internal cycle currents cancel at each node, and host outer currents vanish. The remaining contact terms are

\[ x'_{H,c,j}=\frac\gamma4\sin\beta,\qquad x'_{D,j}=-\frac{5\gamma}4\sin\beta,\qquad \theta'=0. \tag{20} \]

Thus all derivatives vanish at beta=0, whereas at beta=pi/2 each host cell gains b*kappa*gamma/4 and each donor cell loses 5*b*kappa*gamma/4 in physical-time charge units. The total remains zero: 45 host contributions cancel the nine donor contributions. Disjoint shapes make the density derivative in the beta=pi/2 preparation nonzero as a spatial function.

Consequently no deterministic density-only evolution, including (16), can represent both states through (19). This is stronger than two equal net inventories having different currents: the entire mapped spatial density and all reference inputs agree. The site classification explains why adding a circular phase term to an identical local conserved density does not fix this full-domain map. It does not prohibit retaining phase as additional material state, a collective density, or a justified smaller invariant family.

The phase-sensitive transfer mechanism was already established by the regional interaction owner. Equation (20) specializes its cancellation argument to the actual uniform quarter law and support. The new conclusion is the specified physical-map obstruction, not a newly discovered phase response. The execution controls check all 54 rates and reciprocal balance through the shared contact observer; they are neither a physical experiment nor proof of the general classification.

The gate therefore closes with a scoped exact map/law incompatibility. Installing (17) as a TNFR readout alone would merely supply the conventional electrostatic law. Matching that static readout would give no independent discriminator; omitting phase from the full transport still fails (20). Physical charge, non-Ohmic materials, polarization state, memory, other laws and prepared subdomains remain open. The earlier P2 and Volts decisions retain their distinct pure-EPI laws and failed source admissions. No archived response was replayed and no empirical dataset was admitted here.

docs.title: Homogeneous local edge redistribution does not close one density field
docs.text:
The edge allocation in (15) preserves the total inventory algebraically. That property does not establish an autonomous law for its spatial density. The following obstruction covers one explicitly specified extension and uses the unchanged complete quarter law, without a numerical trajectory.

Give each edge an arbitrary orientation. Let the incidence matrix B have -1 at its tail and +1 at its head, so that L=BB^T and S(theta)=-B sin(B^T theta). Retain one held reference r and a nonzero scale kappa. Consider the observation

\[ q(x,\theta)=\kappa(x-r\mathbf1) +B\,p(B^Tx,B^T\theta),\qquad \kappa\ne0. \tag{E1} \]

Here the same scalar C1 function p(u,v) is applied to every edge. It is 2pi-periodic in v and satisfies p(-u,-v)=-p(u,v), so reversing a supplied edge orientation leaves q unchanged. Dependence on other edges, independent material state, unequal edge laws and history is excluded from this class. The observation is defined on a full-state neighborhood of the equilibrium under consideration; a selected lower-dimensional preparation set is a different domain. Its total remains kappasum_i(x_i-r).

By a smooth density closure mean a C1 field G with

\[ Dq(x,\theta)F(x,\theta)=G(q(x,\theta)) \tag{E2} \]

throughout that neighborhood, where F is both full rows of (1). The claim allows an arbitrary G, including spatially nonlocal linearizations. No specific electrostatic kernel or conductivity is needed for the obstruction.

docs.title: Necessary mode condition
docs.text:
First take a uniform equilibrium x=r1, theta=theta_01. Put a=p_u(0,0) and b=p_v(0,0). Since p(0,0)=0, q=0 there, and

\[ Dq_*=[\kappa I+aL,\ bL],\qquad DF_*={1\over4} \begin{pmatrix}-L&-\gamma L\\ \gamma L&0\end{pmatrix}. \tag{E3} \]

At an equilibrium the derivative of (E2) gives Dq_* DF_=DG(0)Dq_. For an eigenvector of L with positive eigenvalue lambda, define c_lambda=(kappa+alambda,blambda). A perturbation on that mode which belongs to ker(c_lambda) must have zero observed derivative. Consequently c_lambda times [[-1,-gamma],[gamma,0]] must be proportional to c_lambda when that row is nonzero. Equivalently,

\[ P(\lambda)= \gamma(\kappa+a\lambda)^2 -b\lambda(\kappa+a\lambda) +\gamma b^2\lambda^2=0. \tag{E4} \]

If c_lambda=0, (E4) also holds automatically. Thus a mode erased by the observation does not evade this necessary condition. The argument does not assume that DG(0) is a function of L or initially diagonal in its eigenbasis: kernel preservation alone implies (E4).

The polynomial P has degree at most two and constant term gamma*kappa^2, which is nonzero. A graph with at least three distinct positive Laplacian eigenvalues therefore cannot admit (E2) for any a,b, and hence for any p in the declared class. This is a necessary linearization obstruction to exact nonlinear closure; satisfying it on some smaller spectrum would not prove nonlinear closure.

docs.title: The obstruction also holds near an acute C9 twist
docs.text:
This conclusion need not rely on a uniform-phase neighborhood. Orient a C9 cycle consecutively and take x=r1 and theta_j=theta_0+2pij/9 modulo 2pi. Every oriented edge has the same circular difference delta_=2pi/9. The closing edge differs by a full turn, so periodicity gives the same p and derivatives there. A constant edge allocation has zero incidence divergence on this oriented cycle, hence q_*=0. Put

\[ c=\cos(2\pi/9)>0,\qquad a=p_u(0,\delta_*),\quad b=p_v(0,\delta_*). \]

The true tangent at this equilibrium replaces the upper-right block in (E3) by -gammacL; the lower-left block remains gamma*L. The required polynomial is therefore

\[ P_c(\lambda)= \gamma c(\kappa+a\lambda)^2 -b\lambda(\kappa+a\lambda) +\gamma b^2\lambda^2=0. \tag{E5} \]

Its constant term is gammackappa^2, again nonzero. The cycle has the four distinct positive eigenvalues

\[ \lambda_k=2-2\cos(2\pi k/9),\qquad k=1,2,3,4. \]

They are strictly increasing because their arguments lie in (0,pi). Four distinct roots are impossible for the nonzero polynomial (E5). Thus no observation (E1) has a smooth autonomous density law on any full-state neighborhood of this acute winding-one equilibrium. This uses the actual twisted tangent, not a transferred consensus certificate. It does not show that the retained finite acquisition history fills such a neighborhood, nor exclude a map defined only on an admitted smaller invariant family.

The conclusion strengthens the conservation-only example (15): adding one homogeneous local edge allocation cannot make the mapped density a complete state for the unchanged quarter dynamics on these domains. It does not exclude a density accompanied by independent internal material variables, unequal or nonlocal observations, a memory law, or a different complete model. Nor does it identify the mathematical edge allocation with physical polarization. A fixed nonzero clock conversion rescales the tangent and leaves its kernel condition unchanged.

At the carrier, let K(Phi)=-D S(psi+R Phi). Its exact form is

\[ K(\Phi)=\cos(2\pi/9)(I_5\otimes L_9) +L_5^{\cos(\Phi)}\otimes I_9, \tag{5} \]

where the weighted outer Laplacian uses the cosine of each current outer phase gap. It can be time dependent and need not be positive for arbitrary Phi. Both K and L_f commute with P and Q. Consequently R^T K Q=0 and Q K R=0: the full collective and hidden variational equations decouple along any carrier trajectory. The hidden tangent generator is
