docs.title: 5.18. Compactness gives a uniform but uncomputed reorganization gap
docs.text:
The dependence on sigma in (17am) leaves a separate question: could PSD stationary states approach common host profiles while their reference rims approach cuts? The cut limits can be included without treating them as admitted targets.

Let K_closed be the closure, in the compact 54-phasor torus, of the original complete marked phase class. Let E_PSD consist of its stationary states with M>=0. Both stationarity and PSD are closed conditions, so E_PSD is compact. Let C_common be the compact set of phases with z_(c,j)=p_j*q_c for all five hosts, with arbitrary unit p, q and arbitrary donor phasors. We show that these two compact sets are disjoint.

At any supposed intersection, the reference rim q lies in the closure of the cut-free winding-one rim class. If it has at least three distinct phasors, the rank-three argument (17aa) still applies, even at marked cuts: stationarity forces the donor to share p with a constant relative origin. The wheel inequality of section 5.1 extends to this rim closure by continuity. The common-profile pair then has quadratic form at most -9/2, contradicting PSD.

The remaining case has at most two distinct rim phasors. A one-point rim has winding zero in an open neighborhood without cuts, so cannot be such a limit. The same holds for two nonantipodal points: every transition between them has a reverse transition, their principal gaps cancel, and all rim edges stay away from cuts. Thus the only possible two-point limit is an antipodal partition, with nonempty host groups P and N at q_plus and -q_plus. Let k be the number of rim edges crossing that partition; k>=2. Put Q=sum_j Re(w_j*conj(p_j*q_plus)). The indicators of all nodes in the respective host groups, with zero donor entries, give exact cut forms

\[ \mathbf1_P^TM\mathbf1_P=-9k+|P|Q,\qquad \mathbf1_N^TM\mathbf1_N=-9k-|N|Q. \tag{17ap} \]

Internal edges do not cross either cut, each crossing rim cosine is -1, and the spoke terms have the displayed opposite signs. If Q is nonpositive choose P; otherwise choose N. The chosen form is at most -9k<=-18, again contradicting PSD. This boundary control requires no donor profile assumption and no stationarity equation. Recentring its indicator preserves the negative relative form.

Define the distance of the actual hosts from the entire common-profile family by

\[ d_{\rm common}(z_H) =\min_{p\in(S^1)^9,\ q\in(S^1)^5} \max_{c,j}|z_{c,j}-p_jq_c|. \tag{17aq} \]

The minimum is attained, this distance is continuous, and it vanishes exactly on the host projections of C_common. Since C_common allows every donor, disjointness gives a number delta_*>0 such that every state in E_PSD satisfies d_common>=delta_*, if E_PSD is nonempty. If it is empty, the exclusion is vacuous. In particular every possible stable stationary target in the original marked class must be separated by a finite host deformation from all common host profiles, including sequences whose reference rims approach cuts. Additional Hessian zero modes are included in this PSD statement.

This is an existence proof of a positive separation, with no value or computable certificate for delta_star supplied. It proves neither that E_PSD is nonempty nor that the remaining genuinely different host profiles are unstable. The explicit reference-dependent bound (17am), the uniform-rim defect (17an), and this global uncomputed gap have different conclusions. Only the uniform-rim result has the conditional complete-flow exit consequence established above. None supplies actual-source capture, general common-profile-tube exit or physical identification. The execution plan retains the stationary feasibility and full stability decision beyond these exclusions.

docs.title: 5.19. Every complete unforced contact trajectory converges to one equilibrium
docs.text:
The same fixed sine law gives a global convergence statement without a marked-class, acute-gap or positive-Hessian premise. Every finite initial state with zero form mean has a global forward solution, finite total phase variation and a single limiting equilibrium. The limit can depend on initialization; this is not uniqueness of the stationary configuration. It does not decide which equilibrium is reached or whether a stable stationary target exists in the original marked class.

Write mathcal H=1^perp, and restrict L to this relative space. Set lambda=lambda_min(L|mathcal H)>0 and mu=||L||<=10. At the conserved lifted phase mean, phase can be represented on the compact flat torus mathcal H/(2*pi*(Z^54 intersect mathcal H)). This quotient retains the given continuous lift locally; no boundedness of that lift is assumed. Let q denote this circular relative phase, let V be the 144-edge phase potential in (1), and put

\[ k= rac{\gamma^2}{16}< rac1{16},\qquad U(q)=kV(q),\quad g= abla U,\quad P=L^{-1}|_{\mathcal H},\qquad v=q'= rac\gamma4Lx. ag{17ar} \]

Since grad V=-S, differentiation of the actual phase row gives the equivalent damped mechanical system and its energy identity

\[ Pv'+ rac14v+g=0,\qquad E= rac12v^TPv+U=kH,\qquad E'=- rac14\|v\|^2. ag{17as} \]

Here P is a mathematical metric on the declared coordinates; it is not an identification of physical mass. The nonnegative energy bounds x and v on the fixed form-mean leaf. The smooth vector field has bounded phase currents and only linear form dependence, so solutions exist for all forward time and their form/circular-phase states are precompact. The invariance argument used in section 5.17 gives a nonempty compact omega-limit set consisting entirely of equilibria: zero loss requires v=0, and invariance of that condition in (17as) requires g=0. In particular v->0, g->0 and E->E_infinity.

To prove convergence to one point rather than just to this stationary set, use the auxiliary real-analytic proof function

\[ F(q,v)=E(q,v)+ rac18g(q)^Tv. ag{17at} \]

F is not a new model law, physical storage or installed diagnostic. The declared H and its loss identity remain unchanged.

The phase Hessian satisfies ||Hess U||<=k*mu: the signed-cosine Laplacian M obeys -L<=M<=L. Along the complete law,

\[ egin{split} F'&=- rac14\|v\|^2+ rac18\left(v^T( abla^2U)v- rac14g^TLv-g^TLg ight),\ rac14|g^TLv|&\le rac12g^TLg+ rac1{32}v^TLv,\ F'&\le- rac{17}{128}\|v\|^2- rac1{16}g^TLg \le-c ig(\|v\|^2+\|g\|^2 ig),\qquad c=\min\left\{ rac{17}{128}, rac\lambda{16} ight\}>0. \end{split} ag{17au} \]

The constant uses only k<1/16 and mu<=10, including nonacute states and marked-cut crossings. F is bounded below on the orbit, decreases, and has limit E_infinity, since its extra term tends to zero. Every point of the omega-limit set is a critical point of F at that same value.

The local analytic gradient inequality therefore applies to F in a coordinate chart around each such point. This is the analytic method for damped second-order systems developed by Haraux and Jendoubi (1998), DOI 10.1006/jdeq.1997.3393; the local gradient-inequality and finite-length argument is also stated in Begout, Bolte and Jendoubi, On damped second-order gradient systems, arXiv version 5. Their bounded Euclidean-trajectory hypothesis is not assumed for a phase lift here. Compactness of the circular omega-limit set supplies a finite chart cover. Taking the minimum of its positive exponents and enlarging its constant gives, for every sufficiently late time,

\[ (F-E_\infty)^{1- ho} \le C\| abla F\| \le C_1(\|v\|+\|g\|),\qquad 0< ho\le frac12. ag{17av} \]

Indeed the orbit eventually stays in every neighborhood of its compact omega-limit set. In combining the finitely many inequalities one can also require 0<=F-E_infinity<1. The last bound follows directly from grad_q F=g+(Hess U)*v/8 and grad_v F=P*v+g/8.

If F reaches its limiting value at a finite time, (17au) makes the state stationary thereafter. Otherwise (17au)--(17av) imply

\[ - rac{d}{d au}(F-E_\infty)^ ho \ge c_1(\|v\|+\|g\|),\qquad \int_0^\infty(\|v\|+\|g\|)\,d au<\infty ag{17aw} \]

for a positive constant c1 at sufficiently late times; the finite initial interval contributes a finite amount. Thus the phase has finite total variation. Its original continuous lift is Cauchy and converges in the fixed-mean affine space. This proves boundedness of the lift as a consequence, rather than using it as a premise. Equation (17as) also gives integrable v', hence integrable x'=(4/gamma)*P*v'. The full state converges to a single point with x=0 and S(theta)=0.

The limit may be a saddle, a degenerate equilibrium or a marked-cut state. The theorem excludes persistent nonstationary limiting motion under (1), while allowing transient motion, connecting orbits and damped oscillations. Even finite phase variation can coexist with infinitely many marked-cut crossings if the limit lies on a cut. If the limit is cut-free, all marked windings are eventually constant; their values are not selected by this argument. No convergence rate, finite settling time, source-to-target capture or physical identification is supplied.

There is a stronger departure consequence for the already admitted outer-one source. Define its distance from the fixed uniform reference rim, with arbitrary common profile and donor, by d_uniform=min_p max_(c,j)|z_(c,j)-p_j*q_c| as in section 5.17. The current floor (17an) forces every stationary state to satisfy d_uniform>=1/(9*sqrt(2)). Consequently the limiting distance of every continued-contact trajectory obeys

\[ d_{ m uniform}( heta_\infty)\ge rac1{9\sqrt2}. ag{17ax} \]

In particular the entire original source family, at every donor origin, eventually stays outside the closed tube of radius 1/25 that initially contains it by (17ao). A finite last-exit time exists but is not bounded here. This permanent exclusion already follows from the compact omega-limit argument and the no-equilibrium gap: arbitrarily late returns would give a stationary accumulation point inside that tube. It does not require the analytic finite-length step. The latter separately proves convergence of the complete state and its continuous lifts.

These statements retain the unchanged complete law, support, capacity and clock, with no later input or event. They reuse the existing source inclusion rather than evaluating a new trajectory or modifying a frozen assessment. Permanent departure from this particular uniform-rim tube does not establish winding loss or departure from every common-host profile. Stable stationary feasibility in the full original marked class, and the actual source's eventual marked identity, remain unresolved.

docs.title: 6. Actual aligned outer-zero control after the full observation word
docs.text:
The local target in (2) becomes a maintenance result only with an actual source inclusion argument. This section uses the separately declared outer-zero control and primitive external origin beta=0. It retains the original twelve allowances, recovered fine states and all five sequential observation blocks. The source owner supplies the actual residual control, not the exactly stationary zero-error target. No coordinate is reset after observation and no settling interval is inserted.

Let r and z be the freshly rebuilt full-form and full-phase error upper bounds from the host source, and q=1e-70 the external source bound. Let g be the upper bound for gamma and T the complete observation-word duration. At the beginning of that word the actual control has ||x_H||_infinity<=r and phase offsets from psi of magnitude at most z. During observation the host has degree four and both rows retain their uniform quarter factor. The diffusion semigroup contracts the maximum norm, and |S_i|<=4, so throughout the complete word

\[ B=r+gT,\qquad \|x_H\|_\infty\le B. \tag{18} \]

All fifteen supplied phase events leave form unchanged. Their accumulated commanded offsets sum to zero at the end of the word, but the continuous phase drift survives. Because |theta_i'|<=2*g*B, the actual reached host phase offsets satisfy

\[ Z_c=z+2gBT,\qquad |\theta_{H,c,j}-\psi_j|\le Z_c. \tag{19} \]

This bound accounts for motion during every commanded phase offset; it does not interpret the final inverse command as restoration of state. The separately recovered external constituent retains form and phase offset magnitudes at most q. Thus define

\[ b=\max(B,q),\qquad e=\max(Z_c,q). \tag{20} \]

The declared beta=0 and preserved zero means put the actual joined source on the same mean leaf as x*=0, theta*_{c,j}=psi_j. Each internal gap is in [alpha-2e,alpha+2e]; ring and spoke gaps have absolute value at most 2e. Initial inclusion in the joined acute target chart follows by checking the strict margins

\[ \alpha-2e>0,\qquad \pi/2-\alpha-2e>0,\qquad \pi/2-2e>0. \tag{21} \]

The first margin is a useful initial property, not an assertion that all internal edge gaps remain positive forever.

docs.title: Present storage and new attachment work
docs.text:
Every form edge difference has magnitude at most 2b. The 144 edges give form storage at most 288*b^2. The target phase gradient vanishes, so the sum of first-order phase terms is zero. Every edge phase perturbation has magnitude at most 2e, and the absolute second derivative of its potential is at most one. Taylor's integral remainder therefore bounds the complete phase excess by 144*(2*e)^2/2=288*e^2. Consequently

\[ H(0)-6V_9\le U_0:=288(b^2+e^2). \tag{22} \]

This is the storage of the actual reached source, including the observation history through (18)--(19). It is not the sum of historical preparation expenditures. For the new 45-edge attachment event alone, 1-cos(a)<=a^2/2 gives the separate bound

\[ 0\le W_B\le\frac{45}{2}\big[(B+q)^2+(Z_c+q)^2\big]. \tag{23} \]

All earlier acquisition, outer attachment and observation events retain their own signed work and expenditure accounting. A small present excess or new attachment cost neither erases these costs nor assigns dissipated storage to an undeclared event reservoir.

docs.title: Full-state trap and convergence
docs.text:
On the joined acute cell, each of the six internal C9 cycles has winding one and phase cost at least V9 by convexity. All 90 wheel edges have nonnegative phase cost. An internal acute boundary costs at least b9-V9 above the six-cycle minimum, where

\[ b_9=1+8[1-\cos(3\pi/16)]. \tag{24} \]

This is the smaller positive-boundary value. A negative internal face leaves the other eight gaps summing to 5*pi/2 and has the larger bound 1+8*(1-cos(5*pi/16)). A wheel-edge acute boundary costs one while the six internal cycles retain their minima. Hence every feasible acute cell boundary has storage excess at least

\[ \mathcal B=\min\{b_9-V_9,1\}>0. \tag{25} \]

No claim that the separate minimizing cycle configurations can be realized simultaneously is needed: these are lower bounds on every actual boundary point. The phase-space cell uses the branches inherited from the aligned target. Within it all edge cosines are positive, so the phase Hessian is positive definite on the zero-mean leaf. Its lifted cell is convex, and the target is its unique stationary phase point.

If the rebuilt actual source satisfies (21) and U0<min(1/100,Bcal), nonincrease of H forbids a first exit from the cell. Use the preserved closed sublevel H-6V9<=U0<Bcal on the fixed-mean leaf inside the target cell. Its closure cannot meet the cell boundary because every boundary point costs at least Bcal. Connectedness bounds form through its quadratic storage and phase through fixed-branch edge differences. The sublevel is therefore compact. Its largest invariant zero-loss set requires Lx=0 and S(theta)=0; it is the single aligned target. The invariance principle therefore proves all-future retention of six internal windings one and nine old outer windings zero, and full-state convergence to the target. It supplies no finite settling time. The proof does not extend source inclusion to beta different from zero or to the outer-one preparation.

docs.title: 7. Fixed actual-source assessment and research boundary
docs.text:
The declared exact-rational rebuild at the maximum of all twelve original allowances certifies source admission and the following conservative bounds:

\[ \begin{split} B&<6.224\cdot10^{-8},& Z_c&<7.746\cdot10^{-15},\\ U_0&<1.116\cdot10^{-12}<1/100,& \mathcal B&>0.2426,\\ W_B&<8.714\cdot10^{-14},& D(\theta_1(0))&<1.395\cdot10^{-16}<8/5<9d. \end{split}\tag{26} \]

The three initial cell margins are strictly positive. All original source directions survive the argument; arbitrary correlation is permitted, and smaller admitted allowances satisfy the same monotone bounds. The actual beta=0 outer-zero control therefore passes the frozen criterion with its whole observation history. It retains all fifteen marked windings for all future time and converges to the aligned target under the supplied continued-contact law. The statement is about an entire admitted source family, not a fitted nominal trajectory.

For the outer-one family, (26) certifies only initial membership in the negative phase-curvature domain, uniformly over the supplied relative origin. Its nonstationary future is not replaced by an equilibrium or an infinitesimal perturbation calculation. The exact carrier cannot remain in the old acute chart indefinitely; a stable full-fine stationary organization retaining that chart would require D to exceed 9d. The existence, acquisition and maintained identity of such a substantially reorganized fine state remain unresolved. An outer gap becoming nonacute would still require a separate winding-loss check. The subsequent full-domain curvature result supplies the stronger necessary condition D>=9/4 without the acute outer-gap restriction and excludes every common internal phase profile. It does not extend the frozen source calculation into a future-retention certificate.

The separate uniform-rim source corollary uses the retained endpoint and observation-history inequalities to prove eventual exit of the full outer-one family from a specified uniform-rim neighborhood, at every donor origin. This is a full-fine departure result, with neither an exit-time bound nor a winding-loss conclusion; the frozen assessment (26) and its flags keep their original scope.

These results separate maintained constituent identity, loss of a convenient capture chart, stationary instability and actual-source identity loss. They do not justify another series of short-horizon refinements or transfer the beta=0 control to another registration. Any following change of organization, interface, state restriction or complete law needs its own admission. The execution plan owns that decision and the property-first physical comparison; none of the present bounds identifies mass, charge or another fundamental physical property.

The reflection classification adds a separate obstruction without an acute-gap or small-defect premise. Its static reflection sector includes nonuniform internal profiles; no stable stationary state there retains all fifteen winding-one identities. An explicit nonacute saddle shows that stationary existence remains distinct from stability. Neither result supplies the actual outer-one source's fate.

docs.text:
The maintenance owner reuses the existing complete contact support and exact interval arithmetic. The dedicated tests exercise complete support and tangent modes, both stationary controls, primitive admission, source rebuilding and scoped source-bound verdicts. The later analytical extension in sections 5.1-5.19 uses exact identities and counterexamples. docs.title: Internal preparation modes and organized contact response
docs.text:
This owner answers the full-fine preparation question declared at b2801170 in the execution plan. Every internal disturbance with zero mean in each child is invisible to the donor mean at first variation along the entire evolving ideal carrier. Opposite internal modes can nevertheless generate a second-order mean response. Exact reflection protection is a separate, stronger condition.

The result concerns conditional perturbations of the exact limiting family in the dynamic cancellation theorem. It does not turn those perturbations into acquired residuals or supply a finite noisy response, transverse stability theorem or physical readout.

The constituent-memory theorem already establishes tangent decoupling, quadratic covariance feedback and closure collisions for the sine \(C_9\mathbin\square C_5\) model. The present contribution is the full \(C_9\mathbin\square W_6\) reciprocal contact under both retained laws: all-time internal-mode invisibility of its donor observable, the distinction between a linear kernel and exact reflection protection, and explicit phase/form disturbances that break the ideal onset behavior. Its coefficients and conclusions are derived on this support rather than transferred from that predecessor.

docs.title: 1. Full model and preparation directions
docs.text:
Retain exactly the two endpoint currents

\[ j_\lambda(a)=\sin a+\frac\lambda{2187} (\sin9a-\tfrac12\sin18a),\qquad \lambda=0,1, \tag{1} \]

and their potential \(V_\lambda\) from the prior owner. On all 54 nodes and 144 unit edges of \(C_9\mathbin\square W_6\), both complete rows are

\[ x'=\tfrac14(-Lx+\gamma S_\lambda(\theta)),\qquad \theta'=\tfrac\gamma4Lx,\qquad S_{\lambda,a}(\theta)=\sum_{b\sim a}j_\lambda(\theta_b-\theta_a), \quad \gamma=\frac1{1023\pi}. \tag{2} \]

Prime means \(\tau=(1023/1024)t\). Forms are signed, capacities are held at one, and phases occupy the full circle with declared lifts. There is no later input or event. The same quarter factor remains in both rows; the donor and host both react to contact.

Write \(\theta^0(\beta)\) for the ideal initial phases \(\psi_j+\phi_c\) on host child \(c=0,\ldots,4\), and \(\psi_j+\beta\) on the donor, where \(\psi_j=2\pi(j-4)/9\), \(\phi_c=2\pi(c-2)/5\). The perturbed initial state is

\[ x(0;\epsilon)=\epsilon u,\qquad \theta(0;\epsilon)=\theta^0(\beta)+\epsilon v, \qquad \mathbf1^Tu=\mathbf1^Tv=0. \tag{3} \]

Both directions have all 54 coordinates. Their constraints fix total form and the phase gauge, so the complete histories have total form zero and lifted phase total \(9\beta\). The amplitude \(\epsilon\) scales specified form and phase directions in their respective structural units; no physical identification of these units is supplied.

Let \(\bar y_c=\frac19\sum_j y_{c,j}\). Each row splits uniquely into its six child means and eight zero-mean modes per child. Thus the constrained preparation space has ten collective and 96 internal real directions. The donor observation is the same linear functional \(d^Tx=\bar x_D=R_D\); it does not consume hidden state directly.

docs.title: 2. Variations along the evolving full carrier
docs.text:
Denote the unperturbed full solution by \((x_0,\theta_0)\). It remains on the twelve-coordinate carrier, but its forms and origins evolve under both rows of (2). Define the amplitude expansion on every fixed finite time interval by

\[ x=x_0+\epsilon x_1+\epsilon^2x_2+o(\epsilon^2),\qquad \theta=\theta_0+\epsilon y_1+\epsilon^2y_2+o(\epsilon^2). \tag{4} \]

The second coefficients are one half of the second amplitude derivatives. They are not additional preparations or frozen source coordinates. Smooth dependence follows from the smooth complete field. Put \(J(\tau)=DS_\lambda(\theta_0(\tau))\) and \(Q(\tau)=D^2S_\lambda(\theta_0(\tau))\). Explicitly,

\[ \begin{split} (Jz)_a&=\sum_{b\sim a}j_\lambda'(\theta_{0,b}-\theta_{0,a})(z_b-z_a),\\ Q[z,w]_a&=\sum_{b\sim a}j_\lambda''(\theta_{0,b}-\theta_{0,a}) (z_b-z_a)(w_b-w_a). \end{split}\tag{5} \]

With \(A=-L/4\), \(b=\gamma/4\) and \(C=\gamma L/4\), the complete variational equations are

\[ \begin{array}{ll} x_1'=Ax_1+bJy_1,& y_1'=Cx_1,\\ x_2'=Ax_2+bJy_2+\tfrac b2Q[y_1,y_1],&y_2'=Cx_2, \end{array} \qquad (x_1,y_1)(0)=(u,v),\quad(x_2,y_2)(0)=(0,0). \tag{6} \]

All four variation rows have zero global mean. In particular, the second-order forcing retains equal opposite edge reactions; it creates no net form. The time dependence of \(J,Q\) is retained throughout.

Let \(T\) be the simultaneous cyclic slot shift in all six children. The combined map \((x,\theta)\mapsto(Tx,T\theta-\alpha\mathbf1)\), \(\alpha=2\pi/9\), fixes every carrier point circularly. It is a symmetry of the complete field because slot shift is a support permutation and common phase translation is a symmetry. Its tangent is \(T\) on both variation rows. Consequently \(J(\tau)T=TJ(\tau)\), for every time along the evolving carrier.

In complex slot mode \(k\in\mathbb Z/9\mathbb Z\), write \(\mu_k=2-2\cos(2\pi k/9)\). The first variation retains the full six-form/six-phase system in that mode, with

\[ L_k=K+\mu_k I_6,\qquad J_k(\tau)=J_{\rm wheel}(\Phi(\tau)) -j_\lambda'(\alpha)\mu_kI_6. \tag{7} \]

Here \(K\) is the wheel Laplacian and \(\Phi\) comprises all six evolving origins. No mode is fed by another at first order. Real directions retain conjugate mode pairs. If \(\bar u_c=\bar v_c=0\) in every child, only \(k\ne0\) is present, and uniqueness in the zero mode gives

\[ \bar x_{1,c}(\tau)=\bar y_{1,c}(\tau)=0 \quad\text{for every child and every }\tau\ge0, \qquad \partial_\epsilon R_D(\tau;0)=0. \tag{8} \]

This is an all-time first-variation statement. It does not assert a uniform amplitude remainder over an infinite horizon or stability of internal modes. Collective directions instead obey the complete wheel tangent system and can affect the donor mean at first order. Equation (8) supplies a 96-real- dimensional invisible subspace; it does not classify every possible additional kernel of the full output history.

docs.title: 3. Quadratic selection and exact reflection protection
docs.text:
Slot equivariance gives \(TQ[z,w]=Q[Tz,Tw]\). Thus modes \(k,l\) force only mode \(k+l\pmod9\) at second order. A mean response receives the collective pair \((0,0)\) or internal pairs \((k,-k)\); a collective/internal pair cannot reach mode zero. In the internal case the mean second-order system is

\[ \begin{split} \bar x_2'&=-\tfrac14K\bar x_2+ \tfrac\gamma4J_{\rm wheel}(\Phi)\bar y_2+ \tfrac\gamma8\overline{Q[y_1,y_1]},\\ \bar y_2'&=\tfrac\gamma4K\bar x_2,\\ \overline{Q[y_1,y_1]}_c &=\sum_{a\sim_{W_6}c}j_\lambda''(\Phi_a-\Phi_c) \overline{(y_{1,a}-y_{1,c})^2}. \end{split}\tag{9} \]

Internal-cycle edge reactions cancel exactly in the last child average. They still affect \(y_1\) through (7). With the Fourier convention \(y_j=\sum_k\widehat y_ke^{2\pi ikj/9}\), the squared gap average is \(\sum_k\widehat{\Delta y}_k\widehat{\Delta y}_{-k}\). For real directions it is a sum of squared magnitudes, but its current coefficient \(j_\lambda''\) can have either sign. Opposite-mode pairing allows mean forcing; it does not guarantee a nonzero response for every internal direction.

Exact zero response has a stronger sufficient condition. At \(\beta=m\pi/5\), let the full-support reflection be \(P(c,j)=(4+m-c\bmod5,8-j)\), \(P(D,j)=(D,8-j)\). The complete-field conjugation fixes (3) for every amplitude whenever

\[ Pu=-u,\qquad Pv=-v. \tag{10} \]

Uniqueness then gives \(R_D(\tau;\epsilon)=0\) for all future time, not merely zero first or second variation. The reflection condition is a constraint on both rows and the complete fine state. It need not follow from child means, winding labels or the zero-mode kernel (8). Directions that satisfy neither this protection nor a nonzero coefficient below remain unclassified beyond the bounded amplitude and time orders; vanishing coefficients are not promoted to an invariance theorem.

docs.title: 4. Complete contact-time jets through order three
docs.text:
The following formulas retain all directions in (3), including mixtures of form, phase and collective perturbations. In this section evaluate \(J,Q\) at \(\theta^0\), let \(T_3=D^3S_\lambda(\theta^0)\), and put \(a=CbS_\lambda(\theta^0)=\theta_0''(0)\). Although \(\theta_0'(0)=0\), this acceleration is generally nonzero.

The linear coefficients of the form time derivatives are

\[ \begin{split} x_1(0)&=u,\qquad z_1:=x_1'(0)=Au+bJv,\\ z_2:=x_1''(0)&=Az_1+bJCu,\\ x_1'''(0)&=Az_2+bJCz_1+bQ[a,v]. \end{split}\tag{11} \]

The quadratic amplitude coefficients are

\[ \begin{split} x_2(0)&=0,\qquad w_1:=x_2'(0)=\tfrac b2Q[v,v],\\ w_2:=x_2''(0)&=Aw_1+bQ[v,Cu],\\ x_2'''(0)&=Aw_2+bJCw_1+bQ[Cu,Cu]+bQ[v,Cz_1] +\tfrac b2T_3[a,v,v]. \end{split}\tag{12} \]

Apply \(d^T\) only after forming these full vectors. The terms containing \(a\), the diffusion terms and both reactions prevent a frozen-host or prescribed-donor interpretation. The factor one half in (12) follows the coefficient convention (4), not a change in the complete law.

For pure phase disturbances the first quadratic donor derivative is

\[ d^Tx_2'(0)=-\frac\gamma8\sum_{c=0}^4 j_\lambda''(\beta-\phi_c)\, \overline{(v_D-v_c)^2}. \tag{13} \]

For pure form disturbances \(v=0\), both quadratic time derivatives of orders one and two vanish. Phase feedback yields at order three

\[ d^Tx_2'''(0)=-\frac{\gamma^3}{64}\sum_{c=0}^4 j_\lambda''(\beta-\phi_c)\, \overline{((Lu)_D-(Lu)_c)^2}. \tag{14} \]

This term would be lost by suppressing the phase row. These are contact-time derivatives; the corresponding Taylor terms in time carry the usual factorials, independently of the amplitude convention.

docs.title: 5. Winding-admissible internal leakage witnesses
docs.text:
Set \(\beta=0\), where the unperturbed response is identically zero for both laws. Choose the rational zero-mean slot vector \(w=(1,-1,0,0,0,0,0,0,0)\), supported in host child \(c=1\) only. Use it first as \(v\), with \(u=0\), then as \(u\), with \(v=0\). Both directions belong to the all-time first-order kernel (8); neither satisfies the full reflection condition (10).

Write \(s_1=\sin(2\pi/5)>0\), \(s_2=\sin(4\pi/5)>0\), and \(q_1=j_\lambda''(2\pi/5)\), \(q_0=j_\lambda''(4\pi/5)\). The actual endpoint laws give

\[ q_1=-(1-\lambda/27)s_1-(2\lambda/27)s_2<0,\qquad q_0=-(1-\lambda/27)s_2+(2\lambda/27)s_1. \tag{15} \]

For the phase witness, \(\overline{w^2}=2/9\), so (13) gives

\[ d^Tx_2'(0)=-\gamma q_1/36>0. \tag{16} \]

For the form witness, the spoke gap in \(Lu\) is \(-(L_{C_9}+4I)w\) at child 1, zero at its two rim neighbors, and \(-w\) at the two remaining host children. Direct integer arithmetic gives \(\|w\|^2=2\) and \(\|(L_{C_9}+4I)w\|^2=100\). The full set of five contact gaps in (14), rather than the disturbed child alone, therefore gives

\[ \begin{split} d^Tx_2'''(0)&=\frac{\gamma^3}{288}(q_0-49q_1)\\ &=\begin{cases} \gamma^3(49s_1-s_2)/288,&\lambda=0,\\ \gamma^3(1276s_1+72s_2)/7776,&\lambda=1. \end{cases} \end{split}\tag{17} \]

Both are strictly positive: \(s_2<s_1\), and the alternative expression has two positive terms. This is the first nonzero quadratic time derivative for the form witness. The linear donor variation is zero at all times in both examples, not just through this jet budget.

An explicit common initial winding allowance is \(0<|\epsilon|\le1/10\). In the phase witness internal edge deviations are at most \(2|\epsilon|\le1/5\), and host outer edge deviations at most \(|\epsilon|\le1/10\). Since \(\alpha-1/5>0\), \(\alpha+1/5<\pi/2\), and \(2\pi/5\pm1/10\in(0,\pi/2)\), every marked internal and outer cycle retains its initial winding-one acute chart. Undisturbed cycles are unchanged. The form witness leaves all initial phases unchanged. No winding is assigned to the new contact loops, and initial admission proves no finite-time maintenance interval.

Nonzero quadratic coefficients imply leakage for sufficiently small nonzero amplitudes inside this admitted range; the range itself is a winding allowance, not a uniform truncated-series error certificate. For the pure form witness the third contact-time derivative is exactly quadratic in \(\epsilon\): differentiating (2) three times introduces at most two initial form factors when initial phases are fixed. Its constant and linear donor terms vanish here. Neither statement identifies an acquired source or requires a trajectory evaluation.

docs.title: 6. Work, storage and the scope of robustness
docs.text:
Attachment preserves the prepared coordinates and adds the actual contact storage. With \(\delta_c=\beta-\phi_c\), \(\Delta u_{c,j}=u_{D,j}-u_{c,j}\), and similarly \(\Delta v\),

\[ \begin{split} W(\epsilon)&=\sum_{c,j}\left[ \tfrac12\epsilon^2(\Delta u_{c,j})^2+ V_\lambda(\delta_c+\epsilon\Delta v_{c,j})\right],\\ W_0&=45+5\lambda/2916,\\ W_1&=\sum_{c,j}j_\lambda(\delta_c)\Delta v_{c,j},\\ W_2&=\tfrac12\sum_{c,j} [ (\Delta u_{c,j})^2+ j_\lambda'(\delta_c)(\Delta v_{c,j})^2]. \end{split}\tag{18} \]

Here \(W_r\) are amplitude coefficients. Internal zero-mean phase directions have \(W_1=0\). The quadratic correction need not be nonnegative because the contacts need not be acute. The positive baseline attachment cost remains supplied work; continuous loss does not fund it without a separate reservoir and occurrence law.

The full storage remains \(H=\frac12x^TLx+\sum_{\text{all edges}}V_\lambda\), with \(H'=-\|Lx\|^2/4\). At preparation its quadratic coefficient is

\[ H_2(0)=\tfrac12u^TLu+ \tfrac12\sum_{\{a,b\}}j_\lambda'(\theta_b^0-\theta_a^0) (v_b-v_a)^2. \tag{19} \]

This is not automatically a coercive perturbation energy. Along the evolving base the quadratic coefficient of the storage-loss identity is \(-[\|Lx_1\|^2+2\langle Lx_0,Lx_2\rangle]/4\), which need not be nonpositive by itself. First-order invisibility therefore implies neither internal damping nor long-time transverse stability.

The mechanism separates three statements: the complete slot symmetry hides all internal modes at first order; opposite modes can feed a collective response at second order; full reflection conditions can protect exact zero response. The leakage witnesses show that zero response at a protected ideal origin is not a property of its full open preparation neighborhood. The ideal law-dependent onset orders consequently require their exact preparation scope. This does not alter the earlier finite acquired-source contact bounds, classify every zero quadratic direction, establish a noisy discriminator, select a unique law or identify a physical property.

docs.title: 7. Detached coefficient observer
docs.text:
The full-fine observer admits both complete primitive direction vectors, the endpoint law and a supplied registration before forming the derivatives in (11)--(12). It reuses the shared contact geometry, unit Laplacian, edge law and outward rational interval arithmetic. The report distinguishes amplitude coefficients from time derivatives and retains the evolving base's initial phase acceleration, work/storage coefficients and initial winding allowance.

Exact child-mean and reflection relations justify their corresponding symmetry flags through (8) and (10). An interval containing zero does not establish a vanishing derivative or invariant output. The symbolic registration and mode statements belong to this proof; the observer at a supplied origin is not a registration scan, source certificate or finite trajectory. Its fixed limits are preparation amplitude order two and contact-time derivative order three. The contract tests differentiate the complete fine-state time rows independently of the amplitude recurrence, and check all form/phase coefficients, work, storage, explicit witnesses, primitive admission and bounded stopping. They evaluate no acquired source or trajectory.

docs.title: A reflection obstruction for full-fine contact identity
Declared numerical illustration
docs.text:
The proof below is analytic. A separate detached illustration is declared here before evaluating its algebraic example; it does not discover a stationary state by fitting a numerical residual.

Item Fixed illustration scope Algebraic object The unique zero z of 16*z^3+36*z^2+24*z+1 in the exact rational bracket (-1/20,0), whose existence and uniqueness are proved in Section 4 Enclosure budget Exactly 128 rational bisections, without adaptive extension, followed by the shared dyadic128 square-root, circular-angle and edge-field arithmetic Complete state Form zero, internal profile psi_j=(2*pi/9)*(j-4), rim origins (0,b,a,-a,-b) and hub zero, with a and b defined by the unit-circle identities in Section 4; preserve the complete law (1) and all 108 coordinates Required observations Enclose all fifteen principal winding sums and certify winding one away from cuts; audit enclosing stationary residuals while retaining the exact cubic identities as the stationarity proof Instability witness Center the indicator of the fixed-rim constituent by subtracting its mean 1/6; certify its full phase quadratic form is strictly negative. Internal edges make zero contribution to this vector Execution boundary No source assessment, trajectory, eigensolver, scan, parameter tuning or root search beyond enclosure of this single analytically proved cubic root

No numerical result or passing verdict is asserted by this declaration. The research program owns activation and the next task; this illustration creates no second queue.

docs.title: 1. Question, complete model and candidate sector
docs.text:
Can a rearranged constituent profile support a stable stationary outer identity on the existing joined support? The continued-contact owner fixes the 54-node unit graph C9 square W6, held unit capacities, complete two-row law, clock and conserved means. This result retains that model:

\[ x'=(-Lx+\gamma S(\theta))/4,\qquad \theta'=\gamma Lx/4,\qquad \gamma=1/(1023\pi), \tag{1} \]

where prime denotes tau=(1023/1024)*t and S_i=sum_{b~i} sin(theta_b-theta_i). No coefficient, support edge, input, event, capacity or preparation is changed.

The marked identity consists of winding one on all six internal C9 cycles and all nine old outer C5 cycles. Each winding is the sum of its oriented principal gaps divided by 2*pi. All marked cycle edges stay away from their cuts at absolute gap pi. Internal and outer gaps may be nonacute. Spoke edges carry no separately prescribed winding identity.

Choose a reflection R of the five rim vertices of W6. It fixes one rim vertex f and the hub h, and exchanges two pairs of rim vertices. Write psi_j=theta_{h,j}. The candidate sector requires the circular identities

\[ \theta_{R(c),j}+\theta_{c,j}=2\psi_j \pmod {2\pi} \quad\text{for every rim vertex c and slot j}. \tag{2} \]

This is a restriction on proposed stationary states. It retains every fine coordinate before applying stationarity and the marked windings; it does not assume a carrier or a prescribed internal profile. Equation (2) is not asserted to define an invariant sector of the complete flow. In particular, the independently perturbed acquired source is not assumed to obey it, and no source trajectory or future source symmetry is inferred.

Conditional obstruction. No stationary state in this sector, retaining all fifteen marked windings, has a positive-semidefinite phase Hessian. Consequently any such stationary state is unstable for the complete two-row law on its fixed-mean leaf. This excludes stable stationary identity in the specified reflection sector, including nonacute charts; it does not exclude stationary targets that break that reflection.

The argument below is analytic and independent of the declared numerical illustration. It performs no trajectory, source assessment, parameter scan or reserved-response evaluation. The illustration supplies implementation evidence for its fixed example, not the proof of the obstruction.

docs.title: 2. Stationarity and identity force slot-independent relative origins
docs.text:
Connectedness and the phase row in (1) imply that stationary form is common. The form row then requires S(theta)=0. Introduce the hub's internal principal gaps

\[ \rho_j=\operatorname{wrap}(\psi_{j+1}-\psi_j),\qquad \sum_{j=0}^{8}\rho_j=2\pi. \tag{3} \]

Indices are cyclic. Reflection pairs have opposite spoke sines, while the fixed rim vertex has relative phase either zero or pi and contributes zero spoke sine. Hub stationarity therefore gives

\[ \sin\rho_j=\sin\rho_{j-1}=s. \tag{4} \]

Because hub edges avoid the winding cut, s=0 would make every rho zero; s<0 would make every rho negative. Both contradict (3). Thus

\[ s>0,\qquad 0<\rho_j<\pi\quad\text{for every j}. \tag{5} \]

These conclusions do not require an acute hub. Its gaps need not be equal: for example, one gap 6*pi/7 and eight gaps pi/7 have the same sine and sum to 2*pi.

docs.title: The fixed rim vertex cannot alternate between its two origins
docs.text: Put epsilon_j=theta_{f,j}-psi_j modulo 2*pi. Equation (2) gives epsilon_j in {0,pi}. On an internal edge where epsilon does not change, the fixed rim gap is rho_j. On an edge where it changes, its principal gap is rho_j-pi, since (5) places rho_j strictly between zero and pi. If N is the number of changes, the fixed rim gap sum is 2*pi-N*pi. Its marked winding one forces N=0. Hence its relative origin is one constant epsilon, either zero or pi.

docs.title: A reflected pair cannot redistribute internal winding
docs.text:
For either exchanged pair, write its phases as psi_j+u_j and psi_j-u_j modulo 2*pi. Let eta_j be a principal representative of u_{j+1}-u_j. Adding the two stationary nodal equations cancels their wheel currents: reflection reverses every corresponding relative phase, including edges to the fixed rim vertex at epsilon zero or pi. Their internal currents give

\[ 2\sin\rho_j\cos\eta_j -2\sin\rho_{j-1}\cos\eta_{j-1}=0. \tag{6} \]

Equations (4)--(5) imply constant cos(eta_j). There is a single d in [0,pi] such that each eta_j is congruent to +d or -d. The two child internal principal gaps at this slot are wrap(rho_j+d) and wrap(rho_j-d), in an order determined by that sign. Their sum is

\[ \begin{cases} 2\rho_j,&d<\pi-\rho_j,\\ 2\rho_j-2\pi,&d>\pi-\rho_j. \end{cases} \tag{7} \]

Equality would put a marked child edge on its winding cut and is excluded. The formula also covers d=pi through its second case. There is no lower cut crossing: rho_j-d>-pi follows from (5).

Both children have winding one, so the sum of their two gap sums must be 4*pi. The hub gap sum is 2*pi; therefore (7) permits no slot of its second kind. In particular d<pi and no child gap requires wrapping. One child's gap sum is consequently

\[ \sum_j(\rho_j+\sigma_j d)=2\pi, \qquad\sigma_j\in\{-1,1\}. \tag{8} \]

It follows that d*sum_j sigma_j=0. Nine signs have an odd, nonzero sum, so d=0. The pair's relative origins are constant across all slots. The argument applies separately to both reflected pairs.

Every candidate stationary state in this sector thus has the derived form

\[ \theta_{c,j}=\psi_j+\Phi_c\pmod {2\pi},\qquad \Phi_h=0,\qquad \Phi_f\in\{0,\pi\}. \tag{9} \]

This reduction uses the odd length nine, both members' retained internal windings and their complete stationary equations. Equality of cosine alone would not justify equal offsets. The shared internal profile may remain nonuniform and nonacute. Its currents cancel because of (4), so the remaining stationary conditions are exactly those of the unit wheel.

docs.title: 3. Unit-wheel classification in the reflected sector
docs.text:
At any slot, list the five rim origins in cyclic order as (epsilon,b,a,-a,-b), with hub origin zero. Take principal representatives for a and b. Rim branch cuts remain excluded; coincident neighboring origins, which give zero gaps, are allowed.

For any phase vector, the phase Hessian is the signed weighted Laplacian

\[ M=B\operatorname{diag}(\cos\delta_e)B^T. \tag{10} \]

A vector constant along each internal C9 has no internal edge difference. Its full quadratic form is nine times its wheel quadratic form. Thus every wheel cut used below is an exact full-state Hessian test, regardless of the shared internal profile in (9).

docs.title: Fixed rim origin zero
docs.text:
The stationary equations at b and a are

\[ \sin(a-b)=2\sin b =-\sin a\,(1+2\cos a). \tag{11} \]

If b were pi modulo 2*pi, its edge to the fixed zero vertex would lie on a marked cut. If b were zero, (11) would force a zero or pi. The pi case again has a marked cut; the zero case has outer winding zero. Consequently a retained nonzero outer winding requires b!=0 and b!=pi modulo 2*pi.

The wheel equations and Hessian are unchanged under reversal of every origin. This reverses the outer winding sign but preserves its being nonzero. For the following exclusion take 0<b<pi without loss of generality.

Suppose that M were positive semidefinite. Test the vector equal to one on the fixed rim constituent and zero on the others, constant in j. Its quadratic form is 9*(1+2*cos(b)), so necessarily

\[ 1+2\cos b\ge0. \tag{12} \]

Equation (11) gives 2*sin(b)<=1. On (0,pi), this requires either b<=pi/6 or b>=5*pi/6; (12) excludes the second alternative. Hence 0<b<=pi/6.

Now sin(a-b)>0. With a principal representative for a, there are only two possible branches: a>b, or a<b-pi<=-5*pi/6. In the latter, -sin(a)*(1+2*cos(a))<0, contradicting (11). Therefore a>b>0. The endpoint a=pi is also impossible in (11), and positivity of its last expression forces

\[ 2\pi/3<a<\pi,\qquad a-b>\pi/2. \tag{13} \]

Test the vector equal to one on the two constituents with origins a and -a, and zero on the other four constituents, again constant in j. Only the two edges to the b pair and the two spokes cross its cut. The full quadratic form is

\[ 9\,[2\cos(a-b)+2\cos a]<0, \tag{14} \]

by (13), contradicting positive semidefiniteness. Thus every stationary candidate of this kind with retained nonzero outer winding has a negative full-fine phase direction.

docs.title: Fixed rim origin pi
docs.text:
At the vertex with origin b, its hub and fixed-rim sine contributions cancel. Its stationary equation is sin(a-b)=0. A difference pi would be a marked rim cut, so a and b coincide modulo 2*pi. The remaining stationary equation is

\[ \sin b\,(1+2\cos b)=0. \tag{15} \]

The possibilities are b zero, pi or +/-2*pi/3, modulo 2*pi. The zero case puts an edge to the fixed pi vertex on a marked cut. The pi case makes all rim origins coincide, with outer winding zero. For b=2*pi/3, the rim principal gaps are (-pi/3,0,2*pi/3,0,-pi/3); for b=-2*pi/3 they have the opposite signs. Both have sum zero. No stationary candidate in this case retains the prescribed outer winding one.

docs.title: 4. An exact retained-identity stationary saddle
docs.text:
The obstruction is to stability, not to existence of any stationary state. An exact nonacute example makes that distinction explicit. Let z be the unique root in (-1/20,0) of

\[ P(z)=16z^3+36z^2+24z+1=0. \tag{16} \]

Existence and uniqueness follow from P(-1/20)=-14/125, P(0)=1 and P'(z)=24*(2*z+1)*(z+1)>0 throughout this interval. This definition requires no numerical root evaluation. Put t=sqrt(1-z^2) and k=1+2*z; choose the circular origins a and b by

\[ (\cos a,\sin a)=(z,-t),\qquad (\cos b,\sin b)=(-(2+z)k/2,tk/2). \tag{17} \]

The second pair has unit norm because (5+4*z)*(1+2*z)^2=4, which is exactly (16). These choices give -2*pi/3<a<-pi/2 and 5*pi/6<b<pi. Direct substitution yields

\[ \sin(a-b)=tk=2\sin b=-\sin a(1+2\cos a), \qquad \cos(a-b)=-k^2/2. \tag{18} \]

Thus the unit wheel with rim origins (0,b,a,-a,-b) and hub zero is stationary. Its five principal ring gaps are

\[ (b,\ 2\pi+a-b,\ -2a-2\pi,\ 2\pi+a-b,\ b). \tag{19} \]

They avoid every marked cut and sum to 2*pi. All five are nonacute: the second and fourth have negative cosine by (18), and the middle gap lies in (-pi,-2*pi/3). Set psi_j=(2*pi/9)*(j-4) in (9) and form equal to zero. The complete 54-node state is stationary, retains all six internal windings one and all nine outer windings one, and has zero global form and lifted phase means.

Its fixed-rim cut, constant along the nine slots, has quadratic form

\[ 9(1+2\cos b)=9(-1-5z-2z^2)<-27/4. \tag{20} \]

It is therefore a strict full-fine saddle. This explicit organization has internal defect zero but lies outside the earlier acute outer chart; it is not a counterexample to that chart's no-equilibrium theorem. A stationary source substitution, capture or maintained actual preparation does not follow from its construction.

docs.title: 5. Complete-law consequence and scope
docs.text:
Section 2 reduces every stationary candidate in the declared reflection sector to (9), without imposing an acute internal or outer chart. Section 3 excludes a positive-semidefinite phase Hessian when the outer winding is retained. Subtract the mean from a negative Hessian test vector: its quadratic form does not change because M*1=0.

The complete tangent argument then applies on the zero-mean subspace. Its symmetric pencil is

\[ P(s)=s^2L^{-1}+sI/4+\gamma^2M/16. \tag{21} \]

A negative eigenvalue at s=0 and positive definiteness for sufficiently large positive s supply a positive growth root. The stationary state is therefore unstable for both coupled rows, not only for a wheel model or a phase-only surrogate. The two conserved common means remain neutral.

This is not another small-defect estimate. Nonacute shared profiles are admitted: the example with one internal gap 6*pi/7 and eight pi/7 can have internal phase defect far outside the earlier near-carrier domain. The new obstruction instead uses reflection, stationary current balance, constituent winding and odd cycle length. It does not transfer to another cycle length or another coupling law without a new argument.

The result leaves open stationary targets that break (2), even if they retain all marked windings. It also leaves open actual source transport, capture, winding loss, a loss deadline and nonstationary maintenance. No instability of an actual moving source follows from this stationary classification. A source's independent fine perturbations cannot be discarded to place it in the excluded sector.

The execution plan owns the next admission and the property-first physical comparison. This conditional obstruction changes neither the earlier finite response nor the separately captured aligned outer-zero control, and identifies no fundamental physical property.

docs.text:

Their shared exact branch identities fix the winding sums; interval overlap alone would not determine an integer winding.

The full-edge quadratic enclosure satisfies the conservative displayed bound

\[ -7.030 < v^TMv < -7.029 < -27/4, \tag{22} \]

where v is the centered fixed-rim cut. The independently evaluated stationary-current boxes all contain zero and have absolute upper bounds below 5e-37. These residuals check the implemented arithmetic; the cubic and trigonometric identities (16)--(18) prove stationarity. A passing residual flag cannot replace those identities or certify an arbitrary numerical candidate. A failed arithmetic audit makes the combined implementation certificate unavailable.

The dedicated tests independently build edge fields, winding sums and the full negative cut, check exact root signs and the fixed budget, and retain the source-free and immutable-report boundaries. No trajectory or frozen source producer is invoked. This one illustrated saddle is not the proof of the general reflection-sector obstruction in Sections 2--3, and no actual acquired source is substituted by it.

docs.text:

docs.title: Root and stability acceptance
docs.text:
For a grounded phase center q, let F=-S on its 53 free nodes and let J be the grounded cosine Laplacian. The absent row follows from the exact zero sum of all currents. Every primitive coordinate and edge is re-admitted; reported residuals or Hessians are not accepted as premises.

Let R be the supplied rational approximate inverse. Outward trigonometric arithmetic at q gives bounds on F(q) and J(q). With exact midpoint matrix J0, interval radius row sums e_k, and radius r, define

\[ \eta\geq\|RF(q)\|_\infty,\qquad q_0=\max_i\left[\sum_j|\delta_{ij}-(RJ_0)_{ij}| +\sum_k|R_{ik}|e_k\right], \qquad q_B=q_0+4d_{\max}r\|R\|_\infty. \]

Here d_max=7. The cosine is 1-Lipschitz and each edge difference changes by at most 2r; the diagonal and off-diagonal row changes together are at most 4*d_max*r. Thus q_B<1 and eta+q_B*r<r make y -> y-RF(y) a strict self-map and contraction on the closed box. Its fixed point is unique there. Also q0<1 makes R*J(q) invertible, so R is invertible and the fixed point is a zero of F, not merely of a singular projection.

For each edge, bound its cosine throughout the box and round the lower bound down to the declared dyadic grid. The exact grounded Laplacian assembled from these lower weights is a Loewner lower bound for every J in the box: the difference is a sum of nonnegative multiples of edge outer products. This remains valid with negative individual edge weights. Strict exact LDL therefore certifies positive definiteness of the entire 53-dimensional phase quotient. Grounding and restricting to mean zero are congruent descriptions; their numerical eigenvalues need not coincide. The complete two-row tangent pencil from the contact theorem then has 106 stable relative directions and the two retained neutral means. A nonpassing LDL check alone proves neither instability nor nonexistence; extra zero directions remain unresolved.

For completeness, positivity suffices without simultaneous diagonalization of L and M. Linearization gives theta''=-L*theta'/4-gamma^2*L*M*theta/16. On the mean-zero subspace, any complex eigenpair satisfies (s^2*L^-1+s*I/4+gamma^2*M/16)v=0. Multiplying by the conjugate transpose of v gives a*s^2+b*s+c=0 with strictly positive real a=v*L^-1*v, b=||v||^2/4 and c=gamma^2*v*M*v/16. Both real roots are negative, and nonreal roots have real part -b/(2*a)<0. The smooth complete law therefore has local exponential stability on each fixed-mean leaf; neither common mean is damped.

For every marked edge, its interval gap minus 2*pi*k must lie strictly between -pi+1/1024 and pi-1/1024. The integer branch sum is -1 around each of the fifteen cycles, so telescoping gives winding one exactly. Interval overlap of a sum with 2*pi is not used as a winding proof.

docs.title: Marked-cycle information and connected chambers
docs.text:
The fifteen prescribed winding numbers do not specify every winding on the marked support. Remove the 45 unmarked spokes. The resulting marked graph has 99 edges, 54 vertices and two connected components: the 45-node host product C9 square C5 and the donor C9. Its real cycle-space dimension is therefore 99-54+2=47. The six internal cycles and nine outer cycles are independent: they are pairwise edge-disjoint, and every one has an edge with nonzero coefficient that appears in no other prescribed cycle. Their span has dimension 15, leaving 47-15=32 cycle-space directions not specified by those observations. This dimension count does not assert that arbitrary integer assignments to the remaining directions are simultaneously realizable by phases with principal gaps.

For an oriented marked edge a -> b, choose real phase lifts and write

\[ \delta_{ab}=\theta_b-\theta_a-2\pi k_{ab}, \qquad -\pi<\delta_{ab}<\pi,\qquad k_{ab}\in\mathbb Z. \]

Changing a vertex lift by 2*pi*m_a changes k_ab by m_b-m_a, an integer coboundary. Its circulation around every cycle is unchanged, and the principal winding of an oriented cycle is minus that circulation. Along a continuous path avoiding all marked cuts, each principal gap is continuous; every integer cycle winding is therefore constant. Thus a marked-cycle class is invariant under such paths, even when only fifteen of its values are retained as the declared identity.

Conversely, suppose two phase configurations have equal windings on every marked cycle. Their branch difference has zero circulation, so integrating it along a spanning tree in each marked component supplies integer vertex shifts that make their branch vectors equal. Linear interpolation of these adjusted lifts keeps every marked gap strictly between its two cuts, because each gap interpolates between two points in the same open interval. Hence the complete realizable cycle class, modulo integer vertex shifts, specifies a connected component of the cut-free phase domain. This is a statement about continuous paths in the configuration space, not reachability under the supplied contact law.

There are two independent common marked-component angles. After quotienting the common phase of the whole connected contact graph, the relative donor angle remains a free circle coordinate; no marked edge constrains it. Spokes enter the stationary equations and storage but introduce no prescribed cut or winding here. Fixing the global lifted mean only chooses a common representative and does not remove this relative angle. The search above retains it as a free optimization coordinate. Its four supplied initial angles are starts, not four fixed-origin subproblems.

The declared branch chamber has zero winding on every elementary marked host square. It is strictly narrower than the class defined by the fifteen observations alone. An exact counterexample uses phases in turns, u=theta/(2*pi). For the five hosts set

\[ u_{c,j}=j/9+c/5+(9/25)s_c t_j,\qquad s=(1,-1,1,-1,1),\qquad t=(1,-1,1,0,0,0,0,0,0), \tag{1} \]

and set u_(5,j)=j/9 for the donor. All marked principal gaps lie strictly between -1/2 and 1/2 turns. On each perturbed internal cycle, the two changes of size 18/25 cross opposite cuts, so their winding changes cancel. The other changed gaps have principal representatives 1/9 +/- 9/25, both inside the interval. Every internal winding remains one. At each of the three perturbed outer slots, two positive and two negative 18/25 changes likewise give cancelling branch crossings. The remaining outer slots are uniform. Thus all nine outer windings also remain one.

Nevertheless, the oriented square (0,2) -> (1,2) -> (1,3) -> (0,3) -> (0,2) has principal gaps

\[ (12/25,\ 106/225,\ -1/5,\ 56/225) \]

in turns, whose sum is one. The unperturbed product state has sum zero on this square. These states therefore share the fifteen prescribed windings but lie in different marked-cut-free components, even after arbitrary integer vertex shifts. Both may be recentered to the same lifted mean without changing this conclusion.

This counterexample concerns retained information and chamber scope only. It is not a stationary or stable target: at node (0,3), the wheel currents cancel, while the internal current is sin(2*pi/9)+sin(112*pi/225)>0. No candidate search or trajectory is needed for these exact identities. The tightened margin and finite start budget further restrict the numerical search; neither expands it to the other 32 unspecified cycle-space directions or proves exclusion there.

For uninterrupted maintenance from the original product chamber, the complete marked class is a necessary target condition: every marked edge belongs to one of the fifteen observed cycles, and the all-times contract excludes its cut. Simultaneous compensating crossings can restore sampled winding values but fail that cut-free contract at the crossing. This is a kinematic restriction on a possible source-to-target connection, not a claim that the actual source reaches any stationary state.

Membership of the actual preparation in this chamber follows from the retained source bounds, rather than from those fifteen labels. The host is psi_j+Phi_c+error with coordinate error at most Z+m, Z<7*10^-70, m=2*g*B_o*T, T=1/5000, g<1/3000 and B_o<1/50; thus m<10^-8. Its carrier outer gaps are bounded by 7/5. The donor's corresponding error is at most 10^-70; its supplied common origin does not affect a marked gap. Scaling these errors to zero avoids every marked cut. The carrier's winding-one outer gaps can then interpolate to 2*pi/5, while internal gaps remain 2*pi/9. This proves membership using the existing admitted source contract, without rerunning its producers or implying that this interpolation is a trajectory of the law. The chosen zero-mean target representative can be translated to any retained common phase mean.

docs.title: Retained finite outcome
docs.text:
The declaration and instrument were frozen in 75497035c5e0840b164897119ce5a50dcf6bda91 before their single execution. The attempt record retains source revision/blobs, numeric backend, the ordered support and branch vector. The same directory preserves all 24 exact binary64 starts and endpoints. The outcome is finite_search_without_certificate.

All 24 SLSQP calls returned a success label for their constrained optimization problem. None passed the independent stationary/interior screen, so there was no root polish or candidate certificate call. They used 925 iterations and 1,581 value/gradient calls in total; per attempt these ranged from 7 to 63 iterations and from 7 to 106 calls. There was no budget extension, exception, source evolution or subsequent retry.

Every endpoint reached an imposed margin face to solver precision. The tiny negative tightened slacks are numerical constraint violations, not exact admission of that tightened closed domain. The actual principal cuts are still approximately 1/1024 radians away. Read-only reconstruction from the stored primitive coordinates checks all fifteen windings and a strictly nonzero current at every endpoint; it invokes neither initialization nor optimization. Numerical negative curvature here is a local storage diagnostic at nonstationary points, not an equilibrium-instability theorem.

The artificial constraints can stop a descent with nonzero gradient. Consequently an optimizer success label does not produce a stationary organization under the unforced complete law. These 24 endpoints supply no stable target, no global nonexistence proof, and no evidence that the actual source crosses a winding cut. Other minima in this chamber, the omitted margin strips, weakly stable or degenerate targets, and other realizable marked classes are not excluded. The new exact certificate remains a reusable acceptance mechanism; its analytic controls do not turn this nonfinding into a successful 54-node candidate.

The mathematical advance is the complete marked-class restriction and its explicit same-fifteen-windings counterexample. A target compatible with uninterrupted maintenance from the original source must lie in its product marked class. Existence and full-state stability within that class remain the missing analytical premise; increasing the number of optimizer starts would not supply it. The execution plan owns the reassessment and next admission, independently of this frozen result.

docs.title: Collective state and a matrix-response comparison
Status and responsibility
docs.text:
This owner specifies one complete collective comparison for the foundational question raised by the physical feasibility review. The law below is a supplied constitutive choice. Its balance and coordinate identities are conditional algebra. The prepared-reference theorem adds own-law identity retention, a finite response separation and a precise state-reduction obstruction. Acquisition of this preparation, fine-source inheritance and physical realization remain unestablished. The research program alone selects work and acceptance conditions.

The question is how retained state, response and storage must change together when an organized object has an additional structural coupling. It does not assume a new primitive capacity or a uniquely selected fundamental law. The NFR ontology requires any claim about constituents to retain their influence in the same configuration.

docs.title: 1. Complete comparison and units
docs.text:
Use the fixed, unit-weight, undirected C5 Laplacian L and five signed forms U with five primitive circular phases Phi. These are the collective reference coordinates in the quarter-law dictionary. They do not include the 45-node source's internal deviations. Retain the same normalized structural clock tau=(1023/1024)t and units, gamma=1/(1023 pi), and held unit scalar capacities. Primes below denote derivatives in tau. Laboratory calibration is a separate obligation. Write m for the conserved mean form; r below always denotes the response parameter, not the mean denoted r in the earlier electrical protocol.

Let r be a supplied finite constant with r>=0, and define

\[ W_r=I+rL^2,\qquad M_r=W_r^{-1},\qquad S_i(\Phi)=\sum_{j\sim i}\sin(\Phi_j-\Phi_i). \tag{1} \]

The dimensionless parameter r changes the response in this declared chart; it is not fixed by the nodal row. The complete driven equations are

\[ W_r U'=(-LU+\gamma S(\Phi))/4+f(\tau),\qquad \Phi'=\gamma LU/4. \tag{2} \]

Input f is an independently specified, neutral, locally integrable five-vector; no phase feedback, support event or input selector is implicit. There are no jumps. Thus the solved form row has input M_r f, not f. The unforced pressure is the independently specified map p=M_r*(-LU+gamma*S)/4, with U'=p at unit capacity. Circular differences enter S without choosing a principal-phase average. Means of phase lifts are used only after declaring those lifts.

W_r is symmetric positive definite, commutes with L and satisfies W_r 1=1. The full equations preserve the form mean under neutral input; on any continuous phase lift they also preserve its common mean. One may fix the neutral form leaf and quotient a common phase origin, while retaining four relative forms and four relative phases. These are symmetry reductions, not removal of response-relevant internal state. An admitted initial set, its lifted chart where needed and every proposed identity must still be specified before a finite claim.

At r=0, (2) recovers the nominal collective quarter law. For r>0 it changes only the form row in these coordinates. This differs from the phase-dependent diagonal reciprocal mobility, which changes both rows and keeps another storage. Its proofs do not transfer.

The electrical audit motivates (1) through an additional positive ring capacitance, with r=c_J/c. That motivation does not force this law on arbitrary NFRs or provide a fine-node electrical realization. In particular, replacing L by L45 would be a further constitutive choice requiring its own admission.

docs.title: 2. Storage and supplied work
docs.text:
Let V(Phi)=sum_edges[1-cos(Phi_j-Phi_i)], so grad V=-S. The comparison's own storage is

\[ H_r(U,\Phi)=\tfrac12 U^TLW_rU+V(\Phi). \tag{3} \]

Since L and W_r commute, LW_r is symmetric and positive semidefinite. Differentiating along (2) gives, almost everywhere for integrable f,

\[ H_r'=(LU)^T W_rU'-S^T\Phi' =-\|LU\|^2/4+(LU)^Tf. \tag{4} \]

The cross terms cancel. This is a storage/work balance, not a formation, stability, recurrence or observation theorem. The old H0 is not the storage in (4); the difference is r*U^T*L^3*U/2. Consequently equal initial states need not have equal storage across r. A comparison must declare which preparation quantities are matched instead of assuming both equalities.

There is an explicit obstruction to reusing the old decay claim. Set f=0, q=LU and H0=H_r at r=0. Along the positive-r law,

\[ H0'=-q^TM_rq/4+\gamma q^T(M_r-I)S/4. \]

Choose Phi=(0,pi/2,0,0,0), so S=(1,-2,1,0,0), and U=-(gamma*r/2)LS. Then q=(gamma/2)(I-W_r)S and, for every r>0,

\[ H0'=\frac{\gamma^2}{16}S^T(M_r-I)W_r(M_r-I)S>0, \qquad H_r'=-\|q\|^2/4<0. \]

The strict inequalities follow because S is a nonzero neutral vector and L is positive definite on that subspace. This example uses the full circular-phase domain of (2); it is not an admitted acute winding source. It disproves a global transfer of the old storage monotonicity, without claiming loss of an acquired identity.

Because W_r is invertible, unforced equilibria of (2) agree with those of the r=0 complete law. Their tangent rates and finite response need not agree. Matching equilibria does not transfer attraction, an initial-state capture bound or an observation certificate. A finite positive-r study must declare its parameter range and horizon before requesting uniform bounds.

docs.title: 3. Coordinate, locality and memory boundaries
docs.text:
The invertible charge-like chart Z=W_r U changes both equations:

\[ Z'=(-LM_rZ+\gamma S(\Phi))/4+f,\qquad \Phi'=\gamma LM_rZ/4, \tag{5} \]

with storage Z^T*L*M_r*Z/2+V(Phi) and work pairing (LM_r Z)^T f. Moving W_r out of the form row while retaining Phi'=gamma*L*Z/4 would therefore change the model. A regular chart change is distinct from discarding state and from choosing a different pressure law.

Although W_r is positive definite, M_r is not generally entrywise nonnegative. For example, at r=1/100 its first row is (2181,81,-19,-19,81)/2305. It is not a convex averaging map or a vector of nonnegative nodal capacities. Its coupling need not have the one-edge locality of the original sine-pressure row; locality must be justified for the actual map, including the phase and input channels.

This fixed matrix is instantaneous. It introduces no temporal memory by itself. Derived memory in the cited reductions comes from eliminating dynamical state under a specified observation, retaining hidden initialization and forcing, as in the memory owner. The inherited-metric result already distinguishes coordinate response factors from primitive capacity. Neither construction justifies replacing nu_f by M_r in the native runtime.

Holding r constant is part of (2). On the neutral form leaf, a time-dependent charge law q proportional to W_r U differentiates to an expression proportional to W_r U'+r' L^2 U; off that leaf the charge map uses W_r(U-m*1). Substituting W_r(tau) into (2) alone would be a different model. Parameter changes or support events also need their storage/work and occurrence laws.

docs.title: 4. Identity, scale and implementation boundary
docs.text:
The state in (2) is sufficient for this declared ten-coordinate ODE. The finite theorem below uses a bounded preparation of these same coordinates, including the relative phases. It is not a proof that ten coordinates predict the full acquired source. The same-slot source remainder, its hidden transport, constituent identities and acquisition use another complete law. They remain valid there. Neither r=0 recovery nor a shared equilibrium establishes those claims at positive r.

A claim about a parent NFR must define whether it concerns this prepared collective reference or a finer organization with retained constituent state. The latter needs a separately declared fine law, a state/clock/input map, exact closure or controlled error, and own-law identity bounds. Static re-encoding or formal associativity of an exact elimination is insufficient as a new capability; finite nonlinear prediction must retain the consumed boundary information. Events additionally require the existing operator descent criterion.

This comparison installs no execution law, SDK method or operator. The independent algebra controls check (1)-(5), the r=0 boundary and deliberate wrong-chart/input controls. They evaluate no reserved response. Exact matrix calculations reuse shared linear algebra. The coordinate-memory owner can split an admitted fixed linear/tangent generator or rational spatial blocks. It does not close the nonlinear sine law. Such reuse must retain nonlinear residuals, hidden initialization and forcing where consumed; rationalizing gamma would specify a different coefficient, not certify the exact comparison above. A nonlinear reduction needs its own proof. Generic runtime integration is justified only by a proved consumer contract.

docs.title: 5. Declared finite prepared-reference question
docs.text:
The analytical comparison fixes the following domain before evaluating any response. It concerns (2) alone, without a fine-node extension, source replay, physical sensor or numerical trajectory. The two models match their complete initial coordinates and prescribed input; their initial storages need not match.

Primitive Declaration Response Fixed r in [1/100,1/10]; separate reference r=0 Prepared identity Either C5 winding w=+1 or w=-1 Phase chart Phi_i=2*pi*w*i/5+theta_i, with a continuous perturbation lift and sum(theta)=0; the closing oriented edge retains its 2*pi*w offset Full preparation sum(U)=0, ||U(0)||_2+||theta(0)||_2 <= delta=2^-26 Input f=a*v for 0<=tau<=T, zero afterwards; a=1/16, v=(1,-1,0,0,0) Clock and horizon The existing structural tau; T=1/1024 Observation y=v^T*U(T) with separate additive error bounded by eta=2^-26 Identity criterion Every oriented phase gap stays within rho=1/10 of 2*pi*w/5 during the pulse and its unforced continuation Finite prediction criterion Whole-preparation observed record intervals for the positive-r family and r=0 are disjoint, with separation strictly greater than 2^-21 Calculation Exact rational inequalities and certified transcendental bounds; no integration, parameter scan, precision search or response fitting

The prediction must retain both evolution rows, the full preparation bound, the input channel M_r*f, and the law's own storage and supplied work. A separate state-sufficiency control tests whether identical forms, winding, conserved means and storage can still conceal different form derivatives. Neither success condition would derive acquisition of this preparation, constitutive selection, a laboratory clock or a physical measurement map.

docs.title: 6. Own-law identity and finite prediction
docs.text: Declaration revision a205a8fe fixes Section 5. The result is analytical: no measured or simulated response is used to set its constants or decide between the laws. Write kappa=2*pi*w/5, let D take the five oriented cyclic differences, and use the declared closing-edge offset. All norms below are Euclidean except the explicitly marked maximum norm. The mixed form/phase norm uses numerical coordinates in the fixed normalized chart of Section 1; it is not an invariant metric or a laboratory calibration.

docs.title: 6.1 Identity uses the actual storage
docs.text:
On the centered form leaf, define excess storage relative to the prepared twist by

\[ E_r=H_r-V_* =\tfrac12 U^TLW_rU+ V(\Phi_w^*+\theta)-V_*,\qquad V_*=5[1-\cos(2\pi/5)]. \tag{6} \]

The full preparation cost includes V_*; E_r is not total storage or a budget that supplies the external input. Consider the convex relative phase cell ||D theta||_infinity <= rho=1/10, sum(theta)=0. Here cos(kappa+d)>1/5 for every |d|<=rho: cosine is 1-Lipschitz and cos(2*pi/5)=(sqrt(5)-1)/4>3/10. The first variation of V at the twist vanishes because sum(D theta)=0. Taylor's integral remainder and LW_r>=0 therefore give

\[ E_r\ge\tfrac1{10}\|D\theta\|^2. \tag{7} \]

Every first contact with this cell's boundary requires E_r>=1/1000. Also ||L||<=4, as follows directly from the edge-square bound sum_edges(z_j-z_i)^2<=4||z||^2. The initial preparation consequently obeys

\[ E_r(0)\le2(1+16r_{\max})\|U(0)\|^2+2\|\theta(0)\|^2 \le(4+32r_{\max})\delta^2=\tfrac{36}{5}\,2^{-52}. \tag{8} \]

The bound also holds for the r=0 reference. Initial cell admission follows from ||D theta(0)||_infinity<=2 delta<rho. Completing the square in the own-law balance (4), rather than transferring H0 decay, yields

\[ E_r'=-\tfrac14\|LU-2f\|^2+\|f\|^2\le\|f\|^2. \tag{9} \]

During the declared pulse, ||f||^2=2a^2. Thus

\[ E_r(\tau)\le\overline E=\tfrac{36}{5}\,2^{-52}+2^{-17} <2^{-16}<\tfrac1{1000}\quad(0\le\tau\le T). \tag{10} \]

Continuity excludes a first boundary contact. After T the input is zero and E_r is nonincreasing, so the same identity survives for all future times. In particular the gaps remain strictly acute with the original winding. The smooth periodic sine term and constant positive-definite W_r give global continuation; there is no hidden event at pulse release.

On the fixed-mean lift, the intersection of E_r<=overline E with the closed relative cell is compact and contained in its interior. Zero dissipation requires LU=0, hence U=0; remaining invariant trajectories also require S=0. The potential is strictly convex on this relative cell by the cosine Hessian bound used in (7), so its only critical point is the prepared twist. The invariant-set argument therefore gives convergence to that twist after the pulse for each fixed r. It supplies no uniform settling time, acquisition from another winding sector or indefinite external activity.

docs.title: 6.2 A finite response with both rows live
docs.text:
Let z(tau)=||U(tau)||+||theta(tau)||. For every phase state, the sine-source Jacobian is an incidence matrix times a diagonal cosine matrix times its transpose; hence ||S(Phi_w^*+theta)||<=4||theta||. Also ||M_r||<=1 and the exact gamma=1/(1023*pi)<1. Both rows of (2) give

\[ D^+z\le2z+2a,\qquad \sup_{0\le\tau\le T}z(\tau)\le Z=\frac{\delta+2aT}{1-2T}. \tag{11} \]

The rational bound follows by taking the supremum in the integrated inequality, using T<1/2; it is not a numerical exponential or a frozen phase approximation. Integrating the form row and taking its v projection gives the finite prediction

\[ y=aT h(r)+R,\quad h(r)=v^TM_rv, \quad |R|\le\mathcal R=2\delta+2TZ. \tag{12} \]

The remainder retains initial form, unknown initial phase shape, damping and the phase response throughout the pulse. Here ||v||=sqrt(2)<2 and ||M_r(-LU+gamma S)/4||<=z supply (12). It is not a tangent trajectory or a finite difference at time zero.

On the neutral C5 space, L^2-5L+5I=0. With d(r)=1+15r+25r^2,

\[ M_r=\frac{(1+20r)I-5rL}{d(r)},\qquad h(r)=\frac{2(1+5r)}{d(r)},\qquad h'(r)=-\frac{20+100r+250r^2}{d(r)^2}<0. \tag{13} \]

The formula for M_r here is restricted to the neutral space; its common mode remains one. Since v^Tv=2 and v^TLv=6, it determines h exactly throughout the parameter interval, not merely at sampled endpoints. Write b=mathcal R+eta. The observed record sets are contained in

\[ \mathcal Y_+=\left[aT\tfrac{12}{11}-b,\; aT\tfrac{840}{461}+b\right],\qquad \mathcal Y_0=[2aT-b,\;2aT+b]. \tag{14} \]

For the fixed declaration, exact arithmetic gives

\[ Z=\frac{8193}{66977792},\qquad \mathcal R=\frac{9215}{34292629504},\qquad \inf\mathcal Y_0-\sup\mathcal Y_+ =\frac{40665805}{3952225550336}>2^{-21}. \tag{15} \]

docs.title: 1. Independently supplied waveform and complete evolution
docs.text:
Write T for repetition over the nine slots and L=I5 tensor L9 + L5 tensor I9. The marked vector k is neutral. On C5,

\[ v=L_5^+k=(2/5,0,-1/5,-1/5,0)^T,\quad L_5v=k. \tag{1} \]

This is the inverse on the neutral sector, with no grounded charge or discarded common phase. Define prescribed offsets and forcing by

\[ \begin{split} h(u)&=a k s(u/d),\\ z(u)&=\frac{4a}{\gamma d}v s'(u/d),\\ f(u)&=\frac{4a}{\gamma d^2}v s''(u/d) +\frac{a}{\gamma d}k s'(u/d). \end{split} \tag{2} \]

The primes on s denote differentiation of its dimensionless argument. Exactly h'=gamma*L5*z/4 and z'=-L5*z/4+f. Both z endpoints vanish; h starts at zero and ends at a*k. Every vector in (2) has zero sum. Bounded jumps of f when it is switched on or off are allowed; the states remain continuous. Finite bandwidth and tracking error have not been admitted.

Equation (2) is an executable time function, independent of the response. It is not asserted to solve the nonlinear unforced model. For the actual solution define

\[ y=x-Tz,\quad \eta=\theta-\theta_{\rm entry}-Th. \]

The complete equations give, without linearizing the sine,

The phase row is live; its background drift is part of the endpoint error. The supplied signal preserves both global means. Smooth finite-dimensional linear growth and bounded sine forcing give a unique solution on the whole finite interval. No numerical integration is needed for the bounds below.

The earlier collective construction also used a uniform input and a same-input comparison, but consumed initial collective observations on a different support.
