docs.title: 2. Actual source, residual state and identity
docs.text:
Rebuild isolated recovery from its primitive allowances and clock, then the outer source from the recovered radius. One equal recovery bound can cover the five independent sources without equating their actual states. Retain both capture branches, acquisition identity, complete law and attachment/storage premises. The outer theorem supplies full Euclidean departures R,Z from its carrier and nominal form bound M*. These cover the outer-zero control as well.

With g=gamma_upper, the initial unforced prefix admits

\[ M_0=M_*+R+g h_0, \quad A_0,B_0=\mathcal T(R,Z,2g h_0), \tag{4} \]

where the shared hidden-transport function is

\[ \mathcal T(A,B,q)=\left(\frac{A+qB}{1-q^2}, \frac{B+qA}{1-q^2}\right),\qquad q<1. \tag{5} \]

Its proof belongs to the source comparison. Let A be an upper bound on the actual principal mean-phase gaps at pulse entry: the largest nominal outer-one gap plus 2Z+4g*M0*h0 also bounds the outer-zero control. Prefix internal gaps use B0 and external gaps retain the same mean and fine errors. This does not select a nominal state in place of an acquired one.

The maximum degree is four, ||L||_infinity<=8, and |S_i|<=4. Heat contraction applied to (3) yields

\[ \|y(u)\|_\infty\le M=M_0+gd,\quad \|\eta(u)\|_\infty\le D=2gMd. \tag{6} \]

Since both z endpoints vanish, the endpoint bounds are

\[ \|x(d)\|_\infty\le M,\quad \|x(d)-x(0)\|_\infty\le (2M+g)d,\quad \|\theta(d)-\theta(0)-Ta k\|_\infty\le D. \tag{7} \]

No small form bound is claimed during the pulse: z can be large. For the within-child orthogonal projection Q, QTf=0, Q commutes with L, and QS(psi+T*Phi)=0. Consequently (5) still transports the actual hidden form and phase norms under the input, with

\[ A_h,B_h=\mathcal T(A_0,B_0,2gd). \tag{8} \]

Thus all internal gaps lie between 2*pi/9-2Bh and 2*pi/9+2Bh. The strict collar margin is pi/2-2Bh. An external fine gap stays at magnitude at most A+|a|+2B0+2D. Strictly positive internal gaps below pi/2 and external magnitudes below pi/2 preserve every declared cycle winding throughout the pulse. There is a sharper comparison with the unforced continuation of the same actual entry state. It is a proof device, not a measured branch required by the actuator. A child-common phase displacement changes only two external edges per slot, so its sine-current increment has infinity norm at most 2|a|s. Using integral_0^1 s=1/2, the sine Lipschitz bound 8 and the same domain 2gd<1,

\[ E_x\le\frac{g|a|d}{4(1-(2gd)^2)},\qquad E_\theta\le2gd E_x. \tag{9} \]

At release this compares with J_a(F_d(state_entry)): first the real unforced elapsed duration, then the phase translation. The order matters. Neither (7) nor (9) identifies the endpoint with the old instantaneous event or admits the original observation inverse.

docs.title: 3. Full storage, supplied work and unavoidable cost
docs.text:
The unchanged full storage is

\[ H=\tfrac12x^TLx+\sum_{e=1}^{90}(1-\cos\delta_e), \quad H'=-\tfrac14\|Lx\|_2^2+(Lx)^TTf. \tag{10} \]

Define W=integral (Lx)^T Tf, Wabs=integral |(Lx)^T Tf|, Wplus=integral max(0,(Lx)^T Tf) and Loss=integral ||Lx||^2/4. Then H(d)-H(0)=W-Loss and Wplus<=Wabs. None is paid from signed hidden storage or the old jump-work estimate. The exact uniform port identity (Lx)^T Tf=9(L5 X)^T f remains valid off the carrier; independent physical calibration is still required to assign amperes, seconds or joules.

For ell=gamma_lower>0, the cubic extrema give

\[ Z_m=\frac{12|a|}{5\ell d},\quad J_z=\frac{24|a|}{5\ell d},\quad F_m=\frac{48|a|}{5\ell d^2}+\frac{6|a|}{5\ell d},\quad J=J_z+8M. \tag{11} \]

These bound respectively ||z||infinity, ||L5 z||infinity, ||f||infinity and ||Lx||infinity. Counting all nodes and edges gives

\[ \sup H\le180(Z_m+M)^2+180,\quad Loss\le45dJ^2/4,\quad W_{abs}\le45dJF_m. \tag{12} \]

The last bound also bounds the sum of positive supplied work over the individual channels: it was obtained by summing absolute node powers before integration, so it does not require cancellation between supplying and absorbing channels.

Finite upper bounds alone could conceal a costly construction. The phase row also forces a lower cost for the actual collective increment Delta Phi=a*k+e, with ||e||infinity<=D. Orthogonal decomposition gives

\[ Loss\ge\frac{36}{\gamma^2d}\|\Delta\Phi\|_2^2,\qquad \sup\tfrac12x^TLx\ge \frac{72}{\gamma^2d^2}\Delta\Phi^TL_5^+\Delta\Phi. \tag{13} \]

These are the C5 electrical pulse inequalities in structural units, with the actual lift and all fine storage retained. Put v=max(0,|a|-2D). The marked-minus-adjacent increment has magnitude at least v; ||e0-e1||^2=2 and (e0-e1)^T L5 (e0-e1)=6. Therefore

\[ Loss\ge18v^2/(g^2d),\qquad \sup\tfrac12x^TLx\ge12v^2/(g^2d^2). \tag{14} \]

They are necessary dissipative and peak-storage costs, not independently measured energies or an optimized input. docs.title: Operational identification of the collective electrical model
Question and decision scope
docs.text:
The electrical construction and actual-source comparison establish a conditional post-contact description. This owner asks which independently measurable relation remains after calibrating that description, and whether the existing preparation is already an admissible electrical experiment.

There are two results. Independently calibrated capacitance and conductance leave a prospective, unfitted sine-current amplitude for the fixed law. However, its dimensionless coefficient is supplied, and the literal instantaneous phase events in the existing source history have no finite-work realization in the unchanged electrical reference. The mathematical results below are symbolic. No physical data, new source response, parameter search, numerical campaign or laboratory apparatus is admitted. Numerical controls use synthetic records and independent algebra; the earlier frozen source evidence remains unchanged.

docs.title: 1. Complete reference, observation and calibration boundary
docs.text:
Retain the six marked electrical islands, floating neutral charge leaf, fixed same-slot wheel support and collective circular observation of the electrical owner. Use its notation L for the wheel Laplacian, B for an oriented wheel incidence, P=I-11^T/6, and the supplied Josephson constant a_0=hbar/(2e)>0. Physical quantities use coulombs, volts, seconds, farads, siemens and amperes; structural quantities retain their original units.

The reference rows are

\[ q=CV,\qquad \dot q=-GV-B\operatorname{diag}(j_e)\sin(B^T\Phi), \qquad \dot\Phi=V/a_0. \tag{1} \]

The declared dictionary remains q=9*kappa*(X-r*1), tau=tau_0+b*t_lab, and unchanged circular Phi, with positive common scales kappa,b and retained neutral reference r. Arbitrary sensor mixing, changed phase coordinates, hidden dynamic circuitry and a different background-charge leaf are outside this particular comparison. Voltage differences require one consistent floating gauge; a common unmeasured phase is not set to a new physical value for every record.

An operational comparison separates the following information:

Information Independent premise and use Node labels, component connections and reference Fix before measuring or comparing records; preserve all fifteen capacitor/resistor pairs and ten wheel junctions C and G Calibrate the full effective linear component matrices from separate records, with the junction contribution, loading, frequency/temperature regime and uncertainty accounted for. That paper describes separate impedance and instrument calibration, and reports model discrepancies attributed to nonsinusoidal behavior and junction variation. Its apparatus and measured parameters are not evidence for this TNFR realization or its tolerances. Direct phase-sensitive measurements of nonsinusoidal profiles, including their loop/sensor model, are reported by English et al. (2016), arXiv v2. docs.title: 2. An unfitted relation after independent linear calibration
docs.text:
Conditional characterization. On an open neutral charge and relative-phase domain, the fixed dictionary realizes the complete quarter sine law if and only if, for positive scalars c, g, j,

\[ C=cL^+,\qquad G=gP,\qquad j_e=j\text{ on all ten edges},\qquad \frac{cj}{a_0g^2}=\gamma^2, \quad \gamma=\frac1{1023\pi}. \tag{2} \]

The statement is within the declared floating six-island reference and observation class, not a classification of every possible electrical map. Its necessity follows from the phase and form rows in the electrical owner:

\[ c=\frac{36\kappa}{a_0b\gamma},\qquad g=\frac{9\kappa}{a_0\gamma},\qquad j=\frac{9b\kappa\gamma}{4}. \tag{3} \]

Equality of the nodal sine fields on an open relative-phase domain forces each edge coefficient. Differentiate a node's current with respect to one neighbor's phase: that single edge coefficient is isolated. Cycle-current ambiguity in a single record does not create a freedom in the complete nonlinear field. Eliminating the two scales in (3) yields

\[ \boxed{b=4g/c,\qquad \kappa=a_0\gamma g/9, \qquad j_{\rm pred}=a_0\gamma^2g^2/c.} \tag{4} \]

Conversely, inserting the positive scales (4) and relation (2) into (3) recovers both full rows and their storage/work relation. This proves sufficiency. After exact independent C/G calibration, both scales are unique; changing either to fit a reserved j would contradict that calibration. The scalar c has units farads, g siemens, j amperes; cj/(a_0*g^2) is dimensionless. It is independent of the arbitrary charge and clock scales.

The complete component shape must be checked before using (4). From the proved wheel inverse, the mutual-capacitance coefficients are 5/396, 41/396, 11/396 times c for adjacent rim, nonadjacent rim and rim-hub pairs, respectively. Every resistor branch has conductance g/6. Equivalently, symmetric floating matrices satisfy C L=cP and G=gP. Although c=tr(CL)/5, g=tr(G)/5, traces alone cannot establish those matrix identities. Changing two branch values can preserve a trace and still violate the required shape.

The same restriction must hold across independently prepared states of the same fixed assembly. Preparation cannot retune c, g, j, gamma or sensor gains. A conventional circuit with calibrated C and G but all amplitudes 2*j_pred is a positive passive reference outside this fixed-law dictionary; it gives a concrete distinguishable alternative on an open phase domain. A conventional circuit satisfying (2) is exactly equivalent on the ideal carrier. No response in that common model can distinguish the two descriptions.

docs.title: 3. Why the number is not a derived universal constant
docs.text:
The fixed coefficient comes from the earlier specified weights e=1023/1024, w=1/1024, giving gamma=w/(e*pi) in the complete-law owner. It is not selected by the nodal identity, neutrality, positive dissipation or the passive circuit construction. The constitutive comparison class explicitly retains positive coefficient and current-profile freedom.

If gamma is allowed to be fitted after measuring a positive triple c,g,j, then

\[ \gamma_{\rm fit}=\sqrt{\frac{cj}{a_0g^2}},\qquad b=4g/c,\qquad \kappa=a_0\gamma_{\rm fit}g/9 \tag{5} \]

matches every such triple with the required component shapes. The scalar restriction has disappeared. Thus (2) tests the previously fixed complete law, not TNFR with unrestricted constitutive coefficients. Replacing the sine profile by another admitted current law also needs its own comparison; its formation, finite source bounds and sensor inference do not transfer merely because equilibria or tangents match.

There is a limited composition statement. If a different organization of m nodes independently admits the same exact collective law, phase map and passive coarse inverse, replacing 9 by m in the aggregate charge map gives

\[ c=\frac{4m\kappa}{a_0b\gamma},\quad g=\frac{m\kappa}{a_0\gamma},\quad j=\frac{mb\kappa\gamma}{4}. \]

The ratio (2) is unchanged. This is conditional cancellation of an admitted replication factor; it does not prove arbitrary-scale formation, physical scale invariance or the same law at every scale.

docs.title: 4. Uncertainty, actual source and a possible reserved balance
docs.text:
Let c in [c_-,c_+], g in [g_-,g_+], and a_0 in [a_-,a_+] be independently admitted positive calibration boxes. The exact monotone envelope for the fixed mathematical gamma is

\[ j_{\rm pred}\in \left[\frac{a_-\gamma^2g_-^2}{c_+}, \frac{a_+\gamma^2g_+^2}{c_-}\right]. \tag{6} \]

The implementation uses the shared outward enclosure of gamma. Disjoint reserved amplitude bounds exclude the fixed-map relation under the supplied premises. Overlap is necessary compatibility only: it proves neither the physical premises nor a joint noisy trajectory. Correlations discarded by these boxes can weaken exclusion. If capacitance or conductance shape intervals have empty intersection, calibration already excludes this dictionary; averaging them into a best fit would erase that finding.

The actual-source theorem starts its ideal comparator at the actual collective coordinates. Its very small intrinsic error is not an experimental initialization error budget. With initial Euclidean coordinate uncertainty e_X,e_Phi, its same coupled argument gives

\[ E_X\le\frac{e_X+c_We_\Phi+h\rho}{1-c_W^2},\qquad E_\Phi\le\frac{e_\Phi+c_We_X+c_Wh\rho}{1-c_W^2}, \quad c_W=3\gamma_+h/2. \tag{7} \]

Physical sensor, coefficient and clock errors require their own additional terms; (7) holds for the otherwise unchanged model. On that same source, ||R||_1<=rho and sum R=0. For any union A of complete children, one possible reserved observable is the integrated balance

\[ \Delta q_A+\int (GV)_A\,dt+ j_{\rm pred}\int[B\sin(B^T\Phi)]_A\,dt =9b\kappa\int R_A\,dt. \tag{8} \]

Across the original structural horizon h its intrinsic right-hand bound is 9*kappa*h*rho/2. Independent measurements, integration aperture, inputs, initial phases and uncertainty must be declared before (8) becomes a physical test. It avoids differentiating noisy charge but does not eliminate the phase observation requirement. The bound is an allowed model discrepancy, not an observable lower bound or a TNFR-only signal. docs.title: 5. A concrete preparation obstruction: instantaneous phase events
docs.text:
The original fifteen observation events occur on the five-child host before donor attachment. The six-island contact capacitance cannot simply be used for those earlier events. Its ideal host carrier does, however, have a separate exact passive realization: repeat the electrical derivation for C5. The centered inverse of the C5 Laplacian has diagonal 2/5, adjacent entries zero and nonadjacent entries -1/5, so

\[ C_5=cL_{C5}^+,\qquad G_5=gP_5. \tag{9} \]

Five positive mutual capacitors c/5 join the nonadjacent pairs, all ten resistor pairs have conductance g/5, and five ring junctions have amplitude j. These matrices have the same scalar formulas (3) if the same dictionary is stipulated. This admits the ideal fixed-support host circuit, not the uncertain acquisition, observation actuator or later support switch.

The source's event changes phase by Delta Phi=a*k_c, where k_c=e_c-1/5, and leaves form unchanged. Its three amplitudes in each block are a=epsilon,-2*epsilon,epsilon, epsilon=1/10. Each is a nonzero relative circular change, not a common gauge or an integer full turn.

Finite-work obstruction. On a fixed floating circuit with positive capacitance and conductance on the neutral subspace, the Josephson row dot Phi=V/a_0, imposed in its integral solution sense, makes relative phase absolutely continuous when voltage has finite squared integral. Finite dissipated work guarantees that property. It therefore excludes a nonzero relative phase jump in zero time.

More quantitatively, any pulse of laboratory duration d>0 realizing a declared continuous lifted increment Delta Phi satisfies

\[ \begin{split} \int_0^d V^TGV\,dt&\ge \frac{a_0^2}{d}\Delta\Phi^TG\Delta\Phi,\\ \int_0^d E_C(t)\,dt&\ge \frac{a_0^2}{2d}\Delta\Phi^TC\Delta\Phi,\\ \mathop{\rm ess\,sup}_{[0,d]} E_C(t)&\ge \frac{a_0^2}{2d^2}\Delta\Phi^TC\Delta\Phi, \qquad E_C=\tfrac12V^TCV. \end{split} \tag{10} \]

Each follows from the positive quadratic-form Cauchy--Schwarz inequality and integral V=a_0*Delta Phi. The integrated capacitor energy is an energy-time quantity, not work; Joule heat in the first row is dissipated energy. A finite initial energy reservoir cannot make the first row bounded as d tends to zero. The result concerns the fixed reference and declared lift; other lifts or supports need their own endpoint and work accounting.

For the host event, k_c^T C_5 k_c=2c/5 and k_c^T G_5 k_c=4g/5, so these lower bounds become respectively

\[ \frac{4a_0^2a^2g}{5d},\qquad \frac{a_0^2a^2c}{5d},\qquad \frac{a_0^2a^2c}{5d^2}. \tag{11} \]

This proves that the literal instantaneous phase-only word has no finite-work implementation in this reference. It does not rule out a finite-duration current pulse or another preparation reaching an admissible endpoint. No endpoint form restoration, fine-source inclusion, winding retention or finite-pulse budget follows from the lower bounds alone. The original structural event-work budget cannot be converted into a payment for (11).

The separate finite-input construction now supplies those source, identity and resource obligations for one approximate intervention, retaining a nonzero endpoint form error. It does not admit the original complete observation word or a physical actuator.

There is also a conditional clock restriction. docs.title: Five-child electrical observation protocol
Question and result scope
docs.text:
The finite-input observation identifies collective winding on one continuing acquired organization. This owner translates that complete history to the fixed five-island electrical reference, including its actual fine deviations, observation uncertainty, initialization and supplied work. No donor or support change is required.

The result is a conditional specification and symbolic source-error theorem. It also gives a necessary current-amplitude consequence without requiring measured hidden phases. The exact sine-current and voltage-phase laws are supplied constitutive premises. Equations (1)-(2) of Babenko et al. (2020) state that reference. docs.title: 1. Complete state, support, source and clock
docs.text:
Keep the acquired five-child source immediately after outer formation, before the first plateau. The complete fine state has 45 signed forms and 45 circular phases on the unit-weight C9-by-C5 support, held unit capacities, and both rows

\[ x'=(-L_{45}x+\gamma S(\theta))/4+Rf,\qquad \theta'=\gamma L_{45}x/4,\qquad \gamma=1/(1023\pi). \tag{1} \]

R repeats five child coordinates over nine slots. Prime denotes tau=(1023/1024)*t, not laboratory seconds. Use the entire fixed word: 15 cubic ramps of duration one, 15 preceding plateaus of length h=1e-5, total T=15.00015, marked increments epsilon,-2*epsilon,epsilon, epsilon=1/10, and all 150 endpoint mean-form readings. Its input, phase command, release state, identity and work proof remain with the finite-word owner. The waveform consumes no phase measurement or future response.

On the admitted circular collar, use continuous lifts and the zero-mean template psi_j=2*pi*(j-4)/9 to write

\[ x=RU+u,\qquad \theta=\psi+R\Phi+z,\qquad R^Tu=R^Tz=0. \tag{2} \]

The shared circular observer defines these coordinates without averaging arbitrary principal representatives. A common phase is retained. The actual acquired hosts have zero total form and lifted phase; in the larger inference class retain r=sum(U)/5 and the conserved common phase. Neutral inputs do not change either. A physical circuit observes relative voltage and charge; it does not measure the discarded constant r or absolute common phase.

Let L be the five-cycle Laplacian, P=I-11^T/5, and B an oriented ring incidence with S5(Phi)=-B sin(B^T Phi). Mean cancellation gives

\[ U'=(-LU+\gamma S_5(\Phi))/4+f+\mathcal R,\qquad \Phi'=\gamma LU/4,\qquad \mathbf1^T\mathcal R=0, \tag{3} \] \[ \mathcal R_c=\frac\gamma4\sum_{d\sim c}\left\{ \frac19\sum_j\sin(\Phi_d-\Phi_c+z_{d,j}-z_{c,j}) -\sin(\Phi_d-\Phi_c)\right\}. \tag{4} \]

This remainder belongs to the retained fine state. It is not an external current invented from a measured response. On the exact carrier u=z=0 it vanishes; actual acquisition only bounds it.

docs.title: 2. Passive C5 dictionary and independent calibration
docs.text:
On the neutral floating leaf define

\[ q=9\kappa(U-r\mathbf1),\quad \tau=b t_{lab},\quad V=v_* LU,\quad v_*=a_0b\gamma/4, \qquad a_0,\kappa,b>0. \tag{5} \]

Laboratory time zero is the start of observation, not substrate acquisition. Both rows transform. The exact identities are

\[ C=cL^+,\quad G=gP,\quad c=\frac{36\kappa}{a_0b\gamma},\quad g=\frac{9\kappa}{a_0\gamma},\quad j=\frac{9b\kappa\gamma}{4}, \tag{6} \] \[ q=CV,\quad \dot q=-GV-jB\sin(B^T\Phi)+I_{ext}+I_{res},\quad \dot\Phi=V/a_0, \qquad I_{ext}=9b\kappa f(bt_{lab}),\ I_{res}=9b\kappa\mathcal R. \tag{7} \]

The centered inverse L+ has diagonal 2/5, adjacent entries zero and nonadjacent entries -1/5. Thus five positive capacitors c/5 join the pentagram pairs, ten resistor branches have conductance g/5, and five ring junctions have amplitude j. Multiplying L+ by L gives P; the pentagram and complete resistor graph are connected, so both matrices are positive on the neutral subspace. The absent adjacent/ground capacitances are exact reference premises; parasitics are not automatically part of this model.

Independent calibration must admit the full shapes, not just their traces. For positive branch boxes intersect all five capacitance multiples and all ten conductance multiples before computing

\[ b=4g/c,\quad \kappa=a_0\gamma g/9,\quad v_*=a_0\gamma g/c,\quad j_{pred}=a_0\gamma^2g^2/c,\quad K=\frac{a_0b\kappa\gamma}{4} =\frac{a_0^2\gamma^2g^2}{9c}. \tag{8} \]

Empty shape intersections exclude this dictionary. Nonempty intervals establish only necessary compatibility, not component calibration or a joint physical realization. The later current response must not fit c, g, gamma, sensor gain or clock. Fitting gamma removes the scalar restriction c*j/(a0*g^2)=gamma^2, as in the identification theorem. A conventional circuit satisfying these rows is an equivalent description, not an empirically distinguishable rival to the same mathematical model.

docs.title: 3. Actual-source transport through every finite input
docs.text:
Let ||u(0)||2<=R0, ||z(0)||2<=Z0, and gamma<=gbar. The within-child projection Q commutes with L45 and annihilates the complete input Rf. On the carrier Q S is zero. The full-circle sine Hessian and ||L45||2<=8 give exactly the shared coupled transport majorant

\[ s=2\bar g T<1,\qquad A=\frac{R_0+sZ_0}{1-s^2},\quad Z=\frac{Z_0+sR_0}{1-s^2}. \tag{9} \]

It holds throughout all ramps and plateaus, including their switches; large uniform commanded form does not directly drive hidden deviations. The strict observation collar follows when 2Z<pi/2.

The linear term in each edge's sine departure averages to zero. Since ||L||2<=4, Taylor's theorem yields

\[ \sum_{\{c,d\}}|e_{cd}|\le\frac1{18} z^T(L\otimes I_9)z\le2Z^2/9,\qquad \|\mathcal R\|_1\le\bar g Z^2/9=:\rho. \tag{10} \]

Initialize the ideal driven circuit at the actual U and Phi, use the same f and compare on the same clock. This initialization defines a mathematical comparator; it does not assert knowledge of the hidden phases. Heat contraction and the five-cycle sine Lipschitz constant four imply

\[ k=\bar g T<1,\quad E_U=\frac{T\rho}{1-k^2},\quad E_\Phi=kE_U. \tag{11} \]

These are uniform Euclidean trajectory differences. With independently bounded initial errors e_U,e_Phi, replace them by

\[ E_U=\frac{e_U+k e_\Phi+T\rho}{1-k^2},\qquad E_\Phi=\frac{e_\Phi+k e_U+kT\rho}{1-k^2}. \tag{12} \]

Physical component, timing and tracking errors are absent from (11)-(12). They cannot be hidden in the very small intrinsic source remainder.

For the already proved source with q0=1e-8, outer acquisition supplies Z0=6*q0*(1+gamma_upper) and R0=3*q0+24*gamma_upper*Z0. The elementary bounds gamma_upper<1/3000, T<16 imply R0<3.1e-8, Z0<6.01e-8, then A<3.2e-8, Z<6.1e-8 and E_U<2.3e-18. These loose symbolic inequalities follow from (9)-(11) and the existing source inclusion; they are not a replay of its assessor or a new reserved numerical observation. They do not set a laboratory noise floor. The frozen 1e-14 total reading allowance must include any comparator mismatch when transferring its readings to the actual source.

docs.title: 4. Accessible readings, uncertainty and initialization
docs.text:
With the independent linear calibration, each five-voltage endpoint gives

\[ U=r\mathbf1+\alpha L^+V,\quad \alpha=1/v_* =c/(9\kappa),\qquad (L^+V)_c=(2V_c-V_{c+2}-V_{c-2})/5. \tag{13} \]

One common voltage gauge cancels. Differing unknown sensor offsets do not. All five simultaneous coordinates, in the declared marking and endpoint order, are required. This is a model-based inference of charge from CV; it cannot independently test that capacitor law. It needs no phase reading.

For independently bounded alpha in [alpha_-,alpha_+], take midpoint alpha_m and radius alpha_r, primitive readings Vhat, and baseline rhat with error eta_r. Admit a uniform voltage error eta_V, including its sensor transfer and offsets. With w=L+ Vhat, use the exact rational center Uhat=rhat+alpha_m*w. Since ||L+||infinity=4/5, a uniform bound over all 150 inferred scalars is

\[ \eta_U=\eta_r+\frac45\alpha_+\eta_V +\alpha_r\max_{samples,c}|w_c|+\eta_{additional}. \tag{14} \]

The additional allowance must independently cover any source-comparator, aperture, timing or other admitted discrepancy. A nonnegative supplied number is not proof of that bound. No input or clock error is automatically admitted by (14). The adapter retains the frozen requirement eta_U<=1e-14 before using the existing finite-word inverse. Over-budget records leave that transfer unavailable; they do not justify changing the frozen noise.

The actual source's baseline is r=0. A constant unknown r cancels from the diffusion-corrected increments, because L annihilates constants, but voltage data cannot thereby establish the absolute initial-form prior. Retain a preparation bound on r and |x_i(0)|<=.01.

No exact relative-phase initialization follows from a winding label. For example U=0, Phi=0 and U=0, Phi=(delta,-delta,0,0,0) have the same zero winding and initial voltage for sufficiently small nonzero delta, but different immediate sine currents and form derivatives. A valid prediction therefore uses the complete preparation set: the initial mean-form bounds, fine-deviation bounds, all principal mean gaps in [-7/5,7/5], correlations and conserved origins. It may retain a set of possible initial phases instead of supplying unobserved values. The winding inverse is uniform over this set; an individual voltage trajectory is not determined by its returned label.

Laboratory durations are 1/b, h/b and T/b; the input is (7). An uncertain clock changes the applied waveform as well as timestamps. For an aperture confined to an unforced plateau, the exact mean row bounds |U'|infinity<=M+gamma/2, where M=.01+gamma_upper*T, so a structural timing radius delta_tau contributes at most (M+gamma_upper/2)*delta_tau. A nominal endpoint is also an input switch: two-sided jitter may enter a ramp, invalidating that smaller bound. One-sided plateau apertures or a separately proved whole-word bound are necessary. No finite-bandwidth or exact-switch implementation is certified.

docs.title: 5. Full resource account and physical units
docs.text:
Let H5=U^T L U/2+sum_ring(1-cos(delta)) and H_int=45*(1-cos(2*pi/9)). The C5 coefficients give

\[ H_{45}=H_{int}+9H_5+R_H,\quad -4Z^2\le R_H\le4(A^2+Z^2),\quad \int_0^T\|L_{45}u\|^2/4\le16TA^2. \tag{15} \]

The remainder is signed. It is not a free energy reservoir. If |U|<=M_* over the complete driven history, including its commanded form offset,

\[ \left|\int_0^T(LU)^T\mathcal R\,d\tau\right| \le4M_*T\rho,\quad H_5'=-\|LU\|^2/4+(LU)^T(f+\mathcal R), \quad R_H'=-\|L_{45}u\|^2/4-9(LU)^T\mathcal R. \tag{16} \]

The collective electrical energy is E_co=9K H5. Its lab-time balance contains resistive heat, supplied input power and the signed endogenous correction 9K*b*(LU)^T R. The input pairing is exact even off carrier:

\[ (L_{45}x)^TRf=9(LU)^Tf,\qquad \int V^TI_{ext}\,dt_{lab}=K\int(L_{45}x)^TRf\,d\tau. \tag{17} \]

The same factor converts the positive part of total supplied power integrated over time, as well as signed net work and absolute work. The full finite-word bounds therefore remain part of the mapped actual-source specification. Resistive heat corresponds to K*(Loss_fine-Loss_hidden), not all fine loss. Its lower bound must subtract the upper hidden loss in (15), with zero as a floor. Likewise collective energy is K*(H45-H_int-R_H), not an assertion that K H45 is the energy of a realizable passive fine-node circuit. No earlier acquisition or support-event work is mapped to joules by extending (5) without proof.

Those equalities concern actual collective coordinates with I_res retained. For the ideal comparator with I_res absent, its input-work difference is at most 36*K*E_U*integral(||f||1) over structural time; use ||L*(U_ideal-U)||infinity<=4*E_U in the power pairing. The same bound controls the difference of positive-work integrals because the positive-part map is 1-Lipschitz. The frozen input peak F_m and 15 active units give integral(||f||1)<=75*F_m. Thus ideal comparator work needs this additional allowance; equal initial winding alone cannot transfer the actual-source work certificate.

For exact calibration and only voltage readout error, (14) permits eta_V<=5*a0*b*gamma*eta_U/16. The largest commanded voltage peak is (6/25)*a0*b; the actual background changes it by at most a0*b*gamma*M. The commanded-peak to allowed-noise ratio is consequently (96/125)/(gamma*eta_U), independent of b and kappa. Changing units or clock scale cannot remove this ratio. It constrains a single sensor range covering both ramps and plateau resolution; gated sampling or separate ranges have different requirements. It is not a proof of instrumental impossibility or a physical noise estimate.

docs.title: 6. An unfitted consequence and the remaining admission
docs.text:
Use the same endpoint combinations as the finite-word inverse, now on charges inferred using independently calibrated C: D_q=9*kappa*D_U. The constant baseline cancels. If d_h=h/b, define the two unnormalized current quadratures

\[ A_c=\frac{D_{q,+}-D_{q,-}}{2d_h\sin\epsilon},\qquad B_c=\frac{D_{q,+}+D_{q,-}-2D_{q,0}} {2d_h(1-\cos\epsilon)}. \tag{18} \]

In the supplied model these enclose j_pred*C_c and j_pred*S_c, where C+iS is the initial fine interface phasor. Its modulus lies between cos(2*zeta) and one, with zeta=1e-6. Thus a radial current statistic can test an amplitude interval without first inserting a reconstructed phase into the very law being tested. If beta_D is the full corrected-form error from the finite-word theorem, then

\[ |A_c-j_{pred}C_c|\le e_A=\frac{9b\kappa\,\beta_D}{h\sin\epsilon},\qquad |B_c-j_{pred}S_c|\le e_B=\frac{18b\kappa\,\beta_D} {h(1-\cos\epsilon)}. \tag{19} \]

Set e_J=sqrt(e_A^2+e_B^2) and m_c=sqrt(A_c^2+B_c^2). The reverse triangle inequality gives the necessary prediction

\[ \max(0,j_{pred}\cos(2\zeta)-e_J)\le m_c\le j_{pred}+e_J. \tag{20} \]

No division by the predicted amplitude enters the measured statistic. With calibration/reading intervals, enclose its norm by [m_-,m_+] and retain their correlations where known. A necessary current-amplitude interval is [max(0,m_--e_J),(m_++e_J)/cos(2*zeta)], using outward bounds. Nonintersection with the independently predicted amplitude excludes the supplied law and map under their observation premises. Intersection is only compatibility, not a complete trajectory or physical identification. The model-derived beta_D cannot be transferred to a different current law.

The coefficients, error budget and complete finite input remain model assumptions; this is not a standalone experimental verification of the sinusoidal profile. In particular, an inverse normalized by j_pred and returned as a phase is not independent phase evidence for validating j_pred.

The conditional specification is now complete for exact input, support, clock and admitted endpoint errors. Before a physical test it still needs independent preparation information, component shape/calibration, a voltage transfer model, clock and finite-aperture evidence, and an actuator tracking bound valid at every switch. The same complete uncertainty must be carried into any competing constitutive model. A supplied physical coefficient cannot be derived by recognizing the equivalent circuit.

docs.title: Complete-state electrical comparison of the organized sine law
Question, reference and scope
docs.text:
The charge observation owner excludes a specified charge-density-only closure. Here phase remains part of the state. The question is whether the same organized quarter law, its retained-reference charge inventory and its full storage can be realized by a conventional passive network of capacitors, resistors and ideal sinusoidal Josephson junctions.

This is a conditional constitutive comparison, not a physical identification or a derivation of the Josephson relations. The reference uses those relations as independently supplied physical laws. A formal positive quadratic storage is not sufficient to establish electrostatic realizability in physical island charge and voltage coordinates.

The result below excludes a declared direct island-charge and phase map on C9 and the same-slot 54-node contact, even allowing a dense passive capacitance network, a ground reference, unobserved common phase and statically eliminated passive capacitor nodes. A separate constructive result realizes the exact organized six-child carrier by passive components after retaining one collective charge and phase per child. The direct obstruction does not classify arbitrary collective charge maps, ideal-transformer coordinate mixing, dynamic hidden circuitry, active synthesis, or a map defined only on a lower-dimensional prepared trajectory. Those alternatives need their own independent observation, law and work admissions.

This detached proof changes no execution law, consumes no newly evaluated trajectory and installs no operator or event selector. Its organized states remain conditional test cases of the supplied complete law, as required by the NFR ontology. The research program alone selects subsequent work.

docs.title: Independent passive electrical reference
docs.text:
Orient each junction edge once, and let \(B\) be its node-edge incidence matrix, so \(\delta=B^T\vartheta\). There is no supplied magnetic flux, phase frustration, external current source or time-dependent component. Electrical island phases are circular; a local continuous lift defines their derivatives without making the lift an additional observable charge. Geometric inductance, electromagnetic retardation, thermal noise and quantum fluctuations are omitted in this classical lumped reference. Component laws and that approximation require separate physical admission for an apparatus.

The ideal single-junction reference is

\[ I=I_c\sin\delta+\frac VR+C\frac{dV}{dt}, \qquad \frac{d\delta}{dt}=\frac V{a_0}, \qquad a_0=\frac{\hbar}{2e}>0. \tag{1} \]

Equations (1) and (2) of Babenko et al., Characterization of a Josephson Junction Comb Generator (2020) give the current balance and voltage-phase relation. The exact sine law is an ideal reference premise; admitting it does not establish that every physical junction obeys it on every regime. The quantum constant in (1) comes from the reference and is not obtained from TNFR.

Kirchhoff balance and capacitor storage assemble the reference into

\[ q=C V,\qquad \dot q=-G V-B\mathop{\rm diag}(I_{c,e})\sin(B^T\vartheta), \qquad \dot\vartheta=V/a_0, \tag{2} \]

with the appropriate common-potential gauge for a floating network. Here \(q\) is physical island charge relative to any independently fixed background offset, \(V\) is voltage, \(C\) is a symmetric capacitance matrix and \(G\) a symmetric passive conductance matrix. Dots in this owner mean laboratory time \(t\), in contrast to the structural prime below. All junction critical currents satisfy \(I_{c,e}>0\). The storage and loss are

\[ E=\frac12 V^T C V+ a_0\sum_e I_{c,e}[1-\cos\delta_e], \qquad \dot E=-V^T G V\le0. \tag{3} \]

Indeed \(\dot E=V^T\dot q+a_0\sum_e I_{c,e}\sin\delta_e\, \dot\delta_e\); substituting (2) cancels the junction terms. This derivation fixes the orientation and restoring sign rather than relying on a visually similar sine term.

Ordinary passive two-terminal capacitors give

\[ C_{ij}=-c_{ij}\le0\quad(i\ne j),\qquad C\mathbf1=c_g\ge0, \tag{4} \]

where \(c_{ij}\ge0\) is a mutual capacitor and \(c_g\) contains capacitors to the reference. The same sign, symmetry and row-sum conditions hold for the grounded Maxwell capacitance matrix of conductors in the reference's fixed linear electrostatic regime; see Díaz and Herrera, The positivity and other properties of the matrix of capacitance: physical and mathematical implications, equations (3)-(8). A floating complete matrix has zero row sums and the common-potential null mode. A grounded restricted matrix is positive definite under the reference's usual connectedness assumptions. These are conditions on physical conductor charges and potentials, not on arbitrary linear coordinates of a positive energy.

The two primary sources were reviewed on 2026-10-10; the capacitance reference is pinned to arXiv version 4. Only their constitutive relations and matrix conditions are used here, not their measured responses as TNFR evidence.

The proof below only needs symmetry, positive energy, (4), and the exact laws (2). No numerical material value, apparatus or experimental dataset is admitted.

docs.title: Complete TNFR state and the declared direct map
docs.text:
The separate operational identification derives the remaining component relation after independent calibration and the finite-work boundary for the source's phase interventions. It changes neither this reference nor the exact construction below.

On a fixed connected simple unit graph with \(n\ge2\), write

\[ L=BB^T,\quad S(\theta)=-B\sin(B^T\theta),\quad x'=\frac{-Lx+\gamma S(\theta)}4,\quad \theta'=\frac{\gamma Lx}4,\quad \gamma=\frac1{1023\pi}. \tag{5} \]

Prime denotes the structural clock \(\tau\). Forms are signed real, phases are circular, capacities are held at one, and there is no forcing or event. The organized interaction owner proves

\[ H=\frac12 x^T Lx+\sum_e[1-\cos(B^T\theta)_e],\qquad H'=-\frac14\|Lx\|^2,\qquad (\mathbf1^Tx)'=0. \tag{6} \]

Retain a fixed reference \(r\), and specify before comparing responses

\[ q=\kappa(x-r\mathbf1),\qquad \vartheta=\theta,\qquad \tau=\tau_0+b t,\qquad \kappa>0,\quad b>0. \tag{7} \]

These are supplied observation and clock scales, not fitted consequences. With the normalized coordinates of (5), \(\kappa\) has units coulombs, \(b\) inverse seconds and \(a_0\) volt-seconds. An independently declared form unit must be retained in \(\kappa\); the numerical normalization is not a laboratory-unit bridge.

Start on the invariant neutral leaf \(\mathbf1^Tq=0\), equivalently \(r=\bar x\) for that preparation, and let \(P=I-\mathbf1\mathbf1^T/n\). This is a stated restriction, not universal neutrality. Keeping the reference \(r\) is necessary when comparing inventory between regions or supports. The map on this leaf is invertible after the same common-phase convention is adopted on both sides. Simultaneously reversing charge and phase, or consistently permuting nodes and support, does not change the conclusions. An independent sign flip of only one coordinate changes the required capacitance sign or junction restoring sign.

The map is tested on an open set of form variations in the neutral leaf and independent circular phase variations. It is not merely a match at one equilibrium or along one response trace. The linear phase-row restriction therefore applies in an arbitrarily small full-state neighborhood of an organized twist as well as on the full leaf.

docs.title: Necessary voltage, capacitance, conductance and energy scales
docs.text:
The phase row and the reference's voltage-phase relation force

\[ V=d Lq,\qquad d=\frac{a_0 b\gamma}{4\kappa}>0. \tag{8} \]

Let \(L^+\) denote the Moore-Penrose inverse, with \(LL^+=L^+L=P\) and \(L^+\mathbf1=0\). A floating capacitance satisfying \(q=CV\) for every neutral \(q\) must be exactly

\[ C_* = c_*L^+,\qquad c_* = \frac1d =\frac{4\kappa}{a_0 b\gamma}>0. \tag{9} \]

This is necessary, not a convenient choice: multiplying \(q=dCLq\) on the neutral subspace by its inverse gives (9). Symmetry and the zero common mode fix its full floating extension. Positive definiteness of \(L^+\) on \(\mathbf1^\perp\) establishes positive quadratic energy, but does not yet establish (4).

The form row becomes

\[ \dot q=-\frac b4 Lq-\frac{b\kappa\gamma}4 B\sin(B^T\vartheta). \tag{10} \]

Consequently each original junction needs \(I_c=b\kappa\gamma/4\), and the conductance must act on every relative voltage as

\[ G|_{\mathbf1^\perp}=g_*I,\qquad g_* = \frac{\kappa}{a_0\gamma}>0. \tag{11} \]

For a floating resistor network this gives \(G_*=g_*P\), implemented formally by an all-pairs resistor graph with conductance \(g_*/n\) on each pair. Unless the original support is complete, this dissipative support differs from the TNFR adjacency. Equality of nodal divergence or regional total current does not identify its individual physical wires with the original structural edges. Ground shunts \(G=g_*I\) give the same neutral voltage action but also require explicit ground-current accounting. A same-sparse-support resistor realization is already excluded by (11), independently of the capacitance issue.

If one temporarily permits the formal positive matrix (9), the complete field and storage match exactly:

\[ E=K H,\qquad K=\frac{a_0 b\kappa\gamma}4>0,\qquad \dot E=-\frac{Kb}4\|Lx\|^2=-V^TG_*V. \tag{12} \]

The capacitor term follows from \(q^TC_*^+q/2=dq^TLq/2\); the junction term has the same factor \(K\). The scales retain two unselected positive parameters, \(\kappa\) and \(b\), even with \(a_0\) fixed by the physical reference. Neither complete field matching nor energy matching determines a measurement calibration.

Thus (9)-(12) are an exact formal charge-phase representation of (5). The remaining question is whether its capacitance is a physical passive Maxwell capacitance in these particular charge coordinates.

docs.title: C9 gives an exact passive-capacitance obstruction
docs.text:
For the unit cycle \(C_n\), the entry of \(L^+\) at graph distance \(d_{ij}\) is

\[ (L^+)_{ij}=\frac{n^2-1}{12n} -\frac{d_{ij}(n-d_{ij})}{2n}. \tag{13} \]

This identity is checked without a spectral approximation: the displayed circulant has zero row sums, and applying the cycle's second difference gives \(LL^+=P\). For C9 its diagonal and distances one through four are

\[ \frac{20}{27},\quad \frac8{27},\quad -\frac1{27},\quad -\frac7{27},\quad -\frac{10}{27}. \tag{14} \]

In particular, every adjacent off-diagonal entry of \(C_*\) is \(8c_*/27>0\), whereas every passive Maxwell off-diagonal entry is nonpositive. No positive charge or clock calibration can remove that sign. Node relabeling only relocates it; simultaneous charge and phase reversal leaves the capacitance relation unchanged.

Conditional obstruction. The direct map (7), with the complete quarter law on C9 and independent neutral form variations, has no realization of (2) by ordinary passive capacitors or electrostatic conductor capacitance. The contradiction already occurs in the phase/voltage/charge relations; fitting a current response, changing resistor values, or adding more response samples cannot repair it. docs.title: 1. Complete state, support and balances
docs.text:
Let \(H\) denote the 45-node host and \(D\) the nine-node external constituent, called the donor below only to distinguish its coordinates. The sign of its measured form exchange is a conclusion, not a premise of that name. The joined support is \(C_9\mathbin\square W_6\), where \(W_6\) consists of the five-cycle and one hub connected to every cycle vertex. It has 54 nodes and 144 undirected unit edges. The complete rows are

\[ x'=(-Lx+\gamma S(\theta))/4,\qquad \theta'=\gamma Lx/4,\qquad S_i(\theta)=\sum_{b\sim i}\sin(\theta_b-\theta_i). \tag{1} \]

Here prime denotes elapsed contact time in the declared tau clock. Forms are signed, all capacities are held at one, and the phase law is smooth on the full circle; real lifts are retained for the stated means. The form row specifies pressure independently of the response. The supplied uniform quarter factor applies to both rows even though the two vertex degrees are five and seven. Degree normalization would define a different model. The original clock multiplies both rows by \(1023/1024\).

Common form and common phase translations leave the complete field and difference storage unchanged. Vertex phase representatives may change by integer turns with their retained lifts transported consistently. Simultaneous cyclic slot relabeling of all six children, and cyclic relabeling of the five host children, are support symmetries when the state and marked observations are relabeled together. Independent child phase translations cease to be symmetries after their contacts are present; the relative donor origin is therefore consumed boundary information.

Reciprocity gives the full storage and conserved totals:

\[ \begin{split} H_{\rm all}&=\frac12x^TLx+ \sum_{\{a,b\}}[1-\cos(\theta_b-\theta_a)],\\ H_{\rm all}'&=-\frac14\|Lx\|_2^2,\qquad (\mathbf1^Tx)'=(\mathbf1^T\theta)'=0. \end{split}\tag{2} \]

Indeed the phase gradient of storage is \(-S\), so the two mixed terms cancel directly. Finite-dimensional global Lipschitz continuity of (1) gives a unique complete solution. The proof needs neither acute new edges nor native U3 admission. This remains the detached smooth-sine comparison, not an implementation of a registered operator or its occurrence law.

docs.title: 2. Actual source and observation-history transport
docs.text:
Re-admit all twelve primitive source allowances before rebuilding any source. Five copies are the original paired host preparations; the sixth is independent. Their zero-sum form and phase errors retain all 96 relative directions. Write \(q=10^{-70}\), and let the rebuilt outer acquisition supply \(R<4q\), \(Z<7q\), and primitive carrier phase intervals \(P_c\) at host elapsed time 200. For outer one,

\[ \theta_{c,j}(200)=\psi_j+\Phi_c+z_{c,j},\quad \Phi_c\in P_c,\quad \|z\|_2\le Z, \qquad \psi_j=\frac{2\pi(j-4)}9. \tag{3} \]

These are freshly derived finite endpoint intervals, rather than the limiting twist. The outer-zero carrier has all \(\Phi_c=0\), with its own actual transported residual bounded by the same Z. Matching primitive errors does not equate these two reached residuals. The source inclusion also places both actual families in the observation class, with initial form bound \(X=1/100\), internal phase error \(\zeta=10^{-6}\), and outer origin-gap bound \(A=7/5\).

Let \(g\) be the outward upper bound on \(\gamma\), and put

\[ T=\frac1{5000},\qquad B_o=X+gT,\qquad m=2gB_oT,\qquad D_o=2m. \tag{4} \]

The degree-four heat contraction and complete phase row give \(\|x\|_\infty\le B_o\) throughout the sequential word and per-node continuous phase drift at most m. All commanded phase offsets are zero at its final endpoint. The actual continuous drift and changed forms remain. Consequently the contacted host has the phase description (3) with an additional coordinate error of at most m; the control uses the same assertion about its zero carrier. No measurement inverse or winding label supplies these endpoint coordinates.

The independently rebuilt donor has, at its synchronized recovery endpoint,

\[ \|x_D\|_2\le q,\qquad \theta_{D,j}=\psi_j+\pi/2+z_{D,j},\qquad \|z_D\|_2\le q, \quad \sum_jx_{D,j}=\sum_jz_{D,j}=0. \tag{5} \]

Its phase translation is supplied at primitive preparation and is an exact symmetry of the isolated law and storage. The quarter-factor isolated law is the original half-factor law at half speed in both rows, so formation time 100 and recovery dwell \(10^{13}\) become 200 and \(2\cdot10^{13}\) in tau. Preparation starts are synchronized to reach (5) at contact; no later waiting or freezing premise is inserted.

Every sequential event leaves form unchanged and has zero global phase sum. Both host totals therefore remain zero. At contact the joined form total is exactly zero and the joined lifted phase total is \(9\pi/2\). These correlations are conserved under (1). They are supplied and derived source information, not inferred from noisy readings.

docs.title: 3. Both port channels and the carrier restriction
docs.text:
Orient each new edge from host node \((c,j)\) to donor node j, and set

\[ u_{c,j}=x_{D,j}-x_{H,c,j},\qquad \delta_{c,j}=\theta_{D,j}-\theta_{H,c,j},\qquad f_{c,j}=\frac{u_{c,j}+\gamma\sin\delta_{c,j}}4,\qquad g_{c,j}=-\frac{\gamma u_{c,j}}4. \tag{6} \]

Let \(P\) sum contact coordinates over c at each donor slot j. With \(L_H,S_H\) including all 90 original host edges and \(L_D,S_D\) the donor internal cycle, the full rows split exactly as

\[ \begin{array}{ll} x_H'=(-L_Hx_H+\gamma S_H)/4+f, &\theta_H'=\gamma L_Hx_H/4+g,\\ x_D'=(-L_Dx_D+\gamma S_D)/4-Pf, &\theta_D'=\gamma L_Dx_D/4-Pg. \end{array}\tag{7} \]

Thus the external constituent reacts to both channels. It is not a prescribed input signal. With \(a_H=L_Hx_H\), \(b_H=-S_H\) and the analogous donor quantities, the internal regional balances are

\[ \begin{split} H_H'&=-\tfrac14\|a_H\|_2^2+a_H^Tf+b_H^Tg,\\ H_D'&=-\tfrac14\|a_D\|_2^2-a_D^TPf-b_D^TPg,\\ H_B&=\sum_{c,j}\left[\tfrac12u_{c,j}^2+1-\cos\delta_{c,j}\right],\\ H_B'&=\sum_{c,j}\left[u_{c,j}u_{c,j}' +\sin\delta_{c,j}\delta_{c,j}'\right]. \end{split}\tag{8} \]

Adding these three balances gives (2). The isolated regional losses alone are not the joined loss, and regional supply is not generally form times form input. The contact storage keeps the existing coordinates; it does not introduce an independent reservoir variable.

For the exact carrier let \(c=0,\ldots,5\), with donor c=5, and write \(x_{c,j}=X_c\), \(\theta_{c,j}=\psi_j+\Phi_c\). Let K be the unnormalized Laplacian of the five-cycle plus its hub. Opposite internal C9 currents cancel, while same-slot contact differences are constant in j. Uniqueness therefore preserves this family, and the complete inherited law is

\[ X'=(-KX+\gamma S_{W_6}(\Phi))/4,\qquad \Phi'=\gamma KX/4. \tag{9} \]

All twelve coordinates are retained. With \(V_9=9[1-\cos(2\pi/9)]\), the actual pullback and its derivative are

\[ H_{12}=6V_9+\frac92X^TKX+ 9\sum_{\{c,b\}\in W_6}[1-\cos(\Phi_b-\Phi_c)], \qquad H_{12}'=-\frac94\|KX\|_2^2. \tag{10} \]

The actual source need not lie on this invariant carrier. The finite argument below uses the full state and its transported errors instead.

docs.title: 4. Exact donor mean and a finite whole-law remainder
docs.text:
Define the true donor mean form and the complete contact phase moment by

\[ R_D(t)=\frac19\sum_jx_{D,j}(t),\qquad \mathcal A(t)=\frac19\sum_{c=0}^4\sum_{j=0}^8 \sin\delta_{c,j}(t). \tag{11} \]

The normalization makes \(|\mathcal A|\le5\). Internal donor currents cancel in the mean. The contact form contribution is \(5R_D-\sum_cX_c\), where \(X_c\) now denotes each actual host child mean. Zero total form gives \(\sum_cX_c=-R_D\), hence the following identities hold for arbitrary admitted fine states:

\[ R_D'=-\frac32R_D-\frac\gamma4\mathcal A, \qquad \Psi_D'=\frac{3\gamma}{2}R_D, \qquad R_D(0)=0. \tag{12} \]

Here \(\Psi_D\) is the actual mean lifted donor offset. Thus no unknown host form distribution remains in the mean diffusion term. The nonlinear contact moment still consumes full boundary phases. Its being an instantaneous observable does not make it an autonomous state variable.

Set the fixed readout \(h=1/1000\) and

\[ B=B_o+\frac74gh. \tag{13} \]

The joined heat semigroup is a maximum-norm contraction, and \(\|S\|_\infty\le7\). Since \(q<B_o\), (4)--(5) and the complete first row give \(\|x(t)\|_\infty\le B\) for \(0\le t\le h\). Host phase rates have magnitude at most \(5gB/2\), while donor phase rates have magnitude at most \(7gB/2\). Each contact gap therefore changes by at most \(6gBt\), and the global sine Lipschitz bound proves

\[ |\mathcal A(t)-\mathcal A(0)|\le30gBt. \tag{14} \]

Variation of constants in (12), with its nonnegative damping kernel, gives \(|R_D(t)|\le5gt/4\). Integrating the complete first equation in (12), without dropping either damping or phase motion, now yields

\[ \left|R_D(h)-R_D(0)+\frac{\gamma h}{4}\mathcal A(0)\right| \le E:=\frac{15}{16}gh^2+\frac{15}{4}g^2Bh^2. \tag{15} \]

The first term bounds \((3/2)\int_0^h|R_D(t)|\,dt\); the second bounds \((\gamma/4)\int_0^h|\mathcal A(t)-\mathcal A(0)|\,dt\). This is a finite nonlinear bound for the whole 54-node system, including source reaction, form diffusion and phase feedback. It is not an onset-only prediction or a transfer of the earlier degree-four probe remainder.

For the initial moments, let \(e=Z+m+q\). Equations (3)--(5) and \(\sin(\pi/2-a)=\cos a\) give the outward enclosures

\[ \mathcal A_1(0)\in\mathcal I_1:= \sum_{c=0}^4\cos(P_c+[-e,e]),\qquad \mathcal A_0(0)\in\mathcal I_0:=5\cos([-e,e]). \tag{16} \]

The source intervals and added errors retain the actual observed endpoint; no equalities with a limiting or ideal outer profile are used. Interval addition does not assert that all corners are jointly realizable. It only enlarges the actual correlated source.

Let \([\gamma]\) be the shared outward interval. The true finite increments and the four-reading observed contrast consequently satisfy

\[ \begin{split} R_{D,w}(h)-R_{D,w}(0)&\in -\frac{h[\gamma]}4\mathcal I_w+[-E,E],\\ \Delta_{\rm obs}&\in\frac{h[\gamma]}4(\mathcal I_0-\mathcal I_1) +[-2E-4\eta,2E+4\eta],\qquad \eta=10^{-10}. \end{split}\tag{17} \]

All four primitive reading errors are retained even though the actual initial donor mean is exactly zero. No noise independence or authenticated records are assumed. These enclosures concern actual sources obeying the declared preparation, dynamics and measurement premises. Subtracting the two separately rounded increment enclosures is also valid; the implementation retains that potentially wider outward contrast rather than requiring shared-factor interval cancellation.

docs.title: 5. Attachment work and joined initial storage
docs.text:
The contact event changes only support. Its exact supplied work is \(W_B=H_B(0)\) from (8), evaluated on the reached states. In particular

\[ 0\le W_B\le W_+:=90+\frac{45}{2}(B_o+q)^2. \tag{18} \]

This uses every one of the 45 new edges, its full form difference and the global phase cost \(0\le1-\cos\delta\le2\). The relative origin was free only while disconnected; its contact storage is counted here.

Let \(V_5=5[1-\cos(2\pi/5)]\), and let U denote the rebuilt actual outer-one endpoint excess at time 200. The existing source proof gives \(U<11/1000\), while the control storage is at most \(5V_9+40q^2\). The sequential word's fifteen signed works have total absolute value at most 36, and its continuous segments only dissipate. The recovered donor storage is at most \(V_9+4q^2\). Therefore valid joined initial bounds are

\[ \begin{split} H_{{\rm all},1}(0)&\le6V_9+9V_5+U+36+4q^2+W_+,\\ H_{{\rm all},0}(0)&\le6V_9+36+44q^2+W_+. \end{split}\tag{19} \]

Equation (19) is the storage present at the new contact, not the total historical cost of forming these sources. The six original preparation costs, the earlier outer attachment work and all observation events retain their separate accounting. Past dissipation is not a reservoir or a source of payment for (18). The new positive-work contact remains supplied.

docs.title: 6. Finite retention of the marked identities
docs.text:
Attachment changes no coordinate, so all marked identities survive that instantaneous event. At the end of the observation word the commanded offset has vanished; only the continuous edge drift \(D_o\) remains. The host therefore has internal gaps in \([\alpha-2\zeta-D_o,\alpha+2\zeta+D_o]\), where \(\alpha=2\pi/9\), and each original outer gap has magnitude at most \(A+2\zeta+D_o\). The donor internal gaps lie in \([\alpha-2q,\alpha+2q]\).

Both endpoints of any joined edge have phase rates bounded by \(7gB/2\), so a common conservative joined drift is

\[ D_j=7gBh. \tag{20} \]

It is sufficient to check the following five strict margins with the same outward arithmetic:

\[ \begin{split} &\alpha-2\zeta-D_o-D_j>0,\qquad \pi/2-\alpha-2\zeta-D_o-D_j>0,\\ &\pi/2-A-2\zeta-D_o-D_j>0,\\ &\alpha-2q-D_j>0,\qquad \pi/2-\alpha-2q-D_j>0. \end{split}\tag{21} \]

These bounds keep all six internal cycles positive and acute and all nine original outer cycles strictly acute on their inherited branches. Each marked cycle's lifted increments telescope, so its integer winding cannot change without leaving the chart. The six internal winding-one identities and each host's original nine outer windings consequently persist throughout the finite contact interval. No identity is assigned to a new contact loop, and no new edge is required to be acute. The old disconnected or product storage traps do not transfer to this support; no post-horizon capture or all-future maintenance conclusion follows from (21).

docs.title: 7. Fixed finite assessment
docs.text:
The exact-rational source rebuild and outward 128-bit assessment of (13)--(21) give the following conservative strict enclosures:

\[ \begin{split} -0.069910&<\mathcal A_1(0)<-0.069711, &4.999999993&<\mathcal A_0(0)\le5,\\ E&<2.918\cdot10^{-10}, &D_j&<2.179\cdot10^{-8},\\ 5.13\cdot10^{-9}&<R_{D,1}(h)-R_{D,1}(0)<5.73\cdot10^{-9},\\ -3.89234\cdot10^{-7}&<R_{D,0}(h)-R_{D,0}(0) <-3.88649\cdot10^{-7},\\ 3.93\cdot10^{-7}&<\Delta_{\rm obs}<3.96\cdot10^{-7}. \end{split}\tag{22} \]

The last enclosure includes all four raw reading errors and exceeds the frozen \(10^{-7}\) threshold uniformly over the original source family. It establishes a finite organization-dependent external exchange after the complete single-history observation word. The two individual true increment signs are also resolved; raw single-pair errors retain their own declared allowance and are not silently omitted from an observation.

The same fixed assessment gives

\[ W_B<91<100,\qquad H_{{\rm all},1}(0)<170<200,\qquad H_{{\rm all},0}(0)<139<200. \tag{23} \]

Every margin in (21) exceeds \(0.17\). All six internal and nine original outer identities are therefore retained throughout the contact interval. Response, event work, present storage and identity have separately admitted bounds; none is inferred solely from another's passing verdict. The work bound is conservative and does not claim the actual event cost equals 91. No protocol value, source error or precision was changed after evaluating the declared comparison.

docs.title: 8. Collective information and interpretation boundary
docs.text:
On the carrier, the contact phase moment is \(\sum_c\sin(\Psi_D-\Phi_c)\). Thus the complete external exchange depends on the collective boundary registration, even when all child windings and global form means agree. Identifying an outer winding does not reconstruct that registration or the fine contact correlations.

For an explicit sufficiency counterexample, hold all forms zero and the donor origin at \(\pi/2\). Compare host origins \((0,0,0,0,0)\) and \((a,-a,0,0,0)\), with \(0<a<\pi/4\), and no fine residuals. Both have the same zero mean lifted origin, outer winding zero and five internal winding-one identities. Their contact moments are respectively 5 and \(3+2\cos a\), hence their donor form rates differ by (12). This is a counterexample to mean-and-winding sufficiency on the stated state domain, not a claim that these two configurations are reached by the frozen source preparation.

Even retaining the full complex contact moment does not generally close the dynamics with only the two organizations' mean forms and lifted phase means. On the carrier define

\[ Q=\sum_{c=0}^4e^{i(\Psi_D-\Phi_c)},\qquad Q'=\frac{i\gamma}{4}\sum_c e^{i(\Psi_D-\Phi_c)} [(KX)_D-(KX)_c]. \tag{24} \]

Fix host origins \((a,-a,0,0,0)\), \(0<a<\pi/4\), and donor origin \(\pi/2\). Compare all forms zero with host forms \((b,-b,0,0,0)\) and donor form zero, where \(b\ne0\). Both states have the same host and donor mean forms, the same mean phases, the same marked windings, and \(Q=i(3+2\cos a)\). They lie on the same conserved form and lifted phase leaves as the declared contact. For the second state the host entries of KX are \((4b,-4b,b,0,-b)\), while the donor entry is zero. Equation (24) therefore gives

\[ Q'_{\rm zero\ form}=0,\qquad Q'_{\rm changed\ form}=-2i\gamma b\sin a\ne0. \tag{25} \]

Their instantaneous donor form rates agree, but differentiating (12) shows that their donor form accelerations differ by \(\gamma^2b\sin a/2\). The retained moment and pair means thus do not define an autonomous complete port state on this domain. The missing information includes the phase/form correlation in (24); the twelve-coordinate carrier state retains it. This independent algebraic counterexample concerns the admitted model's state domain, not two asserted members of the frozen acquired-source family.

Likewise, an independently changed donor registration changes its external interaction; it is not determined by the host's winding label. The carrier law (9) and general fine-state port (7) retain the information responsible. No scalar coarse nodal law, winding-only force, nonadditivity or unique physical constitutive law is inferred. Any physical comparison still needs an independent preparation, clock and measurement bridge.

docs.title: Boundary information, ideal cancellation and the missing source premise
docs.text:
The regular-information theorem applies here first as an instantaneous response formula. Remove the supplied donor origin beta from its residual and retain the actual marked matching:

\[ Q_n=\frac19\sum_{c=0}^4\sum_{j=0}^8 e^{in(z_{D,j}-H_{c,j})},\qquad \mathcal A_{j_*}(\beta)=\sum_{n\in\mathcal N} b_n\operatorname{Im}(e^{in\beta}Q_n),\qquad j_*(a)=\sum_{n\in\mathcal N}b_n\sin(na). \tag{26} \]

Here H contains the reached host offsets and observation backaction, as in the relative-origin owner. This is the theorem's query at phi=-beta with normalization 1/9. The 45 summands are contact edges, not one node's degree. Their permutation as a list does not permit rewiring their donor/host associations. All beta values describe separately prepared donor origins; they are not an operational sweep of one attached object.

Information obligation What this contact already retains Sine current at contact for every beta Both quadratures of Q_1, reconstructed from full marked fine phases; the finite all-origin envelope is already certified by the relative-origin owner Complete instantaneous field and reaction All 54 forms, 54 phases and the 144-edge support, including both rows (7); a single aggregate moment does not replace nodewise reactions Future response Full fine state and source bounds; the twelve-coordinate restriction is exact only on its invariant carrier, and (24)--(25) already rule out general closure by Q_1 plus organization means Response of an acquired organization under a different law Its own source, observation-history and contact bounds; neither the moment formula nor the old sine certificate supplies them

Thus no missing static moment prevents the existing sine prediction. The universal two/six/ten minima are not minimal state counts for this acquired family: its gaps are correlated, and its exact carrier has only five distinct contact gaps, each repeated nine times. No unrestricted rank witness is asserted to belong to the original source. Even equal phase moments of every order would not erase the phase/form association needed by (24).

A scoped collective consequence. Consider the ideal carrier configuration with host origins Phi_c=Phi_0+2pi(c-2)/5 and donor origin beta, and with zero internal residuals. This is a static comparison state, not the reached endpoint of the source. Geometric summation gives

\[ Q_n=e^{-in\Phi_0}\sum_{c=0}^4e^{-2\pi in(c-2)/5} =\begin{cases}5e^{-in\Phi_0},&5\mid n,\\0,&5\nmid n,\end{cases} \qquad \boxed{\mathcal A_{j_*}(\beta) =5\sum_{\substack{n\in\mathcal N\\5\mid n}} b_n\sin[n(\beta-\Phi_0)].} \tag{27} \]

The nine same-slot repetitions cancel the normalization in (26). For 5 not dividing n the finite geometric sum vanishes; otherwise all five terms equal one. This proves (27) for every registration, without a phase scan. An aligned host instead gives 5j_(beta-Phi_0).

Consequently both sine and the retained {1,9,18} alternative have zero aggregate phase current at this ideal outer-one configuration, despite their different universal information costs. This cancellation cannot distinguish that pair of laws. It does distinguish the ideal organized and aligned configurations at suitable registrations. It is not universal across compatible currents: the separate composition-compatible family has b_10=10epsilon, so its same static aggregate is 50epsilonsin[10(beta-Phi_0)]. That countercontrol transfers no acquisition claim and activates no third-law comparison.

Equation (27) concerns only the instantaneous phase contribution. A donor mean-form rate also contains the diffusion term in (12); a vanishing aggregate does not make the complete joined field stationary or guarantee zero finite response. Actual sources have nonzero departures from the ideal configuration. The established sine envelope already includes them; it must not be replaced by (27) or interpreted as exact cancellation.

Applicability decision. The proposed new property is persistence of organization-dependent suppression of contact response under the retained nonsine law, using an organization actually generated by that law. The first missing premise was own-law formation and retention of the five-child outer identity from the original preparation. Own-law isolated C9 acquisition and recovery already exist in the constitutive source owner. They do not cover the five-child outer transit: the outer acquisition rebuilds deformation zero, while the two-law observation theorem assumes an initial class and explicitly does not acquire it. In particular, the alternative does not share the outer C5 tangent merely because it matches the internal C9 target.

This closes the applicability question with an obstruction to the ideal static discriminator and a named source dependency. The subsequent own-law source result closes that dependency with unchanged preparation and deadlines. It does not transfer the earlier observation inverse, or this owner's history transport and finite contact certificate. The subsequent own-law contact result derives its own history, resource and finite response bounds and certifies the original all-registration contrast. Neither endpoint law's finite bound establishes exact dynamical cancellation. The dynamic cancellation theorem classifies the exact limiting family: complete-law reflection protects special origins, while reciprocal feedback regenerates donor response elsewhere at law-dependent orders. It does not promote these ideal derivatives to an actual-source or finite-readout certificate. No old response is reevaluated. In the physical-property atlas, this addresses whether generated organizations have reproducible distinct interactions; physical preparation, measurement, units and clock remain additional obligations. Neither cancellation nor a harmonic count is an identification with electric charge, a particle or shielding in matter.

docs.title: 9. Shared implementation and verification boundary
docs.text:
The detached owner constructs the complete support, observes its two fine rows and contact reaction, and assesses the frozen finite comparison. Its observer admits all 54 signed forms and 54 real offset coordinates before field arithmetic. The offsets are relative to \(\psi_j\), with the donor's exact \(\pi/2\) added symbolically; raw donor offset means therefore omit that supplied origin. Complete phase lifts and the fixed geometry retain it. No floating approximation to pi is installed as primitive preparation. The contact reaction and potential reuse the matching edge fields from that same complete-state evaluation; they require no second trigonometric pass or separately cached state.

The assessor re-admits all twelve original allowances and rebuilds the host acquisition, independent donor recovery, sequential observation protocol and actual-source inclusion. It consumes shared coordinate admission, form-cost and interval sine kernels. Cached report flags or winding labels are not substitutes for those primitive premises. Its work, identity and response verdicts retain source admission and explicit unavailable margins. This owner also supplies the source-failure names used by the registration and maintenance assessors; each keeps its own acceptance conditions. These readers install no support, choose no event and advance no state.

The contract tests check independent fine graph calculations, both reaction channels, clocks, storage and the six-pair carrier, as well as the retained moment's failure to close an autonomous port. Finite comparisons separately check carried source inclusion, measurement errors, work and identity bounds. Invalid domains and unavailable source certificates remain distinct from an observed failure of formation or interaction. Tests establish implemented behavior; the conditional analytical statements are (1)--(27). The boundary-information controls check the static specialization against the existing law evaluators, including the surviving harmonic and departures from exact organization. They assess no source, trajectory or finite contact certificate and introduce no new executor or public API.

docs.title: Finite collective interaction across relative phase origins
Declared family and prospective capability comparison
docs.text:
The fixed external contact resolves a response at supplied relative origin pi/2. This admission separates the finite response envelope from that particular alignment, retaining the same actual acquired and observed sources. It does not create an alignment selector or replace the complete state with an instantaneous boundary moment.

Item Fixed choice and scope Actual sources Both earlier acquired host families after the complete sequential observation word, plus the independently recovered external C9. No source reset, target substitution or waiting interval Variable preparation Replace only the external constituent's supplied primitive common phase origin pi/2 by beta in R modulo 2*pi, relative to the same conserved zero host lifted mean. Its isolated relative trajectory is unchanged by this symmetry. A successful result would establish an origin-independent distinction between the finite interaction envelopes of these two prepared organizations under this interface and law.
