docs.title: 1. One continuous history and the global phase bound
docs.text:
Let R repeat a child vector over nine slots (called T in the complete row in the declaration), and use L=I5 tensor L9+L5 tensor I9. For marked child c set k_c=e_c-1/5 and v_c=L5^+ k_c. On a ramp with signed increment a and local fraction r=u/d, the reused waveform is

\[ s(r)=3r^2-2r^3,\quad z(u)=\frac{4a}{\gamma d}v_c s'(r),\quad f(u)=z'(u)+L_5z(u)/4. \tag{1} \]

The command H evolves from its current value by a*k_c*s; it is constant on the plateaus. Both z endpoints vanish. The complete H is continuous, with H'=gamma*L5*z/4, starts and ends at zero, and never changes any edge by more than epsilon. The middle increment has magnitude 2*epsilon, but crosses from +epsilon to -epsilon; this is not an excursion of 2*epsilon. The fine input Rf is zero on plateaus and after release. Bounded switches in f jump no state. Endpoint readings are state values; the plateau estimates use the unforced one-sided dynamics.

For the one actual solution throughout the entire program, put

\[ y=x-Rz,\qquad e=\theta-\theta(0)-RH. \]

Every switching boundary retains y and e continuously. The exact rows are

\[ y'=-Ly/4+\gamma S(\theta)/4,\quad e'=\gamma Ly/4=-\gamma y'+\gamma^2S(\theta)/4. \tag{2} \]

With g=gamma_upper, heat contraction and ||S||infinity<=4 give

\[ \|y(t)\|_\infty\le M=X+gT_{obs},\qquad e(t)=\gamma\{x(0)-y(t)\} +\frac{\gamma^2}{4}\int_0^t S(\theta(u))\,du, \] \[ \boxed{\|e(t)\|_\infty\le E=2gX+2g^2T_{obs}}. \tag{3} \]

This exact integration uses the live phase row and form diffusion. It avoids treating a transient large prescribed form offset as uncontrolled phase drift. No stationary background, phase feedback or reset is used. Global form and lifted-phase sums are conserved because every input is neutral and the edge currents sum to zero. Common means need not vanish in the larger inference class; the actual acquired hosts retain their original zero totals.

At every sampling endpoint z vanishes, so abs(X_c)<=M. At final release both z and H vanish, yielding ||x_end||infinity<=M and ||theta_end-theta_initial||infinity<=E. For example ||x_end-x_initial||infinity<=M+X; neither state is restored exactly. The subsequent unforced flow must start at this actual endpoint.

docs.title: 2. Complete identity and actual-source inclusion
docs.text:
Initial internal fine gaps are 2*pi/9 plus differences of z; outer fine gaps are the admitted principal mean gaps plus those residual differences. Using (3), sufficient whole-history identity margins are

\[ \begin{split} m_{internal,+}&=2\pi/9-2\zeta-2E,\\ m_{internal,acute}&=\pi/2-2\pi/9-2\zeta-2E,\\ m_{outer,acute}&=\pi/2-A-\epsilon-2\zeta-2E. \end{split} \tag{4} \]

Strict positivity prevents a cut crossing on each of the five internal and nine outer marked cycles. Every initial outer identity is retained, including negative winding in the larger admitted class. Removing the current child mean from e changes a within-child residual by at most 2E, so a sufficient strict circular-collar margin is

\[ m_{collar}=\pi/2-2\zeta-4E. \tag{5} \]

The actual source is rebuilt from the recovery and resource primitives and outer acquisition, not from the old observation or contact reports. If the latter proof gives nominal form bound M, nominal outer-gap bound A, and full Euclidean departures R,Z, the inclusion checks are

\[ M_*+R<X,\qquad Z<\zeta,\qquad A_*+2Z<A. \tag{6} \]

Within-child mean removal is an orthogonal projection, so Z still bounds its residual; there is no state change in this decomposition. These bounds also cover the outer-zero control with stationary nominal carrier. Independent child acquisition/recovery, matching law and clock, support, capture, and historical storage/work premises remain necessary. Equality of their five resource bounds does not equate five actual preparations. The first plateau supplies the unforced first window; no extra prefix is inserted before it.

docs.title: 3. Form readings isolate the interaction current
docs.text:
Let U be the five actual child mean forms. Internal sine currents cancel exactly within a child, including off the carrier, leaving two external currents per child. On an unforced plateau,

\[ U'=-L_5U/4+\gamma\bar S/4. \tag{7} \]

The observer supplies two ordered vectors P,Q of measured mean forms at that plateau's endpoints. For the receiver r=(c+1) mod 5, form the exact primitive combination

\[ D=Q_r-P_r+\frac h8\{L_5(P+Q)\}_r. \tag{8} \]

All terms are in form units. The second term compensates diffusion rather than equating the observed increment to a sine-current response. Integrating (7) shows that its true-value counterpart equals gamma/4 * integral(bar S_r) plus the trapezoid error in the diffusion term. The fine unforced rows bound each mean's second derivative by

\[ M_2=4M+2g+4g^2M. \tag{9} \]

Since ||L5||infinity=4, the trapezoid error in D is at most M2*h^3/12. During any plateau the command is fixed. Each of the two external phase differences differs from its initial shifted counterpart by at most 2E, so the mean current differs by at most 4E. The plateau integral may therefore be compared to the initial shifted current with error at most g*h*E, irrespective of its block's position.

The two receiver-reading coefficients in (8) are -1+h/4 and 1+h/4; the four neighboring endpoint coefficients are -h/8. With h<4, their absolute sum is exactly 2+h/2. Correlations need not be discarded. For every measured corrected increment,

\[ D=\frac{\gamma h}{4}\bar S_r(\theta(0)+RH_q)+\delta, \quad |\delta|\le b=g h E+M_2h^3/12+(2+h/2)\eta_{raw}. \tag{10} \]

No derivative or phase is measured. Reads from different plateaus belong to one carried state history; the initial state in (10) is a proof reference, never a copied or observed branch.

docs.title: 4. Quadratures, circular geometry and the initial winding
docs.text:
For interface c define the initial fine edge phasor by

\[ C_c+iS_c=\frac19\sum_j e^{i d_{c,j}},\quad d_{c,j}=a_c+z_{c+1,j}-z_{c,j},\quad |a_c|\le A. \tag{11} \]

The three plateau levels of block c affect just its receiver's boundary with marked child c. Their initial currents satisfy

\[ \bar S_r^{\pm}-\bar S_r^0 =\mathord\pm\sin\epsilon\,C_c +(1-\cos\epsilon)S_c. \]

Use the three new corrected increments to compute

\[ O_c=D_+-D_-,\quad V_c=D_++D_--2D_0. \] \[ O_c=\frac{\gamma h\sin\epsilon}{2}C_c+\delta_C, \quad V_c=\frac{\gamma h(1-\cos\epsilon)}2 S_c+\delta_S, \quad |\delta_C|\le2b,\quad |\delta_S|\le4b. \tag{12} \]

The coefficients and initial class in (12) exactly match the shared quadrature-to-cycle inverse. Consequently its existing geometry and circular kernel apply unchanged after the new primitive reading combinations and new complete-history errors have been established. This transfers only that algebraic inverse, not the earlier matched-branch or instantaneous sequential theorem.

In particular C_c>=cos(A+2*zeta)>0, the phasor modulus is at least cos(2*zeta), and its circular argument differs from a_c by at most 2*zeta. The kernel intersects those constraints, bounds each mean gap, and tests their sum against 2*pi*w, w in {-1,0,1}. It retains shared outward rounding and the existing angle-arithmetic allowance. A uniform returned cycle width strictly smaller than 2*pi admits at most one winding; an actual valid history supplies its included winding. This proves conditional identification for every admitted state and error record.

Malformed primitive readings reject before arithmetic. Impossible raw magnitudes, incompatible phasor annuli or absent cycle candidates remain explicit. A candidate or even a singleton for arbitrary supplied records does not authenticate their origin, their law, their error bounds or their joint realizability. Noise that defeats the uniform certificate leaves protocol admission unavailable, even if particular data look decisive.

docs.title: 5. Complete continuous resource account
docs.text:
The storage and balance remain

\[ H=\tfrac12x^TLx+\sum_e(1-\cos\delta_e),\qquad H'=-\|Lx\|_2^2/4+(Lx)^TRf. \tag{13} \]

Let ell=gamma_lower. The largest ramp has amplitude 2*epsilon and duration one. With the full-history residual M, the pulse extrema give

\[ Z_m=\frac{24\epsilon}{5\ell},\quad J=\frac{48\epsilon}{5\ell}+8M,\quad F_m=\frac{108\epsilon}{5\ell}. \] \[ \sup H\le180(Z_m+M)^2+180,\quad Loss\le45T_{obs}J^2/4,\quad W_{abs}\le45\cdot15 JF_m. \tag{14} \]

The input is present only over the fifteen ramps. The last bound also bounds total positive supplied work, including the sum of positive individual channel contributions. It uses absolute powers before summing, so simultaneous supplying and absorbing channels do not conceal costs. Storage change, loss and supplied work are distinct ledger quantities; old event work and signed hidden storage supply no reservoir.

Returning the command to zero does not erase the cost. On each ramp, the actual collective phase increment is its command plus at most 2E componentwise. The marked-minus-adjacent increment has magnitude at least delta_a=max(0,abs(a)-4E). The previously proved C5 contrast inequalities then imply, on disjoint ramp intervals,

\[ Loss\ge\frac{90}{g^2} (2\delta_{\epsilon}^2+\delta_{2\epsilon}^2),\qquad \sup\tfrac12x^TLx\ge12\delta_{2\epsilon}^2/g^2. \tag{15} \]

Plateau loss is nonnegative. Since initial storage is at most 180X^2+180, positive supplied work is at least max(0,Loss_lower-180X^2-180). These structural bounds prove neither calibrated joules nor optimal cost. Finite bandwidth, tracking uncertainty and physical sampling remain additional premises before interpreting this protocol as a realizable measurement.

docs.title: 6. Instrument and handoff boundary
docs.text:
The pure protocol, word and inverse admit only their primitive time, noise and ordered form readings. The source assessor separately rebuilds actual acquisition and inclusion, then assesses the fixed corner through the exclusive driver. The independent controls exercise synthetic algebra and source failures without generating a reserved response. No existing frozen driver or inverse is rewritten.

The final state belongs to this new finite-input history. Neither the old post-observation contact response nor its source-specific electrical error certificate transfers merely because the same winding was retained. Their full source, means, support, law and clock must match the new endpoint. The execution plan alone selects the next dependency. No physical dataset, autonomous actuator, laboratory calibration or material identity is admitted by the inverse.

docs.title: 7. Frozen source-inclusive decision
docs.text:
The declaration, consuming source and driver were committed at 0d46c82f46e722618920b6b8ebce0db475f13c64 before the single assessment. The preserved attempt and result retain verdict finite_input_observation_admitted, fourteen true source flags, eleven positive source margins and nine positive protocol margins. No actual-source trajectory, raw response record or physical experiment was generated by this assessment: it evaluated the uniform analytical bounds. The read-only evidence controls reconstruct the receipt, source inclusion, observation errors, cycle resolution and resource margins without importing or rerunning the assessor.

Quantity Outward summary of the archived bound Whole-history phase departure from the prescribed command less than 9.128e-6 radians Mean form magnitude at every reading and release less than 0.014668 Returned initial cosine / sine interval widths less than 0.001247 / 0.049824 Each returned initial mean-gap interval width less than 0.336298 radians Returned cycle-sum interval width less than 1.681488 radians Winding-resolution margin below 2*pi greater than 4.60169 radians Minimum outer acute-gap margin throughout the word greater than 0.070776 radians Within-child circular-collar margin greater than 1.5707578 radians Peak full storage less than 4.284e8 structural units Full integrated loss greater than 5.5748e7 and less than 1.607e9 structural units Positive supplied work greater than 5.5748e7 structural units Absolute supplied work and summed positive channel work less than 1.446e10 structural units

The cycle width is strictly smaller than the separation 2*pi between adjacent possible winding sums. Hence every valid record within the admitted class and error allowance identifies its actual initial winding. Both acquired families belong to that class; the broader inference also covers winding minus one without asserting its acquisition by the supplied preparation. All five internal and nine respective outer identities survive throughout the 15.00015 structural-time history. Large transient form, supplied work and residual release state remain explicit consequences of the finite inputs.

This closes the finite-input observation gate. Reusing the same prior and quadrature kernel preserved one algebraic owner while the new current correction and whole-history proof replaced the inapplicable instantaneous reading formula. The earlier frozen evidence and producers remain unchanged. The result supplies an observable collective identity under a complete conditional protocol; it establishes neither a physical sensor nor an autonomous force or material constituent.

docs.title: A freely reacting organized probe through one full relative turn
docs.text:
Two formed C9 constituents can traverse every relative registration on one freely evolving history while both internal identities remain acute. An initially supplied difference of their common forms drives the turn; neither constituent is held, and no phase reset or continuous input is used after contact. The actual mean-form record determines the relative phase through the already declared kinetic row. An integral identity then reads a current harmonic without differentiating that record. The finite-record construction below bounds the same readout from finitely many uncertain samples, under explicit timing and kinetic calibration premises. Separately admitted primitive phase and form snapshots provide a circular necessary test of that kinetic row, without reconstructing phase from it. The preparation result below distinguishes the large supplied form contrast from what any unforced common-contact schedule can generate.

This is conditional operational access under the existing supplied constitutive family. It does not select that family, establish physical measurement, or replace source, event-work and observation admission. The research program alone selects further work. The phase-faithfulness classification still distinguishes a complete operational alphabet from one current channel's invisible shifts.

docs.title: 1. Complete law, preparation and observation
docs.text:
Item Declaration Nodes and order Two marked C9 rings, nodes \(9c+k\), \(c=0,1\), \(k=0,\ldots,8\); ring A is \(c=0\), ring B is \(c=1\) Support Eighteen unit internal edges and nine same-slot matching edges of weight \(a=\gamma^2/1000\), added without resetting any coordinate Law The existing potential family \(0\le\lambda\le1\), with every edge weight used in both quarter-factor rows Capacity and clock Held unit capacities, \(\gamma=1/(1023\pi)\), unchanged structural clock \(\tau\); \(s=a\tau/2\) is only a declared common time coordinate Initial means Zero global form and lifted phase means, \(X_A-X_B=12/\gamma\), \(\Phi_A-\Phi_B=0\) Initial fine state Separate zero-mean residuals in each child's forms and lifted phases; the norm-derived bound \(F_0<1/40000\) below Horizon \(0\le s\le1\), equivalently \(0\le\tau\le T=2000/\gamma^2\) Retained identity Both internal winding-one C9 identities; no fixed joined acute chamber or conserved cross-contact winding is required Readout The continuing relative mean-form record; ending the integral at one reconstructed turn is an observation convention, not an event

Write \(\alpha=2\pi/9\), with the fixed closing-edge turn on each internal cycle. The actual primitive state is represented by continuous lifts

\[ x_{c,k}=X_c+z_{c,k},\qquad \theta_{c,k}=\alpha(k-4)+\Phi_c+q_{c,k},\qquad \sum_k z_{c,k}=\sum_k q_{c,k}=0. \tag{1} \]

Both forms and fine phases have 16 independent residual coordinates; the relative means contribute two more to the 34-dimensional fixed-mean full state. Keeping these residuals is essential: the reached state need not be the exact carrier \(q=z=0\).

The potential, current and uniform bounds are

\[ \begin{split} V_\lambda(u)&=1-\cos u+ \lambda\frac{(1-\cos9u)^2}{6\,9^4},\\ j_\lambda(u)&=\sin u+ \frac{\lambda}{2187} \left(\sin9u-\frac12\sin18u\right),\\ |j_\lambda|&\le J_0=\frac{1459}{1458},\qquad |j_\lambda'|\le J_1=\frac{245}{243},\qquad |j_\lambda''|\le J_2=\frac{10}{9}. \end{split} \tag{2} \]

Let \(L_9\) be the unit C9 Laplacian, \(L=I_2\otimes L_9+aL_{\rm match}\), and \(U_\lambda=\sum_e w_eV_\lambda(\theta_i-\theta_j)\). The full nondimensional structural law and its balance are

\[ x_\tau=\frac{-Lx-\gamma\nabla U_\lambda}4,\qquad \theta_\tau=\frac{\gamma Lx}4,\qquad H=\frac12x^\top Lx+U_\lambda,\qquad H_\tau=-\frac14\|Lx\|^2. \tag{3} \]

There is no input or later support change. Both conserved global means are retained. The smooth bounded currents and linear form terms give global continuation on phase lifts. This comparison is not a native operator word or a reciprocal-degree normalization.

Admit primitive residual norm bounds \(\|q(0)\|\le\rho_\theta\), \(\|z(0)\|\le\rho_x\), and define

\[ F_0=\frac12(\rho_\theta+\gamma\rho_x)^2 +\frac12\gamma^2\rho_x^2<\frac1{40000}. \tag{4} \]

The triangle inequality makes this an upper bound on the actual quadratic functional used below. Bounds are derived from the primitive preparation, not accepted as a cached source verdict.

docs.title: Preparation by a symmetry, not a reset to a target
docs.text:
An isolated C9 under this law is invariant under a constant common-form translation. Its Laplacian annihilates that constant, both evolution rows are unchanged, and its internal storage and identity are unchanged. Thus an independently admitted own-law formation/recovery history can be prepared from the outset with common forms \(+6/\gamma\) and \(-6/\gamma\), while retaining every reached residual and its original error correlations. Conserved zero phase means give the stated relative lift zero without an attachment-time phase reset.

This is the same exact symmetry used in own-law outer acquisition. Its use here is conditional on that law's source admission and the inequality (4). It does not transfer an endpoint law's source certificate to another law, authenticate records, or evaluate a source producer. The large common forms are supplied preparation. Their lack of isolated Laplacian-storage cost is an identity of (3), not a claim that physical preparation is free or that a native operator creates this state.

docs.title: 2. Exact mean rows and a monotone full turn
docs.text:
Put

\[ r=X_A-X_B,\qquad \delta=\Phi_A-\Phi_B,\qquad v=\gamma r,\qquad s=\frac a2\tau,\qquad \overline J=\frac19\sum_{k=0}^8 j_\lambda(\delta+q_{A,k}-q_{B,k}). \tag{5} \]

Internal currents cancel in each child mean, and the matching edges retain exactly the same relative mean form. Summing (3) therefore gives the exact full-state equations

\[ r_\tau=-\frac a2(r+\gamma\overline J),\qquad \delta_\tau=\frac{\gamma a}2r,\qquad \boxed{v_s=-v-\gamma^2\overline J,\quad \delta_s=v.} \tag{6} \]

Both constituents react. On the invariant carrier this reduces to \(\overline J=j_\lambda(\delta)\); no such substitution is needed for the following transit bound.

Write \(c_0=\gamma^2J_0\). The canonical constants give \(0<c_0<1/2\), hence also \(c_0\le1\). Variation of constants with \(v(0)=12\) gives, for \(0\le s\le1\),

\[ 12e^{-s}-c_0(1-e^{-s}) \le v(s)\le 12e^{-s}+c_0(1-e^{-s})\le12. \tag{7} \]

Using \(e^{-1}>1/3\) and \(c_0<1/2\) in the lower bound yields \(v(s)>11/3\). Integration of the lower bound, with \(e^{-1}<2/5\) and the weaker \(c_0\le1\), gives

\[ \begin{split} \delta(1)-\delta(0) &\ge12(1-e^{-1})-c_0e^{-1}\\ &>\frac{34}{5}>2\pi. \end{split} \tag{8} \]

The elementary estimates on \(e\) follow from its positive series: \(5/2<e<3\). The final comparison follows, for example, from \(\pi<22/7\). Thus a unique \(s_*\in(0,1)\) satisfies \(\delta(s_*)=2\pi\). In fact \(s_*>\pi/6\), since \(v\le12\). No trajectory or numerical root is needed to prove this statement. The flow continues freely; \(s_*\) merely ends the readout integral.

This establishes access to every intermediate relative registration in one actual history, without holding either phase fixed or independently preparing a separate contact for every query.

docs.title: 3. Fine-state retention through the nonacute transit
docs.text:
Let \(P\) project onto the separate zero-mean subspaces of the two rings. It commutes with \(L\). Write \(L_f=L|_{\operatorname{ran}P}\). The fine projection of the gradient is zero on the carrier for every \(\delta\): each ring's two internal currents cancel and its cross current is constant over slots. Consequently the exact fine rows are

\[ q_\tau=\frac\gamma4 L_fz,\qquad z_\tau=-\frac14L_fz-\frac\gamma4 g(q,\delta),\qquad g(q,\delta)=A(q,\delta)q. \tag{9} \]

Here \(A\) is the integrated projected Hessian on the straight fine segment from zero to \(q\), at the current relative mean phase. On the bootstrap tube \(\|q\|<1/100\), every internal gap differs from \(\alpha\) by less than \(1/50\). In particular its magnitude is below \(18/25\). With \(C_6(u)=1-u^2/2+u^4/24-u^6/720\),

\[ j_\lambda'(u)\ge\cos u-\frac2{243} \ge C_6(18/25)-\frac2{243}>\frac7{10} \quad\hbox{on those internal gaps}. \tag{10} \]

The cross-edge curvature can be negative during the turn, but is bounded below by \(-J_1\). On the two fine ring spaces the internal Laplacian has lowest eigenvalue \(2-2\cos(2\pi/9)>2/5\) and norm at most four; the matching Laplacian has norm two. Therefore the actual bounds are

\[ L_f\succeq\frac25I,\qquad \frac14I\preceq A(q,\delta)\preceq5I, \tag{11} \]

uniformly in the complete relative phase circle. For the lower bound, \((7/10)(2/5)-2aJ_1>1/4\); the upper norm is bounded by \(J_1(4+2a)<5\). These are own-law bounds for every \(0\le\lambda\le1\), not a transfer from the sine tangent. For the internal spectral bound, \(\alpha>2/3\) and cosine decreases on this interval, while \(\cos(2/3)\le1-(2/3)^2/2+(2/3)^4/24=191/243<4/5\).

Define the positive functional

\[ F=\frac12\|q+\gamma z\|^2+\frac12\gamma^2\|z\|^2, \qquad \|q\|^2\le4F,\qquad F\le\|q\|^2+\frac32\gamma^2\|z\|^2. \tag{12} \]

Substitution of both fine rows gives the exact identity

\[ F_\tau=-\frac{\gamma^2}{4} \left[q^\top g+z^\top L_fz+2\gamma z^\top g\right]. \tag{13} \]

Since \(\|g\|\le5\|q\|\), Young's inequality gives \(2\gamma|z^\top g|\le\|q\|^2/8+200\gamma^2\|z\|^2\). The canonical \(\gamma<1/3000\) satisfies \(2/5-200\gamma^2>1/8\) and \(3\gamma^2/2<1\). Equations (11)--(13) consequently imply

\[ \boxed{F_\tau\le-\frac{\gamma^2}{32}F,\qquad F(\tau)\le F_0e^{-\gamma^2\tau/32} =F_0e^{-125s/2}.} \tag{14} \]

Initially (4) and (12) place \(q\) strictly inside the tube. The same strict bound remains at any proposed first exit, so continuity closes the bootstrap through the whole observation horizon. Both internal cycles stay acute with winding one, including every allowed fine direction. No stationary profile replaces the actual state.

The full relative turn necessarily passes nonacute matching gaps and their phase cuts. This proves retention of the two constituent identities, not a fixed acute identity of the joined graph or fixed windings on every new mixed cycle. U3 at a support event is a separate admission; it is not reapplied as a filter of the unchanged global smooth current during (3).

For later observation, put \(d_k=q_{A,k}-q_{B,k}\). Its sum is zero. Taylor expansion and (2) give the quadratic error

\[ \begin{split} |\overline J-j_\lambda(\delta)| &\le\frac{J_2}{18}\sum_kd_k^2 \le\frac{J_2}{9}\|q\|^2\\ &\le\frac{4J_2F_0}{9}e^{-125s/2}. \end{split} \tag{15} \]

The first-order correction cancels because the fine means are retained.

docs.title: 4. Supplied contact work
docs.text:
Immediately before attachment the two rings are disconnected. Their state is unchanged by adding the nine weighted edges. At the declared \(\delta(0)=0\), the exact storage jump is

\[ \Delta H=a\sum_k\left[ \frac12(r_0+z_{A,k}-z_{B,k})^2+ V_\lambda(q_{A,k}-q_{B,k})\right]\ge0. \tag{16} \]

The cross term linear in \(r_0\) vanishes by the separate fine zero means. Since \(V_\lambda(0)=j_\lambda(0)=0\), \(0\le V_\lambda(u)\le J_1u^2/2\). Using \(r_0=12/\gamma\) gives the source-inclusive bound

\[ \boxed{\Delta H\le \frac{81}{125} +a\left(\rho_x^2+J_1\rho_\theta^2\right).} \tag{17} \]

The ideal carrier's cost is exactly \(81/125\); the residual term is retained for the actual source. The earlier isolated formation/storage history is separate from this positive attachment work. Nothing in the continuous loss supplies a reservoir, an autonomous attachment time or a native event realization. The horizon \(T=2000/\gamma^2\) and weak contact are explicit parts of this operational design, not a change of the constitutive law or a laboratory time estimate.

docs.title: 5. A derivative-free harmonic observation
docs.text:
The mean-form record gives \(v(s)=\gamma(X_A(s)-X_B(s))\). The unchanged phase row gives exactly

\[ \delta(s)=\delta(0)+\int_0^s v(u)\,du. \tag{18} \]

This uses the declared initial relative lift and kinetic law. It does not use an inverse of the current being tested, hidden fine phases, or a held phase reference. It cannot simultaneously validate an unknown kinetic row or recover an unadmitted initial phase.

For any positive integer \(n\), define from the same continuing record, up to its one-turn readout time \(s_*\),

\[ B_n=\frac1{\pi\gamma^2} \left\{ \frac n2\int_0^{s_*}\cos(n\delta)\,v^3\,ds -\int_0^{s_*}\sin(n\delta)\,v^2\,ds -\frac12[\sin(n\delta)v^2]_0^{s_*} \right\}. \tag{19} \]

To verify it, multiply \(v_s+v=-\gamma^2\overline J\) by \(v\sin(n\delta)\), integrate, and use \(\delta_s=v\) to integrate the \(vv_s\) term by parts. The result is exactly

\[ B_n=\frac1\pi\int_0^{s_*} \overline J(s)\sin(n\delta(s))\,v(s)\,ds. \tag{20} \]

No derivative of a measured record remains. In the primary preparation \(\delta(0)=0\), \(\delta(s_*)=2\pi\), so the endpoint term in (19) vanishes. It is displayed because it must be retained for an independently admitted nonzero starting phase and a complete turn from that phase.

Strict monotonicity permits \(d\delta=v\,ds\). If \(b_n\) is the actual sine Fourier coefficient of \(j_\lambda\), orthogonality and (15) imply

\[ \boxed{|B_n-b_n|\le\frac{8J_2F_0}{9}.} \tag{21} \]

Indeed the absolute integral of the fine current error over a turn is at most \(2\pi\) times its uniform upper bound. For this supplied family, \(b_1=1\), \(b_9=\lambda/2187\), \(b_{18}=-\lambda/4374\), and the other positive-index coefficients vanish. Formula (21) concerns the actual freely reacting fine state, not a nominal carrier sampled at imposed registrations.

docs.title: Exact access is not finite-resolution identification
docs.text:
Let \(A_n\) denote the expression in braces in (19). On the ideal carrier its ninth-harmonic value is \(\pi\gamma^2\lambda/2187\). This raw contrast is small; the normalization in (19) does not increase measurement accuracy. For the fixed declared \(\gamma\) and normalization, if a separately admitted complete record and quadrature error bounds \(|\widehat A_n-A_n|\) by \(E_n\), its total coefficient uncertainty is at most

\[ \frac{E_n}{\pi\gamma^2}+\frac{8J_2F_0}{9}. \tag{22} \]

That error budget must include reconstruction of \(\delta\), the readout endpoint and all affected integrals. If the kinetic calibration or clock is uncertain, its uncertainty must instead be propagated through the whole observation map, including the normalizing denominator; a numerator-only error at nominal \(\gamma\) does not suffice. For example, distinguishing two deformations through \(n=9\) with a common such bound requires twice (22) to be smaller than \(|\lambda_1-\lambda_0|/2187\). The next section supplies a finite sampling construction and its conditional uncertainty budget. It does not admit an instrument or a physical observation map.

docs.title: 6. Finite records with explicit uncertainty
docs.text: The mathematical question is whether finite observations can retain the information in (20), rather than whether the ideal continuous integral exists. Keep the complete law, primitive preparation, contact and horizon of section 1. In particular the actual initial means remain \(v(0)=12,\delta(0)=0\). The initial phase uncertainty introduced below belongs only to the readout; it does not enlarge the preparation class.

docs.title: 6.1 Subtracting the known free relaxation
docs.text:
Define a reference and two residuals from the actual mean record:

\[ h(s)=12e^{-s},\qquad w(s)=v(s)-h(s),\qquad R(s)=\frac{v(s)^2-h(s)^2}{2\gamma^2} =\frac{h(s)w(s)+w(s)^2/2}{\gamma^2}. \tag{23} \]

The complete mean rows, without any carrier substitution, give

\[ \begin{split} w_s+w&=-\gamma^2\overline J,\qquad w(0)=0,\\ R_s+2R&=-v\overline J,\qquad R(0)=0,\\ |w|&\le\gamma^2J_0,\qquad |w_s|\le2\gamma^2J_0,\\ |R|&\le R_0:=6J_0,\qquad |R_s|\le24J_0. \end{split} \tag{24} \]

The last two estimates follow by variation of constants and \(v\le12\). Multiplying the second row by \(\sin(n\delta)\) and integrating yields, at any \(b\in[0,1]\),

\[ \frac1\pi\int_0^b\overline J\,v\sin(n\delta)\,ds =\frac1\pi\left\{ \int_0^b R\bigl(nv\cos(n\delta)-2\sin(n\delta)\bigr)\,ds -[R\sin(n\delta)]_0^b\right\}. \tag{25} \]

At \(b=s_*\) this is the same \(B_n\) as (19). The factorized expression in (23) avoids forming the difference of the two large integrals in (19). It does not remove the accuracy needed to read the small form residual or to calibrate \(\gamma\).

The finite interpolation bound must also retain the actual fine state. Writing \(d_k=q_{A,k}-q_{B,k}\), equations (9), (12) and \(s=a\tau/2\) give

\[ \|d\|\le2\sqrt{2F},\qquad \|d_s\|\le\frac{5\sqrt F}{a},\qquad \sum_k(d_k)_s=0. \tag{26} \]

Here \(\|L_f\|<5\) and \(\gamma\|z\|\le\sqrt{2F}\). Differentiate the actual average current and subtract the zero quantity \(j_\lambda'(\delta)\sum_k(d_k)_s/9\). Then

\[ \begin{split} |\overline J_s| &\le12J_1+\frac{J_2}{9}\|d\|\|d_s\|\\ &\le12J_1+\frac{10\sqrt2J_2}{9a}F \le12J_1+\frac{5J_2}{3a}F,\\ |w_{ss}|&\le \gamma^2(2J_0+12J_1)+\frac{5000}{3}J_2F_0. \end{split} \tag{27} \]

Thus the fast fine relaxation has a declared contribution to the interpolation budget; it is not replaced by the carrier derivative.

docs.title: 6.2 Finite sampling, reconstruction and stopping
docs.text:
Use \(N+1\) samples at nominal scaled times \(s_i=i/N\), \(i=0,\ldots,N\), with \(N\) a positive integer and \(H=1/N\). The following are independently supplied observation premises:

  • A raw reading \(\widehat r_i\) differs from the actual relative form \(r(s_i^{\rm act})\) by at most \(\varepsilon_r\).
  • Its exposure time satisfies \(|s_i^{\rm act}-s_i|\le\xi\), with every actual exposure in \([0,1]\). This is an error in the declared scaled clock, including any error in converting a reading's timestamp to that clock.
  • A single kinetic calibration obeys \(\widehat\gamma/\gamma\in[1-\kappa,1+\kappa]\), \(0\le\kappa<1\).
  • The readout origin \(\widehat\delta_0\) obeys \(|\widehat\delta_0|\le\zeta\).

These premises do not follow from the nodal identity. In particular, a sensor value has not been identified with EPI by this theorem. The true kinetic law and \(\gamma=1/(1023\pi)\) remain unchanged; \(\widehat\gamma\) is only an observation calibration. An arbitrary unknown clock scale is not admitted unless it satisfies the uniform exposure bound throughout this horizon. The error allowances are deterministic joint uniform bounds and may be correlated. Independent justification means justification apart from the evaluated response; no statistical independence or stochastic averaging is assumed.

For computable enclosures let \(g_-\le\gamma\le g_+\) be positive rational bounds and let \(\pi_-\le\pi\le\pi_+\). Use the norm-derived sufficient upper bound \(F_0\) from (4), replacing \(\gamma\) by \(g_+\) there. Define

\[ \begin{split} C&=g_+^2J_0,\\ E&=12\kappa+(1+\kappa) \bigl[g_+\varepsilon_r+(12+C)\xi\bigr],\\ M_w&=g_+^2(2J_0+12J_1)+\frac{5000}{3}J_2F_0,\\ \varepsilon_v&=E+\frac{M_wH^2}{8},\qquad E_\delta=\zeta+\varepsilon_v,\qquad G_-^2=(1-\kappa)^2g_-^2. \end{split} \tag{28} \]

Indeed \(|v_s|\le12+C\). Multiplication of the raw reading by \(\widehat\gamma\), followed by comparison with \(v(s_i)\), gives

\[ |\widehat v_i-v(s_i)|\le E,\qquad \widehat v_i=\widehat\gamma\widehat r_i. \tag{29} \]

The term \(12\kappa\) retains the error in the large form mean; it cannot be dropped merely because the constitutive contrast is small.

At each nominal time form \(\widehat w_i=\widehat v_i-h(s_i)\), and let \(\widetilde w\) be their piecewise linear interpolant. Define the continuous reconstruction

\[ \widetilde v=h+\widetilde w,\qquad \widetilde\delta(s)=\widehat\delta_0+ \int_0^s\widetilde v(u)\,du,\qquad \widetilde R=\frac{h\widetilde w+\widetilde w^2/2} {\widehat\gamma^2}. \tag{30} \]

The elementary linear interpolation remainder bounded by \(\sup|w_{ss}|H^2/8\), together with (29), proves

\[ |\widetilde v-v|\le\varepsilon_v,\qquad |\widetilde\delta-\delta|\le E_\delta. \tag{31} \]

The integral in (30) uses only an exponential and the integral of a linear function on each cell; it requires no derivative of any reading.

Require the strict stopping margin

\[ \varepsilon_v< \min\left(\frac{11}{3},\,\frac{34}{5}-2\pi_+\right). \tag{32} \]

Then \(\widetilde v>0\) and there is a unique \(\widehat s_*\in(0,1)\) at which \(\int_0^{\widehat s_*}\widetilde v\,ds=2\pi\). This is a full reconstructed increment, so that \(\widetilde\delta(\widehat s_*)=\widehat\delta_0+2\pi\); it does not reset the true phase or absorb the readout offset. Moreover

\[ |\delta(\widehat s_*)-2\pi|\le\varepsilon_v,\qquad |\widehat s_*-s_*|\le\frac{3\varepsilon_v}{11}. \tag{33} \]

The second bound uses the true lower speed in (7). The readout origin error affects the harmonic factors and both endpoint terms, but not this increment stopping rule.

docs.title: 6.3 Calibration, quadrature and endpoint errors
docs.text:
The residual normalization in (30) uses the uncertain kinetic calibration. Its complete error, rather than a numerator-only error, is bounded by

\[ \varepsilon_R= \frac{(24+\varepsilon_v)\varepsilon_v}{2G_-^2} +R_0\left((1-\kappa)^{-2}-1\right),\qquad |\widetilde R-R|\le\varepsilon_R. \tag{34} \]

To see this, first compare \(\widetilde v^2\) with \(v^2\), using \(v\le12\); then compare \(\gamma^2/\widehat\gamma^2\) with one in the true residual. Both errors are retained in (34).

For an explicit finite quadrature, take a positive integer \(K\). Subdivide each data cell into \(K\) equal subcells and retain their portions before \(\widehat s_*\), clipping the last one at that endpoint. Use the midpoint of each retained portion. Each has length at most \(H/K\), no portion crosses a data knot, and there are at most \(NK\) such evaluations. This splitting matters because \(\widetilde w_s\) can jump at a data knot.

The following constants bound derivatives inside each data cell:

\[ \begin{split} W&=C+E,\qquad D=2C+2E/H,\qquad V=12+W,\qquad V_1=12+D,\\ \widehat R_0&=(12W+W^2/2)/G_-^2,\\ \widehat R_1&=(12W+VD)/G_-^2,\\ \widehat R_2&=(12W+24D+D^2)/G_-^2,\\ A_0&=nV+2,\\ A_1&=nV_1+n^2V^2+2nV,\\ A_2&=12n+3n^2VV_1+n^3V^3+2nV_1+2n^2V^2,\\ M_{f,2}&=\widehat R_2A_0+ 2\widehat R_1A_1+\widehat R_0A_2,\\ E_Q&=\frac{M_{f,2}}{24(NK)^2}. \end{split} \tag{35} \]

For example \(|\widetilde w|\le W\), \(|\widetilde w_s|\le D\) and \(\widetilde w_{ss}=0\) inside a cell. Therefore

\[ \widetilde R_{ss} =\frac{h\widetilde w-2h\widetilde w_s+ (\widetilde w_s)^2}{\widehat\gamma^2}. \tag{36} \]

This proves the three residual bounds in (35). For \(\widetilde A=n\widetilde v\cos(n\widetilde\delta) -2\sin(n\widetilde\delta)\), the bounds on \(|\widetilde A|,|\widetilde A_s|,|\widetilde A_{ss}|\) are respectively \(A_0,A_1,A_2\), using \(\widetilde\delta_s=\widetilde v\) and \(|\widetilde v_{ss}|=h\le12\). The product rule bounds \(|(\widetilde R\widetilde A)_{ss}|\) by \(M_{f,2}\). The midpoint remainder summed over the separate subcells is at most \(M_{f,2}(H/K)^2/24\), since their total length is at most one. No differentiability across data knots is assumed.

Let \(Q_{N,K}\) be this quadrature of \(\widetilde R\widetilde A\), and retain the reconstructed endpoint correction:

\[ \widehat B_n^{\,\rm exact}=\frac1\pi\left\{ Q_{N,K}-[\widetilde R\sin(n\widetilde\delta)] _0^{\widehat s_*}\right\}. \tag{37} \]

Both sine factors at these endpoints are \(\sin(n\widehat\delta_0)\); they need not vanish. Define the deliberately conservative observation bound

\[ E_O=\varepsilon_R(nV+4) +R_0\left[n\varepsilon_v+(12n^2+4n)E_\delta\right] +J_0\varepsilon_v. \tag{38} \]

Here is a direct comparison with the true full-turn integral. For \(A=nv\cos(n\delta)-2\sin(n\delta)\), equations (31) and (34) imply

\[ |\widetilde R\widetilde A-RA| \le\varepsilon_R(nV+2) +R_0\left[n\varepsilon_v+(12n^2+2n)E_\delta\right]. \tag{39} \]

Each endpoint difference is at most \(\varepsilon_R+R_0nE_\delta\). Finally the true current integral between \(\widehat s_*\) and \(s_*\) is bounded by \(J_0\varepsilon_v\), using \(d\delta=v\,ds\), \(|\overline J|\le J_0\) and (33). Adding these terms proves (38), including the true and reconstructed endpoints. The last term could be sharpened near a full turn but no such improvement is used here.

Allow a further certified coefficient error \(\varepsilon_{\rm num}\) in evaluating (37). Combining (21), (35) and (38) gives the finite-record theorem

\[ \boxed{|\widehat B_n-b_n|\le \mathcal E_n:= \frac{8J_2F_0}{9}+\frac{E_O+E_Q}{\pi_-} +\varepsilon_{\rm num}.} \tag{40} \]

The terms separately retain fine-state bias, raw readings, clock exposures, calibration, phase readout, interpolation, stopping, endpoints, quadrature and numerical evaluation. This is a sufficient theorem domain; failure of (32) or of a discrimination margin does not prove that a particular record is uninformative.

The numerical allowance can be supplied constructively. There are finitely many cell formulas and quadrature values; bounded-argument exponential and trigonometric Taylor series, with rigorous remainders, and convergent rational enclosures of \(\pi\) enclose them to arbitrary positive accuracy. The positive lower slope \(11/3-\varepsilon_v\) in (32) gives an explicit inverse bound for bisection of the reconstructed increment. For the integrand in (37), put \(M_0=\widehat R_0A_0\) and \(M_1=\widehat R_1A_0+\widehat R_0A_1\). Moving the clipping endpoint by \(e_s\) changes the midpoint sum by at most \((M_0+HM_1/(2K))e_s\): the derivative of a partial-cell term of length \(\ell\) is \(f(\mathrm{midpoint})+\ell f_s(\mathrm{midpoint})/2\). The corresponding endpoint product changes by at most \((\widehat R_1+n\widehat R_0V)e_s\). These bounds also apply when an endpoint crosses a data knot, by continuity and the bounds on each side. They permit a finite root enclosure and arithmetic precisions whose total coefficient error is any prescribed \(\varepsilon_{\rm num}>0\). This is an existence and error allocation argument, not a claim about unchecked floating point evaluation. Setting this allowance to zero describes ideal exact evaluation, not a generic machine implementation.

docs.title: 6.4 Frozen finite budget and an ambiguity control
docs.text:
The prospective budget frozen at revision fd5dc157 uses

Primitive allowance or design Frozen value Harmonic and two hypotheses \(n=9,\ \lambda=0\) versus \(\lambda=1\) Fine form and phase norm bounds \(\rho_x=0,\ \rho_\theta=10^{-6}\) Data intervals and quadrature subdivisions \(N=10000,\ K=100\) Raw relative-form reading error \(\varepsilon_r=10^{-11}\) Exposure error in scaled time \(\xi=10^{-18}\) Relative kinetic calibration error \(\kappa=10^{-18}\) Initial phase readout error \(\zeta=10^{-10}\) Certified coefficient evaluation allowance \(\varepsilon_{\rm num}=10^{-8}\)

Thus \(F_0=5\,10^{-13}\). Rebuilding (28)--(40) with rational enclosures gives the following approximate values only as readable summaries of the bounds:

Derived bound Approximate upper bound Scaled sample error \(E\) \(3.13554\,10^{-15}\) Interpolation error \(\varepsilon_v\) \(4.84310\,10^{-15}\) Residual error \(\varepsilon_R\) \(6.00283\,10^{-7}\) Observation contribution \(E_O\) \(6.78369\,10^{-5}\) Quadrature contribution \(E_Q\) \(6.95902\,10^{-7}\) Total coefficient bound \(\mathcal E_9\) \(2.18247\,10^{-5}\)

The exact rational comparison is

\[ \mathcal E_9<\frac{219}{10^7} <\frac1{4374} =\frac12\left|\frac1{2187}-0\right|. \tag{41} \]

It proves disjoint coefficient intervals for the two hypotheses if a record and its calibration satisfy these supplied premises. The construction uses 10001 raw readings and at most one million quadrature evaluations; these are finite counts, not a benchmark or a runtime prediction. The budget is stringent, especially its kinetic and clock calibration. No instrument, actual record, observed response or laboratory clock is certified by (41). The calculation admits the frozen budget without retuning it against an evaluated response.

Finite error is also a substantive information restriction. For example, compare the two exact carrier histories under the same frozen support and means, with \(\lambda=0\) and \(1\). Their currents differ by at most \(d=1/1458\) at each phase. Variation of constants in (6), the current Lipschitz bound \(J_1\), and Gronwall's inequality on \(0\le s\le1\) give

\[ \sup_s|v_1(s)-v_0(s)| \le\gamma^2d\,e^{\gamma^2J_1},\qquad \sup_s|r_1(s)-r_0(s)| \le\gamma d\,e^{\gamma^2J_1}. \tag{42} \]

For completeness, the first difference is bounded by \(\gamma^2d+\gamma^2J_1\int_0^s|\delta_1-\delta_0|\,du\). Since the phase difference is the integral of the form difference, on this unit horizon its double integral is at most the corresponding single integral of the running supremum. The scalar Gronwall bound gives (42). If the independently permitted raw reading radius is at least \(\gamma d e^{\gamma^2J_1}/2\), the midpoint of these two raw records is compatible with both laws. This remains true even with continuous reading, perfect clocks and perfect kinetic calibration. It is a sufficient, nonoptimal ambiguity regime for this preparation, not a sharp noise threshold or a claim that every noisier record is ambiguous. More samples alone cannot remove this admitted overlap.

docs.title: 6.5 A certified consumer of primitive records
docs.text:
The detached reader implements (30)--(40). Its inputs are the ordered raw readings at the canonical nominal grid \(i/N\), the scalar \(\widehat\gamma>0\), the initial lifted-phase readout \(\widehat\delta_0\), and all primitive preparation, error and integer work budgets. It rebuilds the family and fine-state bounds; a cached budget, derivative bound or earlier report is not a premise. Every raw scalar is admitted before interval arithmetic. Malformed values, a wrong sample count and unsupported theorem budgets retain their domain errors.

Some necessary consistency conditions can be checked before evaluating the observation. In addition to \(|\widehat\delta_0|\le\zeta\), they are

\[ \begin{split} 1-\kappa&\le1023\pi\,\widehat\gamma\le1+\kappa,\\ |\widehat w_0|&\le E,\qquad |\widehat w_i|\le C+E,\\ |\widehat w_{i+1}-\widehat w_i| &\le2CH+2E,\qquad \widehat w_i=\widehat\gamma\widehat r_i-12e^{-iH}. \end{split} \tag{43} \]

The first line checks the declared calibration against the unchanged model constant. The other lines follow from \(w(0)=0\), \(|w|\le C\), \(|w_s|\le2C\), and the sample error (29). A separated violation is incompatible with the joint supplied premises. If an outward enclosure overlaps a threshold without certifying its side, the reader abstains numerically. Passing these conditions is not a sufficient test that a record came from the declared dynamics, preparation or instrument.

All numerical enclosures concern the supplied represented readings themselves. Sensor and calibration uncertainty are already propagated by (28)--(40); they are not applied a second time as numerical uncertainty on every raw value. The shared exact exponential bounds and outward rational interval arithmetic enclose the reference heat values, residuals and their cumulative integrals. For example, define

\[ P_i=\sum_{j<i}\frac H2(\widehat w_j+\widehat w_{j+1}), \qquad d_i=\frac{\widehat w_{i+1}-\widehat w_i}{H}. \]

For \(s=iH+u\), \(0\le u\le H\), the reconstructed increment is

\[ D_{\rm inc}(s)=12(1-e^{-s})+ P_i+\widehat w_i u+\frac12d_i u^2. \tag{44} \]

This exact cell formula avoids numerical integration of the phase. Grid heat values may be formed by outward recurrence with the common factor \(e^{-H}\), retaining the accumulated enclosure width. The shared positive exponential enclosure on \([0,1]\) also encloses \(e^{-s}\) by taking its reciprocal. No new decay law is introduced.

On each cell the lower bound

\[ \widetilde v(s)\ge 12e^{-(i+1)H}+\min(\widehat w_i,\widehat w_{i+1}) \tag{45} \]

gives a directly checkable positive slope \(\mu\) for the reconstructed increment. The reader encloses \(D_{\rm inc}(1)-2\pi\) and brackets the first complete turn. Bisection uses certified signs, not a floating root followed by a claimed tolerance. If the enclosure of \(D_{\rm inc}(m)-2\pi\) straddles zero, the inverse slope bound still contains the root within \(m\pm |D_{\rm inc}(m)-2\pi|/\mu\), using an upper bound on the absolute residual. A root bracket is retained through every step. The initial phase readout remains outside this increment equation.

Let the certified root interval be \(S\), let \(b\) be its rational midpoint and let \(r_S\) be its radius. Evaluate the prescribed midpoint sum clipped at \(b\), including both endpoint terms, with outward function and arithmetic enclosures. Denote this coefficient enclosure by \(I_b\). The root sensitivity derived after (40) gives

\[ \begin{split} L_{\rm end} &=\frac{1}{\pi_-}\left[ \widehat R_0A_0+\frac{H}{2K} (\widehat R_1A_0+\widehat R_0A_1) +\widehat R_1+n\widehat R_0V\right],\\ I_{\rm obs}&=I_b+[-L_{\rm end}r_S,L_{\rm end}r_S]. \end{split} \tag{46} \]

Thus \(I_{\rm obs}\) encloses the exact discrete functional (37), including its exact reconstructed turn endpoint. The numerical certificate requires the computed radius \(\operatorname{rad}(I_{\rm obs})\le\varepsilon_{\rm num}\); the requested numerical allowance alone never proves that inequality. Quadrature truncation is accounted for separately, through \(E_Q\). If certified, the final conditional coefficient enclosure is

\[ I_{\rm coefficient}=I_{\rm obs}+[-E_{\rm an},E_{\rm an}], \qquad E_{\rm an}=\frac{8J_2F_0}{9}+\frac{E_O+E_Q}{\pi_-}. \tag{47} \]

The measured numerical width already lies in \(I_{\rm obs}\). Adding \(\varepsilon_{\rm num}\) again in (47) would count it twice. The midpoint of \(I_{\rm obs}\) also satisfies the conservative bound (40), conditional on the independent observation premises.

The implementation distinguishes five outcomes:

Status Meaning Certified The necessary record checks, reconstructed turn and requested numerical width have been enclosed; (47) remains conditional on the supplied model and observation premises Incompatible record A checked necessary condition is separated from its admitted interval; the record and joint premises cannot all hold Unresolved numeric Fixed-precision enclosures cannot settle a required comparison or fit the requested numerical allowance Unresolved endpoint A sufficient monotone reconstruction or complete-turn bracket has not been certified within the endpoint iteration and precision limits Work limit The quadrature evaluation cap is insufficient for the reconstructed endpoint

These statuses do not replace domain rejection and do not identify a physical law. The interval owner uses a fixed dyadic precision; its bounded computation need not attain every positive tolerance allowed by the mathematical existence argument. In particular, zero numerical allowance is an exact ideal and will generally remain unresolved. Work limits are computation policies, not a failure of TNFR dynamics. Input admission precedes a work-limit return. The coefficient enclosure remains unavailable for every noncertified status, even if intermediate endpoint or observation bounds are retained.

Independent controls use manufactured analytic records. For example, an ideal constant residual \(w=c\) gives

\[ v=h+c,\quad R=(hc+c^2/2)/\widehat\gamma^2,\quad R_s+2R=cv/\widehat\gamma^2. \tag{48} \]

Its corrected continuous full-increment functional is zero for every initial readout origin: the corresponding test current is constant \(-c/\widehat\gamma^2\), whose sine integral over a turn vanishes. For nonzero origin and \(c\), the endpoint term itself need not vanish. Rational approximations to these analytic samples, with independently bounded remainders, test the numerical reconstruction and endpoint correction. Such records are controls of an observation algorithm, not evaluated histories of the supplied constitutive family. No scientific producer, source replay or physical-data comparison is needed to verify this reader.

docs.title: 7. Independently observed phase and clock
docs.text: The preceding reader reconstructs phase using the kinetic row it consumes. An independent test of that row instead observes the eighteen primitive phases as well as the eighteen signed forms, in the fixed order 9*c+j. This section supplies a conditional structural observation protocol. The phase readout and its error and timing bounds are additional premises; they are not inferred from the form record. The global product channel needs no internal phase chart; an optional finer channel admits its own collar. Support, unit capacities, the two-C9 marking and the fixed model constant \(\gamma=1/(1023\pi)\) remain unchanged. No observing NFR or physical sensor is introduced, and detached reading installs no feedback or event.

docs.title: 7.1 Global products and marked arithmetic means
docs.text:
For arbitrary continuous primitive lifts define \(\delta=(\sum_j\theta_{A,j}-\sum_j\theta_{B,j})/9\). The directly observed product \(P_9=\prod_j e^{i\theta_{A,j}}\prod_j e^{-i\theta_{B,j}} =e^{i9\delta}\) is independent of their displayed turns. This identity needs neither a fine-state bound nor retained internal winding. The fixed support and labels are needed to compare its rate with the mean form row. The product alone retains a ninefold ambiguity in circular \(\delta\).

At a snapshot subtract the known frame \(\alpha(j-4)\) from each primitive phase, obtaining circular offsets \(d_{c,j}\). Retain the strict coherent collar used by the shared child observation. In exact notation, let \(Z_c=\sum_j e^{i(d_{c,j}-d_{c,0})}\), require \(\operatorname{Re}Z_c>0\), and define

\[ \begin{split} b_c&=d_{c,0}+\operatorname{Arg}Z_c,\\ r_{c,j}&=\operatorname{Arg}e^{i(d_{c,j}-b_c)}, \qquad |r_{c,j}|<\pi/2,\\ M_c&=b_c+\frac19\sum_{j=0}^8r_{c,j},\qquad m_c=e^{iM_c}. \end{split} \tag{49} \]

The resultant selects a regular anchor; the reported mean is the arithmetic mean of the collar lifts, not its direction. On the marked fine chart \(d_{c,j}=\Phi_c+q_{c,j}\), with zero fine mean and compatible collar lifts, (49) gives \(m_c=e^{i\Phi_c}\) exactly. All fine deviations are retained. Adding independent full turns to displayed primitive phases preserves this circular mean; it can change the displayed anchor lift. That snapshot lift is not automatically a continuous temporal lift.

This distinction matters even on the existing organization. The ordinary first resultant is exactly zero on the winding-one carrier: \(\sum_j e^{i[\alpha(j-4)+\Phi_c]}=0\). Demodulation removes that cancellation, but its resultant direction need not equal the arithmetic mean. For \(q=(a,a,-2a,0,\ldots,0)\), \(a>0\) small, the fine mean vanishes while the demodulated resultant has imaginary part \(2\sin a-\sin2a>0\). Formula (49) removes this fine-state bias by retaining the individual phases.

Snapshot collars alone do not connect (49) to the continuous nodal means between readings: an individual node could leave and re-enter the collar after one full turn. The optional local test below therefore requires an independent no-slip certificate. The product channel avoids this issue.

docs.title: 7.2 Independent boxes and a circular kinetic test
docs.text:
Choose exact increasing nominal times \(s_i\) in \([0,1]\). At each snapshot all eighteen forms and phases refer to one actual exposure \(s_i+e_i^{\rm time}\in[0,1]\), where \(|e_i^{\rm time}|\le\xi\). Supply per-node form error \(\varepsilon_x\), circular angular error \(\eta\), and independent absolute-continuity bounds \(|v_s|\le L_v\) and \(|\theta_{c,j,s}|\le L_\theta\) throughout the window. These bounds are independently justified regularity assumptions; no values are taken from the kinetic row under test. Frame-registration and phase-readout errors must be included in \(\eta\), and uncertainty in conversion to the declared scaled clock must be included in \(\xi\). When \(\xi=0\), no node phase-speed bound is needed for exposure transport; take \(L_\theta\xi=0\) without supplying \(L_\theta\). It is still needed for the implemented optional local no-slip test.

A conservative \(L_v\) can follow from the unchanged form row alone. For any phase path, \(v_s+v=-\gamma^2\overline J\), \(|\overline J|\le J_0\), and \(v(0)=12\) imply \(|v|\le12+C\), \(|v_s|\le12+2C\), with \(C=\gamma^2J_0\). Thus \(L_v=12+2C\) is available when those independent form-law premises are retained. No phase kinetic identity is used in this bound.

For the recorded primitive phases \(\widehat\theta_{c,j,i}\), use local real boxes whose circular images contain the nominal phases:

\[ P_{c,j,i}=\widehat\theta_{c,j,i} +[-e_\theta,e_\theta],\qquad e_\theta=\eta+L_\theta\xi,\qquad e_v=2\gamma\varepsilon_x+L_v\xi. \tag{50} \]

These boxes directly enclose the global product angle by summation. Optionally apply (49) to their demodulated values with outward arithmetic and the shared strict collar checks. This gives \(M_{c,i}\) enclosing a representative of the nominal circular mean. An unresolved collar leaves only that local mean unavailable; it does not block the product channel. No phase is reconstructed from form or replaced by a resultant direction.

The signed sample means independently give \(\widehat v_i=\gamma(\sum_j\widehat x_{A,j,i} -\sum_j\widehat x_{B,j,i})/9\). Simultaneous exposure and the two mean errors imply \(v(s_i)\in V_i=\widehat v_i+[-e_v,e_v]\). For \(h_i=s_{i+1}-s_i\), define

\[ A_i=\frac{h_i}{2}(V_i+V_{i+1}) +[-L_vh_i^2/4,L_vh_i^2/4]. \tag{51} \]

This encloses \(\int_{s_i}^{s_{i+1}}v\,ds\). Indeed the trapezoid error equals \(\int_{s_i}^{s_{i+1}}(s-(s_i+s_{i+1})/2)v_s\,ds\), whose absolute value is at most \(L_vh_i^2/4\). Endpoint reading uncertainty is already in the intervals \(V_i\); it is not added twice.

Let \(S_i=\sum_jP_{A,j,i}-\sum_jP_{B,j,i}\). The tested mean kinetic row and its globally observable necessary condition are

\[ \delta_s=v,\qquad e^{i9[\delta(s_{i+1})-\delta(s_i)-\int_{s_i}^{s_{i+1}}v\,ds]}=1, \qquad C_{9,i}=2\bigl(1-\cos(S_{i+1}-S_i-9A_i)\bigr). \tag{52} \]

Every independently displayed primitive turn cancels under this cosine. For the sharper local test, require endpoint collars and, for both children, an independently bounded \(L_\theta\) and the strict certificate

\[ \max_j|\operatorname{Arg}e^{i(d_{c,j,i}-d_{c,0,i})}| +2L_\theta h_i<\pi,\qquad C_{1,i}=2\bigl(1-\cos(D_{i+1}-D_i-A_i)\bigr), \quad D_i=M_{A,i}-M_{B,i}. \tag{53} \]

The maximum is bounded over the phase boxes. Node-to-first-node phase differences have speed at most \(2L_\theta\), so their left principal lifts cannot cross a cut during the interval. The endpoint arithmetic means therefore match the continuous means up to a common whole turn. This suffices for \(C_{1,i}\); no collar is assumed between snapshots. Alternatively an independently admitted whole-window marked fine chart justifies the same local identity. The implemented certificate uses (53).

Each available defect is enclosed outwards in \([0,4]\). A strictly positive lower bound refutes the joint observation and kinetic premises; zero inclusion is inconclusive. Unresolved collars or no-slip bounds do not erase a product-channel exclusion. These are necessary tests, not proofs of the kinetic law, a selected current or an authenticated sensor. They test the collective row only: even exact agreement leaves zero-mean fine phase motions unchecked. Eighteen primitive inputs do not make this compressed observation a test of all eighteen phase equations.

An exact analytic control changes only the phase row to \(\theta_s=0\), retaining the form row and the carrier initial state \(q=z=0\), \(\delta=0\), \(v=12\). The held phases give \(\overline J=0\), hence \(v(s)=12e^{-s}\). Over \([0,1/4]\) the phase increment is zero while the form integral is \(12(1-e^{-1/4})\in(21/8,85/32)\subset(0,\pi)\), using the quadratic and cubic alternating bounds for \(e^{-1/4}\). Nine times this interval lies strictly between \(6\pi\) and \(8\pi\), so the product defect is positive too. This is a complete-row control, not a numerically evaluated trajectory or a transferred formation certificate.

docs.title: 7.3 Aliasing and clock scope
docs.text:
Even perfect finite phase readings do not generally determine a temporal lift. On the uniform grid \(s_i=i/N\), the changes

\[ \theta_{A,j}(s)\longmapsto\theta_{A,j}(s)+2\pi Ns, \qquad \theta_{B,j}(s)\longmapsto\theta_{B,j}(s)-2\pi Ns \tag{54} \]

leave every sampled primitive phasor, both fine states and the zero global phase mean unchanged. They add \(4\pi Ns\) to the relative lift. These are alternative observation-level histories, not asserted solutions of the held complete law. They show why the circular necessary test can miss added whole turns; it is not an exact temporal reconstruction.

With independently justified bounds \(\epsilon_i^\delta\) on circular registration reading errors, the familiar sufficient no-alias condition is

\[ |\delta(s_{i+1})-\delta(s_i)|+\epsilon_i^\delta+\epsilon_{i+1}^\delta<\pi. \tag{55} \]

It permits unique principal increments after an admitted initial lift; consistent endpoint errors telescope. A known independent variation bound can supply the first term. Equation (55) may not be justified by the very phase row being tested. The present circular instrument supplies neither this temporal lift nor an independently observed turn counter.

Finally, an external clock \(u\) with \(ds/du=\chi(u)>0\) transforms both complete rows. With the unchanged weighted support and \(s=a\tau/2\), they become

\[ x_u=\frac{\chi}{2a}(-Lx-\gamma\nabla U),\qquad \theta_u=\frac{\chi\gamma}{2a}Lx,\qquad \delta_u=\chi\gamma r. \tag{56} \]

An unknown constant clock scale and an unknown phase kinetic coefficient appear only through their product in the last observation. They are not separately identified by that row. A clock or another independently justified complete-law premise is needed to separate them. Declaring nominal structural timestamps is not a laboratory clock calibration. This protocol is a structural observation in the NFR ontology; native phase/U3 access is not a physical sensor. An interacting observing NFR would additionally need its own state, laws, coupling, backreaction and admission. No such object, trajectory, source replay or physical response is evaluated here.

docs.title: 8. Preparation reachability and its supplied resources
docs.text: The common-form symmetry in section 1 relates different initial states; it does not generate their different means along an unforced history. This section asks whether a lower-resource initial state can acquire the probe's \(v=12\), allowing a much larger class of contact schedules than the fixed contact used in sections 1--7. It changes neither the eighteen marked nodes, the unit internal edges, the held unit capacities nor the canonical \(\gamma\). Fix any one \(\lambda\in[0,1]\).

docs.title: 8.1 Exact full-state contrast and invariant band
docs.text:
Let the nine matching edges share a nonnegative, measurable, locally integrable weight \(a(\tau)\). Both quarter-factor rows use this same weight. Allow a separately supplied locally integrable nodal form source \(\Gamma(\tau)\) and finitely many finite form jumps \(\Delta x_j\) at declared times \(\tau_j\), keeping primitive phases unchanged at those jumps. Between jumps the complete law is

\[ x_\tau=\frac{-L(a)x-\gamma\nabla U_\lambda(a,\theta)}4+\Gamma, \qquad \theta_\tau=\frac{\gamma L(a)x}4, \qquad L(a)=I_2\otimes L_9+aL_{\rm match}. \tag{57} \]

The additive source is outside the quarter factor. It is the supplied form-rate channel described by the parameter foundation and integrator contract, not a pressure reconstructed from the response. Equation (57) declares the phase row as well; using the source channel does not assert that a native operator runtime implements this whole comparison law. No phase, capacity or internal-support events are added here. The fixed-contact clock \(s=a\tau/2\) from (5) is not used for variable or vanishing contact. Zero contact can pause accumulated exposure while the declared structural clock \(\tau\) and isolated dynamics continue.

This flow has unique continuation on every finite interval: the linear coefficient has norm bounded by \(4+2a\), while the current is globally bounded and globally Lipschitz with locally integrable weighted coefficients. The resulting integral bounds prevent finite-time escape of either form or a continuous phase lift. The argument needs no acute fine chart, carrier assumption or constituent-retention certificate.

Write \(\overline\Gamma_c=\frac19\sum_k\Gamma_{c,k}\), and put

\[ \begin{split} k(\tau)&=a(\tau)/2,\qquad C=\gamma^2J_0,\\ u(\tau)&=\gamma(\overline\Gamma_A-\overline\Gamma_B),\qquad d_j=\frac\gamma9\left(\sum_A\Delta x_j-\sum_B\Delta x_j\right),\\ \mathcal E(\tau,\sigma)&= \exp\left(-\int_\sigma^\tau k(\zeta)\,d\zeta\right). \end{split} \tag{58} \]

Internal diffusion and odd-current terms cancel in each child mean. The common matching weight leaves exactly \(a(X_A-X_B)\) in its mean form sum, even for arbitrary fine forms. Thus the actual full state obeys \(v_\tau=-kv-\gamma^2k\overline J+u\), with \(|\overline J|\le J_0\) for all primitive phases and every admitted \(\lambda\). At a form jump, \(\Delta v=d_j\). State-preserving support changes have no direct contrast jump. The integrating-factor identity, with right-continuous values at the finite jumps, is

\[ \begin{split} v(\tau)={}&\mathcal E(\tau,0)v(0) -\gamma^2\int_0^\tau\mathcal E(\tau,\sigma)k(\sigma) \overline J(\sigma)\,d\sigma+\mathcal R(\tau),\\ \mathcal R(\tau)={}&\int_0^\tau\mathcal E(\tau,\sigma)u(\sigma)\,d\sigma +\sum_{0<\tau_j\le\tau}\mathcal E(\tau,\tau_j)d_j. \end{split} \tag{59} \]

Any initial jump is included in the declared \(v(0)\). Since \(\int_0^\tau\mathcal E(\tau,\sigma)k(\sigma)\,d\sigma =1-\mathcal E(\tau,0)\), (59) gives the signed enclosure

\[ \mathcal E(\tau,0)v(0)+\mathcal R(\tau)-C(1-\mathcal E(\tau,0)) \ \le v(\tau)\le \mathcal E(\tau,0)v(0)+\mathcal R(\tau)+C(1-\mathcal E(\tau,0)). \tag{60} \]

Without sources or form jumps, \([-C,C]\) is invariant; an arbitrary initial contrast stays in the convex hull of its initial value and this band. In particular, from \(v(0)=0\), \(|v(\tau)|\le C(1-\mathcal E(\tau,0))\le C<10^{-7}\). The last strict inequality follows from \(\pi>157/50\) and \(J_0=1459/1458\). No duration, strength or timing of these common nonnegative contacts can reach \(v=12\). At \(a=0\), both child means are separately conserved in the unforced model. The equal weight over all nine slots is essential: slot-dependent weights would retain fine forms in the mean boundary term and define another preparation problem. The separate reciprocal resource theorem bounds that broader class using all initial fine forms and the node count; its bound does not replace this sharper common-matching result.

docs.title: 8.2 Necessary source and jump variation
docs.text:
Reaching \(v(\tau)=12\) requires the signed discounted resource

\[ \mathcal R(\tau)\ge 12-\mathcal E(\tau,0)v(0)-C(1-\mathcal E(\tau,0)). \tag{61} \]

Replacing \(u,d_j\) by their positive parts in \(\mathcal R\) gives a larger quantity and the same necessary lower bound. Neither this inequality nor the current bound supplies the current's realized sign or sufficient conditions for reaching the target.

A simpler envelope uses only primitive bounds on the initial contrast and total nodal input variation through the proposed horizon: \(|r(0)|\le R_0\), \(B_{\rm cont}\ge\int\sum_i|\Gamma_i|\,d\tau\), and \(B_{\rm jump}\ge\sum_j\sum_i|\Delta x_{i,j}|\). Because \(|u|\le\gamma\sum_i|\Gamma_i|/9\), with the same projection bound for each jump, and \(0<\mathcal E\le1\),

\[ \begin{split} |v(\tau)|&\le M_0+\frac\gamma9(B_{\rm cont}+B_{\rm jump}), \qquad M_0=\max(\gamma R_0,C),\\ B_{\rm cont}+B_{\rm jump}&\ge \frac9\gamma[12-M_0]_+\quad\text{is necessary to allow the target}. \end{split} \tag{62} \]

These budgets count unsigned nodal form variation, not stored energy, net form creation or work. Indeed the global form mean \(\mu=(X_A+X_B)/2\) has \(\mu_\tau=(\overline\Gamma_A+\overline\Gamma_B)/2\), and its jump is the average of the two child-mean jumps. Equal opposite inputs can increase contrast while keeping \(\mu\) fixed. A zero net input therefore does not establish a zero preparation-resource budget.

docs.title: 8.3 Work accounting and a supplied positive control
docs.text:
The contrast theorem allows merely locally integrable \(a\); a differentiable storage ledger requires stronger regularity. If \(a\) is absolutely continuous between its finitely many declared support jumps, define

\[ K(x,\theta)=\frac12\sum_k(x_{A,k}-x_{B,k})^2 +\sum_kV_\lambda(\theta_{A,k}-\theta_{B,k})\ge0. \qquad H_\tau=-\frac14\|Lx\|^2+(Lx)^\top\Gamma+a_\tau K. \tag{63} \]

The cross terms between the two continuous rows cancel exactly. A state-preserving support jump has \(\Delta H=(a^+-a^-)K\). At fixed support a pure form jump has \(\Delta H=(Lx^-)^\top\Delta x+\frac12\Delta x^\top L\Delta x\). For simultaneous state and support changes, use the exact difference \(H(a^+,x^+,\theta)-H(a^-,x^-,\theta)\), or explicitly order the events and evaluate their separate changes at the proper states. \[ \Delta H=a_*K\ge a_*\frac92(X_A-X_B)^2 =\frac{81}{125}. \tag{64} \]

This follows from the mean-square inequality and \(V_\lambda\ge0\), independently of the fine state. It is a floor for this declared attachment, not for the cumulative work of every possible schedule. For the admitted fine states of section 1, the corresponding upper bound remains (17).

The isolated Laplacian annihilates both added constants, so (65) is an exact solution transformation of (57). docs.text:
