It does not derive physical charge, spin, a quantum state or a unique law. The execution plan alone selects further investigation.

docs.title: Joint acquisition on existing fine support
docs.text:
Every member of the declared phase-flat preparation acquires winding one in all three marked C9 constituents by structural time \(T=200\), for both fixed connected supports. Its complete form and phase state enters the joined target's trapping sublevel at that deadline and subsequently converges to the equal or unequal stationary registration. The initial whole-network storage is below the frozen ceiling \(10^9\).

This is conditional joint formation on supplied fine support under the declared reciprocal sine law. It does not attach previously recovered children, create an edge, or supply an autonomous preparation mechanism. The assembly-work obstruction remains valid for its different late-attachment experiment. The present proof retains the substantial initial form storage, including the contact contribution. Storage is measured in this model's structural units, without a laboratory energy identification.

docs.title: Complete law, preparation and identity
docs.text:
Use the 27 labelled nodes \((r,j)\), ordered as \(9r+j\), where \(r=0,1,2\) and \(j=0,\ldots,8\). Each constituent has its unit-weight C9 edges. For the oriented contacts \(e=(0,1),(1,2),(2,0)\), include the undirected edges

\[ (r,j)--(t,j)\ \text{with weight }1-s_e,\qquad (r,j)--(t,j+1)\ \text{with weight }s_e, \tag{1} \]

where indices are modulo nine. The two controls are

\[ s^{\mathrm{eq}}=(1/2,1/2,1/2),\qquad s^{\mathrm{un}}=(1/4,1/2,3/4). \tag{2} \]

All 81 positive edges are present at preparation and remain unchanged. Every node has weighted degree four. The contacts and node markings are supplied model data; the law does not select either support.

Let \(L_f\) be the actual weighted Laplacian, let \(x=\mathrm{EPI}\) be signed real form, and retain primitive circular phases with continuous lifts \(\theta\). Capacities are held at one, the structural clock is \(\tau=(1023/1024)t\), and \(\gamma=1/(1023\pi)\). The complete law is

\[ \begin{split} S_i(\theta)&=\sum_{j\sim i}w_{ij}\sin(\theta_j-\theta_i),\\ x'&=\tfrac14[-L_fx+\gamma S(\theta)],\qquad \theta'=\tfrac\gamma4L_fx,\\ H(x,\theta)&=\tfrac12x^TL_fx+ U(\theta),\qquad U(\theta)=\sum_{\{i,j\}}w_{ij}[1-\cos(\theta_j-\theta_i)],\\ H'&=-\tfrac14\|L_fx\|_2^2 . \end{split}\tag{3} \]

Primes denote structural time. Both rows acquire the factor \(1023/1024\) in original time. Equation (3) independently supplies pressure and the companion phase law. There is no forcing, live source, state reset, support event or conductance evolution. This is the detached weighted comparison from the network-law owner, separate from native unique-neighbor phase pressure and registered operator execution.

Set

\[ q_{r,j}=j-4,\qquad m=\frac{2046}{9}\left(\frac{355}{113}\right)^2, \qquad \alpha=\frac{2\pi}{9},\qquad \Theta=\alpha q . \tag{4} \]

The fresh connected-source declaration is

\[ \begin{split} x(0)&=mq+\eta_x,\qquad \theta(0)=\eta_\theta,\\ |\eta_{x,r,j}|&\le r_x=10^{-10},\qquad |\eta_{\theta,r,j}|\le r_\theta=10^{-10},\\ \sum_j\eta_{x,r,j}&=\sum_j\eta_{\theta,r,j}=0\quad(r=0,1,2). \end{split}\tag{5} \]

Every combination satisfying these bounds and correlations is included. The rational \(355/113\) in the preparation is retained exactly; it is not replaced by \(\pi\). The common initial lifted phase origin is zero. Although these primitive ramps also appear in the isolated-source work, none of its acquisition, recovery or residual verdicts is consumed here.

Antisymmetry of the sine currents gives \(\mathbf1^TS(\theta)=0\). Therefore the global form and lifted phase means remain zero. Constituent means need not remain zero after connected evolution starts. All 54 fine coordinates remain in the proof; a six-coordinate registered family is not used as a transient quotient.

For each marked C9, winding means the sum of its oriented principal circular phase differences divided by \(2\pi\), when no edge is on the branch boundary. At preparation all actual differences have magnitude at most \(2r_\theta<\pi\) and telescope to zero. Each constituent therefore starts at winding zero. The acquisition question is a change of actual circular geometry, followed by retention and convergence; the node labels alone do not provide that result. The retained constituent and boundary state matches the NFR ontology.

docs.title: Whole-network preparation cost
docs.text:
The deadline \(T=200\), original-time deadline \(204800/1023\), and initial storage ceiling \(10^9\) are fixed before evaluating the certificate. The phase-flat nominal source has zero phase storage. On one C9 the form ramp has eight differences of magnitude \(m\) and one of magnitude \(8m\), giving storage \(36m^2\). Matching contacts have zero nominal form difference. Each shifted contact contributes \(36s_em^2\). Thus both controls have the same complete nominal cost

\[ H(mq,0)=108m^2+36m^2\sum_es_e=162m^2 . \tag{6} \]

In particular, \(54m^2\) of this cost is already on the contact edges. It cannot be omitted by treating preparation as three isolated objects.

The exact residual accounting can use the actual Laplacian. Write \(s_{\mathrm{out},r}\) and \(s_{\mathrm{in},r}\) for the two incident oriented contact weights. Direct evaluation gives

\[ (L_fq)_{r,j}= \begin{cases} -9-s_{\mathrm{out},r}-8s_{\mathrm{in},r},&j=0,\\ s_{\mathrm{in},r}-s_{\mathrm{out},r},&1\le j\le7,\\ 9+8s_{\mathrm{out},r}+s_{\mathrm{in},r},&j=8. \end{cases}\tag{7} \]

Consequently

\[ \kappa_s:=\|L_fq\|_1 =54+18\sum_es_e+7\sum_r|s_{\mathrm{in},r}-s_{\mathrm{out},r}| =\begin{cases}81,&s=s^{\mathrm{eq}},\\88,&s=s^{\mathrm{un}}. \end{cases}\tag{8} \]

The degree bound gives \(0\preceq L_f\preceq8I\). Expanding the form quadratic, bounding its linear term by \(m\kappa_s r_x\), and using \(1-\cos z\le z^2/2\) for the phase term yields

\[ 162m^2-m\kappa_sr_x \ \le H(x(0),\theta(0))\le 162m^2+m\kappa_sr_x+108(r_x^2+r_\theta^2)<10^9 . \tag{9} \]

The nominal value is approximately \(815531786.0449456\). Even the larger linear correction is less than \(1/50000\); all bounds in (9) are exact rational calculations. This is supplied preparation storage. The later loss in (3) is not an inferred preparation source or an event reservoir.

docs.title: Global complete-law transport to the fixed deadline
docs.text:
The graph contains the Cartesian support formed by the three unit C9s and matching contacts of weight \(1/4\) between each constituent pair. Its nonzero Laplacian gap is

\[ \min\{2-2\cos\alpha,3/4\}>2/5. \tag{10} \]

The remaining contact conductance is positive semidefinite. Thus \(A=L_f/4\) has gap greater than \(1/10\) on the global mean-zero space. This is a full-support gap, with no requirement that the three constituent means remain separately zero. Degree four also implies the global forcing bound

\[ |S_i(\theta)|\le4,\qquad \|S(\theta)\|_2\le4\sqrt{27} \tag{11} \]

for every lifted phase configuration. Neither (10) nor (11) assumes an acute sector or a winding class.

Variation of constants in the actual form row, together with \(\|q\|_2=\sqrt{180}\), gives

\[ \begin{split} \|x(T)\|_2&\le b_x,\\ b_x&=e^{-20}\bigl(m\sqrt{180}+r_x\sqrt{27}\bigr) +10\gamma\sqrt{27}<1/50 . \end{split}\tag{12} \]

The forcing integral is bounded by \(\int_0^T e^{-(T-v)/10}\,dv\le10\). It includes the coupled phase history rather than substituting an externally prescribed phase.

Adding the two evolution rows after scaling the form row by \(\gamma\) gives an exact integrated relation,

\[ (\theta+\gamma x)'=\frac{\gamma^2}{4}S(\theta),\qquad \theta(T)=\theta(0)+\gamma x(0)-\gamma x(T) +\frac{\gamma^2}{4}\int_0^T S(\theta(v))\,dv . \tag{13} \]

It retains both original errors and the rational ramp mismatch. Therefore

\[ \begin{split} \|\theta(T)-\Theta\|_2&\le b_\theta,\\ b_\theta&=\sqrt{180}|\gamma m-\alpha| +\sqrt{27}(r_\theta+\gamma r_x) +\gamma b_x+200\gamma^2\sqrt{27}<1/5000 . \end{split}\tag{14} \]

The mismatch is independently evaluable from the supplied preparation:

\[ \gamma m-\alpha =\frac{2}{9\pi}\left[\left(\frac{355}{113}\right)^2-\pi^2\right]. \tag{15} \]

Outward rational enclosures give \(b_x\) approximately \(0.01623004820\) and \(b_\theta\) approximately \(0.00010725580\). The strict rational thresholds in (12) and (14), not rounded displayed decimals, are used below.

The reusable prepared-transit kernel applies with scaled form \(a=\gamma x\), generator \(A=L_f/4\), feedback \(\gamma^2\), forcing bound \(\sqrt{27}\), gap bound \(1/10\), and decay bound enclosing \(e^{-20}\). Its phase remainder is measured from the actual \(\theta(0)+a(0)\); (14) separately adds the initial errors and the difference from \(\Theta\). This transfers a proved method, with every coefficient and source bound re-admitted for (3).

The vector field is globally Lipschitz. Equations (12)--(14) are analytic bounds for the uninterrupted full flow and require no numerical trajectory, step-size assumption or replacement of a reached state by its nominal reference. In particular, no all-window acute certificate is asserted. The winding change from zero necessarily involves a principal-phase branch crossing before the deadline; these global estimates permit it.

docs.title: Actual entry, winding and eventual joined registration
docs.text:
Reuse only the targets and conditional barrier from the full-state capture theorem. The target for the equal control is \((0,\Theta)\). For the unequal control it is \((0,\theta_*)\), with nonzero constituent origins and the unique current-balance root declared there. In both cases the target has global lifted mean zero, all fine registered edge gaps have magnitude below \(22/25\), and all three internal windings equal one. Its complete stationarity is established on all fine nodes.

Let \(H_*=H(0,\theta_*)\), and retain the corresponding fixed seam integers in each lifted edge difference \(\delta_e\). The prior target calculation gives

\[ E_{\mathrm{nom},s}=H(0,\Theta)-H_* =0\quad(s^{\mathrm{eq}}),\qquad 0<E_{\mathrm{nom},s}<27/100\quad(s^{\mathrm{un}}). \tag{16} \]

The barrier proof applies on the common mean-zero leaf to the full cell

\[ \mathcal D_s=\{(x,\theta): |\delta_e(\theta)|<2 \text{ for every fine edge}\} . \tag{17} \]

Its every boundary point satisfies \(H-H_*\ge196/625\). Internally,

\[ H-H_*\ge\tfrac12x^TL_fx +\tfrac3{20}(\theta-\theta_*)^TL_f(\theta-\theta_*). \tag{18} \]

That proof uses the exact weighted-support resistance certificate and a Bregman bound relative to the actual target. The cell need not have a positive Hessian everywhere. These are target and geometry premises; the old independently recovered source is not a premise of (17)--(18).

Write \(z=\theta(T)-\Theta\). Equations (12)--(14) imply that every fine edge at \(T\), using the fixed seam integers, has gap of magnitude at most \(\alpha+\sqrt2b_\theta<1\). Hence the actual state lies inside (17). On each marked internal C9 its principal gaps are \(\alpha+z_{r,j+1}-z_{r,j}\), with the seam treated by the same integer as the target. Summation gives exactly \(9\alpha=2\pi\). All three actual windings at the deadline are therefore one.

For the energy entry test it is essential to retain the first variation at \(\Theta\). The unequal aligned reference is not stationary, and there is no separate constituent-mean cancellation at \(T\). Direct fine-node evaluation gives

\[ g_s:=\|\nabla U(\Theta)\|_2=\|S(\Theta)\|_2 =3\sin\alpha\sqrt{\sum_r(s_{\mathrm{out},r}-s_{\mathrm{in},r})^2} =\begin{cases}0,&s^{\mathrm{eq}},\\ \sqrt{27/8}\sin\alpha,&s^{\mathrm{un}}. \end{cases}\tag{19} \]

The global absolute quadratic remainder is at most \(\tfrac12z^TL_fz\le4\|z\|_2^2\). Thus the complete reached excess has the sufficient bound

\[ \begin{split} E_T&:=H(x(T),\theta(T))-H_*\\ &\le E_{\mathrm{nom},s} +4b_x^2+4b_\theta^2+g_sb_\theta <196/625 . \end{split}\tag{20} \]

For example, the coarse common bound \(g_s\le4\sqrt{27}<24\) and the rational thresholds in (12), (14) already imply

\[ E_T<\frac{27}{100}+\frac4{2500} +\frac4{25000000}+\frac{24}{5000} =\frac{1727501}{6250000}<\frac{196}{625}. \tag{21} \]

Using the actual values in (19) gives excess upper bounds below \(11/10000\) for the equal control and \(263/1000\) for the unequal control. Both inequalities cover every initial source in (5).

The dissipation law now prevents escape through the boundary of (17). The conditional full-state theorem consequently retains all three windings for every \(\tau\ge200\) and proves

\[ (x(\tau),\theta(\tau))\longrightarrow(0,\theta_*) \quad\text{as }\tau\longrightarrow\infty . \tag{22} \]

Its invariant-set argument applies because the trapped sublevel is compact on the conserved mean leaf, zero dissipation forces \(x=0\), and the only invariant critical phase point in the cell is \(\theta_*\). No numerical settling time is claimed. At the deadline the fine state need not belong to the exactly registered family; the residual coordinates remain part of the same convergence proof.

docs.text:
The joint-acquisition certificate re-admits primitive error bounds, reconstructs both actual weighted supports, accounts for (6)--(9), and uses shared prepared-transit and target/barrier owners for (12)--(22). The source-independent target and barrier owner rebuilds its geometry from primitive weights and supplies no acquisition verdict. Shared outward dyadic128 intervals retain the irrational coefficients; exact rationals retain the preparation, conductance and error data. Other nonnegative error allowances require their own freshly evaluated inequalities; the frozen source verdict is not transferred to them. Failed sufficient inequalities remain unavailable and do not demonstrate nonformation.

The independent controls check full fine support and degree, exact ramp cost and residual coefficients, the complete-law transport bounds, initial and final winding conditions, the unequal first variation, mean premises and invalid raw inputs. They also guard the reuse boundary: the old isolated recovery and its \(10^{-70}\) endpoint are not inputs to this new preparation.

The theorem establishes acquired constituent winding, full-state capture and eventual joined registration under one unchanged supplied law and connected support. These are distinct from autonomous edge birth, selection of a preparation or a constitutive law, collective operator admission, a finite-reservoir mechanism, scale selection and physical identification. The same support also admits the zero-form, phase-flat stationary state; the result does not assert that every preparation forms the organization. The execution plan alone assigns the next research question.

docs.title: 1. A coupled sufficient domain
docs.text:
Write x=EPI, and let \(\alpha=2\pi/9\), \(\gamma=1/(1023\pi)\), \(V_n=n[1-\cos(2\pi/n)]\). On every fixed support in this history,

\[ x'=(-Lx+\gamma S(\theta))/4,\qquad \theta'=\gamma Lx/4,\qquad H=\tfrac12x^TLx+\sum_e[1-\cos\delta_e],\qquad H'=-\|Lx\|_2^2/4. \tag{1} \]

The support changes and phase commands have their actual complete storage jumps. They are supplied events, not continuous pressure flows or inferred occurrence laws. Common phase and form translations are isolated symmetries; relative child origins and common forms become consumed state after contact. The NFR ontology retains membership, constituent and boundary state separately from the observed winding label.

The following conditions define the resource domain. Each must be admitted on the actual history: isolated acquisition and recovery, full-state outer acquisition and capture, inclusion in the observation class, sequential inference and work, then external response, work and finite identity. A successful last inequality cannot replace an unavailable earlier premise.

docs.title: Isolated acquisition and class-one recovery
docs.text:
Use the fresh source estimates (20)--(23) of the own-law acquisition proof at deformation zero, half-factor time 100 and the admitted primitive errors \(\rho_x,\rho_\theta\). Their form and target-phase radii are denoted \(b_x,b_\theta\). The initial class-one cost bound is

\[ B_{s}=36m^2+32m\rho_x+18(\rho_x^2+\rho_\theta^2). \tag{2} \]

Require the original source budget, initially zero winding, actual entry into the radius-\(r=1/12\) ball and its strict storage trap. No source error is multiplied by a forcing constant or silently replaced by a target. Inside this class-one ball every principal edge gap differs from \(\alpha\) by at most \(\sqrt2r\). Consequently

\[ c_1L\preceq\nabla^2U\preceq L,\qquad c_1=\cos(\alpha+\sqrt2r)>0. \tag{3} \]

This is the actual nonlinear Hessian on the retained trap. The earlier two-class proof used a smaller common curvature to include class two; that frozen result is unchanged. Its existence does not require using its smaller curvature for this class-one-only preparation.

In the half-factor clock put \(A=L/2\), \(g_0=1/5\), \(\Lambda=2\), \(\eta=\gamma^2\), \(\epsilon_L=g_0/4\), \(\xi=A^{-1/2}(\theta-\Theta_1)\), \(v=\gamma A^{1/2}x\). On the relative leaf the modified energy is

\[ \mathcal V=\tfrac12\|v\|^2+\tfrac\eta2(U-U_*) +\epsilon_L\xi^Tv+\tfrac{\epsilon_L}2\xi^TA\xi. \]

With outward lower and upper bounds indicated by subscripts, define

\[ \begin{split} \mu&=\eta_-c_{1,-}g_0^2,&M&=\eta_+\Lambda^2,\\ a_-&=\mu/2+g_0^2/16,& a_+&=M/2+\epsilon_L\Lambda/2+\epsilon_L^2,\\ \kappa&=\min\{4(g_0-\epsilon_L)/3,\epsilon_L\mu/a_+\},& V_0&=3\eta_+\Lambda b_x^2/4+a_+b_\theta^2/g_0. \end{split} \tag{4} \]

The shared modified-energy proof gives \(\mathcal V'\le-\kappa\mathcal V\) and \(\mathcal V\ge\|v\|^2/4+a_-\|\xi\|^2\). A quarter-factor dwell D therefore admits the handoff radius q whenever

\[ \kappa D/2\ge80,\qquad \frac{4V_0\,2^{-80}}{\eta_-g_0}<q^2,\qquad \frac{\Lambda V_0\,2^{-80}}{a_-}<q^2. \tag{5} \]

Indeed \(e^{-\kappa D/2}\le e^{-80}<2^{-80}\). Every bound concerns the uninterrupted reached state; q is a derived recovery enclosure, not a primitive accuracy requirement. All six separate sources must pass (2)--(5) before any joined-source conclusion is admitted.

The two return bounds in (5) retain more information than the common q enclosure. The preparation-aware initialization proof uses their separate form and phase allowances to bound constituent variances and carry a collective forecast from attachment. It preserves this source, dwell and decay budget; it neither infers a microstate nor replays the assessor.

docs.title: Actual outer acquisition and observation-class inclusion
docs.text:
The exact same carrier, support and clock as the outer-acquisition owner retain their fresh nominal endpoint intervals and radii \(P_c,f_x,f_\theta\). For the actual five-child deviations its global heat argument gives

\[ Z=6q(1+\gamma_+),\qquad R=3q+24\gamma_+Z. \tag{6} \]

Require \(\alpha-2Z>0\), \(\alpha+2Z<\pi/2\) throughout the transit, and the nominal endpoint outer gaps enlarged by \(2Z\) strictly inside \((0,\pi/2)\). Rebuild the nominal storage excess \(U_{\rm nom}\) from the same carrier estimate. The actual excess obeys

\[ U=U_{\rm nom}+8\|\bar x\|_2R+4R^2+14Z+4Z^2. \tag{7} \]

Require \(U<\min\{b_9-V_9,b_5-V_5\}\), where \(b_n=1+(n-1)[1-\cos(3\pi/(2(n-1)))]\), and require the control bound \(40q^2<\min\{b_9-V_9,1\}\). These are the actual full-product barriers, not the primitive C5 capture verdict.

To enter the unchanged observation class set \(X=1/100\), \(\zeta=10^{-6}\), \(A_o=7/5\). Require

\[ f_x+R<X,\qquad 2Z<\zeta, \qquad\max|\hbox{nominal outer gap}|+2Z<A_o. \tag{8} \]

The factor two in (8) is essential: subtracting each child's actual mean phase error produces the observation class's zero-child-mean residual. Its coordinate magnitude is bounded by \(2Z\), while the mean corrections enlarge adjacent origin gaps by at most \(2Z\). Initial childwise means are not asserted conserved after the outer edges are added.

docs.title: One observation word and the following contact
docs.text:
Keep \(T_o=1/5000\), \(h_o=1/100000\), \(\epsilon=1/10\), and put \(B_o=X+\gamma_+T_o\), \(D_o=4\gamma_+B_oT_o\). With the same quantities \(M_3,E_C,E_S\) and response factors \(f_C,f_S\), only the admitted reading errors change:

\[ b_C=E_C+\tfrac23M_3h_o^3+\tfrac{16}3\eta_o+f_CD_o, \qquad b_S=E_S+2M_3h_o^3+6\eta_o+f_SD_o. \tag{9} \]

Rebuild the outward initial-angle width d from these errors and require \(5d<2\pi\), including the fixed interval-rounding allowance. Retain the positive cosine chart, finite-comparison domain and all three identity margins. Every event costs at most 3.6 in absolute storage and the cumulative absolute expenditure is at most 36. These are actual-state bounds and do not cancel inverse commands or spend previous loss. Inference remains conditional on an admitted source; arbitrary readings are not authenticated.

At external contact let \(m_o=D_o/2\), \(e=Z+m_o+q\), \(h=1/1000\). Retain the larger initial form bound when necessary:

\[ B=\max\{B_o,q\}+7\gamma_+h/4,\qquad E=15\gamma_+h^2/16+15\gamma_+^2Bh^2/4. \tag{10} \]

For each actual source its contact moment Q has the same source-derived rectangle as the relative-origin proof: sum \(\cos(P_c+[-e,e])\) for its real coordinate and \(-\sin(P_c+[-e,e])\) for its imaginary coordinate. The control uses \(P_c=\{0\}\). These enclosures retain actual recovery errors and the entire preceding observation history. They supply amplitude bounds \(A_{w,-}\le|Q_w|\le A_{w,+}\).

The exact donor mean obeys \(R_D'=-3R_D/2-\gamma\mathcal A/4\). The whole-law remainder (10) therefore gives

\[ L_w=\max\{0,\gamma_-hA_{w,-}/4-E-2\eta_c\},\qquad U_w=\gamma_+hA_{w,+}/4+E+2\eta_c. \tag{11} \]

Require \(U_1<10^{-8}\), \(L_0>3\cdot10^{-7}\) and the fixed-origin signed contrast lower bound above \(10^{-7}\), retaining its separate \(2E+4\eta_c\) error. The first capability bound holds at every origin; the second has a source-dependent witness preceding the choice of reading errors. Neither supplies an alignment selector.

docs.title: Work, present storage and finite identity
docs.text:
The outer attachment has exact nominal cost \(W_0=1507001760\) and \(W_0\le W_{\rm outer}\le W_0+20q^2\). Require both this upper bound and \(5V_9+W_0+40q^2\) below \(2\cdot10^9\). At the new contact put

\[ W_+=90+\tfrac{45}2(B_o+q)^2,\qquad D_j=7\gamma_+Bh. \tag{12} \]

Require \(W_+<100\) and both present-storage bounds \(6V_9+9V_5+U+36+4q^2+W_+<200\) and \(6V_9+36+44q^2+W_+<200\). Check every strict margin in (21) of the external-interaction owner using this q and \(D_o,D_j\). The six internal and nine old outer windings then persist through the whole finite contact, independently of the supplied donor origin. The historical account remains \(\sum_{s=1}^6B_s\), outer attachment, the fifteen absolute observation payments and the new contact payment. Present storage and dissipated storage cannot replace that account.

All these conditions are simultaneous. Acquisition radii, recovery V0, initial cost and transported errors increase with primitive allowances; phase and moment enclosures are nested as errors increase. The source-class and identity margins consequently decrease, observation widths increase with \(\eta_o\), and contact error increases with \(\eta_c\). Curvature, decay rate, dwell and q are fixed. Thus the declared maximal corner suffices for the full box without a parameter scan. This is an inclusion argument, not a monotonicity assertion about individual trajectories. It does not extend the single-corner verdict to different dwells, handoff radii or decay powers. Those require their own simultaneous checks.

docs.title: 2. Necessary restrictions that sufficient bounds cannot remove
Finite-time compression of an original phase family
docs.text:
Choose two admitted original sources with identical forms and opposite phase errors \(\pm r_0v\), where v is a mean-zero unit vector and \(0<r_0\le\rho_\theta\). Their initial phase separation is \(2r_0\). Eliminate their form difference in the quarter law, writing \(z=\Delta\theta\):

\[ z(t)=z(0)+\frac{\gamma^2}4\int_0^t (I-e^{-L(t-s)/4})\Delta S(s)\,ds. \tag{13} \]

On C9, \(\|I-e^{-Lt/4}\|\le1\) and \(\|\Delta S\|\le4\|z\|\). Gronwall gives \(\|z(t)-z(0)\|\le2r_0(e^{\gamma^2t}-1)\), hence \(\|z(t)\|\ge2r_0(2-e^{\gamma^2t})\). If both reached phases lie within q of the same lifted target, then, when \(q<r_0\),

\[ T_{\rm prep}\ge\gamma^{-2}\log(2-q/r_0),\qquad D\ge\gamma^{-2}\log(2-q/r_0)-200. \tag{14} \]

This global argument covers the nonacute formation transit. It does not prove that the earlier supplied dwell was necessary, and gives no positive restriction from this pair when \(q\ge r_0\). For the whole declared box one may take \(r_0=\rho_{\theta,\max}\). An exact rational lower witness can use \(\log(1+u)\ge2u/(2+u)\), \(u=1-q/r_0>0\), without introducing a new logarithm evaluator.

docs.title: Reading error and the minimum contact horizon
docs.text:
The two contact readings permit a difference error of either sign and magnitude \(2\eta_c\). An upper capability threshold \(U_{\rm th}\) that must hold for every such error therefore necessarily requires \(2\eta_c<U_{\rm th}\). A witness response above a positive lower threshold \(L_{\rm th}\) for every error requires its true magnitude to exceed \(L_{\rm th}+2\eta_c\). Since the exact donor mean starts at zero, its damping equation and \(|\mathcal A|\le5\) give

\[ |R_D(h)|\le\frac{5\gamma}{6}(1-e^{-3h/2}) \le\frac{5\gamma h}{4},\qquad \frac{5\gamma h}{4}>L_{\rm th}+2\eta_c. \tag{15} \]

For the declared capability these thresholds are \(10^{-8}\) and \(3\cdot10^{-7}\). These are necessary observation restrictions; they do not replace the sufficient nonlinear, work or identity checks. Replacing \(\gamma\) by \(\gamma_+\) in the signal margin gives an upper bound: a nonpositive upper margin proves an obstruction, whereas a positive one alone supplies no capability certificate.

docs.title: Winding acquisition, duration and supplied contact work
docs.text:
For a fixed-support unforced interval of duration \(T_a\), Cauchy--Schwarz and (1) give, with \(\mathcal L=\int_0^{T_a}\|Lx\|^2/4\,dt\),

\[ T_a\mathcal L\ge4\|\theta(T_a)-\theta(0)\|^2/\gamma^2. \tag{16} \]

Initially each raw same-slot outer gap has magnitude at most \(2q\). At an outer-winding-one endpoint, principal gaps sum to \(2\pi\) but raw lifted gaps telescope to zero. Some raw gap in each slot is therefore below \(-\pi\), with the endpoint away from winding cuts. The corresponding two coordinates have squared total displacement at least \((\pi-2q)^2/2\). The nine slots are disjoint coordinate sets, so \(\|\Delta\theta\|^2\ge9(\pi-2q)^2/2\), for \(2q<\pi\).

If the endpoint retains the declared acute internal and outer cycles, Jensen's bounds give \(H_{\rm final}\ge5V_9+9V_5\); the initial disconnected source has storage at most \(5V_9+20q^2\). Thus

\[ W_{\rm outer}\ge9V_5+ \frac{18(\pi-2q)^2}{\gamma^2T_a}-20q^2. \tag{17} \]

This necessary duration--work relation is weaker than the exact fixed-ramp cost \(W_0\), but demonstrates that the preparation cost is not entirely a pessimistic recovery estimate. It applies to the stated support, law, clock and endpoint identity, not arbitrary TNFR acquisition protocols.

docs.text:

docs.title: Constitutive law and unknown collective initialization
Analytical scope and result
docs.text:
The unchanged joint form observations distinguish the sine law from its retained analytic countermodel throughout the declared initial class, even when initialization is independently unknown under each law. The whole-record theorem proves that their complete finite noisy record sets are disjoint. Its retained strict certificate includes both nonlinear histories and each law's fine-source error. This is a conditional information result; no measured record or physical law is selected. The earlier record-only forecast still predicts under its supplied sine law.

This owner establishes the alternative's own carrier, hidden-state error, finite identity and numerical growth bounds. It also proves a local obstruction: two distinct admitted initial phase gaps under the two endpoint laws have exactly the same two ideal frozen-current quadratures. An admitted adjacent gap can also match the three ideal receiver currents. Neither local test uniformly selects the law. The complete 150-by-35 formal sampled map is injective, but a direction with exact low-order cancellations obstructs every global scalar or positive block bootstrap using the retained unconstrained coefficient and remainder bounds. Those preliminary results alone establish neither separation nor overlap of the complete noisy nonlinear record sets.

A constrained continuation uses the actual shared harmonic phase. Two long-ramp contrasts cancel the fundamental without dividing by the short plateau duration, and their ideal joint signal has a uniform positive phase-circle margin. The middle ramp supplies stronger same-mode contrasts. Joint observations also force equal winding and bound the fundamental phasor difference. These restrictions, actual late-time heat decay and correlated phase transport close the nonlinear separation theorem. A separate heat bridge through the same readings retains its historical phase-increment error bound below 2.8e-8; the final theorem does not need to reconstruct an individual record's phase history.

docs.title: 1. The complete alternative on the present support
docs.text:
Retain the current/potential owner:

\[ V_\lambda(a)=1-\cos a+\lambda\frac{(1-\cos9a)^2}{6\,9^4},\qquad j_\lambda(a)=\sin a+\frac\lambda{2187} (\sin9a-\tfrac12\sin18a). \tag{1} \]

With L_f=I5 tensor L9+L5 tensor I9, S_lambda,i=sum_(k~i) j_lambda(theta_k-theta_i) and gamma=1/(1023*pi), the full rows are

\[ x'=(-L_fx+\gamma S_\lambda(\theta))/4+Rf,\qquad \theta'=\gamma L_fx/4. \tag{2} \]

The signed nodal pressure is specified by the original-clock form row; both rows undergo the same clock conversion. The phase channel is not an independently supplied synchronization law. Odd periodic current preserves the global form and lifted-phase sums for neutral input. Its own storage is

\[ H_\lambda=\tfrac12x^TL_fx+\sum_{e}V_\lambda(\delta_e),\qquad H_\lambda'=-\|L_fx\|_2^2/4+(L_fx)^TRf. \tag{3} \]

Reciprocity cancels the current/phase work exactly. Storage values and preparation costs remain law-dependent; (3) transfers no earlier resource or acquisition verdict.

The shared derivative bounds give

\[ J_\lambda=1+\lambda/1458,\quad L_\lambda=1+2\lambda/243,\quad B_\lambda=1+\lambda/9 \tag{4} \]

as global bounds for |j|, |j'|, |j''|. The full lifted field is globally Lipschitz on the fixed finite support, and the prescribed piecewise-smooth input gives one continuous state history through its switches.

Write P=RR^T/9, Q=I-P, x=RU+u and theta=psi+R*Phi+z. Internal helical currents cancel by oddness and periodicity. Same-slot outer currents are constant within a child at z=0. Thus u=z=0 is an exact invariant carrier for both laws and every uniform-child input:

\[ U'=(-L_5U+\gamma S_{\lambda,5}(\Phi))/4+f,\qquad \Phi'=\gamma L_5U/4. \tag{5} \]

The full stiffness on this carrier is

\[ K_\lambda(\Phi)=j_\lambda'(2\pi/9)(I_5\otimes L_9) +L_5^{j_\lambda'(\Phi)}\otimes I_9. \tag{6} \]

It commutes with P and Q, so the collective/hidden tangent blocks still decouple. This is not a transverse-stability theorem. At internal gaps 2*pi/9 the deformation's first relevant derivatives vanish, but at the outer 2*pi/5 gaps they generally do not. The complete C9 x C5 tangent is therefore not matched by the old C9 target construction.

The original command removal remains exact: Y=U-z_cmd, Psi=Phi-H, with H'=gamma*L5*z_cmd/4, gives

\[ Y'=-L_5Y/4+\gamma S_{\lambda,5}(\Psi+H)/4,\qquad \Psi'=\gamma L_5Y/4. \tag{7} \]

This reuses the waveform and coordinates, not the sine-specific forecast gain.

docs.title: 2. Own-law hidden transport, identity and growth
docs.text:
Let g=1/3000, a0=31/10^9, b0=601/10^10, and s=2*g*T. The hidden form row contains Q S_lambda(psi+R*Phi+z), which vanishes at zero z and has Euclidean Lipschitz bound 8*L_lambda. The graph Laplacian has norm at most 8. Conservatively bound both coupling rows with 8*L_lambda and reuse the shared integral majorant:

\[ A_\lambda=\frac{a_0+sL_\lambda b_0}{1-(sL_\lambda)^2},\qquad Z_\lambda=\frac{b_0+sL_\lambda a_0}{1-(sL_\lambda)^2}. \tag{8} \]

All denominators are positive at the fixed corner. These are full nonlinear hidden bounds under each law, not transported sine-source states.

On an outer edge, the nine hidden gap differences have zero sum. Taylor expansion of the actual current cancels the linear correction and bounds the mean remainder by B_lambda/18 times their squared sum. External Laplacian norm at most 4 then gives a mean-form forcing bound

\[ \rho_\lambda=gB_\lambda Z_\lambda^2/9. \]

Compare each fine history with its own carrier starting at its actual initial means. Heat contraction and ||D S_lambda,5||2<=4*L_lambda give, with k=gT,

\[ E_U\le T\rho_\lambda+L_\lambda k E_\Phi,\quad E_\Phi\le k E_U,\qquad \boxed{E_\lambda=\frac{T\rho_\lambda}{1-L_\lambda k^2}}. \tag{9} \]

Consequently E_U<=E_lambda and E_Phi<=k*E_lambda on the entire horizon. Unknown means are proof initializations, not new observation inputs.

For finite identity, remove the form command at the fine level. With ||S_lambda||infinity<=4*J_lambda, the same exact integrated phase identity now yields

\[ M_\lambda=X+gJ_\lambda T,\qquad F_\lambda=2gX+2g^2J_\lambda T. \tag{10} \]

Substitute F_lambda for the drift in the original internal-positive, internal-acute, outer-acute and collar margins, with zeta=1e-6, A=7/5, epsilon=1/10. Their explicit expressions are

\[ 2\pi/9-2\zeta-2F_\lambda,\quad \pi/2-2\pi/9-2\zeta-2F_\lambda,\quad \pi/2-A-\epsilon-2\zeta-2F_\lambda,\quad \pi/2-2\zeta-4F_\lambda. \tag{11} \]

All are strictly positive. This preserves each initially admitted marked winding and collar throughout this word and tail, without proving that the alternative acquired the state from the earlier preparation.

For numerical reuse, the carrier Jacobian's quadratic form has cross term gamma*a^T(L5-K_lambda)*b/4 and negative form-diffusion term. Since ||L5-K_lambda||2<=4*(1+L_lambda), its identity-metric logarithmic norm is at most gamma*(1+L_lambda)/2. For every lambda in [0,1], using pi>3,

\[ \mu_2\le\frac{244}{745767}<\frac1{3000}. \tag{12} \]

The existing growth allowance is thus re-admitted. Actual-law Taylor derivatives, Picard tubes and source corrections must still be rebuilt; the frozen sine integrator consumer is unchanged.

At lambda=1, the exact bounds above imply

Quantity Rationally controlled bound Hidden form A_1 <3.17e-8 Hidden phase Z_1 <6.05e-8 Own-carrier mean-form error E_1 <2.42e-18 Fine endogenous phase drift F_1 <1.023e-5 Outer acute margin >0.06997

If two fine histories under the two laws admit the same raw record, their own carriers satisfy, at every sample simultaneously,

\[ \|U_0(t_j)-U_1(t_j)\|_\infty\le \delta=2\eta+E_0+E_1. \tag{13} \]

This is a necessary joint condition. It proves neither record separation nor realizability of independently chosen sample boxes.

docs.title: 3. Exact local ambiguity after removing the unknown phase
docs.text:
The original finite observer uses three command levels to recover two quadratures. First consider its ideal frozen initial current references, before temporal and reading errors. For the interface c -> c+1, let a be its initial gap. The receiver's reference current at command level q is K-j(a-q), where the unmodulated neighbor contribution K cancels from the two contrasts. For epsilon=1/10, the normalized contrasts are

\[ C_j(a)=\frac{j(a+\epsilon)-j(a-\epsilon)}{2\sin\epsilon},\qquad S_j(a)=\frac{2j(a)-j(a+\epsilon)-j(a-\epsilon)}{2(1-\cos\epsilon)}. \tag{14} \]

These have exactly the orientation and scaling of the original O,V statistics. In particular (C_0(a),S_0(a))=(cos a,sin a). For the alternative,

\[ \begin{aligned} C_1(a)&=\cos a+ \frac{\sin(.9)\cos9a-\tfrac12\sin(1.8)\cos18a}{2187\sin(.1)},\\ S_1(a)&=\sin a+ \frac{(1-\cos(.9))\sin9a-\tfrac12(1-\cos(1.8))\sin18a} {2187(1-\cos(.1))}. \end{aligned} \tag{15} \]

There exist distinct gaps a and b, both of magnitude less than 1/2, with (C_1(a),S_1(a))=(cos b,sin b). Thus even exact ideal local quadratures need not distinguish these two laws when the phase is unknown.

To prove this, put F(a)=C_1(a)^2+S_1(a)^2-1, r=cos(.9)>0 and c9=sin(.9)/(2187*sin(.1))>0. At zero, S_1=0 and C_1=1+c9*(1-r)>1, so F(0)>0. At a=pi/9,

\[ S_1(a)=\sin a,\quad C_1(a)=\cos a-q,\quad q=c9(1+r)=\frac{\sin(.9)+\tfrac12\sin(1.8)}{2187\sin(.1)}. \]

The elementary bound sin(.1)>599/6000 gives 0<q<9000/(2187*599)<1/100. Hence F(pi/9)=q*(q-2*cos(pi/9))<0. Continuity supplies a_* in (0,pi/9) with F zero, without locating a root numerically.

For every a in that interval, C_1(a)>=cos(pi/9)-q>1-8/81-1/100>8/9, using pi<4. There is therefore a unique principal b with the matching unit phasor. Since cos(1/2)<=337/384<8/9, it satisfies |b|<1/2. Also a_*<pi/9<1/2, inside the original collective gap prior.

The matching phases are distinct. If b=a_*, both perturbations in (15) would vanish. Writing x=cos(9*a_*), the sine correction, with sin(9*a_*)>0, forces x=1/[2*(1+r)] in (0,1/2). But then the cosine correction is c9*(x+r-2*r*x^2)>0, a contradiction.

Each gap embeds in an admitted primitive initial state: choose U=u=z=0 and Phi=(0,d,3*d/4,d/2,d/4) for d equal to a_* or b. Its outer gaps are (d,-d/4,-d/4,-d/4,-d/4), with winding zero; the internal helical cycles retain winding one. The nuisance neighbor current cancels in the selected contrasts. The other interfaces and the absolute current baseline need not agree. Finite plateau increments also contain endogenous drift and integration error. This witness therefore excludes the local compressed statistic as a uniform selector; it is not a common complete record, an acquisition witness or a physical observation.

docs.title: Retaining the local current baseline does not suffice either
docs.text:
The neighboring gap can realize the needed baseline, rather than treating K as a free unphysical offset. At a circle collision write kappa=S_1(a_*)-j_1(a_*)=sin b-j_1(a_*). Put s9=(1-cos(.9))/(2187*(1-cos(.1))). The bounds 1-cos(.9)<81/200 and 1-cos(.1)>1199/240000 give s9<1/26. Since 1+cos(.9)<2, (15) and (4) imply

\[ |\kappa|<3/26+1/1458<1/8,\qquad j_1(1/2)\ge\sin(1/2)-1/1458>1/8. \]

Continuity and oddness supply d in (-1/2,1/2) with j_1(d)=-kappa. Choose the initial outer gap cycles

\[ (b,0,-b/3,-b/3,-b/3),\qquad (a_*,d,-(a_*+d)/3,-(a_*+d)/3,-(a_*+d)/3) \]

for sine and the alternative, respectively. They sum to zero and obey the original gap bounds. Set all forms and hidden deviations to zero. Receiver 1 now has K_0=0 and K_1=-kappa. Equal O,V contrasts force the three edge-current differences to equal their baseline difference j_1(a_*)-sin b=-kappa. Therefore the complete receiver currents K_0-j_0(b-q) and K_1-j_1(a_*-q) agree at every q=0,+epsilon,-epsilon. This strengthens the local obstruction within admitted primitive states; other receivers and the continuous dynamics remain unconstrained by it.

docs.title: 4. The complete formal harmonic information remains distinct
docs.text:
For a cross-law carrier difference u=Y_0-Y_1, freeze each initial edge phasor in (7) while retaining the prescribed command h=B^T H. The formal heat response has five initial form coefficients and sine/cosine pairs on five edges for each frequency n in {1,9,18}: 35 real coefficients. Its equation is

\[ V'=-L_5V/4-B\sum_{n\in\{1,9,18\}} [b_{s,n}\odot\cos(nh)+b_{c,n}\odot\sin(nh)]. \tag{16} \]

The fundamental pair is the difference of the two initial phasors scaled by gamma/4. The ninth pair is the alternative's phasor scaled by -gamma/(4*2187), and the eighteenth by gamma/(8*2187). Their circle norms and shared underlying phase are constraints; treating these formal coefficients as free only enlarges the comparison.

The formal coefficient map is injective if the entire continuous V history is supplied. Indeed, a zero history forces zero initial form and zero divergence of the edge currents. On C5 all currents then equal one circulation. During a marked-child ramp three unactuated edges have constant command, so this circulation is constant. Each of its two actuated edges has a trigonometric polynomial of frequencies 1,9,18 equal to that constant on an open interval of command values. Independence of those sine/cosine functions and the constant forces all six coefficients on that edge to vanish. Every edge is actuated somewhere in the word, proving injectivity.

This theorem neither supplies continuous observations in the actual protocol nor proves rank or conditioning of its 150-row sampled matrix. It concerns the formal linear response, before nonlinear endogenous phase drift.

For the actual pair, let B_n=max(||b_s,n||infinity,||b_c,n||infinity) and D=4*g*X+2*g^2*J_1*T, bounding each endogenous edge-phase drift. Here the carrier has only two incident outer currents, so ||S_lambda,5||infinity<=2*J_1 and ||Y||infinity<=X+g*J_1*T/2. Integrating its live phase row gives coordinate drift at most 2*g*X+g^2*J_1*T, hence the stated edge bound D. This is separate from the fine-state drift F_lambda in (10). The fundamental difference remainder and the two one-law higher-harmonic remainders give

\[ u'=-L_5u/4-B\sum_n[b_{s,n}\cos(nh)+b_{c,n}\sin(nh)]+r,\quad \sum_c r_c=0, \] \[ \|r(v)\|_\infty\le 3D(B_1+9B_9+18B_{18})+g^2\int_0^v\|u(s)\|_\infty\,ds. \tag{17} \]

For the fundamental term, use the original complex-phasor difference identity and |d_0-d_1|<=2*g*integral||u||infinity. For a higher harmonic, |exp(i*n*d)-1|<=n*|d|; its scaled phasor norm is at most sqrt(2)*B_n. Two incident edges and 2*sqrt(2)<3 yield (17). The zero-sum heat integral bound of 6 therefore implies

\[ \sup\|u-V\|_\infty\le 18D(B_1+9B_9+18B_{18})+6g^2T\sup\|u\|_\infty. \tag{18} \]

The old 15-column gain does not certify (16)-(18). A finite joint test must retain these harmonic blocks, their constitutive phase constraints, the two own-law source errors and every sample correlation. The finite-rank and relaxation results below distinguish information in the formal design from what this global remainder can certify about the nonlinear pair.

docs.title: 5. Exact rank of the actual finite formal design
docs.text: The 150-by-35 sampled map of (16), at the original thirty observation times, has column rank 35. This is an exact statement about the formal linear heat response. It supplies neither a quantitative inverse bound nor a noisy or nonlinear law discriminator. No sampled matrix is evaluated in the proof.

docs.title: The recorded plateaus and first ramps determine scalar moments
docs.text:
Suppose a coefficient vector produces zero V at every recorded time. The first reading gives V(0)=0, eliminating all five initial-form coefficients. Write A=L5/4. On each plateau its forcing is a constant vector f, and the two recorded endpoints satisfy

\[ 0=e^{-hA}0+\left(\int_0^h e^{-sA}\,ds\right)f. \tag{19} \]

The integral matrix is positive definite: its eigenvalues are h for the constant mode and (1-exp(-h*mu))/mu>0 for every positive eigenvalue mu of A. Thus f is zero on each of the fifteen plateaus. At command zero, this means that all baseline edge currents sum_n b_s,n,e equal one circulation, because the kernel of the oriented C5 incidence matrix is the constant edge vector.

For an edge e define its command-dependent increments

\[ E_e(q)=\sum_n b_{s,n,e}(\cos(nq)-1),\qquad O_e(q)=\sum_n b_{c,n,e}\sin(nq),\qquad n\in\{1,9,18\}. \tag{20} \]

When a child is marked, only its two incident edges have nonzero commands, with opposite signs. The other three edges retain the baseline circulation. Zero divergence at the two nonzero plateau levels therefore gives E_e(epsilon)+O_e(epsilon)=E_e(epsilon)-O_e(epsilon)=0 on each incident edge. Every edge is incident to a marked child, so

\[ E_e(\epsilon)=O_e(\epsilon)=0\quad\hbox{for every edge e}. \tag{21} \]

Every child's first ramp starts at the recorded endpoint of its zero-level plateau and ends at the recorded beginning of its positive-level plateau. Both V values are zero. This includes child 4; its first ramp ends before the last reading. With local ramp time t in [0,1], put q(t)=epsilon*t^2*(3-2*t). After subtracting the zero-divergence baseline, the forcing is supported on the two incident incidence columns.

The two distinct nonzero eigenvalues of A are

\[ \mu_1=(5-\sqrt5)/8,\qquad \mu_2=(5+\sqrt5)/8. \tag{22} \]

Each has a real two-dimensional Fourier eigenspace. The projections of two adjacent incidence columns onto either eigenspace are linearly independent: in complex Fourier coordinates their ratio is exp(plus_or_minus 2*pi*i*k/5), for k equal to 1 or 2, which is not real. The zero ramp endpoint consequently forces each incident edge's weighted forcing integral to vanish separately for each mu.

Each edge is probed once from each endpoint in two child blocks. Their first ramps use the same q(t) and reverse that edge's command sign. Adding and subtracting the two integral equations therefore gives

\[ \int_0^1 e^{-\mu_j(1-t)}E_e(q(t))\,dt=0,\qquad \int_0^1 e^{-\mu_j(1-t)}O_e(q(t))\,dt=0, \quad j=1,2. \tag{23} \]

Only recorded endpoints and the known linear response between them were used. Neither derivatives nor extra within-ramp observations are supplied. Equations (21)-(23) reduce coefficient recovery on every edge to two three-by-three homogeneous systems. Their common matrix construction is

\[ M_f=\begin{pmatrix} f_1(\epsilon)&f_9(\epsilon)&f_{18}(\epsilon)\\ \int_0^1 w_1(t)f_1(q(t))dt&\int_0^1 w_1(t)f_9(q(t))dt& \int_0^1 w_1(t)f_{18}(q(t))dt\\ \int_0^1 w_2(t)f_1(q(t))dt&\int_0^1 w_2(t)f_9(q(t))dt& \int_0^1 w_2(t)f_{18}(q(t))dt \end{pmatrix},\qquad w_j(t)=e^{-\mu_j(1-t)}, \tag{24} \]

using either f_n(q)=sin(nq) or f_n(q)=1-cos(nq). The latter differs from (20) only by a common minus sign. Both matrices are nonsingular, as the following argument proves without computing their entries.

docs.title: Strict independence of both trigonometric triples
docs.text:
For |z|<pi, the analytic function h(z)=z*cot(z) has expansion

\[ h(z)=1-\sum_{m\ge1}a_m z^{2m},\qquad a_1=1/3,\qquad (2m+1)a_m=\sum_{k=1}^{m-1}a_k a_{m-k}>0\quad(m\ge2). \tag{25} \]

The recurrence follows directly from z*h'=h-h^2-z^2; the first poles are at plus and minus pi. Thus for every positive d,

\[ H_d(\sigma)=\sqrt\sigma\cot(d\sqrt\sigma) =\frac1d-\sum_{m\ge1}a_m d^{2m-1}\sigma^m \quad\Longrightarrow\quad H_d'<0,\quad H_d''<0 \tag{26} \]

on 0<d*sqrt(sigma)<pi, where the derivatives are with respect to sigma. Termwise differentiation is valid inside that convergence domain.

First take f_n(q)=sin(nq), with 0<q<=epsilon=1/10 and n equal to 1, 9 or 18. Every f_n is positive because 18*epsilon=1.8<pi. For sigma=n^2, its logarithmic derivative and normalized second derivative are f_n'/f_n=H_q(sigma) and f_n''/f_n=-sigma. The first two-column Wronskian is negative by the strict decrease in (26). Factoring the positive functions from the three-column Wronskian leaves

\[ \det\begin{pmatrix} 1&1&1\\ H_q(1)&H_q(81)&H_q(324)\\ -1&-81&-324 \end{pmatrix}\ne0, \tag{27} \]

because strict concavity makes the three points on the graph of H_q noncollinear.

For g_n(q)=1-cos(nq)=2*sin(nq/2)^2, every g_n is also positive and

\[ g_n'/g_n=H_{q/2}(\sigma)=H,\qquad g_n''/g_n=(H^2-\sigma)/2. \tag{28} \]

Again its first two-column Wronskian is negative. Invert the strictly decreasing map in (26) locally as sigma=sigma(H). Throughout the interval between its three values,

\[ \sigma''(H)=-H_{q/2}''(\sigma)/(H_{q/2}'(\sigma))^3<0, \qquad \frac{d^2}{dH^2}(H^2-\sigma(H))>0. \tag{29} \]

The three-column Wronskian is therefore nonzero by strict convexity of the last row in (28) as a function of the middle row.

These Wronskian conditions imply that each triple has a nonzero evaluation determinant at any three distinct q values in (0,epsilon]. One direct Rolle argument is to divide a proposed three-zero linear combination by its positive first function. Put r=f_9/f_1 and s=f_18/f_1; r' never vanishes, and (s'/r')' is the three-column Wronskian divided by f_1^3*(r')^2, hence never zero. Applying Rolle twice forces the combination to be trivial. The evaluation determinant has a constant nonzero sign on the connected domain of ordered triples.

docs.title: The two weighted moments retain that independence
docs.text:
Expanding (24) and interchanging its finite integrals gives exactly

\[ \det M_f=\int_{0<t<u<1} [w_1(t)w_2(u)-w_1(u)w_2(t)] \det\begin{pmatrix} f_1(\epsilon)&f_9(\epsilon)&f_{18}(\epsilon)\\ f_1(q(t))&f_9(q(t))&f_{18}(q(t))\\ f_1(q(u))&f_9(q(u))&f_{18}(q(u)) \end{pmatrix}\,dt\,du. \tag{30} \]

The weight bracket is strictly positive: mu2>mu1 and w2(t)/w1(t)=exp(-(mu2-mu1)*(1-t)) strictly increases. Also q(t) strictly increases on (0,1), so 0<q(t)<q(u)<epsilon on the integration domain. The evaluation determinant consequently has a constant nonzero sign. Thus (30) is nonzero for both bases. Equations (21)-(24) force all thirty edge coefficients to vanish. Together with the five initial forms this proves the claimed rank 35.

This finite theorem strengthens the continuous formal injectivity result; it does not make the local collision in section 3 into a complete-history collision or transfer formal linear identifiability to nonlinear dynamics. No determinant lower bound, inverse norm, finite-error separation or numerical budget verdict follows from strict nonvanishing alone.

docs.title: 6. Why the unconstrained global bootstrap cannot close the question
docs.text: This obstruction concerns a specified proof method, not the actual laws' record sets. It needs no coefficient-matrix evaluation, proposed inverse, nonlinear history or choice of an unknown initial state.

docs.title: One formal direction with a uniformly small response
docs.text:
Set the five initial-form coefficients and all b_c coefficients to zero. Repeat the same b_s coefficients on every edge:

\[ (a_1,a_9,a_{18})=(1,-323/19683,20/19683),\qquad b=(1,323/19683,20/19683). \tag{31} \]

The vector b lists their three block infinity norms. Direct rational algebra gives

\[ \sum_n a_n n^2=\sum_n a_n n^4=0,\qquad \sum_n|a_n|n^6=1+8721+34560=43282. \tag{32} \]

The command-zero current is a constant circulation and has zero divergence. At any instant only one child c is marked, with scalar command q satisfying |q|<=epsilon. The two changed edge commands are opposite; cosine is even. Consequently the complete formal forcing is exactly

\[ F(q)(e_{c-1}-e_{c+1}),\qquad F(q)=\sum_n a_n(\cos(nq)-1). \tag{33} \]

Taylor's theorem through degree five, with (32), gives for the entire command range

\[ |F(q)|\le f_*:=\frac{43282\epsilon^6}{720}. \tag{34} \]

The dipole in (33) has zero sum and Euclidean norm sqrt(2). The smallest nonzero eigenvalue of L5/4 is greater than 1/3. Variation of constants, including every change of marked child, therefore yields

\[ \sup_v\|V(v)\|_\infty \le\sqrt2 f_*\int_0^\infty e^{-s/3}\,ds <\frac92 f_* =:m=\frac{21641}{80000000}. \tag{35} \]

This bounds the complete formal history and hence every actual sample. It does not assert a zero response; it is consistent with rank 35. The retained elementary remainder coefficient is strictly larger:

\[ a=18D>m,\qquad D=4gX+2g^2J_1T. \tag{36} \]

All quantities in (31)-(36) are fixed rational bounds. In particular, m=0.0002705125, whereas 18D>0.000304.

docs.title: Both scalar and block recovery inherit the obstruction
docs.text:
Let M denote the exact sampled formal map. Any proposed recovery K of all thirty harmonic coefficients has row norm k and harmonic residual block norm e for J=[0 I]-KM. Applying that identity to (31), whose initial forms vanish and harmonic infinity norm is one, gives

\[ 1\le e+k\|Mp\|_\infty\le e+km. \tag{37} \]

A scalar bootstrap with remainder coefficient at least a would require 1-e-k*a>0. Equations (36)-(37) exclude this for every K, even one obtained from an exact inverse. Taking upper residual bounds cannot improve it.

Keeping separate harmonic block norms also does not rescue this particular global envelope. Write B_n=max(||b_s,n||infinity,||b_c,n||infinity) for an arbitrary actual pair, and U_*=sup||u||infinity. Its last preceding sample is at most two units earlier, including the final unobserved ramp and tail. The static force and (17) then give

\[ cU_*\le\delta+6\sum_n(1+nD)B_n,\qquad c=1-2g^2T>0. \] \[ R_*:=\sup\|u-V\|_\infty\le\sum_n A_nB_n+B_0\delta, \quad A_n=18nD+\frac{36g^2T(1+nD)}c,\quad B_0=\frac{6g^2T}c. \tag{38} \]

Here delta=2*eta+E_0+E_1 retains both own-law source errors. For arbitrary block recovery matrices K_n, let k_n be their row norms and E_nm the nonnegative row-norm bounds of their residuals on harmonic block m. Their proposed componentwise bootstrap has feedback matrix

\[ H=E+kA^T. \tag{39} \]

Using the formal witness instead of an actual pair in the exact recovery identities gives b<=E*b+k*m. But A^T*b>=A_1>18D>m, so

\[ Hb\ge b,\qquad b>0. \tag{40} \]

Thus I-H cannot have a nonnegative inverse: otherwise multiplying (I-H)b<=0 by that inverse would imply b<=0. This excludes the positive block bootstrap for every choice of dual weights and their certified residual bounds. Positive diagonal changes of coefficient units preserve the same obstruction. A more accurate matrix or a different inverse cannot repair (38)-(39); a sharper correlated remainder or constrained argument is a different method and is not excluded.

docs.title: The obstruction is not an admitted cross-law history
docs.text:
An actual alternative has ninth and eighteenth phasor radii r9=gamma/(4*2187) and r18=r9/2. In complex notation z_n=b_c,n+i*b_s,n, its coefficients on each edge satisfy

\[ z_9=-r_9e^{9ia},\qquad z_{18}=(r_9/2)e^{18ia} =z_9^2/(2r_9). \tag{41} \]

Both are tied to the same phase a that occurs in the fundamental cross-law difference. On each edge the witness has phasor modulus ratio 323/20, instead of 2, so even rescaling it cannot produce these actual coefficients. This uses its zero b_c coordinates; general block infinity norms need not have the same ratio as phasor moduli. It also supplies no pair of initial cycle phases or nonlinear histories. Its role is to prove a limitation introduced by allowing independent formal coefficients and independent norm remainders. Finite formal rank, exact local ambiguity and this obstruction do not by themselves decide the joint question. The constrained theorem resolves it under the same word, noise and horizon using additional joint phase restrictions and stronger contrasts.

docs.title: 7. Constrained contrasts from recorded long-ramp endpoints
docs.text: The following construction avoids dividing a form difference by the short plateau duration. It cancels the formal initial-form response, constant forcing and fundamental harmonic before using the alternative's shared phase. It supplies a conditional finite separation criterion. The complete certificate in sections 9-11 instead uses the middle ramp as well, while retaining this construction as a control and reusable conditional result.

docs.title: An explicit functional of the unchanged readings
docs.text:
Orient each edge as e -> e+1, with incidence column b_e=e_(e+1)-e_e. Choose edge 1 -> 2 and its two marked-child blocks, c=1,2. Let h_p=1e-5 and s_c=3*c*(1+h_p). The first and third ramps have recorded endpoints

\[ a_{c,1}=s_c+h_p,\quad b_{c,1}=a_{c,1}+1,\qquad a_{c,3}=s_c+2+3h_p,\quad b_{c,3}=a_{c,3}+1. \tag{42} \]

The third endpoint is the next child's zero-level plateau beginning. All eight endpoints in this construction belong to the existing thirty times. Use command-removed form Y, or a difference u of two carrier forms, for which the common command already cancels.

For either positive eigenvalue mu in (22), let P_mu be its orthogonal spectral projector. Put Q_c,mu=[P_mu*b_(c-1),P_mu*b_c] and let R_c,mu,e be the row of its left inverse selecting edge e=1. Define

\[ \mathcal T_{c,\mu,e}(w)=-R_{c,\mu,e} [w(b_{c,1})-e^{-\mu}w(a_{c,1}) -w(b_{c,3})+e^{-\mu}w(a_{c,3})]. \tag{43} \]

The row already lies in the range of P_mu. Its norm is explicit: the Gram matrix of Q has diagonal d=8*mu/5 and off-diagonal d*(1-2*mu), with d*(1-(1-2*mu)^2)=1/2. Hence ||R_c,mu,e||2=sqrt(2) for both modes. Coordinate errors at most delta in the four inputs to (43) change its value by at most 2*sqrt(10)*(1+exp(-mu))*delta.

For the frozen formal equation (16), the first-minus-third ramp difference cancels every constant edge current. Only the marked child's two incident edges remain, so (43) extracts their separate weighted current contrasts. The command on edge 1 is positive when child 2 is marked and negative when child 1 is marked. Therefore define its two parity moments by

\[ \mathcal E_\mu(w)=-\frac{e^{\mu/2}}8 [\mathcal T_{2,\mu,1}(w)+\mathcal T_{1,\mu,1}(w)],\qquad \mathcal O_\mu(w)=\frac{e^{\mu/2}}8 [\mathcal T_{2,\mu,1}(w)-\mathcal T_{1,\mu,1}(w)]. \tag{44} \]

Each has observation error at most sqrt(10)*cosh(mu/2)*delta<4*delta. This bound uses the recorded forms themselves, without estimating a plateau derivative or an unknown initial form.

docs.title: Positive kernels after removing the fundamental
docs.text:
Write the centered ramp coordinate as r=t-1/2 and put xi(r)=epsilon*(3*r/2-2*r^3). On 0<=r<=1/2, xi increases from zero to epsilon/2. The first and third commands are epsilon/2+xi(r) and -epsilon/2+xi(r). Their trigonometric difference gives the exact kernels

\[ C_{\mu,n}=\int_0^{1/2}\sinh(\mu r)\sin(n\xi(r))\,dr,\qquad D_{\mu,n}=\int_0^{1/2}\cosh(\mu r)\cos(n\xi(r))\,dr. \tag{45} \]

For the formal history, (44) equals respectively sum_n b_s,n,e*sin(n*epsilon/2)*C_mu,n and sum_n b_c,n,e*sin(n*epsilon/2)*D_mu,n. Set

\[ \alpha_E=C_{\mu_1,1}/C_{\mu_2,1},\qquad \alpha_O=D_{\mu_1,1}/D_{\mu_2,1},\qquad 0<\alpha_E,\alpha_O<1, \] \[ \mathcal E=\mathcal E_{\mu_1}-\alpha_E\mathcal E_{\mu_2},\qquad \mathcal O=\mathcal O_{\mu_1}-\alpha_O\mathcal O_{\mu_2}. \tag{46} \]

The fundamental coefficients vanish exactly. The remaining coefficients are

\[ K_{E,n}=\sin(n\epsilon/2)(C_{\mu_1,n}-\alpha_E C_{\mu_2,n}),\qquad K_{O,n}=\sin(n\epsilon/2)(D_{\mu_1,n}-\alpha_O D_{\mu_2,n}), \quad n=9,18. \tag{47} \]

All four are strictly positive. Indeed, each numerator in (47) is an ordered double integral of a weight determinant times a function determinant. Both weight ratios sinh(mu2*r)/sinh(mu1*r) and cosh(mu2*r)/cosh(mu1*r) strictly increase for positive r. Both function ratios sin(n*x)/sin(x) and cos(n*x)/cos(x) strictly decrease for 0<x<=epsilon/2, where 18*x<=.9<pi/2. Consequently both determinants have the same positive orientation. This proves strict positivity without evaluating an integral.

The same positive representation bounds their frequency ratios. For 0<x<y<=epsilon/2, the sine determinant sin(n*x)*sin(y)-sin(x)*sin(n*y) is (n^2-1)*sin(y) times the positive Dirichlet Green integral of sin(n*s) on [0,y], with operator -d^2/ds^2-1. Since sin(18*s)=2*sin(9*s)*cos(9*s), its n=9 to n=18 ratio is at most 40/(323*cos(.45)). For the cosine determinant use

\[ \left(\frac{\cos(ns)}{\cos s}\right)' =-\frac{n^2-1}{\cos^2s}\int_0^s\cos(nt)\cos t\,dt. \tag{48} \]

The n=9 to n=18 ratio is at most 80/(323*cos(.9)). Multiplying in each case by sin(.45)/sin(.9)=1/(2*cos(.45)) gives

\[ 0<\rho_E:=K_{E,9}/K_{E,18} \le\frac{20}{323\cos^2(.45)}<\frac1{12},\qquad 0<\rho_O:=K_{O,9}/K_{O,18} \le\frac{40}{323\cos(.9)\cos(.45)}<\frac14. \tag{49} \]

The strict rational comparisons already follow from cos(.45)>719/800 and cos(.9)>119/200. No sampled coefficient matrix or kernel magnitude is computed here.

docs.title: A finite certificate with explicit remaining obligations
docs.text:
Let theta=9*a for the alternative's edge gap at one common reference time, and let r9=gamma/(4*2187). Retaining its actual coefficients (41) in the frozen contrasts gives

\[ \frac{2\mathcal E_{\rm fr}}{K_{E,18}} =r_9(\sin2\theta-2\rho_E\sin\theta),\qquad \frac{2\mathcal O_{\rm fr}}{K_{O,18}} =r_9(\cos2\theta-2\rho_O\cos\theta). \tag{50} \]

The Euclidean norm of this pair is at least r9*(1-2*max(rho_E,rho_O))>r9/2. This conclusion uses the shared phase and fixed radii, not independent bounds on two harmonic blocks.

For two histories sharing a noisy record, (13) bounds every input to (43) by delta. Their two final observation allowances are

\[ N_E=\sqrt{10}[\cosh(\mu_1/2)+\alpha_E\cosh(\mu_2/2)]\delta<8\delta, \quad N_O=\sqrt{10}[\cosh(\mu_1/2)+\alpha_O\cosh(\mu_2/2)]\delta<8\delta. \tag{51} \]

Suppose uniform, own-law arguments additionally establish |mathcal E(u)-mathcal E_fr|<=epsilon_E and |mathcal O(u)-mathcal O_fr|<=epsilon_O. A sufficient separation criterion for the actual record sets is then

\[ \sqrt{\left(\frac{2(N_E+\epsilon_E)}{K_{E,18}}\right)^2+ \left(\frac{2(N_O+\epsilon_O)}{K_{O,18}}\right)^2} <\frac{r_9}{2}. \tag{52} \]

This criterion alone supplies no passing verdict: it requires certified kernel magnitudes and actual-history departures from one shared reference phase. Reconstructing phase increments accurately does not make those increments zero: even known nonzero endogenous drift changes the frozen kernels. It must be incorporated into the contrasts or bounded, together with the uncertainty of the reconstruction and both laws' source errors. Local resetting must also retain transport between the two child blocks. The same-mode extension in sections 9-11 meets those obligations with stronger kernels and a common late-time reference. No trajectory, fit or reserved response is evaluated by either construction.

docs.title: 8. The same form readings constrain historical phase transport
docs.text:
The exact carrier phase row depends on the observed form history, not on an independently chosen phase velocity. This allows the initial phases to remain unknown while bounding their increments more tightly. This section uses only the historical interval 0<=v<=t_last=14+15/100000; it does not reconstruct the unobserved return ramp or the tail to time 16.

Put A=L5/4 and w_lambda=gamma*S_lambda,5/4 in (7). Then

\[ Y'=-AY+w_\lambda,\qquad \Psi'=\gamma AY,\qquad \|Y\|_\infty\le M_\lambda:=X+gJ_\lambda T/2. \tag{53} \]

At each reading the commanded form offset vanishes, so the raw fine-mean reading y differs from this law's carrier Y by at most epsilon_lambda=eta+E_lambda in each coordinate. Both compared laws use the same raw record if one is jointly compatible; this is a conditional argument for any such record, without evaluating one.

docs.title: A bridge that retains arbitrary heat relaxation
docs.text:
On each interval of length h between successive readings, define

\[ Q(s)=\int_0^s e^{-rA}\,dr,\qquad V_h(s)=Q(s)Q(h)^{-1},\qquad \widehat Y(s)=(I-V_h(s))y_i+V_h(s)y_{i+1}. \tag{54} \]

The matrix Q(h) is positive definite, including its constant-mode eigenvalue h. The eigenvalues of V_h(s) lie in [0,1]. This bridge exactly reproduces every solution with constant forcing, including arbitrary initial heat relaxation. It is an observation-based interpolation, not a new supplied evolution law. It need not reproduce the actual current. Joining the intervals yields one continuous form interpolant. Define the common edge-phase increment reference

\[ \widehat d(v)=\gamma B^TA\int_0^v\widehat Y(s)\,ds. \tag{55} \]

The initial circular edge phase is not reconstructed. For each law its actual carrier increment d_lambda=B^T(Psi_lambda(v)-Psi_lambda(0)) is compared with this same reference.

With exact carrier endpoints, e=Y-hat Y obeys e''+Ae'=w_lambda', with zero values at both cell endpoints. For a spectral value 0<=mu<=1, let q_mu(s)=(1-exp(-mu*s))/mu, using s when mu is zero. The absolute scalar Dirichlet Green kernel is

\[ G_\mu(t,s)= \frac{q_\mu(\min(t,s))q_\mu(h-\max(t,s))}{q_\mu(h)} e^{-\mu\max(t-s,0)}. \]

For h at most one, q_mu(r)<=r and mu*h/(1-exp(-mu*h))<=1/(1-exp(-1))<8/5, with the continuous value one at mu zero. Consequently

\[ 0\le G_\mu(t,s)\le\frac85G_0(t,s),\qquad \int_0^hG_0(t,s)\,dt=\frac{s(h-s)}2. \tag{56} \]

The C5 geometry gives ||B||2<=2, ||A||2<=1, and each row of B^T A has squared Euclidean norm 5/4. The actual current derivative therefore satisfies, when the marked command level is q,

\[ \|w_\lambda'\|_2\le \frac{\gamma L_\lambda}{2} (\sqrt2|q'|+2\gamma\sqrt5 M_\lambda). \tag{57} \]

The bound uses B^T H', which has exactly two nonzero entries of opposite sign, and the complete phase row in (53). It is an own-law estimate, not an observed derivative.

docs.title: Separate reading, command and endogenous errors
docs.text:
For a cubic ramp of amplitude a and duration h, q'=6*a*s*(h-s)/h^3, so integrating its absolute value against the weight in (56) gives |a|*h^2/10. Combining (56)-(57) with the edge-row norm gives at most sqrt(10)*gamma^2*L_lambda*|a|*h^2/25 in phase increment error. Use sqrt(10)<19/6. The endogenous contribution is at most gamma^3*L_lambda*M_lambda*h^3/3.

Endpoint perturbations have Euclidean norm at most sqrt(5)*epsilon_lambda. Both spectral bridge weights have norm at most one. After applying gamma*B^T A and integrating, their contribution is at most 5*g*epsilon_lambda*h per cell. No derivative estimate divides these errors by the short plateau duration.

Thus a uniform historical bound is

\[ \|d_\lambda(v)-\widehat d(v)\|_\infty\le R_\lambda, \] \[ R_\lambda= 5g\epsilon_\lambda t_{last} +\frac{19}{150}g^2L_\lambda\sum_{\rm cells}|a|h^2 +\frac{g^3L_\lambda M_\lambda}{3}\sum_{\rm cells}h^3. \tag{58} \]

There are exactly fourteen observed ramps and fifteen short plateaus:

\[ \sum|a|h^2=19/10,\qquad \sum h^3=14+15\cdot10^{-15}. \tag{59} \]

The last return ramp has no right endpoint reading and is excluded. Summing only completed cells and the full nonnegative allowance for the current cell gives a valid bound also at interior times. In particular, for both endpoint laws (and uniformly through 0<=lambda<=1),

\[ R_\lambda<2.8\cdot10^{-8}. \tag{60} \]

The report retains the three error contributions and cumulative cell allowances separately. Unlike the old absolute drift D, the interpolation error has no term of order g*X; initial form enters only the much smaller endogenous term of order g^3*X. This uses additional information already present in the same record, without tightening its noise allowance.

This is a carrier edge-phase increment bound. A statement about the fine collective mean-phase increment must additionally retain twice the own-law mean-phase source error; individual hidden constituent phases remain unobserved. Neither version identifies the initial phase, its winding or the law. In particular, the nonzero common reference d_hat must be retained when using the contrasts in section 7: a small reconstruction error does not justify replacing the reconstructed motion by zero. The complete theorem in section 11 instead bounds actual motion about one late-time reference directly and retains relative transport from the same two form histories. This bridge remains a separate conditional reconstruction bound.

docs.title: 9. The observed middle ramp supplies a second command shape
docs.text:
The middle ramp also has recorded endpoints in blocks c=1,2 and c=2,3. For the continuation below select edge 2 and blocks c=2,3, whose complete ramps lie between local times 6.00007 and 12.00012. No final unobserved return ramp or additional reading is used. Translation of the child labels preserves the C5 projector and frozen-kernel algebra in section 7.

Write F_c,i(w)=w(b_c,i)-exp(-mu)w(a_c,i). Retain the first-minus-third functional T in (43), and define

\[ {\cal Q}_{c,\mu,e}(w)=-R_{c,\mu,e} [F_{c,1}(w)+F_{c,3}(w)-2F_{c,2}(w)]. \]

All three intervals have unit duration. The coefficients sum to zero, so constant forcing cancels. At centered ramp coordinate r, their commands are respectively epsilon/2+xi(r), -2xi(r), and -epsilon/2+xi(r). Combining the two marked-child orientations gives

\[ W_{E,\mu}=e^{\mu/2}({\cal Q}_{3,\mu,2}+{\cal Q}_{2,\mu,2})/8,\qquad W_{O,\mu}=e^{\mu/2}({\cal Q}_{3,\mu,2}-{\cal Q}_{2,\mu,2})/8. \]

Their frozen harmonic coefficients are respectively

\[ L_{D,n}=\cos(n\epsilon/2)D_{\mu,n}-D_{\mu,2n},\qquad L_{C,n}=\cos(n\epsilon/2)C_{\mu,n}+C_{\mu,2n}. \]

Thus E_mu-alpha_E W_E,mu and O_mu-alpha_O W_O,mu cancel the fundamental at a single mode when alpha_E and alpha_O take the ratios declared below. The signed high-harmonic coefficients still obey one common phase-circle relation. The new functional retains existing samples; it changes the analysis of their information, not the preparation or waveform. Actual phase motion and cross-law transport still require their own bounds.

docs.title: Prospective scalar-moment evaluation
docs.text:
This is one analytical assessment of the scalar kernels, not a record, trajectory, fit, law selection or complete nonlinear separation. Commit this declaration, the helper and its exclusive driver before evaluation. Preserve the attempt and exact interval report; do not retry or change numerical budgets after observing it. The following choices are fixed:

Item Declaration Kernel set Both exact C5 modes mu=(5-sqrt(5))/8,(5+sqrt(5))/8; harmonics 1,2,9,18,36; twenty scalar C,D integrals total Arithmetic Shared outward rational dyadic128 intervals; exact rational polynomial coefficients and antiderivatives; shared interval square root and trigonometry Fixed series Twenty terms in each hyperbolic and trigonometric series, giving odd degrees through 39 and even degrees through 38 Kernel budget Every complete C,D enclosure must have radius at most 1e-28; zero-crossing elimination denominators give unavailable arithmetic Derived quantities Original across-mode contrasts and the three-ramp contrast at each mode, retaining signed coefficients and the full observation-noise multipliers Selected continuation Mode 2 is selected before evaluation; mode 1 and the old construction are retained controls, not candidates in a result-dependent search No additional evaluation No response, reconstructed phase history, nonlinear fit, sampled matrix, frozen source producer or physical observation is evaluated

Since xi(r)=r*(3/20-r^2/5), define exact rational polynomial moments

\[ J_{m,k}=\sum_{j=0}^{k}\binom{k}{j}(3/20)^{k-j}(-1/5)^j \frac{(1/2)^{m+k+2j+1}}{m+k+2j+1}. \]

Integrate the finite products by substituting J into

\[ C^{[20]}_{\mu,n}=\sum_{p,q=0}^{19} \frac{\mu^{2p+1}(-1)^qn^{2q+1}J_{2p+1,2q+1}} {(2p+1)!(2q+1)!}, \] \[ D^{[20]}_{\mu,n}=\sum_{p,q=0}^{19} \frac{\mu^{2p}(-1)^qn^{2q}J_{2p,2q}}{(2p)!(2q)!}. \]

Combine each rational coefficient, including the exact J, before interval multiplication by a power of mu. The finite sums and every subsequent operation retain outward arithmetic rounding. On this domain abs(mu*r)<=1/2 and abs(n*xi)<=9/5. Uniform omitted-series bounds are

\[ E_{sh}=\frac{(1/2)^{41}}{41!}\frac1{1-1/(4\cdot42\cdot43)},\quad E_{ch}=\frac{(1/2)^{40}}{40!}\frac1{1-1/(4\cdot41\cdot42)}, \] \[ E_s=(9/5)^{41}/41!,\qquad E_c=(9/5)^{40}/40!. \]

The hyperbolic tails use the decreasing positive-term ratio; the trigonometric bounds use Taylor's theorem with derivatives bounded by one. Every hyperbolic partial sum is below two and the actual sine/cosine has absolute value at most one. Consequently append the symmetric integrated product tails (E_sh+2*E_s)/2 and (E_ch+2*E_c)/2 to C and D respectively. These are product errors, not derivative or trajectory error estimates.

For a single mode put s_n=sin(n/20), c_n=cos(n/20) and

\[ \alpha_E=\frac{s_1C_{\mu,1}}{c_1D_{\mu,1}-D_{\mu,2}},\qquad \alpha_O=\frac{s_1D_{\mu,1}}{c_1C_{\mu,1}+C_{\mu,2}}. \]

The signed remaining coefficients are

\[ K_{E,n}=s_nC_{\mu,n}-\alpha_E(c_nD_{\mu,n}-D_{\mu,2n}),\qquad K_{O,n}=s_nD_{\mu,n}-\alpha_O(c_nC_{\mu,n}+C_{\mu,2n}), \quad n=9,18. \]

Their raw common-record uncertainty allowances are respectively sqrt(10)*cosh(mu/2)*(1+2*abs(alpha_E))*delta and the same expression with alpha_O. The factor two retains the doubled absolute ramp weights in the first+third-2*second functional. Evaluate cosh with the same fixed positive series and its admitted tail. docs.title: 10. Necessary joint phase bounds from a shared complete record
docs.text:
These are necessary conditions for two admitted histories sharing one noisy record. No record is constructed or evaluated. Write r=gamma/4, r9=r/2187, g=1/3000, h=1e-5 and retain the own-law source errors in delta=2*eta+E0+E1<2.01e-14. Since pi<22/7, gamma>1/3300. For each endpoint law the command-removed carrier obeys

\[ Y'=-AY+rS_\lambda,\qquad \Psi'=\gamma AY, \qquad A=L_5/4. \]

The infinity norm of A is one and that of each row of B^T A is two. Thus on the entire horizon,

\[ \|Y\|_\infty\le M_\lambda=X+gJ_\lambda T/2<.013, \quad \|B^T(\Psi(v)-\Psi(0))\|_\infty \le D_\lambda=4gX+2g^2J_\lambda T<17\cdot10^{-6}. \]

On a plateau the command is constant. Therefore

\[ \|Y'\|_\infty\le M_\lambda+gJ_\lambda/2, \qquad \|Y''\|_\infty\le M_\lambda+gJ_\lambda/2+g^2L_\lambda M_\lambda =:M_{2,\lambda}<3/200. \]

docs.title: The same winding follows before a detailed phase inverse
docs.text:
For one plateau with endpoint forms P,Q, use the original diffusion-corrected combination, now vector-valued,

\[ D(P,Q)=Q-P+\frac h2 A(P+Q). \]

For the difference of two carriers its receiver coordinate has absolute value at most (2+h/2)*delta: the coefficients are -1+h/4, 1+h/4 and four neighboring coefficients -h/8. Integrating the form equation gives

\[ D(Y(a),Y(a+h)) =r\int_a^{a+h}S_\lambda(v)\,dv+\mathcal R_\lambda, \qquad |\mathcal R_{\lambda,i}|\le M_{2,\lambda}h^3/12. \]

The error is the trapezoid error of the diffusion integral A int Y, not a trapezoid approximation of the current. Dividing by h gives an h^2/12 term per law, hence (M20+M21)*h^2/12, bounded by (3/200)*h^2/6, in the cross-law force estimate. No observed derivative or unknown intermediate state is inserted.

At any of the three levels q in a marked-child block, each of the two receiver edge gaps departs from its initial gap plus the stipulated command by at most D_lambda. Its current consequently departs by at most 2*L_lambda*D_lambda. A shared record therefore requires the two ideal initial receiver currents at that q to differ by at most

\[ \kappa=\frac{4}{\gamma_{lo}} \left\{\frac{(2+h/2)\delta}{h} +\frac{M_{2,0}+M_{2,1}}{12}h^2 +\frac g2(L_0D_0+L_1D_1)\right\}<\frac1{7500}, \qquad \gamma_{lo}=1/3300. \]

Taking the second three-level contrast cancels the adjacent baseline. If a0,a1 are the two initial gaps of that edge, its ideal sine quadratures obey

\[ |S_0(a_0)-S_1(a_1)| \le\frac{2\kappa}{1-\cos(.1)}<3/50. \]

The alternative quadrature deformation has magnitude less than 3/26: write s9=(1-cos(.9))/(2187*(1-cos(.1)))<1/26; the eighteenth coefficient is (1+cos(.9))*s9<2*s9. Thus

\[ |\sin a_0-\sin a_1|<3/50+3/26. \]

On the admitted interval [-7/5,7/5], cosine is larger than 1/6. For example its alternating Taylor lower bound 1-A^2/2+A^4/24-A^6/720 at A=7/5 is larger than 1/6. The mean-value theorem gives |a0-a1|<342/325. Both initial gap cycles sum to 2*pi*w, so

\[ 2\pi|w_0-w_1|\le\sum_e|a_{0,e}-a_{1,e}| <342/65<6<2\pi. \]

Hence the two histories must have the same initial outer winding. This is a necessary compatibility statement, not a reconstruction of it.

docs.title: Initial current balance bounds the fundamental phasor
docs.text:
At the first plateau there is no preceding command. Replace D_lambda in the preceding force estimate by the tighter direct increment bound 2*g*M_lambda*h. Then, with

\[ b_{s,e}=r(\sin a_{0,e}-\sin a_{1,e}),\qquad f_e=b_{s,e}-r_9\{\sin(9a_{1,e})-\tfrac12\sin(18a_{1,e})\}, \]

the necessary initial force estimate is

\[ \|Bf\|_\infty\le\zeta:={ (2+h/2)\delta\over h} +{M_{2,0}+M_{2,1}\over12}h^2 +g^2h(L_0M_0+L_1M_1)<4.1\cdot10^{-9}. \]

Adjacent f values differ by at most zeta. The five-cycle has diameter two, so max f-min f<=2*zeta. The deformation's range is at most 3*r9. Equal winding and monotonicity of sine on the initial gap domain imply min b_s<=0<=max b_s. Consequently

\[ \|b_s\|_\infty\le2\zeta+3r_9<\frac{13}{4}r_9. \]

The last strict inequality follows using r9>1/(3300*4*2187). For m=(a0+a1)/2, the fundamental phasor identity gives

\[ r|e^{ia_0}-e^{ia_1}|= {|b_s|\over\cos m}<6|b_s|<\frac{39}{2}r_9. \]

At any later common reference time in the admitted horizon, removing the common command, the change in this phasor difference is at most r*(D0+D1). Hence its magnitude P_ref satisfies

\[ \boxed{P_{ref}<\{39/2+2187\cdot34\cdot10^{-6}\}r_9<20r_9.} \]

This bound uses all sampled blocks to establish equal winding and the initial plateau to constrain the fundamental. The 9th and 18th harmonic radii retain their exact common-phase relation. No nonlinear record separation verdict follows from these bounds alone.
