docs.title: Endpoint functional and ideal coefficients
docs.text:
Put \(h=10^{-5}\), \(s_c=3c(1+h)\) and \(\mu=\mu_2=(5+\sqrt5)/8\). Use all three unit ramps in each of children \(c=2,3\); every endpoint is an existing reading. With the spectral left-inverse row \(R_c\) selecting edge \(2\to3\), define

\[ F_{c,i}(w)=w(b_{c,i})-e^{-\mu}w(a_{c,i}),\qquad \mathcal T_c=-R_c(F_{c,1}-F_{c,3}),\qquad \mathcal Q_c=-R_c(F_{c,1}+F_{c,3}-2F_{c,2}). \]

The two parity pairs are

\[ \mathcal E_0=-\frac{e^{\mu/2}}8(\mathcal T_3+\mathcal T_2),\qquad \mathcal O_0=\frac{e^{\mu/2}}8(\mathcal T_3-\mathcal T_2), \] \[ W_E=\frac{e^{\mu/2}}8(\mathcal Q_3+\mathcal Q_2),\qquad W_O=\frac{e^{\mu/2}}8(\mathcal Q_3-\mathcal Q_2). \]

The target command is positive in child 3 and negative in child 2. The centered ramp profiles are \(\epsilon/2+\xi,-2\xi,-\epsilon/2+\xi\). Suppressing the fixed mode index, the frozen harmonic coefficients of \(\mathcal E_0,\mathcal O_0\) are \(\sin(n\epsilon/2)C_n,\sin(n\epsilon/2)D_n\), while those of \(W_E,W_O\) are

\[ L_{E,n}=\cos(n\epsilon/2)D_n-D_{2n},\qquad L_{O,n}=\cos(n\epsilon/2)C_n+C_{2n}. \]

The ratios declared in section 9 therefore cancel the fundamental in

\[ \mathcal E=\mathcal E_0-\alpha_EW_E,\qquad \mathcal O=\mathcal O_0-\alpha_OW_O, \] \[ K_{E,n}=\sin(n\epsilon/2)C_n-\alpha_EL_{E,n},\qquad K_{O,n}=\sin(n\epsilon/2)D_n-\alpha_OL_{O,n}. \]

Both higher harmonics retain the same alternative-law phase \(\theta=9a_1(s_3)\) on the selected edge. The coefficients are rebuilt from the primitive intervals; their signs and magnitudes are not assumed. With \(\delta=2\eta+E_0+E_1\) from (13), the observation allowances are

\[ N_E=\sqrt{10}\cosh(\mu/2)(1+2|\alpha_E|)\delta,\qquad N_O=\sqrt{10}\cosh(\mu/2)(1+2|\alpha_O|)\delta. \]

docs.title: Uniform actual phase motion on the late blocks
docs.text:
Set \(\mathcal I=[s_2,s_4]\), \(t_*=s_3\) and \(L=3(1+h)=3.00003\). For each edge, let \(a_\lambda(v)=(B^T\Psi_\lambda(v))_e\). Section 10 proves

\[ P(v):=\frac\gamma4\max_e |e^{ia_{0,e}(v)}-e^{ia_{1,e}(v)}|<20r_9, \qquad r_9=\frac\gamma{4\cdot2187}, \]

at every historical time. Equal winding, the first plateau and the acute initial gap prior first bound the initial amplitude; the absolute phase drift bound then preserves this containing bound.

For either law, decompose the command-removed edge-phase increment into homogeneous heat and forced contributions. The row \(Y'=-AY-(\gamma/4)Bj\) gives

\[ d_{\mathrm{heat}}(v)=\gamma B^T(I-e^{-vA})Y(0),\qquad d_{\mathrm{forced}}'(v)=-\gamma^2\int_0^v A_{\mathrm{edge}}^2e^{-(v-s)A_{\mathrm{edge}}}j(s)\,ds. \]

Here \(A_{\mathrm{edge}}=B^TB/4\) is the same C5 generator in edge order; incidence intertwining gives the second identity. Its positive-mode projectors satisfy \(\|P_\mu\|_\infty=(2+2\sqrt5)/5<13/10\), and \(\mu_1+\mu_2=5/4\). Consequently

\[ \int_0^\infty\|A_{\mathrm{edge}}^2e^{-sA_{\mathrm{edge}}}\|_\infty\,ds <\frac{13}{8},\qquad \|d_{\mathrm{forced}}'(v)\|_\infty\le\frac{13}{8}\gamma^2J_1. \]

The exact homogeneous edge-row norms are

\[ \|\operatorname{row}(B^TP_{\mu_1})\|_1 =1+\frac1{\sqrt5}<\frac{29}{20},\qquad \|\operatorname{row}(B^TP_{\mu_2})\|_1 =1+\frac3{\sqrt5}<\frac{47}{20}. \]

Each spectral exponential difference is monotone away from \(t_*\). Thus the larger endpoint sum of these row norms times \(|e^{-\mu t}-e^{-\mu t_*}|\), multiplied by \(\gamma X\), bounds the homogeneous motion throughout \(\mathcal I\). Adding the forced allowance \((13/8)\gamma^2J_1L\) gives

\[ \sup_{v\in\mathcal I} \|d_\lambda(v)-d_\lambda(t_*)\|_\infty \le D_{\mathrm{late}}<10^{-6},\qquad \lambda=0,1. \]

The shared rational exponential owner verifies this without a nonlinear response. An elementary coarse bound uses \(\bar\gamma=1/3200>\gamma\), from \(\pi>3.14\). The left heat row is below \(1.45(0.127-0.044)+2.35(0.005)=0.1321<0.14\); the right is below \(1.45(0.045)+2.35(0.001)=0.0676<0.14\). Hence

\[ D_{\mathrm{late}} <\frac{0.14X}{3200}+\frac{13J_1L}{8\cdot3200^2}<10^{-6}. \]

Both laws retain their actual phase motion about the common reference; no reconstructed increment is set to zero.

docs.title: Joint difference and nonlinear current remainder
docs.text:
Let \(u=Y_0-Y_1\) and \(U=\sup_{\mathcal I}\|u\|_\infty\). The actual fundamental phasor difference is below \(20r_9\), and the additional harmonics total at most \(3r_9/2\) per edge. Each node has two incident edges, so the exact pair forcing has infinity norm below \(43r_9\). Every historical cell has length at most one and two observed endpoints. Heat contraction from its preceding reading yields

\[ U\le\delta+43r_9<44r_9. \]

Since \(\|B^TA\|_\infty=2\), the same pair of histories satisfies

\[ \|[d_0(v)-d_0(t_*)]-[d_1(v)-d_1(t_*)]\|_\infty \le2\gamma LU. \]

Freezing both laws at \(t_*\), the complex-phasor difference identity bounds the fundamental current error by \(20r_9D_{\mathrm{late}}+(\gamma/4)2\gamma LU\) per edge. The two higher-harmonic errors total at most \((9r_9+18r_9/2)D_{\mathrm{late}}=18r_9D_{\mathrm{late}}\). The resulting uniform current remainder is therefore bounded by

\[ \mathcal R :=r_9\bigl(38\cdot10^{-6}+22\bar\gamma^2L\bigr) <46\cdot10^{-6}r_9. \]

This bound retains the correlation between relative phase motion and form differences. It does not use the unconstrained remainder excluded in section 6.

docs.title: Exact contrast operator bounds
docs.text:
At mode two, \(R_cB\) has entries, up to cyclic order and reflection, \((1,0,-1,\varphi,-\varphi)\), where \(\varphi=(1+\sqrt5)/2\). Its row norm is \(3+\sqrt5\). Put \(q_\mu=(1-e^{-\mu})/\mu\). The final ramp weights at each child are, up to the overall and child signs in the odd contrast,

\[ w_E=(1+\alpha_E,-2\alpha_E,\alpha_E-1),\qquad w_O=(1-\alpha_O,2\alpha_O,-1-\alpha_O). \]

Writing \(S_E=\|w_E\|_1\), \(S_O=\|w_O\|_1\), the two child blocks and normalization \(e^{\mu/2}/8\) give

\[ H_E=\frac{e^{\mu/2}q_\mu(3+\sqrt5)}4S_E,\qquad H_O=\frac{e^{\mu/2}q_\mu(3+\sqrt5)}4S_O. \]

These bounds allow signed interval coefficients. The retained inequalities \(0<\alpha_E<1<\alpha_O\) simplify them to \(S_E=2+2\alpha_E\), \(S_O=4\alpha_O\); the consumer instead rebuilds the full absolute-value sums. The inclusive error budgets are

\[ T_E=N_E+H_E\mathcal R,\qquad T_O=N_O+H_O\mathcal R. \]

For nonzero high-harmonic denominators define

\[ m=1-2\max\left\{ \left|\frac{K_{E,9}}{K_{E,18}}\right|, \left|\frac{K_{O,9}}{K_{O,18}}\right|\right\},\qquad e^2=\left(\frac{2T_E}{r_9|K_{E,18}|}\right)^2 +\left(\frac{2T_O}{r_9|K_{O,18}|}\right)^2. \]

The shared phase-circle theorem excludes a common record whenever the outward bounds satisfy \(m_{\mathrm{lower}}>0\) and \(e^2_{\mathrm{upper}}<m_{\mathrm{lower}}^2\). Equality does not certify separation. Both hidden source errors are already included in \(\delta\).

docs.title: Result: the two complete noisy record sets are disjoint
docs.text:
The single final assessment, declared at b9b2e49a8146d6544407eed55a395377d91504c4, passed the strict squared comparison. Its attempt and exact result retain the source, input receipts, primitive moment intervals and rebuilt history/error bounds. Conservative outward summaries are

\[ D_{\mathrm{late}}<8.737\cdot10^{-7},\qquad e^2_{\mathrm{upper}}<(0.337)^2<(0.716)^2<m_{\mathrm{lower}}^2. \]

The decision uses the retained rational squared inequality, not rounded display values. This closes the stated distinction: under the unchanged initial class, complete laws, waveform, clock and noise allowance, no 150-coordinate raw record is compatible with both endpoint laws, even when each law may start from a different admitted state and have its own hidden constituent deviations.

The conclusion concerns these two supplied models and this protocol. It does not identify a law of nature, select a unique member of the wider constitutive family, reconstruct all initial phases, or prove acquisition under the alternative law. No raw record, nonlinear trajectory, physical observation or frozen source producer was evaluated in the assessment.

docs.title: 12. Shared implementation and verification
docs.text:
The detached consumer reuses the canonical potential/current, product geometry, hidden transport, interval/jet arithmetic and waveform. Its conditional phase-circle checker re-admits coefficient and total-error primitives and excludes simultaneous membership in two zero-centered error bands only under the declared shared-phase contrast premises. Unsafe denominators and nonpositive circle margins are unavailable; equality at the squared error threshold does not certify exclusion. The phase-transport bound rebuilds the historical grid, current variation and both own-law source budgets. It consumes no raw record and does not implement an individual phase reconstruction. Neither consumer installs a runtime law or evaluates a trajectory. The shared prescribed-time validator remains the execution owner for any separately declared future numerical test.

The joint phase owner rebuilds the necessary shared-record conditions from the same source and plateau premises. The complete certificate re-admits primitive moments and rebuilds the late grid, decay, contrast and strict exclusion. Admission and field controls check invalid domains, the fine/carrier projection, both clock rows, derivative bounds, source denominators and identity/growth margins. Finite-rank controls check the actual endpoint schedule, reversed edge probes and C5 spectral independence used in section 5. Relaxation controls check moment cancellation, actual forcing orientation, the dipole heat bound, own-law remainder constants and the obstruction's constitutive exclusion. Constrained-contrast controls check shared-phase synthetic cases, strict margins and primitive rejection. Phase-transport controls check the actual historical domain, exact C5 norms, independent scalar Green and constant-forcing cases, and separate reading/source/command budgets. Joint phase controls check the trapezoid, cycle and phasor arguments. Complete theorem controls independently check C5 projector/dual norms, exponential bounds, three-ramp parities and primitive admission. The evidence controls rebuild the strict inequality and source associations without producer replay; input controls separate fixed-byte admission from scientific inference. These controls exercise proof premises; the proofs establish their stated mathematical conclusions. No root search, fit, sampled coefficient assessment or frozen producer is run.

docs.title: Result: preparation admits what the loose observation class cannot
docs.text:
Under declaration 6c16052d, the existing preparation admits five zero variance estimates with joint error below 8.72e-23, well within 1e-17. Carrying a ten-coordinate reference from that origin through formation and observation gives a uniform mean-form error below 1.6e-24 and lifted-phase error below 1.2e-25. docs.title: 1. Retaining separate recovery information
docs.text:
The joint-resource proof retains own-law entry into the full relative ball and the independent energy trap before recovery. At that entry, the actual class-one state has ||x||^2+||theta-Theta1||^2<r^2, r=1/12. This is the complete entry condition, not a consequence of phase trapping alone. For eta=gamma^2, the shared pi bounds imply 9e-8<eta<1e-7. With g0=1/5, Lambda=2 and epsilon_L=1/20, the unchanged class-one curvature satisfies

\[ c_1=\cos(2\pi/9+\sqrt2/12)>2/3. \tag{1} \]

For example, pi<22/7, sqrt(2)<99/70 put its argument below 2057/2520, and cos(y)>=1-y^2/2 gives the strict lower bound. The modified-energy coefficients from the existing proof then obey

\[ a_->1/400,\quad a_+<3/50,\quad \kappa>2\cdot10^{-9}, \qquad V_0<3/1000. \tag{2} \]

The last inequality follows directly from the pointwise modified-energy upper bound and the admitted entry ball. Even bounding each of its two norms separately by r gives V0<[(3/2)*1e-7+3/10]/144<3/1000. No archived returned norm or energy estimate enters this calculation.

The quarter-factor dwell is still D=8e10; both rows inherit the original half-time comparison. Thus kappa*D/2>80, and the unchanged upper bound 2^-80 on decay gives

\[ \begin{aligned} \|x_{handoff}\|^2 &<\frac{2\cdot10^6}{3}\,2^{-80}<10^{-18},\\ \|\theta_{handoff}-\Theta_1\|^2 &<\frac{12}{5}\,2^{-80}<4\cdot10^{-24}. \end{aligned} \tag{3} \]

Use the conservative radii q_x=1e-9, q_theta=2e-12. They describe the same uninterrupted reached state, not a smaller supplied preparation box. The sixth constituent in the historical resource comparison is not attached in the present five-child word; all five hosts must individually satisfy the original preparation hypotheses.

docs.title: 2. One reference from attachment through observation
docs.text:
Let tau=0 denote outer attachment, after the isolated recoveries. Each child retains its separate zero form and target-phase residual means up to this event. The supplied translations therefore give exactly

\[ U_c(0)=M_c,\quad \Phi_c(0)=0,\qquad M_c=4092(c-2)\quad\hbox{or}\quad M_c=0. \tag{4} \]

The branch is part of the supplied preparation. No hidden residual is set to zero. Define a mathematical carrier reference by these same means, unforced evolution for 200 units, and then the unchanged finite input word:

\[ \overline U'=(-L_5\overline U+\gamma S_5(\overline\Phi))/4+f, \qquad \overline\Phi'=\gamma L_5\overline U/4. \tag{5} \]

Here f is zero during formation and is exactly the original prescribed waveform during observation. The reference continues across the boundary; its post-formation means are not reset to the actual means or reconstructed from later readings.

For full differences from this carrier, five independent recovered children give initial Euclidean radii r0<sqrt(5)*q_x<3e-9 and z0<sqrt(5)*q_theta<6e-12. The global sine Lipschitz bound and the outer heat identity hold under the identical input: its contribution cancels from the difference rows. They allow the original nonacute outer transit. For H=216, 2g^2 H<1/2 and exp(1/2)<2, so the shared heat-error kernel gives

\[ Z=2(z_0+g r_0)=1.4\cdot10^{-11},\qquad R=r_0+24gZ, \quad \|\theta-\overline\theta\|\le Z,\quad \|x-\overline x\|\le R. \tag{6} \]

The radii on the right use the conservative bounds r0=3e-9, z0=6e-12. The form convolution uses the same global zero-mean difference and spectral gap lambda2(L_f)>1/3. This is a conditional nonlinear transport theorem; the kernel neither assesses a source nor evaluates an exponential trajectory.

Orthogonal removal of child means is contractive. Consequently the actual hidden phase z also has norm at most Z, without a factor-two Euclidean inflation. In particular, at the observation start

\[ \sum_e m_e^0=\frac19\|D_o z\|^2 \le\frac49 Z^2<8.72\cdot10^{-23}<10^{-17}. \tag{7} \]

Choosing all five estimates zero therefore satisfies the compressed initialization target on every source member covered by the preparation. Their actual values need not be zero. The old collision at a=2^-26 lies outside this sharpened prepared enclosure, although it remains within the old larger inference class.

docs.title: 3. Mean prediction with carried initialization
docs.text:
The full form radius R is unnecessarily loose for predicting means. The initial collective difference in (4) is exactly zero. The actual projected row differs from (5) by the quadratic sine remainder, with ||R_mean||2<=rho=gZ^2/9 throughout the combined history. Heat contraction and the live phase row therefore give, with k=gH=9/125<1,

\[ E_U\le H\rho+k E_\Phi,\qquad E_\Phi\le k E_U, \qquad E_U\le\frac{H\rho}{1-k^2}<1.6\cdot10^{-24},\qquad E_\Phi\le\frac{kH\rho}{1-k^2}<1.2\cdot10^{-25}. \tag{8} \]

The bound is uniform on 0<=tau<=200+15.00015<216, not merely a fitted endpoint estimate. It includes uncertainty in all admitted fine preparation directions. It meets the declaration's 1.5e-20 intrinsic target without five measured statistics or separately known means at tau=200. No extra gain is asserted from comparing the carrier with itself using the same priors; the tighter prediction follows from retaining stronger source information.

The actual formation and complete input word retain their original identity proofs; formation is allowed to acquire outer winding. The small observation phase difference also transfers the existing strict mean-gap margin to the reference. This does not reconstruct fine-node identities from five phases. The actual external power remains 9(L5 U)^T f; the predicted work differs by at most 36 E_U integral ||f||1. Absolute and positive parts refer to the total external power, not separate fine-node channels. Preparation and attachment work, hidden loss and fine storage retain their original owners.

Equation (8) is an exact-solution comparison. A numerical approximation adds its own propagated residual; an empirical forecast also needs an independently justified preparation, clock, input and observation bridge. Neither budget is included in the small intrinsic error above.

docs.title: 4. Why the noisy records alone do not supply the variances
docs.text:
For the observation-only route retain the common coarse bounds a0=31/10^9, b0=601/10^10 and the original larger inference class. The two declared states have equal initial collective coordinates and norm certificates. The first lies on the exact carrier. The second has the proved variance difference

\[ \|m^{(1)}-m^{(0)}\|_1=4a^2/9>2\cdot10^{-17}, \qquad a=2^{-26}. \tag{9} \]

Both solutions exist under the same complete finite input word and retain the original class's identities. The shared carrier bound, freshly rebuilt from these coarse primitives on T=16, gives

\[ \sup_\tau\|U^{(1)}(\tau)-U^{(0)}(\tau)\|_2 \le E_0<2.3\cdot10^{-18}<\eta_{raw}=10^{-14}. \tag{10} \]

For every one of the 150 samples, define a symbolic record equal to the first solution's true mean. Its noise is zero for that solution; for the second solution its noise is their coordinate difference, uniformly smaller than eta_raw. These two error vectors are admitted simultaneously with their respective complete histories. Thus the joint sets of possible records overlap. This constructs existence without evaluating or inventing an acquired response and does not rely on marginal interval compatibility.

Any single-valued estimator of m receives the same record and even the same gifted exact initial means in both cases. The triangle inequality and (9) exclude error at most 1e-17 for both. The original noise permits arbitrary correlations, so treating samples as independent noise or averaging them does not repair this worst-case obstruction. Additional sample times in the same bounded history retain (10). Noiseless data, different observations, different inputs or a more restrictive preparation require their own proof.

This excludes a uniform observation-only inverse on the containing class, not initialization of the actual prepared image. It also leaves the existing winding inverse intact: both states here have the same winding.

docs.title: 5. Consolidation and remaining execution boundary
docs.text:
Fine states with the same initial means and the coarse hidden bounds are each within E0 of one common carrier history. Their mean-output diameter is therefore at most 2E0, much smaller than the raw reading allowance, even when their variance statistics cannot be identified at the requested precision. This is a finite output cover, not an exact state quotient or a transitive equivalence relation inferred from noisy-record overlap.

The prepared route is stronger: it supplies accurate initialization and prediction from the original history. The observation-only route identifies a genuine information limit for a larger class. Retaining both avoids treating a discarded source bound as a fundamental dynamical obstruction. The conditional compression theorem and its general counterexamples remain valid; the five-statistic representation is useful only when a selected source and prediction actually require that information.

The static controls reuse the modified-energy, heat-error and exact-arithmetic owners. They check the recovery constants, anisotropic transport, mean initialization, joint error inequalities and record-overlap obstruction without source replay, trajectories or frozen-response evaluation. The separate computable forecast uses this initialization with shared validated integration and preserves source, numerical and observation errors separately. The sole queue owns the next observation-to-prediction question.

docs.title: Complete-law compatibility of three organized C9 constituents
docs.text:
The pairwise sine charts do not generally combine into one chart for a network. For the three prescribed oriented contacts, an unchanged normalized reciprocal sine law requires both equal contact amplitudes and a vanishing phase sum around the triangle. These conditions are necessary and sufficient in the positive nodewise affine form charts, constant phase-origin shifts and common clock specified below. Among the actual co-oriented nonnegative contacts, only the all-zero-offset control satisfies them.

The complete inherited dynamics still closes exactly on six registered coordinates for every admitted contact. Retaining the contact amplitudes and phase registrations gives that law without fitting or additional evolving variables. The obstruction concerns a more restrictive scalar network representation; it does not invalidate the supplied fine law, its storage balance or its conditional organized identity.

The pairwise owner supplies the interface family and its conditional sine-profile selection. This note fixes sine and tests whether those pair descriptions coexist on one cycle. The NFR ontology permits retained constituent and boundary information. It does not require the restrictive chart whose obstruction is proved here.

docs.title: Supplied support, complete law and retained identity
docs.text:
There are three marked C9 constituents, with nodes \((r,\ell)\), \(r=0,1,2\), \(\ell=0,\ldots,8\), ordered as \(9r+\ell\). Each has its unit-weight internal cycle. Put \(\alpha=2\pi/9\) and orient the constituent triangle as

\[ \mathcal E=((0,1),(1,2),(2,0)). \tag{1} \]

For each oriented pair \(e=(r,t)\), fix \(s_e\in[0,1]\) and add the undirected contacts

\[ (r,\ell)--(t,\ell),\quad w=1-s_e,\qquad (r,\ell)--(t,\ell+1),\quad w=s_e . \tag{2} \]

Indices are modulo nine. Zero-weight edges at the endpoints are absent; every positive edge acts at both ends with the same weight. Orientation records which constituent port is shifted, not a directed force. Each node has cross conductance two and total weighted degree four. There are 27 internal edges and between 27 and 54 positive contact edges.

The fine state retains signed real form \(x\), primitive circular phase with specified continuous lifts \(\theta\), held unit capacities, the marked support and its three fixed weights. Use the inherited structural clock \(\tau=(1023/1024)t\), a supplied constant \(\gamma>0\), and the actual weighted fine Laplacian \(L_f\). The complete law is

\[ \begin{split} S_{f,i}(\theta)&=\sum_{m\sim i}w_{im}\sin(\theta_m-\theta_i),\\ x'&=\tfrac14[-L_fx+\gamma S_f(\theta)],\\ \theta'&=\tfrac\gamma4 L_fx,\\ H_f&=\tfrac12x^TL_fx+ \sum_{\{i,m\}}w_{im}[1-\cos(\theta_m-\theta_i)]. \end{split}\tag{3} \]

Primes denote \(\tau\)-derivatives. In original time both rows acquire the same factor \(1023/1024\). The form row specifies pressure in the unit-capacity nodal equation; it does not reconstruct pressure from an observed derivative. The common degree factor is neither a derived capacity nor an inverse mass. Structural units and any laboratory clock conversion remain those of the parameter foundation.

This is a detached supplied weighted reciprocal law. In particular, its weighted phase current differs from the native pressure rule's unweighted unique-neighbor phase channel. No operator word, support selector or native runtime is installed by (3). Odd exchange, symmetric weights and the supplied reciprocal row give

\[ H_f'=-\tfrac14\|L_fx\|_2^2,\qquad (\mathbf1^Tx)'=(\mathbf1^T\theta)'=0. \tag{4} \]

These identities concern continuous flow with no additional input.

The candidate registered organized family is

\[ \mathcal M:\qquad x_{r,\ell}=X_r,\qquad \theta_{r,\ell}=\Phi_r+\alpha(\ell-4). \tag{5} \]

Each constituent keeps its winding-one internal geometry. The six coordinates include three signed forms and three lifted phase origins; the constituent labels, marked port embeddings and contact parameters remain part of the law. Independent changes of these phase origins without corresponding changes to the contacts are not symmetries of the fixed network. A common phase shift is a symmetry. A common signed form offset is also a symmetry of this supplied difference-only law.

The winding one's vanishing first phase resultant and registration-losing ninth moment cannot replace \(\Phi_r\) with its marked embedding. Equation (5) is a prescribed invariant family, not an acquired source. Arbitrary fine states outside it still retain their internal coordinates.

docs.title: Exact six-coordinate dynamics and full storage
docs.text:
Let \(B\) be the three-by-three incidence matrix with a positive entry at an edge's tail and a negative entry at its head, in order (1):

\[ B=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&-1\\-1&1&0\\0&-1&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad L=BB^T=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1&-1\\-1&2&-1\\-1&-1&2\end{pmatrix}. \tag{6} \]

Define \(\Delta=-B^T\Phi\), so \(\Delta_e=\Phi_t-\Phi_r\), and

\[ \begin{split} m_e&=1-s_e+s_e e^{i\alpha}=\rho_e e^{i\phi_e},\\ J_e(\Delta_e)&=\operatorname{Im}(m_e e^{i\Delta_e}) =\rho_e\sin(\Delta_e+\phi_e),\\ U_e(\Delta_e)&=1-\operatorname{Re}(m_e e^{i\Delta_e}) =1-\rho_e\cos(\Delta_e+\phi_e). \end{split}\tag{7} \]

The real part of \(m_e\) is positive. Thus its continuous argument is unambiguously chosen in \([0,\alpha]\), and

\[ \rho_e=\sqrt{1-2s_e(1-s_e)(1-\cos\alpha)}>0. \tag{8} \]

For a node at the tail of \(e\), the weighted cross current equals \(J_e\); at its head it equals \(-J_e\). Internal currents cancel pairwise. Form diffusion is constant within each constituent and equals \((LX)_r\). Consequently the exact restriction is

\[ \boxed{ X'=\tfrac14[-LX+\gamma BJ(\Delta)],\qquad \Phi'=\tfrac\gamma4 LX .} \tag{9} \]

Both fine rows are tangent to (5). The fine vector field is globally Lipschitz in its lifted coordinates, so uniqueness proves invariance. This is exact nonlinear closure on (5), with fixed boundary coefficients; it makes no off-family approximation or transverse-attraction claim.

The internal potential baseline is \(B_0=27(1-\cos\alpha)\). Counting nine fine copies of every collective edge gives

\[ \begin{split} H_f|_{\mathcal M} &=B_0+9\left[\tfrac12X^TLX+\sum_{e\in\mathcal E}U_e(\Delta_e)\right],\\ H_f'|_{\mathcal M}&=-\tfrac94\|LX\|_2^2 . \end{split}\tag{10} \]

Indeed the gradients of the bracket are \(LX\) and \(-BJ\); the reciprocal cross terms cancel exactly. Its potential remains nonnegative because each \(U_e\) is the actual convex combination of two fine sine potentials. The constants \(B_0\) and \(1-\rho_e\) are not removed from the support-work account.

docs.title: Necessary and sufficient simultaneous chart conditions
docs.text:
The comparison target is the same unweighted three-edge triangle, with the normalized complete reciprocal sine law

\[ \frac{dZ}{d\sigma}=-LZ+\Gamma B\sin(-B^T\Psi),\qquad \frac{d\Psi}{d\sigma}=\Gamma LZ, \qquad \Gamma>0. \tag{11} \]

Sine acts componentwise. The comparison uses every state on (5), not only an equilibrium, one trajectory or finitely many sampled responses. It does not allow edge-dependent diffusion, an independently adjustable phase-row support, nodewise clocks, state-dependent charts or an added forcing law. Those would be different comparison classes.

Allow any fixed positive nodewise affine form chart, constant phase origin shifts and one positive constant common clock:

\[ X=AZ+b,\quad A=\operatorname{diag}(a_0,a_1,a_2),\ a_r>0, \qquad\Psi=\Phi+\beta,\qquad\sigma=c\tau,\ c>0. \tag{12} \]

All chart constants may depend on the supplied contact weights, but not on state or measured response. We retain the transformations of the marked ports, inputs and observations below.

Theorem. A chart (12) turns both rows (9) into (11) if and only if

\[ \rho_{01}=\rho_{12}=\rho_{20}=\rho>0,\qquad \Theta:=\phi_{01}+\phi_{12}+\phi_{20}=0\pmod{2\pi}. \tag{13} \]

Every such chart has

\[ \begin{gathered} c=\tfrac14,\qquad a_0=a_1=a_2=\sqrt\rho,\qquad b=b_*\mathbf1,\qquad \Gamma=\gamma\sqrt\rho,\\ \beta_t-\beta_r=\phi_{rt}\pmod{2\pi}\quad(e=(r,t)). \end{gathered}\tag{14} \]

The common form offset \(b_*\) and common phase origin are arbitrary symmetries, not fit parameters that remove the compatibility conditions.

To prove necessity, compare the terms linear in \(Z\) in the form row. The transformed diffusion matrix is \((4c)^{-1}A^{-1}LA\). Its diagonal entries must equal those of \(L\); since they are two, \(c=1/4\). The off-diagonal entries then force \(a_t/a_r=1\) on every edge. Hence \(A=aI\). The phase row independently requires \(Lb=0\) and \(\Gamma=\gamma a\). Connectedness gives \(b=b_*\mathbf1\).

The remaining form-row equality is

\[ B\operatorname{Im}\left[ \left(m_e e^{-i(\beta_t-\beta_r)} -a^2\right)e^{i(\Psi_t-\Psi_r)}\right]_{e\in\mathcal E} =0\quad\text{for all }\Psi. \tag{15} \]

The three oriented edge characters on the node-phase torus are distinct up to sign. In a given node row the two incident nonconstant Fourier characters are also distinct. Uniqueness of their Fourier coefficients therefore implies, for each edge separately,

\[ m_e e^{-i(\beta_t-\beta_r)}=a^2. \tag{16} \]

This step uses the full network vector field: merely assuming individual edge equality would miss the need to exclude cancellation of net nodal currents. The identity \(B\mathbf1=0\) permits constant circulating edge currents, but the nonconstant characters in (15) cannot produce such an unobserved circulation for every independent node phase.

Taking magnitudes gives \(\rho_e=a^2\); summing the argument differences around the triangle gives \(\Theta=0\) modulo \(2\pi\). Conversely, when (13) holds, set \(\beta_0=0\), \(\beta_1=\phi_{01}\), \(\beta_2=\phi_{01}+\phi_{12}\). The closing edge then satisfies (16) as well. Equations (14) transform both rows directly to (11), proving sufficiency.

This theorem classifies the declared affine/phase/clock maps. It is not a theorem ruling out every nonlinear state conjugacy, observation equivalence or model with additional boundary variables.

docs.title: The co-oriented family and the two fixed controls
docs.text:
For the actual contacts (2), \(0\le\phi_e\le\alpha\), with \(\phi_e=0\) if and only if \(s_e=0\). Therefore

\[ 0\le\Theta\le3\alpha=2\pi/3<2\pi. \tag{17} \]

Vanishing modulo \(2\pi\) is possible only when every \(s_e=0\). Then every \(\rho_e=1\), and the complete target law (11) follows with \(\Gamma=\gamma\) and \(\sigma=\tau/4\). All other contacts in this specified co-oriented cube fail at least the cycle condition. Changing an interface orientation changes the supplied support and must be treated as a different model, not used to erase this result.

For the equal-weight control \(s=(1/2,1/2,1/2)\),

\[ \rho_e=\cos(\alpha/2),\qquad \phi_e=\alpha/2,\qquad\Theta=3\alpha/2=\pi/3. \tag{18} \]

All pairwise form and reciprocal scales agree, but their phase-origin charts cannot coexist around the cycle. This isolates the phase obstruction independently of amplitude mismatch.

For the unequal control \(s=(1/4,1/2,3/4)\), the identity \(m(1-s)=e^{i\alpha}\overline{m(s)}\) yields \(\phi(1/4)+\phi(3/4)=\alpha\), so again \(\Theta=\pi/3\). Its magnitudes satisfy

\[ \rho_{01}^2=\rho_{20}^2 =1-\tfrac38(1-\cos\alpha) >1-\tfrac12(1-\cos\alpha)=\rho_{12}^2. \tag{19} \]

Thus this fixed control also fails the common positive form/reciprocal scale condition. Choosing a different form unit for each pair would assign incompatible values to a constituent shared by two pairs; the nodewise argument leading to (14) makes that failure explicit.

Failure of (13) does not imply absence of an equilibrium. At equal \(s_e=s\), take \(X=X_*\mathbf1\), \(\Phi=\Phi_*\mathbf1\). Every edge current is \(s\sin\alpha\), so \(BJ=0\) and both rows vanish. The same cancellation holds at every fine node in (3), making this an exact fine equilibrium. For \(s>0\) the structural edge-current terms form a nonzero cycle with zero net nodal current. This algebraic statement assigns no transported physical quantity. The static control makes no source-acquisition or neighborhood-stability assertion. At unequal weights the same aligned state instead has \(X'=\gamma\sin\alpha\,Bs/4\), which is nonzero for (19).

docs.title: A sufficient retained boundary law when the chart fails
docs.text:
For all contacts, fix the same spanning-tree phase chart

\[ \beta_0=0,\qquad\beta_1=\phi_{01},\qquad \beta_2=\phi_{01}+\phi_{12},\qquad\Psi=\Phi+\beta. \tag{20} \]

Use \(Z=X\), \(\sigma=\tau/4\), and retain the transformed contact phases

\[ \chi_{01}=0,\quad\chi_{12}=0,\quad\chi_{20}=\Theta \pmod{2\pi}. \tag{21} \]

The complete law becomes

\[ \frac{dZ}{d\sigma} =-LZ+\gamma B[\rho_e\sin(\Psi_t-\Psi_r+\chi_e)]_e, \qquad \frac{d\Psi}{d\sigma}=\gamma LZ. \tag{22} \]

It retains exactly the amplitudes and the closing-edge phase that the unmodified scalar-node law (11) cannot absorb. All quantities are determined by the supplied interfaces. No new evolving coordinate, memory approximation, controller or hidden force is added on (5).

A different spanning tree redistributes the residual phases among edges. A constant change of node phase origins changes each edge phase by a node difference, whose sum around the cycle is zero. The product \(\prod_e m_e/\rho_e=e^{i\Theta}\) is therefore unchanged by this coordinate change. This is a property of the marked contact law. It is not evidence of a physical gauge field, a charge or the separate auxiliary gauge construction.

The original fine storage in this chart is

\[ H_f=B_0+9\left[\tfrac12Z^TLZ+ \sum_e\{1-\rho_e\cos(\Psi_t-\Psi_r+\chi_e)\}\right], \qquad \frac{dH_f}{d\sigma}=-9\|LZ\|_2^2. \tag{23} \]

Each potential term splits into \((1-\rho_e)+ \rho_e[1-\cos(\Psi_t-\Psi_r+\chi_e)]\). If \(\Theta\ne0\) modulo \(2\pi\), all three second terms cannot vanish simultaneously: their effective angles sum to \(\Theta\). Thus the sum of isolated pair minima is unattainable on this triangle. This conclusion does not identify the minimizing network state or prove how it is reached.

More generally one may retain a common positive scale \(X=aZ+b_*\mathbf1\) in (20). Then the phase coefficient is \(\Gamma=\gamma a\) and the form-current coefficients in its reciprocal normalization are \(\rho_e/a^2\). Retaining these edge coefficients is legitimate; declaring them all equal to one without (13) changes the model.

docs.title: Inputs, support work and measured coordinates
docs.text:
Constituent-uniform fine inputs \(f_r(\tau)\) in the form row and \(g_r(\tau)\) in the phase row preserve (5). Their complete balance is

\[ H_f'=-\tfrac94\|LX\|_2^2 +9[(LX)^Tf-(BJ)^Tg]. \tag{24} \]

For \(X=aZ+b_*\mathbf1\), \(\Psi=\Phi+\beta\) and \(\sigma=\tau/4\), their transformed rows receive \(4f(4\sigma)/a\) and \(4g(4\sigma)\), respectively. The support and charts stay fixed. Applying these transformations to the full storage gives exactly four times the work rate in (24). Original coordinate observations retain

\[ x_{r,\ell}=aZ_r+b_*,\qquad \theta_{r,\ell}=\Psi_r-\beta_r+\alpha(\ell-4). \tag{25} \]

A form sensor therefore does not generally read \(Z_r\), and a phase sensor does not discard \(\beta_r\). Other observations must compose with this same embedding. No physical sensor calibration is derived.

When (13) is satisfied, the full storage in the target chart (11) is

\[ H_f=B_0+9\sum_e(1-\rho) +9\rho\left[\tfrac12Z^TLZ+ \sum_e(1-\cos(\Psi_t-\Psi_r))\right], \qquad \frac{dH_f}{d\sigma}=-9\rho\|LZ\|_2^2. \tag{26} \]

This explicitly retains the multiplicative scale and additive boundary cost, rather than equating two differently normalized storages.

Starting with the three isolated cycles, attach (2) without changing any fine form or phase. The support-work jump is exactly

\[ \mathcal W_{\rm attach} =\sum_{\text{new }\{i,m\}}w_{im} [\tfrac12(x_m-x_i)^2+1-\cos(\theta_m-\theta_i)]\ge0. \tag{27} \]

On (5) it equals

\[ \mathcal W_{\rm attach} =9[\tfrac12X^TLX+\sum_eU_e(\Delta_e)]. \tag{28} \]

At the aligned state with constant forms and phase origins, this is \(9(1-\cos\alpha)\sum_e s_e\), equal to \(27(1-\cos\alpha)/2>0\) for both fixed controls. A positive jump requires supplied work; the continuous loss in (4) is not an available reservoir or a reason for the contact to occur.

At fixed support, a uniform form jump \(h_r\) becomes \(h_r/a\), while a uniform phase jump keeps its angle and the fixed origin offsets. Its work is the difference of the full storage. These coordinate facts do not admit or select a registered hybrid operator. Its live preconditions, atomic targets, collective descent and occurrence need their own contracts. Time-varying weights would add explicit support-work and chart-derivative terms absent from (3).

docs.title: Consequence for inheritance and the remaining scope
docs.text:
Pairwise same-profile representations require compatibility at every shared constituent and every network cycle. Even the sine profile selected by the additional pairwise premise has a nontrivial boundary law on the prescribed triangle. The sufficient inherited description is (9), or its explicit tree chart (22), with marked boundary information retained. The collective interaction owner already distinguishes such information from a universal scalar-node representation; this is an exact organized example of that distinction.

The winding-one geometry is preserved for every trajectory initially on (5). This is conditional invariant-family identity, with no assertion that arbitrary nearby states remain there or that previously acquired two-object error budgets survive this different support and degree. Matching target geometry and local coefficients does not transfer nonlinear recovery or acquisition certificates. The separate acquired-assembly proof establishes full-state capture and winding retention for the two fixed controls from their actual independently recovered sources, with supplied attachment work retained. Other mixtures, later inputs and event selection require their own admissions. No trajectory, source producer, physical dataset, topology search or new numerical protocol was evaluated here.

This result neither identifies a fundamental physical interaction nor rules out a hierarchy carrying its actual boundary laws. The execution plan owns the next admission decision.

docs.title: Implementation and independent controls
docs.text:
The detached static owner _organized_network_compatibility.py rebuilds the actual fine support, degree, contact coefficients, complete collective rows and full storage from admitted primitive data. Its fine reciprocal coefficient is fixed to \(1/(1023\pi)\); the proof permits any positive fixed \(\gamma\). The shared contact factors in _oriented_interface_constitutive.py carry no pair-model degree, source certificate or network verdict.

The static observation admits three joint node-phase phasors, then derives the three edge differences from that assignment. Three independently supplied edge differences need not satisfy the cycle identity and are not substituted for joint state. These circular observations do not construct continuous lifts or run the fine law. Exact primitive conditions decide chart compatibility: all weights vanish for the phase condition, and all \(s_e(1-s_e)\) agree for the amplitude condition. Overlapping rounded intervals cannot substitute for these equalities. A compatible common amplitude scale is reported separately even if the phase condition fails; it then belongs to a law retaining its phase lags, not to (11).

The independent controls compare these reports with the full 27-node edge construction and cover the fixed equal and unequal contacts, the compatible zero-offset control, the tree chart, storage/loss and admitted-state boundaries. No trajectory or source-acquisition producer is part of these static checks.

docs.title: Admission of an observation-based collective forecast
Conditional admission result
docs.text:
The retained observation-to-future certificate bounds differences between complete histories without supplying their unknown initialization. This owner derives the contract for using one proposed carrier history as a forecast. Sections 1-4 establish its analytical admission; section 5 declares one operational test on archived synthetic readings. The research program owns its evaluation status and subsequent dependencies.

Retain the complete fine law, source class, command, support, held capacities, structural clock and sample schedule in the original declaration. Local time runs from zero at tau=200 to T=16. There are thirty vector samples, each with five mean-form coordinates, and arbitrary correlated coordinate error at most eta=1e-14. The initial common form remains unknown. Neither a zero-sum prior nor the attachment preparation may be supplied to an observation-only proposal. A common phase rotation can fix Phi_0=0; it does not fix any relative phase or winding.

docs.title: 1. The retained gain applies to an arbitrary sample discrepancy
docs.text:
Consider two exact carriers with initial mean forms bounded by X=1/100, arbitrary circular initial phases, and the same complete prescribed input. Remove the command using the original coordinates Y=U-z_cmd, Psi=Phi-H. At all readings and the future endpoint, z_cmd=0, so the observed form is Y. Let their difference be u and suppose

\[ \max_j\|u(t_j)\|_\infty\le\delta,\qquad\delta\ge0. \tag{1} \]

The static phasor construction and difference remainder do not require that delta equal the earlier fine-pair noise allowance. They use initial-form boundedness, global sine bounds, the shared command and the maximum two-unit distance from the latest sample. Their estimates are homogeneous in the carrier differences. In the notation of that proof,

\[ R_*\le A_* B_*+B_0\delta,\qquad B_*\le k(\delta+R_*)+e_0\delta+e_bB_*. \] \[ d=1-e_b-kA_*>0,\qquad Q=\frac{k(1+B_0)+e_0}{d},\qquad B_*\le Q\delta. \tag{2} \]

Substitution into the same future residual identity gives

\[ G=w+n_0+n_bQ+(1+w)(A_*Q+B_0),\qquad \boxed{\|u(T)\|_\infty\le G\delta.} \tag{3} \]

The retained interval matrices and rational weights certify this G. Its displayed approximation 3.9317888454 is descriptive; admission uses the rebuilt exact/outward bound. Neither an assumed inverse nor a cached verdict can replace the residual and positive-denominator checks.

The comparison allows arbitrary initial edge phasors, so the two carriers need not share a winding or satisfy the original acute-gap identity. The candidate must still solve the same full-circle law. This broader comparison does not enlarge the class from which the unknown fine truth is assumed to come, or certify an NFR identity for a candidate outside that class.

docs.title: 2. One candidate history and its complete record residual
docs.text:
Let y contain the 150 admitted raw readings. Propose one exact candidate initial state (Uhat_0,Phihat_0) from y and declared model information alone, with ||Uhat_0||infinity<=X. Retain its common form and declare its phase gauge and circular representatives. Rounded proposal coordinates define the candidate actually validated; they are not exact inverses of an unknown state.

Suppose a validated numerical calculation encloses the same candidate's exact form at every reading in coordinate intervals C_jc, and its future form in intervals C_Tc about a reported center m_T, with uniform radius r_T. These enclosures must follow one uninterrupted initial state through the complete word and tail. Define the upper residual

\[ \rho=\max_{j,c}\sup_{v\in C_{jc}}|v-y_{jc}|. \tag{4} \]

For symmetric sample bounds with center m_jc and radius r_jc, this is max_(j,c)(abs(m_jc-y_jc)+r_jc). It includes historical numerical error. Intersecting a sample interval with a reading band does not prove that the exact candidate lies inside that band. Independent per-sample states likewise do not certify one jointly compatible history.

Assume the record was produced by some fine history in the original class. Its exact carrier starts at that history's actual unknown collective means. The unchanged hidden transport bound gives uniform mean-form error E_0<2.3e-18 over the entire local horizon. Rebuild E_0 from the original hidden bounds and laws; the stronger error bound from known attachment preparation does not apply here. At every reading,

\[ \|U_{truth\ carrier}(t_j)-U_{candidate}(t_j)\|_\infty \le\eta+E_0+\rho. \tag{5} \]

Apply (3), add the truth's future source error and the candidate's numerical endpoint radius, and obtain

\[ \boxed{\|U_{fine}(216)-m_T\|_\infty\le R:=G(\eta+E_0+\rho)+E_0+r_T.} \tag{6} \]

Historical numerical error is already in rho and is not added again. Only the truth needs the fine-to-carrier correction: the candidate is the exact carrier specified by its proposed initial state. A future reading with allowance eta_future has error at most R+eta_future against the forecast.

The true-form policy radius 1e-13 is admitted whenever (6) proves R<=1e-13. For example, rho<=eta+E_0 is a sufficient fitting policy if the remaining endpoint budget also satisfies this inequality. That residual cap is not necessary: the complete inequality can admit a larger residual. A future numerical protocol must fix its policy and budgets before evaluation.

docs.title: 3. Conditional accuracy and exact feasible witnesses
docs.text:
Equation (6) is conditional on fine-record membership. A carrier proposal with a small residual does not establish that a fine-class source generated the record, or that the carrier itself is a fine-class feasible witness. The record might come from a different law or violate the supplied source bounds. Good fitting does not authenticate those premises.

A stronger sufficient witness has a separate admission. Require the candidate initial collective gaps and winding to satisfy the original circular class, as well as the initial form bound. Set u=z=0 and lift

\[ x_{c,j}=\widehat U_c,\qquad \theta_{c,j}=\psi_j+\widehat\Phi_c. \tag{7} \]

The invariant-carrier proof shows this is an exact fine history for the same uniform-child input. If its whole-record upper residual satisfies rho<=eta, it is a genuine fine-class feasible member and proves nonemptiness. The retained fine-future diameter then bounds its distance from every compatible fine future; add r_T when reporting a numerical endpoint center. A residual allowed up to eta+E_0 does not establish this stronger claim.

docs.title: 4. Record, numerical and failure contracts
docs.text:
An operational consumer must retain and check:

  • All 150 finite signed readings, their five-coordinate node order, exact thirty sample times, observation map, units and the declared error allowance.
  • The complete law, gain, support, capacity, input and clock associations; source-class assumptions; and any preparation information actually supplied.
  • The proposal's exact represented initial coordinates, circular phase conventions and common gauge, with source/algorithm/budget provenance.
  • One validated candidate history, its sample enclosures and future enclosure, numerical precision/backend, stage partition, residuals and failure status.
  • The retained gain evidence and rebuilt source/model-error budgets. Supplied summaries, matching labels or stale bounds cannot replace these premises.

Admission precedes float conversion. Reject nonfinite or Boolean physical values and malformed records. Circle-valued phase admission and any chosen continuous lifts remain distinct; an optimizer's representatives do not authenticate a fine-state identity. Numerical integration must retain the declared clock in both carrier rows, split actual input stages and preserve the reached state across their boundaries.

Malformed input is rejection. A failed proposal, unsupported candidate domain, inconclusive trajectory enclosure or exceeded numerical budget is unavailable candidate evidence. A failed residual or radius bound rejects that candidate for the declared policy. None establishes that every candidate fails or that the raw record is incompatible with the model. A successful bound remains conditional on its stated truth and numerical premises.

The shared prediction-transfer arithmetic and independent budget controls implement the residual/error combination, including invalid domains. That arithmetic consumes supplied enclosures and a supplied gain; it does not certify their trajectories, provenance, record membership or model identity. The shared prescribed-time integrator and retained evidence readers remain the applicable owners for those obligations. No new nonlinear trajectory, raw response or physical experiment is evaluated by this analytical result.

docs.title: 5. Fixed record-only software protocol
docs.text: This protocol fixes one synthetic record, one deterministic proposal and one validated candidate history before extraction or numerical evaluation. Its purpose is to make the conditional forecast operational without supplying generating-state coordinates. The historical archive and its future are already public: this is a software demonstration, not a reserved response, independent validation, law comparison or physical experiment.

docs.title: One untrusted numerical proposal
docs.text:
The proposal owner receives only the thirty times, 150 readings and static 150 x 15 observation matrix. The law, command and clock are declared model information. Source phases, source initialization, extraction errors, truth labels and future values are not inference arguments. The fixed algorithm is:

  1. Solve the midpoint linear design with NumPy linalg.lstsq, rcond=None, requiring rank 15. Initialize oriented edge angles with atan2 of its formal sine/cosine coefficients. Fix Phi_0=0 and obtain the other four phase representatives by cumulative sums of the first four edge angles. Initialize forms from the first five readings clipped to binary64 [-.01,.01], preserving the unknown common form.
  2. Fit five forms and four phase representatives with one SciPy least_squares call: method trf, max_nfev=80, ftol=None, gtol=None, xtol=1e-13, x_scale=(.01,.01,.01,.01,.01,1,1,1,1) and residual scale 1e-4. Form bounds are binary64 [-.01,.01]; phase lifts are unbounded. Require optimizer success. Cache paired residual/Jacobian requests at identical parameters; there is no restart or alternative initializer.
  3. Each trial carries the full ten-coordinate command-removed sine state and its analytic 10 x 9 sensitivities. Use DOP853 with rtol=1e-11, atol=1e-17, max_step=1/8, splitting every prescribed input stage. Integrate only the 15 plateaus and first 14 ramps, stopping at the last reading. Both rows retain the same structural clock; no state coordinate is reset at a stage boundary. This is a detached numerical proposal, not validated trajectory evidence.
  4. Convert the returned finite binary64 coordinates to exact represented rationals. Clip the five forms again to the exact interval [-1/100,1/100] and set initial Phi_0=0 exactly. This represented state is the sole candidate. Retain the numerical start, optimizer status, evaluation and forward-call counts, diagnostic residual and numerical backend metadata. Backend metadata includes NumPy/SciPy versions, compiler/build architecture, BLAS/LAPACK configuration and integer widths, and available SIMD features; omit machine paths, commands and environment values.

docs.title: One validated forecast and decision
docs.text:
The candidate consumer re-admits the record and exact candidate before integration. Run one carried candidate from tau=200 to 216 through the complete word and released tail, using the shared prescribed-time metric Taylor kernel, order 16, outward 128-bit dyadic intervals, identity metric and growth bound g=1/3000. Split at every stage and use maximum step 1/8: 143 successful steps cover the fixed horizon. The initial candidate radius is zero and the propagated numerical radius may not exceed 1e-15. Keep every compact tube, polynomial, remainder, growth and endpoint witness. No refinement or retry follows failure.

Construct all sample enclosures from this single fresh history and calculate the upper residual (4), then (6) with the rebuilt G, containing-class E_0 and eta=1e-14. Admit only if the trajectory is complete and the true-form radius is at most 1e-13. Report the five endpoint centers with their true-form bounds and separate future-reading bounds enlarged by eta. Do not inspect the archived future as an acceptance criterion. The stronger exact feasible witness in section 3 is not part of this protocol.

Failure of proposal, enclosure or policy yields explicit unavailability without a new candidate, budget, tolerance or source choice. Malformed inputs reject before use; unexpected software errors retain an incomplete attempt. A successful case establishes one operational conditional forecast, not optimizer convergence for every admissible record, source-class membership for arbitrary data, or a uniquely justified evolution law.

Run the single fixed instrument only after committing this declaration and all consumed source. Its shared exclusive assessment lifecycle records the source inventory and attempt before extraction; exact record, proposal and validated response follow in the result. Archive those bytes and receipt for read-only verification.

docs.title: Predictive sufficiency of finite collective form records
Fixed observation-to-future comparison
docs.text:
The retained information comparison removes the exact collective initialization consumed by the preparation-based forecast. It asks whether two complete histories compatible with one existing noisy record must have nearby future mean forms. The target is an output diameter, not an inverse for every phase or hidden constituent coordinate.

The class contains the previously acquired sources, but acquisition of every member is not asserted. This is a structural information comparison with an unchanged complete law. A numerical result cannot supply physical preparation, calibration, a laboratory clock, a unique fundamental law or a physical identity.

docs.title: 1. Fine-source uncertainty is retained on both sides
docs.text:
For each valid fine history introduce the carrier with its own actual initial means. Those means are unknown to the observer; this is a proof comparison, not an initialization procedure. Rebuild the shared hidden transport from the declared primitive bounds, with g=1/3000:

\[ s=2gT,\qquad Z=\frac{b_0+s a_0}{1-s^2},\qquad \rho_0=\frac{gZ^2}{9},\qquad E_0=\frac{T\rho_0}{1-(gT)^2}<2.3\cdot10^{-18}. \tag{1} \]

Both denominators are positive. The projected nonlinear sine remainder and heat contraction give this uniform Euclidean mean-form error, hence the same coordinate error, on the full 16-unit history. It includes the hidden initialization without identifying its variances. It is not the much smaller preparation-specific error requiring known attachment means.

If two fine histories admit one common raw record, their true forms differ by at most 2*eta at every one of the 150 coordinates simultaneously. Their two carrier histories consequently satisfy

\[ \|u(t_j)\|_\infty\le\delta:=2(\eta+E_0) \quad\text{at all 30 vector sample times}. \tag{2} \]

No independence or cancellation of errors is assumed. Conversely, (2) alone does not authenticate a raw record or prove joint realizability. At the future endpoint, a carrier-difference bound must again add 2*E0 for the two fine histories.

The original identity proof also extends to this containing class through local time 16. Substitute T=16 in its full fine-state bound E_f=2gX+2g^2T and retain the internal, outer and collar margins. The known command never shifts an edge by more than 1/10 and vanishes after release; all those margins remain strictly positive. This is a whole-history fine-state statement, independent of whether the new information certificate passes. Work, storage and the additional unforced loss retain their separate account.

docs.title: 2. A static design with unknown circular phases
docs.text:
Let L=L5, A=L/4, and orient edge e from child e to child e+1 mod 5. Let B have tail -1 and head +1, so L=B B^T and S5(Phi)=-B sin(B^T Phi). Remove the exact prescribed offsets as in the carried forecast:

\[ Y=U-z_{cmd},\qquad \Psi=\Phi-H,\qquad Y'=-AY+\frac\gamma4 S_5(\Psi+H),\qquad \Psi'=\gamma AY. \tag{3} \]

At every reading and at the future endpoint, z_cmd=0, so Y=U. The two compared histories share H and every input stage. Their difference u=Y^(1)-Y^(2) equals their form difference also between readings.

For each history let a_e=(B^T Psi(0))_e, understood modulo 2*pi, and put

\[ p=\left(u(0),b_s,b_c\right),\qquad (b_s)_e=\frac\gamma4\left(\sin a_e^{(1)}-\sin a_e^{(2)}\right),\qquad (b_c)_e=\frac\gamma4\left(\cos a_e^{(1)}-\cos a_e^{(2)}\right). \tag{4} \]

These fifteen formal coefficients need not be independently realizable. Allowing arbitrary coefficients enlarges the comparison and cannot invalidate a bound for the actual subset. Initial-edge phasors are independent of the common phase gauge and branch representatives. No real phase difference between the two histories, common winding or angle inverse is required.

Write h(v)=B^T H(v). Define the static heat response V by

\[ V'=-AV-B\left[b_s\mathbin\odot\cos h +b_c\mathbin\odot\sin h\right], \qquad V(0)=u(0). \tag{5} \]

It is linear in p. Let M stack its five coordinates at all thirty sample times, and let N be its five-coordinate map at time 16. Thus V_samples=M p and V(16)=N p. M and N depend only on the declared support, clock and known command; computing them neither chooses an unknown state nor evaluates a nonlinear future response.

docs.title: 3. A difference remainder rather than an absolute model bias
docs.text:
Use B_* = max(||b_s||infinity,||b_c||infinity) and U_* = sup_[0,T] ||u||infinity. Since the carrier has two incident sine currents per node, ||S5||infinity<=2. Equation (3) and heat contraction imply

\[ \|Y(v)\|_\infty\le X+gv/2,\qquad \Psi(v)-\Psi(0)=\gamma\{Y(0)-Y(v)\} +\frac{\gamma^2}{4}\int_0^v S_5(\Psi+H)\,ds. \] \[ \|\Psi(v)-\Psi(0)\|_\infty\le2gX+g^2T, \qquad D:=4gX+2g^2T. \tag{6} \]

Hence each endogenous edge-phase drift d has magnitude at most D. For q_k=exp(i*a_e^(k)), the difference left after freezing the two initial phasors is

\[ q_1(e^{id_1}-1)-q_2(e^{id_2}-1) =(q_1-q_2)(e^{id_1}-1)+q_2(e^{id_1}-e^{id_2}). \tag{7} \]

Its modulus is at most D*abs(q1-q2)+abs(d1-d2). The scaled phasor difference obeys (gamma/4)*abs(q1-q2)<=sqrt(2)*B_*. Moreover ||B^T A||infinity=2, so the complete phase row gives abs(d1-d2)<=2g integral_0^v ||u(s)||infinity ds. There are two incident edges per node and 2*sqrt(2)<3. Consequently the exact pair row can be written

\[ u'=-Au-B[b_s\odot\cos h+b_c\odot\sin h]+r, \quad \sum_c r_c=0, \quad \|r(v)\|_\infty \le3D B_*+g^2\int_0^v\|u(s)\|_\infty\,ds. \tag{8} \]

This remainder vanishes with differences. Substituting an absolute single-history phase error here would create an unrelated error floor and would not prove a finite-noise continuity statement.

The zero-sum remainder benefits from the heat spectral gap. For zero-sum w, lambda2(L)=(5-sqrt(5))/2>4/3, sqrt(5)<9/4, and norm conversion yield

\[ \|e^{-vA}w\|_\infty \le\min\{1,(9/4)e^{-v/3}\}\,\|w\|_\infty. \]

Split the integral at 3 and use exp(1)>8/3. The integral of this majorant on the positive half-line is at most 3+(27/4)*exp(-1)<177/32<6. Applying it to (8) gives

\[ R_*:=\sup_{[0,T]}\|u-V\|_\infty \le a B_*+\beta U_*,\qquad a=18D,\quad\beta=6g^2T. \tag{9} \]

All sampled difference vectors satisfy (2), including local time zero. For any time up to T, its most recent sample is at most two time units earlier. This includes the last ramp and the release tail; there is no unobserved two-unit interval mistakenly shortened to the tail alone. The static force in (8) has norm at most 3*B_*. Heat contraction from that most recent sample, followed by (8), therefore gives

\[ U_*\le\delta+6(1+D)B_*+2g^2T U_*. \] \[ c=1-2g^2T>0,\qquad A_*:=a+\frac{6\beta(1+D)}c,\qquad B_0:=\frac\beta c,\qquad R_*\le A_* B_*+B_0\delta. \tag{10} \]

The symbols B_*, B and B_0 respectively denote a scalar coefficient norm, the incidence matrix and a scalar remainder coefficient; none is a hidden-state observation.

docs.title: 4. Verifiable weights and the prospective diameter inequality
docs.text:
Retain rational proposed matrices K_b of shape 10-by-150 and W of shape 5-by-150. The former proposes recovery of the ten scaled phasor coefficients. The following nonnegative quantities are maximum absolute row sums, with interval matrix products and upper endpoints used where M and N are enclosed:

\[ k=\|K_b\|_\infty,\qquad w=\|W\|_\infty, \qquad J=[\,0_{10\times5}\ I_{10}\,]-K_bM. \] \[ e_0=\|J_{[:,0:5]}\|_\infty,\quad e_b=\|J_{[:,5:15]}\|_\infty,\quad F=N-WM, \quad n_0=\|F_{[:,0:5]}\|_\infty,\quad n_b=\|F_{[:,5:15]}\|_\infty. \tag{11} \]

No inverse identity is taken on trust. Since the first sample is at zero, ||u(0)||infinity<=delta. Applying K_b to u_samples=M p+(u-V)_samples and retaining the residual J gives

\[ B_*\le k(\delta+R_*)+e_0\delta+e_b B_*. \]

If the declared assessment proves

\[ d:=1-e_b-k A_*>0,\qquad Q:=\frac{k(1+B_0)+e_0}{d}, \tag{12} \]

then B_*<=Q*delta and R_*<=(A_* Q+B_0)*delta. The future identity u(T)=W u_samples+F p+(u-V)(T)-W(u-V)_samples then yields

\[ G:=w+n_0+n_b Q+(1+w)(A_*Q+B_0), \qquad \boxed{\|U_{fine}^{(1)}(216)-U_{fine}^{(2)}(216)\|_\infty \le\delta G+2E_0.} \tag{13} \]

The fixed decision is delta*G+2*E0<=2e-13, in addition to every numerical, domain and evidence obligation. An unavailable bound is not a constructed pair whose future separation exceeds the target.

This is a theorem about the set of future states jointly compatible with one complete record. If nonempty, its coordinate midranges have error at most half the proved diameter. Computing that nonlinear feasible set is a separate operational problem. In particular, W applied to a single raw record is not automatically such a forecast: (7)-(13) bound pair differences, not the single-history nonlinear bias.

docs.title: 5. Fixed validated computation of the static matrices
docs.text:
Each of the fifteen coefficient columns solves q'=-A*q+f_H(v). A first-form column starts at one basis vector with zero forcing. A phasor column starts at zero and has forcing equal to an incidence column times the known sine or cosine command, so ||f_H||infinity<=1. All exact columns obey ||q(v)||infinity<=1+v<=17.

For each fixed cell, form the degree-16 jet of the exact local command polynomial using the shared interval Taylor owner. Its sine and cosine jets give the forcing coefficients F_j. The normalized solution coefficients obey the linear recurrence

\[ q_{j+1}=\frac{-Aq_j+F_j}{j+1}. \tag{14} \]

Use point-center coefficients through degree 16. For the degree-17 Taylor remainder, let F be the maximum absolute zeroth forcing coefficient over the entire cell. Heat contraction supplies the center-started local bound ||q||infinity<=||center||infinity+duration*F. Use the symmetric box from that bound as the zeroth state in the same recurrence, and let the local clock's zeroth coefficient equal the entire cell; its first clock coefficient is one and the others zero. The recurrence therefore encloses the required normalized seventeenth derivative everywhere on that local solution. This analytically derived local tube avoids an independent existence assumption. No scalar trigonometric error is substituted for a derivative or ODE remainder.

The degree-16 polynomial plus this remainder times the cell duration to power 17 encloses the local endpoint. Choose the polynomial's exact rational midpoint as the next center. Add the maximum sum of polynomial radius and absolute remainder to the carried column radius: the homogeneous heat flow is contractive in the infinity norm, so this retains initialization and rounding errors without box wrapping or an uncertain auxiliary clock. Check the 1e-12 radius cap through the final radius of each column. The propagated radii are nondecreasing, so this checks every cell and sample endpoint as well.

Both plateau endpoints are stored. Stage boundaries preserve coefficient centers and radii, and the future matrix follows the final unforced tail. Record all enclosures, exact grid times and each column's polynomial, remainder and carried radius for read-only recurrence checks. Those checks retain the shared kernel's derivative-enclosure premises; cached residuals alone cannot establish arbitrary supplied matrix provenance. The first five initial-form columns carry the common form mode; no projection discards it.

The midpoint normal-equation solve only proposes fixed weights. Its rank, conditioning, rounding and backend cannot certify (12)-(13). Those statements follow only from the retained rational K_b and W, outward interval products against all coefficient enclosures, and the exact scalar comparisons. The interval matrices do not authenticate their source; the evidence receipt retains the frozen implementation and configuration separately.

docs.title: 6. An unavoidable common-form floor
docs.text:
The common form has not been fixed to zero. Translation by a constant multiple of the all-ones vector changes neither the Laplacian, pressure currents nor the phase row. Take the admissible exact carrier with zero initial mean forms and equal collective phases, and compare its common form translations by +eta and -eta. They satisfy the same complete law, hidden bounds and initial class. Their form difference is exactly 2*eta at every node and time under the same neutral word.

The midpoint of their true 150-reading vectors is one common admitted record, with opposite errors of magnitude eta at every scalar. Their future mean-form separation is also 2*eta. This proves a uniform diameter floor of 2e-14, or a forecast-radius floor of 1e-14, without evaluating a trajectory. It does not decide the looser declared 2e-13 target.

All conclusions concern this law, class, word, ideal clock and finite observation allowance. The independent physical preparation and measurement bridge remains open. The sole execution queue owns any subsequent work; this owner creates no parallel campaign.

docs.text:

The Taylor derivative enclosure continues to rely on the proved shared kernel and declared forcing law; receipts are content associations, not execution authentication. Preserve this response and the declaration prefix without replaying the producer.

docs.title: Observing outer winding with unknown child phase origins
Declared state class, probes and observation contract
docs.text:
The finite response comparison distinguishes two known preparations. This gate asks whether collective form readings can identify an unknown outer winding without supplying its phases to the inverse.

docs.text:

docs.text:

\[ C_c=\frac19\sum_{j=0}^8\cos d_{c,j},\qquad S_c=\frac19\sum_{j=0}^8\sin d_{c,j}. \tag{3} \]

The positive or negative child-c probe changes the receiver's incident phase difference by \(s\epsilon\), where \(s=+1\) or \(-1\); the other initial incident differences at receiver child \(c+1\) are unchanged. \[ A_c^s=\frac\gamma4 \{s\sin\epsilon\,C_c+(1-\cos\epsilon)S_c\}. \tag{4} \]

The finite increment proof uses heat contraction, \(\|L\|_\infty=8\), degree four, \(\|S(\theta)\|_\infty\le4\), and the global sine derivative bound. These are the same full law and support here. Reapply its argument with the present \(\epsilon,h,X\), including the unknown background, rather than transferring the earlier evaluated response. \[ R_c^s=hA_c^s+e_c^s,\qquad |e_c^s|\le E, \quad E=2g\epsilon h^2+2g^2\epsilon(X+gh)h^2 +\frac43g^3\epsilon h^3. \tag{5} \]

This bound retains both continuous rows, form diffusion, background phase motion and nonlinear probe feedback. In particular, the observed endpoint is not identified with the initial derivative. It applies to every actual fine state in the admitted class, with either probe sign and every receiver.

For one interface write the three noisy raw readings as \(B,P,M\). The same unprobed reading B occurs in both differences. Define

The odd combination cancels baseline motion and its actual reading error exactly. The even combination carries twice that error. No independence, zero-mean noise, stationary baseline or equality of different branches' later fine states is assumed. All eleven branches share the same initial actual state; measurements from different unknown preparations do not satisfy this contract merely because they have equal winding labels.

Let outward intervals enclose \(\gamma\), \(\sin\epsilon\) and \(1-\cos\epsilon\), and form the positive scale intervals

\[ K_C=\frac2{[\gamma]h[\sin\epsilon]},\qquad K_S=\frac2{[\gamma]h[1-\cos\epsilon]}. \tag{8} \]

docs.title: 3. Angle inclusion, cycle consistency and uniform identification
docs.text:
Every phasor in (3) has its argument in \([a_c-2\zeta,a_c+2\zeta]\), an acute interval. Positive averaging therefore keeps its nonzero resultant in the same angular cone. If \(\beta_c=\arg(C_c+iS_c)\), then

\[ |\beta_c-a_c|\le2\zeta. \tag{10} \]

This argument uses the actual fine boundary deviations. It does not set them to zero or equate the argument of an average phasor with an arithmetic mean phase. Since the entire rectangle (9) has positive real part, the shared outward principal-argument calculation is regular. Define

\[ \mathcal A_c= \left(\arg(\mathcal C_c+i\mathcal S_c)+[-2\zeta,2\zeta]\right) \cap[-A,A],\qquad \mathcal T=\sum_{c=0}^4\mathcal A_c. \tag{11} \]

Each true \(a_c\) belongs to its interval. Keep precisely those \(w\in\{-1,0,1\}\) for which the outward enclosure of \(2\pi w\) intersects \(\mathcal T\). These are necessary sector candidates. Independent interval corners need not correspond to one jointly realizable source, so the retained set is not a collection of constructed witnesses. Nevertheless, under the declared actual-source premises it contains the true sector; a singleton then identifies that sector, simultaneously on all nine fine cycles by (2).

A uniform bound shows that every admitted source and every allowed reading error yields a singleton. For a scale interval K, write \(K^+\) for its upper endpoint and \(\operatorname{wid}(K)\) for its width. Set

\[ \begin{split} F_C&=g h[\sin\epsilon]^+/2,& F_S&=g h[1-\cos\epsilon]^+/2,\\ w_C&=2K_C^+b_C+\operatorname{wid}(K_C)(F_C+2b_C)+\rho_{K_C},& w_S&=2K_S^+b_S+\operatorname{wid}(K_S)(F_S+2b_S)+\rho_{K_S},\\ \rho_K&=(2K^++\operatorname{wid}(K)+2)u,&u&=2^{-128}. \end{split}\tag{12} \]

Since \(|C_c|,|S_c|\le1\), (7) gives \(|D_C|\le F_C+b_C\) and \(|D_S|\le F_S+b_S\). The product-width inequality therefore bounds the two pre-intersection moment widths by \(w_C,w_S\), including the outward uncertainty in the scale intervals. Materializing \(D+[-b,b]\) adds at most u at each endpoint. Its width is therefore at most \(2b+2u\), and its maximum magnitude at most \(F+2b+u\). Multiplication by K followed by endpoint rounding adds the remaining \(2u\), giving exactly the additional allowance \(\rho_K\). Clipping cannot increase either width. On \(C\ge c_0\), \(|S|\le1\), \(\arg(C+iS)=\arctan(S/C)\), and the elementary derivative bounds give

\[ \operatorname{wid}(\mathcal A_c) \le d:=\frac{w_S}{c_0}+\frac{w_C}{c_0^2}+4\zeta+10^{-20}. \tag{13} \]

The last term covers the shared argument evaluation and subsequent interval arithmetic uniformly, not a sampled rounding error. Here \(c_0>1/6\) and \(|S|\le1\), so \(|S/C|<6\); division adds fewer than ten grid units to its endpoint enclosure. The shared arctangent reduces point arguments to magnitude at most \(1/2\). Its 64 alternating terms have omitted tail at most \((1/2)^{128}/129\); interval term multiplication contracts by less than \(0.251\), and bounding each term and accumulated sum rounding gives fewer than \(10^4u\) of point-enclosure width. At most two pi-based argument transformations, both endpoints and the remaining additions/clips/cycle sum stay below the looser total \(10^6u<3\cdot10^{-33}\). The \(10^{-20}\) allowance in each angle is consequently sufficient. The transcendental owners and their precision are unchanged.

\[ \begin{split} E&<6.224\cdot10^{-15},&c_0&>0.169965,\\ w_C&<0.000186022,&w_S&<0.004231968,\\ d&<0.031343,&\operatorname{wid}(\mathcal T)&<0.156715. \end{split}\tag{14} \]

docs.title: 2. Finite nonlinear increment under the complete rows
docs.text:
Fix either actual source. Let \((x,\theta)\) denote its unprobed continuation and \((x^+,\theta^+)\) its probed continuation. Define

\[ y=x^+-x,\qquad v=\theta^+-\theta,\qquad y(0)=0,\quad v(0)=k. \]

Their exact difference equations are

\[ y'=\{-Ly+\gamma\Delta S\}/4,\qquad v'=\gamma Ly/4,\qquad \Delta S=S(\theta+v)-S(\theta). \tag{4} \]

Use \(g\ge\gamma\), the shared outward rational upper bound, and let \(X\) bound the actual initial form maximum norm. Heat contraction in the unprobed first row gives, for \(0\le t\le h\),

\[ \|x(t)\|_\infty\le X+gt,\qquad |d(t)-d(0)|\le4g(X+gh)t \tag{5} \]

for every lifted edge gap \(d\). The second bound follows from the complete phase row, \(\|\theta'\|_\infty\le2g\|x\|_\infty\). It retains the background's own motion even when its initial form is small.

Put \(A(t)=\|y(t)\|_\infty\) and \(B(t)=\|v(t)-k\|_\infty\). Every initial edge jump has magnitude at most \(\epsilon\). Sine is globally one-Lipschitz, so each edge's current increment is at most \(\epsilon+2B(t)\) in magnitude. The heat representation of the first row and direct integration of the second give

\[ A(t)\le g\epsilon t+2g\int_0^t B(s)\,ds, \qquad B(t)\le2g\int_0^t A(s)\,ds. \tag{6} \]

For every \(T\le h\), the supremum \(A_T\) on \([0,T]\) satisfies \(A_T\le g\epsilon T+2g^2T^2A_T\). The checked condition \(2g^2h^2<1/2\) therefore implies the pointwise estimates

\[ A(t)\le2g\epsilon t,\qquad B(t)\le2g^2\epsilon t^2. \tag{7} \]

To retain the finite nonlinear remainder, write an edge increment as \(F(d,u)=\sin(d+u)-\sin d\). The exact inequalities \(|\partial_dF(d,u)|\le|u|\) and \(|\partial_uF(d,u)|\le1\) imply

\[ |F(d(t),u(t))-F(d(0),u(0))| \le\epsilon|d(t)-d(0)|+|u(t)-u(0)|. \]

The initial edge jump \(u(0)\) is held fixed in the first difference; no small-angle replacement has been made. Summing the four incident edges, using (5) and \(|u(t)-u(0)|\le2B(t)\), yields

\[ \|\Delta S(t)-\Delta S(0)\|_\infty \le16\epsilon g(X+gh)t+8B(t). \tag{8} \]

Finally integrate the complete first difference row (4), retaining its heat term \(\|Ly\|_\infty/4\le2A\). Equations (7)-(8) prove

\[ \left\|y(h)-\frac{h\gamma}{4}\Delta S(0)\right\|_\infty \le E(X):= 2g\epsilon h^2+2g^2\epsilon(X+gh)h^2 +\frac43g^3\epsilon h^3. \tag{9} \]

An arithmetic child mean has norm at most one as a functional on these coordinates, so the same error bounds the receiver readout. It is not an assertion that the initial derivative is the measured response.
