This is a local conditional classification, not a new evaluation of the earlier acquired source. Any trapping condition is an explicit restriction on initial state; it does not prove that the original preparation enters it. No finite convergence time, trajectory campaign, response retuning, source refinement or replay of frozen producers is authorized by this question.

The auxiliary coordinate, its origin, reciprocal coupling and preparation remain supplied constitutive premises. The continuous path installs no operator, support event or occurrence selector. This comparison neither identifies a physical bath nor selects a unique TNFR law or material property.

The declaration above was committed as 53cc7b68 before this proof. The zero-leakage law has a family of locally attracting equilibria indexed by the retained lifted quantity. Attraction to a particular member is relative to its invariant leaf. With the original positive leakage, only the zero-reservoir equilibrium survives in the declared chart, and it has a full-state local trapping neighborhood. Neither result admits the earlier acquired preparation into that neighborhood.

docs.title: 1. Complete law, lift and retained quantity
docs.text:
Let \(\sigma_a[g,a,j]=2a-1\), \(\alpha=2\pi/9\), and \(\psi[g,a,j]=\alpha(j-4)\). Write

\[ U(\theta)=\sum_{\{i,k\}}[1-\cos(\theta_k-\theta_i)],\qquad S_i(\theta)=\sum_{k\sim i}\sin(\theta_k-\theta_i),\qquad c=\frac{\sigma_a}{3}=\frac{4b}{\gamma}. \tag{1} \]

Every sum has the fixed 72 unit edges. Thus \(\nabla U=-S\), \(\mathbf1^Tc=0\), \(\|c\|_2=2\), and \(c^T\psi=0\). The declared chart is an open convex subset of the mean-zero lifted phase space: all its gap constraints are strict affine inequalities in \(\theta-\psi\). On a closing child edge, the fixed added turn is \(2\pi\). The cosine and its derivatives are unaffected by that turn, while the chart and winding statement depend on retaining it.

The two fixed means are conserved by the complete law. Its vector field is globally Lipschitz on the finite-dimensional real lifted state, so solutions exist uniquely for every finite time. The joint balance and retained quantity follow directly, without restricting to child-constant states:

\[ \begin{split} (H_{\rm joint})_\tau &=-\frac14\|Lx\|_2^2-\lambda r^2,\\ J&=r+c^T\theta,\\ J_\tau &=-b^TLx-\lambda r+c^T\frac{\gamma Lx}{4} =-\lambda r . \end{split}\tag{2} \]

For the slow clock, put \(\ell=2\lambda/\gamma^2\), which is either zero or one. Every row becomes

\[ x_s=\frac{-Lx+\gamma S(\theta)}{2\gamma^2} +\frac{2b}{\gamma^2}r,\quad \theta_s=\frac{Lx}{2\gamma},\quad r_s=-\frac{2b^TLx}{\gamma^2}-\ell r,\quad J_s=-\ell r . \tag{3} \]

The positive clock changes do not change equilibrium or local attraction. They do not supply a laboratory time scale.

The conserved quantity for zero leakage is lift dependent. Replacing \(\theta\) by \(\theta+2\pi k\) while retaining the same physical auxiliary state changes its numerical label by \(2\pi c^Tk\). Such a change cannot be used to compare preparations in different charts without transporting the chart and its retained data. The following classification uses exactly the lift and means in the declaration.

docs.title: 2. Full equilibrium classification in the declared chart
docs.text:
First take \(\lambda=0\) and a fixed \(J\). Eliminating the auxiliary coordinate on its invariant leaf gives

\[ r=J-c^T heta,\qquad U_J( heta)=U( heta)+ rac12(J-c^T heta)^2,\qquad abla U_J=-S-c(J-c^T heta). ag{4} \]

The complete restricted rows and their storage are

\[ x_ au=- rac{Lx}{4}- rac{\gamma}{4} abla U_J( heta), \qquad heta_ au= rac{\gamma Lx}{4},\qquad H_J= rac12x^TLx+U_J( heta),\qquad (H_J)_ au=- rac14\|Lx\|_2^2. ag{5} \]

In the acute chart, the Hessian of \(U\) is the graph Laplacian whose edge weights are the positive cosines of the adjusted gaps. The graph is connected. Consequently \(U\), and also \(U_J\) with Hessian \( abla^2U+cc^T\), are strictly convex on the mean-zero chart. This is a statement about every fine phase direction, including directions outside the four-child invariant family.

Any equilibrium has \(Lx=0\), hence \(x=0\) under the fixed form mean. Its remaining equation is \( abla U_J=0\). A candidate can be constructed without assuming that the equilibrium must inherit a particular symmetry:

\[ egin{split} 6B_*+3\sin B_*&=J,\ x_*&=0,\qquad heta_*=\psi+ rac{\sigma_a B_*}{2},\qquad r_*=3\sin B_* . \end{split} ag{6} \]

The scalar left-hand side is strictly increasing; its derivative is \(6+3\cos B\ge3\). For \(|J|\le3\), its unique root satisfies \(|B_*|<1/2\): its value at \(1/2\) is strictly greater than three. For nonnegative \(J\), useful enclosing inequalities are \(J/9\le B_*\le J/6\); negative roots follow by odd symmetry. At this candidate all child gaps equal \(\alpha\), all interparent gaps vanish, and all intraparent gaps equal \(B_*\). It lies inside the declared chart. The internal sine contributions cancel, and \(S( heta_*)=-\sigma_a\sin B_*=-c r_*\), so it is an exact equilibrium. Strict convexity then proves that it is the only equilibrium in that chart on this \(J\) leaf. This uniqueness argument does not discard transverse coordinates or infer equilibrium from a scalar root alone.

Both parents are registered at equilibrium precisely when

\[ |J|<J_{ m reg},\qquad J_{ m reg}= rac32+3\sin(1/4). ag{7} \]

At equality their gaps equal the strict identity boundary. For \(J_{ m reg}<|J|\le3\), both equilibrated parents are unregistered while all four children retain winding one. In particular \(J=0\) gives registered parents, whereas \(J=3\) gives unregistered parents, since \(J_{ m reg}<9/4<3\). These are different preparations of the same zero-leakage law, not different fitted couplings.

For \(\lambda=\gamma^2/2>0\), equilibrium again requires \(Lx=0\). The reservoir row then requires \(r=0\), and the form row requires \(S( heta)=0\). Strict convexity of \(U\) in the declared chart, together with the explicit critical point \(\psi\), gives the unique equilibrium

\[ (x_*, heta_*,r_*)=(0,\psi,0). ag{8} \]

The variable \(J\) is not a constraint on this positive-leakage equilibrium: equation (2) changes it during evolution. Removing \(r\) as though \(J\) were conserved would change this complete model.

docs.title: 3. Uniform local trapping bounds
docs.text:
The fixed product graph has \(\lambda_2(L)>1/3\) and \(\|L\|_2\le8\). Indeed its Laplacian spectrum is the sum of the C9 spectrum and two copies of \(\{0,2\}\); the C9 gap is \(2-2\cos\alpha>1/3\). The acquisition proof establishes these same fixed-support bounds. No graph coefficient from a different support is used here.

Set \( ho=1/8\) and write \(\eta= heta- heta_*\), with zero mean. In the closed phase ball \(\|\eta\|_2\le ho\), every edge-gap perturbation has magnitude at most \(2 ho=1/4\). The adjusted internal gaps lie in \((\alpha-1/4,\alpha+1/4)\subset(0,\pi/3)\); the absolute matching gaps are at most \(|B_*|+1/4<3/4<\pi/3\). The positive-leakage target is the case \(B_*=0\). Thus the entire closed ball stays strictly inside the declared chart, retains all four child windings, and has every edge cosine greater than \(1/2\). In particular,

\[ abla^2U\succeq rac12L,\qquad abla^2U_J\succeq rac12L,\qquad \eta^TL\eta\ge rac13\|\eta\|_2^2. ag{9} \]

For zero leakage, use the storage excess on the actual fixed \(J\) leaf,

\[ egin{split} E_J(x, heta) &= rac12x^TLx+U_J( heta)-U_J( heta_*)\ &= rac12x^TLx+ U( heta)-U( heta_*)-(c r_*)^T\eta + rac12(c^T\eta)^2 . \end{split} ag{10} \]

The second equality uses both \( abla U( heta_*)=c r_*\) and \(r-r_*=-c^T\eta\). It is the affine cancellation that makes this excess positive near the target. The separate differences \(U( heta)-U( heta_*)\) and \((r^2-r_*^2)/2\) need not be positive. Nor is this a positive excess relative to an arbitrarily selected target on a different \(J\) leaf.

For positive leakage use the full-state excess

\[ E_+(x, heta,r)= rac12x^TLx+U( heta)-U(\psi)+ rac12r^2 . ag{11} \]

Taylor's formula along the line segment in the ball, the critical-point identities, and (9) give the lower bounds

\[ egin{split} E_J&\ge rac16\|x\|_2^2+ rac1{12}\|\eta\|_2^2,\ E_+&\ge rac16\|x\|_2^2+ rac1{12}\|\eta\|_2^2+ rac12r^2 . \end{split} ag{12} \]

Every point on the phase-ball boundary therefore has excess at least

\[ E_{ m boundary}= rac{ ho^2}{12}= rac1{768}. ag{13} \]

A sufficient initial-state condition is

\[ \|\eta(0)\|_2< rac18,\qquad 0\le E(0)\le e< rac1{768}, ag{14} \]

where \(E=E_J\) on the specified zero-leakage leaf, or \(E=E_+\) for the positive-leakage model. The phase-ball admission is required in addition to the energy bound; a low periodic storage elsewhere is not an entry certificate. The storage derivative is nonpositive. If a solution first reached the phase-ball boundary, (13) would contradict \(E\le e\). It remains in the ball for all future time.

For a simple rational sufficient admission from norm allowances, let \(\|x(0)\|_2\le X\), \(\|\eta(0)\|_2\le\Theta<1/8\). The global Hessian upper bounds \( abla^2U\preceq L\preceq8I\) and \( abla^2U_J\preceq L+cc^T\preceq12I\) imply

\[ egin{array}{ll} \lambda=0,\ \hbox{same }J: &4X^2+6\Theta^2<1/768,\[2pt] \lambda=\gamma^2/2,\ |r(0)|\le R: &4X^2+4\Theta^2+R^2/2<1/768 . \end{array} ag{15} \]

These are sufficient bounds, not the exact basin. On a fixed zero-leakage leaf the auxiliary deviation is constrained by \(r-r_*=-c^T\eta\). An independent auxiliary perturbation must instead be included when determining the state's actual \(J\) and target. It cannot be dropped while invoking the first row of (15).

docs.title: 4. Full-state attraction and the remaining neutral information
docs.text:
For each \(e<1/768\), the portion of the closed phase ball with \(E\le e\) is compact and positively invariant under the corresponding complete law. Compactness follows from the form bound in (12), the bounded phase ball, and either \(r=J-c^T\theta\) or the reservoir bound in (12). Invariance was proved by the boundary barrier, not assumed from passivity.

In the zero-leakage case, zero storage loss requires \(Lx=0\), hence \(x=0\). To remain in this zero-loss set, the form row in (5) also requires \(\nabla U_J=0\). The unique equilibrium in (6) is therefore the largest invariant subset of the zero-loss set. The finite-dimensional LaSalle invariance argument gives

\[ (x(\tau),\theta(\tau),r(\tau)) \longrightarrow(0,\theta_*(J),r_*(J)) \quad\hbox{as }\tau\longrightarrow\infty . \tag{16} \]

This controls every fine transverse form and phase direction on the invariant leaf: with the two means fixed, the full joint state has dimension 71 and the fixed-\(J\) leaf has dimension 70. It is not only stability in the scalar \(B\) direction or in the four-child invariant family. The positive energy bounds also establish Lyapunov stability relative to that leaf.

In the positive-leakage case, zero joint loss requires both \(x=0\) and \(r=0\). Invariance additionally requires \(S(\theta)=0\), so the largest invariant zero-loss set is the single equilibrium (8). The same argument proves local asymptotic stability in all 71 mean-fixed joint directions, including independent auxiliary perturbations. This conclusion does not give global attraction from the full acute chart or entry from the previous finite-reservoir source.

For zero leakage, a particular equilibrium cannot attract arbitrary nearby states on different \(J\) leaves: nearby members of (6) are exact equilibria themselves. The locally attracting object without fixing \(J\) is the family, with each sufficiently close state subject to its own conditions (14). Its target varies continuously, since

\[ \frac{dB_*}{dJ}=\frac1{6+3\cos B_*}>0 . \tag{17} \]

This is retained initial information, not an unforced periodic motion. For a trapped state whose \(J\) lies strictly below the threshold in (7), convergence implies eventual registration. Strictly above that threshold, it implies eventual nonregistration of both parents. At the threshold, convergence to the identity boundary alone settles neither strict finite-time alternative. The uniform phase ball by itself preserves children, not registration of every parent throughout the transient.

The extra Hessian term \(cc^T\) is positive semidefinite at a fixed phase state. It does not show that every transverse stiffness increases when comparing different equilibria: the equilibrium shift also changes the edge cosines. Neither this rank-one term nor dissipation selects the port law, the auxiliary coordinate or its initial value.

docs.title: Restoring response of an acquired organized parent
Fixed intervention and analytic question
docs.text:
This declaration continues the actual source family of parent acquisition at its slow time s=4. It fixes one supplied intervention and its paired comparison before evaluating the analytic response bounds. It does not evaluate a numerical trajectory.

Item Fixed choice Source The four original independently uncertain recovered C9 children, each with form and phase allowances 1e-10, carried through the unchanged acquisition law to s=4; retain all original fine errors and reached forms and phases Complete continuous law The matching 36-node law, held unit capacities, all 72 unit edges and the original structural clocks tau=(1023/1024)*t, s=gamma^2*tau/2, gamma=1/(1023*pi) Supplied event At s=4, simultaneously set theta+[0,a,j]=theta-[0,a,j]+(2*a-1)/4 for every slot of parent zero; leave all other phases, all forms, support and capacities unchanged Event interpretation A specified zero-duration hybrid phase intervention with marked targets and no autonomous occurrence law; no registered operator name is claimed Preserved observations Each child's winding and both parents' form and lifted-phase means at the event; retain the same continuous phase lifts Work Account for the exact complete storage jump H+ - H-, supplied externally with a fixed budget of three structural storage units; previous dissipation is not a reservoir Paired control The same actual acquired state continued without the event, under the same complete continuous law and clocks Finite response readout At s=5, the intervened outer parent lifted-phase gap minus the paired control gap must exceed 1e-6 for the entire original source family Predictive state Initialize the exact eight-child-mean law from the actual post-event child means; its outer parent phase-gap error at s=5 must be below 1e-7. The declaration above was committed as 37add507 before its analytic certificate was assessed. The proof below retains those choices and the complete original uncertainty. No fine or reduced trajectory is evaluated.

docs.title: 1. The actual event and the retained continuous law
docs.text:
Write \(\sigma_g=2g-1\), \(\sigma_a=2a-1\), \(\alpha=2\pi/9\) and \(\psi_j=\alpha(j-4)\). The matching graph is \(C_9\square K_2\square K_2\), with its original marked nodes and unnormalized Laplacian \(L\). Between events the complete rows remain

\[ x_\tau=(-Lx+\gamma S(\theta))/4,\qquad \theta_\tau=\gamma Lx/4,\qquad S_i(\theta)=\sum_{k\sim i}\sin(\theta_k-\theta_i). \tag{1} \]

The supplied jump is the simultaneous map \(T\) declared in the table: add \(-1/4\) to every phase of child \((0,0)\), add \(1/4\) to every phase of child \((0,1)\), and preserve the other state. It acts on the actual pre-event state, not on its nominal target. Uniform translation within a child preserves every internal phase difference and its winding. The opposite translations preserve each parent's lifted phase mean; all form means are unchanged. Retain the existing lifts through the jump.

This defines a detached hybrid intervention with explicit fine realization, target marks and externally supplied work. It does not claim registered Mutation, Self-organization or another runtime operator: their live evidence, grammar, descent and occurrence obligations are separate. No finite-duration pressure input is invented for the jump. The subsequent sine current is evaluated from the post-event phases under (1).

docs.title: 2. The exact four-child reference after intervention
docs.text:
The original moving reference reaches its own values \(B_4,\Delta_4,v_4,u_4\) at \(s=4\). These are the acquired values from the previous theorem; none is reset. After applying the same jump to that reference, the eight-coordinate child-constant family remains exactly invariant under (1). Its zero-global-mean relative chart is

\[ \begin{split} x^*_{g,a,j}&=\tfrac12(\sigma_g U+\sigma_a V+ \sigma_g\sigma_a W),\\ \theta^*_{g,a,j}&=\psi_j+\tfrac12(\sigma_g D+\sigma_a B+ \sigma_g\sigma_a C). \end{split}\tag{2} \]

The conserved common form and phase origins can be added independently. Here \(D\) is the outer parent phase gap, the two intraparent child gaps are \(B-C\) and \(B+C\), and \(C\) records their difference and the associated outer-port mismatch. Direct substitution into both fine rows gives

\[ \begin{array}{ll} U_\tau=-U/2-\gamma\sin D\cos C/2,&D_\tau=\gamma U/2,\\ V_\tau=-V/2-\gamma\sin B\cos C/2,&B_\tau=\gamma V/2,\\ W_\tau=-W-\gamma(\cos B+\cos D)\sin C/2,&C_\tau=\gamma W. \end{array}\tag{3} \]

The internal cycle currents cancel. The three graph modes have Laplacian eigenvalues two, two and four, respectively; omitting the last mode would change both the form and phase dynamics after this intervention.

Use elapsed slow time \(h=s-4\), \(\varepsilon=\gamma^2\), and

\[ K=-C,\qquad y_D=-U/\gamma,\qquad y_B=-V/\gamma, \qquad z=2W/\gamma. \]

Both rows transform, yielding

\[ \begin{array}{ll} D_h=-y_D,&\varepsilon(y_D)_h=\sin D\cos K-y_D,\\ B_h=-y_B,&\varepsilon(y_B)_h=\sin B\cos K-y_B,\\ K_h=-z,&\varepsilon z_h=2[(\cos B+\cos D)\sin K-z]. \end{array}\tag{4} \]

The post-event reference initialization is exactly

\[ D(0)=\Delta_4,\quad B(0)=B_4+1/4,\quad K(0)=1/4, \quad y_D(0)=-u_4/\gamma,\quad y_B(0)=-v_4/\gamma, \quad z(0)=0. \tag{5} \]

The first two velocities are the nonzero acquired form coordinates. Setting them to zero or to an assumed equilibrium current would be a different initial-value problem. The no-event reference instead continues the original separated family, with \(C=W=0\).

docs.title: 3. Full source transport and retained children
docs.text:
Rebuild the four original isolated sources and their acquired-state bounds as in parent acquisition. Let \(q=10^{-70}\) be the unchanged recovered norm allowance per child and per channel. The global initial deviations from the moving reference have norms at most \(2q\). All 64 independent fine source directions remain admitted; no smaller preparation, later dwell or symmetry is imposed.

Apply the same jump to the actual and reference phases. Their differences \(r=x-x^*\), \(\zeta=\theta-\theta^*\) have no jump. The support and diffusion operator remain fixed. Consequently the exact integrated heat identity from the acquisition proof applies piecewise across the event, with the same global constants

\[ \lambda_2(L)>1/3,\qquad \|L\|_2\le8,\qquad \|S(\theta)-S(\theta^*)\|_2\le8\|\zeta\|_2. \]

It gives, on either paired branch throughout \(0\le s\le8\),

\[ Z_8=2q(1+\bar\gamma)3^{32},\qquad R_8=2q+24\bar\gamma Z_8,\qquad \|\zeta\|_2\le Z_8,\quad\|r\|_2\le R_8. \tag{6} \]

Here \(\bar\gamma\) is an outward upper bound, and \(2\gamma^2\tau=4s\le32\). The form deviation stays globally mean zero. This is the original-source comparison with a moving exact reference, not a new source at the event and not a local energy trap.

For every marked C9 the reference's internal edge branches remain \(\alpha\). Actual branches therefore lie in \([\alpha-2Z_8,\alpha+2Z_8]\subset(0,\pi/2)\); their residual differences telescope around the cycle. The branch integer on the closing edge is retained, giving winding one throughout the declared interval. The uniform event translations preserve that winding exactly at the jump.

docs.title: 4. Disruption and a finite restoring response
docs.text:
Put \(a=1+2\varepsilon\). The earlier source theorem supplies

\[ 1/1200<\Delta_4<1/500,\qquad 0<B_4<1/64, \quad 0\le-u_4/\gamma\le a\Delta_4, \quad 0\le-v_4/\gamma\le aB_4. \]

In the notation of (5), this says directly \(0\le y_D(0)\le a\Delta_4\) and \(0\le y_B(0)\le aB_4<aB(0)\). Also \(B(0)<4/15\), \(K(0)=1/4\), and \(z(0)=0\).

For \(0<\varepsilon<10^{-7}\), the domain

\[ \begin{split} &0<D\le D(0),\quad 0<B\le B(0),\quad 0<K\le1/4,\\ &0\le y_D\le aD,\qquad 0\le y_B\le aB, \qquad 0\le z\le2aK \end{split}\tag{7} \]

is invariant. At either \(y=aD\) boundary, the scaled outward derivative is at most \((1-a+\varepsilon a^2)D<0\); replacing the forcing by \(\sin D\cos K\le D\) only strengthens that bound. At \(z=2aK\), it is at most \(4(1-a+\varepsilon a^2)K<0\). Lower velocity boundaries have nonnegative derivatives. The cones imply positive exponential lower bounds for all three gaps, precluding a finite-time exit through zero.

Thus the three positive gaps decrease. Elementary sine/cosine bounds on the above rectangular domain give

\[ \sin B\cos K\ge(19/20)B,\qquad (\cos B+\cos D)\sin K\ge(19/10)K. \tag{8} \]

For example, use \(\sin B/B\ge1-B^2/6\), \(\cos K\ge1-K^2/2\), and the corresponding bounds for \(B<4/15\), \(D<1/500\), \(K\le1/4\). The variation-of-constants formulas for the velocities, their nonnegative initial values and monotonicity of \(B,K\) then imply

\[ B(h)\le(B_4+1/4)e^{-(19/20)(h-\varepsilon)},\qquad K(h)\le\tfrac14e^{-(19/10)(h-\varepsilon/2)}. \tag{9} \]

Define \(B_+,K_+\) by these right sides at \(h=4\), with outward source/coefficient bounds. The fixed inequalities give \(B_++K_+<1/50\). At the event, every parent-zero same-slot gap is at least \(B_4+1/2-2Z_{\rm pre}>1/4\), so the entire actual family leaves that parent's registration domain. Here \(Z_{\rm pre}\) is the previous acquisition phase-error bound, valid at \(s=4\).

At the fixed recovery deadline, let \(X_g\) be the actual parent form mean and \(\Phi_g\) the mean of \(\theta_{g,a,j}-\psi_j\). The latter equals the raw lifted phase mean because the winding carrier has zero mean. Define the phase residual using those offsets, not by subtracting only the parent mean from the primitive winding phase:

\[ r_{\theta,g}=\max_{a,j}|\theta_{g,a,j}-\psi_j-\Phi_g|, \qquad r_{x,g}=\max_{a,j}|x_{g,a,j}-X_g|. \]

Both actual parents then satisfy

\[ \begin{split} \max_j|\theta_{g,1,j}-\theta_{g,0,j}| &\le B_++K_++2Z_8<1/4,\\ r_{\theta,g}&\le(B_++K_+)/2+2Z_8<1/100,\\ r_{x,g}&\le\bar\gamma(1+2\bar\varepsilon)(B_++K_+)/2 +2R_8<1/100. \end{split}\tag{10} \]

The last two residuals are taken about each actual parent mean. They use \(|B\pm K|\le B+K\) and \(|V\pm W|\le\gamma a(B+K)\), together with the full-source deviations. Thus the parents return even to the stronger centiradian domain, with all children retained. This proves a finite return by the supplied deadline, not indefinite post-return stability or physical binding.

docs.title: 5. A finite interaction that four parent coordinates cannot determine
docs.text:
Let \(d=\Delta_4\). In the intervened reference, the hidden mode \(K\) reduces the external restoring current to \(\sin D\cos K\). The invariant cone gives \(K(h)\ge(1/4)e^{-2ah}\). Therefore the missing unit-time restoring factor obeys

\[ I_K:=\int_0^1[1-\cos K(h)]dh \ge\frac{1-e^{-4a}}{192a}>1/200. \tag{11} \]

This uses \(1-\cos K\ge K^2/3\) on \([0,1/4]\). One simple rational lower bound for implementation replaces the numerator by \(1-e^{-4}\) and the denominator by \(192\bar a\).

Write \(G(t,d)=2\arctan(e^{-t}\tan(d/2))\) for the solution of \(G_t=-\sin G\). The gradient approximation with the actual reference history \(K(h)\) ends at \(G(1-I_K,d)\); the no-event gradient approximation ends at \(G(1,d)\). Since \(G\) decreases and \(G(1,d)\ge d/e\),

\[ \begin{split} G(1-I_K,d)-G(1,d) &\ge I_K\sin G(1,d)\\ &>\frac1{200}\frac3{10000} =\frac3{2\cdot10^6}. \end{split}\tag{12} \]

Indeed \(\sin G(1,d)>(99/100)d/e>3/10000\), using \(d>1/1200\), \(d<1/500\) and \(e<11/4\). This is a finite response bound, not the already known instantaneous port-current difference.

The gradient approximations are controlled without replacing either form row. For the intervened reference, let \(f=\sin D\cos K\) and \(\ell=y_D-f\). Then

\[ \ell_h=-\ell/\varepsilon-f_h,\qquad |\ell(0)|<1/400,\qquad |f_h|\le a d(1+2K(0)^2)<1/400. \tag{13} \]

The bounds follow directly from (7), with the actual acquired initial form coordinate in (5). Exponential convolution gives \(\int_0^1|\ell|dh<\varepsilon/200\). The time-dependent gradient row \(-\sin D\cos K(h)\) is nonexpansive on the positive small-angle domain, so this integral bounds its endpoint error. The no-event reference retains the previous lag error at most \(\varepsilon/10\). A common safe bound for their sum is \(\varepsilon/5\).

Each actual branch differs from its corresponding reference parent phase gap by at most \(2Z_8\). Combining this with (12)-(13) proves the prospectively selected contrast for every paired original source:

\[ D_{\rm actual,kick}(5)-D_{\rm actual,control}(5) >\frac3{2\cdot10^6}-\frac{\bar\varepsilon}{5}-4Z_8 >10^{-6}. \tag{14} \]

Both actual preparations have exactly the same four parent means immediately after the event. The induced event map on those four observations is the identity. Their later responses nevertheless differ by (14), so those four coordinates alone do not determine this finite response. An intervention label, retained child association or memory would supply additional state; the result does not exclude such an augmented predictor. In particular, one forecast based only on the common four-coordinate state must miss at least one paired endpoint by more than \(5\cdot10^{-7}\), which exceeds the fixed \(10^{-7}\) prediction budget.

docs.title: 6. Eight-coordinate prediction from actual post-event observations
docs.text:
Initialize the exact four-child law from all eight actual child means just after the event, including their reached forms. In full child coordinates that law is

\[ X_h=\frac{-\bar L X+\gamma\bar S(\phi)}{2\gamma^2}, \qquad \phi_h=\frac{\bar L X}{2\gamma}, \tag{15} \]

where \(\bar L\) is the unit square Laplacian and \(\bar S\) sums sine currents over its two neighbors. This transforms both rows of the existing eight-coordinate restriction; it installs no additional law and makes no exact-quotient claim for arbitrary fine states.

The averaging projection onto child means is orthogonal after constant lifting. For a 36-vector of fine errors, its four mean errors therefore have Euclidean norm at most one third of the fine norm. Also \(\|\bar L\|_2=4\), so the same integrated-heat argument amplifies the predictor's initial phase/form discrepancy by at most \(e^{2h}\). The parent gap is the child-mean linear observation with coefficients \((-1/2,-1/2,1/2,1/2)\), of norm one. Consequently, at the readout,

\[ |D_{\rm actual}-D_{\rm eight}| \le\frac{Z_8+e^2(Z_{\rm pre}+\bar\gamma R_{\rm pre})}{3} <2Z_8+18(Z_8+\bar\gamma R_8)<10^{-7}. \tag{16} \]

The first term is the actual fine-source error about the moving reference; the second carries the eight-coordinate predictor's true initialization. Using the looser shared bound in the last expression keeps every original fine direction and the fixed resolution. These correlations come from the carried source and event history. A generic parent residual ball or a tangent restriction alone would not justify this slow-time prediction.

docs.title: 7. Event work and its actual-state correction
docs.text:
With the complete storage from the acquisition theorem, the exact jump is

\[ W_T=H(T(x,\theta))-H(x,\theta) =\sum_{\text{affected }\{i,k\}} [\cos(\theta_k-\theta_i)-\cos(\theta_k-\theta_i+\delta_{ik})]. \tag{17} \]

All forms, internal C9 phase differences and support remain unchanged. There is no additional form-storage term. The nine intraparent contacts of parent zero have relative increment \(1/2\); the eighteen outer contacts have increments of magnitude \(1/4\). On the moving pre-event reference,

\[ W_T^*(B_4,\Delta_4) =9[\cos B_4-\cos(B_4+1/2)] +18\cos\Delta_4[1-\cos(1/4)]. \tag{18} \]

The acquired residual child means need not vanish. There is no first-order cancellation analogous to the initial attachment, and no quadratic error claim is made. For \(g_k(v)=\cos v-\cos(v+k)\), \(|g_k'(v)|\le|k|\); each actual edge-gap error is at most \(2Z_{\rm pre}\). Thus

\[ |W_T-W_T^*|\le18Z_{\rm pre}. \tag{19} \]

Elementary bounds using \(0<B_4<1/64\) and the small positive outer gap give

\[ 1<W_T^*<225/128, \qquad 0<W_T<3. \tag{20} \]

For the upper bound, the intraparent term is at most \(9(B_4/2+1/8)\), and the outer term at most \(18/32\). For the lower bound, the intraparent term alone exceeds \(9[1-\cos(1/2)]>1\). The signed correction (19) leaves strict margin to the fixed external-work budget. This event is not passive, its occurrence is supplied, and earlier continuous loss does not fund it. The original preparation and initial contact work remain separate obligations.

docs.text:

docs.title: Complete state, potential and reciprocal law
docs.text:
Keep all 27 nodes, the 27 internal cycle edges and the two bridges (4,13) and (13,22). All edges have unit weight. Node order is 9*c+j, with component index c=0,1,2 and local index j=0,...,8. Let \(L\) be the unnormalized graph Laplacian,

For \(0\le\lambda\le1\), define

\[ q=Lx,\qquad S_{\lambda,i}=\sum_{j\sim i}j_\lambda( heta_j- heta_i),\qquad abla U_\lambda=-S_\lambda. ag{3} \]

In the original clock and the structural clock respectively, the complete rows are

\[ egin{array}{ll} \displaystyle rac{dx}{dt}=-eD^{-1}q+ rac w\pi D^{-1}S_\lambda, &\displaystyle rac{d heta}{dt}= rac w\pi D^{-1}q,\[3pt] x'=-Ax+\gamma D^{-1}S_\lambda, & heta'=\gamma Ax. \end{array} ag{4} \]

No laboratory time, energy unit, inverse-mass interpretation or physical identity is supplied.

For

\[ H_\lambda= rac12x^TLx+U_\lambda( heta), \]
