The skew part cancels between the two rows. Consequently, on the actual full state,

\[ H_\lambda'=-(Lx)^TD^{-1}(Lx)\le0,\qquad rac{dH_\lambda}{dt}=-e(Lx)^TD^{-1}(Lx). ag{6} \]

The same positive loss law is retained, not merely its value on a target. Odd edge currents and Laplacian row sums also give

\[ (\mathbf1^TDx)'=0,\qquad (\mathbf1^TD heta)'=0. ag{7} \]

These are lifted means in the declared coordinates, not circular-resultant angles. Adding the same constant to all forms or to all phases preserves the dynamics and storage differences.

docs.title: Global admission and constitutive derivative bounds
docs.text:
For every real gap and integer \(r\ge0\), differentiating (2) gives

\[ |j_\lambda^{(r)}(\delta)| \le1+\frac{\lambda}{2187} \left(9^r+\frac{18^r}{2}\right). \tag{8} \]

In particular, \(|j_\lambda'|\le1+2\lambda/243\). Thus the complete real-lift field (4) is globally Lipschitz: its form-row difference is bounded by \(2\|\Delta x\|_\infty+ 2\gamma(1+2\lambda/243)\|\Delta\theta\|_\infty\), and its phase-row difference by \(2\gamma\|\Delta x\|_\infty\). It has a unique global solution from every finite full state, in either time direction, between the explicitly supplied events. This does not assert global convergence to one winding target.

Equation (8) supplies real derivative bounds for this law. Although (2) also extends analytically to complex phases, its ninth and eighteenth harmonics have different complex growth from sine. The earlier sine Cauchy tails, source bounds, finite-time intervals and error budgets do not transfer without a new estimate.

docs.title: Target storage and full local dynamics agree
docs.text:
Let \(\alpha=2\pi/9\), choose mediator class \(k\in\{1,2\}\), and use the nominal joined target

\[ x=0,\qquad \Theta_{k,9c+j}=k_c\alpha(j-4),\qquad (k_0,k_1,k_2)=(1,k,1). \tag{9} \]

Each cycle's principal edge gaps are \(\pm k_c\alpha\); the bridges have gap zero. The closing-edge lifts differ by known full turns, which do not change the periodic current or its derivatives. Direct differentiation gives

\[ \begin{split} W''(\delta)&=\frac{\cos9\delta-\cos18\delta}{243},\\ W'''(\delta)&=\frac{-\sin9\delta+2\sin18\delta}{27},\\ W''''(\delta)&=\frac{-\cos9\delta+4\cos18\delta}{3}. \end{split}\tag{10} \]

At every \(\delta=2\pi m/9\), \(m\in\mathbb Z\),

\[ W=W'=W''=W'''=0,\qquad W''''=1. \tag{11} \]

Therefore both classes have the same equilibrium, target storage value, gradient and full phase Hessian for every \(\lambda\). In particular,

\[ H_{*,k}=18(1-\cos\alpha)+9(1-\cos k\alpha),\qquad L_{c,k}=\nabla^2U_\lambda(\Theta_k) \]

are independent of \(\lambda\). Opposite internal currents cancel at every cycle node, and both bridge currents vanish. The full 54-coordinate tangent is

\[ J_k=\begin{pmatrix}-A&-\gamma D^{-1}L_{c,k}\\ \gamma A&0\end{pmatrix}. \tag{12} \]

The entire quadratic field is also identical: it consumes \(j_\lambda''=V_\lambda'''\), whose target values do not change. The cubic field consumes \(j_\lambda'''=V_\lambda''''\), and does change. No hidden quadratic mode is removed by this matching statement.

docs.title: A locally re-admitted identity and exact event work
docs.text:
Let \(y=\theta-\Theta_k\), \(P_0=I-\mathbf1\mathbf1^T/27\), and \(Z^2=\|P_0x\|_2^2+\|P_0y\|_2^2\). This is a quotient radius, not an operation that resets the state or its weighted means. Within \(Z\le r=1/12\), every edge residual has magnitude at most \(\sqrt2r\). The graph diameter is ten: four cycle edges, the two bridges, then four cycle edges suffice between any pair. For any real vector \(v\), its range and the variance bound give \(\|P_0v\|_2^2\le27\operatorname{range}(v)^2/4 \le(135/2)v^TLv\), by Cauchy-Schwarz along a shortest path joining its extreme values. Thus \(\lambda_2(L)\ge2/135\), independently of the phase law. The existing angular bound is \(\cos(4\pi/9+\sqrt2r)>1/20\). It also follows from \(\pi>31/10\), \(\sqrt2<17/12\) and \(\sin(13/240)>13/240-(13/240)^3/6>1/20\).

Writing \(c=\cos9\delta\), equation (10) gives \(W''=(1+c-2c^2)/243\ge-2/243\). Hence throughout this chart,

\[ V_\lambda''>\frac1{20}-\frac2{243} =\frac{203}{4860}>\frac1{25}. \tag{13} \]

Integrating the Hessian along the segment from the target yields

\[ H_\lambda-H_{*,k} \ge\frac12x^TLx+\frac1{50}y^TLy \ge\frac{Z^2}{3375}. \tag{14} \]

An initial state inside the chart with relative storage below \(r^2/3375=1/486000\) cannot reach its boundary under unforced flow, by (6) and (14). The target is the unique phase critical orbit there. On a fixed weighted-mean leaf the trapped sublevel is compact. The largest invariant subset with zero loss has \(Lx=0\); invariance then requires \(D^{-1}\nabla U_\lambda\) to be common across nodes. Its degree-weighted sum is zero, so that gradient vanishes. Thus LaSalle's argument gives local convergence to the corresponding target orbit. No common form or phase is forced back to zero.

For any prescribed form jump \(f\), phases do not jump, and each law has the exact work

\[ \Delta H_\lambda=f^TLx^-+\frac12f^TLf. \tag{15} \]

For simultaneous donor and receiver jumps \(f=ae_4+be_{22}\), \(L_{4,22}=0\), so (15) is \(a(Lx^-)_4+b(Lx^-)_{22}+3(a^2+b^2)/2\). It is the same functional in each model, but later pre-event states need not coincide. The weighted form mean changes by \(3(a+b)/58\), with the phase mean unchanged.

From the prescribed nominal source (9), the existing amplitudes \(a=b=m=7/10000\) give work \(3m^2<1/486000\) and \(Z_+^2=50m^2/27<r^2\). The single-input and zero-input branches also satisfy these bounds. All four branches consequently retain the joined quotient identity for both laws, without borrowing an acquisition theorem. Any support change needs its own edge-storage work; continuous loss is not an undeclared event reserve.

docs.title: A changed interaction of the same prescribed organized states
docs.text:
Use the same complete nominal pre-input state (9) in four histories with form jumps \(0,ae_4,be_{22},ae_4+be_{22}\). Observe the mediator form and define, as in the distinct-neighbor owner,

\[ M_{\lambda,k}(a,b,T)=x_{13}^{11}(T)-x_{13}^{10}(T) -x_{13}^{01}(T)+x_{13}^{00}(T). \tag{16} \]

Immediately after the joint jump, the phase slopes are \(\theta'_4=\gamma a\), \(\theta'_{22}=\gamma b\), \(\theta'_{13}=-\gamma(a+b)/4\), and \(\theta'_{12}=\theta'_{14}=0\). Thus the four incident gap slopes into node 13 are \(\gamma(5a+b)/4\), \(\gamma(a+5b)/4\), and twice \(\gamma(a+b)/4\). The first two edges are bridges; the other two are internal mediator edges.

The form derivatives through order two are linear in the impulses. The third derivative is at most quadratic. In the fourth derivative, the only cubic contribution is the current's third derivative applied to three initial gap slopes; every other term is at most quadratic. Port-fixing ring reflection with simultaneous form/phase-deviation sign reversal is a symmetry of every even potential (2). At the nominal source, the central output is odd in \((a,b)\), so its quadratic contributions vanish. Hidden quadratic modes generally remain nonzero.

The mixed bridge cubes sum to \(90ab(a+b)\), and the two mixed internal cubes sum to \(6ab(a+b)\). Including the degree-four normalization, gap denominators and \(4!\) gives the complete nonlinear local onset

\[ \begin{split} M_{\lambda,k}(a,b,T) &=\frac{\gamma^4ab(a+b)}{1024} [15j_\lambda'''(0)+j_\lambda'''(k\alpha)]T^4+O(T^5)\\ &=\boxed{\frac{16\lambda-15-\cos(k\alpha)}{1024} \gamma^4ab(a+b)T^4+O(T^5)}. \end{split}\tag{17} \]

For fixed positive \(a,b\), the sine member \(\lambda=0\) has negative onset, whereas \(\lambda=1\) has positive onset, since \(1-\cos(k\alpha)>0\) for both classes. Analyticity supplies a positive local time neighborhood in which the corresponding exact signs hold; (17) supplies no declared numerical horizon or measurement resolution.

The leading coefficient vanishes at \(\lambda_{\mathrm{crit},k}=(15+\cos k\alpha)/16\). Since \(\cos2\alpha<\cos\alpha\), \(\lambda_{\mathrm{crit},2}<\lambda_{\mathrm{crit},1}\). Between these two values the classes have opposite local orientations under one law. For example, the fixed rational \(\lambda=31/32\) gives the factor \(1/2-\cos(k\alpha)\): it is negative for class one and positive for class two because \(\alpha<\pi/3<2\alpha\). At \(\lambda=1\), the bridge contribution vanishes and the entire positive onset comes from the internal mediator edges. Omitting those edges would therefore give a false null. Within this particular family, the normalized class-one-minus-class-two coefficient remains \((\cos2\alpha-\cos\alpha)/1024\); that robustness is not asserted for every matched-target potential. At a critical value only the order-four coefficient is known to vanish; exact additivity does not follow. Zero input in either channel cancels (16) for every common source. At the nominal source, \(a=-b\) is also an exact null by outer-ring exchange and the sign symmetry.

docs.title: Own-law acquisition from the original isolated C9 sources
docs.text:
This section changes support explicitly to one isolated unit C9, with nodes \(0,\ldots,8\), edges \(j--(j+1\bmod9)\), degree matrix \(D=2I\), capacities one and the same \(e,w,\gamma\) and clocks as (4). It does not apply the joined graph's spectral bound to an isolated component or identify the two supports' reached states. The original two-class preparation supplies the following unchanged experiment for each law:

  • Classes \(k=1,2\), rational slope \(m=(2046/9)(355/113)^2\), initial form \(x_j(0)=km(j-4)+\xi_j^x\), and initial phase lifts \(\theta_j(0)=\xi_j^\theta\).
  • Bounds \(|\xi_j^x|\le\rho_x=10^{-10}\) and \(|\xi_j^\theta|\le\rho_\theta=10^{-10}\), with separate exact zero sums \(\sum_j\xi_j^x=\sum_j\xi_j^\theta=0\). Each class has a complete sixteen-dimensional relative source neighborhood, not an independently selectable eighteen-dimensional ambient box.
  • Acquisition time \(T=100\) in \(\tau\), original time \(102400/1023\), radius \(r=1/12\), and common whole-source storage budget \(10^9\). No input, support event, state reset or coefficient change occurs.
  • Target \(x^*=0\), \(\theta_{k,j}^*=k\alpha(j-4)\), with \(\alpha=2\pi/9\). Targets label the endpoint comparison, not replacement endpoint states.

Write \(A=L/2\), \(z=\gamma x\), \(\eta=\gamma^2\), and \(f_\lambda=S_\lambda/2\). The complete scaled law is

\[ z'=-Az+\eta f_\lambda(\theta),\qquad \theta'=Az,\qquad (\theta+z)'=\eta f_\lambda(\theta). \tag{18} \]

Odd currents preserve both zero means. The full real-lift field is globally Lipschitz by (8), including nonacute states during acquisition. Continuous lifts are therefore retained through any winding changes.

For \(P_9=I-\mathbf1\mathbf1^T/9\) and the norm \(\|u\|_{2I}=\sqrt2\|u\|_2\), the C9 graph gives the same law-independent semigroup gap \(g=1/5\): \(\|e^{-A\tau}P_9\|_{2I}\le e^{-g\tau}\). Indeed \(1-\cos(2\pi/9)>1/5\), so \(\lambda_2(L)>2/5\), while \(\lambda_{\max}(L)\le4\). The forcing and Hessian constants must instead be re-admitted:

\[ \begin{aligned} J_\lambda&=1+\lambda/1458,& \|f_\lambda(\theta)\|_{2I}&\le F_\lambda=\sqrt{18}\,J_\lambda,\\ u_\lambda&=1+2\lambda/243,& \nabla^2U_\lambda(\theta)&\preceq u_\lambda L . \end{aligned}\tag{19} \]

The first bound uses \(|\sin9\delta-\tfrac12\sin18\delta|\le3/2\); the second uses (10) and \(\cos\delta\le1\). They hold globally, not only near a target. The raw initial metric norms remain \(\sqrt{18}\rho_\theta\) and \(\sqrt{18}\gamma\rho_x\); multiplying those errors by the enlarged forcing constant would confuse distinct premises.

The nominal phase storage initially vanishes. Since \(1-\cos(9v)\le81v^2/2\), the new potential term obeys \(0\le W(v)\le v^4/24\). The entire source family therefore has

\[ B_{\lambda,k} =36k^2m^2+32km\rho_x+18(\rho_x^2+\rho_\theta^2) +6\lambda\rho_\theta^4 \quad\hbox{as a storage upper bound}. \tag{20} \]

The linear form term uses the sum \(16km\) of the absolute nominal edge differences; the last term uses all nine edges and \(|\Delta\xi^\theta|\le2\rho_\theta\). The exact nominal costs \(36k^2m^2\) are unchanged and differ by a factor four. The quartic source correction is retained even though at these budgets it is below one dyadic128 grid spacing. No equality of later losses or phase histories follows.

Let \(\rho\) be an outward upper bound for \(e^{-g T}\). Define

\[ \begin{aligned} V_k&=\sqrt{120}\,k\gamma m,& E_x&=\sqrt{18}\gamma\rho_x,& E_\theta&=\sqrt{18}\rho_\theta,\\ R_{z,\lambda,k}&=\rho(V_k+E_x)+\eta F_\lambda/g,& R_{x,\lambda,k}&=R_{z,\lambda,k}/(\gamma\sqrt2),\\ D_k&=\sqrt{60}\,k|\gamma m-\alpha|,& Y_{\lambda,k}&=D_k+ (E_x+E_\theta+R_{z,\lambda,k}+\eta F_\lambda T)/\sqrt2,\\ Z_{\lambda,k}^2&=R_{x,\lambda,k}^2+Y_{\lambda,k}^2 . \end{aligned}\tag{21} \]

Variation of constants bounds \(\|z(T)\|_{2I}\) by \(R_z\). Integrating the last row of (18) gives

\[ \theta(T)-\gamma x^{\rm nom}(0) =\xi^\theta+\gamma\xi^x-z(T) +\eta\int_0^T f_\lambda(\theta(s))\,ds . \]

Consequently every actual endpoint satisfies \(\|x(T)\|_2\le R_x\), \(\|\theta(T)-\theta_k^*\|_2\le Y\) and the full radius bound \(Z^2\). This uses the entire nonlinear forcing and all initial residuals; it is not a tangent trajectory or a Cartesian reset of the reached family.

Target stationarity and the global Hessian upper bound yield the split endpoint estimate

\[ H_\lambda(T)-H_k^* \le E_{\lambda,k}:= 2R_{x,\lambda,k}^2+2u_\lambda Y_{\lambda,k}^2,\qquad H_k^*=9(1-\cos k\alpha). \tag{22} \]

The form and phase terms retain their different coefficients. For the common capture ball set

\[ \mu=\pi/2-4\pi/9-\sqrt2r,\quad c_r=\cos(4\pi/9+\sqrt2r),\quad c_\lambda=c_r-2\lambda/243,\quad b_\lambda=c_\lambda r^2/5 . \tag{23} \]

When \(\mu>0\) and \(c_\lambda>0\), the own-law phase Hessian throughout the ball is bounded below by \(c_\lambda L\). With the zero means and the isolated graph gap, this gives \(H_\lambda-H_k^*\ge(c_\lambda/5) (\|x\|_2^2+\|\theta-\theta_k^*\|_2^2)\). Thus \(Z_{\lambda,k}^2<r^2\) and \(E_{\lambda,k}<b_\lambda\) prove forward trapping under the own-law identity \(H_\lambda'=-\|Lx\|_2^2/2\).

docs.title: Uniform fixed-budget result and its provenance
docs.text:
The shared outward dyadic128 square-root, Machin-pi, cosine and negative-exponential arithmetic applied to (19)--(23) at \(\lambda=1\) gives the following strict rational bounds for both classes:

\[ \begin{gathered} \mu>56/1000,\qquad c_1>48/1000,\qquad Z_{1,k}^2<23/10^6<r^2,\\ E_{1,k}<45/10^6,\qquad b_1>672/10^7,\qquad b_1-E_{1,k}>222/10^7,\\ B_{1,1}<181230000,\qquad B_{1,2}<724918000<10^9 . \end{gathered}\tag{24} \]

Here the subscript one on \(c_1,b_1\) means deformation one, not winding class one. The bounds are rounded outward from direct scalar interval evaluation of the displayed formulas, not from a sampled trajectory or the earlier sine report. In particular the computed storage-margin lower bounds exceed \(2.29504274\,10^{-5}\) for winding one and \(2.22733831\,10^{-5}\) for winding two.

Only the endpoint \(\lambda=1\) is needed: \(F_\lambda,u_\lambda\), the source-cost bound and the endpoint bounds increase with \(\lambda\), whereas \(c_\lambda,b_\lambda\) decrease. Hence (24) proves acquisition and capture uniformly for all \(0\le\lambda\le1\), including both laws used in (17). This is an analytic family argument, not a parameter sweep.

Every initial phase edge has its small principal lift, so winding starts at zero. Endpoint membership in the target's acute ball fixes winding \(k\); it remains there thereafter. The change requires an intervening antipodal passage, allowed by (18); an acute constraint during the whole acquisition would be a different model. On the compact trapped zero-mean leaf, zero loss forces \(x=0\), and invariance forces \(S_\lambda=0\). Strict phase convexity leaves only \(\theta_k^*\). LaSalle therefore gives convergence; the unchanged positive target Hessian also retains local exponential stability of the complete form/phase tangent. For each positive eigenvalue \(\ell\) of \(L/2\), its characteristic polynomial is \(s^2+\ell s+\gamma^2\cos(k\alpha)\ell^2\), whose roots have negative real parts. Winding magnitudes one and two remain inequivalent under cycle automorphisms, common origins and joint sign reversal.

This establishes acquisition from the same prescribed source family, with the same time, uncertainty and cost limits. It does not identify the reached fine states between laws, reproduce later very small residual budgets, or transfer a dwell, support-contact, joined-source or finite-response certificate. Those require the new law's own bounds.

docs.title: Carrying actual acquired states through recovery and contact
docs.text:
Use three copies of the original class-one ramp family from the acquisition section, each with its full separate zero-sum form and phase residuals bounded by \(10^{-10}\). Use \(\lambda=0\) or \(\lambda=1\) consistently throughout each complete history. At \(\tau=100\), each actual state is in the forward-trapped radius-\(r=1/12\) neighborhood of its isolated winding-one target. The following dwell changes no source, mean, state coordinate or law.

Re-admit the modified-energy argument using the actual nonlinear potential. Put \(g=1/5\), \(\Lambda=2\), \(c_\lambda=\cos(4\pi/9+\sqrt2r)-2\lambda/243\), and \(u_\lambda=1+2\lambda/243\). The common lower curvature is conservative for class one. On the retained mean-zero chart, with \(y=\theta-\Theta_1\), the proof coordinates \(\xi=A^{-1/2}y\), \(v=\gamma A^{1/2}x\) obey

\[ \xi'=v,\qquad v'=-Av-\nabla\mathcal W_\lambda(\xi),\qquad \mathcal W_\lambda=\frac{\eta}{2} [U_\lambda(\Theta_1+A^{1/2}\xi)-U_\lambda(\Theta_1)]. \]

With freshly reconstructed \(\underline\eta,\overline\eta\), its Hessian lies between \(\mu I\) and \(MI\), where

\[ \mu=\underline\eta c_\lambda g^2,\quad M=\overline\eta u_\lambda\Lambda^2,\quad \epsilon_L=g/4, \quad a_-=\mu/2+g^2/16,\quad a_+=M/2+\epsilon_L\Lambda/2+\epsilon_L^2. \]

The upper coefficient includes this law's \(u_\lambda\). Target tangent matching does not justify setting it to one. The modified energy

\[ \mathcal V=\tfrac12\|v\|^2+\mathcal W_\lambda +\epsilon_L\xi^Tv+\tfrac{\epsilon_L}{2}\xi^TA\xi \]

satisfies the same algebraic sandwich and derivative inequality,

\[ \tfrac14\|v\|^2+a_-\|\xi\|^2\le\mathcal V \le\tfrac34\|v\|^2+a_+\|\xi\|^2,\qquad \mathcal V'\le-\kappa\mathcal V, \quad \kappa=\min\{4(g-\epsilon_L)/3,\epsilon_L\mu/a_+\}. \]

This controls the actual nonlinear evolution inside its already admitted trap. It is not a tangent-only convergence claim.

Fix a common unforced dwell \(D=10^{13}\) in \(\tau\). The elementary own-law bounds \(0.048<c_\lambda<0.06\), \(9\,10^{-8}<\eta<10^{-7}\), \(u_\lambda<1.01\) give

\[ a_->1/400,\quad 21/400<a_+<53/1000,\quad 10^{-10}<\kappa<8/(35\,10^9),\quad 1000<\kappa D<16000/7<4096. \]

The initial modified-energy bound is \(V_0=3\overline\eta\Lambda b_x^2/4+a_+b_\theta^2/g<1/500\), using the freshly proved acquisition radii. Thus \(e^{-\kappa D}<2^{-512}\), with an exponent inside the shared arithmetic work limit. Exact rational return estimates yield

\[ \|x\|_2^2\le\frac{4V_0\,2^{-512}}{\underline\eta g} <\frac{4\,10^6}{9}2^{-512}<10^{-148},\qquad \|y\|_2^2\le\frac{\Lambda V_0\,2^{-512}}{a_-} <\frac85\,2^{-512}<10^{-148}. \]

Both norms are consequently below \(\varepsilon=10^{-70}\) at the common actual handoff \(\tau_h=100+10^{13}\), or \(t_h=(1024/1023)(100+10^{13})\). These conservative structural budgets are not laboratory times. The tiny bounds are retained as exact rationals.

Now prescribe the two bridges \((4,13)\), \((13,22)\), keeping the reached state unchanged. Each new edge has form and phase differences at most \(2\varepsilon\), so its actual work and the total joined excess obey

\[ 0\le\Delta H_{\rm attach}\le4(1+u_\lambda)\varepsilon^2, \qquad H_\lambda^- -H_{*,1}\le10(1+u_\lambda)\varepsilon^2. \]

The second estimate combines three isolated excesses bounded by \(2(1+u_\lambda)\varepsilon^2\) with both bridge costs. It preserves the relative phase origins and includes form storage. No loss is spent as an undeclared event reserve.

For each prescribed input \(f=ae_4+be_{22}\), with \((a,b)\in\{0,m\}^2\), \(m=7/10000\), formula (15) gives

\[ \left|\Delta H_{\rm input}-\tfrac32(a^2+b^2)\right| \le6(a+b)\varepsilon, \]

and the actual quotient radius after that input satisfies

\[ Z_+^2\le6\varepsilon^2+2(a+b)\varepsilon+a^2+b^2 -(a+b)^2/27<r^2. \]

Every branch's complete excess is less than \(1/486000\), because the largest nominal input work is \(3m^2=1.47\,10^{-6}\) and the retained corrections fit strictly below that barrier. Equations (13)--(14) therefore preserve the joined identity throughout all four unforced observation histories and afterwards. Contact and input occurrence are supplied events, not consequences of passivity or an autonomous selector.

The new degree-weighted means are retained explicitly. Just before input,

\[ \bar x_D^-=(x_4+2x_{13}+x_{22})/58,\quad \bar y_D^-=(y_4+2y_{13}+y_{22})/58,\quad |\bar x_D^-|,|\bar y_D^-|\le2\varepsilon/29. \]

Input adds \(3(a+b)/58\) only to the form mean. The four-history mean combination cancels by common pre-input state and affine jumps; individual histories need not have zero means. Reached states and event work need not agree between laws. Within each law all four branches share the same actual pre-input state. The entire joined raw state remains within \(\varepsilon\) of its nominal target before those inputs, which supplies the next proof's actual-state premise without resetting it.

docs.title: A finite observation with the actual law's nonlinear remainder
docs.text:
This section fixes the mediator to class one, both endpoint laws \(\lambda\in\{0,1\}\), and the same two form impulses \(a=b=m=7/10000\). It proves a finite nominal estimate and its transfer to a full pre-input state within a declared radius. The following bounds use the alternative law's real derivatives, including its extra harmonics. They do not reuse a sine complex-analytic tail or evaluate a time-coefficient producer, a trajectory or a reserved response.

In the estimates below, \(t\) denotes elapsed \(\tau\)-time, not the original clock; the observation duration is converted back explicitly.

For a nominal post-input branch write \(u=ae_4+be_{22}\), with each amplitude either zero or \(m\), and introduce the analytical coordinate \(v=(\theta-\Theta_1)/\gamma\). The pair \(X=(x,v)\) retains all 54 coordinates; this scaling is neither a reduced model nor a phase reset. Use the maximum norm on this pair. The target-normalized quadratic and cubic current maps, including their factorials, are denoted by \(Q,C\). Their static target jets in (11) give

\[ \|Q(v,w)\|_\infty\le2\|v\|_\infty\|w\|_\infty, \qquad \|C(v,w,z)\|_\infty\le\frac43 \|v\|_\infty\|w\|_\infty\|z\|_\infty. \]

Indeed \(|j''|\le1\) and \(|j'''|\le1\) at every target edge for these two laws and class one. The fourth-derivative bound is instead the own-law global value from (8), \(|j_\lambda^{(4)}|\le1+(9^4+18^4/2)/2187=28\). Taylor's real remainder on each complete edge therefore gives the exact field

\[ X'=\mathcal J X+ \bigl(\gamma^3Q(v,v)+\gamma^4C(v,v,v)+R_4(v),0\bigr), \qquad \|R_4(v)\|_\infty\le\frac{56}{3}\gamma^5\|v\|_\infty^4, \]

where \(\mathcal J\) is the full tangent in these scaled coordinates. The normalized Laplacian and target phase Hessian have maximum-norm operator bounds two. Thus \(\|\mathcal J\|_\infty<3\), and the complete scaled field is globally Lipschitz with constant below three because \(2+2\gamma^2(1+2/243)<3\). For \(0\le t\le1/100\), \(e^{3t}<11/10\); this last rational bound also follows from \(e^{3/100}\le(1-3/100)^{-1}<11/10\).

Define the first three full amplitude variations by variation of constants: \(X_1=e^{\mathcal Jt}(u,0)\), with the second and third forced by \((\gamma^3Q(v_1,v_1),0)\) and \((2\gamma^3Q(v_1,v_2)+\gamma^4C(v_1,v_1,v_1),0)\), respectively. These are definitions used in inequalities, not evaluated histories. The phase row is always \(v_i'=Ax_i\). Direct integration gives

\[ \begin{array}{lll} \|X_1\|_\infty\le11m/10,& \|v_1\|_\infty\le11mt/5,& \|v_1-Aut\|_\infty\le9mt^2/4,\\ \|X_2\|_\infty\le4\gamma^3m^2t^3,& \|v_2\|_\infty\le2\gamma^3m^2t^4,&\\ \|X_3\|_\infty\le4\gamma^4m^3t^4,& \|v_3\|_\infty\le2\gamma^4m^3t^5.& \end{array} \]

For example, \(\|x_1'\|_\infty<9m/4\) proves the first-row phase approximation. The second-state coefficient is at most \((11/10)2(11/5)^2/3=1331/375<4\); the third-state coefficient is at most

\[ \frac{11}{10}\left[ \frac{(4/3)(11/5)^3}{4} +\frac{(88/5)\gamma^2t^2}{6}\right]<4. \]

All these bounds use \(\gamma<1/3000\) and \(t\le1/100\). The quadratic history has not been deleted: it contributes to the third variation and can be nonzero at unobserved coordinates.

To control the entire remaining amplitude series without assuming its convergence, let \(X_{\rm app}=X_1+X_2+X_3\). Its phase coordinate satisfies \(\|v_{\rm app}\|_\infty<9mt/4\), and \(\|v_2+v_3\|_\infty\le3\gamma^3m^2t^4\). Substitution into the exact field leaves quadratic and cubic defects each bounded by \(\gamma^5m^4t^4\): their sharper coefficients relative to that quantity are at most \(18\gamma^2t^2+18\gamma^4t^4\) and \(243\gamma^2t^2/4\), respectively. The fourth-order remainder is bounded by \((56/3)(9/4)^4\gamma^5m^4t^4\). Global Lipschitz stability and time integration therefore give

\[ \|X-X_{\rm app}\|_\infty \le\frac{11}{50} \left[2+\frac{56}{3}\left(\frac94\right)^4\right] \gamma^5m^4t^5 <106\gamma^5m^4t^5. \]

It remains to compare the complete cubic history to its first nonzero time term. Since \(\|e^{\mathcal Js}-I\|_\infty\le33s/10\), transport of the leading direct force contributes at most \((44/25)\gamma^4m^3t^5\). Replacing \(v_1(s)\) by \(Au s\) in its cubic force contributes at most \((10923/1250)\gamma^4m^3t^5\): the force difference before integration is bounded by

\[ \frac43\frac94 \left[\left(\frac{11}{5}\right)^2+ 2\frac{11}{5}+4\right]m^3s^4 =\frac{993}{25}m^3s^4. \]

The retained quadratic recoupling contributes at most \((242/75)\gamma^6m^3t^6\). Consequently

\[ \left\|x_3(t)-\frac{\gamma^4}{4}C(Au,Au,Au)t^4\right\|_\infty \le\left[\frac{44}{25}+\frac{10923}{1250} +\frac{242}{75}\gamma^2t\right] \gamma^4m^3t^5 <11\gamma^4m^3t^5. \]

At the nominal source the exact reflection/sign symmetry makes the central second variation zero, while the first variation cancels in the mixed observation. Combining the last two bounds costs less than \(12\gamma^4m^3t^5\) in each nonzero-input branch, since \(106\gamma m<1\). The zero-input nominal branch stays at equilibrium. The complete onset calculation (17), with all internal and bridge edges, therefore yields the finite estimate

\[ \boxed{\left|M_{\lambda,1}(m,m,T;0) -\frac{16\lambda-15-\cos\alpha}{512} \gamma^4m^3T^4\right| \le36\gamma^4m^3T^5},\qquad 0\le T\le\frac1{100}. \]

Fix the common observation duration to \(T=10^{-6}\) in \(\tau\), or \(1024T/1023\) in the original clock. Since \(\alpha>2/3\), cosine monotonicity and its alternating Taylor bound give \(\cos\alpha<1-2/9+2/243=191/243<4/5\). This and \(\gamma>1/3300\), together with \(1/2560-36/10^6>1/3000\), give opposite nominal signs with the same explicit lower margin:

\[ M_{1,1}(m,m,T;0)>S,\qquad M_{0,1}(m,m,T;0)<-S, \qquad S=\frac{m^3T^4}{3000\,3300^4}>9\,10^{-52}. \]

Now retain an actual pre-input full state satisfying \(\|(x,\theta-\Theta_1)\|_\infty\le\varepsilon=10^{-70}\), with its actual continuous lifts. Each law's four branches start from that same reached state before their prescribed form inputs. In these unscaled coordinates the global field Lipschitz constant is also below three. Each actual-to-nominal branch discrepancy at the observation time is below \(2\varepsilon\), hence the mixed discrepancy is below \(8\varepsilon\). This estimate retains arbitrary symmetry-breaking residuals; it does not impose nominal reflection on a reached source.

Declare a supplied absolute error allowance \(\delta=10^{-54}\) for each of the four raw mediator readings. Their mixed reading has error at most \(4\delta\), and \(8\varepsilon+4\delta<10^{-53}\). Thus every admitted reached state and every admitted readout error preserve the signs, with measured mixed responses above \(8\,10^{-52}\) for \(\lambda=1\) and below \(-8\,10^{-52}\) for \(\lambda=0\).

This is a prospective mathematical observation allowance. Its very small scale is not established laboratory resolution, and the finite horizon is in structural time. Reaching the pre-input radius, preserving identity at contact, and accounting for support and impulse work are supplied by the own-law handoff above. The theorem supplies neither a physical identification nor an evaluated experimental response.

docs.title: Independent scalar calibration and the recorded distinction
docs.text:
Retain both complete laws, the original acquired class-one sources, their own-law recovery, attachment work, four prescribed inputs and fixed \(T=10^{-6}\) in structural \(\tau\)-time from the preceding theorem. Every elapsed duration below uses that clock. This section changes only the prospective observation. For each law write its four actual mediator readings as \(Y_{ij}=x_{13}^{ij}(T)\), and supply one static scalar sensor

\[ r_{ij}=h(Y_{ij})+\eta_{ij},\qquad |\eta_{ij}|\le\delta_h. \]

The same \(h\) is used in all four histories and both candidate laws. Its domain, orientation, units and calibration are specified independently of those responses. No particular sensor is measured here. The error \(\delta_h\) is in sensor units, not a transferred raw-form error allowance. The map is a passive observation, not a state-chart change; it changes none of the laws, inputs, capacities, clocks or work balances.

docs.title: Absolute operating range and single-input increments
docs.text:
Let \(\varepsilon=10^{-70}\), \(m=7/10000\), and

\[ q=Y_{00},\qquad u=Y_{10}-q,\qquad v=Y_{01}-q,\qquad M=Y_{11}-Y_{10}-Y_{01}+q. \]

These are actual readings, with no resetting or subtraction of a newly chosen source mean. The full unscaled vector field is globally Lipschitz with constant below three. Within one law, branches with and without one input have initial full-state maximum-norm distance \(m\), while their mediator form initially agrees. Hence

\[ |u|,\ |v|\le m(e^{3T}-1)<4mT=:B. \]

Indeed the mediator derivative difference is bounded by \(3me^{3t}\); integrating it and using \(e^{3T}\le(1-3T)^{-1}\) proves the estimate. The same argument bounds \(|Y_{11}-q|<B\), because the two simultaneous inputs still have maximum norm \(m\). The zero-input branch stays within \(2\varepsilon\) of its nominal equilibrium, so \(|q|<2\varepsilon\). The raw readings therefore lie in the smaller interval with radius \(R_{\rm raw}=2\varepsilon+B\). Every \(q+s+t\) with \(s\) between zero and \(u\) and \(t\) between zero and \(v\), and the segment from \(q+u+v\) to \(Y_{11}\), lie in

\[ [-R_*,R_*],\qquad R_*=2\varepsilon+2B<10^{-8}. \]

This derives an absolute operating range from the admitted source origins; common form shifts would require a correspondingly shifted calibrated domain. The individually nonzero post-input means are still retained.

docs.title: Calibration for a mixed threshold and the opposite signs
docs.text:
Supply a convex interval \(I\) containing \([-R_*,R_*]\), a sensor \(h\in C^2(I)\), and independently justified constants

\[ h'(z)\ge g>0,\qquad |h''(z)|\le K \quad(z\in I),\qquad \delta_h\ge0. \]

Here \(g\) has sensor units per form unit and \(K\) has sensor units per squared form unit. An arbitrary common sensor offset cancels. No upper gain bound is needed for the following one-sided sign certificate. Two applications of the fundamental theorem of calculus give the exact identity

\[ \begin{split} h(Y_{11})-h(Y_{10})-h(Y_{01})+h(Y_{00}) &=a_h M+\int_0^u\int_0^v h''(q+s+t)\,dt\,ds,\\ a_h&=\int_0^1 h'(q+u+v+\sigma M)\,d\sigma\ge g. \end{split} \]

The integrals are oriented when an increment is negative; their absolute value is at most \(K|uv|\le KB^2\). Let \(s_0,s_1>0\) be the fresh carried raw-response margins, so every admitted source obeys \(M_0\le-s_0\) and \(M_1\ge s_1\). These margins include the full nonlinear tail and actual-state residual, but no raw-reading error: the sensor error is added separately. The recorded mixed scalars therefore obey

\[ M_{r,0}\le-\sigma_0,\qquad M_{r,1}\ge\sigma_1,\qquad \sigma_\lambda=g s_\lambda-KB^2-4\delta_h. \]

Strictly positive \(\sigma_0,\sigma_1\) certify opposite recorded signs. Strict separation by a mixed threshold needs only \(\Delta_h=\sigma_0+\sigma_1>0\): the fixed threshold \((\sigma_1-\sigma_0)/2\) lies strictly between the two admitted mixed ranges even when one sign margin is nonpositive. The resulting complete four-record distance is at least \(\Delta_h/4\) in maximum norm. The four errors may be correlated or adversarial; no cancellation or independence is assumed. A nonpositive sufficient margin is an unavailable certificate for its stated statistic, not proof of observational equivalence.

One explicit prospective contract, in the chosen structural and sensor units, is

\[ I=[-10^{-8},10^{-8}],\qquad g=\tfrac12,\qquad K=10^{-35},\qquad \delta_h=10^{-54}. \]

The preceding theorem gives \(s_\lambda>8\,10^{-52}\), whereas \(KB^2=7.84\,10^{-53}\). Thus \(\sigma_\lambda>3\,10^{-52}\) under both endpoint laws. This class is nonempty and includes nonlinear maps: for example \(h(z)=b+z+z^2/(2\,10^{35})\) satisfies the contract for any fixed offset \(b\). The small curvature allowance is a calibration premise, not a discovered property of an apparatus. No laboratory access to that allowance, the source accuracy, recovery dwell or observation clock follows.

docs.title: Full records, sensor nuisance and a nonlinear sign counterexample
docs.text:
There is a separate consequence needing only positive gain. Fix one common \(h\) with \(h'\ge g\) throughout the interval containing all raw readings. For any pair of admitted raw four-vectors \(Y^0,Y^1\), possibly from different reached sources under their respective laws, the mixed functional has coefficient norm four, so

\[ \|Y^1-Y^0\|_\infty\ge\frac{s_0+s_1}{4}. \]

Applying the same increasing sensor to both vectors and then admitting their individual errors yields the complete-record bound

\[ \boxed{\ \|r^1-r^0\|_\infty \ge \frac{g(s_0+s_1)}4-2\delta_h\ }. \]

A positive right-hand side separates those four-reading record sets for that common sensor even without a curvature bound. With \(g=1/2\) and \(\delta_h=10^{-54}\) it exceeds \(10^{-52}\). This is a fixed-common-map statement, uniform over the admitted choices of that map. It does not establish separation after independently unioning the two laws over different nuisance maps \(h_0,h_1\). By contrast, whenever the curvature-based \(\Delta_h\) is positive, the same mixed threshold works for every admitted sensor, so even those separately unioned classes retain that separation. The explicit calibration above also preserves both signs. Neither argument fits an observation law to a response.

Monotonicity alone does not preserve the mixed sign, even for these actual TNFR histories. The mediator derivative difference at the input time is exactly \(m/4\) for either single input: only its adjacent form value changes, and the phases initially agree. Relative to the common target, the initial full-state norms are at most \(m+\varepsilon\) for that branch and \(\varepsilon\) for the zero-input branch. Since the field vanishes at the target, their displacements through time \(t\le T\) are bounded by \(4(m+\varepsilon)t\) and \(4\varepsilon t\). Lipschitz continuity and integration then give

\[ |u-mT/4|,\ |v-mT/4|\le6(m+2\varepsilon)T^2, \qquad u,v>mT/8. \]

The finite raw-response bound also implies \(|M_\lambda|<10^{-48}\): the absolute leading coefficient is at most \(\gamma^4m^3/32\), the additional time-tail coefficient is \(36T<1/32\), and \(\gamma<1/3000\), with the residual \(8\varepsilon\) retained. Now fix the single sensor \(h(z)=z+z^2\) on \(I=[-10^{-8},10^{-8}]\). It has \(h'(z)\ge1-2\,10^{-8}>1/2\), but its curvature is two. Its exact noiseless mixed scalar is

\[ [1+2(q+u+v)+M]M+2uv. \]

The bracket lies between \(1-2\,10^{-8}\) and \(1+2\,10^{-8}\), because it is the average derivative on the segment already admitted. Thus the recorded mixed scalar under either law exceeds

\[ \frac{m^2T^2}{32}-2\,10^{-48}-4\,10^{-54}>10^{-20}. \]

Both signs are positive although the raw signs are opposite. This example uses the actual full source families and declared error bounds, not a synthetic trajectory or an evaluated response. Nevertheless, the fixed-common-map complete-record separation above remains positive. Losing this particular mixed-sign statistic therefore does not erase the law distinction or establish an overlap of complete recorded observations.

docs.title: What this comparison constrains, and what it leaves open
docs.text:
The prescribed source in (17) is an exact organized target. The acquisition section proves own-law capture from the original isolated source families; it does not replace that nominal source by a reached fine state or transfer the onset sign to its residuals. Arbitrary residuals need not have the nominal reflection symmetry. The finite theorem above retains those residuals under its explicit pre-input radius and readout allowance, with recovery and contact now admitted separately above. Acquisition alone does not establish that smaller radius or admit contact. No sign at the earlier \(T=1/8\) is asserted for the alternative law.

The interaction differs in the held structural chart with the same form impulses and mediator readout. A common clock rescaling cannot account for it while leaving the nonzero tangent (12) fixed. This does not exclude every nonlinear conjugacy accompanied by changed inputs and observations.

The supplied additive current consumes first, ninth and eighteenth phase harmonics. Its extra information is outside a law depending only on degree and the first neighbor phasor. The existing first-moment sufficiency theorem can constrain that freedom only if its information restriction is independently justified. Restating that restriction, imposing cosine storage globally, or assuming the desired current is not a new derivation.

These complete models retain signed form, primitive circular phase, whole-state memory, common-origin covariance, held capacities and the declared identity. Additive edge currents, fixed support, constant reciprocal mobility and the pressure completion remain supplied hypotheses. No registered operator's descent, autonomous event occurrence, inherited scale law, composite binding energy or fundamental constituent follows. The foundation compatibility audit owns those distinctions; the execution plan owns subsequent work.

The separate registered-composition comparison derives inherited complete laws for two different two-C9 interfaces, with their own support work and actual-source bounds. Those conditional maps do not supply an inherited law for the three-C9 support used here.

docs.title: Implementation and independent controls
docs.text:
_sine_class_constitutive_comparison.py provides detached exact/static descriptions of this family, target jets, local interaction coefficients and whole-support balance observations. These static descriptions allow every \(\lambda\ge0\); the uniform local trapping proof above is restricted to \(0\le\lambda\le1\). Its independent controls rebuild target derivatives and mixed edge weights on all 27 nodes, check both evolution rows and event/loss balances, and retain invalid-domain and symmetry controls. This does not install an alternative live law or reuse a sine response as evidence for it. No trajectory, selected time-coefficient producer or frozen scientific response is regenerated.

The separate _sine_class_constitutive_acquisition.py rebuilds the isolated full-family transit, law-specific storage bounds and capture margins from primitive inputs, using shared semigroup arithmetic without treating the sine preparation's storage as the alternative law's. Its controls check the forcing versus initial-error norms, quartic source correction, split endpoint storage and strict capture margins. The uniform conclusion uses the proved monotonic dependence and the endpoint \(\lambda=1\); it does not require a sweep or a trajectory producer.

The actual-source handoff uses the shared modified-energy kernel with the actual potential's upper Hessian. Its controls retain raw source errors, uninterrupted recovery, support work, input work and joined identity. The finite discriminator then combines fresh handoff and static onset with the real nonlinear tail. Its independent controls rebuild the tail constants and response coefficients, retain exact tiny rational records and reject unsupported source or readout margins. The returned intervals admit a prospective comparison; they are not evaluated responses or calibration records.

The scalar-sensor assessment rebuilds that raw comparison with zero raw-reading error before admitting the independent operating-domain, gain, curvature and sensor-error bounds. It distinguishes uniform mixed-threshold separation, preservation of both signs and a fixed-common-map complete-record certificate. Its controls exercise strict calibration margins, the retained absolute range and the actual-source quadratic-sensor sign counterexample. No sensor callable, cached report or response-derived calibration substitutes for these primitive premises.

docs.title: Constitutive inheritance through registered organized patterns
docs.text:
Two prescribed interfaces between winding-one C9 patterns admit an exact four-coordinate collective restriction of the matched-potential family. Matching local nodes preserves every constitutive parameter. Adding the two neighboring registrations changes the first phase harmonic while preserving the ninth and eighteenth ones. The resulting law belongs to an enlarged algebraic family with a mapped reciprocal coefficient, under an explicitly derived form chart, clock and parameter map. This is conditional inheritance through one specified grouping, not selection of a fundamental law or formation of a universal hierarchy.

The exact restriction and the later acquired-state bounds have different domains. The restriction permits arbitrary collective coordinates on its registered invariant family. Actual recovered sources have small internal residuals and are handled through the full fine-state law, including the new support work. Neither support event is selected by the continuous equations.

docs.title: Complete fine state and registered organizations
docs.text:
Retain node order \(9r+j\), with \(r=0,1\) and \(j=0,\ldots,8\). Each component has its nine unit cycle edges. Let \(\alpha=2\pi/9\) and choose exactly one of the two supplied sets of cross-edge offsets:

\[ \mathcal S_1=\{0\},\qquad \mathcal S_3=\{0,-1,1\}. \tag{1} \]

For each \(j\) and \(s\in\mathcal S_q\), add the undirected unit edge \((0,j)--(1,j+s)\), with indices modulo nine. The number of cross edges is \(9q\), every final degree is \(d=2+q\), and the full support is connected. No cross edge is repeated. Orientation, constituent partition, local indices and attachment registration are retained data.

Use signed real form, primitive circular phase and declared continuous phase lifts. Fine capacities stay one, and there are no continuous inputs unless explicitly supplied below. With the actual support Laplacian \(L\), keep

\[ \begin{split} W(\delta)&=\frac{(1-\cos9\delta)^2}{6\,9^4},\\ V_\lambda(\delta)&=1-\cos\delta+\lambda W(\delta),\\ j_\lambda(\delta)&=\sin\delta+ \frac{\lambda}{2187} \left(\sin9\delta-\frac12\sin18\delta\right),\\ S_{\lambda,i}(\theta)&=\sum_{\ell\sim i} j_\lambda(\theta_\ell-\theta_i). \end{split}\tag{2} \]

The source-admitted fine constitutive parameter is \(0\le\lambda\le1\), as in the acquisition theorem. Expressions (2) and the exact restriction and chart identities also apply to every \(\lambda\ge0\); that extension carries no automatic acquisition, capture or source-error certificate. The normalized pair comparison below permits the reciprocal coefficient \(\gamma>0\) to vary as a second parameter; the fine source-admitted model retains its fixed value.

The original clock is \(t\), and \(\tau=e t\), \(e=1023/1024\), \(\gamma=1/(1023\pi)\). In structural time the complete unforced rows and storage are

\[ x'=-d^{-1}Lx+\gamma d^{-1}S_\lambda(\theta),\qquad \theta'=\gamma d^{-1}Lx,\qquad H_\lambda=\tfrac12x^TLx+\sum_{\{i,\ell\}}V_\lambda(\theta_\ell-\theta_i). \tag{3} \]

In \(t\), both right-hand sides acquire the factor \(e\). The pressure in the unit-capacity nodal row is the independently specified first row in that clock, with the structural units retained. No laboratory clock or energy unit is inferred.

The reciprocal cancellation uses the actual complete law:

\[ H_\lambda'=-d^{-1}\|Lx\|_2^2,\qquad (\mathbf1^Tx)'=(\mathbf1^T\theta)'=0. \tag{4} \]

The phase mean here uses the declared lifts. The inherited state is the four-dimensional family

\[ \mathcal M:\quad x_{r,j}=X_r,\qquad \theta_{r,j}=\Phi_r+\alpha(j-4). \tag{5} \]

Its two collective phases are circular, with local continuous lifts where rates and means are evaluated. This is an embedding of a particular family in the full state space, not a quotient of arbitrary fine states. Away from \(\mathcal M\), constituent means alone need not close; the mean-closure obstruction and retained hidden-state requirements still apply.

The first phase resultant of either ideal C9 is zero. The ninth moment is \(e^{9\mathrm i\Phi_r}\), which loses \(\Phi_r\) modulo \(2\pi/9\). For example, changing only \(\Phi_1\) from zero to \(\alpha\) preserves both ninth moments but changes the matching-interface current from zero to \(\sin\alpha\). Thus a ninth moment without registration is insufficient even on (5). Here the retained labels and offsets determine \(\Phi_r\); no undefined circular-mean angle is used.

docs.title: Invariant restriction and the interface harmonic map
docs.text:
Define

\[ \Delta=\Phi_1-\Phi_0,\quad u=X_1-X_0,\quad k_q=\frac q{2+q},\quad r_q=\frac1q\sum_{s\in\mathcal S_q}\cos(\alpha s). \tag{6} \]

Thus

\[ r_1=1,\qquad r_3=\frac{1+2\cos\alpha}{3}\in(0,1). \tag{7} \]

On (5), the two internal form differences vanish. The two internal phase currents cancel because \(j_\lambda\) is odd and periodic. Every node in component zero has the same cross form sum \(-q u\) and the same cross current sum \(\sum_s j_\lambda(\Delta+\alpha s)\). Wraps of local indices change the lifted gap by an integer multiple of \(2\pi\), leaving these currents and potentials unchanged. The reverse component has the opposite sums, since the offset set is symmetric.

The complete vector field is therefore tangent to (5) at every point. Its global Lipschitz property gives unique continuation in this invariant family. This applies to both rows and all collective coordinates, not just to a target equilibrium. Let

\[ \begin{split} J_{\lambda,q}(\Delta) &=\frac1q\sum_{s\in\mathcal S_q}j_\lambda(\Delta+\alpha s)\\ &=r_q\sin\Delta+ \frac{\lambda}{2187} \left(\sin9\Delta-\tfrac12\sin18\Delta\right) =r_q j_{\lambda/r_q}(\Delta). \end{split}\tag{8} \]

The first equality is the fine-state restriction. The second follows by pairing the first harmonics and using \(9\alpha s=2\pi s\) for each integer offset. In \(\tau\), the exact collective rows are

\[ \begin{array}{ll} X_0'=k_q[u+\gamma J_{\lambda,q}(\Delta)],& X_1'=-k_q[u+\gamma J_{\lambda,q}(\Delta)],\\ \Phi_0'=-\gamma k_q u,& \Phi_1'=\gamma k_q u. \end{array}\tag{9} \]

Both collective sums are constant. Equivalently, \(u'=-2k_q[u+\gamma J_{\lambda,q}(\Delta)]\) and \(\Delta'=2\gamma k_q u\). The factors \(k_1=1/3\) and \(k_3=3/5\) use the final degrees; retaining the old isolated degree two would give a different model.

This calculation extends the existing phase-offset partition criterion to this particular positive-loss, multiple-harmonic law. A first-harmonic criterion alone could not establish the second equality of (8).

docs.title: Storage, dissipation and support-event work
docs.text:
Because \(W(\alpha)=0\), the 18 internal edges contribute \(18(1-\cos\alpha)\) on the whole invariant family. The averaged cross potential is

\[ \overline V_{\lambda,q}(\Delta) =1-r_q\cos\Delta+\lambda W(\Delta) =(1-r_q)+r_q V_{\lambda/r_q}(\Delta). \tag{10} \]

Set \(B_q=18(1-\cos\alpha)+9q(1-r_q)\). The exact pullback is

\[ H_\lambda|_{\mathcal M} =B_q+9q\left[\tfrac12u^2+r_qV_{\lambda/r_q}(\Delta)\right], \qquad \frac{dH_\lambda}{d\tau}=-18qk_q u^2. \tag{11} \]

Indeed, \(Lx\) equals \(-qu\) at every node of the first component and \(qu\) at every node of the second; substitution into (4) gives the loss. Differentiating the displayed collective storage using both rows of (9) gives the same result. The inherited storage is not an independently postulated pair energy.

The prescribed support event keeps all form and phase values unchanged. For a general fine state its work is exactly

\[ \mathcal W_q(x,\theta)= \sum_{j,s\in\mathcal S_q} \left[\tfrac12(x_{1,j+s}-x_{0,j})^2+ V_\lambda(\theta_{1,j+s}-\theta_{0,j})\right]\ge0. \tag{12} \]

On \(\mathcal M\), this becomes \(9q[\tfrac12u^2+(1-r_q)+r_qV_{\lambda/r_q}(\Delta)]\). At the aligned zero-form target its value is zero for matching edges and \(18(1-\cos\alpha)>0\) for the three-offset interface. The constant in (10) disappears from continuous derivatives but cannot be discarded when comparing the before and after support storage. Any positive event work requires a declared external supply; earlier continuous dissipation is not a reservoir. These formulas neither supply that reservoir nor cause the event.

docs.title: Complete-law equivalence, coordinates and capacity scope
docs.text:
Specify the allowed comparison before removing coefficients. A positive common clock factor acts on both evolution rows. In the unchanged form chart, comparison with the unit-capacity normalized reciprocal pair law allows a common rate multiplier and a new reciprocal coefficient, but retains its normalized diffusion and first-harmonic coefficients.

No choice within that class puts the three-offset law directly into the original normalized family. Matching the diffusion coefficient fixes the common multiplier to \(k_q\). Matching the phase row then fixes the reciprocal coefficient to \(\gamma\). The first-harmonic form coefficient would consequently be \(k_q\gamma\), whereas (9) has \(k_q\gamma r_3\). Distinct Fourier harmonics cannot repair that discrepancy by changing \(\lambda\). Matching edges have \(r_1=1\), so they preserve the entire family under their derived common clock factor.

The regular form chart permitted by the form-chart contract does give an exact parameter map:

\[ \sigma=k_q\tau=k_q e t,\qquad X_r=\sqrt{r_q}\,Z_r,\qquad \lambda_{\rm eff}=\frac{\lambda}{r_q},\qquad \gamma_{\rm eff}=\gamma\sqrt{r_q}. \tag{13} \]

Keeping \(\Phi_r\) unchanged, both rows become

\[ \begin{array}{ll} \displaystyle\frac{dZ_0}{d\sigma} =Z_1-Z_0+\gamma_{\rm eff}j_{\lambda_{\rm eff}}(\Delta),& \displaystyle\frac{dZ_1}{d\sigma} =Z_0-Z_1-\gamma_{\rm eff}j_{\lambda_{\rm eff}}(\Delta),\\ \displaystyle\frac{d\Phi_0}{d\sigma} =\gamma_{\rm eff}(Z_0-Z_1),& \displaystyle\frac{d\Phi_1}{d\sigma} =\gamma_{\rm eff}(Z_1-Z_0). \end{array}\tag{14} \]

Writing \(z=Z_1-Z_0\), their inherited storage and loss are

\[ H_\lambda|_{\mathcal M} =B_q+9qr_q\left[\tfrac12z^2+V_{\lambda_{\rm eff}}(\Delta)\right], \qquad \frac{dH_\lambda}{d\sigma}=-18qr_q z^2. \tag{15} \]

The form chart transforms the pressure, the phase coupling and the storage scale together. Reusing the original pressure formula with the new form coordinate would violate (14).

More generally, a positive form-unit chart \(X_r=aZ_r\), after the diffusion coefficient has fixed \(\sigma=k_q\tau\), gives phase coefficient \(\gamma a\) and first-harmonic form coefficient \(\gamma r_q/a\). Their reciprocal equality forces \(a^2=r_q\) and hence the value of \(\gamma_{\rm eff}\) in (13). Consequently the three-offset restriction belongs to the enlarged two-parameter family \((\lambda_{\rm eff},\gamma_{\rm eff})\); it does not belong to the original fixed-\(\gamma\) line merely by extending the allowed \(\lambda\) interval. Keeping that original coefficient excludes exact same-law inheritance for this interface even under the stated positive form-unit charts and common clock maps.

The factor \(k_q\) is a derived common response factor of this complete restricted law. One may represent it as a common effective capacity only after specifying that the capacity-dependent complete model multiplies both reciprocal rows by that factor. The nodal identity alone specifies only the form row and does not justify such a phase law. Allowing arbitrary independent form and phase mobilities is a larger complete family; the unchanged-chart obstruction above does not exclude that different comparison. Fine capacities here remain the declared value one.

For matching edges, all constitutive parameters in (13) are unchanged. For three offsets, every \(\lambda>0\) increases and \(\gamma\) decreases: \(\lambda_{\rm eff}\gamma_{\rm eff}^2=\lambda\gamma^2\). This last equality is an algebraic property of (13), not a physical conservation law. If \(\lambda>r_3\), the effective parameter is outside the source-admitted interval \([0,1]\), although it is still in the larger algebraic family. Even when \(\lambda\le r_3\), a pair of collective nodes does not inherit a C9 acquisition proof merely by sharing a parameter value. The fixed point \(\lambda=0\) of this particular parameter map does not select sine: the supplied matching interface preserves every \(\lambda\), and the larger family accommodates the three-offset map.

Even imposing an unchanged constitutive profile under both interfaces does not select sine. The analytic classification and counterfamily retain the same target storage and local derivatives while preserving a different nonlinear profile. Its new laws have their own admission scope; the acquired-state certificates below remain specific to (2).

docs.title: Inputs, observations and event boundaries
docs.text:
Suppose an independently supplied continuous form input adds \(b_r(\tau)\) to every fine form row in component \(r\). It preserves (5) and adds \(b_r/k_q\) to \(dX_r/d\sigma\), or \(b_r/(k_q\sqrt{r_q})\) to \(dZ_r/d\sigma\). If a phase input \(c_r(\tau)\) is separately declared and constant within each component, it transforms to \(c_r/k_q\) in the phase row. An input specified in original-time units first transforms by the additional factor \(1/e\). No phase input is inferred from a form input.

The corresponding continuous boundary work follows from the same full storage:

\[ \frac{dH_\lambda}{d\tau} =-18qk_q u^2+ 9q\left[u(b_1-b_0)+J_{\lambda,q}(\Delta)(c_1-c_0)\right]. \]

The transformed input coefficients and storage (15) reproduce this balance after division by \(k_q\). A common input to both components shifts its retained mean without doing work on the difference-only storage.

Similarly, a prescribed uniform form jump \(X_r^+=X_r^-+a_r\) becomes \(Z_r^+=Z_r^-+a_r/\sqrt{r_q}\). A uniform phase jump keeps its angular increment. Its event work is the difference of the full pulled-back storage (11) or (15), with identical result in either chart. A single fine-node input generally leaves \(\mathcal M\); its subsequent full dynamics cannot be replaced by (14). The registered fine event and its collective admissibility remain separate from any grammar, history or occurrence rule of a named engine operator.

For an independently specified observation \(y=h(x,\theta)\), the exact collective observation is \(h\) composed with (5). In the new chart it is the same map with \(X_r=\sqrt{r_q}Z_r\). In particular, a raw constituent form reading \(X_r\) is represented by \(\sqrt{r_q}Z_r\), not by \(Z_r\). Both prescribed support events map the exact family (5) to itself while changing its vector field and storage. Their specified event rule therefore has an exact restriction on this family. docs.title: Actual acquired sources, new support work and full-state identity
docs.text:
Use two copies of the original class-one uncertain ramp preparation, with each original form and phase coordinate error at most \(10^{-10}\) and the separate exact zero-sum constraints. The own-law recovery theorem gives, for every fine \(\lambda\in[0,1]\), the common uninterrupted handoff time \(\tau_h=100+10^{13}\) and

\[ \|x_r\|_2\le\varepsilon,\qquad \|y_r\|_2\le\varepsilon,\qquad y_{r,j}=\theta_{r,j}-\alpha(j-4),\qquad \varepsilon=10^{-70}. \tag{16} \]

The component means of \(x_r,y_r\) are still exactly zero. Their complete reached coordinates and absolute origins are retained; (16) does not replace either source by its target. Only isolated recovery is reused. The previous three-C9 bridge event, its four input branches and their work or identity certificates are not premises of this composition.

The present event adds exactly the chosen cross support and changes no coordinate. Let \(\Theta_{r,j}=\alpha(j-4)\), \(u_\lambda=1+2\lambda/243\), and

\[ W_q^*=9q(1-r_q),\qquad H_q^*=18(1-\cos\alpha)+W_q^*. \tag{17} \]

All deformation potentials vanish on the target edges, whose circular differences are \(0,\alpha\) or \(-\alpha\). The target cross-edge gradient is zero: matching currents vanish separately, and the two offset currents cancel at every node. Thus the first variation of the complete added potential is zero, even though its individual offset terms need not be stationary.

The cross-support Laplacian is bounded above by \(2qI\); the full one is bounded above by \(2dI\). Also \(|V_\lambda''|\le u_\lambda\) globally. On the cell

\[ \mathcal B=\{(x,y):\mathbf1^Tx=\mathbf1^Ty=0,\ \|x\|_2^2+\|y\|_2^2<R_0^2\}, \qquad R_0=1/12, \tag{18} \]

every edge Hessian is strictly greater than \(1/2\). Indeed,

\[ V_\lambda''(\delta) \ge \cos(\alpha+\sqrt2R_0)-2/243 > 47/72-2/243>1/2. \tag{19} \]

Here \(\alpha+\sqrt2/12<5/6\), using \(\pi<22/7\) and \(\sqrt2<3/2\), and \(\cos z\ge1-z^2/2\). Periodic edge representatives handle the cycle seam without changing the fixed lifts or the winding.

Taylor's formula for the whole added potential, including cancellation of its first variation, and (16) now give the actual event work

\[ W_q^*\le \Delta H_{\rm support} \le W_q^*+2q(1+u_\lambda)\varepsilon^2. \tag{20} \]

The lower bound uses convexity along the segment from the target to the actual state, which lies within (18). The added form storage is nonnegative. For matching edges \(W_1^*=0\); for three offsets \(W_3^*=18(1-\cos\alpha)>0\). This event therefore requires an explicit external work supply covering its actual cost. The statement is conditional on that supplied event and work, not a passivity result or a deduction of an occurrence rule. No previous continuous loss is credited as an available reserve.

The matching support is the Cartesian product \(C_9\mathbin{\square}K_2\). Its smallest nonzero Laplacian eigenvalue is \(2-2\cos\alpha>2/5\). For example, \(\pi>3\) gives \(\cos\alpha<\cos(2/3)\le191/243<4/5\). The three-offset support adds positive semidefinite edge Laplacians, so it keeps the same lower bound. Together with (19), this proves the full transverse coercivity, throughout (18),

\[ H_\lambda(x,\Theta+y)-H_q^* \ge \tfrac1{10}\bigl(\|x\|_2^2+\|y\|_2^2\bigr). \tag{21} \]

This is positivity on the full zero-mean quotient, including all internal residual directions; it is not a test only along the collective family. At the actual unchanged state after contact,

\[ \|x\|_2^2+\|y\|_2^2\le4\varepsilon^2,\qquad E_q:=H_\lambda-H_q^*\le2d(1+u_\lambda)\varepsilon^2 <\frac{201}{10}\varepsilon^2<\frac1{1440}. \tag{22} \]

The constant degree makes the new conserved weighted means proportional to the total means, which remain zero. The boundary of (18) has excess at least \(R_0^2/10=1/1440\). The exact loss law (4), (21) and (22) therefore keep every actual source inside (18) for all future unforced time under its own constitutive law. Both constituent cycle windings remain one. In particular,

\[ \|x(\tau_h+T)\|_2^2+\|y(\tau_h+T)\|_2^2 <201\varepsilon^2,\qquad T\ge0. \tag{23} \]

Thus the distance to the aligned target on \(\mathcal M\) is below \(15\varepsilon\) for all future time. On this compact trapped mean leaf the only invariant set with zero loss is the target: \(Lx=0\) forces \(x=0\), invariance of the form row forces a critical potential, and the strictly convex potential has only \(y=0\) in the cell. The usual invariant-set argument consequently also gives convergence. This proves local full-state identity and attraction for these actual sources, not transverse attraction of every arbitrarily excited point of the entire family (5).

docs.title: Finite carried-state comparison and collective row defect
docs.text:
Fix the prospective comparison interval \(0\le T\le1/10\) in \(\tau\), with original duration \(T/e\). No input is applied during it. The full vector field (3) has global raw-coordinate sup-norm Lipschitz constant at most

\[ \max\{2+2\gamma u_\lambda,2\gamma\}<3. \tag{24} \]

Comparing the actual source with the exact aligned equilibrium, the same actual law and support therefore give

\[ \|(x,y)(\tau_h+T)\|_\infty \le e^{3T}\varepsilon \le \frac{\varepsilon}{1-3T} \le R_T:=10\varepsilon/7. \tag{25} \]

This bound carries every fine coordinate, including the asymmetric internal errors that need not lie on \(\mathcal M\).

For actual collective observations define \(\bar X_r=\frac19\sum_jx_{r,j}\) and \(\bar\Phi_r=\frac19\sum_jy_{r,j}\), retaining the original lifts. Their centered phase fluctuations have magnitude at most \(2R_T\). Since both internal and cross degrees are regular, summing the fine linear rows closes the diffusion contribution and the entire phase row exactly. Only the nonlinear cross current has a remainder:

\[ \begin{split} \bar X_0'&=k_q\{\bar X_1-\bar X_0+ \gamma J_{\lambda,q}(\bar\Phi_1-\bar\Phi_0)\}+\rho,\\ \bar X_1'&=-k_q\{\bar X_1-\bar X_0+ \gamma J_{\lambda,q}(\bar\Phi_1-\bar\Phi_0)\}-\rho,\\ \bar\Phi_0'&=\gamma k_q(\bar X_0-\bar X_1),\qquad \bar\Phi_1'=\gamma k_q(\bar X_1-\bar X_0),\\ |\rho|&\le4\gamma k_q u_\lambda R_T. \end{split}\tag{26} \]

For each cross edge the actual phase difference differs from the registered mean-plus-offset difference by at most \(4R_T\). The global current derivative bound \(u_\lambda\) and the \(9q\) edges give the last inequality in (26); internal currents cancel exactly. The opposite remainders retain total form conservation. Formula (26) is a controlled defect of collective closure, not an additional autonomous law for hidden fluctuations or a memory-free quotient.

Here the actual component means at handoff are zero, so the exact collective reference is the aligned equilibrium. These estimates do not claim that this particular source launches a nonzero collective excitation. Arbitrary collective initial coordinates still obey the exact restriction proved above, but their physical preparation and full transverse stability require their own premises.

docs.title: A nominal symmetry that does not restrict source errors
docs.text:
Let \(R\) be the node permutation

\[ R(0,j)=(1,8-j),\quad R(1,j)=(0,8-j),\quad R(2,j)=(2,8-j). \]

It preserves the complete weighted support, has thirteen two-node orbits and one fixed node \((2,4)\), and satisfies \(R^2=I\). Because sine is odd and the support is invariant, \(F(-Rz)=-RF(z)\). Thus the antisymmetric space \(\mathcal V_-:=\{z:Rz=-z\}\) is invariant for the reference equation \(y_u=F(y)\), and \(P\in\mathcal V_-\).

Choose one node \(a_k\) from each pair and define \(C_-e_k=e_{a_k}-e_{Ra_k}\). The nominal reference can be integrated in thirteen coordinates, with lift \(y=C_-v\) and

\[ C_-^TC_-=2I,\qquad \|C_-v\|_2^2=2\|v\|_2^2. \tag{2} \]

The full initial-error family is not projected onto this space. Its transverse directions stay in the radius carried under (1). Choosing a symmetric reference changes the cost of the calculation, not the quantified source.

docs.title: Validated reference and full-state error transport
docs.text:
At one step, let \(c\in\mathcal V_-\) be the rational reference center and let \(e\) bound the Euclidean difference between the actual phase and \(c\). The shared metric Taylor owner is called on the thirteen coordinates with metric \(2I\), initial radius zero, growth bound two, duration \(h\) and order eight. Strict Picard inclusion gives a whole-time reference tube; the normalized solution jets and whole-tube order-nine remainder give its endpoint enclosure. The metric is exactly the lifted norm (2).

Radius zero applies only to this local exact reference solution. The actual source error \(e\) remains external and is propagated by the following comparison. In particular, the reference validation is not evidence that the actual full law starts at its center.

The global Jacobian bound \(\|DF\|_2\le2\) holds on all phase lifts. Writing

\[ \phi(\mu,s)= \begin{cases}(e^{\mu s}-1)/\mu,&\mu\ne0,\\s,&\mu=0,\end{cases} \]

it gives the prospective global discrepancy bound

\[ G=e^{2h}e+\rho\phi(2,h),\qquad R_*=\tfrac54(G+2^{-80}). \tag{3} \]

All arithmetic in (3) is outward. The convex sum of the lifted reference Picard box and the mean-zero ball of radius \(R_*\) contains both local solutions throughout the step. The strict margin follows from \(R_*>G\), not from presuming the validity of a future local growth estimate.

For each fine edge, its reference phase difference is bounded from that box; the complete discrepancy enlarges the edge interval by \(\sqrt2R_*\) on both sides. This factor is the norm of the edge incidence vector. It retains arbitrary mean-zero errors, including errors outside \(\mathcal V_-\).

Let \(\ell_e\) be a lower bound for cosine on the enlarged edge interval. Round it downward to the declared dyadic grid, with the exact global floor \(-1\), and take the minimum over the reflected edge orbit. For every point in the prospective convex domain,

\[ DF=-\tfrac14 B\operatorname{diag}(w_e\cos\delta_e)B^T \preceq J_*:=-\tfrac14B\operatorname{diag}(w_e\ell_e)B^T. \tag{4} \]

This Loewner bound follows term by term from \(w_e(\cos\delta_e-\ell_e)b_eb_e^T\succeq0\), including edges with negative cosine. Independent interval matrix entries are not mistaken for an exact Jacobian.

The orbit minimum makes \(J_*\) commute with \(R\). Both \(J_*\) and the actual Jacobians annihilate the common-phase vector. To certify an upper logarithmic growth rate on the entire mean-zero leaf, the calculation uses both reflection sectors. The antisymmetric sector has basis \(C_-\) and Gram matrix \(2I\). A basis for the symmetric mean-zero sector is

\[ C_+e_k=e_{a_k}+e_{Ra_k}-2e_{(2,4)},\qquad C_+^TC_+=2I+4\mathbf1\mathbf1^T. \tag{5} \]

These orthogonal sectors each have dimension thirteen and together span all 26 mean-zero directions. Hence the two exact rational PSD tests

\[ \mu C_\pm^TC_\pm-C_\pm^TJ_*C_\pm\succeq0 \tag{6} \]

prove \(DF|_{\mathbf1^\perp}\preceq\mu I\). Testing only the antisymmetric block would omit source directions and is insufficient. The upper search endpoint two is valid because \(\ell_e\ge-1\) and \(J_*\preceq L/4\preceq2I\). The lower search endpoint minus one is a search policy, not an asserted lower bound on the actual logarithmic norm. Each retained rate is checked by exact rational semidefinite elimination.

Pairing the actual-reference difference equation with its normalized error and using (1), (4)--(6) yields

\[ D^+\|\theta-y\|_2\le\mu\|\theta-y\|_2+\rho. \]

Therefore a whole-step discrepancy bound is

\[ E(s)=e^{\mu s}e+\rho\phi(\mu,s),\quad 0\le s\le h, \qquad E_{\max}=\max\{e,E(h)\}. \tag{7} \]

The scalar solution is monotone or constant on a step, so its maximum is at an endpoint. Outward scalar exponential enclosures handle either sign of \(\mu\). Strict inclusion \(E_{\max}<R_*\) is checked explicitly. An unavailable inclusion stops the validated prefix; it cannot be replaced by a favorable endpoint alone.

Let \(d\) be the full \(2I\)-metric Taylor endpoint recentering error. The next exact rational reference center and carried full phase radius obey

\[ e_{\rm next}=E(h)+d. \tag{8} \]

No observation box is converted back into a smaller radius, and neither the Taylor error nor the complete-law defect is discarded. The reference may change at the step boundary; (8) accounts for its entire jump. The original complete trajectory itself has no reset or discontinuity.

docs.title: Identity, capture and the meaning of a failed margin
docs.text:

A failed sufficient donor margin is recorded permanently for the positive whole-history claim, but does not end the enclosure. The actual state may still be enclosed at later steps, and its donor winding may become decidable there. For an endpoint, freshly determine principal-difference integers with strict branch margins for every internal edge. Their signed sum gives the integer winding; do not infer it from a rounded phase plot.

If a donor's entire endpoint ball has winding different from one, the continuous full law must have lost that donor identity after its certified acquisition. Since the ball encloses every original admitted source, such a verdict is a whole-family donor-loss result. It refutes the requested donor-retaining acquisition claim for this preparation and law. It does not prove that the receiver can never acquire winding, that other preparations cannot do so, or that all compatible TNFR laws share the outcome.

For positive joined capture, the endpoint center \(c_*\) and radius \(e_*\) must pass the same complete-state contract:

\[ \max_{\text{fine }e}|\delta_e(c_*)|+\sqrt2e_*<2, \tag{9} \] \[ U(c_*)-U(\Theta)+\|\nabla U(c_*)\|_2e_* +4e_*^2+4X_0^2<196/625,\qquad \Theta=\alpha(q,q,q). \tag{10} \]

The fine-edge integers in (9) are those registered to \(\Theta\), not freely chosen local seams. The potential, gradient and form contribution refer to the same complete weighted support and same endpoint. The linear gradient term in (10) remains present. Joined capture plus certified continuous donor history gives the requested positive result and invokes the existing future trapping and convergence theorem.

An endpoint capture inequality without that history may establish an endpoint property, but does not repair unavailable donor retention. Likewise, a reference donor losing winding without the complete error margins proves nothing about the actual source family. Numerical validation failure, phase-error budget exhaustion, unresolved winding or a horizon without capture remain explicit unavailable outcomes; none is silently promoted to nonformation.

docs.text:

docs.text:
