\[ A=L/4,\quad a=\gamma x,\quad \epsilon=\gamma^2,\quad F(\theta)=S(\theta)/4,\quad z=\theta+a . \tag{8} \]

The exact complete rows are

\[ a'=-Aa+\epsilon F(\theta),\qquad \theta'=Aa,\qquad z'=\epsilon F(\theta). \tag{9} \]

The connected-support proof gives a mean-zero gap \(g=1/10\) for \(A\), while \(|F_i|\le1\) and \(\|F\|_2\le M=\sqrt{27}\) globally. Hence

\[ \|a(\tau)\|_2\le \gamma e^{-\tau/10}(m\sqrt{120}+r_x\sqrt{27}) +10\epsilon\sqrt{27}. \tag{10} \]

Define its time-200 upper bound

\[ B=\gamma e^{-20}(m\sqrt{120}+r_x\sqrt{27}) +10\epsilon\sqrt{27}. \tag{11} \]

The norm bound (10) is at most \(B\) for every \(\tau\ge200\). The appropriate reference phase is now

\[ P=\alpha Q=(\alpha q,\alpha q,0), \tag{12} \]

which is flat on the receiver. Integrating the exact mixed row gives

\[ \|\theta(200)-P\|_2\le b, \quad b=\sqrt{120}|\gamma m-\alpha| +\sqrt{27}(r_\theta+\gamma r_x)+B +200\epsilon\sqrt{27}<1/5000 . \tag{13} \]

In particular, \(B\) is approximately \(0.00000504649136123\), \(B/\gamma<1/50\), and \(b\) is approximately \(0.00010696036\). The rational ramp mismatch is retained rather than setting \(355/113=\pi\).

Each donor's principal internal edge difference at time 200 is \(\alpha\) plus an error of magnitude at most \(\sqrt2b\), with its one seam integer fixed as in the winding-one target. Their sums equal \(2\pi\), so both donor windings are one. The receiver's real edge differences have magnitude at most \(\sqrt2b<\pi\), telescope to zero and give winding zero. These are actual full-state conclusions for every source in (3). In particular this state has not entered the all-winding-one joined capture cell. The earlier three-ramp source certificate cannot replace the missing receiver source in (12).

docs.title: No receiver branch crossing throughout the certified delay
docs.text:
The receiver's winding is zero throughout the initial layer as well as at its endpoint. To prove this without a trajectory, split \(A=A_I+A_C\) into internal-cycle and contact Laplacians divided by four. On the equal support they are commuting convolution operators on \(\mathbb Z_3\times\mathbb Z_9\). Their heat kernels are nonnegative and preserve constants.

Let \(h_\tau\) be the internal C9 heat kernel. Its nonconstant Fourier modes decay at least as fast as \(e^{-\tau/10}\), whence

\[ |h_\tau(j)-1/9|\le(8/9)e^{-\tau/10}. \tag{14} \]

The contact heat kernel started in region two has total mass

\[ p(\tau)=\tfrac23(1-e^{-3\tau/4}) \tag{15} \]

in the two donor regions. This is the exact marginal three-region heat law; it does not assume independence between region and offset. Aggregate those donor offsets into a nonnegative C9 kernel of mass \(p\). Since the forward difference of the ramp is \(\Delta q=1-9\delta_{\mathrm{seam}}\), (14) bounds every receiver edge of the unforced transported source by

\[ |\Delta(e^{-A\tau}Q)_{2,j}| \le8p(\tau)e^{-\tau/10}<4 . \tag{16} \]

For completeness, the maximum of \(e^{-\tau/10}(1-e^{-3\tau/4})\) is \((15/17)(2/17)^{2/15}<3/4\). The strict inequality is the integer comparison \(4\,20^{15}<17^{17}\).

Variation of constants in (9) gives the exact full-law identity

\[ \theta(\tau)=\theta(0)+(I-e^{-A\tau})a(0) +\epsilon\int_0^\tau (I-e^{-A(\tau-v)})F(\theta(v))\,dv . \tag{17} \]

Use (16) for the nominal receiver source, Markov contraction for the initial errors, and \(|F_i|\le1\) for both integral terms. For every receiver edge and \(0\le\tau\le200\),

\[ |\Delta\theta_{2,j}(\tau)| <4\gamma m+2r_\theta+4\gamma r_x+4\epsilon\tau \le4\gamma m+2r_\theta+4\gamma r_x+800\epsilon<\pi . \tag{18} \]

The upper bound is approximately \(2.79260473077\). Thus no receiver edge can have crossed a principal-phase boundary in that layer.

For later times the integrated mixed row in (9), the zero nominal receiver value of \(z(0)\), and (10) instead give

\[ |\Delta\theta_{2,j}(\tau)| \le2(r_\theta+\gamma r_x)+\sqrt2B+2\epsilon\tau, \qquad \tau\ge200 . \tag{19} \]

Define the derived threshold

\[ T_*:=\frac{\pi-2(r_\theta+\gamma r_x)-\sqrt2B} {2\epsilon}. \tag{20} \]

It is approximately \(16224447.0054\), and outward bounds certify \(T_*>16000000\). Combining (18) and (19), every member of (3) retains receiver winding zero on \([0,T_*)\). At \(T_*\) the strict edge estimate ends; the result does not claim that a crossing occurs then, or at any later time. No corresponding long-window donor-retention conclusion follows from this receiver bound.

docs.title: Nonlinear interaction and a controlled slow comparison
docs.text:
The delay is not a symmetry cancellation of all receiver interaction. At the reference (12), direct evaluation on the oriented fine support gives, with \(q=q_j\),

\[ \begin{split} S_{0,j}(P)&=\tfrac12\sin\alpha-\sin(\alpha q),\\ S_{1,j}(P)&=-\tfrac12\sin\alpha-\sin(\alpha q),\\ S_{2,j}(P)&=(1+\cos\alpha)\sin(\alpha q). \end{split} \tag{21} \]

For example, the receiver sees donor phases at offsets \(j-1,j,j+1\), with weights one half, one and one half. This gives the last row of (21), not a prescribed replacement of its own phase by a donor ramp. The receiver current is positive for \(j=5,\ldots,8\), negative for \(j=0,\ldots,3\), and zero at the central reference node.

These noncentral signs also hold for the actual state at time 200. The sine Lipschitz bound and (13) imply

\[ |S_i(\theta(200))-S_i(P)|\le4\sqrt2 b . \tag{22} \]

The smallest noncentral reference magnitude is \((1+\cos\alpha)\sin(\pi/9)>3/5\), while \(4\sqrt2b<1/500\). Thus the exact row \(z'=\epsilon S/4\) at the end of the layer drives each noncentral receiver coordinate with the sign of its desired donor ramp. This is a statement about the mixed-coordinate rate. The actual phase row remains \(\theta'=Aa\); (21) is not its instantaneous replacement.

The nominal preparation respects the graph involution \((r,j)\mapsto(1-r\pmod3,8-j)\) combined with sign reversal of both form and lifted phase. The full law preserves that symmetry. The all-winding-one target respects it as well, so this symmetry does not exclude the desired outcome. General errors in (3) need not obey that nominal symmetry.

For an exact description of the slow mechanism put \(s=\epsilon\tau\), retaining the same phase lifts and form. Equation (17) becomes

\[ \theta(s)=\theta_0+(I-e^{-As/\epsilon})a_0 +\int_0^s(I-e^{-A(s-v)/\epsilon})F(\theta(v))\,dv . \tag{23} \]

This is the actual nonlinear memory equation with its original form source. Equivalently,

\[ z_s=F(z-a),\qquad a_s=-\epsilon^{-1}Aa+F(z-a),\qquad \theta=z-a . \tag{24} \]

The reference phase-descent law \(y_s=F(y)\) is an approximation to (23), not an independently exact closure of (1).

A finite-window comparison can be admitted without discarding the initial layer. Let \(y(0)=P\), \(K=2\), \(M=\sqrt{27}\), \(k=g/\epsilon\), and

\[ A_0=\gamma(m\sqrt{120}+r_x\sqrt{27}),\qquad d_0=\sqrt{120}|\gamma m-\alpha| +\sqrt{27}(r_\theta+\gamma r_x). \]

The global Lipschitz constant \(K\) follows from \(\|DF\|_2\le\|L\|_2/4\le2\). Subtract the integral equation for \(y\) from (23), use the mean-zero heat gap on the source and on \(F\), and apply the scalar Gronwall resolvent. This gives the full-source bound

\[ \|\theta(s)-y(s)\|_2 \le d_0e^{Ks}+A_0e^{-ks} +\frac{KA_0+M}{k+K}(e^{Ks}-e^{-ks}). \tag{25} \]

Indeed the pre-resolvent error is bounded by \(d_0+A_0e^{-ks}+(M/k)(1-e^{-ks})\); evaluating its convolution with \(Ke^{Ks}\) gives (25). Form retains its own bound (10). A future phase comparison must keep both errors, the fixed source and clock, and actual joined-capture margins. A large right-hand side is an unavailable sufficient estimate, not a failure of acquisition. No reduced trajectory or infinite-time interchange is used here.

docs.title: Regional boundary work and the remaining capture obligation
docs.text:
For a marked region let \(L_Ix\) and \(S_I\) contain its internal cycle terms, while \(L_Cx\) and \(S_C\) contain its incident contact terms. Restrict these vectors to the region and write \(\ell=L_Ix\), \(b_C=L_Cx\), \(u=S_I\), \(v=S_C\). Its internal storage

\[ H_r=\tfrac12x_r^TL_{I,r}x_r+ \sum_{\{i,j\}\subset r}[1-\cos(\theta_j-\theta_i)] \]

satisfies the exact balance

\[ H_r'=-\tfrac14\|\ell\|^2 -\tfrac14\ell\cdot b_C +\tfrac\gamma4(\ell\cdot v-u\cdot b_C). \tag{26} \]

To verify it, use \(\nabla_{x_r}H_r=\ell\), \(\nabla_{\theta_r}H_r=-u\), and both actual rows in (1). The internal reciprocal terms cancel. The remaining contact terms are the regional boundary work; they have no fixed sign and are not an externally supplied forcing. Adding regional storage alone omits contact storage. Including that contact storage recovers the complete loss identity (4).

Equations (21)--(26) specify a causal route for later phase-mediated change while retaining its form memory and work. They do not yet show that the receiver reaches winding one before a donor loses its own identity, or that the complete state reaches the joined trapping sublevel. The subsequent frozen full-source enclosure resolves that transfer question negatively on its validated interval: both donors lose winding while the receiver retains zero winding. The regional retention theorem turns (26) into a conditional all-prefix work budget and derives its exhaustion at each donor's first boundary contact. Neither the three-ramp certificate nor an equilibrium tangent supplies an alternative two-ramp retention result. Later acquisition or regeneration remains unresolved.

The implementation re-admits primitive error allowances, rebuilds the support and complete source cost, and evaluates the preparation, fast-layer, delay and current-sign inequalities with shared exact rational and outward interval owners. It reuses the prepared form-cost and transit kernels also consumed by the three-ramp assessment. The slow comparison (25) is a proved method for a future admitted consumer; this assessment does not evaluate it or a reduced trajectory. Its frozen conclusion uses the original errors in (3); different admitted errors require fresh inequalities. Failed sufficient bounds remain unavailable. The execution plan is the sole owner of the next research task.

docs.title: Complete-law admission for slow receiver acquisition
docs.text:

For every later time, the complete phase velocity differs from the sine descent field by less than \(11\times10^{-6}\) in Euclidean norm. This uniform velocity bound does not identify the full trajectory with a phase-only trajectory. It supplies a source-aware differential inclusion and a precise corridor and terminal-capture contract. docs.title: Retained source, law and identity
docs.text:

Each contact uses offsets zero and one with weights one half. All support is present at preparation; its weighted Laplacian is \(L\), and every node has weighted degree four. Capacities remain one. \[ \tau=(1023/1024)t,\qquad s=\epsilon\tau,\qquad \gamma=1/(1023\pi),\qquad \epsilon=\gamma^2. \tag{1} \]

No forcing, state reset, support event or evolving conductance is added. This is neither native unique-neighbor phase pressure nor execution of a registered operator. The nodal identity alone does not select (3).

Let \(q_j=j-4\), \(\alpha=2\pi/9\), and let \(Q\) contain \(q\) in regions zero and one and zero in region two. Retain

\[ m=\frac{2046}{9}(355/113)^2,\quad x_0=mQ+\eta_x,\quad \theta_0=\eta_\theta, \quad |\eta_{x,i}|\le r_x=10^{-10},\quad |\eta_{\theta,i}|\le r_\theta=10^{-10}. \tag{4} \]

Both errors have separate exact zero sums within each original C9. Every allowed combination is included. Only the global means remain conserved after evolution begins. The common phase origin and continuous lifts remain fixed. All 54 fine coordinates, boundary contacts and the full preparation cost are retained. The nominal storage is \(150m^2\), including \(78m^2\) on contacts; its error allowance and the regional boundary-work identity remain in the linked source owner.

The relevant identity is principal-difference winding around each marked C9. docs.title: Exact second-order phase representation
docs.text:
All vectors below lie on the global mean-zero leaf. The actual connected support makes \(A\) positive definite there, with

\[ A\succeq gI,\quad g=1/10,\qquad \|A\|_2\le2, \qquad \|F\|_2\le M=\sqrt{27},\quad \|DF\|_2\le K=2 . \tag{5} \]

The last inequality follows from the symmetric weighted cosine Laplacian: \(DF=-B\operatorname{diag}(w_e\cos\delta_e)B^T/4\), whose absolute quadratic form is bounded by that of \(L/4\). These bounds hold globally in the supplied continuous lifts, including phase-branch passages. They require no all-time acute assumption.

Put \(v=\theta_s\). Equation (3) gives an invertible representation on this leaf:

\[ v=Ax/\gamma,\qquad x=\gamma A^{-1}v,\qquad \boxed{\epsilon A^{-1}\theta_{ss}+\theta_s=F(\theta).} \tag{6} \]

Indeed, differentiating \(\theta_\tau=\gamma Ax\), substituting the form row and changing both derivatives to the same clock yields \(\epsilon\theta_{ss}=A(F-\theta_s)\). Conversely, (6) and the reconstruction of \(x\) give both original rows. The initial velocity is fixed by the original source:

\[ \theta(0)=\eta_\theta,\qquad \theta_s(0)=\frac{A(mQ+\eta_x)}{\gamma}. \tag{7} \]

It is not a freely reset slow initial condition. Form memory is retained as this velocity. If a nonzero global form mean were admitted, its conserved value would also have to be retained separately; it is zero under (4).

Let

\[ U(\theta)=\sum_{\{i,j\}}w_{ij}[1-\cos(\theta_j-\theta_i)], \qquad H=\tfrac12x^TLx+U(\theta). \]

Since \(\nabla U=-4F\), the same storage becomes

\[ \mathcal E:=H/4 =\frac\epsilon2v^TA^{-1}v+\frac14U(\theta),\qquad \boxed{\mathcal E_s=-\|v\|_2^2.} \tag{8} \]

Multiplication of (6) by \(v\) proves (8); it is the original loss identity in the new coordinates and clock. The matrix \(\epsilon A^{-1}\) is a derived structural coefficient for this model. Its occurrence does not identify an inertial mass, mechanical energy or a physical equation. Dropping the second derivative changes the model and needs an error bound.

docs.title: Uniform defect from the phase-descent field
docs.text:
Define the actual velocity defect

\[ r=v-F(\theta) =\frac{Lx-\gamma S(\theta)}{4\gamma} =-\frac{x_\tau}{\gamma}. \tag{9} \]

This is a consequence of both declared rows, not a pressure reconstructed from the response. Differentiating in structural time gives the exact law

\[ r_\tau=-[A+\epsilon DF(\theta)]r -\epsilon DF(\theta)F(\theta). \tag{10} \]

Both \(r\) and the forcing in (10) are globally mean zero. For \(\lambda=g-K\epsilon>0\), the Euclidean norm therefore satisfies

\[ D^+\|r\|_2\le-\lambda\|r\|_2+\epsilon KM. \tag{11} \]

For nonzero \(r\), this follows by pairing (10) with \(r/\|r\|_2\) and using (5); the upper right derivative extends the inequality through zero.

The source gradient from the actual weighted support satisfies \(\|LQ\|_2^2=2277/2\). Since \(F(0)=0\), a full-source initial bound is

\[ R_0=\frac{m\sqrt{2277/2}}{4\gamma} +\frac{2\sqrt{27}\,r_x}{\gamma} +2\sqrt{27}\,r_\theta\ \ge\ \|r(0)\|_2 . \tag{12} \]

It retains the two independent errors and does not replace the original source by a recovered or stationary state. Solving (11) gives

\[ \|r(\tau)\|_2\le R(\tau):= R_0e^{-\lambda\tau} +\frac{\epsilon KM}{\lambda}(1-e^{-\lambda\tau}). \tag{13} \]

In particular, the simpler monotone upper envelope \(R_0e^{-\lambda\tau}+\epsilon KM/\lambda\) is available without deciding whether \(R_0\) exceeds the asymptotic bound.

At the analytic release time \(\tau_0=400\), outward rational enclosures give

\[ R_0e^{-400\lambda}+\frac{\epsilon KM}{\lambda} <\rho:=\frac{11}{10^6}. \tag{14} \]

The left side is approximately \(0.000010061734672\). It decreases thereafter, so the complete law satisfies, for every \(\tau\ge400\),

\[ \boxed{\|\theta_s-F(\theta)\|_2<\rho.} \tag{15} \]

No phase trajectory was evaluated to choose (14). Time 400 is an analytic release for a uniform estimate, not a reserved acquisition deadline. For other nonnegative primitive error allowances, (12)--(14) must be recomputed and may be unavailable. The original errors in (4) supply the frozen conclusion.

The bound is uniform on velocity defect, not on distance to any chosen first-order trajectory. Small persistent defects can accumulate or act across a basin boundary. It would be invalid to replace (15) by an infinite-time shadowing or common-attractor assertion.

The actual phase potential nevertheless obeys the useful inequality

\[ U_s=-4F(\theta)\mathbin{\cdot}[F(\theta)+r] \le-4\|F(\theta)\|_2\,[\|F(\theta)\|_2-\rho]. \]

Thus it strictly decreases wherever \(\|F\|_2>\rho\) after release. Near the critical set this inequality is inconclusive; the complete storage (8) remains the exact monotone quantity everywhere.

docs.title: Actual receiver phase motion at release
docs.text:
The source-controlled transport estimate in the mechanism proof applies at any declared time. Set \(P=\alpha Q\), and define

\[ \begin{split} A_0&=\gamma(m\sqrt{120}+\sqrt{27}\,r_x),\\ B_0&=e^{-40}A_0+10\epsilon\sqrt{27},\\ b_0&=\sqrt{120}|\gamma m-\alpha| +\sqrt{27}(r_\theta+\gamma r_x) +B_0+400\epsilon\sqrt{27}. \end{split} \tag{16} \]

Then

\[ \|\gamma x(400)\|_2\le B_0,\qquad \|\theta(400)-P\|_2\le b_0<21/100000 . \tag{17} \]

The phase radius is approximately \(0.000207559164\). The rational ramp mismatch remains explicit: \(355/113\) is not set equal to \(\pi\). At release the donor principal internal differences are \(\alpha\) plus at most \(\sqrt2b_0\), while receiver differences have magnitude at most \(\sqrt2b_0\). Their respective windings are therefore still \((1,1,0)\). More strongly, for every \(200\le\tau\le400\), the phase radius is bounded by

\[ \sqrt{120}|\gamma m-\alpha| +\sqrt{27}(r_\theta+\gamma r_x) +e^{-20}A_0+10\epsilon\sqrt{27}+400\epsilon\sqrt{27}. \]

This also has positive donor branch margin. Thus neither donor loses its acquired winding between its certified time-200 state and release. The earlier receiver-delay theorem already covers that whole interval.

The exact reference receiver current is

\[ F_{2,j}(P)=\tfrac14(1+\cos\alpha)\sin(\alpha(j-4)). \tag{18} \]

The degree-four support and the sine Lipschitz bound give, nodewise,

\[ |F_i(\theta(400))-F_i(P)|\le\sqrt2b_0 . \tag{19} \]

For all eight noncentral receiver nodes, (15), (18) and (19) imply

\[ \operatorname{sign}(j-4)\,\theta_{s,2,j}(400) >\tfrac14(1+\cos\alpha)\sin(\pi/9)-\sqrt2b_0-\rho >\frac3{20}. \tag{20} \]

The estimate keeps every permitted source error, so it is not restricted to the exactly symmetric nominal source. No sign is claimed for the central receiver node. In structural time the rate bound is multiplied by \(\epsilon\), and in original time also by \(1023/1024\). Positive instantaneous phase motion does not guarantee a branch crossing, monotone motion at later times or retained donor identity thereafter.

docs.title: Source-aware corridor and terminal-capture contract
docs.text:
Use elapsed slow time \(u=\epsilon( au-400)\). The actual post-release phase is an absolutely continuous solution of the inclusion

\[ heta_u=F( heta)+r(u),\qquad \|r(u)\|_2< ho, \qquad \| heta(0)-P\|_2\le b_0. ag{21} \]

The error \(r\) is the dynamically constrained defect (9), not a supplied controller. The inclusion is an outer description: proving a property for every admissible disturbance proves it for the full law, while an unsuccessful inclusion bound does not refute acquisition.

For example, let a proposed differentiable phase corridor be described by \(h_k( heta)\le0\). A strict outward-boundary estimate

\[ abla h_k( heta)\mathbin{\cdot}F( heta) + ho\| abla h_k( heta)\|_2<0 ag{22} \]

on each active boundary, together with source inclusion, prevents a first exit of the actual phase. A separately admitted finite reference can instead provide a tube. On an interval of slow length \(h\), let \(w(u)\) have global mean zero, continuous declared lifts, and a rigorously bounded residual \(\|w_u-F(w)\|_2\le\eta\). Suppose both the reference and its prospective error ball lie in a convex domain \(D\) within the conserved global mean-zero phase leaf, and freshly bound

\[ \mu\ge\sup_{z\in D} \lambda_{\max} igl(DF(z)|_{\mathbf1^\perp} igr). ag{23} \]

The symmetric Jacobian preserves \(\mathbf1^\perp\). The restriction retains the actual error directions and permits a negative relative growth bound; the full 27-coordinate Jacobian always has the common-phase zero mode. Every error ball below is taken within the same mean-zero leaf. If the incoming phase error is at most \(e_0\), then a sufficient whole-interval error envelope is

\[ e(u)=e^{\mu u}e_0+( ho+\eta) egin{cases} (e^{\mu u}-1)/\mu,&\mu e0,\ u,&\mu=0. \end{cases} ag{24} \]

The proof pairs the error equation with its normalized error, uses the signed logarithmic bound (23), and integrates its scalar inequality. Strict inclusion of \(w(u)+\overline B_{e(u)}\) in \(D\) closes the first-exit argument; a presumed future tube cannot certify its own premise. The global choice \(\mu=K=2\) is always available, but sharper local bounds may be essential. At the first interval take \(w(0)=P\), \(e_0=b_0\); later intervals inherit the complete preceding endpoint error, without resetting it to zero. Any residual, state, lift, Jacobian or source premise must be re-admitted rather than copied from a report's cached verdict.

Throughout that finite transport, each donor's fixed registered internal edge must satisfy

\[ |\delta_e(w(u))|+\sqrt2e(u)<\pi . ag{25} \]

The seam integers are the winding-one donor integers admitted at release. Equation (25) retains each donor identity continuously. The receiver must be allowed to cross its initial principal branch; an imposed all-time acute receiver cell would exclude the outcome being tested.

For terminal capture, use the equal-support target \(\Theta=\alpha(q,q,q)\) and the full-state barrier from the capture owner. The full form remains bounded for every \( au\ge400\) by \(\|x( au)\|_2\le X_0:=B_0/\gamma\). At a proposed terminal reference \(w_*\), with certified phase error \(e_*\), require both

\[ \max_{ ext{fine }e}|\delta_e(w_*)|+\sqrt2e_*<2, ag{26} \]

and

All edge integers in (26) are the fixed integers registered to \(\Theta\), including the receiver and contact edges. The potential and gradient in (27) use the actual complete weighted support. The global Hessian bound \(\| abla^2U\|_2\le8\) proves the phase remainder \(4e_*^2\); the same Laplacian bound proves the form contribution \(4X_0^2\). The linear gradient term generally does not vanish and must be retained. A phase-only energy or separately passing marginal budgets cannot replace (26)--(27) on the same state.

If a source-admitted corridor or finite tube proves donor retention and (26)--(27), the actual full state enters the joined trapping sublevel. The existing barrier then proves winding one in every constituent for all future time and convergence to the equal registered organization. No such corridor or endpoint is asserted here. The contract identifies the remaining nonlinear estimate without changing the source, law or clock.

The implementation rebuilds the primitive source, support, gradient norm, release transport and velocity-defect inequalities. It uses the shared preparation kernel and outward rational arithmetic. Its report certifies the reduction and release motion only; it accepts no trajectory or capture verdict. The execution plan remains the sole queue. A later numerical response must have its horizon, observation, source and budget frozen before evaluation. docs.title: Complete law, clock and regional balance
docs.text:
Use exactly the receiver source and support: three unit C9s with the fixed reciprocal contacts of offsets zero and one, each of weight one half, on the oriented region pairs \((0,1),(1,2),(2,0)\). Every node has weighted degree four. Write

\[ A=L/4,\qquad S_i(\theta)=\sum_jw_{ij}\sin(\theta_j-\theta_i), \qquad \gamma=1/(1023\pi). \]

In the declared structural clock \(\tau=(1023/1024)t\), the full law is

\[ x_\tau=\tfrac14[-Lx+\gamma S(\theta)],\qquad \theta_\tau=\tfrac\gamma4Lx. \tag{1} \]

Retain all 54 form and phase coordinates. Common form translation and common phase rotation preserve (1); global means are conserved. Regional means need not be. The circular phase is represented by a continuous lift for the following balances, whose energies and branch-normal rates do not depend on a common phase origin. Storage and integrated work are in this model's nondimensional structural storage units. None has an admitted laboratory-energy interpretation.

For one region \(r\), let \(L_{I,r}\) be its unit-cycle Laplacian. Restrict the internal and contact forces to that region:

\[ \ell_r=L_{I,r}x_r,\qquad b_r=(L_Cx)_r,\qquad s_r=(S_I(\theta))_r,\qquad c_r=(S_C(\theta))_r. \]

Its internal phase potential and complete internal storage are

\[ U_r(\theta_r)=\sum_{j=0}^8 [1-\cos(\theta_{r,j+1}-\theta_{r,j})],\qquad H_r=\tfrac12x_r^TL_{I,r}x_r+U_r, \tag{2} \]

with indices modulo nine. Define the nonnegative internal loss and signed boundary power by

\[ D_r=\tfrac14\|\ell_r\|^2,\qquad P_r=-\tfrac14\ell_r\cdot b_r +\tfrac\gamma4(\ell_r\cdot c_r-s_r\cdot b_r). \tag{3} \]

The regional balance then reads

\[ \frac{dH_r}{d\tau}=-D_r+P_r. \tag{4} \]

Indeed, \(\nabla_xH_r=\ell_r\) and \(\nabla_\theta H_r=-s_r\); applying both rows of (1) cancels the internal sine exchange. Boundary power has no fixed sign. It is determined by the retained neighboring state, rather than an independently chosen external input.

For a declared release time \(a\), put

\[ \mathcal W_r(\tau)=\int_a^\tau P_r(v)\,dv,\qquad \mathcal D_r(\tau)=\int_a^\tau D_r(v)\,dv\ge0. \]

The exact all-prefix identity is

\[ H_r(\tau)=H_r(a)+\mathcal W_r(\tau)-\mathcal D_r(\tau). \tag{5} \]

Changing to elapsed slow time \(u=\gamma^2(\tau-a)\) multiplies both instantaneous powers by \(\gamma^{-2}\); the integrated work and loss in (5) are unchanged. Omitting this clock factor changes the budget.

docs.title: A first-boundary barrier for winding zero and one
docs.text:
Fix the principal-branch integers at release, and continue the registered oriented gaps

\[ \delta_j(\tau)=\theta_{r,j+1}(\tau)-\theta_{r,j}(\tau)-2\pi k_j \tag{6} \]

until their first contact with \(\{-\pi,\pi\}\). Before that time, \(\delta_j\in(-\pi,\pi)\), and \(\sum_j\delta_j=2\pi w\) is the constant winding sum. At the first boundary contact all gaps lie in \([-\pi,\pi]\), and at least one is \(\pi\) or \(-\pi\). Winding at the boundary itself is not used.

For every \(|d|\le\pi\), concavity of sine on \([0,\pi/2]\) gives

\[ 1-\cos d=2\sin^2(|d|/2)\ge 2d^2/\pi^2. \tag{7} \]

Suppose first that \(w=1\). If one boundary gap is \(+\pi\), the remaining eight sum to \(\pi\). By Cauchy--Schwarz and (7),

\[ U_r\ge2+\frac2{\pi^2}\frac{\pi^2}{8}=\frac94. \tag{8} \]

If the chosen boundary gap is \(-\pi\), the other eight sum to \(3\pi\), giving the stronger bound \(U_r\ge17/4\). Simultaneous boundary contacts cause no problem: select any one of them in the same argument. Since the form part of (2) is nonnegative, every first boundary contact from a winding-one cell obeys

\[ H_r\ge U_r\ge B,\qquad B=9/4. \tag{9} \]

For winding zero, a boundary gap \(\pm\pi\) leaves a sum \(\mp\pi\) for the other eight. Equations (8)--(9) therefore hold for its first boundary contact too.

The number \(9/4\) is a conservative lower bound, not an asserted sharp barrier or a universal TNFR constant. The theorem uses the marked unit C9 and the cosine potential in (2); different weights, cycles or constitutive potentials require their own bounds. Reaching this storage is necessary for a first branch passage, but does not prove that passage occurs.

docs.title: Reserves for the original full source family
docs.text:
Use the unchanged preparation with two original form ramps, nominal zero phase and independent per-coordinate errors bounded by \(10^{-10}\), with the separately declared regional zero sums at preparation. The slow-admission theorem rebuilds, at \(a=400\),

\[ \|x(a)\|_2\le X_0,\qquad \|\theta(a)-P\|_2\le b_0, \quad P=\alpha(q,q,0),\quad \alpha=2\pi/9,\quad q_j=j-4. \tag{10} \]

Here \(X_0\) is approximately \(0.016168003\), and \(b_0\) is approximately \(0.000207559164\). They are consequences of the original source, not new release preparations. Donor winding one is certified from \(\tau=200\) through release, while the receiver still has winding zero.

For the unit cycle, \(0\preceq L_{I,r}\preceq4I\). The Hessian of \(U_r\) is a cosine-weighted cycle Laplacian and satisfies \(\nabla^2U_r\preceq L_{I,r}\preceq4I\) at every lifted phase. Both the winding-one twist \(\alpha q\) and the zero phase are critical points of the internal potential. Taylor's integral remainder thus gives

\[ U_r(\vartheta+e)\le U_r(\vartheta)+2\|e\|_2^2 \quad\text{for }\vartheta\in\{\alpha q,0\}. \tag{11} \]

There is no omitted linear term here: it vanishes at these internal critical points. This does not assert that \(P\) is a critical point of the complete contact potential.

Each regional restriction of the errors in (10) has norm at most the full-state bound. Consequently, simultaneously for both donors,

\[ H_r(a)\le\overline H_D :=9(1-\cos\alpha)+2X_0^2+2b_0^2,\qquad r=0,1, \tag{12} \]

and for the receiver

\[ H_2(a)\le\overline H_R:=2X_0^2+2b_0^2. \tag{13} \]

The associated guaranteed reserves are

\[ R_D=B-\overline H_D>143/1000,\qquad R_R=B-\overline H_R>2249/1000. \tag{14} \]

Their outward evaluations are approximately \(0.143877\) and \(2.249477\), respectively. The implementation rebuilds the source, support and outward trigonometric bounds before asserting positivity. All original error directions remain; no nominal symmetry is imposed. The separate regional upper bounds reuse full-state norm budgets and must not be mistaken for an exact additive partition of the initial storage or of its uncertainty.

docs.title: Conditional retention and necessary receiver work
docs.text:
Consider a donor starting in the release winding-one cell with (12). If, for every \(\tau\in[a,T]\),

\[ \mathcal W_r(\tau)-\mathcal D_r(\tau)<R_D, \tag{15} \]

then it cannot touch a branch boundary on that interval. Otherwise its first contact \(\sigma\le T\) would satisfy (9), whereas (5), (12) and (15) imply \(H_r(\sigma)<B\), a contradiction. This proves continuous winding-one retention, including the already admitted time-200 to release bridge.

A certified upper bound for the supremum of the net work over the whole interval is sufficient when it is strictly smaller than \(R_D\). Because each prefix includes release, this supremum is nonnegative. An endpoint-only budget cannot exclude an earlier passage and return. Equality at the barrier is inconclusive. The stronger all-prefix condition \(\mathcal W_r<R_D\) is sufficient because \(\mathcal D_r\ge0\). Likewise, a proved pointwise bound \(P_r\le D_r\) on a domain reached by the actual source would make its net work nonincreasing. None of these power restrictions follows from complete-system dissipation alone.

Conversely, if a donor first touches its branch boundary at \(\sigma\), then the exact balance gives

\[ \mathcal W_r(\sigma)-\mathcal D_r(\sigma) =H_r(\sigma)-H_r(a)\ge B-H_r(a)\ge R_D, \tag{16} \]

or \(\mathcal W_r(\sigma)\ge R_D+\mathcal D_r(\sigma)\). This is a condition at first contact, not a claim that the threshold was already crossed strictly before contact. A touch without a change in winding also satisfies it. Budget failure alone proves no loss.

For the receiver, any first exit from its winding-zero branch cell needs

\[ \mathcal W_2(\sigma)-\mathcal D_2(\sigma)\ge R_R, \qquad \mathcal W_2(\sigma)\ge R_R+\mathcal D_2(\sigma). \tag{17} \]

The receiver's necessary net-work bound exceeds the upper bound sufficient to certify donor retention through (15). This compares the declared reserves; it neither makes (15) necessary for retention nor specifies the actual power ratios. Equation (17) is only a necessary precursor: it does not select the crossing direction, prevent a return, or prove joined capture.

The joint question is whether the actual contact dynamics can satisfy both donor all-prefix conditions while delivering a receiver passage and the separate complete-state capture conditions. The inequalities alone are neither an existence proof nor an incompatibility proof. In particular, the receiver need not receive its net work by increasing donor internal storage. Contact storage must remain in the accounting. If

\[ H_C=\tfrac12x^TL_Cx+ \sum_{\text{contact }\{i,j\}}w_{ij}[1-\cos(\theta_j-\theta_i)], \qquad \mathcal D_{\rm all}(\tau) =\int_a^\tau\tfrac14\|Lx(v)\|^2\,dv, \]

then \(H=\sum_rH_r+H_C\) and the complete loss identity imply

\[ \sum_r[\mathcal W_r(\tau)-\mathcal D_r(\tau)] =H_C(a)-H_C(\tau)-\mathcal D_{\rm all}(\tau). \tag{18} \]

Internal losses do not add to complete loss without the contact cross terms. The already supplied contact state, its own storage change and complete loss all constrain work distribution. Loss is not an event reserve, and this continuous balance supplies no contact-occurrence law.

docs.title: Why a phase-only cell does not enforce retention
docs.text:
For an internal oriented edge let \(b=e_j-e_i\). Its registered gap in (6) has exact normal velocity

\[ \delta_\tau=\gamma b^TAx. \tag{19} \]

At any fixed boundary phase, both forms \(x=cb\) and \(x=-cb\), \(c>0\), are finite signed forms with zero global mean. On this support, the two endpoint degrees are four and the internal edge weight is one, so

\[ b^TAb=\tfrac14(4+4+2)=5/2, \qquad \delta_\tau=\pm5\gamma c/2. \tag{20} \]

Thus the same boundary phase admits both inward and outward normal motion under the unchanged law. The amplitude \(c\) can be arbitrarily small; an unsigned small-form assertion alone does not select the sign. Boundary phases with only that gap on the boundary exist, for example one gap \(\pi\) and eight gaps \(\pi/8\) for winding one. They can be represented on the global mean-zero phase leaf. Smoothness then also provides nearby interior states with an outward passage.

Consequently a winding cell extended over all admitted mean-zero forms is not forward invariant. This is a complete-law obstruction to a phase-only universal retention argument, not a claim about which boundary states the original source actually reaches. It does not invalidate a full-state storage sublevel, a source-specific tube or an independently proved contact-work budget. Retaining form and boundary state is essential even when a reduced phase reference approximates one source accurately.

docs.title: Consequence of the preserved donor-loss evidence
docs.text:
The frozen enclosure already proves that both donors lose winding one for every original admitted source, while the receiver stays winding zero throughout the validated interval. It retains both donor identities through elapsed slow time \(37/4\), and establishes both losses by \(19/2\). Each donor therefore has a first boundary contact in that interval, possibly at a different time for different sources or donors.

Combining that preserved conclusion with (16) proves that each donor's actual accumulated boundary work reaches at least its guaranteed reserve plus its internal accumulated loss at its first contact. Accordingly, neither donor satisfies (15) over the complete evaluated interval. This is a derived necessary-work consequence of existing full-family evidence. It is not a newly measured work integral or a new trajectory evaluation; the frozen response is neither rerun nor rewritten.

Receiver retention in winding zero does not conversely establish that its net work stayed below (17): the barrier is necessary for passage, not sufficient. Nor does a failure of the donor sufficient budget prove that every preparation or every compatible TNFR law loses its donors. The three-ramp theorem retains its different source and its valid conditional acquisition result.

The source-rebuilding assessment in _organized_regional_retention.py evaluates the three release-storage bounds and reserves. Its optional supplied donor net-work prefix bound tests only the conditional inequality; it does not supply a measured history or establish its premise. The companion stored-state work observer rebuilds the regional powers from primitive form and phase and checks the instantaneous partition balance. A state observation is not an integrated work certificate. The observer's optional constitutive parameter is admitted by the shared composition-compatible law; zero preserves the sine calculation. Its own-law extension and distinct geometric barriers belong to the constitutive comparison. The source assessment above remains sine-only and supplies no changed-law release bound.

These results identify the missing mathematical obligation: control of the actual distribution of contact work, together with directional receiver passage and full-state capture. They provide no new forcing, operator event, constitutive selection or physical identification.

docs.title: Current-amplitude discrimination with calibrated uncertainty
Prospective decision and scope
docs.text:
The five-child specification gives a phase-free current statistic for an exact model. This gate asks whether one fixed input and one fixed observation separate that amplitude from a doubled amplitude after admitting nonzero uncertainty. It does not ask which law nature follows. No physical record, apparatus or new acquisition is evaluated.

Item Fixed declaration Models Full C9-by-C5 laws (3) with mu equal to 1 or 2; 45 forms and phases, 90 unit edges, held unit capacities, full-circle sine, neutral uniform-child inputs. The C5 carrier is an exact electrical reference; discarded fine state remains in the full model Preparation Independently supplied observation-start class: zero global form mean, abs(x_i)<=X=.01, theta_cj=psi_j+Phi_c+z_cj, zero child means of z, abs(z_cj)<=zeta=1e-6, principal mean gaps at most Aphase=7/5, winding in {-1,0,1}. Common phase is retained. This is not a formation certificate for the alternative or for changed calibration coefficients Input Same nominal cubic word for both laws: fifteen unit-duration ramps, each preceded by a plateau h=1e-5; epsilon .1, marked increments .1,-.2,.1; duration T=15.00015. Nominal coefficients and sensor conversion are fixed before any response Calibration and clock Independent positive ratios C,G,A,D defined below, each in [1-1e-8,1+1e-8]. Exact C5 component shapes and a constant command-clock ratio; arbitrary parasitics or time-dependent clock drift are outside this first domain Tracking Neutral child-uniform discrepancy d in (3), with total integral(norm_inf(d))<=F=1e-4; on each nominal plateau its integral is at most P=1e-15. No derivative or pointwise bound is presumed Observation Same 150 nominal-voltage-to-form scalars in (5,3,2,5) order for both laws; arbitrary correlated additive error eta_raw<=1e-14. Each reading is a sample or positive normalized average within its own inward endpoint aperture of radius delta<=1e-13 in nominal clock units Statistic Five unnormalized current norms (13), computed with nominal coefficients; no measured or inferred phase and no amplitude-dependent redefinition of the observed statistic Decision Require every whole-history identity/collar margin to be positive for both laws and the upper mu=1 current envelope to be strictly below the lower mu=2 envelope. Failed sufficient bounds mean unavailable separation, not impossibility or physical rejection Evidence Commit declaration, helper and driver before one analytical assessment of the stated joint box using outward dyadic128 intervals. No trajectory, scan, source replay, fitting or reserved experimental response

The error allowances are prospective mathematical premises, not measured instrument capabilities. A common initial-state class need not specify identical hidden states under the two hypotheses: separation must hold uniformly for either admissible initial state. The existing acquired source is included at mu=1 and nominal coefficients through its earlier proof. That proof does not establish acquisition under mu=2 or perturbed laws.

docs.title: 1. One nominal laboratory input and observation
docs.text:
Choose independently calibrated nominal c0,g0,a00>0 and keep

\[ \gamma=1/(1023\pi),\quad b_0=4g_0/c_0,\quad \kappa_0=a_{00}\gamma g_0/9,\quad v_0=a_{00}\gamma g_0/c_0, \quad j_0=a_{00}\gamma^2g_0^2/c_0. \tag{1} \]

Here a00 is the nominal voltage-phase constant, not a derived TNFR constant. Let C=c/c0, G=g/g0, A=a0/a00. A positive constant D relates the command coordinate to actual laboratory time by s=b0*D*t_lab. Thus D is instrument clock calibration, separate from the matching relation b=4g/c.

The physically specified current is I_cmd=9*b0*kappa0*f(s), with the same f for every calibration member and both laws. Delivery discrepancy is retained explicitly. Readout always uses the nominal voltage coordinate U=L5+ V/v0 and nominal inferred charge q_nom=c0*L5+ V=9*kappa0*U. Actual charge is q=C*q_nom. A common voltage gauge cancels; different unknown offsets require the declared sensor error. For per-island voltage error eta_V the nominal form error is at most 4*eta_V/(5*v0). Calibration is not silently refitted in this conversion.

For a circuit with j_actual=mu*a0*gamma^2*g^2/c, transforming both rows to these fixed coordinates gives the coefficients

\[ \lambda=G/(CD),\quad \rho=1/(CD),\quad \eta=1/(AD),\quad \beta=AG^2/(C^2D). \tag{2} \]

The full fine comparison explicitly supplies the corresponding laws

\[ x'=(-\lambda L_{45}x+\mu\gamma\beta S(\theta))/4 +R(\rho f+d),\qquad \theta'=\gamma\eta L_{45}x/4. \tag{3} \]

Prime denotes s. R repeats a child coordinate across its nine slots. On the helical carrier these equations give exactly the C5 circuit rows. Off it, internal cancellation leaves the actual mean external currents, not an assumed closed sine law. The complete fine extension is a model premise; a passive physical fine-node circuit has not been constructed. In particular the full fine source is not replaced by an ideal carrier.

Physical current discrepancy maps to d=delta_I/(9*b0*kappa0*C*D). The total integral F must be admitted from independent delivery evidence, including switch timing and leakage. The separate bound P is essential: a small total input error can otherwise concentrate in a reading window and mimic its signal. Neutrality preserves the zero form mean; nonneutral errors require another law and observation.

docs.title: 2. Whole-history bound for each law
docs.text:
Reuse only the explicit waveform, not the old response bound. Let z(s) be its known form offset and H(s) its phase command:

\[ f=z'+L_5z/4,\qquad H'=\gamma L_5z/4, \quad \|H\|_\infty\le4\epsilon/5, \quad J_z:=\int_0^T\|L_5z\|_\infty ds=32/(5\gamma). \tag{4} \]

The last equality follows from L5*z=4*a*k_c*s_cubic'/gamma, norm_inf(k_c)=4/5, nonnegative cubic derivative and total absolute increment two. Each offset vanishes at its ramp endpoints and throughout plateaus. H is continuous, starts and ends at zero, and each ring edge has nominal excursion at most epsilon.

Write y=x-rho*R*z. Its actual residual input is w=rho*(1-lambda)*R*L5*z/4+R*d. Heat contraction on the unchanged support and norm_inf(S)<=4 give, for each fixed calibration member,

\[ J=\rho|1-\lambda|J_z/4+F,\qquad M_\mu=X+\mu\gamma\beta T+J,\qquad \|y\|_\infty\le M_\mu. \tag{5} \]

The phase drift after subtracting the actual command etarhoH satisfies

\[ e_b'=\gamma\eta L_{45}y/4 =-\frac{\gamma\eta}{\lambda}y' +\frac{\mu\gamma^2\eta\beta}{4\lambda}S +\frac{\gamma\eta}{\lambda}w. \tag{6} \]

Integration across the whole word, including every switch, bounds the departure from the nominal initial shifted state by

\[ \|\theta(s)-\theta(0)-RH(s)\|_\infty\le E_\mu=2\gamma\eta M_\mu/\lambda +|\eta\rho-1|\,4\epsilon/5. \tag{7} \]

No stationary background or hidden-phase input is used. The sufficient identity margins are, separately for mu=1 and mu=2,

\[ 2\pi/9-2\zeta-2E_\mu,\quad \pi/2-2\pi/9-2\zeta-2E_\mu,\quad \pi/2-A_{phase}-\epsilon-2\zeta-2E_\mu,\quad \pi/2-2\zeta-4E_\mu. \tag{8} \]

Positive margins retain all five internal and nine outer identities and the circular collar. They neither select a winding nor prove formation. At final release the command and offset vanish; residual state is retained.

For boxes, compute positive upper bounds using shared outward gamma and coefficient intervals, lambda's positive lower endpoint where divided, and the absolute maxima of 1-lambda and eta*rho-1. Discarding box correlations enlarges the bounds; it cannot silently improve a verdict.

docs.title: 3. Readings with aperture and arbitrary integrable tracking
docs.text:
On a nominal plateau, actual child means obey

\[ U'=-\lambda L_5U/4+\mu\gamma\beta\bar S/4+d, \qquad \|U\|_\infty\le M_\mu,\quad \|\bar S\|_\infty\le2. \tag{9} \]

An inward aperture stays entirely within that plateau. Relative to its endpoint the form error of a sample, or positive normalized average, is bounded by

\[ n_\mu=\eta_{raw}+(\lambda M_\mu+\mu\gamma\beta/2)\delta+P. \tag{10} \]

The P term needs no pointwise tracking bound. Signed observation kernels need their own total-variation bound and are outside this declaration. Two-sided jitter crossing a ramp cannot use (10). The first sample looks forward into its plateau and the last backward; windows may overlap but must remain inside it. We require 0<=delta<=h.

Keep the same nominal corrected increment at receiver (c+1) mod 5: D=Q_r-P_r+h*[L5(P+Q)]_r/8. Its reference current is the initial fine current shifted by nominal H. Define

\[ B_{2,\mu}=4\lambda^2 M_\mu+2\lambda\mu\gamma\beta +4\mu\gamma^2\beta\eta M_\mu. \tag{11} \]

The corrected-increment error is bounded by

\[ b_\mu=\mu\gamma\beta hE_\mu +|1-\lambda|hM_\mu+B_{2,\mu}h^3/12 +P(1+h/2+\lambda h^2/4)+(2+h/2)n_\mu. \tag{12} \]

The first term bounds phase/current transport; the second is the unmatched diffusion coefficient in the nominal correction. The last is the exact absolute sum of the six raw endpoint coefficients. Arbitrary correlations between raw errors are permitted.

The tracking/trapezoid terms do not differentiate d. To see this, set v(s)=integral_plateau_start^s R*d and w=x-v on that plateau. The smooth drift differentiated along the absolutely continuous state has norm at most B2 apart from -lambda*L45*R*d/4. The trapezoid Peano kernel has maximum h^2/8; norm_inf(L45)<=8 therefore contributes at most lambda*h^2*P/4. The integral of d in v has trapezoid kernel s-h/2, bounded by h/2, contributing h*P/2. Direct input in the mean increment contributes P. This proves (12) for integrable tracking, without assuming finite derivative, exact switches or an unforced actual plateau.

docs.title: 4. A common phase-free amplitude observation
docs.text:
For every marked block form O=D_+-D_-, W=D_++D_--2*D_0 from its same three corrected readings. Define the physical nominal-current statistic with coefficients fixed before comparison:

\[ A_c=\frac{2j_0 O_c}{\gamma h\sin\epsilon},\qquad B_c=\frac{2j_0 W_c}{\gamma h(1-\cos\epsilon)},\qquad m_c=\sqrt{A_c^2+B_c^2}. \tag{13} \]

Neither candidate changes the raw readings, the input or this conversion. There is no division by its tested amplitude and no reconstructed phase. Equivalently compute the quadratures directly from nominal charge using the nominal plateau duration h/b0. Gamma cancels from the resulting charge conversion because 2*j0/(9*kappa0*gamma)=b0/2; it also cancels from the physical nominal waveform after substituting kappa0 and the cubic f. Thus choosing the command and observation does not fit the tested amplitude. Since q_nom=q/C and nominal instrument seconds equal D*t_lab, the reference amplitude in this statistic is j_actual/(C*D)=mu*beta*j0. It is not the uncorrected physical current amplitude when C or D differs from one.

Let Cc+iSc be the initial fine interface phasor. The initial residual prior gives cos(2*zeta)<=abs(Cc+iSc)<=1. For each model,

\[ |A_c/j_0-\mu\beta C_c|\le a_\mu=4b_\mu/(\gamma h\sin\epsilon),\qquad |B_c/j_0-\mu\beta S_c|\le b_\mu^*=8b_\mu/[\gamma h(1-\cos\epsilon)]. \tag{14} \]

The normalized bounds below are only a dimensionless way of displaying the same measured current, not an amplitude fit. With r_mu=sqrt(a_mu^2+(b_mu*)^2) and coefficient endpoints beta_minus/plus,

\[ m_c/j_0\in I_\mu= [\max(0,\mu\beta_-\cos(2\zeta)-r_\mu), \mu\beta_++r_\mu]. \tag{15} \]

Use outward sine, cosine and square-root enclosures. If the lower endpoint of I2 exceeds the upper endpoint of I1, the complete 150-reading record sets are disjoint: even one marked norm cannot belong to both intervals. This is uniform over the admitted unknown phases, fine deviations and correlated errors. It is a prospective discriminator, not an identification of either law by an unevaluated experiment. Real records outside both envelopes can invalidate premises or exclude both hypotheses; records inside one envelope still need complete physical admission.

docs.title: 5. Storage and boundaries of physical interpretation
docs.text:
With fixed positive coefficients each model has its own storage

\[ H_\mu=\tfrac12x^TL_{45}x+ \frac{\mu\beta}{\eta}\sum_e(1-\cos\delta_e),\qquad H_\mu'=-\lambda\|L_{45}x\|_2^2/4 +(L_{45}x)^TR(\rho f+d). \tag{16} \]

This follows by cancellation using both rows. It is not the earlier mu=1 storage when the coefficients change. Explicit finite bounds follow without a pointwise tracking assumption. Set Zpeak=24*epsilon/(5*gamma_lower), Gpeak=48*epsilon/(5*gamma_lower), Xpeak=rho*Zpeak+M_mu, Gfull=rho*Gpeak+8*M_mu and F1=56/(5*gamma_lower), an upper bound on the nominal input integral. Then

\[ \sup H_\mu\le180X_{peak}^2+180\mu\beta/\eta,\quad Loss\le45\lambda T G_{full}^2/4,\quad W_{abs}\le45G_{full}(\rho F_1+F). \tag{17} \]

The last bound also covers the sum of positive powers over all fine input channels integrated over time; no slot cancellation hides cost. Use positive interval upper endpoints throughout. The earlier numerical work ceilings are not inherited, and an L1 tracking bound does not supply an actuator peak or bandwidth limit. Preparation costs under the alternative and a physical fine-state energy map remain separate. All inputs and their timing are supplied; no autonomous force or event occurrence is inferred.

Constant scalar component ratios preserve the reference's exact shapes. Parasitics, nonuniform junction variation, nonlinear capacitance, phase noise and a time-dependent clock require additional terms and their own admission. This first comparison changes one scalar current amplitude; it is not a classification of possible laws or a proof that the sine profile is uniquely selected. The ontology continues to separate mathematical organization from physical identity.

docs.title: 6. Execution and evidence boundary
docs.text:
The pure bounds and raw statistic admit primitive intervals, nonnegative errors and ordered readings using shared owners. They rebuild all consumed fields; no cached margin or source report certifies the present law. The fixed corner is reserved to the exclusive analytical driver. The instrument tests and independent theory controls use other synthetic inputs and algebraic counterexamples, without assessing that corner or executing previous frozen producers.

The execution plan owns the result-dependent next gate. No physical observation or claim of practical sensor capability follows from evaluating this sufficient bound.

docs.title: 7. Frozen joint-box decision
docs.text:
Declaration, consuming helper and driver were committed at 98ccd8686592eea15ad22151802d731d683d70e2 before one assessment. The preserved attempt and result record verdict conditional_current_discrimination_admitted. Both models retain all four positive identity/collar margins, their current envelopes are strictly separated, and no unresolved condition remains within this declared sufficient-bound decision. The read-only evidence controls reconstruct its receipt, coefficient intervals, both laws' errors and identity margins, and the strict separation from archived primitives. They do not import or rerun the bound, driver or assessor.

docs.title: Observing outer winding on one continuing organization
Declared single-history observation contract
docs.text:
The matched-source inverse identifies a collective winding but assumes eleven continuations of one initial state. This gate asks whether one prescribed observation history can remove that premise while retaining unknown background motion and probe backaction.

Item Fixed choice and scope Complete model Same 45-node C9-by-C5 product, nodes 9*c+j, 90 unit edges, held unit capacities and smooth-sine phase domain; x_tau=(-Lx+gamma*S(theta))/4, theta_tau=gamma*Lx/4, gamma=1/(1023*pi), with no continuous input Clock tau=(1023/1024)*t; elapsed tau starts at the actual unknown initial source; all intervals and both continuous rows use this clock Initial class Exactly the earlier admitted class: every abs(x_i)<=X=1/100; theta[c,j]=2*pi*(j-4)/9+Phi_c+z[c,j], unknown lifted origins Phi, zero child-mean z and every abs(z[c,j])<=zeta=1e-6; principal adjacent origin gaps have magnitude at most A=7/5 and common winding w in {-1,0,1} Source scope Both earlier actually acquired families belong to this initial class by the existing inclusion theorem. Apply jumps +epsilon*k_c, -2*epsilon*k_c, +epsilon*k_c at local times h, 2h, 3h, with epsilon=1/10; forms, support and capacities are unchanged.
