The analytical task is to justify the sequential cancellation under the complete rows, not to substitute sequential samples into the earlier matched-source formula. A successful result would remove a mathematical preparation dependency while retaining externally supplied interventions, known law and clock, and an independently uncalibrated observation model.

The declaration above was committed as 8c0d4cca before assessment. The following proof evaluates its fixed rational bounds without integrating a trajectory or changing the protocol after observing the result.

docs.title: 1. One actual history and the initial identity
docs.text:
Write \(\psi_j=2\pi(j-4)/9\), and let \(a_c=\operatorname{wrap}(\Phi_{c+1}-\Phi_c)\) denote the initial child-origin gaps. The initial fine boundary gaps and their moments are

\[ d_{c,j}^0=a_c+z_{c+1,j}-z_{c,j},\qquad C_c^0=\frac19\sum_j\cos d_{c,j}^0,\qquad S_c^0=\frac19\sum_j\sin d_{c,j}^0. \tag{1} \]

The actual initial fine errors telescope around every outer slot cycle; each has sum \(2\pi w\), with the same unknown integer \(w\in\{-1,0,1\}\). The internal C9 cycles have winding one. These are identities of all 45 actual phase coordinates, not five assigned labels. The matched-source state argument establishes this initial class and includes both previously acquired sources without resetting their residuals. The present argument does not require the larger class to have a demonstrated acquisition mechanism.

Let \(g\) be the upper endpoint of the shared outward interval for \(\gamma\), and set

\[ T=20h,\qquad B=X+gT,\qquad D=4gBT. \tag{2} \]

Heat contraction for \(-L/4\), together with \(\|S(\theta)\|_\infty\le4\), gives \(\|x(t)\|_\infty\le X+gt\le B\) along the entire history. Phase events leave x unchanged. The full phase row gives \(\|\dot\theta\|_\infty\le2gB\), hence every edge accumulates continuous phase drift of magnitude at most D. Remove only the explicit cumulative commanded offset from the phase lift; its remaining drift is continuous through all fifteen events. At the start of every block the cumulative command is zero, but the evolved form and phase drift remain.

For a block starting at \(s_c=4ch\), let \(C_c^s,S_c^s\) be its actual boundary moments before any of that block's events. The global Lipschitz bounds for sine and cosine imply

\[ |C_c^s-C_c^0|\le D,\qquad |S_c^s-S_c^0|\le D. \tag{3} \]

Thus the proof can transport local information back to the original moments. It does not identify the starts of different blocks or reuse a state discarded by an earlier observation.

docs.title: 2. Exact cancellation and the unobserved comparison
docs.text:
For one block let \(Y_k\) be its five actual receiver mean forms, temporarily without readout error. In endpoint coordinates the two fixed combinations are

\[ \begin{split} D_C&=(Y_0-4Y_1+6Y_2-4Y_3+Y_4)/3,\\ D_S&=Y_0-2Y_1+2Y_3-Y_4. \end{split}\tag{4} \]

Both annihilate every quadratic polynomial in time. Their raw coefficient absolute sums are \(16/3\) and 6, respectively, giving exactly the declared worst-case reading-error bounds. A common endpoint is one reading, even when it occurs in two adjacent increments.

For the proof alone, continue the block's actual initial state without its three local events for a time \(H=4h\). Denote this hypothetical reference by \((\bar x,\bar\theta)\), and its receiver mean form by b. It is not measured and is never passed to the inverse. Its form bound is also B: it begins with \(\|x(s_c)\|_\infty\le X+gs_c\), and \(s_c+H\le T\). In particular, each block's reference retains all history accumulated before that block.

The degree-four full rows imply

\[ \begin{split} \|\dot{\bar x}\|_\infty&\le2B+g,\\ \|\ddot{\bar x}\|_\infty&\le4B+2g+4g^2B,\\ |b'''|\le\|\bar x'''\|_\infty &\le M_3:=8B+4g+16g^2B+4g^3+16g^3B^2. \end{split}\tag{5} \]

Indeed, each edge phase rate is at most \(4gB\), each edge phase acceleration at most \(4g(2B+g)\), and differentiating the four sine terms gives \(\|S''\|_\infty\le64g^2B^2+16g(2B+g)\). Together with \(\|L/4\|_\infty=2\), these yield (5). No equilibrium or constant background is assumed.

Writing \(E_h\) for time translation by h, the first combination on b is \((E_h-1)^4b/3\), and the second is \(-(E_h+1)(E_h-1)^3b\). A third finite difference is an integral of \(b'''\) over a cube of side h. Bounding the two third differences in each expression therefore gives

\[ |D_C[b]|\le\frac23M_3h^3,\qquad |D_S[b]|\le2M_3h^3. \tag{6} \]

This is the residual unknown background motion after the exact algebraic cancellation. It differs from the matched-source cancellation, where the same independently measured endpoint baseline cancels directly.

docs.title: 3. Complete nonlinear backaction within each block
docs.text:
At local time t let \(q(t)\in\{0,+\epsilon,-\epsilon,0\}\) be the commanded amplitude in its four windows. Write

\[ y=x-\bar x,\qquad v=\theta-\bar\theta-q(t)k_c. \tag{7} \]

The explicit event is removed from v, so both y and v are continuous and start at zero. Their differential equations, away from the event times, retain the full form diffusion and phase feedback. The phase row yields \(\|v(t)\|_\infty\le2g\int_0^t\|y(r)\|_\infty\,dr\). Every edge of the commanded offset has magnitude at most \(\epsilon\), and the global sine Lipschitz bound yields

\[ \|y(t)\|_\infty \le g\epsilon t+2g\int_0^t\|v(r)\|_\infty\,dr. \tag{8} \]

If \(2g^2H^2\le1/2\), a supremum argument at every time up to H gives

\[ \|y(t)\|_\infty\le2g\epsilon t,\qquad \|v(t)\|_\infty\le2g^2\epsilon t^2. \tag{9} \]

These estimates do not reset y or v at an event. In particular, setting q back to zero in the fourth window leaves the accumulated backaction.

Freeze only the reference phase at the block's initial state when defining the leading vector slope

\[ F_q=\frac\gamma4 \{S(\bar\theta(0)+qk_c)-S(\bar\theta(0))\}. \tag{10} \]

The function \(\sin(a+u)-\sin a\) has derivative with respect to a of magnitude at most \(|u|\). The reference edge drift at time t is at most \(4gBt\); the additional phase v has edge magnitude at most \(2\|v\|_\infty\). Using all four incident edges and (9),

\[ \|\dot y-F_q\|_\infty \le J(t):=4g\epsilon(1+gB)t+4g^3\epsilon t^2. \tag{11} \]

The first term includes \(\|Ly/4\|_\infty\), not just the pressure perturbation. This keeps the complete finite evolution rather than replacing a mean-form increment by an onset derivative.

For the receiver child \(c+1\), the mean of (10) at the two nonzero amplitudes is exactly

\[ A_\pm=\frac\gamma4 \{\mathord\pm\sin\epsilon\,C_c^s +(1-\cos\epsilon)S_c^s\}. \tag{12} \]

The four leading mean slopes are consequently \(0,A_+,A_-,0\). Integrate (11) using the absolute increment weights \((1/3,1,1,1/3)\) and \((1,1,1,1)\). Their first time moments are \((16/3)h^2\) and \(8h^2\), and their second time moments are \((116/9)h^3\) and \((64/3)h^3\). The resulting backaction remainders are

\[ \begin{split} E_C&=\frac{64}{3}g\epsilon(1+gB)h^2 +\frac{464}{9}g^3\epsilon h^3,\\ E_S&=32g\epsilon(1+gB)h^2 +\frac{256}{3}g^3\epsilon h^3. \end{split}\tag{13} \]

This argument applies independently to every block's actual carried start; the uniform constants retain all earlier effects through B and D.

docs.title: 4. Initial quadratures and uniform winding identification
docs.text:
Define positive outward response factors \(f_C=g h[\sin\epsilon]^+/2\) and \(f_S=g h[1-\cos\epsilon]^+/2\), where a plus denotes the interval upper endpoint. Combining the background terms (6), the backaction terms (13), the exact reading coefficients, and the transport bound (3) gives

\[ \begin{split} D_C&=\frac{\gamma h\sin\epsilon}{2}C_c^0+\delta_C, &|\delta_C|&\le b_C:=E_C+\frac23M_3h^3 +\frac{16}{3}\eta+f_CD,\\ D_S&=\frac{\gamma h(1-\cos\epsilon)}2S_c^0+\delta_S, &|\delta_S|&\le b_S:=E_S+2M_3h^3+6\eta+f_SD. \end{split}\tag{14} \]

The two inferred moments are now explicitly those of the original unknown state. Later blocks need no pretended common preparation. Both errors are uniform over all allowed initial forms, fine phases and reading errors.

The initial-moment inverse therefore applies with these new error bounds: scale the raw combinations by \(K_C=2/([\gamma]h[\sin\epsilon])\) and \(K_S=2/([\gamma]h[1-\cos\epsilon])\), and intersect with the original cosine prior \([c_0,1]\), \(c_0=[\cos(A+2\zeta)]^->0\), and sine prior \([-1,1]\). The original annulus \(\cos(2\zeta)\le|C_c^0+iS_c^0|\le1\) remains a necessary check because (14) transports to the initial moments. Every raw form reading must also have magnitude at most \(B+\eta\).

Take the outward argument of each surviving moment rectangle, enlarge by \(2\zeta\) on each side, and clip to \([-A,A]\). This encloses each original origin gap \(a_c\). Sum the five intervals and retain the candidate sectors whose outward \(2\pi w\) intervals intersect that sum. Under the actual-source premises the true sector is retained. A singleton then identifies it; the filters and sector intersections alone do not prove that arbitrary raw records arise from one admitted trajectory.

For clarity, the uniform interval-width bound uses the same shared outward rounding allowances as the matched-source proof. With \(u=2^{-128}\),

\[ \begin{split} \rho_K&=(2K^++\operatorname{wid}(K)+2)u,\\ w_C&=2K_C^+b_C+\operatorname{wid}(K_C)(f_C+2b_C)+\rho_{K_C},\\ w_S&=2K_S^+b_S+\operatorname{wid}(K_S)(f_S+2b_S)+\rho_{K_S},\\ d&=w_S/c_0+w_C/c_0^2+4\zeta+10^{-20}. \end{split}\tag{15} \]

Here d bounds each initial-angle interval width, and \(5d\) bounds the cycle-sum width. The existing argument-evaluation proof applies on the same domain \(c_0>1/6\), \(|S|\le1\); no precision or transcendental kernel is changed. The fixed exact-rational outward assessment gives conservative strict bounds

\[ \begin{split} B&<0.010000063,&D&<2.489243\cdot10^{-9},&M_3&<0.081245127,\\ b_C&<7.176748\cdot10^{-14},&b_S&<1.057319\cdot10^{-13},&c_0&>0.169965,\\ w_C&<0.000924139,&w_S&<0.027207175,&d&<0.192069229,\\ 5d&<0.960346143,&2\pi-5d&>5.322839. \end{split}\tag{16} \]

The separated winding values are more than 6.28 apart, whereas the cycle interval is less than 0.961 wide. Outward widths of the three fixed \(2\pi w\) enclosures are smaller than the positive separation margin. Thus every actual admitted initial state and every allowed reading error yields exactly one necessary sector. This is a uniform conditional identification theorem, not a classification of sampled sources.

docs.title: 5. Signed event work and retention of the continuing identity
docs.text:
Each event changes eighteen outer edges and no internal gaps or forms. For its actual pre-event gaps, the signed storage jump is

\[ W=\sum_{e\ \mathrm{changed}} \{\cos d_e-\cos(d_e+\Delta q\,\Delta k_{c,e})\}. \tag{17} \]

The cosine Lipschitz bound gives \(|W|\le18|\Delta q|\). The three event amplitudes in each block have magnitudes \(\epsilon,2\epsilon,\epsilon\); hence every absolute work is at most \(36\epsilon=3.6<4\), and

\[ \sum_{\text{15 events}}|W| \le5\cdot18(\epsilon+2\epsilon+\epsilon)=36<40. \tag{18} \]

These bounds evaluate the storage law on each event's actual state without prescribing the sign of its work. The final inverse command does not undo the middle event's payment or return the evolved state. No continuous loss is credited as a reserve, and no reservoir or event-occurrence law is deduced.

At any point in the word, each commanded outer edge offset has magnitude at most \(\epsilon\), including the endpoints of the larger middle jump. The full continuous drift is bounded by D. Thus

\[ \begin{split} \alpha-2\zeta-D&>0.698129698,\\ \pi/2-\alpha-2\zeta-D&>0.872662623,\\ \pi/2-A-2\zeta-\epsilon-D&>0.070794324, \qquad \alpha=2\pi/9. \end{split}\tag{19} \]

Internal gaps remain positive and acute; outer gaps remain strictly acute at all times and on both sides of every event. Each supplied event is a single-valued vertex phase offset, so its increments telescope around every marked cycle. Continuous drift cannot cross a phase-chart boundary. All five internal winding-one identities and all nine original outer windings therefore persist throughout \([0,T]\). Identification of the original winding consequently identifies the continuing object's winding over this finite history. This does not prove future maintenance after T or recovery under indefinitely repeated observations.

docs.title: 6. Result and implementation boundary
docs.text:
The fixed word identifies the unknown outer winding from 25 collective form readings of one carried organization. It removes the earlier need for eleven matched initial-state branches. The theorem retains unknown background motion, nonlinear backaction, the complete fine state, all fifteen signed events and arbitrary bounded reading errors. Work and identity have separately proved finite bounds.

The sequential observation owner admits primitive readings and rebuilds the fixed protocol before applying the shared necessary initial-moment inverse. Its contract tests cover exact observation coefficients, actual signed event transformations, invalid domains, uniform margins and conditional inference. Algebraic synthetic records exercise the proved information envelope; they are not presented as numerically evaluated trajectories or new formation evidence. The previous matched-source protocol and its result remain unchanged.

Known support, law and structural clock, access to each prescribed event, and the bounded mean-form observation model remain assumptions. The word is externally supplied, not an autonomously selected sensor or an admitted registered operator sequence. The collective NFR keeps its declared identity together with constituent and boundary state; a winding label does not replace that state or establish a physical identification.

docs.title: Information from a small phase preparation
docs.text:
The two admitted constitutive laws can produce different finite observations without an initial mean-form contrast or a complete relative phase turn. For the two-C9 quarter-factor model, a supplied small relative phase \(d\) gives an endpoint mean-form separation proportional to \(\gamma d^3\). This owner bounds that separation from both sides and retains independent preparation and observation errors for the two candidate laws.

The question is a resource-information tradeoff for one specified observation, not the minimum resource for every possible experiment. The earlier organized nonlinear comparison already establishes finite constitutive discrimination on its different complete model. The new obligation is to relate a small declared phase resource to both distinguishable and indistinguishable endpoint records. Task status belongs to the research program.

docs.title: 1. Complete law and the endpoint observation
docs.text:
Keep the ordered eighteen nodes \(9c+k\), with \(c=0,1\) and \(k=0,\ldots,8\). Each marked child is a unit-weight C9. The nine matching edges have the fixed common weight \(a=\gamma^2/1000\), where \(\gamma=1/(1023\pi)\). Capacity is held at one; no input, impulse, capacity change or later support event is admitted. The state-preserving initial attachment and its work are supplied separately from the continuing flow.

With \(L=I_2\otimes L_9+aL_{\rm match}\), the complete structural law in clock \(\tau\) is

\[ \begin{split} V_\lambda(u)&=1-\cos u+ \lambda\frac{(1-\cos9u)^2}{6\,9^4},\\ j_\lambda(u)&=\sin u+\lambda h(u),\qquad h(u)=\frac{\sin9u(1-\cos9u)}{2187},\\ U_\lambda(\theta)&=\sum_e w_eV_\lambda(\theta_i-\theta_j),\\ x_\tau&=\frac{-Lx-\gamma\nabla U_\lambda}4, \qquad \theta_\tau=\frac{\gamma Lx}4, \qquad 0\le\lambda\le1. \end{split} \tag{1} \]

Both rows use the same weights and the unchanged canonical \(\gamma\). The pressure is specified by the form row, independently of the response. This is the retained comparison law, not a native operator word or a reciprocal-degree normalization. Smooth bounded currents and the linear form terms give global continuation in continuous phase lifts. The uniform current bounds, derived from (1), are

\[ |j_\lambda|\le J_0=\frac{1459}{1458},\qquad |j_\lambda'|\le J_1=\frac{245}{243},\qquad |j_\lambda''|\le J_2=\frac{10}{9}. \tag{2} \]

Write \(\alpha=2\pi/9\) and retain the marked closing-edge turn. The actual state decomposes as

\[ x_{c,k}=X_c+z_{c,k},\qquad \theta_{c,k}=\alpha(k-4)+\Phi_c+q_{c,k},\qquad \sum_k z_{c,k}=\sum_k q_{c,k}=0. \tag{3} \]

Thus \(r=X_A-X_B\) is a raw mean-form difference, \(v=\gamma r\), and \(\delta=\Phi_A-\Phi_B\) is a relative continuous phase lift. The time coordinate \(s=a\tau/2\) transforms both rows; the nominal readout \(s=1\) corresponds to \(\tau=2000/\gamma^2\), not to a claimed laboratory duration. Internal edge sums cancel exactly, giving

\[ v_s=-v-\gamma^2\overline J_\lambda, \qquad \delta_s=v, \qquad \overline J_\lambda= \frac19\sum_k j_\lambda(\delta+q_{A,k}-q_{B,k}). \tag{4} \]

The nominal preparation has \(x=0\), \(q=z=0\), \(\Phi_A=d/2\), \(\Phi_B=-d/2\), with

\[ 0<d\le\frac1{100}. \tag{5} \]

The carrier \(q=z=0\) is invariant: internal currents cancel and each matching current is constant over its child. On it, \(\overline J_\lambda=j_\lambda(\delta)\), \(v(0)=0\), and \(\delta(0)=d\). The observation is one endpoint raw contrast \(R_\lambda(d)=r_\lambda(1)\). It is neither a derivative estimate nor the harmonic integral used by the full-turn probe. Every nominal child retains its winding-one phase profile exactly.

This preparation supplies a relative phase. It does not derive the formation of either C9, autonomous attachment, an observation apparatus or a source of the required work. The NFR ontology distinguishes this conditional structural observation from physical identification.

docs.title: 2. A two-sided nominal information bound
docs.text:
Let \(G=\gamma^2\). The canonical parameter satisfies \(G<10^{-7}\), using \(\pi>157/50\). On \(0<u\le d\), both \(\sin u\) and \(h(u)\) are positive, while \(j_\lambda(u)\le J_1u\). Variation of constants in (4), until a possible first exit from \(0<\delta_\lambda\le d\), gives

\[ \begin{split} -GJ_1d(1-e^{-s})&\le v_\lambda(s)\le0,\\ d-GJ_1d(s-1+e^{-s})&\le\delta_\lambda(s)\le d,\\ \delta_\lambda(s)&\ge d(1-GJ_1s^2/2)>\frac{99}{100}d \qquad(0\le s\le3/2). \end{split} \tag{6} \]

Here \(s-1+e^{-s}\le s^2/2\). The positive lower bound excludes exit through zero, and \(v_\lambda\le0\) excludes exit through the upper endpoint. This closes the corridor for every admitted \(\lambda\).

The perturbing current has a cubic bound obtained directly from its trigonometric factors:

\[ |h(u)|\le\frac{|u|^3}{6}\quad(u\in\mathbb R),\qquad h(u)\ge\frac{1081}{6912}u^3\quad(0<u\le1/18). \tag{7} \]

The upper bound uses \(|\sin9u|\le9|u|\) and \(1-\cos9u\le(9u)^2/2\). For the lower bound, put \(z=9u\le1/2\): \(\sin z\ge(23/24)z\) and \(1-\cos z\ge(47/96)z^2\) follow from the cubic and quartic Taylor bounds. In particular, (6) yields

\[ \frac{d^3}{7}<h(\delta_1(s))\le\frac{d^3}{6}. \tag{8} \]

For the endpoint comparison restrict again to \(0\le s\le1\). Put \(D(s)=\delta_1(s)-\delta_0(s)\). Subtract their exact Volterra equations, using the shared initial state:

\[ D(s)=-G\int_0^s(1-e^{-(s-t)}) \left[\sin\delta_1(t)-\sin\delta_0(t)+h(\delta_1(t))\right]dt. \tag{9} \]

Since sine is globally one-Lipschitz and the kernel lies in \([0,1]\), \(|D(s)|\le G\int_0^s(|D(t)|+d^3/6)\,dt\). The integral comparison and \(e^G-1\le2G\) give

\[ |D(s)|\le\frac{d^3}{6}(e^{Gs}-1)\le\frac{Gd^3}{3}. \tag{10} \]

Combining (8)--(10), with the strict canonical bound on \(G\), gives

\[ \frac{d^3}{8} <h(\delta_1(s))+\sin\delta_1(s)-\sin\delta_0(s) <\frac{d^3}{5}. \tag{11} \]

Both histories react freely. Their endpoint contrast difference, directly from the form row rather than separate approximations to each history, is

\[ \begin{split} R_0(d)-R_1(d) &=\gamma\int_0^1e^{t-1} \left[h(\delta_1(t))+\sin\delta_1(t)-\sin\delta_0(t)\right]dt,\\ \boxed{\frac{\gamma d^3}{20} <R_0(d)-R_1(d)<\frac{\gamma d^3}{6}.} \end{split} \tag{12} \]

For these deliberately loose constants it suffices to use \(3/5<1-e^{-1}<2/3\). The sine endpoint is larger, although both nominal form contrasts are negative. The proof compares the two actual solutions analytically; it evaluates no numerical trajectory. Subtracting independent endpoint approximations with an \(O(\gamma^3d)\) error would not prove a uniform cubic law as \(d\to0\). The direct difference (9) retains the shared linear response and controls its constitutive correction at order \(Gd^3\).

docs.title: 3. Full fine state and independent preparation errors
docs.text:
For each candidate separately, admit the primitive bounds

\[ |r(0)|\le\varepsilon_r,\qquad |\delta(0)-d|\le\varepsilon_\delta,\qquad \|z(0)\|\le\rho_x,\qquad \|q(0)\|\le\rho_\theta. \tag{13} \]

The last two norms combine all eighteen residuals in (3); their means vanish separately in each child. The relative phase error uses the declared initial lifts. A common form offset or phase rotation is immaterial by the complete law's exact symmetries. The candidates may choose different actual preparations anywhere in these bounds; no hidden pairing cancels their errors.

The uniform fine-retention proof uses neither a large mean form nor a particular mean phase. Its Hessian bounds hold over the entire relative phase circle. Consequently it applies here, and through the extended timing horizon, if

\[ F_0=\frac12(\rho_\theta+\gamma\rho_x)^2 +\frac12\gamma^2\rho_x^2<\frac1{40000}. \tag{14} \]

Both fine identities are retained, and the true current defect satisfies

\[ |\overline J_\lambda-j_\lambda(\delta)|\le B e^{-Ks}, \qquad B=\frac{4J_2F_0}{9},\qquad K=\frac{125}{2}. \tag{15} \]

This is the existing own-law estimate on every retained fine direction. It does not set the reached state to its carrier, infer the preparation from an operator label, or transfer a different law's source certificate.

Compare an actual history with the nominal history of its own law. Let \(\Delta r=r-r_{\lambda,\mathrm{nom}}\) and \(\Delta\delta=\delta-\delta_{\lambda,\mathrm{nom}}\). Variation of constants in the two actual mean rows gives

\[ \begin{split} \Delta r(s)&=e^{-s}r(0)-\gamma\int_0^s e^{-(s-t)} \left[j_\lambda(\delta(t))-j_\lambda(\delta_{\lambda,\mathrm{nom}}(t)) +e_f(t)\right]dt,\\ \Delta\delta(s)&=\delta(0)-d+\gamma(1-e^{-s})r(0) -G\int_0^s(1-e^{-(s-t)}) \left[j_\lambda(\delta(t))-j_\lambda(\delta_{\lambda,\mathrm{nom}}(t)) +e_f(t)\right]dt, \qquad |e_f(t)|\le Be^{-Kt}. \end{split} \tag{16} \]

For \(0\le t\le3/2\), define the following rational bounds:

\[ A=\varepsilon_\delta+\gamma\varepsilon_r+\frac{GB}{K}, \qquad P_t=\frac{A}{1-GJ_1t}. \tag{17} \]

The denominator is positive. Taking a supremum in the second row of (16) gives \(M_t\le A+GJ_1tM_t\), hence \(|\Delta\delta(s)|\le P_t\) for every \(s\le t\). At the nominal readout, the exact fine convolution is \((e^{-1}-e^{-K})/(K-1)\). Using \(e^{-1}<2/5\) and \(1-e^{-1}<2/3\) in the first row of (16) therefore gives

\[ |r(1)-R_\lambda(d)|\le E, \qquad E=\frac25\varepsilon_r+ \frac23\gamma J_1P_1+\frac25\frac{\gamma B}{K-1}. \tag{18} \]

The factor involving \(K\) keeps the fast decay of the fine state. A persistent fine forcing was not inserted in its place. This bound is applied once to each candidate, without assuming equal hidden states.

docs.title: 4. Reading sets, separation and a true overlap witness
docs.text:
Fix nonnegative exposure, gain and additive reading allowances \(\eta\le1/2\), \(g\), and \(\varepsilon_y\). The sole observation is

\[ Y_\lambda=(1+\kappa)r_\lambda(1+\xi)+b, \qquad |\xi|\le\eta,\quad |\kappa|\le g,\quad |b|\le\varepsilon_y. \tag{19} \]

Here \(\xi\) is an error in the independently declared \(s\) clock, and \(\kappa\) changes the readout, not a kinetic coefficient. An unknown clock rate or physical sensing law is not supplied by these allowances. A gain allowance exceeding one is permitted but may destroy useful information.

Put \(T=1+\eta\). The nominal corridor (6) gives \(|r_{\lambda,\mathrm{nom}}(s)|\le\gamma J_1d\) through \(T\). Also, \(\int_0^s e^{-(s-t)}e^{-Kt}dt\le1/K\). Equations (16)--(17) and the actual mean form row imply

\[ \begin{split} |r(s)|&\le R=\varepsilon_r+\gamma J_1(d+P_T)+\frac{\gamma B}{K},\\ |r_s(s)|&\le L=\varepsilon_r+2\gamma J_1(d+P_T) +\gamma B(1+1/K),\qquad 0\le s\le T. \end{split} \tag{20} \]

For the derivative bound, use \(|\delta(s)|\le d+P_T\), \(|j_\lambda(\delta)|\le J_1|\delta|\), and (15). All exposures in (19) are nonnegative. The resulting error around each nominal endpoint is

\[ |Y_\lambda-R_\lambda(d)|\le E_{\rm obs}=E+\eta L+gR+\varepsilon_y. \tag{21} \]

The gain term already bounds the entire actual endpoint, so another gain factor on the preparation or timing error would count that uncertainty twice. Let \(\mathcal Y_\lambda\) be the set of all readings (19) from all allowed preparations of that candidate. The positive gap (12) gives the sufficient full-state conclusion

\[ 2E_{\rm obs}<\frac{\gamma d^3}{20} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \mathcal Y_0\cap\mathcal Y_1=\varnothing. \tag{22} \]

Both candidates can choose their nuisance values independently; the factor two is essential. A failed inequality establishes no intersection by itself. There is, however, a separate sufficient ambiguity condition:

\[ \varepsilon_y\ge\frac{\gamma d^3}{12} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \mathcal Y_0\cap\mathcal Y_1\ne\varnothing. \tag{23} \]

To prove it, use the exact nominal preparations, zero timing and gain errors, and the common reading \(Y_*=(R_0(d)+R_1(d))/2\). Under each law choose the additive error \(b_\lambda=Y_*-R_\lambda(d)\). Equation (12) places both magnitudes below the allowance. This is an actual common-reading witness, not overlap of two conservative enclosures. It establishes failure of uniform identification in this observation class; it does not make every possible record ambiguous or rule out richer observations.

docs.title: 5. Attachment resource and what the scaling means
docs.text:
At the supplied state-preserving initial attachment, the exact new storage is

\[ W=a\sum_{k=0}^8\left[ \frac12(r(0)+z_{A,k}-z_{B,k})^2+ V_\lambda(\delta(0)+q_{A,k}-q_{B,k})\right]\ge0. \tag{24} \]

The linear fine terms cancel because their means are zero. Using the global curvature bound and \(V_\lambda(u)\le J_1u^2/2\) gives

\[ W\le a\left[\frac92\varepsilon_r^2+\rho_x^2+ \frac92J_1(d+\varepsilon_\delta)^2+J_1\rho_\theta^2\right]. \tag{25} \]

For the exact nominal preparations, \(W_\lambda=9aV_\lambda(d)\). The Taylor bounds \(d^2/2-d^4/24\le V_\lambda(d)\le d^2/2+d^4/24\) imply

\[ 4ad^2<W_\lambda<5ad^2. \tag{26} \]

Thus this fixed model and observation have a nominal signal of order \(\gamma d^3\) for nominal attachment storage of order \(ad^2\). At fixed canonical parameters, the signal is of order \(\gamma(W_\lambda/a)^{3/2}\). Reducing preparation reduces the signal faster than this attachment cost. This is not a universal thermodynamic measurement bound; formation, phase preparation, sensing and timing costs are separate, and \(W\) is the declared structural storage jump.

For sufficiently small constants, (22) admits nonzero errors with \(\varepsilon_r,\varepsilon_y\) of order \(\gamma d^3\), \(\varepsilon_\delta,F_0\) of order \(d^3\), and \(\eta,g\) of order \(d^2\). These are sufficient joint scalings, not separately proved necessary ones. The explicit additive-noise obstruction (23) is retained independently. The horizon remains \(\tau=2000/\gamma^2\); reducing \(d\) does not shorten it.

docs.title: 6. Detached calculation and scope
docs.text:
The shared calculator re-admits all primitive error allowances and the nominal phase before rebuilding (14)--(26). It reuses the current family, canonical parameter enclosures and fine-energy owner from the free probe. Its statuses distinguish guaranteed_separation, observation_class_nonidentifiable and not_certified. The static controls check direct difference algebra, fine convolution, independent uncertainty, work cancellation, precision boundaries and a strictly positive budget with all error allowances nonzero. No trajectory, source producer or physical response is evaluated. A phase preparation, a clock and a sensor remain independent obligations before comparing with measured physics.

docs.title: 1. Full lifted cell, stationary target and storage
docs.text:
Write \(\alpha=2\pi/9\), \(\psi_j=\alpha(j-4)\), and \(\theta_{c,j}=\psi_j+\delta_{c,j}\). On every oriented internal cycle edge use the continuous angle

\[ a_{c,j}=\alpha+\delta_{c,j+1}-\delta_{c,j}, \qquad j+1\pmod9, \qquad \sum_j a_{c,j}=2\pi . \tag{1} \]

This includes the fixed closing-edge turn. On a matching edge between children \(c,b\) at slot \(j\), use \(a_{cb,j}=\delta_{b,j}-\delta_{c,j}\). The declared cell is the intersection of all 90 strict inequalities \(|a_e|<\pi/2\), on the leaf

\[ \sum_{c,j}x_{c,j}=0,\qquad \sum_{c,j}\delta_{c,j}=9/8. \tag{2} \]

All 90 fine coordinates are retained; the two linear conservation laws remove only their common origins. This affine phase cell is convex. Its closure has \(|a_e|\le\pi/2\), and every boundary point has at least one saturated edge. It is the closure of the open cell: mixing with the strict target below approaches every closed-cell point from the interior. The five marked cycle sums are fixed by (1), rather than inferred from selected phase snapshots.

For the actual 90-edge Laplacian and sine current, the complete law is

\[ x_\tau=\tfrac14[-Lx+\gamma S(\theta)],\qquad \theta_\tau=\tfrac\gamma4Lx, \qquad \gamma=\frac1{1023\pi}. \tag{3} \]

The coefficients remain uniform despite unequal node degrees. The first row supplies the pressure at held unit capacity. Both rows, and the storage derivative below, acquire the factor \(1023/1024\) in original time \(t\); the phase row is not exempt from this clock change.

Set

\[ V_9=9(1-\cos\alpha),\qquad H_*=5V_9,\qquad x^*=0,\qquad \theta^*_{c,j}=\psi_j+1/40. \tag{4} \]

The two internal sine currents cancel at every fine node of this target; all matching currents vanish separately. Thus \(S(\theta^*)=0\), and both rows in (3) vanish. All internal angles are \(\alpha\), all matching angles are zero, and (2) holds. This verifies a fine-state equilibrium with five winding-one cycles, independent of carrier closure.

The storage and exact identities are inherited from the source-port balance:

\[ H=\tfrac12x^TLx+\sum_e(1-\cos a_e),\qquad H_\tau=-\tfrac14\|Lx\|_2^2,\qquad (\mathbf1^Tx)_\tau=(\mathbf1^T\delta)_\tau=0. \tag{5} \]

There is no later input or support event. The given vector field is globally Lipschitz in finite real lifts, so every finite initial state has a unique complete solution. The proof below concerns this supplied continuous law, not a numerical time step or a native operator execution.

docs.title: 2. Every acute boundary face has a positive excess
docs.text:
The function \(f(a)=1-\cos a\) is convex on \([-\pi/2,\pi/2]\). Jensen's inequality and each exact cycle sum in (1) give \(\sum_j f(a_{c,j})\ge V_9\) on the whole closed cell. The five cycle edge sets are disjoint. All other edge costs and the form storage are nonnegative. In particular, \(H-H_*\ge0\).

If an internal edge reaches \(+\pi/2\), the other eight angles of that cycle sum to \(3\pi/2\). Its cycle storage is therefore at least

\[ b_9=1+8[1-\cos(3\pi/16)]. \tag{6} \]

If it reaches \(-\pi/2\), the remaining angles sum to \(5\pi/2\) and its lower bound is \(1+8[1-\cos(5\pi/16)]>b_9\). These arguments cover both signs of every one of the 45 internal edges. No feasibility of an independently minimized face is required: a lower bound valid on the larger cycle domain is valid on the actual full face.

If instead any of the 45 matching edges reaches either acute boundary, that edge contributes one, while the five internal cycles still contribute at least \(5V_9\). Other matching edges can only add storage. Consequently all 180 signed faces satisfy

\[ H-H_*\ge\beta_{\rm face},\qquad \beta_{\rm face}=\min\{b_9-V_9,1\},\qquad b_9-V_9=9\cos(2\pi/9)-8\cos(3\pi/16). \tag{7} \]

The shared outward 128-bit rational trigonometric bounds give \(6/25<b_9-V_9<1\), hence \(\beta_{\rm face}>6/25\). For orientation, this excess is approximately \(0.24264308965044\). The strict rational inequality, not the displayed decimal, is used below. This is a complete boundary lower bound, not a claim that a full-support boundary minimizer attains it. Additional cycle correlations may strengthen it but are unnecessary for this source.

docs.title: 3. Re-admitting the actual reached family and its complete storage
docs.text:
Rebuild the attachment source from all ten primitive allowances. The host retains its reached state at \(s=4\) and its moving reference

\[ \begin{split} x^H_{g,a,j}&=\tfrac12[(2g-1)u+(2a-1)v]+r_{g,a,j},\\ \delta^H_{g,a,j}&=\tfrac12[(2g-1)\Delta+(2a-1)B]+z_{g,a,j},\\ |v|&\le\bar\gamma A\,\overline B,\qquad |u|\le\bar\gamma A\,\overline\Delta,\qquad A=1+2\bar\eta,\\ 0<B&\le\overline B<1/64,\qquad 0<\Delta\le\overline\Delta<1/640,\qquad \|r\|_2\le R<10^{-60},\quad \|z\|_2\le Z<10^{-60}. \end{split}\tag{8} \]

Here \(\bar\gamma\) and \(\bar\eta\) are the outward upper bounds on \(\gamma\) and \(\gamma^2\), respectively, using the shared interval square for the latter. The overlined gaps are the freshly rebuilt host entry bounds. The original host proof supplies \(R,Z\) for the four independent recovered children. They bound all actual fine deviations; (8) does not set them to zero or require them to match between children.

The independent donor retains \(x^D=r_D\), \(\delta^D=1/8+z_D\), with separate exact zero means of \(r_D,z_D\) and \(\|r_D\|_2,\|z_D\|_2\le q=10^{-70}\). Its quarter-factor isolated dynamics is the original half-factor dynamics at half speed in both rows. Thus its formation time 200 and recovery dwell \(2\cdot10^{13}\) are the already declared transformed durations, not a new simulation or an additional waiting period. All five original families, and their 80 relative initial directions, remain in this source.

Initial cell membership follows on every edge: internal angles lie in \([\alpha-2\max(Z,q),\alpha+2\max(Z,q)]\subset(0,\pi/2)\); host matching angles have absolute value at most \(\max(\overline B,\overline\Delta)+2Z<\pi/2\); donor-contact angles satisfy the strictly positive acute bounds from the fresh attachment. The event changes no coordinate, so this is the actual post-event state.

For the host's four internal cycles the reference forms are constant and the reference phase gradients cancel at each node. The block cycle Laplacian has norm at most four. The internal form storage and the Taylor remainder of the internal phase storage are therefore at most \(2R^2\) and \(2Z^2\), respectively. This phase bound uses cancellation of the whole cycle's first variation, rather than treating each edge as individually stationary.

There are 18 host matching edges with reference gap \(B\), and 18 with reference gap \(\Delta\). On each such edge the actual form gap has magnitude at most \(\bar\gamma A d+2R\), and its phase gap at most \(d+2Z\), for the corresponding upper bound \(d\). Using \(1-\cos a\le a^2/2\) yields the source-inclusive host excess

\[ \begin{split} H_H-4V_9&\le U_H,\\ U_H&=2(R^2+Z^2)+9\sum_{d\in\{\overline B,\overline\Delta\}} [(\bar\gamma A d+2R)^2+(d+2Z)^2]. \end{split}\tag{9} \]

This estimate needs no childwise residual mean conservation after host assembly. Its nominal part is \(9[1+(\bar\gamma A)^2](\overline B^2+\overline\Delta^2)\); all remaining nonnegative cross terms and squares are retained exactly, including terms below the trigonometric interval grid. The donor excess is at most \(4q^2\) by the same internal-cycle calculation.

Write \(b=(\overline B+\overline\Delta)/2\), and retain the actual new-edge work upper bound

\[ \begin{split} W_+&=\tfrac92\{[\bar\gamma A b+R+q]^2+ [1/8+b+Z+q]^2\},\\ 0\le H(0)-H_*&\le U_+:=U_H+4q^2+W_+<1/10. \end{split}\tag{10} \]

The last strict inequality already follows with the coarse rational bounds in (8), \(\bar\gamma<1/3000\), \(\bar\eta<1/9000000\), and \(q=10^{-70}\): the resulting upper bound is less than \(0.082533\). The calculator uses the actual outward host entry bounds, preserving the stronger source association. An old upper bound before host acquisition is not substituted for (9).

Equation (10) adds the donor's complete reached storage and the actual contact work to the reached host storage. The separately admitted positive work \(1/16<H_B<1/10\), five primitive preparation costs, original host assembly work and prior dissipation keep their source owner's accounting. Past loss funds none of these supplied events. Neither (9) nor (10) changes a source coordinate or introduces a work reservoir.

docs.title: 4. Permanent winding retention and full-state convergence
docs.text:
Combining (7) and (10) gives a strict whole-source separation:

\[ \beta_{\rm face}-U_+>\frac6{25}-\frac1{10}=\frac7{50}>0. \tag{11} \]

Suppose a member of the admitted family first reached the cell boundary. By (5), its storage could not exceed its initial value, while every boundary face requires at least \(H_*+\beta_{\rm face}\). This contradicts (10)--(11). The strict gap also excludes accumulation at the boundary. Hence every source member remains in the acute fixed-branch cell for all elapsed post-attachment \(\tau\ge0\), and all five marked windings remain exactly one.

For convergence, the support is connected. On the fixed zero-form-mean leaf, bounded \(x^TLx\) bounds the form coordinates. Bounded fixed-branch edge angles and the fixed lifted mean similarly bound all phase offsets. The trapped storage sublevel is thus compact and separated from the phase boundary. On its interior the phase Hessian is the weighted graph Laplacian with edge weights \(\cos a_e>0\). It is positive definite on the fixed-mean tangent space. Strict convexity therefore makes the stationary phase configuration (4) the only critical point in this cell and mean leaf.

In the zero-loss set of (5), \(Lx=0\); the form mean then forces \(x=0\), and the phase row vanishes. To remain in that set, the form row further requires \(S(\theta)=0\). Its largest invariant subset is consequently the single equilibrium (4). The invariance principle on the compact trapped sublevel proves, for every independently perturbed member of the original prepared family,

\[ x_{c,j}(\tau)\longrightarrow0,\qquad \theta_{c,j}(\tau)\longrightarrow\psi_j+1/40 \quad(\tau\longrightarrow\infty). \tag{12} \]

The common phase origin follows from the retained raw total \(9/8\) divided by 45. The result concerns every fine coordinate; it is not an inference from five observed means or the ten-coordinate restriction. It reuses the method of the acute-sector capture theorem with the present support, uniform quarter mobility, source and all edge faces proved explicitly. No global settling time or finite readout is supplied.

docs.title: 5. A collective registration distinguished by the control
docs.text:
Define the lifted relative-registration observation

\[ \rho(\tau)=\frac19\sum_{j=0}^8\delta_{4,j}(\tau) -\frac1{36}\sum_{c=0}^3\sum_{j=0}^8\delta_{c,j}(\tau). \tag{13} \]

It is invariant under a common change of phase origin and retains the specified lifts. At the actual initial source, the host mean is zero and the donor mean is \(1/8\), so \(\rho(0)=1/8\) for the whole family. For the connected law, (12) gives \(\rho(\tau)\to0\).

In the disconnected control only the nine donor contacts are omitted. Both complete rows keep their uniform quarter factor, the same structural clock, held capacities and every reached coordinate. Edge cancellation now separately conserves each component's form sum and lifted phase sum. The host mean is therefore zero forever, the donor mean is \(1/8\) forever, and

\[ \rho_{\rm disconnected}(\tau)=1/8\qquad(\tau\ge0). \tag{14} \]

Thus this control cannot converge to any state with a common child phase origin, including (4). No disconnected convergence theorem or finite response calculation is needed for the obstruction. This alternative starts from the same reached coordinates on its own declared support; it is not a later removal event with an unaccounted storage jump.

The joined whole approaches common relative registration that the unchanged separate components cannot approach together. This is a conditional collective property caused by the admitted interaction. The child windings already existed; their permanent retention is a separate conclusion. The result supplies no new primitive state variable or fundamental law, and does not make fine means an exact autonomous reduction. Continuous retention of the two earlier parent registration neighborhoods, autonomous contact selection, physical identification and emergence at other sizes remain outside this theorem.

docs.text:

docs.title: Exact organized-source state modulo a global child exchange
docs.text:
Conditional construction. The two exchangeable children need not have equal form or phase. Their averaged coordinates together with one joint rank-at-most-one Gram matrix retain the complete primary state up to the single exchange of those children. On the specified organized-source law, these coordinates close both nonlinear continuous rows, energy and loss, the fixed energy guard and the admitted marked Reception–Coherence–Silence maps. Separate pair summaries can lose the relations required for this prediction.

This extends the represented domain of the fixed-sector chart, whose 72 primary coordinates require equal children. It does not replace its separate finite-error results. The present generic primary dimension is still 90. Removing a redundant global label is different from reducing the number of continuous degrees of freedom. Section 7 separately proves a quantitative approach to that sector in the admitted acute energy domain, with finite tolerance deadlines and decaying instantaneous prediction defects. Section 8 bounds the accumulated error of a separately evolved symmetric core, for unit capacities without events.

The construction applies the existing support-symmetry criterion and joint Gram method to the actual 45-node source, reciprocal phase row and marked ideal word. Its new obligation is to identify which relations across the nine paired slots this support preserves. It introduces no new constitutive law.

docs.title: 1. Actual symmetry and retained state
docs.text:
Use the source support and law: nodes 9*c+j, five nine-cycles and the matching child edges (0,1),(2,3),(0,2),(1,3),(0,4). All ninety edges have unit conductance. The global permutation J exchanges whole children one and two and fixes children zero, three and four. It fixes the marked targets zero and one. The cycles couple adjacent slots, so swapping just one corresponding pair of nodes is generally not a support automorphism.

Keep the ordered child orbits A={0}, B={1,2}, C={3}, D={4}, with nine slots each. Their masses are 1,2,1,1; write M_mass for the diagonal 36-coordinate mass matrix. P copies projected coordinates to their fine nodes and R=M_mass^-1 P^T averages the fibers. Thus Pi=PR=(I+J)/2. The inherited weighted Laplacian is L_w, as derived in the fixed-sector owner; its 63 edges have total weight ninety.

Declare the raw real carrier lift psi_(9c+j)=alpha*(j-4), alpha=2*pi/9. Retain 36 projected forms u and 36 projected real phase offsets d. Write vartheta=bar_psi+d. The unequal children have

\[ x_{1j}=u_{Bj}+a_j,\quad x_{2j}=u_{Bj}-a_j,\qquad \Theta_{1j}=\vartheta_{Bj}+b_j,\quad \Theta_{2j}=\vartheta_{Bj}-b_j. \]

All other children are copied from their singleton orbit. Positive held capacities must satisfy nu_(1j)=nu_(2j). Their 36 retained coordinates are separate law parameters, not part of the 90-primary-coordinate count. They may vary between slots and between the four child orbits.

Set v=(a_0,...,a_8,b_0,...,b_8) and retain

\[ G=vv^T= \begin{pmatrix}G_{aa}&G_{ab}\\G_{ab}^T&G_{bb}\end{pmatrix}. \]

The domain requires one jointly symmetric positive-semidefinite matrix of rank at most one. Its 171 distinct entries are redundant coordinates. They are products of one deterministic hidden vector, not an ensemble covariance, and cannot be replaced by unrelated positive local blocks. The joint-realizability owner explains the general distinction between pairwise admissibility and a common underlying state.

If G is nonzero, choose its first positive diagonal entry G_kk and set v_k=sqrt(G_kk)>0, v_i=G_ik/v_k. Rank-one realizability proves that these values reconstruct G, and its only real lifts are v and -v. At G=0 the only lift is zero. Hence (u,d,G,nu) reconstructs the fine primary state up to exactly J. Separate signs for different slots or for the form and phase blocks do not describe the same equivalence relation.

The generic dimension is 72+18=90, with a singular zero-hidden stratum. The canonical sign rule is an algebraic representative, not a globally smooth choice of labeled state. At v=0 the differential of v -> vv^T vanishes; this coordinate singularity does not make the fine flow singular. Labeled nonsymmetric observations need a choice between the two lifts. Invariant observations and fixed-target values do not.

These coordinates retain declared real phase lifts. They do not quotient independent turns, define a global chart on circular phases, or infer a preferred lift from wrapped observations.

docs.title: 2. Closed projected nonlinear law
docs.text:
The complete unforced law in structural time tau is

\[ \dot x=\tfrac14D_f[-L_f x+\gamma S_f(\Theta)],\qquad \dot\Theta=\tfrac\gamma4D_fL_f x,\qquad \gamma=(1023\pi)^{-1}, \]

where S_f(Theta)_i=sum_(k~i) sin(Theta_k-Theta_i) and Gamma is absent. Every consumed capacity is held between events; the same capacity multiplies both rows. Define q=M_mass^-1 L_w u and let D be the diagonal retained capacity matrix. Hidden form cancels in the projected Laplacian, so R L_f x=q even away from the fixed sector.

For nonnegative r, put

\[ C(r)=\cos\sqrt r,\qquad F(r)=\frac{\sin\sqrt r}{\sqrt r},\quad F(0)=1. \]

Their power series in r remove any division at zero. For a B-cycle edge jk define

\[ r_{jk}=G_{bb,jj}+G_{bb,kk}-2G_{bb,jk}=(b_k-b_j)^2, \qquad r_j=G_{bb,jj}=b_j^2. \]

The projected sine current s_G=R S_f(Theta) is obtained by these exact contributions; each displayed term is added to the indicated row:

Row and neighbor Contribution B slot j, adjacent B slot k sin(vartheta_Bk-vartheta_Bj)*C(r_jk) B slot j, U slot j, U=A or C sin(vartheta_Uj-vartheta_Bj)*C(r_j) U slot j, B slot j, U=A or C 2*sin(vartheta_Bj-vartheta_Uj)*C(r_j) Every unaffected cycle or A–D edge Its original fine sine term

These follow from sin(t+b)+sin(t-b)=2*sin(t)*cos(b) and the inherited neighbor counts. Consequently both projected rows close:

\[ \dot u=\tfrac14D(-q+\gamma s_G),\qquad \dot d=\tfrac\gamma4Dq. \]

The phase row does not depend directly on hidden coordinates, but the form row consumes cross-slot entries of G_bb. Their evolution will also consume the mixed block G_ab. Keeping just the phase correction at one instant does not establish future closure.

docs.title: 3. Joint Gram evolution and exact balance
docs.text:
Let H=L_C9+2I, with diagonal four and adjacent entries minus one, and V=diag(nu_Bj). Define the symmetric matrix K as a weighted cycle Laplacian with edge weight

\[ \cos(\vartheta_{Bk}-\vartheta_{Bj})F(r_{jk}), \]

plus the diagonal entry

\[ [\cos(\vartheta_{Aj}-\vartheta_{Bj})+ \cos(\vartheta_{Cj}-\vartheta_{Bj})]F(r_j). \]

The half-difference of the two fine sine currents is exactly -K b. Subtracting the complete fine rows therefore gives

\[ \dot a=-\tfrac14VHa-\tfrac\gamma4VKb,\qquad \dot b=\tfrac\gamma4VHa,\qquad \dot v=\mathcal A v,\quad \mathcal A=\tfrac14 \begin{pmatrix}-VH&-\gamma VK\\\gamma VH&0\end{pmatrix}. \]

The entries of K depend on (d,G_bb), not on the lift's overall sign. The exact joint equation is thus

\[ \boxed{\dot G=\mathcal A G+G\mathcal A^T.} \]

These equations are smooth on the realized domain, including G=0; the power series also define a smooth extension to ambient coordinates. Starting from a realized G, the fine lifted solution proves preservation of rank-one realizability and supplies the unique projected solution. The two signs give the same retained trajectory. This is a constructive closure proof, not a prescription to integrate redundant unconstrained entries or repair a matrix that has drifted out of its domain.

Let bar E be the fixed-sector excess at (u,d), and H_*=45*(1-cos(alpha)). Exact edge grouping yields

\[ \begin{split} E={}&\bar E+\operatorname{tr}(H G_{aa})\\ &+2\sum_{jk\in C_9}\cos(\vartheta_{Bk}-\vartheta_{Bj})[1-C(r_{jk})]\\ &+2\sum_j[\cos(\vartheta_{Aj}-\vartheta_{Bj})+ \cos(\vartheta_{Cj}-\vartheta_{Bj})][1-C(r_j)]. \end{split} \]

Each unoriented cycle edge appears once. This identity does not require acute angles; the correction need not be nonnegative outside an acute projected domain. For arbitrary admitted symmetric positive capacities,

\[ \rho=\tfrac14q^T M_{\rm mass}Dq+ \tfrac12\operatorname{tr}(H V H G_{aa}),\qquad \dot E=-\rho. \]

Indeed the two hidden fine gradients are q_B+Ha and q_B-Ha, whose weighted squares cancel the cross terms. Slot-dependent V must remain between the two H factors. The fine inverse-capacity-weighted form and phase-offset totals reduce to sum(mass/nu*u) and sum(mass/nu*d); hidden terms cancel because the paired capacities agree.

These are exact identities for the supplied law. They neither select its constitutive coefficients nor identify these quantities with laboratory energy, time or measured information.

docs.title: 4. Guard and marked hybrid maps
docs.text:
Use the same supplied fixed energy level and mandatory first downward crossing from the guard owner. Since the full energy is reconstructed exactly, its crossing set is the same for both fine lifts and the retained trajectory. Existence, positive first occurrence and transversality remain the guard owner's separate premises; this representation does not establish them anew.

For the complete ideal word, intersect with the section 23 word domain: initial unit capacities, its acute lift cell, E<1/100, abs(initial form mean)<1/30, and complete supplied admission context. The continuous identity above allows more general held capacities; it does not widen this particular first-word admission theorem.

Let beta, lambda and kappa be the already admitted Reception, Coherence and Silence factors. Each stage uses one common fine snapshot at the fixed targets i=0,1. Reception retains the same inherited mean:

\[ u_i^+=(1-\beta)u_i+\frac\beta5\sum_bN_{ib}u_b. \]

The hidden forms cancel in the two exchanged neighbors. Only these two singleton projected forms change; d, G and capacities are held.

For Coherence, write j=i for the target's slot. Its relative resultant is

\[ z_i=\sum_{k\in\{\text{two A-cycle neighbors, D slot }j\}} e^{i(\vartheta_k-\vartheta_i)} +2e^{i(\vartheta_{Bj}-\vartheta_i)}C(G_{bb,jj}). \]

This is the exact five-neighbor fine sum. On the existing regular argument branch, d_i^+=d_i+lambda*Arg(z_i); every other projected phase, all forms, G and capacities are held. Silence then sends the two target capacities to kappa*nu_i, holding u, d and G. It preserves equality between the capacities of children one and two, so the subsequent held-capacity law remains in this domain.

Each primary stage commutes with J. The represented state therefore reconstructs the marked ideal word and its changed-capacity continuation up to that same global exchange. The hidden vector itself is unchanged by these marked maps; a capacity jump does not reset G.

Histories, ordinals, debt, prior Coherence, policies and any labeled selector inputs remain separately retained and admitted. Arbitrary runtime contexts are not functions of G. Full labeled execution needs the matching fine context and lift; no quotient of arbitrary context or new occurrence law follows. Stored-pressure jumps and fresh-law association retain their existing contracts. See the operator descent and grammar descent conditions. The proof concerns the primary ideal maps under those premises, not a new runtime executor.

docs.title: 5. Frozen information-loss controls
docs.text: Both controls were fixed at h=1/128, unit capacity and carrier projected phase before evaluation. They are static state and derivative identities, not samples from a trajectory or unknown crossing states. They disprove the named omissions; they do not prove that all 171 entries are a minimal collection of stored numbers.

docs.title: Cross-slot phase association is visible immediately
docs.text:
Set projected form h*(e0-e1) on child A, every other projected form zero, and a=0. In the first hidden phase vector all b_j are +h except b_2=-h; in the second, only b_4=-h. Every local pair Gram is (a_j^2,a_j*b_j,b_j^2)=(0,0,h^2). Their hidden means agree, so the means of each labeled child also agree. Both states have

\[ E=6h^2+4\cos\alpha(1-\cos2h)+36(1-\cos h) \le32h^2=1/512<1/100,\qquad \rho=20h^2. \]

Their marked targets and every incident initial form, phase and capacity agree. Thus initial fresh target pressure and direct ideal word outputs at the targets agree as well, conditional on equal admitted context. The largest cycle gap is at most alpha+2h<pi/2, matching gaps have magnitude h and the global form mean is zero.

Nevertheless their projected B-slot-1 form rates differ, first minus second, by

\[ \dot u^{(1)}_{B1}-\dot u^{(2)}_{B1} =\frac\gamma4\sin\alpha(\cos2h-1)<0. \]

The missing entry G_bb,1,2 is respectively -h^2 and +h^2. Adjacent phase associations matter even when local pair Grams, child means, energy, instantaneous loss and initial target data all agree.

docs.title: Separate complete form and phase Grams still lose mixed information
docs.text:
Now set every projected form to zero, a=h*e0, and compare b=+h*e1 with b=-h*e1. All local pair Grams agree because the two supports are disjoint. Even the full separate matrices G_aa and G_bb agree, as do both projected first derivative rows. Both preparations are acute, have zero global form mean, and satisfy

\[ E=4h^2+4(1+\cos\alpha)(1-\cos h)\le8h^2<1/100, \qquad \rho=9h^2. \]

But G_ab,0,1 is respectively +h^2 and -h^2. Since (Ha)_1=-h, the squared hidden phase has

\[ \frac{d}{d\tau}b_1^2=\mp\frac\gamma2h^2. \]

This distinction reaches a projected observable at the next derivative:

\[ \ddot u^{(+)}_{B0}-\ddot u^{(-)}_{B0} =\frac58\gamma^2h\sin\alpha\sin h>0. \]

To verify the coefficient, the initial projected phase rate is zero and the two projected form rates coincide, so their q derivatives coincide. Only the derivative of the cycle phase correction differs. Here dot b_1-dot b_0=-5*gamma*h/4; differentiating the two cosines gives a projected sine-rate contrast 5*gamma*h*sin(alpha)*sin(h)/2. The additional form-row factor gamma/4 yields the stated curvature. The mixed block records a relative association between hidden form and phase that neither separate full Gram retains.

docs.title: 6. Detached implementation and boundary
docs.text:
The private orbit reader encodes fine primitives, decodes admitted invariant coordinates to a canonical fine lift and observes the same complete law through the shared fine capacity reader. Projected rows are actual fiber averages; selecting one representative off the fixed sector would be incorrect. The joint Gram derivative is built from the fine hidden derivatives. No second sine kernel, numerical integrator or event executor is introduced.

The shared exact rank-one lift normalizes every matrix entry before checking symmetry and realizability. It also serves the existing P5 invariant decoder. The implementation retains exact rational or exactly represented real input values and rational canonical lifts. A realizable rational Gram whose canonical square root is irrational is explicitly unsupported by this decoder, though it is a valid point of the real mathematical domain. It is not rounded to a nearby lift or declared physically impossible.

The encoded fine state and every consumed primitive are readmitted; cached reports, Boolean scalars, nonfinite values, unequal paired capacities or arbitrary positive-semidefinite higher-rank matrices do not replace these premises. The fine state in a decoded report is the canonical representative, not a claim to recover the original labeled preparation without its missing overall sign.

Independent controls compare exact reconstruction, the shared-law observation and the prospectively fixed state/derivative distinctions. Algebraic closure and the conditional word proof establish sufficiency under this selected law. These reconstruction results alone establish neither a minimal state, faster simulation, an attractor, autonomous hierarchy formation, nor an empirical mapping.

docs.title: 7. Quantitative approach to the symmetric sector
docs.text:
The exact joint state explains what unequal children retain. A different question is when their difference becomes small enough for a declared approximation. The existing full-state capture already implies eventual equality on its admitted source. The result here adds a uniform decay rate and a finite tolerance deadline while the projected environment continues to move. It uses the same complete law; no feedback, noise removal or equality reset is added.

This is a common quadratic argument for a time-varying hidden stiffness. The weak-contact residual theorem provides a related method on a different support. The formed-class maintenance theorem uses a fixed-target potential. Neither its constants nor a fixed-potential derivative can be imported into the present moving hidden subsystem.

docs.title: Domain, phase collar and capacities
docs.text:
Admit the actual fixed winding-one acute lift cell and E<1/100 from the full fine primitives. Keep positive held capacities, with equal values on paired children as in section 1. The source word-domain argument gives, on this unrestricted acute cell,

\[ \sum_e u_e^2\le4E<1/25, \]

where u_e is each edge's deviation from its carrier angle. This follows from the cycle Taylor bound with cancellation of the carrier's first variation, together with nonnegative form and matching storage. Thus every cycle angle has magnitude below alpha+1/5<pi/3, and every matching angle has magnitude below 1/5. These inequalities concern the complete actual state, rather than only its projected phase.

The straight lifted segment from a state to its global child exchange has the same bounds: each edge angle interpolates two angles inside the same interval. Each weight in the secant matrix K from section 3 is an average of cosine along this segment. Therefore, throughout the admitted flow,

\[ \tfrac12H\preceq K(\tau)\preceq H,\qquad H=L_{C_9}+2I\succeq2I. \]

The shared acute boundary barrier exceeds 1/100, and the actual positive-capacity storage balance is nonpositive. Initial membership therefore retains this domain. Capacities of the other three children may be nonuniform; they affect the moving projected environment but do not enter the paired matrix V. This proof does not differentiate K or require it to commute with H or V.

docs.title: A common quadratic metric for both hidden rows
docs.text:
Define the auxiliary quantity

\[ W=a^TV^{-1}a+b^TV^{-1}b+2\gamma a^TV^{-1}b, \qquad N=\|a\|_2^2+\|b\|_2^2=\operatorname{tr}G. \]

W is a positive proof metric in the declared normalized coordinates, not the physical storage or a new primitive parameter. It is a linear functional of the diagonal and same-slot mixed entries of G. Keeping this scalar supplies an envelope; section 5 still excludes those local entries as a complete predictive state.

With nu_min=min_j V_jj and nu_max=max_j V_jj, the metric sandwich is

\[ rac{1-\gamma}{ u_{\max}}N\le W \le rac{1+\gamma}{ u_{\min}}N. \]

Differentiate using both actual hidden rows, including the reciprocal phase row. The capacity factors cancel exactly:

\[ W'=- rac{1-\gamma^2}{2}a^THa - rac\gamma2a^TKb- rac{\gamma^2}{2}b^TKb. \]

From 0<=K<=H, congruence gives K H^-1 K<=K; no simultaneous diagonalization is used. Young's inequality then gives

\[ rac\gamma2|a^TKb| \le rac14a^THa+ rac{\gamma^2}{4}b^TKH^{-1}Kb \le rac14a^THa+ rac{\gamma^2}{4}b^TKb. \]

Since 0<gamma<1/2, the remaining form coefficient 1/4-gamma^2/2 is at least gamma^2/4. Using the two matrix lower bounds proves

\[ W'\le- rac{\gamma^2}{4}N\le-r_*W, \qquad r_* = rac{ u_{\min}\gamma^2}{4(1+\gamma)}>0. \]

Consequently, for every elapsed structural time tau in the declared law,

\[ W( au)\le W(0)e^{-r_* au},\qquad N( au)\le rac{ u_{\max}}{1-\gamma}W(0)e^{-r_* au}. \]

The rate is not uniform when paired capacity tends to zero; zero paired capacity is outside this certificate. A common clock rescaling must rescale the rate and elapsed time consistently. The represented norm does not identify form and phase with the same laboratory unit.

docs.title: Passage through the marked word and prediction scope
docs.text:
The separately admitted ideal Reception–Coherence–Silence word at targets zero and one holds a, b and V exactly. Thus it has Delta W=0 and Delta N=0, including Silence's change of the A-target capacities. The existing passivity theorem retains the same acute energy domain. Before and after this word, the same rate applies, without restarting the bound or requiring the environment to have equilibrated first. Elapsed tau is the sum of the continuous segments; the ideal jumps have no invented finite duration. Word admission, history, policy, selection and any represented map error remain separate premises.

This proves acquisition of any positive declared tolerance, not entry into exact equality at a finite time. A nonzero hidden vector cannot reach zero under its smooth homogeneous differential equation in finite time: uniqueness applied backwards from zero would contradict its nonzero initial state. The marked word also cannot make it zero because it holds that vector. Exact symmetry remains an asymptotic statement.

At one actual state compare its projected field with the fixed-sector field evaluated at the same projected coordinates and capacities. The earlier quadratic sine defect gives

\[ \|R\dot x-f_{\rm sector}(u,d)\|_\infty \le\frac{5\gamma\nu_{\rm all,max}}4\|b\|_\infty^2 \le\frac{5\gamma\nu_{\rm all,max}}4N,\qquad R\dot\Theta-g_{\rm sector}(u,d)=0. \]

The global capacity maximum is held on a continuous segment; the admitted Silence factor is at most one, so its initial value also bounds the segment after this marked word. At a target, the actual and projected Coherence resultants differ by at most b_j^2. Both have real part greater than four in the admitted energy domain, so their argument difference is at most N/4, and their ideal phase reset difference is at most lambda*N/4 for 0<=lambda<=1. Reception commutes with this projection, and Silence holds the primary coordinates. These instantaneous defects inherit the displayed decay.

This section does not follow a separately evolved reduced trajectory. Its accumulated error has the separate coupled stability proof in section 8, under narrower capacity and event premises. Nor does a small N give a uniform late-time energy-guard timing error: that question still needs a strictly positive crossing-loss margin.

docs.title: Prospectively fixed static controls
docs.text:
Both controls fix unit capacities, h=1/128, and zero projected form and phase offsets. They evaluate algebra and bounds, not a trajectory or a performed operator event.

First take a=h*e0, b=h*e1. The section 5 mixed-information control already establishes its acute energy admission; its initial metric is exactly W(0)=2h^2. For outward gamma bounds g_lo<=gamma<=g_hi, define the rational certified rate and elapsed time

\[ r=\frac{g_{\rm lo}^2}{4(1+g_{\rm hi})},\qquad T=10/r. \]

Since exp(-10)<2^-10 and g_hi<1/2, the certificate implies

\[ N(T)\le\frac{2h^2}{1-g_{\rm hi}}e^{-10}<h^2/256. \]

Initially N(0)=2h^2; the declared approximation tolerance is therefore absent initially and guaranteed by this conservative structural deadline. This finite-tolerance acquisition does not assert formation of a new NFR identity, spontaneous support selection or a physical timescale.

Second take a=epsilon*h*e0, b=h*e0, with epsilon=1/65536. Here K_00=2*(1+cos(alpha))*sinc(h), so the complete fine law gives

\[ N'=h^2[-2\epsilon^2+ \tfrac{\gamma\epsilon}{2}(4-K_{00})]>0. \]

Indeed cos(alpha)<4/5, sinc(h)<1 and gamma>1/4096 imply gamma*(4-K_00)>1/10240>4*epsilon. Its excess is 4*epsilon^2*h^2+4*(1+cos(alpha))*(1-cos(h))<1/100, and all fine edge angles are acute. Meanwhile the proved inequality gives W'<0. Thus exponential control by W does not assert monotonically decreasing Euclidean hidden distance. Both rows and their mixed term matter.

docs.title: Primitive certificate and numerical boundary
docs.text:
The relaxation reader rebuilds the canonical fine lift, shared observation, raw offset angles, energy and boundary margins from primitives. It supplies a conditional metric and squared-distance allowance, with explicit unavailability when the geometric premises or exponential work budget are not certified. It admits no event context and performs no integration or reset.

The report-free quadratic kernel keeps this common-metric theorem separate from its existing fixed-potential helpers. The reader uses the existing exact rational negative-exponential evaluator, whose nonnegative exponent is limited to 4096. That limit is a numerical work boundary; it does not limit the analytical theorem. Exact rational scalar bounds preserve nonzero allowances below the trigonometric interval grid rather than materializing them as zero.

Independent controls check the full fine derivative, the metric sandwich, nonuniform capacities, the frozen deadline and transient-growth distinction, event-map invariance and unavailable domains. The result supplies a justified tolerance for discarding this asymmetry in instantaneous predictions under the selected law. It neither establishes a unique canonical constitutive law nor makes the lossy reduced state exactly sufficient at finite time.

For the frozen first control, the rational certificate gives r>2.4196e-8 and T<4.133e8 in structural tau units, with a joint squared-norm allowance below 5.544e-9, compared with the declared h^2/256>2.384e-7. The instantaneous form-field defect is bounded by 2.157e-12 and the target argument defect by 1.386e-9. These are conservative analytical allowances at the prescribed deadline, not observed errors or a laboratory settling time.

docs.title: 8. An independently evolved symmetric approximation
docs.text:
Small instantaneous defects do not by themselves bound an accumulated prediction error. Here the complete state z evolves under the same fine law while a symmetric state w evolves independently from w(0)=Pi z(0). All capacities are exactly one and remain held; Gamma, external input, events and changes of support are absent. Time is the same structural tau in both rows. The initial fine state must lie in section 7's actual winding-one acute cell with E<1/100.

The prediction is the error between Pi z(tau) and w(tau), including both form and lifted phase. The result is uniform for all nonnegative tau and decays to zero. It strengthens the earlier finite comparison on this narrower invariant domain; it does not replace that comparison's global-sine or first-hit scope. Neither calculation evaluates a trajectory.

docs.title: Two retained domains and the correct error space
docs.text:
In the acute lifted cell the storage is convex and invariant under the whole-child exchange J. Consequently

\[ E(\Pi z)\le\tfrac12[E(z)+E(Jz)]=E(z). \]

The projection stays in the same convex lift cell. The initial core therefore satisfies E(w(0))<=E(z(0))<1/100. Each independent solution retains its acute sublevel by the actual storage loss and boundary barrier. The core remains symmetric because the complete law commutes with J. At every time, Pi z and w both have the section 7 phase collar. The segment joining their lifted phases stays in that collar, so its sine secant Hessian obeys L/2 <= K_e(tau) <= L as quadratic forms.

Write p=(Pi x)-w_x and q=(Pi delta)-w_delta in the fine 45-node lift. At unit capacity both complete rows conserve their ordinary sums, and Pi preserves those sums. Matched initialization therefore gives sum(p)=sum(q)=0 for every time. The initial source means may be nonzero. The actual full-support spectral bound is p^T Lp >= (4/15)||p||^2 on this mean-zero space, and likewise for q. The hidden nine-slot gap two is not the gap for these errors.

All norms below use the 45-node lift. Equivalently, the 36-coordinate norm weights the child orbits by their masses 1,2,1,1. An unweighted 36-coordinate norm does not give the displayed identities.

docs.title: Actual edge forcing and a forced common metric
docs.text:
Orient each edge and let B have +1 at its tail and -1 at its head, so L=B B^T and the sine field is B sin(theta_head-theta_tail). The difference between the projected sine field and the sine field at the projected state is B j. On each of the two copies of a B-child cycle edge from slot l to k, put

\[ j_e=\sin(\bar\theta_e)[\cos(b_k-b_l)-1]. \]

On each of the four matching edges adjacent to the exchanged children at slot l, use j_e=sin(bar theta_e)[cos(b_l)-1], with its own oriented projected angle. Other entries vanish. Pairing the two child currents proves this identity at singleton as well as paired nodes; the linear form row and reciprocal phase row commute with Pi exactly.

Since |1-cos v|<=v^2/2, the actual edge multiplicities give

\[ \|j\|^2\le\tfrac12\sum_{C_9}(b_k-b_l)^4+\sum_l b_l^4 \le 5\|b\|^4. \]

For the last inequality, each squared edge difference is at most 2||b||^2, their sum is at most 4||b||^2, and the fourth-power slot sum is at most ||b||^4. No nodal maximum-degree approximation replaces this fine edge count. The error obeys both complete rows:

\[ p'=-(Lp+\gamma K_e q)/4+\gamma Bj/4,\qquad q'=\gamma Lp/4. \]

Define W_e=||p||^2+||q||^2+2 gamma p^T q. It lies between (1-gamma)(||p||^2+||q||^2) and (1+gamma)(||p||^2+||q||^2). The common-metric argument of section 7, now on the full mean-zero space, bounds the homogeneous derivative by -p^T Lp/8-gamma^2 q^T Lq/8. The additional term is (gamma/2)(p+gamma q)^T B j. Apply Young's inequality separately:

\[ \begin{split} \tfrac\gamma2\sqrt{p^TLp}\,\|j\| &\le \tfrac1{16}p^TLp+\gamma^2\|j\|^2,\\ \tfrac{\gamma^2}2\sqrt{q^TLq}\,\|j\| &\le \tfrac{\gamma^2}{16}q^TLq+\gamma^2\|j\|^2. \end{split} \]

Using 0<gamma<=1/2, the full spectral gap and the metric sandwich yields

\[ W_e'\le-r_eW_e+10\gamma^2\|b\|^4,\qquad r_e=\frac{\gamma^2}{60(1+\gamma)}. \]

Both stiffnesses may change with the moving environment. This proof neither differentiates them nor assumes simultaneous diagonalization.

docs.title: Uniform accumulated error and its limits
docs.text:
For unit capacities let C_0=W_h(0)/(1-gamma), with W_h the hidden metric of section 7. Then ||b(tau)||^2<=C_0 exp(-r_h tau) and r_h=15 r_e. Integrating the forced scalar inequality from W_e(0)=0 gives

\[ W_e(\tau)\le \frac{600(1+\gamma)}{29}C_0^2 [e^{-r_e\tau}-e^{-30r_e\tau}],\qquad \|p\|^2+\|q\|^2\le\frac{W_e(\tau)}{1-\gamma}. \]

The bracket is nonnegative, bounded by one and converges to zero. Since C_0 is quadratic in the initial hidden coordinates, the projected error norm has a uniform quadratic dependence on their amplitude. This is a controlled lossy approximation; it does not make the symmetric state exactly sufficient for a nonzero hidden preparation at finite time.

For comparison with the unprojected fine state, orthogonality gives ||z-w||^2=2N+||p||^2+||q||^2. Its hidden contribution has the factor two from the two copies of each slot. Thus the quadratic projected-norm claim must not be attributed to the full reconstructed error, whose leading norm contribution can be linear in hidden amplitude.

Matched initialization is essential: a reference with a different common phase offset has a constant error even at zero hidden state. This result does not extend through the marked word, whose Silence changes capacities and whose resets require a separate error budget. It supplies no guard-time accuracy without crossing transversality, new NFR identity, physical identification or unique selection of the constitutive law.

docs.title: Detached certificate and prospectively fixed controls
docs.text:
The tracking reader admits all primitives and unit capacities, rebuilds the section 7 domain at time zero, and constructs the matched reference with the existing exact quotient lift. No supplied report or proposed reference replaces these premises. From outward g_lo<=gamma<=g_hi, use

\[ r=\frac{g_{\rm lo}^2}{60(1+g_{\rm hi})},\qquad C=\frac{W_{h,0}^{\rm upper}}{1-g_{\rm hi}},\qquad F=10g_{\rm hi}^2 C^2. \]

The evaluated metric allowance is F integral_0^T exp[-r(T-s)] exp[-30r s] ds; the uniform allowance is F/(29r). Divide each by 1-g_hi for the lifted joint squared error. The shared convolution kernel uses the smaller of a simple positive bound and the exponential difference quotient, keeping exact zero at T=0 and avoiding small-time cancellation. The existing cycle relaxation consumer delegates to that same kernel. The shared negative-exponential evaluator admits each argument up to 4096; this is a numerical work cap, not a bound on the analytical time domain. If only this cap fails, the uniform bound remains available and the requested pointwise evaluation is explicitly unavailable.

The prospective preparation fixes unit capacities, h=1/128, zero projected form and offsets, a=h e0, and b=h e1. Its reduced reference is the carrier equilibrium. At time zero the comparison error is exactly zero, yet its projected form-rate defect at child-one slot zero is (gamma/4) sin(alpha) [cos(h)-1]<0. The full and reduced evolutions therefore need not agree even from matched projected initialization. The frozen acceptance thresholds are a uniform joint squared-error allowance below h^2/128 and, at T=10/r, a pointwise allowance below h^2/2^20. A companion preparation with h/2 must reduce both allowances by exactly 1/16. The time and thresholds were fixed before evaluation.

Primitive and numerical controls, independent edge and forced-metric controls and convolution controls test these contracts, including means, raw lifts, tiny rational scaling and unavailable domains. They evaluate static derivatives and analytical allowances, not independent trajectories, measured errors or solver speed.

The frozen certificate gives a uniform joint squared-error allowance below 3.087e-7, against h^2/128>4.768e-7. Its certified rate exceeds 1.6131e-9, and the prescribed structural time is below 6.200e9. At that time the allowance is below 1.402e-11, against h^2/2^20>5.820e-11. The companion has exactly 1/16 of both allowances; the initial projected form-rate defect is strictly negative. These numbers are conservative proof bounds in structural units, not measured settling times. No historical continuation supplies evidence for this comparison.

docs.title: Sufficient hybrid state on the organized child-swap sector
docs.text:
Conditional construction. Equality between children one and two at every slot defines a 72-primary-coordinate representation of the organized source. It exactly reconstructs both continuous rows, the energy guard, the admitted Reception–Coherence–Silence word and its changed-capacity continuation. Inherited neighbor counts are essential to that word.

Section 6 separately bounds a nearly symmetric source up to its first fixed energy-level crossing. That approximation uses an explicit projection and retains a finite error allowance; it does not extend the exact restriction to unequal inputs. Section 7 carries that allowance through the first ideal word, comparing each successor at its own event time. The separate global child-exchange state retains a joint hidden Gram to reconstruct unequal children up to their single swap. Its generic primary dimension remains 90; it does not turn this 72-coordinate restriction into an exact averaging of arbitrary states.

The exact chart supplies a sufficient representation for both preparations in the same-guard predictive-state obstruction. It does not give a minimum dimension or compress arbitrary fine states by averaging. The rigid carrier and signed slot-reflection representations remain distinct: the former is not preserved by this marked word, and the latter does not contain both of those preparations.

docs.title: 1. Retained sector and exact reconstruction
docs.text:
Keep the 45 labeled nodes 9*c+j, the ninety unit edges and the exact carrier psi_(9c+j)=alpha*(j-4), alpha=2*pi/9. The child edges are (0,1),(2,3),(0,2),(1,3),(0,4), with matching slots on each edge. The permutation exchanging children one and two and fixing the others is a support automorphism. It fixes each marked target, nodes zero and one.

The sector requires equal form, equal declared real phase lifts and equal held positive capacities at corresponding slots of children one and two. Use four child orbits, ordered

\[ A=\{0\},\quad B=\{1,2\},\quad C=\{3\},\quad D=\{4\}, \qquad (m_A,m_B,m_C,m_D)=(1,2,1,1). \]

Each orbit retains its nine separate slots. Let P copy the resulting 36 coordinates to their fine nodes, R select the representatives, and M=P^T P=diag(m_a), with each child multiplicity repeated for nine slots. Then RP=I_36. Write

\[ x=Pu,\qquad \Theta=P(\bar\psi+\delta),\qquad \nu=P v, \qquad \bar\psi_{9a+j}=\alpha(j-4),\quad v_a>0. \]

The represented primary state has 36 form and 36 phase-offset coordinates. Capacity remains a separately retained law parameter between events. The lift is injective, and restriction is defined only on its image. Equal circular phases with unequal raw lift turns are not equal coordinates in this chart. No wrapping, mean subtraction or projection is part of restriction.

Retain the target marks and original labeled context consumed by the word: histories, monotonic ordinals, debt, prior Coherence, kind and admission configuration. Non-target context can remain in its original fine record; the 72-coordinate count concerns primary continuous state, not total runtime storage. Any context claimed to share the child symmetry must itself agree on exchanged nodes. Neither the chart nor copied values authenticate history.

This transfers the existing weighted partition method and capacity descent condition after deriving this actual law. It does not transfer their different clock or constitutive coefficients.

docs.title: 2. Inherited support, both rows and energy
docs.text:
Here a and b index the 36 node fibers, each comprising one fixed slot in one child orbit. Let N_ab count neighbors in fiber b of one fine member of fiber a. The partition is equitable and m_a N_ab=m_b N_ba. There are no edges inside a node fiber. The aggregated conductance is therefore w_ab=m_a N_ab, symmetric in a and b.

There are 63 distinct reduced edges: four nine-cycles and three matching interfaces. Cycle weights are respectively 1,2,1,1; the interfaces A-B, B-C, A-D have weights 2,2,1 at every slot. Their total weight is ninety. The two target rows have four distinct reduced neighbors but five inherited fine neighbors.

Let L_w be the aggregated weighted Laplacian, and set

\[ q=M^{-1}L_wu,\qquad s_a=M_{aa}^{-1}\sum_b w_{ab}\sin(\vartheta_b-\vartheta_a), \qquad \vartheta=\bar\psi+\delta. \]

Direct edge counting gives L_f P=P M^-1 L_w and S_f(P*vartheta)=P*s. With D=diag(v) and gamma=(1023*pi)^-1, the complete reduced law in the same structural time tau is

\[ p=\tfrac14(-q+\gamma s),\qquad \dot u=D p,\qquad \dot\delta=\tfrac\gamma4Dq. \]
