The pressure p is per fine member. Equivalently both rows use D M^-1 with the unnormalized aggregate fields. Orbit multiplicity is not capacity: v remains the fine capacity consumed by Silence and its floor. The effective capacity of a strength-normalized pure-EPI quotient belongs to another model and cannot supply this aggregate-sum mobility.

The fine vector field intertwines with this lift. Smooth uniqueness thus preserves the sector on every held-capacity segment. This is an exact nonlinear statement for all admitted sector coordinates, not only the carrier tangent. All clock changes multiply both rows by the same existing conversion factor.

The pulled-back excess and its complete balance are

\[ \bar E=\tfrac12u^TL_wu+ \sum_{a<b}w_{ab}[1-\cos(\vartheta_b-\vartheta_a)]-H_*, \quad H_*=45(1-\cos\alpha), \qquad \dot{\bar E}=-\tfrac14 q^T M Dq. \]

They equal the fine energy and loss exactly. The five original child cycles and their winding observations are reconstructed; treating the merged child as one unweighted cycle would change storage. On a fixed positive-capacity segment the conserved form and phase-offset totals are sum_a(m_a/v_a)*u_a and sum_a(m_a/v_a)*delta_a. Their weighted means divide by sum_a m_a/v_a. These are the original fine inverse-capacity totals; the word may change them according to its existing event maps.

docs.title: 3. The marked word consumes inherited counts
docs.text:
Intersect the sector with the section 23 ideal word domain: initial unit capacities, its acute lift cell, E<1/100, abs(initial form mean)<1/30 and the complete supplied context and policies. These inequalities define a relatively open domain in the 72 primary coordinates. Membership in the sector alone does not imply them.

Let beta, lambda and kappa be the shared admitted Reception, phase-locking and Silence factors. Targets i=0,1 are singleton orbits. Each stage uses its own common input snapshot, so the two target proposals are simultaneous.

Reception has the exact inherited form map

\[ u_i^+=(1-\beta)u_i+\frac\beta5\sum_bN_{ib}u_b, \qquad i\in\{0,1\}. \]

All other forms and every phase/capacity are held. Coherence then holds form and capacity and applies, on the existing regular argument branch,

\[ z_i=\sum_bN_{ib}\exp(i(\vartheta_b-\vartheta_i)),\qquad \vartheta_i^+=\vartheta_i+\lambda\operatorname{Arg}z_i. \]

These are the fine neighbor mean and phasor sum grouped by equal values. The multiplicities are inherited integers, not new fitted weights. Silence finally sends v_i to kappa*v_i on both targets, holding primary form and phase. Both swapped children are untouched by each event. All three maps therefore remain in the sector, and lifting each reduced stage reconstructs the full fine primary stage exactly.

The grammar request and live admission are evaluated with the same retained target context, fine capacities, fresh pressure and configuration. In particular, initial AL, IL histories have ordinal two, and successful stages advance through ordinals three, four and five with zero relevant debt and the stated prior-Coherence condition. The IL event-domain policy and actual EN ceilings and SHA floor remain those of the word owner. No new threshold or grammar rule is inferred from the representation.

Original labels and support remain available for any fine-context lookup; replacing source discovery or telemetry with a bare reduced graph is not part of this construction. Stored-pressure event updates remain their own maps, followed by the stipulated fresh-law association before continuation. Lifecycle timestamps do not become structural time. Each stage is separately atomic; there is no new whole-word rollback guarantee.

docs.title: A bare simple graph changes Reception and Coherence
docs.text:
For Reception, put form a at slot zero of the merged child B and zero elsewhere, with carrier phase. At target zero the inherited mean is 2a/5; the four-neighbor unweighted mean is a/4. With target form zero, the successor difference is 3*beta*a/20. For a=1/128, fine excess is 4*a^2<1/100 and the mean is 2*a/45<1/30, so this is inside the same ideal admission domain.

For Coherence, put a small positive phase offset epsilon only at that merged slot. Write r=1+2*cos(alpha)>0. The two relative resultants at target zero are

\[ z_{\rm fine}=r+2e^{i\varepsilon},\qquad z_{\rm bare}=r+e^{i\varepsilon}. \]

For 0<epsilon<pi/2, both real parts are positive and Im(z_fine*conjugate(z_bare))=r*sin(epsilon)>0. Their arguments differ; for positive lambda so do their Coherence increments. Sufficiently small epsilon with zero form is inside the acute energy domain by continuity. At epsilon zero both arguments vanish, so a carrier-only control would miss this error. A weight-two edge does not repair native EN/IL on a simple graph: their current kernels consume unique unweighted neighbors. The support-count owner explains this general inheritance boundary.

docs.title: 4. The same guard, occurrence time and continuation
docs.text:
Use the same fixed level ell and mandatory first downward crossing from the guard owner. Until that first event, the lifted reduced solution is the fine solution and bar E(t)=E_f(t). Their crossing sets agree exactly. Wherever the prior transversality and source-domain conditions admit a unique positive first time, that time is the same in both representations.

At the crossing, lift and all three admitted stage maps commute. Target ordinals and urgency select the same complete word. Its changed capacities are still equal on the exchanged children, so the same continuous intertwining applies afterwards. The full primary hybrid response and its admitted fine observations are reconstructed at every common structural time for which the stated one-word model is defined. This is a conditional solution identity, not an evaluated numerical trajectory.

Both previous matched-summary preparations repeat their profile in all five children and therefore belong to this sector. They give different u vectors in this chart. The reconstruction retains the arrangement that their equal means, energy and loss had discarded; their different occurrence times are consistent with a sufficient reduced state.

The chart admits perturbations only within its fixed sector. It does not bound arbitrary departures of children one and two, establish attraction back to equality, or derive the preparation's symmetry. Other words or targets require their own preservation and context checks. This is neither an all-operator quotient nor a minimum-state or performance theorem.

docs.title: 5. Detached implementation and independent controls
docs.text:
The private child quotient reader derives support from the existing organized-source geometry. It reuses observe_quotient_structure only for exact neighbor counts and aggregated conductance; that metadata observer's pressure/rate normalization is not this complete law.

Lift and restriction admit primitive real values before comparisons. They retain all offsets and positive capacities and reject off-sector inputs. The observation adapter lifts to the existing complete _observe_organized_source_capacity with shared_capacity, then selects representative rows while retaining the fine report. No second sine kernel, integrator or reduced event executor is installed. The mathematical word identity is separate from represented binary64 rounding and optional runtime telemetry.

Independent controls rebuild the fine incidence and count the inherited support, compare both nonlinear rows, energy, loss and weighted totals, check strict reconstruction and both earlier preparations, and compare complete ideal word algebra. The bare-neighbor controls require both a form discrepancy and an off-carrier phase discrepancy. Runtime events, trajectories and frozen response producers remain excluded from these checks.

docs.title: 6. A finite first-hit certificate near the sector
docs.text: The exact chart leaves an operational question: if the two children are only approximately equal, how far apart can their predicted first guard times be? The following certificate derives both crossing existence and a timing allowance from initial primitives, without a numerical trajectory. Its useful conclusion is the fixed-level bracket, beyond the quadratic projected-error mechanism already available in repeated composition and compressed memory.

docs.title: Two incoming-law extensions and an explicit projection
docs.text:
This section fixes all 45 capacities to one, the ninety-edge support, both complete rows and structural time from section 2. No additional forcing, capacity update or support change is allowed on the comparison interval. Let J exchange children one and two, and let Pi=(I+J)/2 act on both form and continuous raw phase offsets. Initialize a full solution z by arbitrary finite real primitives and a symmetric reference w by w(0)=Pi*z(0). The latter is the fine lift of the exact 36-node chart.

Both are mathematical extensions of the incoming law through the declared interval [0,T], even if their actual hybrid executions would already have reset. The smooth vector field is globally Lipschitz, so these extensions exist uniquely. Real lifts need not remain in an acute cell for the estimates below. Crossing this energy level does not itself admit an organized identity, the subsequent word or its grammar context; those retain their separate source-domain requirements.

At each slot write the hidden deviations as

\[ a_j=(x_{1,j}-x_{2,j})/2,\qquad b_j=(\delta_{1,j}-\delta_{2,j})/2,\qquad h_0=\max(\|a(0)\|_\infty,\|b(0)\|_\infty). \]

These are declared normalized coordinates, with the same source units and clock; the joint norm does not identify form and phase as one physical unit. The averaging operation is separate from strict restriction, which still rejects unequal primitives without a tolerance or phase wrapping.

docs.title: Quadratic defect and uniform state allowance
docs.text:
The fine Laplacian commutes with Pi. Therefore the projected phase row has zero direct defect, and only the sine term of the form row contributes. Let vartheta=Pi*Theta, with child orbit labels A, B, C, D as in section 1. For example the defect at A and at B is

\[ \begin{aligned} d_{A,j}&=2\sin(\vartheta_{B,j}-\vartheta_{A,j})(\cos b_j-1),\\ d_{B,j}&=\sum_{k=j\pm1}\sin(\vartheta_{B,k}-\vartheta_{B,j}) [\cos(b_k-b_j)-1]\\ &\quad+\sum_{U=A,C}\sin(\vartheta_{U,j}-\vartheta_{B,j})(\cos b_j-1). \end{aligned} \]

The C row has the same paired-neighbor expression as A and the D row is zero. Since 1-cos(s)<=s^2/2, the two cycle terms in a B row each contribute at most 2*||b||_infty^2 and its two matching terms at most ||b||_infty^2/2 each. Thus

\[ \|\Pi S(\Theta)-S(\Pi\Theta)\|_\infty\le5\|b\|_\infty^2. \]

Let g be a certified upper bound for gamma and set L=5*(1+g)/2, c=5*g/4. The fine degree is at most five, so ||L_f||_infty<=10, the sine map is 10-Lipschitz in the infinity norm, and the complete joint vector field is L-Lipschitz. Comparison of z with Jz gives ||(I-Pi)z(t)||_infty<=h0*exp(L*t).

Choose outward upper bounds G>=exp(L*T) and Phi>=(exp(L*T)-1)/L, and define the allowances

\[ H=h_0G,\qquad e=cH^2\Phi. \]

On the entire interval the hidden state is bounded by H, while ||Pi*z(t)-w(t)||_infty<=e. Indeed the latter error starts at zero and satisfies the upper-Dini comparison e'(t)<=L*e(t)+c*H^2. Consequently fine reconstructed error is bounded by H+e, not by e alone. Hidden form cannot be omitted: it generates hidden phase through the second row even when b(0)=0. No attraction toward the symmetric sector is asserted.

docs.title: Energy and whole-bracket loss from primitives
docs.text:
Put K=L_C9+2I, so ||K||_2<=6. Pairing exchanged edges cancels the linear energy term. With d_j=vartheta_(B,j+1)-vartheta_(B,j) and g_(U,j)=vartheta_(B,j)-vartheta_(U,j), the exact hidden energy difference is

\[ \begin{aligned} E(z)-E(\Pi z) &=a^TKa+2\sum_j\cos d_j[1-\cos(b_{j+1}-b_j)]\\ &\quad+2\sum_j[\cos g_{A,j}+\cos g_{C,j}](1-\cos b_j). \end{aligned} \]

For global real lifts its absolute value is at most a^T K a+b^T K b<=54*(||a||_infty^2+||b||_infty^2)<=108*H^2. It need not be positive outside an acute cell. The same splitting gives the exact instantaneous loss identity rho(z)-rho(Pi*z)=||K*a||_2^2/2; this does not equate the projected state with the separately evolved reference.

Set X0=||x(0)||_infty. The diffusion maximum principle and |S_i|<=5 bound both incoming forms by X(t)=X0+5*g*t/4. Comparing ninety fine edges bounds the form-energy discrepancy between Pi*z and w by 360*X(T)*e, and their phase-energy discrepancy by 180*e. Hence the uniform energy allowance is

\[ B_E=108H^2+[360X(T)+180]e,\qquad |E(z(t))-E(w(t))|\le B_E\quad(0\le t\le T). \]

This is quadratic in the initial hidden norm at fixed horizon and bounded form amplitude. To establish transversality without sampling a response, use q=L_f*x and

\[ \|\dot q(t)\|_\infty \le25X_0+\frac{25g}{2}+\frac{125g}{4}t,\qquad D_q=\left(25X_0+\frac{25g}{2}\right)T+\frac{125g}{8}T^2. \]

For each of the full and reference initial gradients, computed separately, define

\[ r_f=\tfrac14\sum_i\max(|q_{f,i}(0)|-D_q,0)^2,\qquad r_c=\tfrac14\sum_i\max(|q_{c,i}(0)|-D_q,0)^2. \]

These bound the respective losses below on the whole interval. They are source-derived sufficient floors; zero does not imply actual zero loss. The use of raw X0 is conservative: adding a common form offset can change these numerical allowances and their availability, although it leaves the underlying form differences and dynamics unchanged.

docs.title: Same fixed level, existence and timing
docs.text:
Let the shared observer enclose the two initial excess energies in [E_f^-,E_f^+] and [E_c^-,E_c^+]. Keep a single unchanged level ell and require all the strict conditions

\[ E_f^->\ell,\qquad E_c^->\ell,\qquad r_f>0,\qquad r_c>0, \qquad E_c^+-r_cT+B_E<\ell. \]

The loss floors make both energies strictly decreasing. Integration bounds the reference endpoint above by E_c^+-r_c*T, and the energy allowance bounds the full endpoint by an additional B_E. Both therefore cross ell once in (0,T), with transverse first-hit times tau_f,tau_c satisfying

\[ |\tau_f-\tau_c|\le\frac{B_E}{\min(r_f,r_c)}. \]

To see the timing bound, evaluate reference energy at the full hit. Its distance from ell is at most B_E; integration of the reference loss between the two times bounds that distance below by r_c*|tau_f-tau_c|. Replacing r_c with the smaller common floor gives the displayed allowance. Failure of any sufficient inequality makes this timing conclusion unavailable; it does not establish absence of a crossing.

The primitive error reader derives every constant and floor, retains the projected chart and reports the strict margins and unavailable reasons. It accepts unit capacities only. It computes G and Phi using the shared scalar_affine_upper, with the numerical work policy T>0, L*T<=1. Initial radii and their squares remain exact rationals outside the outward growth kernel, preserving exact zero and quadratic scaling even below its interval grid. This short-horizon policy is not a physical time limit. The reader neither integrates nor locates either hit numerically.

Independent controls include strict input admission, projection/exchange identities, exact symmetry, hidden-form-only input, off-carrier quadratic sine cancellation, tiny rational scaling, and unavailable crossing margins. The fixed static certificate preparation is

\[ x(0)=\frac{e_0-e_1}{64}+2^{-20}(e_9-e_{18}),\qquad \delta(0)=2^{-20}(e_9-e_{18}),\qquad T=\frac1{100},\quad\ell=\frac{59}{40960},\quad\nu_i=1. \]

Its threshold and horizon are fixed before evaluation. The unperturbed reference has E_c(0)=3/2048 and rho_c(0)=5/1024; the certificate evaluates primitive inequalities, not a reserved dynamical response.

The fixed control certifies all strict margins. In conservative decimal bounds, both loss floors exceed 0.0043, the uniform energy allowance is below 1.033e-10, and the first-hit difference is below 2.4e-8 in structural-time units. Both hits lie strictly inside (0,0.01); their individual times were not evaluated. These are certificate bounds, not measured errors or a claim about general TNFR preparations.

The result stops at the first-hit bracket. Between unequal event times one actual hybrid solution may already have undergone a finite jump while the other has not. Neither the state allowance nor the incoming energy comparison is an all-time hybrid error bound. Through-word comparison needs separately admitted reset derivatives, context, phase-resultant margins and a choice of aligned or common post-event observation time.

docs.title: 7. Predictive compression through the first guarded word
docs.text: The retained-state question now concerns the action itself: how accurately does the symmetric reference predict form and phase immediately after the first Reception--Coherence--Silence word? These are nonlinear hybrid successors, beyond the incoming crossing comparison of section 6. The marked targets are singleton fibers, so a bound on their projected outputs is also a bound on their actual fine coordinates.

docs.title: Source domain and the chosen observation
docs.text:
Keep section 6's complete incoming law, primitive preparation, first fixed guard and short-horizon arithmetic domain. Independently certify both initial states in the fixed winding-one acute lift cell, with excess below 1/100 and absolute unit-capacity form mean below 1/30. Use the registered default Reception factor beta, phase-locking coefficient lambda and Silence factor kappa; unit incoming capacities become kappa at targets zero and one and remain one elsewhere.

The section 23 word domain retains the complete supplied context: established AL, IL histories with ordinal two, zero debt, prior Coherence, common organized-source kind, initialized core grammar, rejection mode raise, explicit IL event_domain, the represented signed Reception ceilings and inclusive Silence pre-call floor, fresh pressure associated with this independent law, and no optional controllers or mutating callbacks. Neither state nor a detached certificate authenticates that history or establishes a runtime execution receipt.

On the two trajectories, the same prescribed mandatory first crossing is followed urgently by the same ideal primary maps. Each stage uses a common snapshot on targets zero and one, the stages are separately atomic, and no continuous time elapses between them. Write

\[ z_f^+=W(z(\tau_f^-)),\qquad z_c^+=W(w(\tau_c^-)). \]

The observation compares these two complete-word successors, with their structural timestamps tau_f and tau_c retained. Event alignment neither sets the clocks equal nor resets either clock's origin. It compares the same completed action in each execution. There is no claim about a common-time state during the interval between unequal events or about subsequent flow.

docs.title: The comparison states have a derived resultant margin
docs.text:
The acute cell is convex in the declared real offsets and is preserved by the child exchange J. Joint storage is convex on that cell: its form term is quadratic and each phase edge has positive second derivative cosine. Since E(Jz)=E(z), averaging gives

\[ E(\Pi z)\le\tfrac12[E(z)+E(Jz)]=E(z). \]

The cell, capacities and ordinary form mean are also preserved by Pi. The existing boundary/loss theorem maintains both incoming states in the domain up to their own hits. It follows that the actual fine input, its projected comparison input and the reference input at their respective hits all have acute excess below 1/100. The same remains true through Reception, which holds phase and is passive.

The existing local-resultant theorem therefore gives Re Z_i>4 at both targets for each of these phase inputs. This margin is derived from the source domain, rather than supplied as an arbitrary constant. The straight chord between any two such resultants stays in Re Z>4, so the continuous principal argument has Lipschitz bound 1/4 along the chord. No phase branch change or zero resultant is crossed.

The one-word mean/rail budget supplies unit rails and strict Reception form/pressure margins for the admitted defaults. The unit pre-Silence capacity satisfies its supplied inclusive floor. Those mathematical and policy-parameter checks remain distinct from the contextual premises above.

docs.title: Separate the timing contribution from the reset defect
docs.text:
Let H, e, X and Delta denote the section 6 hidden-state, projected-state, whole-window form and first-hit time-difference bounds. Both incoming rows give the joint velocity allowance

\[ V=\max\left(\frac{10X+5g}{4},\frac{5gX}{2}\right),\qquad D=e+V\Delta. \]

Comparing at one time using e, then integrating the reference incoming row between the two hit times, proves

\[ \|\Pi z(\tau_f^-)-w(\tau_c^-)\|_\infty\le D. \]

Only the mathematical incoming extension is used in that integration; no actual reset trajectory is silently continued by the old law.

Reception is a convex linear form map for 0<beta<=1. It commutes with Pi because the marked targets are fixed and both swapped neighbors are retained with their inherited counts. Its infinity-norm Lipschitz bound is one. It changes no phase, so the complete-word projected form allowance will remain D.

For Coherence at target i, the only hidden contribution is the paired matching neighbor from children one and two. With symmetric relative phase u and hidden phase b at that slot, its phasor difference is exactly

\[ Z_i(z)-Z_i(\Pi z)=2e^{iu}(\cos b-1),\qquad |Z_i(z)-Z_i(\Pi z)|\le b^2\le H^2. \]

The target itself is a singleton, so its input lift has no hidden part. The argument margin gives a direct phase-reset defect at most lambda*H^2/4. Between the projected fine and reference inputs, each relative angle changes by at most 2D; five neighbors yield a phasor difference at most 10D. Including the target's retained input lift, the resulting complete-word bounds are

\[ F=D,\qquad P=\left(1+\frac{5\lambda}{2}\right)D+ \frac{\lambda H^2}{4}, \] \[ \|\Pi x_f^+-x_c^+\|_\infty\le F,\qquad \|\Pi\delta_f^+-\delta_c^+\|_\infty\le P, \qquad \nu_f^+=\nu_c^+. \]

Silence establishes the exact last equality while holding form and phase. All three stages leave the hidden child coordinates unchanged. Thus full fine reconstruction has joint error at most H+max(F,P), whereas each marked target directly has the finer form/phase allowances F and P.

At a fixed horizon and bounded X, the projected allowances are quadratic in the initial hidden size provided the two loss floors remain uniformly bounded away from zero. That positive denominator is necessary: the timing allowance alone need not be uniformly quadratic as transversality degenerates. The fine reconstruction remains generally first order in hidden size.

An immediate energy observation follows from the same edge accounting:

\[ |E_f^+-E_c^+|\le108H^2+360XF+180P. \]

Reception keeps both form extrema within X, and subsequent stages hold form. The hidden energy term is unchanged in structure, with both hidden norms at most H. Each actual ideal successor separately has E^+<=ell by word passivity. These are energy bounds at the aligned successors, not a balance over an interval spanning different hybrid laws.

docs.title: A nonzero quadratic Coherence defect
docs.text:
The approximation is not an exact off-sector word descent. A static control makes this explicit without claiming to know either actual hit state. Set form to zero, give node 9 offset phi+b and node 18 offset phi-b, and set every other offset to zero. Fix phi=1/128, b=2^-20. Both the full and projected preparations have acute edge angles, zero form mean and excess at most 4*(phi^2+b^2)<1/100.

At target zero, with r=1+2*cos(alpha), their relative resultants are

\[ Z_f=r+2e^{i\phi}\cos b,\qquad Z_c=r+2e^{i\phi},\qquad \Im(Z_f\overline{Z_c})=2r(\cos b-1)\sin\phi<0. \]

Both lie in the right half-plane, so their arguments differ. More precisely, as b tends to zero at fixed positive phi,

\[ \operatorname{Arg}Z_f-\operatorname{Arg}Z_c =-\frac{r\sin\phi}{|Z_c|^2}b^2+O(b^4). \]

The default positive lambda preserves this nonzero quadratic correction in the target phase. A carrier-only control with phi zero would miss it. The sign here belongs to the supplied static pair, not to the separate unknown states at the two actual crossings. This distinguishes a useful finite approximation from exact closure after hidden phase has been discarded.

docs.title: Detached implementation and acceptance boundary
docs.text:
The word-error reader rebuilds the incoming certificate from primitives and resolves the registered default factors. It reuses the source barrier, shared offset-edge geometry and one-word reuse budget to check the mathematical domain and applicable scalar margins. The same offset helper serves the existing reflection retention reader; it retains the closing-edge lift and never substitutes rounded raw phases for the exact carrier.

Conditional endpoint bounds are absent when a source, crossing or sufficient word-domain margin fails. The report retains the available evidence and reasons; an unavailable certificate does not prove that an event fails or that its successor loses organization. It installs no selector, performs no ideal or represented reset, and neither locates a hit nor integrates flow. Binary64 event errors, stale pressure, callbacks and runtime history require their own admission outside this mathematical certificate.

Independent controls check the branch-sensitive source domain, inherited factors and capacities, the local nonlinear word algebra, exact symmetry, tiny nonzero deviations, and unavailable conditions. The first-hit static preparation from section 6 is fixed unchanged for the successor certificate; the separate off-carrier control above tests the nonzero reset defect. Neither control evaluates a reserved trajectory or an actual first-word response.

For the fixed first-hit preparation, all successor-certificate conditions pass. Conservative bounds on the aligned projected outputs are F<9.5e-10 and P<1.7e-9; full fine reconstruction is bounded by 9.8e-7 and the aligned energy discrepancy by 3.1e-7. These are bounds in the declared model coordinates, not evaluated errors. The independent static phase control has the exact negative sign proved above; its high-precision default Coherence increment difference is approximately -2.62782e-16. That value belongs only to the supplied static pair.

docs.title: State-guard sensitivity of the organized word
docs.text:
Conditional result. A mandatory first downward crossing of a supplied energy level gives a locally unique occurrence of Reception (EN), Coherence (IL) and Silence (SHA) near the existing organized-source witness. Its response derivative contains the change in event time as well as the reset derivative. The correction is nonzero in a fixed internal observation, even after both compared words have completed at a common structural time.

Under one fixed guard, equal child means, energy and instantaneous loss can still give different next occurrence times. The predictive-state obstruction identifies fine information omitted by that instantaneous summary.

This owner extends the complete flow/word comparison. The new statement is a local hybrid sensitivity law, not another generic argument that policies are supplied. Existing support-law countermodels and transverse admission crossings retain their separate models. Neither a guard's mathematical regularity nor its implementation would derive the choice of threshold from TNFR.

docs.title: 1. Complete model and mandatory occurrence
docs.text:
Retain the organized source's 45 labeled nodes, ninety unit edges, marked targets (0,1), raw form, primitive phase lifts and structural clock tau. The support and targets are supplied. Initially all capacities are one; after the word they are kappa at the targets and one elsewhere. Let L be the actual fine Laplacian, q=Lx, gamma=(1023*pi)^-1 and

\[ S_i(\Theta)=\sum_{j\sim i}\sin(\Theta_j-\Theta_i),\qquad F_D(x,\Theta)=\frac14 \begin{pmatrix}D[-q+\gamma S(\Theta)]\\ \gamma Dq\end{pmatrix}. \]

Both rows use the same positive held capacity matrix D. Pressure is the independent formula p=(-q+gamma*S)/4, refreshed before admission and continuation. There is no external forcing. The actual excess is

\[ E(x,\Theta)=\tfrac12 x^T Lx+ \sum_{\{i,j\}}[1-\cos(\Theta_j-\Theta_i)]-H_*, \qquad H_*=45[1-\cos(2\pi/9)]. \]

Use the section 23 ideal domain, including its acute lift branch, E<1/100, initial abs(m(1))<1/30, shared represented factors and all execution-context premises. These include the common organized-source kind, initial AL, IL history, ordinal two, zero debt, prior Coherence, initialized core grammar, raise, hard unit rails, explicit IL event_domain policy, actual Reception ceilings and Silence floor. Retain the actual context updates and weighted means, with carrier subtraction for phase origins. No custom monitor or additional callback mutation is present.

For a fixed constant ell, supply the following occurrence policy:

  1. With both target ordinals two, flow while E>ell. At the first downward crossing E=ell, Reception is mandatory; continued pre-word flow through that crossing is not another permitted choice.
  2. After successful Reception both target ordinals are three. Immediately apply Coherence, then Silence at ordinal four. Each two-target stage reads its own snapshot and is separately atomic. There is no intervening flow and no claim of a single rollback transaction.
  3. At ordinal five disable further word requests and continue with the changed held capacities. No second word or renewal mechanism is present.

The monotonic ordinal is existing retained context, owned by read_grammar_state and current_operator_step; it is not the length of a bounded trace. This policy specifies how that context is consumed; recording an ordinal alone would neither execute nor authenticate an event. Urgency and the ordered requests are additional model premises. Starting on or below the guard, mismatched ordinals and failed live admission lie outside the source domain proved below.

The rule reads the complete network state. No local sensor, unmarked-target selection or default native-selector realization is established. It is autonomous on the mathematical and grammar state because it does not read absolute time. Silence's wall-clock timestamp remains execution telemetry. The threshold, target marks and request policy are supplied law parameters, not an unrecorded clock or an additional hidden latch. In particular ell is not recomputed from each perturbed initial state's energy.

docs.title: 2. Local positive waiting and unique crossings
docs.text:
Write z=(x,Theta) on the fixed-capacity source slice. The energy differential and its pre-word rate are

\[ n=DE=(q^T,-S^T),\qquad nF_1=-\tfrac14 q^Tq=-\rho. \]

The phase terms cancel because both complete rows are retained. Nonincrease alone does not imply rho>0; transversality is a separate local hypothesis.

Use the exact prior witness x_*=h(e_0-e_1), h=1/64, and Theta_*=psi, where psi_(9c+j)=2*pi*(j-4)/9. Its values are

\[ E_*=6h^2=3/2048,\qquad \|Lx_*\|^2=80h^2, \qquad\rho_*=20h^2=5/1024>0. \]

The previous radius-10^-5 box is already inside the ideal domain. In that box the degree-five target rows give abs(q_i-q_*i)<10*epsilon for i=0,1, hence

\[ \rho\ge\tfrac12(6h-10\varepsilon)^2>0, \qquad\varepsilon=10^{-5}. \]

This estimate applies to independent phase perturbations as well. Smoothness gives a short pre-word flow segment remaining inside the box. Its energy decreases strictly, so every sufficiently close level below E_* is reached once on that segment, at a positive time. The first crossing is unique; the prescribed urgent stages and subsequent smooth flow then give a unique local hybrid solution for each specified level and admitted initial state. There are only three zero-duration stages and no recurrent event sequence.

For a crossing state y=Phi^-_tau(s), define G(s,ell,tau)=E(Phi^-_tau(s))-ell. Since G_tau=-rho(y)<0, the implicit-function theorem gives a smooth crossing time in a neighborhood of each such source and level. For each fixed sufficiently close level the initial neighborhood can be chosen open in all ninety continuous coordinates, with E(initial)>ell, the same context and a positive waiting time. This does not claim all section 23 levels or preparations cross transversely.

docs.title: 3. The derivative at a common structural time
docs.text:
Let W be the complete primary word and let F_+=F_D use its actual Silence successor capacities. On the fixed discrete-context domain define

\[ K(y)=DW(y)F_1(y)-F_+(W(y)). \]

The earlier complete formula retains Coherence's nonidentity phase derivative. At a fixed common time T strictly after the crossing, set

\[ Z(T;s,\ell)=\Phi^+_{T-\tau(s,\ell)} W\Phi^-_{\tau(s,\ell)}(s), \quad M_-=D\Phi^-_\tau(s),\quad M_+=D\Phi^+_{T-\tau}(W(y)). \]

All quantities below are evaluated at this crossing. Differentiating G gives

\[ \delta\tau=\frac{nM_-\delta s-\delta\ell}{\rho}. \]

Differentiating the full endpoint, including the changed duration of the post-word flow, then gives

\[ \begin{split} \delta Z&=M_+\{DW M_-\delta s+K\delta\tau\}\\ &=M_+\left\{\left(DW+\frac{K\otimes n}{\rho}\right) M_-\delta s-\frac K\rho\delta\ell\right\}. \end{split} \]

Thus the event-local derivative at matched clocks, often called the saltation matrix, and the threshold sensitivity are

\[ \mathcal S=DW+K\otimes n/\rho, \qquad\partial_\ell Z=-M_+K/\rho. \]

Using only DW would omit the rank-one timing correction. Its sign has an independent consistency check:

\[ \mathcal S F_1=DW F_1+K(nF_1)/\rho=F_+\circ W. \]

A perturbation along the incoming flow must follow the outgoing flow after matching clocks. Both phase and form participate in this identity. Under a common constant clock rescaling, K and rho scale by the same factor, so K/rho and the timing correction retain their coordinate meaning; the crossing-time covector itself transforms with the clock unit.

These derivatives concern the full ninety-coordinate primary state on the declared fixed initial-capacity and fixed-factor domain. Successor capacity is the same D for every compared level and contributes no threshold derivative. The observation clock T is held fixed. Derived fresh pressure has variation delta p=(-L*delta x+gamma*DS*delta Theta)/4. Record/lifecycle updates remain their separate maps. Neither weighted means nor primary coordinates are projected away to obtain this derivative.

docs.title: 4. An exact internal correction and two fixed levels
docs.text:
At the carrier, n=(q^T,0) although the incoming phase row is nonzero. For the fixed observation

\[ \mathcal O(z)=\bigl(x_8-x_2, (\Theta_8-\psi_8)-(\Theta_2-\psi_2)\bigr), \]

the previous exact result gives D O K_*=(3*beta*h/5)*(1,-gamma). Consequently the event-local threshold coefficient is

\[ -D\mathcal O K_*/\rho_* =\frac{48\beta}{25}(-1,\gamma)\ne0. \]

This is a local crossing-state coefficient, not an untransported coefficient at an arbitrary later T. A separate initial-state control takes the direction v=(e_0,0). Here n v/rho=96/5 and

\[ D\mathcal O(\mathcal S-DW)v =\frac{9\beta}{50}(1,-\gamma)\ne0. \]

In that direction DW alone gives zero for this contrast. The timing correction therefore changes an actual prediction of the local derivative, not just a bookkeeping label. Common form translations and common phase rotations give n v=0; the correction vanishes on those offset directions. As before, only offsets that stay inside the admitted absolute rails are compared.

To relate this derivative to two positive waiting times, fix the two law parameters ell_1=E_*-eta and ell_2=E_*-2*eta for sufficiently small eta>0. Their common initial state is s_*, and

\[ \tau_1=\eta/\rho_*+O(\eta^2),\qquad \tau_2=2\eta/\rho_*+O(\eta^2). \]

There is a T_0>0 such that, for every fixed 0<T<T_0, a sufficiently small positive eta makes both crossings occur before T and gives

\[ \mathcal O(Z(T;s_*,\ell_2))-\mathcal O(Z(T;s_*,\ell_1)) =\eta\,D\mathcal O\,D\Phi^+_T(Ws_*)K_*/\rho_*+O(\eta^2). \]

The displayed coefficient tends to (48*beta/25)*(1,-gamma) as T tends to zero, so both components remain nonzero for sufficiently small fixed positive T. This continuity statement includes the required post-word transport; the bare event-local coefficient cannot replace it at finite T.

For each chosen such eta and T, continuous dependence gives a smaller open initial neighborhood where both positive crossings and the observed distinction persist, with the two levels held fixed. It need not be uniform as eta tends to zero. Both histories have completed AL, IL, EN, IL, SHA, both capacities equal D and both structural clocks equal T. The source's geometric identity, form rails and fresh-pressure bounds follow from the existing one-word domain.

This is a distinction between two complete models with different supplied thresholds, not two solutions of one fully specified law. The internal contrast removes common coordinate offsets. No numerical value for T_0, eta's admissible radius or a finite separation margin has been evaluated. There is no claim of asymptotic separation, optimized activation or physical identification.

docs.title: 5. Detached implementation and controls
docs.text:
The private _assess_organized_source_carrier_guard_sensitivity reuses the complete carrier timing reader. It re-admits the primitive form and represented factors, derives rho from the shared gradient, and rejects a zero-loss carrier state before division. Its guard level is only the energy at the supplied crossing point; the reader does not choose a threshold for another preparation or predict a first-hit time.

The report retains K, the exact event-time covectors, the factorization of the timing correction, and -K/rho in both rows. Phase expressions retain their rational coefficients of cos(2*pi/9) and their gamma factor, with outward interval enclosures. Noncarrier crossings and propagation to T are covered by the conditional theorem, not evaluated by this carrier reader.

Independent tests check the incidence loss, the implicit crossing condition, complete incoming and outgoing flow consistency, the failure of a reset-only derivative, threshold signs, common-offset controls and nontransverse/invalid rejection. Runtime events, integration and frozen producers are prohibited in these algebraic checks. No live guard, scheduler or new occurrence policy is installed.

The result identifies what a supplied state guard contributes to a complete prediction: its level and urgency, a transverse crossing, and the event-time term in the derivative. Justifying that guard from an independent premise, or using it in a finite numerical prediction, remains a separate question.

docs.title: 6. Collective summaries do not predict the same guard time
docs.text:
Conditional obstruction. Even with the threshold and occurrence policy fixed, the five child form/phase means, capacities and grammar context, excess energy E and instantaneous loss rho do not form sufficient predictive state for the next guard occurrence. Two admitted fine preparations have the same such snapshot but different first-hit times. They also have identical initial primary state, fresh pressure and continuous rates at the marked targets. The distinction concerns hidden fine preparation under one law, rather than different choices of event threshold.

This specializes the collective descent criterion to the first occurrence time of this word. Generic failures of scalar storage and loss as predictive state already appear in constituent memory and the native formation controls. Those results keep their own supports, complete laws and predictions; the present calculation derives the same-guard time distinction on this support.

docs.title: Observation and complete incoming law
docs.text:
Let m_c=(1/9)*sum_j x_(9c+j) and a_c=(1/9)*sum_j(Theta_(9c+j)-psi_(9c+j)), using the admitted primitive lifts. These are phase-offset means, not arguments of circular resultants; the resultant of the exact winding-one carrier is zero. Retain the five pairs (m_c,a_c), the initial capacity vector and common supplied grammar context, E and rho. The support, marks, factors, clock origin and fixed level are the same. The strengthened snapshot may additionally retain the primary coordinates, fresh pressure and both continuous rates at targets zero and one. It does not retain the full fine form, fine pressure or their association.

For unit incoming capacities, the complete law gives

\[ \dot E=-\rho=-\tfrac14q^Tq,\qquad \dot q=\tfrac14L[-q+\gamma S(\Theta)],\qquad \ddot E=\tfrac18\{q^TLq-\gamma q^TLS(\Theta)\}. \]

At the exact initial carrier S(psi)=0, so ddot E(0)=x^T L^3 x/8. This is an instantaneous identity of the coupled model: dot Theta=gamma*q/4 is generally nonzero, and the subsequent phase is not held at the carrier. Away from that initial point the displayed phase-dependent term remains part of the law.

docs.title: An exact matched pair in the admitted domain
docs.text:
Let h=1/128 and repeat one profile in all five children:

\[ x^A_{9c+j}=h(\delta_{j3}-\delta_{j6}),\qquad x^B_{9c+j}=h(\delta_{j3}-\delta_{j7}),\qquad \Theta^A=\Theta^B=\psi. \]

All child form and phase-offset means are zero. Matching edges have zero form and phase difference because corresponding child profiles agree. The repeated-child subspace is invariant before the event: matching currents vanish and every child obeys the same two coupled cycle rows, regardless of its degree in the child graph. Antisymmetry of the cycle currents therefore preserves each of those means during pre-word continuation.

For the nine-cycle Laplacian L_9, write A_k for its distance-k adjacency matrix. Exact multiplication gives

\[ L_9^2=6I-4A_1+A_2,\qquad L_9^3=20I-15A_1+6A_2-A_3. \]

The two signed pairs have cycle distances three and four. Both have first quadratic moment four and second moment twelve; their third moments are forty-two and forty. The matching-edge terms vanish also on their successive Laplacian images. Thus the full fine quantities are

Quantity Preparation A Preparation B Initial excess E_0 10*h^2 = 5/8192 10*h^2 = 5/8192 Initial loss rho_0 15*h^2 = 15/16384 15*h^2 = 15/16384 Initial energy acceleration sigma 105*h^2/4 = 105/65536 25*h^2 = 25/16384

Both have E_0<1/100, unit capacities and zero initial global form mean; the exact carrier lies in the required acute lift branch. They therefore belong to the section 23 ideal one-word domain with the shared initialized context and explicit IL event-domain policy. Zero target forms are permitted with the retained established history. No claim of acquiring these fine preparations by that history is made.

The source is different from section 2's particular witness and radius box. Here both target form values and q values are zero initially, so fresh target pressure and both target rates are zero in both preparations. The full q is nonzero and rho_0>0. Smoothness gives a neighborhood of each preparation with strictly positive loss; the general transverse-crossing argument applies without using the earlier degree-five target lower bound.

No support-preserving relabeling identifies the pair: x^T L^3 x is invariant under every such permutation but differs here. A common form shift cannot remove that difference, and both states already have the same zero means. The observation has discarded dynamically relevant fine arrangement.

docs.title: One fixed level, different positive occurrence times
docs.text:
Choose one constant level ell=E_0-eta with sufficiently small eta>0, and hold it fixed for both preparations. Apply the same mandatory first crossing and EN–IL–SHA policy from section 1. Strict positive initial loss gives a unique positive first crossing for each preparation in a short pre-word interval. Both words remain within the shared ideal admission domain.

For a fixed preparation with initial loss rho_0 and acceleration sigma, smoothness and the implicit-function theorem give

\[ E(t)=E_0-\rho_0t+\tfrac12\sigma t^2+O(t^3),\qquad \tau(\eta)=\frac{\eta}{\rho_0} +\frac{\sigma}{2\rho_0^3}\eta^2+O(\eta^3). \]

This is an expansion in a family of fixed levels for one initial point, not the fixed-level derivative with respect to a varying source in section 3. At every chosen eta the two compared experiments use exactly the same law parameter ell. Substitution of the exact pair yields

\[ \tau_A(\eta)-\tau_B(\eta) =\frac{\eta^2}{5400h^4}+O(\eta^3)>0 \]

for every sufficiently small positive eta. Preparation A reaches the level later despite equal initial energy and loss. The nonzero quadratic term proves unequal exact times by the local remainder statement; it is not a computed finite waiting time or an evaluated error bar. No numerical eta radius, crossing forecast or later endpoint separation is claimed.

docs.title: Predictive-state consequence and implementation boundary
docs.text:
A deterministic next-time function of this instantaneous summary, with the same fixed level and parameters, would give the same output for both inputs. The proved distinction rules it out on any source class containing this pair. The summary also fails the continuous descent criterion directly: dot rho=-sigma differs at the matched snapshot. It cannot have a single autonomous first-order evolution law reproducing the full projected flow on that source class.

This does not obstruct detection from an externally supplied exact live energy stream: that stream already reveals when E=ell. Predicting its future evolution from a snapshot is the question decided here. Retaining sigma resolves the displayed quadratic discrepancy, but neither that fact nor the pair proves closure of a larger moment system, minimal sufficient state, or sufficiency of a finite noisy observation history.

The existing detached carrier guard reader additionally reports exact energy_second_time_derivative and drop_time_quadratic_coefficient. It rebuilds Lq using the shared support and primitive-state admission; the second value is sigma/(2*rho^3). Independent incidence tests check both complete-law derivatives, the matched pair, exact series reversion, scale and offset controls and tiny positive loss. No integration, live guard, event execution or frozen response producer is used for this result.

The child-swap hybrid representation provides a sufficient state on a declared invariant sector containing both preparations. It retains their distinct internal profiles, the counted word maps and the same guard. It neither makes the insufficient summary above closed nor reconstructs arbitrary off-sector fine states from averaged data.

Declared model, preparation and admission question
docs.text:
