  • the selected history channel, last two signed scalar EPI samples, their declared clock/units and timestamps when present, plus the live EPI endpoint and its sample association;
  • finite active capacity, any explicitly configured minimum, the threshold and its units, and the actual stored pressure used for prediction and the phase-reset direction, including its represented signed-zero branch;
  • the ordered recent glyphs, persistent prior-coherence and debt records, complete-word context, target order and all consumed runtime configuration;
  • any third sample required by the separately requested acceleration diagnostic and the provenance of all intervening events and refreshes.

Per-port histories cannot be replaced by a mean-form history of the whole organization: an average rate need not equal either target's rate. Physical twin equality also does not identify independently associated lifecycle or temporal records. A collective transition is a partial map on this richer context, not an operation determined by winding and instantaneous fields.

The current timestamped reader uses the last two replayable (time, epi) records. It requires finite signed real samples, a finite positive interval and agreement of the final represented EPI with the current EPI. Runtime uses zero endpoint tolerance; the pure certificate can declare a finite nonnegative absolute tolerance, without weakening the strict rate threshold. Current uniform-real BEPI is admitted through the shared signed-scalar boundary; a magnitude projection cannot supply signed growth. Nonfinite, Boolean and nonzero values lost on materialization are not valid primitive evidence, and output arithmetic must remain representable.

When epi_time_history is supplied, it is authoritative: invalid or stale endpoint evidence does not fall back to an untimestamped alternative. Without it, a nonempty epi_history takes precedence over _epi_history; the existing empty-canonical compatibility case can use the latter. These legacy channels declare one operator step between samples and do not check a current endpoint. They are explicitly not continuous-time evidence.

The field physical_time_resolved records that an interval was supplied by timestamps. It is not laboratory calibration or provenance authentication. The pure certificate and runtime adapter do not consume an independently authoritative live clock: equal final EPI values alone cannot establish that the last timestamp is the present instant. In this research model, the observation protocol must additionally bind the endpoint to the declared live structural time, target identity, source, law and intervening events. The graph's _t cannot be compared blindly when another execution path uses it for operator positions. A record reader cannot establish these missing associations by inspecting two scalar values.

The current product nu_f*p is an endpoint prediction; the secant is an interval average. Their difference is not automatically a solver residual or a law violation, even with valid records. A bound on rate variation and the complete intervening model would be needed for that interpretation. The optional three-sample acceleration diagnostic is separate from both the strict two-sample trigger and the independent U4b check.

docs.title: 5. Clock changes cannot manufacture a genuine crossing
docs.text:
For an affine change s=c*t+b with c>0, transform both rows, not only the history timestamps:

\[ \frac{dx}{ds}=\frac1c MS,\qquad \frac{d\theta}{ds}=\frac1c Mq. \tag{6} \]

One consistent parameterization retains p and uses nu_s=nu_t/c, hence M_s=M_t/c. Histories transform to s_k=c*t_k+b and the rate-calibrated threshold transforms to xi_s=xi_t/c. Then

\[ r_s=\frac{r_t}{c},\qquad r_s>\xi_s\ \Longleftrightarrow\ r_t>\xi_t, \qquad \nu_s>\pi\xi_s\ \Longleftrightarrow\nu_t>\pi\xi_t. \tag{7} \]

Capacity floors and every other consumed dimensional setting need their own corresponding transformation. This is not an automatic equivalence of all configured event policies. Keeping xi numerically fixed while compressing timestamps changes the trigger policy; changing only the nodal form row changes the complete model.

For a nonlinear monotone clock, a finite secant transforms by the interval ratio Delta t/Delta s, not just the inverse clock derivative at the final sample. No endpoint-only rescaling proves finite-window equivalence. Untimestamped operator-step histories need a separately declared timing model before either clock comparison applies. None of these structural clock choices supplies a laboratory-unit bridge.

docs.title: 6. Represented measurements and model-domain checks
docs.text:
Suppose two recorded forms differ from their true same-law values by errors of magnitude at most epsilon_0 and epsilon_1, at exact declared times separated by h>0. Before accounting for arithmetic, their secant error obeys

\[ |\widehat r-r|\leq\frac{\epsilon_0+\epsilon_1}{h}. \tag{8} \]

Solver, scalar-conversion and division errors require their additional budget. Timestamp uncertainty requires a positive interval enclosure and its own quotient bound. The analytical ceiling B in (5) implies a represented non-crossing only when B plus all applicable rate errors does not exceed xi. A very short interval can amplify fixed endpoint errors; increasing sampling precision does not establish missing grammar or source provenance.

Conversely, a record-level crossing alone does not refute (3) or (5). Its history may come from a different clock, an intervening jump, another capacity/law, an out-of-sector interval or unresolved numerical error. These possibilities must be distinguished rather than classifying every rejection as a dynamical obstruction. Invalid primitive evidence must reject; unavailable evidence must remain unavailable, not acquire an invented zero-rate estimate.

docs.title: 7. Scope of the resulting admission decision
docs.text:
The complete sine law is compatible with strict continuous growth on states satisfying the sharp condition in section 2. The actual NAV successor is not ready for ZHIR: its temporal evidence is unavailable and its recent grammar independently rejects the transformer. Its retained acute winding-one continuations also have the conditional obstruction (5). None of these results excludes Mutation in every TNFR model or requires this one organization to realize every registered operator.

Reopening an actual collective event comparison requires independently justified source/capacity/clock and grammar context, real endpoint-bound temporal evidence with an adequate error budget, and admission of the actual reset and post-event observation. A supplied event selector would remain separate from eligibility. The general integration question is which states and laws admit each operator's contract; it does not impose EN/IL/SHA/NAV as a compulsory causal chain for all operator studies.

Synthetic reader and runtime controls exercise missing/stale evidence, signed strict comparisons, representation boundaries, independent grammar rejection and declared clock behavior. They are not observed research histories or a new response campaign. The shared owners above retain execution; this analysis introduces no alternative trigger reader.

The collective Mutation admission controls exercise these reader and grammar boundaries on independent inputs. The verification guide owns the maintained test selection.

docs.title: Collective phase families and live contact feedback
docs.text:
Unit and weighted phase-offset partitions, nearby full-state moving windows, contact/storage exchange and complete receiver-rigidity conditions.

Part of Sine pattern geometry and dissipative capture. Section numbers are stable across the collection; hypotheses and model changes remain local to each result.

docs.title: 39. Compatible internal geometry and collective phase dynamics
docs.text: A region can retain phase differences while its common form and phase continue to evolve. The full nodal rows determine when this is possible; an instantaneous equality of phase rates does not suffice. This section classifies exact collective families under Section 35's conservative unit law, fixed finite connected simple support, unit held capacities and tau=t/pi. No input, event or change of support is introduced.

docs.title: A declared partition with fixed internal phase offsets
docs.text:
Partition every fine node into nonempty blocks B_a. Supply fixed circular offsets psi_i; a consistent real lift can be used for differentiation. Consider the whole family

\[ \mathcal M_\psi: \qquad x_i=X_a,\qquad \theta_i=\Theta_a+\psi_i \quad(i\in B_a), \]

with freely varying collective forms X_a and phases Theta_a. Internal phase differences are fixed, but different nodes need not share a phase. The block partition and offsets are supplied geometry, not inferred membership or a newly created node. Define, using full graph degrees,

\[ q_{ib}=\frac{|N(i)\cap B_b|}{d_i},\qquad Z_{ib}=\frac1{d_i} \sum_{j\in N(i)\cap B_b}e^{\mathrm i(\psi_j-\psi_i)}. \]

The family is invariant under the complete law if and only if, in each block a, the following conditions hold:

  1. For every external block b!=a, q_ib=q_ab is independent of i.
  2. For every external block b!=a, the full complex value Z_ib=Z_ab is independent of i.
  3. Every internal sine sum vanishes: Im Z_ia=0 for all i in B_a.

These are conditions on support and phase offsets for all collective states. Failure does not exclude an accidental special trajectory with additional relations between its collective coordinates. In particular, equal neighbor counts alone do not settle the nonlinear form row.

docs.title: Necessity and sufficiency use both consumed rows
docs.text:
On the proposed family the phase row at i in B_a is

\[ heta_i'=\sum_{b e a}q_{ib}(X_a-X_b). \]

For its value to be independent of i for every independent choice of X, each external coefficient must agree. The form row is

\[ x_i'=\operatorname{Im}Z_{ia} +\sum_{b e a}\operatorname{Im} \left[Z_{ib}e^{\mathrm i(\Theta_b-\Theta_a)} ight]. \]

Independent variation of the collective phase differences makes the external sine and cosine coefficients independent Fourier components. Their equality forces equality of the external complex values Z_ib. The remaining internal imaginary parts must be one common constant c_a. Undirected internal edges give

\[ \sum_{i\in B_a}d_i\operatorname{Im}Z_{ia} =\sum_{\substack{i,j\in B_a\j\sim i}} \sin(\psi_j-\psi_i)=0. \]

Since sum_(i in B_a) d_i>0, that common constant is zero. There is no additional condition on Re Z_ia: the form row does not consume it and the phase row has zero internal form differences. For example a one-block P3 with offsets (0,0,pi) has internal real values (1,0,-1), zero internal sine current and uniform-form equilibria. Requiring the complete internal complex sums to agree would wrongly reject this family.

Conversely, the three conditions make both fine rows constant within their respective blocks. The field is tangent to M_psi everywhere; smooth uniqueness therefore preserves the family. Its exact closed law is

\[ oxed{ egin{aligned} X_a'&=\sum_{b e a}\operatorname{Im} \left[Z_{ab}e^{\mathrm i(\Theta_b-\Theta_a)} ight],\ \Theta_a'&=\sum_{b e a}q_{ab}(X_a-X_b). \end{aligned}} \]

Thus phase-offset geometry and support determine whether all constituents maintain compatible rates while the collective coordinates move. This is an invariant-family reduction, not a quotient for every fine state.

docs.title: Reciprocity, inherited storage and conserved means
docs.text:
Let m_a=sum_(i in B_a) d_i, N_ab=m_a q_ab and P_ab=m_a Z_ab. Counting the same undirected cross edges in reverse gives

\[ N_{ab}=N_{ba},\qquad P_{ab}=\overline{P_{ba}},\qquad |Z_{ab}|\le q_{ab}. \]

The full fine storage restricted to the family is exactly

\[ \begin{aligned} E_{\mathcal M} &=E_{\mathrm{int}}(\psi) +\sum_{a<b}\left[ \frac{N_{ab}}2(X_a-X_b)^2+N_{ab} -\operatorname{Re}\left( P_{ab}e^{\mathrm i(\Theta_b-\Theta_a)}\right)\right],\\ E_{\mathrm{int}}(\psi) &=\sum_a\sum_{\{i,j\}\subset B_a,\ i\sim j} [1-\cos(\psi_j-\psi_i)]. \end{aligned} \]

The closed rows consequently satisfy

\[ X_a'=-\frac1{m_a}\frac{\partial E_{\mathcal M}}{\partial\Theta_a}, \qquad \Theta_a'=\frac1{m_a}\frac{\partial E_{\mathcal M}}{\partial X_a}. \]

This is a restriction of the existing storage and reciprocal field, not an independently supplied energy. It preserves that storage and the collective weighted sums sum_a m_a X_a and sum_a m_a Theta_a in continuous lifts. The fixed contribution sum_i d_i psi_i restores the full lifted phase sum.

In general the inherited form coupling Z_ab and phase coupling q_ab are different. Phase cancellation can give |Z_ab|<q_ab, and complex offsets can remain in the interaction. Replacing both by the weights of a bare normalized-sine graph would then change the complete law. This is the same retained-information boundary as in nonlinear replica inheritance.

For each block separately, internal form storage is zero and internal phase storage is constant. In fact q_R=S_R=0 at every point of this family, not only initially. Section 36's internal channels and the net regional power P_R therefore vanish throughout its motion. This does not remove interaction: the collective forms and phases, cross-edge storage and common regional rates can change. Internal regional storage does not count that cross-edge organization.

docs.title: One moving realization on the retained private-leaf support
docs.text:
Use the same C5 plus five private leaves as Section 37, with blocks R=(0,...,4) and Q=(5,...,9). Supply offsets psi_i=psi_(5+i)=sigma*2pi*i/5, for sigma=+1 or -1. The external coefficients are

\[ q_{RQ}=Z_{RQ}=\frac13,\qquad q_{QR}=Z_{QR}=1. \]

Every receiver internal sine sum cancels between the two cycle directions; the leaves have no internal edges. Write the block forms as a,b and phases as Theta,Psi. The complete reduced rows are

\[ a'=\tfrac13\sin(\Psi-\Theta),\qquad b'=-\sin(\Psi-\Theta),\qquad \Theta'=\tfrac13(a-b),\qquad \Psi'=b-a. \]

Putting u=a-b, phi=Psi-Theta gives

\[ u'=\tfrac43\sin\phi,\qquad \phi'=-\tfrac43u,\qquad \tfrac12u^2+1-\cos\phi=\text{constant}. \]

The receiver retains its exact acute winding and internal storage V_5 while interacting with its moving environment. Its collective weighted form sum is 15a+5b; the analogous lifted phase sum has the same weights. The common regional phase motion is compensated by the environment, in accord with Section 38's global phase balance. The inherited pendulum reuses the reciprocal exchange mechanism; it is not another fundamental oscillator, frequency identification or universal permanent-pulse postulate.

docs.title: Exact compatibility is not finite-time formation into the family
docs.text:
The complete smooth field has a unique flow in both time directions. If a trajectory met this invariant family at a finite time, the unique backward solution through that point would also lie in the family. Therefore a preparation outside M_psi cannot enter it exactly at finite time under this unchanged autonomous law. In particular, globally flat phases cannot enter the displayed nonzero-twist family exactly.

This does not exclude entry into a neighborhood with nonzero width, nor finite retention of a less restrictive identity. Those require an actual entry state, declared finite error bounds and a comparison under the same complete law. The existing full-state finite-window argument illustrates that separate obligation on its own support; it is not automatically a certificate for these arbitrary partitions. No acquisition trajectory or attraction theorem is supplied by the exact classification.

docs.title: Shared admission distinguishes proof from undecided equality
docs.text:
The partition owner provides assess_sine_phase_offset_partition(source, blocks, phase_offset_turns) and SinePhaseOffsetPartition. Declared rational-turn offsets specify the phase geometry independently of a response. Its .evaluate(...) returns a SinePhaseOffsetState for admitted collective coordinates, retaining fine reconstruction, the inherited rows and storage. It does not install a coarse runtime, select a partition or certify that the source already belongs to the supplied family.

The all-real mathematical criterion is stronger than any particular finite equality recognizer. Exact cancellations admitted by the implementation, including sine oddness and angle reflection, can prove the required identities. Certified interval exclusion of zero can prove a failed equality. An unrecognized symbolic cancellation or an interval containing zero remains unavailable; it is not evidence of inequality and must not be converted into a failed mathematical criterion.

The held native joint quotient, the replica family and the independent-swap criterion retain their different models and quantifiers. This theorem concerns supplied fixed offsets and all collective states on their invariant family; it does not claim closure of arbitrary fine states, autonomous formation, support selection or physical identification.

docs.title: 39a. Weighted form and held nonuniform capacities
docs.text:
Section 39 retains its unit law and rescaled clock. The following extension uses the weighted form, bare-sine law in the original structural time t. Let the finite bare support U be connected, simple and undirected, with strictly positive symmetric conductances W_ij on every edge. Its bare degrees are d_i>0. Hold every capacity nu_i>0, conductance and edge fixed during continuous evolution; there is no forcing, continuous loss or event on that segment. The complete rows and independently specified pressure are

\[ p_i= rac1{\pi d_i}\sum_{j\sim i}\sin( heta_j- heta_i),\qquad \dot x_i= rac{ u_i}{\pi d_i} \sum_{j\sim i}\sin( heta_j- heta_i),\qquad \dot heta_i= rac{ u_i}{\pi d_i} \sum_{j\sim i}W_{ij}(x_i-x_j). \]

The sine row and degree use bare neighbors; only the form-gradient channel uses conductances. The pressure is not inferred by dividing an observed rate by capacity. These are selected constitutive premises, not a unique consequence of the nodal identity or the native neighbor-resultant law.

Supply a partition into k nonempty blocks, with 2<=k<n, and fixed circular offsets with declared real representatives psi_i. Consider the entire family M_psi of Section 39: x_i=X_a and theta_i=Theta_a+psi_i for i in B_a, with freely varying collective forms and phases. Set

\[ \kappa_i= u_i/d_i,\qquad ho_i=d_i/ u_i,\qquad A_{ib}=\kappa_i\sum_{j\in N(i)\cap B_b}W_{ij},\qquad Z_{ib}=\kappa_i\sum_{j\in N(i)\cap B_b} e^{\mathrm i(\psi_j-\psi_i)}. \]

docs.title: Necessary and sufficient conditions on the whole family
docs.text:
The complete field preserves M_psi if and only if, for each block a:

  1. Every external coefficient A_ib=A_ab, b!=a, is independent of i in B_a.
  2. Every external complex coefficient Z_ib=Z_ab, b!=a, is independent of i in B_a.
  3. Im Z_ia=0 for every i in B_a.

No equality of the internal A_ia or Re Z_ia is required. Nonuniform capacities can compensate different degrees; equality of the capacities within a block is not a premise.

To prove necessity, restriction of the fine rows gives

\[ \dot heta_i= rac1\pi\sum_{b e a}A_{ib}(X_a-X_b),\qquad \dot x_i= rac1\pi\left\{\operatorname{Im}Z_{ia} +\sum_{b e a}\operatorname{Im} [Z_{ib}e^{\mathrm i(\Theta_b-\Theta_a)}] ight\}. \]

Independent variation of the forms forces the external A coefficients to agree. Independent collective phase differences separate the sine and cosine coefficients, forcing equality of each external complex Z. The remaining internal imaginary part must be a common constant c_a. But

\[ c_a\sum_{i\in B_a} ho_i =\sum_{i\in B_a} ho_i\operatorname{Im}Z_{ia} =\sum_{\substack{i,j\in B_a\j\sim i}}\sin(\psi_j-\psi_i)=0. \]

Each internal undirected edge cancels with its reverse, and the sum of positive rho_i is nonzero, so c_a=0. Conversely, these three conditions make both rows constant within each block at every collective state. The complete smooth field is tangent to the family; uniqueness preserves it. The descended law, still in the original clock, is exactly

\[ oxed{ egin{aligned} \dot X_a&= rac1\pi\sum_{b e a}\operatorname{Im} [Z_{ab}e^{\mathrm i(\Theta_b-\Theta_a)}],\ \dot\Theta_a&= rac1\pi\sum_{b e a}A_{ab}(X_a-X_b). \end{aligned}} \]

Fine pressures need not agree within a block: when capacities differ, the products nu_i p_i can agree without equality of p_i. Failure of the criterion excludes preservation of this whole family, not every special trajectory with further coordinate constraints. As in Section 39, smooth backward uniqueness also prevents exact finite-time entry from outside under the unchanged law. Neither invariance nor its classification proves attraction, formation or robustness to transverse errors.

docs.title: Two inherited couplings, storage and lifted means
docs.text:
Define m_a=sum_(i in B_a) rho_i. For different blocks put

\[ \begin{aligned} N^W_{ab}&=\sum_{\substack{i\in B_a,j\in B_b\\j\sim i}}W_{ij} =m_aA_{ab},\\ N^0_{ab}&=|\{\{i,j\}\in U:i\in B_a,j\in B_b\}|,\\ P_{ab}&=\sum_{\substack{i\in B_a,j\in B_b\\j\sim i}} e^{\mathrm i(\psi_j-\psi_i)}=m_aZ_{ab}. \end{aligned} \]

Reversing the same cross edges gives the reciprocal identities

\[ N^W_{ab}=N^W_{ba},\qquad N^0_{ab}=N^0_{ba},\qquad P_{ab}=\overline{P_{ba}},\qquad |P_{ab}|\leq N^0_{ab}. \]

The bound uses the bare edge count, not the weighted total N^W. The inherited sine coupling and weighted form coupling are distinct data. In particular, replacing both by one coarse adjacency matrix would generally change the law.

The fine structural storage and its exact restriction are

\[ \begin{aligned} H&=\frac12\sum_{\{i,j\}\in U}W_{ij}(x_i-x_j)^2 +\sum_{\{i,j\}\in U}[1-\cos(\theta_j-\theta_i)],\\ H_{\mathcal M} &=H_{\mathrm{int}}(\psi) +\sum_{a<b}\left[\frac{N^W_{ab}}2(X_a-X_b)^2+N^0_{ab} -\operatorname{Re}(P_{ab}e^{\mathrm i(\Theta_b-\Theta_a)})\right],\\ H_{\mathrm{int}}(\psi) &=\sum_a\sum_{\substack{\{i,j\}\in U\\i,j\in B_a}} [1-\cos(\psi_j-\psi_i)]. \end{aligned} \]

Internal form storage vanishes on the family. Direct differentiation yields

\[ \dot X_a=-\frac1{\pi m_a}\frac{\partial H_{\mathcal M}}{\partial\Theta_a}, \qquad \dot\Theta_a=\frac1{\pi m_a}\frac{\partial H_{\mathcal M}}{\partial X_a}. \]

Thus H_M, sum_a m_a X_a and sum_a m_a Theta_a are conserved during held-capacity flow. This is restriction of the existing storage, not a new independently supplied energy or an identification of m_a with physical mass. To recover the full fine lifted phase mean, retain

\[ \eta_a=\frac1{m_a}\sum_{i\in B_a}\rho_i\psi_i,\qquad \mu_\theta= \frac{\sum_a m_a(\Theta_a+\eta_a)}{\sum_a m_a}. \]

The offsets contribute even though their derivatives vanish. Changing phase representatives changes a lifted mean unless the associated lift convention is changed consistently. The continuous reduction retains X, Theta, m, N^W, N^0, P and the declared offset registration; these data do not by themselves retain operator histories or admission context. This is an invariant-family law, not an all-state quotient or automatically another bare normalized-sine graph.

docs.title: Which primary capacity resets preserve the family dynamics?
docs.text:
Assume the preceding criterion holds. Consider a zero-duration primary reset that preserves forms, phases, support, conductances and structural time, with strictly positive capacities

\[ \nu_i^+=r_i\nu_i,\qquad r_i>0. \]

Every such reset preserves instantaneous membership in M_psi: its defining forms and phases did not change. The post-reset vector field preserves the entire same family if and only if the actual ratios r_i=r_a are constant within each block.

Indeed, the new external rows are A_ib^+=r_i A_ab and Z_ib^+=r_i Z_ab; the internal imaginary rows remain zero. Block-constant ratios are sufficient. For necessity, connected support and a proper partition give each block an edge to some other block b. Strictly positive conductances and original closure then give A_ab>0 for every node in that block. Equality of the new external phase coefficients r_i A_ab forces equality of all its r_i. The connected positive-support and proper-partition premises matter: one block, zero conductances or zero capacities require separate analysis and are not covered by this iff.

For an admitted block-constant reset,

\[ A_{ab}^+=r_a A_{ab},\qquad Z_{ab}^+=r_a Z_{ab},\qquad m_a^+=m_a/r_a. \]

The two rows of block a acquire the common factor r_a, whereas N^W, N^0, P and H_M are unchanged. The storage jump is exactly zero because H has no capacity term. There is a single constant clock scaling of the whole family law precisely when all block factors agree: each block has a nonzero external phase coefficient, so comparison with one common multiplier forces the same multiplier everywhere. Different block factors preserve the family while changing its relative dynamics.

Mean leaves generally change. For q_a=X_a or q_a=Theta_a, let mu_q=sum_a m_a q_a / sum_a m_a. The unchanged coordinates give

\[ \mu_q^+-\mu_q= \frac{\sum_a(m_a^+-m_a)(q_a-\mu_q)}{\sum_a m_a^+}. \]

For the full fine phase mean use q_a=Theta_a+eta_a. Block-constant ratios leave each eta_a fixed, but change its contribution to the global mean through the new block weights. Subsequent conservation uses those new weights. Zero event storage does not transfer the old mean leaves or a future trajectory certificate. These are the collective consequences of the existing form-capacity event identities.

docs.title: Weighted star: positive family and local-reset obstruction
docs.text:
Take A={0,1,2,3} and B={4}. The internal star edges 0--1, 0--2, 0--3 have weight 3; each node in A has one edge to 4 of weight 2. Choose zero offsets and

\[ d=(4,2,2,2,4),\qquad \nu=(4,2,2,2,8). \]

Then kappa_i=1 throughout A and kappa_4=2. The exact inherited data are

\[ \begin{gathered} A_{AB}=2,\quad A_{BA}=16,\quad Z_{AB}=1,\quad Z_{BA}=8,\\ m_A=4,\quad m_B=\tfrac12,\quad N^W_{AB}=8,\quad N^0_{AB}=P_{AB}=4. \end{gathered} \]

Every internal imaginary row vanishes. The internal real Z value is 3 at the center and 1 at a leaf, so requiring equality of full internal moments would reject this valid example. The center and leaves also have different degrees: this block is not an orbit requiring equal capacities under a graph automorphism.

Writing u=X_A-X_B and Delta=Theta_B-Theta_A, the original-clock rows are

\[ \dot X_A=\frac{\sin\Delta}{\pi},\quad \dot X_B=-\frac{8\sin\Delta}{\pi},\quad \dot\Theta_A=\frac{2u}{\pi},\quad \dot\Theta_B=-\frac{16u}{\pi},\qquad H_{\mathcal M}=4u^2+4(1-\cos\Delta). \]

A common capacity factor s>0 on all of A multiplies its two rows by s and changes m_A to 4/s; the rows of B remain unchanged. This preserves the family. In contrast, resetting only node 0 by s!=1 gives it external coefficients (A_0B,Z_0B)=(2s,s), while the other members retain (2,1). At u=1, Delta=pi/2, its form/phase rates are (s/pi,2s/pi), instead of (1/pi,2/pi) at the leaves. Tangency fails immediately, despite unchanged instantaneous family membership and zero event storage. This counterexample requires no numerical trajectory.

docs.title: Represented SHA, full operator context and implementation scope
docs.text:
For a mathematical common attenuation 0<s<1, the preceding primary map is compatible with SHA's capacity action. For an implemented proposal, use the ratio of the actual represented output capacity to the represented input capacity, not merely its configured factor. The shared AL/SHA proposal owner admits those outputs. Multiplication by the same binary64 factor does not in general give exactly equal rational ratios on arbitrary nonuniform capacities; a tolerance cannot prove exact family invariance.

For this star, the capacities in A are powers of two. Multiplication by the normal represented default SHA factor, approximately 0.9204225284540524, is exact for 4,2,2,2, with finite normal outputs. Therefore its actual ratios agree exactly. This is a statement about the represented factor, not exact evaluation of the real expression 1-1/(4*pi). No SHA event is executed by this analytical example.

The complete canonical operator still needs live fine-node preconditions, grammar, target order, histories, operator steps, debt and lifecycle state, as required by the event contract. SHA also writes latent/lifecycle metadata, including wall-clock metadata distinct from structural time. Fine states with the same continuous collective coordinates can have different admission contexts. The present primary-map descent therefore does not establish a complete collective SHA operator, an autonomous occurrence rule, a newly acquired history sample or future freezing of both continuous rows.

The weighted partition owner provides assess_sine_weighted_phase_offset_partition(source, blocks=..., phase_offset_turns=...), returning SineWeightedPhaseOffsetPartition; .evaluate(...) returns SineWeightedPhaseOffsetState. assess_sine_weighted_capacity_reset(partition, capacity_after=...) and .capacity_reset(...) assess actual positive represented output capacities. Consumers re-admit primitive source state and rebuild coefficients rather than trusting cached verdicts. They install no event or coarse runtime and do not claim the supplied source already lies in the declared family.

The theorem allows real offsets; the implementation admits rational-turn offsets and reuses Section 39's sound but incomplete symbolic/interval recognizer. Its certified, excluded and unavailable results distinguish proved identities, proved obstruction and undecided equality. This finite recognizer is not a complete decision procedure for the mathematical iff. The independent controls check the weighted star, the two fine/coarse channels, inherited storage and means, represented reset ratios, invalid primitive domains and rebuilding of report-derived quantities.

The unit partition owner and the support-involution owner retain their narrower domains. This extension allows arbitrary supplied blocks with capacity/degree compensation and distinct weighted/bare couplings; it does not replace their results or the native joint quotient. The star is a supplied mathematical control, not evidence that the retained formed organization has this partition, that such a family forms autonomously, or that its structural coefficients are physical observables.

docs.title: 39b. A transverse linear-stability band for the weighted star
docs.text:
Retain exactly Section 39a's five-node weighted star, zero offsets and complete conservative law, with held capacities

\[ \nu=(4s,2s,2s,2s,8),\qquad \frac{23}{25}\leq s\leq1. \]

This is a fixed band of supplied models and preparations. The parameter s is constant along each segment, not a new capacity evolution law. The question is whether all infinitesimal transverse perturbations of its collective librations remain bounded. It differs from invariance of the exactly prepared family, finite-error retention and formation.

docs.title: Full fine variation and the retained transverse directions
docs.text:
Let L be the unweighted four-node internal-star Laplacian. Along a collective solution write Delta=Theta_B-Theta_A and c=cos Delta. Use a,phi in R^4 for fine form/phase perturbations on A, and b,psi for the two perturbations on node B. Direct differentiation of both consumed rows in the original time gives the full ten-dimensional system

\[ \begin{aligned} \dot a&=-\frac{s}{\pi}[(L+cI)\phi-c\psi\mathbf1],& \dot b&=\frac{2c}{\pi}(\mathbf1^T\phi-4\psi),\\ \dot\phi&=\frac{s}{\pi}[(3L+2I)a-2b\mathbf1],& \dot\psi&=\frac4\pi(4b-\mathbf1^Ta). \end{aligned} \]

The factors 3 and 2 in the phase rows are the internal and external conductances. The form rows instead use bare sine derivatives. They cannot be obtained by replacing both channels with one weighted Laplacian.

Put bar_a=1^T a/4, bar_phi=1^T phi/4. Their rows with b,psi form the four-dimensional collective variation:

\[ \dot{\bar a}=\frac{sc}{\pi}(\psi-\bar\phi),\qquad \dot b=\frac{8c}{\pi}(\bar\phi-\psi),\qquad \dot{\bar\phi}=\frac{2s}{\pi}(\bar a-b),\qquad \dot\psi=\frac{16}{\pi}(b-\bar a). \]

The complementary subspace

\[ \mathbf1^Ta=\mathbf1^T\phi=0,\qquad b=\psi=0 \]

is invariant: the sums and the two B rows remain zero. Every perturbation splits uniquely into these collective and transverse components. The internal L eigenvalues on the zero-sum subspace are 1,1,4. The two-dimensional lambda=1 eigenspace consists of leaf contrasts with zero center component; (3,-1,-1,-1) spans the lambda=4 eigenspace. Thus all six transverse directions, including both copies of the first mode, obey independent two-dimensional systems

\[ \boxed{\quad \dot a_\lambda=-\frac{s}{\pi}(\lambda+\cos\Delta)\phi_\lambda, \qquad \dot\phi_\lambda=\frac{s}{\pi}(3\lambda+2)a_\lambda, \qquad \lambda=1,1,4. \quad} \]

This is an exact decomposition of the full variational equation. It does not discard a fine direction or replace the evolving collective state by an independently forced waveform.

docs.title: The reference libration and its declared clock
docs.text:
For u=X_A-X_B, the collective rows are

\[ \dot u=\frac{s+8}{\pi}\sin\Delta,\qquad \dot\Delta=-\frac{2(s+8)}\pi u,\qquad H_{\mathcal M}=4[u^2+1-\cos\Delta]. \]

Transform every row with the positive constant clock

\[ \tau=\frac{\sqrt2(s+8)}\pi t. \]

Primes in this subsection denote d/dtau. Then u'=sin Delta/sqrt(2), Delta'=-sqrt(2)u and Delta''+sin Delta=0. On a nonconstant libration around consensus choose the continuous lift with |Delta|<=Delta_max<pi and set

\[ k=\sin(\Delta_{\max}/2),\qquad 0<k\leq\tfrac14,\qquad u^2+1-\cos\Delta=2k^2,\qquad H_{\mathcal M}=8k^2. \]

The conserved energy gives the period directly by the substitution sin(Delta/2)=k sin v in a quarter-cycle quadrature:

\[ P(k)=4\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{dv}{\sqrt{1-k^2\sin^2v}},\qquad 2\pi\leq P(k)\leq\frac{2\pi}{\sqrt{1-k^2}}<\frac{13}{2}. \]

For the last strict bound, k<=1/4, pi<22/7 and sqrt(15)>387/100 give P<=8pi/sqrt(15)<17600/2709<13/2. The original-time period is T=P*pi/[sqrt(2)(s+8)]. No trajectory or sampled period is needed for this enclosure. The full reference period is used; no shorter coefficient period or relabeling is assumed.

Eliminating a_lambda using the constant coefficient in its phase row gives, for y=phi_lambda,

\[ y''+\alpha_\lambda(\lambda+\cos\Delta(\tau))y=0,\qquad \alpha_\lambda=\frac{s^2(3\lambda+2)}{2(s+8)^2}>0. \]

The potential is periodic because the independently derived reference librates. Its positivity alone would not prove stability: a periodic coefficient can transfer amplitude between the two tangent coordinates.

docs.title: A rigorous rotation comparison for the whole return
docs.text:
Set

\[ r_\lambda=\sqrt{\alpha_\lambda(\lambda+1)},\qquad q_\lambda(\tau)=\alpha_\lambda(\cos\Delta(\tau)-1),\qquad |q_\lambda|\leq2\alpha_\lambda k^2. \]

For z=(r_lambda y,y'), its fundamental equation is

\[ z'=(A_0+E(\tau))z,\quad A_0=\begin{pmatrix}0&r_\lambda\\-r_\lambda&0\end{pmatrix},\quad E=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\-q_\lambda/r_\lambda&0\end{pmatrix}. \]

The unperturbed fundamental matrix R(tau)=exp(A_0 tau) is orthogonal. Writing the actual fundamental matrix as R(tau)V(tau) gives V'=R^{-1}ER V, with V(0)=I. Its spectral-norm integral inequality and Gronwall's inequality imply

\[ \|V(P)-I\|_2\leq e^{B_\lambda}-1,\qquad B_\lambda=\frac{2\alpha_\lambda k^2P}{r_\lambda} =\frac{2r_\lambda k^2P}{\lambda+1}. \]

This bound retains the time ordering of the full equation; it does not replace the return by an exponential of an averaged stiffness. For its monodromy matrix M_lambda, orthogonality and |tr D|<=2||D||_2 give

\[ \boxed{\quad \left|\operatorname{tr}M_\lambda-2\cos(r_\lambda P)\right| \leq2(e^{B_\lambda}-1). \quad} \]

The generator has trace zero, so the Wronskian identity gives det M_lambda=1 exactly. Constant changes of modal coordinates and the positive clock conversion preserve this determinant and the return eigenvalues. The comparison applies to every starting phase of the same libration, since its amplitude and period bounds do not depend on that phase.

docs.title: Uniform rational margins on the fixed band
docs.text:
Monotonicity of s/(s+8) and squaring positive rational endpoints give

\[ r_1=\frac{s\sqrt5}{s+8}\in\left(\frac{23}{100},\frac14\right), \qquad r_4=\frac{s\sqrt{35}}{s+8} \in\left(\frac{61}{100},\frac{33}{50}\right). \]

Together with the fixed amplitude and period ceilings, these imply

\[ B_1<\frac{13}{128}<\frac19,\qquad B_4<\frac{429}{4000}<\frac19,\qquad e^{B_\lambda}-1\leq\frac{B_\lambda}{1-B_\lambda}<\frac18. \]

The exponential inequality follows by comparison of its power series with the geometric series for 0<=B<1. The two reference-rotation angles have elementary enclosures

\[ \frac{23\pi}{50}<r_1P<\frac{13}{8},\qquad \frac{61\pi}{50}<r_4P<\frac{429}{100}. \]

The first interval is within distance 1/5 of pi/2, using 3<pi<22/7; hence |cos(r_1P)|<1/5. The second lies strictly inside (pi,3pi/2), and its distance above pi is greater than 33/50. Monotonicity there and the alternating cosine upper bound give

\[ |\cos(r_4P)|<\cos(33/50) \leq1-\frac{(33/50)^2}{2}+\frac{(33/50)^4}{24} =\frac{118515921}{150000000}<\frac45. \]

Consequently the actual, unevaluated returns satisfy the strict bounds

\[ \boxed{\qquad |\operatorname{tr}M_1|<\frac{13}{20}<2, \qquad |\operatorname{tr}M_4|<\frac{37}{20}<2. \qquad} \]

These are uniform sufficient margins, not computed multipliers. Each real two-dimensional return has determinant one and trace strictly between -2 and 2, so its two eigenvalues are distinct conjugates of unit modulus. It is diagonalizable, and all its positive and negative integer powers are bounded. The fundamental matrix on one finite period is bounded as well, proving bounded continuous-time motion of each infinitesimal transverse mode. The repeated lambda=1 sector is a direct sum of two identical uncoupled blocks, so repetition does not introduce a linear Jordan block. All six transverse directions are covered.

The boundedness can also be made uniform on the declared band. Write d=tr M_lambda/2=cos varphi. The same comparison gives ||M_lambda||_2<9/8 and |d|<37/40. Cayley--Hamilton gives, for every integer n,

\[ M_\lambda^n=\cos(n\varphi)I +\frac{\sin(n\varphi)}{\sin\varphi}(M_\lambda-dI),\qquad \|M_\lambda^n\|_2 \leq1+\frac{9/8+37/40}{\sqrt{1-(37/40)^2}} =1+\frac{82}{\sqrt{231}}. \]

The one-period propagator has norm below 9/8 at every intervening time, so its composition with this bound controls all real times. The modal coordinate changes and their inverses are uniformly bounded on the fixed positive s band. This supplies uniform linear transverse boundedness; it does not bound nonlinear errors or the separate collective variation.

docs.title: Equilibrium, represented SHA and the boundary of the conclusion
docs.text:
At k=0, u=0 and Delta=0 modulo 2pi. This reference is stationary; it has no nonzero minimal period. The transverse equations directly reduce to y''+r_lambda^2 y=0, with r_lambda>0, so their solutions are bounded without assigning a fictitious reference period or using a limiting monodromy as measured data.

The supplied default SHA factor has the exact represented value

\[ \widehat s=\frac{518151819521135}{562949953421312},\qquad \widehat s-\frac{23}{25} =\frac{5946559338199}{14073748835532800}>0,\qquad 1-\widehat s=\frac{44798133900177}{562949953421312}>0. \]

For this star's source capacities 4,2,2,2, its represented products are exact and have the common ratio widehat s, as established in Section 39a. Thus both the original s=1 law and this hypothetical post-SHA law lie in the proved band. A capacity-only reset keeps u, Delta and H_M=8k^2, hence the libration amplitude parameter, unchanged. The new period and transverse coefficients have nevertheless been re-admitted above; they are not copied from the old law. This establishes conditional linear stability on either held-capacity segment, not execution of SHA or admissibility of its fine-node grammar and lifecycle.

Collective variations remain separate. Changing a libration's amplitude can change its period and produce tangential phase shear; common form and phase origins also belong to the collective sector. No boundedness claim for a fixed full ten-dimensional reference trajectory follows from the transverse result. Nor do unit-modulus linear multipliers establish nonlinear orbital stability: finite perturbations can couple modes, and the two equal-frequency leaf modes retain a possible nonlinear resonance. There is no attraction, finite-error retention, acquisition, autonomous formation or physical identification theorem here.

The unit moving-window estimate and the replica-pulse variation supply related methods under their own supports and complete laws. Their coefficients and verdicts were not transferred to this star. The present result follows from its full fine linearization and scalar bounds on the declared band, without a trajectory, return-matrix scan or fitted period.

The shared transverse owner exposes assess_sine_weighted_star_transverse_band, returning SineWeightedStarTransverseBand. It recomputes its period, frequency, rotation and exponential bounds from the supplied capacity interval and amplitude ceiling. Its generic outward cosine enclosure can be wider than the hand-derived rational margins above; it independently tests whether the resulting complete trace intervals lie strictly inside (-2,2). An inconclusive interval remains unavailable, not evidence of instability. At zero amplitude, positive constant oscillators supply the verdict; any reported period bound describes the nonzero-libration limit. The independent controls check the full fine/modal equations, multiplicities, scalar bounds, clock, representation and rejection boundaries without integrating a trajectory.

docs.title: 39c. Sufficient state of the weighted collective NFR and its boundary
docs.text:
Retain the same weighted star, original structural time and held capacities (4s,2s,2s,2s,8), with 23/25<=s<=1. The marked region A={0,1,2,3} is the candidate collective NFR; node B={4} remains its dynamical boundary, not an imposed waveform. Support, conductances and the complete conservative law remain supplied. No forcing, capacity evolution, event or trajectory is added. The following identities hold for any fixed s>0, without requiring the exact collective family.

Following the ontology's state and language distinction, a complete study has several responsibilities:

Responsibility Result or boundary in this model Identity and boundary Marked four-node A with distinguished center and three leaves, interacting with retained dynamical B; membership and support are supplied Continuous state and law The full internal coordinate extension below is invertible and sufficient for the specified ten-dimensional A+B dynamics Maintenance Sections 39a–39b prove exact-family invariance and the specified linear transverse band; Section 39d separately certifies finite-amplitude identity retention Canonical actions Fine histories, temporal eligibility, grammar, targets and lifecycle still require the shared event/word admission contract Occurrence and interpretation Autonomous formation, event selection and physical identification remain open

A sufficient chart is not itself a newly formed NFR. The present question is which observations retain enough information to predict the existing fine law, not whether every NFR must have this support or representation.

docs.title: Declared lifts, collective coordinates and internal state
docs.text:
Use continuous real lifts of the primitive circular phases, recording their initial representatives. Define arithmetic means on A, the single-node boundary coordinates and zero-sum internal deviations:

\[ \begin{gathered} X_A=\tfrac14\sum_{i\in A}x_i,\quad X_B=x_4,\quad \Theta_A=\tfrac14\sum_{i\in A}\theta_i,\quad\Theta_B=\theta_4,\\ \xi_i=x_i-X_A,\quad\eta_i=\theta_i-\Theta_A,\quad \sum_{i\in A}\xi_i=\sum_{i\in A}\eta_i=0,\\ u=X_A-X_B,\quad\Delta=\Theta_B-\Theta_A,\quad M=\tfrac14\sum_{i\in A}e^{\mathrm i\eta_i},\quad F=\operatorname{Im}(e^{\mathrm i\Delta}\overline M) =\tfrac14\sum_{i\in A}\sin(\Delta-\eta_i). \end{gathered} \]

Here M uses the positive internal phase exponent and has modulus at most one. Theta_A is the declared arithmetic lift mean, not arg M or an inferred primitive phase. No angle is assigned to a vanishing resultant. The lift registration makes these coordinates unambiguous even when a circular mean is unavailable.

Let L be the bare internal-star Laplacian and K=3L+2I. Its nonlinear internal sine row is

\[ G_i(\eta)=\sum_{\substack{j\sim i\\j\in A}}\sin(\eta_j-\eta_i), \qquad \sum_{i\in A}G_i=0. \]

The coefficients 3 and 2 in K come from internal and boundary conductances. They do not weight G_i or F.

docs.title: Exact nonlinear collective and internal equations
docs.text:
Summing the fine form rows cancels every internal sine pair. Summing the phase rows cancels the internal weighted form gradient. Therefore

\[ \boxed{\quad \dot X_A=\frac{s}{\pi}F,\quad \dot X_B=-\frac8\pi F,\quad \dot\Theta_A=\frac{2s}{\pi}u,\quad \dot\Theta_B=-\frac{16}{\pi}u. \quad} \]

Subtracting these means from the fine equations gives every internal row:

\[ \boxed{\quad \dot\xi_i=\frac{s}{\pi} [G_i(\eta)+\sin(\Delta-\eta_i)-F],\qquad \dot\eta=\frac{s}{\pi}K\xi. \quad} \]

Their sums vanish, so both zero-sum constraints persist. In particular,

\[ \dot u=\frac{s+8}{\pi}F,\qquad \dot\Delta=-\frac{2(s+8)}{\pi}u. \]

Section 39b's collective pendulum is recovered when xi=eta=0, hence M=1 and F=sin Delta. Away from that family the same complete law supplies the correction; the boundary node and its reaction remain part of the state.

Differentiating the internal moment exposes the next information need:

\[ \boxed{\quad \dot M=\frac{\mathrm i s}{4\pi} \sum_{i\in A}e^{\mathrm i\eta_i}(K\xi)_i. \quad} \]

Since sum_i(K xi)_i=0, the exponential can equivalently be replaced by exp(i eta_i)-M in that sum. The derivative consumes a mixed internal form/phase moment, including which form belongs to which phase and internal edge. An unassociated phase distribution or form norm does not retain that information.

The independently specified fine pressures are

\[ p_i=\frac{G_i(\eta)+\sin(\Delta-\eta_i)}{\pi d_i} \quad(i\in A),\qquad p_B=-\frac{F}{\pi}. \]

Consequently the aggregate form row preserves the nodal identity:

\[ \dot X_A=\tfrac14\sum_{i\in A}\nu_i p_i=\frac{sF}{\pi}, \qquad \dot X_B=8p_B. \]

An average of nodal products is generally not the product of average capacity and average pressure. For coarse nodal notation, one consistent declared normalization is nu_A=s, nu_B=8, P_A=F/pi, P_B=-F/pi. These pressures are defined from the fine constitutive map before evaluating a response. This choice neither selects a unique collective capacity nor removes the internal state needed to evolve F; it is not pressure reconstructed from a measured derivative.

docs.title: Storage, conserved means and lift covariance
docs.text:
The full fine storage becomes

\[ \begin{aligned} H&=4u^2+\tfrac12\xi^TK\xi+V_{\mathrm{int}}(\eta) +4[1-\operatorname{Re}(e^{\mathrm i\Delta}\overline M)],\\ V_{\mathrm{int}}(\eta) &=\sum_{\substack{\{i,j\}\in U\\i,j\in A}} [1-\cos(\eta_j-\eta_i)]. \end{aligned} \]

Expanding the four weighted cross-edge form differences uses sum_i(u+xi_i)^2=4u^2+sum_i xi_i^2. The phase storage retains the full complex moment. Both H and the weighted sums

\[ Q_x=\frac4sX_A+\frac12X_B,\qquad Q_\theta=\frac4s\Theta_A+\frac12\Theta_B \]

are conserved. Dividing by 4/s+1/2 gives the full fine normalized means. No internal term is omitted: the fine inverse-capacity weights are 1/s throughout A and both internal deviations have zero sum.

For comparison let H_col=4[u^2+1-cos Delta]. Its exact off-family remainder and exchange are

\[ \begin{aligned} R&=H-H_{\mathrm{col}} =\tfrac12\xi^TK\xi+V_{\mathrm{int}}(\eta) +4[\cos\Delta-\operatorname{Re}(e^{\mathrm i\Delta}\overline M)],\\ \dot H_{\mathrm{col}} &=\frac{8(s+8)}{\pi}u(F-\sin\Delta),\qquad \dot R=-\dot H_{\mathrm{col}}. \end{aligned} \]

This is exchange between a chosen collective observation and its internal remainder, without an added reservoir or changed total storage. Neither R>=0 nor conservation of H_col holds in general. In particular, H/8 is the squared libration amplitude parameter only on the exact family; it does not identify an off-family amplitude or supply Section 39b's reference orbit.

For integer changes of lift theta_i -> theta_i+2pi n_i, with bar_n=sum_(i in A) n_i/4 and boundary integer n_B, one obtains

\[ \begin{gathered} \Theta_A^+=\Theta_A+2\pi\bar n,\quad \eta_i^+=\eta_i+2\pi(n_i-\bar n),\quad M^+=e^{-2\pi\mathrm i\bar n}M,\\ \Delta^+=\Delta+2\pi(n_B-\bar n). \end{gathered} \]

Thus exp(i Delta) conj(M), fine pressures and rates, and full H are unchanged. The registered lifted mean instead changes by 2pi[(sum_A n_i)/s+n_B/2]/(4/s+1/2). The observation H_col and its remainder can change too. For example, let every form and physical phase be zero, but use theta_0=2pi and every other phase lift zero. Then H=0, Theta_A=pi/2, Delta=-pi/2, M=-i, H_col=4 and R=-4. A globally nonnegative remainder claim would be false even for this physical equilibrium. Positivity needs an independently admitted phase chart and its convexity premises.

docs.title: Matched means and full storage do not determine collective response
docs.text:
For an autonomous first-order law on a proposed observation Y=O(z), DO(z)f(z) must agree for every fine state with the same Y. This is the continuous part of the shared descent criterion. The following comparisons keep support, law, capacities, clock and lift convention fixed; equality of their observations is exact.

Set all forms and both collective phase means to zero. For 0<a<pi/2, compare

\[ \xi=0,\qquad \eta^\pm=\pm a(3,-1,-1,-1). \]

Both states have the same four collective coordinates, conserved fine means and full storage

\[ H^\pm=3(1-\cos4a)+(1-\cos3a)+3(1-\cos a). \]

But the triple-angle identities give

\[ M_\pm=\cos^3a\mp\mathrm i\sin^3a,\quad F_\pm=\pm\sin^3a,\quad \dot X_A^\pm=\pm\frac{s}{\pi}\sin^3a,\quad \dot X_B^\pm=\mp\frac8\pi\sin^3a. \]

The proposed state (X_A,X_B,Theta_A,Theta_B,H) has two different derivatives at the same value. No single-valued autonomous first-order vector field on that observation represents all these fine states. As a approaches zero the witnesses approach the exact consensus family; this is not a large-amplitude exception.

docs.title: Adding the complex moment and storage still does not close
docs.text:
Let e=(0,1,-1,0), so L e=e and K e=5e. For a,b>0 with a<=pi/2 prepare

\[ X_A=X_B=\Theta_A=0,\quad\Theta_B=\delta,\qquad \eta=ae,\quad\xi^\pm=\pm be . \]

The phase vector is identical in both states. Their moment and full storage are

\[ M=\frac{1+\cos a}{2},\qquad H^\pm=5b^2+2(1-\cos a)+4-2(1+\cos a)\cos\delta . \]

Thus collective coordinates, both components of M, full H, conserved means and all instantaneous collective rates agree. The exact mixed moment nevertheless gives

\[ \boxed{\qquad \dot M_\pm=\mp\frac{5sb}{2\pi}\sin a\ne0.\qquad} \]

The augmented observation (X_A,X_B,Theta_A,Theta_B,Re M,Im M,H) also fails projectability. With delta=0 and a,b tending to zero, both states approach the same equilibrium family while their derivative contrast remains nonzero for every positive parameter choice. The distinction is internal form/phase association, not a different law, operator or environment.

These instantaneous comparisons exclude the two named reduced states. They do not measure accumulated future separation, show that every finite moment hierarchy fails, or identify a minimal sufficient state. Linear transverse boundedness does not erase the missing information.

docs.title: An invertible sufficient extension and its symmetries
docs.text:
Retain the four collective coordinates and every xi_i,eta_i subject to the two zero-sum constraints. The inverse is explicit:

\[ x_i=X_A+\xi_i,\quad\theta_i=\Theta_A+\eta_i\quad(i\in A), \qquad x_4=X_B,\quad\theta_4=\Theta_B. \]

There are four collective and six independent internal coordinates, exactly the original ten continuous degrees of freedom in the declared lift chart. The equations above are closed and reconstruct both fine rows, pressures and storage. This is a sufficient organization of the complete state, not dimension reduction or a minimality proof. Retaining the dynamical B is essential; this extension does not make A autonomous.

The continuous law respects a common form translation, a common phase rotation and simultaneous permutations of the three identical leaves. The center and boundary remain distinguished. A leaf-label quotient must keep the joint form/phase pairing and edge/target associations consumed by the intended observations or actions. Permuting forms independently of phases is not that symmetry. Common origins may be discarded for an admitted relative-flow question; actions consuming absolute form or marked constituents need their own descent proof.

The obstructions identify information lost by smaller observations. One can retain more state as above, or derive a causal memory description with its hidden initialization and boundary premises. No memory kernel is supplied by the witnesses, and a stored operator history cannot replace it. This is the ontology's distinction between dynamical memory and execution history, not evidence that the fine law needs a new force or operator.

Continuous sufficiency likewise supplies no measured temporal eligibility, grammar debt, glyph history, lifecycle state, target marks, stored-pressure provenance or configuration consumed by canonical actions. The ordered-word admission contract must hold for the selected actions and reachable successors. This state analysis executes none and selects no autonomous event. Continuous sufficiency alone proves no nonlinear stability or finite-error retention; Section 39d supplies a separate identity certificate. Neither proves formation or physical identification.

docs.title: Shared observation and reconstruction
docs.text: The weighted-state owner provides assess_sine_weighted_star_state and reconstruct_sine_weighted_star_state. Exact rational-turn phase lifts retain registration; the equations above use radians and original-time rates. Reconstruction enforces zero-sum constraints rather than projecting incompatible supplied state. The independent controls compare fine and collective/internal equations, storage, lift covariance and both matched-state obstructions. These are detached computations without a trajectory, operator event or replay of frozen evidence.

docs.title: 39d. All-time retention of a declared finite-width internal identity
docs.text:
The complete state of Section 39c permits a separate nonlinear geometric question. Retain the same positive weighted support, conservative weighted-form/bare-sine law, original clock and strictly positive held capacities. Declare the following identity of the marked four-node region A:

\[ |x_0-x_j|<\tfrac12,\qquad d_{\mathbb S^1}(\theta_0,\theta_j)<\tfrac\pi2, \qquad j=1,2,3. \]

The phase distance is the absolute principal circular difference. These tolerances are a supplied identity policy for this mathematical organization, not universal NFR constants or a replacement for other identity definitions. The boundary node B remains dynamical and contributes to the full storage. Internal storage alone is not the certificate.

docs.title: The exact form barrier uses the whole weighted network
docs.text:
Fix one center-to-leaf form difference a=x_0-x_1. Common translation allows x_1=0, x_0=a when minimizing the nonnegative form storage

\[ H_x=\tfrac12\sum_{\{i,j\}\in U}W_{ij}(x_i-x_j)^2. \]

The free-coordinate quadratic is strictly convex. Its unique minimizer has equal other-leaf forms x_2=x_3=v and boundary form x_4=w. The stationary equations are

\[ 5v=3a+2w,\qquad 4w=a+2v, \qquad v=\tfrac78a,\quad w=\tfrac{11}{16}a. \]

The weighted gradient at node 0 at this minimizer is

\[ 3a+6(a-v)+2(a-w)=\tfrac{35}{8}a. \]

Equivalently the effective conductance between the fixed terminals is 35/8. Substitution into the quadratic gives the exact constrained minimum and, by leaf symmetry, the inequality for every internal arm:

\[ \min H_x=\frac{35}{16}a^2,\qquad H\geq H_x\geq\frac{35}{16}(x_0-x_j)^2 \quad(j=1,2,3). \]

Reaching |x_0-x_j|=1/2 therefore costs at least 35/64 in full storage. This improves on keeping only the weight-three internal edge, because the remaining positive support also constrains the contrast.

For the phase condition, one offending bare edge contributes

\[ d_{\mathbb S^1}(\theta_0,\theta_j)\geq\tfrac\pi2 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad 1-\cos(\theta_j-\theta_0)\geq1. \]

All other terms in H are nonnegative. This phase lower bound alone exceeds the form barrier; it need not be the sharp constrained phase minimum.

docs.title: Strict full-storage admission gives all-time identity retention
docs.text:
Consequently

\[ \boxed{\qquad H<\frac{35}{64}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad |x_0-x_j|<\frac12,\quad d_{\mathbb S^1}(\theta_0,\theta_j)<\frac\pi2 \quad(j=1,2,3).\qquad} \]

The phase conclusion actually holds on every bare edge because 35/64<1. The form bound can be read quantitatively as |x_0-x_j|<=4 sqrt(H/35). The full fine field in continuous lifts is globally Lipschitz: its form row is a finite sine sum and its phase row is linear in form, with fixed finite coefficients. Solutions exist uniquely for all real times and conserve H. The displayed implication therefore holds for all time from any admitted state, including finite internal and boundary deviations from the exact collective family. No linearization, sampled endpoint or phase-chart assumption is needed.

The strict inequality matters. With equal phases and (x_0,x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4)=(1/2,0,7/16,7/16,11/32), one has exactly H=35/64 and an internal form difference on the excluded boundary. Thus this is the exact minimum storage outside the declared strict identity. It is a sufficient all-time certificate, not a claim that states with greater storage lose identity or ever reach its boundary. An unresolved numerical storage enclosure likewise cannot certify loss.

This is retention, not acquisition: the same inequality already places the initial state inside the identity, and its conservation applies in both time directions. It does not say that a preparation lacking the identity evolves into it.

docs.title: An explicit open neighborhood of the entire coherent band
docs.text:
Every exact collective reference in Section 39b's band has H_*=8k^2<=1/2, leaving the positive gap 3/64 to the barrier. The neighborhood need not be restricted to an internal mode or to a fixed collective phase. A uniform bound follows from the squared-norm representation

\[ H=\|\mathcal V(x,\theta)\|_2^2,\qquad \mathcal V= \left( \left(\sqrt{W_{ij}/2}(x_i-x_j)\right)_{\{i,j\}\in U}, \left(\sqrt2\sin((\theta_j-\theta_i)/2)\right)_{\{i,j\}\in U} \right). \]

Keep the edge orientations and phase lifts fixed when comparing a reference and its perturbation. If every one of the five form errors has magnitude at most epsilon_x and every lifted phase error at most epsilon_theta radians, the global sine Lipschitz bound gives

\[ \|\mathcal V-\mathcal V_*\|_2^2 \leq34\epsilon_x^2+14\epsilon_\theta^2,\qquad \sqrt H\leq\sqrt{H_*} +\sqrt{34\epsilon_x^2+14\epsilon_\theta^2}. \]

The constants use sum_e W_e=17 and seven bare edges: each edge difference error is at most twice the corresponding nodal error. This retains both fine channels and the boundary perturbations.

For epsilon_x=1/256 in the declared form units and epsilon_theta=1/256 radians, any reference with H_*<=1/2 satisfies

\[ H\leq\left(\frac1{\sqrt2}+\frac{\sqrt3}{64}\right)^2 =\frac12+\frac{\sqrt6}{64}+\frac3{4096} <\frac{2211}{4096} <\frac{2240}{4096}=\frac{35}{64}. \]

The strict rational comparison uses sqrt(6)<5/2 and leaves a storage margin greater than 29/4096. In exact-turn coordinates, nodal phase errors at most 1/2048 turn are sufficient, since 2pi/2048<1/256 radians. The box includes all ten fine form/phase coordinates and has nonempty interior around every reference in the coherent band. In fact the same estimate applies to any full reference with H_*<=1/2, whether or not it belongs to the exact family.

Every state in these boxes retains the declared internal identity for all time under its admitted complete law. Its internal motion, collective amplitude and accumulated phase can differ from those of the reference. This proves finite-amplitude geometric retention, not nonlinear tracking of a chosen periodic orbit, attraction or convergence.

docs.title: Capacity-only changes and the execution boundary
docs.text:
Storage contains no capacity term. A hypothetical capacity-only reset preserving forms, phases, support and conductances therefore preserves H and this certificate. Each resulting well-defined segment with strictly positive held capacities and the same conservative rows again retains the identity. Exact-family preservation is a different condition: Section 39a requires block-constant actual capacity ratios, whereas this storage argument also covers a singleton reset that breaks that family. The structural geometry can remain bounded while its internal motion ceases to be a synchronized collective waveform.

This statement neither executes SHA nor bypasses its represented output, live grammar, target and lifecycle requirements. Other operator maps can change forms, phases or support and must account for their own storage jumps. No previous trajectory certificate is transferred through an unspecified event.

The shared weighted-state owner provides assess_sine_weighted_star_retention(state) and SineWeightedStarRetention. It rebuilds the complete primitive state and full storage before comparing its upper enclosure strictly with 35/64. This reader retains its declared capacity family (4s,2s,2s,2s,8); applying the broader capacity-reset corollary requires independent admission of the actual successor's complete law. The independent controls cover the form minimizer, strict boundary, stored-report rebuilding and capacity independence. The result complements the sufficient state and linear band: it supplies the declared finite-width identity guarantee, without proving autonomous formation or physical identification.

docs.title: 39e. Composition of maintained identities with a dynamic boundary bridge
docs.text: Two individually maintained regions need not inherit their isolated certificates after contact. This section supplies one exact composition law, accounts for its support work and proves a nonempty preparation domain with nonzero exchange and retention of both declared identities. It retains all constituent and boundary state; it does not infer a new autonomous organization from contact.

docs.title: Joined support, complete state and actual normalization
docs.text:
Take two copies r=1,2 of Section 39c's five-node weighted star, both with held scale s=1. Each has its marked center, three leaves and dynamic boundary B_r. Keep every original weight and capacity and supply one undirected boundary edge {B_1,B_2} of conductance one. The joined graph has ten nodes, fifteen bare edges and total conductance 35. Its capacities are two copies of (4,2,2,2,8), but its bare degrees are two copies of (4,2,2,2,5).

On this actual support the complete conservative law is

\[ S_i=\sum_{j\sim i}\sin(\theta_j-\theta_i),\quad q_i=(L_Wx)_i,\quad p_i=\frac{S_i}{\pi d_i},\qquad \dot x_i=\nu_i p_i,\quad \dot\theta_i=\frac{\nu_i}{\pi d_i}q_i . \]

Use original structural time t and registered continuous phase lifts. Capacity is held positive; there is no forcing, loss or further support event. The bridge is bare phase support as well as weighted form support. In particular, reducing a hypothetical conductance would not remove its sine term or undo the degree change. This result concerns the declared unit bridge, without a weak-contact limit.

For each copy retain the complete chart (X_Ar,X_Br,Theta_Ar,Theta_Br,xi_r,eta_r) from Section 39c, with both internal deviations summing to zero. Define

\[ \begin{gathered} u_r=X_{Ar}-X_{Br},\quad \Delta_r=\Theta_{Br}-\Theta_{Ar},\quad M_r=\tfrac14\sum_{i\in A_r}e^{\mathrm i\eta_{ri}},\quad F_r=\operatorname{Im}(e^{\mathrm i\Delta_r}\overline M_r),\\ f=X_{B1}-X_{B2},\quad \delta=\Theta_{B2}-\Theta_{B1},\qquad \sigma_1=1,\quad\sigma_2=-1 . \end{gathered} \]

The two charts have twenty independent real coordinates in the chosen lifts. The displayed f,delta,u_r,Delta_r,M_r,F_r are functions of that state, not extra independent coordinates or a substitute for the internal form/phase associations.

The four A_r nodes have their old degrees and mobility one. Therefore their mean and internal rows remain

\[ \begin{aligned} \dot X_{Ar}&=F_r/\pi,&\qquad \dot\Theta_{Ar}&=2u_r/\pi,\\ \dot\xi_{ri} &=[G_i(\eta_r)+\sin(\Delta_r-\eta_{ri})-F_r]/\pi,& \dot\eta_r&=K\xi_r/\pi , \end{aligned} \]

with the same G and K=3L+2I as before. The boundary mobility is now 8/5, so its independent pressure and two rows are

\[ \boxed{\quad p_{Br}=\frac{-4F_r+\sigma_r\sin\delta}{5\pi},\qquad \dot X_{Br}=\frac8{5\pi}[-4F_r+\sigma_r\sin\delta],\qquad \dot\Theta_{Br}=\frac8{5\pi}[-8u_r+\sigma_r f]. \quad} \]

Both rows must change together. Reusing the old d_B=4 normalization and simply adding a bridge current would be a different law. Useful consequences of the actual rows are

\[ \begin{aligned} \dot u_r&=\frac{37F_r-8\sigma_r\sin\delta}{5\pi},& \dot\Delta_r&=\frac{-74u_r+8\sigma_r f}{5\pi},\\ \dot f&=\frac{32(F_2-F_1)+16\sin\delta}{5\pi},& \dot\delta&=\frac{64(u_1-u_2)-16f}{5\pi}. \end{aligned} \]

These equations with the internal rows are a sufficient exact chart of the joined fine law. They neither discard the two dynamic boundaries nor close on the displayed collective variables alone.

docs.title: Insertion work, component supply and conserved joint storage
docs.text:
Let H_r be the full five-node storage of copy r, including its four original boundary edges. At the same primitive forms and phases, the joined storage is exactly

\[ \boxed{\qquad H_{\mathrm{join}}=H_1+H_2+E_b,\qquad E_b=\tfrac12f^2+1-\cos\delta . \qquad} \]

Thus E_b>=0 is the support-insertion storage work for this supplied comparison. The degree changes do not add a term to storage, but they do change its subsequent field. No unrecorded loss or reservoir pays this work, and this comparison is not a runtime operator event.

For any complete joined state, \(\partial H_{\mathrm{join}}/\partial x_i=q_i\) and \(\partial H_{\mathrm{join}}/\partial\theta_i=-S_i\). Consequently the derivative cancels separately at each node:

\[ \dot H_{\mathrm{join}} =\sum_i\frac{\nu_i}{\pi d_i}(q_iS_i-S_iq_i)=0 . \]

The individual H_r are generally not conserved. At their boundary their own gradients are q_{Br}^{(r)}=-8u_r and S_{Br}^{(r)}=-4F_r. Internal cancellation still holds with the actual boundary mobility; the bridge supplies the remaining terms:

\[ \boxed{\qquad \dot H_r=\frac{8\sigma_r}{5\pi} [-8u_r\sin\delta+4F_rf]. \qquad} \]

This is a full-storage supply balance, not just a form-channel balance. The bridge storage has derivative

\[ \dot E_b =f\dot f+\sin\delta\,\dot\delta =\frac{32f(F_2-F_1)+64(u_1-u_2)\sin\delta}{5\pi} =-\dot H_1-\dot H_2 . \]

The two supplies need not be negatives of one another: the bridge can temporarily store the difference. The original isolated certificates therefore cannot be applied as if H_1 and H_2 remained invariant.

The actual inverse-capacity weights d_i/nu_i are one on each A_r node and 5/8 at each boundary. With

\[ Q_{xr}=4X_{Ar}+\tfrac58X_{Br},\qquad Q_{\theta r}=4\Theta_{Ar}+\tfrac58\Theta_{Br}, \]

their two exchange channels are

\[ \dot Q_{xr}=\frac{\sigma_r}{\pi}\sin\delta,\qquad \dot Q_{\theta r}=\frac{\sigma_r}{\pi}f . \]

Both joined sums Q_x1+Q_x2 and Q_theta1+Q_theta2 are conserved; division by the total weight 37/4 gives the normalized fine means. The phase mean retains its declared lift registration. The former isolated boundary weight 1/2 does not transfer through the support change.

docs.title: The exact joint identity sublevel
docs.text:
Declare both copies' three center-leaf form and circular phase inequalities from Section 39d. This is the conjunction of six internal arm identities; it adds no condition on the bridge itself. Nonnegative storage gives, for each copy and each of its leaves,

\[ H_{\mathrm{join}}\geq H_r \geq \frac{35}{16}(x_{r0}-x_{rj})^2,\qquad j=1,2,3 . \]

Any internal phase gap at least pi/2 also contributes at least one to the joined storage. Hence

\[ \boxed{\qquad H_{\mathrm{join}}<\frac{35}{64} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \text{both declared internal identities persist for all real time}. \qquad} \]

As before the complete lifted field is globally Lipschitz, so the conserved storage and pointwise inclusion give a global result. The phase bound additionally keeps every bare edge, including the bridge, strictly within a circular gap of pi/2. Quantitatively every internal form gap is at most 4 sqrt(H_join/35).

The joint threshold remains sharp despite adding support. Take the first copy's forms as (1/2,0,7/16,7/16,11/32), all five forms of the second copy equal to 11/32 and every phase equal. Then the bridge and second copy have zero storage, while the first copy reaches one form boundary with exactly H_join=35/64. This establishes the minimum storage outside the joint strict identity. It does not say that greater storage causes escape or that every identity-retaining state must pass this sufficient certificate.

docs.title: A strict source with exchange and a full twenty-coordinate neighborhood
docs.text:
At the reference preparation, both copies have all four A forms equal to 1/16 and their boundary forms zero. All phases in copy one are zero, and all phases in copy two are pi/8, namely 1/16 turn. Thus

\[ u_1=u_2=\tfrac1{16},\quad f=0,\quad \Delta_1=\Delta_2=0,\quad F_1=F_2=0,\quad \delta=\tfrac\pi8,\qquad H_1=H_2=\tfrac1{64}. \]

The source storage and initial supply are

\[ \begin{gathered} H_*=\tfrac1{32}+1-\cos(\pi/8)<\tfrac18<\tfrac{35}{64},\\ \dot H_1=-\frac4{5\pi}\sin(\pi/8)<0,\qquad \dot H_2=\frac4{5\pi}\sin(\pi/8)>0,\qquad \dot E_b=0 . \end{gathered} \]

For the first strict inequality use 1-cos z<=z^2/2 and pi^2<12. The zero instantaneous bridge-storage derivative does not eliminate its nonzero sine current or the transfer between component storages.

The witness is not confined to exact internal coherence. Perturb every one of the ten forms by at most epsilon_x and every one of the ten phase lifts by at most epsilon_theta radians. Section 39d's edge-norm representation on the joined support yields

\[ \sqrt{H_{\mathrm{join}}} \leq\sqrt{H_*} +\sqrt{70\epsilon_x^2+30\epsilon_\theta^2}. \]

The constants are twice the total conductance 35 and twice the fifteen bare-edge count, respectively. For both errors at most 1/256, sqrt(H_*)<3/8 gives the strict rational bound

\[ H_{\mathrm{join}}< \left(\frac38+\frac5{128}\right)^2 =\frac{2809}{16384} <\frac{8960}{16384}=\frac{35}{64}. \]

The same box preserves the initial supply signs without a trajectory. For both copies,

\[ u_r\geq\tfrac7{128},\qquad |F_r|\leq\tfrac1{128},\qquad |f|\leq\tfrac1{128},\qquad |\delta-\pi/8|\leq\tfrac1{128}. \]

The contact-sine bound follows from its four initially zero differences and |sin z|<=|z|. For the bridge, 47/128<delta<pi/2. Monotonicity of sine and its elementary lower bound on this interval give

\[ \sin\delta>\sin(47/128) \geq \frac{47}{128}-\frac16\left(\frac{47}{128}\right)^3 >\frac13 . \]

Consequently each component's bracket satisfies

\[ -8u_r\sin\delta+4F_rf <-\frac7{48}+\frac1{4096}<-\frac18, \qquad \dot H_1<-\frac1{5\pi},\quad \dot H_2>\frac1{5\pi}. \]

All twenty coordinates can vary independently in the interior of this box. Phase errors at most 1/2048 turn suffice for the radian bound. Every such initial state has nonzero exchange and retains both identities for all time under the joined law. The supply signs are initial-time conclusions; neither their future persistence nor monotonic component-storage transfer is asserted.

docs.title: Individually certified does not imply jointly certified
docs.text:
Keep the same forms and coherent phase within each copy, but shift the entire second copy by pi/2 instead. Both isolated source storages remain 1/64, and both internal identities are initially present. The supplied bridge adds one, giving

\[ H_{\mathrm{join}}=\tfrac1{32}+1=\tfrac{33}{32} >\tfrac{35}{64}. \]

The individual old-law certificates pass while the sufficient joint storage certificate is unavailable. In this particular control, the internal rows give an independent exact answer: xi_r=eta_r=0 is invariant for each copy, since G=0, F_r=sin Delta_r and K xi_r=0. Every center-leaf form and phase difference therefore stays zero for all time, whatever the retained boundary motion. Thus the joint storage certificate is demonstrably sufficient but not necessary for retention. Its unavailability is not identity loss or a solver failure. The storage comparison isolates the additional joint preparation and support-work obligation of this particular certificate.

docs.title: Shared assessment and canonical boundary
docs.text:
The contact owner provides assess_sine_weighted_star_contact(left,right) and SineWeightedStarContact. It re-admits both full source states at exact scale one, reconstructs the joined field and pressure from the new support, and independently checks them against the sufficient charts. The old source rate fields stay associated with their isolated laws. Joined storage, supplies, means and the strict identity bound belong to the new law. The independent controls cover the fine chain rule, degree change, insertion work, strict barrier and unavailable control.

This establishes compatibility of maintained identities with nonzero exchange on a supplied complete support. It does not establish autonomous bridge formation, a larger NFR identity, attraction or physical identification. An actual UM or another canonical event must separately admit its targets, grammar, live configuration, history and complete output, following the collective action contract and event owner. An event producing different capacities, conductances or support must re-admit that successor law; neither this detached bridge nor the old isolated certificates can substitute for those premises.

docs.title: 40. A finite-width window around compatible moving geometry
docs.text: Section 39's exact family is not an acquisition target that can be entered from outside at finite time. A neighborhood with nonzero width has a different obligation: errors in both the receiver and its environment must remain controlled while the reference moves. The following sufficient certificate uses the actual storage and complete conservative field. It proves finite retention for an independently supplied entry neighborhood; it does not produce that neighborhood from an earlier preparation.

docs.title: Reference motion, error chart and declared duration
docs.text:
Retain the C5 with five private leaves, unit capacities, e=0, w=beta=1, no input or events, and tau=t/pi. Use Section 39's certified two-block family with receiver winding sigma=+1 or -1, matching receiver/leaf phase offsets and alpha=2pi/5. Reference block forms are a,b, their phases are Theta,Psi, and

\[ u=a-b,\qquad \phi=\Psi-\Theta,\qquad h=\tfrac12u^2+1-\cos\phi. \]

The inherited pendulum preserves h and satisfies |phi'|<=4sqrt(2h)/3. Choose a radian contact envelope 0<Gamma<pi/2, with |phi(0)|<Gamma and h<1-cos(Gamma). Energy and continuity then keep the reference contact phase in (-Gamma,Gamma) for all positive and negative times. This includes the zero-pulse reference; a nonzero pulse is not required.

Fix a finite duration T>0 in tau and two radian error radii:

\[ 0<\rho_R<\frac\pi{10},\qquad 0<\rho_C<\frac\pi2-\Gamma. \]

Set kappa_R=cos(alpha+rho_R)>0 and kappa_C=cos(Gamma+rho_C)>0. The internal receiver and contact errors use different margins. Contact convexity is a sufficient premise of this certificate, not a defining property of a regional identity. Exact compatible families can also move through nonacute contacts; this estimate does not assess their transverse robustness.

For an actual full solution and the reference, use continuously matched phase lifts. On oriented edge i->j, write f_e=x_i-x_j, delta_e=theta_j-theta_i, xi_e=f_e-f_e^* and eta_e=delta_e-delta_e^*. Admit the initial chart separately: |eta_e(0)|<rho_R on receiver edges and <rho_C on contacts. A small scalar storage value alone does not establish these phase-chart premises.

docs.title: The moving-reference relative-storage identity
docs.text:
For U(delta)=1-cos(delta), define

\[ D=\frac12\sum_e\xi_e^2 +\sum_e\left[U(\delta_e^*+\eta_e)-U(\delta_e^*) -\sin(\delta_e^*)\eta_e\right]. \]

This is the Bregman remainder of the existing full storage, not another physical energy or a new evolution rule. The complete field has the constant reciprocal matrix with blocks 0,-K;K,0. Differentiating the remainder along both actual solutions cancels the quadratic form terms and gives exactly

\[ \boxed{D' =\sum_e(\delta_e^*)' [\sin(\delta_e^*+\eta_e)-\sin(\delta_e^*) -\cos(\delta_e^*)\eta_e].} \]

Internal reference gaps are fixed at sigma*alpha; only the five contacts contribute, each with reference gap phi. While the admitted chart holds, convexity and Taylor's remainder imply

\[ D\ge\frac12\sum_e\xi_e^2 +\frac{\kappa_R}2\sum_{e\in R}\eta_e^2 +\frac{\kappa_C}2\sum_{e\in C}\eta_e^2, \qquad |D'|\le\frac{|\phi'|}{\kappa_C}D\le\lambda D, \]

where

\[ \lambda=\frac{4\sqrt{2h}}{3\kappa_C},\qquad d_* =\frac12\min\{\kappa_R\rho_R^2,\kappa_C\rho_C^2\}. \]

Thus a proved initial upper bound D(0)<=D_0, together with the initial chart and the prospective strict inequality

\[ \boxed{D_0e^{\lambda T}<d_*} \]

retains the complete error chart for every |tau|<=T. Indeed a first chart exit would require D>=d_*, contradicting the integrated bound. This is a full-interval proof, not a claim inferred from sampled endpoints.

For independent initial nodal form/phase error radii r_i,p_i>=0, the shared sufficient initial bound is

\[ D_0=\frac12\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E} [(r_i+r_j)^2+(p_i+p_j)^2]. \]

The same component sums must pass the separate initial edge-chart tests. During the window, every edge form error is at most sqrt(2D_max); receiver and contact phase errors are at most sqrt(2D_max/kappa_R) and sqrt(2D_max/kappa_C), respectively, where D_max=D_0 exp(lambda T). Initial weighted form/phase mean errors remain their conserved values. Retaining those origins with the edge bounds controls the relative full state on this connected support; no hidden environmental coordinate has been replaced by an imposed boundary drive.

docs.title: Internal identity and actual work remain compatible
docs.text:
The reference receiver has uniform form and equal oriented principal gaps sigma*alpha. Its internal linear phase term cancels because sum_(e in R) eta_e=0. The receiver's contribution to D is therefore exactly E_R-V_5. Nonnegative contact contributions give

\[ 0\le E_R-V_5\le D\le D_{\max}. \]

The receiver retains acute winding sigma throughout the window, with bounded internal form as well as phase. The environment continues its own nodal motion. The regional work identity still determines its actual net work; zero work for the exact reference does not imply zero work for every nearby trajectory.
