In the separate composition-compatible family the coefficient of the first harmonic is \(1-3\epsilon/2\), which is nonzero throughout its admitted interval; each of its other four coefficients is nonzero exactly when \(\epsilon\ne0\). Its \(\epsilon=0\) member also needs two coordinates. These families retain their own support, law and source hypotheses. The coordinate count transfers neither acquisition nor capture certificates, and introduces no alternative preparation into the frozen record protocol.

Storage and units. If the supplied unscaled periodic potential obeys \(U'=j\), with \(U(0)=0\), the same moments and separately retained degree also recover its instantaneous incident sum:

\[ \sum_a U(\delta_a-\varphi) =d\sum_{n\in\mathcal N}\frac{b_n}{n} -\sum_{n\in\mathcal N}\frac{b_n}{n} \operatorname{Re}\!\left(e^{-\mathrm i n\varphi}Z_n(A)\right). \]

Thus requesting this potential sum as well does not increase the minimum when the current queries remain required. This algebraic primitive does not establish nonnegative storage, a whole-network balance or a physical energy. Declared dimensional current, pressure and storage scales remain separate; the moment coordinates are dimensionless and supply no laboratory unit or structural-to-laboratory clock bridge.

Limits of the conclusion. A known single query permits the scalar summary \(J_A(\varphi_0)\); a query-independent summary valid for every angle is the different obligation proved here. The lower bound is uniform over arbitrary finite degrees. It does not assert six independent local phase directions at a degree-four node, or the same minimum on a restricted preparation family. Discontinuous encodings, nonsmooth decoders, unknown law parameters, approximate responses and noise tolerance are outside the theorem. In particular, an arbitrarily small nonzero harmonic still counts for exact representation; this says nothing about its experimental resolvability.

Minimum dimension alone does not select a fundamental law. Even the single-harmonic laws \(j(\delta)=\sin(n\delta)/n\) each have minimum two and unit consensus slope, although they differ globally. The conditional first-resultant theorem fixes which statistic is retained; the present theorem does not derive that premise. Nor does an instantaneous sufficient statistic close its own evolution: differentiating \(Z_n\) consumes phase/rate associations, as the motion-information owner shows. Constituent identity, boundary evolution, memory, events, formation and physical identification retain their separate obligations under the NFR ontology.

The shared static owner re-admits finite Fourier coefficients, removes only exact zeros, and returns the theorem's dimension and symbolic signed grid spectrum. Its separate response reader rebuilds active moments and the unnormalized current from primitive exact unit phasors; it consumes neither cached moments nor a prior verdict. The 128-row, order-128 and 128-gap implementation budgets do not restrict the theorem's all-degree statement. The symbolic witness can exceed the response reader's gap budget and is not a materialized irrational grid. Independent controls exercise rational Jacobian ranks, exact expansions, rotation, aggregation, degeneracy and invalid inputs. The law integration controls compare the response to both existing owned law evaluators, preserving the distinct counterfamilies and the lack of a noise guarantee. No law is installed, no trajectory is evolved and no frozen scientific assessment is replayed.

docs.title: Phase-response faithfulness and the boundary of a quotient
docs.text:
A distinct candidate requirement is boundary-channel faithfulness: no nonzero relative phase shift is invisible to every independently specified gap or registration query of the declared current. Its motivation is operational irredundancy of this particular phase-response channel, independently of which organized pattern it might favor. It is an additional hypothesis when the primitive phase and this channel have already been fixed. Neither the nodal equation nor the NFR participation contract requires each individual channel to distinguish every part of the full state. Other currents, observations, identities or events can consume phase information that this channel omits.

This requirement is not injectivity of one scalar current reading: even sine has equal values at distinct gaps. It asks whether the entire family of shifted responses distinguishes the two phases. It is also not the removal of common phase-origin symmetry. The shift below changes the phase relative to independently held probes.

Exact stabilizer. Fix the same finite odd Fourier class as in the preceding information theorem:

\[ j(\delta)=\sum_{n\in\mathcal N}b_n\sin(n\delta),\qquad b_n e0,\qquad \mathcal N\subset\mathbb N_{>0}. ag{F1} \]

Only exact zero coefficients are omitted. Define the invisible-shift subgroup of the primitive phase circle by

\[ H_j=\{a\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z): j(\delta+a)=j(\delta)\ \hbox{for every }\delta\}. ag{F2} \]

Because singleton boundaries are among the independent queries, (F2) is also the set of shifts invisible to every boundary list and every registration of the additive current. Uniqueness of the finite complex Fourier coefficients gives

\[ a\in H_j \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad e^{\mathrm i n a}=1\quad\hbox{for every }n\in\mathcal N. ag{F3} \]

For a nonempty active set put \(d=\gcd\mathcal N\). Every active index is a multiple of \(d\); conversely, an integer combination of the active indices equals \(d\). Equation (F3) therefore proves exactly

\[ oxed{H_j=\{2\pi k/d:0\le k<d\},\qquad ext{channel faithful}\ \Longleftrightarrow\ d=1.} ag{F4} \]

The fundamental period is \(1/d\) turn. If \(j=0\), the active set is empty and the entire circle is invisible. There is then no least positive period and no finite subgroup order; faithfulness is false. This degenerate case must not be assigned order zero or period zero.

Faithfulness is preserved by invertible changes of the declared state and observation charts when the entire query family is transformed with them. In a group-respecting radian chart, origin changes and orientation reversal leave (F4) unchanged. Nonzero constant current scaling or a common positive clock conversion does not change \(H_j\). An arbitrary phase reparametrization must also transport the phase-shift action; its transformed law need not still be a finite Fourier difference kernel.

What this restricts, and what it does not. A single harmonic \(j_n(\delta)=\sin(n\delta)/n\) has unit consensus slope and minimum boundary-information dimension two for every \(n\). It is faithful exactly when \(n=1\). Accordingly, within (F1),

\[ igl[m_{\min}=2,\ H_j=\{0\},\ j'(0)=1 igr] \quad\Longrightarrow\quad j(\delta)=\sin\delta. ag{F5} \]

Here the previous theorem supplies \(m_{\min}=2|\mathcal N|\); the new argument supplies the stabilizer. Requiring the minimum to equal two and requiring faithfulness are separate additional premises. Neither is derived by combining them, by calling phase a single primitive coordinate, or by naming the representation minimal. Higher moments are functions of that same primitive phase, not automatically extra primitive state variables.

Faithfulness alone does not require a first harmonic. For example,

\[ j_{23}(\delta)= rac{\sin2\delta+\sin3\delta}{5},\qquad V_{23}(\delta)= rac{1-\cos2\delta}{10} + rac{1-\cos3\delta}{15} ag{F6} \]

has \(\gcd(2,3)=1\), \(j_{23}'(0)=1\), and nonnegative periodic potential \(V_{23}'=j_{23}\), without any first harmonic. Nor does faithfulness imply positive curvature on the U3 acute domain. The also faithful law

\[ j_{13}(\delta)= rac{\sin\delta+\sin3\delta}{4},\qquad V_{13}(\delta)= rac{1-\cos\delta}{4} + rac{1-\cos3\delta}{12} ag{F7} \]

has unit consensus slope and nonnegative potential, but \(j_{13}'(\pi/3)=-5/8\). Thus it does not supply the positive boundary-curvature premise of the collective constraint theorem. Both retained nonsine families, with active sets \(\{1,9,18\}\) and \(\{1,8,10,17,19\}\), already have gcd one. Their source, formation and interaction distinctions remain; this condition selects neither endpoint law nor a unique kinetic law.

A genuine quotient of one complete flow. To distinguish a restricted channel hypothesis from an inadmissible chart change, consider the held-unit-capacity two-row comparison on fixed connected weighted support in its nondimensional structural chart and unchanged clock \( au\):

\[ x'= rac{-Lx-\gamma abla U_j( heta)}4,\qquad heta'= rac{\gamma Lx}4,\qquad U_j( heta)=\sum_{\{i,l\}}w_{il}V_j( heta_i- heta_l), \quad V_j'=j,\quad V_j(0)=0. ag{F8} \]

Here signed form and primitive circular phases are retained, \(\gamma>0\) and the support are held, and the complete observation/event alphabet is declared separately. \(L\) denotes the conductance Laplacian, positive definite on its relative space. This is the supplied two-row comparison, not a replacement of the native operator executor. Its storage is \(H_j=x^ op Lx/2+U_j\), with \(H_j'=-\|Lx\|^2/4\).

For \(d>1\) in (F4), each independent local shift \( heta_i\mapsto heta_i+2\pi k_i/d\), with forms unchanged, preserves both rows and this normalized potential. The phase row does not consume the phase, and every edge current and potential has that period. Thus this fixed-support flow has an exact quotient by those finite phase symmetries.

For the pure harmonic \(j_n\), the potential is \(V_n=(1-\cos(n\delta))/n^2\). Define

\[ \phi_i=n heta_i\pmod{2\pi},\qquad X_i=n x_i. ag{F9} \]

Both quotient rows become exactly

\[ X'= rac{-LX-\gamma abla U_1(\phi)}4,\qquad \phi'= rac{\gamma LX}4,\qquad H_1(X,\phi)=n^2H_n(x, heta). ag{F10} \]

No clock or reciprocal coefficient was changed. The form scale and any form observation must be transformed as stated. For \(n>1\), however, (F9) is an \(n\)-fold covering at each node, not an invertible regular chart on the original primitive phase. It discards discrete phase sectors. The fixed-support quotient does not establish equivalence of all the original observables or events, and its storage identity does not admit an undeclared support event.

Two exact controls make the discarded information explicit. For \(n=2\), a primitive pair gap zero and a gap \(\pi\) have identical \(j_2\), \(V_2\) and quotient phase. The native U3 gate with ceiling \(\pi/2\) accepts the former and rejects the latter. It therefore does not descend to this quotient. For \(n=3\), take an oriented three-cycle with phases \((0,2\pi/3,4\pi/3)\) and zero forms. Its three principal oriented edge increments equal \(2\pi/3\), so its winding is one. The quotient phases are all zero, just as for the primitive consensus state of winding zero. Both are stationary under (F8) with \(j_3\), but their marked primitive windings differ. No protected-source or phase-compatibility claim is made about that three-cycle control.

The operation alphabet sets the scope. Native U3 consumes the primitive wrapped separation, and public phase proposals can consume first resultants. These are separate declared paths. Adding such a gate or readout to the observation alphabet can distinguish shifts invisible to a continuous current; it does not force that current to acquire a first harmonic. A translated proper U3 acceptance arc has no nontrivial circle-period, so faithfulness of the whole query family including that gate would already follow from the gate rather than constrain (F1).

An operational definition of phase as equivalence under all admitted observations and interventions could instead justify a quotient. Its equivalence relation must then preserve that entire alphabet, identity and future response. The ontology's faithful full-state representation requirement does not imply that every individual boundary channel is faithful. Requiring faithfulness of a single fixed aggregate contact would be different again: organized phase cancellation can suppress that contact while other retained state and interactions remain relevant. In particular, the fivefold registration torque can have period \(2\pi/5\) even with primitive sine current. Its marked boundary state retains distinctions absent from that scalar torque; (F4) cannot be imposed on every collective observable.

Equations (F2)--(F4) quantify over abstract independent phase queries. They supply no admitted apparatus, autonomous probe selection, finite-resolution inverse or observation horizon. An arbitrarily small exact Fourier coefficient can remove an alias without making it experimentally resolvable. The missing independent admission is whether this boundary-current channel, under a declared accessible query class, must distinguish the primitive phase sectors. Without that premise, a current may retain its proper period while other full-state channels distinguish those sectors.

The free two-C9 probe supplies one conditional realization of an entire relative-registration traversal. Both constituents react, with their own fine state, supplied initial form contrast and contact work retained. Its integral current observation uses a declared kinetic row. Its finite-record theorem also bounds reconstruction and numerical errors under stipulated reading, clock and calibration accuracies. It neither derives current-channel faithfulness nor establishes a physical sensor's accuracy.

The shared static information owner derives this classification from re-admitted coefficients. Its faithfulness report retains the normalized coefficients, the finite shift-subgroup order and fundamental period in exact rational turns, and the faithful flag. For the zero law, the order and period are unavailable rather than zero. Independent controls exercise exact stabilizers, coefficient admission, both retained counterfamilies, the complete two-row covering and its U3/winding obstructions. No law is installed, no source or trajectory is evaluated, and no finite-accuracy identifiability follows.

docs.title: Balanced geometry does not independently select the phase current
docs.text:
Consider the structural proposal that every finite phase neighborhood whose unit vectors sum to zero must exert zero net phase current:

\[ \sum_a e^{\mathrm i\delta_a}=0 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \sum_a j(\delta_a)=0. \tag{BC} \]

For a bounded additive odd kernel on the full phase circle, this proposal is equivalent to first-moment sufficiency, not an independent deduction of it. A two-member balanced list first gives \(j(\delta+\pi)=-j(\delta)\). For any equal-resultant lists \(A,B\), append the half-turn shift of \(B\) to \(A\). The combined resultant vanishes, so (BC) gives \(\sum_A j=\sum_B j\). Applying the preceding classification and oddness selects \(j(\delta)=\kappa\sin\delta\); conversely that current obeys (BC). Without oddness, (BC) permits a cosine term as well. It forbids the constant term which degree-aware first-moment sufficiency alone permits.

Thus calling the first phase resultant a geometric balance does not prove that it contains all the information used by pressure. The smooth cubic alternative above supplies an exact control. On the rotated balanced triad \(\delta_a=\pi/6+2\pi a/3,\ a=0,1,2\), both the resultant and sine sum vanish, but \(\sum_a\sin^3\delta_a=-3/4\). Its normalized phase pressure is therefore \(-\epsilon/(4\pi)\). Both complete smooth laws admit this configuration. The native argument-pressure law does not: its zero-resultant direction is undefined. This test does not extend that native domain by convention.

Checking only pairs and balanced triads is insufficient. For any \(\eta>0\),

\[ j_\eta(\delta)=\frac{\sin\delta+\eta\sin(5\delta)}{1+5\eta}, \qquad U_\eta(\delta)= \frac{1-\cos\delta+(\eta/5)(1-\cos(5\delta))}{1+5\eta} \]

is odd, has unit consensus slope, and derives from a nonnegative even potential. It cancels on every antipodal pair and every rotated balanced unit triad, but not on a regular pentagon rotated by \(\pi/10\): its current sum there is \(5\eta/(1+5\eta)>0\). A balanced unit triad is necessarily an equilateral phase arrangement; the fifth harmonic survives its symmetry. These are phase-space configurations, not physical spatial polyhedra. This counterexample is an algebraic admission control, not a new engine law.

The premise audit consequently closes with a nonselection result: (BC) is a meaningful candidate constitutive restriction, but its unrestricted version restates the information choice and its pair/triad version leaves other smooth conservative potentials. None of the nodal identity, reciprocity or existing persistence results establishes (BC). An independent structural principle or observation is still required.

docs.title: Equal first moments conceal a higher-harmonic response
docs.text:
Use phase turns and fix u=1/6. On a degree-three star, set the root phase to zero and compare leaf-gap lists

\[ A=(-u,u,\alpha),\qquad B=(0,\alpha-u,\alpha+u), \qquad 0<|\alpha|<1/12. \]

Both preparations have strictly acute edges. Their root resultants are nonzero with positive real part, and each degree-one leaf is also regular. Thus the whole supplied star is admitted; it need not be an equilibrium. For Z_k=\sum exp(2*pi*i*k*gap_turn), direct phasor algebra gives

\[ Z_1(A)=Z_1(B)=1+e^{2\pi\mathrm i\alpha},\qquad Z_3(A)-Z_3(B)=3(e^{6\pi\mathrm i\alpha}-1). \]

Since sin(delta)^3=(3*sin(delta)-sin(3*delta))/4, the existing j_epsilon=sin(delta)+epsilon*sin(delta)^3 has

\[ \boxed{g_\epsilon(A)-g_\epsilon(B) =-\frac{\epsilon\sin(6\pi\alpha)}{4\pi},\qquad \sum_AU_\epsilon-\sum_BU_\epsilon =\frac\epsilon4[\cos(6\pi\alpha)-1].} \]

Cosine storage and the sine root source agree between these lists. At the fixed choice alpha=1/24, the cubic differences are respectively -epsilon*sqrt(2)/(8*pi) and epsilon*(sqrt(2)-2)/8. Forms, capacities, coefficients and clock can be held identical on the same star; these are initial source and storage identities, not sampled future predictions or equilibrium certificates.

The shared phase-response reader provides PhaseMomentInformationAssessment through assess_phase_moment_information(left, right, epsilon=...). Its primitive inputs are exact rational unit phasors (cos(delta),sin(delta)), retaining first and third moments, both candidate sources and both potentials. It does not decode arbitrary roots of unity or install a new runtime law. One exact rational control uses three copies each of (1,0),(3/5,4/5) on the left, and five copies of (4/5,3/5) plus one (4/5,-3/5) on the right. Both have degree six and Z_1=(24/5,12/5). Their right-minus-left cubic source and storage differences are -14*epsilon/(125*pi) and -24*epsilon/125. The information controls retain exact equality and admission, alongside the existing composition controls. Such finite controls exercise this reader; the classification is the proof above, not an inference from those examples.

Scope under composition and observation. The stationary mediator result already gives a collective phase cost k-|Z_1|. This is nonpairwise but still a function of the first resultant. It therefore violates primitive edge additivity, not first-moment sufficiency by itself. Its retained finite capacity also brings memory and hidden initialization; that earlier proof must not be replaced by a claim that every coarse law needs higher harmonics.

Likewise, sufficiency for the root's instantaneous source or storage does not make d,Z_1 a sufficient full state or future predictor. Neighbor dynamics, form, capacities and hidden state retain their separate contracts. The result identifies what a primitive information restriction would select and what the known alternative retains. Why that restriction should hold fundamentally remains open; no physical selection, autonomous support mechanism or new default law follows.

docs.title: A finite observation of the information restriction
docs.text:
The existing exact degree-six preparations give a prospective test without reconstructing pressure from an evaluated derivative. For each preparation, use a seven-node star with fixed undirected unit support, unit held capacities, zero loss, unit phase weight and storage coefficient, and no inputs or events. Set all ideal forms to zero and the root phase to zero. The six leaf phasors are the rational lists above: three copies each of \((1,0),(3/5,4/5)\) for \(A\), and five copies of \((4/5,3/5)\) plus one \((4/5,-3/5)\) for \(B\). They have the same first resultant and degree. They need not have equal storage under the alternative law.

In the declared common clock \(\tau=t/\pi\), the complete supplied family is

\[ x_i'=\frac1{d_i}\sum_{j\sim i}j_\epsilon(\theta_j-\theta_i), \qquad \theta_i'=x_i-\frac1{d_i}\sum_{j\sim i}x_j, \qquad j_\epsilon(\delta)=\sin\delta+\epsilon\sin^3\delta. \]

The phase row and the associated \(U_\epsilon\) are retained from the complete storage family above. This is not a held-phase pressure experiment. Compare \(\epsilon=0\) with one prospectively fixed \(\epsilon>0\). The observation is the difference of the two root form readings at the same finite time \(h>0\), \(D_\epsilon(h)=x_{0,B}(h)-x_{0,A}(h)\). Its ideal initial derivative is \(-14\epsilon/125\).

Let \(J_\epsilon=1+\epsilon\) and \(L_\epsilon=1+3\epsilon\); these globally bound \(|j_\epsilon|\) and \(|j_\epsilon'|\). Admit independent initial errors of at most \(\rho\ge0\) in each form and lifted phase coordinate around each ideal preparation. The laws, capacities, support and clock are held exact. Then, on the full nonlinear star and for \(\tau\ge0\),

\[ |x_i(\tau)|\le\rho+J_\epsilon\tau,\qquad |\theta_i'(\tau)|\le2\rho+2J_\epsilon\tau, \] \[ |\delta_{ij}(\tau)-\delta_{ij}^{\rm ideal}(0)| \le 2\rho+4\rho\tau+2J_\epsilon\tau^2. \]

Integrating the Lipschitz bound on each root's phase current, including its initial form error, gives

\[ \left|x_0(h)-h\,\overline j_\epsilon^{\rm ideal}(0)\right| \le \rho(1+2L_\epsilon h+2L_\epsilon h^2) +\frac23L_\epsilon J_\epsilon h^3. \]

If each endpoint root reading additionally has error at most \(\sigma\ge0\), the measured difference belongs to

\[ \boxed{D_\epsilon^{\rm measured}(h)\in -\frac{14\epsilon h}{125}+[-R_\epsilon,R_\epsilon],\qquad R_\epsilon=2\rho(1+2L_\epsilon h+2L_\epsilon h^2) +\frac43L_\epsilon J_\epsilon h^3+2\sigma.} \]

These bounds use every node's evolving form and phase; no numerical trajectory, linearization or discarded leaf state enters the proof. Absolute current bounds give at most linear form growth and exclude finite-time escape, so the complete smooth solutions exist over the declared window. The bound is sufficient, not an optimized noise budget.

For the declared example \(\epsilon=1,h=1/16,\rho=\sigma=0\), the two prediction intervals are

\[ D_0\in[-1/3072,1/3072],\qquad D_1\in-7/1000+[-1/384,1/384]. \]

Their separation is \(521/128000\). Allowing the separately declared \(\rho=\sigma=1/100000\) still leaves the exact positive separation \(25453/6400000\), before outward numerical materialization. These are structural-coordinate budgets, not a claim about laboratory precision.

Equal initial information is not equal future response. Writing \(\mu=\operatorname{mean}_a j(\delta_a)\), the full zero-form star rows give \(\delta_a''(0)=-j(\delta_a)-3\mu\) and

\[ x_0'''(0)=\operatorname{mean}_a \big[j'(\delta_a)(-j(\delta_a)-3\mu)\big]. \]

For the sine member, the two values are \(-6/5\) and \(-32/25\). Consequently \(D_0'''(0)=-2/25\); in particular the future sine contrast is not identically zero. The finite error interval, rather than an assumed zero baseline, is what permits the law comparison.

The shared phase-response owner supplies assess_phase_information_response. It reuses exact phasor admission and the source comparison, propagates declared preparation/readout budgets and exports both predictions through the SDK. Exact unit phasors specify generally irrational ideal angles; floating angle conversion error belongs in the preparation budget. The controls compare independent full-star evolution and include inconclusive budgets. This report neither installs a law nor admits physical data. Disjoint predictions distinguish the two supplied models, not every possible kernel; agreement with a sine interval cannot prove universal first-moment sufficiency. Independent physical preparation, observation and clock identification remain the missing admission.

The finite receiver collision uses this same complete kernel family for a separate inverse question. One exact endpoint can coincide for different law coefficients and internal orientations; this does not contradict selection of sine when first-moment sufficiency is independently required.

docs.title: Phase information must retain its pairing with motion
docs.text:
The existing resultant chain rule already differentiates the first moment. Its higher-harmonic version connects the preceding static source comparison to response and work without adding a primitive coordinate or changing a law. On fixed support, let each relative gap have a declared angular rate r_a=dot(delta_a) in one specified clock, and define

\[ Z_m=\sum_a e^{\mathrm i m\delta_a},\qquad M_m=\sum_a r_a e^{\mathrm i m\delta_a},\qquad \boxed{\dot Z_m=\mathrm i m M_m.} \]

For the existing cubic-sine current, put A=1+3*epsilon/4 and B=epsilon/4. Its source and incident potential are pi*d*g=A*Im(Z_1)-B*Im(Z_3) and V_inc=d*(1+2*epsilon/3)-A*Re(Z_1)+(B/3)*Re(Z_3). Consequently

\[ \boxed{\pi\dot g= \frac{A\operatorname{Re}M_1-3B\operatorname{Re}M_3}{d}, \qquad \dot V_{\rm inc}=A\operatorname{Im}M_1-B\operatorname{Im}M_3.} \]

These identities assume fixed coefficients and support. The potential rate counts root incidences once; it is not a whole-network storage balance. Phase rates are supplied with their provenance or derived from the complete chosen law, never reconstructed from the source response being predicted.

A complete-law pairing control. On the three-node star 0--1,0--2, use unit capacity, e=0,w=beta=1 and the conservative sine law in tau=t/pi. Keep the labeled relative phasors fixed at (3/5,4/5) and (4/5,3/5) and compare

\[ x^{(A)}=(0,3/4,-1/4),\qquad x^{(B)}=(0,-1/4,3/4). \]

The full phase row theta'=D^{-1}Bx gives the common root rate -1/4 and the respective relative-rate lists (1,0) and (0,1), where B is the unnormalized graph Laplacian and primes here use tau. Both states have the same labeled phases, hence every unweighted circular moment, the same form and rate multisets, the same degree-weighted form mean 1/8 and the same full storage 73/80. Nevertheless

\[ x'_0(A)=x'_0(B)=7/10,\qquad x''_0(A)=3/10,\quad x''_0(B)=2/5, \] \[ V'_{\rm inc}(A)=4/5,\qquad V'_{\rm inc}(B)=3/5. \]

Thus even all phase moments together with a separate rate multiset discard information needed for the next response: which motion belongs to which phase. The example changes that association, not the pressure law. The different incident work is compatible with conservation of total storage.

The shared derive_phase_moment_motion returns PhaseMomentMotion from exact unit phasors and declared gap rates, reusing the static moment admission. The existing sine comparison's resultant_kinematics() derives its first-moment rates from rebuilt full-law state. The native joint-response owner instead consumes the argument-source Jacobian; its law must not be replaced by this sine or cubic derivative.

Retaining M_m still does not establish an autonomous reduction. Where the rates are differentiable,

\[ \dot M_m=\sum_a\dot r_a e^{\mathrm i m\delta_a} +\mathrm i m\sum_a r_a^2 e^{\mathrm i m\delta_a}. \]

Accelerations and further phase/rate correlations therefore enter unless an admitted invariant family or observation closure determines them. This is the same information-retention issue addressed by the existing complete-law and hidden-memory owners, not a reason to introduce free fitted moments.

There is a scoped sufficient-state exception, already connected to the unordered pair and its temporal reconstruction. For the same three-node star, the regular moment chart reconstructs the full relative state from (Z1,M1) when 0<|Z1|<2, and derives its exact evolution. It retains four real degrees of freedom; it does not close generic moment statistics. Coincident phases hide internal form variance. Antipodal phases with nonzero M1 retain the unordered phase pair but hide its mean form relative to the root. Those boundary controls are part of the same retained-state argument, not new primitive variables.

docs.title: Existing acute-star observations separate the premises
docs.text:
Reuse the preceding composition control's incident-gap preparation: a star with root phase zero and leaf phases (0,0,t), 0<t<pi/2. The balance control fixes t=1/2, x=(0,0,0,0), capacities (1,2,3,4) in root-first order, e=0, w=beta=1, no Gamma or events, and epsilon=1 for the current-squared comparison. The source laws, clock and exact preparation are declared before this static evaluation; no trajectory is acquired. Reuse of the earlier gaps is distinct from evaluating these whole-form observations. No earlier frozen response or producer is regenerated.

More generally, at uniform form and arbitrary positive held capacities, all three laws have zero phase velocity and zero instantaneous storage loss at this star. Their weighted-form mean rates nonetheless differ:

\[ \dot M_{\rm native} =\frac{w}{\pi W}\left[ 3\arctan\!\left(\frac{\sin t}{2+\cos t}\right)-t\right]<0, \qquad \dot M_{\rm sine}=0, \] \[ \dot M_{\rm current^2} =-\frac{8w\epsilon\sin^3t}{9\pi W}<0 \qquad(\epsilon>0). \]

The native sign is the already proved merger defect. For the existing current-squared family, the root contributes (1+epsilon*sin(t)^2/9)*sin(t)/pi to sum_i d_i*g_i, and the nonaligned leaf contributes -(1+epsilon*sin(t)^2)*sin(t)/pi. Their difference gives the displayed expression. These are exact conditional initial-rate identities; the shared static readers check represented-state observations and intervals separately. The comparison reuses the existing laws and preparation rather than installing a new dynamics or claiming physical selection from a computed response.

The composition controls exercise these balance and branching boundaries. Whole-graph form balance concerns the held-support continuous law. Changing degrees or capacities changes its weights, and hybrid events need their own jump accounting. The invariant is not identified with physical mass, energy or a substrate origin. The conservation-only equivalence concerns the gap-only information class; the induced-neighborhood extension also requires exact cosine exchange. Neither conclusion selects a universal law or changes the native runtime and retained evidence.

docs.title: 11.9 Form balance, common origins and the primitive information contract
docs.text:
The conservation premise in section 11.8 has different content on a relative state and on a primitive nodal law. Fix a connected simple unit graph with at least two nodes, held strictly positive capacities, the original clock and an unforced complete field

\[ F=\dot x=Np,\qquad p=-eD^{-1}Bx+wg(\theta),\qquad \dot\theta=H(x,\theta). \]

Assume both rows are invariant under x -> x+s*1 for constant real s. The native and sine exchange rows have this property on their respective phase domains. Use their local existence/uniqueness domains; no global continuation through a native phase singularity is assumed. Put

\[ a_i=d_i/\nu_i,\quad W=a^T\mathbf1,\quad Q=a^Tx,\quad m=Q/W,\quad P=I-\mathbf1a^T/W,\quad \sigma(\theta)=\sum_i d_i g_i(\theta),\quad h=\dot Q/W=w\sigma/W. \]

The weights are held, so P^2=P, P*1=0 and a^T*P=0. Changing capacities, support, clock or inputs requires the separate continuous/event accounting.

docs.title: Exact relative equivalence and its retained reconstruction coordinate
docs.text:
The unique correction along the common form direction that makes this Q constant while preserving the phase row is

\[ \widehat F=F-h\mathbf1=PF,\qquad \widehat H=H. \]

It satisfies a^T*Fhat=0. Every form difference has the same derivative, Fhat_i-Fhat_j=F_i-F_j; both full fields induce the same phase derivative. Because both rows depend only on the form quotient, this is a trajectory equivalence on the quotient, not just an instantaneous identity. With the same initial complete state, throughout their common existence interval,

\[ \widehat x(t)=x(t)-c(t)\mathbf1,\qquad \widehat\theta(t)=\theta(t),\qquad c(0)=0,\quad \dot c=h(Px(t),\theta(t)). \]

The notation for h allows the general shift-invariant case; the displayed phase-only pressure makes h a function of phase and held capacities alone. Every fixed state-observation map invariant under common form shifts has the same history. Model-dependent pressure and raw-rate reports use different maps for the two fields and need not agree. In particular, grad_x E=Bx=q and 1^T*q=0, so the original storage E=E_D+beta*V_phi and its total exchange work are unchanged by this correction, including along the paired trajectories. An exact loss identity already satisfied by the selected original law is therefore preserved; the arbitrary phase row displayed above does not establish it by itself. Nodal form-work contributions instead change by -h*q_i, whose sum is zero. This statement compares a law with its own projection, not native trajectories with sine trajectories.

The complete coordinate description (y,m)=(Px,Q/W) instead has

\[ \dot y=PF(y,\theta),\qquad \dot m=h(y,\theta),\qquad x=y+m\mathbf1. \]

Dropping m loses the absolute common form origin. Keeping its initial value but imposing mdot=0 changes the full law whenever h is nonzero. A trajectory-dependent moving frame must retain c and its reconstruction row; it is not a proof of conservation of the original Q. A time-independent invertible origin chart requires the separate derivative equation and domain hypotheses of the asymptotic-origin construction. Constant translation symmetry alone supplies neither that chart nor Q balance.

docs.title: The balancing pressure consumes global state and capacity ratios
docs.text:
On positive capacities the corrected nodal pressure is

\[ \widehat p_i=p_i-\frac{w\sigma(\theta)}{\nu_i W}. \]

Unless sigma vanishes identically on the admitted domain, this is generally outside the primitive information class in section 11.8: it reads the whole support's phase-source sum and the capacity ratios in nu_i W. Uniformly rescaling all capacities cancels from this pressure correction, but changing one remote capacity generally does not. Conservation can therefore be enforced on a chosen relative model without deriving a primitive-local, capacity-independent conserving law.

There is a stronger uniqueness restriction. Suppose two pressures p and p_tilde in the same original form chart are independent of capacities. If their nodal rows N*p and N*p_tilde give the same relative-form rates at every state for every independently varied positive capacity vector, then they are equal. Indeed, writing r=p_tilde-p, quotient equality requires nu_i*r_i=nu_j*r_j for every pair. Vary nu_i alone while retaining all other capacities and the same form/phase state: r_i=0, then r_j=0. Thus no nontrivial common-direction freedom survives these primitive premises across the capacity family. This is not a derivation of conservation or capacity independence. It distinguishes those added premises from an unobserved common offset at one fixed capacity assignment.

docs.title: Zero-capacity rates and pressures have different limits
docs.text:
The correction need not diverge at a freezing boundary. For positive capacities,

\[ \left|\widehat p_i-p_i\right| \le \frac{|w\sigma|}{d_i},\qquad |h|\le |w\sigma|\frac{\nu_k}{d_k}\quad\text{for every }k. \]

At fixed regular form/phase state, h tends to zero whenever any capacity tends to zero. If the original full field is continuous there, the projected full field extends continuously by that original field on each zero-capacity face. Its form row still freezes at every zero-capacity node. This extension does not define inverse-capacity Q on the face.

Pressure has a subtler boundary. If only nu_i -> 0 while all other capacities stay positive, its correction tends to -w*sigma/d_i; the corrections at the other nodes vanish. If two capacities satisfy nu_i=r*epsilon, nu_j=epsilon, with fixed r>0 and every other capacity positive, then

\[ \widehat p_i-p_i\longrightarrow-\frac{w\sigma}{d_i+r d_j},\qquad \widehat p_j-p_j\longrightarrow-\frac{w\sigma}{d_i/r+d_j}. \]

For nonzero sigma these limits depend on r. There is no continuous single-valued pressure extension through that corner, although the full velocity extension exists. The nodal product at zero capacity cannot resolve that pressure ambiguity. These claims hold at retained regular states; they do not control a simultaneous phase singularity or a changed capacity law.

docs.title: Frozen static discriminators and existing consumers
docs.text:
The origin controls fix a native acute K1,3 preparation before evaluation: root-first phases (0,0,0,t), t=atan(3/4), uniform zero form, capacities (1,2,3,4) and e=0,w=beta=1, admitted through the regular-domain reader. A separate shift/work control uses form (0,1,-1,2), a common shift of 8 and e=w=1/2,beta=1. There is no trajectory or parameter fit. Write alpha=atan(3/14). Since sin(t)=3/5, cos(t)=4/5 and tan(3*alpha)=1737/2366<3/4 on the same acute branch,

\[ \sigma_{\rm native}=(3\alpha-t)/\pi<0,\qquad \sigma_{\rm sine}=0. \]

Projection conserves Q but preserves the native difference between the nonaligned and an aligned leaf, -4*w*t/pi. Sine instead gives -4*w*sin(t)/pi; hence the projection does not recover sine even after removing the common origin. At this preparation an originally zero form rate on an aligned leaf also becomes -h!=0, excluding a positive common clock rescaling. All phase rates and the instantaneous storage loss vanish because form is uniform; zero storage loss does not certify zero full motion.

A second fixed support has edges 0-1,0-2,0-3,3-4,4-5,4-6, zero form, unit capacities and phases (0,0,t,0,0,0,u). Changing the remote u=0 to u=t preserves the complete induced root ball at node 0, but doubles the nonzero sigma with W=12 unchanged. The original root pressure stays the same while its projected pressure changes. Holding u=0 and changing only the capacity at node 6 from 1 to 2 instead preserves sigma and changes W from 12 to 23/2. Exact symbolic identities and the shared native reader are checked separately from binary64 rounding; no support or evolution law is installed by these tests.

Existing relative-state reports already retain moving-reference rates and reconstruction information. Recovery admission refuses absolute mean-slab membership from relative observations, while replica membership consumes the absolute mean when its declared family requires it. These consumers cannot silently inherit a quotient-only conservation convention.

Nor can two disconnected patterns be recentered independently before a join: their bridge form gap contains the difference between their two origins. One common translation preserves it; two independent translations do not. The internal quotient descriptions must retain that relative offset or explicitly leave contact observations unavailable. The same information obligation holds for relative phase origins. A native attachment observer does not transfer its complete law to a sine composition.

Conclusion. Common-origin symmetry permits a closed relative description and a conserving lift when its extra information is admitted. It does not derive conservation of the original primitive Q. Primitive locality and capacity independence make that balance an additional restriction, not a free relabeling. Together with section 11.8 this closes the equivalence question without selecting a unique microscopic law, justifying cosine storage, changing an executor or revising any retained response.

docs.title: Stationary and energy geometry of the actual sine contact support
1. Frozen analytical question and complete marked chamber
docs.text:
This declaration precedes numerical response evaluation. It fixes the next analytical question after actual contact: whether the admitted joined support permits a stationary organization in the original complete acute chamber. It does not evolve the contacted source or replace its complete law.

  • Retain the twenty labelled nodes A_(k,s),B_(k,s), with k=0,...,4 and s in {+,-}. Each old doubled C5 has all four edges between successive pairs. Add the actual internal A_0 edge and the twelve actual edges from A_0 to B_0,B_1,B_4. There are 53 edges. Retain their generated positive conductances, held post-word capacities, zero forcing and the original structural clock from the contact protocol.
  • Use exactly the conservative weighted-form/bare-phase completion with e=0,w=beta=1: x_dot=M*S_U(theta), theta_dot=M*L_W*x, where M_ii=nu_i/(pi*d_i)>0 and d_i is the bare degree. Actual support and conductances remain held, including member-to-boundary association. No pair synchronization is assumed.
  • Orient every old cycle block from pair k to pair k+1 mod 5. For each of its four fine edges set branch b_e=0 when k<4 and b_e=-1 on the closing block 4 -> 0. Orient the internal edge from A_(0,+) to A_(0,-) and set its branch to zero. Orient all cross edges from A to B: their branches are zero for B_0,B_1 and one for B_4. These orientations and branches cover every support edge.
  • With real phase lifts define delta_e=theta_head-theta_tail-2*pi*b_e. The declared chamber requires -pi/2<delta_e<pi/2 for every one of the 53 edges. Quotient only the common phase translation, using sum theta=sum theta_* if a representative is needed, where theta_*(A_(k,s))=theta_*(B_(k,s))=2*pi*k/5. Keep all fine coordinates and the full branch vector, rather than only the two constituent winding observations.
  • Derive the full stationary equations first. Use exact current balances, strict acute-angle monotonicity and the connected-chamber method from marked-cycle information. Any pair reduction must follow from those full equations and their phase-domain symmetries. No fixed-weight dynamical pair closure is assumed.
  • The bounded outcome is either a proved stationary target with a strict relative-storage minimum or a proved obstruction in this exact chamber. No numerical root finder, optimizer, trajectory, parameter search or precision retry is authorized by this declaration. Static checks may independently verify the support, branch inventory and algebraic identities; they cannot replace the proof.

Stationary exclusion in this chamber would not imply winding loss, the absence of nonstationary organizations, or the absence of stationary states in other phase chambers. A stationary candidate would not establish source entry, attraction, maintenance from the actual preparation or a new NFR.

docs.title: 2. Full stationary equations and source chamber admission
docs.text:
Let U,W,nu retain the actual contact values. The bare graph is connected, all conductances are positive, and all held capacities are positive. Every node has positive bare degree. Consequently the diagonal mobility M is invertible and the full twenty-node stationary equations are exactly

\[ L_Wx=0,\qquad S_U(\theta)=0. \]

The first equation implies constant form because

\[ x^TL_Wx=\sum_{\{i,j\}\in U}W_{ij}(x_j-x_i)^2, \]

and positivity propagates equality along the connected support. No conductance has been replaced by one, averaged across a pair or discarded. The remaining stationary phase problem depends on bare support. This separation holds at stationarity under this complete law; it does not make the full weighted evolution independent of member-to-boundary association.

Define the bare phase potential and its gradient by

\[ V_U(\theta)=\sum_{e\in U}(1-\cos\delta_e),\qquad \nabla V_U=-S_U. \]

The common phase direction is neutral. The conserved lifted means with weights rho_i=d_i/nu_i exclude a nonzero rigid common form or phase drift: sum rho_i*x_dot_i=sum rho_i*theta_dot_i=0. Thus an equilibrium modulo these two common translations is an ordinary stationary state. A nonstationary organized motion with changing internal coordinates is a different possibility.

The declared chamber is nonempty: the common reference theta_* has old forward gaps alpha=2*pi/5, internal and zero-pair contact gaps zero, and cross gaps +alpha,-alpha at B pairs one and four. All are strictly acute. The actual post-word family belongs to the same chamber. The existing contact phase bound gives |theta_i(0)-theta_*,i|<=a_0=5/1536. Every old or cross reference gap therefore changes by at most 2*a_0=5/768, and

\[ \alpha+\frac5{768}<\frac\pi2. \]

The internal-edge gap is at most 5/768. These strict bounds retain each listed branch, rather than inferring chamber membership from two winding values alone. The joined graph has cycle-space dimension 53-20+1=34; the complete branch vector also retains the mixed and fine-member cycles. Branch changes induced solely by integer changes of vertex lifts describe the same circular chamber and do not enlarge this cycle class.

docs.title: 3. Acute phase uniqueness and stationary pair synchronization
docs.text:
Let C denote the open chamber from Section 1 and let C_bar denote its closed version, obtained by replacing every strict acute inequality by -pi/2<=delta_e<=pi/2, with the same branches. The closure extension is proved separately here; no trajectory or numerical response is used to change the frozen question.

Both sets are convex on real lifts. For theta,phi in C_bar, orient each edge as in the declaration and take their gradient difference. Exact summation by parts gives

\[ (\theta-\phi)^T[\nabla V_U(\theta)-\nabla V_U(\phi)] =\sum_{e\in U} (\delta_e(\theta)-\delta_e(\phi)) [\sin\delta_e(\theta)-\sin\delta_e(\phi)]. \]

Sine is strictly increasing on the whole closed interval [-pi/2,pi/2]. Every summand is nonnegative, and it is positive whenever the two edge gaps differ. Connectedness implies that all gaps agree only when theta-phi is a common constant. Hence there is at most one stationary phase configuration in C_bar modulo common phase. This conclusion does not assume that a stationary point exists.

In the open chamber the Hessian is the positive cosine Laplacian and is strictly positive on relative phase directions. At an acute boundary some edge cosines may vanish. The preceding strict monotonicity argument still applies there and does not infer a positive Hessian from those zero values.

Each independent interchange of the two members of one pair preserves bare support, all the declared branch constraints and the potential. On old or cross blocks it permutes equal-branch edges. At the internal A_0 edge it reverses the zero-branch gap. Thus a stationary phase point would be carried to another stationary point of the same closed chamber. Choose the representative with sum theta=sum theta_*. Interchange preserves this sum, so the uniqueness result forces it to fix that point. Every stationary pair therefore has equal lifted member phases:

\[ \theta_{A,(k,+)}=\theta_{A,(k,-)}=A_k,\qquad \theta_{B,(k,+)}=\theta_{B,(k,-)}=B_k. \]

This is a consequence of the full fine stationary equations. The actual conductances need not have pair symmetry, and an evolving state with equal member phases need not remain on that stratum. No fixed-weight pair closure is used in the argument.

docs.title: 4. Branch-preserving reflection of a possible stationary phase
docs.text:
The bare graph also preserves the reversal k -> -k mod 5 in both components. Combine it with phase conjugation and the fixed lift correction

\[ (\mathcal R\theta)_{C,(k,s)}= \begin{cases} -\theta_{C,(0,s)}, & k=0,\\ 2\pi-\theta_{C,(5-k,s)}, & k=1,2,3,4, \end{cases} \qquad C\in\{A,B\}. \]

Old forward gaps are carried to reversed-index forward gaps with the same acute bounds, including the declared closing-edge correction. The A_0 -> B_0 gaps change sign, the A_0 -> B_1 and A_0 -> B_4 gaps exchange with a minus sign, and the internal A_0 gap changes sign. Thus R preserves the full closed chamber and V_U; it also maps S_U=0 to S_U=0. It need not preserve the actual weighted dynamical field, which is not required for this stationary phase argument.

After the derived pair equality, choose the common phase representative A_0=0. This is possible without altering any branch gap. Reflection preserves that representative. Uniqueness therefore forces R theta=theta, giving

\[ B_0=0,\qquad B_4=2\pi-B_1,\qquad B_3=2\pi-B_2. \]

Write a=B_1, so B_4=2*pi-a. The two contact branches give -pi/2<=a<=pi/2. These relations have been derived without fixing the receiver's origin or internal shape in advance.

docs.title: 5. Exact obstruction in the complete acute chamber and its closure
docs.text:
The fine members of B pairs two and three have only their four old neighbors. With the stationary member equality just proved, the current equation at B pair two is

\[ 0=2\sin(B_1-B_2)+2\sin(B_3-B_2). \]

Both consecutive forward gaps lie in [-pi/2,pi/2]. Strict injectivity of sine on that interval makes them equal. The same argument at B pair three gives a common gap q on the whole three-edge chain from B pair one through pairs two and three to pair four:

\[ B_2-B_1=B_3-B_2=B_4-B_3=q,\qquad -\frac\pi2\le q\le\frac\pi2. \]

Together with the derived reflection this gives

\[ 2a+3q=2\pi,\qquad a\ge\frac\pi4. \]

The endpoint B pair one has two neighbors in each of B_0,B_2,A_0. Its full fine current equation, with no changed edge multiplicities, is

\[ 0=2[-\sin a+\sin q-\sin a],\qquad \sin q=2\sin a. \]

But pi/4<=a<=pi/2, so the right side is at least sqrt(2), while the left side is at most one. The strict contradiction proves

\[ \boxed{\text{There is no stationary state in the declared complete acute chamber, or in its closed acute boundary.}} \]

The conclusion holds for every actual positive conductance assignment and positive held capacity produced by the frozen contact family, not only the nominal split control. Those quantities enter the full evolution and its storage but cancel from the necessary phase stationary problem after the full form equation has forced constant form. The proof changes neither the UM fan nor the pressure, phase law or clock.

An independent interior obstruction avoids reflection and helps identify the conflicting currents. Normalize A_0=0 after stationary member equality, and put a=B_1, b=B_4-2*pi, c=B_0. The uncontacted B chain gives 3*q=2*pi+b-a, hence d=a-b=2*pi-3*q>pi/2. Both contact gaps are acute, so a,-b>0. The remaining cycle gaps r=a-c,t=c-b are acute and have r+t=d, so they too are positive. The two endpoint balances require

\[ 2\sin q=(\sin r+\sin t)+(\sin a-\sin b). \]

Each parenthesis is strictly greater than one: for positive acute u,v with u+v>pi/2, one has sin v>cos u and sin u+cos u>1. The displayed right side is therefore greater than two, while its left side is less than two. This second argument is confined to the open chamber; the preceding reflection proof supplies the boundary result.

docs.title: 6. What the obstruction establishes
docs.text:
The actual UM contact fan cannot support an equilibrium retaining all of the original fine and cross-edge acute branches. In particular, there is no stationary relative-storage minimum of the complete law there. A minimum constrained to the closed chamber can have nonzero boundary forces; it is not a stationary solution of the unconstrained nodal rows. The result is an exact feasibility obstruction, rather than a failed optimizer or an uncertified small residual.

The earlier result required the receiver to leave its original small radius-1/16 identity tube. The present result is stronger about possible stationary targets: merely enlarging that tube within this complete acute chamber cannot produce a stationary continuation. It does not assert a time at which the actual trajectory leaves the chamber, or that it ever does. The conservative law can support motion without an equilibrium at the moving state; excluding equilibrium does not exclude bounded nonstationary organization.

An edge reaching |delta|=pi/2 also does not imply a winding change. It is a boundary of the acute certificate, whereas a principal phase cut lies at |delta|=pi. The actual winding observations can therefore survive loss of acuteness. Stationary states with nonacute edges, other complete cycle classes, nonstationary identities and acquisition from the actual contacted source retain their separate obligations. No statement about physical particles, a unique fundamental law, or autonomous contact occurrence follows from this graph-specific theorem.

The principal-class curvature analysis below resolves the larger stationary-minimum question: nonacute saddles exist, but no stable equilibrium is available in the same complete open class. Actual nonstationary motion remains a separate question.

docs.title: 7. Independent static controls and comparison scope
docs.text:
The static controls check all 53 edge orientations and branches, incidence rank nineteen and 34 independent cycle directions. Exact turns check the complete reference class. Independent fine edge sums check the monotonicity, reflected current map and receiver-current equations without calling a root finder. The fixed algebra probes use 100-digit arithmetic; graph-capture comparisons retain their represented phases and absolute tolerance 2^-46 separately.

The auxiliary positive conductances cycle through 3/8,...,7/8. They test the complete weighted field and stationary reduction; they are not new UM outputs or replacements for the preceding contact's frozen conductances. The theorem itself applies to every admitted actual positive weight list. No event or frozen response producer is replayed by these controls.

Two comparisons keep the exclusion's domain explicit. The disconnected original twists have zero phase current before the fan is added. On the same connected contact support, constant form and constant phase give an equilibrium in the distinct zero-winding class: its relative storage Hessian consists of positive weighted-form and bare-phase Laplacians. This does not place that equilibrium in the excluded original chamber or show that the contacted source reaches it. Nonconstant form at constant phase also checks that a zero sine current alone does not satisfy both complete stationary rows.

These finite checks support implementation and algebraic consistency. They neither prove the chamber-wide theorem nor certify a new organized source.

docs.title: 8. Frozen nonacute minimum question and static controls
docs.text:
This declaration precedes the new static evaluations. Retain the complete model, actual conductances, capacities, clock, support, orientations and branches of Section 1. Enlarge only the admitted phase domain to -pi<delta_e<pi on every edge. The question is whether a stationary local minimum of the full relative storage exists anywhere in this open marked class. A nonstrict minimum is included. The complete fine Hessian must be positive semidefinite, but that necessary condition alone is not sufficient.

Derive any pair or receiver restriction from full stationarity and local minimality. Preserve zero neighbor resultants and zero curvature until an argument on this actual graph excludes them as minima. The old acute uniqueness/reflection proof and the odd-degree bound for another contact graph are unavailable here. Holding the donor's relative phases fixed while varying its common phase is an allowed variation, not a dynamical closure.

The bounded evaluation is analytical. Independent static controls may check the zero-resultant fiber identity, adjacent-twin splitting curvature, the exact receiver restriction, all eight cosine-sign cases of the three-edge chain, and the final endpoint inequalities. Use exact rational matrices and turns where available and 100-digit arithmetic for fixed trigonometric identities. Auxiliary probes use the quadrature C4, adjacent-twin half-split pi/3, a rotation increment 1/64, and receiver phases (0, pi/8, pi/3, 3*pi/4, 5*pi/4, 7*pi/4) in order (O,B_0,B_1,B_2,B_3,B_4). These are algebra controls, not proposed equilibria or source responses. Retain the earlier represented-phase tolerance for shared-reader comparisons. No optimizer, root search, trajectory, event or frozen producer is replayed. A minimum obstruction would leave stationary saddles, nonstationary organization and principal-cut crossings separate.

docs.title: 9. Full stationary curvature in the principal marked chamber
docs.text:
Let P be the open principal chamber declared in Section 8. The full stationary reduction from Section 2 remains valid there: x is constant and S_U(theta)=0. The full storage Hessian is block diagonal,

\[ \nabla^2 H=\begin{pmatrix}L_W&0\\0&K\end{pmatrix},\qquad K=L_{\cos\delta}. \]

The actual positive weighted form block is positive on relative form directions. A stationary relative-storage minimum therefore requires the signed phase Hessian K to be positive semidefinite on all relative fine directions. Since K*1=0, this is equivalent to K>=0 on the whole phase space; changing a test vector by a common constant leaves its curvature unchanged. Fixing either conserved common mean does not discard a negative relative direction.

The following proof excludes every stationary point satisfying this necessary PSD condition in P, including singular Hessians. It thus excludes nonstrict as well as strict local minima. It does not apply the acute uniqueness or reflection argument outside its domain.

docs.title: 10. Stationary PSD conditions force fine twin equality
docs.text:
For each fine node define its bare neighbor resultant and Hessian diagonal

\[ R_i=\sum_{j\sim i}e^{i\theta_j},\qquad r_i=\Re(e^{-i\theta_i}R_i)=K_{ii}. \]

Stationarity makes Im(exp(-i*theta_i)*R_i)=0; PSD gives r_i>=0. If R_i is nonzero, these two conditions force exp(i*theta_i)=R_i/|R_i|. If r_i=0, PSD forces the whole row and column of K to vanish, so every incident edge has zero cosine. This zero case cannot be dropped merely because another graph had odd degrees.

Every pair except A_0 consists of nonadjacent twins with exactly the same external neighbors. Both members therefore share one resultant R. If R is nonzero, the alignment just derived gives equal circular phases. For any one common neighbor, the two incident edges have the same branch when oriented outward from the twin pair. Their strict principal bounds give |theta_+-theta_-|<2*pi. Equal circular phases must consequently have equal lifts in this chamber.

Now retain the possibly zero resultant R=0. Both PSD rows vanish, so every common neighbor is perpendicular to both twins. Unequal circular twins must then be antipodal. The same strict branch bound makes their lifted separation exactly pi in absolute value. Write them, after possibly interchanging their names, as Theta+pi/2,Theta-pi/2.

For a common neighbor j, let eta_j be its lift adjusted by the common outward edge branch, so both principal gaps are eta_j-theta_+ and eta_j-theta_-. Their two strict cut inequalities imply

\[ -\frac\pi2<\eta_j-\Theta<\frac\pi2. \]

The zero incident cosines require sin(eta_j-Theta)=0, hence eta_j=Theta. All common neighbors have the same circular phase, and there is at least one of them. Their resultant is therefore degree*exp(i*Theta), contradicting R=0. Unequal zero-resultant twins are excluded. Equal twins with zero resultant have not been excluded by this lemma; they remain covered by the subsequent argument.

The internal A_0 edge makes that pair adjacent twins. A separate local curvature calculation applies. Put theta_+=Theta+epsilon,theta_-=Theta-epsilon; the internal principal cut gives |epsilon|<pi/2. With every external phase fixed, define C=Re(exp(-i*Theta)*R) for their common external resultant. The part of the potential depending on epsilon is

\[ f(\epsilon)=-2C\cos\epsilon-\cos(2\epsilon)+\text{constant}, \qquad f'(\epsilon)=2\sin\epsilon(C+2\cos\epsilon). \]

If a stationary split has epsilon!=0, then C=-2*cos(epsilon) and

\[ f''(\epsilon)=-4\sin^2\epsilon<0. \]

That is a full fine antisymmetric phase direction and contradicts PSD. Thus the adjacent pair also has equal lifted phases. This argument retains zero external resultants and does not divide by them.

Every hypothetical stationary PSD state in P therefore has equal lifted members in all ten pairs. This is a necessary stationary restriction, not a weighted dynamical pair-closure claim. It used the actual complete branch class to handle the degenerate nonadjacent twins.

docs.title: 11. Exact receiver variation and a second twin restriction
docs.text:
Keep the derived fine-member equality. Vary each B pair through its common phase, and vary all ten A phases by one common rotation, holding every A relative phase fixed. This is a six-dimensional family of configurations, not a proposed invariant dynamical subsystem. Every internal A edge retains its phase gap exactly. With O=A_0 and the five B pair phases as its coordinates, the restricted phase potential is

\[ V_{\rm restricted}=\text{constant}+4V_G, \]

where G is the six-vertex graph consisting of the B cycle and the three edges O--B_0,O--B_1,O--B_4. The factor four is the actual fine edge multiplicity of every complete pair block. No actual conductance is averaged or altered: this is a restriction of the bare phase potential.

Full stationarity makes every derivative of this restricted potential zero. In particular, the O derivative sums all A node currents, whose internal contributions cancel. Full PSD makes its restricted Hessian PSD. No separate classification of the A cycle is required.

In G, the vertices O and B_0 are adjacent twins: both have the same two external neighbors B_1,B_4. Their internal contact edge has branch zero and strict principal gap. The adjacent-twin calculation in Section 10 therefore forces B_0=O. It is valid even if their common external resultant vanishes. This equality has been derived without reflection, acute uniqueness or a supplied relative origin.

Use the common phase freedom to put O=B_0=0, and write

\[ a=B_1,\qquad b=B_4-2\pi. \]

The actual contact branches give -pi<a,b<pi. The retained B cycle has the three interior chain gaps

\[ q_1=B_2-B_1,\quad q_2=B_3-B_2,\quad q_3=B_4-B_3, \qquad q_1+q_2+q_3=2\pi+b-a. \]

All three gaps lie strictly between -pi and pi by the original branch declaration. The identity on their sum retains the complete marked class; it is not obtained by wrapping a sum after the calculation.

docs.title: 12. The uncontacted chain retains no negative-cosine alternative
docs.text:
Stationarity at B pairs two and three gives sin(q_1)=sin(q_2)=sin(q_3). Thus their cosine magnitudes are equal: write cos(q_j)=epsilon_j*c, with c>=0 and signs epsilon_j when c>0. Restrict the six-vertex Hessian further to the two coordinates B_2,B_3, holding its other coordinates fixed. Apart from the positive factor four, its matrix is

\[ T=\begin{pmatrix} \cos q_1+\cos q_2&-\cos q_2\\ -\cos q_2&\cos q_2+\cos q_3 \end{pmatrix}\succeq0. \]

If c>0 and the middle cosine is -c, the two nonnegative diagonals force both endpoint cosines to be +c. The resulting determinant is -c^2, a contradiction. If the middle cosine is +c but an endpoint cosine is -c, one diagonal is zero while the off-diagonal is nonzero, again contradicting PSD. The only remaining case for c>0 is that all three cosines are positive. Their strict principal domains and equal sines then make all three gaps equal in (-pi/2,pi/2).

The singular case c=0 is retained explicitly. Each principal gap is +pi/2 or -pi/2; equality of their sines again makes all three equal. Consequently every hypothetical PSD state satisfies

\[ q_1=q_2=q_3=q,\qquad -\frac\pi2\le q\le\frac\pi2,\qquad 3q=2\pi+b-a. \]

Because a,b are strict principal contact gaps, 2*pi+b-a>0. Thus 0<q<=pi/2, including the possible zero-cosine endpoint. It follows that

\[ a-b=2\pi-3q\ge\frac\pi2. \]

No inverse cosine or square-root division has removed a singular case.

docs.title: 13. Endpoint currents and curvature contradict the marked winding
docs.text:
The B pair-one and pair-four equations in the restricted graph are

\[ \sin q=2\sin a=-2\sin b. \]

The two terms at each endpoint come from its distinct edges to O and B_0, whose phases have been proved equal. Their Hessian diagonals must also be nonnegative:

\[ 2\cos a+\cos q\ge0,\qquad 2\cos b+\cos q\ge0. \]

Since 0<q<=pi/2, stationarity gives 0<sin(a)=-sin(b)<=1/2. On the strict principal interval this puts a in either (0,pi/6] or [5*pi/6,pi), and -b in the same two intervals. The distant alternative is impossible for either endpoint: its cosine is at most -sqrt(3)/2, so its Hessian diagonal is at most 1-sqrt(3)<0. Therefore

\[ 0<a\le\frac\pi6,\qquad 0<-b\le\frac\pi6,\qquad a-b\le\frac\pi3. \]

This contradicts the necessary lower bound a-b>=pi/2 from the same retained chain. Hence

\[ \boxed{\text{No stationary phase in the original open principal marked chamber has a positive-semidefinite full fine Hessian.}} \]

Every stationary state in that chamber, if any exists, has a strictly negative relative phase-curvature direction. The full storage therefore has no stationary local minimum there, including nonstrict or degenerate minima. The conclusion holds for every actual positive conductance and positive held capacity in the frozen contact family: those actual values remain in the complete law and the positive form block, while stationary phase and its curvature use bare support.

docs.title: 14. Scope beyond the acute obstruction
docs.text:
This result closes the nonacute stationary-minimum question in the same complete cycle class. It derives all reductions from full stationarity, fine curvature and strict principal branch admission. Even-degree zero resultants, zero chain cosines and singular PSD tests have been retained until the graph-specific contradiction excludes the whole candidate set. No odd-degree resultant estimate, acute convexity, reflection ansatz, optimizer outcome or numerical Hessian eigenvalue is a premise.

The result excludes a stationary local-storage minimum, rather than every possible stationary state in the enlarged chamber. It does not extend to principal-cut boundary points, where the strict twin branch intersection changes, or to other complete cycle classes. The synchronized equilibrium from Section 7 remains a valid minimum in its distinct zero-winding class.

Nor does the theorem show that the actual contacted trajectory changes winding, approaches any equilibrium or acquires a different identity. Nonstationary organization, finite retention, full-time confinement and source entry retain separate dynamical obligations. The absence of a stationary minimum is a geometric restriction on one candidate maintenance mechanism under the supplied law, not a failure of the nodal identity or an identification with fundamental physical behavior.

docs.title: 15. Fixed algebraic stationary saddle control
15.1. Prospective declaration
docs.text:
Before evaluating this additional static control, fix

\[ c=\frac{1+\sqrt{17}}8,\qquad t=\arccos c,\qquad q=2t,\qquad a=\pi-3t. \]

Use synchronized members in each pair, the original A winding A_k=2*pi*k/5, and the B lifted phases

\[ (B_0,B_1,B_2,B_3,B_4) =(0,a,a+q,a+2q,2\pi-a). \]

Retain the same 53-edge support and every original branch, positive actual conductance, positive held capacity and complete law. Put x_i=m constant at any admitted common form origin. The fixed predictions are full stationarity, strict principal-chamber membership and negative fine phase curvature K_ii=4*cos(q)<0 at either B pair-two member. The algebraic constant is not fitted or retuned. Any static numerical check uses 100-digit arithmetic and the already declared controls; no root finder, trajectory, source re-preparation or actual event is performed.

docs.title: 15.2. Exact stationary and negative-curvature verification
docs.text:
The fixed algebraic constant satisfies

\[ 4c^2-c-1=0,\qquad \frac12<c<\frac1{\sqrt2}, \qquad \frac\pi4<t<\frac\pi3. \]

Consequently 0<a<pi/4, pi/2<q<2*pi/3 and 2*a+3*q=2*pi. The B cycle's forward gaps are exactly (a,q,q,q,a). They are all strict principal gaps with winding one. The cross gaps are zero, a and -a; the internal gap is zero. Together with the old A twist these are precisely the original complete branch assignments, although the three B chain gaps are nonacute.

The algebraic relation for c gives an exact current identity:

\[ \sin q=2\sin t\cos t =2\sin t(4\cos^2t-1) =2\sin(3t)=2\sin a. \]

Thus the two receiver endpoints satisfy their full current balances. The three identical chain gaps cancel at B pairs two and three, and the symmetric +a,-a contacts cancel at B pair zero and A pair zero. All remaining A currents are those of the original twist and vanish. Fine member synchronization supplies the exact factors two in each node current. Hence every fine sine current is zero. Constant form also gives L_W*x=0 for every retained actual conductance assignment, so both complete stationary rows vanish.

At either member of B pair two, all four incident edge cosines equal cos q. Its fine Hessian diagonal is

\[ K_{ii}=4\cos q=4(2c^2-1)=2(c-1)<0. \]

The corresponding one-node variation, recentered by any common phase constant to retain the declared mean, has strictly negative curvature. This is an explicit stationary saddle in the retained principal chamber. It distinguishes the no-minimum theorem from a claim that no stationary configuration exists there. The construction does not describe a state acquired by the actual contacted source.

docs.title: 16. Instability of every stationary point under the actual weighted law
docs.text:
The negative phase direction also has a dynamical implication for this specific conservative two-row model. Keep the actual mobility M=diag(nu_i/(pi*d_i)), positive weighted Laplacian L_W and stationary phase Hessian K. The tangent equations are

\[ \dot\xi=-MK\eta,\qquad \dot\eta=ML_W\xi, \qquad \ddot\eta=-AK\eta,\qquad A=ML_WM. \]

Let rho_i=d_i/nu_i and let E be the tangent space rho^T*v=0 of either conserved weighted-mean leaf. The symmetric matrix A has kernel span(rho) and is strictly positive on E; denote that positive restriction by A_E. For the orthogonal projection P_E, put K_E=P_E*K|_E. The complete second-order phase equation on that leaf is eta_ddot=-A_E*K_E*eta, because A annihilates the omitted rho component.

A negative fine curvature direction from Section 13 can be shifted by a common constant to lie in E, without changing its quadratic form since K*1=0. Hence K_E has a negative direction. The product A_E*K_E is similar to the symmetric matrix A_E^(1/2)*K_E*A_E^(1/2), which also has a negative eigenvalue. It follows that -A_E*K_E has a strictly positive eigenvalue sigma^2 and a real nonzero eigenvector v in E.

The growing solution of the full first-order tangent system is recovered without dropping the form row:

\[ \eta(t)=e^{\sigma t}v,\qquad \xi(t)=-\frac{e^{\sigma t}}\sigma MKv. \]

The form perturbation also lies in E, because rho^T*M=(1/pi)*1^T and 1^T*K=0. Both tangent equations therefore hold on the actual two conserved-mean leaves. Every stationary state in the retained open principal chamber has a real growing tangent mode under the same actual weighted law. Smooth finite-dimensional linearized instability then gives instability of that equilibrium on its relative leaf.

This result supplies no uniform growth rate over the chamber or conductance family, no departure time for the contacted preparation, and no claim that the preparation approaches one of these stationary states. A growing mode near an equilibrium does not itself select a principal-cut crossing or exclude every nonstationary organized motion.

The static controls check the full fine restriction, every chain cosine-sign case, a zero-resultant counterexample outside the retained branch class, and the fixed saddle's negative direction on its exact weighted-mean leaf. The rounded saddle is checked with an independent captured-state residual and enclosing rate bounds; neither an exact represented root nor a bound on the entire interval width is inferred from the declared midpoint tolerance. These finite checks support the shared arithmetic and field consumers, not a numerical substitute for the analytical exclusions.

docs.title: 17. Frozen conservative confinement question
docs.text:
Fix each exact actual post-word source from the contact protocol, its actual 53-edge support, generated positive conductances, held capacities, original structural clock and conservative weighted-form/bare-phase law. Retain every marked branch from Section 1 and the open principal chamber from Section 8. No new event, forcing or loss is inserted.

Let rho_i=d_i/nu_i, m_rho=sum(rho*x_0)/sum(rho), Q_0=(1/2)*x_0^T*L_W*x_0, V_0=V(theta_0) and h=Q_0+V_0. The question is whether storage and the two conserved lifted means can isolate the actual preparation from every principal cut of this complete marked class. The analytical prediction is a continuous configuration path starting at that source and ending on a first principal boundary, with H=h, both source means unchanged, and every edge strictly inside its original branch until the endpoint. Such a path is not claimed to satisfy either evolution row or select the cut reached by the actual source.

Use the full fine state, fixed-mean compactness, the no-minimum result and strict sublevel components. Preserve the actual positive form storage as a coordinate of H; its variation along a comparison path does not add an event reserve or an external reservoir. Prove source-specific positivity before dividing by Q_0. No optimizer, root finder, trajectory, frozen producer or new precision campaign belongs to this declaration.

Before static evaluation, fix these independent algebra controls. Reuse the existing auxiliary positive conductance list, capacities and 100-digit arithmetic; those weights are not regenerated UM outputs. Check the exact post-AL nominal forms m=5/16, increment b=1/1024 on A pair zero only, the component mean difference, the support diameter and weighted centering. For radial form lifting use the original doubled twists and the phase path that decreases B pair one by s and increases B pair four by s, recentered to its original weighted phase mean, at s=0,1/128,1/64. Check storage and means with both this nonconstant nominal form and a separately declared uniform-form comparison; the latter is not an actual post-word source.

For the separate cycle-information control, rigidly rotate all B phases by s=0,pi/2,3*pi/5,4*pi/5, with common weighted recentering. Predict unchanged old constituent cycle gaps and a first cross-edge cut at 3*pi/5; do not attribute the energy-path theorem to this rigid rotation. Exact turn and matrix checks precede represented shared-reader comparisons, whose residual, enclosure and existing 2^-46 midpoint tolerance remain distinct.

docs.title: 18. The actual source has strictly positive form storage
docs.text:
Fix one exact source from Section 17, including its actual W,nu and post-word forms and lifts (x_0,theta_0). All following means and paths refer to this one source; differing sources retain their own invariant values and generated conductances. Put

\[ Q(x)=\frac12x^TL_Wx,\quad V(\theta)=V_U(\theta),\quad H=Q+V,\qquad m_\rho=\frac{\rho^Tx_0}{\rho^T1},\quad \theta_\rho=\frac{\rho^T\theta_0}{\rho^T1},\quad \rho_i=\frac{d_i}{\nu_i}>0. \]

These are the actual weighted form mean and the declared lifted phase mean, not circular or separate constituent means. Both remain conserved under the selected complete law because rho^T*M=(1/pi)*1^T and both the sine current and weighted form gradient sum to zero.

Before the word, each constituent's arithmetic form mean is the same m. AL increases only the two selected A forms by b=1/1024; UM and SHA leave all forms unchanged. Thus the actual endpoint has

\[ \overline x_A=m+\frac b5,\qquad \overline x_B=m. \]

These arithmetic means certify an initial difference only; they are not claimed to be conserved after contact. The difference proves that x_0 is nonconstant. Since the actual positive weighted graph is connected, Q_0=Q(x_0)>0. This remains true for the synchronized-member control and does not require a nonzero selected internal split.

A uniform lower bound follows directly from the admitted source geometry. Some A node i has x_i>=m+b/5, and some B node j has x_j<=m. A path from i to the selected A pair has at most two edges. A contact edge followed, when necessary, by one B edge reaches j, so a joined path has length ell<=4. Every actual conductance is greater than 3/4. Cauchy's inequality on that path gives

\[ Q_0\ge\frac12\sum_{e\in\text{path}}W_e(\Delta_ex_0)^2 >\frac{3}{8\ell}(x_i-x_j)^2 \ge\frac{3b^2}{800} =\frac3{838860800}>0. \]

The strict inequality uses at least one nonzero path difference. It is a bound on the existing positive form term in H, not an additional reservoir or an event-work allowance. Write V_0=V(theta_0) and h=Q_0+V_0.

docs.title: 19. Compactness on the two fixed-mean leaves
docs.text:
Let A_theta be the affine phase leaf rho^T*theta=rho^T*theta_0, and write Omega=P intersect A_theta for the original strict principal chamber on that leaf. The actual source lies in Omega by Section 2. Its closed chamber replaces all strict gap inequalities by -pi<=delta_e<=pi. It is the closure of Omega: interpolation from any closed-chamber point to the strict source makes all edge inequalities strict before the closed endpoint.

This phase closure is compact. The joined graph has diameter at most four: any A node is within two edges of either selected A member, any B node is within two edges of that member, and the within-component distances are at most two. Along each edge, the retained branches b_e in {-1,0,1} give

\[ |\theta_j-\theta_i|\le\pi+2\pi|b_e|\le3\pi. \]

Consequently the full lifted phase range is at most 12*pi. Positivity of rho puts its mean inside that range, so every coordinate obeys |theta_i-theta_rho|<=12*pi. The closed edge inequalities and mean constraint make this bounded set closed.

The full closed storage sublevels on both source mean leaves are compact as well. For H<=E, nonnegativity of V gives Q<=E. With w_min=min_e W_e>0, Cauchy's inequality along a path of at most four edges yields

\[ |x_i-x_j|^2\le\frac{8E}{w_{\min}}. \]

The fixed positive weighted mean then bounds every |x_i-m_rho|<=sqrt(8*E/w_min). Together with the phase bounds, continuity of H proves compactness of each nonempty closed sublevel. This argument retains the actual conductances and means; it does not substitute an arithmetic mean or a unit-weight Laplacian.

There is no local minimum of V in Omega. Indeed a constrained critical point there has grad V=lambda*rho; translation invariance gives 1^T*grad V=0, hence lambda=0. At a local minimum its relative phase Hessian would be PSD. Since K*1=0, every phase test direction can be shifted by a common constant onto the weighted-mean tangent leaf without changing its curvature. This would make the full fine Hessian PSD, contradicting Section 13. Thus the no-minimum result applies on this actual phase leaf, including all possible singular candidates.

docs.title: 20. A strict phase sublevel must reach a principal boundary
docs.text:
Choose the source-specific threshold

\[ E_* = V_0+\frac{Q_0}{2}<h, \]
