To control the sign of the phase contribution, apply the existing barrier to the auxiliary state with x=0 and this same phase. Its Z is no larger than the original Z, so V(theta)-H_*>=0. It follows that each hypothetical stage has H^+-H_*>1/6400.

At the same time only two forms change, and the centering projection is nonexpansive. With x_max=2569/8192,

\[ Z^+\leq Z+\|h\|<1/256+\tfrac32(x_{\max}/12+e) <0.043107<1/16. \tag{13} \]

Thus the endpoint remains inside the declared identity ball while lying outside the previously certified storage sublevel. This is a conditional endpoint bound, not an executed response or a prediction of future escape. It identifies a limitation of the certificate, not a failure of TNFR.

There is also a useful closure restriction. Any later map that preserves this form and support, including phase/capacity-only IL/SHA actions, cannot restore H-H_*<1/6400 while staying inside this identity ball: the same form-storage floor persists and the auxiliary-state argument again gives V-H_*>=0. This does not exclude a different maintenance criterion, a form-changing word, or separately admitted organizations. It avoids executing a phase-only closure merely to retest this already unavailable certificate.

docs.title: 6.2 Sharpening the same scalar storage cannot resolve the gap
docs.text:
The obstruction is stronger than a loose constant in the previous barrier. Let sigma equal +1 on the ten A nodes and -1 on the ten B nodes, and put s=r/sqrt(20). For any prescribed post-event rho^+-weighted means, choose

\[ x_b=\mu_x^+\mathbf1,\qquad \theta_b=\theta_*+s\sigma+c\mathbf1, \qquad c=\mu_\theta^+-\frac{\rho^{+T}(\theta_*+s\sigma)}{R^+}. \tag{14} \]

This state has both required means and Z_b=r. Common translations affect neither Z nor H. The forty original edges and the internal A0 edge retain their reference phase gaps. Only the four cross edges change, from zero to a gap of magnitude 2s. Thus

\[ H_b-H_*=4(1-\cos 2s)\leq8s^2 =\tfrac25r^2=1/640. \tag{15} \]

This is smaller than both form-storage floors in (12). The minimum energy on the identity boundary with the new means is therefore below the actual hypothetical endpoint energy. No sharper lower estimate of that same boundary energy can certify this endpoint by an H-sublevel lying inside the ball.

Restricting to a connected sublevel component does not rescue that argument. Within the ball, every phase-edge cosine is positive: its reference wrapped gap is zero or has magnitude 2*pi/5, and its perturbation is at most sqrt(2)*r, with 2*pi/5+sqrt(2)*r<pi/2. The form Hessian is positive semidefinite as well. H is consequently convex along the segment from the interior endpoint to (14). This segment remains on the same two mean leaves and within the closed ball. Its energy never exceeds the larger endpoint energy, which is H^+. The H-sublevel component containing the reset endpoint already reaches the identity boundary.

This is a configuration-space accessibility argument, not a solution of (1) or evidence of actual escape. It excludes confinement by an H-sublevel, including its connected component, restricted to the two mean leaves for these endpoints. Additional invariants, directional bounds or controlled nonlinear dynamics could still settle retention. A phase/capacity-only closure with the form and support held also retains the floor in (12); while inside the ball it cannot recover this scalar-sublevel certificate. Other form-changing words and other identity definitions have not been excluded.

docs.title: 7. Live admission, projection and evidence boundaries
docs.text:
The selected capture matters. Its target stored pressures are positive and its retained scalar values pass the default optional strict VAL/NUL policies; an earlier inherited capture has a negative target pressure and fails VAL's strict pressure policy. Neither scalar check admits a complete word. The retained OZ history still has its own U2 debt; preceding IL does not prepay that later destabilizer. NUL has no active U1/U2 role and is neither a stabilizer nor a closing token. VAL followed by NUL is not thereby a complete word. Any future word must preserve the live prefix and use the shared grammar with rejection enabled.

Default factors 1+t and 1-t, t=1/(4*pi), have ideal product 1-t^2<1; they are not reciprocals. Even supplied reciprocal factors would not make the complete actions inverses: NUL rescales pressure, projection can lose information, and histories change. A soft projection is not generally a unit-Lipschitz map; asymmetric rails can also reverse the nominal direction of a NUL form reset. Reuse actual endpoints rather than a contraction label.

Runtime admission is shared across the direct and atomic scale proposals: the edge-aware flag uses Boolean admission; active clip mode, bounds and soft steepness use the shared clip-policy resolver; active strict scalar thresholds reject nonfinite and Boolean values. Configured soft steepness must reach the proposal. Inactive clipping is not consumed by the disabled form branch. Public execution retains its existing EPI preflight domain, which is narrower than the pure disabled-branch kernel. These checks do not turn supplied thresholds into derived universal safety or identity laws.

docs.title: 8. Implementation and verification owners
docs.text:
The shared scale kernel, direct dispatcher, atomic stage and strict preconditions own execution. The event contract owns transactional and observation boundaries. No parallel operator kernel, new pressure law, event selector or field reader is introduced here.

Algebraic controls use independent edge storage, exact rational means and the existing weighted-law reader. They distinguish complete work, untouched-neighbor phase response, stored products, common clocks, charge/mean differences, form-origin dependence and projection. Read-only source controls reconstruct existing primitive state and verify the margins in (11)--(13); they execute no new maintained-source proposal or trajectory. Runtime regressions separately check invalid domains, configured clipping and rollback. Testing owns selections.

These controls are distinct from the separate IL/OZ phase-certificate correction, which resolves the numerical subclaim while preserving the frozen 8/9 report. The directional maintenance study uses additional state and nonlinear information beyond this sublevel obstruction. No physical identification, spontaneous event occurrence or universal realization of all registered operators follows from this conditional action analysis.

docs.title: Exact and controlled form-phase reductions
docs.text:
Equivalent form/phase/memory representations, controlled slow-time comparison and its full-state capture handoff; hidden initialization and transient errors remain explicit.

Part of Sine pattern geometry and dissipative capture. Section numbers are stable across the collection; hypotheses and model changes remain local to each result.

docs.title: 28. Exact form, phase and memory representations
docs.text:
The completed composition, capture and prepared-entry results share more than their graph. They use the same reciprocal exchange, conserved means and phase potential. The following identities connect those results to the existing memory and resonance owners without introducing a new primitive coordinate, deleting the initial form information or assuming a slow phase approximation.

Retain finite connected simple unit support with at least two nodes, positive held capacities, e,w,beta>0, the declared clock and no forcing or events. Use A=KL, M=K^-1, W=1^T M1, and the weighted centering projector P_M=I-1*(1^T M)/W. The means mu_x and mu_theta are those of the actual state; the latter belongs to a chosen continuous phase lift. Uncertain relative sources retain one conserved pair of means per member, with their absolute common origins unobserved. Neither mean is replaced by a nominal value in the identities below.

docs.title: The sum coordinate retains the full joint state
docs.text:
In Section 27's variables tau=e*t, z=(b/e)P_Mx and eta=ab/e^2, define the mixed coordinate y=theta+z. The exact rows become

\[ \boxed{\qquad \theta'=A(y-\theta),\qquad y'=\eta KS(\theta). \qquad} \]

This change is invertible on consistent real lifts: z=y-theta, x=mu_x*1+(e/b)z, with 1^T Mz=0. Thus it retains both consumed coordinates and the conserved form mean. A change of circular representative sends (theta,y) to (theta+2*pi*m,y+2*pi*m) for the same integer vector m; their real difference is unchanged. Equivalently, retain real z and circular exp(i*y), from which exp(i*theta)=exp(i*y)*exp(-i*z) is reconstructed.

Treating theta and y as two independently wrapped phase vectors loses information. On the unit P2 with unit capacities, K=I. The preparations theta=0,z=0 and theta=0,z=(2*pi,-2*pi) give the same two separately wrapped phase vectors, but their scaled phase rates are respectively 0 and A z=(4*pi,-4*pi). The real form contrast has been discarded by that wrapping, although it is consumed by the phase row.

Nor does y alone close the dynamics. On the same P2, y=0 can arise from theta=z=0, giving y'=0, or from theta=(delta,-delta),z=(-delta,delta), giving y'=eta*(-sin(2*delta),sin(2*delta)). For 0<delta<pi/4 these rates differ even on the same conserved-mean leaf. A first-order law depending only on y therefore needs an additional approximation or restricted invariant family.

The cancellation behind this coordinate is already used operationally in the hidden-state inverse: dot(x)+(e/b)*dot(theta)=aKS removes the form-gradient contribution from paired rate observations. Its time derivative supplies the paired acceleration channel there. The present transformation and the entry estimate reorganize that same complete-law identity; they do not select a new pressure law from those observations.

docs.title: Exact elimination gives second-order phase and retained memory
docs.text:
In the original clock, differentiate the complete phase row and use the form row. The following second-order identity and velocity reconstruction also hold at e=0, with positive w,beta and held positive capacities; they do not use the preceding change of variables dividing by e. With the actual ordered matrix products this gives

\[ \boxed{\ddot\theta+eA\dot\theta=abAKS(\theta),\qquad \dot\theta(0)=bAP_Mx(0).} \]

The constraint 1^T M dot(theta)=0 must remain. An unconstrained second-order equation on all phase lifts would also permit a constant common phase velocity, which the original positive-capacity law does not supply. On the weighted-mean-zero space, A is invertible and the phase velocity reconstructs the full centered form as P_Mx=b^(-1)A^(-1)dot(theta). The constant form mean must be retained separately if the original absolute form is needed. This is a same-information representation, not a removal of a state variable.

docs.title: What an emergent-form hypothesis must distinguish
docs.text:
Formation of an organized pattern from joint evolution is different from an all-state instantaneous identity x=F(theta,nu,support,p). The latter does not hold for the admitted conservative sine law. On unit P2, take e=0,w=beta=nu_1=nu_2=1 and theta=(0,0). The states x=(0,0) and x=(q,-q), with nonzero real q, have the same phase, capacity, support, form mean and instantaneous pressure p=(0,0). Their phase rates are respectively zero and (2q/pi,-2q/pi). The common observed coordinates therefore do not determine form or the ensuing response.

Phase velocity, together with the original form mean, supplies the missing information through the inverse above. This uses the independently specified phase law, not the nodal identity alone. At zero loss its exact history representation is

\[ \theta(t)=\theta(0)+btAP_Mx(0) +ab\int_0^t(t-s)AKS(\theta(s))\,ds. \]

The initial form remains an independent source, or equivalently the initial phase velocity. This equation does not derive it from phase alone. At positive loss, pressure computed from the full state can encode form differences; that does not make such pressure an independent measurement or remove the state information needed to compute it. A special invariant or controlled slow family could restrict form in terms of other variables, but its preparation, domain and error require separate proof. Neither global reconstruction nor impossibility of every restricted family follows.

Thus the supported synergy is a same-information description of relative form as phase-motion information. The stronger claim that primitive form emerges from the other instantaneous parameters remains unestablished. The channel-geometry analysis keeps this state question separate from unequal response of the two channels.

Alternatively, variation of constants and integration give the exact nonlinear Volterra equation for e>0

\[ \boxed{\begin{aligned} \theta(t)={}&\theta(0) +\frac be\left(I-e^{-eAt}\right)P_Mx(0)\\ &+\frac{ab}{e}\int_0^t \left(I-e^{-eA(t-s)}\right)KS(\theta(s))\,ds. \end{aligned}} \]

The source term is the retained initial form, not an external input. The phase current in the integral uses the actual earlier phase state; this is not a fixed linear convolution in theta. Differentiating the identity with its supplied initial state recovers the second-order row, and reconstructing form recovers the original joint system. Global Lipschitz continuity of the full sine field supplies uniqueness. The projector could be omitted only from the first source term because I-exp(-eAt) annihilates the common form mode; displaying it makes the mean accounting explicit.

No commutation of K with L is used. In particular AK=KLK, whereas KA=K^2L is generally different. The corresponding phase-velocity memory operator is

\[ \mathcal R_e(s)=A e^{-eAs}K =K^{1/2}B e^{-eBs}K^{1/2},\qquad B=K^{1/2}LK^{1/2}. \]

It is symmetric positive semidefinite for each nonnegative lag, but its individual entries need not be nonnegative. Spectral integration gives

\[ \int_0^\infty\mathcal R_e(s)\,ds =\frac1e\left(K-\frac{\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}}W\right). \]

Acting on a sine-current vector, whose ordinary sum is zero, this integrated operator gives KS/e. This explains the frozen-history gain behind a candidate slow phase law; it does not bound the error made by replacing the moving history by its current value. It also does not remove the initial source or justify exchanging an infinite-time limit with a constitutive limit.

The single-intermediary sine owner already derives a nonlinear second-order representation and derivative-free Volterra memory, including the hidden initial state and moving visible boundary. The general elimination owner owns the variation-of-constants principle and its source obligation. The identities here specialize that principle to eliminating the entire form coordinate of this complete nonlinear sine model. They neither turn the existing signed intermediary kernel into a positive-entry kernel nor transfer a pure-diffusion or conservative-memory conclusion between models.

docs.title: The nonlinear storage representation contains the existing resonance pencil
docs.text:
Remove the conserved origins, and put

\[ h=K^{-1/2}\mathbf1,\quad\mathcal Q=h^\perp,\quad \xi=K^{-1/2}P_Mx,\quad \vartheta=K^{-1/2}P_M\theta,\quad \Phi(\vartheta)=V(K^{1/2}\vartheta). \]

The symmetric matrix B above is positive definite on Q; all inverse matrices in this paragraph act only there. Since grad(Phi)=-K^(1/2)S, the exact nonlinear transformed rows and their equivalent second-order equation are

\[ \dot\xi=-eB\xi-a\nabla\Phi(\vartheta),\qquad \dot\vartheta=bB\xi,\qquad B^{-1}\ddot\vartheta+e\dot\vartheta +ab\nabla\Phi(\vartheta)=0. \]

Their storage and loss are still the original quantities:

\[ b^2E=\frac12\dot\vartheta^{\mathsf T}B^{-1}\dot\vartheta +ab\Phi(\vartheta),\qquad \frac{d}{dt}(b^2E)=-e\|\dot\vartheta\|^2. \]

The velocity contribution is the original form storage in different coordinates. The derived quotient matrix B^-1 depends on the graph and held capacities; this supplies no identification of capacity with inverse physical mass. Initial velocity, nonlinear phase history and the conserved origins remain part of the model.

At a critical phase geometry with Hessian H, the Hessian of Phi is C=K^(1/2)HK^(1/2). Linearizing the displayed equation gives precisely the existing full-support resonance pencil, B^-1*ddot(vartheta)+e*dot(vartheta)+ab*C*vartheta=0 for perturbations. The matrices B and C need not commute, so scalar cycle discriminants still cannot classify a general attachment. Strict acute-sector convexity, equilibrium recovery and the full storage capture barrier use the same phase curvature; the nonnegative velocity/form term is why a phase-only storage check cannot replace the capture certificate.

docs.title: A phase-flat preparation distinguishes the full law from phase descent
docs.text:
Take equal initial phases and any nonconstant initial form on the retained connected graph. Then S(0)=0, H(0)=L and

\[ V(0)=\dot V(0)=0,\qquad \ddot V(0)=b^2(Ax(0))^{\mathsf T}L(Ax(0))>0, \qquad \dot E(0)=-e(Lx(0))^{\mathsf T}K(Lx(0))<0. \]

For strict positivity, Ax(0) has zero weighted mean. If it were a constant vector, it would vanish; positivity of K and connectedness would then force x(0) constant, contrary to preparation. Thus phase potential initially increases while total storage decreases. The form reservoir and reciprocal phase row account for both signs under one law.

In contrast, the candidate phase-gradient flow dpsi/dsigma=KS(psi) initialized at that same uniform theta(0) remains there by uniqueness. It would discard the prepared form information. Initializing a proposed comparison from theta(0)+z(0) retains that information, but the exact identities alone do not prove closeness to this comparison flow. Section 29 derives the finite-horizon error bound while retaining the initial transient. A later capture handoff, support creation and physical identification remain separate obligations.

The full-law equivalence controls differentiate the shared field with interval jets, check the two opposite storage signs and the failure of a sum-coordinate-only closure, and retain noncommuting capacity/Laplacian products. Independent numerical quadrature checks the nonlinear memory identity along a complete trajectory; it is an equivalence check, not a reserved-response prediction or the analytic proof.

docs.title: 29. A controlled fast-form and slow-phase comparison
docs.text: The exact representations in Section 28 permit a quantitative comparison with a first-order phase flow. This is an approximation theorem for the same complete sine law, with an explicit transient and error. It does not install that reference flow as a replacement pressure or remove the prepared form information.

docs.title: Complete state, reference initialization and clocks
docs.text:
Fix the finite connected unit support, positive held K, positive beta and positive complete-law coefficients e,w. Retain Section 27's M=K^-1, A=KL, alpha=b/e, z=alpha*P_Mx, tau=e*t and eta=ab/e^2=beta*alpha^2. For the actual initial state write z_0=z(0) and take a proved bound Z>=||z_0||_M. Define the slow time and reference on consistent phase lifts by

\[ \sigma=\eta\tau=\frac{ab}{e}t,\qquad \frac{d\psi}{d\sigma}=f(\psi),\qquad f(\theta)=KS(\theta),\qquad \psi(0)=\theta(0)+z_0. \]

Both the complete and reference fields are globally Lipschitz, so their solutions exist uniquely for all finite times. The reference is initialized with the actual retained form contribution, not only the initial phase. As in Section 28, the mixed coordinate uses real z_0 and consistent lifts; wrapping its two summands independently would discard information.

Let lambda>0 be a certified weighted quotient gap for A, and set

\[ F=\left(\sum_i\nu_i d_i\right)^{1/2},\qquad \ell=2\max_i\nu_i. \]

The earlier forcing bound gives ||f(theta)||_M<=F globally. Its derivative is -KH(theta), where H is the cosine-weighted phase Hessian. The edge formula gives -B<=K^(1/2)H(theta)K^(1/2)<=B for B=K^(1/2)LK^(1/2). The similar matrix KL has Gershgorin intervals [0,2*nu_i], so the symmetric matrix B has norm at most ell. Integrating the derivative along a segment therefore proves the global Lipschitz estimate ||f(u)-f(v)||_M<=ell*||u-v||_M. This bound needs no acute phase domain for either path or the segment between them.

docs.title: Explicit composite, phase and form bounds
docs.text:
For a supplied finite sigma>=0, put tau=sigma/eta and D(tau)=exp(-A*tau). Define

\[ \boxed{\begin{aligned} R(\tau)&=\frac{\eta F}{\lambda} \left(1-e^{-\lambda\tau}\right),\\ C(\sigma)&= \frac{\eta(\ell Z+F)}{\lambda+\eta\ell} \left(e^{\ell\sigma}-e^{-\lambda\tau}\right). \end{aligned}} \]

Then the exact complete solution and its reference satisfy

\[ \boxed{\begin{aligned} \|z(\tau)-D(\tau)z_0\|_M&\le R(\tau),\\ \|\theta(\tau)+D(\tau)z_0-\psi(\sigma)\|_M&\le C(\sigma),\\ \|\theta(\tau)-\psi(\sigma)\|_M &\le Ze^{-\lambda\tau}+C(\sigma). \end{aligned}} \]

The middle quantity is the composite correction. It retains the fast initial form contribution instead of calling the corrected angle the actual phase. For y=theta+z, the same estimates also give ||y(tau)-psi(sigma)||_M<=C(sigma)+R(tau).

The form estimate follows from the exact variation-of-constants identity

\[ z(\tau)=D(\tau)z_0+ \eta\int_0^\tau D(\tau-s)f(\theta(s))\,ds. \]

All integrand vectors have zero weighted mean. Thus the quotient semigroup bound ||D(s)||_M<=exp(-lambda*s) applies to them and gives R. Section 28's exact phase memory, now in scaled time, gives

\[ \theta(\tau)+D(\tau)z_0 =\theta(0)+z_0+ \eta\int_0^\tau\left[I-D(\tau-s)\right]f(\theta(s))\,ds. \]

Subtract the reference integral equation. If q(tau)=theta(tau)+D(tau)z_0-psi(eta*tau), the forcing and Lipschitz bounds imply

\[ \|q(\tau)\|_M\le \eta\ell\int_0^\tau\|q(s)\|_M\,ds+ \frac{\eta(\ell Z+F)}{\lambda} \left(1-e^{-\lambda\tau}\right). \]

Here the ell*Z term retains the initial transient inside theta-psi=q-D(s)z_0; the F term bounds the remaining memory integral. The scalar comparison function with zero initial value solves c'=eta*ell*c+eta*(ell*Z+F)*exp(-lambda*tau). Its explicit solution is the displayed C, proving the composite bound by Gronwall's inequality. The uncorrected phase bound then follows by the triangle inequality. No phase linearization, commuting K,L assumption or sampled response enters this argument.

Conversion back to the original form coordinate is also explicit:

\[ \left\|P_Mx(t)-e^{-eAt}P_Mx(0)\right\|_M \le\frac ae\frac F\lambda \left(1-e^{-\lambda\tau}\right) =\sqrt{\beta\eta}\frac F\lambda \left(1-e^{-\lambda\tau}\right). \]

Thus the original form remainder after its homogeneous transient is O(sqrt(eta)) at fixed support, K and beta. A small scaled z remainder alone would not establish this original-coordinate statement. The homogeneous form term remains until its own transient has decayed.

docs.title: Uniform finite-time meaning and the retained storage budget
docs.text:
Fix a finite slow-time horizon Sigma, the support, K, beta and a uniform bound Z on the scaled initial form. For 0<=sigma<=Sigma,

\[ C(\sigma)\le \eta\frac{\ell Z+F}{\lambda}e^{\ell\Sigma}. \]

This is a uniform O(eta) composite comparison including the initial instant. It is not uniform O(eta) proximity of the actual phase from that instant: exactly theta(0)-psi(0)=-z_0. For any fixed sigma_0>0, the uncorrected estimate on [sigma_0,Sigma] instead has the additional transient Z*exp(-lambda*sigma_0/eta). More generally, the finite displayed inequalities decide whether a chosen transient is sufficiently small, without retuning the requested horizon.

The original-clock comparison time is

\[ t=\frac{\sigma}{e\eta} =\beta\pi^2\frac e{w^2}\sigma. \]

As eta changes, the constitutive ratio changes; this is not just a common clock rescaling. Keeping a nonzero scaled preparation fixed also retains the original initial storage

\[ E(0)=\frac{\beta}{2\eta}z_0^{\mathsf T}Lz_0 +\beta V(\theta(0)). \]

Its form term grows as 1/eta. For uncertain preparations the expression and its enclosing budget apply to every actual member, rather than to its nominal source alone.

docs.title: Means, uncertain sources and phase potential
docs.text:
Since 1^T M f=1^T S=0, the reference conserves its weighted phase mean. Its initialization has the same weighted phase mean as the complete trajectory because z_0 is centered. Common form shifts cancel from z_0; common phase shifts move the actual and reference solutions together. All comparison differences and the composite correction have zero weighted mean on the selected lift.

For a SineRelativePattern, reuse Section 27's original residual set and its weighted initial norm bound. Each member is compared with its own reference initialized at that member's theta(0)+z_0. A uniform Z makes the displayed error uniform over the family but does not replace these references by a single nominal reference trajectory. Doing that would require a separate bound on the initialization differences. Unknown absolute origins and memberwise conserved means remain explicit.

The potential satisfies the global bound |V(u)-V(v)|<=F*||u-v||_M, since ||grad(V)||_(M^-1)=||KS||_M<=F. Hence

\[ |V(\theta(\tau))-V(\psi(\sigma))| \le F\left[Ze^{-\lambda\tau}+C(\sigma)\right]. \]

The reference itself obeys dV(psi)/dsigma=-S(psi)^T K S(psi)<=0. This does not make the actual phase potential monotone: Section 28's phase-flat, nonconstant-form preparation has strictly positive initial second phase-potential derivative while total storage decreases. Initializing the reference only at that uniform phase would leave it at consensus and discard the preparation mechanism; the shifted initialization and explicit transient resolve that mismatch in the comparison theorem.

docs.title: Shared certificate and bounded numerical controls
docs.text:
bound_sine_slow_phase accepts an admitted exact or relative source and a supplied rational slow time. It reuses the complete-law preparation admission, weighted norm and exact reversible gap owners, and returns outward analytic comparison bounds. The scaled and original times are enclosed directly from their mathematical-pi formulas; these are enclosures of the declared comparison instant, not a new class of independently uncertain times. The reader runs neither the full trajectory nor the reference phase solver. It does not issue an endpoint capture or final-basin verdict.

The reduction tests freeze a small heterogeneous support with edges (0,1),(1,2),(2,3),(0,2), capacities (1,3/2,2,5/4) and beta=2. The primary constructor weight ratio is 16:1; the stored normalized coefficients remain authoritative, with exact ratio w/e=1/16. The declared preparation is x=(beta*e/w)*(1/2,-3/4,5/4,-1) and theta=(1/8,-1/4,1/2,-3/8), with slow horizon 1/16. A separately fixed 8:1 comparison retains the same scaled initial form and checks the feedback-parameter dependence. Independent SciPy integrations of the complete and reference rows cross-check the inequalities under the test's explicit numerical settings; they are not validated trajectory enclosures or a search over sources, ratios or horizons. The analytic certificate does not depend on their sampled responses.

The error grows with the declared slow horizon and is not an infinite-time theorem. It proves neither a final basin match nor an exchange of the limits eta->0 and t->infinity. Section 30 supplies a separate capture criterion that admits the actual full-state endpoint, including the form remainder and all sector margins. The result controls a mechanism within the supplied law and preparation; it does not select that law, support, source budget or physical interpretation.

docs.title: A conditional comparison using acute geometry and dissipation
docs.text:
The two-port transit proof derives a different finite-horizon estimate for its unit-capacity, beta-one model. On a common acute chart, the slow phase field is dissipative in the degree metric. Integrating the complete law's storage loss bounds the squared scaled-form norm over time, yielding a comparison error that grows with the square root of the slow horizon. A strict first-exit argument must establish that both the actual and mixed phases stay in that chart. The nominal reference also retains its explicit initialization mismatch against every actual source member.

That conditional argument supplies a finite deformation result with the original form coordinate retained. It does not replace the global, possibly nonacute comparison above or establish eventual capture. Its model-specific coefficients and prepared phase origins do not transfer without admission of the new complete model.

docs.title: 30. Full-state capture from controlled phase geometry
docs.text: Section 29 bounds the difference from a reference flow but does not by itself locate that reference at the requested endpoint. A sufficient handoff needs both a justified reference neighborhood and the remaining original form storage. The following construction supplies these from the admitted preparation and an exactly verified stationary phase geometry. It requires neither a supplied response endpoint nor a reference solver.

docs.title: A proved reference neighborhood from the preparation
docs.text:
Retain all hypotheses and notation of Section 29. Supply exact rational node turns q_i, in the source node order, and put phi_*=2*pi*q on the selected real lift. Require every principal target edge angle delta_*e to lie strictly between -pi/2 and pi/2, and require S(phi_*)=0. The shared target owner verifies these hypotheses using the exact acute geometry and sine cancellation; a floating residual close to zero does not prove criticality. This implemented algebraic admission is sufficient, not a classification of all possible sine equilibria.

For each actual preparation member, shift phi_* by a common constant so that its weighted mean equals that of theta(0). Write the resulting lift as phi_*^m. Its phase geometry and potential V_* are unchanged. The reference psi(0)=theta(0)+alpha*P_Mx(0) has this same weighted mean. Choose a proved bound

\[ D_0\ge \left\|P_M\left(\theta(0)+\alpha P_Mx(0)-\phi_*\right)\right\|_M. \]

Since f(phi_*^m)=0, the constant curve phi_*^m solves the reference equation. The global Lipschitz bound from Section 29 and Gronwall give

\[ \|\psi(\sigma)-\phi_*^m\|_M \le D_{\rm ref}(\sigma):=e^{\ell\sigma}D_0. \]

This estimate assumes no contraction or acute evolution of the reference. The supplied stationary geometry is a proof reference; it is not inserted into the complete law or assigned to the evolving state.

For a relative source, retain exactly Section 27's original residual family. If its componentwise form and phase error radii are epsilon_xi,epsilon_thetai, a uniform choice is

\[ \begin{aligned} D_0={}& \left\|P_M\left(\theta_{\rm nom} +\alpha P_Mx_{\rm nom}-\phi_*\right)\right\|_M\\ &+\left(\sum_i m_i\epsilon_{\theta i}^2\right)^{1/2} +\alpha\left(\sum_i m_i\epsilon_{x i}^2\right)^{1/2}, \qquad m_i=M_{ii}. \end{aligned} \]

This follows from the triangle inequality and the contractivity of the weighted orthogonal projection P_M. Every member keeps its own reference, mean-matched target and conserved means. Unknown common origins cancel before bounding the mismatch; no absolute phase or form origin is inferred. The estimate uses the selected consistent phase lifts, with the chart and quotient distinctions from Section 28.

docs.title: The actual endpoint and its complete storage
docs.text:
At the supplied slow time sigma, set tau=sigma/eta and define

\[ \begin{aligned} Q(\sigma)&=Ze^{-\lambda\tau}+C(\sigma),\\ \rho(\sigma)&=D_{\rm ref}(\sigma)+Q(\sigma),\\ X(\sigma)&=e^{-\lambda\tau}N_x+ \frac ae\frac F\lambda\left(1-e^{-\lambda\tau}\right), \qquad N_x\ge\|P_Mx(0)\|_M. \end{aligned} \]

Section 29 proves that the actual endpoint satisfies ||theta(t)-phi_*^m||_M<=rho and ||P_Mx(t)||_M<=X, where t=sigma/(e*eta). The phase bound includes the initial transient; substituting only the composite error C would not prove this statement. The form bound is in the original coordinate, with its conversion factor retained.

For an edge ij, write k_i=K_ii and g_ij=sqrt(k_i+k_j). Weighted duality gives

\[ \left|(\theta_j-\theta_i) -(\phi_{*j}^m-\phi_{*i}^m)\right|\le g_{ij}\rho, \qquad |x_j-x_i|\le g_{ij}X. \]

Thus a sufficient strict acute margin on every edge is

\[ \boxed{\quad |\delta_{*ij}|+g_{ij}\rho<\frac\pi2 \quad\text{for every retained edge}.\quad} \]

Use the integer edge offsets that reduce the supplied target lift to its principal acute angles. They place every enclosed actual endpoint in the target's cycle-period sector, without inferring a future unwrapping from samples.

A useful storage bound retains the correlations lost by independent edge intervals. Let h=theta(t)-phi_*^m. The phase Hessian satisfies H<=L globally, since every edge cosine is at most one. Taylor's integral formula and the exact criticality of the target therefore give

\[ V(\phi_*^m+h) =V_*+\int_0^1(1-s)h^{\mathsf T}H(\phi_*^m+sh)h\,ds \le V_*+\frac12h^{\mathsf T}Lh \le V_*+\frac\ell2\rho^2. \]

The linear term vanishes because grad V(phi_*^m)=0. The segment need not remain acute for this upper bound. Likewise x^T Lx<=ell*||P_Mx||_M^2, so the complete storage obeys

\[ \boxed{\qquad E(t)\le E_{\rm handoff}:= \frac\ell2X^2+\beta\left(V_*+\frac\ell2\rho^2\right). \qquad} \]

This uses the same cancellation principle as local recovery, now with a preparation-derived phase neighborhood. Bounding every cosine separately can lose that cancellation and fail to establish a margin that the correlated bound proves. The admitted endpoint set retains the norm and storage constraints together with the edge intervals and memberwise mean leaf; arbitrary corners of the independent outer intervals need not obey the correlated storage bound. Global existence of the complete law makes the set nonempty for every admitted preparation member.

docs.title: Handoff to the whole-sector theorem
docs.text:
Let B_k be the shared certified lower bound for the phase potential on every boundary face of the target sector, as in Section 26. If all strict edge margins above hold and

\[ \boxed{\qquad E_{\rm handoff}<\beta B_k,\qquad} \]

then Section 26 applies to the actual full-state endpoint of every source member. Subsequent complete evolution stays in that sector and converges on its conserved-mean leaf to its unique acute equilibrium. The admitted target already supplies the stationary geometry in that sector, so uniqueness identifies the limiting phase geometry with it. The theorem does not assume that geometry was the initial winding or that the reference and actual paths shared their earlier sectors.

certify_sine_slow_capture recomputes the preparation and slow comparison, admits the exact target, and passes producer-proved edge and correlated storage bounds to the shared sector-capture owner. The outer report retains the enclosed original endpoint time; its nested capture is neither a timestamped observation nor a sampled forecast. Outward rational arithmetic encloses the pi, trigonometric, norm and exponential quantities. Malformed inputs are rejected; insufficient strict margins return unavailable. An unavailable sufficient condition proves neither instability nor impossibility.

docs.title: Fixed analytic controls and scope
docs.text:
The handoff tests reuse Section 27's published C5 preparation unchanged: nu_i=beta=1, e=1023/1024, w=1/1024, x_i(0)=4092*(i-2) and theta_i(0)=0 for i=0,...,4. The supplied target is q_i=(i-2)/5 and the fixed slow time is 1/16. Its initial form budget remains 160*1023^2; neither that budget nor the ratio is retuned to obtain the handoff. The analytic bounds give

\[ \begin{aligned} D_0&<0.074249,&\rho&<0.084137,\\ \frac\ell2X^2&<0.000002028,& E_{\rm handoff}&<3.461996083,\\ B_k&>3.469266270,& \beta B_k-E_{\rm handoff}&>0.00727018. \end{aligned} \]

All edge margins are positive. The same previously fixed independent radii epsilon_x=1/16 and epsilon_theta=1/65536 also pass, with total storage below 3.462017026 and margin above 0.00724924. These are analytic endpoint certificates, with no integrated reference or complete trajectory used as their producer. Initial zero winding is separately known for these preparations, so their captured nonzero sector also establishes acquisition. The general API does not assume zero initial winding and therefore does not label every capture an acquisition.

Here the declared original time is approximately 646182.7393 structural units, obtained from t=beta*pi^2*e*sigma/w^2. This fixed handoff is not an optimized entry time or a replacement for the earlier tau=100 entry certificate. Controls with resolved phase but excessive remaining form storage, and with unresolved phase margins, remain unavailable under their respective sufficient conditions.

The result connects one justified reference geometry to complete-state capture at a finite declared instant. It supplies neither autonomous support creation, selection of the preparation or target, a unique constitutive law, nor a physical identification. It also does not turn the finite comparison into a uniform infinite-time approximation.

docs.title: Hierarchy-to-contact composition under an explicit intermediate law
docs.text:
This owner studies actual THOL birth followed by parent-target UM. The isolated prefix uses an explicitly supplied frozen-isolate completion; the connected sine reader is not silently widened. The result concerns a conditional mechanism on an open connected-state family, not the formation or maintenance of the previously studied winding organizations.

The research program owns status. The hierarchy owner, actual UM owner and native birth/transport comparison retain their contracts. Their laws and earlier finite responses are not substituted for the model below.

docs.title: 1. Protocol fixed before event evaluation
docs.text:
The analytical source is the ordered two-node graph (0,1) with one unit edge, parent target 0, and independent coordinates

\[ \frac{31}{64}<A=x_0<\frac{33}{64},\quad \frac{47}{64}<B=x_1<\frac{49}{64},\quad \frac{31}{16}<\nu_0,\nu_1<\frac{33}{16},\quad \theta_0=\gamma,\quad\theta_1=\gamma+\phi,\quad \frac7{64}<\phi<\frac9{64}. \tag{1} \]

Phases use one declared lift; gamma is a common origin. This is a regular acute connected-state family, not a claimed formed composite identity. The represented nominal control is (A,B,nu_0,nu_1,gamma,phi) equal to (1/2,3/4,2,2,0,1/8).

The complete word is OZ -> THOL -> UM -> SHA, always targeting only the original parent. Use initialized nonzero form, supplied AL,IL history and zero initial debt; validate the whole word and every live prefix with the core grammar and GRAMMAR_REJECTION_MODE="raise". Enable strict operator preconditions. Begin with empty hierarchy and no child records. The original parent and neighbor have sense index zero through the declared existing default; the newborn has the same default. No learned sense observation is claimed. Pressure is refreshed from the selected complete law at boundaries.

Keep THOL's default positive acceleration gain, default threshold 0.1, metabolism enabled with its default gains and the default child-capacity damping. The source has an admitted three-sample parent history with abs(A_hat)>tau; this is an independent event-admission premise. The static runtime control supplies [(0,A),(1,A-1/4),(3,A)], whose acceleration is exactly 1/4, and structural time 3. These are manufactured reader inputs, not observed samples from the selected law. Section 3 separately proves that genuine sufficiently short same-law windows are possible in (1).

All four UM flags are true: bidirectional phase updates, capacity blending, stored-pressure relief and functional links. Fix all three active UM factors to 1/8. Keep the default compatibility threshold pi/(pi+1), phase limits DELTA_PHI_MAX=UM_MAX_PHASE_DIFF=pi/2, candidate count zero (all candidates), mode proximity, execution seed 17 and no restricted _node_sample. The candidate inventory is rebuilt after birth. No parent-child edge or conductance is externally installed.

Use SHA factor 1/2, SHA_MIN_VF=1/8, EPI_LATENT_MAX=1, form rails [0,1] and hard clipping. Inputs remain interior where those rails are consumed. Other consumed configuration retains its shared canonical defaults. Retain node order, actual aliases, event records and phase lifts. The frozen-isolate law below supplies the intermediate refresh; the ordinary connected reader must still reject the full born graph.

The prospective discriminator is an actual connected child with negative phase rate, positive form rate and positive form acceleration, against a separately specified null with UM_FUNCTIONAL_LINKS=False. The null uses the same word, source, history, old-neighbor phase/capacity reset and child construction, but retains the isolated child under the frozen law. It is not a failed coupling attempt relabeled as an interaction.

No continuous trajectory, retained producer, parameter search or experimental physical comparison is part of this protocol. Exact-real family statements and finite represented endpoint checks remain distinct. Operator occurrence, history provenance and a physical clock are supplied, not inferred.

docs.title: 2. Prefix law and the connected restriction
docs.text:
On each connected component with at least two nodes, retain the selected weighted-form/bare-phase completion

\[ q=L_Wx,\quad S_i=\sum_{j\sim i}\sin(\theta_j-\theta_i),\quad m_i=\frac{\nu_i}{\pi d_i},\qquad p_i=\frac{S_i}{\pi d_i},\qquad \dot x_i=m_iS_i,\quad\dot\theta_i=m_iq_i. \tag{2} \]

Support is finite, simple, loop-free and undirected. Conductances and held capacities are nonnegative; the constructive family has positive ones. There is no forcing or continuous loss. Bare degree counts edges, including zero-conductance support; it is not weighted strength. At every isolate explicitly declare p=xdot=thetadot=0, held form, phase and capacity. This is the supplied frozen-isolate completion, not a value assigned to the undefined quotient 0/0 in (2).

The shared detached owner keeps bound_relational_sine_support_exchange restricted to connected support and exposes the distinct opt-in bound_relational_sine_frozen_isolates comparison. Such a report supplies instantaneous fields for the declared law; it installs no integrator, event selector or autonomous hierarchy mechanism.

Use edge-only storage

\[ H=\frac12\sum_{\{i,j\}}W_{ij}(x_i-x_j)^2 +\sum_{\{i,j\}}[1-\cos(\theta_j-\theta_i)]. \tag{3} \]

Each nontrivial component conserves H under (2); isolates contribute no term. An intrinsic child storage would change the birth budget and is outside this completion. With positive capacities, inverse-capacity means are defined on each nontrivial component using rho_i=d_i/nu_i. Frozen child coordinates are independent constants; assigning them zero mean weight merely ignores them and is not a complete observation of the enlarged state.

This declaration admits the original graph, the actual isolated birth prefix and the connected UM successor under one explicit piecewise state-domain contract. On the final connected support its fields are exactly those of (2). No elapsed evolution is inserted between events by this admission theorem.

docs.title: 3. True history compatibility and every prefix's live domain
docs.text:
Write u=B-A>0. Before any event, the parent has positive selected pressure sin(phi)/pi and its true form acceleration from the complete two-row law is

\[ \ddot x_0= rac{ u_0( u_0+ u_1)}{\pi^2}\,u\cos\phi. ag{4} \]

In (1), nu_0,nu_1>19/10, u>1/5, cos(phi)>99/100 and pi^2<10. Thus (4) exceeds 35739/250000>7/50>1/10. This has a strict margin on the whole open source box. Smooth local backward flow exists in its fixed finite-dimensional law. For sufficiently short three-sample windows ending at each source, the divided difference converges to (4), so genuine same-law acceleration evidence can exceed the default THOL threshold. The window can remain inside the form rails and phase sector by continuity. No particular sampling interval, numerical record or source acquisition is proved by this existence statement.

The shared history reader still has to admit the actual supplied record. The synthetic nominal acceleration 1/4 is not the nominal constitutive value 2*cos(1/8)/pi^2. Their agreement on a strict threshold decision does not authenticate the supplied record as a trajectory. Timestamped history, the structural clock, signed form and explicit event records remain separate execution inputs.

OZ preserves source form, phase, capacity and support. Its stored-pressure write is erased by the declared refresh, so the physical source and (4) are unchanged when THOL is considered. THOL's strict form/capacity minima, positive-pressure gate, nonzero degree, temporal history and depth conditions all have the stated margins. Its threshold crossing proposes one child c. The default metabolic input has one neighbor, hence exact-real circular phase variance zero and form gradient u. The unclipped child is

\[ z=x_c= rac3{10}A+ rac{u}{2\pi},\qquad u_c= rac{19}{20} u_0,\qquad heta_c=\gamma,\qquad p_c=0. ag{5} \]

This is the ideal form of the actual construction; the runtime materializes its declared coefficients, circular variance and endpoint arithmetic. It creates no edge. The source interval gives

\[ rac{113}{640}<z< rac{129}{640},\qquad D=A-z> rac{181}{640}> rac7{25}. ag{6} \]

For example, 1/7<1/(2*pi)<1/6 proves these bounds from (1). They keep the child strictly inside the clipping rails. The old component is unchanged apart from stored pressure and context; the explicit isolate law supplies the newborn's zero rows and pressure. A connected-only refresh at this prefix would reject rather than advance to UM.

UM must target the original parent. Its old neighbor 1 passes U3, both before and after the phase proposal. The child as the first target has no existing neighbor and fails the mandatory U3 gate, irrespective of its equal phase. Including it in an all-node atomic UM stage rejects the stage as well. Parent targeting is therefore a substantive prefix condition, not a label.

All live nonneighbor candidates are enumerated after birth. For this P2 source the actual child is the parent's only nonneighbor; no other potential edge is suppressed. A stale prebirth node sample would omit it, and an otherwise valid UM call would not create a connected successor. Pre-event candidate phase and post-merge phase tests both apply. The hierarchy association itself does not bypass either test or the compatibility score.

The complete word provides the OZ context needed by THOL, uses THOL's stabilizing action before UM and closes with SHA. Live preconditions remain independent of whole-word validity. U5's hierarchy record is not a numerical parent/child coherence assessment; a newborn has no measured change-rate observation, so a numerical U5 assessment lacks a required input. U6 is a separate configured monitoring contract: its current comparison requires the same complete node support in both observations. At birth the before-state has no child observation, so that comparison is unsupported. Supplying an invented zero baseline would not repair the missing observation. The actual word and stage gates pass; neither these gates nor equation (4) supplies the missing U5/U6 evidence or selects an occurrence.

docs.title: 4. The actual parent-target UM map and its connected domain
docs.text:
The old compatible neighborhood contains only node 1. The bidirectional consensus phase of the parent and its old neighbor is gamma+phi/2 on the declared lift. The child was not a neighbor when proposals were read. With the supplied push and capacity factor 1/8, ideal endpoints are

\[ \delta= rac{\phi}{16},\quad heta_0^+=\gamma+\delta,\quad heta_1^+=\gamma+ rac{15\phi}{16},\quad heta_c^+=\gamma,\qquad n:= u_0^+= rac{7 u_0+ u_1}{8}. ag{7} \]

The other capacities remain nu_1,nu_c; every form remains A,B,z. The old edge gap contracts to 7*phi/8; the prospective new gap is delta. Both are strictly acute. The child's capacity must not be inserted into the same-call neighbor mean in (7).

The parent stored-pressure relief uses the old compatible neighbor and its final gap: its multiplier is 1-(1/8)*(1-(7*phi/8)/pi). This remains a stored-channel reset; the selected post-event pressure is rebuilt from the new support.

With equal zero sense indices, the actual scalar compatibility formula has the exact-real form

\[ \omega=1- rac{\delta}{2\pi} - rac{D}{4(A+z+\epsilon)},\qquad\epsilon=10^{-9}. ag{8} \]

The kernel evaluates its EPI ratio through the shared scaled arithmetic. Since 3*z>A follows from (6) and A<33/64, the last ratio before its factor 1/4 is below 1/2. Also delta<1/100, so

\[ \omega> rac78- rac1{600}> rac45> rac\pi{\pi+1}. ag{9} \]

Thus both U3 tests and the default compatibility threshold pass with strict margins. UM creates exactly the edge {0,c} with the generated positive conductance omega. It is neither externally imposed nor replaced by one. The final bare degrees are (2,1,1) in order (0,1,c), and the weighted form gradients are

\[ q_0^+=-u+\omega D,\qquad q_1^+=u,\qquad q_c^+=-\omega D. ag{10} \]

The whole successor is now in the connected selected-law domain. Parent-only SHA subsequently changes n to n/2, keeps phase/form/support fixed and supplies its lifecycle context; the other capacities are unchanged. Its output capacity is positive and above the declared floor. No symmetry, winding or old identity tube is inferred from this small graph's connectedness.

All general endpoint identities below are exact for admitted represented endpoints viewed as real coordinates. Equations (5), (7) and the simplified family bounds describe the ideal event map. Production coefficients, circular variance, consensus, modulo and multiplication can have represented defects. Finite controls re-admit actual endpoints and check the margins directly; they are not a uniform proof of every floating-point realization of (1). No conclusion requires forcing the generated conductance to its ideal value.

docs.title: 5. Complete event work, degree changes and mean leaves
docs.text:
For a general admitted UM stage that preserves form, let F be its actual set of newly committed edges, E the old support, and theta^+ its complete phase endpoint, including old-neighbor writes. Old conductances are unchanged. The exact storage jump is

\[ \begin{split} H^+-H^-={}&\frac12\sum_{\{i,j\}\in F}\omega_{ij}(x_i-x_j)^2\\ &+\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E} [\cos(\theta_j-\theta_i)-\cos(\theta_j^+-\theta_i^+)]\\ &+\sum_{\{i,j\}\in F}[1-\cos(\theta_j^+-\theta_i^+)]. \end{split} \tag{11} \]

Ignoring the middle line would omit bidirectional UM's work on old edges. Capacity is absent from this storage, so its reset has no additional term. THOL birth has zero edge-storage jump under the explicitly selected isolate convention; this is not a claim of zero physical creation cost.

For the source family, (11) becomes

\[ \Delta H_{\rm UM}=\frac12\omega D^2 +\cos\phi-\cos(7\phi/8)+1-\cos(\phi/16). \tag{12} \]

The old-edge phase term is negative. Nevertheless (6), (9), phi<3/20, and 1-cos(phi)<=phi^2/2 give

\[ \Delta H_{\rm UM}> \frac25\left(\frac7{25}\right)^2- \frac12\left(\frac3{20}\right)^2 =\frac{2011}{100000}>\frac1{50}. \tag{13} \]

The final SHA leaves H unchanged. OZ and refreshed THOL also leave the old edge storage unchanged. Thus the complete word's positive storage jump is accounted for by (12), not claimed as energy conservation or an unbudgeted autonomous gain. An event reservoir or selection law has not been derived.

Degree normalization changes both rows. For a general old node, define a_i=sum_{new j}omega_ij*(x_i-x_j), and let Delta S_i include the phase change on old edges and all new sine terms. With m_i^+=nu_i^+/(pi*d_i^+),

\[ \dot x_i^+-\dot x_i=(m_i^+-m_i)S_i+m_i^+\Delta S_i, \qquad \dot\theta_i^+-\dot\theta_i=(m_i^+-m_i)q_i+m_i^+a_i. \tag{14} \]

These are fresh-law comparisons, not the raw pressure-relief map. For a former isolate use its explicitly zero old rows and the full new rows; there is no old nu/(pi*0) to substitute into (14).

The old P2 means use weights (1/nu_0,1/nu_1) and total R. Let mu_x and mu_theta denote those means before birth. Immediately after UM set r_0=2/n, r_1=1/nu_1, r_c=1/nu_c, and R^+=r_0+r_1+r_c. Then

\[ \mu_x^+-\mu_x= \frac{(r_0-1/\nu_0)(A-\mu_x)+r_c(z-\mu_x)}{R^+}, \tag{15} \] \[ \mu_\theta^+-\mu_\theta= \frac{(r_0-1/\nu_0)(\gamma-\mu_\theta) +(r_0-r_1)\delta+r_c(\gamma-\mu_\theta)}{R^+}. \tag{16} \]

The new child's weight and the changed parent degree/capacity are all retained. The isolated prefix did not already possess this connected mean. For the final SHA endpoint replace r_0 by 4/n; all other terms are unchanged. Each ensuing fixed-support segment conserves its own new means, not the old metric's values. Phase means require the declared continuous lifts.

docs.title: 6. A dynamically active child and its disconnected null
docs.text:
Let k=1 immediately after UM and k=1/2 after parent-only SHA, so the parent capacity is k*n. Equations (7), (10) give the child's full rows

\[ \dot x_c= rac{ u_c}{\pi}\sin\delta>0,\qquad \dot heta_c=- rac{ u_c\omega D}{\pi}<0. ag{17} \]

The instantaneous form acceleration follows by differentiating the declared two-row law with held support/capacity, not by inferring it from telemetry:

\[ \ddot x_c= rac{ u_c\cos\delta}{\pi^2} \left[ rac{k n}{2}(-u+\omega D)+ u_c\omega D ight]. ag{18} \]

For both k values, dropping a nonnegative contribution gives

\[ rac{k n}{2}(-u+\omega D)+ u_c\omega D > rac95 rac45 rac7{25}- rac{21}{20} rac3{10} = rac{441}{5000}. ag{19} \]

Here nu_c>9/5, n<21/10, u<3/10 and D>7/25. With cos(delta)>99/100 and pi^2<10,

\[ \ddot x_c> rac{(9/5)(99/100)(441/5000)}{10} = rac{392931}{25000000}> rac3{200}. ag{20} \]

The parent phase gradient need not be positive throughout the source box; (19) does not assume it. The child's negative phase rate and the resulting relative phase velocity suffice. This accounts for the actual UM parent capacity blend and for its later SHA reduction.

In the disconnected null, the child construction, phase and capacity are the same, and the UM phase/capacity/pressure proposals on old nodes are identical: functional candidates are not members of that snapshot's old neighborhood. Disabling only functional links therefore leaves the child isolated under the declared extension. Its form rate, phase rate and form acceleration are identically zero. A stale prebirth candidate inventory is a second nonattachment control, not a proof that the live-inventory protocol fails.

This discriminates a connected dynamical degree of freedom from an added hierarchy record. It does not establish that the enlarged system is a persistent composite, that the old organization is retained, or that nature selects either event. Rates and local derivatives provide no finite-time response amplitude or lifetime without further analysis.

docs.title: 7. Scope of the composition result and checks
docs.text:
Under the declared state, history, grammar, configuration and intermediate law premises, the actual operator mechanisms admit a THOL/UM composition: birth supplies an isolated coordinate; parent-target UM admits the actual child candidate, generates a positive edge and returns the full graph to the connected weighted-sine domain. The ideal source family has strict birth, candidate, acute-domain and dynamical-response margins. Actual represented endpoints must satisfy their own admitted arithmetic and checks.

The runtime and algebra controls use the shared operator stages and both explicit sine readers. They check live prefix context, connected-reader rejection before UM, parent versus isolated-child targeting, the actual candidate/weight, metabolic construction, degree and mean changes, full work and child rows/acceleration, and the disconnected controls. Manufactured temporal data and constitutive derivative predictions are separately identified. Finite same-node-support U6 checks pass for OZ, UM and SHA; the cross-dimension birth comparison rejects. There is no whole-word U6 certificate, and equations (11)--(20) do not claim universal U6 confinement. The fixture's initial [-1,1] rail transcription was corrected to the frozen [0,1] protocol and rerun; all consumed forms were positive interior values in both, so this correction changed no selected source, event map or analytical discriminator.

The frozen-isolate reader controls check component reuse, explicit zero isolate rows, primitive admission and the unchanged connected-reader boundary. Testing owns suite selection. Neither report installs the supplied law as a native flow.

For a previously formed organization, (11), (14) and the typed prefix contract remain available methods. One must re-admit its actual histories, candidate inventory, phase/capacity map, generated edges and identity conditions. This small connected example does not transfer those premises or prove composite formation for the marked winding contact. No new trajectory or physical identification is part of the result.

docs.title: Local capacity and joint temporal admission in the maintained contact
docs.text: A capacity-only VAL action at the fixed first A1 member admits a nonempty open domain in which the maintained contact retains its identity and fresh positive parent pressure while genuine three-sample histories exceed the unchanged THOL child threshold. This is a conditional mathematical admission with a separate observation-precision obligation. It supplies neither measured samples nor an executed child event. The research program owns status and subsequent work.

docs.title: 1. Fixed source, target and actual capacity-only action
docs.text:
Retain the aligned twenty-node, 45-edge source of the proximity-contact protocol. The original AL/UM/SHA word acts on A0, whose members are nodes 0 and 1. The prospective local VAL and THOL target here is node 2, the first A1 member. This target was fixed before the present derivation. No target-0 history or threshold verdict is transferred to it.

Retain the original support, each actual generated conductance, source origin 9/32<m<11/32, twist alpha=2*pi/5, increments b=h=1/1024, lifts, rails, candidate policy and execution state. The original independent centered form and phase deviation balls have joint radius z=1/512 in each ten-node component. Use the following open subset in those same prepared coordinates:

\[ \|(\xi_C,\eta_C)\|_2<\varepsilon=2^{-18},\qquad C=A,B. \tag{1} \]

This shrinks the admitted source domain without changing the contact word or retuning its output. The old weights are one; every actual new weight lies in (3/4,1]. Before the new action, capacities are one except nu_0=nu_1=1/2. Degrees are seven on A0, six on B0 and four elsewhere.

Apply the supported capacity-only VAL branch with EDGE_AWARE_ENABLED=False, at node 2 alone. Keep strict operator preconditions and the unoverridden VAL_MIN_DNFR=1e-6. Fresh pressure is the constitutive evaluation in (3), admitted below. Write c for the actual post-action capacity of node 2, whose prior capacity is one. The analytical factor interval is

\[ 128\leq c\leq256. \tag{2} \]

This interval follows from the estimates below; no trajectory or gain scan selects it. A requested factor must produce this represented endpoint. Multiplication of the original unit capacity by a represented c is exact; other representations or a changed initial capacity need their own endpoint check. The unchanged strict VAL_MAX_VF=10 policy checks the incoming capacity one; it is not a ceiling on the proposed endpoint. The source form also exceeds the unchanged VAL_MIN_EPI=1/(2*pi). A second VAL immediately after this one would fail that incoming-capacity check. This action does not establish unrestricted repeatability or a physical upper-capacity law.

The complete VAL primary endpoint retains form, primitive phase, support, conductances and stored pressure. No elapsed continuous time occurs in the action. Its secondary execution records remain associated with node 2. With the inherited empty glyph history there, the actual local VAL produces ['VAL'] and U2 debt one; it supplies a registered destabilizer for THOL's U4b context. It supplies no EPI history. Neither this prefix nor a prospective THOL event is a completed word with its closing obligations discharged.

The continuing law, at the same structural clock with the completed action at absolute time 7, is

\[ q=L_Wx,\quad S_i=\sum_{j\sim i}\sin(\theta_j-\theta_i),\quad M_{ii}=\frac{\nu_i}{\pi d_i},\quad p_i=\frac{S_i}{\pi d_i},\qquad \dot x=MS,\quad\dot\theta=Mq. \tag{3} \]

Here nu_2=c, the other capacities retain their preceding values, and all capacities are held. Retain e=0,w=beta=1, no forcing, no continuous loss, fixed conductances and bare support. There are no events on the subsequent observation interval. Pressure is independently specified by (3), not reconstructed from an observed derivative. The local change is not the global time conjugacy used in the common-capacity study. Both actual rows and the new mean weights are retained.

docs.title: 2. Zero event work, changed means and all-time identity
docs.text:
Use the original storage and relative identity,

\[ H=\frac12x^TL_Wx+\sum_{\{i,j\}\in U}(1-\cos(\theta_j-\theta_i)),\qquad Z^2=\|Px\|_2^2+\|P(\theta-\theta_*)\|_2^2,\quad P=I-\frac{11^T}{20},\quad r=\frac1{16}. \tag{4} \]

The capacity-only action has exactly zero H work and leaves Z unchanged. The existing source and barrier proof gives Z(7)<r, H(7)-H_*<1/8192 and H-H_*>=Z^2/25 throughout Z<=r. These statements depend on the actual support, weights and state, not on a common value of the positive capacities. Equation (3) conserves H for the nonuniform diagonal M as well. Consequently the same first-exit argument gives

\[ Z(t)<\frac1{16}\qquad(t\geq7). \tag{5} \]

The conserved means after VAL use rho_i=d_i/nu_i. The original total weight is 104; after the event it is R_c=100+4/c. For either form or the declared continuous phase lift v, the mean change is exactly

\[ \mu_{v,c}-\mu_{v,1} =\frac{4(c^{-1}-1)(v_2-\mu_{v,1})}{100+4/c}. \tag{6} \]

These new means, rather than their old values, are conserved during the continuation. Positivity of their weights and (5) bound the common coordinates and give global smooth continuation, as in the maintenance argument.

The live form gate can also be kept explicitly. Put w=rho/R_c. Then sum rho_i^2=704+16/c^2<=720, R_c>=100, and

\[ \|e_i-w\|_2^2=1-2w_i+\|w\|_2^2 <1+\frac{720}{10000}<\left(\frac{21}{20}\right)^2. \tag{7} \]

Every initial form is between m-epsilon and m+b+epsilon, so the conserved positive weighted mean is in the same interval. Since x_i-mu_x=(e_i-w)^T Px, (5)--(7) give, for every node and every future time,

\[ \frac{69}{320}-\varepsilon <x_i(t)<\frac{131}{320}+b+\varepsilon. \tag{8} \]

In particular 1/5<x_i(t)<1/2, retaining the strict THOL form gate and the weaker (1/8,1/2) range used for reader arithmetic below. This is an all-time identity and form-range result, not a claim that the parent pressure keeps its sign forever or that the organization remains maintained after child birth.

docs.title: 3. Exact nominal pressure and nonuniform acceleration
docs.text:
Use the exact unsplit source at its own common m. Its actual post-word coordinates and generated cross weight are derived in the preceding source calculation. Write

\[ \gamma=(1-h)\alpha,\quad K=\cos\gamma,\quad J=\cos((1+h)\alpha),\quad \omega=1-\frac{b}{4(2m+b+\epsilon_E)},\qquad \frac34<\omega<1, \tag{9} \]

where epsilon_E is the unchanged represented regularizer 1e-9. Node 2 has phase gamma and form m. Its four neighbors are the two A0 nodes, with phase zero and form m+b, and the two A2 nodes, with phase 2*alpha and form m. Consequently

\[ p_{2,\mathrm{nom}}(7) =\frac{\cos\alpha\sin(h\alpha)}\pi>\frac{9h}{100}. \tag{10} \]

For the inequality, use cos(alpha)>3/10 and sin(h*alpha)>(3/4)*h*alpha. The latter follows directly from sin u>=u-u^3/6 and 0<u=h*alpha<1/100. Thus this is a positive-pressure candidate before any capacity change, independently of c.

The weighted gradients are q_2=-2b, q_0=q_1=(4+2*omega)b, and zero on A2. Differentiating both rows of (3), with capacities held, gives

\[ a_i:=\ddot x_i =M_{ii}\sum_{j\sim i}\cos(\theta_j-\theta_i) (M_{jj}q_j-M_{ii}q_i). \tag{11} \]

Keeping the two distinct neighbor contributions at node 2 yields

The previous internal-edge bound gives W_internal>1-sqrt(2)*z>3/4. Every predicted candidate therefore passes both the final phase gate and the score threshold. The output has exactly 53 edges: forty retained unit edges and thirteen actual new edges, all with positive weight at most one. New edges have the actual weight attribute and no inserted length.

The two selected degrees are eleven. The six B members in pairs 0,1,4 have degree six, while every other degree remains four. This is a connected support. The connection is a six-member contact fan, even for the nominal synchronized-tip control; the unchanged pi/2 phase gate and 3/4 threshold do not select B pair zero alone.

Only the selected targets execute the word's lifecycle/history transitions. The four old A neighbors receive merged phase writes; new B contacts do not receive such writes during this same UM stage. Selected stored pressure is relieved using the original four neighbors. The new continuous pressure later uses all actual neighbors and is a separate evaluation. docs.title: 3. Sufficient boundary state and an explicit loss of pair closure
docs.text:
Every independent pair interchange preserves the new bare support. It need not preserve its actual conductances: the compatibility score depends on the constituent form and phase at each endpoint. For generic source states, the four boundary pairs A_0,B_0,B_1,B_4 therefore have nonconstant rows or columns in their cross-conductance blocks. Equal bare neighbor counts do not restore the missing weighted symmetry.

The full state with its weighted incidence and associated execution records remains sufficient. A mixed collective description can retain the original unordered coordinates for nonboundary pairs and the already available marked-port offsets u_p=x_p-X, v_p=sin(theta_p-Theta) for a marked member of each boundary pair, together with the actual cross matrices and their association to those members. Since R>0, these offsets reconstruct both member states without division by a possibly vanishing split. Quotienting the joint state and boundary data by simultaneous relabeling is also sufficient. Discarding the association between a weight row and a member state is not.

An exact obstruction is already present at the nominal split source. The target consensus is symmetric, so after UM its phases are +/-delta'. The B zero-pair phases are zero, and its member forms are m. Put D_E=2*m+b+epsilon_E. The cross weights from the plus and minus A members to either B zero-pair member are

\[ w_\pm=1-\frac{|\delta'|}{2\pi} -\frac{b\pm u}{4(D_E\pm u)},\qquad w_+-w_-=-\frac{u(2m+\epsilon_E)}{2(D_E^2-u^2)}<0. \]

Here the frozen 0<u<b ensures that both form differences have the displayed sign. Hold the actual weighted graph fixed and interchange both x,theta of the two A target members. Every old retained pair coordinate X,Theta,R,U,Q is unchanged. The two B zero-pair nodes each have degree six and capacity one. Their mean phase rate nevertheless changes by

\[ \boxed{\Delta\dot\Theta_{B_0} =\frac{u(w_+-w_-)}{3\pi} =-\frac{u^2(2m+\epsilon_E)}{6\pi(D_E^2-u^2)}\ne0.} \]

The difference follows directly from the two weighted form-gradient terms: their change is 2*u*(w_+-w_-) at each B node. All other incident terms are unchanged. This supplies an obstruction to a future law on the old unordered pair state alone on this same weighted graph. It is not an obstruction to the retained full-state law or to the connected organization.

If the two weight rows and associated records are interchanged with the A member states, the full continuous field is instead relabeled covariantly. Likewise the actual all-candidate word maps a jointly relabeled source to the corresponding jointly relabeled output in exact arithmetic. The complete event therefore descends on the orbit of state and boundary data, while its output generally leaves the old fixed-weight independent-swap stratum. Finite binary64 controls retain their arithmetic tolerance rather than asserting universal bitwise equivariance.

docs.title: 4. Admitted continuation and complete work accounting
docs.text:
Let U be the actual connected bare support, W its held conductances, d_i its bare degrees and nu_i its post-word held capacities. The selected weighted completion has, in the original structural clock,

\[ q=L_Wx,\quad S_i=\sum_{j\in N_U(i)}\sin(\theta_j-\theta_i),\quad M=\operatorname{diag}\frac{\nu_i}{\pi d_i},\qquad \dot x=MS,\quad\dot\theta=Mq. \]

Its independently specified pressure is p_i=S_i/(pi*d_i). The stored UM pressure does not replace it. The exact full storage is

\[ H=\frac12x^TL_Wx+ \sum_{\{i,j\}\in U}[1-\cos(\theta_j-\theta_i)], \qquad \dot H=q^TMS-S^TMq=0. \]

The old unit-only reader still correctly rejects generic output weights. The new completion admits them without weakening that separate model. For rho_i=d_i/nu_i, the global lifted form and phase means weighted by rho_i are conserved. Separate constituent means and storages need not be conserved after contact. Reusing their pre-contact conservation as an identity certificate would omit the newly acquired boundary exchange.

For example, let q_A,S_A denote sums over A's internal support, including its new within-pair edge, and q_C,S_C the cross-contact sums at A. Its internal storage obeys

\[ \dot H_A=q_A^TM_A S_C-S_A^TM_Aq_C. \]

The corresponding formula holds for B; together with the derivative of the cross-contact storage they sum to zero. The actual total-degree normalization remains in M_A,M_B. The boundary terms explain how a conservative total law can change a constituent's old identity geometry.

For the supplied word, let E_A,E_B be the forty old edges and C the twelve cross contacts. AL acts before any added support, with work

\[ \Delta H_{\rm AL} =4b\sum_{j\sim0}(X_{A,0}-X_{A,j})+4b^2. \]

UM's phase work on old edges is

\[ \Delta H_{\rm UM,old} =\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E_A\cup E_B} [\cos(\theta_j-\theta_i)-\cos(\theta_j'-\theta_i')]. \]

Here phases in the first term are the post-AL snapshot; AL leaves them unchanged. B contributes zero because its state does not reset. The full attachment cost, evaluated at the actual common post-UM endpoint, is

\[ \Delta H_{\rm attach} =2\omega u_{A,0}^2+2\sin^2\delta_{A,0}' +\sum_{(i,j)\in C} \left[\frac{W_{ij}}2(x_i'-x_j')^2+ 1-\cos(\theta_j'-\theta_i')\right], \]

where omega is the actual internal-edge conductance. Thus H_after-H_before=DeltaH_AL+DeltaH_UM,old+DeltaH_attach exactly. Capacity synchronization, pressure relief and SHA change subsequent rates but add no direct term to this storage. No sign is assigned to the old-edge phase work and no reservoir pays for the new edges. Conservation between events does not make the supplied contact passive.

docs.title: 5. Uniform finite retention of both original identities
docs.text:
For each component let P be its ten-node arithmetic-centering projection and define the original geometric identity radius along continuous lifts by

\[ Z_C(t)^2=\|P x_C(t)\|^2+ \|P(\theta_C(t)-\theta_*)\|^2,\qquad C\in\{A,B\}. \]

This removes each component's instantaneous common form and phase origin; it does not assume those means remain conserved. The identity tube is Z_C<r=1/16. It implies the old winding neighborhood, acute old edges and nonantipodal pair chart. It is a particular declared identity, not a definition of every possible organized state.

Use elapsed time zero immediately after the whole word. The preceding reset bounds give

\[ Z_A(0)<\frac{13z}{4},\qquad Z_B(0)<z, \qquad R_0=2z+b=\frac{5z}{2}, \]

where R_0 bounds the initial global form range. Because all actual conductances satisfy 0<W<=1 and 0<nu<=1, the complete rows imply globally

\[ |\dot x_i|\le\frac1\pi,\qquad \max_i x_i(t)-\min_i x_i(t)\le R_0+\frac{2t}{\pi}, \] \[ |\dot\theta_i(t)|\le\frac1\pi \left(R_0+\frac{2t}{\pi}\right),\qquad |\theta_i(t)-\theta_i(0)| \le\frac{R_0t}{\pi}+\frac{t^2}{\pi^2}. \]

These bounds also exclude finite-time escape of the smooth lifted solution; they require no local acute-domain premise. Since centering is a contraction, each constituent's full centered-state displacement is at most

\[ B(t)=\frac{\sqrt{10}\,t}{\pi} \sqrt{1+\left(R_0+\frac t\pi\right)^2}. \]

For 0<=t<=1/64, use sqrt(10)<10/3, pi>3 and sqrt(1+(R_0+t/pi)^2)<101/100 to obtain

\[ Z_A(t),Z_B(t) <\frac{13}{2048}+\frac{101}{5760} =\frac{2201}{92160}<\frac1{32}<r. \]

Both source identities therefore survive the actual contact for the full frozen finite interval. In particular, old edge gaps remain below alpha+sqrt(2)*r<pi/2 and internal pair gaps below sqrt(2)*r. The exact fine flow and retained boundary state remain sufficient throughout this interval. This theorem does not identify a new common identity or transfer an all-time independent-component barrier to the joined graph.

docs.title: 6. The receiver necessarily leaves its original identity tube
docs.text:
The connection changes the complete field even at the original exact twists. Each node of B pair one acquires two zero-phase A neighbors, giving an additional sine sum -2*sin(alpha); B pair four acquires the opposite sum. Their old internal sine sums vanish at that reference. Thus the old reference is not a critical point of the joined phase storage. A copied pre-contact critical-point barrier cannot prove joined maintenance.

A stronger conclusion follows from the full rows without a trajectory. Let

\[ D(t)=X_{B,1}(t)-X_{B,4}(t) =\frac{x_{12}+x_{13}-x_{18}-x_{19}}2. \]

Its four nonzero coefficients sum to zero and have Euclidean norm one, so |D(t)|<=||P x_B(t)||<=Z_B(t) and |D(0)|<z. Every absolute phase error from the original common-reference twist after the word is bounded by

\[ a_0=z+\frac{4h}{3}=\frac{5z}{3}. \]

Indeed this covers the four old A-neighbor phase writes, the smaller target writes and the unchanged B coordinates. The global phase bound above then gives, for all twenty retained lifted phases,

\[ |\theta_i(t)-\theta_{*,i}| \le a(t)=a_0+\frac{R_0t}{\pi}+\frac{t^2}{\pi^2}. \]

Each of the six sine terms at a B pair-one or pair-four member differs from its reference value by at most 2*a(t), using the global Lipschitz bound for sine. Their capacities are still one and their degrees six. Consequently the difference of their pair-mean form rates satisfies

\[ \dot D(t)\le-\frac{2\sin\alpha}{3\pi} +\frac{4a(t)}\pi. \]

Integration retains the signed nominal response and bounds its whole nonlinear remainder:

\[ D(T)<z-\frac{2\sin\alpha}{3\pi}T +\frac{4a_0}\pi T+ \frac{2R_0}{\pi^2}T^2+ \frac4{3\pi^3}T^3. \]

At the frozen T=3/8, the elementary strict bounds sin(2*pi/5)>19/20 and 3<pi<22/7 give the entirely rational estimate

\[ \boxed{D(3/8)<-\frac{374311}{5406720} <-\frac1{16},\qquad Z_B(3/8)>\frac1{16}.} \]

The sine bound follows directly from sin(2*pi/5)=sqrt(10+2*sqrt(5))/4. The rational comparison retains strict margin 36391/5406720 beyond the tube radius. The argument does not stop at a local derivative or assume the state stayed in that tube; its form-range and phase-displacement bounds are global on the declared fixed-support segment. Thus every exact source in the frozen family has left the old B identity tube by t=3/8, although both identities were retained throughout 0<=t<=1/64.

This is a precise obstruction to all-time retention of the original small identity tube for this supplied contact fan and complete law. It is not a proof of winding loss, disappearance of all organized structure, failure of UM, or failure of the weighted law. A deformed continuing organization or a larger common identity would need its own state, identity definition and maintenance argument. Replacing that target after evaluating this response would not convert the present scoped exit into a retained-source success.

docs.title: 7. Static controls and the resulting admission boundary
docs.text:
The independent static controls retain both frozen nominal preparations. They check each separate source's barrier, actual whole-word support and associated writes, all generated weights, the admitted connected field, complete event work, fixed-boundary state-swap discrimination and joint relabeling. Exact rational and interval controls also check the finite-retention and signed-exit bounds. No continuous trajectory is evaluated. Source preparation, represented input defects and the exact-real family remain separately identifiable.

The independent reset/weight oracle uses 100-digit arithmetic with absolute error allowance 2^-46. The smaller boundary discriminator instead compares exact rational phase-rate numerators reconstructed from the stored forms and conductances; its algebraic equality has no floating tolerance. It does not substitute the exact symmetric-source weight formula for represented weights. The dyadic twist also has a small common phase-origin and shape defect relative to k*(2*pi/5). The source controls re-admit its centered geometry; they do not assert equality to the exact frozen coordinates. The retention and exit inequality controls use the exact mathematical twist independently of that materialization. Common phase rotation is an exact-law symmetry, not a universal bitwise guarantee for the represented event implementation.

The gate therefore admits an actual supplied connection with sufficient boundary state and finite retention, and excludes perpetual retention of the declared original small receiver tube for this family. The exact result requires no higher-precision response campaign. Its remaining mathematical question is what continuing identity, if any, is supported by the actual joined system after this obligatory deformation; neither connectivity, conservation nor the old pair quotient answers that question alone.

docs.title: A THOL birth obstruction inside the maintained contact
docs.text:
The existing count-three contact is a maintained organization under its declared conservative sine law. Its continuous dynamics nevertheless cannot supply a true three-sample EPI acceleration above the unchanged default THOL threshold while retaining that preparation, capacity and clock. The obstruction holds for every event-free sampling window after the contact word, not only for one snapshot or a small-window limit.

This is a source-specific result about the child-creation condition. THOL also has a pressure action that does not require crossing the child threshold. The research program owns research status; the hierarchy contract owns the operator's temporal observation and separate admission requirements.

docs.title: 1. Frozen source, identity and temporal question
docs.text:
Select the exact aligned post-word family already admitted by the proximity-contact protocol. Before its supplied emission,coupling,silence word, there are two independently perturbed doubled C5 components with pairs A_k=(2*k,2*k+1) and B_k=(10+2*k,11+2*k), k=0,...,4. Each has its original twenty unit edges and unit capacities.
