The shared owner exposes assess_sine_port_relaxation and SinePortRelaxation in relational_sine_port_relaxation.py. The contract and guide retain admission, availability and separate channel criteria. The independent controls cover the fine-state parity identities, spectral and energy premises, initial-state exchange, mean restoration and strict reporting boundaries; they do not substitute sampled times for the uniform proof.

docs.title: Fine preparation information selects different acquired winding classes
docs.text:
Under one fixed complete law, equal initial phase, conserved means and storage do not determine the acquired winding magnitude. This owner constructs two explicitly paired source families on C9. Every pair has exactly those same preparation observations, yet its two complete trajectories acquire winding magnitudes one and two. The pairing retains full form and phase uncertainty; equality is not inferred from overlapping error intervals.

The law is the sine member of the constitutive family. No constitutive parameter is varied. The construction and scalar semigroup certificate use no trajectory, reverse-flow definition, coefficient search or frozen scientific response.

docs.title: Fixed law and an algebraic preparation pair
docs.text:
Use the isolated unit C9, nodes \(0,\ldots,8\), edges \(j--(j+1\bmod9)\), unnormalized Laplacian \(L\), degree matrix \(2I\) and held capacities one. Keep

\[ e=1023/1024,\quad w=1/1024,\quad \tau=et,\quad\gamma=1/(1023\pi),\quad A=L/2 . \tag{1} \]

The entire state is signed real form \(x\) and primitive circular phases with continued real lifts \(\theta\). In the two clocks the complete rows are

\[ \dot x=-eLx/2+(w/\pi)S(\theta)/2,\qquad \dot\theta=(w/\pi)Lx/2, \qquad x'=-Ax+\gamma f(\theta),\quad\theta'=\gamma Ax, \tag{2} \]

where \(S_i=\sum_{j\sim i}\sin(\theta_j-\theta_i)\) and \(f=S/2\). Storage and structural-time loss are

\[ H(x,\theta)=\tfrac12x^TLx+\sum_{\{i,j\}}[1-\cos(\theta_j-\theta_i)], \qquad H'=-\tfrac12\|Lx\|_2^2. \tag{3} \]

Both ordinary means, equivalently the degree-weighted means on this regular support, are conserved. Pressure, support, capacity and structural units are supplied premises. There is no event, forcing or state reset during acquisition.

Define the exact rational vectors and scale

\[ r_j=j-4,\qquad h=e_3-e_4,\qquad m=\frac{2046}{9}\left(\frac{355}{113}\right)^2,\qquad a=(9M+M^{-1})h+r,\quad b=(9M-M^{-1})h+2r . \tag{4} \]

The declared integer is \(M=512\). These are algebraic source coordinates, not states selected from an evaluated future trajectory. Direct graph arithmetic gives

\[ \mathbf1^Tr=\mathbf1^Th=0,\quad r^TLr=72,\quad h^TLh=6,\quad h^TLr=0,\quad a^TLa=b^TLb=486M^2+180+6/M^2 . \tag{5} \]

The equal energy comes from the compensating \(M^{-1}h\) terms. The unmodified ramps \(r,2r\) have unequal energy and would not answer this question.

Set \(d=a-b=2h/M-r\), and define the full form map

\[ R=I-\frac{2d(d^TL)}{d^TLd},\qquad d^TLd=72+24/M^2>0 . \tag{6} \]

This metric reflection obeys

\[ R^2=I,\quad R^TLR=L,\quad Ra=b,\quad R\mathbf1=\mathbf1,\quad \mathbf1^TR=\mathbf1^T . \tag{7} \]

For example equal norms in (5) imply \(d^TLa=d^TLd/2\), proving \(Ra=b\); expanding (6) proves the energy identity. The two mean identities use \(L\mathbf1=0\) and \(\mathbf1^Td=0\). This is not assumed to preserve Euclidean error norms. It is not a graph or complete-flow symmetry. In particular the form-only transformation \((x,\theta)\mapsto(Rx,\theta)\) could preserve the phase row only if \(AR=A\); invertibility of \(A\) on the mean-zero space would require \(R=I\) there, contrary to \(Ra=b\ne a\).

Declare latent errors \(\xi,\zeta\) satisfying

\[ |\xi_j|,|\zeta_j|\le\epsilon=10^{-10},\qquad \mathbf1^T\xi=\mathbf1^T\zeta=0 . \tag{8} \]

For every such pair use the two complete initial states

\[ (x_1(0),\theta_1(0))=(ma+\xi,\zeta),\qquad (x_2(0),\theta_2(0))=(mb+R\xi,\zeta). \tag{9} \]

Each branch is the invertible image of a sixteen-dimensional relative source neighborhood. The paired experiment has sixteen latent dimensions, not thirty-two independently selectable ones.

For \(s_i=\sum_j|R_{ij}|\), the second branch satisfies \(|(R\xi)_i|\le s_i\epsilon\). Exact matrix arithmetic gives

\[ K:=\max_i s_i=\frac{1968129}{786433}<\frac{251}{100}. \tag{10} \]

We use \(K\epsilon\) as a sufficient common coordinate bound for that branch. The initial phase bound remains \(\epsilon\) in both branches. The matching claim does not require equal marginal form-error limits.

docs.title: Exact equality of the preparation observations
docs.text:
Consider the coarse preparation map consisting of the entire initial phase vector, both conserved means and the scalar storage \(H\). Equations (7)--(9) imply, for every admitted latent pair,

\[ \theta_1(0)=\theta_2(0)=\zeta,\quad \overline x_1=\overline x_2=\overline\theta_1 =\overline\theta_2=0,\quad H(x_1(0),\zeta)=H(x_2(0),\zeta). \tag{11} \]

The last equality holds because \(x_2(0)=Rx_1(0)\), so their complete form energies coincide, and their phase potential is literally the same. Storage may vary with the latent errors; it is equal within each pair. The result therefore concerns equal observed values, not only equal nominal centers or membership in a common storage budget.

An edgewise upper bound on that common source cost is

\[ B=\frac12\sum_{\{i,j\}} (m|a_j-a_i|+2\epsilon)^2+18\epsilon^2 <320680599854722<10^{15}. \tag{12} \]

The phase term uses all nine edges and \(1-\cos v\le v^2/2\). For the fixed vector, \(\sum_{\{i,j\}}|a_j-a_i|=2361089/128\). Branch two has the same cost by exact isometry; applying an unrelated Cartesian error box to its form coordinates would discard that equality. The nominal common form cost is \(m^2(486M^2+180+6/M^2)/2\).

Every initial principal phase difference equals its small lift difference, since \(2\epsilon<\pi\). Summing around the cycle gives winding zero for every source member. Neither source initially has the claimed nonzero phase-winding identity, despite its deliberately structured fine form.

docs.title: Acquisition without evaluating trajectories
docs.text:
Declare the common structural time \(T=200\), original time \(204800/1023\), capture radius \(r_c=1/12\), source budget \(10^{15}\) and shared outward dyadic128/Machin scalar arithmetic. These are the new preparation's fixed budgets; they are not presented as the older ramp experiment's time or cost. The error scale in (8) is unchanged.

Let \(\alpha=2\pi/9\) and define the continued target lifts

\[ \Theta_k=\alpha(9Mh+kr),\qquad k=1,2 . \tag{13} \]

Their extra term is \(2\pi Mh\), a nodewise integer-turn shift. Consequently the circular targets, their currents, storage and Hessians are exactly the usual winding-\(k\) targets. No corresponding shift is applied to an actual trajectory. These lifts have zero mean and specify the endpoint comparison in the same continued chart as (9).

The graph and complete nonlinear forcing satisfy

\[ \|e^{-A\tau}P_9\|_{2I}\le e^{-\tau/5},\quad P_9=I-\mathbf1\mathbf1^T/9,\quad \|f(\theta)\|_{2I}\le F=\sqrt{18},\quad \lambda_{\max}(L)\le4 , \tag{14} \]

as proved in the isolated acquisition owner. Only these graph and law estimates are reused; the new source norms and target distances are rebuilt.

Write \(a_1=a,a_2=b\), \(\epsilon_1=\epsilon\), \(\epsilon_2=K\epsilon\), \(\eta=\gamma^2\), and take \(\rho\ge e^{-T/5}\). For each complete source family define

\[ \begin{aligned} V_k&=\gamma m\sqrt{2a_k^Ta_k},& E_{x,k}&=\sqrt{18}\gamma\epsilon_k,& E_\theta&=\sqrt{18}\epsilon,\\ R_{z,k}&=\rho(V_k+E_{x,k})+5\eta F,& R_{x,k}&=R_{z,k}/(\gamma\sqrt2),\\ D_k&=\|\gamma m a_k-\Theta_k\|_2,& Y_k&=D_k+(E_{x,k}+E_\theta+R_{z,k}+\eta FT)/\sqrt2,\\ Z_k^2&=R_{x,k}^2+Y_k^2 . \end{aligned}\tag{15} \]

The first estimate follows from variation of constants for \(z=\gamma x\), \(z'=-Az+\eta f(\theta)\). The integrated complete rows give

\[ \theta(T)-\gamma ma_k =\zeta+\gamma\xi_k-z(T)+\eta\int_0^T f(\theta(s))\,ds , \quad \xi_1=\xi,\quad\xi_2=R\xi . \tag{16} \]

Therefore \(\|x_k(T)\|_2\le R_{x,k}\), \(\|\theta_k(T)-\Theta_k\|_2\le Y_k\), and the complete endpoint radius is at most \(Z_k\). In particular the large integer-turn part of the target has not been dropped from the initial norm or proxy error. The small rational approximation error in \(\gamma m-\alpha\) is retained separately in every component of \(D_k\).

Target stationarity and the global Hessian upper bound give \(H(T)-H_k^*\le2Z_k^2\), where \(H_k^*=9(1-\cos k\alpha)\). Put

\[ c=\cos(4\pi/9+\sqrt2r_c),\qquad b_c=cr_c^2/5 . \tag{17} \]

The acute margin is positive. Within either radius-\(r_c\) ball, the phase Hessian is bounded below by \(cL\); the fixed zero means and \(\lambda_2(L)>2/5\) give the same full-state storage barrier \(b_c\).

docs.title: Strict fixed-budget margins
docs.text:
Direct scalar interval evaluation of (12)--(17), with no parameter sweep, gives the conservative bounds

Complete source branch \(R_{x,k}\), upper \(Y_k\), upper \(Z_k^2\), upper \(2Z_k^2\), upper Winding one \(0.004667300447\) \(0.002760425304\) \(2.940364132\,10^{-5}\) \(5.880728263\,10^{-5}\) Winding two \(0.004667300447\) \(0.001215414795\) \(2.326092658\,10^{-5}\) \(4.652185316\,10^{-5}\)

These decimals denote exact outward rational bounds. The common barrier satisfies \(b_c>7.868256725\,10^{-5}\). The directly computed strict storage margins exceed \(1.987528462\,10^{-5}\) and \(3.216071409\,10^{-5}\), respectively. In particular, for both branches,

\[ Z_k^2<3/10^5<r_c^2,\qquad 2Z_k^2<59/10^6,\qquad b_c>78/10^6,\qquad b_c-2Z_k^2>19/10^6 . \tag{18} \]

The preparation and these budgets were specified algebraically before this scalar assessment. Its output is an analytic bound on all complete flows, not a simulated response or an observed endpoint.

By storage nonincrease, every endpoint is forward trapped in its target's acute ball. Its attained winding is \(k\) and remains so thereafter. On the compact zero-mean leaf, zero loss requires \(x=0\), and invariance then requires \(S(\theta)=0\). Strict phase convexity leaves only the declared target lift. LaSalle gives convergence. Winding acquisition includes an intervening antipodal crossing, which the smooth complete law allows; no acute constraint has been imposed throughout the transit.

docs.title: Information consequence and scope
docs.text:
There is already a direct rate witness for the information discarded at preparation. Since \((Ld)_0=9\), the nominal initial phase-rate contrast is \((9/2)\gamma m\). For every paired residual it satisfies

\[ \left|\theta'_{1,0}(0)-\theta'_{2,0}(0) -\frac92\gamma m\right| \le2\gamma(1+K)\epsilon . \tag{19} \]

This follows from \(\|L\|_\infty=4\) and \(\|(I-R)\xi\|_\infty\le(1+K)\epsilon\). It is independent of the common phase error because the complete phase row consumes form directly. The bound is much smaller than the nonzero center. A difference in initial rates alone would not establish different acquired identities; that stronger conclusion uses the full-family transit and capture proof above.

Absolute winding one and two are inequivalent under C9 rotations, reflections, common origins and joint form/phase sign reversal. Equations (11) and (18) therefore disprove sufficiency of the declared coarse preparation map for determining acquired identity on these paired families. Deterministic full-state evolution remains well posed: it is the discarded fine form arrangement and its exact correlations that the observation fails to specify.

This does not prove a minimal sufficient preparation statistic, a probability of either mode, or an autonomous selector. The algebraic sources deliberately encode information and require substantial storage. No claim is made that unstructured or laboratory-accessible preparations realize them. Capacity, support, positive loss and the sine law remain supplied. No new constitutive selection follows.

The endpoint bounds are actual-family inclusions, not target resets. Any later dwell, contact, finite response or effective-interface use must re-admit the reached states, hidden initialization, support, clock and errors. Equal initial storage does not imply equal instantaneous loss, accumulated loss, or complete histories.

The continuous source-path comparison retains these distinctions when interpolating the fine preparation. Its endpoint residual map is newly admitted, and a transient winding label does not replace the complete-state capture premise.

docs.title: A whole-family unit-winding selector through the actual phase passage
docs.text:
Every source in the previously declared interior corridor \(s\in[3/4,4/5]\) acquires and permanently retains winding \(+1\) under the same complete C9 sine law. The proof follows the original trajectories, including their form state and correlated errors. It uses an exact mixed coordinate, a finite phase-passage cone and an acute contraction estimate. No independently initialized phase-gradient solution replaces the actual dynamics.

The 57-state limit theorem gave necessary terminal alternatives, including exceptional saddles. The source-specific argument here excludes those saddles, consensus and the negative unit winding for this entire corridor. It does not assert a universal attractor for other preparations or for other constitutive laws.

The constitutive extension proves the same source-specific capture for the already declared potential family by rebuilding its current, continuation, contraction and storage bounds. The present sine proof and its tighter contraction rate remain unchanged.

docs.title: The original source and an exact continuation coordinate
docs.text:
Retain all source, law and clock premises from the Cayley path owner: the isolated unit C9, degree matrix \(D=2I\), capacities one, \(A=L/2\), \(\gamma=1/(1023\pi)\), \(\eta=\gamma^2\), \(\tau=(1023/1024)t\), and

\[ x'=-Ax+\gamma f(\theta),\qquad \theta'=\gamma Ax,\qquad f_i(\theta)=\tfrac12\sum_{j\sim i}\sin(\theta_j-\theta_i). \tag{1} \]

The source is exactly

\[ x_s(0)=Q_s(ma+\xi),\quad \theta_s(0)=\zeta,\quad s\in[3/4,4/5],\quad |\xi_j|,|\zeta_j|\le10^{-10},\quad \mathbf1^T\xi=\mathbf1^T\zeta=0 . \tag{2} \]

The original \(M=512\), rational \(m\), latent correlations, equal initial storage and source budget \(10^{15}\) are unchanged. No event, forcing or state reset is introduced.

At the certified transit time \(\tau_0=200\), continue the actual state in the invertible coordinates

\[ z=\gamma x,\qquad y=\theta+z,\qquad \sigma=\eta(\tau-\tau_0). \tag{3} \]

The exact rows, in both clocks, are

\[ \begin{array}{ll} z'=-Az+\eta f(\theta),&y'=\eta f(\theta),\\ z_\sigma=-Az/\eta+f(y-z),& y_\sigma=f(y-z)=f(y)+e,\quad e=f(y-z)-f(y). \end{array}\tag{4} \]

The consumed primitive phase remains \(\theta=y-z\); \(y\) is an auxiliary mixed coordinate, not an assumed primitive phase or a new law. Both original conserved means remain zero.

On the zero-mean space the exact bounds

\[ \|e^{-A\tau}\|_D\le e^{-\tau/5},\qquad \|f\|_D\le F=\sqrt{18},\qquad \|f(v)-f(w)\|_D\le2\|v-w\|_D \tag{5} \]

give a uniform bound on the complete later form:

\[ \|z(\tau)\|_D\le Z:=\max\{R_z(\tau_0),\,5\eta F\},\qquad \|e\|_D\le\varepsilon:=2Z,\qquad \tau\ge\tau_0 . \tag{6} \]

Here \(R_z(\tau_0)\) is rebuilt from the actual source semigroup estimate. An edge-difference functional has dual \(D\)-norm one, so every edge perturbation \(e_j-e_i\) has magnitude at most \(\varepsilon\); every actual phase edge differs from its \(y\)-edge by at most \(Z\).

The exact integrated identity is particularly useful at the handoff:

\[ y(\tau_0)-\gamma mQ_sa =\zeta+\gamma Q_s\xi+\eta\int_0^{\tau_0}f(\theta(v))\,dv . \tag{7} \]

It retains the same source and complete past history. The initial mixed error is bounded in \(D\)-norm by \(E_\theta+E_x+\eta F\tau_0\), with the transported source errors of the path owner. It does not include a second fast-form remainder; the \(z(\tau_0)\) terms have canceled by identity.

Fresh scalar bounds for the fixed whole source family give

\[ Z<0.000002054,\qquad \varepsilon<0.000004108<5\,10^{-6},\qquad \|y(\tau_0)-\gamma mQ_sa\|_D<0.000082152 . \tag{8} \]

These are exact outward rational bounds on actual states, not observations of a trajectory.

docs.title: A finite cone for the actual mixed phase passage
docs.text:
Use the eight consecutive nonclosing \(y\)-gaps \(d_0,\ldots,d_7\) and the continued closing gap \(\beta\), with the same fixed integer offsets used at the original winding-two handoff. Thus

\[ \sum_{i=0}^7d_i+\beta=4\pi,\qquad q=\pi-\beta,\qquad \sum_{i=0}^7d_i-q=3\pi . \tag{9} \]

Explicitly, put \(\widetilde y=y-2\pi Mh\), \(d_i=\widetilde y_{i+1}-\widetilde y_i\) and \(\beta=\widetilde y_0-\widetilde y_8+4\pi\). These fixed offsets define a chart of the continued state; they perform no state jump and remove nothing from the earlier form or transit bounds. The proxy and (7) certify the initial conditions

\[ 0<q(0)<63/100,\qquad \min_i d_i(0)-q(0)/2>9/10,\qquad \max_i d_i(0)<13/10 . \tag{10} \]

For example the rebuilt bounds are \(0.3489<q(0)<0.6285\), \(\min_i d_i(0)>1.2215\), \(\max_i d_i(0)<1.2570\), and the independently bounded minimum-minus-half-maximum expression exceeds \(0.9072\). Each is uniform in \(s,\xi,\zeta\).

All derivatives in the rest of the proof use slow elapsed time \(\sigma\). The edge equations from (4) are

\[ \begin{aligned} d_i'&=\tfrac12[\sin d_{i-1}-2\sin d_i+\sin d_{i+1}]+r_i,\\ q'&=\sin q-\tfrac12(\sin d_0+\sin d_7)+r_q, \qquad |r_i|,|r_q|\le\varepsilon . \end{aligned}\tag{11} \]

At the two chain endpoints the missing neighbor's sine is \(\sin q\). These are exact actual mixed-state equations with a bounded residual, not a substituted gradient trajectory.

Declare the passage target \(q_*=-7/4\) and slow-time budget eight. Set \(m_d=\min_i d_i\), \(M_d=\max_i d_i\) and \(C=m_d-q/2\). While \(q\in[-7/4,63/100]\), the nonclosing gaps remain acute, and \(\Delta=\sin m_d-\sin q\ge0\), their one-sided extrema satisfy

\[ C'\ge-\tfrac32\varepsilon,\qquad M_d'\le\varepsilon,\qquad q'\le-\Delta+\varepsilon . \tag{12} \]

To verify the first inequality, an interior minimum has unperturbed derivative at least zero. At an endpoint minimum its derivative is at least \(-\Delta/2\), whereas \(q'/2\le-\Delta/2+\varepsilon/2\). Both cases give the claimed lower derivative of \(C\). At a maximum all neighboring sine currents are at most \(\sin M_d\). The same inequalities hold at tied extrema using one-sided derivatives.

For \(0\le\sigma\le8\), (10)--(12) imply the strict bounds

\[ C>0.9-\tfrac32(5\,10^{-6})8>0.899,\qquad M_d<1.3+(5\,10^{-6})8<1.301,\qquad m_d>0.899+q/2\ge0.024 . \tag{13} \]

The required sine ordering and a uniform speed follow without evaluating a flow. For \(q\ge0\), the function \(\sin(0.899+q/2)-\sin q\) decreases on \([0,0.63]\), so

\[ \Delta\ge\sin(1.214)-\sin(0.63)>1/3 . \tag{14} \]

For \(-1/2\le q\le0\), \(\Delta\ge\sin(0.649)>1/3\). For \(-7/4\le q\le-1/2\), positivity of \(m_d\) and \(-\sin q\ge\sin(1/2)>1/3\) give the same conclusion. The three strict rational sine inequalities can be certified directly by alternating Taylor bounds or the shared outward sine kernel. Thus \(q'<-3/10\).

Equations (13)--(14) also close the bootstrap: every nonclosing gap is strictly between zero and \(\pi/2\), and the required current ordering cannot fail before the declared target or deadline. Consequently the first hitting time \(\sigma_*\) of \(q_*\) exists and satisfies

\[ 0<\sigma_*< \frac{63/100+7/4}{3/10}=\frac{119}{15}<8 . \tag{15} \]

This first hitting time is a proof coordinate. It is not an admitted hybrid event, a change of law or an observed trigger.

At that time the closing principal \(y\)-gap is

\[ \beta-2\pi=7/4-\pi, \tag{16} \]

and the other eight gaps lie between \(0.024\) and \(1.30004\). Their principal sum is now \(2\pi\). Subtracting the actual \(z\)-edges changes each gap by at most \(Z\), so the actual phase also lies strictly in the winding-one acute cell. The actual trajectory had winding two at \(\tau_0\); a phase passage has therefore occurred. This does not count its primitive-phase branch-cut crossings or assert monotonicity of the primitive closing phase.

docs.title: Finite acute relaxation and a full storage handoff
docs.text:
Acute entry alone is not yet the full trapping certificate. Beginning at the same actual \(\sigma_*\), declare a further slow elapsed time \(\Sigma=128\). Use the nine principal \(y\)-gaps in the new winding-one cell. As long as they remain acute, the edge maximum principle for (11) gives extrema drift at most \(\varepsilon\Sigma\). Together with (16) and \(\varepsilon<5\,10^{-6}\), this gives

\[ \begin{aligned} \min(\text{\(y\)-gaps})&\ge7/4-\pi-128\varepsilon>-7/5,\\ \max(\text{\(y\)-gaps})&\le1.3+136\varepsilon<7/5 . \end{aligned}\tag{17} \]

The inequalities have enough strict margin to include the extra actual-phase error \(Z<2.5\,10^{-6}\). Hence both \(y\) and \(\theta=y-z\), and their connecting segments, remain within the common chart with absolute phase gaps less than \(7/5<\pi/2\) throughout this finite stage. This is again a first-exit bootstrap, not an infinite-time inference from a small perturbation.

Let \(\Theta_1\) be the regular winding-one target in that same cell, with the same zero mean. Its nine principal gaps are \(2\pi/9\). In the retained lift it is \(\Theta_1=2\pi Mh+(2\pi/9)r\), with \(r_j=j-4\), as in the original target construction. The cycle bound \(\lambda_2(L)\ge2/5\) and \(\cos(7/5)>1/6\) imply

\[ \langle v-\Theta_1,f(v)-f(\Theta_1)\rangle_D \le-\frac1{30}\|v-\Theta_1\|_D^2 \tag{18} \]

on this chart. This uses the complete sine Hessian and the \(D=2I\) metric; it does not identify the actual full dynamics with phase-only gradient descent.

At the start of this stage every target edge error has magnitude less than \(7/5+2\pi/9<21/10\). Poincare's inequality therefore gives

\[ R(0):=\|y(\sigma_*)-\Theta_1\|_D<15,\qquad R(v)\le15e^{-v/30}+30\varepsilon,\quad 0\le v\le128 . \tag{19} \]

The second inequality follows by applying (18) to the actual row \(y'=f(y)+e\), with \(\|e\|_D\le\varepsilon\). For example, the squared initial bound is at most \(5\cdot9(21/10)^2<15^2\).

The positive Taylor sum through degree twelve proves \(e^{64/15}>70\). Thus

\[ R(128)<15/70+30(5\,10^{-6})<0.215 . \tag{20} \]

The full actual state, including its form, now satisfies

\[ \begin{aligned} H-H_1^* &\le\|y-\Theta_1-z\|_D^2+\|z\|_D^2/\gamma^2\\ &\le [R(128)+Z]^2+Z^2/\gamma^2<1/20, \qquad H_1^*=9[1-\cos(2\pi/9)] . \end{aligned}\tag{21} \]

Target stationarity and the global phase-Hessian upper bound \(L\) give the phase estimate; the form term follows from \(\lambda_{\max}(L)\le4\) and \(z=\gamma x\). For the final coarse inequality one may use \(R+Z<0.216\), \(Z<2.5\,10^{-6}\) and \(\gamma>1/3300\).

The acute winding-one boundary barrier is \(B_1=9-8\cos(3\pi/16)\). The same outward scalar arithmetic gives

\[ H_1^*<2.106,\qquad B_1>2.348,\qquad H<2.156<B_1,\qquad B_1-H>0.192 . \tag{22} \]

Thus every actual source is inside the acute winding-one cell with complete storage below its full boundary cost. Storage nonincrease traps it there. The only critical relative phase geometry in that cell is the regular winding-one target, so the full-state LaSalle argument gives convergence and permanent winding \(+1\).

docs.title: A common deadline and the resulting source-specific selection
docs.text:
Every member reaches the storage handoff by slow elapsed time \(\sigma_*+128<136\). Once trapped, it remains trapped. Consequently the entire original uncertain corridor is captured by the common structural and original-time bounds

\[ \tau_{\rm cap}=200+\frac{136}{\eta},\qquad t_{\rm cap}=\frac{1024}{1023} \left(200+\frac{136}{\eta}\right). \tag{23} \]

These are finite and conservative structural deadlines. They are not laboratory times or a speed-of-formation claim. No sampled trajectory was used to choose them.

The conclusion includes every admitted latent residual, including any source that could not previously be dismissed by a stable-manifold volume argument. The earlier 57-state list remains a valid necessary energy classification; the additional source-local cone and full-state handoff now exclude its other 56 relative outcomes for this corridor. Other path intervals, constitutive laws and source classes retain their separate obligations.

Capture here is entry into a forward-trapped acute identity cell below its boundary storage. The deadline does not assert the older \(r_c=1/12\) Euclidean radius, a \(10^{-32}\) recovery radius, a contact readiness certificate or any subsequent response. Convergence gives eventual entry into smaller target neighborhoods, without assigning those stronger postconditions the same deadline.

The proof retains both full state channels, the actual hidden initialization, both means and all loss from the original preparation. The parameter \(s\) is a source coordinate, not a time-varying controller. Failure of the sufficient initial cone, error ceiling, tube or storage inequalities for another admitted input is an unresolved selector result, not evidence of a different basin or failed formation.

docs.title: Whole-family limits after the certified winding-two passage
docs.text:
Every complete trajectory from the previously declared interior preparation corridor converges to one of 57 energy-compatible, labeled relative critical geometries. Only three are locally attracting: consensus and the two uniform unit windings. The other 54 are hyperbolic saddles. Their stable manifolds give a precise exceptional-source qualification, not permission to omit them from a whole-family statement.

This result continues the same trajectories from the energy-isometric source path. It uses neither a new preparation nor a later sampled endpoint. The list is an energy-compatible set of possible limits, not a claim that this source family reaches every listed geometry. The argument proves convergence but does not select a limit, a final winding for an antipodal limit, or a uniform capture time.

docs.title: The carried source and its strict energy threshold
docs.text:
Keep the isolated unit C9 with labeled nodes \(0,\ldots,8\), unnormalized Laplacian \(L\), degree matrix \(2I\), capacities one and complete state \((x,\theta)\). The two rows, structural clock and storage are

\[ \begin{gathered} A=L/2,\qquad \gamma=1/(1023\pi),\qquad \tau=(1023/1024)t,\\ x'=-Ax+\gamma f(\theta),\qquad \theta'=\gamma Ax,\qquad f_i(\theta)=\tfrac12\sum_{j\sim i}\sin(\theta_j-\theta_i),\\ H(x,\theta)=\tfrac12x^TLx+ \sum_{\{i,j\}}[1-\cos(\theta_j-\theta_i)],\qquad H'=-\tfrac12\|Lx\|_2^2. \end{gathered}\tag{1} \]

The original-time rows are both multiplied by \(1023/1024\). The complete sine law, support, positive loss and clock are unchanged. Form and lifted-phase means remain zero. No forcing or event is added.

For preparation parameter \(s\in[3/4,4/5]\), retain exactly

\[ x_s(0)=Q_s(ma+\xi),\qquad \theta_s(0)=\zeta,\qquad |\xi_j|,|\zeta_j|\le10^{-10},\qquad \mathbf1^T\xi=\mathbf1^T\zeta=0 . \tag{2} \]

The exact \(M=512\), \(m\), source \(a\), Cayley map \(Q_s\), correlated errors, initial phase/mean/storage equality and source budget \(10^{15}\) are those of the path construction. In particular \(Q_s\) is an invertible map of the zero-mean form space; it is not a time-dependent input or a symmetry of the full flow.

The uniform interior certificate proves that every such actual source has winding two at \(\tau=200\) and

\[ H(200)<\overline H:=7.337282704 <H_2^*:=9[1-\cos(4\pi/9)],\qquad H_2^*>7.437166400 . \tag{3} \]

All decimals in this owner denote exact rationals. Subsequent storage cannot exceed \(H(200)\). The state at \(\tau=200\), its hidden coordinates, both means and its accumulated loss are carried from (2); none is replaced by the source proxy.

Equation (3) already excludes persistent residence in the closed winding-two sector. The additional conclusion here requires classifying all critical states below this energy and proving convergence to one of them. The certified transit time remains 200; no new finite observation horizon is introduced.

docs.title: Exact critical geometries below the inherited energy
docs.text:
At a complete equilibrium, the phase row gives \(Lx=0\), so the zero form mean gives \(x=0\). The form row then gives \(f(\theta)=0\). Orient every cycle edge from \(j\) to \(j+1\bmod9\). Criticality is equivalent to one common oriented sine current on all nine edges.

First suppose that current is positive and less than one. There is \(0<\delta<\pi/2\) such that every principal gap is either \(\delta\) or \(\pi-\delta\). If \(j\) gaps are obtuse, put \(n=9-2j\). The winding \(k\) and potential satisfy

\[ n\delta+j\pi=2\pi k,\qquad U=9-n\cos\delta . \tag{4} \]

Since \(U<\overline H<9\), one must have \(n>0\), hence \(j\le4\). The positive gaps sum to less than \(9\pi/2\), so \(k\) is one or two. For \(k=1\), positivity of \(\delta\) leaves exactly

\[ \begin{array}{c|c|c} j&\delta&U\\ \hline 0&2\pi/9&9[1-\cos(2\pi/9)]\\ 1&\pi/7&9-7\cos(\pi/7). \end{array}\tag{5} \]

For \(k=2\), the possibilities \(j=0,1,2,3\) instead have

\[ \delta=\pi/2-\pi/(2n),\qquad U=9-n\sin\frac{\pi}{2n}\ge H_2^* . \tag{6} \]

The inequality follows because \(n\sin(c/n)\) increases on this range: its derivative is \(\sin z-z\cos z>0\) for \(0<z<\pi/2\). These states are excluded by (3). Negative current is the exact sign-reflected classification.

Current \(+1\) or \(-1\) would require all nine gaps to equal \(+\pi/2\) or \(-\pi/2\). Their sum is not an integer multiple of \(2\pi\), so neither case is a cycle geometry. This excludes the zero-cosine degeneracy.

For zero current, every circular gap is zero or \(\pi\). Cycle closure requires an even number \(j\) of antipodal edges, and \(U=2j\). The only cases below \(\overline H<8\) are \(j=0\) and \(j=2\). Assigning signs to the representative \(\pi\) gaps does not create different circular configurations. An arbitrary wrapping convention at these edges does not define a robust winding.

The complete below-threshold census is therefore:

Relative critical geometry Number on labeled C9 Potential Relative negative Hessian index Consensus \(1\) \(0\) \(0\) Uniform gaps \(+2\pi/9\) or \(-2\pi/9\) \(2\) \(9[1-\cos(2\pi/9)]\) \(0\) One gap \(\pm6\pi/7\), the other eight \(\pm\pi/7\), with a common sign \(18\) \(9-7\cos(\pi/7)\) \(1\) Two antipodal edges, the other seven aligned \(\binom92=36\) \(4\) \(2\) Total \(57\)

All displayed potentials are below \(\overline H\): the two nonzero-current values are less than \(9/2\) and \(11/2\), respectively, by \(\cos(2\pi/9)>1/2\) and \(\cos(\pi/7)>1/2\). Thus the table is exactly the critical set permitted by this energy threshold. It removes one common phase origin but retains node labels and the two handedness choices. Graph rotations or reflections are not divided out. This count is not a count of physically identified objects or a reachability result.

docs.title: Shared exact odd-cycle closure
docs.text:
The underlying geometric enumeration extends to any odd cycle size \(N\ge3\). Write its principal sine branch in turns as \(a_{\rm pr}\in(-1/4,1/4)\). Every edge is either \(a_{\rm pr}\) or \(1/2-a_{\rm pr}\) modulo one turn. For a chosen mask of \(j\) supplementary edges, exact closure has the form

\[ p=(N-2j)a_{\rm pr}+j/2,\qquad a_{\rm pr}=\frac{2p-j}{2(N-2j)},\qquad p\in\mathbb Z,\quad -N/4<p<3N/4,\quad |a_{\rm pr}|<1/4 . \tag{6a} \]

Oddness makes \(N-2j\ne0\). The missing quarter-turn endpoints would require all edges to have the same current \(+1\) or \(-1\), impossible for odd cycle closure. Thus (6a) and all masks give every labeled critical geometry once. The zero-current masks are included; closure then requires \(j\) even. These representatives are continuous edge turns for solving closure, not necessarily principal winding increments.

For C9 the numbers of admitted periods for masks with \(j=0,\ldots,9\) are \(5,4,3,2,1,0,1,2,3,4\). Weighting by \(\binom9j\) gives 630 complete critical geometries modulo common phase before applying the energy test. The preceding table is their 57-member below-threshold subset.

docs.title: Relative nondegeneracy and the complete two-row stability
docs.text:
Let \(B\) be the oriented cycle incidence matrix. At any listed geometry, the phase Hessian is

\[ H_\theta=B^T\operatorname{diag}(c\sigma_e)B,\qquad c>0,\quad \sigma_e\in\{-1,1\}, \tag{7} \]

with \(j=0,1,2\) negative signs. Relative nodal perturbations map isomorphically to edge perturbations \(v\) with \(\mathbf1^Tv=0\). On the full edge space, the diagonal form has inertia \((9-j,j,0)\). Its orthogonal complement to that constrained subspace, in this quadratic form, is spanned by \(\operatorname{diag}(c\sigma_e)^{-1}\mathbf1\), whose squared form is

\[ \mathbf1^T\operatorname{diag}(c\sigma_e)^{-1}\mathbf1 =(9-2j)/c>0 . \tag{8} \]

Removing this one positive direction proves relative inertia \((8-j,j,0)\). In particular every listed equilibrium is nondegenerate after removing common phase. For the general odd-\(N\) closure in (6a), the same scalar is \((N-2j)/c\), which is never zero. Removing its sign from the full diagonal inertia proves

\[ \operatorname{ind}_-(H_{\rm relative}) =j-\mathbf1_{\{2j>N\}},\qquad \operatorname{null}(H_{\rm relative})=0 . \tag{8a} \]

This is the shared geometric count; it does not itself supply a dynamical stability or basin verdict.

The positive-loss reciprocal Jacobian argument applies to the actual C9 matrices. On the common-mean-zero space set \(C=H_\theta/2\). Linearization of both rows in (1) gives

\[ \begin{pmatrix}X\\Y\end{pmatrix}'= \begin{pmatrix}-A&-\gamma C\\ \gamma A&0\end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix}X\\Y\end{pmatrix}. \tag{9} \]

Writing \(Y=A^{1/2}z\) reduces the characteristic equation to

\[ P(\lambda)=\lambda^2I+\lambda A+ \gamma^2 A^{1/2}CA^{1/2}. \tag{10} \]

Here \(A\) is positive definite on the eight-dimensional relative space. For a nonreal characteristic root, the imaginary-part identity forces strictly negative real part. On the nonnegative real axis, \(P'(\lambda)=2\lambda I+A\) is positive definite. Each negative stiffness direction crosses zero once, and there is no relative zero root. Thus exactly \(j\) full-state modes are unstable, and \(16-j\) are stable. All 57 equilibria are hyperbolic on the conserved-mean leaf.

Consequently consensus and the two uniform unit windings are the only locally exponentially attracting geometries below the energy threshold. They represent three oriented geometries and two winding magnitudes, zero and one. The 18 one-obtuse configurations have one unstable direction; the 36 two-antipodal configurations have two. Phase Hessian stability alone is not substituted for the coupled form/phase calculation.

docs.title: Every actual source converges to one listed complete state
docs.text:
At and after \(\tau=200\), the zero form mean and \(\tfrac12x^TLx\le H(200)\) bound the form coordinates. Circular phases lie in a compact torus, so the carried storage sublevel is a compact forward-invariant state domain. LaSalle's invariance principle confines the omega-limit set to the largest invariant subset of \(Lx=0\). There \(x=0\), and invariance of the form row requires \(f(\theta)=0\).

The conserved lifted phase sum supplies the additional circular invariant

\[ \prod_{j=0}^8 e^{i\theta_j(\tau)} =e^{i\sum_j\theta_j(0)}=1 . \tag{11} \]

Each relative critical geometry intersects this product-phase slice in exactly nine common rotations: a rotation by \(\varphi\) multiplies the product by \(e^{9i\varphi}\). Therefore the relevant circular equilibrium set has only \(9\cdot57\) points, even though unrestricted common rotation is a continuous symmetry.

An omega-limit set of a precompact continuous trajectory is nonempty, compact and connected. For completeness, each closure of a trajectory tail is connected, and the omega-limit set is their nested intersection. A connected subset of the finite critical set in (11) contains a single point. Hence every actual source in (2) converges in form and circular phase to one complete equilibrium from the table.

This also proves convergence of the originally continued real phase lifts. Around the limiting circular phases choose fixed small arcs. At sufficiently late times each phase remains in its arc; continuity fixes its integer lift branch there. Each real phase therefore converges, and the limiting lift sum retains its original value zero. The terminal integer-turn vector and common phase origin are consequences of the actual history, not reinitialized coordinates. No convergence rate, common deadline or last-passage time is derived by this argument. The same finite-set argument proves convergence for any finite source on this declared C9 mean leaf, using all 630 relative geometries. The inherited strict energy bound narrows the possible limits to 57; it is not needed for the general convergence fact.

The limits with no antipodal edge have eventual constant winding: zero for consensus and \(\pm1\) for both the uniform and the one-obtuse configurations. A two-antipodal limit has no convention-independent winding at the limit; convergence to it does not prove eventual residence in one open winding sector. All trajectories eventually avoid the closed sectors with winding magnitude at least two, because none of the listed limits lies in those closed sectors. For a two-antipodal geometry their possible limiting signed gap sums are only \(-2\pi,0,2\pi\).

docs.title: Exceptional saddle sources and what remains undecided
docs.text:
For each fixed \(s\), the map

\[ (\xi,\zeta)\longmapsto\bigl(Q_s(ma+\xi),\zeta\bigr) \tag{12} \]

is an invertible affine chart from the sixteen-dimensional zero-sum latent space onto the corresponding full-state mean leaf near this source. The phase-error box is small enough to be an injective local chart of the circular phases. No latent coordinate is discarded.

The stable-manifold theorem gives the full-state saddle basins as global stable manifolds of dimensions 15 or 14, respectively. Equivalently these sets can be covered by countably many backward images of local stable manifold charts. The smooth complete flow and the fixed-\(s\) source chart preserve their dimensions. The latent sources converging to an index-one saddle therefore lie in a countable union of codimension-one immersed submanifolds; those converging to an index-two saddle lie in the corresponding codimension-two union.

In particular the union of all saddle-source subsets has sixteen-dimensional Lebesgue measure zero for every fixed \(s\). Outside that exceptional set, each source converges to consensus or one of the two uniform unit windings. This is a statement about the dimension and measure of specified sets, not an assigned probability of any outcome. It does not give the basin volumes of the three attractors, an outcome distribution, or a deterministic class selector.

Nor does it remove the exceptional sources from the admitted closed error family. Their intersection with that family has not been proved empty. A one-dimensional nominal source path may intersect or even locally follow a stable manifold; ambient measure zero cannot settle its outcome. No claim that every source is captured by a stable identity follows.

If a particular trajectory converges to one of the three attractors, it eventually enters a small forward-trapped identity neighborhood of that target. The preceding argument neither supplies that entry time nor decides which target is selected. A saddle limit is a convergent critical configuration, not an attracting acquired identity. The present restriction is therefore stronger than exclusion of winding two but weaker than whole-family capture by one organization.

The separate source-specific capture proof now supplies that additional bridge for the original interior corridor. It carries the actual mixed state into the winding-one storage trap and excludes the other 56 candidates there, including every saddle exception. The energy classification above remains valid for other sources; its candidate list alone supplies no such selector.

docs.title: Implementation and evidence boundary
docs.text:
The path source owner owns the exact preparation, coupled semigroup bounds and inherited storage threshold. The private limit classifier rebuilds the C9 critical geometries, their energy admission and relative inertias; the independent controls check closure, label counts, excluded energy classes and complete stability dimensions. Its finite algebraic list is not an evaluated forward history. The exact closure and signed-edge inertia are shared in phase cycle geometry through the odd-cycle formulas (6a) and (8a). Existing C5 consumers retain their own support and complete-law admission; their topology-specific reports are not transferred to C9.

The private limit API also accepts other primitive path intervals, times and error budgets admitted by the source owner. It rebuilds that source and storage bound, rather than accepting an incoming report. Finite-set convergence remains valid when a source-policy flag fails; the source policy and the energy filter have different responsibilities. Equality with a critical energy, or an unresolved interval comparison, retains the critical candidate. Antipodal candidates have unavailable winding. If either latent error row has zero radius, the source is no longer full dimensional and the API withholds the fixed-\(s\) null-volume conclusion.

The conclusions use the fixed sine law and complete source family in (1)--(3). They cannot be transferred merely from a winding label to another support, constitutive law, contact geometry, clock or later interface. No new trajectory, time-coefficient series, frozen response, source reset or observed limit is used. Autonomous preparation and physical identification remain separate questions.

docs.title: Constitutive robustness of the source-specific winding selector
docs.text:
Every member of the declared matched-potential family acquires the same winding-one identity from the original uncertain Cayley corridor. This is a uniform statement for all preparation parameters \(s\in[3/4,4/5]\), all admitted latent errors and all fixed constitutive parameters \(\lambda\in[0,1]\). It is proved from each law's own source transport, current ordering, curvature and full storage. Matching the targets or their tangents alone would not imply this result.

The sine selector supplies the two-stage argument. The constitutive family supplies the alternative complete laws. This owner joins those mechanisms only after re-admitting their hypotheses. No trajectory, source sweep, coefficient producer or frozen response is evaluated.

docs.title: Complete laws and the retained identity
docs.text:
Use one isolated unit C9, signed form \(x\), primitive phase lifts \(\theta\), degree matrix \(D=2I\), unnormalized Laplacian \(L\) and \(A=L/2\). Hold capacities at one and retain the same structural clocks and coefficients:

\[ e=1023/1024,\qquad \tau=et,\qquad \gamma=1/(1023\pi),\qquad \eta=\gamma^2. \tag{1} \]

For each fixed \(\lambda\in[0,1]\), the potential and current are

\[ \begin{aligned} V_\lambda(\delta)&=1-\cos\delta+\lambda W(\delta),& W(\delta)&=\frac{(1-\cos9\delta)^2}{6\,9^4},\\ j_\lambda(\delta)&=\sin\delta+ \frac{\lambda}{2187} \left(\sin9\delta-\tfrac12\sin18\delta\right),& f_{\lambda,i}(\theta)&=\tfrac12\sum_{j\sim i} j_\lambda(\theta_j-\theta_i). \end{aligned}\tag{2} \]

The actual complete rows and storage balance are

\[ \begin{aligned} x'&=-Ax+\gamma f_\lambda(\theta),& \theta'&=\gamma Ax,\\ H_\lambda&=\tfrac12x^TLx+ \sum_{\{i,j\}}V_\lambda(\theta_j-\theta_i),& H_\lambda'&=-\tfrac12\|Lx\|_2^2. \end{aligned}\tag{3} \]

Primes here denote \(\tau\). Both original-time rows are multiplied by \(e\), as is the loss. The first row independently supplies the pressure for the unit-capacity nodal equation. Both ordinary means remain zero. Support, capacity, loss, clock and source are supplied premises; there are no events, controllers, coefficient changes or state resets.

The organization is the same winding identity as in the sine proof: full constituent form and phase remain available, and a phase cell with an admitted full-storage margin is forward trapped. The conclusion concerns acquisition on the supplied substrate. It does not derive constituent birth, a support selector, an autonomous preparation, a collective event or realization of the thirteen operator contracts. The execution path is a detached continuous-law proof, not an operator word or the native relational runtime.

docs.title: Sufficient constitutive conditions for the mechanism
docs.text:
For an even periodic potential \(V\) and odd current \(j=V'\), the same reciprocal rows admit the mixed coordinate

\[ z=\gamma x,\qquad y=\theta+z,\qquad \sigma=\eta(\tau-200),\qquad y_\sigma=f(y-z)=f(y)+r. \tag{4} \]

This is an identity on the actual full solution; \(y\) is not a replacement primitive phase. The following are sufficient conditions, not claimed necessary properties of every selector or every TNFR law:

  1. Complete source transport. A globally admitted field with \(\|f\|_D\le F\), \(D\)-Lipschitz constant \(L_f\), the declared spectral gap and the original correlated source gives a uniform future form bound \(Z\), hence \(\|r\|_D\le\varepsilon=L_fZ\). Its own mixed initialization must satisfy the source cone below.
  2. Passage ordering. The current increases on the ordinary gap interval. With \(k(q)=j(\pi-q)\), its actual closing current, require \(j(m)-k(q)>3/10+\varepsilon\) whenever the proof has \(-7/4\le q\le63/100\), \(m\ge0.899+q/2>0\), and the admitted ordinary gaps. This closes the cone and bounds the passage time.
  3. Finite contraction. On the subsequent chart \(|\delta|\le7/5\), require \(V''\ge\mu>0\), an admitted contraction rate \(\alpha\le\mu/5\), and enough finite time to lower the full state storage. The bounded residual must keep both \(y\) and the actual \(\theta=y-z\) in this chart during that stage.
  4. Permanent storage protection. The actual reciprocal loss must hold, with an upper bound on complete reached storage below every face of the enclosing winding-one cell. Uniqueness of its critical relative phase geometry must be proved for this current. Positive curvature over the entire open acute cell is one sufficient condition for that uniqueness.

The retained source correlations, both means and the full form energy are part of these conditions. The following sections verify them uniformly for (2). They do not infer them from equilibrium agreement.

docs.title: Own-law transport of the original uncertain source
docs.text:
Keep the exact Cayley preparation, including \(M=512\), \(m=(2046/9)(355/113)^2\), \(h=e_3-e_4\), \(r_j=j-4\), \(a=(9M+M^{-1})h+r\), and

\[ x_s(0)=Q_s(ma+\xi),\qquad \theta_s(0)=\zeta, \qquad s\in[3/4,4/5]. \tag{5} \]

The two latent vectors have separate exact zero sums and coordinate bounds \(\rho_x=\rho_\theta=10^{-10}\). The form residual is \(Q_s\xi\), not an independently chosen box after transport. The full sixteen-dimensional relative source neighborhood and its zero-error member are included at every fixed \(s\).

The exact \(L\)-isometry gives equal initial form storage along this path for each latent realization. Since the same \(\zeta\) occurs for every \(s\), complete initial storage is equal along the path within each law. Storage across different potentials need not be equal. The old source upper bound acquires its own additional term:

\[ B_{\lambda,\mathrm{source}}= \frac12\sum_{\{i,j\}} (m|a_j-a_i|+2\rho_x)^2 +18\rho_\theta^2+6\lambda\rho_\theta^4 <320680599854722<10^{15}. \tag{6} \]

Indeed \(0\le W(v)\le v^4/24\) and \(|\zeta_j-\zeta_i|\le2\rho_\theta\) on nine edges. This positive quartic term is retained even below the interval grid scale. Every source has initial winding zero, independently of the chosen law.

For a uniform bound over \(0\le\lambda\le\Lambda\le1\), put

\[ a_\Lambda=\Lambda/1458,\qquad u_\Lambda=1+2\Lambda/243,\qquad F_\Lambda=\sqrt{18}(1+a_\Lambda). \tag{7} \]

Direct real derivative bounds for (2) give

\[ |j_\lambda-\sin|\le a_\Lambda,\qquad |j_\lambda'|\le u_\Lambda,\qquad \|f_\lambda\|_D\le F_\Lambda,\qquad L_f\le2u_\Lambda,\qquad \nabla^2U_\lambda\preceq u_\Lambda L. \tag{8} \]

They give global existence and uniqueness in the retained real lifts. The graph semigroup estimate \(e^{-\tau/5}\) is law independent. The raw error norms are still \(E_x=\sqrt{18}\gamma(1025/1023)\rho_x\) and \(E_\theta=\sqrt{18}\rho_\theta\); the enlarged forcing constant does not multiply those independent source errors.

Let \(N\) be the exact-source nominal norm bound and \(\rho\ge e^{-40}\), rebuilt as in the path owner. At \(\tau_0=200\), and uniformly for every later time, variation of constants gives

\[ \begin{aligned} R_{z,\Lambda}(200)&=\rho(N+E_x)+5\eta F_\Lambda,\\ Z_\Lambda&=\max\{R_{z,\Lambda}(200),5\eta F_\Lambda\},& \varepsilon_\Lambda&=2u_\Lambda Z_\Lambda. \end{aligned}\tag{9} \]

Integrating the exact mixed row instead gives

\[ y(200)-\gamma mQ_sa =\zeta+\gamma Q_s\xi+ \eta\int_0^{200}f_\lambda(\theta(v))\,dv, \qquad E_{y,\Lambda}=E_x+E_\theta+200\eta F_\Lambda. \tag{10} \]

There is no extra \(R_z\) in (10): the final fast form cancels exactly in this mixed identity. It remains fully present in (9) and later storage.

At \(\Lambda=1\), outward rational arithmetic gives

\[ Z_\Lambda<2.056\,10^{-6},\qquad \varepsilon_\Lambda<4.145\,10^{-6}<5\,10^{-6},\qquad E_{y,\Lambda}<8.221\,10^{-5}. \tag{11} \]

These are own-law estimates, not sine transit estimates reused as premises.

docs.title: Passage ordering with the correct closing current
docs.text:
Use the same fixed lift offsets as the sine proof:

\[ \widetilde y=y-2\pi Mh,\quad d_i=\widetilde y_{i+1}-\widetilde y_i\ (0\le i<8),\quad \beta=\widetilde y_0-\widetilde y_8+4\pi,\quad q=\pi-\beta. \tag{12} \]

Thus \(\sum_i d_i-q=3\pi\). The original source proxy and (10) prove, uniformly over the complete family,

\[ 0.3489<q(0)<0.6285<0.63,\qquad \min_i d_i(0)>1.2215,\qquad \max_i d_i(0)<1.2570, \qquad \min_i d_i(0)-q(0)/2>0.9073>0.9. \tag{13} \]

The primitive phase edges differ by at most \(Z_\Lambda\). They therefore have winding two at \(\tau=200\), with the same strict cut margins. This finite-time winding alone is not a capture certificate.

The actual continued closing current is

\[ k_\lambda(q)=j_\lambda(\pi-q) =\sin q+\frac{\lambda}{2187} \left(\sin9q+\tfrac12\sin18q\right). \tag{14} \]

In general it is not \(j_\lambda(q)\). The eighteenth harmonic changes sign under this reflection. The mixed edge equations are

\[ \begin{aligned} d_i'&=\tfrac12[j_\lambda(d_{i-1})-2j_\lambda(d_i) +j_\lambda(d_{i+1})]+r_i,\\ q'&=k_\lambda(q)-\tfrac12[j_\lambda(d_0)+j_\lambda(d_7)]+r_q, \qquad |r_i|,|r_q|\le\varepsilon_\Lambda . \end{aligned}\tag{15} \]

Primes now denote \(\sigma\), and missing endpoint neighbors have current \(k_\lambda(q)\). An edge functional has dual \(D\)-norm one.

Write \(m_d=\min_i d_i\), \(M_d=\max_i d_i\), \(C=m_d-q/2\), and \(\Delta_\lambda=j_\lambda(m_d)-k_\lambda(q)\). Where the ordinary current increases and \(\Delta_\lambda\ge0\), the same endpoint cancellation gives the one-sided inequalities

\[ C'\ge-\tfrac32\varepsilon_\Lambda,\qquad M_d'\le\varepsilon_\Lambda,\qquad q'\le-\Delta_\lambda+\varepsilon_\Lambda. \tag{16} \]

For eight slow units these retain \(C>0.899\), \(m_d>0.024\) and \(M_d<1.301\), until the target \(q_*=-7/4\). The sine comparison in this same cone gives

\[ \sin m_d-\sin q\ge \min\{\sin(1.214)-\sin(0.63),\sin(0.649),\sin(0.5)\}>1/3. \tag{17} \]

Both \(j_\lambda\) and \(k_\lambda\) differ from their sine terms by at most \(a_\Lambda\). Consequently

\[ \Delta_\lambda>1/3-2a_\Lambda,\qquad 1/3-1/729-5\,10^{-6}>3/10. \tag{18} \]

The positive curvature proved below also supplies the ordinary current ordering. The strict cone closes by first exit, and each actual source reaches \(q_*\) at its own time

\[ 0<\sigma_*<\frac{0.63+1.75}{0.3}=119/15<8. \tag{19} \]

Its closing principal mixed gap is then \(7/4-\pi\); the eight other gaps are positive and less than \(1.30004\). Subtracting the retained \(z\)-edges places the actual primitive phase in the winding-one acute cell. This passage is smooth full-state evolution, not a named event. No coincidence of mixed and primitive branch-cut times is asserted.

docs.title: Own-law curvature, storage and permanent capture
docs.text:
Differentiate the supplied potential:

\[ V_\lambda''(\delta)=\cos\delta+ \frac{\lambda}{243}(\cos9\delta-\cos18\delta). \tag{20} \]

This is strictly positive throughout \(|\delta|<\pi/2\), as follows without extrapolating a target tangent. On \(|\delta|\le3/2\), \(V_\lambda''\ge\cos(3/2)-2/243>0\). On the remaining acute interval, \(17\pi/36<3/2\) ensures \(\cos9\delta\ge0\) and \(\cos18\delta\le0\); the added curvature is nonnegative and \(\cos\delta>0\). Evenness covers negative gaps.

For a further 128 slow units after each actual \(\sigma_*\), the edge maximum principle and (11) keep the mixed gaps within \([7/4-\pi-128\varepsilon_\Lambda, 1.3+136\varepsilon_\Lambda]\). Including the actual phase edge error \(Z_\Lambda\), their absolute magnitudes are less than \(7/5\). At \(\Lambda=1\) the rebuilt bound is less than \(1.392126\). This is a finite first-exit argument for both coordinates, including their connecting segments.

On that smaller chart,

\[ \mu_\Lambda:=\cos(7/5)-2\Lambda/243 >1/6-2/243=77/486>5/32. \tag{21} \]

Combined with the graph quotient gap \(1/5\), this admits the uniform contraction rate \(\alpha=1/32\). The sine rate \(1/30\) is not silently carried into the new law. The target in this same lift is \(\Theta_1=2\pi Mh+(2\pi/9)r\); its mean is zero and its currents cancel for every law. Let \(R=\|y-\Theta_1\|_D\). The same geometric Poincare bound gives \(R(0)<15\) at the passage endpoint, and the actual perturbed mixed row gives

\[ R(v)\le15e^{-v/32}+32\varepsilon_\Lambda, \qquad 0\le v\le128. \tag{22} \]

The positive Taylor sum through degree nine proves \(e^4>54\), so \(R(128)<15/54+32(5\,10^{-6})<0.278\).

The full storage upper bound uses the actual primitive phase and the global own-law Hessian bound (8):

\[ H_\lambda\le H_1^*+ u_\Lambda[R(128)+Z_\Lambda]^2+Z_\Lambda^2/\gamma^2, \qquad H_1^*=9[1-\cos(2\pi/9)]. \tag{23} \]

The target value is unchanged because \(W(2\pi/9)=0\). Since \(W\ge0\), the sine all-face acute boundary bound remains a valid lower bound on this law's own boundary storage:

\[ B_{\lambda,1}\ge B_1=9-8\cos(3\pi/16)>2.348. \tag{24} \]

No equality of boundary minima or later losses between laws is required. Using \(H_1^*<2.106\), \(u_\Lambda<1.009\), \(R+Z<0.279\), \(Z<2.5\,10^{-6}\) and \(\gamma>1/3300\), the storage excess in (23) is below \(0.079\). Thus \(H_\lambda<2.185<B_1\), a strict full-state margin greater than \(0.163\). Tighter outward bounds at \(\Lambda=1\) are

\[ R(128)<0.274868,\qquad H_\lambda<2.181819,\qquad B_1-H_\lambda>0.166424. \tag{25} \]

Full storage nonincrease now traps every member in the acute winding-one cell. Equation (20) proves strict convexity of its potential on the relative lift chart, so the regular winding-one phase is its unique relative critical geometry. On the fixed zero-mean leaf the trapped sublevel is compact. Zero loss forces \(Lx=0\); remaining in the zero-loss set then requires \(f_\lambda(\theta)=0\). LaSalle's argument therefore gives convergence of the actual full state to \((0,\Theta_1)\) and permanent winding \(+1\).

Every member is captured by its own time \(\sigma_*+128<136\). Only the subsequent storage trapping carries that result to a common deadline and all later times:

\[ \tau_{\mathrm{cap}}=200+136/\eta,\qquad t_{\mathrm{cap}}=(1024/1023)(200+136/\eta). \tag{26} \]

The numerical budgets coincide with those of the sine proof because these new bounds suffice, not because the old deadline transfers automatically. They remain conservative structural times without a laboratory unit bridge.

docs.title: What this robustness establishes and leaves free
docs.text:
The captured identity agrees throughout this already declared law family on the entire original uncertain source corridor. This particular formation observation consequently does not discriminate \(\lambda\). The laws still have different currents, transient histories and higher nonlinear fields. Their nominal distinct-neighbor interaction onset can even have opposite signs. That separate interaction theorem retains its own joined support, nominal preparation, supplied inputs and local time scope; acquisition here does not install its contact or replace reached states with nominal targets.

The result is conditional robustness over a bounded class of complete laws. It establishes neither one attractor shared by all TNFR dynamics, absence of fixed natural laws, unique constitutive selection nor physical identity. The earlier 57-state sine critical census is neither transferred to \(\lambda>0\) nor needed here: convergence follows from this law's own acute Hessian, loss and means after full-storage trapping. Other source-path intervals remain unresolved. Capture at (26) means a protected acute identity cell; it does not assert the older \(1/12\) radius, a specified recovery precision, contact readiness or a closed collective response at that deadline.

The private own-law calculator re-admits primitive deformation/source intervals and error budgets, reuses the shared exact source geometry, and evaluates the bounds above. Its independent controls check current reflection, source errors, uniform margins, full storage, representation boundaries and explicit abstention when sufficient conditions fail. An incoming report, cached verdict or sine transit result cannot replace an actual-law premise. The execution plan alone owns subsequent research admission.

docs.title: Source-local capture and a transient-winding obstruction on an energy-matched path
docs.text:
One continuous family of preparations, under one fixed complete law, has source intervals that provably acquire different winding classes. An interior interval has actual winding two at the declared observation time but cannot retain that winding. Thus the finite-transit winding is not a sufficient selector of the eventual organized state, even when initial phase, means and storage are held exactly equal for each correlated source realization.

This result extends the matched preparation pair. It supplies two positive capture corridors and one negative selector result; it does not locate a basin boundary or identify the eventual class in the negative corridor. All assessments below are analytic scalar bounds. No trajectory, reverse-flow source, time-coefficient producer or parameter sweep is used.

docs.title: Fixed complete law and source budgets
docs.text:
Use the isolated unit C9 with nodes \(0,\ldots,8\), cycle edges \(j--(j+1\bmod9)\), unnormalized Laplacian \(L\), degree matrix \(2I\), held capacities one, signed form \(x\), and primitive circular phase with continued lifts \(\theta\). The complete law, clocks and storage are

\[ \begin{gathered} e=1023/1024,\quad w=1/1024,\quad \tau=et,\quad \gamma=1/(1023\pi),\quad A=L/2,\quad \eta=\gamma^2,\\ x'=-Ax+\gamma f(\theta),\qquad \theta'=\gamma Ax,\qquad f_i(\theta)=\tfrac12\sum_{j\sim i}\sin(\theta_j-\theta_i),\\ H(x,\theta)=\tfrac12x^TLx+U(\theta),\qquad U(\theta)=\sum_{\{i,j\}}[1-\cos(\theta_j-\theta_i)],\qquad H'=-\tfrac12\|Lx\|_2^2 . \end{gathered}\tag{1} \]

Both original-time rows are \(e\) times their structural-time rows. Both ordinary means, equivalently the degree-weighted means on this regular support, are conserved. Support, pressure, capacity and clock are supplied; there are no events, controllers or state resets during acquisition. The sine law is fixed throughout: no constitutive parameter is varied.

Retain the exact preparation constants

\[ \begin{gathered} M=512,\qquad m=\frac{2046}{9}\left(\frac{355}{113}\right)^2,\qquad \epsilon=10^{-10},\qquad T=200,\qquad B_{\rm source}=10^{15},\\ r_j=j-4,\qquad h=e_3-e_4,\qquad a=(9M+M^{-1})h+r,\qquad b=(9M-M^{-1})h+2r . \end{gathered}\tag{2} \]

The original time is \(204800/1023\). The earlier reference radius \(r_c=1/12\) remains a possible eventual recovery radius, but the broad corridors below use an acute-cell capture criterion at \(T\); they do not assert entry into that small Euclidean ball at \(T\).

The graph identities

\[ r^TLr=72,\quad h^TLh=6,\quad h^TLr=0,\quad \mathbf1^Tr=\mathbf1^Th=0,\quad a^TLa=b^TLb=486M^2+180+6/M^2 \tag{3} \]

are the algebraic basis for exact storage matching.

docs.title: A continuous exact energy isometry, including the errors
docs.text:
Put

\[ \begin{gathered} u=a+b=18Mh+3r,\qquad v=b-a=-2h/M+r,\\ U_L=u^TLu=648(3M^2+1),\qquad V_L=v^TLv=24(3M^2+1)/M^2,\qquad u^TLv=0,\qquad \kappa=V_L/U_L=1/(27M^2),\\ \mathcal K=\frac{v u^TL-u v^TL}{U_L}. \end{gathered}\tag{4} \]

Direct multiplication gives \(\mathcal Ku=v\), \(\mathcal Kv=-\kappa u\), \(\mathcal K^3=-\kappa\mathcal K\), \(\mathcal K^TL=-L\mathcal K\), and \(\mathcal K\mathbf1=\mathbf0=\mathbf1^T\mathcal K\). For the preparation parameter \(s\in[0,1]\), define

\[ Q_s=(I-s\mathcal K)^{-1}(I+s\mathcal K) =I+\frac{2s}{1+\kappa s^2}\mathcal K +\frac{2s^2}{1+\kappa s^2}\mathcal K^2 . \tag{5} \]

The polynomial formula proves existence without a numerical matrix inverse. It implies \(Q_s^TLQ_s=L\), preservation of both mean functionals, \(Q_0=I\), and \(Q_1a=b\). The map is continuous and invertible. It is an isometry of preparation energy, not a symmetry of the complete form-and-phase flow.

For every single latent pair

\[ |\xi_j|,|\zeta_j|\le\epsilon,\qquad \mathbf1^T\xi=\mathbf1^T\zeta=0, \tag{6} \]

the entire source path is

\[ x_s(0)=Q_s(ma+\xi),\qquad \theta_s(0)=\zeta . \tag{7} \]

Thus initial phase, both means and complete storage are exactly the same for every \(s\) in that realization. Each fixed-\(s\) source family retains the full sixteen-dimensional relative interior of its form/phase error domain. Cartesian marginal bounds do not replace the correlations in (7). In particular \(Q_1\) need not equal the previous pair's metric reflection on errors; its uncertainty is re-admitted here.

Uniform admission follows from

\[ \begin{gathered} \|u\|_\infty=18M,\quad \|v\|_\infty=4,\quad \|Lu\|_1=144M+54,\quad \|Lv\|_1=18+16/M,\\ \|\mathcal K\|_\infty\le \frac{4(144M+54)+18M(18+16/M)}{U_L} =\frac{461304}{509608584}<\frac1{1024},\\ \|Q_s\|_\infty\le \frac{1+\|\mathcal K\|_\infty}{1-\|\mathcal K\|_\infty} < C_Q:=\frac{1025}{1023}. \end{gathered}\tag{8} \]

The last inequality uses the Neumann expansion of \(I-s\mathcal K\). Hence every mapped form error has magnitude at most \(C_Q\epsilon\); phase errors still have magnitude at most \(\epsilon\).

The common source cost is bounded once, at \(s=0\):

\[ H(x_s(0),\zeta)\le \frac12\sum_{\{i,j\}}(m|a_j-a_i|+2\epsilon)^2+18\epsilon^2 <320680599854722<10^{15}. \tag{9} \]

Equation (5), not a second box estimate, transfers this same cost to all \(s\). Every source has initial winding zero.

docs.title: Source-local predictors with complete transient errors
docs.text:
Write \(Q_sa=p(s)h+q(s)r\). With \(D_s=1+\kappa s^2\), \(P_0=9M+M^{-1}\) and \(C=18M\kappa-2/M=-4/(3M)\), the exact scalar formulas are

\[ p(s)= rac{P_0+Cs-\kappa P_0s^2}{D_s},\qquad q(s)= rac{1+s+\kappa(3s-s^2)}{D_s} =1+s+ rac{\kappa s(1-s)(s+3)}{D_s}. ag{10} \]

Here \(p\) decreases from \(9M+M^{-1}\) to \(9M-M^{-1}\); \(q\) increases from one to two. Indeed,

\[ p'= rac{C(1-\kappa s^2)-4\kappa P_0s}{D_s^2}<0,\qquad q'= rac{1+3\kappa-4\kappa s-\kappa s^2-3\kappa^2s^2}{D_s^2}>0. ag{11} \]

For the latter, the numerator is at least \(1-2\kappa-3\kappa^2>0\).

The isolated acquisition estimate gives \(\|e^{-A au}P_9\|_{2I}\le e^{- au/5}\), \(\|f\|_{2I}\le F=\sqrt{18}\), and \(\lambda_{\max}(L)\le4\). Let \( ho\ge e^{-40}\). A single bound valid over the whole path is

\[ egin{aligned} N&=\gamma m\sqrt{2(2P_0^2+240)},& E_x&=\sqrt{18}\gamma C_Q\epsilon,& E_ heta&=\sqrt{18}\epsilon,\ R_z&= ho(N+E_x)+5\eta F,& R_x&=R_z/(\gamma\sqrt2),& E&=(E_x+E_ heta+R_z+\eta FT)/\sqrt2 . \end{aligned} ag{12} \]

The source norm uses \(\|ph+qr\|_2^2=2p^2-2pq+60q^2\le2P_0^2+240\). An implementation may replace this global upper bound by the corresponding interval's endpoint bounds, retaining the same inequality.

Variation of constants for \(z=\gamma x\) and integration of both complete rows give, for every admitted source,

\[ \|x_s(T)\|_2\le R_x,\qquad \| heta_s(T)-\gamma mQ_sa\|_2\le E,\qquad heta_s(T)-\gamma mQ_sa =\zeta+\gamma Q_s\xi-z(T)+\eta\int_0^T f( heta_s(v))\,dv. ag{13} \]

The large source lift is retained in (12); it is not removed from the semigroup or uncertainty calculation. Outward scalar arithmetic gives

\[ R_x<0.004667300447,\qquad E<0.000059542394,\qquad 2R_x^2+6E<0.000400821752 . ag{14} \]

These decimal constants are exact rational upper bounds.

For circular phase and potential calculations alone write the proxy as

\[ \gamma mQ_sa=2\pi Mh+t(s)r+\delta(s)h,\qquad t(s)=\gamma mq(s),\quad\delta(s)=\gamma mp(s)-2\pi M . ag{15} \]

No integer-turn shift is applied to the actual trajectory. Since \( abla U(tr)\cdot h=0\), \( abla^2U\preceq L\) globally, and \(\| abla U\|_2\le6\),

\[ egin{gathered} U_0(t)=U(tr)=9-8\cos t-\cos8t,\qquad U(tr+\delta h)\le U_0(t)+3\delta^2,\ H(x_s(T), heta_s(T)) \le\max_{t\ { m in\ the\ interval}}U_0(t) +3\delta_{\max}^2+6E+2R_x^2 . \end{gathered} ag{16} \]

This correlated estimate avoids replacing the nine cosine arguments by unrelated extrema. The maximum uses the two endpoints and only the analytic stationary points in the admitted \(t\)-range:

\[ U_0'(t)=16\sin(9t/2)\cos(7t/2)=0. ag{17} \]

The possible interior candidates over this path are \(2\pi/9,3\pi/7,4\pi/9\). Candidate inclusion is checked against the interval; in particular the saddle value at \(3\pi/7\) is not charged to an interval that excludes it. This is a finite extrema theorem, not a grid or response search.

The oriented proxy gaps consist of five copies of \(t\), two copies of \(t+\delta\), one \(t-2\delta\), and the closing gap \(-8t\). For a winding-\(k\) chart replace the latter by \(-8t+2\pi k\). Every actual gap differs by at most \(\sqrt2E\). Strict inclusion in \((-\pi,\pi)\) certifies actual winding \(k\) at \(T\); inclusion in \((-\pi/2,\pi/2)\) additionally certifies acute-cell entry.

docs.title: Positive capture corridors and their energy barriers
docs.text:
In the acute winding-\(k\) cell the nine principal gaps have sum \(2\pi k\). At a boundary with one gap \(+\pi/2\), Jensen's inequality on the other eight gives the phase-energy barrier

\[ B_k=1+8\left[1-\cos\frac{2\pi k-\pi/2}{8}\right] =9-8\cos\frac{(4k-1)\pi}{16},\qquad k=1,2 . \tag{18} \]

A gap \(-\pi/2\) gives a larger bound for \(k=1\); it is incompatible with the remaining acute gaps' required sum for \(k=2\). The nonnegative form energy cannot lower this boundary barrier.

If a complete endpoint is in the acute cell and has \(H(T)<B_k\), storage nonincrease prevents leaving that cell. The fixed form mean and the bounded phase-gap chart make the relevant storage sublevel compact. Zero loss requires \(x=0\); invariance then requires \(f(\theta)=0\). In an acute cell all equal sine currents have equal gaps, so the only relative equilibrium is the regular winding-\(k\) target. LaSalle therefore gives convergence to that target, with the common phase origin determined by the retained lift mean and chart. It also gives eventual entry into any positive target-neighborhood radius, without supplying a uniform additional entry time.

The three parameter intervals below were declared before the scalar assessment. Shared outward dyadic128/Machin arithmetic applied to (10)--(18) yields the following conservative rational bounds.

Source interval Certified geometry at \(T=200\) Complete \(H(T)\), upper Relevant threshold, lower Strict energy margin, lower \(0\le s\le1/8\) Acute, winding one \(2.343558461\) \(B_1>2.348243101\) \(0.004684640\) \(3/4\le s\le4/5\) Winding two \(7.337282704\) \(H_2^*>7.437166400\) \(0.099883696\) \(63/64\le s\le1\) Acute, winding two \(7.438205301\) \(B_2>7.439277423\) \(0.001072122\)

Here \(H_2^*=9(1-\cos(4\pi/9))\). The actual acute-gap margins exceed \(0.783403918\) and \(0.087184187\) in the first and third rows. The interior row's actual principal-gap margin exceeds \(0.348983859\), so its winding assertion is separated strictly from an antipodal ambiguity. All margins apply uniformly to the complete correlated error family, including the transported form errors. Equations (18) and (1) prove permanent winding-one and winding-two capture in the first and third corridors, respectively.

docs.title: Winding two at the transit time cannot persist in the interior corridor
docs.text:
The middle row has energy below every critical point in the closure of the winding-two sector. To see this, a cycle critical point has a common sine current on all oriented edges. For positive current, write every non-antipodal gap as \(\delta\) or \(\pi-\delta\), \(0<\delta<\pi/2\). If \(j\) gaps are obtuse, winding two requires

\[ (9-2j)\delta+j\pi=4\pi,\qquad j\in\{0,1,2,3\},\qquad n=9-2j,\quad \delta=\pi/2-\pi/(2n). \tag{19} \]

Its potential is

\[ U_j=9-n\sin\frac{\pi}{2n}\ge 9-9\sin\frac{\pi}{18}=H_2^* . \tag{20} \]

Indeed \(n\sin(c/n)\) increases with \(n>0\) on this range, since \(\sin z-z\cos z>0\) for \(0<z<\pi/2\). Negative current gives negative principal gaps and cannot have winding two. The limiting all-\(\pi/2\) case is incompatible with the C9 winding sum. At an antipodal critical point the common current is zero; all gaps are \(0\) or \(\pm\pi\). A limiting sum \(4\pi\) requires at least four antipodal edges, so \(U\ge8>H_2^*\).

Now fix any source in \(s\in[3/4,4/5]\). Its actual winding at \(T\) is two, while \(H(T)<H_2^*\). On the form-mean-zero leaf the storage sublevel bounds \(x\); circular phases lie in a compact torus. LaSalle implies that every omega-limit point has \(x=0\) and \(f(\theta)=0\). By (20), no such point can lie in the closed winding-two sector. Arbitrarily late visits to that closed sector would have a convergent subsequence there and would create such an omega-limit point. Therefore there is a finite later time after which the trajectory stays outside the entire closed winding-two sector.

This is a phase-passage obstruction for actual complete trajectories, not merely a proxy observation. It concerns the sector itself, not one chosen lift cell: simultaneous cancelling branch-cut crossings need not change winding. A phase passage must occur after \(T\), but the certificate does not determine its time, the last passage, or the eventual class.

docs.title: Information consequence and implementation boundary
docs.text:
The source parameter and the complete source formulas give sufficient local selectors on two nontrivial intervals. In contrast, the claim that the actual finite-transit winding, or its correctly certified proxy winding, always specifies the acquired persistent class is false on the interior interval. Equal initial phase, means and storage still hold throughout this comparison. The fine form information in (7) is retained; it is not an inferred pressure or a controller.

The intervals \((1/8,3/4)\) and \((4/5,63/64)\) remain undecided by these bounds. Their endpoints are certificate boundaries, not located basin boundaries. Nor does the interior result show convergence to winding one. The two positive corridors establish acute-cell capture at the fixed time, not the earlier small-ball radius condition at that time. The complete law permits antipodal passage during formation; no acute constraint is imposed on the whole transit.

The result is conditional on the supplied isolated support, complete sine law, clock and correlated preparation. It derives neither autonomous preparation nor a uniquely selected constitutive law, substrate, size or physical identification. No old acquired-source certificate is transferred through the new map without re-admitting its errors.

The terminal-limit theorem continues these same histories. It proves complete-state convergence and narrows the interior corridor's energy-compatible critical configurations, while retaining saddle exceptions. The additional source-specific capture proof uses the actual mixed state to select winding one for this corridor and exclude those exceptions; the other path intervals retain their own scope.

The private path calculator admits a closed parameter interval, structural time, and separate latent form and phase error budgets. It rebuilds the exact generator and source identities, uses the shared semigroup radius and acute-sector boundary owners, and retains all phase-gap, storage and source-policy margins. Its source-budget and initial-winding flags are separate from the sufficient capture or exit classification. A supplied interval with unresolved bounds is not classified as a failed formation experiment.

The independent controls check the exact Cayley isometry, correlated error transport, canonical cycle offsets, analytic potential extrema, all-face energy bounds and the critical energy comparison. The three fixed corridor assessments evaluate scalar inequalities only. The code supplies neither a trajectory nor a crossing history, and it does not consume an earlier acquisition verdict.

docs.title: Pressure completion: compatibility, balances and operator scope
docs.text: This owner classifies extensions of the maintained weighted conservative contact after the IL/OZ handoff. The result is a conditional incompatibility between specified requirements, with explicit countermodels when a requirement is dropped. It neither selects a pressure-memory law nor requires every organization to realize every operator. The research program owns task status. No trajectory or new operator response is evaluated here.

docs.title: 1. State, units and the question being tested
docs.text:
Use the actual-law state, including member-associated boundary weights, fixed bare support U, held positive capacities N=diag(nu), signed form x and circular phase theta with declared continuous lifts. Put D=diag(d), with positive bare degrees, and

\[ M=N(\pi D)^{-1},\quad q=L_Wx,\quad S_i=\sum_{j\sim i}\sin(\theta_j-\theta_i),\quad \Phi=(\pi D)^{-1}S,\quad \rho_i=d_i/\nu_i. \]

The current contact has connected positive symmetric conductances. Algebraic balances below only need symmetric fixed conductances and reciprocal bare support; connected positive weighted support is used explicitly for kernel and equilibrium conclusions. Zero capacity is outside the inverse-capacity mean argument. These formulas do not substitute the native neighbor-argument pressure or the default mixed pressure for this selected sine law.

An independently specified driver is a law specified before evaluating its response. It need not be an independent dynamical coordinate. The current model independently specifies p=Phi(y) for y=(x,theta,nu,U,W). Conversely, declaring an independent pressure coordinate requires its own evolution and initialization. The parameter foundation and pressure-state closure boundary retain this distinction; a change of coordinates alone adds no new freedom.

To study that freedom conditionally, define the pressure deviation r=p-Phi(y) and consider

\[ \dot x=MS+Nr=Np,\qquad \dot\theta=Mq,\qquad \dot r=f(y,r). \tag{1} \]

The nodal row is retained. The phase row, clock, support and capacity premises are also retained; f is not selected. A complete extended model would still need f, its admissible domain, event maps, initialization and any inputs. Operator context k remains separate. If a future law consumes k, it must declare that dependency rather than assuming pressure memory from a history record. This is a fine-state analysis, not a closed scalar macro-node law.

Use the original normalized structural chart and clock. In general [r]=[p]=[x]/([nu][t]) and [f]=[r]/[t]. Added storage must have the units of H below. A quadratic pressure storage needs its own dimensional coefficient; pressure squared is not automatically physical energy. Every new evolution row must transform under a clock change. No laboratory-unit bridge is supplied.

docs.title: 2. Constitutive graph and pressure-coordinate evolution
docs.text:
Suppose an event starts on p=Phi(y), leaves y unchanged and changes p by a nonzero amount. Its output cannot remain on that same single-valued graph: Phi(y^+)=Phi(y^-)=p^-, whereas p^+!=p^-. An off-graph event could instead land on the graph; the obstruction concerns preserving it from a point on it. Refreshing pressure projects back onto this constraint, as already proved for OZ. This is an algebraic statement about the chosen constitutive law.

The existing derivative uses the bare cosine Hessian K(theta) and gives, under (1),

\[ \dot p=f(y,r)-(\pi D)^{-1}K(\theta)Mq. \tag{2} \]

Thus r_dot=-gamma*r and p_dot=-gamma*(p-Phi(y)) are different laws. The second has r_dot=-gamma*r+(pi*D)^(-1)*K*M*q and generally leaves r=0. Held pressure p_dot=0 has the same constitutive-drift term. Holding pressure is not holding its deviation from an evolving Phi. Extending the derivative of Phi away from its graph without accounting for this term would silently change the model. Unique invariant-flow claims additionally require appropriate well-posedness; the pointwise tangency condition alone is f(y,0)=0.

docs.title: 3. Exact means, power and the retained OZ endpoint
docs.text:
Let R=sum_i rho_i. Reciprocal support gives sum S=0 and sum q=0. On a continuous phase lift, (1) therefore implies

\[ \frac{d}{dt}\frac{\rho^Tx}{R}=\frac{d^Tr}{R},\qquad \frac{d}{dt}\frac{\rho^T\theta}{R}=0. \tag{3} \]

Keeping the original weighted form mean requires r in E=d^perp at every time. An evolution intended to preserve E must have d^T f=0 there, and an event must land in E. Neither property follows from operator admission.

For the existing structural storage

\[ H=\tfrac12x^TL_Wx+\sum_{\{i,j\}\in U}(1-\cos(\theta_j-\theta_i)), \]

the gradients are H_x=q, H_theta=-S. Hence

\[ \dot H=q^T(MS+Nr)-S^TMq=q^TNr. \tag{4} \]

This is the existing off-graph work identity, now combined with the mean constraint. It identifies a power pair within this model; it is not an electrical or physical-energy identification. Preserving the nodal identity does not by itself preserve these means or storage.

docs.title: Detached consequence of the already retained action
docs.text:
The frozen response contains the same y before and after raw OZ. Re-admit its primitives and rebuild Phi, degrees and capacities through the weighted-law reader. With j=p_OZ_raw-p_IL_completed, exact represented arithmetic gives

\[ R=104,\qquad d^Tj=\frac{33762929380696061}{147573952589676412928}>0. \]

Stored pressure has a materialization residual, so j must not be substituted for the ideal deviation without that residual. Independently enclosing r=p_OZ_raw-Phi(y) gives the hypothetical rate

\[ \frac{d^Tr}{R}\ \in\ [2.1998702728\,10^{-6},\ 2.1998702782\,10^{-6}], \tag{5} \]

where displayed endpoints round the retained rational bounds outwards. Consequently consuming this raw pressure in (1) would immediately change the old weighted form mean. A mean-preserving extension cannot admit this output unchanged. Projecting it onto E, adding a compensating input or redefining the conserved quantity would be additional premises, not the recorded OZ action. The actual form gradient is nonzero after the inherited contact word; the preparation's phase-axis name cannot replace inspection of that endpoint.
