Equation (5) is a new read-only consequence of saved state, not an executed held-pressure interval. The actual experiment immediately refreshed pressure and did not follow (1) off the constitutive graph. Its original 8/9 verdict and unresolved ideal-phase accuracy certificate remain unchanged. The retained evidence reader owns source associations and primitive reconstruction; hashes associate bytes, not execution authenticity.

docs.title: 4. An obstruction to smooth passive extensions preserving the old law
docs.text:
Fix y0 with q(y0)!=0. Suppose all of the following are required:

  1. The two form/phase rows in (1), with held support, capacity and clock.
  2. A two-sided relative neighborhood of r=0 in E=d^perp is admitted, and f takes values in E there.
  3. f(y,0)=0 and f is continuous near (y0,0).
  4. Added storage V(y,r) is C2, locally nonnegative, and V(y,0)=0 for every nearby y. Derivatives in r are relative to E.
  5. Autonomous passivity d(H+V)/dt<=0 throughout that neighborhood.

These requirements are incompatible. Passivity and zero added storage on the original graph are additional hypotheses, not universal TNFR axioms.

Proof. Since zero minimizes V in the pressure directions and V(y,0) vanishes identically, V_y(y,0)=V_r(y,0)=V_yr(y,0)=0. At fixed y0 and any v in E, C2 regularity gives

\[ V_y(y_0,\epsilon v)=o(\epsilon),\qquad V_r(y_0,\epsilon v)=O(\epsilon). \]

Continuity and f(y0,0)=0 give f(y0,epsilon*v)=o(1). The y rows are bounded nearby, so V_dot=o(epsilon). Let P be the orthogonal projector onto E and take v=PNq(y0). This v is nonzero: otherwise Nq=c*d, and 0=sum q=c*sum(d_i/nu_i) forces c=0 and then q=0. Therefore (4) gives

\[ \frac{d}{dt}(H+V)(y_0,\epsilon v) =\epsilon\|PNq(y_0)\|^2+o(\epsilon)>0 \]

for sufficiently small positive epsilon, contradicting requirement 5. The C2 argument needs only the displayed little-o remainder, not an assumed quadratic remainder for V_y. No quadratic ansatz or positive-definite storage Hessian is necessary. The pointwise contradiction does not require integrating a trajectory. For actual flow invariance, supplement tangency with suitable local uniqueness assumptions. The same proof applies without the mean constraint by taking E to be the full pressure space. QED.

For a smaller permitted linear space E, the first-order obstruction occurs when P_E Nq!=0. It does not automatically apply to one-sided cones, isolated event outputs, nonsmooth storage, independent reservoirs, domains lacking those directions or a changed phase row. It proves neither a unique extension nor the impossibility of pressure memory in TNFR.

docs.title: 5. Zero instantaneous work and moving constraints
docs.text:
At q=0 the linear power vanishes; full equilibrium at r=0 additionally needs S=0. On connected positive weighted support, q_dot=L_W M S cannot vanish when S is nonzero. Indeed L_W M S=0 would give MS=c*1, and sum S=0 forces c=0. A constant-form state with S!=0 thus leaves q=0 under the original law; its phase rate is zero at the initial instant while form starts moving. The theorem above does not claim a positive first-order power at such an instant.

Instantaneously work-neutral, mean-preserving deviations lie in

\[ E(y)=\ker d^T\cap\ker(Nq)^T. \]

Its dimension is n-2 for q!=0 and n-1 at q=0. The two constraints remain true along a differentiable solution only if

\[ d^Tf=0,\qquad [L_W(MS+Nr)]^TNr+(Nq)^Tf=0. \tag{6} \]

This is an additional evolution obligation. At a base-law equilibrium q=S=0, any nonzero r in d^perp makes the second expression strictly positive on connected positive weighted support: (Nr)^T L_W(Nr)>0. Otherwise Nr would be constant, and d^Tr=0 would force r=0. Equivalently, H has zero first but strictly positive second derivative at that state. Instantaneous neutrality does not certify a persistent work-neutral channel. Disconnected conductance support has a larger kernel and needs separate component constraints.

docs.title: 6. Explicit alternatives and the premise each changes
docs.text:
The following are mathematical controls delimiting the obstruction, not installed laws or newly selected TNFR coefficients. They retain (1) unless an altered row is stated. Let P=I-dd^T/(d^Td) and r lie in E.

Retain the constitutive graph and permit exchange work. Setting f=0 preserves r and both means but leaves H_dot=q^TNr of either sign. Residual relaxation f=-gamma*r, gamma>=0, also preserves r=0. With V=kappa*||r||^2/2, kappa>0, its total storage rate is

\[ \dot H+\dot V=q^TNr-\kappa\gamma\|r\|^2. \]

No fixed finite damping gain controls every sufficiently small two-sided deviation at q!=0. Adding damping alone does not resolve the stated conflict.

Permit reciprocal exchange to leave the original constitutive graph. Set

\[ f=-\kappa^{-1}PNq-\gamma r,\qquad V=\tfrac\kappa2\|r\|^2. \]

Both means are preserved and d(H+V)/dt=-kappa*gamma*||r||^2<=0, but f(y,0)!=0 at q!=0. The original conservative flow is not an invariant subsystem. This transfers the cancellation method of the existing auxiliary reservoir, with a fresh derivation for N and E. Its 36-node positive-loss coefficients, clock, initialization and frozen negative response do not transfer here.

Change the phase law on a restricted domain. When S!=0, put a=P_(rho^perp)*S. Then a!=0 since sum S=0 and sum rho>0. Adding h=(q^TNr)*a/||a||^2 to the phase row preserves its weighted mean and supplies -S^Th=-q^TNr. With residual relaxation and the quadratic V above, total storage is nonincreasing and r=0 is invariant. This has changed the phase law and is undefined at S=0. It supplies no global smooth completion; at S=0 a finite phase correction cannot cancel nonzero q^TNr through H_theta.

Retain an independently initialized reservoir. Adding e>0 with e_dot=-q^TNr, r_dot=0 conserves H+e while e stays in its admitted domain. This leaves the zero-baseline storage premise and introduces initial content, depletion and event-work obligations. Neither global positivity nor a natural reservoir follows. Previous dissipative loss is not such a reservoir without a declared retained coordinate and law.

Consume pressure over a declared interval. The THOL handoff calculation shows how a held-pressure interval can leave a form change after later refresh. Its duration, complete rows and work are part of a different hybrid model. It needs no permanently independent pressure coordinate, but does not change the outcome of the immediate-refresh IL/OZ word. Held pressure generally leaves r=0 and need not preserve the old weighted form mean.

docs.title: 7. Events, identity and symmetry obligations
docs.text:
For an admitted y-preserving event starting at r=0, nonnegative zero-baseline added storage obeys Delta(H+V)=V(y,r^+)>=0. Strict positivity requires an accounted event source, another changing coordinate or reservoir depletion. A semidefinite V can have nonzero zero-cost directions, whose subsequent admission is still separate. Continuous passivity neither pays event work nor selects its occurrence. OZ's context changes must remain available to later grammar and event consumers even when continuous futures coincide.

The existing identity barrier uses the original H and its conservative continuation. It does not transfer merely because an extension preserves the nodal row. If an extension independently establishes nonincreasing H+V, V>=0, initial identity membership Z(0)<1/16 and H(y0)+V(y0,r0)-H_*<1/6400, the unchanged pointwise barrier excludes a first exit while the admitted extended solution exists continuously. Keep its support, reference, phase-lift conventions and applicable domain/mean hypotheses unchanged. Semidefinite V does not ensure pressure boundedness; global continuation needs separate bounds on all added state. Conservation of H+V alone does not bound H by its old initial value when V initially stores work. Formation, attraction and a new collective identity still need their own proof.

Common form shifts and common phase rotations leave q,S and Phi unchanged. A full extension must make f and storage compatible with any claimed symmetry. Joint relabeling transports d,N,W,r, constituent marks and event context; the projector P transforms with them. An added coordinate, reservoir or held interval also requires its own preparation and clock declaration. None of these conditional symmetries identifies physical gauge freedom.

docs.title: 8. Consolidated inference and verification
docs.text:
The current algebraic pressure law and its OZ refresh neutrality are consistent. An independent pressure extension is possible, but it cannot freely retain all of the theorem's rows, mean constraints, invariant constitutive graph, smooth zero-baseline added storage and autonomous passivity at once. The retained raw OZ output additionally fails the old form-mean constraint if consumed unchanged. These are useful model restrictions, not a reason to force OZ persistence or replace the nodal equation.

Other operator mechanisms can be studied under the existing complete law without selecting one of the alternative memory laws above, provided their actual consumed state and continuation requirements are admitted. The execution plan alone selects such work; this classification introduces no queue.

The exact algebra and retained-state controls compare whole-edge derivatives with complete nodal rows on varied rational supports/capacities, test the projected positive-power direction and explicit countermodels, and retain equilibrium/disconnected-support boundaries. Exact quarter-turn phase fixtures keep separate coefficients of 1 and 1/pi, so the clock is not silently rescaled. The read-only OZ control rebuilds Phi from captured primitives and retains its materialization residual. These controls support the derivations and finite consequence; samples do not prove the universal theorem. Testing owns the combined selection.

docs.title: Phase-nearest UM contact and joint identity maintenance
docs.text: This comparison changes one existing UM policy parameter in the actual organization-contact protocol: UM_CANDIDATE_COUNT=3 replaces its unrestricted value 0. The source family, ordered word, remaining parameters, actual generated weights, continuous law and structural clock retain their declared premises. The earlier unrestricted-support results remain valid for their own model.

docs.title: 1. Frozen comparison protocol
docs.text:
Before evaluating the actual word or its reserved static controls, freeze the following comparison. Reuse the complete source and operator settings in the original protocol, including independently perturbed doubled-C5 components A and B, their common prepared form mean and phase origin, z=1/512, the strict full-state source balls, the actual target pair (0,1) and the ordered word emission,coupling,silence. Change only UM_CANDIDATE_COUNT to 3; retain proximity selection and the complete candidate inventory. No receiver action, new operator, controller, input or continuous loss is introduced. The actual event remains supplied.

The prospective support prediction is the old forty edges plus five: the internal A0 pair edge and all four A0-to-B0 edges. Every generated conductance must retain its actual value and endpoint association. Admit all actual operator preconditions and the full weighted continuation, including changed degree normalization and capacity. Do not substitute a pair-constant dynamics for generic boundary conductances.

The prospective common identity uses one twenty-node arithmetic projection P=I-11^T/20, the original common-aligned twists theta_*, and

\[ Z^2=\|Px\|^2+\|P(\theta-\theta_*)\|^2<r^2, \qquad r=1/16. \]

The phases in this expression are declared continuous lifts of the original twists. One common origin is removed; the relative A/B form and phase origins remain observable identity coordinates. The target is maintenance of this identity for the entire unchanged source family under the fixed post-word law, not just existence or linear stability of a symmetric reference. Establish a common stationary reference, exact balances and a strict energy barrier, or record precisely which obligation fails. Do not enlarge the identity radius, shrink the source or retune the word after examining a response.

Reuse the original split and unsplit nominal controls, source representation, seed, timestamps, execution order and independent 100-digit static oracle with ordinary response allowance 2^-46. Add independent exact algebraic controls for support, mean weights, stationarity, coercivity, full-source energy bounds and event-work accounting. Analytical bounds apply to the exact family; represented controls re-admit their own input defects. No continuous trajectory, time sweep, topology search or physical calibration is part of this gate. No frozen response from the unrestricted-support study is regenerated or reinterpreted as a result of this comparison.

docs.title: 2. Actual candidate selection and the five added edges
docs.text:
Write alpha=2*pi/5 and retain b=h=1/1024=z/2, where b is the AL form increment and h the UM phase push. Before UM, each selected A member has its four original A neighbors. The shared candidate reader excludes the target and existing neighbors, applies the snapshot U3 phase gate, then orders admitted missing neighbors by absolute circular phase gap, using the retained node rank only to break ties.

The selected member's partner and the two B0 members have snapshot gaps at most 2*z. Every member of B1 or B4 instead has gap at least alpha-2*z>2*z; the distance-two A and B pairs fail the unchanged pi/2 phase gate. Thus the three nearest candidates are exactly the partner and both B0 members for every source in the unchanged family. Their internal ranking can vary without changing the selected set. The two target proposals create one common internal edge and four cross edges, not duplicate undirected edges. No external candidate list or new neighbor-selector law is supplied.

The selected candidate count changes only these link proposals. The existing-neighbor consensus, four bidirectional neighbor phase writes, capacity blend, selected stored-pressure relief and SHA reset are still the actual primary map. They read the immutable old support, not prospective new edges. B node state and execution history do not reset during this word. All inherited live form/capacity, circular phase, grammar and associated-history preconditions retain their original strict margins.

The final compatibility score uses the actual post-AL forms and merged phases, with homogeneous Si=1/2 as before. A new cross gap is below 2*z+3*h*z<3*z, its form difference is below 2*z+b=5*z/2, and both forms exceed 1/4. The shared score therefore satisfies

\[ W_{ij}>1-\frac{3z}{2\pi}-\frac{5z}{4}>\frac34. \]

The internal edge retains its previous bound omega>1-sqrt(2)*z>3/4. Every selected candidate therefore passes the final phase and score gates. Every generated weight lies in (3/4,1] and remains attached to its actual endpoints. New edges have the actual weight attribute; no length or unit conductance is inserted by the analysis.

The resulting connected support has 45 edges: forty retained unit edges, the internal A0 edge, and the complete four-edge A0--B0 block. Selected A0 members have bare degree seven, B0 members have degree six, and all other nodes have degree four. Their post-word capacities are respectively 1/2,1,1. Consequently the actual mean weights are

\[ \rho_i=\frac{d_i}{\nu_i}= \begin{cases} 14,&i\in A_0,\\ 6,&i\in B_0,\\ 4,&\text{otherwise}, \end{cases} \qquad \sum_{i\in A}\rho_i=60,\quad \sum_{i\in B}\rho_i=44,\quad \sum_i\rho_i=104. \]

The old unrestricted fan's degree normalization and mean weights do not transfer to this graph. For the nominal post-word forms the weighted form mean is m+7*b/26; arbitrary admitted deviations retain their own weighted correlations rather than being replaced by that nominal value.

docs.title: 3. Complete law, reference and joint identity
docs.text:
Keep the conservative weighted-form/bare-phase completion with e=0,w=beta=1, zero forcing, held actual support and conductances, held post-word capacities and the original structural clock:

\[ S_i=\sum_{j\sim i}\sin(\theta_j-\theta_i),\quad q=L_Wx, \quad M=\operatorname{diag}\frac{\nu_i}{\pi d_i},\qquad \dot x=MS,\quad\dot\theta=Mq. \]

The independently specified pressure is p_i=S_i/(pi*d_i), evaluated on the new support. It is distinct from the stored pressure relieved by UM on the old support. The actual storage and conserved means are

\[ H=\frac12x^TL_Wx+\sum_{\{i,j\}\in U}(1-\cos(\theta_j-\theta_i)), \qquad \dot H=q^TMS-S^TMq=0, \] \[ \frac d{dt}(\rho^Tx)=0,\qquad \frac d{dt}(\rho^T\theta)=0. \]

Use the common-aligned reference x_*=m*1 and theta_*(A_(k,s))=theta_*(B_(k,s))=k*alpha, on the original lifts. Every old fine current cancels at that twist. All five new edges have zero reference form and phase differences. The reference is therefore stationary under the complete actual weighted law, with

\[ H_*=40(1-\cos\alpha). \]

Either common origin can be translated to match a particular source's conserved weighted mean, without changing H or the identity. The relative geometry uses one twenty-node arithmetic projection,

\[ P=I-\frac{11^T}{20},\qquad Z^2=\|Px\|^2+\|P(\theta-\theta_*)\|^2. \]

If eta=theta-theta_*, this identity separates exactly as

\[ Z^2=Z_A^2+Z_B^2+ 5\left[(\overline x_A-\overline x_B)^2+ (\overline\eta_A-\overline\eta_B)^2\right]. \]

Here Z_A,Z_B are the earlier ten-node centered constituent norms. Thus the joint identity retains relative form and phase origins rather than quotienting them away independently. A bound on Z protects both constituent geometries and their relative registration. The arithmetic means used in this observation are not asserted to be conserved.

The whole reference has zero first circular phase resultant: sum_i exp(i*theta_*,i)=4*sum_(k=0)^4 exp(i*k*alpha)=0. There is no defined global resultant angle there. The arithmetic lift projection is the declared geometric observation; it is not a new primitive collective phase or a circular-mean reconstruction.

Generic actual cross conductances still require the member-to-boundary association identified by the earlier contact result. The proof below works on the complete fine state. Equal reference phases or equal bare neighbor counts do not turn the actual weighted evolution into a closed pair-symmetric model.

docs.title: 4. A full relative spectral bound for comparison matrices
docs.text:
Let L_0 be the unit Laplacian of the two disjoint original doubled C5 graphs, and N the unit Laplacian of the five added edges. The actual bare Laplacian is L_U=L_0+N. Since all actual edge weights exceed 3/4,

\[ L_W\succeq\frac34 L_U. \]

This is a quadratic-form comparison, not a replacement of W in the law. To lower-bound lambda_2(L_U), first omit the internal A0 edge from a unit comparison graph. The remaining graph is the two-member doubling of a ten-vertex base graph consisting of two C5 cycles joined by the single A0--B0 base edge.

Only this unit comparison matrix is decomposed by its symmetries. Fine pair-antisymmetric directions have eigenvalues four or six. On pair-common directions its Laplacian acts as twice the base Laplacian. Exchanging the two identical base cycles splits that base matrix into the symmetric block L_C5 and the antisymmetric block L_C5+2*e_0*e_0^T. The first block has one common zero mode and its next eigenvalue is (5-sqrt(5))/2>1/5.

For the second block, five times its shift by I/5, in cyclic node order, is the exact matrix

\[ 5\left(L_{C5}+2e_0e_0^T-\frac15I\right)= \begin{pmatrix} 19&-5&0&0&-5\\ -5&9&-5&0&0\\ 0&-5&9&-5&0\\ 0&0&-5&9&-5\\ -5&0&0&-5&9 \end{pmatrix}. \]

Its leading principal minors are 19,146,839,3901,909, all positive. Sylvester's criterion gives lambda_min(L_C5+2*e_0*e_0^T)>1/5. Restoring the omitted internal edge adds a nonnegative quadratic form. Consequently

\[ \boxed{\lambda_2(L_U)>\frac25.} \]

The argument controls every relative fine direction, including independent member splits and the relative A/B origin. It imposes no symmetry on the actual W, source perturbations or future trajectory.

For the source upper bound below, two further simple facts suffice: lambda_max(L_0)<=8 from its degree-four support, and lambda_max(N)=4. The latter follows by restricting to the four A0/B0 members: N is the Laplacian of K4 with the B0 internal edge removed, with eigenvalues 0,2,4,4; the other sixteen directions are zero.

docs.title: 5. Lower storage barrier on the unchanged joint radius
docs.text:
Take the frozen r=1/16. On Z<=r, any edge phase error from the reference is at most sqrt(2)*r. Every old principal reference gap has magnitude alpha and every added reference gap is zero. The old gaps remain acute, and their cosines obey

\[ \cos(\alpha+\sqrt2r) \ge\cos\alpha-\sqrt2r >\frac3{10}-\frac3{32} =\frac{33}{160}>\frac15. \]

Here cos(alpha)=(sqrt(5)-1)/4>3/10, sqrt(2)<3/2, and alpha+sqrt(2)*r<pi/2. The added-edge cosines exceed the same lower bound. Thus the phase Hessian throughout this whole radius obeys L_(cos delta) >= L_U/5. The actual form block also dominates L_U/5 because L_W >= 3*L_U/4.

Translate the common origins away and Taylor-expand about the stationary reference along the straight centered-state segment, which remains in the radius. The full Hessian comparison and Section 4 give

\[ \boxed{H-H_*\ge\frac{Z^2}{25}\qquad (Z\le r).} \]

At the radius boundary this requires

\[ H-H_*\ge\frac{r^2}{25}=\frac1{6400}. \]

The bound uses both complete rows and all fine directions. The same reference is a strict relative-storage minimum, but its existence alone would not establish retention of the actual post-word source.

docs.title: 6. Upper storage bound for the entire actual post-word family
docs.text:
Let v_0=(xi,eta) be the initial twenty-node deviation from the common reference, before the supplied word. The independent constituent source balls give

\[ \|v_0\|^2<2z^2. \]

Let a=b*1_(A0) be the actual AL form increment and let d be the actual UM phase increment, with all other phase entries zero. The previously admitted consensus bounds give two selected increments below 3*h*z in absolute value and four old-neighbor increments below 4*h/3. Consequently

\[ \|d\|^2<\left(\frac{64}{9}+18z^2\right)h^2<9h^2. \]

B phases are unchanged; SHA changes capacity only. The full post-word deviation is exactly v_1=v_0+(a,d), with its retained phase lifts. Centering is a contraction, so Z_1<sqrt(2)*z+sqrt(11)*h<7*h<r. This admits the initial state to the frozen radius before using an energy certificate.

A sharper storage estimate keeps the different form and phase curvatures. The full post-word phase-error norm is below sqrt(2)*z+3*h<6*h. Therefore every old-edge error is below 6*sqrt(2)*h<1/64. Along the straight segment from the reference to this actual endpoint, the old-edge cosines are at most

\[ \cos\alpha+\frac1{64} <\frac5{16}+\frac1{64}=\frac{21}{64}<\frac13. \]

Every new-edge cosine is at most one. Actual conductances are at most one. Define the positive-semidefinite comparison form

\[ \mathcal B=\operatorname{diag} \left(L_0+N,\frac13L_0+N\right),\qquad \mathcal Q(v)=\frac12v^T\mathcal Bv. \]

Taylor's formula at the stationary reference then yields H_post-H_*<=Qcal(v_1). The use of 1/3 is local to this small source segment; it is not asserted as an upper cosine bound throughout the larger radius-r identity.

Since lambda_max(B)<=12, the original source contribution is

\[ \mathcal Q(v_0)<12z^2=48h^2. \]

The AL increment has eight old boundary edges and four new cross edges; the internal edge has zero increment difference. Its exact comparison form cost is therefore

\[ \frac12a^T(L_0+N)a=6b^2=6h^2. \]

For the old phase part, the norm bound above gives d^T*L_0*d/6<12*h^2. On the five new edges only the two selected phase increments contribute, each of magnitude below 3*h*z. If those increments are d_+,d_-, then

\[ d^TNd=(d_+-d_-)^2+2d_+^2+2d_-^2 \le4(d_+^2+d_-^2)<72h^2z^2. \]

Hence the complete reset comparison cost satisfies

\[ \mathcal Q(a,d)<(18+36z^2)h^2<19h^2. \]

The square root of a nonnegative quadratic form is a seminorm, so its triangle inequality retains the worst allowed correlation between the initial source and the reset:

\[ \boxed{ H_{\rm post}-H_*\le\mathcal Q(v_1) <(\sqrt{48}+\sqrt{19})^2h^2 <128h^2=\frac1{8192}<\frac1{6400}. } \]

For the last strict algebraic inequality, (sqrt(48)+sqrt(19))^2=67+2*sqrt(912)<128, since 4*912<61^2. No source correlation, selected-member asymmetry or actual boundary conductance has been averaged away. The bound covers the entire original source family with the frozen radius and word constants.

docs.title: 7. Joint identity is maintained for all structural time
docs.text:
The actual completed source has Z_1<r and storage excess below 1/8192, while any first radius exit would require storage excess at least 1/6400. The complete fixed-support flow conserves H, so such a first exit is impossible. Therefore

\[ \boxed{Z(t)<\frac1{16}\quad\text{for every }t\ge0} \]

for every exact source in the frozen family, with time measured after the completed word in the original structural clock. All old and new fine edges remain acute, both original constituent winding neighborhoods and nonantipodal member charts persist, and the relative form and phase origins remain inside the joint bound. A common translation was removed; relative A/B motion was retained rather than assumed absent.

The conserved actual weighted means control the remaining common lifted coordinates. Together with the bounded relative state they prevent finite escape. Equivalently, the complete finite-dimensional field has bounded form rates and phase rates linear in the form range, giving global smooth continuation. The barrier is thus an all-time result, not a bound that silently stops at an unproved existence horizon.

This is conservative geometric maintenance. It does not imply convergence to the stationary reference, a period, asymptotic attraction, synchronization at a specified time, or acquisition of an initially absent organization. The two constituent organizations and their near-common registration were prepared, and their connection was supplied by the declared word.

docs.title: 8. Restoring relative-origin storage and complete event work
docs.text:
The connection contributes a joint geometric property absent from the disconnected phase potential. Consider a configuration variation that keeps each component's internal reference shape fixed but changes their relative form and phase origins by Delta x,Delta theta. Its new cross storage is exactly

\[ \Delta H_{\rm cross} =\frac12\left(\sum_{e\in A_0--B_0}W_e\right)(\Delta x)^2 +4(1-\cos\Delta\theta). \]

The actual weight sum exceeds three, and the phase curvature at zero relative origin is four. Each old edge and the internal A0 edge retains its reference difference along this variation. Thus the joined storage penalizes relative registration changes that were flat directions for the disconnected storage. This is an exact potential restriction and local restoring curvature; actual weighted flow need not preserve rigid component shapes or close on these two origin coordinates. Common recentering can preserve both actual weighted means along this configuration variation without changing its storage formula.

The hybrid work uses the actual endpoints and generated weights. Write X_(A,k) for an A pair's mean form, u_(A,0) for half its selected form split and delta_(A,0)' for half the post-UM selected phase split on the retained member chart. The AL and old-edge UM terms are unchanged from the whole-word accounting:

\[ \Delta H_{\rm AL} =4b\sum_{j\in\{1,4\}}(X_{A,0}-X_{A,j})+4b^2, \] \[ \Delta H_{\rm UM,old} =\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E_A\cup E_B} [\cos(\theta_j-\theta_i)-\cos(\theta_j'-\theta_i')]. \]

The actual attachment term now contains the internal edge and four cross edges only:

\[ \Delta H_{\rm attach} =2\omega u_{A,0}^2+2\sin^2\delta_{A,0}' +\sum_{\{i,j\}\in A_0--B_0} \left[\frac{W_{ij}}2(x_i'-x_j')^2+ 1-\cos(\theta_j'-\theta_i')\right]. \]

Thus H_after-H_before=DeltaH_AL+DeltaH_UM,old+DeltaH_attach exactly. SHA and capacity synchronization change subsequent rates and conserved mean weights, but add no direct storage term. Continuous conservation does not make the event passive, pay its attachment work or select its occurrence. The conductances remain held at their actual event values; continuously recomputing compatibility weights would define another law.

docs.title: 9. What this policy comparison establishes
docs.text:
The existing phase-proximity selector, with the single declared count change, yields a distinct admitted contact whose entire unchanged source family has a strict joint storage barrier. The unrestricted thirteen-edge attachment still has its earlier stationary and invariant-level obstructions. Those results are not corrected or overwritten: they apply to a different support produced by the other supplied candidate policy.

The comparison isolates the importance of which boundary relations are created. A phase-compatible connection need not preserve a chosen identity, and more admitted links do not automatically strengthen its maintenance. Here the four-edge registered interface preserves a stationary joint geometry and a full-source barrier; the wider fan changes the stationary current constraints. Neither policy is selected as a universal natural rule by this comparison.

The result supplies conditional joint maintenance and relative-origin restoring storage using actual UM semantics and the explicitly admitted continuous completion. It leaves autonomous preparation and contact, acquisition of a new identity, sufficient reduced interaction coordinates, and independently calibrated physical observations as separate claims. Treating the maintained organization as a collective NFR retains its fine state, declared lifts, boundary associations and applicable execution context; it does not reduce it to one scalar node or establish closure under every registered operator.

The independent static controls reuse the existing complete-word executor and leave the earlier source, oracle and unrestricted-policy controls intact. The separate count-three fixture checks actual candidate membership, reset/context writes, every weight, full-field balances and event work. Exact full-matrix comparisons check the spectral and energy inequalities; the two represented preparations retain their own source defects and captured storage. These finite controls check implementation and proof ingredients, while the all-source and all-time claim follows from Sections 2-7. They do not evolve a trajectory or turn a detached field report into a maintenance certificate.

docs.title: 10. Frozen independent-registration protocol
docs.text:
This separately declared extension keeps Sections 1-9 and their evaluated controls unchanged. Before evaluating its new actual-word controls, freeze the open registration square

\[ |a|<h,\qquad |g|<h,\qquad h=1/1024. \]

Here a is B's relative form origin in the declared model form units and g is its relative primitive-phase origin in radians on the declared lifts. A retains x_A=m+xi_A, theta_A=theta_*+eta_A; B now has x_B=m+a+xi_B, theta_B=theta_*+g+eta_B. Retain the complete original independent centered internal balls ||(xi_C,eta_C)||<z=1/512 and the entire original A mean interval 9/32<m<11/32. Re-admit B on its translated mean interval, contained in (9/32-h,11/32+h); do not silently restrict m or demand that B remain in the original narrower absolute mean interval. The two offsets are independently supplied preparation coordinates, not new evolution laws or time-dependent inputs.

Keep the exact count-three proximity word, all other parameters, target order, histories, timestamps, seeds, full candidate inventory and execution path from Section 1. Keep actual generated conductances, held post-word capacities, zero loss/forcing, original structural clock and the same twenty-node identity Z<r=1/16 about the common-aligned reference. Do not move the relative target to the offset source, remove its relative origins, shrink the internal balls or enlarge r to obtain maintenance.

Predict the same five added edges, 45-edge support and mean weights rho_A=60,rho_B=44,rho_total=104 throughout this square. A's old-neighbor reset maps remain unchanged; B retains its shifted state during the word. Recompute every cross conductance and attachment term from the actual shifted endpoint. Admit the full weighted continuation and prove the uniform source bound

\[ H_{\rm post}-H_*<\left(\frac{127}{10}\right)^2h^2 <\frac1{6400}, \]

or record which obligation fails without retuning the square. Reuse the existing bare comparison metric, its exact old-spectrum upper bound 5+sqrt(5)<15/2, and the complete reset displacement bounds. The intended discriminator is a quantitative open domain for both relative origins, beyond aligned-source maintenance or continuity alone. It is a sufficient domain, not a maximal capture region or a failure claim outside the square.

The reserved static controls use the original nominal split source and the eight fixed offsets (a,g)=(+s,+s),(+s,-s),(-s,+s),(-s,-s),(+s,0),(-s,0),(0,+s),(0,-s), where s=3/4096=3*h/4. Shift only B's primitive form and phase by these exact dyadic values before execution. Preserve the original dyadic twist, seed, timestamps, complete word and 100-digit independent oracle with ordinary response allowance 2^-46. Retain represented input defects separately from the exact family. The previously frozen zero-offset split and unsplit controls remain available without changing their producers.

For each fixed offset check actual selection, weights, primary/context writes, both full-field rows, new weighted means, complete hybrid work and the captured joint storage margin. Exact algebraic controls check the source-family inequalities and retained relative-origin coordinates. Axis controls distinguish the form and phase contributions to the declared rigid-registration storage restriction; that restriction is not a closed trajectory model. Use shared word execution, module fixtures and report readers. No trajectory, parameter sweep, event selector, extra input or physical identification belongs to this protocol.

docs.title: 11. Admission throughout the independent registration square
docs.text:
Keep the frozen notation a,g for B's relative form and phase origins. Write f=b*1_(A0) for the AL displacement, to distinguish that vector from the scalar a. The component-centered source deviations remain v_0=(xi,eta) with ||v_0||^2<2*z^2, and b=h=z/2 as before.

The expanded B mean slab is part of this extension's admission. Every B source form satisfies

\[ \frac9{32}-h-z<x_{B,i}<\frac{11}{32}+h+z, \qquad \frac{285}{1024}<x_{B,i}<\frac{355}{1024}. \]

In particular B stays strictly between 1/4 and 1/2. A retains its original mean slab, source ball and live event margins. Both source balls remain complete independent balls; no correlation with a or g is imposed. On the disconnected old graph, a uniform translation of one component's form or primitive phase leaves its own complete continuous rows and internal storage unchanged. Its previously established internal identity therefore admits the translated mean leaf. The later operator score still reads the translated B forms, so that readmission cannot be replaced by an assertion that B's old absolute mean interval was preserved.

Before UM, the selected member's partner has phase gap below 2*z, and the B0 members have gaps below |g|+2*z<5*z/2. Every B1 or B4 member instead has gap above alpha-|g|-2*z>alpha-5*z/2>5*z/2. The distance-two A pairs retain their old exclusion, and the distance-two B pairs have gaps above 2*alpha-5*z/2>pi/2. The exactly three nearest admitted missing neighbors are consequently the partner and both B0 members. Their internal ordering need not be fixed. There is a strict gap between this selected set and every other candidate throughout the entire square.

The primary phase, capacity and stored-pressure proposals read A's old support and old neighbors. B's relative offsets enter none of those reads. Thus the same A source produces exactly the same reset displacement (f,d) as its zero-offset counterpart. In particular the two selected phase increments satisfy |d_i|<3*h*z, the four old-neighbor increments satisfy |d_i|<4*h/3, and B receives no state reset. Its unchanged histories remain associated with the same B nodes; only the selected A targets execute the declared lifecycle and word-context writes.

At the final link-score stage, every selected cross edge has phase gap below

\[ |g|+2z+3hz<\left(\frac52+3h\right)z<3z, \]

and form difference below b+|a|+2*z<3*z. Both forms exceed 1/4. Using the actual compatibility formula and its positive regularizer,

\[ W_{ij}>1-\frac{3z}{2\pi}-\frac{3z}{2}>1-2z>\frac34. \]

The internal A0 weight keeps omega>1-sqrt(2)*z>3/4. Thus every selected link passes its final phase and score gates, the same five edges are added, and all actual conductances lie in (3/4,1]. Cross weights are recomputed from the shifted endpoints; they are generally neither equal to one another nor equal to the zero-offset weights. The resulting 45-edge support, capacities, degrees and rho values are exactly those of Section 2. The full continuation of Section 3 is therefore admitted with each preparation's own actual held W.

docs.title: 12. Retained origins, initial radius and conserved means
docs.text:
Let 1_B denote the indicator of B's ten fine nodes, and define the registration displacement

\[ o=(a1_B,g1_B). \]

For the same A/B internal deviations, the exact final deviation from the common-aligned reference is

\[ v_{a,g}=v_0+(f,d)+o. \]

No relative origin is absorbed into the target reference. Let dbar_A=(1/10)*sum_(i in A) d_i. Since xi and eta are centered separately in each source component, their post-word arithmetic relative origins are exactly

\[ \overline x_A-\overline x_B=\frac b5-a, \qquad \overline\eta_A-\overline\eta_B=\overline d_A-g. \]

Section 3's joint decomposition gives, writing P_10 for independent ten-node centering only in this displayed identity,

\[ \begin{aligned} Z_{a,g}^2={}&\|P_{10}(\xi_A+f_A)\|^2 +\|P_{10}(\eta_A+d_A)\|^2 +\|\xi_B\|^2+\|\eta_B\|^2\\ &+5\left[\left(\frac b5-a\right)^2+ (\overline d_A-g)^2\right]. \end{aligned} \]

Equivalently, relative to the otherwise identical zero-offset completed preparation,

\[ Z_{a,g}^2=Z_{0,0}^2+5(a^2+g^2) -10\left(\frac b5a+\overline d_Ag\right). \]

The cross terms retain the reset/registration correlations. They cannot be discarded by adding independent marginal radius budgets. For a simple uniform initial admission, however, the joint projection is a contraction and ||P o||^2=5*(a^2+g^2)<10*h^2, so

\[ Z_{a,g}<7h+\sqrt{10}h<11h<\frac1{16}. \]

Here P acts on both form and phase blocks, as in Section 3. This admits the actual source to the unchanged identity radius before invoking any energy argument.

With rho_A=60,rho_B=44,rho_total=104, the actual conserved means of the completed preparation are

\[ \mu_x=m+\frac{\rho^T\xi+28b+44a}{104}, \] \[ \mu_\theta= \frac{\rho^T\theta_*+\rho^T\eta+\rho^Td+44g}{104}. \]

Thus relative to its zero-offset counterpart, the two means change by 11*a/26 and 11*g/26, respectively. The nominal form contribution is m+7*b/26+11*a/26; the fine perturbation correlations remain in the actual formula. The common origins of the stationary reference can be translated to match these two means without changing H, Z or the relative target. Arithmetic component means are observations, not separate conserved quantities after attachment.

These phase means use the declared continuous lifts. Even a perfect relative rotation of the two doubled twists leaves each component's first circular resultant zero. The means therefore do not supply a global resultant angle or a new scalar primitive collective phase.

docs.title: 13. Uniform storage margin for both independent offsets
docs.text:
The aligned reference remains stationary for every actual generated W: all new reference differences vanish and all old reference currents cancel. The reference storage is still H_*=40*(1-cos(alpha)). Since the actual weights exceed 3/4, the full comparison gap and lower radius barrier of Sections 4-5 apply without changing any coefficient.

For the upper bound, reuse the positive-semidefinite comparison metric

\[ \mathcal B=\operatorname{diag} \left(L_0+N,\frac13L_0+N\right),\qquad \mathcal Q(v)=\frac12v^T\mathcal Bv. \]

The old-edge cosine bound from Section 6 still holds along the straight reference-to-source segment. The reason is edgewise cancellation: g adds the same phase to both endpoints of every old B edge and adds nothing to any old A edge. Thus every old-edge error along that segment is exactly the corresponding zero-offset error. It remains below 1/64, and the old-edge cosine upper bound remains 1/3. The former bound on the full uncentered phase-error norm need not transfer to the shifted source and is not used here. Every new-edge cosine remains at most one, and all actual form conductances are at most one. Taylor's formula therefore yields

\[ H_{\rm post}-H_*\le\mathcal Q(v_0+(f,d)+o). \]

A slightly sharper upper comparison than Section 6 makes room for both independent offsets. On either original doubled C5, fine pair-antisymmetric directions have eigenvalue four, while pair-common directions have twice the C5 spectrum. Consequently

\[ \lambda_{\max}(L_0)=5+\sqrt5<\frac{15}{2}, \qquad \lambda_{\max}(N)=4. \]

Only these unit comparison matrices use their symmetry; the actual source and W remain generic. It follows that lambda_max(B)<23/2, and hence

\[ \mathcal Q(v_0)<\frac{23}{2}z^2=46h^2. \]

The exact AL comparison cost is still 6*h^2. Keeping the sharper reset norm already established in Section 6 gives

\[ \frac16d^TL_0d<\frac54\|d\|^2 <\frac54\left(\frac{64}{9}+18z^2\right)h^2. \]

The new-edge reset contribution is still d^T*N*d/2<36*h^2*z^2. Thus the entire reset obeys

\[ \mathcal Q(f,d) <\left[\frac{134}{9}+\frac{117}{2}z^2\right]h^2<15h^2. \]

The last strict inequality uses the frozen z=1/512; it follows, for example, from 117/(2*512^2)<1/9. The registration displacement has no old-edge differences and no internal A0 difference. Its only four nonzero edge differences are on A0--B0, so its comparison cost is exactly

\[ \mathcal Q(o)=2(a^2+g^2)<4h^2. \]

This equality is in the unit upper comparison metric. The actual form storage uses the four actual W values and must not be substituted into the equality as if they were all one. Applying the seminorm triangle inequality once to all three contributions gives

\[ \begin{aligned} \sqrt{\mathcal Q(v_0+(f,d)+o)} &\le\sqrt{\mathcal Q(v_0)}+ \sqrt{\mathcal Q(f,d)}+\sqrt{\mathcal Q(o)}\\ &<(\sqrt{46}+\sqrt{15}+2)h <\left(\frac{34}{5}+\frac{39}{10}+2\right)h =\frac{127}{10}h. \end{aligned} \]

The elementary bounds use 46<(34/5)^2 and 15<(39/10)^2. Squaring establishes the frozen prospective inequality on the complete source family:

\[ \boxed{ H_{\rm post}-H_*<\frac{16129}{100}h^2 <\frac{16384}{100}h^2=\frac1{6400}. } \]

In particular the storage gap to the unchanged radius boundary is strictly greater than 51*h^2/20. This is a uniform analytic margin, including the worst allowed source/reset/offset correlations, not a margin fitted to the eight reserved preparations.

docs.title: 14. Maintenance on an open registration domain
docs.text:
For every exact source in the frozen independent square, Section 12 places the actual completed state inside Z<r, and Section 13 places its conserved storage strictly below the radius-boundary requirement. The same first-exit argument as Section 7 therefore gives

\[ \boxed{ |a|<\frac1{1024},\ |g|<\frac1{1024} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad Z(t)<\frac1{16}\quad\text{for all }t\ge0. } \]

Time starts after the completed supplied word and uses the original structural clock. The held actual W, held capacities, both conserved weighted means and absence of forcing/loss are essential premises. The smooth full fine field has global continuation as in Section 7. Old and new edges remain acute, the two original winding neighborhoods persist, and both relative origins remain part of the retained joint identity. The prepared offsets are initial data; their subsequent relative coordinates are not held fixed by an additional law.

This supplies a quantitative open preparation domain around exact registration, with both independent internal balls unchanged. The square is sufficient and need not be maximal. Its boundary is not an inferred failure threshold, and the result does not establish a capture basin, autonomous contact, convergence to alignment, or asymptotic attraction. It establishes conservative maintenance of the prepared joint identity.

The proof needs total storage and its boundary barrier, not a uniformly positive form-storage reserve. In particular the post-word arithmetic form-mean difference is b/5-a, which can vanish inside this square. A positive-reserve argument for the earlier equal-origin family cannot be transferred merely by reusing that family's labels.

There is an admitted exact zero-form-storage example. Set a=b/5,g=0, all initial phase deviations to zero, B's internal form deviations to zero, and A's form deviations to -4*b/5 on its two targets and b/5 on its other eight nodes. The A deviations sum to zero and their squared norm is 8*b^2/5<z^2. After AL every form is m+b/5; UM and SHA preserve those forms. Therefore every weighted form difference and the entire post-word form storage vanish, independently of the generated positive weights. The phase storage and subsequent form evolution need not vanish. This example invalidates a uniform positive form-reserve claim without affecting the total-storage maintenance proof.

docs.title: 15. Actual event work and the registration storage restriction
docs.text:
Before attachment, uniform B origin translations leave every old-edge form and phase difference unchanged. A's AL term and old-edge UM work are therefore identical to those for the same zero-offset internal preparation. B's internal stored energy is also unchanged. The complete hybrid work identity from Section 8 still applies, but its four cross terms use the new endpoint differences and freshly generated weights:

\[ \Delta H_{\rm attach}(a,g) =2\omega u_{A,0}^2+2\sin^2\delta_{A,0}' +\sum_{\{i,j\}\in A_0--B_0} \left[\frac{W_{ij}(a,g)}2(x_i'-x_j')^2 +1-\cos(\theta_j'-\theta_i')\right]. \]

Together with the unchanged AL and old-edge UM terms, this equals H_after-H_before exactly for that preparation. The notation W(a,g) records how the event output depends on its initial offsets; W is held after the word. Recomputing it during continuous evolution would change the model. Neither continuous conservation nor the positive storage margin selects or pays for the supplied event.

For any one such held actual W, the rigid-component reference variation of Section 8 still has exact cross-storage restriction

\[ \Delta H_{\rm cross}(\Delta x,\Delta\theta) =\frac12\left(\sum_{e\in A_0--B_0}W_e\right)(\Delta x)^2 +4(1-\cos\Delta\theta). \]

This formula separates the two geometric storage contributions and can be evaluated on the declared form and phase axes. It does not equal the entire reset source excess in general: the prepared source also contains internal perturbations and the actual word displacement. Nor is it a closed trajectory law for two rigid objects. Generic actual conductances continue to couple the full constituent and boundary state.

docs.title: 16. Meaning and evidence boundary of the extension
docs.text:
Exact common preparation origins were sufficient in Sections 1-9, but are not necessary for their joint-maintenance mechanism. The unchanged count-three word admits a nonempty open square of independently different form and primitive-phase origins, while retaining every original internal perturbation, the original A mean interval and the same joint radius. B's translated absolute mean slab is explicitly re-admitted. The result uses actual selected edges, actual compatibility weights, all fine rows and the appropriate conserved means throughout.

The reserved controls in Section 10 separately check the implementation on fixed represented preparations. Their input defects and event outputs remain distinct from the exact family. The proof of the full-family, all-time claim is Sections 11-14; static samples cannot replace it. No reduced evolution, physical identification or closure under all registered operators follows. A collective TNFR description continues to retain the fine state, declared phase lifts, member-to-boundary associations and the applicable event and grammar contexts.

docs.title: 17. Frozen finite exchange comparison
docs.text:
This bounded comparison closes the response question for the admitted UM contact before the operator/pressure-handoff gate in the sole execution plan. It does not widen the registration square or introduce another contact policy. Freeze the following full-family prediction before evaluating the new paired discriminator and its algebraic controls.

Use the complete independent internal preparation of Section 10, with the original A mean interval, z=1/512, held unit initial capacities and all associated execution-state premises. Pair exactly the same internal form, phase, pressure and history data in two preparations. Keep relative form origin a=0; give B opposite phase origins +g,-g, where g=3/4096. This lies strictly inside the proved registration square. Execute the same count-three emission,coupling,silence word on (0,1) in both preparations, with every parameter, seed, target order and timestamp unchanged. Each output has its own generated conductances W_+,W_-; never substitute one for the other. Continue each completed output under its own held weighted law from Section 3, with zero forcing/loss and the original structural clock.

Observe the fixed linear form contrast

\[ D(x)=\frac1{44}\sum_{i\in B}\rho_i x_i -\frac1{60}\sum_{i\in A}\rho_i x_i, \qquad \rho_i=d_i/\nu_i\text{ on the joined support}. \]

The weights are 14 on A0, 6 on B0 and 4 elsewhere in both preparations. Define the paired response C(t)=D(x_+(t))-D(x_-(t)); its initial value is zero because the completed forms agree. Retain continuous phase lifts initialized by theta_+(0)-theta_-(0)=2*g*1_B. The frozen horizon is T=1/8 after the word, with a readout window [1/16,1/8]. Predict, for every matched source in the full internal family,

\[ C(t)<-\frac{gt}{12}\quad(0<t\le1/8),\qquad C(1/8)<-2^{-17},\qquad C(t)<-2^{-18}\quad(1/16\le t\le1/8). \]

Establish the finite-window sign using both full evolution rows, their actual distinct conductances and the proved identity bounds. A nonzero initial derivative or a rigid-component oscillator approximation is insufficient. Keep the source correlations in the paired comparison; a uniform sign for either preparation's unpaired flux is not required or inferred.

For the null control, take the same completed primitive states, remove only the four A0--B0 cross edges and retain the common internal A0 edge and actual capacities. This is a detached alternative model, not an executed deletion event or an unpaid support jump. Re-admit each connected component with its own degrees and complete law. Retain exactly the same D readout as above, without asserting that its joined weights are conserved in the disconnected model. Predict C_disconnected(t)=0 for all time from independent component phase-rotation symmetry.

The proof and observations are ideal mathematical ones. Reuse the two previously declared pure-phase nominal split preparations from Section 10, including their represented dyadic twist and input defects, as static implementation controls. They are reused evidence, not new independent response samples. Keep the existing 100-digit oracle and 2^-46 ordinary static response allowance. Check actual paired primary state, both cut-current balances, weight differences, detached component admission and the exact finite-error inequalities. Share existing word/report fixtures rather than executing additional source variants. Evaluate no trajectory, time sweep, new input, laboratory readout or physical identification. Preserve all earlier protocols and results regardless of the comparison's outcome.

docs.title: 18. Exact regional inventory balances on the joined support
docs.text:
Orient all four cross edges from A0 to B0. For one of the actual held weighted laws, define its two boundary currents

\[ J=\sum_{i\in A_0,\ j\in B_0}\sin(\theta_j-\theta_i), \qquad K=\sum_{i\in A_0,\ j\in B_0}W_{ij}(x_j-x_i). \]

Define the regional form observations X_C=sum_C(rho_i*x_i)/rho_C and, on the declared continuous lifts only, Theta_C=sum_C(rho_i*theta_i)/rho_C. On the joined support rho_A=60,rho_B=44 and rho_i*M_i=1/pi. Antisymmetry cancels every internal edge separately in each regional sum. The complete fine equations therefore give exactly

\[ \dot X_A=\frac{J}{60\pi},\qquad \dot X_B=-\frac{J}{44\pi},\qquad \dot\Theta_A=-\frac{K}{60\pi},\qquad \dot\Theta_B=\frac{K}{44\pi}. \]

Consequently, for D=X_B-X_A and Y=Theta_B-Theta_A,

\[ \dot D=-\kappa J,\qquad \dot Y=\kappa K, \qquad \kappa=\frac1\pi\left(\frac1{44}+\frac1{60}\right) =\frac{13}{330\pi}. \]

These identities express exchange of the law's weighted inventories. They do not identify those inventories with a measured physical charge, or the lifted phase mean with a primitive collective phase. They also do not close an evolution law for D and Y: J and K retain all four boundary endpoint associations, the actual W and the evolving internal state. The complete fine evolution remains the model used below.

docs.title: 19. Matched preparations retain their distinct actual weights
docs.text:
Use exactly the matched preparations and fixed g=3/4096 of Section 17. Section 11 gives identical A reset displacements and no B reset in the two words. Thus the completed states satisfy

\[ x_+(0)=x_-(0),\qquad \theta_+(0)-\theta_-(0)=2g1_B. \]

The support, capacities and degree normalization M are common. Every old weight remains one, and the internal A0 weight is identical in the two outputs. Only the four cross weights can differ. On a given cross edge, the completed phase gaps are phi_e+g and phi_e-g, on the admitted small-gap lifts, while the two form differences and their score denominators agree. The compatibility formula therefore implies

\[ |W_{+,e}-W_{-,e}| =\frac{\bigl||\phi_e+g|-|\phi_e-g|\bigr|}{2\pi} \le\frac g\pi. \]

Both weights lie in (3/4,1] and each retains its actual value. Equality of the forms and the initial phase displacement does not justify using a common weight matrix. Write Delta W=W_+-W_-; the two independent continuations hold their respective event outputs fixed.

By Section 14, both complete trajectories stay in Z<r=1/16 for all time. Hence each trajectory has full form range below sqrt(2)*r, and every new-edge phase gap has magnitude below sqrt(2)*r. In particular,

\[ \max_{i,j}|x_{\pm,i}(t)-x_{\pm,j}(t)|<\frac1{10}, \qquad |\theta_{\pm,j}(t)-\theta_{\pm,i}(t)|<\frac1{10} \quad(\{i,j\}\in A_0--B_0). \]

The phase gaps here use the retained lifts, with zero cross-edge reference gap. This bound concerns edge differences and therefore is unaffected by a common phase origin. It applies throughout the finite comparison window, not only to the initialized state.

docs.title: 20. A full-law bound on the finite phase-displacement remainder
docs.text:
Let

\[ \Delta x=x_+-x_-,\qquad \Delta\theta=\theta_+-\theta_-,\qquad A(t)=\|\Delta x(t)\|_\infty,\quad B(t)=\|\Delta\theta(t)\|_\infty. \]

These norms keep all fine directions and common coordinates. In particular A(0)=0,B(0)=2*g; no independent component-origin projection is used. The exact difference equations are

\[ \Delta\dot x=M\bigl(S(\theta_+)-S(\theta_-)\bigr), \] \[ \Delta\dot\theta=M L_{W_+}\Delta x+M L_{\Delta W}x_-. \]

The sine function is globally one-Lipschitz. Since every capacity is at most one and every held edge weight is at most one, rowwise triangle inequalities give

\[ \|\Delta\dot x\|_\infty\le\frac2\pi B, \qquad \|M L_{W_+}\Delta x\|_\infty\le\frac2\pi A. \]

The remaining term accounts for the actual difference between the two laws. Only A0 and B0 rows meet changed edges, with exactly two such edges per row. A B0 row has M_i=1/(6*pi); an A0 row has M_i=1/(14*pi). Section 19's weight and form-range bounds thus give

\[ \|M L_{\Delta W}x_-\|_\infty <\frac1{6\pi}\,2\,\frac g\pi\,\frac1{10} =\frac{g}{30\pi^2}. \]

The A0 bound is smaller, g/(70*pi^2), and all other rows have zero weight-difference forcing. This estimate uses the actual cross incidence and new degree normalization; it does not treat all seven neighbors as changed weights or suppress the weight difference.

The upper right Dini derivatives of the two norms consequently satisfy

\[ D^+A\le\frac2\pi B,\qquad D^+B\le\frac2\pi A+\frac{g}{30\pi^2}. \]

Equivalently these inequalities hold almost everywhere for the locally Lipschitz norms, which is enough to integrate them. For s=A+B, use pi>3 to obtain

\[ s'\le\frac23s+\frac g{270},\qquad s(0)=2g. \]

An integrating factor gives, for 0<=t<=T=1/8,

\[ s(t)\le g\left[\left(2+\frac1{180}\right)e^{2t/3} -\frac1{180}\right] <\frac{4321}{1980}g<\frac94g. \]

Here e^(1/12)<1/(1-1/12)=12/11, by comparison of the positive exponential and geometric series. Thus the estimate requires no numerically sampled exponential bound. Integrating the form inequality now gives A(t)<3*g*t/2 for positive t. Finally integrate the full phase-row norm, rather than the derivative of B, to keep its initial displacement explicitly:

\[ \begin{aligned} \|\Delta\theta(t)-2g1_B\|_\infty &\le\int_0^t\left(\frac2\pi A(u)+\frac{g}{30\pi^2}\right)du\\ &<g\left(\frac{t^2}{2}+\frac t{270}\right) \le\frac{143}{17280}g<\frac g{100} \qquad(0<t\le1/8). \end{aligned} \]

The remainder includes every internal form/phase displacement and the separately generated held weights. No pair-symmetric trajectory, rigid component assumption, small-oscillation closure or numerical time step enters this estimate.

docs.title: 21. Uniform signed exchange throughout the finite window
docs.text:
For any cross edge oriented A to B, define phi_(+,e)=theta_(+,B)-theta_(+,A) and similarly for the minus preparation. The full phase-displacement estimate implies

\[ \phi_{+,e}(t)-\phi_{-,e}(t) >2g-\frac{2g}{100}=\frac{99}{50}g \quad(0<t\le1/8). \]

At zero time the difference is exactly 2*g, so the same lower bound also holds there. Both phase gaps remain between -1/10 and 1/10. Throughout the interval between them, cos(u)>9/10, for example from cos(u)>=1-u^2/2. Integrating the cosine between the two actual gaps gives, for every one of the four cross edges,

\[ \sin\phi_{+,e}-\sin\phi_{-,e} >\frac9{10}\frac{99}{50}g. \]

The full boundary-current contrast therefore satisfies

\[ J_+(t)-J_-(t)>\frac{891}{125}g>7g \qquad(0\le t\le1/8). \]

This is a paired inequality; arbitrary admitted internal phase deviations need not give either unpaired current a prescribed sign. With the fixed readout from Section 17, C(0)=0 and the exact regional balance gives

\[ \dot C=-\kappa(J_+-J_-)<-7\kappa g. \]

Hence the prospective finite-time statement holds uniformly over the complete internal source family:

\[ \boxed{ C(t)<-7\kappa gt<-\frac{gt}{12} \qquad(0<t\le1/8). } \]

For the final rational inequality, pi<22/7 implies 7*kappa>637/7260>1/12. Substituting the frozen g=3/4096 gives

\[ \boxed{ C(1/8)<-2^{-17},\qquad C(t)<-2^{-18}\quad(1/16\le t\le1/8). } \]

These are ideal observation bounds in the declared model form units and original structural clock. They are not laboratory-unit claims. The proof retains all source/reset correlations and controls the finite response; it does not infer that response from an initial derivative alone. Both preparations retain their joint geometric identity for all time by Section 14, although this signed contrast is only proved on the frozen finite window.

docs.title: 22. Exact disconnected null with the same fixed observation
docs.text:
Construct the detached control exactly as declared: retain the two completed primitive states, capacities and internal A0 weight, and remove only the four cross edges. The remaining 41-edge graph has two connected components. Its bare degrees are five on A0 and four on every other node. Its own complete-law mean weights are consequently ten on A0 and four elsewhere, with totals

\[ \rho_A^{\rm dis}=52,\qquad \rho_B^{\rm dis}=40. \]

In particular the disconnected normalization on A0 is 1/(10*pi) and on B0 is 1/(4*pi). Keeping the joined normalization would be a different comparison law. The remaining weights in the plus and minus controls agree exactly: old unit edges and the common internal A0 weight.

With these correctly re-admitted laws, independent uniform phase rotation of either disconnected component is an exact symmetry. The two initial control states have identical forms and differ only by 2*g*1_B in phase. Existence and uniqueness for the smooth complete finite-dimensional field therefore give

\[ x_+^{\rm dis}(t)=x_-^{\rm dis}(t),\qquad \theta_+^{\rm dis}(t)=\theta_-^{\rm dis}(t)+2g1_B \]

for all time. Bounded form rates and phase rates linear in the finite form range ensure global continuation. Applying the same fixed linear readout D from the joined protocol yields the exact null

\[ \boxed{C_{\rm dis}(t)=0\quad(t\ge0).} \]

The joined readout weights 14,6,4 and divisors 60,44 remain the observation here; they are not asserted to be conserved disconnected inventories. An individual disconnected D need not be constant for this argument: the two form trajectories coincide, so their contrast vanishes. This construction compares two explicit models at the same primitive states. It executes no support-deletion event and transfers no event-work or passivity claim between them.

docs.title: 23. What the finite comparison adds
docs.text:
The admitted joined organization supports a robust finite response that the corresponding disconnected preparations cannot produce under the same observation. Opposite small prepared phase origins cause a uniformly signed difference in regional weighted form exchange, while both joined trajectories keep the proved geometric identity. The complete internal source balls remain unchanged, and each trajectory consumes its own actual member-associated conductances.

This is autonomous continuous exchange after a supplied word. It does not select that word's occurrence, prove acquisition from an absent organization, infer a unique fundamental law, or establish a closed scalar collective oscillator. The matched preparation is an explicit experimental design within the mathematical model; it does not infer the sign of either unpaired trial from an incomplete observation.

The frozen static controls reuse the earlier pure-phase preparations and the shared complete-word and weighted-field readers. They check actual state matching, both current balances, weight-difference bounds, the alternative support admission and the exact finite-remainder inequalities. Their represented input defects and arithmetic allowances remain distinct from the exact family. Sections 18-22 supply the analytical finite-window and null claims; no numerical trajectory or new independent response sample is needed or asserted.

docs.title: Reduced ports for actually formed sine classes
Prospective transfer claim and frozen protocol
docs.text:
The formed-class contact result establishes one finite donor-class response against receiver class one. This gate asks whether separately derived component models predict an additional contact against receiver class two, without refitting their parameters. The reduction retains five reflection-even spatial coordinates in each of two channels per component, an exact nonlinear bridge, and explicit bounds for all discarded fine-state effects. It is neither an exact nonlinear symmetry quotient nor a replacement of each component by one scalar form/phase pair.

Freeze the following before evaluating the held-out response:

  • Retain the complete positive-loss sine law, structural clock \(\tau=et\), \(e=1023/1024\), \(w=1/1024\), \(\gamma=1/(1023\pi)\), unit capacities and beta one. Two simple unit C9 cycles have local node order \(0,\ldots,8\). A single supplied unit bridge joins their central nodes \(4\); afterward the two port degrees are three and all other degrees two.
  • The donor cases remain \(k=1,2\); the held-out receiver is class \(\ell=2\) in both cases. For either component of class \(j\), retain source form \(jm(i-4)\), with \(m=(2046/9)(355/113)^2\). Donor nominal phases start at zero; receiver nominal phases start at the supplied common origin \(\varphi=1/1000\). This offset is a preparation premise, not a rotation or reset performed at contact.
  • Each component retains initial form and continuous phase-lift residual bounds \(10^{-10}\), with each residual row summing to zero separately. All allowed even and odd perturbations remain. Retain each component's original common storage ceiling \(10^9\); the nominal preparation costs need not agree. Both full source families, including the receiver-class-two source, must be freshly admitted under the original formation theorem.
  • Retain acquisition time \(100\), radius \(r=1/12\), and the uninterrupted unprobed relaxation duration \(D=10^{13}\). Contact occurs at \(\tau_c=100+D\). Retain the endpoint Euclidean bounds \(\epsilon=10^{-32}\) separately for each component's form and phase error, proved with the guarded exact decay bound \(2^{-512}\) and \(512\le\kappa D\le4096\). No target reset or previous maintenance probe is admitted.
  • Derive one component matrix for each class directly from its C9 geometry and the declared one-contact mobility. Retain the radial order \((4),(3,5),(2,6),(1,7),(0,8)\), in form and in real phase deviations from that class's fixed twist. The class dependence is \(\cos(2\pi j/9)\), derived from the internal sine field. Use these same two component matrices and the same two-channel port convention in every composition; no receiver-specific parameter or response fit is admitted.
  • The predictive system has twenty retained coordinates, ten per component. Its internal phase field is the derived linear tangent, while its bridge sine current remains exact and nonlinear. Retain the initial-state source term in the port representation. For the nominal prediction, use the limiting comparison coordinates and enclose the actual source deviations through the proved error terms; never reset the actual fine state.
  • At elapsed scaled time \(h=1/100\) after contact, read actual receiver-port form with independent additive error at most \(d=10^{-30}\) per case. Predict recorded donor-two minus donor-one contrast greater than \(10^{-25}\). Derive its fourth-order leading term from the composed reduced matrices, retaining their first three derivative cancellations. Do not substitute a coefficient or verdict from the earlier full-state contact certificate.
  • Bound the finite reduced prediction by its correlated semigroup tail and reduced nonlinear remainder. Add the separately proved lifted-surrogate discrepancy, complete actual preparation error and independent readout error. Let \(E_{\mathrm{total}}\) be the sum of these nonnegative error bounds and let \(L_{\mathrm{full}}\) be the lower endpoint of the final outward recorded-contrast enclosure. Require \(L_{\mathrm{full}}>10^{-25}\) and the strict error-fraction condition \(E_{\mathrm{total}}<(1/4)L_{\mathrm{full}}\). The denominator is a certified full-law recorded gap, not its formal leading amplitude.
  • Retain the supplied contact-work allowance \(10^{-6}\), both actual cycle identities and full joined-family recovery. Rebuild the contact storage, quotient radius, weighted means and barrier for donor \(k\) and receiver two. Removing the bridge must leave receiver evolution independent of donor data; retain the preparation/readout control band.
  • Use exact rational primitives and outward dyadic128 trigonometric intervals, keeping the tiny warmup squared bounds as exact rationals. Preserve the protocol and producing source before the first reserved evaluation. There is no trajectory integration, parameter search, new horizon sweep or precision search. If any prerequisite, error fraction, identity, work or contrast condition fails, retain that outcome without changing this protocol.

The earlier receiver-one result is a retained reference, not a calibration dataset for these component matrices. The new question is the controlled transfer of a derived reduced model to one declared receiver change. The structural dwell, initial source control and tiny readout budget have no independent laboratory realization here.

docs.title: The retained component state and one-contact normalization
docs.text:
Use local reflection \(R:i\mapsto8-i\), fixing the central port \(p=4\). For each channel, let \(S\) take the values or averages on the five layers

\[ (4),\quad(3,5),\quad(2,6),\quad(1,7),\quad(0,8). \]

Let \(T\) lift a five-vector by assigning its value to each node in its layer. Then \(ST=I_5\) and \(TS=(I+R)/2\). Both maps are contractions in the maximum norm. The reduced state is \(z_k=(\bar x_k,\bar y_k)\in\mathbb R^{10}\), where \(\bar x_k=Sx_k\) and \(\bar y_k=S(\theta_k-\Theta_k-o_k\mathbf1)\). Here \(\Theta_{k,i}=k\alpha(i-4)\), \(\alpha=2\pi/9\), and the declared common origin \(o_k\) is zero for the donor and \(\varphi\) for the receiver. This projection defines retained coordinates of a fine state. Evolving equation (2) instead defines a surrogate trajectory, which generally differs from the projection of the evolving nonlinear fine state.

The phase deviations are real retained lifts. Wrapping them before applying the internal linear operator changes this model. The internal reference twist and known origins must be restored when forming a circular bridge difference.

The component has one admitted unit contact. Its internal mobility is \(K_*=\operatorname{diag}(1/2,\ldots,1/3\text{ at }p,\ldots,1/2)\), even though \(L_{\mathrm{C9}}\) contains only its internal edges. Its reduced internal operator is

\[ \bar A=SK_*L_{\mathrm{C9}}T= \begin{pmatrix} 2/3&-2/3&0&0&0\\ -1/2&1&-1/2&0&0\\ 0&-1/2&1&-1/2&0\\ 0&0&-1/2&1&-1/2\\ 0&0&0&-1/2&1/2 \end{pmatrix}. \tag{1} \]

The edge joining nodes zero and eight lies inside the outermost layer and contributes zero on reflection-even vectors. The layer weights are \((3,4,4,4,4)\), of total nineteen. This is not the isolated-cycle normalization \(L_{\mathrm{C9}}/2\). A different number or arrangement of contacts would require its own mobility and reduction admission.

Every internal edge of the class-\(k\) twist has cosine \(c_k=\cos(k\alpha)>0\). Linearizing only those internal sine currents gives the following component model:

\[ \begin{aligned} \bar x_k'&=-\bar A\bar x_k-\gamma c_k\bar A\bar y_k +\frac{e_0}{3}(u_x+\gamma u_\theta),\\ \bar y_k'&=\gamma\bar A\bar x_k-\frac{\gamma e_0}{3}u_x. \end{aligned} \tag{2} \]

The two input channels have the definite convention

\[ u_x=x_{\mathrm{other},p}-x_{\mathrm{own},p},\qquad u_\theta=\sin(\theta_{\mathrm{other},p}-\theta_{\mathrm{own},p}). \]

They are not two unspecified forces. In the actual composition they are determined by the other component's retained port outputs.

For \(z_k=(\bar x_k,\bar y_k)\), define

\[ J_k= \begin{pmatrix} -\bar A&-\gamma c_k\bar A\\ \gamma\bar A&0 \end{pmatrix},\qquad B=\frac13 \begin{pmatrix} e_0&\gamma e_0\\ -\gamma e_0&0 \end{pmatrix},\qquad Cz_k=(\bar x_{k,0},\bar y_{k,0}). \]

The exact input/output identity for this component model is

\[ Cz_k(t)=Ce^{J_kt}z_k(0) +\int_0^t Ce^{J_k(t-s)}B\,u_k(s)\,ds. \tag{3} \]

Thus \(G_k(t)=Ce^{J_kt}B\) is its derived two-channel port kernel. It depends on class, supplied law and contact normalization, not on a fitted receiver response. The initial-state term is essential: the kernel does not determine the initial internal shape.

The twenty-coordinate realization retains both component means. Writing \(m_*=(3,4,4,4,4)^{\mathsf T}\), equation (1) gives

\[ (m_*^{\mathsf T}\bar x_k)'=u_x+\gamma u_\theta,\qquad (m_*^{\mathsf T}\bar y_k)'=-\gamma u_x. \]

Opposite inputs on the two components preserve the combined degree-weighted charges, while the separate component means can change. Holding them independently fixed after contact would introduce a different law.

This is a strict reduction from thirty-six fine coordinates to twenty retained coordinates, or an equivalent port history with its initial source. No minimality theorem is asserted. In particular, writing a kernel is not evidence that all hidden initialization can be discarded or that one scalar state per formed class closes the dynamics.

docs.title: Autonomous composition keeps the bridge nonlinear
docs.text:
Compose the two component models using

\[ \begin{aligned} u_{\mathrm D} &=\left(\bar x_{\mathrm R,0}-\bar x_{\mathrm D,0},\ \sin(\varphi+\bar y_{\mathrm R,0}-\bar y_{\mathrm D,0})\right),\\ u_{\mathrm R}&=-u_{\mathrm D}. \end{aligned} \tag{4} \]

The resulting twenty-coordinate system is autonomous after the supplied support event. No observed response is installed as an input, and no port is held to an externally selected future history. Only the choice \(\ell=2\) of the receiver's already defined component matrix changes in the held-out experiment.

Put

\[ \bar D=\operatorname{diag}(\bar A,0),\quad \bar R=\operatorname{diag}(0,\bar A),\quad q=e_0-e_5,\quad \bar C_b=qq^{\mathsf T}/3,\quad \bar A^+=\bar D+\bar R+\bar C_b. \]

In ten-component vectors \(\bar x,\bar y\), (2)--(4) become

\[ \begin{aligned} \bar x'&=-\bar A^+\bar x -\gamma(c_k\bar D+c_\ell\bar R)\bar y +\frac{\gamma q}{3} \sin(\varphi+\bar y_5-\bar y_0),\\ \bar y'&=\gamma\bar A^+\bar x. \end{aligned} \tag{5} \]

The first row is linear in the internal deviations but not in the bridge phase difference. Replacing that sine by a fitted gain or by its initial value would be another approximation requiring an additional error term.

docs.title: Why the discarded nonlinear modes remain controlled
docs.text:
The exact fine sine law does not preserve this even subspace in general. Around a winding-\(k\) twist, an internal edge contributes

\[ \sin(k\alpha+\delta) =\sin(k\alpha)+c_k\delta+O(\delta^2). \]

The terms proportional to \(\sin(k\alpha)\delta^2\) can generate reflection-odd deviations under an even drive. Linear reflection symmetry alone cannot prove an exact nonlinear quotient.

For the error proof, extend (5) to all nine coordinates of each component: use the linearized internal \(c_kK_*L_{\mathrm{C9}}\) and the exact bridge sine, without projecting either channel. This thirty-six-coordinate surrogate is a proof device. Its matrices commute with each component reflection and its bridge depends only on the fixed ports. Its ideal initial deviations are zero, so its ideal flow stays even and is exactly the lift of (5). The actual predictive realization remains twenty-dimensional.

Compare this lifted ideal surrogate to the ideal full sine flow with the same zero form and target twists plus receiver origin \(\varphi\). Let \(y_{\mathrm{fine}}(t)\) be phase displacement from those initial comparison phases and put \(s=|\sin\varphi|\). The complete joined field has initial normalized sine forcing \((\sin\varphi/3)(e_a-e_b)\), irrespective of \(k,\ell\). The contraction/Volterra argument in the contact remainder proof uses only this forcing, the normalized row bounds and \(\eta=\gamma^2\). It therefore applies with receiver class two:

\[ \|y_{\mathrm{fine}}(t)\|_\infty \le\frac{2\gamma^2s}{3}t^2 \quad(0\le t\le h\le1,\ \gamma^2h^2\le3/4). \tag{6} \]

At the actual fine phase state, the omitted internal Taylor terms have normalized magnitude at most \(2\|y_{\mathrm{fine}}\|_\infty^2\). They enter the physical form row multiplied by \(\gamma\) and do not directly enter the phase row. Both the full field and the extended surrogate have maximum-norm Lipschitz constant at most \(2+2\gamma<3\). Thus for \(0<h<1/3\), their full-state discrepancy obeys

\[ E_{\mathrm{sur}}(h) \le\frac{2\gamma}{1-3h} \int_0^h\|y_{\mathrm{fine}}(t)\|_\infty^2\,dt \le\frac{8\gamma^5s^2h^5}{45(1-3h)}. \tag{7} \]

Taking the supremum in the integral difference inequality proves the denominator: \(E_h\le3hE_h+\int_0^h\|\mathrm{defect}\|\,dt\). The same argument applies to every prefix of the window. Generated odd modes and their subsequent feedback are included through the full fine trajectory in (6), not set to zero.

For each actual formation image, arbitrary initial even and odd errors remain within the endpoint bound \(\epsilon\). Comparison of the actual full flow to the ideal full flow gives the separate maximum-norm bound

\[ E_{\mathrm{prep}}^{\mathrm{one}}(h) \le\frac{\epsilon}{1-3h}. \tag{8} \]

This is precisely the complete-field argument in the actual-state contact handoff. Combining (7) and (8) bounds the actual receiver form against the nominal reduced flow without resetting any actual coordinate. Unknown initial shape is handled by a proved family enclosure, not inferred from winding, means or port values alone.

docs.title: A finite prediction computed from the reduced matrices
docs.text:
The analytic evaluator of (5) starts with \(\bar x=\bar y=0\). Put

\[ f=\frac{\sin\varphi}{3}q,\qquad \bar B_{k,\ell}=c_k\bar D+c_\ell\bar R+\cos\varphi\,\bar C_b. \]

Direct differentiation of the reduced rows gives

\[ \begin{aligned} \bar x'&=\gamma f,\\ \bar x''&=-\gamma\bar A^+f,\\ \bar x'''&=\gamma(\bar A^+)^2f -\gamma^3\bar B_{k,\ell}\bar A^+f,\\ \bar x''''&=-\gamma(\bar A^+)^3f +\gamma^3\left( \bar A^+\bar B_{k,\ell}\bar A^+ +\bar B_{k,\ell}(\bar A^+)^2\right)f. \end{aligned} \tag{9} \]

The receiver is reduced coordinate five. Because its row of \(\bar D\) vanishes, the two donor cases have identical receiver derivatives through order three. Their fourth derivative is obtained from the rational reduced matrices through

\[ \begin{aligned} \chi_4&=-e_5^{\mathsf T} \left(\bar A^+\bar D\bar A^+ +\bar D(\bar A^+)^2\right)(q/3),\\ \Delta\bar Y''''(0)&=\chi_4\gamma^3\sin\varphi\,(c_1-c_2). \end{aligned} \tag{10} \]

For example, (1) gives \((\bar A^+q)_0=4/3\), \((\bar A^+q)_1=-1/2\), and \((\bar D\bar A^+q)_0=11/9\). The receiver bridge entry is \(-1/3\), so \(\chi_4=11/81\). This value is derived by composing the reduced operators. It is not a copied parameter from the earlier contact report. The changed receiver class also changes the individual derivative rows in (9), even though it cancels from this donor contrast.

Let \(d_c=c_1-c_2>0\). The exact reduced leading expression is

\[ P=\frac{\chi_4}{24}\gamma^3\sin\varphi\,d_c\,h^4. \tag{11} \]

Its finite response is not identified with this derivative alone. The normalized joined matrix \(\bar A^+\) has a contracting nonnegative semigroup, and \(\|\bar A^+\|_\infty,\|\bar D\|_\infty\le2\). The correlated first-\(\gamma^2\) semigroup expansion has the receiver terms

\[ e_5^{\mathsf T}\sum_{p,q\ge0} \frac{(-1)^{p+q}(\bar A^+)^p\bar D(\bar A^+)^{q+1}f} {(p+q+3)!}\,h^{p+q+3}. \]

All \(p=0\) terms vanish. Bounding the \(n=p+q\ge2\) tail uses \(n\) terms and successive ratio at most \(h/2\). Restoring the physical factors gives

\[ E_{\mathrm{tail}} =\frac{4s\,d_c\gamma^3h^5}{45(1-h/2)}. \tag{12} \]

This derives the tail from the reduced rows and their shared forcing, rather than subtracting two unrelated marginal estimates.
