docs.title: 9. Exact quartic cancellation and its actual-source limitation
docs.text: This bounded quartic comparison keeps Section 8's source, actual support, capacities, structural clock, quadratic G and common-registration target. It asks whether a homogeneous quartic correction removes the leading sine drift, then whether the resulting bounds inform this source. No event, trajectory, preparation change or higher-order sequence is evaluated. The answer separates exact formal cancellation from an unsuccessful source-domain certificate.

docs.title: 9.1. The fixed polynomial question
docs.text:
Write z=(x,theta) in the eight relative coordinates (8.1), and set R(z)=pi*r(z). Thus the full sine law is pi*z_dot=A*z+R(z). Let m_ij count neighbors in block j of a representative in block i, and mu_i be that representative's actual capacity divided by its fine unweighted degree. Blocks are ordered A,H,U,V,D; set theta_A=0 when computing differences. The cubic part of R is exactly

\[ q_i(\theta)=-\frac{\mu_i}{6}\sum_j m_{ij} (\theta_j-\theta_i)^3,\qquad r_3(z)=(q_H-q_A,q_U-q_A,q_V-q_A,q_D-q_A,0,0,0,0). \tag{9.1} \]

Bare neighbor counts, rather than conductances, enter this form row. The phase row is already linear. Subtracting the moving base row preserves the actual relative law; r_3 includes the factor pi relative to a rate in structural time. For I=z^T Gz, define J=I+P_4 and require

\[ \mathcal L P_4:=DP_4(z)Az=-2z^\mathsf T G r_3(z). \tag{9.2} \]

Use homogeneous degree-four monomials z^a, ordered by descending lexicographic exponent tuples in (8.1). The domain contains even total form degree, 0, 2 or 4: its dimension is 35+100+35=170. The codomain contains odd form degree, 1 or 3: its dimension is 80+80=160. A's off-diagonal block form maps the first sector into the second; G is block diagonal and (9.1) is phase-cubic, so the right side belongs to that codomain. The exact matrix entries are

\[ L_{b,a}=\sum_{i,j=1}^8 a_i A_{ij} \mathbf1_{\{b=a-e_i+e_j\}},\qquad f_b=[z^b](-2z^\mathsf T G r_3). \tag{9.3} \]

Terms with a_i=0 contribute zero. This is a specified 160-by-170 rational system, not a fit to sampled dynamics.

All denominators in L are invertible modulo the verified prime 65521. Its first 160 columns satisfy

\[ \det L_{[:,0:160]}\pmod {65521}=53426\ne0. \tag{9.4} \]

Consequently L has rational rank 160, its leftmost pivots are columns 0 through 159, and the fixed sector's kernel has dimension ten. The ten products (z^T G_i z)(z^T G_j z), 0<=i<=j<=3, lie in that kernel by Section 8. Their exact coefficient rank is ten, so they span it. This statement concerns the declared parity sector; it does not classify the entire 330-dimensional space of homogeneous quartics.

Setting coefficients 160 through 169 to zero therefore gives a unique rational P4 in the declared gauge. Exact sparse differentiation verifies (9.2) independently of the elimination used to obtain it. Full row rank also means every right side in this odd-form sector is removable here. The result is not a sine-specific solvability condition or a selection of the sine constitutive law. Changing the gauge adds tangent invariant products and can change actual-source correction and remainder bounds.

docs.title: 9.2. Cancellation does not improve the actual initial drift
docs.text:
At the unchanged source (8.2), exact rational evaluation gives

\[ \frac{29}{1000}<P_4(z_0)<\frac3{100},\qquad \frac{328}{1000}<J(z_0)<\frac{329}{1000}, \tag{9.5} \]

with approximate values 0.029345935642430904 and 0.32860219558033166. Retain alpha, c and k from (8.11)-(8.12), and put ell=DP_4(z0)c. The independently differentiated polynomial gives ell approximately -0.9125382876424339. At this source, r_3(z0)=-alpha^3*c/6, so (9.2) gives DP_4(z0)Az0=k*alpha^3/6. The complete sine derivative, including the correction's nonlinear drift, is

\[ \pi\dot J(0)= k\left(\sin\alpha-\alpha+\frac{\alpha^3}{6}\right) +\ell(\sin\alpha-\alpha). \tag{9.6} \]

Outward rational trigonometric evaluation certifies

\[ \frac{29}{10000}<\dot J(0)<\frac3{1000},\qquad \dot J(0)>20\dot I(0)>0. \tag{9.7} \]

The value is approximately 0.0029054773480158866 per structural time unit. Thus this prescribed correction increases the initial signed drift by more than a factor of twenty. Formal cancellation near consensus is not a smaller remainder at the retained finite-amplitude source. Neither I nor J is identified with physical energy or support-event work.

For every state in this lifted family, the exact remaining derivative is

\[ \pi\dot J(z)=2z^\mathsf T G\bigl(R(z)-r_3(z)\bigr) +DP_4(z)R(z). \tag{9.8} \]

Its Taylor expansion starts at total degree six: R-r_3 starts at degree five, and DP_4 has degree three. Equation (9.8), rather than degree counting alone, supplies the actual-source bound. No finite-amplitude smallness follows from that local order statement.

docs.title: 9.3. A continued source domain and explicit remainder bounds
docs.text:
The actual conserved sine storage is h=H(z0) approximately 0.4180275409303929, with h<21/50<1/2. Each initial bare-edge phase gap has absolute value below pi/3. Nonnegative edge storage prevents any such continued gap from reaching pi/3, where that edge alone would contribute 1/2. On this continued component, 1-cos(delta)>=9*delta^2/(2*pi^2) first gives V>=(9/10)*V2. For every coarse edge direction d, exact inversion of (8.4) gives d^T E_theta^(-1)d<=1/3. Hence delta^2<14/45. The Taylor inequality 1-cos(delta)>=delta^2*(1-delta^2/12)/2 improves coercivity to 97/100; applying the same resistance bound gives delta^2<28/97<3/10, and a second Taylor use gives 39/40. Consequently, throughout the actual continued source domain,

\[ z^\mathsf T D z\le2h,\qquad D=\operatorname{diag}(E_x,\tfrac{39}{40}E_\theta). \tag{9.9} \]

These are bounds for the exact nonlinear law, not its tangent energy. Let h_+ be the rational upper endpoint of the admitted storage enclosure. Choose outward rational radii b_i>=sqrt(2*h_+*(D^(-1))_ii) and edge bounds g_ij>=sqrt(2*h_+*d_ij^T D^(-1)d_ij), with d embedded in the phase coordinates. These correlated edge bounds retain the grounded Laplacian; subtracting unrelated coordinate bounds is unnecessary. For P_4=sum_a p_a z^a, define

\[ B_4=\sum_a|p_a|\prod_i b_i^{a_i},\qquad d_i=\sum_{a:a_i>0}|p_a|a_i\prod_j b_j^{a_j-\delta_{ij}}. \tag{9.10} \]

For s=3,5, put v_(s,i)=mu_i*sum_j m_ij*g_ij^s/s!, with g_ii=0, in each of the five absolute block rows. Let b_(s) have relative form entries v_(s,i)+v_(s,A) for nonbase blocks and four zero phase entries. The scalar sine inequalities bound |R| by b_(3) and |R-r_3| by b_(5). Equation (9.8) therefore gives the rational certificate

\[ |P_4|\le B_4,\qquad |\dot J|\le\varepsilon_6:=\frac{1}{\pi_-} \left(2\sum_{i,j} b_i|G_{ij}|b_{(5),j} +\sum_i d_i b_{(3),i}\right), \tag{9.11} \]

where pi_- is the rational lower endpoint of pi. The implementation returns B4 approximately 97.41432691428348 and epsilon6 approximately 10.559048741729947; the retained rational values, not rounded decimals, are the bounds. They imply, for structural t>=0,

\[ Q(t)\ge J(z_0)-\varepsilon_6t-B_4. \tag{9.12} \]

This lower bound is already below 1/4 at time zero. The initial value of Q itself is known separately; (9.12) fails as a uniform transfer certificate.

docs.title: 9.4. The symmetric-bound obstruction is not merely loose intervals
docs.text:
Reuse the same-storage/means target construction from Section 2. Set all relative phases to zero and only relative form x_H=a, where a^2=2h/(E_x)_HH. Reconstruct the two origins using the unchanged weighted means. This configuration has exactly H=h, lies in the continued short-arc component and retains both marked constituent identities. Its observations and the fixed polynomial are

\[ Q_* =\frac9{10}\frac{2h}{(E_x)_{HH}}<\frac3{50},\qquad P_{4,*}=p_{(4,0,0,0,0,0,0,0)} \left(\frac{2h}{(E_x)_{HH}}\right)^2<-\frac{43}{100}. \tag{9.13} \]

The values are approximately 0.05982303634503962 and -0.43208384351250384. Thus any symmetric absolute bound for P4 on this same-storage/means domain must exceed 0.43, whereas J(z0)-1/4<0.079. Even a sharp symmetric bound cannot make (9.12) certify separation at time zero. Refining the enclosing coordinate boxes alone cannot fix this particular method. The target is a static comparison; no claim is made that the actual source reaches it or follows the earlier configuration path. A smaller reachable set would need its own proof.

docs.title: Chemical observation: sufficient state and predictive information
Result and scope
docs.text:
For the supplied three-field chemical model below, an ideal catalyst snapshot does not close its own evolution. Its first two temporal derivatives recover the complete finite-dimensional state on a specified regular domain. Every smooth exact realization of these output histories on an open preparation family therefore needs at least three real state coordinates per retained spatial site. Singular preparations need a separate analysis; some become identifiable with one more derivative, while a restricted counterexample keeps a hidden field unobservable for the entire history.

This is conditional mathematics about an independently supplied comparison model, not a derivation of chemical dynamics from TNFR. Physical admission remains not_admitted, and empirical evaluation remains not_tested. No response array, experiment, trajectory or fitted pressure is used. The atlas admission owns source selection and measurement gaps; the research program owns scheduling. The ontology permits collective observations without identifying a sensor with primitive EPI.

docs.title: 1. Supplied source, state and clock
docs.text:
Use the modified Oregonator rows in Azhand, Totz and Engel (2014), Section 3, Eq. (1), reviewed on 2026-10-16. The paper associates u,v,w with three chemical concentrations; v is the immobilized catalyst channel. Illumination enters the bromide source phi. Its model time is dimensionless. The numerical discussion also uses spiral-derived length/time units, which supply no independent laboratory-clock calibration here. The text's ordering of epsilon_u,epsilon_w and its later unassigned epsilon,epsilon' numerical notation are not silently reconciled: retain independent positive row coefficients. No numerical parameter set is imported.

Declare n sites and a fixed known real matrix L with nonnegative off-diagonal entries and L*1=0. These conditions preserve constants and support the positivity argument; they do not certify that an arbitrary matrix realizes the article's geometry or its nineteen-point stencil. Any PDE approximation and Neumann-boundary discretization need their own consistency/error justification. Both mobile fields use this declared spatial operator, while the catalyst has no diffusion. Componentwise,

\[ \dot u=\epsilon_u^{-1}[u-u^2+(q-u)w]+Lu,\qquad \dot v=u-v,\qquad \dot w=\epsilon_w^{-1}[\phi+fv-(q+u)w]+\delta Lw. \]

Assume epsilon_u,epsilon_w,q>0, f,delta>=0, nonnegative concentrations and a prescribed continuous nonnegative input phi(t). Coefficients and support are held; no event, stochastic forcing or additional reservoir law is inferred. At each zero concentration, its derivative is nonnegative when the other concentrations are nonnegative. The orthant is therefore forward invariant on the local existence interval. This does not assert global continuation for arbitrary unbounded input or reproduce a laboratory preparation. Interior positive preparations supply the open domains below.

The ideal output is the entire labeled field y=v in this model clock. It is not identified with the experimental camera image; depth integration, optical response and calibration remain unadmitted. Derivatives below are exact model derivatives, not finite differences of data.

docs.title: 2. Regular reconstruction and the minimum exact state
docs.text:
Write y_j=d^j y/dt^j and define

\[ U=y_0+y_1,\qquad D=y_1+y_2,\qquad N=\epsilon_u(D-LU)-U+U^2,\qquad a=q-U. \]

The source rows imply U=u, D=dot u and N=a*w. On the domain a_i!=0 for every site, the inverse is exactly

\[ v=y_0,\qquad u=y_0+y_1,\qquad w_i=N_i/a_i. \]

No illumination value is needed for this instantaneous inverse. It follows from the first two supplied rows; it neither infers the third row nor defines TNFR pressure from the observed response.

In state order (v,u,w), the Jacobian of Psi_2=(y_0,y_1,y_2) is block lower triangular with diagonal blocks I,I,diag((q-u)/epsilon_u). Thus

\[ \det D\Psi_2=\epsilon_u^{-n}\prod_i(q-u_i),\qquad \operatorname{rank}D\Psi_2=3n \]

on the regular domain. This is a nonlinear local observation theorem, not an equilibrium linearization or a rank count of sampled traces.

For completeness, hold the same input history and clock fixed. Suppose a target with m real state coordinates and smooth initialization J reproduces these ideal histories for every state in an open positive preparation set. Require its order-two output-jet map K_2 to be C^1 in target state. Smooth autonomous dynamics/readout with a fixed constant input suffice; arbitrary continuous inputs are not silently differentiated. The output jet then factors as Psi_2=K_2 o J. Consequently 3n<=rank(DJ)<=m wherever the source is regular. Every such open set contains regular points: the exceptional hyperplanes u_i=q have empty interior. Hence m>=3n is necessary for this exact all-state claim. Three source fields also suffice when the supplied input is retained.

In particular, n TNFR nodes with only signed scalar form and circular phase evolving, and all capacities/support held, have local dimension 2n. They cannot give that exact realization on an open source family. This does not exclude more nodes, additional justified evolving state, an admitted restricted preparation, approximate predictions or causal memory. Counting a third coordinate alone would not establish a TNFR constitutive map.

Two elementary comparisons explain the obstruction. Holding v fixed while changing u changes y_1. Holding both v,u fixed while changing w changes y_2 by (q-u)*Delta w/epsilon_u. On regular positive states, neither a snapshot nor the pair (y_0,y_1) is a closed predictive state. This reuses the general closure criterion and the earlier circuit observation method, with the chemical model's own nonlinear coefficient and singular domain.

docs.title: 3. Singular observations are not automatically unobservable
docs.text:
At a site with a_i=0, second-jet consistency requires N_i=0 and does not determine w_i. Let D=dot u as above and

\[ \dot N=\epsilon_u(y_2+y_3-LD)+(2U-1)D. \]

Differentiating N=a*w gives dot N=-D*w+a*dot w. Thus, if D_i!=0 at that singular site,

\[ w_i=-\dot N_i/D_i. \]

This transverse recovery uses the third derivative but not illumination. For a spatially uniform u=q*1, D=q(1-q)/epsilon_u; all singular sites therefore recover this way when q!=1.

There is also a spatial route. With known instantaneous illumination, the entire third-jet consistency problem is the linear system

\[ \begin{pmatrix}A\\B\end{pmatrix}w =\begin{pmatrix}N\\\dot N-A(\phi+fv)/\epsilon_w\end{pmatrix}, \quad A=\operatorname{diag}(a), \quad B=\delta AL-\operatorname{diag}(D) -\operatorname{diag}(a(q+u))/\epsilon_w. \]

Full column rank supplies a unique solution, subject to nonnegative-state and residual admission. Regular neighbors can reveal a tangential singular site through diffusion even when its own D_i=0. If the stacked matrix has a kernel, it produces nearby distinct positive states with identical jets through order three at an interior preparation. It does not prove identical full histories. At a positivity boundary, intersection with the nonnegative cone may remove this ambiguity. Unknown illumination introduces another ambiguity in the regular rows and cannot be silently eliminated.

A genuine full-history exception exists within the symbolic model family. Take q=1, spatially uniform u=1, any uniform positive v(0) and two different uniform positive w(0), with the same nonnegative uniform input. Then u stays one and dot v=1-v, independently of w; distinct bromide histories remain invisible. This is a lower-dimensional invariant preparation at a particular parameter value, not a counterexample to the open-family dimension theorem or a claim about the paper's experimental parameters.

docs.title: 4. Recovering state does not recover future input
docs.text:
On the regular domain, substituting w=N/a into the third source row yields the exact input/output identity

\[ a\dot N+ND =\frac{a^2}{\epsilon_w}\left[\phi+fv-(q+u)\frac Na\right] +\delta a^2L\left(\frac Na\right). \]

Products and divisions are componentwise; L(N/a) is the full spatial operation, not (LN)/a. Together with u=y_0+y_1, this is a third-order output description on the regular domain. It is a rewriting of the supplied chemical law with its full state information retained, not a two-field reduction or a TNFR pressure law.

At the same state, changing the prescribed input changes the third output derivative by

\[ \Delta y_3=(q-u)\Delta\phi/(\epsilon_u\epsilon_w). \]

Thus identical y_0,y_1,y_2 do not predict y_3 without input information. More generally, agreeing past inputs need not determine their future. An externally prescribed source is not rendered autonomous by reconstructing internal state. Any controller or environment generating it needs its own law.

docs.title: 5. Exact information versus recoverable information
docs.text:
Fix the source coefficients, spatial operator and clock. Suppose the true state satisfies ||u||_infinity<=M_u, ||w||_infinity<=M_w and min_i|q-u_i|>=rho>0. Let supplied approximate jets have independent supremum error allowances eta_0,eta_1,eta_2. Set

\[ \alpha=\eta_0+\eta_1,\qquad b=\eta_1+\eta_2,\qquad B_N=\epsilon_u(b+\|L\|_\infty\alpha) +(1+2M_u+\alpha)\alpha. \]

If alpha<rho, algebraic reconstruction satisfies

\[ \|\widetilde u-u\|_\infty\le\alpha,\qquad \|\widetilde w-w\|_\infty \le\frac{B_N+M_w\alpha}{\rho-\alpha}. \]

Indeed the numerator error is at most B_N, the reconstructed denominator is at least rho-alpha, and tilde N-tilde a*w=(tilde N-N)+(tilde u-u)*w. The inverse becomes poorly conditioned as the separation vanishes. Near u=q, a fixed bromide difference can produce arbitrarily small second-jet separation. This bound assumes derivative-error allowances; it does not derive them from finitely sampled noisy images, calibrate the camera or cover parameter, spatial-discretization or clock uncertainty. The transverse inverse similarly requires control of its own nonzero denominator.

The information result is therefore about distinguishable states and prediction, not bits or a universal entropy balance. Shannon quantities would additionally require a preparation distribution and an observation/noise channel. EPI, structural capacity and coherence are not probabilities, channel capacity or entropy by name. Existing TNFR memory and nonlinear hidden-state elimination provide reusable methods, not coefficients that transfer to this chemical law.

docs.title: 6. Execution and verification
docs.text:
The detached exact control module admits rational or represented-real coefficients before calculation. It evaluates source jets and reconstructs regular or pointwise transverse states; the general stacked singular solver is a theorem here, not an implemented reconstruction mode. An unsupported singular inverse is explicit abstention. Optional y_3 is consumed only by that transverse inverse and does not certify the full source/input law. The implementation is capped at 32 sites as an algebraic resource policy, not a theorem dimension restriction.

Independent controls differentiate the supplied polynomial field symbolically, check exact rank, hidden-state/input counterexamples, diffusion-assisted recovery, singular domains and scalar admission. They do not differentiate measured traces or run the chemical reactor. Existing shared exact scalar and linear-observation owners remain unchanged. No engine solver, native law, operator, grammar rule, SDK export or physical measurement map is installed by this module.

The remaining physical obligations are the complete optical observation, retained depth/spatial state, preparation, input law, laboratory clock, uncertainty and independent acquisitions. Any exact TNFR realization must also satisfy all mapped evolution rows, including its phase/capacity/support premises. The result selects no such law and does not identify a chemical organization with an elementary constituent.

Selected comparison and decision scope
docs.text:

docs.title: Primary-source evidence
docs.text:
The following factual ledger summarizes the selected paper's Sections 1, 5, 6 and Appendices A/C. Its equations are analyzed separately below.

Published premise Relevance to admission CD4046B circuits combine XOR detection, low-pass filtering and voltage-controlled oscillation. Retain detector, filter and oscillator state and constitutive domains. A microcontroller supplies transmission delays; tested networks contain two, three or nine oscillators. Delays and the actual support are part of the source model. The phase approximation uses an even triangular coupling function and suppresses high-frequency detector terms. Neither the target sine kernel nor a quantified reduction error follows. Oscillators initially run independently for a random duration before coupling. This is not the target's prescribed complete-state preparation. Oscilloscope output traces supply phase time series and frequency/relaxation estimates. Admit the extraction and instrument observation law separately. The paper treats idealized dynamics without phase noise and identifies oscillator clipping. Nominal formulas do not certify full-domain model or measurement errors.

These statements are supported by the primary article. Its experimental supplement is identified but was not opened or downloaded for this audit. Published figures consulted during selection are prior information and cannot later become reserved TNFR observations.

Manufacturer documentation supplies further component-level checks. The TI application report, Section 3.1 describes comparator I's XOR/triangular characteristic and its duty-cycle dependence; Section 3.2 discusses buffered observation of the control voltage. The PicoScope 2205 MSO specification, page 4 lists two analog and sixteen digital channels, 8-bit analog resolution, DC accuracy of ±3% full scale and timebase accuracy of ±100 ppm. These are published specifications, not a calibration certificate for the experimental setup. They provide neither a transformed TNFR noise bound nor a validated source or clock map. No instrument acquisition is proposed here.

The source receipt records the selected primary URLs and retrieved-byte hashes. It is a methods provenance record, not a reserved response, an authentication certificate or independent validation of the published specifications.

docs.title: State, law and clock admission
docs.text:
The target complete sine law evolves both signed form and primitive phase on a fixed eighteen-node support. The source must supply either a complete state/clock map into that model or a separately proved approximation with bounded defects in both evolution rows. A scalar phase fit or a common frequency label does not meet this requirement. A source-specific reduction must retain its history, initialization, input and discarded-state assumptions.

For a first-order loop filter and identical nominal parameters, a local realization of the paper's phase model (Eq. 8 and Appendix C) is

\[ \begin{aligned} \dot\phi_i(t)&=\omega+K z_i(t),\\ b\dot z_i(t)&=-z_i(t)+\sum_j\frac{c_{ij}}{d_i} \Delta\!\left(\phi_j(t-\tau_d)-\phi_i(t)\right),\\ \Delta(\psi)&=\frac{2}{\pi}|\operatorname{wrap}_{\pi}\psi|-1, \qquad d_i=\sum_jc_{ij}. \end{aligned} \tag{1} \]

Here t, the filter time b>0 and delay tau_d>0 are in seconds; phi is in radians, omega and K>0 are in inverse seconds, and z is dimensionless. Any clock change must transform both evolution rows. Equation (1) has an independent-initial-value realization with phase history on [-tau_d,0] and current filter state. Matching a convolution initialized from an infinite past additionally constrains that filter state, or requires its homogeneous initialization term. Arbitrary pairs of initial history and filter state used below are supplied admissible preparations of this delay realization; this audit does not establish their experimental reachability or compatibility with every convolution history. Nor does it bound the phase approximation's discrepancy from all circuit states.

docs.title: An exact obstruction to a regular current-state identification
docs.text:
The following deduction uses (1), without measured response data. Consider a domain admitting two phase histories with the same current y=(phi(0),z(0)) and a nonzero current phase-velocity vector u=omega*1+K*z(0). Choose one incident delayed neighbor value strictly inside a linear branch of Delta, and perturb that value while preserving the current phase and filter state. Smooth history perturbations away from zero can also preserve the current history derivative. The affected z_dot changes because the branch slope is nonzero, while phi_dot=u does not. The two current-state derivative vectors at that state have the form

\[ F_1=(u,v),\qquad F_2=(u,v+d),\qquad u\ne0,\quad d\ne0. \tag{2} \]

They are not collinear: F1=a*F2 would give a=1 from the phase block and then d=0, a contradiction. A differentiable current-state map J(y) with injective differential preserves this noncollinearity. If it produced one autonomous target vector at J(y) under positive clock factors r1,r2, then

\[ DJ(y)F_1=r_1F_{\rm target}(J(y)),\qquad DJ(y)F_2=r_2F_{\rm target}(J(y)). \tag{3} \]

Injectivity would imply F1=(r1/r2)*F2, contradicting (2). Thus even history-dependent positive clock rescaling cannot close this regular current-state identification on a family containing the two histories. The conclusion also covers a regular embedding into a larger current-state target; merely appending coordinates determined by y does not retain the missing independent history. The map is regular in the current coordinates, not injective on the complete state that includes history.

This is a mapping obstruction on the stated domain. It does not exclude restricted initialized histories, a history-dependent state map, a lossy observable with its own closure proof, or an independently bounded approximation. The triangular detector, filtering, support and input differences remain separate admission obligations even after such a history restriction. An exact phase equation on a selected synchronized family would not establish a transient full-state realization.

An independent rational control makes the two-history premise explicit. In phase turns psi=phi/(2*pi), take b=tau_d=1 second, omega=K=pi/4 radians per second and z(0)=(0,0). In the following formulas, t is the numerical time in seconds. On -1<=t<=0, set

\[ \psi_0(t)=t/8,\qquad \psi_1^{A}(t)=1/4+t/8,\qquad \psi_1^{B}(t)=1/4+t/8+t^2/32. \]

Both histories have current phase (0,1/4) and derivative (1/8,1/8); their history derivatives remain positive. The current delayed arguments are (1/8,-3/8) and (5/32,-3/8), strictly inside regular detector branches. Using Delta_turn(a)=4*abs(wrap_turn(a))-1, the two current vectors in (psi,z) coordinates are (1/8,1/8,-1/2,1/2) and (1/8,1/8,-3/8,1/2). The minor from their first and third components is 1/64, proving noncollinearity. The independent controls derive the detector from exact square-wave XOR overlap before checking these vectors. This supplied initial-value example proves neither experimental reachability nor an extension obeying the unforced source law throughout the negative-time history.

docs.title: Phase readout and rotating-frame boundaries
docs.text:
Changing to a fixed rotating frame theta=phi-Omega*t retains the delayed detector argument

\[ \theta_j(t-\tau_d)-\theta_i(t)-\Omega\tau_d. \tag{4} \]

Dropping its last term changes the source law. A biased triangular detector can have different parity from the unshifted one; evenness alone is not an obstruction to every coordinate or phase-origin change.

There is a further obstruction to simply using these phases as the target phases on the same undirected support. The target has constant degree-weighted mean phase because d.T*A=0. The source instead gives d.T*theta_dot=d.T*(omega*1+K*z-Omega*1), which varies with independently initialized filter state. One fixed carrier subtraction cannot make that expression vanish on an open filter-state domain. This statement addresses the direct phase readout; a constrained mean leaf or a different collective observable needs its own proof. It does not turn the paper's smaller supports into the target's eighteen-node geometry.

docs.title: Preparation, observation and uncertainty obligations
docs.text:
The following are requirements of this comparison, not additional facts about what the instrument can achieve. Missing evidence remains unavailable.

Obligation Required evidence before using the target certificate Complete preparation Joint bounds for every consumed source state and retained history, a declared initialization law and its map to the target source family. A phase-only specification does not establish a form/phase norm ball. Support and capacities Actual node ordering, contacts, weights, degree normalization and capacity map. Adding nodes or replacing the support changes the model rather than completing missing metadata. Inputs and events An independently specified action realizing the two target phase interventions, or a bounded finite-duration input model. A coupling switch is not automatically a phase-only jump with unchanged form. Observation A causal map from recorded voltages/timestamps to the proposed collective quantity, including extraction, bandwidth, aperture alignment and instrument memory. It must justify the fixed four normalized averages and held gain/offset if those are consumed. Clock and units A calibrated conversion from physical time to the structural clock, transformed in every row, with units for form, pressure, sensor gain and additive errors. Clock synchronization alone supplies no such conversion. Uncertainty Independent source, constitutive, timing, kernel and measurement bounds over the declared horizon. Nominal resolution, repeat dispersion and deterministic numerical enclosure width have different meanings. Alternatives and evaluation A prospective discriminator under equally informed alternatives, separated calibration and reserved response, and a frozen source/event/observation/numerical protocol.

The finite-noise theorem propagates declared budgets under its supplied model. It cannot certify their physical attainability. A continuous mapped-law defect is not an initial-state error or an additive sensor error; transporting one into the other requires its own finite-flow argument. Repeated recordings do not repair missing dynamics or an unsupported preparation map.

docs.title: Physical feasibility of the organized current discriminator
Decision and scope
docs.text:
Physical status: not admitted. Experimental evaluation: not tested. The reviewed primary sources do not supply a laboratory realization of the frozen current discriminator. The failure has three distinct parts: its voltage observation has an extreme clock-independent precision/aperture requirement; ordinary junction capacitance changes an exact matrix premise; and independent preparation of the full organized state has not been established. This is a scoped admission result, not a physical rejection of either candidate law or TNFR.

The two conditional current envelopes and their frozen evidence remain unchanged. This audit derives laboratory-unit consequences and reviews methods/specifications; it acquires no experimental response, fits no coefficient and reruns no frozen producer. A published method is not a calibration certificate for a proposed assembly. The research program alone owns the next task.

docs.title: 1. Complete object and physical reference
docs.text:
The subject remains the 45-node C9-by-C5 organization, its two complete evolution rows, fixed support and held capacity. The comparison supplies mu equal to 1 or 2, a common observation-start state class and one finite input word. It does not prove alternative-law acquisition. Its exact five-coordinate electrical carrier and bounded fine departures are different objects: a prepared ideal five-island circuit cannot stand in for the formation of five constituent C9 organizations.

Use the fixed-support dictionary and the robust owner's fixed nominal coordinates. Write L for the C5 Laplacian, P for its neutral projection and L+ for its centered inverse. The supplied physical reference has capacitance matrix c L+, conductance matrix g P, five sine-current branches and voltage-phase constant a0. Nominal calibration fixes

\[ b_0=4g_0/c_0,\quad \kappa_0=a_{00}\gamma g_0/9,\quad v_0=a_{00}\gamma b_0/4,\quad j_0=a_{00}\gamma^2g_0^2/c_0,\quad \gamma=1/(1023\pi). \tag{1} \]

The ratios C=c/c0, G=g/g0, A=a0/a00 and D are constant and independently bounded by 1 +/- 1e-8. Laboratory time maps to s=b0 D t. Readout always uses U=L+ V/v0 and nominal charge q_nom=c0 L+ V; actual charge is C q_nom. Changing nominal conversion after viewing the current would change the test.

For numerical illustrations only, set a00=h_P/(4 pi e), where h_P denotes Planck's constant, not the plateau length. The SI definitions, NIST SP 330 Section 2 give h_P=6.62607015e-34 J s and e=1.602176634e-19 C exactly. Thus a00 is approximately 3.291059785e-16 V s. Those supplied physical constants and the Josephson reference law are not derived from TNFR. An exact SI constant does not eliminate uncertainty in its realization or prove that a device obeys the reference law.

docs.title: 2. Voltage precision and time cannot be chosen separately
docs.text:
The frozen word has h=1e-5, fifteen unit-duration ramps, duration T=15.00015, raw nominal-form error eta_raw=1e-14 and inward endpoint aperture delta=1e-13. For every constant D,

\[ t_{\rm plateau}=h/(b_0D),\quad t_{\rm ramp}=1/(b_0D),\quad t_{\rm word}=T/(b_0D),\quad t_{\rm aperture}\le\delta/(b_0D). \tag{2} \]

All 150 scalars require their declared marking and windows. Clock accuracy does not substitute for sensor bandwidth or an inward averaging kernel.

Because the rows of L+ contain 2/5, zero, -1/5, -1/5, zero, its infinity norm is 4/5. Arbitrarily correlated voltage errors of size e_V therefore give form error at most 4 e_V/(5 v0). The bound is sharp for the admitted error class: signs aligned with one row attain it, whereas a common offset cancels. Allocating the entire raw allowance to voltage requires

\[ e_V\le {5\over16}a_{00}b_0\gamma\eta_{raw}. \tag{3} \]

Any other raw conversion error consumes part of this allowance. Known sensor correlations may permit a different bound, but cannot be assumed from independent channel labels.

Suppose an independently specified sensor mode needs an averaging support of duration at least t_min and offers a uniform absolute error guarantee e_V for that mode. Fitting its support inside each frozen aperture and using (3) requires

\[ e_V t_{min}\le {5a_{00}\gamma\eta_{raw}\delta\over16D} \simeq {3.200075958\,10^{-47}\over D}\ {\rm V\,s}. \tag{4} \]

For one apparatus guarantee over the entire D box, use D_max. This is a necessary compatibility condition for the specified error-box admission, not a universal uncertainty principle or a lower bound on every possible sensor. It does not apply to an unmodeled charge, flux or current readout. Positive averages must stay inside the window; a manufacturer's response time alone does not establish their support or positivity.

The following unit conversions have D=1. They are illustrative scales, not independently realizable component choices or new assessed protocols.

b0 (s^-1) Maximum aperture (s) Maximum voltage error (V) Word duration (s) 1e-12 1e-1 3.2001e-46 1.500015e13 1 1e-13 3.2001e-34 15.00015 1e12 1e-25 3.2001e-22 1.500015e-11

Merely slowing the experiment lengthens the aperture while lowering the allowed voltage error by the same factor. Increasing precision in the existing interval calculation does not repair (4).

The nominal waveform has peak voltage (6/25) a00 b0. In the actual robust decomposition its commanded part is multiplied by rho=1/(C D), with background bounded by a00 b0 gamma M_mu. A single range covering the nominal ramps and resolving the plateaus therefore encounters the nominal commanded-component/error ratio

\[ {96\over125\gamma\eta_{raw}}\simeq2.468236251\,10^{17}. \tag{5} \]

This is not an ADC bit-depth theorem. Separate ranges or gated protection change the range problem and need their own settling/loading evidence; they do not alone remove (4).

docs.title: 3. Delivery, leakage and work in the same units
docs.text:
The robust law consumes u=rho f+d. Its physical current discrepancy obeys d=delta_I/(9 b0 kappa0 C D). Consequently, for any part J of the word,

\[ \int_{J_{lab}}\|\delta_I\|_\infty dt =9\kappa_0 C\int_J\|d\|_\infty ds. \tag{6} \]

The total F=1e-4 and each plateau P_leak=1e-15 thus require respective integrated absolute current errors at most a00 gamma g0 C F and a00 gamma g0 C P_leak, in coulombs. A bound uniform over C uses C_min. These are integrals of absolute error, not the absolute value of net delivered charge; cancellation cannot certify them.

On a plateau the permitted mean absolute leakage is

\[ {\overline{|\delta I|}_{max}\over j_0} ={4CD P_{leak}\over\gamma h} \simeq 1.28554\,10^{-6}CD. \tag{7} \]

This is not a pointwise leakage bound. For the prescribed cubic r(ramp)=3 ramp^2-2 ramp^3, k_c=e_c-1/5 and v=L+ k_c,

\[ I_{cmd}=a_{00}g_0b_0 a(4v r''+k_c r'),\qquad \max\|I_{cmd}\|_\infty={48\over25}a_{00}g_0b_0. \tag{8} \]

The largest increment has absolute amplitude 1/5. Substitution of the five coordinates gives the peak at a ramp endpoint. Dividing (8) by the allowed plateau average gives 48 h/(25 gamma C D P_leak), approximately 6.17059e13/(C D). This is an on/off integrated-delivery demand; it does not require that many DAC levels. An L1 discrepancy budget supplies neither a peak bound nor a bandwidth. Every switch, transient, sensor loading current and nonneutral leakage needs its own admission.

For resources let K0=kappa0 v0 and use the robust coefficients lambda=G/(C D), beta=A G^2/(C^2 D), eta=1/(A D). Direct power pairing gives

\[ \int V^TI_{actual}\,dt =C K_0\int (L_{45}x)^TRu\,ds,\qquad E_{co}=9C K_0\left[{U^TLU\over2} +{\mu\beta\over\eta}\sum_{ring}(1-\cos\Delta\Phi)\right]. \tag{9} \]

Indeed I_actual=9 b0 kappa0 C D u and (L45 x)^T R u=9 (L U)^T u. The positive part of total supplied power scales by the same positive factor. Resistive heat equals C K0 times fine loss minus hidden loss, each with coefficient lambda. The existing finite resource majorants translate only on this same model and time interval. K0 times full fine storage is not the energy of a constructed fine electrical substrate. The dictionary starts at observation and does not convert earlier constituent recovery/formation into lab time or joules without an extended map.

docs.title: 4. Component shape is an independent obstruction
docs.text:
The exact capacitance matrix c L+ has zero adjacent off-diagonal entries. Suppose the five ring junctions also have a positive mutual capacitance c_J each, as permitted by the supplied RCSJ reference. Then

\[ C_{phys}=cL^++c_J L\ne\widetilde cL^+ \quad\hbox{for every }c_J>0\hbox{ and every scalar }\widetilde c. \tag{10} \]

At each adjacent off-diagonal the left side is -c_J and the right side is zero. This remains a disagreement on the neutral leaf: both matrices annihilate the common mode, so equality there would imply full equality. It cannot be covered by widening only the scalar capacitance interval. Unequal branches or ground capacitance introduce additional changes; sensor loading can also change the dynamical law.

Equation (10) excludes exact shape matching for this explicit passive realization with nonzero ring capacitance. It neither sets a universal parasitic lower bound nor excludes a controlled approximate reduction. A small shape departure needs a matrix perturbation theorem carrying both rows, preparation, memory, observation and discrimination error. It cannot be assigned the intrinsic fine-state remainder by terminology.

On the neutral collective leaf, V=v0 L U gives q=c*v0*(I+(c_J/c)*L^2)*U. The matrix-response comparison owns the resulting changed rows, storage and charge-coordinate contract. This collective reference supplies no automatic transfer of the fine-source acquisition or frozen discrimination certificates.

docs.title: 5. Independent source review and preparation gap
docs.text:
The methods receipt records the reviewed sources and retrieval availability. Retrieved-byte hashes, where available, are provenance associations, not authentication. The following are source facts; their admission consequences are our inferences. No reviewed figure or response becomes reserved evidence.

Primary source Supported facts Remaining admission Babenko et al. (2020), pp. 937-939 RCSJ and voltage-phase equations; a 1500-junction array at 4 K with 5 GHz excitation and calibrated microwave measurements. The authors discuss junction variation and nonsinusoidal response. No C5 matrix, 45-state preparation or error guarantee for this word. Junction capacitance is explicit in the reference equation. English et al., arXiv v2, pp. 1-2 Phase-sensitive observation through a superconducting loop, flux transformer and DC SQUID; 10 mK base temperature and a nonhysteretic operating condition. An independent phase method is possible, but its loop state, loading and calibration must be retained. It does not establish our initial phase collar. AH2700A brochure, pp. 1-2 Published 1 kHz capacitance accuracy of +/-5 ppm. This specification alone is 500 times wider than the frozen 0.01 ppm scalar allowance, and is not a matrix calibration at the proposed operating conditions. NIST impedance metrology, Major Accomplishments A specialized resistor/capacitor comparison reports combined standard uncertainty of 5 ppb near 1592 Hz. The scalar budget is not universally unattainable; this is not a complete cryogenic matrix certificate or a deterministic error bound. Keithley 2182A manufacturer page, Features Two channels, 1 nV sensitivity, typical 15 nV peak-to-peak noise at 1 s response and 40-50 nV at 60 ms. No five-coordinate synchronized transfer, positive inward kernel or simultaneous absolute guarantee meeting (3)-(4). Response time, sensitivity and typical noise must not be substituted for those distinct premises. JCGM 100:2008, Sections 2.3.5, 6.2, 7.2.5 Expanded uncertainty carries a stated coverage interpretation; multiple outputs require their uncertainty/covariance information. RMS, typical noise and marginal coverage intervals do not supply the frozen simultaneous deterministic error box.

For magnitude context only, the hypothetical pair e_V=1 nV and t_min=1 ms has product 1e-12 V s, exceeding (4) by about 3.1e34 at D=1. This pair is not asserted to be a manufacturer guarantee or a fundamental noise floor. The reviewed voltmeter specifications cannot certify the required pair, and do not supply the observation kernel in the first place. Neither a finite typical peak-to-peak sample nor calibration uncertainty may be promoted to a hard bound on every future reading. A statistical protocol would instead need a joint confidence event over all readings, preparation and calibration; the deterministic theorem could apply conditionally on that event if all its other premises were met.

Preparation remains separate from precision. The model needs independently justified bounds on the complete initial signed forms, hidden constituent deviations and admitted relative phase set. Zero voltage does not establish relative phases or internal deviations. Even the ideal carrier allows identical U=0 with Phi=0 or Phi=(d,-d,0,0,0), with small positive d: both have winding zero and zero voltage, but different sine-current vectors. Winding alone is insufficient. The prior need not identify an exact phase, yet must be independently justified as a set under both candidate laws. None of the reviewed sources supplies that preparation or extends the physical map through the TNFR acquisition.

docs.title: 6. Consequence for research
docs.text:
There is no admitted physical candidate in this review. Equation (4) identifies a limitation of the frozen endpoint-voltage method, (10) an exact shape mismatch for a specified junction-capacitance realization, and the preparation audit missing independent evidence. These are different conclusions and must not be combined into a universal no-go.

A successor must explicitly change the observation/protocol or prove an appropriate approximation; repeating the same arithmetic at higher precision supplies neither. Finite-window observables, direct current or flux sensing, a prepared collective reference and a generatively acquired organization have different obligations. Any successor must keep the source distinction, declare loading and matrix deviations, retain its own law and work, and freeze its unfitted prediction before response selection. The conditional current result is useful as an ideal comparison, not as evidence that the required physical apparatus already exists.

The independent algebra controls check inverse-matrix error propagation, scale cancellation, current/work conversion and a positive-capacitance counterexample. They establish no instrument performance. No runtime capability or public API is added by this documentary and mathematical admission audit.
