Declared question and candidate
docs.text:
This design admission follows the prepared matrix-response theorem. It asks whether a finite observation with an explicit passive sensor can preserve a predictive consequence and support an independent physical test. The analytical declaration and result below remain reusable under their stated premises; the research program alone selects further work. No apparatus, measured response, source acquisition or fine-node extension is supplied by this mathematical design.

Keep the complete C5 law, signed forms U, circular phases Phi, held unit capacities, fixed support, normalized structural clock tau and exact gamma=1/(1023*pi) of the owner. Write v=(1,-1,0,0,0), W_r=I+r*L^2, y=v^T*L*U. Add one sensor state z with

\[ W_r U'=(-LU+\gamma S(\Phi))/4+f-kv(y-z),\qquad \Phi'=\gamma LU/4,\qquad \tau_s z'=y-z. \tag{1} \]

The sensor loads the form row through its actual current; it is not an additive observation error. The selected observable y differs from the earlier v^T*U: it is proportional to a physical differential voltage in the declared electrical dictionary.

Primitive Fixed analytical declaration Response family and control Fixed r in [1/100,1/10], compared separately with r=0 Full preparation The earlier centered winding w=+1 or w=-1 reference, ||U(0)||_2+||theta(0)||_2<=delta=2^-26; the same continuous perturbation lift and closing-edge offset Sensor preparation Independently bounded |z(0)|<=delta_s=2^-26 Input f=a*v on [0,T], zero afterwards; a=1/16, T=1/1024 Sensor law k=1/64, tau_s=T; no resets, phase forcing or support events Observation J=(1/T)*integral_0^T z(tau) d tau, with separate additive error |e|<=eta=2^-26 Identity criterion Every oriented phase gap remains within rho=1/10 of its prepared 2*pi*w/5 during the pulse and later unforced evolution Matrix-response criterion Whole-preparation observed intervals for positive r and r=0 are disjoint with separation >2^-21 Phase-sensitive control Compare with a passive linear reference having the same r, form/sensor initialization, input, clock and sensor but omitting the sine-current branch; determine whether permitted records must be disjoint or can overlap Physical admission Independent complete preparation, loaded transfer and matrices, delivery, clock and observation error/coverage under the same laboratory protocol Calculation Exact rational inequalities and certified exponential/trigonometric bounds; no trajectory, parameter scan, fitted response or physical dataset

The phase-blind reference tests what this observable resolves after linear calibration. It does not override independently established junction data. An independently justified sine-current law would be additional evidence, not something inferred from an unresolved pulse observation.

Source review concerns terrestrial methods and specifications only. Earlier frozen protocols, source archives, responses and the separate endpoint-voltage feasibility review remain unchanged. A conditional sensor equation is not a manufacturer performance claim or a hardware implementation.

docs.title: Analytical result and admission boundary
docs.text: Revision 34baddca freezes the declaration above. The following calculations use its complete loaded law, without a trajectory, measured response or parameter scan. The candidate retains the prepared identity and separates the positive-r matrices from r=0. However, its permitted records overlap those of the declared phase-blind linear reference. It therefore does not admit an organization-sensitive physical test. Independent full preparation, component/input/clock calibration and observation coverage also remain open.

docs.title: Own storage, identity and resources
docs.text:
Write H_r=U^T*L*W_r*U/2+V(Phi), V=sum_edges[1-cos(Phi_j-Phi_i)] and V_*=5[1-cos(2*pi/5)], as in the matrix-response owner. For the loaded law, the correct storage and its derivative are

\[ H_{r,s}=H_r+\frac{k\tau_s}{2}z^2,\qquad H_{r,s}'=-\frac14\|LU\|^2-k(y-z)^2+(LU)^Tf. \tag{2} \]

Indeed, the form row adds -k*y*(y-z) to the original balance, while the sensor contributes k*z*(y-z). Their sum is the displayed loss. Treating the sensor as a detached reading would omit both terms. The form mean and common mean of the declared phase lift remain fixed: v and f are neutral and the phase row is unchanged. The solved input and loading channels are M_r*f and -k*M_r*v*(y-z).

Let theta be the declared centered perturbation lift. In the relative cell max|D theta|<=rho=1/10, the earlier cosine bound gives V-V_*>=||D theta||^2/10. Initial admission follows from 2*delta<rho. A first boundary contact would require excess storage E_s=H_{r,s}-V_*>=1/1000. Using ||L||<=4 and completing the square in (2), including the sensor's nonnegative energy, gives

\[ E_s(0)\le(4+32r_{\max})\delta^2+\frac{kT}{2}\delta_s^2, \qquad E_s'\le\|f\|^2,\qquad E_s(\tau)\le\overline E_s=E_s(0)_{\rm upper}+2a^2T <2^{-16}<\frac1{1000}. \tag{3} \]

This excludes boundary contact throughout the pulse. After T, (2) is nonincreasing, so the identity remains inside the collar for all subsequent unforced time. The globally Lipschitz sine source and constant invertible matrices ensure continuation. This is retention of the supplied identity, not acquisition. The full preparation cost includes V_*; the excess in (3) is neither total storage nor a source for the external input.

For finite response bounds put X=||U||+||theta||. The sine source obeys ||S(Phi_w^*+theta)||<=4||theta|| globally; ||M_r||<=1, ||v||<2, ||Lv||=sqrt(20)<5, and gamma<1. The stable sensor convolution bounds sup|z|<=delta_s+5*sup X. Integrating both live evolution rows gives, when (2+20k)T<1,

\[ \sup_{[0,T]}X\le Z= \frac{\delta+2aT+2kT\delta_s}{1-(2+20k)T},\qquad B=(1+20k)Z+2k\delta_s, \tag{4} \]

and ||U(tau)-a*tau*M_r*v||<=delta+tau*B. These inequalities hold without freezing phase or relying on the identity flag. In particular, they retain unknown sensor initialization and back-action. The separate resource bounds are

\[ \int_0^T|(LU)^Tf|\,d\tau\le8aTZ,\quad \int_0^T\frac14\|LU\|^2\,d\tau\le4TZ^2,\quad \int_0^Tk(y-z)^2\,d\tau\le kT(\delta_s+10Z)^2. \tag{5} \]

Equation (2) retains the signed supplied work and both continuous losses. The growth allowance 2a^2T in (3) is not an equality for delivered work.

docs.title: Sensor memory and finite matrix separation
docs.text:
The exact sensor solution is

\[ z(\tau)=e^{-\tau/\tau_s}z(0)+\frac1{\tau_s} \int_0^\tau e^{-(\tau-u)/\tau_s}y(u)\,du. \tag{6} \]

Eliminating z from the form row leaves the term -k*v*y(tau)+k*v*exp(-tau/tau_s)*z(0) plus the convolution in (6) multiplied by k v. Thus a reduced form law retains both sensor memory and initialization. Replacing z by y instantaneously would change the model. Integrating (6) over the declared window yields

\[ J=\frac{\tau_s}{T}(1-e^{-T/\tau_s})z(0) +\frac1T\int_0^T[1-e^{-(T-u)/\tau_s}]y(u)\,du. \tag{7} \]

For tau_s=T, let alpha=1/2-exp(-1)>1/8. Equation (4) then implies

\[ J=aT\alpha\,g(r)+R_J^{\rm actual},\qquad |R_J^{\rm actual}|\le R_J=\delta_s+5\delta+\frac{5T}{2}B, \qquad g(r)=v^TLM_rv=\frac{6+20r}{1+15r+25r^2}. \tag{8} \]

The positive kernel in (7), with total weight at most one, bounds the initialization and constant port remainder; its first moment is at most T/2. The neutral C5 identity L^2-5L+5I=0 supplies the exact gain. Its derivative has numerator -70-300r-500r^2, so it decreases strictly. For the fixed family, g in [32/11,2480/461], whereas g(0)=6. Writing b_J=R_J+eta, the entire permitted record sets lie within

\[ \mathcal J_+= [aT\alpha(32/11)-b_J,\ aT\alpha(2480/461)+b_J],\qquad \mathcal J_0=[6aT\alpha-b_J,\ 6aT\alpha+b_J]. \tag{9} \]

Both use the same alpha. Exact rational substitution already gives

\[ \inf\mathcal J_0-\sup\mathcal J_+ \ge\frac{aT}{8}\frac{286}{461}-2b_J>2^{-21}. \tag{10} \]

The implementation also encloses alpha tightly through the shared rational exponential bounds. Independently widening alpha to unrelated coarse values in the two records would discard their correlation and needlessly weaken the separation. This is a finite loaded-response distinction between specified matrices, conditional on the complete preparation and error bounds.

docs.title: What the same observation cannot distinguish
docs.text:
The declared reference keeps the same r, U(0), z(0), input, clock and sensor:

\[ W_r\widehat U'=-L\widehat U/4+f-kv(\widehat y-\widehat z), \qquad \widehat y=v^TL\widehat U,\qquad T\widehat z'=\widehat y-\widehat z. \tag{11} \]

It consumes no phase coordinate. Its own passive storage is Uhat^T*L*W_r*Uhat/2+k*T*zhat^2/2; its derivative is (2) with hats. The comparison matches calibrated linear components and omits the sine-current branch. Independently established junction data could exclude this reference; the present calculation tests what the finite pulse adds by itself.

For the actual complete law, ||theta(tau)||<=delta+gamma*tau*Z. Write E=sup_[0,T]||U-Uhat||. Equal sensor initialization and (6) give sup|z-zhat|<=5E. The form difference therefore satisfies

\[ E\le(1+20k)TE+\gamma\delta T+\frac{\gamma^2ZT^2}{2},\qquad |J-\widehat J|\le5E\le \frac{5\bar\gamma(\delta T+\bar\gamma ZT^2/2)} {1-(1+20k)T},\quad \bar\gamma=\frac1{3000}>\gamma. \tag{12} \]

The first term bounds both diffusion and actual sensor back-action; the remaining terms bound the full sine source about the twist. These are global Lipschitz estimates, not a tangent reduction. The fixed declaration gives Z<1/8000. Even the looser substitution Z<=1/4000 proves

\[ |J-\widehat J|\le \frac{47003}{1930258022400000000}<2^{-44}<\frac\eta{100}. \tag{13} \]

This establishes overlap of actual allowed noisy records, not just overlap of two outer enclosures: the common record (J+Jhat)/2 requires opposite errors of magnitude |J-Jhat|/2<=eta in the two models. Hence no uniformly error-robust discriminator exists for this pulse, scalar observation and declared error class. It does not assert equality of the noiseless responses, equality for every error realization, or impossibility for another experiment. The matrix separation in (10) remains valid. It cannot be attributed to a resolved phase-organization effect by this observation.

docs.title: Independent preparation cannot be inferred from energy and winding
docs.text:
Within an independently admitted centered collar, L>=I on neutral forms and phases gives

\[ E_r\ge\tfrac12\|U\|^2+\tfrac1{10}\|\theta\|^2, \qquad (\|U\|+\|\theta\|)^2\le12E_r. \tag{14} \]

Thus an independent E_r<=delta^2/12 certificate is sufficient there, with separate sensor admission. It does not establish the collar itself or make phase-dependent energy an independently available reading.

There is a global counterexample even with exact target energy. Set winding w=1, kappa=2*pi/5, U=z=0 and choose oriented gaps

\[ d(q)=\left(q,\frac{2\pi-q}{4},\frac{2\pi-q}{4}, \frac{2\pi-q}{4},\frac{2\pi-q}{4}\right), \quad V(q)=5-\cos q-4\cos((2\pi-q)/4). \tag{15} \]

At q=kappa+rho, the local bound used in (3) gives V(q)-V_*>=rho^2/8=1/800>0. At the limiting endpoint q=pi, V(pi)=6-2*sqrt(2)<16/5, whereas V_*=(25-5*sqrt(5))/4>55/16; hence V(pi)-V_*<-19/80. Continuity supplies a q0 in (kappa+rho,pi) with exactly V(q0)=V_*. All five gaps are in (0,pi) and sum to 2*pi, so winding remains one. Reconstruct a continuous lift by cumulative gaps and subtract its perturbation mean. This preserves the gaps and places both states on the same mean leaf.

The constructed state and the prepared twist have identical zero nodal and sensor voltages, winding, means and total own storage, yet the constructed state lies outside the required collar. Its existence follows without locating a root or evaluating a trajectory. Consequently these aggregate preparation quantities cannot globally certify the local phase prior.

docs.title: Physical dictionary and method evidence
docs.text:
Under the separately supplied electrical reference, choose c,g,a0>0 and r=c_J/c. The laboratory clock is tau=b*t_lab, with both clocks zero at observation start. With P the neutral projector, retain

\[ C_{\rm phys}=cL^++c_JL,\quad G=gP,\quad b=4g/c,\quad v_0=a_0b\gamma/4,\quad V=v_0LU,\quad j=a_0\gamma^2g^2/c,\quad I_{\rm ext}=cv_0bf. \tag{16} \]

A series resistor-capacitor branch across the v port has capacitor voltage V_s=v0*z, conductance g_s and capacitance C_s. Its exact dictionary is

\[ k=\frac{g_s}{cb}=\frac{g_s}{4g},\qquad \tau_s=\frac{bC_s}{g_s},\qquad k\tau_s=\frac{C_s}{c}. \tag{17} \]

Thus the fixed candidate requires g_s=g/16 and C_s=c/65536. Kirchhoff's current equation and the capacitor equation give (1), including loading. The physical storage scale is c*v0^2=a0*j, so physical sensor energy is C_s*V_s^2/2 and (2) transforms with the same clock as every row. These equalities specify a conditional component model; they do not establish its fabrication or accuracy. Any subsequent voltmeter loading must also be admitted rather than silently removed.

The physical mean is J_lab=v0*J over t_window=T/b. If the stipulated structural error eta is to cover a uniform mean-voltage error e_V, a necessary compatibility condition is

\[ e_V\,t_{\rm window}\le\frac{a_0\gamma T\eta}{4}. \tag{18} \]

Slowing b alone leaves this product unchanged. For the conventional supplied Josephson conversion a0=h/(4*pi*e), it is approximately 3.7254e-31 V s at the declared T and eta. The exact SI constants h and e come from NIST SP 330, Section 2. They are not derived from TNFR. Equation (18) is a requirement of this protocol, not a noise floor, uncertainty principle or universal impossibility theorem. Independent timing, input, transfer and parameter errors would also need their own propagated allowances before using (9) as a physical prediction.

The Keithley measurement handbook describes resistance, bias and capacitive loading (Section 2.2.1), bandwidth and settling (2.6.4), finite integration (3.2.8), and distinct accuracy/uncertainty/noise considerations (1.4.2-1.4.4). These support modeling sensor state and averaging. They do not certify this exact one-pole law, the full C5 preparation or the joint deterministic error bound. The source receipt records reviewed sections and limits. It claims web-text review, not archived source bytes, measured arrays, admitted apparatus or an evaluated response.

docs.title: Reusable consequence and remaining question
docs.text:
The detached exact bound uses shared loaded-pulse admission for the pulse and preparation primitives, sensor energy, forced growth and identity bound. It separately admits the observation error and short-window norm denominator, then rebuilds the response bounds in (3)-(13). Its independent controls check matrix gain, sensor storage, convolution coefficients, arithmetic domains, preparation obstruction and the physical scaling. This private proof consumer installs no runtime law or SDK pathway. Earlier frozen protocols and responses retain their original models and budgets.

The short-window mean supplies a scoped obstruction and reusable sensor accounting. The subsequent recovery-area result conditionally distinguishes restoring phase feedback from the same calibrated passive linear response under a separately declared observation and error contract. It does not identify a unique restoring law or supply independent physical preparation and measurement. Repeating the short-window mean with tighter arithmetic does not supply those missing premises. The sole active task and its acceptance conditions remain in the execution plan.

docs.title: Integrated sensor response during prepared-pattern recovery
Declared finite recovery question
docs.text:
The loaded-window result resolves matrix response but proves overlap with a matched phase-blind reference during its short pulse. This candidate keeps that complete loaded law, pulse and sensor, and changes the observation to a signed integral covering recovery. The research program owns admission. The form/phase memory identities motivate retaining the endpoint information exactly; their decay coefficients are not transferred to the loaded model.

Let L be the unit C5 Laplacian, v=(1,-1,0,0,0), W_r=I+r*L^2, gamma=1/(1023*pi), and keep the declared normalized clock tau, unit held capacities, circular phases and continuous centered perturbation lift theta about winding w=+1 or w=-1. The complete law is

\[ W_r U'=(-LU+\gamma S(\Phi))/4+f-kv(y-z),\qquad \Phi'=\gamma LU/4,\qquad \tau_s z'=y-z,\qquad y=v^TLU. \]

The alternative omits the sine-current branch, consumes only U and z, and retains the same r, U(0), z(0), input, clock and sensor. It is the passive linear reference of the preceding owner, not a different response matrix.

Primitive Fixed analytical declaration Response family Fixed r in [1/100,1/10] in both models Preparation sum(U(0))=sum(theta(0))=0, ||U(0)||_2+||theta(0)||_2<=delta=2^-26, |z(0)|<=delta_s=2^-26; same lifted winding chart as the preceding owner Input f=a*v for 0<=tau<=T, then zero; a=1/16, T=2^-10 Sensor k=1/64, fixed tau_s=T throughout pulse and recovery Observation Raw signed area A_H=integral_0^H z(tau) d tau; no endpoint correction or phase reading is added to the observable Horizon H=T+D, with fixed recovery duration D=2^40 in the declared structural clock Error One independently bounded additive area error |e_A|<=eta_A=2^-18, separately for each candidate; this is an integral error, not an instantaneous reading allowance Identity Full-law phase gaps remain within rho=1/10 of their prepared twist during pulse and recovery Finite criterion Whole-preparation permitted area intervals for the full and phase-blind models are disjoint with gap >2^-14, uniformly over the declared r family Calculation Exact inequalities and rational decay bounds from the complete nonlinear loaded law; no trajectory, response fit, parameter scan or physical dataset

This analytical declaration supplies no laboratory realization of the very long structural horizon or the area-error bound. Physical preparation, input/clock/matrix calibration, sensor drift/loading and joint coverage remain independent obligations. The exact electrical dictionary must be used to translate the integral and horizon together.

A successful comparison would distinguish these two declared complete laws. It would not uniquely identify winding, a sine constitutive law, material constituents or TNFR among all models with restoring state. In particular, the endpoint identity must be checked for alternative restoring potentials, not treated as a unique signature of the prepared winding pattern.

Earlier declarations, source receipts, responses and producers remain frozen. No law is installed in the runtime and no fine-node acquisition is inherited.

docs.title: Finite nonlinear result
docs.text: Declaration revision 46df23f1 fixes the candidate above. The area intervals are disjoint by more than 2^-14 under those premises. The proof combines exact integrated evolution rows with a new decay estimate for the actual loaded nonlinear law. It evaluates no trajectory or physical response. The result distinguishes restoring phase feedback from the declared passive phase-blind reference. A separate countermodel below prevents interpreting that distinction as unique identification of sine dynamics or winding.

docs.title: Pulse admission and shared preparation
docs.text:
Retain the loaded storage and pulse bounds:

\[ E_s=\tfrac12U^TLW_rU+V(\Phi)-V_*+\tfrac{k\tau_s}{2}z^2, \qquad E_s'=-\tfrac14\|LU\|^2-k(y-z)^2+(LU)^Tf. \tag{1} \]

The unchanged pulse gives E_s(T)<=Ebar<2^-16, and its first-exit argument preserves max|Dtheta|<1/10 throughout the pulse and all later unforced time. Here Ebar includes initial sensor energy and the allowance 2*a^2*T; it is not delivered work. The full preparation cost still includes V_*. There is no event or state reset at pulse release. After release the supplied work is zero and the sum of the two continuous losses over any recovery interval is at most Ebar, by (1) and nonnegative excess storage within the retained collar.

The common preparation calculation (4+32*r_max)*delta^2, collar radius and barrier now have one shared owner. The unloaded and loaded consumers retain distinct observations, gains, sensor terms and balances. A separate loaded-pulse owner re-admits the seven pulse primitives and rebuilds sensor energy, forced growth and identity. Both observation consumers use this energy calculation; recovery requires no short-window gain or mean-response interval. The energy bound itself does not require the short-window norm denominator to be positive. Passing H as the pulse horizon would change the supplied pulse and sensor law: sensor time remains tau_s=T=2^-10 throughout recovery.

docs.title: A decay estimate that retains the sensor
docs.text:
Put q=LU, d=y-z, sigma=k*tau_s=2^-16, and N=||U||^2+||theta||^2+sigma*z^2. On the admitted centered collar, I<=L<=4I on the neutral space, I<=W_r<=(13/5)I, and

\[ \tfrac1{10}\|\theta\|^2\le V-V_*\le2\|\theta\|^2, \qquad \theta^T\nabla V\ge\tfrac15\|\theta\|^2. \tag{2} \]

These use the full phase potential's Hessian throughout the collar, not just the tangent at the twist. N and the modified energy below use the fixed normalized chart; they are not additional physical observables or invariant metrics. Define

\[ \mathcal F=E_s+ \gamma\theta^T(W_rU+\sigma vz)+\tfrac12\|\theta\|^2. \tag{3} \]

The sensor-corrected quantity obeys (W_rU+sigma*v*z)'=-q/4-gamma*grad(V)/4 after release. The derivative of the last term in (3) cancels the mixed theta^T*q term. Thus, exactly along the full nonlinear recovery,

\[ \mathcal F'=-\tfrac14\|q\|^2-kd^2+ \tfrac{\gamma^2}{4}U^TLW_rU+ \tfrac{\gamma^2\sigma}{4}yz- \tfrac{\gamma^2}{4}\theta^T\nabla V. \tag{4} \]

This cancellation uses the actual matrix input and sensor state. A cross term inserting L^+ before the nonlinear potential gradient would need a further sign proof; its matrices need not commute.

For completeness, E_s+||theta||^2/2 lies between N/2 and 26*N/5. Since ||v||=sqrt(2)<3/2, the absolute mixed term in (3) is at most (23/10)*gamma*N<N/4. Consequently

\[ N/4\le\mathcal F\le8N. \tag{5} \]

Also U^TLW_rU<=(13/5)||q||^2 and yz=y^2-yd<=3||q||^2+d^2/2. Applying gamma<1/3000 and the fixed sensor coefficients to (4) gives

\[ \mathcal F'\le-\|q\|^2/8-kd^2/2-\gamma^2\|\theta\|^2/20. \tag{6} \]

Because z=y-d, one has N<=2||q||^2+||theta||^2+2*sigma*d^2. Equations (5)-(6) therefore imply

\[ \mathcal F'\le-\gamma^2N/20 \le-\gamma^2\mathcal F/160 \le-2^{-32}\mathcal F. \tag{7} \]

The last inequality uses gamma>1/4096, following from pi<4. These coefficients belong to this loaded C5 model and its fixed collar and sensor. Earlier reciprocal-potential energy methods motivate (3); their different-law coefficients are not reused as certificates.

At pulse release, N(T)<=10*Ebar, so F(T)<=80*Ebar. At any later duration D, let n=floor(D/2^32). Since exp(-n)<=2^-n,

\[ N(T+D)\le320\overline E\,2^{-n}<2^{-7-n}. \tag{8} \]

The phase-blind reference has its own storage E_L=Uhat^T*L*W_r*Uhat/2+sigma*zhat^2/2 and loss E_L'=-||qhat||^2/4-k*dhat^2. With N_L=||Uhat||^2+sigma*zhat^2, the bounds N_L/2<=E_L<=8*N_L and N_L<=2||qhat||^2+2*sigma*dhat^2 give E_L'<=-E_L/64. The same forced growth allowance bounds E_L(T)<=Ebar. It therefore satisfies the weaker common endpoint envelope (8) as well. No phase coordinate is invented for this reference.

An entirely rational norm bound follows without an exponential evaluator or a trajectory grid:

\[ \chi=2^{-\lfloor(n+7)/2\rfloor},\qquad \|U_H\|,\ \|\theta_H\|,\ \|\widehat U_H\|\le\chi, \qquad |z_H|,|\widehat z_H|\le256\chi. \tag{9} \]

For the declared D, n=256 and chi=2^-131. This is a conservative finite deadline, not an optimized settling time or a proposed laboratory duration. The rational tail avoids losing small bounds to a fixed absolute interval grid. The detached consumer limits n to 4096 as an arithmetic-work policy; that limit is not a physical restriction or a failed convergence claim.

docs.title: Exact finite area and separation
docs.text:
Integrating the live phase and sensor rows gives, at every finite H,

\[ A_H=\frac4\gamma v^T(\theta_H-\theta_0) -\tau_s(z_H-z_0). \tag{10} \]

This is an identity for the raw sensor integral. It neither adds a phase measurement nor deletes sensor endpoint memory from the proof. Integrating the actual phase-blind form row, with the same pulse, gives separately

\[ \widehat A_H=8aT+4v^TW_r(U_0-\widehat U_H) -(1+8k)\tau_s(\widehat z_H-z_0). \tag{11} \]

In particular, the factor 1+8k retains the sensor's back-action as well as its observation memory. Omitting either changes this identity. Use the common endpoint envelope (9) and define

\[ \begin{aligned} b_F&=6(4096)\delta+\tau_s\delta_s +[6(4096)+256\tau_s]\chi,\\ b_L&=6(13/5)\delta+(1+8k)\tau_s\delta_s +[6(13/5)+(1+8k)256\tau_s]\chi. \end{aligned} \tag{12} \]

The permitted observed record sets are enclosed by

\[ \mathcal A_F=[-b_F-\eta_A,b_F+\eta_A],\qquad \mathcal A_L=[8aT-b_L-\eta_A,8aT+b_L+\eta_A]. \tag{13} \]

For the frozen candidate, exact rational arithmetic yields

\[ \inf\mathcal A_L-\sup\mathcal A_F =8aT-b_F-b_L-2\eta_A>2^{-14}. \tag{14} \]

One coarse check is that the input area minus the full-law initial-phase allowance is 2^-13, the remaining initial allowances sum to less than 2^-22, the two observation errors sum to 2^-17, and the two terminal allowances sum to less than 2^-115. These bounds imply (14) without sampling a trajectory or fitting a gain. The result holds over the entire declared preparation and r interval, not only at exact twist initialization.

At exact zero perturbation and sensor preparation, (10) tends to zero as recovery completes, while (11) tends to 8aT=1/2048. The positive early sensor response of the earlier theorem is therefore followed by a negative signed contribution in the full model. This compensation is a consequence of return to the same phase lift and the complete sensor law. A small late value of z by itself would not certify that accumulated area. Signed voltage area and dissipated energy have different units and balances; the late sign reversal is consistent with both nonnegative losses in (1).

docs.title: What the area identifies, and what it leaves unresolved
docs.text:
A distinct restoring law shares the decisive endpoint property. In the declared local lift, replace V-V_* by Q(theta)=cos(2*pi/5)*theta^T*L*theta/2 and its sine source by -cos(2*pi/5)*L*theta. Keep both evolution rows, W_r and the sensor. This local quadratic law matches the twist and its full tangent but differs from the nonlinear sine field away from that state. It consumes phase information and is not the phase-blind reference of (11). The law is declared on the retained local lift; it is not a globally periodic potential.

Its own potential satisfies the same collar Hessian bounds, so its own storage, trapping and calculation (3)-(9) apply. For matched initial states, the initial terms of (10) agree exactly between the sine and quadratic laws. Their finite areas differ by at most twice the full terminal allowance in (12), less than 2*eta_A at the declared horizon. Their actual permitted records overlap by the midpoint-error construction. Thus this area detects restoring feedback relative to the calibrated phase-blind alternative, but does not uniquely select the sine law or its nonlinearity. The two winding signs also retain the same bounds. Further physical identification must state which property and which alternative it intends to distinguish.

docs.title: Physical scaling and remaining admission
docs.text:
Under the existing electrical dictionary, tau=b*t_lab, V_s=v0*z and v0=a0*b*gamma/4. The laboratory voltage area and its corresponding error requirement are

\[ \mathcal A_{\rm lab}=\int_0^{H/b}V_s(t)\,dt =\frac{a_0\gamma}{4}A_H,\qquad \varepsilon_{\rm area}\le\frac{a_0\gamma}{4}\eta_A. \tag{15} \]

Changing b rescales duration and voltage together; it does not change this area conversion. The integral allowance is a new observation premise with different units from the short-window mean-error allowance. Neither implies the other.

docs.title: Operational admission of the frozen candidate
docs.text: Physical status: not admitted. Experimental evaluation: not tested. The review below concerns direct voltage-area measurement with the supplied Josephson conversion and voltage-only initialization checks. Its published instrument error allowance does not certify the frozen integral error, while those initialization checks cannot establish the full phase preparation. These are separate scoped obstructions. They preserve the conditional theorem and do not establish a universal physical impossibility or an experimental rejection of either law.

docs.title: Clock, duration and joint residual error
docs.text:
Let p denote the laboratory pulse duration and h the total observation duration, avoiding confusion with Planck's constant h_P. The unchanged candidate and sensor imply

\[ p=T/b,\qquad h=H/b=Rp,\qquad R=H/T=1+2^{50},\qquad (\tau_s)_{\rm lab}=p. \tag{16} \]

If an independently admitted input-delivery mode requires p>=p_min>0, and preparation, calibration and measurement coverage hold only through h_max, any compatible b must satisfy

\[ H/h_{\max}\le b\le T/p_{\min},\qquad Rp_{\min}\le h_{\max}. \tag{17} \]

This constrains delivery of the actual input, not sampling of its short pulse. A continuous integrator need not resolve that pulse in separate samples. Conversely, a finite rise time requires a justified input-error bound; a nominal pulse-width setting does not realize the ideal rectangular current exactly.

For the supplied conversion a0=h_P/(4*pi*e), the SI defining constants give h_P=6.62607015e-34 J s and e=1.602176634e-19 C exactly. Then

\[ C_A=\frac{a_0\gamma}{4} =\frac{h_P}{16(1023)\pi^2e},\qquad B_A=C_A\eta_A=\frac{h_P}{1023\,2^{22}\pi^2e} \simeq9.7658568\,10^{-26}\ {\rm V\,s}. \tag{18} \]

The nominal phase-blind area is C_A/2048, approximately 1.2500297e-23 V s; the proved structural gap corresponds to more than 1.5625371e-24 V s. These are unit translations, not measured responses. The physical constants and Josephson reference remain supplied premises.

Suppose an independent residual-error model after calibration has |offset(0)|<=e0 and |offset'(t)|<=d0. Over [0,h], its sharp worst-case absolute integrated error is e0*h+d0*h^2/2, attained by aligned affine offset and drift. Allocating the entire integral allowance to these errors would require

\[ e_0h+\tfrac12d_0h^2\le B_A, \qquad e_0Rp_{\min}+\tfrac12d_0(Rp_{\min})^2\le B_A. \tag{19} \]

For constant offset alone, e0*p_min<=B_A/R, approximately 8.6738233e-41 V s. As a scale illustration only, a 1 ns minimum delivered pulse entails an observation longer than 1.1258999e6 s and requires a residual constant-offset bound below 8.6738233e-32 V even if it consumes the whole allowance. Neither value is a hardware specification or a fundamental noise floor. This calculation assumes the stated error class; it does not assert that all noise accumulates coherently.

Independent calibration can subtract a known offset, but its residual and drift still need joint coverage. A final small voltage cannot certify a small accumulated error. A gain error, gate-timing error, sensor loading, input tracking or uncertain matrix changes further terms and cannot be assigned the same full allowance simultaneously. Finite-time calibration uncertainty is not an admitted perturbation of the exact dynamical law. Changing the horizon, using paired pulses or resetting/subtracting part of the response requires a new observation or input declaration and proof.

docs.title: Independent preparation information
docs.text:
The voltage map V=v0*L*U and sensor voltage V_s=v0*z contain no initial relative-phase information. This fails even locally: at U=z=0, both theta=0 and theta=2*delta*(e_0-e_1) have identical voltage readings and winding and lie in the retained collar, while only the first satisfies ||U||+||theta||<=delta. The equal-energy counterexample separately prevents zero voltage, winding and target storage from globally certifying the collar. Allowing the reference law to omit phase does not remove the full law's preparation obligation.

A phase-sensitive measurement or independently validated preparation process must therefore bound the missing relative coordinates without using the reserved recovery area. Any reading's loading, disturbance, uncertainty and transport to pulse start belong to that certificate. A winding label does not replace the four relative phases, and an acquired 45-node source does not transfer to this supplied C5 matrix law without its own reduction and state-error proof. Common phase origin can be quotiented; response-relevant relative phase cannot.

For example, admit the neutral form leaf, a calibrated v0>=v_min>0, projected nodal voltage estimate Vhat, sensor estimate Vshat and an independently admitted centered perturbation lift thetahat. Let their joint errors at pulse start be bounded in the respective Euclidean/absolute norms by eps_V, eps_s and eps_theta. Since ||L^+||_2<1 on C5, sufficient bounds are

\[ B_U=\frac{\|P\widehat V\|+\varepsilon_V}{v_{\min}},\qquad B_\theta=\|\widehat\theta\|+\varepsilon_\theta,\qquad B_s=\frac{|\widehat V_s|+\varepsilon_s}{v_{\min}}, \quad B_U+B_\theta\le\delta,\quad B_s\le\delta_s. \tag{20} \]

This is a sufficient information contract, not a constructed phase sensor. Alternatively, independently admitted oriented phase gaps around the chosen twist give d=Dtheta; after checking their circular branches and cycle consistency, L>=I on the neutral space yields ||theta||<=||d||. A bound on their estimate and joint error can therefore supply B_theta. The phase origin need not be measured, but neither a winding integer nor a single gap replaces the full relative-state bound. Separate marginal confidence statements are not the joint coverage required by (20).

docs.title: Reviewed direct-area method and scope of the decision
docs.text:
The Lake Shore 480 manual, Sections 2.1.1 and 4.6.1, describes continuous voltage integration in DC non-peak mode. Section 8.9.6 calibrates it using an independently measured terminal voltage and the specified burst duration. This is a relevant direct-area method. Sections 5.9.1 and 5.9.3 distinguish pre-run drift estimation from DriftTrak, which treats sufficiently small changes as drift. Unmodeled tracking can therefore remove a slow contribution of the intended recovery signal. Resetting, taking peaks or using AC RMS also changes the frozen statistic; these modes do not automatically preserve its signed integral.

The published DC specifications give an offset allowance of +/-10 microvolt seconds plus integrator drift and a gain allowance of +/-0.25% of reading below 10 V s/s. The quoted drift, +/-1 microvolt second/minute, applies on the 300 mV s range with 100 kilohms input resistance at constant temperature. The offset allowance alone is more than 10^20 times B_A. This published error envelope cannot establish the frozen requirement; it is not a lower bound on actual error or all possible instruments. No long-term drift extrapolation is used. The ground-referenced, finite-resistance input also requires a loading and grounding model when attached to the retained sensor.

The Keithley measurement handbook, Sections 3.2.3-3.2.4, 3.2.8 and 3.3.2, separately explains application zero, drift, periodic-noise rejection and reversal/offset-compensated sequences. These methods do not supply joint coverage of this uninterrupted signed area. In particular, treating the predicted late signal as a measured zero would use the reserved response to calibrate away a candidate difference.

The source receipt records reviewed primary sections and their limits. This is web-text review, not archived source bytes, measured arrays or an apparatus calibration. The reviewed direct-area route supplies neither the required error coverage nor independent complete preparation. The local preparation counterexample also survives arbitrary improvement of voltage precision. Thus the scoped operational review closes without admitting a physical evaluation. Other independently justified observation/preparation methods remain possible; they cannot inherit this candidate's admission or alter its frozen premises.

docs.title: Implementation and verification boundary
docs.text:
The detached recovery consumer rebuilds the shared pulse energy bounds, admits recovery duration and integral error, and calculates (8)-(14) with normalized exact arithmetic. Its fixed law and pulse are explicit; changing them requires a new proof. A shorter duration or larger error can leave separation unavailable without proving a physical collision. The independent controls check the complete modified-energy derivative, sensor endpoint factors, nonlinear collar constants, alternative restoring law, arithmetic boundaries and laboratory-unit cancellation. Frozen producers and responses are not run.

The same controls check the clock-independent requirements, sharp residual offset/drift bounds and preparation-information obstruction. They do not evaluate an instrument or turn a published specification into a measured error. Frozen producers and earlier source receipts remain unchanged.

The sole queue records this scoped closure and selects the next foundational question. Physical preparation and observation remain dependencies of a future physical test; more trajectory precision would not supply those missing premises.

docs.title: Passive transport measurement protocol
docs.text:
Scope: a supporting measurement/error contract for two declared pure-EPI transport models. Physical admission is not_admitted; an admitted physical prediction has not been tested. The research program owns P1-P5 and any reopening. No data search, acquisition or refit is active.

The mathematical candidates below remain useful with their own hypotheses. Their observation maps are proposed realizations, not identification of primitive EPI with every sensor reading or proof of material emergence. The user has a computer and no laboratory apparatus; apparatus descriptions are requirements for a matching public terrestrial source, not purchase tasks.

The archived source reviews and Volts experiment preserve inspected-source metadata, rejected routes, source hashes and the unfavorable affine-control comparison. The separate TCLab record retains its own model and evaluated data. These observations cannot become unseen again.

docs.title: Historical source and experiment routes
docs.text: These earlier anchors refer to the archived review and experiment, not additional current tasks.

docs.title: Derived fixed-reference candidate
docs.text:
On the same fixed symmetric positive P2 support, select pure EPI pressure and capacities (nu,0), with nu>0. All other pressure channels are inactive; otherwise the capacity difference itself could contribute another channel. The canonical nodal equation gives

p = (r-x, x-r),           x' = nu*(r-x),           r' = 0
d = x-r,                 d' = -nu*d
x(t) = exp(-nu*t)*x(0) + (1-exp(-nu*t))*r.

This follows from the nodal law without importing the circuit or cooling equation. The arithmetic mean is NOT conserved; the reference r is. An inactive node may retain nonzero pressure: stationarity is not structural equilibrium. The existing diffusion energy owner accepts degenerate mobility; positive-capacity certificates using d_i/nu_i do not cover this boundary.

Physical use requires an independently specified constant reference and support, adequate state observation and bounded external loading. Flat bath measurements do not prove that a bath is a zero-capacity TNFR node; an active controller may instead be an external input. A varying reference requires a distinct driven model and its complete input history, not a fitted final asymptote. No held-out value may estimate r or the clock conversion.

For this candidate, existing log/exp enclosures can be reused with contrast x-r and decay factor exp(-nu*t). The capacity ratio divides by elapsed time, not twice elapsed time. There is no constant-mean rejection rule. Do not fabricate a second observed channel or reuse the equal-capacity adapter unchanged. The mathematical implementation now lives in p2_transport_reference.py: bound_fixed_reference_capacity and bound_fixed_reference_transport reuse the same contrast/log, decay/exp and convex interval kernels as the equal- capacity model. The reference may be a declared interval and the initial contrast may have either strict sign. The returned outer intervals do not prove one common latent fit. These functions do not mutate a live graph or admit empirical observations. Physical admission still requires the source contract; this remains one candidate within P2.3, not another queue.

docs.title: Reference apparatus and canonical equal-capacity prediction
docs.text:
The reference design uses two nominally equivalent capacitive elements, observed simultaneously, prepared separately and then interconnected through one fixed passive link. Charging sources are disconnected before the declared observation interval. Record wiring, switch timing, sensor input loading, component characterization and ambient conditions. Equivalence and negligible external forcing over the finite interval require measured bounds; component labels alone do not establish them. The initial experiment changes only the prepared contrast, keeping the link and apparatus fixed.

The hardware is a candidate realization, not an imported circuit law. The proposed TNFR model is the isolated EPI channel on fixed P2 support, with one common positive capacity and no active phase or capacity-feedback channel. Each physical voltage is mapped to a signed EPI coordinate x_i by a fixed sensor scale and offset. Both channels must share the same structural unit after independently calibrated sensor correction. Define structural time by t = b * (tau - tau_0), where tau is the independently checked acquisition clock and b > 0 is fixed before capacity estimation. A declared unit convention for b is permitted if labeled as a convention; it is not evidence of a universal physical-to-structural conversion.

The canonical diffusion owner then gives, without using a circuit governing law as an axiom,

p_1 = x_2 - x_1,                 p_2 = x_1 - x_2
dx_1/dt = nu * p_1,              dx_2/dt = nu * p_2,       nu > 0
m = (x_1 + x_2)/2,               d = x_1 - x_2
dm/dt = 0,                      dd/dt = -2 * nu * d
d(t) = d(0) * exp(-2 * nu * t)
x_1(t) = m(0) + d(t)/2,          x_2(t) = m(0) - d(t)/2

These are predictions of the stated nodal model. Pressure is calculated from the two observed coordinates, never defined as a measured derivative divided by fitted capacity. Only the product nu * b is identifiable from a physical-time contrast trace if both are unknown. Fixing the clock bridge is therefore an admission condition, not a second fit parameter. Estimate one positive nu from calibration runs alone and freeze its uncertainty set. Nonpositive or unidentifiable capacity blocks this positive-capacity model; it is not clipped into its domain.

For P2, uniformly scaling the single positive edge weight leaves L_rw unchanged. Changing a resistor or link strength cannot be represented merely by rescaling that edge at fixed capacity. This first protocol consequently does not sweep link strength or infer a universal relation between capacity and hardware component values. An intervention is a recorded preparation, not automatically a canonical glyph or a U3 certificate.

docs.title: State, clock and measurement admission
docs.text:
Item Required frozen specification Current missing evidence State map Two sensor identities; common EPI unit; fixed offsets/scales; range and linearity bounds Apparatus and sensor calibration absent Time Raw timestamps, synchronization/skew bounds, finite positive bridge, origin rule and gap policy Physical clock, sampling period and uncertainty absent Support and input Known P2 wiring, fixed link, source disconnection, observation interval and loading/leakage bounds Wiring and external-input characterization absent Capacity Calibration-only common positive rate and identified uncertainty; no outcome-dependent choice No calibration runs Phase Unavailable as an oscillatory observable; phase channel explicitly inactive in the selected model Physical adequacy of that restriction untested State sufficiency Actual generator and observation map; distinguish unknown source terms from measurement noise Model-specific apparatus check pending Reserved observations Disjoint preparation/run IDs, hashes, initial-sample allowance and fixed forecast horizon No acquired runs or reserved data Decision Predeclared joint finite-trajectory acceptance tube, rejection and abstention rules Instrument, calibration and numerical error budgets unset

With both EPI coordinates measured, the selected two-state model has observation matrix C = I. Its algebraic state observability is immediate; this does not prove that the apparatus has only those two relevant states. With contrast alone, the mean is hidden but the contrast equation closes under the common-capacity hypotheses. Do not promote that to a full-state claim. Reuse observability on the actual generator and observation map, and the hidden-source distinction in derived EPI memory if a reduction is proposed. An algebraic rank result supplies neither noise conditioning nor an instrument error bound. A material unmodeled leakage/loading contribution requires a revised admitted model, not a retrospectively invented pressure.

docs.title: Calibration, forecast and finite decision
docs.text:
Use separate whole preparations for calibration and evaluation. Calibration may estimate only the declared common capacity after sensor and clock mapping are fixed. Freeze the fit rule, accepted domain, parameter interval, data identities and code revision. No graph, normalization, filter, channel, capacity, tolerance or horizon is selected using a reserved outcome.

The evaluation initialization allowance is the first synchronized sensor pair, with its uncertainty, at a predeclared forecast origin after the switching interval. Choose this origin from the hardware timing/calibration rule, not from the later relaxation trace. Forecast all subsequent requested timestamps before reading their values. No full-record centering, Hilbert transform, interpolation across unexplained gaps or future-aware smoothing is needed for this prediction.

Primary observation: the held-out contrast trajectory under the frozen capacity and clock bridge. The constant-mean prediction is a separately reported check of the same admitted model, not an ignored nuisance when it fails. Construct a simultaneous finite-trajectory tube from the declared initial-state, sensor, time, capacity and numerical uncertainty. A collection of pointwise confidence intervals is not automatically such a tube. If the uncertainty cannot be bounded at the declared scope, report inconclusive. Exceeding the frozen acceptance rule rejects this mapping on these runs; agreement supports only its declared finite domain. Report every reserved run, including failures, missing samples and exclusions with reasons.

docs.title: Implemented continuous-time uncertainty boundary
docs.text: The numerical part of admission now has an executable owner: p2_transport_reference.py, with measurement/run integration in validation/p2_transport.py. It uses the existing rational logarithm and negative-exponential enclosures; it introduces no pressure term, circuit governing law or new nodal solver. All uncertainty bounds below are supplied hypotheses. Their instrumental justification is still missing and remains a physical admission gate.

docs.title: Continuous capacity, distinct from the Euler control
docs.text:
The earlier P1 finite-increment fit remains an engineering control. Even for an ideal noiseless P2 trajectory sampled at a common structural step h, its fitted coefficient is

nu_Euler = (1 - exp(-2*nu*h)) / (2*h) < nu,     nu>0, h>0.

It cannot be silently relabeled as the continuous physical rate. Irregular pooled increments do not in general have this single-step conversion. The new calibration uses each declared run's fixed first and last samples; interior samples are not fitted, and endpoint consistency does not validate the whole calibration trajectory. Durations and endpoint selection must not be changed after opening reserved outcomes.

After fixed sensor conversion, suppose the initial and final contrast have one resolved common sign. Reverse both signs if negative, giving positive intervals D0=[a,b] and D1=[c,d]. For elapsed structural time T=[sL,sU], sL>0, require resolved decay d/a<1. Then

r = D1 / D0 is enclosed by [c/b, d/a] = [rL,rU]
nu is enclosed by [-log(rU)/(2*sU), -log(rL)/(2*sL)].

Rational log bounds round the interval outward. Initial/final mean intervals must overlap. Each run must resolve nonzero contrast and positive decay; incompatible, sign-ambiguous or unidentifiable inputs raise explicit errors. Intersect all run capacity enclosures. A nonempty intersection is a necessary outer consistency condition, not proof of one joint latent fit. Finally round the capacity bounds outward to binary64 rational endpoints to limit arithmetic growth; a lost positive lower bound or infinite upper bound blocks this path. This computational enclosure is separate from measurement uncertainty.

docs.title: Reserved joint outer tube
docs.text:
P2MeasurementBounds freezes two offsets/scales, total EPI-coordinate errors, timestamp error and a positive structural-time bridge interval. Coordinate errors include uncertainty in the sensor conversion itself. A bound eps_t on each timestamp gives elapsed-time error 2*eps_t; time zero is the same initial event, so its duration interval is exactly zero. Unresolved positive durations are rejected. The declared sensor/clock bounds must hold jointly throughout the full finite experiment; no confidence level is inferred. Both channels in each pair must represent the same latent observation time. Acquisition skew needs synchronization evidence or an independently derived coordinate-error allowance for time alignment. Timestamp error alone cannot align asynchronous channels or justify their constant-mean test.

For capacity in [nuL,nuU] and elapsed time in [tL,tU], the decay lies in [exp(-2*nuU*tU), exp(-2*nuL*tL)], evaluated with rational enclosures. Coordinates use the positive semigroup directly:

x1(t) = ((1+e)*x1(0) + (1-e)*x2(0))/2
x2(t) = ((1-e)*x1(0) + (1+e)*x2(0))/2,   e=exp(-2*nu*t).

Monotonicity in the initial coordinates and corner extrema in e give sound boxes while preserving the mean/contrast dependency. The mean and contrast are also retained as separate observable tests. The shared exponent cap is 4096 and the reference accepts at most 10,000 samples; these are computation guards, not physical constants. Rational output endpoints must not be converted to ordinary floats and called certified bounds.

calibrate_p2_transport checks the known undirected two-node positive edge; forecast_p2_transport consumes only frozen calibration, reserved identities, initial measurements and timestamps. The latter must be a predeclared schedule or clock metadata available without inspecting future response values. write_p2_transport_forecast saves exact rational endpoints as hexadecimal numerator/denominator strings; retain its content hash before opening outcomes. score_p2_transport reuses the whole-acquisition separation and requires that issued hash, matching units/times and unchanged initialization.

Disjoint coordinate, mean or contrast boxes give incompatible_with_declared_bounds. If every outer box overlaps, the result is only not_falsified_by_enclosures: different boxes may admit different latent parameters. That is neither a joint-feasibility proof nor statistical acceptance. The physical status remains not_admitted_by_this_score in both cases. Excessive tube width requires a preregistered resolution/power decision; it cannot become positive evidence just because all observations overlap.

Independent analytic/Decimal fixtures and wrong-mean, wrong-identity and changed-forecast controls exercise this boundary. These are software/model tests, not measured data. Existing manifest/sidecar owners can bind the saved bytes without acquiring a second evidence ledger. P1's Euler tests and their historical checkpoint remain unchanged.

docs.title: Proposed pilot resources, not instrument tolerances
docs.text:
The following are provisional engineering caps for admission planning. They do not authorize acquisition with unresolved physical tolerances and are not TNFR constants or a statistical power calculation. Under the computer-only constraint these apparatus/preparation rows are requirements a matching public archive would need to document, not tasks for the user to build or acquire equipment.

Resource Proposed cap and stop rule Apparatus One P2 setup, two synchronized observation channels, one unchanged link Preparations Two calibration runs at one nonzero prepared contrast; two held-out contrast conditions with three independent preparations each: eight total Record size At most 10,000 paired samples per run and 100 MiB for the complete raw/calibration/prediction bundle Acquisition duration At most 30 minutes per run; choose a shorter fixed horizon only from apparatus/calibration evidence before held-out acquisition Data search/download This metadata review is complete. Before any later signal download, pin exact files and compressed/expanded bounds; proposed pilot caps 100 MiB compressed and 250 MiB expanded Computation One frozen calibration specification and one prediction per reserved preparation; no automatic refitting or larger campaign after rejection/inconclusiveness

Sampling interval, voltage/temperature limits, switch settling allowance, clock accuracy, sensor skew, error bars and acceptance thresholds remain unset. They must be supplied by the selected instrument and calibration, not by these sample/storage budgets. If an adequate record cannot fit the caps, revise and version the protocol before observing reserved outcomes.

docs.title: Evidence bundle and current exit gate
docs.text:
Reuse CoreExperimentManifest and EvidenceSidecar. Retain this annex, exact raw/calibration/evaluation file identities, source revision, raw timestamps/masks, immutable fit, forecasts and complete result ledger in one accessible bundle. validate_metadata() checks declarations only; validate_for_admission(root_dir=...) additionally checks real file bytes. Neither establishes physical adequacy, temporal commitment or scientific truth. Preserve an independently auditable pre-evaluation forecast record; a later digest alone cannot prove when a prediction was issued.

Declare the five measurement-provenance questions explicitly: future samples, outcome-derived wiring, fitting on evaluation data, evaluation labels and post-selection. An affirmative answer can describe exploratory evidence but cannot silently become prospective validation. Numerical certificate tolerance is separate from the instrument/statistical budget.

P2 remains not_admitted until one accessible public-data choice resolves the missing table, freezes all tolerances and resources, and passes the state/clock/identifiability gate. Volts remains a historical exploratory record of the earlier fixed-reference model/map pair, not an evaluation of the revised generative candidate and not reserved data for a later redesign. The execution plan owns when this parked branch resumes; another fit to this same curve cannot supply missing apparatus evidence or independent preparations. No apparatus purchase/acquisition is requested. No admitted physical prediction has yet been tested.

docs.title: Regional phase/amplitude measurement contract
docs.text: Status: 2026-09-26; specification complete, physical admission not_admitted, physical prediction not_tested; exact-model data search parked after the bounded review below. This is the observation annex for the derived phase/amplitude candidate. The research program owns scheduling; the existing source inventory owns general dataset descriptions. This document owns the candidate-specific measurement map, resolution criterion and source admission decision. It does not add a simulator, a physical law or a second task queue.

docs.title: 1. What would be measured
docs.text:
The candidate has six scalar states: two equally oriented directed triangles, with reciprocal links between corresponding vertices. All twelve directed edges have unit relative weight. In the engine's row convention, i -> j means node i reads node j; this must not be confused with a physical material-flow arrow. Each row reads two neighbors. Pressure is only p_i=(x_next+x_cross)/2-x_i, capacity is fixed at a>0 or b>0 within each triangle, and dx_i/dt=nu_i*p_i. There are no operator events, Gamma terms, other pressure channels or independently evolving primitive phases.

An admissible observation would supply six simultaneous scalar channels, fixed channel-to-node labels and their directed connection map. Independently calibrated sensor offsets and gains must recover a common scalar chart; they may not be selected to make the predicted phase appear. One conditional electrical chart is

\[ \widehat V_i=(y_i-\beta_i)/g_i,\qquad \widehat x_i=(\widehat V_i-V_{\rm ref})/V_*,\qquad t=(s-s_0)/\tau_*. \]

Here y is the recorded sensor output; beta_i,g_i are independently calibrated instrument offset/gain with g_i!=0, V_ref is a common reference, V_*>0 is a common scale, and s is physical time in seconds. tau_*>0 is a fixed number of seconds per declared structural time unit. A measured temperature or concentration could use an analogous chart, but would need its own constitutive and support admission. This voltage map is a hypothesis for a suitable apparatus, not evidence that such data exist.

For each ordered triangle, apply the already derived orthonormal contrasts:

\[ \mu=(x_0+x_1+x_2)/3,\quad u=(x_0-x_1)/\sqrt2,\quad v=(x_0+x_1-2x_2)/\sqrt6,\quad z=u+iv. \]

Retain both means and both Cartesian contrasts. Where amplitudes are resolved, report r_0=abs(z_0), r_1=abs(z_1), q=r_1/r_0, and delta=Arg(z_1*conj(z_0)). This is a spatial form angle, not a Hilbert phase of one temporal signal, primitive theta, electrical superconducting phase, or a tetrad replacement. A common calibrated offset cancels from each contrast; unequal calibration errors do not. Fixed node ordering determines orientation and may not be permuted after evaluation to improve agreement. No future-dependent filtering, phase unwrapping or numerical differentiation is needed for this instantaneous observation.

docs.title: 2. Constitutive and clock evidence
docs.text:
The nodal product alone does not identify its factors. An apparatus must independently justify the stated pressure row and absence or bounded effect of additional state, leakage, forcing and delays over the declared interval. One conditional linear realization would have a separately verified law

\[ S_i\frac{dV_i}{ds} =G(V_{\rm next}+V_{\rm cross}-2V_i),\qquad \nu_i=2\tau_*G/S_i. \]

S_i is physical storage (capacitance in an electrical realization), not TNFR capacity itself. G is the equal effective directed transfer coefficient; G/S_i has units of inverse seconds. Both the equality of links and the two regional rate classes require independent evidence and error bounds. Measured components or separate calibration preparations may determine these rates; fitting them to the reserved phase response is prohibited. A calibrated effective rate alone does not identify G and S_i separately. Likewise responses in seconds determine a/tau_* and b/tau_*, not an independent absolute structural clock: fix tau_* before calibration instead of fitting redundant clock and capacity scales.

This equation is a prospective apparatus requirement, not a claim that reciprocal resistors implement it. The reciprocity obstruction proves that a passive reciprocal first-order scalar RC/thermal network with positive storage cannot realize this generator even through an invertible linear state chart. Its spectrum is real, while the directed model's contrast spectrum is complex. Nonreciprocal circuitry or directed transport would need its own justified reduction and recorded external operating conditions. An active apparatus may supply energy while its effective state equation is homogeneous; that is not autonomous substrate creation or a derived TNFR energy source. No apparatus construction is scheduled for the computer-only research route.

The graph and its generator must be specified from wiring/transport evidence, not inferred solely from phase correlation. Removing unobserved nodes or selecting six channels from a larger graph requires an exact closed reduction or an independently bounded memory/error term. The existing memory owner supplies that distinction; it does not certify closure for a new dataset.

docs.title: 3. Sensor, amplitude and phase uncertainty
docs.text:
Use the joint-error conventions already specified by P2MeasurementBounds: calibrated coordinate error includes gain/offset error, digitization and any bounded channel skew. Two timestamp errors contribute to an elapsed interval; timestamp accuracy alone does not make different channels simultaneous. Its executable two-node enclosure is not a six-node predictor and is not reused outside that domain.

For one triangle suppose x_hat=x+e, with simultaneous deterministic bounds abs(e_i)<=epsilon_i. Writing the contrast map as z=U^T*x in real two-vector form gives U^T*U=I and U*U^T=I-11^T/3. Consequently

\[ |\widehat z-z|\le\rho,\qquad \rho=\max_{\sigma_i\in\{-1,1\}} \left\|U^T(\sigma_i\epsilon_i)_i\right\|_2 \le\sqrt{\sum_i\epsilon_i^2}. \]

The finite maximum is valid because a convex norm on a box attains a maximum at a vertex. For a common node bound epsilon, the exact box radius is rho=sqrt(8/3)*epsilon: a mixed-sign corner has squared contrast 8*epsilon^2/3, whereas a common-offset corner has zero contrast. This uses simultaneous channel bounds, not an assumption of independent Gaussian sensor noise.

If r_hat=abs(z_hat)>rho, the disk around the observation excludes zero, and

\[ r\in[\widehat r-\rho,\widehat r+\rho],\qquad d_{S^1}(\widehat\psi,\psi)\le \arcsin(\rho/\widehat r). \]

The angular bound follows from the tangent from the origin to that disk. Relative-angle error is at most the sum of the two regional bounds, capped at pi. The ratio lies in [(r_hat_1-rho_1)/(r_hat_0+rho_0), (r_hat_1+rho_1)/(r_hat_0-rho_0)] when both lower amplitudes are positive. If either disk contains zero, the corresponding phase and the relative-angle comparison are unavailable. A ratio bound still exists when the denominator disk excludes zero: use max(0,r_hat_1-rho_1) for its lower numerator. If the denominator disk contains zero, no uniformly defined finite ratio bound follows. Retain Cartesian observations and report the separate availability of angle and ratio. Neither zeroing an unavailable angle nor dropping low-amplitude endpoints after evaluation is permitted.

A design budget must use a justified lower bound on the future observed amplitudes, including initial-state, parameter, clock and observation errors; nominal predicted amplitudes alone do not guarantee resolution. Capacity and clock uncertainty must be propagated jointly through the declared fine generator. Independent solver agreement is not a rigorous enclosure. Any statistical alternative must predeclare joint coverage over the complete comparison; per-sample standard deviations do not imply this deterministic bound. No sensor accuracy has yet been admitted for this candidate.

docs.title: 4. Frozen finite prediction and decision
docs.text:
Use the full six-node initial-state observation and the independently fixed rate/clock information to forecast both models before reading later responses. The comparator freezes q(t)=q_0, where q_0 is the same initial amplitude ratio, with its uncertainty, used by the full model. Its initial ratio interval must have a strictly positive lower bound and a finite upper bound, since the angular comparator uses both q_0 and 1/q_0:

\[ \dot\delta_{\rm fr} =\frac{\sqrt3}{4}(a-b)-\frac12(b/q_0+a q_0)\sin\delta_{\rm fr}. \]

The nominal equal-amplitude, quadrature preparation gives the previously derived acceleration difference, but a real initial record must not be forced to q_0=1,delta_0=pi/2. No subsequent measured amplitude is fed into either forecast. The main observable is the finite circular phase separation, with amplitudes and complete nodal response retained as checks of the full model. Estimating a second derivative from the reserved signal is unnecessary.

Let the two nominal phase forecasts have independently justified error radii B_full and B_fr, including initialization, parameters, clock, admitted model-reduction error and numerical error. Let B_obs bound the relative-angle observation error. A sufficient robust resolution condition is

\[ d_{S^1}(\delta_{\rm full},\delta_{\rm fr}) >B_{\rm full}+B_{\rm fr}+2B_{\rm obs}. \]

This makes the two possible observation tubes disjoint. It is a sufficient design criterion, not evidence that either model is true. Predeclare finite times, run identities, initial-state admission and joint uncertainty before opening reserved responses. At scoring, use circular distances to the two tubes: full-compatible and comparator-incompatible favors the full reduction over that approximation; both compatible is inconclusive; full-incompatible rejects the tested realization or one of its declared premises. Also check the full predicted scalar traces; a coincidental phase match alone does not admit the nodal model. Pointwise compatibility with outer error tubes need not imply that one joint parameter/preparation realization explains the whole record; it means only that this necessary check did not reject it. An unresolved amplitude yields an unavailable angular test, not support for either model. Reserve independent preparations and retain all declared failures and missing observations.

Scale of the already retained mathematical example. At (a,b)=(1,2), z(0)=(1,i)/16, and t=0.5, the existing finite control predicts a phase gap of about 0.05947 radians (3.407 degrees), with full-model amplitudes about 0.036327 and 0.024267 in its chosen EPI chart. This gives a prospective resolution target; it is not 0.5 physical seconds without a clock bridge. For illustration, if future observed amplitudes are independently bounded below by 0.036 and 0.024, a joint node error epsilon<=0.0001 gives B_obs<=0.011341 radians and leaves about 0.03678 radians for the sum of the two forecast error radii. Those lower amplitudes and errors are hypothetical requirements, not instrument specifications or measured performance. Decay eventually destroys angular resolution; waiting indefinitely for the limiting lag is not the proposed test. This distinguishes a full model from a lossy approximation, not TNFR from mathematically equivalent external physics.

docs.title: 5. Existing-source admission decision
docs.text:
The bounded review on 2026-09-26 rechecked source descriptions and apparatus equations, not reserved arrays. The earlier inventory retains licenses, archive sizes and repeat identities. No signal archive was downloaded, no new response scored and no calibration changed in this review. Published qualitative summaries are prior exposure, not blind evidence.

Existing source Finding for this particular candidate Decision TCLab apparatus/model Two measured temperatures; heater states, supplied inputs and ambient exchange enter its model. It does not provide the six measured scalar states or declared directed generator. Not admitted for this prediction. Preserve the separate frozen exploratory comparison; its scored files are not new holdouts. NED3-008 thermal record and README Six thermocouple channels serve a steady-state conductivity apparatus. Channel count does not establish six closed storage nodes, the required directed support or capacities; fresh-conversion timing remains unresolved. Not admitted. A reciprocal scalar conduction realization would additionally face the proved spectral obstruction. This is not a finding about uninspected transient arrays. Rössler record, primary circuit equations The measured second coordinate has hidden-state and local circuit terms besides diffusive coupling. One observed coordinate per three-state oscillator does not close the specified scalar law. Nominal acquisition/filter specs do not supply its state or clock bridge. Not admitted. Neither temporal phase extraction nor selecting six of the 28 channels removes those missing terms or exterior couplings. Analog learning network record and README Published 4x4 free/clamped node snapshots accompany changing gate voltages and learning steps; the stated continuous scope record contains time, input voltage and output voltage. The documented schema does not establish simultaneous six-node free evolution under the fixed directed law. Not admitted. Gate storage is not an independently identified nodal capacity. Admitting another driven/adaptive model would be a separate decision.

The conclusion is restricted: none of the existing inventory admits this particular phase/amplitude test. It does not show that no suitable public dataset exists, that these sources are scientifically useless, or that TNFR is physically refuted. The missing bridge is both constitutive (known closed nonreciprocal scalar dynamics) and observational (joint state, rate, clock and uncertainty evidence). Six sensor traces or oscillatory-looking signals alone would not close it. The protocol is ready to assess a matching source; the physical objective remains open.

The subsequent bounded directed-source review examined six new studies and admitted none for this exact test. That closes the scheduled search and parks this physical experiment; it does not discard the conditional theorem or its observation/error machinery. MOSTR is retained as a deferred three-tank transport lead under the user's collective-emergence priority. Its directed open cascade has different boundaries and spectrum and cannot inherit the present phase-locking prediction. The source inventory owns that candidate's metadata and missing input/measurement dependencies; the plan owns the next action.

docs.title: Boundary for a future primitive-phase information test
docs.text:
This annex's six-state spatial form angle does not identify primitive phase in a different model. Only its calibration, provenance, uncertainty and reserved-evaluation conventions can be reused for that purpose. The first-moment controls are exact algebraic designs, not instruments or noisy measured phasors; their static source equality does not imply equal future trajectories. A finite test must retain the actual support, companion laws, hidden state and phase/rate association. Imposing unit norm or equal moments on noisy readings would not supply an independent preparation.

A preliminary metadata review on 2026-10-06 located Nijholt et al., Emergent hypernetworks in weakly coupled oscillators. Its four-electrode ring uses nonlinear delayed feedback. The authors' data repository describes time in seconds, four electrode potentials and four extracted phases in coupled and uncoupled files. Only published descriptions were inspected; no signal file was downloaded, no reserved prediction frozen and no response scored. The phase/closure bridge, uncertainty and controlled matched preparations are unadmitted. Published descriptions are prior exposure, not blind evidence.

The information theorem also supplies a design restriction: two incident phasors with nonzero sum are determined up to permutation by that sum. At zero sum, the selected sine/cubic currents both cancel by their half-turn symmetry. Thus a degree-two instantaneous equal-moment witness cannot separate those two kernels. This algebraic restriction is not a rejection of the authors' different delayed-feedback model or of all odd currents.

The following metadata remain a supporting source inventory for a future admitted comparison. The execution plan alone selects whether their missing bridges become active work. They supplement the phase-information option; they do not admit this annex's original six-state law, the two-C6 discriminator or a particle model. No raw signal archive was downloaded or decoded in this review. Published methods and qualitative results are prior exposure.

Supporting source Metadata (initial review 2026-10-06) Remaining admission boundary 28 Rössler circuits CC BY 4.0; documented supports and three repetition labels; only the second circuit coordinate is recorded Direct-source admission below closes application of the existing star test. Additional state, a proved invariant preparation or controlled approximation would require separate admission. Two quartz resonators in one differential accelerometer CC0; the 48.7 MB figure archive is part of a 1.17 GB dataset; apparatus identity and size corrected in the 2026-10-16 admission An observed interaction lead only: sustaining dynamics, joint readout/clock and independent acquisition identities remain unadmitted. Two coupled MEMS resonators CC BY 4.0; 125 kHz sensor records, coupling/feedback settings, about 35 GB total with smaller regime archives External driving and feedback remain supplied. No verified independent-repeat allocation or TNFR measurement bridge. Three Rössler circuits with higher-order interactions CC BY 4.0; x/y channels for three oscillators, 30,000 samples per record; one block about 23.5 GB Hidden z coordinates, programmed nonlinear coupling and unverified repeated acquisitions. Interaction order is not a phase-harmonic order.

The four-electrode repository above was inspected at revision fe79902503e59f8fba1c635b5e01518d13b904dc. Its coupled and uncoupled records are not repeated independent acquisitions; cropping a record does not create one. Delayed feedback and the published phase/filter procedure need causal admission, including possible future-sample access. No explicit data license was found in that repository during this inspection.

All candidates retain physical_status=not_admitted and evaluation=not_tested here. An oscillator phase experiment could test a specified effective law; it would not derive that apparatus's material constituents. The collective-property comparison has the main generative scope. The execution plan owns selection; no archive size, available repetition or attractive waveform starts a campaign.

docs.title: Quartz organization: methods admission
docs.text:
Decision, 2026-10-16: an observational lead, with physical_status=not_admitted and evaluation=not_tested. This review concerns the source's own measured organization, not admission of the six-state law above or another direct application of the star test.

The primary paper reports interacting quartz resonators within one differential accelerometer. The Dryad methods and README describe rotation-controlled acceleration at fixed temperature, frequency counters, oscilloscope phase recordings and separate analyzer measurements. Self-sustained operating modes, imposed frequency sweeps and applied shocks are different preparations. Figure/sheet labels do not establish independent reset acquisitions, and some movies are edited.

The version metadata identify version 8, record 332142, under CC0. The file metadata give 48,665,523 bytes for Data_of_figures.zip and 1,172,345,384 bytes in total. The earlier inventory mislabeled the apparatus and treated one archive's size as the whole dataset; neither correction changes a response.

The inspected material does not admit the complete sustaining electronics, feedback, mechanical state, initialization or environment law. Full publisher methods and a circuit supplement were not accessible in this review. That is a source-access limitation, not a mathematical impossibility theorem. Constant controls could permit an autonomous conditional model; sustained oscillation does not establish absence of external energy supply.

A prospective property could be a specified relative-frequency/phase relation and its loss or recovery under an independently declared perturbation. It still needs a source-specific state/readout map, joint timing and instrument uncertainties, and independent whole acquisitions. Separate instrument records cannot simply be assembled into one simultaneous complete state. A reported phase trace is not automatically primitive TNFR phase, and visible locking does not justify discarding amplitude, inertia or controller memory.

docs.title: A precise observation obstruction
docs.text:
This deduction uses the published nominal circuit law, not the measured arrays. Write u=v1, y=v2, w=v3, with fixed support and coupling. The first two circuit rows have the vector form

\[ u'=-d u-e y-f w,\qquad y'=-a u+M y, \qquad M=bI-cL,\qquad a,d,e,f>0, \]

where L is the unnormalized support Laplacian. In physical seconds, the nominal second row is

\[ y_i'=-10000u_i+\frac{44200}{29}y_i +2000\kappa\sum_j A_{ij}(y_j-y_i). \]

Two circuit states can have identical y and different u, hence different y'. The existing closure criterion therefore excludes an autonomous instantaneous law for y alone on an open source-state family. This is not pressure reconstructed from the response: the different derivatives follow from the independently supplied source law.

The same rows give a stronger information result. The unfiltered observation and its first two derivatives determine all three coordinate blocks:

\[ u=(My-y')/a,\qquad w=(y''-My'-ad u-ae y)/(af). \]

Thus the observation map Psi=(y,y',y'') has rank 3N: in state order (y,u,w), its Jacobian is block lower triangular with diagonal I,-aI,afI. The third evolution row can be nonlinear; it does not enter this identity. Suppose a sufficiently smooth autonomous target of dimension m, with smooth initialization J and readout H, reproduced these voltage histories for every source state in an open set and a fixed clock. Its first two output derivatives would factor through J, so rank(DPsi)<=m. Consequently m>=3N. A same-node-count, fixed-capacity form/phase target has only 2N coordinates: 56 instead of 84 for this source. It cannot be an exact open-family realization of the full unfiltered voltage output.

This does not determine the dimension of a recorded attractor, exclude a separately proved invariant preparation family, or rule out approximations, additional nodes/state or causal memory. It also does not identify the filtered recordings with y: filter dynamics and noisy differentiation need their own causal observation model. An extracted temporal phase is not an automatic escape from the state requirement. The source-matching condition must hold for both mapped rows, with an independently admitted clock. The shared observation kernel controls check the block-rank mechanism with exact rational instances; the rank argument above supplies its general scope, not a numerical reconstruction of these data.

docs.title: 1. Source, actual words and complete continuation
docs.text:
Use the complete retained central preparation in weighted_star_registration_episode/preparation.json, admitted by the full-record reader. The existing record is not regenerated. Its central successor has ten ordered nodes, nineteen undirected edges, actual represented conductances, structural time t=7 and two protected original stars (0,...,4) and (5,...,9).
